articles.fullText:
How to track my spending
[Image: Pill Pro]
As a business owner, you're keeping up with a lot, so we made it easy to track your spending on Thumbtack.
Weekly activity
Check your Services to see a breakdown of your activity, including how much you’re spending each week.
[Image: Services spending]
To see your activity in more detail, view your Performance dashboard and check each of your services. This interactive dashboard shows how you compare to other Thumbtack pros so you can make informed decisions about your business’ growth.
Payment history
Your payment history will show you a breakdown of your charges. You’ll see the cost of each lead and any discounts that were applied. Follow these steps to see your payment history:
App
Open the Thumbtack Pro app.
Tap Profile (from the main menu below).
Tap the gear icon (in the top right corner).
Tap Payments.
Tap View your balance and charges.
The Activity tab shows your pending and completed charges for each direct lead, booking, or opportunity. Tap a transaction to see more details.
The Receipts tab is where you can view your receipts. We’ll also list any preloaded balances or prepaid packages here. Receipts may include multiple charges, credits, discounts, and refunds. Tap any charge to view the receipt.
Desktop
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Click your profile photo (in the top right corner).
Select Payments from the drop-down menu.
Below “Activity,” tap a charge to view more details.
The Activity tab shows your pending and completed charges for each direct lead, booking, or opportunity. We’ll show you the amount you paid along with the status of any refund requests or courtesy credit given. Click any transaction to see more details.
The Receipts tab is where you can view and download your receipts. We’ll also list any preloaded balances or prepaid packages here. Receipts may include multiple charges, credits, discounts, and refunds. Click any charge to download and save the detailed receipt. Or click Download at the top of the list to download a CSV file of all your receipts for a specific year or date range.

articles.fullText:
How to take a background check 
[Image: Pill Pro]
Finding a pro they can trust is at the top of every customer’s to-do list when starting a new project. And background checks build that trust and confidence when hiring.
Here’s how to start your background check:
App
Open the Thumbtack Pro app.
Tap Profile (from the main menu below).
Scroll down to the Credentials section.
Next to "Background Check," select Start.
Submit your information.
Desktop
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Go to your Profile.
Scroll down to the Credentials section.
Next to "Background Check," select Start.
Submit your information.
An SSN isn’t required to take a background check on Thumbtack. You can still submit your information using a passport, driver's license, or a government-issued ID from another country.
Pro Tip
All background checks must be submitted by the account owner. If the background check name doesn’t match the account name, the background check won’t be processed.
Getting results
Results typically take 5 - 7 business days to complete (though some may take longer). To check the status of your background check, head back to the Credentials section of your profile.
We’ll email you when we’ve finished processing your results. After the results have been processed and you pass the background check, it can take an additional 1 - 3 business days for a background check badge to appear on your profile. Customers will be able to see this badge displayed on your profile
Why background checks matter
Background checks are free and easy to take, and we handle everything for you. All you need is your Social Security number (SSN) or a photo ID, like a passport or driver's license. Here is a complete list of supported documents (best viewed on your desktop).
Pro Tip
To qualify for Thumbtack Pro Rewards, you need to take a background check.
Frequently asked questions
Do you require pros to take background checks? 
Yes. All account owners must take and pass a criminal background check through a nationally accredited third-party provider when they create a Thumbtack account.
The account owner is responsible for ensuring their employees, contractors, and workers adhere to our Terms of Use and all applicable federal, state, and local laws (including local licensing requirements).
We also conduct continuous checks on an annual basis, which monitor real-time data sources for changes to a person’s record and help us find recent reportable information.
What happens if I don't pass? 
If your background check isn’t clear, your results may affect your eligibility to be on Thumbtack. We look at this on a case-by-case basis.
What if my background check results aren't correct? 
If you have concerns with your results, you can contact us.
It's been over seven business days and I haven't gotten my results. What should I do? 
If you submitted your information and it’s been over seven business days, please contact us.
Ready to boost your credibility?
[Button: Take a background check ]

articles.fullText:
How to sign up for our partner tools and services
[Image: Pill Pro]
Looking for ways to streamline your day-to-day business operations? You’re in the right place. We’re partnering with select services and tools to help you respond faster, grow at your own pace, and optimize your daily operations. You’ll find these tools (and more) on our marketplace, along with exclusive offers just for Thumbtack pros.
Meet our partners
Take a look around our marketplace to read a summary of each partner service and tool. And if you’d like more details before signing up for one, visit their website to learn more.
Pro tip
Some partners have special offers for first-time users. Keep in mind, these offers are only available to Thumbtack pros so you need to sign up using the link in the marketplace to get the offer.
How to sign up
Once you’ve found a partner service or tool in our marketplace you’re interested in, click Sign up. You’ll be taken to that partnership’s website where you can follow the prompts to complete the signup process.
Frequently asked questions
If I have questions about one of the partners, who can I reach out to?
For questions about one of the listed services or tools, you can contact their support team directly. To find their contact info, click the Sign up link from our marketplace, and look for the option to contact support.
How do I get the Thumbtack Offer with a partner?
To take advantage of an offer for Thumbtack pros, you need to sign up with a partner through our marketplace. That’s it!
I’ve already signed up with a partner. Can I still get the new offer?
No, these are only available to Thumbtack pros who sign up with the partner while the offer is available.
Is there a discount available for every partner on the marketplace?  
No. Only some partners are offering discounts at this time. Every partner on our marketplace offers a service or tool we believe could be valuable to our pros, but not every partner has a special offer for Thumbtack pros.
Is Thumbtack making these offers?
No, Thumbtack is connecting you with our partners, but each partner runs their own business independently. Once you sign up or create an account with a partner, you’ll be dealing with them directly, including for customer service inquiries related to the products.
Ready to check out our partnerships?
[Button: Go to our marketplace]

articles.fullText:
How to set up direct deposit
[Image: Pill Pro]
Set up direct deposit to transfer your earnings to your bank. Getting set up usually takes less than five minutes. Earnings get deposited right into your bank account automatically, with no fees. Standard payouts typically take 3 - 4 business days.
Or, choose to have them instantly deposited and receive your funds within 30 minutes for a 1% fee.
What you need before you get started
To set up direct deposit, you must have a Social Security number (SSN). If you’ve registered your business with the IRS, you’ll set up direct deposit as a Company. If that applies to you, also grab your Employer Identification number (EIN).
Pro tip
Direct deposit is required to get paid for claimable jobs.
How to set up your direct deposit
You’ll share some information about your business and verify your identity – this is done through Stripe, our trusted business partner. Stripe will ask for information about:
The individual creating the Stripe account.
The business associated with the Stripe account.
Any individuals who own or control the business
Pro tip
If you selected the wrong kind of business, contact us so we can help.
Follow these steps to set up your direct deposit:
Individual
To set up a direct deposit as an Individual, you’ll use your SSN.
If you are an employee of a company, or you have a business with an EIN, you must select “Company” as your type of business. This makes sure your income is attributed to your business, not you personally.
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
From your Settings, select Earnings.
Click Set up direct deposit.
Select Individual from the options, then Continue.
Log into your Stripe account, if you have one.
Verify your personal details, then click Continue. ID verification may be asked for if we’re not able to verify your details.
Select your bank account to use for payouts, then click Continue.
Connect your bank account with Stripe.
Select which account you want to use for payouts, then click Continue.
Review and submit your details.
You’ll be redirected to Thumbtack while your information is sent for verification.
Company
To set up a direct deposit as a Company, you’ll use your EIN and the last four digits of your SSN. In some cases, you may have to provide your full SSN.
If you don’t have an EIN, select “Individual” as the type of business.
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
From your Settings, select Earnings.
Click Set up direct deposit.
Select Registered company as the type of business, then select the appropriate “business structure” for your company.
Click Continue.
Log into your Stripe account, if you have one.
Enter your Employer Identification Number (EIN), then click Continue.
Verify your personal details, then click Continue. ID verification may be asked for if we’re not able to verify your details.
Select your bank account to use for pa youts, then click Continue.
Connect your bank account with Stripe.
Select which account you want to use for payouts, then click Continue.
Review and submit your details.
You’ll be redirected to Thumbtack while your information is sent for verification.
It can take up to three business days for Stripe to verify your information before you can receive direct deposits. You can review the status of your verification in your Earnings tab.
Tip
Stripe will automatically send you a 1099k for the year when you're paid through Thumbtack Pay.
Ready to get started?
[Button: Set up direct deposit]
How to update your direct deposit
You can update the bank account you want to use for direct deposit by following these steps:
App
Open the Thumbtack Pro app.
Tap Profile (from the main menu below).
Tap the gear icon (in the top right corner).
Tap Earnings.
Tap Update (next to your current deposit account).
Tap Agree and continue.
Select whether to Continue with Link or Not now.
Select a bank to connect.
Follow the prompts to connect your bank account.
Desktop
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Click your profile photo (in the top right corner).
Select Earnings from the drop-down menu.
Click Update (next to your current deposit account).
Click Agree and continue.
Select whether to Continue with Link or Not now.
Select a bank to connect.
Follow the prompts to connect your bank account.
Frequently asked questions
What if there’s an issue with a payment or my direct deposit account?
We’ll notify you if there are any concerns with a payment or your account information.
I accidentally chose the wrong business type. What should I do?
Contact Thumbtack Support and we’ll be happy to help.
Will I receive a 1099k for direct deposits through Thumbtack?
Yes, Stripe will automatically send you a 1099k for the year.

articles.fullText:
How to review a pro
[Image: Pill Customer]
You can share your experience with a Thumbtack pro by leaving a review. Keep in mind, reviews won’t be removed unless they violate our Content and Review Policy or other Thumbtack policies, so be sure to write your review thoughtfully. But, if your experience changes or you need to explain more about your project, you can update your review once.
Here's how to leave a review for a Thumbtack pro:
App
Open the Thumbtack app.
Tap Inbox (from the main menu below).
Select the pro you want to review.
Tap the option to review the pro (above your conversation).
Select a rating from one to five stars.
Follow the prompts to select highlights and share your experience. If you’d like, you can also add photos.
Submit your review.
After submitting your review, we’ll ask you about the job cost. This won’t be published – we’ll use it to help future customers get accurate estimates. Select between total cost, per-hour, or per-session cost. You can skip this step if you prefer not to fill out the job cost.
Desktop
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Go to your Inbox.
Select the pro you want to review.
Click the option to review the pro (above your conversation).
Select a rating from one to five stars.
Follow the prompts to select highlights and share your experience. If you’d like, you can also add photos.
Click Submit.
After submitting your review, we’ll ask you about the job cost. This won’t be published – we’ll use it to help future customers get accurate estimates. Choose between total cost, per-hour cost, or per-session cost. You can skip this step if you prefer not to fill out the job cost.
If you contacted the pro through Thumbtack, your review is considered verified and will automatically be listed on the pro's profile as "Verified" or "Hired on Thumbtack."
Tip 
While it doesn’t happen often, reviews from Thumbtack customers might not be marked as verified due to review link issues. Reviews are incredibly important for building trust on Thumbtack, so contact us if your review isn’t verified and you think it should be.
Reporting a problem
We expect pros to provide great service, and we’re here to help if you have concerns. If you had a bad experience with a pro, and you’d like help getting it resolved, you can report a problem.
We provide an online solution center where you can discuss your concerns and work towards a resolution with the pro in a neutral environment.
Frequently asked questions
Can I edit or delete my review? 
Because we want to build an environment of trust, we rarely edit or delete reviews unless they violate our Content and Review Policy or other Thumbtack policies. While you can’t edit or delete it, you can update a verified review one time to add new details or clarify your experience. To update a review, head to Thumbtack.com on a web browser (not the app).
Are there any limitations for my review?
Yes. Reviews have a 10,000 character limit, and you can only review a pro once per project. Also, your review must be posted either within six months after the last interaction between you and the pro or within one year of the last day the pro worked on the project, whichever happened most recently.
What are the photo specifications for reviews?
You can add up to 20 photos for each review. Each photo must be less than 10 megabytes and a jpg, jpeg, or png file. And if you use the Thumbtack app, you can upload photos straight from your phone.
Can I edit the project cost I submitted with my review?
Yes. If your review is verified (meaning you contacted the pro through Thumbtack), you can update it once. After submitting the updated review, you’ll be asked to add the project cost again – this is where you can make your changes. To update a review, head to Thumbtack.com on a web browser (not the app).
I'm having trouble leaving a review, what should I do? 
If you’re getting an error, check your internet connection (wifi works best). If it’s not your internet, try our troubleshooting tips.
Why was my review taken down? 
We remove reviews that violate our Content and Review Policy, or other Thumbtack policies. If your review was taken down, it most likely violated one of our policies.

articles.fullText:
How to respond to reviews
[Image: Pill Pro]
It’s a good idea to send personalized review responses to show customers you care. You can respond to each customer review on your profile, and your response will be shown alongside the review.
How to respond to reviews
Responses (like reviews) can’t be edited. When you have your response ready to post, follow these steps:
App
Open the Thumbtack Pro app.
Tap Profile (from the main menu below).
Under “Reviews,” tap the review you want to reply to.
Type your reply and tap Save.
Desktop
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Click your profile photo (in the top right corner).
Click Reviews in the drop-down menu.
Click Respond below the review you want to reply to.
Type your reply and click Submit.
Nobody’s perfect. There might be times when a job doesn’t go quite as planned and the customer gives you a negative review. It’s tough to receive criticism — especially when you work hard to please your customers — but this is your chance to show off your professionalism.
Even if you disagree with the review, focus on the facts and take a moment to respond politely and patiently. That way, other customers (who’ll be able to read your response) can see that you’re willing to receive, listen to and act on customer feedback.
Here are a few ways to respond to negative reviews:
Thank the customer for their feedback.
Tell the customer that you’d like to find a compromise and offer some suggestions.
Say you’re sorry the customer wasn’t pleased with the work.
Let the customer know you’ll reach out so you can fix the situation.
Explain that you’ll keep their feedback in mind for future jobs.
See it in action
Every review is different, so your response should be too. Here are three examples of good review responses:
“Thanks for hiring us, and thanks for your honest feedback. I was running late that day, and I’ll be sure to call ahead or text if I’m behind schedule in the future. Hope you’re loving your new bathroom!”
“I’m sorry you weren’t happy with your photographs. I’ll send over a few more prints today to see if they’re more your style. I’d also be happy to keep working with you until we get it right.”
“Hi Mary, I’ll be sure to consider your feedback for future customers I work with. Many jobs last longer than we’d like (or can expect due to unforeseen circumstances), but I appreciate your ideas on how we can improve. Thanks again for hiring us.”

articles.fullText:
How to reschedule a booking
[Image: Pill Pro]
We get it. Scheduled times for bookings don’t always work out. But instead of canceling, you can simply reschedule the booking with that customer. Here’s how:
App
Open the Thumbtack Pro app.
Tap Messages (from the main menu below).
Tap the customer you need to reschedule.
If you haven’t confirmed the booking yet, tap Reschedule on the booking request. If you’ve already confirmed the booking, tap Manage at the top of the screen, next to the scheduled time. Then, tap Reschedule.
Choose a new time, then tap Next.
Confirm the new time.
Desktop
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Go to your Messages.
Select the customer you want to reschedule with.
If you haven’t confirmed the booking yet, tap Reschedule on the booking request. If you’ve already confirmed the booking, tap Manage at the top of the screen, next to the scheduled time. Then, tap Reschedule.
Choose a new time, then click Next.
Confirm the new time.
Tip
When you reschedule, you'll only see times that are based on both you and your customer's availability.
And that’s it! We’ll update the customer with the new booking time.
If the new time doesn’t work for the customer, they can reschedule based on your availability – so be sure to keep your availability up to date.
Frequently asked questions
Why can I only select certain times to reschedule to?
We’ll only show times that work for you and your customer. That’s based on what the customer confirmed, and your calendar on Thumbtack. If the times don’t look accurate to you, then you may need to update your availability.
When can I reschedule a booked job?
You can reschedule the booking up until the current booking’s job start time. However, for the best experience for you and the customer, we recommend rescheduling as soon as you know the initial time doesn’t work.

articles.fullText:
How to get a personalized plan for your home
[Image: Pill Customer]
Care for your home with ease with Thumbtack. Tell us about your unique home and goals to create your home profile. Then we’ll help you create a personalized plan for your home, all through our all-in-one app.
Tip
​​If you've already created your home profile, you can view and edit it at any time. From the app, tap your address on the Home page.
How to create your home profile
Home profiles are available on our app. If you haven’t already created a home profile, we’ll walk you through it:
Open theThumbtack app.
We’ll share a little information with you. Tap Next until you make it to the address field.
Enter your address, then tap Next.
We’ll pull any data we can about your home. To edit any field, tap the pencil icon.
Tap Looks good! when you’re ready.
Select which projects are at the top of your list. Tap the bookmark symbol next to any project and we’ll save it to your plan.
Tap Finish.
Your home profile is now created. You’ll see personalized projects based on your answers.
Tip
At this time, you can only create one home profile. But you can update your home profile as needed. Just go to the Home tab and tap your address.
Benefits of your home profile
Get custom guides for your home
Our custom guides come with recommended projects based on your home and season. These guides help you care for your home — from lowering your energy bills to baby-proofing, and more. Our tools also help you decide whether you can do a project yourself or if you should hire a pro instead.
You’ll find these guides on the Home tab. Once you find a task you want to tackle from a guide, add it to your plan.
Make a plan
Your plan is here to help you make decisions based on your time, your budget, and your priorities — you’ll know exactly what to do and when to do it.
Use your Plan tab on the app to stay on track with your planned projects. This is where you’ll prioritize tasks, set reminders, and manage your projects.
Build your team
From the Team tab, you message or schedule your favorite pros, or refer them to your friends and neighbors. Here you can find any pros you’ve contacted under ”Past pros.” Tap the heart to add your favorite pros to "Your team.” This is your trusted group of pros you can rely on again and again.
Create your home profile and get more done today.
[Button: Download the app]
Note: Your home profile provides general guidance to help you track what your home needs. But it doesn’t replace a professional’s opinion. Always work with a licensed expert to identify maintenance and safety issues in your home.
Frequently asked questions
How do I set or update reminders for my project?
Want us to remind you to get something done? No problem. Set (or update) reminders for your planned project with these steps:
Open the Thumbtack app.
Tap Plan (from the main menu below).
Tap the project you want to edit.
Under “Project planning,” tap the pencil icon next to Due date.
Let us know when you’d like to be reminded.
Tap Save.
We’ll send you a monthly reminder for your project if you don’t set a custom reminder.
How do I add or remove a pro from my team?
Found a pro you really like? Add them to your team:
Open the Thumbtack app.
Tap Team (from the main menu below).
Tap Past pros.
Find the pro and tap the heart to add them to Your team.
If you want to remove a pro from your team, follow these steps:
Open the Thumbtack app.
Tap Team (from the main menu below).
In Your team, find the pro you want to remove and tap the heart.
I already have a specific project in mind, how can I add it to my plan?
You can add a new project in two ways:
Open the Thumbtack app.
Tap Plan (from the main menu below).
Tap Add project.
From the Search tab, type what you need in the search bar.

How to fix technical issues
[Image: Pill Pro]
[Image: Pill Customer]
Having trouble using Thumbtack? Here are a few troubleshooting tips that can help:
Check for updates
If you’re using our apps, check the Google Play Store or Apple App Store for an update. New app versions often fix minor issues and add new features.
Tip
Keep the Thumbtack app running smoothly by turning on auto-updates. This helps prevent technical issues and improves your app’s security. Since steps vary by device, check your phone’s settings to turn this on.
If you access Thumbtack on an internet browser, check for any available updates for your computer or browser.
Restart
Next, close your app or browser and restart your device. Sometimes, that’s all it takes to fix an issue.
Other troubleshooting steps
After you finish checking for updates and restarting your device, try logging out of your Thumbtack account and log back in. If that still doesn’t fix the issue, try these steps:
Desktop or mobile web: Clear your cache and cookies. These steps vary depending on your browser, so search online for the right steps. For example, you might go to Google and ask “How to clear cache and cookies on Chrome.”
iOS app: Uninstall and reinstall the app. Refer to your device manufacturer for steps.
Android app: Clear the app’s data storage (which can usually be done through your phone’s settings). Refer to your device manufacturer for steps.
Switch browsers or devices
Thumbtack works with most browsers, but if you’re experiencing trouble try switching to another to see if it’s a browser-specific issue.
And if you’re not using it already, you can also switch to the Thumbtack app. There are two apps: one app for customers searching for pros and one app for pros looking for jobs. The app is the easiest way to use Thumbtack, especially on the go.

articles.fullText:
How to continue or cancel my project
[Image: Pill Customer]
Sometimes, you may need to pick up where you left off with a project, or cancel it. Let’s go over your options in detail.
How to continue my project
If you started telling us about a project you had in mind, but haven’t reached out to any pros yet — it’s easy to pick up where you left off. Here's how:
App
Open the Thumbtack app.
Tap Plan (from the main menu below).
Tap a project to add your project details or review a list of potential pros.
Contact a pro you’re interested in.
Tip
If you’ve already been talking with a pro, go to your Inbox instead to keep the conversation going.
Desktop
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Go to your Plan.
Click a project to add your project details or review a list of potential pros.
Contact a pro you’re interested in.
Tip
If you’ve already been talking with a pro, go to your Inbox instead to keep the conversation going.
What’s next
If you’re ready to hire one of these pros, contact them to let them know. If you’re not quite there yet, that’s okay too. You can keep exploring your options and we’ll even suggest a few pros who we think are a great fit.
How to cancel my project
Sometimes things don’t go as planned. Maybe you hit pause on your project because things changed, or the timing isn’t right. When that happens, you have three options:
Cancel your project. This lets pros know you're not moving forward with your project. Your conversations will be archived and you won’t be able to contact pros from this project anymore. If you want to hire someone later on, you’ll need to start a new project. Canceling moves the project's details to the “Done" section of your Plan (in the app). Keep in mind, this option is only available during certain phases of your project. If it's not available, you can either delete or archive the project instead.
Archive your project. You can archive projects you’re no longer focusing on. Archiving moves the project’s details to the “Done" section of your Plan (in the app).
Delete your project. This completely removes the project from your account. If it’s a recurring project, you can either “Delete this instance” (if you want a reminder of when it's time to do this project again), or you can “Delete all future” (if you no longer want to be reminded).
Here’s how you can cancel, archive, or delete your project on the app:
App
Open the Thumbtack app.
Tap Plan (from the main menu below).
Select the project you want to update.
Tap the three-dot menu (in the top right corner).
Tap Cancel project, Archive, or Delete.
Confirm the change.
Tip
The Done section of the Plan tab in the app shows projects that were completed, marked as done, canceled, and archived.
Need more help with that to-do list?
[Button: Start a new project]

articles.fullText:
How my card is charged for leads
[Image: Pill Pro]
Unless you’ve turned on auto-refill, how your card is charged for leads depends on your total spending on Thumbtack since you joined. Your payment history determines when you’re charged. Here's how it works.
If you’ve spent a total of $1 to $999 since you first joined Thumbtack:
You're charged for each lead separately as you receive it.
If the charge couldn't go through, you won't be able to connect with customers until the payment is resolved. Update your payment method to continue getting leads.
If you’ve spent a total of $1,000 or more since you first joined Thumbtack:
You're charged for leads in bulk, either:
On the specific day you choose. You can select the day you prefer to be charged in your Billing settings (only available on desktop). Your card will be charged on your chosen day or once you've spent $50 on leads, whichever comes first. Keep in mind, you can only adjust the day you want to pay for leads once every seven days.
If you haven’t selected a specific day, your card will be charged on Sunday or once you spend $50 on leads, whichever happens first.
Need to update when or how you’re charged? Follow these steps to get to your billing settings (only available on desktop):
Go to Payments.
Under “Billing settings," select Edit.
Here you can view your current balance, change your current payment method, turn auto-refill on or off. And if you’ve turned on auto-refill you’ll also be able to change your refill amount. For pros who’ve spent over $1,000 since joining Thumbtack (and don’t have auto-refill enabled): Below "When you're charged," select the icon for the day of the week you prefer to be charged.
Or you can pay for leads upfront by preloading your balance and turning on auto-refill. Your card is charged at the time you preload your balance (or when you hit $0 if you’ve turned on auto-refill). That way you’ll have a balance ready to go in your Thumbtack account to pay for leads.
Tip
We use Stripe to process credit card transactions. Your credit card or bank statement may show charges from Stripe. The charges will update (usually within 48 hours) to show they’re from Thumbtack. Learn more about how Stripe protects your information.
Frequently asked questions
Can I use a prepaid card or another type of card to pay for leads?
No, credit or debit cards are the only accepted payment method you can add to your Thumbtack account. We’re not able to accept prepaid cards.
How is my card stored on Thumbtack?
You can learn more about stored payment terms and conditions here.

articles.fullText:
Here's a guide to your Thumbtack profile.
[Image: Pill Pro]
Making a great profile isn’t hard, but it does take time. The good news is it’s worth it — the better your profile, the more work you’ll get.
Your profile is your storefront.
Once a customer notices your business in search results, they go to your profile to learn more about you.
It’s like a customer going into your store to see what you have to offer. And an empty profile is like a store with empty shelves. That's one reason new pros need at least one review before customers are shown their profile.
[Image: Profile comparison]
Who would you choose? If a customer likes what they see, they reach out to you. From your profile, customers can:
Message you
Request a call
Request an estimate
What goes into a strong profile?
Your typical customer is looking for a pro they can trust. And someone who can jump right in.
Here’s what’s important to them:
Trustworthiness. A background check is simple to do (and free). And if you’ve got a license, make sure customers know that too.
Experience. Plenty of good reviews, featured projects and photos of your work show customers what you can do.
Price. We know it can be tricky, but customers want to see prices. Being upfront with your prices (and the payment methods you accept) can give customers an idea of what to expect.
[Image: Good profile example]
Now it’s your turn.
Take some of our tips and improve your profile. No matter what you add, just remember it needs to speak to your customers. You know them best. Anticipate their questions and keep them in mind as you go.
Next, learn how to use your preferences to tell us what jobs you want.

articles.fullText:
Guidelines for third party information requests
Last updated January 27, 2023
The following information is provided to inform private parties, including civil litigants, of our current policy on how to obtain information or records from Thumbtack. We may change or update this policy at any time. These guidelines only apply to non-law enforcement requests. Law enforcement requests are governed by our law enforcement guidelines.
Thumbtack requires that private parties obtain a subpoena or other legal process in order to seek disclosure of information maintained by our platform. This legal process must be issued in accordance with any applicable state or federal statutes, rules, and regulations.
Subpoena format and required information Thumbtack responds to valid federal or domesticated California subpoenas requesting information. We review each subpoena and other legal process for facial and substantive validity and will reject requests that are not facially and substantively valid. We will also reject any requests that are overly broad or vague.
In order to make sure your subpoena is valid, please note the following:
It must be a California subpoena;
The best way to get information about a person using Thumbtack is to request it from them directly, especially if they are already a party to your litigation;
You must make a sufficiently narrow request with a defined timeframe and identifying the information sought with particularity;
You must reference a specific person, entity, or reference (i.e., you must uniquely identify a user, phone number, service provider, or some type of other specific characteristic to limit the scope of the request);
Federal law does not allow private parties to obtain account contents such as messages using civil subpoenas. We will not provide such materials in response to a civil subpoena.
Service of third-party information requests We accept courtesy copies through inquiries@thumbtack.com as a convenience but reserve all rights and objections, such as for lack of jurisdiction or improper service. Third-party information requests may also be served at our San Francisco Headquarters:
Thumbtack Inc. Attn: Legal Department 415 Natoma St, Suite 1300 San Francisco, CA 94103
Our acceptance of legal process does not waive any legal objections Thumbtack may have and may raise in response to the request.
Please note that any complaints and other documents naming Thumbtack as a party must be served on our registered agent for service of process. California complaints may also be served at our San Francisco Headquarters, using the address above. We typically include an affidavit of authenticity when responding to records requests, but are generally unable to provide in-person testimony.
Notification to customer If we are required by law to disclose user information, it is our policy to use commercially reasonable efforts to notify the user unless (a) we believe in our sole discretion that providing notice could create a risk of injury or death, or that harm or fraud could be directed to Thumbtack or users; or (b) we are precluded from providing notice by law. This user notice will be sent via email to the email address listed on the account. A third-party seeking non-disclosure of legal process should obtain an appropriate court order establishing that notice is prohibited before serving legal process on Thumbtack or should provide us with a detailed statement of why notice should not be provided under our policy.

articles.fullText:
Get ready to grow
[Image: Pill Pro]
[Image: Pro Goals Course Header]
About this lesson
Learn how to identify whether your business is ready to grow, and what steps you should take to prepare for expansion.
Section 1: Where you are now
Section 2: Do your research
Section 3: Put it into practice
Review
⏱️ Estimated course length: 20 minutes
Always seek the advice of business experts before making changes to your business model or operations, including implementing any of the advice you read in this course. Thumbtack expressly disclaims any warranty regarding the content of this lesson.
[Image: Evaluate your company]
Section 1: Evaluate your business
Part 1: Are you ready to expand? 
It comes down to how busy you are now, and your capacity to take on more work. Watch the video to learn more.
▶️ Let’s watch a video
[Video: Are you ready to grow? (1:24)]
Part 2: Take an inventory
Don't run out and buy new equipment or hire more employees just yet. Reduce your risk by using what you've got to test the waters first.
🗒️  Try it
Activity: Grab a notepad and a pen (and keep it handy — we'll use it throughout the lesson). Take note of all of your company's assets, including equipment you don't regularly use. If you've got it, jot it down.
🔎  Zoom in 
Don't forget to add these to your list:
People: Employees and their roles
Places: The addresses of any physical locations
Things: Work trucks, software, tools of the trade, etc.
Part 3: Set a goal
When most people think of expanding, they see dollar signs. But revenue isn’t the only worthy goal.
🗒️  Try it
Activity: What does success look like for you? Turn your idea of success into three goals that will get you there. Each goal should have a specific action with a due date. Most importantly, they should be realistic.
💡 More ideas
Your goals can be as small or big as you want. Here are a few goals you might want to achieve:
Hire your first employee
Add a new demographic of customers
Open a new physical storefront
Add services that keep you busy in the off season
[Image: Do your research]
Section 2: Do your research
Part 1: Competitive research
Knowledge is power. When you identify the strengths and weaknesses of your competitors, you'll find opportunities for your own business to grow.
🗒️  Try it
Activity: Search for your service online and see what shows up. Then search on Thumbtack to see what your customers see. Your competition's website, social media, how they market their business: it’s all fair game. Draw inspiration from what these businesses do well or could do better — and write down your opportunities.
🔎  Zoom in
Don't overlook these two things:
Your indirect competition. You can learn a lot from local businesses who offer services related to yours, or the same service, but in a different location.
Your current customers. They already tell you what they want. Pay attention to their questions, and ask for their feedback.
💡 More ideas
Keep an eye on 10 businesses. Doing competitive research regularly helps you stay ahead of the game.
Set up Google alerts for your top competitors. If they're in the news, you'll hear about it.
Look at quantity as well as quality. Take note of how saturated your market is.
Part 2: Check in with your local government
Get an idea of what's required ahead of time so you're not surprised by any paperwork. Regulations can vary depending on the state, county, and sometimes even the city you're operating in. And some professions are regulated by the federal government. Thumbtack doesn’t offer legal advice, so always check with a lawyer before proceeding.
Federal
The federal government regulates some business (for example, businesses that operate across state lines). Check out this handy list to learn which federal agency you might need to contact. Once you know where to start, they'll help you get the documents you need.
Local
Head to your state's website for details about:
Taxes (and keep an eye out for possible tax credits or incentives)
Zoning laws
Business registration
Local licenses and permits
[Image: Put in practice]
Section 3: Put it in practice
Part 1: Refresh your brand
A successful brand tells the same story across all of its online accounts, from your Thumbtack profile to your social media. Knowing what you've learned in this lesson — and keeping your goal in mind — is your online presence up to the task?
Messaging
Think about your ideal customer. How would you talk to them, and what are the main things you want them to know about your business? Does your online storefront reflect your goals, and does your language draw in the kind of customers you're after?
Design
What kind of story are you telling with your visual elements? We’re talking about your logo, your colors, and the photos you display. Do they reflect where you want your business to go, or do they need a fresh coat of paint?
Part 2: Build your credibility
Your branding draws guests in, but how do you turn them into paying customers? By building trust. Check out these four ways you can instantly earn trust with new customers.
Credentials
If you've got them, flaunt them. Licenses or special certifications add instant credibility, so add them to your website and Thumbtack profile.
And while you’re adding them to your Thumbtack profile, don’t forget to take your free background check.
Reviews
Customers rely on other people’s experiences with you. That’s why reviews are so important. They’re a personal recommendation.
Don’t be afraid to ask your customers for a review.
Photos
Who doesn't love a good before-and-after photo? Add some photos of jobs you're proud of, and write a little about the job (like how long it took, what it cost, and other details). You can do all these things — and even attach the customer's review — with featured projects.
Part 3: Prepare your team 
You've done your research and you've freshened up your online storefront, but don't forget about all the people in your corner. They'll be along for the ride as you grow, so make sure they're ready and on board. Here's a few ideas:
Share the vision. Get them excited for the opportunities ahead.
Bring them on the journey. Ask for their feedback and ideas, and you might be surprised at what they come up with.
Divvy up the tasks. If you've got someone who's helping you, divide up responsibilities (like who will respond to the new customers, or schedule the extra jobs).
[Image: Lets review]
Let's review
Part 1: What you just learned
Phew, you did it! You just learned how to get your business ready to grow.
[Image: Get-ready-to-grow-gif]
Part 2: What's next
In our next lesson, we'll show you a few low-risk ways your business can expand.
Next lesson: Find opportunities in your market

[Image: Pro Goals Course Header]
About this lesson
You’ll learn several ways you can expand your business on Thumbtack. As you go along through the lesson, keep your competitive research and your goals from our last lesson in front of you for reference.
Section 1: Expand your map
Section 2: Expand your services
Section 3: Other ways to grow
Section 4: Review
⏱️ Estimated course length: 10 minutes
[Image: Expand your map]
Section 1: Expand your map
Part 1: Evaluate your market 
Expanding locally is the easiest way to start growing your business. Here are some ways to evaluate your market before diving in:
Cost
Consider how the new location could impact these costs:
Labor
Materials
Transportation
Taxes
And don’t forget to check for local small business incentives, too.
Customers
Think about your ideal customer and research the area’s population size, income, and how they spend their money. You can learn a lot about a demographic from the US Census Bureau.
Opportunity
Make sure there’s enough work to go around. Check your Insights on Thumbtack to see how many jobs are available compared to the number of active pros in your area.
Part 2: Try it on Thumbtack
By testing out new markets on Thumbtack, you might find it’s a good spot for a brick-and-mortar location, or you might learn it’s time to hire a bigger team.
🗒️  Try it
Activity: Review the travel areas section of your targeting preferences to see which areas you already serve. Next, identify potential new areas for market research. They should be healthy markets that neighbor your current area and that you can get to quickly.
Once you know where you’d like to grow, add to your travel preferences on Thumbtack and try it out for a few weeks.
[Image: Expand your services]
Section 2: Expand your services
Part 1: Evaluate your skills
Have you thought about the basic skills and tools you use on the job site? You might find you’re already prepared to offer new services to your customers.
🗒️  Try it
Activity: Put a pen to paper, and answer these 3 questions:
What are the skills I use daily?
What do my current customers need that I don’t offer today?
What other services to my competitors offer?
Take a look at your list. Circle any opportunities you can start on now, and underline any you could start after a little more practice or with a few new tools.
Part 2: Add a new service 
Once you’ve identified your skills, you might be surprised at how well they translate to new services. Make it official by adding new services to your profile. Here are a few examples:
Housecleaner
If you’ve got a big enough team, try commercial cleaning.
Or, with your targeting preferences, select the option for one-time jobs on larger properties. These jobs typically bring in more money, and can turn into a recurring gig.
Landscaper
Work with future landscaping customers by offering maintenance services, like repairing fire pits, replacing grass, or offering yard maintenance.
Mover
A lot of pros only offer local moving. But long distance moving doesn’t have to take you very far, and has the potential to bring in more money. Sign up for long distance moving and control how far you travel in with your targeting preferences.
Painter
If you’re an expert interior painter, try exterior painting too. Or team up with an exterior painting company and swap referrals.
You can also try other types of jobs to get your foot in the door, like drywall repair, paint touch ups or remodels.
[Image: Other ways to grow]
Section 3: Other ways to grow
Part 1: Change your schedule 
Your business hours should be convenient, consistent, and easy to understand. Figure out a schedule that keeps you busy, then make sure your business hours are easy to find online.
🗒️  Try it
Activity: Print out a calendar with last month’s appointments. Highlight any appointment slots you weren’t able to fill. Take a step back and look for patterns that point to opportunities.
🔎  Zoom in
Based on your calendar, what do you see?
Your books are consistently full. Adding more hours to your schedule (try evenings or weekends) can bring in even more business.
You have a pattern of slow periods. Adapt your hours so you’re closed during times that are slower. That frees you up to add more hours to busier parts of the week.
Once you’ve identified a pattern, update your business hours on Thumbtack
Part 2: Take advantage of the off season
Even if your business is seasonal, there are opportunities to expand your business during the slower months.
🗒️  Try it
Activity: Take five minutes and think about when your business is slow:
What services do your customers need during your slow time?
Which of your tools and equipment could be repurposed for another task?
What skills do you have, and how could you use them in the slower months?
What do your competitors offer in the off season?
Your answers might be the key to unlocking new services.
💡 More ideas
Here are some other ways to make use of downtime:
Create a contest on social media to introduce you to new customers
Offer discounts to fill open appointments
Partner with a local business to trade referrals
Learn a new skill
Rethink your marketing plan before your next busy season
Part 3: Create loyal customers
Your business doesn’t have to change to grow. When you’re good at what you do, you’ll naturally earn your customer’s future business and referrals. Here are some things we know Thumbtack customers care about:
Responsiveness
If you’re not responding quickly, you’re leaving your customers to the competition.
Download our app so you get a notification when a customer contacts you. Or, try designating a person or specific hours in your day to just respond to new messages.
Messages
Make sure every message you send a customer is personalized and helpful.
If you’re not sure where to start, think about the last time you got an email from a business that drew you in. What can you learn from their messaging?
Experience
When you consistently give your customers a good experience, you turn them into loyal customers. And when they really love the work you do, they’ll market for you by referring you to people they know.
[Image: Lets review]
Section 4: Let's review
Part 1: What you just learned
You did it! You identified some low-risk ways to test out new markets and expand your business on Thumbtack. Now it’s time to pick the right method for you and give it a go.
[Image: Find Opportunities Gif]
Part 2: What's next
In our next lesson, we’ll walk you through how to get seen by more customers on Thumbtack.
Next lesson: Ranking 101

Copyright Policy

[Image: Pill Customer]
It is Thumbtack’s policy, in appropriate circumstances at our sole discretion, to disable and/or terminate the account or access of users who repeatedly infringe or are repeatedly believed to be infringing the copyrights or other intellectual property rights of others.
In accordance with the Digital Millennium Copyright Act of 1998, Thumbtack will respond promptly to claims of copyright infringement that are reported to our Designated Copyright Agent in the form shown below.
DMCA Notice of Alleged Infringement ("Notice")
(1) Identify the copyrighted work that you claim has been infringed, or provide a comprehensive list of the copyrighted works that you claim have been infringed.
(2) Identify the material that you claim is infringing (or to be the subject of infringing activity) and that is to be removed or access to which is to be disabled, and information reasonably sufficient to permit us to locate the material, including, if applicable, the URL of the link or a specific description of where the material may be found.
(3) Provide your mailing address, telephone number, and, if available, email address.
(4) Include both of the following statements in the body of the Notice:
(a) “I hereby state that I have a good faith belief that the disputed use of the copyrighted material is not authorized by the copyright owner, its agent, or the law (e.g., as a fair use)."
(b) "I hereby state that the information in this Notice is accurate and, under penalty of perjury, that I am the owner, or authorized to act on behalf of the owner, of the copyright or of an exclusive right under the copyright that is allegedly infringed."
(5) Provide your full legal name and your electronic or physical signature.
Deliver this Notice, with all items completed, to Thumbtack’s Designated Copyright Agent at Copyright Agent, c/o Thumbtack, Inc., 415 Natoma St, Suite 1300, San Francisco, CA 94103, or dmca@thumbtack.com.

Content and Review Policy
[Image: Pill Customer]
[Image: Pill Pro]
By posting content on Thumbtack, you agree to abide by this Content and Review Policy, as well as all of Thumbtack’s other policies. We remove content, in whole or part, that violates our policies. Please notify us if you believe any content on Thumbtack violates one or more of our policies. Keep in mind that content on our site may be disagreeable to you without violating our policies.
User Content
Our Users contribute vital content that helps consumers and pros find one another, such as pro profile descriptions, pro quotes, consumer requests, reviews, and much more. To safeguard our community, we prohibit (in each case, at our discretion):
Content that endorses or promotes any illegal activity.
Content that endorses or promotes harmful activity or violence, or is profane, vulgar, obscene, threatening, or discriminatory.
Content that violates another person’s or entity’s rights, including intellectual property rights and privacy law rights.
Content that is fraudulent, misleading, or deceptive. This includes, but is not limited to, the use of digitally altered or AI-generated media to create a fake portfolio, misrepresent a property's condition, misrepresent work quality, or fabricate evidence.
Content directing consumers to visit additional websites or forms to fill out duplicative information.
Commercial promotion of products or services.
Content that discloses confidential information related to a Thumbtack Trust and Safety investigation.
Content that advertises or solicits a business not related to, or appropriate for, the Thumbtack platform.
Reviews
Genuine, thoughtful reviews provide the trust our community relies on. To that end, we prohibit, in our discretion:
Reviews that are not based on an actual or attempted interaction between the pro and the consumer. Example: If a consumer reaches out to a pro but does not hear back, that consumer has attempted to interact with the pro. The consumer may write a review for the pro based on that interaction.Example: If a consumer receives a quote from a pro, that is an interaction between a consumer and a pro. The consumer may write a review for the pro based on that interaction.
​Reviews unrelated to an interaction between the pro and the consumer, such as political or social commentary, or reviews that are racially motivated or otherwise discriminatory.
Reviews that are not posted after a reasonable period of time following the interaction. Reviews must be posted either within six months after the last interaction between the consumer and the pro, or within one year of the last day the pro worked on the project.
Incentivized reviews – reviews that are provided in exchange for an incentive, such as a discount, an entry into a sweepstake, a rebate, or cash.
Reviews that otherwise violate the User Content policy above.
​In order to maintain trust on our site, Thumbtack doesn't edit or change reviews. Pros will have a chance to respond to reviews left on their profiles. The response cannot be edited or changed once submitted. Thumbtack consumers can make one update to each verified review (i.e. reviews left by a consumer who contacted and worked with a pro directly on Thumbtack), and pros will have a chance to respond once to any updated reviews. Learn more in Review a pro.
All reviews of pros on Thumbtack reflect the opinions of other consumers and do not reflect or represent the opinions, views, or representations of Thumbtack or any of its subsidiaries, affiliated companies, employees, officers, directors, or shareholders. Thumbtack disclaims any and all representations or warranties with regard to reviews.
Further, by leaving a review about a pro, the consumer is providing Thumbtack permission to contact the pro about the interaction or job. If a dispute arises between a consumer and a pro, any relevant reviews submitted by that consumer for that pro may be removed or hidden at Thumbtack's discretion until a resolution is reached. To dispute a review, the user must contact Thumbtack within 30 days of the review being posted. Thumbtack does not assume responsibility or liability for any review or for any claims, damages, or losses resulting from any use of the Thumbtack site or app, or the materials contained therein.

articles.fullText:
Build your brand on Thumbtack
[Image: Pill Pro]
[Image: Pro Goals Course Header]
About this course
Learn how your Thumbtack profile can help you build your brand and business presence online.
Section 1: Your online storefront
Section 2: Building your brand
Section 3: Review
⏱️ Estimated course length: 15 minutes
[Image: Storefront]
Section 1: Your online storefront
Part 1: An online business
You’re a pro on Thumbtack, which means your business is online. You might also have other websites and pages for your business online. That’s important because that’s where your customers are too.
🔎  Zoom in 
Activity: Think of the internet as a busy street, and your Thumbtack profile as a store on that street.
There are lots of different streets and stores on the internet. As a pro on Thumbtack, when customers search online, we direct them to your store.
📖  Let’s go deeper
One of the first things successful businesses do is identify their target audience. In other words: who are your customers and where can you find them?
With Thumbtack, we’re already sending your target customer your way.
Part 2: Finding customers
Customers will walk right by your store if there’s nothing to see (in real life and on the internet).
That means just putting your business online isn’t enough. You’ve got to learn how to catch a customer’s attention so they walk into your store. That’s where branding comes in.
Story
An engaging story helps customers learn who you are. You have a story and customers will stop and listen if you can tell it in the right way.
Reputation 
This can make or break your brand. It’s something that takes effort to build, but your hard work will pay off (and your Thumbtack profile can play a big role).
Value 
You can look at this a few different ways. It’s about:
helping the customer find value in what you offer.
taking time to learn what’s valuable to your customers.
[Image: Build your brand]
Section 2: How to build your brand
Part 1: Telling your story 
So, what’s great about you? There are many things you can tell customers about your business. And they’re probably all good things for them to know. But, if you could only tell a customer three things, what would you say?
🗒️  Try it
Activity: Write down the three most important things you want customers to know about your business. Keep these three things handy because we’ll build on them later in this lesson.
Part 2: Where your profile fits in 
Now that you have an idea of what you want to tell customers, let's learn how to do that online — specifically, on your Thumbtack profile.
🔎  Zoom in 
Activity: Pull up your Thumbtack profile. Now, take the three things you wrote down from the last activity. Are you telling customers these things with your profile? If not, think through how you can use your profile to tell your story.
💡 More ideas
Put the most important information first. The customer has to click "Read more" on your profile after the first three sentences. Don't bury the best part.
Photos tell stories too. Have you created a featured project yet? Featured projects turn you into a visual storyteller too.
Part 3: Building your reputation 
Branding isn't just about what you want to tell customers. Now it’s time to think about how you want customers to feel when they work with you.
🗒️  Try it
There are two sides to every story. Customers tell their version of your brand story with their reviews.
Activity: Take a few minutes and read the reviews on your profile. Next, write down what stands out to you. Are there specific experiences they called out? What was their overall impression of your business?
🔎  Zoom in
Good reviews show you live up to brand promises. They also help you get seen. Highly-rated and reviewed pros are often at the top of search results.
Remember how we compared the internet to a busy street? Appearing at the top of search results is like snagging the best spot on the street, with the most foot traffic.
💡 More ideas
Look yourself up in search results. Try to get more (and better) reviews than other pros in your market.
Timing matters. Send customers a review request as soon as you finish the job. Their review will likely be more detailed since the project is still fresh on their mind.
Part 4: Finding value
What’s most important to Thumbtack customers? We did a little research to find out.
▶️ Let’s watch a video
[Video: What customers want (2:01)]
[Image: Lets review]
Section 3: Let's review
Part 1: What you just learned
Hey, great work! You just learned four key principles for building your business and brand on Thumbtack.
[Image: Build your brand checklist]
Part 2: What's next
In our next lesson, we’ll walk you through how to get seen by more customers on Thumbtack.
Next lesson: Ranking 101

articles.fullText:
1099-K Tax Support FAQs
[Image: Pill Pro]
Please note that neither Stripe nor Thumbtack file taxes on your behalf, so you will need to file taxes through your preferred institution. Thumbtack does not provide tax, legal, or accounting advice and these FAQs are for informational purposes only. You should consult your own tax, legal, or accounting advisors for any such advice.
What are 1099s?
1099 forms are federal income tax information forms used to report earnings and proceeds other than wages, salaries, and tips (which are reported on the federal W-2 form). The forms are filed with the US Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and, if required, state tax departments. On November 21, 2023, the IRS announced that the 1099-K filing threshold will be at $20,000 USD and 200 transactions for tax year 2023.
Keep in mind that states may also have earning requirements and separate deadlines for reporting 1099-Ks and filing them. We recommend consulting a tax advisor to determine your state filing requirements.
Our tax partner, Stripe, will reach out to you via email for you to set up a Stripe Express account to either electronically download your 1099-K form or to select if you would like Stripe to mail your 1099-K.
What is Stripe Express?
Stripe Express allows you to track your earnings, manage tax forms, update your business/personal information, and get direct support from Stripe from a web-based portal and app.
Do I have to download an app?
You can download the Stripe Express app on iOS (the app is not currently available on Android). If you prefer, you can use the web-based portal to access your account and tax information.
Which email address does Stripe use to send Stripe Express invitations?
Stripe uses the email information associated with your Thumbtack account to send you an invitation to sign up for Stripe Express. If you haven’t received that email, contact Stripe Support.
Why haven’t I received a Stripe Express invitation?
Check your spam or junk mail folder in case your invitation landed there.
You might not receive an invitation if Thumbtack doesn’t have your most current email address on file. You need to either update the email address on your account or check the email account corresponding to your Thumbtack account for the Stripe Express invitation. To get more information on when you will receive your form, reach out to Stripe Support.
How do I know if I need a 1099-K form?
If you meet the income threshold of at least $20,000 and the total number of such transactions exceeds 200 in a calendar year — and they're based in the US or are a US taxpayer — you should expect to receive a 1099-K, either through paperless delivery or paper mailing.
While the federal limit is $20,000 USD, some states have different thresholds and deadlines. You can check your state’s requirements here or check with a financial advisor.
You can receive your 1099-K in either digital or paper form. Log into your Stripe Express account to select your preferred delivery methods and/or to download your 1099-K electronically. If you don’t create a Stripe Express account and select a preferred delivery method, or Stripe will mail you your 1099-K form.
When will I receive my 1099-K?
Your 1099-K tax form will be emailed or mailed by Stripe by January 31, 2024 (note: 1099-Ks arriving by mail may take up to 10 additional business days, so they may arrive in early February 2024).
Starting December 4, 2023: Stripe will email you instructions on how to set up a Stripe Express account. If you haven’t already, you’ll need to complete these steps to access your 1099-K tax form electronically.
By January 31, 2024: Your 1099-K tax form will be available to download electronically through Stripe Express.If you have not consented to electronic delivery of your 1099-K tax form through Stripe Express, your 1099-K tax form will be mailed to you from Stripe. Please allow up to 10 additional business days for postal delivery.
April 15, 2024: IRS deadline to file taxes. You’ll need your 1099-K tax form to file your taxes. Please note that neither Stripe nor Thumbtack file taxes on your behalf, so you will need to file taxes through your preferred institution.
In January, we strongly suggest that you ensure all of your tax filing details and delivery preferences are up to date in Stripe Express. Your name, address and Taxpayer Identification Number (Social Security Number /Employer Identification Number) are of primary importance.
Why is Stripe requesting personal information like my Social Security Number?
Your Social Security Number is required to get your 1099-K tax form properly filed with the IRS.
If you have earned enough to qualify for a 1099-K tax form, the IRS requires your full details to be verified ahead of 1099-K filing.
We understand you may have concerns about providing your full Social Security Number/Employer Identification Number when first claiming your account, given the sensitivity of this identifier. We take your privacy seriously and have enabled technical solutions to ensure that your personal information is secure.
How will I know when my 1099-K tax form is available?
Once you’ve set up your Stripe Express account and opted in to e-delivery, Stripe will send an email notification about the availability of your 1099-K tax form to the email associated with your Stripe Express account.
To choose how you would like to receive your 1099 form, log into your Stripe Express account to select your preferred delivery methods.
If you do not set up a Stripe Express account or you do not select a preferred delivery method through Stripe Express, your form will be mailed by Stripe to the address on file with Thumbtack in late January 2024.
My information has changed since I signed up for Thumbtack. How can I edit information?
Update your account information in the Stripe Express Account tab:
Under Stripe Express Account, you can update the email address and phone number used to log in to Stripe Express. Please note that only one contact method can be updated at a time.
Under Language preference, you can choose your preferred language for Stripe Express.
Under Payout and Professional Details, you can update personal and legal entity information and view your bank account or debit card information for payouts.
To update your payout details, open the Thumbtack app settings to view your payout method in your Earnings tab.
Why can I see my earnings from other platforms?
One of the features of Stripe Express is a seamless view of all of your earnings across different platforms. You can see your earnings from other platforms that also use Stripe Express for tax purposes in one place.
If the information on my 1099-K tax form is incorrect, who do I ask for updates - Stripe or Thumbtack?
If you need to correct the information on your tax form after it’s been delivered, you can update your information in your Stripe Express dashboard or reach out to Stripe here.
We understand the numbers on your form might be a bit confusing. Those numbers might represent your net take-home pay, include Stripe fees, or represent total gross volume.
If the numbers seem higher than expected, see “Total Gross Volume” on the 1099-K Form to learn more about gross reporting.
Check here to learn more about the particular 1099-K form you were issued.

Thumbtack’s Quality Commitment Terms
[Image: Pill Pro]
Last updated December 5, 2022
Thumbtack's Quality Commitment comes with the following guarantees for all leads:
Phone Number Guarantee
The Phone Number Guarantee is our commitment to providing verified phone numbers on all leads you’ve paid for.
Phone numbers will only be shown after you pay for a lead from a customer who contacted you directly. Opportunities will also have phone numbers, but the phone number will only show if a customer responds to your quote.
We use an identity-matching process to verify all customers’ phone numbers. But if you get a disconnected or invalid phone number, request a refund and we’ll look into it. While we work to ensure that customer contact information is verified, we can’t guarantee that customers will answer when you call.
Limited competition
Customers can contact no more than five pros from search results per project within four hours of making their first contact. After four hours, customers can contact additional pros.
To the extent permissible by applicable law in the relevant jurisdiction, Thumbtack reserves the right to modify these terms without notice.

articles.fullText:
Thumbtack for Real Estate rebate terms and conditions
[Image: Pill Customer]
Thumbtack for Real Estate users may be granted Thumbtack credit by their real estate agents. This credit comes in the form of a $100 rebate and expires six months after issuance. How to redeem your credit:
Book a project through Thumbtack and pay your pro. (You don’t need to pay your pro through Thumbtack to be eligible for this rebate.)
Get a receipt from your pro.
Go to the rebate request form and fill in the required information.
Your request will be reviewed by Thumbtack within one week of submission. If accepted, you’ll receive an email from our partner Hyperwallet indicating your rebate funds are ready to be redeemed. Hyperwallet will guide you through the next steps from there.
Each credit can only be redeemed on a single project. If your credit is approved, you’ll be issued the full $100 credit value if your project cost is $100 or more (including tax and tip, where applicable). If your total project cost is less than $100, you’ll receive a rebate for the cost of your project and forfeit the remaining amount.
The following terms and conditions apply to this credit:
This credit is valid for Thumbtack users only.
The user’s account must be in good standing.
This is a one-time credit that can only be applied to one project.
The pro who completes this project must have an active profile on Thumbtack and must have been contacted by you through Thumbtack.
Your project must be completed and your credit redemption request received within six months of your real estate agent granting the credit.
You must submit your credit form (following the steps above) and attach your receipt within 30 days of paying for the project.
This rebate can’t be stacked with another discount. Only one discount can be used per project. If you have multiple discounts available, this rebate will be applied first.
On-Demand bookings are not eligible for this rebate.
Thumbtack reserves the right to end or revoke a discount, rebate, or promotion as needed.
This rebate is subject to Thumbtack’s Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Activate your account
[Image: Pill Pro]
[Image: Neighborly Pro Banner]
Welcome to Thumbtack!
You've purchased a preloaded balance, but your account hasn't been activated yet. Complete the three steps below to get set up for leads on Thumbtack.
Step 1: Get reviews (10 minutes)
Step 2: Turn on targeting (15 minutes)
Step 3: Watch a workshop (25 minutes)
Step 1: Get reviews
Ready to receive new leads? First, you need to add reviews to your profile. Try to get at least three, but more is even better.
Import reviews
The easiest way to get reviews? Use the Google reviews you already have.
🗒️  Steps 
Log in to Thumbtack and go to your Reviews page.
Select Ask for Reviews and choose the Add reviews from Google option.
Log in to your business's Google account.
Follow the prompts.
Send your review link 
Not all your reviews need to come from Google. You can ask other past customers to leave you a review on Thumbtack too.
🗒️  Steps 
Click here to go to your Reviews page.
Select Ask for Reviews.

articles.fullText:
Preset Jobs Policy
[Image: Pill Pro]
Last updated: Aug 10, 2022
You’ve read about preset jobs, now let’s go over some fine print.
Cancellations
You can provide a better customer experience by letting the customer know why you need to cancel the job. Keep in mind, they already gave us their credit card details and confirmed this job, so only cancel when necessary. However, we understand things come up and plans change, so here’s what you need to know about canceling claimed jobs.
How to cancel a preset job:
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Select the customer from your Messages.
Scroll to the message bubble with the preset job details, and select the three-dot menu.
Select Cancel this job.
If you cancel the job less than 48 hours before the start time, you‘ll be charged a $15 cancellation fee since there's not enough time to find another pro to do the job. We’ll notify the customer of the canceled job and we’ll email you about the cancellation fee. You can see the cancellation fee on your Payments page.
If you cancel the job more than 48 hours before the start time, you won’t be charged a cancellation fee. We’ll let the customer know that Thumbtack is looking for another pro to complete their job.
If the customer reports that you didn’t show up for the job, you will be charged a $15 fee. Also, if you don’t show up for a job or don’t complete the job without canceling it beforehand, then you must contact support. Failure to do so could result in adverse action against your Thumbtack account.
The customer cancels a job you've claimed.
We’ll always let you know as soon as a customer cancels. Your time is valuable, so if the customer cancels within 24 hours of the job, we'll add a credit to your balance.
Rescheduling
These jobs can’t be rescheduled. Contact support if you aren’t able to make it at the scheduled time.
Changes to the job
Job details for preset jobs can’t be changed because the customer’s already confirmed the job, and they have received a set price for the job. However, if you get onsite and the job scope is completely different, please contact support.
If the customer decides they want additional services for projects that are outside of the job details, that's great! You and the customer will work out the details together, and you'll take payment from the customer outside of Thumbtack. Thumbtack supports you in growing your business and lending your expertise to customers, even if part of the job wasn’t booked through Thumbtack.
Payments
You can only accept payments for the job through direct deposit via Thumbtack. The only time you can accept payment directly from the customer is for additional services offered outside of the job details. Any direct customer payments you accept for the job itself could result in adverse action against your Thumbtack account.
Resolving issues
If the customer is a no-show or there are other issues involving a preset job, contact support. We'll work to make it right.
