The issue being considered for coverage cannot be a result of any of the following:

[Image: Screenshot 2023-06-26 at 9.50.24 AM.png]


EXCLUSION
INELIGIBLE
COULD BE CONSIDERED
Losses are a natural part of the work
Damage done or reasonably expected as part of the agreed work required to perform the job.
 
Pro was hired to install the TV and had to cut a hole in the drywall to access the existing wiring. The hole may not be covered.
If the pro caused damage while doing a job that was not reasonably expected (while installing a new outlet, they damaged plumbing in the home), this could still be reviewed for eligibility.
Ordinary wear and tear (deterioration, rust, etc.)
Issues that are to be expected due to time, conditions, or use.
 
Pro installs a fence, and after some time, the customer reports concern that the latch and hinges have rusted. The latch and hinges are not covered.
N/A
Theft or other intentional acts
The customer claims the pro stole their tools. Even if confirmed through a police investigation, the tools are not covered.
 
The customer states that the pro’s worker came back to the home and vandalized/spray-painted their tile floors.
N/A
Enforcement of law or ordinance
Pro is hired to build a fence. The fence was not built according to the city code, so the city fined the customer. The fine is not covered.
N/A
Act of nature
Pro is hired to install a new roof. In the middle of the project, it rains, and while the pro did cover the roof, the house was still damaged from the rain. The damage is not covered.
N/A
Caused by substance use
The pro smoked meth on the customer’s property. A meth test or replacing the walls would not be covered.
If the pro is under the influence of a substance and causes issues, this could still be considered.
Caused by war or terrorism
If a pro were a member of an environmental terrorist group and lit the customer’s yard on fire, it would not be covered.
N/A
Minor or cosmetic damage
Superficial damage that does not significantly affect appearance and has no impact on the function of the item.
 
Pro was hired to install a TV mount. During installation, their media console received some surface scratches. Because this is minor superficial damage that affects appearance only and not function, this would not be covered.
If the impact on appearance (size, depth, severity) is significant and no longer minor, it can be considered for review. It can be subjective, so you may need to consult a Senior Lead specialist and default to historical case law.
Note: In auto-service categories, any damage that requires auto-body work (dents, windshield chips, etc.) is not considered cosmetic.
Animals (injuries, vet care, etc.)
Pro is hired for dog grooming, and the customer finds multiple nicks on their dog after the session. The customer took the dog to the vet to be examined and was also prescribed an antibiotic to prevent infection. This vet care is not covered.
The amount directly paid to the pro in scenarios that involve animals can still be covered under MBG.
Property in transit
Items that are “on the truck” or on the road, being relocated offsite.
The customer hired movers. When they unload the items at the next location, they find that a lamp was broken on the trip. This is not covered.
Pro is hired to refinish and return a dresser. The pro transports the dresser from their workshop back to the customer’s home, and it ultimately gets damaged on the trip. This is also not covered.
If items are damaged at a location or while being loaded or unloaded from the truck, etc., this could be considered for eligibility. 
Note: Sufficient documentation of where the damage occurred is needed to verify eligibility.
Fine art (originals or antiques)
Original art, vintage, or antique items that are irreplaceable or one of a kind. 
 
A customer had an antique heirloom rug that was damaged during a house cleaning. This would not be covered.
A mass-produced piece of art (from HomeGoods or Target, for example) was damaged during a job. This item could be considered for eligibility.
Currency, precious metal, etc.
Pro causes a flood that destroys cash the customer has in the home. The cash amount is not covered.
N/A
Commercial crops, timber, or barriers
Pro was hired for landscape services, and in the process, they caused damage to a communal canal bordering the property. The canal would not be covered.
N/A
Automobiles, watercraft, aircraft, etc.
Pro hired to mow the lawn, and the blade kicks up a rock that chips a car windshield parked in the driveway. The chip is not covered.
Pro is hired to remodel an RV/motorhome, but the work completed is poor and left unfinished. This would not be covered. 
Note: Automobile damage resulting from an auto-service category IS eligible.
Mold, mildew, fungus, etc.
Pro causes a leak, and mold begins to cause issues. Mold remediation costs are not covered.
If there were other damages from flooding outside of the mold, those could still be considered. 
Unauthorized electronic data access
A customer claims the pro accessed their computer while they were performing the house cleaning job and downloaded their music library for personal use.
N/A
Faulty installation
The pro was hired for plumbing work and did a poor job. The work is considered not up to code and has to be redone. This is not considered physical damage, so is not PDG eligible (though might be reviewed for MBG eligibility) 
The plumber installed a new drain incorrectly, and it caused leaking and water damage in the floor below - The drain itself and any surrounding pipes worked on by the pro are not covered, but the resulting water damage may be covered by PDG.

FRAUD INVESTIGATION
(return to index)
Investigating fraud should be done on every incident before submitting a payout. This is to ensure we’re not paying out to users who are trying to take advantage of our guarantees.
Incident Standard

If there haven’t already been any red flags or concerns, you can perform a basic review for fraud.
Check the customer and pro accounts for previous payouts.
Have both parties been involved together in any previous payouts? (i.e., through any linked accounts or expedited incidents)
Does the customer have a pattern of creating issues to get payment?
Check linked accounts:
Use the show linked users page action in admin.
Are any accounts already blocklisted for previous concerns/do they have a deletion/account hold history?
If so, search these accounts in tack to find if they’ve been involved in previous incidents/payouts.
Do any accounts link between the customer and the pro? 
We want to ensure there isn’t a preexisting relationship that might appear to show collusion.
Search using any additional information provided by the customer that doesn’t match the pro’s admin.
Business names, phone numbers, email addresses, etc.
Check documentation authenticity:
Were their estimates provided by legitimate businesses?
Google the businesses to review their online presence.  
If something seems off, you can also contact the businesses to confirm the estimates.
Is the proof of payment legitimate?
Do receipts or e-payment images appear doctored?
Is it a real check, and is there verification it’s been cashed?
If payment was only confirmed between the two users, do texts/emails appear real?
Suspected Fraud
(return to index)

If there have already been concerns with potential fraud or the Incident Standard process revealed issues, a more in-depth investigation can be completed:
Check for any social media connections.
(Facebook, Yelp, Google, business websites, etc.)
Review any suspicious activity.
Did the customer report their complaint immediately after they hired/communicated with the pro through Thumbtack?
Did the customer submit multiple requests under the same category around the same time as the original request?
Has the customer shown patterns of leaving negative reviews?
Did the customer hire the pro when no communication was exchanged and no other form of contact was provided?
Was there any collusive behavior or language in the Thumbtack Solution Center or other written communications?
Would it help confirm or clarify things to request additional documentation?
Additional more detailed estimates or appraisals.
Proof of ownership for the property. (if PDG)
Are the photos not stock photos and taken in the claimed job location?
Use a reverse Google Image search to make sure they’re not stock photos.
Download the image to your computer.
Go to image.google.com.
Click the image of the camera to search by picture.
Upload the image.
Check the Geo-Date and coordinates to see where they were taken.
Download the image to your computer.
Right-click (Command+Click) the image and select Get Info.
Latitude and longitude are accessible under More Info (if available).
Google the latitude and longitude to see if it matches the job location.
Perform a deeper dive search for linked accounts.
Reach out to your manager or a Sr. Lead specialist for assistance with using their own copy of the Collusion Check Tool.

What to do with the results
If the customer and pro have passed:
Update the Fraud Check field in the Eligibility Review to "Pass."
Proceed with eligible steps.
If the case is $500 or more, you’ll notify your manager to bring them in the loop.
If the customer or pro has failed:
Discuss with a manager to confirm your results.
If a deeper dive is needed, the Risk Analytics team has queries they can run to check for shared IPs, cookies, Admin account or services info, etc.
Update the Fraud Check field in the Eligibility Review to "Fail."
Post a note regarding your findings, and proceed with ineligible steps.

Expedited incidents

Since we want to resolve expedited incidents quickly, they’re lower risk, and we wouldn’t require the pro to repay our payout amount; we don’t need as high of a level of documentation to feel confident in justifying the payout and amount.
The customer paid $200 cash for a house cleaning job and didn’t get a receipt. The pro has been unresponsive. Consider the proof of payment being met if we can see work was done and there are no other red flags.
The customer paid $250 for a handyman. They say the handyman only replaced 2 out of the 4 light fixtures as agreed, so they’re requesting a 50% refund. Consider accepting this as an estimate outlining the cost to remedy the deviation.

Ensure the customer passes a fraud check and the documentation or info they are able to provide adds up to move forward.
Standard incidents
Since standard incidents involve higher dollar amounts, and we would require the pro to pay us back to return, we want to be thorough in justifying the appropriate payout and amount so we can confidently speak to our decision.

Insurance:
You should confirm whether a customer has an insurance policy or coverage for all PDG claims. We'll require the customer to file a claim with their insurance if the following factors are true:
The customer has a policy (personal property, homeowner’s, renters, auto insurance).
The property in question seems likely to be covered by a policy.
The claim amount is $5001+.
If we’re requiring the customer to file with their insurance, they’ll need to provide documentation confirming the outcome of their claim. 
If approved through their personal insurance options, PDG can still help by covering their deductible. 
If denied through their personal insurance, this doesn’t necessarily mean they are ineligible for the PDG. Reference their appraisal as a guide when reviewing eligibility under our own Guarantee Terms. 
NEW ERA AND THE GUARANTEE
(return to index)
Why offer New Era?
This choice would be ideal for dealing with unsatisfied/unfinished work. By using New Era ADR, the customer may get a decision against the pro for everything that would’ve been subject to the Thumbtack Guarantee and any or all remaining amounts.
If the pro doesn’t follow through with the New Era ADR judgment, the customer can still be eligible for a payout under the Guarantee if they meet the additional requirements below.

Use New Era ADR with your case
This is a great option for complicated disputes where it’s still unclear whether there was a deviation if the pro is at fault, or what resolution amount (or potentially payout amount) will be most appropriate.
If the pro fails to sign up with New Era ADR, they will be removed, and you’ll move forward with the Guarantee.
If the pro signs up with New Era ADR and receives a judgment against them but fails to satisfy it, we can proceed with the Guarantee if:
The customer has provided documentation that they’ve exhausted all methods to try and obtain payment through court. 
 
Note: Check in with your manager before proceeding with a payout after New Era.

(return to index)
Crawford is a third-party claims adjuster that we can use to help verify the scope of damage and cost of repair/replacement in property damage cases. We don’t often involve Crawford, but they can be helpful as an additional thorough estimate when:
The claim is very extensive and complex.
The customer provides unclear estimates.
Claim is $25,000+
Claims between $10,000-$25,000 can be evaluated on a case-by-case basis
If you have a PDG incident where utilizing Crawford should be considered, reach out to a Sr. Lead specialist to discuss the option. They’ll loop in Rebecca Fitzsimmons to receive approval prior to moving forward. 
PRO CONTACTS US AFTER PAYOUT
(return to index)
Sometimes, a pro who was removed for not resolving a customer’s concern reaches out after we’ve paid out their customer. In some cases, we’ll allow them to repay us in order to reconcile the situation and reactivate their account. We only require repayment if they were given the chance to address the concern and didn’t.
Review the customer’s resolution status.
If the Thumbtack payout fully resolved their concern, move to step 2.
If the Thumbtack payout didn’t fully resolve their concern, explain they’ll need to work with the customer to do so, in addition to paying us back, before reconsidering the account status.
Conduct a comprehensive review of the pro’s account and determine if they’re a pro we’d want to keep on Thumbtack.
If no, explain that this is a business decision and their account will remain closed.
If they seem like a pro we’d consider having back, we’ll allow them to pay us back. Send them the Payout - Pro reaches out after customer was paid (pro removed) email and send the Thumbtack Reimbursement Agreement via Ironclad through your incident Forms dropdown. 
If they’re unresponsive, you can close the incident.
If they're unwilling or dispute the amount they need to pay us back, send Payout - Pro disagrees with payment amount (pro removed). 
This asks them to send us documentation with an explanation of why they feel the amount is wrong. If their documentation supports their reasoning, we can work with them on what amount we expect them to reimburse us.
If the pro is willing to pay us back and return the signed form, check to ensure the following info matches otherwise, they’ll need to complete a new form:
The dollar amount on the form matches what we’ve told them is needed.
The last 4 digits of their card match the card on file.
If they need to change their payment method, we’ll need to reopen their account and place it on an account hold so they can.
If all the information matches, submit a request to charge their card.
Open the incident.
Go to the Notes & Tasks section on the left of your incident manager.
Click More to get a drop-down menu next to the Notes & Tasks tab.
Click "Charge Card Request".
Enter the amount you need to be charged.
Leave the status as Open.
Note anything you want the approved specialists to know.
Be sure to include the last 4 digits of the pro’s card in your submission.
Click Submit.

If approved, one of the approved T&S Sr. Lead Specialists will attempt to charge the card and will notify you if they’re successful or not.
Note: If the charge is successful, reopen their account and provide coaching. If the charge is unsuccessful, let the pro know then return to step 3. 
T&S Lead Specialist Attempt To Charge the Card
The approved T&S Lead Specialist will first verify that the Thumbtack Reimbursement Agreement form is completed with the last four digits of the approved card and signed by the pro before processing the charge.
To access the Agreement form, check for an orange item labeled "reimbursement form" in the incident feed.
[Image: rtaImage]
After completing the charge attempt in Stripe, the approved T&S Lead Specialist will note in the Notes section of the incident if the Outcome is successful, unsuccessful or the requested credit card is not on file for the specialist to inform the pro and ask them to upload the credit card. 
After leaving a note in the body of the incident, the approved T&S Lead Specialist will update and save the Charge Request page of the incident with the details below.
[Image: rtaImage]
Box A - Status: The most commonly used appropriate Outcome dropdown options are:
Soft Decline - Insuffi

Terms of Service Violations

Terms of Service (ToS) violations overview
(Knowledge index)

INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
The Enforcement Guide
Navigation
Enforcement Criteria
Queue-Specific Instructions
Violation Tiers
What
​​(return to index)
All users (pros, customers, or both) agree to adhere to the Terms of Use set by Thumbtack when they create an account.. Internally, Trust and Safety has segmented Terms of Use issues into four main policies: User Safety, Non-Discrimination, Deceptive Practices, and Platform Violations.
Proactive Ops uses the Thumbtack Enforcement Guide to manage and act on accounts in accordance with these policies. This enforcement guide details the specific criteria, policy definitions, examples, account actioning, and required notes for the following queues:
Profile Review
Image Review
Fake Reviews
Customer Message Review
Contact Verification
IPR/IPSR
Incentive and Referral Fraud
Pro Abuse Investigation
Blocklist Hits
Why
​​(return to index)
The Proactive Ops team reviews user-generated content to ensure users comply with the Terms of Use and to apply the necessary sanctions for any confirmed violation in requests, messages, accounts, etc. This account actioning improves platform quality and prevents further negative impact on Thumbtack users.
When
​​(return to index)
Though the Enforcement Guide is limited to specific queues, the identification and actioning of ToS violations occur across multiple Trust and Safety queues.
These include the following: 


Content Moderation
Deceptive Practices
Additional Queues
Profile review
Fake reviews
Image review
Customer message review
Concerning reviews
Incentive and referral fraud
Contact verification
Blocklist hits
Anomaly detection
Pro Abuse Investigation
Fraud investigations queue
In product reports
Proactive queue
Non-discrimination
Critical escalations
Survey Triage
T&S payments review
Chargebacks
Fraud Investigations
NOTE: There are also instances when the Support team raises concerns on particular cases or profiles to Trust and Safety for further evaluation (e.g., review dispute moderation). 
How
​​(return to index)
 
 Steps
    ​​(return to index)
Once a violation is detected, specialists determine which TOS violations apply and assess their corresponding actions. Violations can be found in several places on the user's account. The following chart displays the most common places to check and the TOS violations typically found there. 


What to Check in Admin
TOS Violations Concepts
Name
Questionable Names
Inappropriate Language/Content
Discrimination
E-mail Address
Inappropriate Language/Content
Discrimination
Messages
Harassment and Profanity
Sexual Content
Discrimination
Legally Questionable Violations
Competitor Services
Non-US Service Location
Not A Service
Not A Thumbtack Service
Pro Violations
Spam
Category
Mismatched Category
Image/Picture
Sexual Content
Contact Avoidance
Age
Minor
Linked Accounts
Sexual Content
Competitor Contact Abuse
Minor
Spam
Similarity Score
Competitor Contact Abuse
Follow the queue-specific KAs for details on investigating these violations, and the Enforcement Guide for specific actioning. If the KAs' instructions conflict with the Enforcement Guide, Specialists should always follow the Enforcement Guide.
Please reference the Terms of Use Snippets document to help identify the exact lines in ToU for each violation concept.
THE ENFORCEMENT GUIDE
​​(return to index)
The Thumbtack Enforcement Guide details the Trust and Safety policies and actioning for most user-generated content. This guide is broken down into several sections, detailed below:
Navigation
​​(return to index)
The navigation page of the enforcement guide contains an easy reference to quickly search and discover relevant TOS violation concepts. This sheet has several columns that provide useful information.
Category
Our top-level policy categories:
User Safety
Non-Discrimination*
Deceptive Practices
Platform Violations.
*Note: The enforcement guide references this category as Discrimination and Inappropriate Content. These titles will be aligned at a later date.
Sub-Category
The more specific categories within the top-level policies, such as:
Sexual Content
Safety Threats
Legally Questionable Violations
Spammy Behavior
These sub-categories group similar violations, making them easier to find in the guide.
Violations
The specific behaviors that create violations of our TOS. These help to identify exactly what a user did that violates our policies. 
Example: The Sexual Services violation falls under the Sexual Content sub-category. This violation includes the specific definitions and criteria for identifying a specific type of policy infringement.
Every violation includes a clickable link that opens the Enforcement Criteria tab. Specialists can use these links to quickly switch between the Navigation and Enforcement Criteria tabs.
Tier
The Navigation tab also contains a shorthand reference to each violation’s tier, which is further detailed below. In general, higher-tier violations are more severe and have more restrictive actioning.
Enforcement Criteria tab
​​(return to index)
The Enforcement Criteria tab breaks down the specific signals needed to identify policy violations in user-generated content. This sheet is broken down into several columns, each containing useful information.
Title
The name of the violation, which corresponds to the ‘Violation’ column of the Navigation tab.
Definition
A shorthand description of what the violation consists of. This column also includes various notes and definitions of key terms that may be needed to understand the violation or its criteria.
Identification Criteria
The specific checklist items required for an account action to be issued. Violations typically have multiple criteria that are denoted as:
ALL OF THE FOLLOWING - All of the criteria listed must be present for the behavior to be considered a violation.
ONE OF THE FOLLOWING - Only one of the criteria listed must be present for the behavior to be considered a violation.
AT LEAST [NUMBER] OF THE FOLLOWING - In some cases, only a certain number of the criteria must be met. This is typically the case when a violation can have multiple signals and/or mitigating context.
Violation Examples
Examples of policy violations that meet the required criteria. These are provided as a quick reference so Specialists can easily understand the types of behavior that would violate our policies.
Exclusion Examples
This column contains exclusions that would meet the enforcement criteria but should not result in an enforcement action. These exclusions are concepts we allow, or benign behaviors that may be confused for policy violations. Before issuing an enforcement action, make sure the user’s behavior isn’t covered by an exception.
Similar Violations
A list of similar violations that may be relevant to the behavior. In instances where a behavior seems inappropriate but a specific violation’s criteria aren’t met, the list of similar violations provides a reference for other criteria to check.
Tier
Similar to the Navigation page, the Enforcement Criteria tab includes a description of the violation’s tier, which is a shorthand reference to its approximate severity.
Applicable Queue(s)
The queues in which the relevant violation can be found. If a queue is highlighted on the sheet, there are instructions for handling that specific violation within that queue.
Specialists can click any highlighted queue name to go directly to the queue-specific instructions for that violation.
Queue-Specific Instructions
​​(return to index)
Each queue included in the Enforcement Guide has its own specific tab. The formatting of these tabs differs slightly depending on the content handled within the queue, but most follow a general formula.
Title
The name of the violation corresponds to the same concepts on the Navigation and Enforcement Criteria tabs. By clicking the link in the title, Specialists can quickly navigate back to the Enforcement Criteria section for that specific violation.
User Type
Whether the violation is relevant for pros, customers, or both within this specific queue.
Picklist
The correct options for the picklists in Salesforce, Admin, the Blocklist, and any content-specific portals.
Required Comments
The information that must be included in the enforcement comments in both Salesforce and Admin.
Tier
A shorthand description of the violation’s severity.
Content Removal
Whether the content (e.g., the image, request, message, etc.) must be deleted, and whether that deletion is manual or automatic.
Admin Action
The required account hold or deletion action in Admin, and whether that action is automatic.
Blocklist Action
The required blocklist action in Admin, and whether that action is automatic.
Escalation
Whether this specific violation must be escalated to a manager, Critical Escalations, or any other source.
Violation Tiers
​​(return to index)
Violation tiers are a shorthand description of the violation’s severity, and the actioning Specialists must take on the content and/or account. Tiers are provided so that Specialists can quickly understand which violations are most severe and the approximate actions required to address them. 
Note that the tiers listed for violations are the base tiers; circumstances may dictate that a higher tier is relevant. 
For example, you may receive an IPR report of Inappropriate Sexual Advances, which would normally be a Tier 3 violation. However, that report may come from a lawyer and mention impending legal action against Thumbtack, which would require escalation as a Tier 4 case, per the Triage Queues KA.
The table below contains a brief description of each tier and the types of violations within them.


TIER
DEFINITION
EXAMPLE VIOLATIONS
Tier 4-6
Particularly severe violations that require the user to be removed from the platform, as well as further attention from the Critical Escalation team.
Violent Threats
Inappropriate Content Involving Minors
Theft of an Animal
Tier 3
Violations severe enough to warrant the user's removal from the platform, typically due to illegal, malicious, or exploitative behavior.
Explicit Minor User
Harassment
Hateful Discrimination
Inappropriate Sexual Advances
Phishing
Tier 2
Violations that aren’t severe enough to warrant account deletion, but may include some account actions or service profile deletions.
Overly Suggestive Content
Offensive Insults or Profanity
Academic Cheating
Not a Thumbtack Service
Tier 1
Violations that are low severity or may be user mistakes. Typically, these violations only require holds for coaching and/or the deletion of the content or request.
Mismatched Category
Contact Without Intent to Hire
Non-English Service Profiles
Partial Nudity

   Voicemail
   (return to index)
“Hi _______. This is _______ from Thumbtack’s Trust and Safety team. I'm reaching out about your customer, _______, who contacted us about their project, and I’d like to speak with you about their concerns. I’ll send you an email with more info and a link to book a call with me. I look forward to hearing from you. Thanks!” 
   Introduction
   (return to index)
“Hi, this is _______ from Thumbtack’s Trust and Safety team. For quality and training purposes, I’m reaching out on a recorded line. How are you doing today?”

LEAD-INS
(return to index)

Thanks for… 
“...scheduling this time to speak with me. Is now still a good time?”
“...your willingness to talk with me about this situation.”

I understand…
“...you were hired for a _______ project and [INSERT DESCRIPTION]...”
“...not all projects can go perfectly. Can you tell me what happened?”

I’d like to…
“...go over the details of _______’s concerns with you…” 
“...ask a few clarifying questions about this situation…”
QUESTIONS
(return to index)
“What still needs to be done on the project?”
“When was the last time you talked with _______?”
“When did the project start?” 
“When do you feel the concern started?”
“How much were you paid in total?”
Was this info clearly communicated to _______?”
“Did you have a contract or any other documentation?” 
“Do you have documentation you could send me?” (See Documentation)
“How have you resolved situations like this in the past?
“What steps have you taken to help _______?”
“What else would you be willing to do to help?” 

EMPATHY
(return to index)
I am sorry…
“...this project didn’t go as smoothly as you’d hoped.”
“...this has been difficult, but we want to help you work it out and move on.”
“...our actions took you by surprise, but we appreciate you following up.”​​​
We/I understand…
“...customers aren’t always easy to work with.”
“...not all projects go smoothly, and sometimes it’s hard to work out.”
“...you’ve run into obstacles while trying to move forward.”
“...there may have been miscommunications between you and _______.”
“...you’re busy and would like to move on from this issue.”
“...how hard it can be to provide quality service since every job is different.”
“...this is a tricky situation, and we’re grateful for your professionalism.”
“...your concerns about your account, and we know this means a lot to you.”
“...why you’d step back when you’re not comfortable completing a project.” 

Thank you for…
“...sharing your side of the story. I’m sorry this project didn’t go as planned.”
“...following up. It’s important that we hear from our pros, and I appreciate it.”
“...taking the time to discuss _______’s concerns with me.”
“...understanding why we’ve reached out about _______’s concerns.”
“...your professionalism and willingness to address these concerns.” 
ENCOURAGEMENT
(return to index)
“We know you care about your customers and doing your job well.”
“All pros, even Top Pros on Thumbtack, have incidents sometimes.”
“We take customer complaints seriously, but we also care about pros.”
“We value you as a pro on Thumbtack and appreciate all your hard work.”
“We understand your position and recognize the effort you’ve put into this.”
“We know how hard it can be to build a business, and we want you to succeed.”
“We are committed to helping you resolve this situation as soon as possible.”
“We’re grateful for your professionalism despite the difficulties of this project.”
“We know you take pride in your work, and we want to help set you up for success.”
“Resolving concerns is a great business practice that will serve you well.”
“We know this has been difficult, and we want to help you resolve the issue.” 
For pros with positive reviews… 
“Thank you for the positive experiences you’ve created through Thumbtack!”
“Based on your positive reviews, your business has a reputation for [QUALITIES].”
“We appreciate the time and effort you put into serving customers.”
“We love seeing this success and want to support you as you continue to grow.”
“It’s crucial to Thumbtack’s success that we have pros like you who do great work.”
“We’ve seen your positive reviews and know you’re capable of completing projects and providing customers with good experiences.” 
   Role
   (return to index)
"At Thumbtack, our role is to help customers and pros connect with each other to complete personal projects. If a problem comes up between customers and pros, we want to help you work together to reach a resolution. Our goal is to help you be successful while also making sure customers are having good experiences.
We understand there are two sides to every story, and disputes can be difficult to resolve. As a third party, we’re not here to tell you how to address these concerns. We’re here to ensure customers and pros work together to resolve issues and to provide support and resources as needed throughout the resolution process.
We’ll hear you out and take note of your understanding of the situation. This is why the Trust and Safety team exists, to gather information and make sure appropriate actions are taken when concerns come up." 
   Expectations (Terms of Use) (User Guidelines) (Code of Conduct)
        (return to index)
"When signing up for Thumbtack, all users agree to abide by our Terms of Use and follow our Code of Conduct, which outlines our expectations for both customers and pros. If a user doesn’t meet those standards, we reserve the right to take necessary action.
We care about your business and want you to succeed. We expect pros who use Thumbtack to be professional and responsive, to address their customer’s concerns, and to abide by any local laws regarding professional credentials or licensing.
We understand how important your business is to you, and we want to help you however we can. We’d like to collect more information and work with you to determine the best next steps to resolve these concerns." (See Account Standing and Coaching)  

COMMON RESPONSES
(return to index)
You’re taking the customer’s side!
“We’re a neutral third party, and we recognize there are two sides to this situation. That’s why we appreciate you sharing more with us. We truly want your business to succeed, and resolving concerns like this can help your business grow.”
“All we’re asking is for you to communicate with _______ and work with them to resolve the situation. If you have documentation showing steps you’ve already taken, we’re happy to review that information, but we expect to see that you’re resolving these concerns.” 
I have extenuating circumstances and can’t fix this.
“Thanks for letting us know you’re dealing with [CIRCUMSTANCES]. We know juggling life with a business can be hard. However, please understand that we expect you to communicate with customers when things come up.”
“We have high standards for Thumbtack pros, and we expect them to take care of their customers. What can I do to help you work with _______ while you’re dealing with [CIRCUMSTANCES]?”
I don’t have time for this. I already told you what happened.
“I know you’re busy and want to focus on other projects. We’d like to help you put this behind you, but we also need to ensure _______’s concerns are addressed.”
“While it can take time, resolving concerns is good for your business. How this gets resolved is up to you and _______, but if we don’t see you making an effort, then we may place your account on hold. We want customers to be confident that the pros they hire will work with them to fix issues.”
The customer is being unreasonable; they’ll never agree to anything.
“Customers are sometimes tricky to work with. I understand you don’t believe they’ll accept any offer you make, but they’re seeking a resolution because of [DESCRIBE CONCERNS], and we need to see that you’re willing to take steps to make it right. What resolution do you feel is appropriate? What’s your reasoning?”
They fired me! I don’t have to do anything. 
“I’m sorry this project hasn’t worked out. From here, we’ll rely on information from you to determine the best next steps. Do you have a contract outlining what happens when customers cancel your services? We’d love to review that information as well as any other documentation you can provide.”
   Approach
   (return to index)
 INCIDENT HANDLING
(return to index)
Start an incident
(return to index)

Wrapping up calls
(return to index)
“Do you have any questions?”
“Thanks for taking the time to speak with me. As we discussed”
“Please update me when…”
“Send this documentation…”
“Sign up by this date…”
“I’ll send an email today with…”
“I’ll follow up by this date…”
“I’ll be your point of contact at Thumbtack as you work with _______. If you have questions, you can email me or book a call using the link in my emails. Please keep me informed of any updates or new developments.”  
Establish timelines and completion dates
(return to index)
“Can you reach out to _______ within the next 24 hours?” 
“When can you send the refund?”
“How long will it take you to complete this project?”
“When can you return to the job site?”
Set correct expectations
(return to index)
“If we don’t hear from you by [DAY], we will place your account on hold until [ACTION REQUIRED].”
“If we don’t receive confirmation by [DAY] that steps have been taken to address these concerns, then we will place your account on hold until [ACTION REQUIRED].”
Facilitate a resolution
(return to index)
“We’re happy to help facilitate a resolution; however, if you’d like to speed up this process, we encourage you to reach out to the customer directly to discuss options and/or any proposed solutions.” 
“I’m happy to reach out to _______ to discuss the situation with them further. I’ll let them know you’re willing to _______. We’ll see if that option will work or if they’d like to request something else.”
If pro is working directly with the customer
(return to index)
“When you reach out to _______, I encourage you to discuss and establish a reasonable timeframe for processing the refund/completing this project. If that doesn’t work, we have online resources available to help facilitate a resolution, and I’d be happy to discuss those options with you. (See New Era ADR  or Solution Center)”
“Please continue to communicate with _______, and set realistic expectations for a finish date and your next steps.”
“Please continue to be responsive to _______ about their concerns and update us once you have completed the project according to your agreement.” 
Request documentation 
(return to index)
“If you have any relevant documentation (such as contracts, invoices, receipts, screenshots of texts/emails, etc.) you can share, it’ll help us to better understand the project and what steps you’ve already taken to address _______’s concerns.” 
“Once steps have been taken, please share documentation of those actions with us. We’d also be happy to review a contract or any other written agreements. This is great information for us to have on record, so we can speak to your actions as a pro.” 
“Please reply to this email and attach documentation to demonstrate  _______. This will help us better understand the situation and determine the best next steps to help facilitate a resolution.” 
Warning the pro
(return to index)
“Keep in mind, if we don’t receive documentation from you by [DATE], we’ll place your account on hold until we can confirm these concerns have been addressed." (See Account Standing)
Disabled pro
(return to index)
“We’re happy to reconsider your account once we can verify these concerns have been addressed. Are you able to provide any invoices, receipts, or screenshots showing the steps you’ve taken?” 
“I understand why it may seem like our request for documentation is unnecessary, but providing additional information, such as [PROVIDE SPECIFICS], is the best way to demonstrate what steps you’ve already taken to resolve this issue.”
If you’re speaking to the pro first
(return to index)
“We know there are two sides to every story, so we wanted to reach out to you as soon as we heard about this concern. We trust you’re taking care of your customers. We’d like to know what you’ve done to address this situation, so we can follow up appropriately with _______.”
End of incident
(return to index)

Pro resolved
“Thanks for taking care of this customer and for [SPECIFY THEIR AWESOMENESS]. Because of the actions you took, we consider this matter resolved.” 
“We’re so glad you and _______ were able to work together to reach a resolution, and we appreciate how [LIST QUALITIES] you were.”  
“We appreciate your time and effort working with _______ to reach a resolution. We see that you care about providing quality work and doing everything you can to help customers. This practice will serve you well as you continue to build your business.”  
“I’ve reactivated your Thumbtack account. You should begin receiving notifications of new jobs within 24 hours.”  
“If there are any new developments or concerns, we’ll reach out to you. We wish you the best with your business moving forward on Thumbtack.” 
See Coaching, Comp Review, Reactivate, and Flagging as needed.
Thumbtack is stepping forward
“From the information that’s been shared, we’re unable to determine [SPECIFY UNCLEAR ISSUE]. For this reason, we’ll be stepping forward at this time. Should any further details be discovered, we’ll reach out to you.” 
“Ultimately, as a business owner, it is your decision how to address _______’s concerns. Even though Thumbtack is stepping forward, we hope you’ll continue working with _______ to find an agreement that works for you both. We appreciate everything you’ve done already.” 
“Thanks for sharing your side of the story. At this time, it doesn’t look like the two of you have been able to reach an agreement on how this issue should be resolved. We’ve reviewed the information from both sides, Thumbtack is inconclusive on what next steps would be most appropriate, so we’ll be stepping forward.”
Unresponsive customer
“We haven’t yet heard back from _______ about your proposed resolution to [DESCRIBE OFFER]. We appreciate you being willing to make an offer to address their concerns. Since we haven’t heard from them, we will consider this matter closed. However, if they reach out to us again or if there are other concerns, we’ll follow up with you as necessary.” 
If we need more info from pro
“We remain focused on helping you and _______ resolve this issue. Since we haven’t yet heard back from _______, we’re unable to confirm these concerns have been fully addressed or review the steps you’ve taken to follow through on your end.”  
“If you could provide documentation (such as invoices, receipts, screenshots of texts/emails, etc.), it could help speed up this process. Once we’re able to confirm _______’s concerns have been resolved, we’d be happy to reconsider your account.” (See Request documentation) 
Customer withdrew dispute
“I’ve spoken with _______, and they decided not to pursue a resolution further. At this time, we will consider the matter closed. If anything changes or if we need any information from you, we’ll reach out. (See Account Standing as needed).”
NEW ERA ADR (New Era ADR)
(return to index)

Introduce New Era
(return to index)
“We have resources available to help facilitate the dispute resolution process, and I’d like to talk to you about those options.”
“Since the two of you haven’t been able to reach an agreement, we may need to consider a different option to help move things toward a decision. We offer online arbitration through our 3rd party partner, New Era ADR.”
New Era overview
(return to index)
“New Era ADR is an online dispute resolution platform where you’ll work with a legally trained arbitrator who can provide a legally binding decision. You provide documentation, statements, etc., and you’ll have a video conference hearing where you’ll be able to speak with the arbitrator directly. We offer this resource to help both parties reach a resolution, and we cover the cost.”
“We have seen a lot of success with New Era ADR. That’s why we offer this resource and even cover the cost. New Era ADR could also potentially save you the time, effort, cost, and stress of other processes like small claims court or any other actions you or the customer may be considering.”
Benefits of using New Era
(return to index)
FREE: “Thumbtack covers the cost to file your case with New Era ADR. Though we’re a third party to the agreement, in difficult situations like this, we genuinely want to help both parties be able to move forward.
FAST: “The process is fairly quick. A hearing would typically be scheduled within a few weeks. It usually takes about half an hour, and then the arbitrator will render a decision soon after, usually within a week or so.”
FAIR: “You don’t have to speak or work with each other directly. The arbitrator is a neutral party. You’ll both have equal opportunity to provide documentation and tell the arbitrator your side of the story.”
MEDIATED: “You won’t have to speak with _______ directly if you don’t want to. During the hearing, you have the option to be in an isolated video conference with the arbitrator, though the other party can hear you.
BINDING: “Once the New Era ADR arbitrator renders a decision, it is final and court enforceable under federal and state arbitration law.” 
Next Steps
(return to index) 
“Once _______ agrees, I'll reach out to my Arbitration to who send you and email with more info andprovide a sign-up link for you to use. You’ll have five days to sign up. If you don’t sign up within that time frame, it may affect your account standing.”
Common New Era Questions
(return to index)

Can I choose the arbitrator?
(return to index)
“No, New Era ADR will assign you an arbitrator to keep the process as neutral as possible. The arbitrators are chosen from all over the US; they’re all qualified and will be randomly assigned to your case.”
Can my attorney be involved? 
(return to index)
“Yes, your attorney can definitely be involved. For specifics on how this works, you should contact New Era ADR directly at support@neweraadr.com.”
Can I respond to what _______ says directly? What if they lie?
(return to index)
“You won’t be addressing each other directly during the hearing; you’ll be speaking to the assigned arbitrator. Five days before the hearing, you’ll see what evidence the other party has provided and address any of those details.”
“This is why it’s important to upload any documentation you have to provide context to the situation. Documentation provides clarity when there are questions about the truthfulness of a statement.”
“The arbitrator will consider all of the information provided. So, even though you can’t respond to the _______’s statement directly, the arbitrators review the evidence and provide a neutral judgment.” 
How is New Era going to help? This customer is unreasonable
(return to index)
“New Era ADR allows the two of you to share your side of the story and work towards a mutual agreement. If the other party is having a hard time doing this, there’s a legally trained arbitrator who steps in to help guide the conversation in a productive way.”
“New Era ADR is free for you, and it’s a great alternative to taking the other party to small claims court.” 
What if the decision doesn’t come out in my favor?
(return to index)
“While we can’t guarantee the outcome, the New Era process is designed for impartial resolution. The arbitrator is a neutral, legally trained third party, and the decision will be based solely on the documentation and statements you and the customer provide. This will mean you will get a final, legally binding decision, save a significant amount of time, and avoid the expense and hassle of going to small claims court.”
Common responses
(return to index)
 I haven’t been paid, so no thanks. I might take them to court. 
“_______ mentioned they haven’t paid for the work you provided, but they also brought up concerns about the quality of work, which is why they’re interested in going through this process." (See Pro Not Paid)
Well, I’m not doing that, I’d rather sue them locally.
“It’s up to you how you’d like to resolve this concern. We do expect that you will address this concern with _______ as quickly as possible. If you choose to forgo the resources we offer, you may, but we’ll place your account on hold until the two of you come to an agreement.”
That’s not fair; you’re forcing me to go through this!
“This resource can reduce the time and cost for you both to reach a resolution. If you choose not to use it, that’s fine. However, we want to do everything we can to make sure things are resolved before we continue with your business.”
SOLUTION CENTER
(return to index) (Thumbtack Solution Center)

Introduce the TSC
(return to index)
“We care about your business and want to help you move forward. We know these situations can be difficult, and we want to make working with your customer easier. To help facilitate a resolution between you and _______, we have the Thumbtack Solution Center.”
TSC Overview
(return to index)
“The Thumbtack Solution Center will help you and _______ work together to find a solution in a neutral, guided platform. Within the center, you’ll be able to explain your position and respond to their concerns directly. You can ask questions, upload documentation, and suggest solutions.”  
“Thumbtack is a third party to disputes between customers and pros, but we know sometimes you might need some help working it out.”  
“We hold pros on Thumbtack to a high standard and expect you to address customer complaints. We understand that miscommunications happen and sometimes customers can be hard to work with, but we expect to see you making an effort to address their concerns.”  
“Though we’ll remain neutral and understanding of both sides, we’ll be here to help things head in the right direction. We’ll interact as necessary to monitor the conversation and make sure it’s productive and meaningful.”
TSC benefits
(return to index)
FREE: “The Solution Center is free for you to use.” 
FAST: “The Solution Center is easy to use and will help you address these concerns quickly so you can move on to other projects.” 
DIRECT: “You’ll have the opportunity to share your side of the story, upload any relevant documentation, and suggest a solution. The customer can do the same, and you’ll be able to respond to, accept, and/or counter their suggested solutions as well.”  
GUIDED: “In the Solution Center, we provide tips and suggestions to help you both move forward. This helps make sure the discussion is productive and working towards a solution.”  
RECORDED: “We can review the conversation to make sure both parties remain professional and productive. That means we’ll also be able to see the efforts you’re making to address these concerns.”
Common questions/concerns
(return to index)

Account hold
“We understand sending quotes is important to you, and we want to help you get back to business as soon as possible. When a dispute occurs, we’ll pause your ability to send quotes while you work with the customer to help you focus on finding a solution. Once we see you’re addressing the concern or have found a solution, we can look at lifting this restriction.” 
“While we understand it can be frustrating, turning off quoting is a fast and easy way for Thumbtack to notify you of a dispute right on your account. Ultimately, we’ve found taking this action helps pros address and move on from issues more quickly.”  
“We want you to be successful on Thumbtack. We restricted your quoting ability because we hadn’t heard from you, and we wanted to contact you about these concerns before taking additional action, like disabling your entire account.” 
Sharing their side of the story with Thumbtack
“We recognize there are two sides to every story, and this dispute is likely a misunderstanding. Our focus is not on why this happened but rather on what can be done to fix it. If you feel you’ve already done everything you can to fix it, use “I have a question for the customer” to remind the customer of the options you’ve already provided and ask for clarification about additional or new concerns.” 
“We created the Thumbtack Solution Center because we want to give you and the customer an opportunity to explain what happened from your perspective and work towards a mutual agreement. You can share your story with Thumbtack, but as a third party, we’re not in a position to determine the appropriate solution for you. It’ll be most efficient and effective for you to take your next step in the Thumbtack Solution Center, whether it is to accept, counter, respond, or ask a question.” 
The customer is “crazy,” ”unreasonable”, or ”impossible to please
“You and _______ have equal opportunity to share your perspective on this situation. We’re not saying the customer is right or that you have to give them exactly what they want. Disputes happen, and when they do, all we ask is that you make a substantial effort to take care of your customers and address the situation.” 
“If you don’t agree with _______’s suggested solution, click “I have a question for the customer” to continue the discussion. You can also click “Counter” to suggest a different solution that you feel may be better.”
Time’s up and the Solution Center closed
(return to index)
Re-opening the TSC
“We’re happy to hear you’re willing to address this situation. I’ve reopened the dispute; you should have received an email with a link to sign up and begin working this out.” 
TSC will remain closed
Disabled pro
“Because you didn’t respond, the dispute closed, and we placed your account on hold. Your account will remain on hold until we can confirm you and _______ reached a solution.”  
“Please contact _______ as soon as possible to continue working towards an agreement and get any new terms or agreements in writing. Once you resolve this concern, let us know, and we’ll be happy to reconsider the standing of your account.”

Active pro: 
“See Documentation, Stepping Forward, and Customer Withdrew as necessary.”
Error message
(return to index)
“Have you tried logging out of Thumbtack and back in? You could also try a different browser or clearing cache and cookies. If it’s still not working, then we recommend you try a different device. If none of these steps fix it, let us know.”
Next Steps
(return to index)
Beginning of dispute:
“Once the customer signs up, you’ll receive an email with a link to sign up as well.” 
“We’ve already started this process for you. Please find the email we sent you on [DATE] and click the link to sign up.”
Mid-dispute:
“Please take whatever next step you feel is best in the Solution Center. Based on what we know, it might be best for you to: 
Reply: In our experience, clear communication is the best course moving forward. We encourage you to respond and explain the reasoning behind your suggested solution.  
Click: “I have a question for the customer”: This is used when you want to know more before making a decision. It’s helpful to ask for clarification if you feel like you’ve already done everything you can to help.  
Upload documentation: You can upload contracts, receipts, invoices, emails, etc. Be sure to include whatever will support your ideas for a solution. There’s no limit to the number of photos or files. The platform accepts pdfs, pings, jpegs, and file sizes up to 2.5 MB.  
Accept: Click “Accept” when you agree to the suggested solution and all specified terms. 
Counter: Click “Counter” if you want to suggest a different solution. Be sure to explain your reasoning. If the project is incomplete, be specific about what you’re willing to complete.” 
“You will be updated via email each time _______ responds, asks questions, or accepts/counters a solution.”
End of dispute:
“Once these concerns are resolved, or once it’s clear you’ve done everything in your power to address the customer’s concerns, we’d be happy to turn on your quoting/reconsider your account standing.” 
“Once terms are settled, be sure to follow through with your agreement. You can use the Thumbtack Solution Center for the next week to finalize any details. After that, you’ll need to communicate with each other directly.”  
“We expect the solution to be carried out by the “Completion Date” you chose. If this date doesn’t work out, communicate with the customer to agree on a new date.”
THUMBTACK GUARANTEE
(return to index) (Thumbtack Guarantee)

If ineligible
“The Thumbtack Guarantee provides coverage if a customer’s project wasn’t finished as agreed or there was accidental property damage. I understand your confusion, but it’s not insurance for professionals.”  
“If a pro fails to address issues or damages, they would be subject to further action in line with our Fraud and Damage Policy.” 
See Expectations and being properly credentialed and insured.

    Coaching
   (return to index)
TIPS
(return to index)
Start with empathy and encouragement.
Thank them. Give them credit for caring, following up, working hard, etc. 
State your intentions. Let them know we care and want them to succeed.  
Be specific. Refer to the Thumbtack Code of Conduct and our expectations. 
Emphasize how these changes will help their business and future customers.
COMMON PAIN POINTS
(return to index)

Unresolved concerns
(return to index) 
“We’ve noticed [DESCRIBE PROBLEM], which can become a pain point for your business. We don’t want you to feel like you have to avoid these situations; we want you to have confidence in your business and in your ability to fix problems. Moving forward, we recommend you [DESCRIBE IMPROVEMENTS].” 
“We want you to succeed. Part of being successful is having great customer service, resolving concerns as they come up, and [DESCRIBE IMPROVEMENT].” 
“Resolving concerns is an important practice that will improve your customers’ experiences and build your reputation as a professional who cares.” 
“When businesses ignore or leave concerns unresolved, they often get worse and more expensive to resolve. That’s why we encourage you to [DESCRIBE IMPROVEMENTS], which can make a huge difference for your business.” 
Follow-through and deadlines
(return to index)
“We have high standards for Thumbtack pros because we need quality pros for Thumbtack to succeed. Having pros like you who care and work hard is important to us, but it’s also important that you’re following through on your agreements and addressing concerns within a reasonable timeframe.”  
“Please reach out to _______ to establish a timeline for resolving their concerns. What many Top Pros do, and what we recommend, is scheduling a date for your return to their property or a specific date/time for when you’ll follow up next.” 
“We understand that sometimes there are unexpected delays. However, for Thumbtack to reconsider your account, we expect you to set a deadline that the customer can agree to and then stick to that schedule. Thus far, several agreed-upon deadlines have not been met.”  
“To avoid similar issues in the future, please do everything you can to follow through on commitments and communicate any updates/changes as necessary.”  
“From here, for your account to remain in good standing, we expect you to make communication and following through on your agreements a top priority. This practice will serve you well moving forward and help build your business.” 
Communication with customers
(return to index)
“We’d like you to be successful with future projects on Thumbtack and encourage you to remain professional in all communications with customers moving forward. All interactions can have an effect on your business.” 
“In our experience, clear communication is key. Quick responses, professionalism, and being open to the customer’s experience can help expedite this process and move the conversation towards a more amicable resolution.” 
“We know customers aren’t always easy to work with. However, moving forward, if other concerns come up, we encourage you to be as professional, accommodating, and communicative as possible.”  
“We understand you’re busy, and we’re happy you have so many projects. We still want to make sure Thumbtack pros follow our Code of Conduct and effectively communicate with their customers throughout projects. Customers may worry if they don’t know what’s going on, so it’s important to keep them in the loop.”  
“We appreciate the steps you’ve taken to move this project forward, but _______ is still concerned about the timeline for getting this project completed and your responsiveness to their questions. We encourage you to provide regular updates and communicate openly with customers about project statuses and timelines.”  
“Often disputes come from miscommunication. While it may be frustrating, keeping communication professional helps demonstrate your commitment to providing a positive experience. We encourage you to review our Code of Conduct, and we’re happy to answer any questions you may have.”  
“It’s important to communicate effectively with customers and set realistic expectations about the scope of your projects and quality of work. It’s important customers feel heard and are aware of what’s happening.” 
“In your reviews, we’ve noticed multiple concerns about communication. We understand sometimes pros will pass or turn down jobs. While it can be hard to say no to customers, it’s better than becoming unresponsive, which can create a poor experience and damage your business.” 
Communication with Thumbtack
(return to index)
“It’s important that we can reach you when there are problems. Moving forward, please be sure to respond to any emails or requests from our team.”
Keeping proper documentation
(return to index)
“We encourage you to consider creating contracts for your projects. This helps establish expectations about prices and the scope of the work. Contracts also help protect you if something goes wrong.”  
“For future projects, we encourage you to use contracts, written agreements, or other forms to document the scope, details, costs, etc. of your projects. With proper documentation, you’ll be in a better position to address concerns and communicate with your customers and Thumbtack if problems come up.”  
“We recommend keeping clear documentation for all jobs, not only those from Thumbtack. It’s reassuring for customers to know the details, and it protects your business if there are disputes about the project. If your agreements change, be sure to update the documentation to avoid any misunderstandings.” 
Being properly credentialed and insured
(return to index)
See Credentials, particularly Licenses.
“We expect pros to be qualified for the jobs they get from Thumbtack and have all required credentials to perform the work they’re hired to complete. This standard must be met to follow our Terms of Use.”  
“Having proper credentials reassures customers and helps protect your business from facing any fines or penalties from performing work out of compliance with local laws. If you’re not sure what credentials you may need, check with your local business resources; they’ll typically have the info you’re seeking.”  
“If you don’t currently have insurance for your business, we recommend you look into those options. Insurance helps protect your customers as well as your business. It would help prevent you from having to carry the full financial burden and cost of resolving any concerns that come up.” 
What about my account?
(return to index)
“To be clear, your account is not being removed at this time. However, I wanted you to be aware of our expectations and policies so you can work to prevent situations that could potentially affect your business.”
Don’t tell me how to run my business.
(return to index)
“We want to help you to be successful and to make sure customers are having good experiences. We’re not telling you how to run your business, but we’d like to set proper expectations with you for the continued use of our platform. We’re telling you how Thumbtack runs its business to make sure you understand and are working in line with our standards.” 
Coaching and Flagging
(return to index)
“Moving forward, we’ll be monitoring your account to help you to succeed on Thumbtack and ensure you’re working in line with our standards.” 
    Account standing
   (return to index)
REMOVAL
(return to index)

Unresponsive
(return to index)
“We placed your account on hold because we didn’t hear from you. We’d be happy to reconsider once we confirm this concern is resolved.” 
“We contacted you about _______’s concerns on [LIST DATES]. Because we haven’t heard from you, we’ve placed your account on hold until these concerns can be addressed.” 
“I understand you’re busy; however, this is still a matter that can affect your business and prevent you from using Thumbtack in the future. We cannot reconsider your account unless we can confirm _______’s concerns have been addressed.”
I didn’t get your messages!
“I’m sorry to hear that. I’m happy to share the same information now and to help make sure any future messages are received. Let’s confirm your contact info so you receive future emails. We recommend adding support@thumbtack.com to your contacts, too, so our messages show up in your inbox like normal.”
Unresolved concerns
(return to index)
If pro isn’t meeting our standards
“We have high standards for Thumbtack pros. Because you have not [SPECIFY ACTIONS], we placed your account on hold. It will remain on hold until we can confirm this has been addressed.” (See Expectations and Coaching)
“We don’t make these decisions lightly, and as a neutral third party to this dispute, we can’t determine the appropriate resolution. At this time, we encourage you to contact _______ directly to work with them to address their concerns.” 
If pro refuses to resolve / requested removal
“Because you’ve decided not to address these concerns, we’ve placed your account and any associated accounts on hold.” 
“If you reconsider and would like to work with Thumbtack to resolve this issue, please reach out anytime.”
If immediately disabled
“Because of the seriousness of these concerns, we placed a temporary hold on your account until this issue can be addressed.”
If already disabled
“Though your account is no longer on Thumbtack, this is still a matter that can affect your business, and we wanted to notify you these concerns were brought to our attention. We’d love to work with you to get this resolved.” 
If self-disabled recently
“We see you recently disabled your account, but this matter can still affect your business, and we want to help you get this resolved.” 
“We really want to find a solution that works for you and _______. If you’re able to resolve this complaint, we’d be happy to reconsider your account on Thumbtack.”
Warning about next steps
“We’ll remain in communication with _______ to assist them however we can. Please note they’ll have options to pursue a resolution further outside of Thumbtack however they see fit.”   
“If we don’t hear from you, we may move forward with additional action to resolve this concern according to our Terms of Use.” 
Comprehensive reviews
(return to index) (Account actions)
“While we appreciate your efforts to address these issues, we remain concerned about your ability to provide quality customer service and resolve concerns when they arise.”  
“We’ve set a high standard for Thumbtack pros, and after doing an in-depth review of your account, we’ve determined to leave your Thumbtack account closed. This is in accordance with our Terms of Use, and while we don’t make this decision lightly, we won’t be reconsidering this action.”  
“At this time, we’ve removed this account as well as any other associated accounts. Although you won’t be using Thumbtack moving forward, we wish you the best of luck with your business.” 
If pro objects / requests additional information
“Our review included an assessment of your interactions on Thumbtack, your actions and professionalism, and more. I’m sorry because I know this is disappointing, but we won’t be reconsidering this decision.”  
“We appreciate the effort you’ve put into working with customers on Thumbtack, and in particular, we’re grateful you resolved _______’s concerns. Resolving customer concerns is a great practice that we hope you continue with your business outside of Thumbtack.”
Linked accounts
(return to index)

If pro denies linked account
“Based on information available to us, we’ve determined that these accounts are associated. Because we’re confident in the connection, both accounts will remain closed until these concerns are addressed.”  
“For privacy purposes, we can’t discuss what the associations are.”
If disputing a linked account
“We understand your concerns about other businesses being impacted by something related to your account. Because we’re focused on making sure unresolved issues are resolved, we take action against associated accounts to help ensure a resolution.” 
“As a matter of trust and safety for our site, we can’t allow associated accounts to continue using Thumbtack. However, once these concerns are addressed, we can investigate further. To reconsider the account, we’d need to see clear documentation showing a separation of the business.” 
REACTIVATION
(return to index)
“Thanks for taking care of these concerns and for your willingness to find a solution. Because of the actions you took, we consider the issue resolved.”  
“Your Thumbtack account has also been reactivated. You should begin receiving notifications of new jobs within 24 hours.”  
“We can see from your reviews that you have a reputation for [DESCRIBE QUALITIES]. We’re happy to have a business like yours on our platform.” 
“We wish you the best of luck and hope we can help you to continue to grow your business on Thumbtack.” 
FLAGGING
(return to index) (Account actions)
“Going forward, we’ll follow up on your account to make sure you’re finding success on our site, and your customers are having good experiences.”  
“To continually provide a good experience to your customers, we recommend” (See Coaching)
“If we receive additional concerns, we may remove you from the platform. Please take time to review your business practices and adjust accordingly.” 
“From here, we’ll be monitoring your account to make sure [DESCRIBE IMPROVEMENTS NEEDED]. We wish you all the best moving forward on Thumbtack!”
[Image: image]
[Image: image]
[Image: image]
[Image: image]
[Image: image]
[Image: image]
[Image: image]

   Call control
   (return to index)
KEEPING CALL PRODUCTIVE
(return to index)
Sometimes customers have unrealistic expectations, such as wanting to review the entire Terms of Use with you or the Thumbtack Guarantee Terms and Conditions. It's okay to let a customer know that to best utilize the time spent on the call, that conversation may best be suited for an email:

"To ensure the productivity of this call and to respect your time, I’m unable to address [CONCERN] on this call. I have taken note of your concerns regarding [DETAILS], and I am happy to follow up with you via email with more information you can reference."
If user pushes back
"I understand why you want to discuss [DETAILS] and recognize how difficult this experience has been. I cannot address each of your concerns regarding [DETAILS] as our time is limited on this call. I am happy to answer any questions you have and follow up with you via email to discuss this in more depth. You can also book another call with me at a time that works best for you."
USER WON’T LET SPECIALIST SPEAK
(return to index)
You may experience users who won't provide you with an opportunity to speak, explain how you will address their concerns, or ask questions. Since some users prefer to correspond over the phone, you can kindly interject:

“Thank you for sharing your experience with me, this is valuable information, and I would love to hear more. I also want to ensure that I have all the information necessary to help you move forward during our time on this call and need the opportunity to speak as I have allowed you to do so without interruption.”
If the user continues
Give the user a couple of minutes to finish their thoughts and then firmly interject):
"Since our time is limited on this call, I want to ensure I have all the information I need to help you move forward from this experience. Can you clarify… [DETAILS]?"
USER BECOMES UNPROFESSIONAL
(return to index)
Depending on the severity of the unprofessionalism, it’s recommended that we provide two warnings before disconnecting when the user is verbally abusive:

First warning

"I’m sorry to hear how frustrating this experience has been for you, and I appreciate the time you’re taking out of your day to discuss your experience; however, I need you to keep our correspondence professional so I can best assist you."
Second warning
"I hear your frustration, but again it's essential that you remain professional or I will have to disconnect this call."
Before disconnecting
"Please expect a follow-up email from me after our call today. I will also follow up with you within the next two business days as well, on any new next steps that I‘ve taken. Take care."
USER ASKS FOR A SUPERVISOR
(return to index)
Users may ask for a supervisor when they’re not happy with the direction the incident is going. We should attempt to continue helping them before considering this step.
User asks for supervisor first time

“I understand you’d like to speak with someone else about this. Because I’m the most familiar with this situation and am trained to handle these specific situations, I’m the best point of contact for this concern. I'd hate to waste your time when we're confident in our next steps, and this decision will not change.”
User asks for supervisor second time
“I’d be happy to set that up. We don’t have anyone available right now, but I’ll reach out, and a supervisor can follow up with you in 1-2 business days.”
USER ASKS SPECIALIST FOR PERSONAL INFORMATI
