“Before submitting more images, you’ll have to wait until it’s your turn again. The TSC was designed this way to help things move towards a resolution quickly.”
“What if they don’t fix the problem?”
“We’re waiting for _______ to [DESCRIBE NEXT STEP]. If that doesn’t happen, we’ll send you your next steps and how we can help from there.” (See Leverage)
Next Steps
(return to index)

Beginning of dispute
(return to index)
“We can start this process today. We’ll send you an email with a link to sign up. Once you sign up, an invite will go out to the pro.”
Mid-dispute
(return to index)
“If it’s your turn, please take whatever next step you feel is best. Based on what we know, it might be best for you to:”
“Accept: Accepting a solution means you agree to the suggested solution and all specified terms. Review the details carefully and click ‘Accept’ to move forward. Click ‘Back’ to return to the main page.”
“If the agreement isn’t completed by the ‘Completion Date’ listed, contact us.”
“Reply: In our experience, clear communication is the best course moving forward. We encourage you to clearly outline what your concerns are, even if you feel you already have.”
“Click ‘I have a question for the pro.' This is used when you want to know more before making a decision. It’s helpful to ask for clarification if you feel like the details of the suggested solution aren’t clear or to help you better understand the pro’s position. Keep all questions focused on finding a solution to help you move forward quickly.”
“Upload documentation: You can upload contracts, receipts, invoices, emails, etc. Be sure to include whatever will support your suggested solution. There’s no limit to the number of photos or files. The platform accepts pdfs, pngs, jpgs, and file sizes up to 2.5 mb.”
“Counter: Click “Counter” if you want to suggest a different solution. Be sure to explain your reasoning. If the project is incomplete, be specific about what you’d like done.”
“You will be updated via email each time _______ responds, asks a question, or accepts/counters a solution.”
End of dispute
(return to index)
“Once a resolution has been reached, a ‘Completion Date’ is provided by the pro and can be set up to one month out. We expect the pro to follow through with the agreement by that date. If they don’t, please let us know.” 
“Once a solution is accepted, you’ll be able to use the Solution Center for the next week to finalize any details. After that, you’ll need to communicate with each other directly.” 
NEXT STEPS
(return to index)

Wrapping up the call
(return to index)

If next steps are clear...
“Do you have any questions?” 
“Thanks for taking the time to speak with me about this. Again, we are so sorry about this experience and want to do everything we can to assist you. [RECAP NEXT STEPS]”
“I'll be your point of contact at Thumbtack as you and _______ work towards a resolution. Look out for an email from me in the next little bit. If you have any additional questions, you can always email me or schedule another call.” 
“If you hear from _______, or if there are any other changes or new developments, please keep me informed.”
“Anything else I can do to help you before I let you go here?” 

If next steps are unclear
“Thanks for taking the time to go over this with me and explain the situation. Again, this is not the experience customers typically have with Thumbtack, and we want to do everything we can to help.” 
“You provided me with a lot of information, and I’d like to take some time to look over everything and decide how we can best move forward. Due to the seriousness of your situation, I may also discuss the situation with my supervisor, and then I’ll follow up with any next steps. I can follow up with you by _______ at the latest. Would you prefer an email or a phone call?” 
STEPPING FORWARD
(return to index)
“Based on the information so far, we’re not in a place to determine the appropriate resolution. This decision needs to be worked out between the two of you or determined by an arbitrator.” 
“As a third party to this dispute, we’re not able to tell you what resolution would be most appropriate. We’re happy to help you to continue to communicate with the service provider and work to reach a middle ground, but we do not seem to be making progress that way.” 
“Any resolution would come directly from the service provider, and you do have the option to pursue the situation however you’d like using the local resources in your area. If you’d like assistance locating those in your area, I'm happy to help however I can.” 
“If you do pursue it further outside of Thumbtack, I would ask that you keep us informed as much as you’re able so that we may be fully informed for any future conversations with the service provider. If there are any significant changes to your case, please let us know.”
“If we learn that a judgment was made outside of Thumbtack and the service provider was ruled to be in the wrong, we would be happy to take appropriate action at that time as well.” 
   Call Control
   (return to index)
KEEPING CALL PRODUCTIVE
(return to index)
Sometimes customers have unrealistic expectations, such as wanting to review the entire TOU with you or the Thumbtack Guarantee Terms and Conditions. It's okay to let a customer know that to best utilize the time spent on the call, that conversation may best be suited for an email:

"To ensure the productivity of this call and to respect your time, I’m unable to address [CONCERN] on this call. I have taken note of your concerns regarding [DETAILS], and I am happy to follow up with you via email with more information you can reference."
If user pushes back
"I understand why you want to discuss [DETAILS] and recognize how difficult this experience has been. I cannot address each of your concerns regarding [DETAILS] as our time is limited on this call. I am happy to answer any questions you have and follow up with you via email to discuss this in more depth. You can also book another call with me at a time that works best for you."
USER WON’T LET SPECIALIST SPEAK
(return to index)
You may experience users who don't provide you with an opportunity to speak, explain how you will address their concerns, or ask questions. Since some users prefer to correspond over the phone, you can kindly interject:

“Thank you for sharing your experience with me, this is valuable information, and I would love to hear more. I also want to ensure that I have all the information necessary to help you move forward during our time on this call and need the opportunity to speak as I have allowed you to do so without interruption.”
If the user continues
(Give the user a couple of minutes to finish their thoughts and then firmly interject): 

"Since our time is limited on this call, I want to ensure I have all the information I need to help you move forward from this experience. Can you clarify… {DETAILS}?"
USER BECOMES UNPROFESSIONAL
(return to index)

Depending on the severity of the unprofessionalism, it’s recommended that we provide two warnings before disconnecting when the user is verbally abusive:
First warning: 

"I am sorry to hear how frustrating this experience has been for you, and I appreciate the time you’ are taking out of your day to discuss your experience; however, I need you to keep our correspondence professional so I can best assist you."
Second warning:
"I hear your frustration, but again it's essential that you remain professional, or I will have to disconnect this call."
Before disconnecting:
"Please expect a follow-up email from me after our call today. I will also follow up with you within the next two business days with as well, on any new steps that I have taken. Take care."
USER ASKS FOR A SUPERVISOR
(return to index)
Users may ask for a supervisor when they’re not happy with the direction the incident is going. We should attempt to continue helping them before considering this step.
User asks for a supervisor first time
“I understand you’d like to speak with someone else about this. Because I’m the most familiar with this situation and am trained to handle these specific situations, I’m the best point of contact for this concern. I'd hate to waste your time when we're confident in our next steps, and this decision will not change.”
User asks for supervisor second time
“I’d be happy to set that up. We don’t have anyone available right now, but I’ll reach out, and a supervisor can follow up with you in 1-2 business days.”
USER ASKS SPECIALIST FOR PERSONAL INFORMATION
(return to index)

Users may ask you invasive or personal questions that do not pertain to the incident. In these instances, you can reply with something like: 
"I can hear that you have some frustrations, but that question doesn't relate to the experience I called about. I value your time, and I would really like to focus on the steps that can help you move forward."
If pushed
"As this is unrelated to your concerns with [USER NAME], I cannot comment further. My focus is facilitating communication with you and [USER NAME] toward a resolution to help you move forward from this experience."
If it continues

"At this time, I need to move forward with reviewing your documentation and will follow up with you via email detailing our discussion. I will also follow up within the next two business days on any next steps that I have taken. Thank you for sharing your side of the situation with me, and have a great day."
   As needed
   (return to index)
LOCAL RESOURCES
(return to index) (Local resources)
“At this time, I would encourage you to explore your local resources to further pursue a resolution from _______. There are options with the Better Business Bureau. If there is any way that Thumbtack can support you in those efforts, please don’t hesitate to reach out to us.”
“While I understand this was not the solution you were seeking, we want you to feel empowered to take whatever action outside of Thumbtack you feel is appropriate to pursue a resolution from _______. If we receive any updates on our end regarding your situation, we’ll be sure to follow up with you.”
“Ultimately, _______ is responsible for their business as well as addressing any concerns that you bring to their attention. We’re sorry to hear that this is not the case, and the next steps would be for you to use the resources in your area to hold _______ accountable beyond the scope of Thumbtack.” 
“I’m going to sue Thumbtack. You’re responsible.”
“You’re able to pursue any action you feel is necessary; however, any resolution would ultimately need to come from _____ since your payment and agreement were with them. [RECAP ACTIONS TAKEN], and we’re here to support you in any way we can as you move forward.” 
PRIVATE INFORMATION
(return to index) (Privacy Policy) (Privacy Policy article)
“We can provide you with whatever they have provided publicly on our platform. This may include contact information like their email, phone number, address, etc. I would be happy to see what we have and provide it to you via email.” 
“All other information is protected under our Privacy Policy. This policy protects the privacy of both customers and service providers and if you require any additional information besides what we can immediately provide, it would need to be subpoenaed through the appropriate channel.” 
“We take privacy matters very seriously and while we want to be super helpful, we have an important responsibility to our users to protect their information as well as legal obligations we must adhere to.” 
“Are they contacting other customers?” 
If service provider’s account is enabled
“I can’t give you a lot of detail as far as what their account activity is, but it does look like their account is still active with us, so I’m happy to reach out and see what I can do to get them back in touch with you.” 
If service provider’s account is active, but they haven’t quoted in a long time
“It looks like they haven’t quoted in a while, but I am still happy to reach out and see what we can do to help get these concerns addressed.” 
If service provider’s account is disabled
“It looks like they’re no longer listing their services on Thumbtack, but I’m happy to reach out and do everything we can to get them back in touch.” 
CUSTOMER SATISFACTION PAYOUT
(return to index) (CSAT payouts)
Introduction
(return to index)
“We truly care about our customers. We know how hard this has been, and we want to help you. As a third party to this dispute, _______ is responsible for these concerns. However, we’ve reviewed the situation further, and to help you move on from this experience, we’d like to send you the amount of [$DOLLARS].”
“We rarely take this step, but this is a particularly tough situation, and while we’re not taking responsibility for _______’s actions, we wanted to do what we can to help alleviate the burden of the situation.” 
The Service Provider
(return to index)
“In the rare instance that a service provider doesn’t resolve a concern themselves, we have additional steps we can take to help. We’ve already [RECAP ACTIONS TAKEN], and now we’d like to provide [$DOLLARS].”
“We don’t want anyone else to have this experience. _______ has been removed and won’t be welcome back on our platform.”
“This payment won’t affect your ability to take additional action outside of Thumbtack if you feel it’s appropriate or would like to pursue further resolution.” 
If the customer wants more money

T&S Triage Queues

T&S Triage Queues
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
How to triage and categorize: quick view
1: Determine if it’s a T&S issue
2: Case or incident
3: Choose a tier
4: Assign to a queue
5: Safety category and subcategory
6: Project category and subcategory
Details
Not enough info

Work ticket outcomes

Contacting Critical Escalations

Forms
Feedback and change request form
Troubleshooting
Error creating incident from a Dispute Request
Error creating incident from a case
There’s an open incident, but you can’t find it
Customer/pro info didn’t populate in incident
Primary cases not attached to incident
Cases created in error
Closing incorrect incidents
What
​​(return to index)
There are four triage queues in Trust and Safety (T&S):

Categorization (CAT)
Reports submitted by customers and pros through help.thumbtack.com/soulutioncenter/report-a-concern and help.thumbtack.com/report-a-concern, emails sent to trustandsafetyteam@thumbtack.com, and any interactions (voice, chat, SMS, email) escalated to T&S from other frontline agents. 
In-product Scam Reports (IPSR)
Reports submitted by pros who “report an issue” through the product (from Messenger or when declining a lead).
In product Refund Requests (IPR)
Refund requests submitted by pros through the product, particularly Payment History.
Concerning Reviews (CR)
Customer reviews of pros with either a 1-2 star rating or a 3-4 star rating, with private feedback.
The triage queue responsibilities and purposes are to:

Determine whether incoming reports and customer reviews are indeed T&S concerns or not.
Create an incident or transfer the case created.
Choose a tier for incidents.
Figure out which queue an issue should be sent to.
Assign a safety category/subcategory and/or project category/subcategory for incidents.
Take action on accounts or bid/quote when user safety is at risk.
Notate any decisions made.
Why
​​(return to index)
To ensure all T&S issues are identified, sent to the correct queue, given a category, and assigned a tier, we need a team dedicated to reviewing all concerning reviews and reports sent to T&S.
When
​​(return to index)
Cases, dispute requests, and work tickets will be auto-assigned to specialists through Omni according to each specialist’s Routing Skill. Below are the SLAs and target handle times for each triage queue.

Queue
SLA
Target Handle Time
CAT
12 hours
10 minutes
IPSR
24 hours
Escalated: 12.2 minutes
Non Escalated: 2.8 minutes
IPR
24 hours
Escalated: 15.2 minutes
Non Escalated: 5.5 minutes
CR
24 hours
Escalated: 16 minutes
Non Escalated: 6 minutes

How
​​(return to index)
  Steps
   (return to index)
HOW TO TRIAGE AND CATEGORIZE: QUICK VIEW
​​(return to index)

Turn your Omni-Channel status to TS - All Work.
Accept a work ticket (WT), case, or dispute request (DR). These will auto-pop based on your skilling.
Skim through the messaging to get a general idea of what the issue is, and keep an eye out for any keywords (i.e., “discrimination,” “threatening,” “uncomfortable”).
Always lookout for sexual content and/or discrimination in the messaging between the customer and pro. If these are not present in the bid, refer to the report itself to identify categorization/tagging.
If the report originates from an IPSR or IPR WT, review the linked bid request and linked accounts as well.
If the report originates from a CR WT, review the linked bid request and Admin.
Determine if it's a T&S issue or not.
If it’s a non-T&S issue, either transfer the case or close the case/WT/DR, as applicable.
If it’s a confirmed T&S issue and related to an existing incident, attach it to the incident.
This includes users reaching out about existing incidents to provide updates or context. 
If it’s a confirmed T&S Issue that doesn’t already have an incident, move to the next step.
Figure out whether you need to transfer as a case or create an incident.
If it’ll stay as a case, assign it to a case queue.
If it’ll become an incident, move to the next step.
For DRs, first pick an Outcome.
Choose a tier.
Assign to an incident queue.
Decide the Safety Category/Subcategory and/or the Project Category/Subcategory.
Leave a note on the case or incident with information about your categorization decisions.
If working from a case, make sure information found under Work Ticket Details or Description is copied to the case feed or incident.
1: DETERMINE IF IT'S A T&S ISSUE
​​(return to index)
The T&S team occasionally receives issues that aren’t meant to be worked on by T&S. The first step for categorization is to double-check whether the case or dispute request is really a T&S issue.
Use the lists below to understand what should and shouldn’t come to T&S, then see the steps below to determine your next steps.
Mini index:
Project disputes between users
Discrimination
Safety Concerns
Behavior Concerns
Account issues
Legal, law enforcement, and media
Thumbtack product and policy
Steps

PROJECT DISPUTES BETWEEN USERS

Confirmed T&S issues:
Not T&S issues:
The user reached out/provided updates about an existing T&S incident.
The customer reports any of the following:
Payment was exchanged and: 
The pro didn’t show up (deposit no-show).
The work is unsatisfactory.
The work isn’t complete.
Note: For reports of unsatisfactory and incomplete work, we should assume payment was made unless it's called out otherwise. 
Their property was damaged.
The payment wasn’t exchanged, but additional work or expenses are now necessary.
Includes when they need to pay a new pro to demolish concrete, the city has fined them, etc.
Pro reports they want help because they weren’t paid or were only partially paid for work they completed.
A lien was placed, or the user stated a lien would be placed.
The user reports that the pro charged too much for the work during/following a natural disaster.
No money was exchanged, and no work was completed.
Includes no-shows for on-demand bookings when pros weren’t paid (see below).
Pro reported their customer has concerns with the project or damage.
The customer reported they didn’t pay the pro.
T&S concern was resolved before an incident was created.
The only concern is that a receipt wasn’t provided to the customer.
DISCRIMINATION

Confirmed T&S issues:
Not T&S issues:
The user stated they were discriminated against. 
Includes using words such as “racist,” “sexist,” “ableist,” “trans-phobic,” “anti-semitic,” etc.
User discriminated against or used discriminatory language towards Thumbtack employees.
The user expressed a preference towards a certain race, gender, minority group, age, etc., to the employee or user.
The user was exposed to discriminatory content. 
Treating/speaking to anyone differently based on age, disability, gender identity, marital status, medical condition, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, or sexual orientation.
We found discriminatory content that users weren’t exposed to.
The user reported that they were discriminated against, but they’re not describing one of our protected characteristics.
Includes when user feels pro discriminated against their job/house because it was too messy or the job was larger than expected.
SAFETY CONCERNS

Confirmed T&S issues:
Not T&S issues:
Physical harm
Has occurred to a human or animal.
Threats to/concerns about physical safety of self, others, or animals (includes requests to harm others, i.e., asking a Pro to beat someone up, etc.).
Includes threats of self-harm, statements about harming users or Thumbtack employees, reports of animal abuse, requests for mercenary services, etc.
User reports of non-consensual aggressive  physical touch (pushing, shoving, etc.) or non-aggressive (taps on the shoulder, etc.)
Sexual harm or misconduct
Sexual contact or sexual assault occurred.
Nudity or sexual content.
If it involves a minor (do not investigate).
The user was exposed to sexual or sexually suggestive content.
The user reports that a pro is on the sex offender registry.
User reported they’re concerned or uncomfortable about flirting, romantic advances/gestures, staring/leering, request details, photos/videos taken, or information other user requested from them (i.e., photos, address).
Unprofessional Behavior
Violent intimidation has been reported.
Includes threats to damage property/undo work, language like “or else” or “I know where you live.”
Users reported they were uncomfortable or scared.
Consider the context of the message. If the message obviously doesn’t concern user-safety, don’t escalate to T&S.
Sexual or suggestive content that users weren’t exposed to.
If a minor is involved, always send it to T&S without further investigation. 
See behavior concerns
BEHAVIOR CONCERNS

Confirmed T&S issues:
Not T&S issues:
The user reports a criminal history.
The user reports illegal activity.
It doesn’t include illegal requests where there are no safety risks, such as “they’re asking me to paint a copyrighted character, which is illegal.”
Theft (reports of a user stealing property, reports of theft occurring between users).
Includes when customers agreed to give their possession(s) to pros while they work on it, but now can’t retrieve the possession(s).
Harassment or unprofessional communication, when:
We might remove the user.
I.e., abusive language.
We need to investigate further.
We may need to communicate back and forth.
Stalking (following someone home, showing up uninvited with no business purpose).
Users saw the presence, use, or dealing of illegal substances.
Includes marijuana - T&S will look at local laws.
Alcohol use that could endanger users.
Including when driving was involved, the user became belligerent, etc.
Credit card fraud.
This includes when someone reports that their credit card has been used on Thumbtack and they don’t recognize the charges.
Early fraud warning.
Includes when we put a hold on a pro’s account and emailed them because they contacted their bank about a charge on the card on their account.
Issues that we won’t remove the reported user for, and can be resolved by one contact/coaching.
The only concern reported is that the user may not be properly licensed.
Mild harassment or unprofessional behavior.
Includes late-night contacts that aren’t sexual, posting negative reviews on other user’s online profiles, excessive contacts, swearing (when we’re not considering removing the user).
Non-illegal substance use (when it doesn’t endanger users).
Includes when the user was drinking on the job, but other users weren’t endangered by it.
Except for marijuana - T&S will look at local laws.
Illegal requests where there are no safety risks.
Includes statements like “they’re asking me to paint a copyrighted character, which is illegal.”
Users didn’t follow safety standards (when it’s not causing physical harm to users).
Includes not wearing a harness on the roof, not wearing protective eye gear, etc.
Includes accusations of infecting others with illness.
Users used words indicative of a T&S issue, but didn’t describe a T&S issue (for vague reports, agents should ask for more information before sending to T&S. NOTE: CAT: send back to source/send to CS. CR: Tag as Indeterminate.)
“Stalking” or “stalker” is mentioned, but:
Didn’t describe someone physically following them or showing up uninvited with no business purpose.
“Thief,” “theft,” or “steal” are mentioned, but:
Didn't describe their property being stolen by a user.
Illegal substances were mentioned (“they smelled like pot,” “I think they were on something”), but:
Didn’t specify they saw the presence, use, or dealing of illegal substances.
Undefined threats like “they threatened me,” “threats were made,” or “I feel threatened.”
Agents should gather more info on whether the threat is violent, but if they can’t and they believe the threat is violent, send it to T&S.
Non-violent threats like “I’ll report you to the BBB” or “if you don’t respond to me, I’ll cancel payment.”
Includes when the only concern reported is that users will take legal action against each other.
ACCOUNT ISSUES

Confirmed T&S issues:
Not T&S issues:
Copyright or trademark concerns.
Includes using business name/logo without permission, using trademarked content without permission, etc.
ID Help issues:
Includes account transfer, authorized license user, updating business info (when the business is verified or has verified licenses), and updating or verifying personal information/identity.
Non-US IP address.
Users are disputing their link to another account.
Inauthentic reviews.
Pro avoided paying for leads or asked the customer to pay for their lead.
Questions about background checks.
LEGAL, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND MEDIA

Confirmed T&S issues:
Not T&S issues:
Official contacts:
From law enforcement or government entities.
From an attorney where they're representing a user, legal action against Thumbtack is mentioned.
About current legal action against Thumbtack.
Threats of legal action against Thumbtack when there’s a T&S issue or concern about user or work quality.
Includes when there’s an open incident related to the person stating they’ll take legal action.
Media or news were involved and there’s a T&S issue or concern about user or work quality.
Note: If the user mentions a lawsuit or legal proceeding but does not want to submit a report this would also be considered a T&S issue.
Law enforcement professionals, government officials, or attorneys need help using Thumbtack.
The user states they’ll take legal action against Thumbtack, but no T&S issue is involved.
THUMBTACK PRODUCT OR POLICY

Confirmed T&S issues:
Not T&S issues:
Review disputes
Concerns about discrimination within Thumbtack product or policy.
These shouldn’t be sent as cases - agents should instead submit here.
On-demand bookings: 
No-shows with the job marked as done (any amount).
Both an on-demand and TRANSFER banner
Pro showed up, and there were safety or quality issues (any amount).
Thumbtack Pay:
No-shows where the pro was already paid, and the pro is unresponsive.
Any safety or project quality issue, even if the customer and pro have already agreed on a refund.
Either the pro or the customer disputes the refund request from the other party.
Questions or assistance with Thumbtack product or policy, including.
Refund requests (with no related T&S concern).
Questions about the guarantee when there isn’t a project concern or other T&S issue.
On-demand bookings:
No-shows of any amount with the job NOT marked as done (the pro wasn’t paid).
An on-demand banner, but no TRANSFER banner.
Thumbtack Pay: 
No-shows where the pro was paid, and the pro confirmed a refund already.
Payments made through the product with no other project or safety concerns. (i.e., seeking to refund because they want to pay outside of Thumbtack; pro doesn’t have direct deposit set up)
Additionally, send the following to T&S:

Anything especially abnormal or sensitive that might be best if T&S handled it.
Consult with a manager or SME if you categorize something like this.
Occasionally, the agent will have been told by the T&S team in Slack to send a situation to us even if it’s not traditionally a T&S issue - send these through.
Steps:

Review the chart above to determine whether this is a confirmed T&S issue or not a T&S issue.
If the issue is not a T&S concern:
If working a case or DR:
If it’s coming from Service and Support, transfer ownership back to the previous owner.
If the case did not need to be escalated to T&S according to current guidance, please add the note: “No T&S concern - invalid transfer”.
If it’s not from Service and Support:
If it’s something Service and Support should handle,  transfer ownership to the “Customer Support - Email” queue.
If you're working from a DR and the customer's report shows under Other Resolution Description, always copy the report and paste it into the case record created.
If it’s noise/mailer email, close the case or DR with no action.

If working on a WT, complete the Outcome section and close the WT.
If a TOS violation is found, make sure to action the account in Admin and/or refund the pro, as applicable.
If the issue is a T&S concern:
Check if this issue is related to an existing T&S incident.
If yes, follow these steps.
If not, and you’re working a WT, skip to step 3 (Choose a tier) to determine which Outcome should be selected:
If the T&S concern falls under an indeterminate scenario, select the “indeterminate” Outcome, the appropriate Outcome Detail, and close the WT.
If the T&S concern does NOT fall under an indeterminate scenario, select the “Escalated MTS Case” Outcome Detail and click Save to automatically create a case.
Go to the Related tab in the WT and click on the newly created case to open it in a new tab.
Move on to the next step (case or incident).
If not, and you’re working a DR or case, move to the next step (case or incident).
Helpful tip: If you're categorizing a case that you believe to be a test case, reach out to the Thumbtack employee whose name or account is attached to the case, then send the case to them if they've confirmed it's theirs. If you can't find the case owner, close the case using the steps under (2. a.) above (do not mark it as a test case, as we can't be certain it's a test without consulting the creator).

The chart below explains (in order of priority) which situations should be categorized as which tiers. Stop once you identify the topmost tier that fits and move on to the next step. articles.fullText:
YourProMail Email Directions

Yourpromail is used to consolidate leads from multiple locations/queues to a central queue for a call center to work out of. The pro's account has a dedicated location-specific yourpromail account, that then gets forwarded on to a middle central yourpromail account, that then gets forwarded on to the call center.
Pro specific yourpromail ---> consolidated yourpromail ---> call center
Section 1:
Open an incognito window
Go to www.gmail.com
Sign in using the following credentials:
nmanning@yourpromail.com
password: Thumbtack
Click the 9 square button on the top right [Image: 3d936ef5-78bf-48a4-a5ac-64dfc5b4efd4-image.png]
Click Admin[Image: 7ffb16ce-0468-451f-b669-1a6f65e163e5-image.png]
Click Users[Image: a083a112-4539-4d2a-8f44-ffcb3c0e3749-image.png]
Click Add new user[Image: 309a3b3b-57ea-4aab-b6ca-4025c2b06aaa-image.png]
Enter the First and Last name of the Pro, the suggested email address (example "junkkingflorida") and under “Organizational unit” click the pencil icon,[Image: 6e19cd62-6678-411e-b1d0-d92c540d9eae-image.png]
Click Pro and then Done[Image: 6071bc9d-ac9b-44cc-9151-0a1d640293c2-image.png]
Enter a password & click Add new user. [Image: 2fc405c1-0bfc-4280-b3ce-28a8b8f2f963-image.png]
Record email and password to a master sheet. Example
Log out of gmail[Image: d79df49f-c288-4e64-8b30-ce3f01fbb9fe-image.png]
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section 2:
Go back to www.gmail.com
Sign in using the new user credentials you just created
Click the Cog button and click Settings[Image: d53d5001-2cab-46a6-acd4-54852feb006b-image.png]
Click Forwarding and POP/MAP[Image: ef4234e4-c3a8-4fd8-b6cf-942d13f89819-image.png]
Click Add a forwarding address[Image: 0f00d334-b66f-4afd-a6b4-613f7a0ce4a7-image.png]
Enter the forwarding email address of the main YourProMail Queue and click Next[Image: 78fbb1cd-196e-4fba-a5b3-8ecddee53034-image.png]
Click Forward a copy of incoming mail to and click Save Changes[Image: 3e46562c-c124-4007-b909-9d398fce5a93-image.png]
Click Filters and Blocked Addresses and click Create a new filter[Image: 2ae48868-1eca-47c0-a81c-f5288b223329-image.png]
Enter do-not-reply@thumbtack.com in the From line and click Create Filter[Image: 20d7df4b-7053-4bf4-bf43-04172a1ac1b1-image.png]
Click Never send it to Spam and click Create Filter[Image: 5bf068e0-09a7-4bdc-a775-46df196e54eb-image.png]
Repeat steps 9 & 10 with the email address do-not-reply@pro.thumbtack.com
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section 3:
Locate the Pro's admin account
Click Edit User[Image: 238e2db1-264a-4749-8c84-3bb61d76a1f2-image.png]
Enter the new yourpromail email address in the Email field, Enter a change reason in the Admin Note and click Submit[Image: 39678682-adf2-404e-acb5-9ab974859e05-image.png]
Click Reset password[Image: a1d032b0-25ed-46fe-838d-dd3da1c34f28-image.png]
Enter the same password used you used when setting up the new yourpromail (Section 1. Step 9). and click Update[Image: a5e7751d-e233-4345-b763-afe78a03cb69-image.png]
Send your Pro their new login credentials
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Section 4:
If you don't have access to 1Password, reach out to the IT department to request access
1 Password is a password manager. It provides a place for users to store various passwords, software licenses, and other sensitive information in a virtual vault that is locked with a master password.[Image: 1pass.png]
All YourProMail login information should be stored in 1Password in the case that an account is transferred to a different CSM.
Once you have access to 1Password you will need to add the pro's YourProMail login information to your personal vault (these "vaults" are transferable and accessible by IT so it will prevent losing login information should a CSM be transferred to a different account, leave the company, etc.)
Click the "+" button and select login[Image: add login.png]
Fill in the users' YourProMail email address, the email field (put www.gmail.com), and fill in the label with the name of the parent account for the franchisee you're creating the YourProMail for[Image: info.png]
OPTIONAL (but recommended): The last step before you save is to create a new more secure password. One feature of 1Password is the ability to randomly generate and store passwords. Since these are randomly generated they are generally more secure. If you click on the cog you will see the option to generate a random password. If you do this, you will need to make sure you go back to YourProMail and paste in the new password for the YourProMail account. It's up to you whether or not you make this password match the actual Thumbtack login password.[Image: 1pass password.png]
Click SAVE to save all the pros login information
When you go to login to YourProMail you should be able to come back to 1Password and copy and paste the pros username and email from 1Password to login to their individual YourProMail
If you have any questions regarding this process, please reach out to Miles Stewart or Melissa Madsen.

articles.fullText:
Verified Reviews

Goal(s):
Ensure pro understands the importance of verified reviews and has a strategy in place to solicit verified reviews
First time through play
I’d like to discuss your strategy for soliciting reviews from your Thumbtack customers.
Reviews are a critical piece of your Thumbtack success. Reviews enable customers to contact you with confidence and can help boost your search rankings by completing your profile.
Do you know how to request reviews from your Thumbtack customers?
What is your current strategy for getting more reviews?
Here are some additional ways other pros have used to get more verified reviews.
Incentivize customers to leave you a review.
You could offer a percent off a second service if the customer leaves you a review.
You could offer customers a $5 gift card to starbucks for completing a survey.
While you can incent customers to leave a review, any incentive cannot be contingent on the customer giving a positive review.
Incentivize your crew or have an employee competition.
You could offer free lunch to your crew that has the most customers leave a review in a month.
You could offer gift cards to individuals or crews that get the most reviews in a month.
Ask for a review at the job site.
As you checkout your customer make sure to ask them if they’d be willing to leave you a review.
Leverage the Thumbtack mobile app to send review request during final walk through or billing discussion.
Schedule a review reminder for all your customers.
We’ll even remind them when the time is right if you schedule a review request.
Which of these strategies sound feasible for your business?
I’d like you to try and get [goal] reviews before our next call. Utilize the tips we’ve discussed to improve your success rate.
objection(s):
I don't want to bother my customers
Do you currently have a process for gathering customer feedback after a job? Pursuing reviews is a worthy investment in your business.
If we can get a direct email or text your customer quickly after the job is done, it will be a simple process and fresh on their minds.
I don't have a google business account, how can I pull in reviews?
We can look at setting up a google account for your business, but you also can contact customers directly with your review link.
Follow up on play
Were you able to get [goal] reviews since our last call?
Yes
Excellent! I know it can be difficult to ask for reviews, good job.
Did you run into any roadblocks this week?
What was the most difficult part of getting more reviews?
Have you noticed a difference in the amount or types of customers reaching out to you?
No
What has been holding you back?
What can I do to help you get reviews?
Do you have any recent customers that I can help you request a review from?
Reviews are still the next best thing for you to do, so I would like to cancel our call today and have you use this time so you can think through how we can hit this goal before our next call.
Now that you have a strategy for getting more verified reviews, I’d like to also talk to you about responding to reviews.
You have the ability to respond to each of your verified reviews.
Your response will be visible to future customers, just like the actual review.
Tell the customer what a joy it was to work with them. Be specific about the kind of work you completed for them and tell them not to hesitate to reach out to you in the future.
Responding to negative reviews is challenging, but can actually help you in the long run.
A customer discrediting your business and work ethic is stressful.
What’s more impactful to a future customer than a negative review is a tactful response from a professional.
Apologize to the customer for their perception of a negative experience.
Tactfully explain your side of things. “While I believed we were on the same page due to x, y, z during our communications, I clearly misunderstood, etc.
Let a future customer know you aren’t leaving the negative review unrectified by explaining in your response that you will be reaching out to the customer to rectify the situation.
Please don’t hesitate to reach out when met with a negative review and I can help you craft a great response
Additional Resource(s)

Internal:
Ask For Reviews [General Knowledge]
Response to Reviews [General Knowledge]
Negative Reviews [General Knowledge]

articles.fullText:
Unverified Reviews

Contents
 
1. Overview
2. Process
a. First time through play
b. Objection handling
c. Follow up on play
3. Resources
I. OVERVIEW
 
Help a pro understand the different ways to add unverified reviews and the differences between unverified and verified. 
II. PROCESS
 
FIRST TIME THROUGH PLAY
 
Reviews are a critical piece of your Thumbtack success.
If you were buying or booking anything online, how important would reviews influence your purchasing decision?
Reviews enable customers to contact you with confidence and can help boost your search rankings.
There are two types of reviews on Thumbtack.
Off Platform Reviews are reviews from past customers that you didn’t get through Thumbtack.
Reviews are so critical, it would be unfair if we didn’t allow you to start with some reviews.
Because these are not verified by Thumbtack, we only display 10 on your profile.
You can always get more than 10, but only the most recent 10 will show on your profile.
Most pros don’t take the time to get all 10 off-platform reviews, so this is a good way to differentiate yourself.
Verified reviews are reviews given from past customers that you did get through customers.
You can get as many verified reviews as possible and these reviews are distinguished as ‘verified’ on your profile.
There are two different ways that you can get unverified reviews:
Do you have past customers that you can email and request a review?
If Yes - Can we send them emails right now?
Once you send a request to a past customer, they only have 30 days to complete the review or you will need to send them a new link.
Do you have past customers that you can text and request a review?
If Yes - Can you text them right now?
Once you send a request to a past customer, they only have 30 days to complete the review or you will need to send them a new link.
OBJECTION HANDLING
 
I don't want to bother my customers.
Do you currently have a process for gathering customer feedback after a job? Pursuing reviews is a worthy investment in your business.
If we can get a direct email or text your customer quickly after the job is done, it will be a simple process and fresh on their minds.
FOLLOW UP ON PLAY
 
Unverified Reviews Are Maxed Out
 
You have maxed out your off-platform reviews!
Have you noticed a difference in the amount or types of customers reaching out to you?
You can still get more unverified reviews, but only the most recent 10 will show up on your profile.
Now that we have earned those 10 unverified reviews, moving forward we will shift to focus on continually getting more verified reviews from your thumbtack customers. 

​​​​​​​Unverified Reviews Are Not Maxed Out
It looks like you haven’t been able to get your off-platform reviews yet.
What has been holding you back?
What can I do to help you reach out to past customers and get unverified reviews?
Unverified reviews are still the next best thing for you to do, so I would like to cancel our call today and have you use this time to reach out to more past customers.
As a reminder, there are two different ways to get unverified reviews: send past customers an email request, and/or send past customers an SMS reminder.
IV. RESOURCES

articles.fullText:
Secure Pay

Contents
 
1. Overview
a. PCI compliance
2. Process
a. Set up
a. Initiate SecurePay
b. Process map
c. Troubleshooting
3. FAQ
4. Resources
1. OVERVIEW
Effective as of  March 24, 2022 a new feature has been added to the phone panel called Secure Pay that takes you out of the equation, keeping you compliant and your job here at Thumbtack protected.  
SecurePay is a way for pros to securely provide their credit card information over the phone. Only the Thumbtack Sales team has access to initiate this with a pro
PCI COMPLIANCE 
 
Be PCI compliant 100% of the time by using Secure Pay. Pros can privately and securely provide their credit card details.
 
The purpose of SecurePay is to help us reach 100% PCI compliance. It only replaces how you collect credit card info over the phone. All other processes should remain the same (e.g. getting an Ironclad, adding credits, etc.). Moving forward you should NEVER have pros give you their credit card details over the phone. 
3. PROCESS
 
SET UP
If you will be using Secure Pay, be sure to enable your queue prompt in Click-to-Dial if you haven't already. 
 
Open the Main Menu.
Click Settings.
Select the Queue option
Check both boxes.  

[Image: rtaImage]
 
INITIATE SECUREPAY
As a best practice, make sure the pro has their card out and is ready to provide the details before you click the Start SecurePay button. You may also want to remind them that if they have any issues, they will automatically be returned to you, so just stay on the line. 
 
SecurePay lives within the phone panel. When it comes time to collect the pro's payment details, follow the steps below to get the pro's card info and stay PCI compliant. 
 
Before starting the interaction, start typing your team's name into the On Behalf of Queue field and select your queue, e.g., Outbound Sales.
Please note: You will only need to do this one time if you have selected the "Remember the last selected queue box" in the setup section above.
In order to have the SecurePay option, you need to enter a queue name to the “On Behalf of Queue” when making an outbound call.  e.g., Outbound Sales.
Please note: You will only need to do this one time if you have selected the "Remember the last selected queue box" in the setup section above.
Before starting the interaction, start typing your team's name into the On Behalf of Queue field and select your queue, e.g., Outbound Sales.
Once the call is connected, you can start Secure Pay in one of two ways: 
Click the Script Icon in the interaction.
Click the Secure Pay widget found in the bottom menu of Tack. 
[Image: rtaImage]
Scroll to the bottom, and enter the amount the pro will be charged, the pros PKID. 

[Image: rtaImage]

Click Submit Payment   
[Image: rtaImage]
Once you click this button, you will no longer be able to hear the pro and the pro will be directed to a private line where they will be asked to provide the following.
Card number
Expiration date
CVV number
Pros will be prompted to enter the information 2 times. If the pro does not respond to the second prompt, they will be returned to you. 
NOTE: Before the pro is asked for their CC information, it will repeat the amount they are being charged.
Once the pro has entered all of the information, the payment will process and they will be able to press 2 to return to you. The SecurePay pop-up will update to let you know the outcome (if the payment was successful or not).

[Image: rtaImage]

PROCESS MAP
  
[Image: jq06Nt89djxGcF5vcbqQsPw9JseJVLFkl3IoqrXQadRx278Wr7E6yT-j-OtK039Ky2O4hqTr76PUDri2hmXcuE7Jp5kI7KZDTk5IKKQKgAvmQlvmWlMjvE4cSY6jkMWTdMhrpVWP]
TROUBLESHOOTING
Remember, you can have the pro complete Secure Pay as many times as needed, but if at any point you are ready to move on and SecurePay is not working, you should default to showing them how to add their credit card to their account themselves. 
Never have them read their number to you. It is not worth risking PCI compliance.
Email a link to payments 
One of the easiest options is to email a link to the pro that takes them directly to their payment options. 
NOTE: This only works if no card is on file.  
 
Click the gray box in the Credit Balance section of Admin and an email will be sent. 

[Image: Dlm5MyCmu8KebZnc1MZ-JlqPgs3sFUjcsA3JB14e4BDtxcerajjqv9OViWHm44ou1uVwLGB5VwWGs7NGJqEh8Ivo649UG-2LuAiIlYcBQAAhEl_A4IidEjRmyI4RnuQc7t8_8UsmKNubpFPxVg]

App
Open the Thumbtack app.
Select Profile (from the main menu at the bottom).
Tap the gear icon in the top corner (see image below).
Select Payments.
Tap Add a credit card.
Enter your payment information and tap Save.
Desktop/Web 
Click the menu (or your photo) at the top right.
From the drop-down menu, choose Payments.  
Click Add a credit card. 
From here, enter your credit card details and click Add credit card.
 
4. FAQ
Before sending the pro through SecurePay do I have to disclose anything?The agent will follow normal disclosure procedure (AKA get the ironclad signed, let the pro know the package is nonrefundable, etc.) 

Can I send a pro through the SecurePay connector multiple times?
Yes, if the pro did not have their credit card ready in time or if they needed to try a new credit card because the previous one failed, the agent can send the pro back through the SecurePay connector. 
 
Do we accept prepaid cards, ACH details and checking/ routing information with SecurePay or are only credit cards accepted? 
Credit cards (including prepaid cards) and debit cards that can be used without a PIN number are accepted payment methods. We accept Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover, Diners Club, and JCB payments from customers worldwide.
 
Does SecurePay remove the need for agents to take credit information over the phone?
Yes, to be PCI compliant, agents should NEVER take credit card information over the phone. 
 
How can I provide feedback on SecurePay?
If you have any feedback, please pass this on to your manager. They will then compile and share out weekly to the #salessuccessleadership slack channel. 

How does a pro get their additional credit when purchasing a package?
The agent will have to add the credit to the pros account in Admin after the Pro purchases the package.
 
How many times will a pro be prompted to enter their credit card information?
A pro will be prompted to add their credit card information two times. If they do not add in the information after the second prompt, SecurePay will automatically connect the pro back to the agent. Additionally, the flow will not move on to the expiration date and CVV until the previous state is completed. 
 
How will the pro enter their credit card information?
A pro will enter their credit card information through their phone's dial pad. We are working on adding the ability for a pro to read out their credit card information as well but that is not live yet. 
 
If a pro requests a receipt for payment, will an agent still be able to pull one for them? 
Yes. The agent will follow the current process by reaching out to a Sales manager who will pull the receipt from Stripe and share it with them. 
 
If the pro has protection on their bank account and their bank calls them to verify the payment, what will the pending transaction show?
The payment will show on the Pros statement as coming from Thumbtack Inc. .
 
Is the Secure Pay auto attendant able to select Language Preference?
English is currently the only option. (we are looking to expand this in V2)
 
What do we do if the pro either prefers not to enter the information that way or their phone doesn’t let them interact with the secure pay feature? 
Currently the only way a Pro can enter their credit card information through SecurePay is using their phones dial pad. If the Pro is having trouble, guide them on how to enter their credit card information through their account themselves. (in V2 there will be an option for the user to voice their credit card information)
 
What happens if the card is declined?
The Payment IVR Result will show Payment Failed. You can prompt the Pro back through the SecurePay flow to try again, but they may need to call their bank if there is an issue on their side. (we are looking to add failed payment reasons in V2)
 
What happens if the pro doesn’t return back from the conference to the agent?
The agent can pull the Pro back at any time by clicking Cancel Secure Pay.
 
What if I notice a bug while using SecurePay?
Submit a Help Desk Ticket
 
What if the connector is not popping up?
The connector will only pop up if you have your pop ups enabled. Make sure to allow those by updating your browser settings. Browser Preferences > Privacy and Security > Site Settings > Pop-Ups and Redirects 
 
Will an agent know which step a pro is on in the credit card flow?
Yes, an agent can see what step a pro is on under Payment IVR Messages.

▶ Ways to say it - Talking point for Sales team:
Reviews are a critical piece of your Thumbtack success. There are two types of reviews on Thumbtack; Off-site reviews are reviews from past customers that you didn’t get through Thumbtack, and verified reviews are reviews given from past customers that you did get through customers.
Because reviews are so important, it would be unfair if we didn’t allow you to start with some reviews. You can import reviews from a google business page or request them directly from your customer through email or text.
Reviews calculator
Use the internal Reviews Calculator  sheet to:  
See how many 5 star reviews a pro needs in order to reach a desired review rating.
Calculate a pro's current review average. 
How to use the review calculator: 
Input your numbers directly in the internal  Reviews Calculator .
Don’t make a copy of it.
2. Import reviews
Pros cannot import Facebook reviews at this time. 
Pros can import Google reviews.
Google reviews
Importing reviews helps pros build their profile and show more reviews. Pros can import up to 100 of their most recent reviews from Google. While the initial import is a one-time action, pros can manually refresh these imported reviews at any time to reflect their newest Google reviews. If the pro has fewer than 100 Google reviews at the time of initial import, they can refresh their imported reviews again at a later time when they have more. 

Google reviews only import the following: 
Reviewer name
Date
Rating
Review text
No other information will be pulled over in the import — just the review info
NOTE: Imported reviews aren’t considered verified. They’re used to calculate a pro’s star rating, but not their Top Pro status.
When clicking "Ask for reviews" or “Update” under the Reviews section on their profile page, pros will see the "Add Reviews from Google" option. They will then be prompted to log in to their Google account to import or update eligible reviews.
A few things to note about importing Google reviews:
Initial Import and Refresh: Pros can initially import up to 100 of their most recent Google reviews once. However, they can then manually refresh these imported reviews at any time to reflect their newest Google reviews.
Update Imported Reviews: Pros can update their Google reviews to feature their most recent reviews by clicking the 'Update' button in the 'Reviews' section of their Profile tab."
No Selection: Pros cannot choose which specific Google reviews to import; the system pulls their most recent ones up to the 100-review limit.
No Automatic Updates: Imported Google reviews on Thumbtack will not automatically update if the original reviews on Google are changed. However, pros can manually refresh them.
Responses to Imported Reviews: If a pro has responded to an imported Google review on their profile and then refreshes their Google reviews, their response may be removed if the original review is no longer among the 100 most recent reviews imported. Pros should be aware that refreshing can alter the set of displayed reviews and their associated responses.
Reps should refer to the General Important Considerations for All Imported Reviews section of the internal Reviews (Pro) KA for additional key details. 
▶ Ways to say it - talking point for Sales team:
Reviews are a critical piece of your Thumbtack success. There are two types of reviews on Thumbtack; Off-site reviews are reviews from past customers that you didn’t get through Thumbtack and verified reviews are reviews given from past customers that you did get through customers.
Because reviews are so important, it would be unfair if we didn’t allow you to start with some reviews. You can import up to 100 reviews from a Google business page or request up to 10 directly from previous customers through email or text. 
How pros import reviews
 
Pro steps: To import Google reviews, pros will follow the applicable steps in the How to ask for reviews – Thumbtack Help article. This process can be completed via the Thumbtack app or desktop. 
For a step by step walkthrough of this process, reps can refer to the process below: 
Go to your Reviews page.
Select Ask for reviews.
Choose Add reviews from Google.
NOTE: Pros can't import Facebook reviews since FB changed how it integrates with our platform.
Follow the prompts and log in to Google.
The email on the Google account doesn't need to match the email on their Thumbtack account in order to import reviews.
Choose the page you want to import reviews from.
Preview the reviews you're adding, then select Add reviews to post them to your profile.
They don’t get to choose which reviews are imported, and we’ll still only display the most recent reviews from non-Thumbtack customers on their profile (whether from Google or directly from past customers).
Once a pro imports reviews, they can’t edit or delete them.
If the reviews violate the Content and Review Policy, Thumbtack will remove them.
If the reviews are updated on the pro's Google account, the reviews won’t be updated on the pro’s Thumbtack profile. 
For steps on  how to refresh their google reviews, see the internal Reviews (Pro) KA. 
How Google Import Reviews Work: Talking points 
For additional talking points on importing Google reviews, refer to the internal Reviews (Pro) KA. 
This section provides clear talking points for frontline reps to explain the process and limitations of importing reviews, including which platforms are supported and current restrictions.

English talking point
Spanish talking point 
I see Facebook reviews on other pros' profiles, so why can't I import reviews from Facebook?
Veo evaluaciones de Facebook en los perfiles de otros profesionales, entonces, ¿por qué no puedo importar evaluaciones de Facebook?
Facebook recently changed the way its platform integrates with Thumbtack. This has made it so Facebook reviews can't be imported at this time. You can still import reviews from Google, or request reviews from customers not on Thumbtack by sharing your review link.
Facebook cambió recientemente la forma en que su plataforma se integra con Thumbtack. Esto ha hecho que las evaluaciones de Facebook no se puedan importar en este momento. Aún puede importar evaluaciones de Google o solicitar evaluaciones de clientes que no estén en Thumbtack compartiendo su enlace de evaluaciones.
Can I edit or delete an imported review?
¿Puedo editar o eliminar una evaluación importada?
Our Content and Review Policy applies to all reviews on your profile, so imported can’t be removed or changed unless they violate that policy.
Nuestras póliza de contenido y evaluación se aplica a todas las evaluaciones de su perfil, por lo que las importaciones no se pueden eliminar ni modificar a menos que infrinjan esta política.
Can I respond on Thumbtack to imported reviews?
¿Puedo responder en Thumbtack a las evaluaciones importadas?
Yes, you can respond, but keep in mind that the review is not from a Thumbtack customer. That means the customer won’t see your response, but other customers on Thumbtack will. So be sure to respond professionally — just like you would to any other review.
Sí, puede responder, pero tenga en cuenta que la evaluación no es de un cliente de Thumbtack. Eso significa que el cliente no verá su respuesta, pero otros clientes de Thumbtack sí. Así que asegúrese de responder profesionalmente, como lo haría con cualquier otra evaluación.
Why can’t I choose which reviews to import from Google?
¿Por qué no puedo elegir qué evaluaciones importar de Google?
We want your reviews to accurately show how customers feel about working with you. Allowing pros to pick and choose which reviews they want to display could lead to a poor experience for Thumbtack customers.
Queremos que sus evaluaciones demuestren exactamente cómo se sienten los clientes al trabajar con usted. Permitir que los profesionales elijan las evaluaciones que desean mostrar podría generar una mala experiencia para los clientes de Thumbtack.
Facebook

This is currently turned off and pros cannot import Facebook reviews.
3. Different types of reviews
Help a pro understand the different ways to add unverified reviews and the differences between unverified and verified. 
First time through play
Reviews are a critical piece of your Thumbtack success.
If you were buying or booking anything online, how important would reviews influence your purchasing decision?
Reviews enable customers to contact you with confidence and can help boost your search rankings.
There are two types of reviews on Thumbtack.
Off Platform Reviews are reviews from past customers that you didn’t get through Thumbtack.
Reviews are so critical, it would be unfair if we didn’t allow you to start with some reviews.
Because these are not verified by Thumbtack, we only display 10 on your profile.
You can always get more than 10, but only the most recent 10 will show on your profile.
Most pros don’t take the time to get all 10 off-platform reviews, so this is a good way to differentiate yourself.
Verified reviews are reviews given from past customers that you did get through customers.
You can get as many verified reviews as possible and these reviews are distinguished as ‘verified’ on your profile.
There are two different ways that you can get unverified reviews:
Do you have past customers that you can email and request a review?
If Yes - Can we send them emails right now?
Once you send a request to a past customer, they only have 30 days to complete the review or you will need to send them a new link.
Do you have past customers that you can text and request a review?
If Yes - Can you text them right now?
Once you send a request to a past customer, they only have 30 days to complete the review or you will need to send them a new link.
Objection handling
I don't want to bother my customers.
Do you currently have a process for gathering customer feedback after a job? Pursuing reviews is a worthy investment in your business.
If we can get a direct email or text your customer quickly after the job is done, it will be a simple process and fresh on their minds.
Follow up on play
Unverified Reviews Are Maxed Out
You have maxed out your off-platform reviews!
Have you noticed a difference in the amount or types of customers reaching out to you?
You can still get more unverified reviews, but only the most recent 10 will show up on your profile.
Now that we have earned those 10 unverified reviews, moving forward we will shift to focus on continually getting more verified reviews from your thumbtack customers. 
Unverified Reviews Are Not Maxed Out
It looks like you haven’t been able to get your off-platform reviews yet.
What has been holding you back?
What can I do to help you reach out to past customers and get unverified reviews?
Unverified reviews are still the next best thing for you to do, so I would like to cancel our call today and have you use this time to reach out to more past customers.
As a reminder, there are two different ways to get unverified reviews: send past customers an email request, and/or send past customers an SMS reminder.
4. Importance of verified reviews
Ensure pro understands the importance of verified reviews and has a strategy in place to solicit verified reviews
First time through play 
I’d like to discuss your strategy for soliciting reviews from your Thumbtack customers.
Reviews are a critical piece of your Thumbtack success. Reviews enable customers to contact you with confidence and can help boost your search rankings by completing your profile.
Do you know how to request reviews from your Thumbtack customers?
What is your current strategy for getting more reviews?
Here are some additional ways other pros have used to get more verified reviews.
Incentivize customers to leave you a review.
You could offer a percent off a second service if the customer leaves you a review.
You could offer customers a $5 gift card to Starbucks for completing a survey.
While you can incent customers to leave a review, any incentive cannot be contingent on the customer giving a positive review.
Incentivize your crew or have an employee competition.
You could offer free lunch to your crew that has the most customers leave a review in a month.
You could offer gift cards to individuals or crews that get the most reviews in a month.
Ask for a review at the job site.
As you checkout your customer make sure to ask them if they’d be willing to leave you a review.
Leverage the Thumbtack mobile app to send review request during final walk-through or billing discussion.
Schedule a review reminder for all your customers.
We’ll even remind them when the time is right if you schedule a review request.
Which of these strategies sound feasible for your business?
I’d like you to try and get [goal] reviews before our next call. Utilize the tips we’ve discussed to improve your success rate.
Objection handling
I don't want to bother my customers
Do you currently have a process for gathering customer feedback after a job? Pursuing reviews is a worthy investment in your business.
If we can get a direct email or text your customer quickly after the job is done, it will be a simple process and fresh on their minds.
Follow up on play 
Were you able to get [goal] reviews since our last call?
Yes
Excellent! I know it can be difficult to ask for reviews, good job.
Did you run into any roadblocks this week?
What was the most difficult part of getting more reviews?
Have you noticed a difference in the amount or types of customers reaching out to you?
No

What can I do to help you get reviews?
Do you have any recent customers that I can help you request a review from?
Reviews are still the next best thing for you to do, so I would like to cancel our call today and have you use this time so you can think through how we can hit this goal before our next call.
Now that you have a strategy for getting more verified reviews, I’d like to also talk to you about responding to reviews.
You have the ability to respond to each of your verified reviews.
Your response will be visible to future customers, just like the actual review.
Tell the customer what a joy it was to work with them. Be specific about the kind of work you completed for them and tell them not to hesitate to reach out to you in the future.
Responding to negative reviews is challenging, but can actually help you in the long run.
A customer discrediting your business and work ethic is stressful.
What’s more impactful to a future customer than a negative review is a tactful response from a professional.
Apologize to the customer for their perception of a negative experience.
Tactfully explain your side of things. “While I believed we were on the same page due to x, y, z during our communications, I clearly misunderstood, etc.
Let a future customer know you aren’t leaving the negative review unrectified by explaining in your response that you will be reaching out to the customer to rectify the situation.
Please don’t hesitate to reach out when met with a negative review and I can help you craft a great response

1. OVERVIEW
Pros and customers can fill out our reactivation form to request the reactivation of their account. We’ll look into their account and get back to them within three business days.
Once they fill out the form, a work ticket is created and worked on by the Back Office team behind the scenes. Check out the Reactivation Flow Chart.
NOTE: These processes are for the Back Office team only. (see the Escalated CS case and Trust and Safety outcomes sections below.

[Image: rtaImage]

HOW TO ASSIGN AN OUTCOME
Assigning the correct Outcome is important in processing a work ticket. Here are the Outcome options, what they mean and when to use them:

[Image: 9TOwjeJylTIfR3u9-t4s2gV-OT7iZs5YrzPAK24pjBj2EQBk4prx_2hohTEiCKhDLwgFHaD88R-_fEIjp1X_i-bV7b_h7rKl2ot62g1YMUl7GJC80fpDcnjYJxlGY7gRRT_ZVBWAOi7ThfOdsx-awOkhE09G1B_LGjISdFi8wgLrtDD2zXC6mrGy]

Ticket is Duplicate - Only use if you come across a ticket you've already worked on and know it is a duplicate.
Ticket is Pending Further Review - Use only for non–Trust and Safety cases awaiting action. Do not use this for Trust and Safety situations
HOW TO ASSIGN AN OUTCOME DETAIL
Assigning the correct outcome detail is important in processing a work ticket, as this will dictate what email the user is sent, if at all.  See the Outcome detail options below, what they mean, and when to use them:

Escalate MTS Case - Use to auto-create a Quick Case and route it to the Proactive MI Queue for Trust and Safety review. 
Selecting this automatically hides the MTS Deactivated field. This is expected, so complete Internal Notes before saving.
MTS Deactivated - Use for Trust and safety BAU scenarios.
Not Deactivated - If the user is enabled or previously reinstated.

NOTE: If you select "MTS Deactivated" as your Outcome detail, you must also populate the MTS Deactivated Reasons field. See the Trust and Safety Outcomes section below.

HOW TO ASSIGN USER TO WORK TICKET 
Occasionally you’ll come across a Work Ticket that doesn’t have a user assigned. To assign a user to the ticket, follow these steps: 
You will search the email address in Salesforce to find the account. 
Copy the pros PK ID and search in the “Contact Field” in Salesforce. 
Click Save to assign the user. 
Refresh your tab, and the user will appear on the right side under “Outcome”.

Not all Bi-lingual reps will have access to sell to our Spanish professionals.  It is up to each sales representative to qualify a pro and determine who they should be in contact with departmentally. 
PROS WHO QUALIFY FOR SPANISH HANDOFF 
Pros who:
request Spanish assistance, 
professionals who show difficulty communicating outside of the Spanish language, 
or those who have marked Spanish as their primary language in the product, 

should be handed off to the Spanish sales team. 
QUALIFYING QUESTIONS 
Would you prefer assistance/onboarding in Spanish?
Does your business primarily operate in the Spanish language? 
Will we be working with anyone who prefers training or assistance in Spanish? 
II. PROCESS
​​​​​​​
First, attempt to complete a live transfer via the Spanish sales line. 
If no one is available: 
Book a scheduled call: 30-min calendared meeting via YCBM.
Calendar links: Spanish Sales
When booked, send booked rep the following:
Pro AND Spanish sales rep on invite.
Best contact number. 
Pro PK number
Person/s names + role(s) expected in call. 
If neither option is possible, slack #Spanish-Live-Transfers channel with any questions about the pro or process. They will then be assigned for a return call. 
Mark primary language
If not already completed, mark Spanish as pros primary language in the pros contact information.

National Account Handoff Process | Sales

Contents

I. Overview
a. National account qualifications
II. Process
III. Referral
IV. Resources
I. OVERVIEW

This article goes over how to qualify sales leads as a good fit for the National Account Team and the handoff process. 
NATIONAL ACCOUNT QUALIFICATIONS 
 
National Account Qualifications (must meet at least one of the following):
 
Franchise – Is it a franchise, OR
Locations – Multi-state (doing business in 1+ states), AND in a ↓
Home Category – See list of focus Home categories here
*Pro/business is NOT required to be in a home category if they meet criteria #1 or #2.  
 
*All referrals outside the defined focus home categories (listed above) must be approved by a National rep prior to hand off to qualify by sending a slack to #sales_strategic.
II. PROCESS
Confirm – Confirm Account owner - See AccountMappings (Column C - AE) - *Updates daily
Slack – Any questions, referral (account) details, and link to lead/opp. to #sales_strategic.  National rep will confirm calendar for booking (i.e. S. Atwood or J. Ostler)
Book Scheduled Zoom Call: 30-min. calendared meeting (*Must be a scheduled Zoom meeting)
Calendar links: 
Shane Atwood​ (all Neighborly brands + non-franchise)
Yael Emmerich | Jeremy Ostler | Jason Grace | Shoma Lodhia | Holly Nagle (all non-neighborly franchise brands)
Include:
Pro (referral) + National rep on invite
Best contact number (backup to Zoom) 
*Schedule at least 24hrs in advance (unless approved by national rep)
Convert lead to a Strategic Opportunity type 
Move Opportunity stage to SQO (Sales Qualified Opportunity) in SFDC (TACK)
Add your name to: ‘Sent to Strategic by’
Log call notes on Opportunity including any relevant information (i.e. company size, contact's role, goals, etc.)
Handoff Form
Select: ‘Next’ to begin the handoff process.
Then ‘Yes’ to the question: "Is this a Strategic or Managed Account".
Click Finish.
III. REFERRAL
 
Qualified Referrals – Qualified Referrals count as 1/2 sale.  *Note: Referral (pro) MUST attend calendared meeting with a National rep to qualify.  Please be sure to let the pro know that the call will take place via Zoom. 
 
Reporting – After the pro has attended the Zoom meeting, the National AE will update the Opportunity and within 24hrs and the Sales rep will be able to see the ½ sale referral reflected on the Sales Commissions dash within 24-48hrs.
 
No Shows – In cases where the pro is a no call/no show, the National AE will push the referral back to the referring Sales rep to reschedule a booked Zoom meeting between the National AE and the prospective partner.
IV. RESOURCES
 
Agent –
Sales Commissions
AccountMappings 
List of focus Home categories here
#sales_strategic
