b. Pro eligibility
II. Process
a. Onboarding
i. Existing national account
ii. New national account
b. Contract validation
c. Authorized license user
III. FAQs
IV. Resources
I. OVERVIEW

Enterprise pros typically do not engage with in-product flows directly, which causes friction when it comes to license verification. 
 
In order for us to capture the licensed status of Enterprise pros with less friction than our current self-serve process and create a more seamless flow for pros, the National Accounts team will gather license verification information at the time of onboarding/activation when pros are most receptive. 
 
This allows us to increase the number of license-verified pros on Thumbtack. A license-verified status is a great way to communicate the quality of these enterprise pros to customers and help them differentiate themselves from unlicensed pros. 
 
The license verification process allows the national account enterprise pro license to be verified by either:
 
Signing a contract addendum confirming that the business is licensed OR 
Going through the manual verification process in an expedited fashion
 
Highly motivated pros can now get through the process and see the value in getting the license badge to justify value.
HIGH-LEVEL PROCESS OVERVIEW
 
Read Enterprise Pro License Verification: National Accounts Process for additional context behind this SOP.
 

[Image: aCuuVDV0FiPIr4RvpBzUlIHDiZ9T9KUx92LoWXQtL3go9Eqkm8hAE2ozz0biVas2ELq3CSM24mritYU4Ow-ywqv-8e1FquzjmT2MlidvoUkv1wMkPa4O2QoCFS_EXLzaNxc_DdJH9yZwdmfGHKunce9kWJfwbfm-diFt4MmqFBIgHnysisK6xm-WsGb8Rw]


PRO ELIGIBILITY
 
In order for a pro to go through this process, they need to be eligible. Follow the steps to see if a pro qualifies: 
 
Must be considered a “National Account” 
Requirement:
5 locations or multi-state (only needs to cross state lines) and/or franchise
Only pros that offer services for categories falling under the following occupations (i.e. they have a license that we currently verify)
Accountant
Attorney
Carpenter
Drywall Specialist
Electrician
Engineer and Technical Designer (includes Architects)
Floor, Carpet, and Tile Specialist
General Contractor
Gutter Specialist
HVAC Specialist
Inspector and Restorer
Insulation Installer
Landscaper (includes Landscape Architect)
Legal Service Provider
Mason
Massage Therapist
Metalworker
Mover
Painter
Paver (includes Concrete work)
Pest Control Specialist
Plumber
Pool and Spa Specialist
Roofer and Sider
II. PROCESS
 
ONBOARDING [SALES + NATIONAL ACCOUNTS]
 
National Accounts can receive a “License Verified” badge two ways:
 
Contract validation- Pro signs a contract agreeing that all of their services/locations have the necessary licenses
Authorized license user - Pro wants to go through authorized license user flow instead of including licensing verbiage in their contract
 
EXISTING NATIONAL ACCOUNTS
 
[Sales] reaches out to their current accounts (must be an eligible pro) via email then follow up directly 
If account would like to sign an addendum, [Sales] to work with [Legal] to have contract addendum drafted up and signed
Then proceed to Contract validation section
If the account would like to go through the existing authorized license user flow, [Success] to get necessary license information from pro. 
Proceed to Authorized license user section for specifics
 
NEW NATIONAL ACCOUNTS
 
[Success] checks whether the National Account will be verified either via Contract validation or Authorized license user, then proceeds to appropriate section.
CONTRACT VALIDATION
 
Trigger Action: Pro signs a contract agreeing that all of their services/locations have the necessary licenses
 
Once pro fills out required agreements, post the enterprise license request in License Verification for Enterprise Pros (National Accounts) filling in all the requested information.
Post in the #National_Account_Priority_Verification channel and provide the following:
Confirm Ironclad contract has been signed by Thumbtack + National Account 
Provide link to Ironclad doc 
Confirm License Verification for Enterprise Pros (National Accounts) has been filled out
 
Once these steps are completed, Trust and Safety will review the contract, add the license, and confirm their “license verified” status.
AUTHORIZED LICENSE USER
 
Trigger Action: Pro wants to go through authorized license user flow instead of including licensing verbiage in their contract
 
Collects the following information from pro:
License Holder Name
License Holder Email
License State
License Type
License Number
Written confirmation from license holder of who is authorized to work under their license
Signed Ironclad agreement that pro is authorized to work under the license
Fills out ID Help Form on behalf of pro
Go to https://help.thumbtack.com/id-help
In the “Your Name” field, fill in [Pro’s Name] and add “(National Account - Standard)” after the pros name.
Make sure to include “(National Account - Standard)” after the pro’s name, so that ID Help Queue specialists don’t accidentally pick up the ticket  and the team can more easily identify what license verification process to use.
Pro’s Email: Fill in [Pro’s Name] 
Select “Help with a license”
Select “I’m an authorized user of someone else’s license”
Fill in [License Holder’s Name] and [License Holder’s Email] in respective fields
Click “Submit”
Posts in #National_Account_Priority_Verification Slack that a ID Help form has been created. Provides:
Pro’s name/email 
License holder name/email


Once these steps are completed, Trust & Safety will follow the standard authorized license user process to confirm with the license holder and collect a signed contract with both parties before confirming their “license verified” status.
III. FAQs
  
What should we do about enterprise pros that have licenses that we don’t verify (such as brokers)? Should we start verifying additional licenses?
Seth Ellison to coordinate with Ashley Powell, and Ashley to talk to Carmen Groom so that we can scope impact.

articles.fullText:
Leads, Contacts, Opps & Pipeline Management

Contents
I. Overview
II. Process
a. Lead to opportunity
b. Opportunity stages
c. Pipeline management 
d. Opportunity ownership
e. MTS related issues 
f. Other policies
III. Resources 
I. OVERVIEW
 
As you work with pros you are expected to move them through the sales funnel and accurately track their journey.
 
Accurately tracking the type of leads you are working from in Salesforce is a key part of managing your sales pipeline. Here is how to correctly convert Salesforce leads into opportunities and how to move those opportunities through the various sales stages.  
II. PROCESS
 
LEAD TO OPPORTUNITY 
 
Salesforce leads are created when Thumbtack has enough contact information to reach a pro. 
 
The rule of thumb for converting a lead into an opportunity is when the pro shows general interest in speaking with you about Thumbtack. 
 
Examples of interest:
They agree to a future meeting to discuss a partnership
They call you
They respond to an email
They schedule time on your calendar
 
NOTE: 
Qualification should not factor into whether or not you convert a lead. The fact they reached out to you means they are an opportunity. You can qualify them after they have an opportunity.
Make sure a pro/Lead is not working with another AE before converting to an opportunity. Once you convert an opportunity, leave notes that explain why you converted it.  
OPPORTUNITY STAGES 
 
​The following salesforce stages are defined to help you mark the correct opportunity stage:  

[Image: hUYblNUvJf8AgOOFj2I7opFSPRvuqMdV_m7mIZns-Hy4_bl12CFZigdAirseiKgJ1usSoYiOBqm-RKWWaH9K2Wtb_23pjjY9oamyVIpPOceEIUF3cO9GvIvwO0GG_0XSNGDDY-pNmqlnjzca0kGaUc8]

 
STAGE
DEFINTION
EXAMPLE
New
No previous attempts
Pro schedules on your calendar and you have not had any previous call attempts with this Lead/Pro
Attempting
Outreach with no response
Outreach with no response
Contacted
Outreach with response
You called a pro and got their Decision Maker or Gate Keeper but were asked to call back at another time
Sales qualified opportunity 
Contact made, qualification part of script complete
You have contacted the pro and discovered they are a viable pro for one of our programs and have interest in talking more.
You scheduled an appointment with a specific date or you have only made it partially through your pitch.
Pitched
Pitched, awaiting payment
Pro has said yes but you still need to collect payment or contract.
Committed
N/A
** This is only used by the National team.**
Closed lost
Pitch was given/pro decided not to buy package
You have finalized your sale, but the pro decides against purchasing a package
Closed won
Payment collected, handoff form completed
You finalized the sale (collected payment and/or contract)
You scheduled time with the pro and a success agent (when applicable)
And you completed the handoff form
PIPELINE MANAGEMENT 
 
When you own and work an Opportunity, follow the directions below to ensure you stay on top of your Opportunities:
Be in contact with the pro at a minimum of every 30 days
Leave detailed notes that contain your follow-up plan including the date you plan to follow-up.  
If a pro says to call back in six (6) months, check-in once every 30 days or avoid losing the opportunity.
NOTE: If you have not contacted the pro within 30 days, or you have not left notes, the open Opportunity can be assigned to another AE (only managers can update the Opportunity Owner).
OPPORTUNITY OWNERSHIP 
 
Lead Type field: Leads should only be closed by the team marked in the Lead type field. (i.e. if the Lead Type equals Inbound Sales, only an Inbound Sales AE can close it.)
Existing Leads: Check SFDC for an existing Lead/Opportunity associated with the email or phone number to see If a pro is already working with another AE. 
Duplicate Leads, Contacts, or Opportunities: If a duplicate Lead, Contact, or Opportunity occurs (on either the phone number or email), the AE who made the first contact and left notes will assume the sale.
Exception: It’s 30 days past any activity or there is no noted future follow-up dates.
If the pro mentions they spoke to someone prior, even if the pro doesn’t remember the AE’s name, you are to check SFDC for an existing Lead, Contact, or Opportunity.
Booked calls: If and only if a pro books with an AE, is the AE allowed to convert the Lead to an Opportunity and assume ownership.
If the pro requests to work with another AE, you must put the pro and Thumbtack first, and honor the request. If Opportunity is Closed Lost, free game. The pro must proactively bring this up to you.
Closed Lost Opportunities: If a pro calls in and is a previously Closed Lost Opportunity, you can create a new Opportunity.
MTS RELATED ISSUES

See Marketplace Trust and Safety (T&S) issues overview.
Blocklisted: Some pros have been removed from Thumbtack. Do not call or sell to these pros. See Knowledge for how to recognize and handle these pros.  
Account Hold: If a pro has an account hold, you can sell and activate at the pro, however you must resolve the hold. They will only count towards quota, once the account hold has been removed.
Deactivated Account: If an account is deactivated due to MTS-related issues, do not reach out. If the pro has deactivated their account, you can reach out to learn more and attempt to sell and activate them.
OTHER POLICIES
 
There are a few things to consider when determining which leads are acceptable to work. Here are some policies that impact leads:
 
When to call – 
Time zones: Only contact pros between the hours of 8 a.m. (or 9 a.m. in the case of IL, MI & NM) and 8 p.m. (pro’s time zone).
Thumbtack DNC: Some pros have asked Thumbtack not to contact them. Do not call these pros.
 
Handoffs – 
Spanish-speaking pros: If a pro speaks Spanish and would prefer to speak to an AE who also speaks Spanish, they must be transferred to the Spanish team. Follow the process on Spanish Team Handoff. 
​IV. RESOURCES

articles.fullText:
How To Transfer Calls To Support Team (Sales Rep)

Contents

1. Overview
a. Reasons to transfer to Support
2. Process
a. How to transfer to Support
3. Resources
1. OVERVIEW
With Sales routing in place, you may receive calls for pros or customers who have questions related to their actual Thumbtack account and not the related sale. 
If there’s an opportunity to sell the pro, you should try. 
If you receive an inbound call, introduce yourself first.
Talking point: "Thumbtack Strategic Accounts, this is [Your Name], what can I do for you?"
A lead was created and a callback to an inbound call can’t get any warmer. 
If it's Sales related, start by introducing yourself, continuing with your pitch. 
If they have general questions about how Thumbtack works or signing up, answer them. 
If they qualify, suggest they work with a specialist (Thumbtack expert).
Talking point:  My name is [Your Name], it looks like your call was automatically directed to me because we're looking to partner with new pros to help them get set up for success, and your business came up as someone we see a lot of potential in…
If they have questions about their account, or any of the issues listed below, follow the process to transfer to Service and Support.
NOTE: Service and Support phone lines are available Monday - Friday 8 am - 5 pm MST. See Support Ops Guide.
REASONS FOR TRANSFERRING TO SERVICE AND SUPPORT
Background check questions | See Background Checks KA
Disputing a review | See Reviews (Pro) KA
Landing page lead was trying to contact support not Sales
Reactivate a blocklisted account | See Removed or Banned Users  KA
Refund request on a lead | See Lead Refunds  KA
Troubleshooting (Technical difficulties with the app or desktop) | See Basic Troubleshooting | App & Web KA
2. PROCESS
​​HOW TO TRANSFER CALL TO SUPPORT TEAM
To transfer to Service and Support, follow the below steps:
In the Phone Panel, place the caller on hold.
Click the “Transfer” icon [Image: rtaImage] in the communications menu to start the transfer.
Type in the queue you’re transferring to  in the transfers field (e.g., Premier Pro Support, Pro Support, etc). See Genesys > Queues KA for list. 
[Image: rtaImage]
Click “Consult.” to warmly transfer the call to Support and stay on the line-- (this is very important).
Clicking “Blind” will cold transfer the call. We don’t use the “blind” transfer option when transferring calls to Support. 

[Image: rtaImage]

When the transfer starts, you will see a Transfer interaction with the two calls below it. 

[Image: rtaImage]

If you have one call selected and press the Hold icon, it will toggle you over to the other call.
E.g., if you select the destination call (it will turn green) and then click the Disconnect icon, it will only hang up on the destination call and keep the original call. Great for if you transfer to the wrong number. 
If you have one call selected and press the Hold icon, it will toggle you over to the other call.
When the call is answered,  a transfer interaction appears in the display that shows the number of connected participants, and a timer that indicates how long since the transfer was started.
Initially, the original call is on hold and you are connected to the person or queue that you selected to consult.
To interact with one caller, click on the separate interactions using the icons in the communication menu. 
E.g., if you select the destination call (it will turn green) and then click the Disconnect icon, it will only hang up on the destination call and keep the original call. Great for if you transfer to the wrong number. 
If you have one call selected and press the Hold icon, it will toggle you over to the other call.
To talk to all people simultaneously, click All  [Image: rtaImage]between the interactions. All turns green, indicating that the phone connection is live between all people.

[Image: rtaImage]

Once the advocate gives the go ahead, you can complete the transfer and leave the call by clicking “Complete.”
To complete the transfer and send the original call to its destination, you must click Transfer[Image: rtaImage]  again, and then click the Complete button.
The transfer completes and the initial call drops off your interaction list.

[Image: rtaImage]

NOTE: If you aren't able to get in touch with Support, post in #xfnc_depts_help Slack channel with the pros admin, and a description of the pro's issue; these details are crucial to Support advocates, and help them provide the best experience possible.

articles.fullText:
How to Manage a Franchise

Contents
 
I. Overview
II. Best practices
III. Resources
I. OVERVIEW
 
UNDERSTAND WHO THE KEY STAKEHOLDERS ARE
 
Key stakeholders are the individuals that are:
Being held responsible for the franchisees' performance on Thumbtack (corporate)
Paying for leads (corporate or franchisees)
Ensure all key stakeholders are included in communications
FIND OUT WHO IS GOING TO DRIVE CHANGE
 
With how many POC's you have with franchises it's sometimes difficult to figure out who is going to drive change
Corporate
This may be the individuals being held responsible for the franchisees' performance
This may be an individual that's trying to prove themselves for a promotion or striving to be recognized by someone at corporate
Franchisees
This may be the person who's actually paying for leads
This may be the individual that's been appointed by the franchisee to handle Thumbtack
The person who's going to drive change may not always be obvious. It will take digging to see who's truly going to step up when it comes to performance on Thumbtack.
AUTOMATE WHERE POSSIBLE 
 
Find ways to automate profile building and onboarding (ie using the Sales and Onboarding teams) process. Franchisees are often pressed for time. Anything we can do to speed up the process of getting started on Thumbtack is often appreciated and encouraged by corporate.
It's important to note here that finding a balance between helping franchisees but also helping them understand that we won't be doing everything for them is crucial. They need to understand that being on Thumbtack is going to take effort on their part.
Other ways to automate/speed up onboarding:
Collecting profile material from corporate
Pictures
Standardized answers to QA section
Standardized intro section
Standardized profile pictures
BALANCING CORPORATE’S PLAN OR EXECUTION VS. FRANCHISES' PLAN OF EXECUTION 
 
How a corporation wants to carry out a plan might not always align with what the franchisee has in mind.
Again, this is about finding a balance. Look for ways to find a good middle ground.
This might take some time to figure out.
Remember who is paying for the leads, but don't let that be the guiding hand in making decisions.
SET EXPECTATIONS EARLY AND OFTEN
Ensure corporate understands your role as a CSM and what you expect of them in order to achieve success on the platform. Likewise, ask corporate what their expectations being on Thumbtack.
Expectations should be resurfaced often whether that be on phone calls, emails, QBR's, or account planning sessions.
Ensure franchisees understand that it takes effort to succeed on Thumbtack. Corporate may be communicating to franchisees that they have a CSM to help them on Thumbtack which could potentially create a sense that Thumbtack is a more "hands off" platform. Ensure the franchisee understands that, although we want to make things as smooth and seamless for them as possible, that doesn't mean we will be doing everything for them.
II. BEST PRACTICES
Prioritize your Parent Accounts: this is recommended whenever receiving a new account and at the beginning of each quarter.
 
Block time on your calendar to go through all of your parent accounts. Prioritize them by account type.(Decentralized, Centralized, and Large Local)
Then prioritize them by engagement with you (level of neediness), engagement with Thumbtack, and the potential of each account
Potential request volume, revenue, and expansion (# of potential locations or franchisees to onboard)
Create a prioritization list of your parent accounts from 1-10+ (1 being the most important)
 
Based on your new priority list, you should always make sound decisions based off of this list. i.e. putting out fires, responding to emails, calls, daily tasks etc.

Your Decentralized/Franchise accounts will most likely be your priority. So how do you manage your franchise with all of your other accounts?
BEST PRACTICES
 
Use Your Calendar - your calendar is your best friend
For my other accounts (down my priority list), like my large locals, I would block time once a week, pick the cadence that works for you/your accounts, to look into their account
Check on the health of their account, review their account plans and action items, check their revenue, check in/email them if needed.
This allows you to still always be aware of how all of your accounts are doing, but gives you the rest of your week to focus on your priority accounts which is most likely your franchise.
Set up recurring calls with all of your parent accounts and take those schedule times to prep for these calls
This will mostly be monthly, but figure out a cadence that works for you/your accounts
Notice trends from your accounts and change your calendar accordingly
For example: I knew that Monday morning were really busy for me and I would receive a lot of FCI emails because zees would email me with questions/updates/needs from their weekly meeting with their operations manager. Because of this I blocked an hour for emails every Monday morning and every day for the week I block off 30 minutes in the morning for emails and to prep for my day.
I also don’t take calls before 10am to plan my day and keep my mornings open
Block 30 minutes before each call to prepare
Stay Organized
Every doc, sheet, slide deck, mass email templates etc should originate from your company's drive folder. Managing a franchise especially can get hectic. Having one place to go for everything will save you a lot of time and stress.
Organize your drive folder by title that make sense to you so you can easily access files if needed
Document major changes in Tack on the parent account and date the change
This is super helpful to reference when needed for very high level updates/changes
Pull up your account plan regularly and update/take notes on it
Emails
To manage the franchise piece I would make sure with emails and tasks throughout the day that I finish everything by EOD for my priority account and prioritize those tasks over other parent accounts.
I always prioritize my corporate emails over franchise emails
I will respond to emails with other accounts on the same day I received them but tell the accounts I’ll look into it get back to them tomorrow or in a few days depending on the situation.
I set the exception from day one that I’m in meetings and calls all day so the best way to reach me is to email me or book a call with me. If its an emergency you can call me but I am constantly checking my email anyway and we end up playing phone tag if you call since I’m in meetings.
Only if this makes sense for you/your accounts
Recurring Tasks
I block recurring tasks in my calendar to check dashboards for my franchise, revenue, missed contacts etc
Any major tasks from my account plan
Any small to do’s throughout the day
III. RESOURCES
​​​​​​​

articles.fullText:
Getting Approval to Make Account/Profile Changes

Contents
 
I. Overview
a. Request made on recorded line
b. Request made on non-recorded line
c. Request made via email
I. OVERVIEW
 
Only the Account Owner or Authorized User can approve changes to the profile that could result in charges to the pro’s account. These changes are things like:
 
Increasing or decreasing budget
Increasing or decreasing travel preferences
Adding or removing categories
Adding or removing locations
Adding or removing accounts
Adjusting preferences and filters
Turning on targeting preferences
Anything else you think could have a material impact on spend
 
NOTE: This process should not be followed by Service and Support agents. 
REQUEST MADE ON RECORDED LINE
If the Account Owner or Authorized User requests that you make changes to the account or profile and the call is being recorded, send the following template to the Account Owner and copy changes@thumbtack.com:
 
Per our conversation on [date], we are making the following changes to your account that will affect the jobs you are eligible for and pay for:
 
Specific Change #1
Specific Change #2
Specific Change #3
etc.
 
If you believe these changes are in error or if you have any questions, please reply with the corrections or call me at [direct line].

Pro replies -  
If you receive a reply from the pro with corrections, please confirm via email with the pro that the corrections were made and ensure that changes@thumbtack.com is copied on the correction confirmation email.
REQUEST MADE ON NON-RECORDED LINE 
NOTE: This scenario should be very rare as all zoom calls should be automatically set to record, inbound phone calls to AM’s direct line are recorded through Five9, and outbound calls should be made through the Five9 panel in Salesforce. Zoom call links should be added when logging those calls in Salesforce.
 
If the Account Owner or Authorized User requests that you make changes to the account or profile and the call is not being recorded, send the following template to the Account Owner.
 
Per our conversation on [date], we are making the following changes to your account that will affect the jobs you are eligible for and pay for:
 
Specific Change #1
Specific Change #2
Specific Change #3
etc.
 
Please reply to this email with confirmation that you approve these changes. Once we receive confirmation, the changes will be reflected within 1-3 business days.

Pro replies - 
Have the pro reply saying “Approved.” When you receive this approval, forward to changes@thumbtack.com and make the changes to the pro’s account.
If you receive a reply from the pro with corrections, please confirm via email with the pro that the corrections were made and ensure that changes@thumbtack.com is copied on the correction confirmation email.
REQUEST MADE VIA EMAIL
If the Account Owner or Authorized User requests that you make changes to the account or profile via email, send the following template to the Account Owner and copy changes@thumbtack.com:
 
Per your request on [date], we have made the following changes to your account that will affect the jobs you are eligible for and pay for:
 
Specific Change #1
Specific Change #2
Specific Change #3
etc.
 
If you believe these changes are in error or if you have any questions, please reply with the corrections or call me at [direct line].

Pro replies - 
If you receive a reply from the pro with corrections, please confirm via email with the pro that the corrections were made and ensure that changes@thumbtack.com is copied on the correction confirmation email.

Subject:
You’re missing out on jobs
Template:
Hi [PRO'S FIRST NAME],
I’m reaching out because your account is paused due to a failed payment from [DATE].
Since then, there have been [NUMBER OF CUSTOMERS] customers with jobs averaging [AVERAGE JOB VALUE]. That means you could have earned about [TOTAL VALUE (# OF CUSTOMERS x AVERAGE JOB VALUE)], so let’s update your card today.
It’s easy — just follow these steps:

Click Add a credit card.

Business Verification (Verified Business) (Pro)

Contents
Overview
Why business verification
Pro qualifiers
How it works
Process
Submit business for verification 
Franchisor business verification 
Post verification 
Updates after verification
Talking points
Resources
1. OVERVIEW
▶ KA Overview
This internal KA outlines the process and details of Thumbtack's business verification process. It provides guidelines, qualifications, and processes for Sales teams to help pros get verified, enhancing their visibility and credibility on the platform.


Understanding “Verified Business” on Thumbtack
Thumbtack offers an opportunity for pros to verify their business during onboarding.
Pros will be able to display up to 20 unverified reviews on their profile instead of the standard limit of 10. If a pro does not meet our standards, nothing on their account will change and they will be able to continue using Thumbtack.
WHY BUSINESS VERIFICATION MATTERS
This subsection explains why Business Verification is important for pros. It details how it helps pros differentiate themselves and builds customer trust on the Thumbtack platform.
Thumbtack has heard from pros that there need to be more ways to differentiate businesses so they can stand out from the competition. Things like the Featured Projects feature and business verification are Thumbtack's initial attempts to address these concerns.
Thumbtack wants to make it easier for customers to find the best pros available for their projects. Verifying businesses help customers trust and feel more confident with certain pros.
Pro qualification criteria: Eligibility requirements for business verification 
This subsection outlines the specific criteria pros must meet to qualify for Business Verification. These qualifications ensure that only established and reputable businesses receive verified status.
A pro's business must have been incorporated for at least 2 years
A pro's business cannot be a sole proprietorship
There can be no business bankruptcies within the last 5 years
There can be no unsatisfied liens or judgments more than $100
There can be no liens greater than $5,000 within the last 5 years
How business verification works
This subsection explains how Thumbtack verifies businesses. It describes the process and outcomes for pros who meet or do not meet verification standards.
Thumbtack uses the information the pro provided in their profile to verify aspects of their business from third-party data providers.

Outcome
Result
Pro Does Meets Verification Standards
- Exclusive profile badge displayed to customers
- Increased limit of unverified reviews (20 instead of 10)
Pro Doesn't Meet Verification Standards
- No changes to the account
- Continued use of Thumbtack
NOTE: If verification is rejected, Thumbtack will disclose the reason. Pros can provide additional documentation and ask questions. They can also contest the decision by submitting additional documentation, provided they meet all minimum requirements.
Help Center article: What is a verified business? 
2. PROCESS
(Sales rep) Steps: Submitting a business for verification
This subsection provides the steps for submitting a pro's business for verification. It includes the necessary form and review timeline.
If your pro has met all the qualifications and you'd like to submit them for business verification, Sales reps will follow these steps:
Fill out the Business Verification Form. 
Any submissions through this form will be reviewed on Thursdays in the business verification weekly batch.
Thumbtack verifies the following Information: 
Legal Business Name
Business Address
Business Address City
Business Address State
Business Address Zip Code
Business Phone Number
Verification Decision
(Sales Rep) Steps: Franchisor business verification: Specific steps for Franchises 
This subsection outlines the specific steps for verifying franchisor businesses. It includes document preparation and communication guidelines.
Sales rep steps to complete a franchisor business verification:
Make a copy of this PDF and send it to the franchisor.
Before sending, make sure the person you're sending it to has the authorization to sign it.
Once the agreement is signed, upload the signed agreement to the parent account in Tack.
Upload another copy to the company’s Google Drive folder.
Notify Robyn in Trust and Safety and provide a link to the signed agreement in Tack.
Post verification actions: Monitoring and Communication
This subsection explains what happens after verification is complete. It includes monitoring the status and communicating with pros.
Trust and Safety runs a batch on Fridays unless Thumbtack doesn’t have any businesses to run. 
Our team needs to keep an eye on this sheet for the verification status.  We’re putting notes for our team to have any necessary follow-up conversations with your pros directly.
Once you know your pro passed verification, reach out to them to let them know what this means and how it can help improve their business on Thumbtack.
You can also see the updated list and get answers to your business verification questions in the #bv-pilot2 slack channel.
NOTE: If a pro did not pass, you can inform them of the reason and the process for submitting additional documentation or contesting the decision.
UPDATES AFTER VERIFICATION
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
This subsection explains how to handle updates to verified business information. It emphasizes the policy regarding changes to the business name.
Once a business name is verified, it can’t be changed. 
If you’re a Thumbtack pro who needs to update their verified business, please fill out the Account information and licensing form. 
The pro will need to verify they own this business by uploading proof of business ownership documentation. Reps can refer to the internal ID Help Guide KA for more details. 
Important Note: When a verified business changes its name, the existing 'Verified Business' profile badge will be removed. The pro will then need to resubmit their business for verification under the new name to regain this credential.
3.TALKING POINTS
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
How does Thumbtack verify business information?
We utilize a third-party vendor to help verify any business information filed with the state.
If verification is rejected, will Thumbtack disclose why pros aren't verified?
Yes. Pros can also reach out to Thumbtack to give additional documentation and ask questions.
If verification is rejected, can they contest the decision?
Yes. Pros are welcome to submit additional documentation for review, but the pro must meet all the minimum requirements for business verification.
If a pro has multiple services on Thumbtack, can they verify all of them at once?
It depends on how pros have set up their business. If the pro has multiple Thumbtack services that all roll up into a single legal business entity, the pro can indicate which services apply to the legal business entity. Then if their business is verified, it will be applied to all the services. If pros have multiple Thumbtack services that roll up into multiple legal business entities, Thumbtack will need to verify each business separately unless they agree to the business verification for franchisors.
How and when will a pro's 10 additional reviews show up?
If a pro already has more than 10 off-platform reviews, the additional reviews will show up on their profile immediately.

If their off-platform reviews are imported from Google, we'll display the next most recent 10 reviews.

If a pro doesn't have 10 more off-platform reviews, they'll need to send out review requests to past customers.
4. RESOURCES​​​​​​​

What is a verified business?

Business Critical Compliance and QA | Sales

Contents
 
I. Overview
II. Business critical's
a. On a call
b. Texting a pro
c. Activating a pro  
III. Performance
a. Quality assurance
i. Call listening
ii. QA scorecards
iii. Scoring guide
iv. Audit disputes 
b. Overall business-critical compliance
IV. Resources
I. OVERVIEW
 
Business critical's are non-negotiable actions that must take place with every pro on every sale, without exception.
See related knowledge article Gong | Sales.
II. BUSINESS CRITICALS
ON A CALL 
Gong Trackers have different search criteria in order to report compliance in sales calls.  Blue colored phrases and keywords are what trackers are matching to in transcripts in order to report credit for being compliant.  
BC | Recording Compliance: At the start of the call, state the recording disclaimer "on a recorded line"  State that you are calling from a recorded line on every call and with every new person you speak to.
If the number you call states you are on a recorded line, you are still required to let the person know they will be on a recorded line.
1st Violation: You will be a sent a Performance Expectations Plan as a reminder of 90%+ compliance expectations
2nd Violation: If you drop below 90% twice within a calendar half, you will be issued a Final Warning
3rd Violation: Termination
Washington (WA) pros: For all pros with a Washington state address, after you state your name, reason for calling, and that you’re on a recorded line (should be stated roughly w/in the first 15 seconds of the call), you are required to explicitly ask on every call if the consumer wants to (a) continue the call, (b) end the call, or (c) be removed from the solicitor's telephone directory.
If they want to end the call, you must hang up within 10 seconds.
If a pro books a call with you or is transferred to you, you do not need to ask.
If c, add them to the DNC list. 
BC| Sales Qualified Opportunity for the National Accounts team: Ask qualifying questions to see if the Lead/Pro is a good fit for the National Accounts team (all calls >3 minutes). 
National Account Qualifications must meet at least one of the following:
The Pro must have:
5 or more business locations
OR conducts business in multiple states/ across state lines
Or is a Franchise
Sales Qualified questions to ask on behalf of National Accounts:
Are you Franchise?
Do you conduct business across state lines?
Do you have 5 or more locations?
If the answer is YES to any one of those, follow the National Account Handoff Process | Sale.
BC| Sales Qualified Opportunity for the Spanish team: Pros who speak Spanish and would prefer a Spanish AE and CSM
If the answer is yes follow Qualifying Pros For Spanish Team Handoff. 
BC | Non-Refundable: AE must disclose to the pro that the purchase of a sales offer is "non refundable" when sending out the terms of agreement via ironclad (closed won calls). State thatState that
State that the purchase of a prepaid package is non-refundable at the time of purchase
See Sales Package Refund Process if needed. 
BC | PCI compliant: Never take credit card information over the phone. Instead connect the pro with Five9 SecurePay or walk them through how to enter the information themselves on their account. Failure to comply with this policy will result in the following disciplinary actions:
1st Violation: Written final warning & mandatory retraining
2nd Violation: Termination
BC | Email confirmation: Confirm the pro's email address matches the email address of the opportunity you’re charging. 
AE's who are processing a sales offer must check with the pro while the recording is on to confirm that the email in tack matches the email the pro uses for admin/login to access their Thumbtack profile account, ie., "same email you use to login". 
This step will help avoid or reduce the risk of charging wrong accounts and the correct pro account was chosen (closed won calls).
BC | Product Feedback: (all calls >3 minutes)
Product Feedback and Bug reports were flagged for Cross functional partners
AE completed tack steps correctly in wrapping up a call (dispositioned call, relevant notes were provided for the Success and National Accounts handoff process). See Sales Dispositions Reasons.
TEXTING A PRO
 
BC | SMS compliance - When sending a text, every first text you send a pro, you must include “Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to unsubscribe from Thumbtack texts.”
BC | SMS time restrictions - Cannot text pros before 8am and after 8pm (relative to the pro’s time zone)
Exception: Cannot text pros in IL, MI, NM before 9am and after 9pm
1st Violation: You will lose Quiq capabilities for texting outside these time frames.
ACTIVATING A PRO
BC | Background Check: AE must disclose that in order to join the Thumbtack platform the pro must take and pass a "Background Check" (closed won calls)
See Background Checks for more info.
If you create a business profile on the pro’s behalf, you must take a screenshot of the profile and attach it to the activation email.
Send required Activation email in SFDC.
III. PERFORMANCE
QUALITY ASSURANCE 
Through call listening, scorecards, and Gong insights & trackers the Sales Quality Assurance team helps identify and prioritize behaviors and skills that drive a positive pro experience and accelerate business outcomes.
 
Quality also serves as a mechanism to flag and mitigate misses in compliance to internal and external regulatory requirements.
CALL LISTENING
Using Gong, you are expected to:
 
Listen to your own calls weekly and score yourself. Leave comments on what you did well and what you can work on.
You will be required to listen to other rep’s calls and score them. Those assignments are handed out weekly.
QA SCORECARDS
Each line of business will have a scorecard tailored to its team’s processes and expectations. Each week QA will sample at least one of your conversations, grade it against the relevant scorecard and share out the results with you and your manager.
SCORING GUIDE
Sales Scorecard - Scoring Guide resource should be utilized when completing a Sales | QA & Manager Scorecard, including call calibrations, to ensure feedback and accountability to expectations stay consistent.
 
The official scoring guide includes all of the lines currently audited by the team, as well as context as to why a line should be scored Yes, No, or N/A
AUDIT DISPUTES
If you feel that your call has been scored incorrectly, ensure you’ve discussed it with your manager. If you both agree on the dispute reason, your manager will follow the submission process here.
OVERALL BUSINESS-CRITICAL COMPLIANCE
We monitor interaction to ensure that Business Criticals are met. Outside of weekly audits, QA is monitoring our overall adherence to business-critical standards.
 
Recorded Line - This stat is pulled on a weekly basis, filtering for calls >3 minutes long, with a goal to stay above 90% on a monthly basis.
If you’re below goal, you’ll want to identify your calls that are missing the tracker and determine where your opportunity is.
PCI Compliance - It is our responsibility to prevent any CC information from being captured on a recorded line.
Whether through SecurePay or guiding the Pro to add CC information in the product, it’s a good idea to ensure we’re setting proper expectations of the process including a disclaimer like:
“A small reminder to [wait for secure pay instructions/not say your credit card info out loud as you enter it] as we’re on a recorded line - we want to keep your info safe”
Additional business criticals - Pro Qualification, Background Check, and Non-Refundable
These stats are currently primarily rooted in audit performance, but we are working towards automation that would work similarly to our recording compliance stats.
Metric
You’re accountable for…
Outcomes
PCI Compliance
100% compliance with credit card recording
1st Violation: Final Warning
2nd Violation: Termination
Monthly Call Recording Compliance
Maintain 90% or greater compliance when notifying pro of the recorded line (for calls over 3 mins)
1st Violation: PEP - Reminder of 90%+ compliance expectation
2nd Violation: If AE drops below 90% twice within a calendar half, a Final Warning will be issued.
3rd Violation: Termination

Battle Cards and Thumbtack Competitors

Contents

a. Battle cards

c. Submit comments | card feedback

III. Resources
I. OVERVIEW
When interacting with pros, you can access current stats on our competitors by using Battle cards. They provide you with:
Specific, accurate, and up-to-date information about our competitors
Submit new insights, questions, or feedback


COMPETITORS 
Some of Thumbtacks main competitors are:
HomeAdvisor/Angi
Yelp
Houzz
Porch
BATTLE CARDS
The best way to learn about our competitors is by reviewing their BattleCards in Crayon. You can also access the Battlecards directly in tack (Salesforce) using the Battlecards tab.
 
The Battle Cards tab should appear on all leads/opportunities and Contact pages (see image below). 
You may have to check the More tab if you don't see it at first. If you have checked the More tab and still do not see Battle Cards, you can request access from helpdesk@thumbtack.com.
You can also view them from within Crayon by clicking the View in Crayon link. You may have to sign in to using your SSO.
Simply click on a competitor to see their Battle Card. As Battle Cards are added, you can use the search feature to quickly find the card you are looking for.
 

[Image: taTiS86jbBK8g6pDLCZaoV5JnYMlC76yOiQxdzYcxScFDRBZ8aZmqHhxMYFOzfTSbcN8gEwDLEyFR1LQOjdpDXfBxiUXPLNmdtKGYb8RLd0_plhxMJWECCdSUPRK9s0uD5BhZptBWjJSkxhd5DRGd54n99vK7YQCHQJW6ptioKLVnxeURpXVruKRgw]

 
BATTLE CARD LAYOUT
Card Title: You can see the name of the competitor and date of the last update.
View Options: Change how the information appears by clicking on the stacked, grid, or list view icons. (This screenshot and other screenshots in this course are in the "stacked" view.)
Tile topics: Quickly find the theme of the tile.
Static tiles contain information that does not frequently change. They are updated by owner of the card. (Pricing & Lead Types, Pro/Customer Journey Comparison, and Pros & Cons)
Dynamic tiles contain up-to-date details and are updated as soon as new information is added. (Company Profile, Top Insights, Press Release, Field Intel, and Product and Feature Changes)
Tile Content: See a detailed breakdown of the tile's theme.

[Image: sn85NR2-7Xk64Spff0bXxWnOTPk-DDIfdfcbtOrBbKBa7SCxik_b2rMrHcfOVeQ5a6OIGCawKF4dIf_4T0KC6J_jJtHdayxNBPpzwTL2xIOZJvklANDS05cABqOf-5uGJiI6qQOx_TTaNBwM6JYGAdh0N-K3xPDSNTxi3swZ0H5edxBeOMFi14iZzg]

SUBMIT INTEL | NEW DETAILS ABOUT COMPETITORS

[Image: :feedback:]
Our competitors are frequently changing their approach to stay competitive. To keep the cards accurate, we depend on you to submit any new findings. 

Submit intel by clicking the + Add New Intel link. It is found in the same place both in Salesforce and on Crayon.

[Image: ATD7eDb4BAv8Dc87Tan7vlHlCFTeCYfeMrPZx8EnpXt7TlTJoetfseRZM2jHtGD8i9vLomowrG6vrmqvnEISAYTP08vqigIbBWtOA3vgGfOYW7PcM2AtwOisj3pqjkpM9MWltV7XzQH9pRvj9Rw6K73cTJv65-7_hQHLlxwPDv--3Go2XKuzrNnf-Q]

When you click Add New Intel, you will be given a pop-up to enter your intel. You can add intel for any Battle Card, not just the one you are on.

[Image: Lesson creator uploaded content]

Intel will be added to the card immediately.
NOTE: Although the Battle Card owner will review and validate the intel, use your judgment when deciding which information to submit. Consider the source and validity of the information. Do not submit one-off information that you do not trust.
SUBMIT INTEL FROM SLACK
If you notice a message in Slack that would be a great addition to a Battle Card, simply click the three dots to the left of the message you want to add to intel.
Click Create Insite Crayon. You will be taken directly to Crayon to create an insight.

[Image: Lesson creator uploaded content]

SUBMIT COMMENTS | CARD FEEDBACK 
To increase accuracy and usability, let us know if you see incorrect information or have any general feedback about what you like/dislike about a card. 
Click the Comments icon to submit feedback (see image below).

[Image: Lesson creator uploaded content]

Clicking the Comments icon will open a Comments window for you to enter a comment. Use "@" if you need to direct the comment to someone in specific.

[Image: Lesson creator uploaded content]

COMPETITIVE INTEL UPDATES 
If you want more info or want to stay up-to-date as new intel comes out:
Check out the competitive intel feed in Crayon. There you can also sign up for emails any time new intel comes out about a specific competitor.
[Image: :slack:] Follow the  #competitive-intel Slack channel for continuous posts and updates. If you notice a message in Slack that would be a great addition to a Battle Card, click the three dots to the left of the message and click Create Insite Crayon. You will be taken directly to Crayon to create an insight.
II. COMPETITORS
HOME ADVISOR
According to the Thumbtack Pro Brand Tracker Report in March 2019, awareness of HomeAdvisor among Home pros was 76%, compared to 32% awareness for Thumbtack
April 2020, Thumbtack pros who previously used HomeAdvisor were frustrated with low ROI, difficulty in getting refunds, dead end phone leads, and customers who weren’t expecting phone calls
Some Large Pros (not necessarily all using Thumbtack) view HomeAdvisor as a reliable source of lead volume, regardless of those leads’ conversion to jobs
Midsize businesses were less satisfied with HomeAdvisor than Thumbtack
A recent survey also found that the typical pro spend on HomeAdvisor was 2x the rate of the typical pro spend on Thumbtack

[Image: 8b4202e4-4d99-43d1-b635-6829555162b3-image.png]


[Image: 469facc0-1732-49a8-81d7-d5bd782ad52b-image.png]


[Image: c85d80bd-9192-4b04-a1ad-a20a10c8221f-image.png]


[Image: d9cfe94c-c8f5-4b47-9dbb-b45890473a84-image.png]

COMPETITOR PROS AND CONS 
NOTE: In general, we are not trying to displace other lead generation channels. It's good marketing for any business to leverage a variety of marketing channels to generate more lead flow.  However, we DO want to clearly articulate how we are different than competitors and the advantages of using Thumbtack so pros shift more of their marketing spend our way.

[Image: 6dlyhb-ycchH083mNvkB6rkhbfNZ1oTAvJWdkVawYBPEGqdEwGesYFogmhKghy5UIPxHYiegCWpgOq_LLn90_J3BTn_t3ZqCb_CSuC_plnxDudA_JPybZk8yu_NeGW9qbs2YvOCK]
[Image: chXeHCrCWlM9RJvNRpk-ZLWYRGKK0Nrmu4-lky7hnuUEpNkTFBnDwBEO2scCYjhq3ekUQAvDqmcLJ_9gzzPQASQFqU6iuKA6RXiZcsYHnIzJOHEVOHSA8xyRQixor0G3tHzUY7r9]
[Image: 99S89wCmr8WKxmWRzKx4OFUe9317Tjv3D-miY8a3Itph8zJGsNNQNrLqJ8mSnjE--xy2jkTEVwQ79K8t46oFL5fQHZOjsMQwLnyFr9Mqttr82DCEcFr9Ag-SyTIJsvQKOVrx2BTX]
[Image: DgzRsPj9-GXzu6Vmd7qLyj6yoTBYfbyRBncUA9Crxwxa3aO_xJZ7jHctzsUKPFqjJuWuqEZWACuf5ykW6k3k5HiXyvfncEGsYbXxF5MFK9w5kXKHWFasTOAZLcWigLmcNeM6EPWG]
Pro Experience
- Pay $350 per year to be listed
- Set preferences and budget
- Pro receives email, phone #, project details along with 2-3 others and must chase down lead
- Pay $XXXX per year to be listed for certain jobs/geos
- You’ll list higher as a “top supplier” in those areas
- Customers will scroll Angie’s List to contact you
- If you don’t pay, competitors show up in your profile
- Pros pay on a daily / monthly PPC level for ads or premium placement in competitor profiles
- Limited targeting
- Anyone can leave a review
- Pro shares job preferences and availability with Amazon
- Pro is paid by Amazon for jobs completed (commission-based)
Pros
- Contact info received
- Decent controls over job preferences
- High volume of leads; you can pay for volume (HA chooses the pros)
- Pros can pay for volume
- Trusted brand name, high brand awareness
- Contact info received
- Pros can pay for volume / placement
- Less brand trust for services, more for restaurants
- Get calls directly from customers
- Commission payment: no question of lead value
- No chasing down leads that aren't intentful
Cons
- Customer hasn’t selected you, has no idea who you are
- Almost always competing against 2-3 others
- Pay $350 / year just to be listed
High upfront cost
- No variable cost on leads; could be great or terrible
- Competitors showing in your profile
- Limited targeting of job types
- Open platform: anyone can review your business at any time, no proof they were customer
- Pros can’t upsell customer or control pricing
- Pros don’t own customer relationship; essentially contractors
- High take rate for Amazon
Customer Experience
- Submit project details and contact info
- Matched with 2-4 pros who will call and email you to win job
- Either same as HomeAdvisor or Angie’s List member searches list and selects pros they want to contact
- Customers search directory, see ad results, then organic
- Chooses to request a quote or just calls pros
- Customer finds specific job with pricing
- Selects 3 time windows, checks out through Amazon
Pros
- Low effort: pros will contact you to get job done
- They can find you the right pro for your job
- Pros same as HomeAdvisor
- Option for paying customers to select their own pros
- Pros have paid for placement; could be good or bad
- Fast and easy way to contact pros (find number and call)
- Familiar interface due to high usage for restaurants
- Straightforward ecommerce shopping; efficient
- Trusted brand in Amazon
Cons
- 2-4 pros you haven’t selected will now be calling you and emailing you
- You have no idea who they are or their level of quality
- 2-4 pros that you haven’t selected will now be calling (if you selected)
- Chance that lower quality pros paid for placement
- Frequently pros paying for ads or placement have lower reviews (not always)
- Limited preferences to dial in job details
- Limited to many product-related services, not complex jobs (e.g. painting)
- No customer choice of pro

When
(return to index)
A case in the “MTS - Payments” queue is automatically created when a pro replies to the automated email sent after their account is placed on hold for payment disputes or chargebacks.
Additionally, cases are transferred from CAT to the MTS - Payments queue and auto-assigned to specialists via Omni when they have payment-related concerns. These include reports submitted by customers and pros through the platform, emails sent to trustandsafetyteam@thumbtack.com, and any interactions (voice, chat, SMS, email) escalated to T&S from other frontline agents.
How
(return to index)
   Steps
   (return to index)
PROCESS OVERVIEW
(return to index)
Review the case.
Determine concern and review the account in Admin.
For payment disputes, review the chargeback level and request documentation or repayment, if applicable.
For unauthorized card use, review Stripe transaction(s) and email the user(s).
Action the account in Admin, if applicable.
Note details needed from the user and actions you’ve taken.
Close the case.
REVIEW CASE
(return to index)
Review the case. Check the email and their concern. 
Most cases related to payment disputes will have the subject “Re: Your Thumbtack Account is on Hold - Action Required” or something similar.
If the pro responds by asking a general account-related question, transfer the case to Service and Support.
Most Unauthorized Charge cases will be phone cases sent over from S&S.
Open the user’s account in Admin.
If the pro responds using an unregistered email address, send the "Payment dispute: Pro used a non-registered email address" email macro and close the case.
REVIEW A PAYMENT DISPUTE ACCOUNT HOLD
(return to index)
Check hold flags, hold logs and blocklist records in Admin to confirm payment dispute-related account hold reasons (e.g., “user has Chargebacks”, “early fraud warning”) 
If the pro responds to the auto email and states that they want to reopen their account, use the pro’s PK ID to search the Chargeback Lookup Tool.
If the pro responds requesting an account deletion, send the "PPayment dispute: Pro asks to be removed - not willing to address" email and close the case.
If the account is already deleted, send the "Payment dispute: Account already deleted" email template.
If the pro has remaining prepaid credits and is requesting a refund, send the "Payment dispute: Pro asks to be removed from TT (credits non-refundable)" email template and close the case.
Use the table below to determine the actions needed based on the chargeback hold level, the status of disputes, and whether repayment is required. 
Add notes to the case based on the concern and the actions you’ve taken.
Note actions needed by the pro (i.e., waiting for bank documentation, waiting for pro to acknowledge terms - indicate the case number once acknowledged, etc.)
Note any actions you’ve taken (documentation reviewed - approved, account reopened, invoice sent/paid - indicate the invoice number, etc.)
Actions overview for payment disputes:
(return to index)


LEVEL 
ACCOUNT STATUS
DISPUTE STATUS
STEPS
1

(Less than $150 in dispute)
No hold*
All
*Typically, a Level 1 payment dispute will not result in an account hold. If there is a hold, follow the Level 2 steps to remove it.
2

(Between $150 and $299 in dispute)
On hold
All
Coach pro.
Remove hold
Close case
3

(Between $300 and $799 in dispute)
On hold and may have payment due.
Won/Lost 
no repayment due
Coach pro.
Remove hold
Close case

3

(Between $300 and $799 in dispute)
On hold and may have payment due.
Pending
Coach pro.
Request/Review documentation - send the "Payment dispute: Next steps (documentation)" email template.
Remove hold if documentation is accepted - send the "Payment dispute: Pro resolved" email template.
Close case

3

(Between $300 and $799 in dispute)
On hold and may have payment due.
Lost
repayment due
Coach pro.
Send a Stripe invoice for repayment - send the "Payment dispute: Next steps (sent invoice)" email template.
Remove hold once payment is received - send the "Payment dispute: Pro resolved" email template.
Close case
4

($800 and over in dispute)
On hold and account deleted. May have payment due
Won/Lost 
no repayment due
Review account for reopening.
Coach pro.
Remove hold.
Close case

4

($800 and over in dispute)
On hold and account deleted. May have payment due
Pending
Review account for reopening.
Coach pro.
Request/Review documentation - send the “Payment dispute: Next steps (documentation)” email template.
Remove hold if documentation is accepted.
Close case

4

($800 and over in dispute)
On hold and account deleted. May have payment due
Lost
repayment due
Review account for reopening.
Coach pro.
Send a Stripe invoice for repayment - send the “Payment dispute: Next steps (sent invoice)” email template.
Remove hold once payment is received -  send the “Payment dispute: Pro resolved” email template.
Close case
COACH A PRO WITH PAYMENT DISPUTES
(return to index)
Confirm the Pro understands: 
How will they be charged moving forward?
How to adjust settings/targeting once their account is reopened.
If they didn’t indicate their understanding of the above in the original response, send the "Payment dispute: Next steps (acknowledge terms)" email template.
If we won the payment dispute, send the “Payment dispute: TT Won disputed chargebacks - Pro may return” email template.
If we lost the payment dispute but no repayment is needed, send the “Payment dispute: Chargeback Level 3 / 4 – LOST – No repayment required”  email template.
REVIEW ACCOUNT FOR REOPENING
(return to index)
Open the Dispute Risk Scoresheet, create your own copy, and check for red flags while updating the checklist with results.
Complete the scoresheet and review the Risk Outcome result.
If the results indicate “non-suspicious,” proceed to the next step.
If the result indicates “uncertain,” tag @riskanalytics in the #ts-proactive-ops-questions Slack channel for a second opinion.
If the result indicates suspicious, send the “Payment dispute: Will not reconsider account” email template and close the case.
Note: The Dispute Risk Scoresheet is not the ultimate deciding factor. The specialist retains discretion to deny reopening the account, even if the scoresheet gives a low score, if they suspect real fraud on the account (e.g., a pro having fraud disputes on several different credit cards with zip codes all over the place).
REQUEST/REVIEW DOCUMENTATION FOR PENDING DISPUTES
(return to index)
If there are pending disputes and we are requesting documentation, send the “Payment dispute: Next steps (documentation)” email template and close the case.
Note: There is no option for repayment while disputes are in a pending status.
Review bank documentation once it’s received to make sure we can accept it. Bank documentation needs to be on letterhead and include the following:
Transaction amount(s)
Date(s)
Last 4 of the card
Statement that the transaction(s) has been dropped. 
If documentation is rejected, send the “Payment dispute: Documentation received - Not approved” email template and wait for either additional documentation to be sent or for the bank to determine the dispute outcome as either won/lost.
If the documentation received is approved, remove the account hold and send the “Payment dispute: Pro resolved” email template.
SEND AN INVOICE IF REPAYMENT IS REQUIRED
(return to index)
If repayment is required, check if an existing invoice matching the repayment amount in Chargeback Lookup Tool has already been sent and resend it. 
If no invoice has been sent yet, create and send to the pro. 
Copy the invoice number generated once the invoice has been sent and note it in the case.
Send the “Payment dispute: Next steps (sent invoice)” email template.
Once the payment has been received, remove the account hold, send the “Payment dispute: Pro resolved” email template and close the case.
REVIEW REPORTED UNAUTHORIZED USE OF CREDIT CARD
(return to index)
Search both the Pro and Marketplace (Customer) Stripe portals for the transaction(s) using the information provided and locate which account it is associated with.
If you’re unable to locate the account associated with the reported transaction(s) in either the customer or pro side of Stripe, send the “Payments: UnAuth card: Unable to Locate Unauthorized Charges/Account” email template and close the case.
Unauthorized charge located in account
(return to index)
If the reported transaction(s) is located in an account, do the following:
Send an email to the reporter ("Payments: UnAuth card: Located unauthorized charges - Pro") if the associated account is with a pro, or the “Payments: UnAuth card: Located unauthorized charges - Customer” template if with a customer.
Do not provide any personal information. If a pro account has no business name, provide a description of the service.
If the reporter responds that they know the reported account, send the “Payments: UnAuth card: Reporter knows the person/business that made the charge” email template and close the case.
If the reporter DOES NOT recognize the reported account, BUT we see that they are linked accounts and have a strong linkage on other signals (i.e., name, email address/domain, login IPs, business descriptions and address)
Remove the reported card on file from the reported account.
Send the “Payments: UnAuth card: Not unauthorized charges” email template to the reporter.
Close the case.
If the reporter DOES NOT recognize the reported account and we see that there are no strong links, skip to Step 4.
Create a new case for the reported account using the Quick Case option and enter the following:
Account Name of reported account.
Account email
SUBJECT: Credit Card Issues
Case origin = email
Click Submit.
[Image: rtaImage]
Place the reported account on hold using the “Add Account Hold" link in Admin with the reason: “User has general issues or needs coaching,” and add the note - “Reported Unauthorized Credit Card Use,” including case numbers of the reporter & reported account.
Send email to the reported account: (“Payments: CC fraud - 1st Warning - Pro” if the account is pro or “Payments: CC fraud - 1st Warning - Customer” if customer) and update case status to “Pending Customer”.
Monitor the user’s response in the “MTS - Payments” case queue, and if the reported account didn’t respond to the initial email within 5 days, send a 2nd notice email (“Payments: CC fraud - 2nd Notice - Pro” if the account is pro or "“Payments: CC fraud - 2nd Notice - Customer” if customer).
If the reported account responds (which is rare) and can provide the card details, we’ll consider the explanation and decide whether to remove them or allow them back on the platform. 
If we determine they’re allowed back on the platform, send the "“Payments: CC fraud - Request reporter to confirm charges through reported account” email template to the reported account to advise the reporter to send us an email confirming the charges are authorized.
Once the email confirmation from the reporter is received, remove account hold(s), send the “Payments: CC fraud - Released hold” email template and close the case.
If unsatisfied with their reason, send the “Payments: CC fraud - Request account statement from reported account-explanation unsatisfactory” email template to the reported account to request for a statement of account.
If the reported account doesn’t respond after ten days, or we determine they’re NOT allowed back on the platform:
Delete and blocklist the reported account. Send the “Payments: CC fraud - Account Closed” email template.
Refund all of the unauthorized transactions found in Stripe to the cardholder. 
Remove the reported card on file from the reported account.
Send the cardholder the “Payments: UnAuth card: Case closed - Transactions refunded” email template.
Close the case.
CLOSE THE CASE
(return to index)
Go to the MTS Categorize/Status tab.
Change Category and Do Not Survey to “Marketplace Integrity.”
Change Sub Category to “Other” for non-Unauthorized Use cases and “Payment Fraud” for Unauthorized Use cases.
Change Status to “Closed” if you’re done with the case or “Pending Customer” if the case is awaiting the user's reply.
[Image: rtaImage]
   Talking Points
    (return to index)


QUESTION
RESPONSE
Asking for phone support/call. 
Thank you for getting back to us. Unfortunately, we don’t provide phone support for this particular department. As a security measure, we require all communication related to these types of issues to be in writing. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause, and we’re happy to assist you through written correspondence.
If you need further assistance, please contact our Service and Support team.
Asking if we accept screenshots as proof of the dropped payment dispute.
On certain occasions, we may consider accepting screenshots as evidence that your chargeback has been dropped. To be considered valid, the screenshot should clearly display that it is from the bank and account in question and provide a detailed trail of the dispute process, including the amounts and dates involved.
Ideally, the screenshot should show the original charge, the credit applied by the bank when the dispute was filed, and the amount rebilled to the account once the dispute was dropped. This will help us to verify that the dispute has indeed been dropped and that the charge is valid.
   Emails
   (return to index)
Payment Disputes
Payment dispute: Pro used a non-registered email address: Pro responded using a different email address from their Thumbtack account.
Payment dispute: Pro asks to be removed - not willing to address: Pro doesn't want to pay/address and wants to delete their account.
Payment dispute: Account already deleted: The account is already deleted.
Payment dispute: Pro asks to be removed from TT (credits non-refundable): Pro requesting refund of remaining credits but are non-refundable per Refund Policy.
Payment dispute: Next steps (acknowledge terms): Pro wants to reopen/remove hold account but no clear acknowledgement of understanding the Terms.
Payment dispute: TT Won disputed chargebacks - Pro may return: We won the payment dispute and pro needs to acknowledge understanding of the Terms before we remove account hold.
Payment dispute: Chargeback Level 3 / 4 – LOST – No repayment required: We lost the payment dispute and no re-payment is required from the pro but need to acknowledge understanding of the Terms before we remove account hold.
Payment dispute: Next steps (documentation): Pro has pending payment disputes and we need documentation.
Payment dispute: Documentation received - Not approved: Pro has pending payment disputes and the documentation provided didn't meet the required details.
Payment dispute: Next steps (sent invoice): Repayment is required from Pro on lost payment dispute.
Payment dispute: Pro resolved: Documentation provided to resolve pending payment dispute meets the required details or repayment on lost payment dispute has been received.
Payment dispute: Will not reconsider account: Pro is not allowed back on the platform.
User reported unauthorized use of credit/debit card
Payments: UnAuth card: Unable to Locate Unauthorized Charges/Account: Unable to locate the account associated with the reported transaction(s).
Payments: UnAuth card: Located unauthorized charges - Pro: Able to locate the account associated with the reported transaction(s) in a pro account
Payments: UnAuth card: Located unauthorized charges - Customer: Able to locate the account associated with the reported transaction(s) in a customer account.
Payments: UnAuth card: Reporter knows the person/business that made the charge: User responds that they know the reported account.
Payments: UnAuth card: Not unauthorized charges: Reporter mentions that they do not recognize the reported account but we see a strong link with the reported account.
Payments: CC fraud - 1st Warning - Pro: Initial warning to the pro in question where the reported transaction(s) is located.
Payments: CC fraud - 1st Warning - Customer: Initial warning to the customer in question where the reported transaction(s) is located.
Payments: CC fraud - 2nd Notice - Pro: Final warning to the pro in question where the reported transaction(s) is located.
Payments: CC fraud - 2nd Notice - Customer: Final warning to the customer in question where the reported transaction(s) is located.
Payments: CC fraud - Request reporter to confirm charges through reported account: Reported account is needed for the reporter to reply with acknowledgement that charges are authorized before reinstating their account.
Payments: CC fraud - Request account statement from reported account-explanation unsatisfactory: Reported account needs to send the card’s recent statement of account as additional documentation due to unsatisfied explanation.
Payments: UnAuth card: Case closed - Transactions refunded: Reported account didn’t respond and all unauthorized transactions have been refunded to the cardholder.
Payments: CC fraud - Released hold: Reported account responded with valid explanation and we determined to allow them back on the platform
Payments: CC fraud - Account Closed: Reported account didn’t respond after ten days or is deemed ineligible for platform return, resulting in account deletion and blocklisting.
   Related
   (return to index)
DEFINITIONS
(return to index)
Payment dispute: A Thumbtack user contacted their bank or credit card company and disputed a charge from Thumbtack, indicating that they disagree with it or don’t recognize the transaction.
Chargeback: When a payment dispute is filed, the funds are immediately removed from Thumbtack’s account and given back to the cardholder while the investigation takes place. If we lose the dispute during the investigation, the pro/customer keeps their funds and we’re charged an additional fee from Stripe. If we win, the funds are returned to Thumbtack. The process of the bank taking the funds is called a chargeback. You will often see payment disputes and chargebacks used interchangeably. 
EFW: An early fraud warning (EFW) is a term we previously used to indicate an advanced notification of a payment dispute/chargeback. We no longer use this term, but you may still see it referenced in older cases, notes, or on the Admin page account hold flags. For our purposes, this term is now used interchangeably with chargeback and payment dispute.
Reporter: A person (who may or may not be a user of Thumbtack) who is reporting an unauthorized and/or unrecognized charge from Thumbtack on their credit card. 
Chargeback Lookup Tool: A Tableau tool that was created as a source of truth for looking up the current status of payment disputes. This tool provides:
Total amount of all payments disputed on a pro or customer account 
The level of hold currently on the account (based on dollar amount)
Status of the disputes (pending, won or lost)
Repayment amount due (if any)
Instructions on how to work with the pro/customer to remove the hold.
RELATED DOCS
(return to index)
Dispute Risk Scoresheet
Navigate Stripe
Chargebacks KA 
Account Actions

Survey Triage

Survey Triage
(Knowledge index)
INDEX 
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Quick view
Process overview
Details
Indeterminate email
Troubleshooting
What
(return to index)
Survey triage helps Trust and Safety track and review specific words used in submitted surveys. 
Why
(return to index)
We scan feedback that wasn’t submitted through normal channels to be sure we act on all Trust and Safety issues.

When
(return to index)
Some channels utilize free-text surveys where users can provide feedback to Thumbtack about their product experience.
The current surveys that we check:
help_center_feedback
pro_inbox_feedback
customer_sentiment_survey
customer_feedback
work_ticket_survey
pro_sentiment_survey
managed_account_survey
likelihood_to_continue (ltc)
Pro_nps
cs_csat
Mts_csat
Pro-lead-decline
When a checked word is detected in any of the surveys listed above, it will create a work ticket for our teams to review for potential support opportunities. If there are concerns that need to be addressed, a new case will be created for the appropriate team.
SLA for this queue is 96 hours, and the HT target is 1.5 minutes.

How
(return to index)
   Steps
  (return to index)
QUICKVIEW
(return to index)

[Image: Screenshot 2024-04-17 at 1.41.31 PM.png]


PROCESS OVERVIEW
(return to index)

[Image: Screenshot 2023-01-10 at 9.13.45 AM.png]

Upon receiving the Survey Triage ticket, evaluate the text and determine whether there are any Trust and Safety issues involved.
Select the appropriate Outcome and Outcome Detail based on the evaluation.
Types of Outcome
Confirmed Trust and Safety issue
The text suggests there is a Trust and Safety issue involved.
By selecting this outcome, the case will be forwarded to the Trust and Safety team to further handle the issue.
Indeterminate
The text shows a possible Trust and Safety concern, which could be based on a past experience using Thumbtack.
By selecting "Indeterminate," an automatic email will be sent to the user to ask for more details about the experience.
No MTS issue found
The text does not show any Trust and Safety issues.

OUTCOME
OUTCOME DETAIL
DEFINITION
Confirmed MTS Issue
Escalated MTS Case
This will trigger an automatic creation of a case, which will be validated by the Trust and Safety Categorization Team.
Indeterminate
Email User
This will trigger an automatic email to be sent to the concerned user.
Once the user replies to the email, a new case will be generated. This case will be validated by the Trust and Safety Categorization Team.
No MTS Issue Found
No Action Taken
The survey doesn’t suggest any Trust and Safety issues, and no action is needed.
Click Save after choosing the Outcome and Outcome Detail.
   Details
  (return to index)
INDETERMINATE EMAIL
(return to index)
Below is the text of the email that is sent when the Outcome is “Indeterminate.”

Subject: 
Thanks for submitting a survey!
Body: 
Hi there, 
We’re sorry to hear about this experience and want you to know Thumbtack is here to help.
If you have unresolved concerns and would like to pursue a resolution, please tell us more by reporting here. 
Once we receive your report, we’ll follow up with the next steps. 
Sincerely,
Thumbtack Trust and Safety Team


   Troubleshooting
    (return to index)
Some work tickets do not have email addresses to which to send the email. If this is the case, an error will occur when selecting  “Indeterminate + Email User.” To continue, the agent should skip the Outcome Detail and add “error due to lack of email” in the internal notes.
