New Era ADR approval process (incidents)

New Era ADR approval process (incidents)
(Knowledge link)
Index
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Overview
What may qualify
Do’s and Don’ts
Approval Process
Explain New Era ADR (Specialists)
Talking points
Emails
Related
What 
​​(return to index)
New Era ADR (Advanced Dispute Resolution), doing business as New Era, is an online arbitration platform we’ve partnered with that can help pros and customers resolve their disputes when Trust and Safety have exhausted other resolution options, and the appropriate qualifications have been met. New Era is provided at no cost to both customers and pros. Thumbtack covers the sign-up fee.
Why 
​​(return to index)
In specific situations, Trust and Safety may offer the platform as an effective way for customers and pros to resolve user-to-user disputes with a legally binding outcome. 
When 
​​(return to index)
WHAT QUALIFIES FOR NEW ERA?
Third-party arbitration should be considered when there is credible evidence supporting one or more concerns, but the internal team is unable to determine liability, proportional responsibility, or financial accountability with reasonable confidence.
Arbitration may be appropriate in situations such as:
Unclear Degree of Responsibility
Disputed Financial Accountability
Counterclaim Scenarios
Conflicting but Credible Evidence
How 
​​(return to index)
   Steps 
​​    (return to index)
OVERVIEW
​​(return to index)
In the New Era process, there is a Claimant, the party that files the dispute, and a Respondent, the defendant or the party replying to the dispute. In the Thumbtack New Era process, customers are most often the Claimants since project concerns typically get reported by customers. Pros are most often the Respondents since they are the ones replying to address the concerns brought up by the Claimant. However, Respondents can also enter a counterclaim during the sign-up process.
Once the incident is escalated to New Era, the dispute communication is handled solely by the platform and a designated “Neutral,” also known as an Arbitrator. This Neutral is assigned to each dispute to review documentation, conduct a virtual hearing, and provide a legally binding agreement that can then be enforced in the local jurisdiction, if necessary.

[Image: rtaImage]

WHAT MAY QUALIFY
​​(return to index)

An incident may qualify for New Era if it meets one or more of the following criteria:
Unclear Degree of Responsibility:
There are identifiable gaps, deviations, or failures within the contracted agreement; however, the extent of each party’s financial or performance responsibility cannot be clearly quantified.
Disputed Financial Accountability:
Evidence supports that an issue occurred, but the total cost allocation between parties cannot be reasonably determined through internal review.
Counterclaim Scenarios:
Both parties present substantiated and reasonable claims, and internal review cannot objectively determine primary fault or appropriate cost distribution.
Conflicting but Credible Evidence:
Documentation or testimony from both parties is materially inconsistent, yet each position is supported by some objective evidence.
DO’S AND DON’TS 
​​(return to index)
Do handle sensitive or escalated incidents with high touch initially and offer New Era as an option if appropriate.
Don't promise either party will sign up, but make sure the user you're speaking to knows you'll take the appropriate actions if the other party doesn't.
APPROVAL PROCESS
​​(return to index)

Before submitting for New Era approval, specialists should ensure the following qualifications have been met.
The customer received a quote from the pro through the Thumbtack platform.
The amount in dispute is $5000+.
If the amount in dispute exceeds $15,000, please consult with a manager before seeking approval for the New Era submission. This additional step is important for ensuring careful consideration and support, which helps reduce the risk of escalation. High-value judgments require increased oversight in case things do not go as planned.
The case doesn’t involve sensitive or timely concerns (i.e., sexual, physical, media attention, full displacement (customers don’t have anywhere to stay for the night and/or extreme temperatures with no heat or A/C, running water, etc.))
Pro is active, has quoted within the last 30 days, and is responsive to T&S.
Once qualifications have been fully met, the Specialist should:
Reach out in the  #ts-arbitration-approval-reviews Slack channel for manager approval using the workflow New Era Approval Review.
A manager will review availability. If there isn’t a slot available, a manager will let you know and consult with you to determine the best way to move forward.
Generally, there will only be three New Era openings per month.
If the Incident is approved by management and there’s a slot available, specialists should:
Users are formally introduced to the arbitration process, including an overview of expectations, timelines, and potential outcomes.
Claimant and Respondent have agreed to participate, contingent upon case approval for submission.
Both parties must also be informed that Participation in arbitration is voluntary but binding once agreed.
NOTE: Failure to participate after formally agreeing to proceed may impact their account standing and/or limit Thumbtack’s ability to continue supporting dispute resolution efforts. 
EXPLAIN NEW ERA ADR (SPECIALIST) 
​​​​(return to index)
Explaining New Era to both parties is an important part of making New Era beneficial and ensuring they agree to follow through on sign-up. Not only does explaining the process provide a better experience, but it also makes sure both parties can be held accountable for their part in the process.
Before disputes are transferred to the Arbitration team, both the customer and pro must agree to use New Era.
Before Specialists transfer a dispute, they should: 
Reach out to the Claimant via phone call and tell them about the platform. Explain how it's beneficial, what to expect, and ask if they’d like to use New Era .
If they don’t answer: 
Send a follow-up email that explains New Era and has your Zoom Scheduler link for questions.
If they don’t want to use New Era: 
Look into any other tools we’re able to offer to help them reach a resolution.
If they do want to use New Era: 
Let them know you’ll reach out to the Respondent to discuss the process. Make sure it is clearly understood that both parties must agree to proceed. 
Reach out to the Respondent via phone call to explain the process to them.
If they don’t answer: 
Send a follow-up email that explains New Era and has your Zoom Scheduler link for questions.
If they don’t respond within two business days: 
Send them a removal email and remove their account.
If they’re not willing to use New Era:
Set the expectations with them that we’ll remove their account until the concern is addressed.
If they’re willing to use New Era:
Let them know to expect a follow-up from the Arbitration Team.
Conduct a final review of the account: Provided there are no outstanding issues, you may proceed with removing any holds.
Let the Claimant know you’re ready to submit their dispute for approval, and our Arbitration team will follow up with the next steps.
Reach out via Slack in your original post in #ts-arbitration-approval-reviews, tag @ts-leaders in the comments so management can provide approval as needed and take ownership of the dispute, and then submit the dispute to New Era.
Before transferring the dispute:
Contact the users and let them know New Era was approved, and we will be transferring the case
The File Manager must be fully completed with all documentation clearly labeled. This is to ensure a smoother transfer and to ensure managers have a full understanding of the incident.
Once the dispute is transferred, a manager will create a new dispute in New Era ADR and introduce themselves.  
   Talking points 
     (return to index)
Talking Points Guide for Speaking with Customers: New Era ADR 
Talking Points Guide for Speaking with Professionals: New Era ADR
  Emails 
   ​​(return to index)
SPECIALIST EMAILS
New Era: Introduction to process (to Customer) / NE: Introduction (to CX): Send to the customer to introduce the New Era process.
New Era: Introduction to process (to Pro) / NE: Introduction (to Pro): Send to the pro to introduce the New Era process.
New Era: Unresponsive customer (to Pro) / NE: Unresponsive cx (to Pro): Send to pro when the customer has been unresponsive to the New Era offer.
New Era: Unresponsive pro (to Customer) / NE: Unresponsive pro (to CX): Send to customer when the pro has been unresponsive to the New Era offer, the pro has been removed, and we’re stepping back.
New Era: No Response (to Customer) / NE: No Response (to CX): Send to customer when they have been unresponsive to the offer for New Era.
New Era: Customer confirmed (to Customer) / NE: CX Confirmation (to CX): Send to the customer to thank them for agreeing to use New Era and let them know we’ll reach out when we hear from the Pro.
New Era: Pro willing (to Pro) / NE: Pro willing ( to Pro): Send to the Pro when we’re removing the hold on their account while we wait to hear back from the customer.
New Era: Pro removed ( to Pro) / NE: Pro removed (to Pro): Send to the pro when we haven’t heard back from them, and we’re taking action on their account.
New Era: Contacting New Era for process-related questions (Any Party) / NE: Contacting NE (Both): Send to either party when asking New Era process-specific questions.
GRAMMARLY ONLY
Link: How NE works (Both): Quick link to share the “How New Era ADR works" link.
Link: FAQ’s NE (Both): Quick link to share the “FAQ’s about New Era ADR process" link.

  Related 
    ​​(return to index) 
RELATED KNOWLEDGE ARTICLES
Navigate New Era ADR KA

NEW ERA CONTACT INFO
(return to index)

Contact info for customers and pros: 
General inquiries: support@neweraadr.com
Customer support: support@neweraadr.com
Users should work with New Era to troubleshoot or address questions related to the New Era process or platform.
**Use the content request form to request an update or submit questions/concerns*

articles.fullText:
Navigate the Thumbtack Solution Center

Navigate the Thumbtack Solution Center (TSC)
(Knowledge index)

INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Dispute Control Center
Create a dispute manually
Send tips
Stop or close dispute
Restart or reopen dispute
Turning work tickets off or on
Details
Understanding what’s happened
Incident "solution center" tab
Reading what users said in the TSC
Understanding work ticket posts
Customer Sign Up steps
Pro sign-up steps
Accept steps
Counter steps
Definitions
Status and stage
Closure reasons
Emails
Troubleshooting
User can't sign up
Dispute should have expired
What
(return to index)
The Thumbtack Solution Center (TSC) is a resolution platform we’ve designed to help customers and pros resolve their concerns together. It lets our users communicate in a neutral, online setting so they can outline the problem, upload documentation, and work together to find a solution. When cases are sent to the TSC, they’re called “disputes.”
The TSC is a tool separate from the archived process called "TSCI" or "Thumbtack Solution Center Instant."
Below is a screenshot of what users see when using the TSC:

[Image: rtaImage]


Why
(return to index)
The TSC allows specialists to monitor users working directly with each other, removing T&S as the go-between messenger.

When
(return to index)
Use this article when trying to use the TSC or to understand what’s happened on an incident that came out of the archived TSCI queue.

How
(return to index)
   Steps
    (return to index)

DISPUTE CONTROL CENTER
(return to index)


[Image: rtaImage]


The Dispute Control Center is where Specialists can see what is happening in the TSC, send tips to the customers/pros, and stop or close a dispute. To get to the control center:
Click on the Solution Center section of the incident.
Click View Details.
Click Refresh before moving forward with any next steps.

To see the Solution Center from the customer/pro’s perspective:
Open the Dispute Control Center.
Under Tips and Actions click either View as Initiator or View as Responder.
NOTE: Do not select actions on the customer’s or pro’s behalf.

To see the names of automated emails and tips:

Open the Dispute Control Center.
Click Messages.
This will show all automated emails and tips that have been sent, along with the recipients.
To see attachments:

Any attachments(docs, pictures, etc.) uploaded to the TSC by the customer or pro will be automatically added to the incident.
They will appear under the File Manager section of the Incident view.
CREATE A DISPUTE MANUALLY
(return to index)
Before creating a dispute in the TSC, the specialist should have already determined that the incident is a good fit. If unsure, assess the case's sensitivity or speak with a manager.
Click on the Solution Center section of the incident.
Confirm the Initiating Party field.
This should be the customer's information.
Make sure this is correct, or the wrong person will be sent the TSC information.
Select the Desired Resolution.
Enter the description of the dispute.
This description is eventually shown to the customer and the pro, so make sure the dispute details match what the customer has stated.
Avoid phrases like “customer stated.”
If the conversation was over the phone, use neutral phrases like “work is not complete, refund is requested.”
Be sure the Bid PKID, Request Category, City, State, and Zip sections are completed.
This information should be auto-filled; however, if a specialist doesn’t see it listed, they can find these details in the Project tab of the incident.
Click Next.
Double-check all of the fields to make sure they’re correct. 
Click Submit.
Clicking Submit will send an email to the initiating party with a link to their dispute.
Turn work tickets off.
SEND TIPS
(return to index)
If the customer and pro get stuck, send tips within the dispute to guide them in the right direction. They can’t reply to a tip, and the specialist's name won’t be associated with it, so tips can be direct and short. If a conversation is needed, reach out via email or phone.
Open the Dispute Control Center.
Click the Agent Tips tab.
Select the audience (user) the tip is for.
Choose what kind of tip to send:
A prewritten tip from the dropdown (these can be edited)
Write a new one in the text box.
Click Send Tip to submit the tip to the discussion.
The customer and/or pro will see this below the most recent offer.
[Image: rtaImage]
STOP OR CLOSE DISPUTE
(return to index)
At any point during a dispute, specialists can close or stop a dispute.
Stopping a dispute does not close it completely. Instead, it places it in a state where neither the pro nor the customer can take action. Reasons to stop a dispute could be:
To help redirect the conversation to be more productive.
When assessing whether to change the resolution method.
Closing a dispute prevents either party from communicating further. Reasons to close a dispute could be:
The customer asks to close the dispute.
If the specialist reviews the communication and notices any of the following:
Legal threats.
Continued or excessive Inappropriate language.
Abusive behaviors.
The dispute needs to be handled manually or is becoming sensitive.
There is no progress being made, and tips have been unsuccessful.

How to:
Open the Dispute Control Center.
Click the Tips & Actions tab.
Click Stop Dispute or Close Dispute.
If the dispute is stopped, the customer and pro will see a message that says, “This dispute is under review. An agent will reach out soon.” Reach out to both parties to explain their next steps.
If the dispute is closed, the status will update to “This dispute is closed.”
The customer and pro will not receive a notification if closed manually.
Send an email to the customer/pro explaining that the dispute is closed and what the next steps are.
RESTART OR REOPEN DISPUTE
(return to index)
If a dispute has been stopped or closed and the customer contacts us about continuing the dispute, we can reopen the dispute. 
Open the Dispute Control Center.
In the Agent Tips section, locate the blue Restart button at the top, then click it.
When asked “Are you sure,” click Restart.
The dispute will reopen, and a green message at the top of the page will say “Dispute record restarted successfully.”
Explain to both users that the dispute was restarted and why, as needed.
Once the dispute has been reopened, the users will resume where they left off. If it's reopened before both parties signed up, sign-up emails will be resent automatically based on the stage of the dispute and who it’s still waiting on. 
Note: If a customer withdraws their dispute, it cannot be reopened.
TURNING WORK TICKETS ON OR OFF
(return to index)
Work Ticket (WT) creation was a process used for the Thumbtack Solution Center Instant (TSCi) process, which monitored incidents in the TSC through WTs at various touch points. Since this process was deprecated on October 15, 2025 and is no longer monitored, WTs should always be turned off when you manually create a TSC dispute.
To do so:
In your incident, expand the Solution Center section on the left side.
Click View Details to open the Dispute Control Center.
In the Dispute Control Center, scroll down to find Work Ticket Information on the right side.
Make sure Pause Work Ticket Creation says "Escalated."
If it doesn't, click the pencil icon, select "Escalated," and save.

[Image: rtaImage]


   Details
   (return to index)

UNDERSTANDING WHAT’S HAPPENED IN TSC
(return to index)

Incident “Solution Center” tab
(return to index)
The Solution Center tab within your incident is meant to give you a snapshot of what’s happened in the TSC so far. Here you’ll see:
View details: Access to the Dispute Control Center.
View as initiator: Quickly see the TSC as the customer sees it.
Status and stage.
Overall, offers and messages count.
Last Status Change Date: The date the TSC switched to the status/stage you see.
Solution Center Link: The link to send to users (will not work for you). Right-click to copy the link address.
Initiator Confirmation Due Date: When the customer was expected to sign up.
Initiator Sign Up: When the customer actually signed up (blank if the customer hasn’t signed up, will be the same as the other initiator date if they were automatically signed up).
Responder First Action Due Date: When the pro must sign up before the TSC expires.
Responder Sign Up: When the pro actually signed up (blank if the pro hasn’t signed up yet).

[Image: rtaImage]


Reading what users said in the TSC
(return to index)

It's important that specialists know what the users have already said and done in the Thumbtack Solution Center. To view this: Customer Sign Up.
In your incident, expand the Solution Center section on the left side.
Click View as Initiator to view the TSC as the customer sees it. Be sure to scroll up to read the full history.
In the Dispute Control Center, you can also use View as Responder to see the pro's view.

[Image: rtaImage]

Note: Specialists will not be able to see the users' buttons in this view. The TSC shows buttons based on whose "turn" it is, and it will never be their turn. See Customer Sign-Up and Pro Sign-Up for screenshots of the buttons users may see.
Understanding work ticket posts
(return to index)
The archived TSCI process used work tickets that were posted to the incident feed. Specialists can recognize them by looking for a red/pink icon with a ticket icon. The post will also include the work ticket name, which normally starts with "Dispute."
The format of these posts is: [Work ticket name] > [Outcome] > [Outcome detail] > [Issue Type].
Work ticket name: What caused us to create the work ticket.
Outcome: Whether we decided to escalate.
Outcome detail: Action taken by the agent who worked the ticket.
Issue type: Details on why action was taken (typically, this is null).

[Image: rtaImage]

Customer Sign Up
(return to index)
When starting the TSC process, the customer must first manually sign up for the TSC.
Help the customer sign up

If the customer still needs to sign up, they need to confirm the details of their concerns before they’re sent to the pro. To do so, they need to:
Click Thumbtack Solution Center in the invitation email.
[Image: rtaImage]
The email is sent from no-reply-tsc@thumbtack.com.
Alternatively, users can access their dispute via their Solution Center Homepage. (help.thumbtack.com/solutioncenter)
Read the TSC intro and click Next.
[Image: rtaImage]
Check the Dispute Description and either click Edit to update it or click Next to continue.
[Image: rtaImage]
Add attachments (if desired).
[Image: rtaImage]
If the users don't add attachments here, they'll need to wait until it's their "turn" again to add documentation.
Review their suggested solution and edit it if needed. Once done, they need to explain why they're suggesting that solution, then click Submit to finish signing up.      
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
If they choose to edit their suggested solution, they have three options to choose from:
Complete or redo the work.
Complete or redo the work and refund.
Refund.
Refund Amount only exists when they choose one of the refund options. The amount can be edited.
Click Okay to see the dispute.
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
Wait for the pro to respond.
The pro is expected to respond in the TSC within 3 days unless we email the customer otherwise.
They'll receive auto emails from the TSC letting them know whether the pro responded or the TSC expired.
See if the customer signed up
(return to index)
In the incident under Solution Center, you can see whether the customer has signed up. If the customer has not signed up, the Initiator sign-up date will be blank:
Pro sign up
(return to index)
When a dispute is created in the TSC, the pro will need to sign up and join the conversation. They'll be given information on the concern as well as the customer's suggested solution, and then can work with the customer to find an agreement.
See if pro signed up

In the incident under Solution Center, specialists can see whether the pro has signed up. If the pro has not signed up, the Responder sign-up date will be blank:
[Image: rtaImage]
Help pro sign up

Help the pro take the following steps to get started in the TSC:
Open the TSC via links in either their email or their account hold.
Email:
[Image: rtaImage]
Account hold:
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
A third option is for the pro to go to the TSC Homepage (help.thumbtack.com/solutioncenter)
Read the intro info, then click Next.
[Image: rtaImage]
Read the customer's dispute description and details about the customer and job, then click Next.
[Image: rtaImage]
Read the customer's suggested solution and explanation, then Accept, Counter, or ask the customer a question.
[Image: rtaImage]
Pros must choose one of these options (or reply if the customer has messaged them) to "sign up."
Only selecting Accept or Counter resets the timer - if the pro doesn't choose one of these options in 3 days, the dispute will expire, and we'll evaluate the next steps.
Accept
(return to index)
The TSC is focused on helping users solve their concerns by coming to an agreement. Accept is the button users use to formally make an agreement within the TSC.
Disputes begin with a customer suggesting a solution, then the pro decides if they want to Accept or Counter that solution. If the pro counters, the customer then chooses whether they Accept or Counter. The dispute will continue this cycle until an agreement is made, someone stops responding, or Thumbtack stops the dispute.
Users are given 3 calendar days for each turn, and the dispute will expire if they don't accept or counter within that time.
How
When a user decides they agree with a suggested solution, accepting that solution is simple. To do so, they should:
Click Accept.
[Image: rtaImage]
(Pro only) Choose a completion date. 
[Image: rtaImage]
Only pros can set the completion date. If a customer agrees to a pro's solution, the pro has already entered this date when countering.
Review the details, explain why they agree or add terms, then click Submit to officially make an agreement.
[Image: rtaImage]
Success!
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
Counter
(return to index)
Instead of focusing on what has happened or who's at fault, the TSC is focused on how to solve the dispute that's been reported. Users are expected to suggest potential solutions to each other.
The customer makes the first suggested solution, then the pro can counter with a different solution if they don't agree with what the customer asked for.
Once a user has countered, it's the other user's turn to decide whether to Accept or Counter. Users are given 3 calendar days for each turn, and the dispute will expire if they don't Accept or Counter within that time.
A user can only Counter during their turn; the buttons will disappear during the other person's turn. To counter, they'll need to:
Click Counter.
[Image: rtaImage]
Choose a solution type.
[Image: rtaImage]
They must choose from these three options to Counter.
(Refund options only) Fill in a refund amount.
(Pros only) Choose a completion date.
[Image: rtaImage]
This date will not be shown to the customer unless this solution is agreed to.
Pros can only choose dates within the next 20 days.
Add attachments (if desired).
[Image: rtaImage]
Review the suggested solution, explain why they're suggesting this solution, then click Submit.
[Image: rtaImage]
Once submitted, they'll see their suggested solution on the main page, their buttons will disappear, and it'll be the other user's turn.
[Image: rtaImage]

DEFINITIONS
(return to index)

Status and stage
(return to index)
The status is the overall status of the dispute. Possible statuses are:
Awaiting:
Waiting for either party to enter TSC.
In progress: 
The dispute has been started, and the parties are communicating.
Under review:
The dispute has been stopped or closed on the customer/pro’s end and needs to be reviewed by an incident handling specialist.
Closed:
The dispute is closed.
The stage is where the users are in the discussion.


Initiator confirmation needed
The initiating party needs to confirm the dispute details.
Responder first action needed
The responding party needs to respond to the concerns.
Offer pending
A party has offered a solution and is waiting for it to be accepted or countered.
Agreement made
The parties came to an agreement.
Expired
Time for the user to take action ran out.
Withdrawn
The initiating party withdrew the dispute, and the dispute was closed.
Stopped
The dispute has been stopped.
Changed resolution platform
The dispute needed to be switched to a different resolution platform.
Closure reasons
(return to index)

When closing a dispute, consider why you are no longer using the Solution Center for this incident and select the closure reason that corresponds.
TIP: These closure reasons are meant to tell T&S why the specialist isn’t using the TSC any longer, not what actions were taken after the TSC was closed.
Definitions



CLOSURE REASON
DESCRIPTION
CLOSURE SUB-REASON
DESCRIPTION
Agreement Made
Use this when an agreement was formally accepted and when an agreement is made in the conversation, but neither party formally clicked Accept.
No Sub Categories
Select “Agreement Made” for both fields.
Escalated
You'll be moving forward with a different process.
Arbitration 
Arbitration will be offered instead.

Escalated
You'll be moving forward with a different process.
Manual
Working with both parties directly instead of asking them to work together. (Additionally, use this reason when you’re stepping back from a dispute.)

Escalated
You'll be moving forward with a different process.
Low Dollar Comp
Using the low $ comp program instead.

Escalated
You'll be moving forward with a different process.
Accidental Agreement
One or both parties said they didn’t mean to make an agreement/click Accept.
Stopped
Pro/customer shouldn't be using the Solution Center anymore.
Unprofessional Behavior 
One or both parties were unprofessional, and they should no longer work together in the TSC.

Stopped

   Emails
   (return to index)
TSC - Account hold - notify customer (tscahc): Use this as needed to notify the customer when we’ve added an account hold to the pro’s account related to a TSC dispute.
TSC - Account hold - notify pro (tscahp): Use this to notify the pro when we add an account hold related to a TSC dispute.
TSC - Agreement completed (to either) (tsccomplete): Lets users know that we noticed they made an agreement, and we’ll be closing their dispute.
TSC - Including reviews (to either): Notifies users that we don’t allow reviews to be leveraged in their agreements.
TSC - Customer never responded to pro (to customer) (tscnever): Explains to the customer that their dispute expired due to their non-response and that we’ve reopened it.
TSC - Delete unresponsive pro (to pro) (tscdelete): Notifies pro that we’re disabling their account due to non-response to the TSC.
TSC - Explain TSC (to either) (tscexp): Use this to respond when users want more help or want to tell their side of the story. Explains the purpose and focus of the TSC.
TSC - Incomplete agreement (to customer) (tsccagree): Lets customers know that we’ll reach out to the pro about their agreement if it wasn’t completed on time.
TSC - Incomplete agreement (to pro) (tscagree): Use to follow up with pro if they haven’t completed a TSC agreement on time.
TSC - Keep Communicating (to either) (tsckeep): Lets users know that we’ve reopened the TSC so they can continue working together.
TSC - Reopen dispute (to either) (tscreopen): Explains to users that the reason their dispute expired was that it was expired (used instead of TSC - Keep communicating (to either) when the user thinks there’s an error).
TSC - Resolved per customer (to either) (tscres): Explains to users that we’re closing the dispute because the customer confirmed it was resolved.
TSC - Resolved per pro (to either) (tscpres): Notifies pro that we’ll reach out to the customer to confirm it was resolved, asks the customer if their concern was resolved.
TSC - Stepping forward (to either) (tscstep): Use when we feel it’s appropriate to close the incident without resolution.
TSC - Troubleshooting (to either) (tsct): Troubleshooting steps for when the user experiences an error in the TSC.
TSC - Unofficial agreement (to either) (tscun): Notifies users that we’re closing the incident since they came to an agreement.
TSC - Unprofessional (to either) (tscbehave): Coaching to a user who’s used unprofessional communication in the TSC.

   Troubleshooting
       (return to index)
Many issues can be easily resolved by clicking “sync incident” at the top of the incident. If the specialist or user are still experiencing issues, review the additional steps below.


[Image: rtaImage]


CUSTOMER OR PRO CAN’T SIGN UP
(return to index)

If the TSC isn’t closed or expired, typically, the user is using the wrong Thumbtack account, or they need to clear their cache and cookies. Send the Grammarly Snippet "Troubleshooting macro for TSC" (tsct) to help the user with troubleshooting steps.

DISPUTE SHOULD HAVE EXPIRED
(return to index)
The TSC is designed to expire at certain points when there is no action from the pending user. This can include when a user doesn’t sign up, accept, or counter an offer by the provided deadline. If you notice that this timeline has passed, and the TSC has not expired, submit a Help Desk ticket and consider the time the users have waited to evaluate if we should escalate the incident out of the TSC.
**Use the content request form to request an update or submit questions/concerns**

The Trust and Safety KA structure is different from Support ops or Sales articles in several unique ways.
Articles have a Title heading.
Articles have an “Index” instead of a “Content” section.
If there are articles from multiple organizations with the same name, “T&S” or “incidents” should be included in the title.

T&S: Thumbtack Guarantee (incidents)
The “Category” section will show “Trust and Safety.”
Note: More than one category can show here, and may be available to multiple teams.

Knowledge widget

Click Knowledge at the bottom of your Tack window to open the Knowledge widget.
[Image: AD_4nXc-NI2uRB-ag6tARaVdnQJz1Yx9Ib58DXUNWIRMmTMpoM5w_eVnrLRm_Y66fZkGd1FO5pBvuAyZwmKFKGRb2WGoNmY7JHFAGitqjiQzmCTXUXK6-61BNtQjKetoZ1I4HnJh9wANm4qugO7PFRtHBBD8q6Y]
In the top left side of the widget box, type in what you believe to be part of the article name.
This search can only look through article names.
We have manually input some synonyms, so you can find some articles without knowing the exact name (i.e., “Money-Back Guarantee” shows when you type “MBG”).
Under Categories, on the left side of the widget, click Trust and Safety.
Use the list above to find the category that applies to you.
Look through the subcategories if there are any as well.
Once you’ve opened the relevant category/subcategory, look through the list of articles on the right or use the search box on the left to search through the article list.
When you’ve found the article you need, either click Preview to see it in your widget or click the article title to open it as a Tack tab.
If you didn’t find the right article, try different search terms or use the search method below.
Tip: To search through all Trust and Safety articles, make sure only the Trust and Safety category is open (opening subcategories restricts the search to those sections).
Tack Search bar
(return to index)

[Image: AD_4nXeD6dmWCbTrB_eVSSKNkoqx_J31F3evK-0waGbSjgdoVcP1MJ5o7WiDT2NG19HkEqPiS_yxUkEEsTBgtlr__mxDF2eGiIltW8RNMO8F7UUBn7W9fD5fZyWmFwU7fAbwL5QChUGgT9NvKQYeB7BN2cpngAg]

Click the search bar at the top center of your Tack page.
On the left side of the search bar, click All ▼ to open the drop-down menu.
Find Knowledge on the drop-down and click it to search only Knowledge articles.
[Image: AD_4nXdhyKHoO5RzH9MqDx22W07zsef35LgrKqDnvQLu_36aI5l4JAe_65T4ZB3zzETUasF4GirMg8E_I4q8sz9-H36NNRwSUeljzFZ_NAZbFy0-PNZmfB6gRMdSBWAxBsOMkc6v7hbikW7fnwMu4XyJE67Ib-8r]
You can search without doing this, but you’ll receive many results, so it’s not recommended.
Type in a term related to what you’re looking for and click Enter or Return on your keyboard.
This also searches within the articles, so you don’t need to know the article title to find it.
Some articles will pull up in your preview before you click enter. These are only searching article titles, but they might be what you’re looking for and can be clicked.
Note: This preview also includes articles you’ve recently viewed. If these have been updated since you last viewed them, the older version may populate. 
Look through the results to find the article you need, then click the article title to open it in Tack.
Preview articles
(return to index)
To preview an article, hover the pointer over the search result name. This will bring up a small preview window of the article, and you can scroll up or down to preview further. Using the tips above, you can determine if the article is for the correct department and if it will be helpful. 

[Image: AD_4nXcKxHmeMlhPjIAMnRuE-iTVTTqW7aSXvzUtjviG2Lp8IcI1bvvmQ3fleI8ipVWvePn0qGkiagrOVTGY2gAYv_5h-TocwrtccAJg_US1eg32mXUv3wFF1qjRlLSOR42uLb5Dw2kZTJRS0VnLV35nS-iqefk]

   Troubleshooting
    (return to index)
OPENING LINKS WITH OMNI ACTIVE
(return to index)
Opening new links while using the OMNI tab will disrupt tracking and affect the specialists' stats. Things to keep in mind:
Whenever possible, links to new articles should open in subtabs and not disrupt the OMNI status.

[Image: AD_4nXe15rZB9qBbTomGda686-sYQruXoSMiPj0LXUu1RuZBeMI3K9FfRaQGo0ZPyraltQxqZ9Agc0AM4Cemb7J4J7hN_sXWqvCmh4_QUBoj2hUN75R4FhCk3pc1gjRl-6EMy3oeGDFT0ZPQORlEdEjk3Q6vLFQs]

Pressing the command key as you click the link will open a tab instead of a new window. This should help keep the OMNI status from being disrupted.
If a new window is created this window will appear.

[Image: AD_4nXee49RllFyGlmOtjAxIIkG0xjUcrQLUbuCVpe8inaM6baQLnTRqIuZxI0h2sY4Ybpx1yRg9a_SFrvssFvHV2yLmb5mHb15C13DXOwx8CsjSV9rxK_oHQn7xW16vQB-ZVnlN8a1fjBRq_ahlUBNbNBJNmAZ1]

To avoid losing OMNI, select Cancel when asked to “Continue logging into Omni-channel” in a new window.
Close the new window after use to avoid disrupting OMNI.
OUTDATED ARTICLES
 (return to index)
Occasionally inks are “broken” or appear with an orange “You are viewing an outdated version of this article. Please review the most recent published version” banner. 
If a link is completely “broken,” it means the article has been archived and should no longer be used for reference. Any relevant content should have been moved to a new KA or updated into an existing one. These changes are rare and will always be communicated by Leadership or the Program Managers, so make sure to keep up to date on your email and Slack notifications to stay current. 
Archived articles are a different kind of issue. An orange banner shows that the article has been updated and is now out of date but is still a valid article.

[Image: AD_4nXcvKglQ5EqnYV-XiUeBpQHYFJKRranVGAbsarCxajGRWgSDwOdpDY2uW4bqjgyo-Nj8vONMaVb2d-ANnHTZqx-OMXPZqZxxwI6IUdmC0fRqJa0oegCo47ogI49cQPJ8JatWi0s9RUQ67xdzRjxY4TJapgGP]

To find (and bookmark) the updated article, click on the Versions tab below the orange banner and find the newest article with the largest version number (located at the top of the list). You can also check the date of the last update, located by scrolling to the right on that list, to see when things were last updated.

[Image: AD_4nXeWe5HM3RRcBU-X4ZtDMUB7k3o3BiJw_8x1WnhDZV_Sqc-6k5BfFbokZN8rI-mNhX3nBebQOnX6mUpPUR-QB0BcQNePc5wAPoXPth6c0v3jjwvoIpyJwR1us-zzZPmgweGnVkU_CyqE44DUaE95Bm7YUgw]

REQUEST AN UPDATE
(return to index0)
Updates to articles (including errors/mistakes) can be reported through the Content Request Form located at the bottom of every T&S article. Specialists can use this to request changes to existing content. For more information on this process see the Forms Master List knowledge article.

articles.fullText:
Navigate payout requests

Navigate payout requests
(Knowledge index)

INDEX
WHAT
Types of payouts
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Submitting payout
After payout request submitted
Trolley details
Talking points
Emails
Forms
Troubleshooting
Reissues
Trolley portal auto-email
Payout status
Related


What
(return to index)

Thumbtack sometimes uses payouts to help resolve users’ concerns. Different payout types apply in different situations, but any payout request will be reviewed for approval and sent to the user through Trolley. 
TYPES OF PAYOUTS
 (return to index)

Customer Satisfaction: The user is paid outside of our Guarantee with Thumbtack funds. If manager approval is required based on the CSAT payout guidance, it should be obtained before submitting the payout.
Money-Back Guarantee: The user is eligible for the Money-Back Guarantee and will receive a payment. Make sure the payout amount in the eligibility review matches the payout amount in the payout request.
Property Damage Guarantee: The user is eligible for the Property Damage Guarantee and will receive a payment. Make sure the payout amount in the eligibility review matches the payout amount in the payout request.
Settlement - Use this only if specifically directed to by a manager. 
Why
(return to index)
Trust and Safety is dedicated to helping Thumbtack users resolve their concerns. When mediation is exhausted or insufficient, users may qualify for the Thumbtack Guarantee or Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) payouts.
For guidance on processing and troubleshooting incidents involving In-Product Payouts, please refer to In-Product payments (incidents).

When
(return to index)
Review for a payout once standard mediation is complete or ruled out. Payouts are only issued after:
The specialist collects all required forms.
Payment eligibility is confirmed.
The user provides payout information in the Trolley portal.

How
(return to index)
   Steps   
	(return to index)

Before moving forward, ensure all initial approvals have been obtained, the Guarantee Eligibility Review tab has been updated with the most up-to-date information, and the customer has signed the Thumbtack Guarantee Submission form.
SUBMITTING PAYOUT
(return to index)
Send the Payout Expectations template email to the user receiving reimbursement. 
Select the appropriate template for your dispute and delete any irrelevant information.
Payout amount <$501 & no PDG
Payout amount >=$501 or is PDG
CSAT payout. Specialists must inform the user that the payout is not part of the Guarantee coverages, but is a one-time courtesy on Thumbtack's behalf.
Click on Payout Request on the left side of the incident manager.
Fill out all required fields.
Type: Choose from the Types of payouts.
Amount: Enter the corresponding payout amount already determined for the user, under the selected payout type.
For all Guarantee payouts, the Amount in the payout request must match the payout amount in the Guarantee Eligibility Review Tab.
For CSAT payouts directly related to a Guarantee review, the Guarantee Tab must reflect the Amount as ineligible and include details of the specific ineligibility reasons.
Full Name: The name will auto-fill from the Thumbtack account name, but it must match the legal name the user provided on the Thumbtack Guarantee Submission form, unless a different legal name is provided directly.
Collect the customer's legal name from the submission form.
Note: Dashes, apostrophes, and other special characters are acceptable when entering legal names. Specialists must use standard capitalization. Example: If the form says "JANE DOE" or "jane doe", enter it as "Jane Doe".
Email Address: The email will auto-fill with the Thumbtack account address, but verify it matches the user’s preferred email address. 
If different, default to the address used during the incident unless noted otherwise.
 If a masked relay email address is used (e.g., @privaterelay.appleid.com), request a valid email before finalizing the payout to avoid technical issues.
Click Submit.
If the payment is submitted  correctly, the status will automatically update to "Pending MTS Approval."
If the status does not update to “Pending MTS Approval”, reach out in #ts-payout-questions for assistance.
Note: If the Status is anything other than “Pending MTS Approval,” it will not be sent to the appropriate queue for review and approval, and the payout won't be issued.
AFTER PAYOUT SUBMITTED
(return to index)
Once the Status shows “Pending MTS Approval,” The payment will go through these additional approval statuses:
Pending MTS Approval:  Payout is awaiting manager approval in Tack.
Pending Agreement: Payout approved, but payout type or amount requires the user to complete an Ironclad Payout Agreement.
Pending Sr. Management Approval: High-dollar Payouts of $20k+ require an additional level of T&S approval.
Pending AP Approval: Payout approved, and the Trolley email has been sent to set up the profile.  
Approved (Sent to SVB for Payout): Funds have been sent to the user through Trolley
For MBG payouts less than $501 and no PDG:
Manager Approval flag and note received :
Flag customer and pro accounts,
Complete wrap-up notes and ensure the Guarantee Eligibility Review tab is complete and accurate
Close the incident
Optional: Send a thank-you/survey email to the user.
For MBG/CSAT payouts totalling $501+ and All PDG payouts:
Manager approval flag and note received: 
Send the Ironclad Payout Agreement form to the user (ensure the correct customer name).
Agreement signed and returned by Customer: 
Update the Guarantee tab, 
Flag customer and pro accounts, 
Insert wrap-up notes, 
Close the incident 
Optional: Send a thank-you/survey email to the user.
Payout status will change to Approved (Sent to SVB for Payout) when funds have been sent to the user through Trolley

NOTE: On rare occasions, a specialist may submit a mixed payment to help make a user whole (i.e., damages covered by the property damage guarantee plus the Money-Back Guarantee for other deviations). If this is the case, submit multiple payout requests with the amounts that apply for each payout type.
When submitting multiple payouts for the same incident, post in the #ts-payout-questions to make that team aware. Make sure to include the customer’s name/email, incident number, and payout amounts.
Only one Agreement form is required per incident. The dollar amount listed on the agreement form must reflect the total amount of all payouts issued to the customer.

TROLLEY DETAILS
(return to index)

What Users See

Once a payout status is “Pending AP Approval”, the user will receive an email from trustandsafetyteam@thumbtack.com with the subject line: ”Your Thumbtack Payment Has Been Approved”
[Image: rtaImage]
The email will direct the user to a Thumbtack-branded payout portal powered by Trolley, where they’ll need to verify their account via email.
The user must use the same email address that was submitted on the payout request in Salesforce.
The email address is a unique identifier, and the payout cannot be issued if Salesforce does not match Trolley.
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
Once confirmed, the user will be directed to set up their profile.
  [Image: rtaImage]
Add General Information: The user’s legal name and email will auto-populate based on the information previously submitted in the payout request. The user will need to manually enter their mailing address.
[Image: rtaImage]
Add Payout Method: The user must select their preferred payout method and enter the requested payment information.
Users can select:
 Bank Transfer
[Image: rtaImage]
Once these steps are completed, they’ll be confirmed as active and ready to receive payment.
Note: Trolley Participant Status will change to “Active” on the Payout Request, meaning we can send their payout.
[Image: rtaImage]
Once the user shows as “Active,” the payout will be sent on the following Thursday.

   Talking points
      (return to index)

IS IT SAFE TO USE TROLLEY?
(return to index)

Trolley takes the security of its users very seriously and is compliant with federal guidelines. If customers have any further questions about Trolley, they can contact their support team at support@trolley.com. 

CAN I RECEIVE A PAPER CHECK INSTEAD OF USING THE PORTAL?
(return to index)
We understand you might prefer a physical check, but at this time, we do not offer payouts by check. To ensure your funds reach you as quickly and safely as possible, we exclusively use Trolley for direct bank transfers. This platform uses bank-grade encryption and strict privacy protocols to keep your information secure, similar to the systems used by major financial institutions.
Using this digital method allows us to maintain the highest level of security and ensures you receive your funds within 5 to 7 business days once your portal setup is complete. If you have any specific questions about the security of the platform, you can reach out to the Trolley team directly at support@trolley.com. and they can provide more technical details.


HOW DO I GET STARTED WITH TROLLEY?
(return to index)
To get your payment started, you’ll need to complete a quick one-time setup through our secure payout partner, Trolley. You should have an invitation email in your inbox with a unique link. Just follow that to enter your banking details. Once you’ve finished the portal setup, you can expect to receive your funds within 5 to 7 business days.

WHAT SHOULD I DO IF THE PORTAL GIVES ME AN ERROR OR NO CODE?
(return to index)

If you're having trouble receiving a verification code or seeing an error message, we first recommend clearing your browser's cache or logging in with a different browser. If the system still doesn't recognize your bank account or gives you an "incorrect PIN" notification, please reach out to the Trolley support team directly at support@trolley.com. They have a specialized team that can provide the most detailed assistance to help you complete your setup.
Note: If the user has gone through all the troubleshooting steps and is still unable or unwilling to use Trolley, reach out to the #ts-payout-questions Slack channel for guidance on next steps.

  Emails
    (return to index)

Payout Expectations/ PO: Expect Pay: Specialists should use this email once a Payout Request has been created and submitted for approval. It informs the customer of the next steps and timeline. 

Payout: Notifying pro of expedited payout/ PO: Notify pro of expedited PO: Specialists should use this email when they won’t be taking action on a pro but want the pro to know we paid their customer.

Payout: Pro upset we paid customer (expedited incident)/ PO: Pro upset CX was paid: Specialists should use this email when they didn’t remove a pro’s account, but the pro is upset that we paid the customer.

Payout: Pro disagrees with payment amount (pro removed)/ PO: Pro disagrees w/TG (Pro): Specialists should use this email when the pro doesn’t want to reimburse the amount the customer was paid under the guarantee.

Payout: Pro reaches out after the customer was paid (pro removed)/ PO: Pro reaches out after TG: Specialists should use this email when a removed pro reaches out after the customer received a Thumbtack Guarantee payment. 

Payout: Customer pushback/question about setting up Trolley account/ PO: Trolley questions: Specialists should use this email when the customer gives pushback or has questions about setting up their Trolley account through the portal. 

   Forms
     (return to index)
 
For all payout types, users are required to fill out forms before they’re sent a payment.
“Thumbtack Guarantee Submission form” is required for all payouts.
 “Thumbtack Payment Agreement” is required for:
All PDG payouts
MBG and CSAT payouts totalling $501+ 
 “Wire Transfer Request Form” is required for payouts of $12,000+.
Once the specialist has manager approval, confirm that the Ironclad “Wire Transfer Request Form” has been signed and that the dollar amount listed matches the amount paid out.

Note: Wire transfers are not paid to the customer via the usual Trolley process. Do not send this form before the payout is officially approved in Salesforce and by your manager.

   Troubleshooting
   (return to index)
REISSUES
(return to index)

Specialists should make every effort to confirm that the information submitted in a payout request is accurate. If the payout status is “Approved (Sent to SVB for Payout)” and they discover an error (e.g., an incorrect email address, a non-legal name, etc.), they may need to reissue the payment. When this happens:

Reach out in the #ts-payout-questions Slack channel.
Explain that an error needs to be corrected on a sent payment.
Include the correct information already confirmed with the user.
Leadership will edit the payout request to include the correct information and update the status to “Error.”

Reissues will be processed by the team every Wednesday. Once the payout has been approved by AP and sent via Trolley, the status will be updated again to “Approved (Sent to SVB for Payout).”

TROLLEY PORTAL AUTO-EMAIL
(return to index)

Checking if the email was sent

Once a payout request status is marked “Pending AP Approval,” users will be recorded as “recipients” in Trolley. An automated email will be sent via Trolley. Additionally, as long as the incident is open and the names match, an email will also be sent via Tack

These emails direct the user to the Trolley Portal to complete their profile and payment setup. Specialists can verify this within Tack from either:

From the payout request, select Activity on the right-hand side of the page. 

[Image: rtaImage]

From the user’s contact record, select Activity on the right-hand side of the page.

[Image: rtaImage]


Note: If the payout request status is “Pending AP Approval,” the user should have received an email from Trolley. If the user is having trouble finding the email, specialists can manually send the auto email template, Payout: Trolley payment setup

PAYOUT STATUS
(return to index)

On Thursday of each week, we process all approved payouts where the user’s Trolley Recipient Status is “Active”. Once we’ve sent payment, the user will receive an automated email via Trolley confirming receipt. 

The email isn’t directly visible in Tack. Specialists can verify this within Tack by: 

Selecting Payout Request on the top left side of the incident. 
If the payout status now shows as “Approved (sent to SVB for payout),” funds have been sent, and their payment confirmation email has been sent.
[Image: rtaImage]

If you have additional concerns about payment status, reach out to #ts-payout-questions using workflow Payout Questions.

In-Product payments (incidents)

articles.fullText:
Navigate New Era ADR (Arbitrator)

Navigate New Era ADR (Arbitrator) 
(Knowledge index)
INDEX 
WHAT
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Process Flowchart
Interactive walkthrough
Create a dispute
Details
Dispute cancellation and case closure
Email
Troubleshooting

New Era contact info

What
​​(return to index)

This article will help specialists navigate the New Era ADR (Advanced Dispute Resolution) system when using it for incidents.

When 
​​​​(return to index) 

Use this article to help navigate the New Era dashboard when creating new disputes approved for New Era arbitration and incidents already in New Era.

How
​​​​​​​​(return to index)

   Steps
   ​​​​(return to index)

PROCESS FLOWCHART
(return to index)

[Image: rtaImage]


INTERACTIVE WALKTHROUGH
​​​​​​(return to index)

For a step-by-step interactive demonstration of the New Era process, please use the New Era ADR: Interactive Guide

 CREATE A DISPUTE
​​(return to index)
Once the specialist has followed the steps in the New Era ADR (incidents) KA, and management has approved the incident for New Era, use the steps below to start that process.

Open the New Era platform in a web browser.
Link: http://www.neweraadr.com 
Click Sign In at the top right corner of the screen.
Once signed in, navigate to the case creation utility.
Click the Start New Case button.
[Image: rtaImage]

Enter all required details for the Claimant (usually the customer).
NOTE: Specialists must know the state where the project was completed to ensure accurate jurisdiction setup.
If needed, reach out to confirm this information before continuing to the next step.
[Image: rtaImage]
NOTE: Do not upload any files at this stage.
Customer and pro should upload their own files to remain neutral and ensure that T&S does not alter or omit any necessary documentation.
[Image: rtaImage]
Click Next to continue, then Next again to skip the documentation screen.
Enter all required details for the Respondent (usually the Service Provider/Pro).
NOTE: Confirm that the state where the project was completed matches the state entered for the Claimant.
[Image: rtaImage]
NOTE: Do not upload any files at this stage.
The customer and pro should upload their own files so T&S can remain neutral and ensure we are not altering or missing any necessary documentation.
[Image: rtaImage]
Click Next to proceed, then Next again to skip the documentation screen.
Review the summary screen to ensure all Claimant and Respondent details are accurate.
Click Submit case.
Once the case is submitted, New Era will automatically send sign-up links to both the Claimant and the Respondent. 
*Email sample sent by New Era*
[Image: rtaImage][Image: rtaImage]
Once the Dispute has been created in the New Era Platform, send emails to both the customer and the pro to notify them that the case has been created. They should receive an email directly from New Era with the sign-up links within. These templates can be found in the New Era ADR KA.
Monitor the Dashboard
Because the New Era platform doesn’t provide automated status notifications, manual monitoring is required. Navigate to the New Era dashboard and click on the case name to verify status based on the following steps:
2 Business Days after Link Sent: Confirm both the Customer and Pro have signed up.
Morning of Arbitration: Verify the exact start time to catch any last-minute adjustments from the arbiter.
When a Decision is rendered: Review the dashboard to see if the arbiter set a custom payment deadline (different from the standard 14 days).
Payment Deadline: Check the dashboard on the due date to confirm that compensation has been fulfilled.

[Image: rtaImage]

   Details 
    (return to index) 
NEW ERA DISPUTE CANCELLATION AND CASE CLOSURE
(return to index) 
A case should be formally closed if the Claimant formally rescinds their desire to use the arbitration process with New Era ADR or Thumbtack, or they inform Thumbtack they're moving forward with alternative resolution" (e.g., legal action elsewhere, private settlement, or dropping the claim).
Before requesting closure, log in to the New Era Dashboard to confirm that the case remains in its preliminary stages and has not yet reached the point where fees or arbitrator appointments have been finalized.
To maintain a clean dashboard and prevent unnecessary follow-ups. Do not simply let invitations expire.
Use the Grammarly Snippet A_NE: Contact New Era (Arbitrator) to email to the New Era Support at (support@neweraadr.com) with the following details:
Case Name: (e.g., Claimant v. Professional)
Case Number: The specific 8-digit New Era case ID.
Reason for Closure: A brief statement (e.g., "Claimant has rescinded their desire to participate").
The case is not considered fully "Closed" until New Era confirms that the dispute has been deactivated on their end.
Once New Era confirms the dispute is closed, the incident can be closed through the standard incident processes.
NOTE: Ensure a CSAT survey is sent for these incidents.
   Emails 
   ​​((return to index)
ARBITRATOR
A_NE: Handoff email (to Customer) / A_NE: Handoff email (to CX): Send to the customer after creating a dispute.
A_NE: Handoff email (to Pro) / A_NE: Handoff email (to Pro): Send to pro once the customer has signed up.
A-NE: Reminder to sign up (to Customer) / A_NE: Reminder to Sign Up (cx): Send to the customer when we haven’t heard back from them after explaining New Era.
A_NE Customer confirmed (to Customer) / A_NE: Customer Confirmation: Send to the customer to thank them for agreeing to use FairClaims and let them know we’ll reach out when we hear from the Pro.
A_NE: Unresponsive pro (to Customer) / A_NE: Unresponsive pro (to CX): Send to customer when the pro hasn’t signed up for New Era, has been removed, and we’re stepping back.
A_NE: Customer unresponsive to sign up (to Pro) / A_NE: CX unres sign up (to Pro): Send to pro when customer becomes unresponsive to the sign-up link sent. 
A_NE: Pro removed (to Pro) / A_NE: Pro removed (to Pro): Send to the pro when we haven’t heard back from them, and we’re taking action on their account.
A_NE: No response to sign-up link (to Customer) / A_NE: No Response - (to CX): Send to customer as a follow-up when they have not signed up to the link.
A_NE: After Judgement Pro removed not resolved (to Customer) / A_NE: After Judgement Pro removed (to CX): Send to customer after pro did not comply with New Era judgement, letting them know we are reaching out to pro and providing the pro's information.
A_NE: After Judgment Removing pro (to Pro) / A_NE: After Judgement Pro removed (to Pro): Send to pro after pro did not comply with New Era judgement, letting them know account removed and requesting follow-up. 
A_NE: Registration Confirmed (Any Party) / A_NE: Registration Confirmation (Any Party): Send to either user after both parties have signed up for the New Era.
A_NE: To Guarantee (to Customer) / A_NE: To Guarantee (to CX): Send to the customer when they let us know the pro hasn’t fulfilled their New Era agreement and asks about the Guarantee.
A_NE: Contacting New Era for process-related questions (Any Party) / A_NE: Contacting New Era (Any Party): Send to either party when asking New Era process-specific questions.
A_NE: Contact New Era (Arbitrator) / A_NE: Contact New Era (Arbitrator): Send this when reaching out directly to New Era for questions or to cancel a dispute.
GRAMMARLY ONLY
Link: How New Era works (Any Party): Quick link to share the “How New Era ADR works" link.
Link: FAQ’s New Era (Any Party): Quick link to share the “FAQ’s about New Era ADR process" link.
   Troubleshooting 
    ​​(return to index) 
NEW ERA CONTACT INFO
​​(return to index) 
Contact info for customers and pros: 
General inquiries: support@neweraadr.com
Customer support: support@neweraadr.com
Users should work with New Era to troubleshoot or address questions related to the New Era process or platform.

Contact info for Thumbtack specialists: 
General inquiries and dispute-related questions: support@neweraadr.com (Feel free to cc apowell@thumbtack.com and/or jdoane@thumbtack.com ). All questions from you to New Era should be submitted via your incident. There should be no change in response time.
Click Quick Case.
Click Other 3rd Party.
Use the email addresses above.
Be sure to include the Case Number in the email subject line if applicable.
Example: (8-digit New Era case ID) - Follow-up from Thumbtack Support.
Write the email, and ask the question.
If the specialist needs to follow up again with New Era, reply from the case level. This way, you don’t have to keep creating additional quick cases.
[Image: rtaImage]

    ​​​​​​(return to index)

articles.fullText:
Navigate Ironclad

Navigate Ironclad
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Sending through incident
Sending through case
Details
How to tell if the user completed the form
Talking points
Emails
Forms
Troubleshooting
Issues logging in
Completed forms not found in the incident
Sending a manual reminder in Ironclad
Manual upload if integration fails
Related

What
(return to index)
Ironclad is an application integrated into Salesforce that Specialists use to make signing forms/agreements easier for customers and pros.
Why
(return to index)
Ironclad streamlines the legal agreement process by sending official forms that are easy for users to e-sign. Once completed, these documents are automatically attached to the relevant Salesforce incidents.
When
(return to index)
Specialists can use Ironclad to send submission and agreement forms for Thumbtack Guarantee payouts, payout reimbursements, account transfers, licensing, and wire transfers. 
How
(return to index)
   Steps
   (return to index)
SENDING THROUGH INCIDENT
(return to index)
Specialists initiate these forms directly within the Incident Manager in Salesforce:
On the left-hand side of the incident manager, click the Forms dropdown.
[Image: rtaImage]
In the next screen, a prompt will appear asking, “Is the individual receiving Spanish support?”
If this is a standard incident, check the mark next to “No,” and continue to the next step.
If the user has a Spanish support flag, has received support in Spanish throughout the incident, and/or has requested assistance in Spanish, check the mark next to “yes.”
Currently, only the following forms are available:
Thumbtack Guarantee Submission Form (Spanish)
Thumbtack Payment Agreement (Spanish)
Thumbtack Reimbursement Agreement (Spanish)
Wire Transfer Request Form (Spanish)
[Image: rtaImage]
Click the appropriate form.
On the next screen, verify that the customer’s info is correct. Update it if necessary.
Don’t change the number listed in the incident section, this is how Ironclad connects to the specific incident.
Click Submit.
Keep this page open until the form is sent, then close the tab and add an Internal Note to the incident that it was sent.
Manual Action Required: Ironclad does not auto-note the incident when the form is sent. You must add an Internal Note stating that the form was sen
[Image: Screenshot 2023-08-28 at 12.13.32 PM.png]

SENDING THROUGH CASE
(return to index)
Used primarily for ID Help. Since there is no direct integration for cases yet, ID help specialists must work directly within the Ironclad dashboard. 
Log in to Ironclad using Okta.
[Image: rtaImage]
Click Start Workflow in the top right corner of the IronClad dashboard.
[Image: rtaImage]
Choose Thumbtack Trust & Safety Agreement from the drop-down options in the pop-up window.
[Image: rtaImage]
Choose the appropriate form.
Account Transfer Agreement
Account Transfer Agreement - Multiple Parties
Professional License Use Agreement: Account Owner
Professional License Use Agreement: License Holder
[Image: Screenshot 2023-08-28 at 12.14.32 PM.png]
Note: These are the only forms to use for ID help cases.
Fill out the required fields, then click Submit.
Once the signature is complete, ID help specialists will receive a Gmail notification. 
Download the completed PDF(s)
Manually upload the PDF (s) by selecting the Files tab on the left-hand side of the case.
[Image: rtaImage]
   Details
   (return to index)
HOW TO TELL IF THE USER COMPLETED A FORM
(return to index)
Once an Ironclad form has been completed, Ironclad will send an automated email to the original incident owner's Thumbtack Gmail account, and a new entry from “Ironclad Integration User” will appear in the incident feed.
Note: The email notification will only be sent to the specialist's Thumbtack Gmail account who sent the initial form. Specialists who take over an incident from another specialist should rely on the notification in the Incident Feed.
In the incident manager, Specialists can navigate to the Notes and Attachments section and view the completed Ironclad in two ways.
From the incident feed:
 Click the link in the post created by the Ironclad Integration User."
[Image: Screenshot 2023-01-13 at 2.30.24 PM.png]
From the Details Tab:
Scroll to Ironclad Contracts and click the form name.
[Image: Screenshot 2022-11-21 at 2.49.34 PM.png]
Once you’ve followed either of those steps, click the link in the right corner under Notes and Attachments.
You’ll be able to see a copy of the actual form here.
[Image: Screenshot 2022-11-21 at 1.42.43 PM.png]
Name Discrepancies: The user-entered "User Legal Name" may not match the signature line. Users enter their legal name themselves; however, the signature is information added by Thumbtack during the Ironclad creation process.
Note: This is a two-step process for the user. First, they provide info in Ironclad; second, they sign in HelloSign. HelloSign sends the signature link immediately after the Ironclad step is done.
   Talking points
   (return to index)
HOW DOES IRONCLAD WORK?
(return to index)
“After you’ve provided the information requested, a message will say your details are being reviewed by Thumbtack. You’ll then automatically receive another email from noreply@hellosign.com, which will collect your signature.”
   Emails
   (return to index) 
Thumbtack Guarantee - Request submission: Send this macro when sending the Guarantee submission form.
Payout - Pro reaches out after customer was paid (pro removed): Send this when sending the Thumbtack Reimbursement Agreement asking a pro to pay us back after we paid the customer.
   Forms
   (return to index)
IRONCLAD FORMS
(return to index)
Forms under the “Thumbtack Guarantee Submission Form” link in the incident.
Thumbtack Guarantee Submission Form
Sent to customers when we’re evaluating their eligibility for the Thumbtack Guarantee or if we believe they may be eligible.
Forms under the “Thumbtack Guarantee Payout Agreement” link in the incident.
Thumbtack Payment Agreement
Sent to customers receiving a PDG payout of any amount or an MBG and CSAT payout of $501+.
Thumbtack Reimbursement Agreement
Sent to pros when they need to pay us back to have their account reactivated.
Wire Transfer Request Form
Sent to customers who are receiving a payment above $12k or when we will be wiring the user their payment.
Non-English Forms
Thumbtack Guarantee Submission Form (Spanish)
Thumbtack Payment Agreement (Spanish)
Thumbtack Reimbursement Agreement (Spanish)
Wire Transfer Request Form (Spanish)
   Troubleshooting
   (return to index)
ISSUES LOGGING IN
(return to index)
If you cannot log in to the Ironclad Dashboard, make sure you’ve accessed it through Okta. If access is still denied, contact the TackIT (Helpdesk) to activate your account.
COMPLETED FORMS NOT FOUND IN THE INCIDENT
(return to index)
Confirm that the Ironclad request with the necessary documentation was successfully sent on the Ironclad Dashboard.
If sent by a different specialist, manually check the Ironclad Dashboard (using the "All Workflows" or "Search" function) to verify that an active workflow exists for the customer.
If the signature is confirmed, follow the Manual Upload steps below.
A common reason this happens is that the Ironclad form was completed, but the link in the second email from HelloSign was not completed
Open the workflow in Ironclad Dashboard. If the "Sign" section is incomplete, they haven't signed yet.
Sometimes, the user has completed both steps, but the form hasn’t been attached to your incident yet due to a delay.
Click the Sync Incident button in the top-right corner of the incident to refresh the incident.
Check for a Gmail email notification (unless the forms were initially sent by a different specialist), or manually review the Ironclad Dashboard.
If none of these resolve the issue, cancel the workflow and resend the form through the incident.

SENDING A MANUAL REMINDER IN IRONCLAD
(return to index)
Ironclad sends auto-reminders at 2 and 5 days when a workflow step is incomplete. To send a manual reminder:
Log in to Ironclad through Okta and go to the Owned by me tab on the left-hand side of the screen.
Use the Search option for the specific customer’s name/workflow on the top right-hand side of the screen..
[Image: rtaImage]
Select the customer workflow that’s missing.
Depending on what part of the process you’re in, this will show as follows:
“Thumbtack Guarantee Submission Form for ________”
“Thumbtack Trust & Safety Agreement with ________”
Note: “Thumbtack Trust and Safety Agreements” is used for the final steps in customer payouts AND for Pro reimbursement forms.
Within the workflow, in the expanded details section, find the 3 dots next to the user’s workflow status and the clock symbol, about halfway down the page. Click Resend email to send the user a reminder email to complete the form.
Thumbtack Guarantee submission
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
Thumbtack T&S Agreement
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
Note: This can be done for any incomplete workflow, regardless of what specialist initiated it. If you’re taking over an incident or covering while a specialist is out, use the existing workflow instead of starting a new one whenever possible.

MANUAL UPLOAD IF INTEGRATION FAILS
(return to index)
If the form is signed (confirmed in Gmail or Ironclad Dashboard) but does not appear in the Incident:
Download the completed PDF from the Ironclad Dashboard.
In the Incident, click the File Manager tab on the top-right.
Click Choose File, select the IronClad and click Save.
Add an Internal Note stating the form was manually uploaded due to an integration delay.

   (return to index)

articles.summary: This article guides service professionals on how to navigate the Checkr platform and understand the results of their background checks.
articles.concepts: background check, background screening, Checkr status, trust and safety, provider verification
articles.fullText:
Navigate Checkr

Navigate Checkr
(Knowledge index)
 
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Details
Checkr results meanings
Exceptions
 
What
(return to index)
 
Checkr is a platform that performs background checks for our users.
 
Why
(return to index)
We request background checks to increase trust and safety on Thumbtack. Checkr allows us to run the background checks.
 
When
(return to index)
Checkr is used whenever we’re running a background check (unless it’s SSN-less), but most specialists only need to navigate it when they’re checking the status of a background check.
 
How
(return to index)
   Steps
   ​​​​​​​(return to index)
 
If you don’t already have access to Checkr, get approval from leadership, then submit a helpdesk ticket.
Log in to Checkr, and you’ll be directed to a landing page. 
Enter the pro’s name, email address, phone number, and ID in the Keyword field, then hit enter on your keyboard.[Image: ejpATSH9DjO7-tSu_iPK7aTc0tRmdXrYFeKvRK1IkYUSdWPeHoVZBSOi-mt1seKND9LP0eWI8PM3qKoLDt45VEY08wcCbKtRfyR5vg3w9Onpm4g_XRnIMZtFYK1RhXVFxLJvxcdh]
If the information matches something in the database, the results will be available at the bottom of the page.[Image: oXNmWFaHt0mk_d9-mMeaqt4A79nJ7BQKpRg3RaItdfPwpH4ZFpnQvvaFX9p5vPdOStDFw9X_b2ugLdAsUgjqp7txnqAZsgOR83I33N07a3x7n-FDuDdieOrU0JPYGqJKigor9McV]
Once you have your result in Checkr, click to see more information.[Image: Screenshot 2023-01-19 at 1.50.28 PM.png]
Go to report information and you will see the package type.
Tasker_basic = Full-9
Tasker_basic_ssnless = SSN-Less[Image: Screenshot 2023-01-19 at 1.51.17 PM.png]
To get the report ID, click the dropdown button Download PDF and select “Order summary PDF”.[Image: Screenshot 2023-01-19 at 1.51.46 PM.png]
 Report PDF will be opened in another tab where you will be able to see the report ID.[Image: Screenshot 2023-01-19 at 1.52.08 PM.png]
   Details
   ​​​​​​​(return to index)
CHECKR RESULTS MEANINGS
​​​​​​​(return to index)
Reports list the status of each package individually and include a summary status, both at the top of the page and in the Report Summary section.
Pending
The report is processing. 
Time is dependent on the Screenings run but is usually within 2-3 days. 
Manual County Criminal Records Checks may take significantly longer to complete. 
For more information, see "Why is the background check taking longer than expected?"
Complete
The report is complete and ready for your review.
Clear
The report is complete and doesn’t contain adverse information or includes info that was filtered out by our rules.
Consider
Report is complete, contains info we need to evaluate.
May include criminal records, motor vehicle report violations, or employment/education verifications that aren’t an exact match.
Some incomplete Reports will be listed as Consider if they contain information within them that merits the Consider status.
Dispute
Report is complete, and the user contacted Checkr about its accuracy.
Adjudication can’t proceed while in this status.
We’ll receive an email when the reinvestigation concludes, which can take 30 days.
Suspended
Report is incomplete, or info can’t be verified, and 7 days passed since Checkr requested additional info.
User can visit the Checkr portal to check the status. 
 
EXCEPTIONS
​​​​​​​(return to index)
What is an exception?

Usually a result of inadequate/inaccurate info, exceptions prevent the background check from being processed. It’s resolved by a request for more info. Checkr makes this request to the user in the dashboard and by email.
When an exception occurs, the candidate’s report will display a yellow window describing the exception and listing a document that must be provided for review by Checkr.
If the candidate doesn’t respond within seven days, the report is placed in Suspended status. Suspended reports can be updated and processed if the required document is provided within 30 days of the report's creation.
Resolving exceptions
Resolving exceptions requires users to submit additional information. They can do so by.
Visiting the Candidate Portal and following the steps listed in the exception.
Using a link we send.
Find the link in the exception within the Checkr dashboard.
Once an exception is resolved, the window is greyed out, and a green checkmark is added to the exception's description. Once all exceptions are resolved, the report will resume processing.
**Use the content request form ​​​​​​​ to request an update or submit questions/concerns**
​​​​​​​

articles.fullText:
Navigate Au10tix

Navigate Au10tix
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
 
What
(return to index)
Au10tix is a platform that allows us to perform background checks without using social security numbers (SSN).
 
Why
(return to index)
We perform background checks to improve trust and safety on Thumbtack. Some users don’t have a social security number or are uncomfortable sharing it with Checkr, so Au10tix allows us to check them without them disclosing their SSN.
 
When
(return to index)
Currently, Au10tix should only be used for the ID Help queue when we’re following the SSN-less background check process.
 
How
(return to index)
   Steps
   (return to index)
 
If you don’t already have access to Au10tix, get approval from leadership, then submit a helpdesk ticket.
Log in to Au10tix.
Click Upload in the top right corner.
Drag and drop the downloaded file into the Document front image in the dashboard, then click Submit for Processing. 
[Image: bQH5yDAWYgKn6INvOdEhktY6sIGjWeF08L9PyzRhaTcVUyat0BmqNUfE6ioG_BqVnbExRVKMcLF_HUgGmGJOnhi5zTKxu212oqov8Xu3eq-6m7gwdSGTzfdnmVIMWK3AU8kFnrCF]
We typically only collect “Document front image,” but have the ability to run the back image or selfie image if needed.
Go back and refresh the results page to see your image results pop up (may need to wait 10-20 seconds).
[Image: FriSsw9Kk3JEaYqEjJ0-T_uM8MoLQZRv2A-347Y5xykfXmQu42n7wZbQcoAQcMT9RlbdSatWb3lrBnMhDFby42L1NtqquqNexD1sM8NHk-rcudrtIng-q8CIeA6IXXT_iljycJls]
If Results says “passed” next to your user, you’re done using Au10tix and can move forward with your next steps.
If Results doesn’t say “passed,” click on the results to get more information, then follow the relevant article for your next steps.
 

**Use the content request form to request an update or submit questions/concerns**
