Navigate incident management tools

Navigate incident management tools
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Overview
Incident assignment
Communicate in an incident
Sending an email
Close an incident
Details
Call scheduling tool set-up
Stop a user from being surveyed 
Organizing and renaming files
Incident flag meanings
Incident banner meanings
Incident email automation
Troubleshooting
User reports new concern
Wrong user reported
Unable to send emails
Unable to open file, or file isn’t in file manager
Can’t close incident
Product feedback
What
(return to index)
Incident management tools help specialists track communication between users, call scheduling, incident notes, documentation, user flags and account actions. Most of these tools, with the exception of the Call Scheduling Tool, are found in the Incident Manager.
The Incident Manager, our primary incident management tool, is an object in Salesforce that only members of the Trust and Safety team can view. 
Why
(return to index)
The Incident Manager allows Trust and Safety to store all the information and communication about a reported concern between users (incident) in one place. Being familiar with the incident manager and other incident management tools is an important part of incident work. 
When
(return to index)
Incident management tools are used any time there’s a dispute between users. Incidents are created by the Categorization team and worked on by Trust and Safety incident operations specialists.
How
(return to index)
   Steps
    (return to index)

OVERVIEW
(return to index)
Below is a screenshot of an incident in the incident manager. The red numbers in each section correspond with the list below:

[Image: rtaImage]

The incident number, incident name, and the names of the users attached to the incident.
Use the unique incident number when sharing with other specialists. can be used to share the incident
Used to create notes, tasks, payout requests, and card charge requests.
Use the Note option to note any updates on the incident. Once saved, they show in the incident feed (5).
Use the visible to CS check box to leave notes that Service and support can see.
Use the Task option to set personal tasks on the incident. Specialists can select dates for notifications that appear in the incident feed (5).
Check the "Visible to CS" box to post information—such as situational context, account status, and next steps—directly to the primary case feed. This allows support to view details and advance the resolution.
These Drop-downs include:
Cases: links to all cases attached to the incident.
The case with a (c) next to it is the customer’s primary case.
The case with a (p) next to it is the pro’s primary case.
Case statuses can be found here.
Work Tickets: links to all work tickets that are related to the users’ “contacts” in Salesforce.
Not necessarily related to the incident, but could be.
Forms: links to the submission and payout agreement forms in Ironclad.
Solution Center: a form to submit an incident to the TSC or a dashboard of the TSC’s progress.
Arbitration: a form to submit an incident to New Era or a dashboard to manually track progress.
Incident factors: a list to keep track of risk factors that may impact the incident.
“Checking” any incident factors will post a notification to the incident feed (5).
Detail tabs 
MI Incident: categories, tier, owner, and other incident info.
Project: the bid/project data, a link to the project in admin.
Customer and Pro: info about users, links to their admins, other incidents they’re attached to, and previous flags (“customer success guidance”).
This is where you send emails (see 6.d.).
Guarantee: Thumbtack Guarantee eligibility review
File manager: Use this tab to manage the files sent by customers and pros. 
Details: details about the incident.
You’ll rarely need to use this section.
Quick Case: a place to create new cases that’ll be attached to the incident.
Use this when you need to contact a third party within the incident.
The feed includes emails, calls, notes, and other incident posts.
The most frequently used section of the incident.
Recent events are at the top, oldest at the bottom.
Buttons that allow you to take action on the incident.
The green “pencil” icon edits the tab you’re currently on.
The purple “eye” icon clears all incident flags.
The orange “card/checkmark” icon opens the incident closure prompt.
On the Customer and Pro tabs, the grey “envelope” icon allows you to email the user whose tab you’re on. 
Sync incident allows you to refresh the incident
When there is information missing from some of the fields that shouldn’t be, this button will usually resolve that issue. Specialists may need to exit out of the incident and reopen it for the updates to show. 
INCIDENT ASSIGNMENT
(return to index)
Take an incident
[Image: rtaImage]
Specialists will take new incidents by using the “Take an incident” status in Omni. To take an incident, use the steps below:
Set the Omni status to “Take an incident.”
Omni will automatically assign you the highest priority incident, corresponding to the specialists assigned routing skills. 
[Image: rtaImage]
Omni will offer up an incident.
Accept
Specialists should remain in “Take an incident” while reviewing and working on the newly assigned incident. When they’re ready to receive another incident, close the corresponding incident tab in My work.
Change the omni status to “MTS - Available” when no longer ready to take new incidents.
Decline
Update the Omni status to “Offline” and then back to “MTS - Available” to help reset routing.
Specialists should only decline if they aren’t ready to take a new incident. (Eg, mistakenly changing Omni statuses)
[Image: rtaImage]
If the incident needs to be manually assigned, (i.e., taking over an existing incident, manager request, miscategorization, etc.), follow these steps:
Assign to a user:
Open the incident.
Click the green “pencil” icon (see point 6 in overview).
Clear the “assigned to” section in the pop-up box.
Select your name in the same box, then click Save.
  Assign to a queue:
Open the incident.
Go to the Details tab.
Change owner
[Image: rtaImage]
Select Queues from the dropdown and search by the queue name.
[Image: rtaImage]
Note: Do not assign an incident directly to “Take an incident.” If you’re reassigning to a different process queue, select the specific queue as outlined in the “Assign a queue” section of the T&S Triage Queue Knowledge article.  
Select Change Owner.
COMMUNICATING IN AN INCIDENT
(return to index)
Specialists can call and email users through the incident manager.
[Image: rtaImage]
Click-to-call: Once logged in to Genesys, the user’s phone number will link to the phone panel. Click the phone number to start the call and automatically attach the call record to the incident. 
Email: Click the envelope to email the user. This will auto-populate with the email from the users tab you’re in, as the recipient. This can be edited if needed.
To email a third party or unassociated user, use the Quick Case tab and select Other 3rd Party.
[Image: rtaImage]
Sending an email
To send an email through an incident:

[Image: rtaImage]

Click either the Customer or Pro tab, depending on which user the email is for.
Select the grey envelope button on the right side of the user’s tab.
On the email prompt, click Select a Template.
Click the Folder dropdown to select the appropriate folder and view the available email macros.
Select either Marketplace Trust and Safety for department macros.
Select _Blank Letterhead when using a Grammarly snippet or composing an original email.
This information is required before sending an email. It will typically auto-populate from the current tab, but can be edited when needed.
ORGANIZING AND RENAMING FILES
(return to index)
To organize files, rename them.
To rename a file:
Navigate to the File Manager tab in your incident.
[Image: rtaImage]
Hover over the Description you want to change and click the pencil icon.
[Image: rtaImage]
Write the new file name and press the Enter key or click outside of the field.
[Image: rtaImage]
Click Save.
[Image: rtaImage]
To hide/unhide an irrelevant file
To hide: Rename the file to begin with “x” followed by one additional character (e.g., x_, x., xx, x null, x dup)
To show a hidden file: Click the checkmark next to “Show All Files,” then click Apply Filter.
[Image: rtaImage]
Uploading file to the incident
Download the file.
Navigate to the File Manager tab in your incident.
Click Choose file.
[Image: rtaImage]
In the pop-up, select the appropriate file and click Open.
Click Save.
[Image: rtaImage]
TO CLOSE AN INCIDENT
(return to index)
When all the steps from the incident expectations doc are complete, and it’s time to close the incident, follow the steps below. 
Click the orange button with a card and check mark on it to open the incident closure prompt.
[Image: rtaImage]
Fill out each of the required and relevant sections.
Each of these gathers valuable data from each incident and tracks trends.


FIELD
QUESTION IT ANSWERS
Project category, Project subcategory
What’s the user’s primary concern with the project, if any?
Safety category, Safety subcategory
What safety issue is involved, if any?
Communication - Pro, Communication - Customer
Did either user abandon the incident? Was it mid-dispute?
Result - Pro, Result - Customer
What was the result of the users attempting to work together?
Amount in dispute - Pro, Amount in dispute - Customer
What amount did the user expect the other user to pay them, if any?
Resolution Status
Were any project concerns resolved (by either a user or Thumbtack)?
Resolution type
What methods were used to resolve the project concern?
Amount resolved by pro
What amount did the pro refund, if any?
Initiator picklist
Who initially reported this concern to Thumbtack?
Note
If you didn’t CSAT, why? Is there anything else that’s best explained here?
Click Close Incident to save your answers.
   Details
    (return to index)
CALL SCHEDULING TOOL SET-UP
(return to index)
The call scheduling tool used by T&S may occasionally change, but these guidelines should always be followed when setting up the scheduling system. 


Setting
Requirement
Details
Availability 
Monday - Friday;
Your shift start time plus 30 min
Your shift end time minus 30 min
Example: If your shift is M-F 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, your availability will be M-F 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM.
Buffer time between calls
0 minutes
To provide optimal availability, we do not place a buffer between calls.
Maximum Number of Bookings per Day
4
To provide optimal availability while still protecting time, we allow up to 4 scheduled calls daily.
Minimum time before a schedule starts that attendees can book
2 hours
To provide timely access to support, users must be allowed to book 2 or more hours in advance. 
Maximum advance time for attendees to book
7 days
To keep incidents moving, users may book no more than 7 days in advance.
INCIDENT FLAG MEANINGS
(return to index)
Incident Flags are visual indicators within Salesforce that signify recent activity or pending requirements on a specific record. These flags serve as real-time notifications to help Specialists prioritize their workflow, track communications with support or users, and manage time-sensitive tasks.
Note: Flags are "active" markers. They often require a specific action (such as completing a task or reviewing a status) to be cleared from the view, ensuring no communication or deadline is overlooked.
Alarm clock = A task is due (need to mark the task as done to remove the flag).
[Image: rtaImage]
Phone = a call was attached to the incident.
[Image: rtaImage]
Briefcase = a case was attached to the incident.
[Image: rtaImage]
Envelope = a new email was received.
[Image: rtaImage]
Text bubble = a note was left on the incident.
[Image: rtaImage]
Sign post = The Thumbtack Solution Center status is “Under Review” (need to decide the next steps for the TSC).
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
INCIDENT BANNER REASONS
(return to index)
Thumbtack on Demand (Ttod).

[Image: rtaImage]

Managed Accounts

[Image: rtaImage]

INCIDENT EMAIL AUTOMATION
(return to index)
Identify whether the incident has been processed through email automation.
Customer automation
If the incident was previously owned by the T&S Automation queue, customer automation occurred before the incident appeared in the General UA queue.
Depending on the incident details outlined here, the corresponding automation flow will begin. If the incident went through the 1, 2, escalate flow, and the customer never responded, the two auto-emails will show in the incident feed.:

[Image: rtaImage]

Pro automation
If the incident was previously owned by the T&S Automation queue, the project category is “Deposit No Show,” and the amount in dispute is $251+, then pro automation should also have occurred.

[Image: rtaImage]

If it’s unclear whether automation occurred, specialists can also check the incident Details tab under “System Information” to view the last T&S Automation email sent.

[Image: rtaImage]

INCIDENT CLOSURE DEFINITIONS
(return to index)
A “response” is an email reply, phone call, or any direct communication with Trust and Safety.
Use the chart below to decide on which picklist answer should be chosen for each field:


FIELD NAME
PICKLIST ANSWER
USER ANSWER
Communication - pro, 
Communication - customer
Unresponsive - became unresponsive mid-dispute

The user replied to Trust and Safety but stopped responding (emails/calls) before the incident was closed.
Communication - pro, 
Communication - customer
Unresponsive - never responded to Trust and Safety

The user never replied to Trust and Safety when a response was expected.
Communication - pro, 
Communication - customer
Responsive 

The user continued replying via email, phone, or any direct communication to Trust and Safety until the incident was closed.
Communication - pro, 
Communication - customer
No response required
Trust and Safety contacted the user but didn’t expect a response (e.g., GSR, notifying a Pro of expedited payout).
Communication - pro, 
Communication - customer
Never contacted user
Trust and Safety never contacted the user.
Result - pro
Resolved customer concern
The pro resolved the concern.
Result - pro
Offered to resolve
The pro was willing to put in a good-faith effort and reasonable resolution, and the customer did not accept the offer, or the offer is pending. 
Result - pro
Did not resolve
The pro was unwilling to put in a good-faith effort or offer a reasonable resolution when the specialist identified a deviation or fault by the pro. 
Result - pro
Not requiring to resolve
The specialist did not identify a deviation or fault of the pro. Trust and Safety will not require the pro to resolve the concern.
Result - pro
PNP - Accepted customer resolution
The customer was asked to resolve the pro’s concern, pro agreed to the customer’s solution.
Result - pro
PNP - Did not accept customer resolution
The customer put in a good-faith effort, and a reasonable resolution was offered, which was declined by the pro. 
Result - pro
PNP - Customer did not resolve
The customer declined/failed to make a good-faith effort toward a reasonable resolution of the payment concern, despite the pro being willing to make one.
Result - pro
PNP - Did not want to use TT process
Pro didn’t want TT to hold the customer responsible for resolving the concern (i.e., didn’t want us to reach out, didn’t want to use the tools offered, etc.).
Result - pro
PNP - Not requiring customer to resolve
Specialists decided not to require the customer to resolve (i.e., specialists didn’t reach out, or documentation absolved them).
Result - pro


Result - pro
N/A
Use ONLY when the only reported issue is a safety concern.
Result - Customer
Accepted pro resolution
The Pro was asked to resolve the customer’s concern, and the customer agreed to the pro’s offered solution.
Result - Customer
Did not accept pro resolution
The Pro provided a good-faith effort and a reasonable resolution to resolve the customer’s concern, but the customer didn’t agree to the reasonable resolution.
Result - Customer
Pro did not resolve
Pro declined to act in a good-faith effort to provide a reasonable resolution to resolve the customer’s concern.
Result - Customer
Did not want to use TT process
The customer didn’t want Thumbtack to hold the pro responsible for resolving the concern (i.e., didn’t want the specialist to reach out, didn’t want to use the tools we offered, etc.).
Result - Customer
Not requiring pro to resolve
The specialist decided not to require the pro to resolve (i.e., we didn’t reach out or documentation absolved them).
Result - Customer
PNP - Resolved pro concern
The customer resolved the payment concern. 
Result - Customer
PNP - Offered to resolve
The customer provided a good-faith effort and reasonable resolution, but the pro or a circumstance prevented them from resolving.
Result - Customer
PNP - Did not resolve
The customer declined to act with good-faith effort and did not provide a reasonable resolution 
Result - Customer
PNP - Not requiring to resolve
The specialist decided not to require the customer to resolve the payment concern 
Result - Customer


Result - Customer
N/A
Use ONLY when the only reported issue is a safety concern.
Amount in dispute - Pro
[insert dollar amount]
This applies only when the pro states that the customer still owes them payment. Write the amount the pro said the customer owes. 
Amount in dispute - Customer
[insert dollar amount]
Required for all project issues.
If the customer has asked for a refund, fill this field with the most recent dollar amount they requested or agreed to accept from the pro. If no dollar amount has been mentioned, write $0.
If they didn’t provide a specific number, you can determine the dollar amount via the information they provided (i.e., if they stated only 20% of the work has been done, but they paid the full $1,000, we can assume that $800 is in dispute). Feel free to add an estimate in this field.
Project status
Fully resolved
.Cx received the amount in dispute, and/or the Pro fully completed the scope of the project.
Project status
Partially resolved
Part of the customer's requested resolution has been met, but pending actions are still required from the Pro or the customer to fully complete the resolution.
Project status
Not resolved
No part of the user’s concern has been resolved, and no agreement has been made to resolve it.
Project status
Withdrawn
The user(s) withdrew before we could assist them in resolving their concern. (User does not want to use TT process, or just wants to make Thumbtack aware of a concern) 
Project status
Unknown
Use this in rare situations where both parties have not responded and the details of the concern are unclear. This can apply when we cannot determine the customer's specific concerns, and they have gone unresponsive.
Project status

NOTE: For incidents marked as a Safety Concern only this field is not required and can remain blank.

Resolution type
Refund
Pro refunded customer.
Resolution type
Fix/complete work
Pro-fixed or completed their work.
Resolution type
Customer paid outstanding balance
The customer paid pro the amount they owed.
Resolution type
TT compensation
Thumbtack provided any compensation (Guarantee, customer satisfaction, etc.).
Resolution type
Other
The resolution isn’t listed here (i.e., pro-provided receipt). Write a note explaining what the resolution was.
Amount resolved by pro
[insert dollar amount]
If the pro provided a refund, type the amount refunded here.
Initiator picklist
Customer
The customer notified the specialist of the concern, including Concerning Reviews.
Initiator picklist
Pro
The pro notified us of the concern, including IPSR and IPR.
Initiator picklist
Both
The customer and pro each reported the concern before we reached out to the other party (Tack isn't able to figure this one out, so if you have this situation, update your incident).
Initiator picklist
Offsite Party
The reporter didn’t connect with the reported party through TT - including External Reports.
Initiator picklist
TT Agent
A Thumbtack agent proactively reported something, and neither party asked for our help. (T&S comes across concern while working) 
STOP A USER FROM BEING SURVEYED
(return to index)
In the rare case that a survey should not be sent after closing an incident:
Check the Do not survey - Pro or Do not survey - Customer box, depending on which user the action applies to.
Note the reason for preventing a survey.
[Image: rtaImage]
   Troubleshooting
    (return to index)
USER REPORTS NEW CONCERN
(return to index)
Occasionally, while working on an incident, a user may report a new concern with a different user. Specialists should direct the user to report the concern through the Help Center form or follow the directions below, depending on the customer's preferences.  
Select the Quick Case option on the bar at the bottom of the screen.
[Image: rtaImage]
In the new window, fill out the Full Name and Email Address with the reporting party’s information.
The Subject field should be a brief description of the issue.
e.g., “Deposit no-show report.”  
The Case Origin field should remain “Email.”
Follow the steps provided here to transfer to T&S. (The Categorization team will review and triage the issue to the correct place.)
Note: If the specialist decides to work the new incident themselves (e.g., the user is escalated, the issue is related/for the same project, or it would be a poor experience to wait in the queue), follow the same steps to create a new incident as when the wrong user is reported.
WRONG USER REPORTED
(return to index)
There may be times when a user mistakenly reports the wrong account/CAT attaches the incorrect user. While it's best that concerns are reported through the usual avenues for tracking purposes, the specialist can step in when already in communication with them.
Select the Quick Case option on the bar at the bottom of the screen.
[Image: rtaImage]
In the new window, fill out the Full Name, Email Address, and Subject fields with the reporting party’s information.
The Case Origin field should remain “Email.” 
Back in the original incident, click the reporting parties tab and select their PKID. This will lead to the user’s admin.
Select the Customer Contact or Project drop-down (depending on whether it’s a customer or pro reporting), and find and copy the PKID for the correct request.
In the new case, select the Quick Incident tab.
Paste the correct bid PKID in to the designated area, and click Continue.
[Image: rtaImage]
If  prompted to enter the customer’s and pro’s PKIDs and names, then the PKID originally entered is likely incorrect:
Click Back, then double-check whether the Bid PKID matches the number in Admin on the quote with both users.
If it isn’t, correct it and click Continue again.
If it is, fill in the requested details and click Continue.
Note: If there’s an existing incident with this bid PKID, the specialist will need to remove the new case from the old incident. Follow these steps to do so. 
Choose Primary Case Owner:
This will be the reporting party, so double-check the names under Customer MTS Persona and Pro MTS Persona.
Setting this incorrectly causes problems in the incident.
Fill out the Incident Details section. Make sure to include the originally reported notes from the original incident and describe why a new incident was made (wrong cx, wrong pro, etc.) 
Check the User Flags for the managed account or Spanish language flags to determine a queue for the Owner. Otherwise, assign it to yourself.
Click Submit.
Make a note of the original incident and why a new one was created. 
Note: Make sure to record both incident numbers in each incident to ensure no part of the report is lost.

NO INFORMATION ON NEW INCIDENT
(return to index)
Typically, if there’s no information on a new incident, clicking Sync Incident should resolve it. If it doesn’t, it might mean the Categorization team missed a step. Follow these steps to attempt to find the missing info:
If there’s a post on the incident feed that says, “This case has been created via an automated process,” click the post to expand the section.
Often, this will have all of the information needed to move forward.
If there’s nothing there, click Details at the top of the incident.
Use page search (command+f on Mac, control+f on PC) to look for Dispute Request.
Click the link under Dispute Request.
Read the information under Form Questions & Answers and post relevant info on the incident.
If there’s no post about an automated process, open the customer and/or pro’s primary case.
Look for a case with the Case Origin “dispute form.”
In this case, click Details.
Find the Description section, then copy the information saved there and paste it into the incident.
UNABLE TO SEND EMAILS
(return to index)
If the specialist is unable to send emails to one or both of their users:
Double-check that there’s a case for each user.
If there’s not, follow the steps below to create a case for each missing user.
If there are cases for each user, but the incident doesn’t have two primary cases ((c) for customer and (p) for pro), follow the steps below to mark the cases as “primary.”
To create a case:
If one or both cases are missing from the incident:
Create a quick case, either at the bottom of Salesforce or the top of the incident.
In the quick case, click the Find User tab, then search for a user and attach their contact to the case.
Follow the steps below to mark the case as a primary case.
To mark cases as “primary”:
Open each case, then navigate to the Details tab
Under Marketplace Integrity Info, find “MI Case Primary - Pro” and “MI Case Primary - Customer” and check the correct box.
Check “MI Case Primary - Pro” in the pro’s case and “MI Case Primary - Customer” in the customer’s case.
Click Save.
Note: if the Categorization team makes a mistake when creating the incident, it’s possible to switch the name on the original case (i.e., the customer reported via that case, but now it has the pro’s name attached). Switch the original case back to its original owner by using Find User, then follow the steps above to change the primary case designations.
UNABLE TO OPEN FILE, OR FILE ISN’T IN THE FILE MANAGER
(return to index)
Unable to open file
Ask the user to resend it in another format.
Send it as a .jpeg or .pdf.
OR save the image to your computer and re-upload it to the incident.
NOTE: ALL downloaded files from an incident should be immediately deleted and cleared from the specialist's trash bin.
File not in file manager
Download it and then upload it to the incident.
I.e., if it’s in a shared drive or email instead of in the file manager.
If the specialist doesn’t know the location of the file, it’s likely that it was attached to the user’s primary case instead.
Open the user’s primary case.
Navigate to the Related tab in the case.
The specialist may have to click More to find this.
Scroll to the Google Docs & attachments section.
Download any images listed as missing from the incident and then upload the file to the incident.
CAN’T CLOSE INCIDENT
(return to index)
Typically, if an incident won’t close, it’s because a field on the incident hasn’t been completed correctly. To fix this, first, save what has already been filled out:
Click Close Incident, if it’s not already (this saves what has been written).
Click Cancel or exit by clicking the x in the top right corner of the closure prompt.
Without exiting your current incident tab, update the section that needs updating, then return to the closure prompt.
Don’t exit the Incident tab, or all the info previously entered in the closure prompt will be erased.
Fields that commonly cause this error include:
Solution Center
The dispute must be closed.
Payout request
The payout status can’t be “open” or “Payment sent.”
Guarantee
The Guarantee Eligibility Review must be submitted.
In-product refund request
[Image: rtaImage]
Open the user’s case (usually the pro’s).
Under “Work Ticket Details,” click the link under Refund Request Link.
Update the picklist under “Refund Decision.”
See Credits, Returns, and Grants and choose Refundable Reasons to determine if a refund applies.
Add a brief, factual note in “Admin Note.”
If it’s a sensitive situation or we shouldn’t notify the user of the refund, select Skip Notification (MTS only).
Click Submit.
Attempt to close the incident again.

PRODUCT FEEDBACK
(return to index)
We value feedback from users. Sometimes they share product feedback in the course of an incident, or while troubleshooting an issue or resolving a case. We want to be diligent about capturing this feedback to enable product development.
When a user shares feedback, please use the Product Feedback Report feature, which is accessible directly in the Salesforce case. For full details on how to fill out the feedback form, please refer to the internal support KA, Product Feedback (Rep).
NOTE: If closing the work ticket doesn’t resolve the issue, submit a bug report. 

**Use the content request form to request an update or submit questions/concerns**

Navigate a Work Ticket

Navigate a work ticket
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Opening the Work Ticket
Work Ticket Overview
Work Ticket Workflow
Details
Work Ticket Fields
Outcome section fields

Admin Actions Quickview
What
(return to index)
Work Tickets (WTs) are Salesforce records generated from various process flows that require review for triage, action, or escalation to the appropriate team.
Why
(return to index)
WTs are essential for managing and resolving issues that arise from various processes. They ensure issues are promptly investigated, actioned and directed to the appropriate team when needed. 
When
(return to index)
When the system identifies activities marked for review, it generates WTs based on various events and signals.
For some specialists, WTs are automatically assigned when they’re logged into Omni. This will depend on their assigned routing skills.

How
(return to index)
 
 Steps
      (return to index)

OPENING THE WORK TICKET
(return to index)
There are two ways to get a WT:
Log in to Omni Channel - TS ALL WORK. You will automatically receive a new work item based on your assigned routing skills.
You will be assigned a ticket (this will be visible in your “My Assigned Work Tickets” view).
WORK TICKET OVERVIEW
(return to index)

[Image: AD_4nXddcxgUS6fuL2ZLNcMTJ5RPTg8k-MsjSLCm0i5PQb0smy-aFZiiARa_GM0qjaSXQ7OTPCqWSQqUiVoKbxtCTTbNUE_-rrXpHE8mEGoOOytsQQTmWK4t5IAIDF6wV4BLO_Ql8U44H0N3zVNHGoOY5U_mpBY]

The Details/Info section contains useful information and quick links essential for reviewing and evaluating the task.
The Outcome section identifies the ticket’s queue or routing skill and summarizes the ticket's resulting actions and status.
The Admin Actions section is used to document any actions that were taken on a user’s account. 
In some queues, there is no Admin Actions section. Instead, there is an Account Actions field under the Outcome section.
WORK TICKET WORKFLOW
(return to index)
Investigate the Details section of the WT.
Click on the links provided in this section to take a deeper dive.
If necessary, take the appropriate Admin actions and check for managed accounts if applicable.
Once you’ve made your final determination on the WT, edit all applicable Outcome section fields in Tack.*
Outcome
Outcome Detail
Issue Type
ToS Violation/s
NOTE:  Multiple ToS violations can be selected
Account Action
If available, edit the Admin Action section in Tack based on the account actions completed in Admin.*
Click Save.
*Refer to your specific procedure to determine which selections you should make within each field.
   Details
       (return to index)
WORK TICKET FIELDS
(return to index)

[Image: AD_4nXcgipp-5ieIGHoUtJklIgW0JBmAsIBmulNEg5NlGlU1hcxkFxHlwm2yLtQT83VWiKRFPixPtRRsRlrg8Dj_67klAUu7tvMgt2QwnybPUZbjOAaw_nvE1u36QlMY2x-khrcYqMX8HawzqfJrSzoPkXy26IM]

Outcome section fields:
(return to index)
The following Outcome section fields are determined by the investigation and the procedures specific to their queue. The correct selections will differ depending on the specific procedure.
NOTE: Certain procedures may have additional queue-specific WT requirements that are not covered in this article.
Outcome: This is a drop-down field used to report the result of a work ticket. Depending on the queue, it may reflect the accuracy of the work ticket (“Accurate,” “Inaccurate,” etc.) or whether the ticket confirms a T&S issue (“Confirmed Violation,” “No Violation Found,” etc.).
Outcome Detail: This field provides a list of predefined options to capture specific actions, results, or classifications related to the outcome. This field includes actions taken (e.g., "Email Customer," "Escalated Case"), assessments (e.g., "Spammy," "Responsive"), severity levels (e.g., "Level 1, 2, 3, 4").
Internal Notes: This field is available to add additional notes related to the investigation or decision for documentation or future review. 
Issue Type: This field is used to triage queues and identify the subtype for T&S or Service. Examples include "Pro Not Paid," "Copyright or Intellectual Property," and "Harassment or Threats."
TOS Violations: This section provides a picklist of specific ToS violations. If there is a confirmed ToS violation, select all violations that apply.
Signals: This section provides a picklist of account signals to help confirm a violation (currently not in use)
Account Actions: This field is used to note what account actions have been taken in Admin (e.g., Deleted and Blocklisted, Ghosted, Hold, etc.).
NOTE: In some queues instead of an Account Action field under the Outcome section, there is a separate Admin Actions section. 
The following fields are auto-populated; specialists do not need to take action:

articles.fullText:
Managed accounts (incidents)

Managed accounts (incidents)
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Identify an enterprise pro
Incident overview
Final warning for a managed account
Professional Performance Plans
Verification steps
Business Verification
License Verification
Standard WT process
Authorized license use
Enterprise licensing
Linked Accounts
Details
Corporate Entities
Banned users
Resources
Emails
What
(return to index)
The Enterprise program caters to high-revenue pros by providing an "above and beyond" experience. These pros are invited to join the program based on the National team’s qualifications for business success, revenue, and locations. They’ll be assigned an account manager on the National team, who oversees their account and makes sure the pro continues to be successful. 
When enterprise pros have a Trust and Safety issue, our Managed Accounts (MA) team partners closely with them and their account managers (AM) to maintain an elevated experience.
Why
(return to index)
Thumbtack values all pros and seeks to help them be successful using the platform. We offer elevated care to maintain a successful partnership with pros who fit under the enterprise pro criteria.
When
(return to index)
Incidents involving an enterprise pro are sent to the managed accounts queue and are worked on by the MA team. 
When other T&S issues come up, this group helps assist and address critical concerns, stepping outside usual processes. This includes:
Licensing
Business verification (BV)
Account statuses
Linked accounts  
How
(return to index)   
  Steps
   (return to index) 
IDENTIFY AN ENTERPRISE PRO
(return to index)  
Within Tack, you’ll be able to identify an enterprise pro by looking for the managed account tag.
Incident view:

[Image: Screenshot 2022-12-07 at 9.11.22 AM.png]
WT/Case view:

[Image: Screenshot 2022-12-07 at 9.11.38 AM.png]
Note: To confirm that these tags are calculated correctly, you can also reference the Current List of Account Managers.
INCIDENT OVERVIEW
(return to index) 
If an incident involving an enterprise pro was not sent to the correct queue, reassign the incident to “MTS Managed Accounts” and leave a note.
Assign the incident to yourself.
Check the T&S MA Accounts sheet to ensure the business is not already assigned to a specific specialist. 
Review past incidents, existing flags, and alternate contact information.
Begin the usual steps to start an incident.
If the pro has been unresponsive to the initial two contacts:
Notify AM in the #national_accounts_team Slack channel (Grammarly: MA: Notify AM of action).
If the assigned AM is out of the office, please also tag the manager of the Nationals Team, Yael Emmerich.
Send a third follow-up email to pro (Macro: MA: Pro unresponsive - no answer). 
If the pro is still unresponsive to T&S and their AM after two additional business days:
Cold call pro.
If unable to get a hold of them, place the pro's account on hold.
Note: If this action is taking place on a Friday or before office closure/time off, consider the following:
Can this action wait till Monday or the return of the specialist? (i.e., is it risky for Thumbtack's brand to keep the account open over the weekend?)
If it can wait, send a follow-up email on Friday and action on the next day back in the office if the pro doesn’t respond.
If it can’t wait, Slack the pro’s account executive (and manager, Yael Emerich, if the AM is out of office) and let them know you need to take action on the account. 
Ask them to contact the pro to gather any needed information. (i.e., I am off at 4:30 MST, so I need this info by 4.)
Send an email to pro letting them know action has been taken on their account, and they’ll need to address concerns before we will reconsider.
FINAL WARNING FOR A MANAGED ACCOUNT
(return to index)
If we coach an enterprise pro but continue to receive similar complaints, we should consider a final warning.
Notify the pro's AM.
Tell them about the concerns and our decision.
Work together to set up a conference call with the pro.
Utilize phone calls or Zoom.
Discuss Thumbtack’s expectations and be clear about the penalties.
Consider implementing a Professional Performance Plan.
Send a follow-up email to the pro summarizing what was discussed and agreed upon.
Note: Concerns about chargebacks, past due balances, etc., can lead to a final warning without consulting the pro's AM. Consult the T&S payments team when these come up.
PROFESSIONAL PERFORMANCE PLANS (PPP)
(return to index) 
A PPP is a written, detailed, and time-sensitive action plan designed to encourage better performance. We may decide to implement a PPP:
As a final warning for repeated coaching with no improvement.
Pro consistently not responding to T&S, has a lot of concerning reviews regarding deposit no-shows and isn’t following up on the reviews.
When we are reactivating a disabled pro, but want to monitor their behavior.
Pro was removed due to refusing to take ownership of property damage, but is reaching out again, wanting to resolve the issue.

Note: Keep in mind we should be basing consideration on the percentage of revenue affected, not only the incident count. Consult with a manager if you notice trends that might warrant a PPP.
Once we’ve determined a PPP is necessary, follow the steps below: 
Fill out the ”Account Overview” and “Areas of Concern” sections of the MA Review Template. 
Present the concerns to the MA manager and discuss why you feel a PPP is appropriate.
With help from the MA manager, fill out the remainder of the MA Review Template.
Add to MA Review Tracker.
Notify pro’s AM.
Schedule a conference call with the enterprise pro, their AM, and yourself to put the PPP into action. 
Outline the specific action items needed to continue a successful partnership on Thumbtack.
Make adjustments to the MA review template during your call if needed.

If the pro is unable to fulfill the PPP in their timeframe, the pro will be removed, and their account will not be reconsidered (typically 30-90 days, but based on T&S and AM recommendation).
   Verification Steps
   (return to index)
BUSINESS VERIFICATION
(return to index)
The business verification batch usually runs on Fridays. If you need an update for an AM outside of that time frame, check the #bv-pilot2 Slack channel or the most recent week’s tab on this sheet.
If you have questions regarding the status of one of the businesses listed in the sheet, reach out to the person regularly completing the batches in #bv-pilot2.
Enterprise business verification

If an enterprise pro wants to go through business verification, we can assist them directly instead of going through the usual process.
Gather the business name and full address for any one of their franchise locations within the US.
Reach out to the person regularly completing the batches in #bv-pilot2 so they can pull the pro’s LXNX business report.
We use LXNX to gather information needed to meet the BV badge requirements.
Years in business
Legal entity type
Bankruptcies
Judgments and liens
Seleid/LXNX ID
Once you receive the Seleid/LXNX ID, add that information to the National Accounts BV and Adjustments sheet.
For new businesses, create a new tab.
For existing business tabs, add the new location.
Add the business verification badge:
Open Admin for the user.
Click on the Service name.
Click Business Verification in the Page Actions.[Image: Screenshot 2022-12-07 at 11.11.26 AM.png]
Scroll to the Verification section.
Use the dropdown to change the Verification Decision to “Verified.”
Copy and paste the LXNX Business ID number to the “LexisNexis Business ID” field.
Change the Last Verified Date to today’s date.
Click Submit.[Image: Screenshot 2022-12-07 at 11.18.00 AM.png]
Update business name on verified account

For managed accounts, we can skip the ID Help process to help these pros add or remove cities from their business name faster. You’ll need to remove the existing business verification badge and verified license, edit their business name, and then re-add the verifications.
Verify the pro is on the National Accounts BV and Adjustments sheet.
Make sure you have the Seleid/LXNX ID number before moving forward. 
Check for any verified licenses on their account.
If there’s no verified license, move to the next step.
If they do have a verified license:
Delete the license from the Admin.
Let the AM know the pro will need to resubmit their license unless it’s an enterprise license. Then you’ll add it back for them.​​​​​​[Image: Screenshot 2022-12-07 at 12.02.14 PM.png]
Check Business Verification status.
Open the pro’s service profile in Admin.[Image: Screenshot 2022-12-07 at 12.04.12 PM.png]
If it says “Not Verified,” the pro or their AM can update the account name.
If it says “Verified,” remove the business verification badge.
Click on Business Verification in Page Actions.
Scroll to the bottom and click Submit without changing anything to remove the business verification badge.
Edit their business name:
Log in as the user.
Click on Profile.
Find the business that needs to be changed and click Edit to update the name as requested.[Image: Screenshot 2022-12-07 at 12.14.26 PM.png]
Click Last admin to log out as the user.
Add the business verification badge back.
If you removed an enterprise license, add it back.
LICENSE VERIFICATION
(return to index)
Account managers may reach out for assistance when a pro’s license shows as “not verified.” There are 3 different ways a managed account can receive a verified license:
Standard WT Process
A license is submitted through the pro’s service profile, and a work ticket (WT) is created for our team to verify manually. 
This will only be successful if the pro’s account and business name match the name on the license, and it’s a license type we verify.
Authorized License User
The Pro fills out the ID help form with the pro’s information.
If they are an enterprise pro, the AM will fill this out on their behalf.
This is done when the pro’s account or business name is different from the names on the license, but the license holder allows them to use their license.
Enterprise Licensing
The pro completes the contract validation process by signing a contract with Thumbtack, agreeing that all of their services/locations have proper licensing.
Pro must be a “national account”: They have 5 locations or multi-state (crosses state lines) and/or is a franchise.
Standard WT Process
((return to index)
If the enterprise pro uploads their license through their profile, the WT that gets generated will be transferred to “Unassigned - Man. Acct. /License Verification” to be worked by MA incident specialists. For each WT, be sure to reach out to the pro’s AM if it appears they qualify for the enterprise license process.

Go to the queue and sort by the oldest work tickets first.
Assign work tickets to yourself:
Click on the work ticket.
Next to “Owner”, it should say “Work Ticket.”
Click on the person icon to change it.
[Image: Screenshot 2022-12-07 at 2.14.58 PM.png]
In the pop-up, search for your name, then click Change Owner.
Follow the license verification general process starting at step 4.

Unlike the usual process, if you run into any issues where a WT needs to be escalated, you won’t use the manager's queue. Instead, tag @proactive in #global_trust_and_safety_ops for assistance.	
Note: This queue will also house the WTs for the licenses uploaded on the pro’s behalf through the enterprise licensing process.
Authorized License User
(return to index)
If the names on their Thumbtack account don’t match the names on the license, the pro needs to reach out through ID Help to start the usual authorized license user process.
If a pro qualifies for the Enterprise license process but doesn’t want to include licensing verbiage in their contract with Thumbtack, they can move forward with this process as well. AM's will submit the ID Help request on the pro’s behalf then reach out in #National_Account_Priority_Verification so our team can help complete the process.
Take ownership of the ID Help case. 
These cases will show “[Pro’s Name] (National Account - Standard)” in the name field.
Follow the standard authorized license user process to verify the license.
The AM should have already collected this information, so request the following from them:
License State
License Type
License Number
Written confirmation from the license holder of who is authorized to work under their license.
Link to signed Ironclad doc.
Once the license is verified, notify the AM.
Enterprise Licensing
(return to index)
If an enterprise pro meets the National team's requirements, they’ll help the pro move forward with the contract validation process. The National team will have the pro sign a contract agreeing that all of their services/locations have the necessary licenses. Once they’ve completed this step, they’ll reach out in #National_Account_Priority_Verification to share the completed Ironclad agreement and move forward.
Open “License Verification for Enterprise Pros (National Accounts)” and scroll to the bottom for any columns that are blank under “License Verified?“Confirm in Ironclad (IC) that the correct form was signed.
Log in to Ironclad using Okta.
Click on the Repository tab. 
Search the business name or the user’s name if it’s under a parent account.
If it’s not listed, you may need to reach out to the AM.
Under the Record Name field, click on the Managed Account License Verification under the correct counterparty name.
Click on the PDF icon in the panel.
Verify it’s titled “Managed Account License Verification Agreement” and the signature matches the owner's name.[Image: Screenshot 2022-12-08 at 12.31.08 PM.png]
Submit the enterprise license.
In “License Verification for Enterprise Pros (National Accounts),” click the link under Admin link-Parent.
Log in as the user.
Click on Profile.
Scroll down to the “credentials” section and click add a license or edit.
Location: “District of Columbia”
License Type: “Multi-State National Account - Ask Pro about exact licensing”.
License #: “00000"
Click Submit.
From the bottom black bar, click Admin and then Last admin to log out.
From their admin account, scroll to licenses and click Full License Check on the license you just created.
Under “Do all license information match?” click on Yes.
Select the issue date as today’s current date and leave the expiration date blank.
Click Verify License Information is Valid.
A screen will appear that you are not authorized to view the page - it should still go through.
Go back to the user's admin and refresh to confirm the license status is “Verified.”
Complete the license verification work ticket (WT).
Go to the “Unassigned - Man. Acct. /License Verification” WT queue.
Click into the WT that matches the “Full user license” number from the license and change the owner to yourself.
Change the Outcome to “Approved.”
Make sure the status in the center of the page changes from "New" to “Completed.”
Click Save.
Notify AM.
Go back to “License Verification for Enterprise Pros (National Accounts).”
Change the “Licensed Verified?” column to “Yes.”
Reply in the #national_account_priority_verification channel or tag them on the sheet directly.
LINKED ACCOUNTS
(return to index)
The blocklist hits process will create work tickets when information on an active account matches information on a blocklisted account. Since enterprise pros typically share links such as phone number, business name, etc., these will be flagged for review as well. 
However, managed accounts typically are not trying to circumvent our system and can be handled differently. To help with this, blocklist hits WTs for enterprise pros will be sent to its own queue for review.
Select “Work Tickets” from the dropdown, then go to “A06: Unassigned - Man. Acct. /Blocklist Hits” and sort by oldest work tickets first.
Assign the work ticket to yourself.
Click on the work ticket.
Next to Owner, it should say “Work Ticket.”
Click on the person icon to change the owner.[Image: Screenshot 2022-12-07 at 3.52.12 PM.png]
In the pop-up, search for your name, then click Change Owner.
Verify that the Thumbtack User (flagged account) is an Enterprise Pro.
If it’s not, change the routing skill on the WT to “Blocklist Hits” to be worked through the usual team.
Verify that the blocklisted account is a managed account.
If it’s NOT an enterprise pro, keep the account blocklisted.
If this happens, investigate the link to see if it’s valid (following the normal Blocklist Hits process KA).
If you’re unsure/need help, then post in #ts-incident-ops-questions and tag @proactive, making sure to mention that it’s a managed account linked to a non-managed account.
If the blocklisted account is an Enterprise Pro, remove the account from the blocklist.
Keep the account on hold and/or deleted.
If they have a past due balance account hold for $100 or less, credit the account for the past due amount to remove the account hold.
Do not action the flagged account.
If the accounts are true duplicates or test accounts, determine which one may need to be reactivated/refunded.
Fill out the work ticket accordingly in Tack:
Outcome in Tack: Inaccurate.
Brief Description: The accounts are managed accounts.
Note: Follow the same account action steps for situations where an AM reaches out, but a WT was not created.

Linked account disputes
(return to index)
If a user is disputing a link to a non-enterprise pro, follow the usual linked account dispute process to investigate further. If it seems likely that they’re no longer associated:
Communicate the following to the AM before creating the corporate entity account:
Create a Quick Case.
Attach necessary documentation to confirm they’re no longer associated.
Documentation confirming separation from the company. 
Proof that the user no longer works at the company.
Etc. 
Transfer the case to the “Proactive MI Queue.”
Notify @proactive in #global_trust_and_safety_ops.
    Details
   (return to index)

CORPORATE ENTITIES
(return to index)
When an AM creates a new account for a franchise that won’t have an individual account owner, they’re allowed to use the business name of the franchise for the account owner as long as the National team gathers the proper signed documentation. This is known as a corporate entity.
Communicate the following to the AM before creating the corporate entity account:
The pro won’t be eligible for a BGC immediately, which will exclude them from pro loyalty and ToD.
T&S needs a point of contact who may represent the entire brand should a dispute arise - add to POC for Corporate Entity Accounts.
Business verification and license verification are separate processes.

Once the National team creates the account, following their steps in Corporate Account Creation, they’ll reach out to the MA team to share the admin link, date of incorporation, business address, point of contact, and business phone number. After you have this info, confirm the agreement has been signed and follow these steps to remove the account hold in Admin:
Add the point of contact/business information to POC for Corporate Entity Accounts if not already.
Open their account in Admin.
Edit Identity Information.
Make sure the name is correct.
Date of Birth: 01/01/2000
Enter the street address (no state needed).
Enter the Zip Code.
Click Update on Identity Status.
Select “Identity Verified” in the dropdown.
Notes: “National Account Corporate Entity, ID Ok’d.”
Click Submit.
Scroll to the bottom of the user’s admin and make sure the Minimum Requirements (EMR) shows “true.”
If it shows “false,” click Waive.

BANNED USERS
(return to index)
What if a managed account franchise owner does something really bad, and we legitimately don’t want them on Thumbtack?
We expect this to be an extremely rare circumstance. Typically, the corporation will remove the franchise owner or offending employee from the business and then take over their account until they can hire someone else. We’ll still allow that franchise on Thumbtack as long as the franchise owner or offending employee is no longer associated with the account. 
If the removed user sets up their own business account on Thumbtack, reach out to @proactive to set up monitoring. 
RESOURCES
(return to index)
MTS/Sale Quick Reference Guide  - Information for the National Team to answer many of their questions related to Trust and Safety.

   Emails
       (return to index)
MA: Pro unresponsive - no answer: Used on the 3rd contact attempt with an MA to provide a 2-day deadline before taking account action. 

Grammarly Snippets

MA Notify AM of action-slack: Used to tag Pro’s account manager for managed accounts before taking actions on their account. 

MA Notify AM of dispute-slack: Used to tag Pro’s account manager to inform them of a new incident.

MA Book of business-slack: Used to tag Pro’s success manager to inform them of a new incident.

Local resources guide
(Knowledge index)
INDEX

What
(return to index)
When we've exhausted the options we have to help our customers resolve their concerns, we can give customers some direction about their local resources – to help them get a resolution through other means.
This is not Thumbtack "stepping back," but rather helping the customer "step forward."
Why
(return to index)
We’re not always able to resolve customers’ concerns with the resources available to us. Helping the user find their local resources can help them continue to pursue a resolution.
When
(return to index)
Introduce the idea early. No specifics are needed.
Talk to the customer about their local resources at the beginning of the incident. Don't go into a ton of detail so the customer doesn't immediately feel like we're trying not to help. But explain that we'll do everything we can to help them work together, however, customers also have multiple options at their disposal.
Once the Trust and Safety team has exhausted options, share specific and relevant info.
If Thumbtack’s processes don't help the customer, we can be more specific by sharing links and information about their next options – to empower them to take their next steps.
How
(return to index)
   Steps
   (return to index)
Keep the incident progressing towards a positive outcome, and be creative in seeking solutions. Some examples of things you can look into before it’s absolutely clear that Thumbtack cannot provide further assistance:
Consider eligibility for New Era ADR if the customer AND pro have been responsive and seem willing to work together, but the Solution Center or direct communication was unsuccessful.
Delete/blocklist pro account - this is not always a ‘final’ action, but can instead be used as leverage to motivate a pro to be more responsive and make progress towards resolution
Evaluate whether the Thumbtack Guarantee applies.
Evaluate whether a Customer satisfaction payout is appropriate.

If we’ve truly exhausted our resources, use the information below to find what might apply to your user’s situation and provide this information to the user.

   Details
   (return to index)
CONTRACTOR'S LICENSE
(return to index)
A contractor’s license is a credential given to contractors who've proven they've received the required training necessary to complete the service they offer. It proves the contractor holds the minimum insurance and/or bonding required by the municipality of their state/city. Often, a license is required for a contractor to be able to pull a permit to begin a project at the local building department.
Most states require that contractors demonstrate proof of insurance as part of obtaining a trade license or registering.
When to send info about contractor licensing
Customer wants to take further action with the pro and is not sure where to start.
Customer wants to attempt to receive reimbursement via the pro’s bond.
Customer wants to file a complaint with the contractor licensing board.
They want to check if there are further complaints/disciplinary actions against the company.
You can provide information about both the business license and contractors licensing if the contractor licensing applies to their project/pro.
Common Terminology and talking points:
Licensed: Contractors have been granted a trade license as mandated by state and local laws. It generally requires passing competency tests about business practices and trade skills, paying a fee, and proving insurance and/or bonding.
Registered: Typically less stringent than licensing, it often requires contractors to prove insurance and pay a fee. Sometimes it requires bonding, but rarely tests competency. A few places use licensing and registration interchangeably.
Bonded: Contractors have an arrangement with a third party (a private bond issuer or a recovery fund held by the licensing municipality). Homeowners may petition for reimbursement through that third party if contractors harm them financially because of shoddy work or failure to pay subcontractors as promised.
Insured: All contractors hired should be insured. Customer should ask for Certificate of Insurance, then call to verify the policy is current and carries enough coverage for any project.
Important: Please research the state to see if they regulate home-repair related trades such as plumbing, HVAC technicians, electricians, general contractors. etc. Some states don’t regulate, additionally, some cities, counties, and other municipalities require their own licenses for trades, but many don’t.

ATTORNEY GENERAL
(return to index)
An Attorney General (AG) is a state-appointed lawyer and law enforcement official that protects and serves the people, and interests of their state. Their responsibilities include safeguarding the public from violent criminals, enforcing civil rights laws, and helping victims of identity theft, mortgage-related fraud, illegal business practices, and other consumer crimes.
Helpful info
If a customer wants to take a pro to court to get a judgment, they should work with their local court.
A customer can report a complaint to the Attorney General, while going to the licensing board, or Department of Transportation  (moving/transportation).
When to send info about contacting the Attorney General
You'll send a user more information about Attorney Generals and how they can help when they:
Want to take further action with the pro, and they're sure where to start.
Mention the pro has more reviews about similar situations with other customers on other platforms- i.e., Yelp, Google, Facebook, etc.
Aren't necessarily seeking monetary compensation but want to prevent this from happening to others.
Don't want to spend the money going through their local courts.
When not to send this info
You won't want to send information about an Attorney General in situations involving:
An overall negative disposition towards Thumbtack
A customer who's taking legal action involving Thumbtack
A customer who's located in California or New York.

U.S. DEPT. OF TRANSPORTATION
(return to index)
The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) is an agency in the Department of Transportation (DOT) that regulates the trucking industry in the United States. They're responsible for coordinating federal transportation projects and setting safety regulations for all major modes of transportation.
The FMSCA and DOT have created a partnership between federal, state, and local officials and the moving industry itself to help protect consumers.
When to provide info about the Department of Transportation

You'll send a user more information about the D.O.T. and how they can help when they:
Have had issues with a mover keeping their belongings, increasing their price, damaging or losing items, not licensed, etc.
Want to take further action with the pro and is not sure where to start.
Mention the pro has more reviews about similar situations with other customers on other platforms- i.e., Yelp, Google, Facebook, etc.
Aren't seeking monetary compensation, but want to help prevent this from happening to others.
Customers may also file a complaint through, and learn more at protectyourmove.gov.
When not to send this info

Don't send this information to any customers who aren't reporting a local or long-distance move – this would be irrelevant to their situation.
Local resources: Business license/registration
Business licenses are permits that allow companies (or individuals) to conduct business within a geographical jurisdiction - it's the authorization to start a business issued by the local government.
There are many licenses, registrations, and certifications required to conduct a business in a single location and vary between countries, states, and local municipalities. Other determining factors may include the number of employees and the form of business ownership, such as sole proprietor or corporation.
Businesses can be fined or closed for operating without the required business licenses.
When to send info about licensing bodies
We can always send the customer more information regarding a business license/and or business entity. However, search for the professional's license beforehand. If you can't find a license, don't provide a link to the licensing board for their state - this isn't a positive experience and highlights the fact that there are unlicensed pros on our site.

Quick talking point reference

See more license talking points on the talking points topic.
Licenses are required for three main purposes:
To identify the business and make sure they are accountable for their actions.
To protect the public health and safety.
To keep track of finances for tax purposes.
If no business license is found, they can file a complaint with the licensing board.
Most licensing sites give consumers tips and recommendations when hiring professionals in their area and what to look for. Along with our safety page. This is a great resource for their protection and next steps.
Licensing websites by state
See state license websites here.
SMALL CLAIMS
(return to index)
Depending on the state, small claims ( AKA county or magistrate) courts primarily resolve disputes typically limited to between $3,000 and $10,000. Common types of cases involve failure to repay a loan, fix an appliance properly, return a security deposit, or meet the terms of a service contract -- for example, properly remodel a kitchen or install a new roof.
When to send info about small claims court

You'll send a user more information about small claims court and how it can help when they:
Want to take further action, but they're not sure where to start.
Want monetary compensation
Need help resolving a contractual disagreement.
Such as incomplete work, unsatisfactory work, damages, product/service not received.

Before sending any info, check if their state clarifies a dollar amount limit and the location of the project. The state the service took place will typically be the state where they'll have to file with small claims.
When not to send this info
You won't want to send information about small claims court in situations involving:
An overall negative disposition towards Thumbtack.
A user taking legal action involving Thumbtack.
A customer who already has filed for small claims.
A dollar amount over the small claims limit in their state/county.
Civil issues such as domestic violence.
Small claims links by state
Not all sites will have specific details for claim amount limits, documents, etc. Some states offer their contact information or provide details on how the process works. Please review the state-specific link for further talking points with the customer. (We cannot give legal advice, but are happy to direct them to their local courts for more information.)

Linked Account checking and universal actioning

Linked account checking and actioning 
(Knowledge index)
INDEX 
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Overview
Details
FAQs
What
(return to index)
Checking linked accounts is important in identifying possible TOS violations. This article tackles when to check linked accounts and how to action an active account if found linked to a banned user. It follows the Universal Linked Account Action Policy and will be used in the queues that are currently doing manual actioning of active linked accounts:
Contact Verification
Customer Message Review
In-Product Reports
Why
(return to index)
To prevent banned users from creating requests by using alternate accounts, specialists should manually check any link between active and banned users by following the steps provided below. Also, to maintain uniformity in linked account actioning across WT queues, the universal linked account action policy was created.
When
(return to index) 
Specialists should check for linked accounts when they encounter any of the scenarios below:
The user/request/message was deemed suspicious. This may include but is not limited to the examples below:
Any fides rules were hit
The requester or account owner may be a minor
Any contact information was provided in the request note/message (note: contact info found should also be used in linked account checking)
The request is classified as a risky category (prone to TOS violations):
Massage Therapy
Private Yoga
Personal Training
House Cleaning
Boudoir Photography
Video Production
How
(return to index)
Specialists should check linked accounts if the user/request/message is classified as suspicious or it is under risky categories. Following the hierarchy below, the specialist needs to establish that the active user is strongly linked to a banned user via either of the following:
Featured Linked Users (Admin) or;
Override Linked Users (Admin) or;
Combined multiple weak links (e.g., same default phone number + other comparable info)
Each step above must be carried out until at least one link with a banned user has been found.

[Image: Screenshot 2024-03-13 at 9.16.18 AM.png]

   Overview 
   (return to index)
STEP-BY-STEP GUIDE
(return to index)
Check first if the user/request/message is what we consider suspicious or under a risky category. If yes, proceed to the next steps. Otherwise, checking of links will not be applied.
Identify user linkage using the following steps. Each step below must be carried out until at least one link with a banned user has been found. A banned user is defined as any of the following:
deleted & blocklisted
ghosted & blocklisted 
on-hold & blocklisted
If there are multiple linked banned accounts, prioritize using this hierarchy:
Ghosted & Blocklisted over Deleted & Blocklisted
Highest similarity score
The most recent “last seen time”
Check linked users via Admin Page.
On the Page Actions panel found on the right of the user account page, click Show Linked Users.

[Image: 0KpygK1KvUe67gyRujhvY2jPCcixRvUZEjy4cKC_iozH65Q0L49w67J4QPsUdedHXzi6gvP7yE55SA50F9Ad70H--MeXrUWy67fSZV6Qwx99Qj2PN2kyLa8bUePyfZMr0yiwcmCd5DvxZQIo9viC9Og]

Click Show Linked Users to see Featured Linked Users.

[Image: cmJsRN6Vz_OapjomWPrCu5a0sRMMgIrbYEQBuNvORQBt7De6fkuVj3_XuhsDincWDkz9DKKApAVOoYx4mQbH0EzknX_YhD4rARTgdMGLACGL9tDlCVbglIFB_ZI22hB_PZSDLz9oPh4Nb9yLMjFQQrg]

Check linked users in Override Linked Users

[Image: BECJdcs2vYo3oJ_OYvF006uqrlG79Idx6sDcO89cDgYAHC40CR_2mlj7MQYsQGSw-QPzSzH9mZZpSnEMu1m2sCLgNMSB5pQYRVgTHsSckAtEuG-BSIfTHr6haICvLSIkvp2c58CKl4kInGR5PYLSMYI]

Check linked users using the default Phone Number. 
Go to the user admin page to see the default phone number.

[Image: AkMZcnJyxWlsIzoB469t4Cv4E0QHgT8j27TBUTyJ8PX5-RILnWqLST88doqdWzf36FdlqAJc9I508JYOj9vuY-PkgaRUOvcy_9bd_5ateweGo8W4RT0ZzMVoraf9FvM22cRIk8KoeDvZTD_rOrJDQbg]

Use the default phone number found to search for links. Do this by clicking Users and pasting the default phone number. Then click Go to User.

[Image: eLpV_KO8MvqBRStj1cwk5egE2cZij_f27fbPO15LOpEL5rPZuGDbAwu4JX5rylfR_t6QN_c0el6KFkPEqz3T8AH4dmCoMgPCQvc-Z1XDYa2bYZPex7CE4W2T12C3ubhSXaCjb6LsLuBsjdkLu3H5H_U]


[Image: qG-c9LoI9sSGoh2qPxAIQJsxWR-pkx-XqZQFyLPVmuz9RsfvZegvcMtoF8qtPGyMnpTDPp3y5S-TatijdvlD5vMgNQaKe3OLS5f98jrFHI6Sj8UMA4XepE5NXFoeveRnAIL3r1hENssCLT9eTlJ17eg]

In the case of any linked user, you will see a list of such under Users. If multiple banned users were shown, pick the one with the most recent sign up date. (Note: On-hold accounts will still have “Active” user status on this page; to identify possible on-hold users, open each “Service Provider” user)

[Image: xrKuwc8dobc5_5mbc4dWuuEjtyJzggZ8xoh1jB5RXMWIC3zD6cavth5UJbyxRoLWthPRH5a4OL5KGH4j1gZPsNeVzb6_idMQyyyP7iUTGc16V-zy90u8fAZoUFUNMwrYrCCPqkrwZx28dnlWYstYSkk]

Notes:
For request-based queues, remember that a Pro can act as a customer, too - they can send requests. So, all the account actions in the Universal policy can be applied to them.
No need to check linked users if they are from Site Intercept.
In checking linked accounts, we consider first-degree checks only.
The only time we need to double-check the actioning on the first-degree link (if it is correct) is when the action reason is about auto-ghosting or link-related, such as “previously linked to a banned user.”
No need to search using junk default phone numbers.
There is no need to follow all steps in checking for linked users; as long as one banned linked user has been identified, that will be used as the basis for actioning the current account.
Once you have identified that the active user is strongly linked to a banned user, open the Universal Linked-Account Action Policy to find the appropriate account action for the active user.
Review the linked banned account’s user type, status, and specific deletion/ghost/on-hold reason to identify the corresponding action for the active user. (Tip: press Control+F to easily find the banned user’s action reason).

[Image: Screenshot 2024-03-13 at 9.14.09 AM.png]

Example above: The banned user’s action reason was related to sexual content, so I pressed control+F and typed ‘sexual’ to find the specific actioning for the active user - which is ‘Delete and Blocklist’ that is applicable to both an active Pro and active Customer.
Implement account action on the active user through Admin and complete the tagging in the work ticket on Tack.
Note: 
If you encounter an active account that is linked to a banned user but not blocklisted, check the deletion/ghost reason. If the reason falls under any of the reasons found in Tier 4 from this guide: Universal Linked-Account Action Policy, the active account should be actioned following column E in the same document.
   Details
   (return to index)
If a specific action reason is not listed in the Google sheet, reach out to the queue’s Proactive ops POC so they can add a new entry for it or escalate it to the @riskanalytics team if any assistance is needed.
   FAQs
   (return to index)
Do we still need to check the phone number links if we’ve already identified a strong one in LADS (Show Linked Users in Admin)?
No, if one banned linked account was already identified in LADS, there is no need to check the phone number links.
If the linked banned user is only deleted/ghosted, but not blocklisted, should we still action the active account?
Yes, only if the violation of the banned user is under Tier 4 from this guide: Universal Linked-Account Action Policy. Otherwise, linked active accounts should not be actioned.
Do we need to double-check if the action on the linked banned account is correct before we action the current account?
The only time we need to double-check the actioning on the first-degree link (if it is correct) is when the action reason is about auto-ghosting or link-related, such as “previously linked to a banned user. You’ll need to find the root account to check if the actioning was correct. Decide whether or not to action the active user based on the findings you've identified. If the first-degree linked account or root account was actioned incorrectly, reach out to SMEs (delete/un-delete/blocklist) or the Anomaly Detection team (ghosting/un-ghosting/blocklist) for corrective actions.
If there’s already a violation in the request itself and another violation was found upon checking links, what do we do?
Select the graver violation as your reference in actioning the active account.
Do we consider the number of years the linked account is deleted/blocklisted before actioning?
No. As long as the linked banned user is blocklisted, we will be actioning the active account.
When searching links through the default phone number, can we delete junk mobile numbers?
No. These queues are time-sensitive queues, so we don’t have to do many extra steps.
What phone numbers do I need to use when checking for possible links?
Only the default number of the customer (check links through "Show Linked Users" / LADS) and contact numbers that could be found on the request notes and messenger

What
(return to index)
The License Verification queue is used to review and validate professional licenses submitted by pros through their Service Profile or during onboarding. Specialists are responsible for investigating and verifying these licensees.
​​We only verify government-issued licenses found in a state licensing board public databases and for the following job categories:
Accounting or tax professions
Architecture
Attorney
Car towing
Carpentry
Concrete and foundation work
Drywall
Electrical work
Engineers
Financial professions
Flooring and carpet
General contracting
Home improvement and home building
HVAC work
Insulation
Landscaping
Law
Masonry
Metalworking
Moving
Painting
Paving
Plumbing
Pool and spa
Roofing
Tiling
NOTE: This list is subject to change.
Why
(return to index)
License verification ensures compliance for regulated services, and helps customers confidently choose qualified pros, ultimately benefiting both the business and our users by building trust on the Thumbtack platform.
When
(return to index)
When a pro submits a license for verification from either their Service Profile or in the Service setup flow during onboarding, a new work ticket (WT) is generated.
SLA for the License Verification queue is 48 hours, and the HT target is 4.5 minutes.
How
(return to index)
