SEARCH LICENSE DATABASE
(return to index)
Steps to Search:

Copy the pro’s license number from the Proofread Portal.
Use the database link provided in Step 1 of the Proofread Portal in Admin.
Some state databases require a U.S.-based IP address for access. If you encounter any issues, contact IT for VPN support.
Note: Some links lead to a webpage hosting a PDF of licensees, not a direct search tool.
Search using the following order:
License Number: Enter the number exactly as provided. Adjust the format if needed based on database requirements (e.g., "ABC.1234.DE" → "1234").
License numbers that are very similar to the one provided by the pro can be accepted.
If there is an obvious typo, escalate to the manager’s queue (MQ).
If the license number submitted by the pro in Admin does not match the license number in the DB, but does match another identifier in the DB, escalate to the manager’s queue (MQ) for verification.
Examples include, but aren’t limited to: UBI Numbers, License Record IDs, License Keys, Registration Numbers, Filing Numbers, or Case Numbers
Refer to the Match vs. Mismatch table for acceptable variations.
Pro’s Name: Search using the pro’s last name or full name. Follow database formatting guidelines (e.g., "Last Name, First Name").
Accept similar name variations or nicknames as valid.
Consult the Name Variations guide if needed.
If there is a discrepancy in the pro’s name due to the use of initials:
Attempt to validate the pro’s identity by searching their information online.
If the pro and license holder appear to be the same person, proceed to escalate to the manager’s queue (MQ).
If the pro’s name matches, but the license number doesn’t match, escalate to the Manager’s Queue.
Business Name: Search using the business name provided.
Use keywords or the initial words of the business name (e.g., "Jane Doe’s Cleaning Services" → search for "Jane Doe").
Note:  If the database defaults to individual license searches, switch to the business search view when necessary.
Compare Results:
Cross-check the information in the database with the details displayed in Step 2 of the Proofread Portal.
Use the Verify License or Deny License sections for next steps based on your findings.
If discrepancies occur, consult the Match vs. Mismatch table for guidance.
Doing Business As: Search using both the pro’s name and business name.
Some databases have a field for DBA or ‘Doing Business As.’ If the profile name and/or business name match the DBA, consider that information a match for the purposes of verifying the license.
Pro’s Phone Number
This option is usually necessary only for databases that don’t allow searches based on name or license number
In order to find the pro’s phone number:
Click ‘View’ next to the business name to navigate to the service profile
Copy the PKID from the service profile URL and search it in Admin
Look for a phone number attached to the business, if there is one, and search it on the licensing database
Click on the owner’s name to open their Admin page
Search the pro’s phone numbers on the licensing database

MATCH VS. MISMATCH
​​(return to index)
Once you’ve located the license, you’ll need to compare what is listed on the database to the information the pro provided to Thumbtack (shown in the Proofread Portal).

MATCH, MISMATCH, MISSING
CRITERIA
EXAMPLES
Match
Common nickname, minor spelling variations, or shortened name variation used on either the license or on the account

See common name variations doc​
Jon vs. Jonathan, Mel vs. Melissa, Jil vs. Jill, Jhon vs. John.
Match
Business name contains word variations or common abbreviations
If it’s not immediately clear if an abbreviated name is valid, search for the business online and see if they’ve used the abbreviated name elsewhere.
If a match is still unclear based on the search results, escalate to the Manager’s Queue.
Thumbtack Floors vs Thumbtack Flooring
Smith Brothers Plumbing vs. Smith Bros. Plumbing
Rainbow Painting Company vs. Rainbow Painting Co.
Match
Business name variations based on text to identify the location or available services.
If it’s not immediately clear if an abbreviated name is valid, search for the business online and see if they’ve used the abbreviated name elsewhere.
If a match is still unclear based on the search results, escalate to the Manager’s Queue.
Jim Davis Plumbing vs. Jim Davis Plumbing of Chicago
Seals Plumbing vs. Seals Plumbing, Heating, and Cooling
Match
Titles, credentials, or legal entity suffixes used in their profile name or license
Dr., Mr., Mrs., Ms., etc. 
MA, PhD, LL.D.
LLC, Inc., Co., Services, Group,
Match
Familial designations, unless there’s a direct contradiction
(see name variations mismatch criteria for contradiction examples)
John Smith vs. John Smith Jr.
Dave Simmons Sr. vs. Dave Simmons
Match
Missing/extra letters on the license number.  
Sample
Admin License number: 12345-B*
DB License number: 12345
Type Class: B

*As long as the letters are relevant to the license.
Match
Leading 0’s
We can pass this since the 0’s are considered leading 0’s used for accounting purposes.
Example: Admin - 1234 but in DB 0001234
Missing letters + Leading 0s + numbers
Texas Licenses
Admin - ABCD1234E
DB - ABCD001234E
Match
Names obscured through the use of initials.
(Attempt to search the pro’s information online to verify their identity. If a match looks reasonable, escalate the case to the manager’s queue.)
Bob J. R. Smith vs. Bob J. Rodgers
Dave F. Grey vs. Dave Folks
Match
Names with at least two matches 
Jane Marie Ocasio-Cortez vs. Jane Ocasio or Jane Cortez
Dave Cottonsmith vs. Dave Cotton or Dave Smith
John Smith vs. Smith John
Emmanuel Hurtado Cisca vs. Emmanuel Hurtado

Mismatch
Names with only one match
Jane Marie Ocasio-Cortez vs. Marie Lopezor Jane Hernandez

Mismatch
Significant name or spelling variations (i.e., not the same name)
Dan vs. Don, Joan vs. Jean, Gary vs. Mary

Mismatch
Business names as initials in admin

(Initials could mean anything. If these businesses are related, then pro should go through ID Help.) 
Sample:
Admin Business name: JDPS
DB: John Doe Painting Services
Reject > Mismatched Business Name (if the Profile Name is not available)

Mismatch
License Type is a Mismatch, and license is inactive.
This should be tagged as License Inactive and should not be escalated to MQ.

VERIFY A LICENSE
​​​​(return to index)
Once you determine that the license can be verified, move forward with the steps below to update the Proofread Portal.

Select ‘Yes’ from the dropdown in Step 2 of the Proofread Portal.
This will reveal new fields that need to be completed.
Fill in License Details:
Include as much information as possible, even if the database does not provide all the details. Most databases will include:
Issued (or Effective) Date
Expiration Date
Enter the Issued Date:
Use the 'Issued Date' ,'Effective Date,' or ‘Admission Date’ provided in the database.
NOTE: If multiple “issued dates” are listed (e.g., 'First Issue Date: 10/16/2000' and 'Last Issue Date: 10/28/2020'), always use the first/original issued date that corresponds to the license type chosen by the pro.
Enter the Expiration Date:
Input the 'Expires On' date as shown in the database.
If no expiration date is listed: Leave the field blank.
Next Registration Date is when the license should be renewed. (e.g. Next registration date: Sep 2023 means the license will expire on Aug 31, 2023)
If the expiration date is 50 or more years in the future: Leave the field blank and include the expiration information in the Notes section.
NOTE: Any blank expiration dates will automatically default to two years from the verification date.
Once all information is recorded, click Verify License Information is Valid.

If you determine the license cannot be verified, move forward with the steps below to update the Proofread Portal.

Select “No” from the dropdown in Step 2 of the Proofread Portal.
This will display a list of checkboxes where you can indicate which specific data points do not match between the Proofread Portal and the database.
Select each item that does not match.
In each text box associated with the box checked, enter the information as it appears in the database. 
Make sure to add this information in the WT internal notes as well.
Once all mismatched information is recorded, click License Does Not Match.

ESCALATE TO MANAGERS QUEUE (MQ)
​​(return to index)
When to escalate a ticket? 

Database Issues:

The link to the database isn’t working or is broken.
First, check if it has a workaround in the Broken Database Escalations sheet.
Make sure your VPN gateway is connected to the U.S.
If the database needs login credentials, and licenses cannot be searched using the general search bar on the website.
If the linked database provides no way to verify the license provided in the task.
If the database provided does not match the pro's license type (e.g., Pro's license is for Attorneys in TN, but the database links to Engineers and Surveyors in SC).
If you come across multi-state national accounts, escalate to MQ. These should be worked on by Incident Ops

License Mismatches:

If two license numbers are provided in the license number field and either one matches.
If the pro’s name matches, but the License Number doesn’t match.
If the provided license number matches another unique identifier in the license database.
If two different search criteria (e.g., license number and business name) produce conflicting results.
If the license includes numbers and letters, and the numbers match but the letters cannot be verified.
Note: If the letters relate to the license type, state, or similar details, and the numbers match, the license can be approved.
If the listed effective date on the database is tomorrow or in the next 7 days.
If there is an obvious error or typo in the license number, either in the Proofread Portal or database.
Typos are 1-character variations in a license number. If any more than 1 character, it is not considered to be a typo and should be tagged as a mismatch.
If the license number is in another field (e.g., Business Name or License Name) and the number in that field matches the license, it can be approved without escalation.
If the name variation is not in the name variation doc.
If the name cannot be directly verified due to the use of initials, but the user and license holder otherwise seem to be the same person.
If a Business Name Match is Unclear
If a license would otherwise be verified, but it’s unclear if the business name matches.
Note: Instances where a business name mismatch does not impact the license verification should not be escalated
License Classification Discrepancies:

If a specialty license found in the database falls under a general license, we verify but it is not listed in the License Type section of Admin.
If what appears in the license type section/classification on Admin is different from what appears on the database, but they are showing the same license code (example: S260 - General Contractor on Admin vs. S260 - Asphalt and Concrete Qualifier on Database).

Specialist Errors:

 If a specialist accidentally verifies a license that should be rejected in the Proofread Portal, they should escalate the WT to have it corrected.
If a specialist accidentally rejects a license that should be approved in the Proofread Portal, they should escalate the Work Ticket to have it corrected.
If the issue date or expire date was incorrectly added in the Proofread Portal.

How to escalate to MQ:

Update Internal notes in Tack on why the ticket is being escalated
Transfer the Ticket to the Manager’s / Task POC’s queue
Fill out the LVMQ Workflow in the LV slack channel.
Include screenshots of the database (the error and your VPN connection to a U.S. gateway, if it is inaccessible) and the Proofread portal in the LVMQ Workflow.

Note: Remember to check that you're connected to a U.S. gateway in your GlobalProtect. Do not use the "Best Available" option.
LICENSE VERIFICATION FAQ’S
​​(return to index)

CATEGORY
QUESTION
ACTION

Specialized License Types
What do we use to verify a moving license?

USDOT vs MC #
Only use a USDOT number or a state-specific license number to verify a license.

Do not use MC # to verify moving licenses.

Specialized License Types
When do we use SAFER?
Use SAFER only to determine if a moving license is INTERSTATE. If it is, use FMCSA to verify the license.

If the license is Intrastate, rely on the linked database (DB).
If the linked DB is SAFER, note this in Tack's internal notes and escalate to MQ.

SAFER is no longer used to verify licenses directly.

Specialized License Types
Intrastate / Interstate Moving Licenses - when to approve or reject or escalate to MQ?
We will approve if the cargo they carry is something we verify (Household Goods) and their operation matches (eg., Admin - Intrastate, DB - Intrastate).

NOTE: We will reject if the cargo they carry is something that we don’t verify (ex. General Freight, Motor Vehicles, Liquids).

We will escalate Intrastate / Interstate licenses if the cargo they carry is something we verify (ex. Household Goods) and their operation doesn’t match (ex. Admin - Intrastate, DB - Interstate).

If unsure, escalate to SME on shift.

Special Handling
If the license status says "Inactive," but the date has not yet passed, what do we do?  
Approve* -  but first check that the license is not suspended before tagging it as Active. The database was probably not updated. 

Special Handling
If I get an error message when verifying or rejecting a license on admin, what should I do?
Consult with an SME or manager, and they will let you know if an IT helpdesk ticket should be sent.

Special Handling
What if the license type found in DB shows multiple similar entries in admin (one is hidden/deleted and the other one is something we verify)? Do we verify the license or tag it as TTDNV?
Approve.

We will follow the License Type we verify.

The following emails will be automatically sent out to pros based on the reason for denying their license and can be found in the License verification email index.
License Submitted: Confirms receipt of the license and informs the pro it's under review.
License Approved: Notifies the pro their license is verified, and the badge has been added to their profile.
Profile / legal name does not match: Informs the pro that the license verification failed due to a name mismatch and asks them to update their info.
License number does not match: Alerts the pro the license number doesn’t match the state database and requests an update.
Business name does not match: Notifies the pro of a mismatch between the business name on the license and their account.
Cannot find license: Informs the pro that their license couldn’t be found in the state database and asks them to resubmit.
Expired License: Lets the pro know their badge was removed due to an expired license and asks them to resubmit.

What
(return to index)
This Knowledge Article provides instructions for handling non-standard reports, including external reports, mentions of lawsuits, and comprehensive reviews of user accounts. It is designed to ensure thorough investigations, assess potential risks, and maintain the safety and integrity of the Thumbtack platform.

Why
(return to index)
Even if we’re not able to directly help users reach resolutions or resolve disputes, it’s important that T&S does our due diligence to evaluate user risks and ensure platform safety. When we investigate accounts or user concerns, we ensure that we’ve been thorough in reviewing and preventing future risk.
When
(return to index)
Sometimes we receive reports that don’t fit into our normal incident handling processes but still require action or investigation on our end. Refer to this Knowledge Article when investigating:
External Reports:  Incident reports from someone who did not hire a pro through Thumbtack (no bid ID available).
Mentions of Lawsuit: Incidents where users have confirmed they are engaged in legal action with another user, but they didn’t want to report the concern to TT.
Comprehensive Reviews: Times where we need to complete an in-depth review of a user, both on the platform and outside of Thumbtack. 
How
(return to index)
   Steps
   (return to index)
EXTERNAL REPORTS
(return to index)
External reports, formerly known as “Good Samaritan Reports,” are incidents from someone who didn’t hire a pro through Thumbtack (no Negotiation bid ID available).
When two people didn’t meet on Thumbtack, reaching out to a business and requesting that they address a concern may not be appropriate since we weren’t involved in the interaction and our Terms don’t apply. However, we do care that there are concerns with the business, and it’s a good opportunity to review the pro’s account to see if there are other issues we need to look into.

We require pros to operate within their local laws and regulations for the services they are performing.
Pros are responsible for managing their licenses.
Pros aren’t required to upload their licenses, and customers should be verifying licenses on their own.
Work a report
(return to index)

Confirm there is no available account for the reporting user, and no negotiation between the customer and the pro they’re reporting.
Reach out to the customer by their preferred method, phone or email.
Explain we will be investigating the pro, and we’ll take the appropriate action based on what we find.
If you’re emailing them, send them the macro External report: Reviews - Thank for info - cx: in Tack and customize it to the situation.
Complete a comprehensive review of the pro’s business to determine what action we should take:
Remove
Warn/Flag
Coaching
Do nothing
Close the incident.

What if the customer has a Thumbtack account?
Sometimes, Thumbtack customers will contact us about a pro, and they “just want us to know” about the situation. While they open the case stating this, it could also be because they aren’t aware of what we can do to help.
Ask them if they’d like our help getting back in touch with the pro.

If they want our help, you can help them get in touch with the pro.
If the situation doesn’t involve a project they hired for on Thumbtack, the Thumbtack Guarantee doesn’t apply. We can’t require the pro to work towards a resolution with us, and we won’t spend much time mediating.
If the customer does have a connection to the pro through Thumbtack (bid PKID is available), this is now considered a regular incident, not an external report. Move forward with the usual steps to determine the best process approach.
If they don’t want help, let them know we'll make note of their concerns and take any appropriate action on our end.
"We’re happy to respect your wishes and consider your report anonymous. If that’s the case, from here, we would make note of your concerns and take appropriate action on our end, including reviewing their account to determine if this is someone we want doing business on our site moving forward."

MENTIONS OF LAWSUITS
(return to index)
If a user reaches out regarding a project in a risky category and mentions a lawsuit or legal proceeding, but doesn't want to submit a report through Thumbtack the issue is escalated to the Trust and Safety team.
Risky Categories

Massage Therapy
Private Yoga
Personal Training
House Cleaning
Boudoir Photography
Video Production
Pet Categories 

If you receive one of these incidents, review the reported individual's account for: 

A history of incidents
Fraud signals
Collusion
If user is a pro also check: 
Negative reviews (1-2 stars)
Background check status (did they pass?)

If no issues are found, the incident can be closed.
If issues are found: 

Reach out to the user who reported the issue to collect more information. 
"We have made a note of your concerns and will take appropriate action on our end, including reviewing their account to determine if this is someone we want doing business on our site moving forward."
Close the incident.

   Comprehensive Reviews
    (return to index)
A comprehensive review can be conducted when a user incurs several ToU violations, negative reviews, or complaints. It can also be helpful in situations where a previously removed user returns to resolve an old issue or request reconsideration.
Based on the results, we’ll decide whether we’d like to keep the pro’s business on our platform or if we’re no longer a good fit.
WHAT TO REVIEW
(return to index)
When you’re reviewing a pro’s business, you’ll take into consideration aspects of their business, on and off, of Thumbtack. This means looking into their account in Admin and Tack and doing internet searches.
Look at the following:

ON THUMBTACK
OFF THUMBTACK
Time on Thumbtack
Tenure since sign-up
How active are they?
Effect on revenue
Overall revenue from the pro vs. total incidents and payouts to customers.
BBB, check:
Rating
Accreditation
Complaints or review histories, including responses and if disputes were resolved.
If associated businesses are found, research those as well.
If the pro has previous T&S incidents or concerns, and:
The severity of what was brought to our attention (high dollar, legal, law enforcement, etc.).
The outcome of the incident.
If the pro was flagged or coached
Yelp
Review averages and trends.
Has the pro received multiple reviews about the same behavior?
Have they received multiple negative reviews?
Their responses to the reviews.
True People Search
Inappropriate messaging
Profane or sexual content
Continually messaging customers
Facebook
Updated BGC/ID info
Other service-related platforms
Linked accounts - check for additional business names or phone numbers associated with their account:
Avoiding negative reviews
Linked to banned user
Check if their prior incidents are similar violations/trends.
Avoiding paying
Referral fraud
Google
Open an Incognito browser; review their Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, etc. for any concerning reviews or information.
Search the pro’s name, business name, city/state, etc., online to locate any news stories, background concerns, judgments against them, etc.
Licensing/credentials
Research requirements in their job category if relevant.
Check for a license through the pro’s state licensing website. If they’re not licensed, or it has been suspended, discuss with leadership before taking action.


OUTCOMES
(return to index)
Once you’ve completed your review, decide the outcome of the account and note your reasoning in the case. Choose from the following:

OUTCOME
ACTIONS
No Action
No flag/coaching or removal is warranted.
Request BGC
We’ve requested to have a background check completed by the pro. 
This can be done even if we know we won’t allow the pro to stay on site; we need the info to help gather additional information and linked accounts.
Flag & Coach
Specific coaching is provided, and the account is flagged. 
If a flag is added with no coaching, add notes to your case/incident explaining any actions taken.
Remove
The account is deleted. 
If the user has other open incidents, work with those specialists before actioning. 
If the removal is temporary, pending a required action, make a clear note of what the pro needs to do to be reactivated.
If the removal is permanent, refund any outstanding credit or package balance in Admin.
Stay Removed
The pro was previously removed, and though they’ve resolved the concerns, we’ve determined they won’t be reactivated.
Update the deletion logs to say this is a business decision removal that won’t be reconsidered.
If they have any outstanding credit or package balance, refund them in Admin.
Talking points
(return to index)

Some customers may request the contact or other information for our pro. See the Privacy Policy for how to handle their questions.
If they want to know what action we will take, let them know that our privacy policy doesn’t permit us to discuss what action we will specifically take. However, in cases like this, we have various options that we can use to address the situation, including:
Actively monitoring the business for signs of other issues that may come up in the future.
Addressing the concerns directly with the pro.
In some circumstances, we will remove a business from our site.

   Emails
   (return to index)
External report: Reviews - Thank for info - cx: This email macro thanks non-Thumbtack customers for reporting issues with a pro, confirms Thumbtack will investigate, but doesn't disclose actions or promise a response. 
External reports: Concerns about pro - cx: Specialists should send this email macro when a non-Thumbtack customer reports concerns with a pro.

**Use the content request form to request an update or submit questions/concerns**

Instant book gaming

Instant book gaming
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Process Overview
Confirm Gaming 
Accurate Examples
Inaccurate Examples
Take Action
Accurate Actioning 
Inaccurate Actioning
Emails
FAQs
Related
 
What
​​(return to index)
The Instant Book Gaming (IBG) queue is used to catch pros who are abusing the 15-minute cancellation policy for instant book job refunds. This abuse occurs when pros exploit the automatic refund system for purposes other than accidental customer bookings and cancellations.
 
Why
(return to index)
Using Thumbtack to find a pro is free for customers, and we want them to feel comfortable reaching out to the pros they’re interested in. It's considered a violation of our Terms of Use for pros to try to avoid lead charges by having customers cancel bookings or pressuring them about lead costs. 
 
When
(return to index)
In order to get assigned an IBG work ticket, you’ll need the “IB Gaming” routing skill in the Salesforce Omni-Channel.
SLA for the IBG queue is 48 hours, and the target handle time is 5 minutes.
 
How
(return to index)
   Steps
   (return to index)
 

[Image: _NF0Im0qSCLcBgpH42Gr6gDf_FCxCnR3LGoquLLokYZfQd03Xcn-O6ddjfNSrKiKz_z6A5zf4aK9fO2SPFzGx6Fdr2TrJ-fhn7gtNLtZ9G_7wHDx79kSH7c5u9HCfepScGqyqmqmwXJiZgQpO0RH7Cw]

*Lucid Link
 
PROCESS OVERVIEW
(return to index)

[Image: Screenshot 2024-02-26 at 12.08.17 PM.png]

Click on the pro admin Link and check to see if the pros account is already on hold for IB gaming. 
If they are, follow the steps for inaccurate outcome.
If not, move to step 2. 
Does the pro have any Bid Pks with: 
15m Refund with 3+ reviews after.
15m Refund with "Cancel" in messages. 
.15m Refund where the Customer indicated pro asked to cancel 
Yes:
Copy the PKs and paste the Bid PKs into the search bar under Negotiations (fka Quotes/Bids) in Admin (if there are a lot, review at least 5 of each). 
Review the customer's review to see if it’s clear the pro performed the job after the customer canceled and/or their messages to see if there is obvious gaming. 
If it’s clear the pro was gaming, follow the steps for accurate outcome. 
If it’s not clear, continue to step 3. 
No - Move on to step 3. 
Go to the pro’s Negotiations (fka Quotes/Bids), and click the first bid ID.

[Image: Screenshot 2024-02-26 at 12.10.35 PM.png]

Scroll down to Auto-refund Status and click on the link with recent manual credit refunds. 

[Image: Screenshot 2024-02-26 at 12.12.10 PM.png]

Scroll down to Recent Manual Credit Refunds and investigate at least 5 recent bids with the Admin Note: “Canceled booking refund.” 
Note: Make sure these are new bids from the last time the pro was reviewed. The most recent prior review date is in the WT Details. 
Review the conversations between the pro and customers and/or customer reviews left for pro gaming. 
If gaming is found, follow the steps for an accurate outcome. 
If gaming is not found, follow the steps for an inaccurate outcome.  

[Image: Screenshot 2024-02-26 at 12.12.54 PM.png]

 
CONFIRM GAMING
(return to index)
 

ACCURATE
INACCURATE
Pro asks the customer to cancel so they don’t get charged by TT. 
The customer cancels, then pro messages about leaving a review, or the customer left a review about the job being done.
Pro says they will give the customer a discount if they cancel.
The customer canceled, or the pro asked the customer to cancel because they didn’t mean to book.
The customer cancels after talking to the pro and realizing they didn’t want the job done.
Pro asks the customer to cancel after realizing the customer is asking for a service not offered (or another valid reason).
 
*NOTE: If you don’t see EXPLICIT signs of gaming, select “Inaccurate,” and no action should be taken on the account. 
 
Accurate Examples
(return to index)
 
Pro asked the customer to cancel but showed a clear intention of still doing the job. 

[Image: d2PS8bDnfZb51z8r34dmQviv7VPq-afeBkC5CBHYn2Qy4_ajwTx_lSNIcVqYFxzTm53wM2AIlpNdlVKJbSEGW5wNNxsvW_fPC27oySEjJ_BK9tVO_5oWcAzIEfsnf-VOVs6YqL1Om_sTwaHhAS6bgTI]

The customer canceled, the pro was refunded, and they asked the customer to review their work. 

[Image: Screenshot 2024-02-26 at 12.17.46 PM.png]

The customer canceled, the pro was refunded, and the customer left a review that made it clear the pro did the job. 

[Image: Screenshot 2024-02-26 at 12.19.05 PM.png]


[Image: Screenshot 2024-02-26 at 12.19.48 PM.png]

 
Inaccurate examples
(return to index)
Pro provides a quote to the customer and asks them to agree or cancel if they don’t agree. 

[Image: Screenshot 2024-02-26 at 12.22.37 PM.png]

The customer canceled, the pro was refunded, and the customer left a review, but it’s not clear the pro actually did the job. 

[Image: Screenshot 2024-02-26 at 12.24.06 PM.png]


[Image: Screenshot 2024-02-26 at 12.24.51 PM.png]

Pro asks the customer to cancel because the customer says they are not ready for the job. 

[Image: J4_K2WojVf9Aep6VcF7NGSFyTl3lfgoOQADWhUqIzG6rzMHZkU5tpqNGqiLeQ5PXYbJrcV5O2W4h8pzvCetRanOhgzt4N65xU4BJfXf1-2kV2Ya20mJIxjaTVwlzXk2fXqTbclG2Vt8fApY1wSf-9Jk]

 
TAKE ACTION
(return to index)
Accurate actioning (confirmed violation)
(return to index)

Steps taken depend on whether the pro has a managed account or not:
Managed Account:
 

1ST VIOLATION
2ND VIOLATION*
Outcome: Accurate
Outcome Detail: 1st Violation Managed Account
Internal Notes: Insert signals found
Account Actions: No Action
Admin Actioning: No Action taken  
 
Reach out to AM, letting them know they need to coach the pro. 
Outcome: Accurate
Outcome Detail: 2nd Violation
Internal Notes: Insert signals found
Account Actions: No Action
Admin Actioning: No Action taken 
 
Transfer ownership of the WT to Tausha Lemus.
 
Not a Managed Account:
 

1ST VIOLATION
2ND VIOLATION*
Outcome: Accurate
Outcome Detail: 1st Violation Warning Issued 
Internal Notes: Insert signals found
Account Actions: Hold
Admin Actioning: Add Pro Account Hold
Reason: The user has general issues or needs coaching
Notes: WT # - Account flagged for instant book gaming. Pro needs to acknowledge the email sent for hold removal. If the behavior continues, it may result in account deletion.    
Outcome: Accurate
Outcome Detail: 2nd Violation
Internal Notes: Insert signals found
Account Actions: Delete & Blocklist
Admin Actioning: Delete and Blocklist pro
Delete Reason: (Pro) Other Violation
Delete Notes: WT # - Instant Book Cancellation Gaming, 2nd offense 
Blocklist Reason: Community Standards Violation  
Blocklist Notes: WT # - Instant Book Cancellation Gaming, 2nd offense 
*Note: If the Prior Accurate Outcome under the WT Details says “Yes,” that means the pro has previously been caught and warned for IB Gaming. If they’re caught gaming again, it would be their 2nd violation.  
 
Inaccurate actioning (not a violation)
(return to index)

If there are no clear signs of IB gaming, the following should be selected:
Outcome: Inaccurate
Outcome Detail: None
Internal Notes: Anything additional to add (Ex., already on IB hold, likely gaming because of X, Y, Z but can’t confirm, etc.)
Account Action: No action
  
   Emails
   (return to index)
1st Violation Warning Issued: Automatically sent via Salesforce when Outcome = Accurate, Outcome Detail = 1st Violation Warning Issued and Save is clicked.  
 
    FAQs
   (return to index)
Q: What if there are other TOS Violations detected?
A: Remove the violating content and leave an internal note on the WT stating what TOS violation was found. If the content is something that should be escalated to the Critical Escalations team, escalate it to your manager so a case can be created and assigned to the team. 
 
Q: What if the pro is already deleted and blocklisted for a business decision?
A: No need to add an account hold. No additional account action is needed in Admin. Add an internal note: Pro was already deleted and blocklisted. Business decision. 
 
   Related
   (return to index)
Terms of Service Violations
  
Use the content request form to submit questions or concerns or to request an update.

articles.fullText:
Incident mediation

Incident mediation
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Project incident lifecycle
Mediation steps
Clarify our role
Be impartial
Help users communicate
Express empathy
Refocus
Agreement made
Know when to end an incident
If the pro is already deleted
Details
Sensitive incidents: HIPAA and privacy concerns
Transitioning out of TSCI
Talking points
Emails
What
(return to index)
Mediating incidents (or handling incidents “manually”) means that you’re working with the customer and pro directly rather than using other tools such as the Thumbtack Solution Center, New Era ADR, or other processes like Concerning Reviews or Pro Not Paid.
This is a great way to manage a case that's sensitive or would benefit from a more "hands-on" approach.
Why
(return to index)
The TSC and New Era help us be efficient and allow customers and professionals to work out issues between themselves, but manually working an incident gives the customer and pro a more personalized experience.

When
(return to index)
Choosing this route is up to your discretion.
These types of incidents typically involve users who:
It has already been through the TSCI process and was escalated out.
Are more upset than the average customer.
Ask you to be more involved.
Have deleted accounts.
Have involved law enforcement.
Are highly escalated.
Are involved in a situation that's highly sensitive.
You can also work the incident manually if the users can’t use other resolution processes or because you feel it’s a better fit.
How
(return to index) 
    Steps
   (return to index)
INCIDENT LIFECYCLE
(return to index)

[Image: Screenshot 2024-04-23 at 8.33.25 AM.png]
MEDIATION STEPS
(return to index)
By now, you should have already taken all the normal steps for the review phase to start an incident  and decided you should work the incident manually.
While working through dispute resolution on manual incidents, keep in mind the communication practices established in incident expectations.
“Dispute resolution” or “mediation” is what we call the portion of incidents where we’re helping the customer and pro work together to find a solution to their disagreement. Use the following principles to help you successfully guide the users through this step:
Clarify our role.
Be impartial.
Help users define and communicate their concerns.
Express empathy and validate concerns.
Remind users of the task at hand.
Help users put in a good-faith effort.
Once an agreement has been made, hold both users to it.
Know when to end an incident.
Clarify our role
(return to index)

Direct the users towards each other.
We expect them to make a good-faith effort to find a solution/middle ground together. Set this expectation about
Thumbtack’s role whenever you feel appropriate.
Even if you’re a go-between, keep them focused on each other
(i.e., “What would you like [user’s name] to do to resolve this concern?”).
Be impartial
(return to index)
Be aware of your unconscious bias and avoid making assumptions.
Give equal opportunity to each to explain their side and suggest solutions.
Use facts to make your decisions.
Make sure decisions can be backed up if challenged.
Help users communicate
(return to index)

Help users define and communicate their concerns.
Many disputes begin from miscommunication. 
Help users clearly and concisely explain their concerns.
Manage the conversation between parties.
Ask questions.
Ask for a bullet point list to help them summarize.
Express empathy
(return to index)

Express empathy and validate concerns.
Signs they need more of this include bickering, fixation on feelings, and repeating themselves.
Help them feel heard so they can move forward.
Refocus
(return to index)

Remind users of the task at hand.
Focus on finding a solution.
After expressing empathy or giving validation, users often need a reminder to re-focus.
Some users are motivated by knowing this will be done sooner if they focus.
Help users put in a good-faith effort.
Remind them to work towards middle-ground.
Use the provided facts to help users see whether their suggestions are reasonable.
Take action where needed.
Agreement made
(return to index)

Once an agreement has been made, hold both users to it. 
Make sure both users are aware of the agreement and related details.
Verify that the terms are realistic.
If the solution no longer works, they should come to a new agreement with the other user.
Set expectations for fulfillment of agreement.
If the responsible party doesn’t follow through on their agreement, we may remove their account until they resolve the concern.
Know when to end an incident
(return to index)

Know when to end an incident.
After an agreement is made, it’s time for us to start stepping back.
Let the users know it’s their responsibility to complete the solution.
If needed, you can offer more help. However, this shouldn’t be standard practice.
Let them know they can follow up if anything changes or the solution isn’t completed.
Return to agreement made if the agreement isn’t completed.
If users don’t agree in a reasonable timeframe despite your help, consider taking action (warn them first).
The Pro/reported party is clearly responsible for the concern: action of their account.
Move forward with the Guarantee afterward, if applicable.
Customer/reporting party is clearly responsible: end the incident.
Direct them to continue working with the pro.
Let them know if additional documentation could change the outcome.
Unclear who’s responsible: Assess eligibility for New Era ADR or end the incident.
Let them know if additional documentation could change the outcome.
If we’ll be waiting on something for more than a few days, close the incident.
Set the expectation with the user(s) that the incident will be closed until you receive the information or documentation you’re waiting on.
If the user(s) stop responding, give them set timeframes to respond by.
Let them know you’ll action their account and/or close the incident if they don’t respond within a certain timeframe (usually two business days).
Note: Make sure you’re following the unresponsive user contact expectations found here.
IF PRO IS ALREADY DELETED
(return to index)
If you notice a pro’s account is already deleted (whether it's a self-delete or T&S deletion), you will update the deletion log to show the most recent incident/reason they were removed. If the logs show “user-delete” or don’t give you the option to Edit, then follow the steps below:
Reactivate the pro.
Note why you’re reactivating them.
Delete the pro again with updated notes about the most recent incident.

Steps:
Review the customer’s situation to determine which route to take with the case.
Though the pro is removed, it doesn’t limit our options completely.
Call the customer to explain the pro is no longer listed on TT, but we’re happy to notify them of the customer’s concern and try to get them back in touch.
Since the pro is already removed from our site, they may not be invested in working with us to address concerns, so try to be realistic in the expectations you set with the customer.
Call the pro to tell them about the concern.
If you’re able to reach the pro, explain the situation and work with them to get back in touch with the customer and move forward with handling your incident as usual.
If they don’t answer, send them an email.
Depending on the response from the pro, update the customer.
If the pro is responsive, move forward with your chosen process approach.
If the pro wasn’t responsive, you can proceed with your next steps for the Thumbtack resolution phase. This can include: 
The Thumbtack Guarantee
CSAT payout.
If Thumbtack isn’t able to resolve it either,  guide the customer to the right local resources.
Close the incident.
   Details
   (return to index) 
SENSITIVE INCIDENTS: HIPAA AND PRIVACY
(return to index)
Incidents where the pro is required by law to adhere to HIPAA (or other confidentiality agreements) and can’t share all of the details of a case. This can involve pros who are attorneys, therapists, counselors, or tax preparers. Confidentiality agreements can prevent pros from sharing specific sensitive details about a case/session that limits the dispute processes available.

We cannot offer dispute resolution if the pro has completed their services for the customer. For example, if you’re working a case involving an attorney:
The court case is completed or ongoing.
The customer is unhappy with the court outcome.
The customer feels like the pro violated ethics rules or malpractice (e.g., the pro didn’t represent them “well enough”).
We can offer dispute resolution options if the pro didn’t complete their services. For example:
The customer paid a deposit, but they don’t want to work with the pro anymore.
The pro still has the customer’s documents.
Documents weren’t filed as agreed.
Do’s and don’ts
Do encourage the customer to speak with the pro directly about their concerns.
Do ask the customer for details when they send a document to the pro. While we’re not asking for the details of the document, knowing when things were sent will help.
Do check eligibility for the MBG.
Don't press the pro to give specific details about the court case/session or any of the conversations they've had with the user.
Don’t promise a resolution tool can be used - we’re not sure what we can offer yet.
Examples of information the pro can share: The number of hours worked, a copy of a retainer,  proof of a refund, etc.
Reviewing the documents
Review the case details – make sure we have a copy of their:
Contract or retainer agreement (redacted if necessary).
Proof of payment.
Copies of their court judgment/decision (if applicable).
Can we determine if we can offer a resolution process?
If we can’t determine our next steps because we don’t have enough information, reach out to the pro/customer and ask them for the missing information.
If we have enough documentation, determine your next steps and follow the steps below.
We can offer a dispute process
Determine which dispute resolution process you’re going to use.
Thumbtack Solution Center
New Ear ADR
Incident mediation
Based on the results of the process you use, you’ll want to do a <comprehensive review> of the pro’s profile.
If you’ve removed the pro, this isn’t necessary.
Check the pro’s licensing/standing with their state Bar.
Look for any disciplinary history.
Add the incident information to this tracker under the “Attorney” tab.
We track these incidents to help us see trends so we can update the process if we need to make it better.

We can’t offer a dispute process
Thank the user for their report and explain why we can’t get involved.
Help the customer understand what options they have for their next steps. They can:
File a complaint for an attorney using their state's regulating board. Use the American Bar Association website to send the customer a link to their state’s board.
Make a Complaint About a Tax Return Preparer.
File a Health Information Privacy or Security Complaint.
Do a comprehensive review of the pro. If the pro is a lawyer, check their license status with the State Bar.
Go to the American Bar Association website.
Find the state the pro is licensed to work in.
Search the pro’s name and review their ABA profile for disciplinary actions and their license status.
Take any appropriate actions based on the outcome of your comp review.
If no concerns are found to warrant removal, notify the pro of the customer’s report and consider flagging the pro.
If the pro is no longer in good standing with their State Bar, or their license isn’t active, it may be appropriate to remove that pro.
Add the incident to the discrimination decision tracker under the Attorney tab.
TRANSITIONING OUT OF TSCI
(return to index)
Thumbtack Solution Center Instant (TSCI) is a process where we handle incidents anonymously via work tickets. When the users need a more hands-on approach, incidents are escalated out of the TSCI queue to be mediated by a Trust and Safety specialist.
Keep in mind:
The users already worked together within the TSC and may be disappointed the issue isn't solved.
You may be headed into an MBG review instead of mediation.
You can continue to use the TSC if you feel the users may still progress there.
Communicate directly with them first, and give them your name.
Transition process

To start an incident that was previously worked in the TSCI queue, follow these steps:
Make sure work tickets are turned off.
Review the work ticket posts to understand what steps specialists have already taken.
Read everything that's already happened, including in the incident feed and within the TSC.
It's a poor experience for users to recap what they've already done when you have access to this information.
Fill out the MBG Eligibility Review.
Determine if you're still mediating between the users.
If both users are still involved, help them work towards a solution.
If the pro is unresponsive and has been removed, it's time to look at the Thumbtack Guarantee.
At this point, your focus is taking care of the customer, not mediating between users.
Determine the correct next steps based on the information you gathered in steps three and five.
Communicate with the user(s).
Give them your name.
Recap what happened so far in the incident.
Validate them.
The TSC didn't work for them, and that's frustrating.
(If applicable) We know that removing the pro doesn't resolve their concerns.
Reassure them that you're here to help now.
Explain your role.
This explanation should look different when both users are still involved vs. when we're looking at the MBG.
Tell them the next step.
   Talking points
   (return to index)
Customer
Pro
   Emails
   (return to index)

GENERAL INCIDENT PROCESS

Intro: Removed pro - Notify of new complaint: This lets the pro know that we’ve received a complaint, and we wanted to let them know even though they aren’t allowed on the site any longer.

Intro: First to customer (after call): Send this to thank the customer for speaking with you after your phone call.

Intro: First to customer (no call): Send this as an introduction to the customer. It explains our role, asks for more information about the concern, and encourages them to schedule a call to discuss the issue further.

Follow-up: Request a call (customer): Send this if you have an update for the customer and would like them to call you.

Follow-up: Doesn't want to work with pro: Send this to explain our role to the customer.

Follow-up: Unresponsive customer: Send this if the customer hasn’t responded to our attempts to contact them, and we’re closing their incident.

Follow-up: Stepping back - Customer upset after pro is removed: This lets the customer know that they can pursue the pro on their own using local resources.

Intro: First to pro - Link: Use this email/snippet when contacting the pro for the first time. It directs the customer to schedule a time to speak directly. 

Intro: First to pro (after call): Send this to thank the pro for speaking with you after your phone call.

Account action: Unresponsive pro (place hold): Send this if the pro hasn’t responded to your attempts to contact them and you’re removing their account.

Account action: Pro unwilling to resolve (disable): Send this if the pro isn’t willing to help and you’re removing their account.

Closing: Cx withdrawn - Flagging (pro): Send this if you’re warning and flagging the pro.

Closing: Pro resolved issue (thank you): Send this to thank the pro for following through with their agreement.

Closing: Unresponsive customer (pro): Send this to the pro if the customer has become unresponsive while you’re working to get them in contact.

Follow-up: Missed call: Send this email/snippet if a user misses their call. It directs them to reschedule. 

Follow-up: Provide account info to customer: Send when the customer asks for information on the pro, and we’re providing what’s available.

Follow-up: Safety tips: Send to the customer when they’ve expressed concerns about pro behavior or need tips on using the platform safely.

Follow-up: Schedule a call: Use this email/snippet when contacting the customer for the first time. It directs the customer to schedule a time to speak directly. 

Follow-up: Late for call: Use this email/snippet to let the user know that we’re running late for their scheduled call. It directs them to reschedule if needed. 

Follow-up: Missed call: Send this email/snippet if a user misses their call. It directs them to reschedule.
Follow up: Thumbtack's role - cx: Specialists should send this email to customers who don’t understand Thumbtack's role in the dispute process.
ACCOUNT ACTIONS
Closing: Cx withdrawn (flagging) - pro: Send this email to the pro to explain that the customer is not interested in pursuing things further, but we’ll be monitoring their account.
Account action: Unresponsive (place hold) - pro: Specialists should use this email macro if the pro hasn’t responded to their attempts to contact them and they're removing the pro's account.
Account Action: Unresponsive/unwilling (disable) - pro: Specialists should send this email macro if the pro isn’t willing to help or is unresponsive, and you’re removing their account.
Account Actions: Business decision (disable) - cx/pro: Specialists should send this email to the customer or pro when they’ve determined they’re not a good fit for Thumbtack and have removed their account.
Account action: Pro removed - cx: Specialists should send this email macro to customers after removing a pro's account.

GRAMMARLY ONLY

Note: Deletion logs: Use this note in the deletion logs when removing a pro for T&S or Incident issues.
 
**Use the content request form  to request an update or submit questions/concerns**

Incident guidelines

Incident guidelines
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Project incident lifecycle
Review phase
Starting an incident
Mediation phase
Thumbtack resolution phase
Closing phase
Details
Call scheduling requirements
Communication
Phone calls 
Voicemails
