How to determine if a user is unresponsive
Unresponsive after automation
Using account actions 
Notes and documentation
Pro is already deleted
User withdraws/doesn’t want to use Thumbtack’s process
Emails
Related
What
(return to index)
This article contains the general practices that should be followed on all standard incidents. This includes the initial incident review, working on an incident, communicating with users, and overall incident management.
Why
(return to index)
Trust and Safety concerns can often be stressful, messy, and unclear, so navigating these situations requires care and nuance. This article covers the incident process best practices to set up successful interactions and expectations with users.
When
(return to index)
These standards apply throughout the review, mediation, Thumbtack resolution, and closing phases on all standard Trust and Safety incidents, unless otherwise authorized by a manager or specific process approach.
How
(return to index)
  Steps
(return to index)
PROJECT INCIDENT LIFECYCLE
(return to index)

[Image: rtaImage]

LUCID

REVIEW PHASE
(return to index)
The review phase of an incident will cover how to start an incident, what to review, and which mediation path to use moving forward.  

Start an incident
(return to index)
After an incident is auto-assigned using Omni, use these steps to review the incident before getting started.
Use the Sync incident button, located at the top right of the incident, to make sure all the relevant details are present.
Complete a thorough review.
Read through all available information to get a full understanding of the timeline and concerns. This includes but is not limited to reviewing incident notes, TT messenger, admin history, previous TS incidents, account flags, and submitted documentation.
Review account banners to confirm the job type. If it is a TTOD (Thumbtack On-Demand) job, note that the customer paid Thumbtack directly, not the pro.
If something feels off, consider investigating further. (i.e., Cx Admin, Pro Admin, Flags, Account logs, etc.)
Identify the main issues.
Determine if the incident has gone through Incident automation.
If the incident was sent to the wrong queue or isn't a T&S issue, consult the T&S Triage Knowledge article for where it should be sent and submit feedback.
Identify what’s needed.
Determine sensitivity and assess Incident Risk Factors.
Select any incident factors found in the incident.
Fill out the Guarantee Eligibility Review (unless the incident doesn't involve a project).
Understand the incident concerns and what the user wants to do about them.
Determine who to contact first.
Always reach out to the user who reported the issue first. 
If the reporting party doesn’t want the other user to know about the report, evaluate for sensitive or safety concerns, and:
If it’s a sensitive incident or has safety concerns.
Follow the steps provided in the Sensitive Incidents knowledge article.
If it is not a sensitive incident and there are no safety concerns.
Make sure the user understands that Thumbtack cannot resolve any concerns without working with both parties to find a resolution. Continue with normal processes.
If anything’s missing or unclear, reach out to the user to gather more information.
Decide on the process approach you'll use to assist the users using the list below. If the case doesn’t fall under any safety or specialized incident type, continue with the standard mediation tools below.
Safety incidents
Non-Discrimination
Sensitive incidents
Critical Escalations
Specialized incident types
In-Product Payments
Pro Reports
Managed Accounts
Copyright and trademark
Spanish/Portuguese support
Investigative reports
MEDIATION PHASE
(return to index)
By now, specialists should have already taken all the normal steps for the review phase to start an incident, and confirmed that mediation between both users will be required.
A specialist's role is to act as the arbitrator of the Terms. Specialists aren't deciding who is "right" in a moral sense; they are deciding what constitutes a "reasonable effort" to resolve the issue.
Key action Items
Lead the Negotiation:
Don't wait for the users to find a middle ground. Take the initiative to present and offer specific compromises.
Use Creative Solutioning:
Look for unconventional ways to bridge the gap between both parties.
Stay Objective:
Avoid the impulse to vilify the Professional. Maintain a neutral stance focused strictly on the facts of the case.
Prioritize Agreement:
When both parties are engaged, your primary goal is to guide them toward a mutual win. However, if the users remain stuck, an agreement is not the only acceptable outcome.
To help an incident move forward, you may choose to use any of the following mediation tools, in addition to manual specialist mediation, when appropriate:
Thumbtack Solution Center
New Era ADR
Account actions
Mediation uses the following incident management principles to help successfully guide users toward a resolution:
Explain Thumbtack’s role
Help users feel understood
Express empathy
Be impartial
Take an active role in pursuing a reasonable resolution
Set expectations and next steps
Help users find a resolution
Explain role
(return to index)
Thumbtack facilitates connections between customers and pros. If issues come up, Trust and Safety’s role is to help users work towards resolutions. 
Specialists should:
Help facilitate communication
Keep users focused on each other, even when acting as a go-between.
(i.e., “What would you like [user’s name] to do to resolve this concern?”).
Keep users on track towards a resolution
Users will need to make a good-faith effort to find a solution/middle ground together.
Help steer conversations toward facts and offer suggested resolutions. 
Ensure expectations and Thumbtack terms are being upheld.

Help users feel understood
(return to index)
Helping users feel understood sets the incident up for success. To give customers confidence that their issues are understood, utilize these skills:
Summarization/paraphrasing.
Ask clarifying questions.
Offer empathy
Request documentation (if relevant)
Express empathy
(return to index)
Express empathy and validate concerns.
Note: Signs they need more of this include bickering, fixation on feelings, and repeating themselves.
Help them feel heard so they can move forward.
Be impartial
(return to index)
Specialists should take an active role in finding a resolution, while focusing on facts.
Be aware of unconscious bias and avoid making assumptions.
Give equal opportunity to both users to explain their experience and suggest solutions.
Use documentation to make decisions.
Ensure that decisions can be supported if challenged, and that an objective decision has been made.
Set expectations and next steps
(return to index)
A big part of incident management is ensuring that things are moving towards a resolution, so it’s important to set clear expectations and next steps in all of your communications. 
Focus users on finding a solution.
It can be easy to get caught up in the details and feelings of a project gone wrong. However, this can hold users back from reaching solutions. 
Remind them to work towards a middle ground, which might require a reasonable compromise.
Help users put in a good-faith effort.
This is required for Thumbtack Guarantee eligibility, so we expect to see genuine efforts to reach a reasonable solution or middle ground together.
Use the provided facts to help users see whether their suggestions are reasonable.
Provide clear timelines
Whenever possible, establish specific dates to either expect follow-up with the user, receive information from a user, or complete an agreement. This is especially important when warning users of consequential account action.
Take an active role in pursuing a reasonable resolution
(return to index)
Specialists must proactively drive the mediation process by proposing solutions and anchoring the negotiation in facts, rather than acting as a passive messenger.
Lead the negotiation. Do not wait for users to find a middle ground. Take the initiative to present specific compromises and set the pace of the conversation.
Arbitrate based on Thumbtack Terms. Focus on what constitutes a "reasonable effort" to resolve the issue according to platform standards, rather than making moral judgments on who is "right."
Initiate cold calls for complex situations. If an incident involves contradictory documentation, multiple trade experts, or high-dollar estimates, call the reporting party immediately rather than waiting for a booking.
Maintain strict objectivity. Focus on documented facts to avoid vilifying the pro or over-identifying with the customer
Propose specific compromises. If parties are at a stalemate (e.g., a 100% refund demand vs. a 0% offer), suggest a concrete midpoint or a phased resolution, such as:
Proposing a refund amount between the pro's and the customer's offers.
Proposing a refund in installments with specific dates and timing.
Apply creative solutioning. Look for unconventional ways to bridge gaps, such as:
Proposing a refund payment plan if the total amount is a barrier.
If the pro spent significant money on materials that cannot be returned, propose a refund of the labor costs only while the customer keeps the materials.
In cases of minor dissatisfaction, suggest the pro provide a heavily discounted or free service for a future, unrelated project (e.g., a free gutter cleaning for a dissatisfied landscaping customer).
Suggest the users split the cost of an independent, licensed inspector to determine exactly what work was done incorrectly, with both parties agreeing beforehand to follow the inspector’s recommendation.
Ground demands in documentation. Use photos, contracts, and chat logs to explain why a user’s demand may be unreasonable.
Example: "Based on the photos of the completed framing, a full refund is not supported, but a refund for the finishing work is reasonable."
Set firm next steps. Use direct language to move the case forward.
Instead of: "What do you want to do next?"
Use: "I expect a response to this refund proposal by [Date] so we can determine the next phase of your account status."
Exhaust all options. Ensure every "creative solution" has been explored and documented before declaring mediation exhausted.
Help users determine a resolution
(return to index)
When both users are responsive but haven’t agreed on a solution, you’ll need to be more involved in setting expectations so you can move on to the Thumbtack resolution and closing phase. 
Determine who’s responsible, based on the documentation available.
Help determine what solution would be reasonable.
The pro/reported party is clearly responsible for the concern:
Take appropriate action
Provide reasonable and clear deadlines for action, make them aware of potential consequences, and then follow through.
Move forward with the Guarantee afterward, if applicable.
The customer/reporting party is clearly responsible:
Provide clear reasoning for helping them step forward.
Direct them to continue working with the pro.
Note: Let them know if additional documentation could change the outcome.
Unclear who’s responsible: 
Consider using other mediation tools, like New Era.
Note: Let them know if additional documentation could change the outcome. 
THUMBTACK RESOLUTION PHASE
(return to index)
If mediation has run its course and the customer and pro were unable to find a resolution together, review the list below to determine if Thumbtack can offer alternative resources to help them. 
Thumbtack Guarantee
Customer satisfaction payouts
Local resources guide
CLOSING PHASE
(return to index)
Every incident is different, but specialists should know when to end an incident. Use the table below to determine when it’s appropriate to end the incident process.


Incident Status
Steps
The reporting party is unresponsive
Follow contact expectations prior to determining that a user is unresponsive.
Provide clear expectations on response deadlines and potential consequences, prior to actioning incidents or accounts.
Notify both users of the action being taken due to unresponsiveness.
Let both parties know you’ll be closing the incident due to this status.
An agreement was made
Confirm details of the agreement.
Due date.
Work to be done
Amount to be paid.
Set closing expectatifcallons.
Notify the users that you’ll be closing the incident as things are considered resolved, and to follow up again if things change.
Specialists should use their best judgment to determine the appropriate closing time when agreements are made vs. completed.
Mediation resources exhausted with no agreement
When both users are responsive, but the initiator hasn’t accepted a reasonable solution, you may need to step forward so you can close the incident.

Based on the documentation available, confirm that Thumbtack cannot determine a fair solution.
Inform both parties that the incident will be closed, and they will need to pursue further resolutions using their local resources.  
Resolution is delayed
Incident progression has stalled due to waiting on documentation, estimates, etc.
Set clear closing expectations.
Notify the user(s) that the incident will be closed while we wait for them to complete their next steps and reply to the emails to move forward.
Reiterate any relevant deadlines.
SENDING SURVEYS
(return to index)
Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) surveys enable Thumbtack to measure user sentiment and pinpoint areas for improvement. 
Trust and Safety handles difficult situations, and sometimes, users may not agree with the resolution they receive. However, their feedback is important to help make Thumbtack's processes better. The survey should always go out, unless one of the following scenarios applies:


CSAT Survey Exemptions
Automated
A specialist never contacted the user.
The user’s account is removed.
The user has already received a Survey through the same incident.
The incident is a “Limited” record. (Critical escalations, etc.)
Manual
The user never responded to Trust and Safety.
The user has explicitly requested no further contact from Thumbtack.
Manager approved based on risk factors.
If approved, Managers should always leave a note on the incident when approved.
If an incident falls under the manual CSAT survey exemptions above, follow the steps in the Navigate Incident tools doc.
NOTE: When closing reopened incidents, Survey options should be selected based on the most recent interactions with the users.

   Details
    (return to index)
CALL SCHEDULING REQUIREMENTS
(return to index)
To ensure customers and pros have access to calls, Specialists are required to complete the call-scheduling-tool setup as outlined, and:
Have an average of 4 or more hours of bookable call-time per day. (This equals 8 bookable slot options). 
Have Calendar availability that offers as much variety as possible (morning and afternoon options) and is considerate of all time zones. 
Whenever possible, maximize bookable time by scheduling calendar events to end at the top of the hour or half-past the hour to avoid blocking bookable call slots.
COMMUNICATION 
(return to index)
Throughout the incident, certain communication expectations will always apply, unless noted otherwise in the specific process approach. 
Reach out the same day you pick up an incident.
Respond to contacts from users within 48 business hours.
This includes contacts users make to Support.
If the user reaches out, mirror the contact method they used.
If they call, call them. If they emailed, email them.
When reaching out:
Provide introduction
Specialists should introduce themselves at the beginning of an incident or when taking over for another specialist who is out of the office.
For reopened incidents, specialists should use their best judgment to assess the need for reintroduction based on how long the incident has been closed. 
Explain role
Thumbtack’s role should be defined early in the incident, with clear expectations for users.
Note: There isn’t a script or set time to explain Thumbtack’s role. Specialists should use their best judgment to ensure it’s communicated clearly.
The role may need to be clarified again later in the incident, if: 
The user doesn’t understand Thumbtack’s position as a neutral third party.
The user expresses confusion about how Thumbtack mediation works. (e.g., thinks Thumbtack employs pros)
User insists that Thumbtack resolves the issue for them (e.g., reimburses them arbitrarily, send another pro, etc.)
Significant time has passed since previous conversations (e.g., the incident reopened after weeks or months)
Verbiage may differ, but the following should be communicated as clearly as possible. 
Thumbtack is a third-party
Thumbtack mediates between users
Set expectations and next steps.
The specialists' next step (i.e., contacting the other user, waiting on their documentation, etc.)
Steps the customer or pro should take.
When the customer or pro will hear back from Thumbtack.
Show understanding through summarization/paraphrasing.
Offer empathy/acknowledgment when appropriate.
Ask clarifying questions.
Request documentation (if relevant).
Always make the user aware when closing an incident.
Note: Only users with whom you have already been in contact should receive a closing message. 
Ex: If you have only reached out to the customer, there is no need to send a closing message to the pro. 
Phone Calls
(return to index)
Use click-to-call whenever possible.
If the user books a call under a different number, be sure to open the incident after manually dialing to ensure the call record is associated with the correct incident.
Specialists must use the Recording Disclaimer Script at the beginning of all conversations with a user. 
Recording Disclaimer Script: “This call is being recorded by Thumbtack for quality and training purposes.”
Use this disclaimer for every individual outbound connection made with a user, including:
If another user joins a call where the disclaimer has already been mentioned. 
If the call drops or disconnects, a callback is needed.
Warm transfers from Thumbtack Support or Sales only require a brief reminder that the call is recorded.
“This is [Name] on a recorded line.”
NOTE: A disclaimer is not needed when leaving a voicemail.
If a call drops or disconnects mid-conversation, call the user back immediately.
Scheduled calls: 
The first call attempt should be made at the beginning of the scheduled time.
Any first attempts made at the 5-minute mark or later will be considered late. (i.e., if the call is scheduled at 8:00 am, call the user before 8:05)
Any first attempts made after the 30-minute booking will be considered missed.
Any call placed before the booking time is considered a cold call, and the scheduled call must still be made at the original time if it didn’t connect.
If the user doesn’t answer, attempt to call them at least twice.
If a specialist is unable to make a call, including existing calls for incidents taken over, specialists must reach out to leadership or their team to ensure coverage.
Do not cancel or reschedule bookings unless the user specifically requests it. If you believe your situation requires an exception, contact your manager.
Specialists should not restrict users who consistently miss scheduled calls to “email only” unless specifically noted by a manager. 
Cold calls:
Only attempt to call the user between 8:00am - 8:00pm in that user’s timezone.
If the call doesn’t connect, leave a voicemail if the option is available.
Voicemail talking points here.
Send a follow-up email the same day as any connected or attempted calls
Recap what was discussed.
Recap any expectations that were set.
Provide the call scheduling link.
Always leave detailed post-call notes on the incident, including:
What phone number was used (if click-to-call wasn’t available. 
The results of the call
Action items or next steps
Reasons for delayed call attempts, etc.
Voicemails
(return to index)
Specialists should:
State their first name and that they're calling from Thumbtack’s Trust and Safety team.
Be neutral. Share that they are reaching out to the user about an open concern.
Share that they will follow up with an email sent to the email address on file with Thumbtack with more details.
Assume that the voicemail could be shared broadly or heard by unintended ears.
Specialists should NOT:
Share user Personally Identifiable Information (PII) (Ex: phone numbers, email addresses, account numbers, bank info, etc.)
Share full names tied to accounts (first name is fine).
Coach the user, explain reasons behind account termination or suspension, or describe policy or procedure.
   Email
    (return to index)
Specialists should include their call scheduling link in all emails.
In some instances, specialists can remain anonymous or introduce themselves, but not send a call scheduling link:
In-product reports
Reports of Non-discrimination policy violations
Sending a business decision/permanent-removal email.
Note: Remaining anonymous or excluding a call scheduling link outside of these examples should be rare. Make sure to consult with a manager before making this determination and note the incident.
Notify users when expecting to be out of the office. 
Typically, a week in advance is enough notice.
When possible, use Thumbtack macros for official processes.
Format your emails to reflect Thumbtack’s brand.
Use the “_Blank letterhead” from the Select a template dropdown when sending self-written emails
Use Arial font size 9
Keep text black with standard formatting.
Don’t overuse bold or italicized lettering.
Don’t use exclamation marks.
Ensure the incident moves forward in a timely manner.
Ensure each email has a purpose. 
Avoid “filler” or “placeholder” emails that don’t provide new information, updates, or reminders.
Note: Specialists should not send emails simply to meet or extend service levels. (i.e., inform users early when review time is needed and provide a specific date they can expect a follow-up.)
If a user hasn’t responded to your last communication:
Specialists should typically follow up after 2 business days, but should use their best judgment on timing for reminder emails or prompts to unresponsive users.
Reasons a specialist may reach out:
To remind the user of something we need. 
To remind the user of the consequences that will result from not responding. (i.e., account removal or incident being closed)
Note: If there’s a reason to provide users with more than 2 days, Specialists should leave detailed notes on the incident.
Note: Occasionally, specialists may see a contact on their incident from Mailer-Daemon. This is an automatic email service, and Specialists should not respond to it. 
How to determine if a user is unresponsive 
(return to index)
At the start of an incident, either user is considered unresponsive if they haven’t responded after at least three attempts to contact them, with at least one phone call. 
If a user becomes unresponsive mid-incident, use your best judgment to determine if additional calls or emails would be most beneficial.
After 2 unacknowledged follow-up attempts within 5 business days, specialists can close the incident as “unresponsive.”
User is unresponsive after incident automation
(return to index)
If users don’t respond during incident automation, they’ll receive 2 emails. Once these incidents are escalated, specialists will typically need to make one phone call before the above requirements are met.
If automation was started for both the customer and the pro, pay attention to when the incident was escalated. If there is a response from one user, automation will stop for both users, so you may need to send additional contacts manually before considering a user unresponsive.
USING ACCOUNT ACTIONS IN AN INCIDENT
(return to index)
Account Holds
Placing a pro account hold is a temporary measure that prevents the pro from interacting with new users on the platform. This action is typically taken to encourage a response or as a precaution while investigating situations further or awaiting resolution.
Account Removals
Removing an account is a more permanent action that is typically taken when a user is unresponsive or poses a significant risk to others.
When to action an unresponsive account
Once a user is considered unresponsive, you’ll either take action on an account or close the dispute. 
If the reported party is completely unresponsive after reminders, send them an email and remove their account. You may choose to place an account hold first, but this action will vary depending on the incident and has no contact requirements before use.
Notify them why they were removed.
For removals, send the Account action: Pro unwilling to resolve (disable) email macro.
For account holds, send the Account action: Unresponsive pro (place hold) email macro.
Let them know what they can do to retrieve their account.
Notify the other party and move on to any additional relevant processes.
An account shouldn’t be reactivated until the user responds or the concerns have been fully resolved. (Some users may choose to resolve concerns directly with the other party instead of responding to T&S.)
NOTE: DO NOT remove a restriction without first reviewing all action logs thoroughly and confirming all noted issues are already resolved. If an action was taken by another Incident Ops specialist, reach out to them directly to confirm the status of their issue.

NOTES AND DOCUMENTATION
(return to index)
Notes
Incident notes are important for understanding the progression of an incident, so they should be unbiased and factual. Generally, it’s good to leave notes in these scenarios:
Overview
Primary concerns or points of interest.
Callouts of relevant documentation. 
Communication summary
Recap of a phone call or important email.
Action item
These are the next steps or actions that need to be taken by a user or by Thumbtack.
Points of decision-making
Identify what course of action you will be taking, with the reasoning explained.
i.e., “Moving forward with New Era due to high dollar amount and signed contracts.”
Notes can only be edited within 24 hours and only by the specialist who created them.
Documentation
Ensuring incident documentation is well-organized helps streamline payout reviews and makes it easier for other specialists to familiarize themselves with or take over an incident as needed. 
It’s also important to prioritize the security and privacy of all information provided, in accordance with Thumbtack's Privacy Policy.
Don’t share one user’s files with another user unless given explicit permission.
Rename documents in the file manager using the guidelines below:
Clearly label the original contract/original agreement.
Add dollar amounts for documentation that includes payments or estimates.
Be specific about the content in the images.
Number multiple images of the same issue.
i.e., Tiles 01, tiles 02, tiles 03.
The Created By Name section will show who uploaded the file. If a name does not appear here, list “c” or “p” at the front of the new file name to separate customer and pro documentation alphabetically.
Label unnecessary files as x null/x duplicate.
Beginning a file name with “x” will automatically hide it from view.
Keep labels professional.
Avoid using subjective descriptors. 

[Image: rtaImage]

Note: Any files downloaded to a specialist's computer must be deleted, and the trash cleared daily.
PRO IS ALREADY DELETED
(return to index)
If the pro’s account is already deleted (whether it's a self-deletion or T&S deletion), the actions on the incident will vary depending on why it was deleted. Review the table below to determine the next steps to take.

Removal Type
Example
Contact Expectation
Rationale
Business decision (Will not be reconsidered) 
Linked to BD account
Failed BGC
Sexual concerns
No contact required. 
Outreach to these Pros is typically non-productive, and we don’t want to expose TT and customers to engaging with pros that have already been deemed unfit for our platform
Removed for non-incident-related concern
Non-US IP
Payment issues
Profile issues
Linked to an account that *could* resolve the concern (is not BD or failing BGC)
3 contacts (2 emails, 1 call)
The user may not have been notified of concerns leading to removal. Because these issues can be resolved, and an incident impacts their ability to return, current T&S contact standards remain.
Incident-related removal 
Any incident removals.
2 contacts (1 email and 1 phone call)
Pro has been removed for an extended period of time. Should be made aware of the new concerns, but multiple contacts are not necessary.
Note: In situations where the specialists think an exception should be made, consult with leadership and note the incident. 
Regardless of the action needed, make sure to update the deletion log to show the most recent incident/reason the user was removed. If the logs show “user-delete” or don’t give the option to edit, follow the steps below:
Reactivate the pro.
Note why they were briefly reactivated. 
Delete the pro again with updated notes about the most recent incident.

Steps:
Call the customer to let them know that the pro has already been removed and explain the action Thumbtack can take based on the table above. 
Try to be realistic in the expectations you set with the customer.
In situations where calling the pro is appropriate:
If you’re able to reach the pro, explain the situation and help them get back in touch with the customer and move forward with handling the incident as usual.
If the pro doesn’t answer, send them an email.
Depending on the response from the pro, update the customer.
If the pro is responsive, move forward with the chosen process approach.
If the pro wasn’t responsive, proceed with the next steps for the Thumbtack resolution phase. This may include: 
The Thumbtack Guarantee
CSAT payout.
If Thumbtack isn’t able to resolve it either, guide the customer to the right local resources.
Close the incident.
USER WITHDRAWS/DOESN’T WANT TO USE TT PROCESS
(return to index)
Sometimes, a reporting user decides not to pursue their concern further due to time, energy, disagreement with an approach, misunderstanding of Thumbtack’s role, etc. When a customer decides not to move forward with the mediation process, follow the steps below:
Review the chosen process approach.
Is there another tool that Thumbtack can offer that might alleviate their concerns?
Ensure the user understands what T&S can do.
Make sure the user understands Thumbtack’s process by clarifying Thumbtack’s role and emphasizing how we can help. 
If the customer doesn’t feel comfortable having Thumbtack contact the pro, and there’s not a serious behavior/safety concern, offer to take over communication so they don’t need to interact directly.
Offer a phone call
Sometimes, info is easily misunderstood through email. To make sure the customer doesn’t feel like this is their only option, speak with them on the phone to help bridge the gap.
If the customer stops responding or confirms they still don't want to pursue their concern, complete the closing phase as usual. Note that this will affect the Result- customer selection in your incident closure steps.
    Emails
     (return to index)
GENERAL INCIDENT WORK
Intro: Removed pro - Notify of new complaint: This lets the pro know that we’ve received a complaint, and we wanted to let them know, even though they aren’t allowed on the site any longer.
Intro: First to customer (after call): Send this to thank the customer for speaking with you after your phone call.
Intro: First to customer (no call): Send this as an introduction to the customer. It explains our role, asks for more information about the concern, and encourages them to schedule a call to discuss the issue further. 
Follow-up: Request a call (customer): Send this if you have an update for the customer and would like them to call you.
Follow-up: Doesn't want to work with pro: Send this to explain our role to the customer.
Follow-up: Unresponsive customer: Send this if the customer hasn’t responded to our attempts to contact them, and we’re closing their incident.
Follow-up: Stepping back - Customer upset after pro is removed: This lets the customer know that they can pursue the pro on their own using local resources.
Intro: First to pro - Link: Use this email/snippet when contacting the pro for the first time. It directs the customer to schedule a time to speak directly. 
Intro: First to pro (after call): Send this to thank the pro for speaking with you after your phone call.
Closing: Pro resolved issue (thank you): Send this to thank the pro for following through with their agreement.
Closing: Unresponsive customer (pro): Send this to the pro if the customer has become unresponsive while you’re working to get them in contact.
Follow-up: Missed call: Send this email/snippet if a user misses their call. It directs them to reschedule. 
Follow-up: Provide account info to customer: Send when the customer asks for information on the pro, and we’re providing what’s available.
Follow-up: Safety tips: Send to the customer when they’ve expressed concerns about pro behavior or need tips on using the platform safely.
Follow-up: Schedule a call: Use this email/snippet when contacting the customer for the first time. It directs the customer to schedule a time to speak directly. 
Follow-up: Late for call: Use this email/snippet to let the user know that we’re running late for their scheduled call. It directs them to reschedule if needed. 
Follow-up: Missed call: Send this email/snippet if a user misses their call. It directs them to reschedule.
Follow up: Thumbtack's role - cx: Specialists should send this email to customers who don’t understand Thumbtack's role in the dispute process.
ACCOUNT ACTIONS
Closing: Cx withdrawn (flagging) - pro: Send this email to the pro to explain that the customer is not interested in pursuing things further, but we’ll be monitoring their account.
Account action: Unresponsive (place hold) - pro: Specialists should use this email macro if the pro hasn’t responded to their attempts to contact them and they're removing the pro's account.
Account Action: Unresponsive/unwilling (disable) - pro: Specialists should send this email macro if the pro isn’t willing to help or is unresponsive, and you’re removing their account.
Account Actions: Business decision (disable) - cx/pro: Specialists should send this email to the customer or pro when they’ve determined they’re not a good fit for Thumbtack and have removed their account.
Account action: Pro removed - cx: Specialists should send this email macro to customers after removing a pro's account.
GRAMMARLY ONLY
Note: Deletion logs: Use this note in the deletion logs when removing a pro for T&S or Incident issues.

articles.fullText:
Incentive and Referral Fraud

Incentive and referral fraud
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Process Overview
Flowchart

What
​​(return to index)
The Thumbtack Referral Program intends to onboard new high-quality pros and increase pro supply on the platform. However, there are some pros who fraudulently use the referral program to get free credits. The Incentive and Referral Fraud (IRF) Work Ticket queue aims to identify and take action on users who are abusing Thumbtack’s referral program.

Why
(return to index)
Fraudulently using the referral program to get free credits is against Thumbtack’s Terms of Use. This queue monitors referrals to make sure users are using the program as intended.
When
(return to index)
A BigQuery data pull flags pro referrals with either the same device ID, credit card fingerprint, phone number, or matching name, city and state.
Flagged pros will trigger WT creation for manual review. In order to get assigned an IRF WT, you’ll need the “Incentive and Referral Fraud” routing skill in Salesforce Omni.
SLA for the IRF queue is 72 hours, and the target HT is 3.5 minutes.

How
(return to index)
   Steps
     (return to index)
PROCESS OVERVIEW
(return to index)

[Image: Screenshot 2024-11-14 at 12.30.03 PM.png]


Click the Referring User Admin Link and Referred User Admin Link in the Details section of the WT.
Using the same Account Investigation Steps of the Blocklist Hits procedure, determine the links between the referred pro and the referred pro.
Exclusions:
Subcontracting: Pros subcontracting other pros and then referring them is allowed.
Same address with different services: Pros of the same household are allowed as long as they offer different services.
Note: Check the shared values (e.g., using the same phone number, etc.) in the messaging. If the referring pro seems to be circumventing the platform by just creating a fake account, we should take action.
Note: If the user profile is blank, it means that they just signed up. Compare accounts using the available info.
If the accounts are strongly linked and aren't considered an exclusion:
Ban both pros from Pro Referral Incentives by checking the checkbox next to “Banned from Pro Referral Incentives?” under Pro Statuses in Admin.
[Image: AD_4nXfJrW-r7f5e0eNzWw7Oe53IjdSRHMyS6N_epobRaUCoL2ku1gqh1RYPWSeG0g2kaNxn0NKeromte0OkR3sl2ndZoAVZVVDVh5xQjf88lthrgTyUVSMnXjnAmeGWdiu3Q5WK0xOF2s6d3QNk-tuoAU1x3w]
Revoke granted user credit.
Go to Credits and click on the Thumbtack Balance link in Admin.
Click on the Revoke Granted Credits link on the right-hand side.
Revoke Amount in (Dollars) = “Credit already Granted to Referred User in Cents” from the WT Details divided by 100.
If the outstanding granted balance is less than the amount to revoke, then revoke the balance they do have. Add Internal Notes on the WT. Reason to revoke granted credits =
Revoke to revoke granted credits = “Revoke for other reasons”
Admin notes = "insert WT#: LInked to referring pro-PK: insert number - Referral Pro PK: insert number.
Then click Submit.
Close the WT.
Outcome:
Accurate - If the accounts are strongly linked.
Inaccurate - If the accounts are not strongly linked or are part of an exclusion.
Internal Notes:
How the pros are linked (if applicable).
If the amount revoked was less than initially granted due to a lower balance (if applicable).
If either or both accounts are already banned from pro referral incentives or have their accounts disabled before working the WT.
FLOWCHART
(return to index)

[Image: Screenshot 2024-11-14 at 12.31.26 PM.png]


**Use the content request form to request an update or submit questions/concerns**

articles.fullText:
In-Product Payments (incidents)

 
 In-Product payments (incidents)
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Process overview
Thumbtack on-demand bookings
Thumbtack Pay
How to refund customers
Customer/pro agreed refund
Reverse pro funds
Guarantee payout
Processing a refund through product
Details
Support vs. Trust and Safety issues
Customers chargebacks
Talking Points
What
(return to index)
Thumbtack now supports payments directly through our product , through Thumbtack Pay and Thumbtack on-demand bookings.
If a customer has paid in-product, incident handling will be the same, except sometimes the refund will be granted through Thumbtack’s platform. 
Why
(return to index)
Thumbtack wants to be the one-stop shop for users to get their jobs done, especially home-related projects. In-product payments make it easier to hire pros and conduct business on our platform.
When
(return to index)
Customers can use Thumbtack Pay to complete pro payment requests directly through Thumbtack or use the on-demand flow to book and pay for jobs immediately. In either case, the customer is charged through product.
When customers have paid through Thumbtack, and there’s a safety or project concern, Trust and Safety will support mediation, facilitate refunds, and grant Guarantee payouts as needed.
Support Operations can handle and process some refunds for in-product payments. If you’ve picked up an incident involving an in-product payment and it looks like a deposit no-show, review if it’s something that can be handled by Support Ops.
Any situation that doesn’t fit Trust and Safety guidelines should be sent back to Support. Submit Categorization feedback as needed. 
How
(return to index)
   Steps
   (return to index)
PROCESS OVERVIEW
(return to index)
Confirm the project involves an in-product payment:
Thumbtack on-demand bookings
Thumbtack Pay
Review for a chargeback.
If a chargeback hasn’t been initiated, inform the customer that filing a dispute with their financial institution can limit our ability to help and extend the timeline of our resolution process.
Begin the appropriate dispute resolution process: 
Expedited incident
Move to step 4b.
Standard incident
Move to step 4.
Review the dispute resolution outcome to decide how to move forward:         
If the customer and pro come to an agreement:
Ensure their agreement is documented in your incident.
Move forward with a customer/pro agreed refund and reverse pro funds.
Before processing, double-check for any new chargebacks.
If the pro didn’t resolve, was unresponsive, or we’re not requiring them to be involved:
Remove or flag the pro as appropriate.
Review Guarantee eligibility.
If eligible, move forward to grant a Guarantee payout.
Before processing, double-check for any new chargebacks.
If ineligible, follow the steps in the Eligibility: Ineligible section of the Thumbtack guarantee knowledge article.
Close the incident.

KEY
✔ = Required
✘ = Not required, but use at your discretion

IN-PRODUCT PAYMENT ACTIONS





  RESOLUTION PROCESS  
  Mediation 
  Resolve Payment Disputes 
  Flag Customer 
  Flag Pro 
  Remove Pro 
Expedited incidents
✘
✔
✔
✔
✘
Standard incident

✔
✔
✔
Tip: If the pro has been involved in 3-4 previous payouts, consider requiring them to participate in mediation. 
THUMBTACK ON-DEMAND BOOKINGS
(return to index)
Thumbtack on-demand bookings (ToD) give customers the chance to book and pay for jobs immediately without having to pick or negotiate with pros.
Thumbtack identifies the pros and schedules the jobs. When the jobs are completed, pros can mark the job as done to get paid for their completed work.
How to identify on-demand projects
Look for an orange banner at the top of the incident stating, “This Incident is related to a Thumbtack on Demand Fulfillment Request.” 

[Image: 2lRze7JxhjJj8DEwRDWUBsRynOnb3Qnx9UzbUNMu8bmms3tui00xoBd1sk03AzRjDXBIOE2qxq_BOjJxy2FCoJT1NB_UIxxbuLuQDeQo9SmXA8Sd694Q3MpXQMwI303b5NDsvw7o7ejzSHwUDKNTj_k]

If you don’t see this banner, move to the next step.
Open the project request in Admin.
Review the Request Intro Type field. If it shows “FULFILLMENT,” this is an on-demand booking. 
You’ll see this same field on both the Request view and the Bid view.
If you didn’t see the banner, but this shows “FULFILLMENT,” update the Request PK in your incident’s Project tab.
 [Image: -o_oqY3WmBuUiTexU20B0rzaOT78JyrdvVtloMstloAGl99wc2w0cctSV3AI8CViRoQueWknPczLQcMNumogNUWOdeTfKJTNmwEQaQ-zXG5TOwI4SdUltY3TKIt9ZawV4_NJ7CpWHsVerBtvpz8yqKs]
Confirm that the customer was charged and the pro received payment. If the customer was charged, the funds will only be released to the pro if they mark the job as done.
Scroll toward the bottom of the page to the Fulfillment section.
Click View Full Transaction History.
[Image: z6PL1vpt7AVmDxOsSElvR3bPLcOg8ENZ5Xc0We07CSJz0pzyFxP1U3Q0MA3BtVMtbYWqGy_sVTmhFZSyQ20DmIrB3ZfQx0GBDxHFREPsM7Pc07Hw-jcXMjwfzmTFI9S_FXJci3N1smnE0_v0hIItMmk]
This will open the Request Payment Activity page.
[Image: 4selug8cWCbz0USjFrKJdeWEq5wnu5PsNCkxuN3y_gughaqy9kqrVMPGiLNQlthJRNMGQ8E4IZbyvrDEhdaB7OWYPQIkBHf6I6GAKqIj4xIiJCu6M4zhF_8Vs136195OE6a96K01ko8AyIgwQoHNysI]
When the Item Type is “JOB,” that row is the customer’s payment.
Transaction Status will show “TRANSACTION_SUCCESS” if the customer’s charge was successful.
When the Item Type is “TRANSFER,” that row is the pro’s payout.
Transaction Status will show TRANSACTION_SUCCESS if the pro was sent the payment.
Note: If the Transaction Status for JOB shows “GATEWAY_FAILED,” it means the customer’s payment was unsuccessful. Review the status of the pro’s payout and their project to confirm if reimbursement should be pursued from either party.
THUMBTACK PAY
(return to index)
Customers have the option to pay a pro through Thumbtack.
How to identify Thumbtack Pay
Look for an orange banner at the top of the incident stating, “This Incident shows a TRANSFER payment type.” 

[Image: zj3mJLFi-CSOeYJqatda6Ofr_9Zs2oog7r0AJL5xNzCLASd69nUGpFQzRtpz5EM6zNj0Z48TxnCcXuwD_MnfJbTL9zp-rvQwpUuOYufaWQ-Wkd2HzS8F_RkI54Ty5Cvi7mTEildFGgsnLQb5ansxSmA]

To confirm payment status, open the bid in Admin. 
Tip: You can click the Bid PKID link in the incident’s Customer tab.
Scroll down below the message thread to “Marketplace Payments.”
If the Customer to Thumbtack Payments Section appears, then the customer initiated payment through Thumbtack, so review the status of the payment underneath the Customer to Pro Payment Transaction Logs.

[Image: uf1d6p4yulc83WRAJi6GtdRaajdqUarhBKF5tXcNfsjiMPwL5ZkcQLYPO5_pJy-gF3u_JS9frlxuzVgt6dliXeItdfRU0k6Clm7DCWDzOuzSYTjRVJKkhZPzpwDmuIHnzNnKh_ZSQMry9EechGusdS4]

When the Item Type is “JOB,” that row is the customer’s payment.
Transaction Status will show “TRANSACTION_SUCCESS” if the customer’s charge was successful.
When the Item Type is “TRANSFER,” that row is the pro’s payout.
Transaction Status will show TRANSACTION_SUCCESS if the pro was sent the payment.

Pros have the option to opt out of direct deposit, in which case they wouldn’t be able to receive the customer’s payment. If a pro doesn’t have direct deposit set up, they wouldn’t have received payment through the product, even if the customer has paid. Many of these scenarios will fall under support issues, so it’s important to verify that the pro did receive the payment.
HOW TO REFUND CUSTOMERS
(return to index)

IN-PRODUCT PAYMENTS REFUNDS





OUTCOME

Guarantee/CSAT eligible
Through payout process
Through product
Reverse pro funds
Customer/pro agreed

N/A
✘
✔
✔
Pro didn’t resolve

✔
✔
✘
✘
Pro involvement not required
$500 or less
✔
✘
✔
✘
Pro involvement not required
$501+
✔
✔
✘
✘

Customer/pro agreed refund
(return to index)

If we’ve gone through the appropriate dispute resolution process and confirmed the customer and pro have agreed on a refund amount, we can facilitate the refund from the pro to the customer through the platform using the refund reasons below. We will not need to gather any Ironclad forms for these refunds.
We can refund any amount up to the amount the customer paid in-product, as long as the customer and pro have both confirmed the resolution amount. Be sure to gather clear confirmation from the pro to refund the amount on their behalf and notate your incident accordingly.
Pros can also refund customers directly outside of Thumbtack, so you may want first to confirm how the customer prefers to receive their refund. If the customer wants it back to the card they paid with, we’ll need to assist.

REFUND REASON
DEFINITION
 Deposit No Show
The pro didn’t show, the pro was paid, and the customer/pro agreed to a refund amount before or through mediation.
 Work Not Complete
The pro didn’t finish the work and the customer/pro agreed to a refund amount before or through mediation. 
 Unsatisfactory Work
The job was done poorly and the customer/pro agreed to a refund amount before or through mediation. 
 Property Damage
Accidental damage occurred on the job and the customer/pro agreed to a refund amount before or through mediation.

Reverse pro funds
(return to index)

When refunding through the platform, you’ll have the option to reverse pro funds. This would take the funds from the pro’s bank account when refunding the customer. Currently, this should only be done in the customer/pro-agreed refund scenarios. Clear confirmation and documentation of their agreement are important to help speak to this action.
If you’ve processed a refund and selected “Yes” on reverse pro funds, you can check the status in the transaction logs. Review this to ensure the pro reversal was successful.

[Image: wZRE9auz7I90jNFB0_cuAhwPq120veKATMLifuCUteuBFmmf6t3sWscmzkCEicRSZ5qAvc4dvNsehxDrZovvnG4zjkLsg6FbHPwdRpLOaMWsqjqb3WXhi1xQ-BKcqP2HVGRX0l1O7Xo29vnpUxwU1Y0]

Note: If you discover the pro reversal failed, action their account accordingly. If they follow up, send them the macro MBG - Pro reaches out after the customer was paid (pro removed) to begin the process of repayment.
Guarantee payout
(return to index)

Guarantee through payout process

If you’re handling a $501+ incident, or it’s below, and you’ve determined to involve the pro in mediation, we won’t be paying out through the platform at this time. These payouts will be handled through the usual MBG/PDG/CSAT payout process.
Reminder: Be sure to check in Salesforce for any corresponding chargebacks before paying a customer out.
Guarantee through product

Based on the scenario, you may choose not to involve the pro in mediation (such as for $250 or less AND expedited incidents). If this is the case and you’ve determined they’re eligible under the Guarantee/CSAT, you may move forward with a Guarantee payout through the product, using the refund reasons below. We will not need to gather any Ironclad forms for these refunds.
Note: There may be times when the full payment was made in-product and outside the Thumbtack platform. If the pro wasn’t involved in mediation, and the amount paid on Thumbtack is $500 or less, refund their in-product payment through the product and the rest of their eligible payout amount through the usual payout process. 

REFUND REASON 
DEFINITION
Money-Back Guarantee
A project dispute occurred, and we’ve determined they’re eligible for the MBG. The pro wasn’t involved in mediation, and the payout amount is $500 or less. 
Property Damage Guarantee
A project dispute occurred, and we’ve determined they’re eligible for the PDG. Pro wasn’t involved in mediation, and the payout amount is less than $250.
Customer Satisfaction Guarantee
Used discretionarily by Trust and Safety for safety, discrimination, and other sensitive and poor experiences outside the norm. The pro wasn’t involved in mediation, and the payout amount is $500 or less. 
Reminder: If we’re not involving the pro and refunding a customer through the product, under any of the Guarantee/CSAT refund reasons, we should select “No” on reversing pro funds.
Processing a refund through product
(return to index)
Confirm the situation has met the above requirements for a refund through product.
Click Refund the Payment in Admin.
For on-demand bookings, this will be found in the job request.
[Image: aIeqlp00cLSM5ZpQiyBwkwfOd5LFLKGrAcokjNQWH2HHq6SAqpgwUDx7dbo-ESIZu_3I5_6ihtmOP6VmbtxxyJZOWCgnWts2k-GEW6HXUQfl0F0-HXG9GUwtKl189z2CPVjdCxbqMmcZgn4xfkVaBHM]
For Thumbtack Pay transactions, this will be found in the bid.

[Image: nZmDOFNwE_u7cxKg8kjbJKnN3nIVD2wZ1sRxFZYLoxwujv7k_penuII-Yp2tAduUT6ET9tFX1bDcAIwZIB1ujpzQkIY9P3pvsHLPzuRh_FMonzOPs0GA2koJNNU6JVINthRY9awN-IMRr3ndUTkF6cQ]

On the Refund Payment page, select the refund reason following the charts above.
Reminder: Don’t utilize the Support Ops’ refund reasons, which include:
Fulfillment Fail, Customer No Show, Pro No Show, Pro Late Cancel, Cancellation Fee Refund, and Other.
Input the appropriate refund amount.
Typically, the amount the customer paid will just be the Job amount, but if there is any Discount amount listed, you will need to subtract that when inputting the refund amount. In this example, the refund amount would be $29.99.
If you’re handling a customer/pro agreed refund situation, select “Yes” for Trigger reversal for pro.
In the notes, include the Trust and Safety case number where the pro’s confirmation/agreement can be found.
Double-check the information to ensure it is correct, then click Refund.
[Image: rtaImage]
Note: If you come across an error, be sure to check for any corresponding chargebacks. You won’t be able to process a refund through product if there has been a chargeback.
   Details
	(return to index)
SUPPORT OPS VS. T&S ISSUES
(return to index)
 
SUPPORT OPS
TRUST AND SAFETY
On-demand bookings
User no-shows (for any reason, canceling, rescheduling, etc.) AND the pro has not marked the job as done.
Fulfillment issues.
User no-shows, AND the pro has marked the job as done.
Any safety or project quality issue, regardless of whether the job is marked as done or not.
Thumbtack Pay
User no-shows where Support Ops has contacted the pro, and they confirmed a refund.
Logistical issues (i.e., the pro only wants to be paid outside of Thumbtack)
User no-shows where the user is unresponsive to the other user and Support Ops.
Any safety or project quality issue, including if the customer and pro have agreed to a refund.
Note: For deposit-no-shows involving Thumbtack Pay, Support Ops will have already attempted to contact the pro prior to escalating to Trust and Safety. You’ll want to search for the Support case and attach it to your incident. Because of the previous attempts, one call attempt and follow-up email will be sufficient before actioning the pro’s account.
Customer chargebacks
(return to index)

Customers may initiate a chargeback on an in-product payment, which would come to the Trust and Safety Payments team.
If we’re refunding an in-product payment through the usual MBG/PDG/CSAT payout process, we’ll want to ensure customers haven’t initiated or won a chargeback already because they’d end up double-paid. To prevent this, follow the steps below:
Use the customer’s PKID to search for a payment dispute work ticket (WT) in Salesforce. 

[Image: ulfEyhfcGylRIcbqE1qJz-L-9G7Pen7Eql2XEQqV1kIj73piKIkXfVYzTkH1jv686CRJSe4yt3A2GtKIeSv-3aeOmIK6xEjZG-8pcT0KGixaPLRHn3OS1lnHdnD5YiM3htxKpNE_-MAPce3N4RX4Hp8]

If there’s a WT for the same in-product payment related to your dispute, open it and check the internal notes for additional information:
Accepted CB means that the chargeback was accepted by our team, and the customer received the money back already.
If the chargeback was accepted, don’t proceed with a refund and notify the customer they’ve already received the money back through their chargeback dispute.
Disputed CB means we responded and are working with the customer’s bank to verify that this was a valid charge.
Use the chargeback dashboard to search for the user PK and check the current status.
If the chargeback status is pending, instruct the customer to contact their bank to drop the dispute and provide documentation before we can move forward with a refund.
Work with your manager and the T&S Payments team to determine if it would be better to accept the chargeback so that they can get their money back instead
If the chargeback status is lost, don’t proceed with a refund and notify the customer that they’ve already received the money back through their chargeback dispute.
If there are no outcomes/notes on the WT, then it likely came in that day and still needs to be actioned by our team.
Use the chargeback dashboard to search for the user PK and check the current status.
If there’s still no information, post in the #ts-proactive-ops-questions Slack channel for more information on the status.
   Talking Points
    (return to index)
FAQ: I paid through Thumbtack. Can’t you just send me my money back? 
While Thumbtack does process the payment, payment is made to the business directly. In the rare cases where the service provider doesn’t resolve a concern themselves, we’re here to help provide further direction.
I can see why you’d like [STATE CONCERNS] resolved right away. Thumbtack has options for customers to pay service providers through our platform, though we remain a third party to the job. We’d like to give _______ the opportunity to address your concerns before we take additional action.

**Use the content request form to request an update or submit questions/concerns**

Image Review

Image Review
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Details
Process overview
Flowcharts

Emails
Related
What
(return to index)
The Image Review (IR) queue screens images uploaded by pros in their profile for any Terms of Service (TOS) violations.
Types of images to review:
Pro Profile Photo
Service Profile Photo
Past Project(s) Photo
Why
(return to index)
Thousands of pros and customers sign up on Thumbtack every day. While most users create profiles and use the platform as intended, some try to use the site in ways that violate our Terms of Use and Content and Review Policy.
To protect the Thumbtack brand and our users' experience, we proactively ensure that no images in a pro's profile violate our TOS. This ensures that the platform remains a trustworthy and safe environment for all users.
When
(return to index)
Any time a pro uploads an image to their user profile, service profile or past project(s), it is sent to an image recognition system (AWS Rekognition) for detection, analysis and labeling. Each label has an assigned threshold that determines whether a work ticket will be generated for manual review. The image is not blocked and will remain live on the site until it is manually reviewed and deleted.
SLA for Image Review is 24 hours, and the HT target is 2 minutes.
OUT OF SCOPE 
Customer review images are out of scope for this queue. Ideally, the workaround is to delete the review containing images that violate our TOS. Please refer to Fake Reviews KA for more information on how to delete a review.
How
(return to index)
   Details
   (return to index)
PROCESS OVERVIEW
(return to index)

[Image: rtaImage]
Review the Work Ticket Details. 
Click the Image Review link in the Work Ticket Details. This will open the image review portal in Admin.
[Image: rtaImage]
Review the image for any TOS violations.
If the image has been removed, click the View Original button to see the original image uploaded. 
If the image is not showing, change your GlobalProtect VPN Gateway location to US (any region) then re-click the Image Review link.
[Image: rtaImage]
NOTE: If there is text in the image that’s not in English, take a screenshot of the text only and utilize Google Lens or Google Translate to translate the text in English. After evaluation, delete the screenshot right away.
Disclaimer: Any images downloaded must be deleted from your computer immediately, and should never be saved, shared, emailed, etc. Downloading personal files/images is a data privacy concern. These should be used only for their purpose, and then deleted immediately.
If the image is something that should be escalated, refer to the Critical Escalations Knowledge Article.
If applicable, delete the image by clicking the Delete Image button*. 
If the button is grayed out, the image has already been deleted, and no further action is required in Admin.  
If the Admin Action(s) depends on the number of offenses, refer to the Check Number of Offenses section for instructions on how to validate.
As applicable, action the user account in Admin by clicking on the User admin link*.
Fill out the Outcome and Admin Actions sections in the WT*. 
NOTE: If there are multiple TOS violations found on an image, action should be taken based on the more serious violation. Tag all TOS violations found in the Work Ticket. 
Save all the changes and close the tab in Salesforce to receive the next Work Ticket.
*Refer to the “Image Review - New” tab under Summary of Admin Action & Tagging for all Admin actions and applicable Salesforce selections.

Click the location you want to connect to.
CHECK NUMBER OF OFFENSES
(return to index)
Copy the Pro’s PKID in User Admin Link under the Work Ticket Details.
Paste it in Salesforce’s Search Bar to search for other Image Review Tickets in Salesforce.
Review all completed Image Review Tickets for this Pro’s PKID with Confirmed Violation in the Outcome field and check Internal Notes for offense count on this TOS violation.
