ID Help

ID Help
(Knowledge index)

INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Disclaimer
Guideline overview
Starting ID Help Cases
Identifying issue type
Personal info change
License verification
Account transfer
Data Privacy Deleted Accounts
SSN-less background check
Business name change
Authorized license user
Minor account (18 and under)
Account access dispute
Email change requests
ID help tricky situations.
Details
Sending emails in cases
Comparing ID to Verification Data
Verifying and deleting licenses
Closing ID Help cases
Talking points
Documentation we accept
Emails
Multi-purpose
Personal info change
License verification
Account transfer
SSN-less background check
Business name change
Authorized license user
Account access dispute
Email change requests
Minor
Account take over
Troubleshooting
Can’t find account
Related
Navigate Au10tix
Navigate Checkr
What
​​(return to index)
The ID Help case queue is where we assist Thumbtack users (mainly pros) who need help with:
Personal information changes.
Account owner name.
Date of birth.
Account transfers.
Business name changes when:
The business is verified.
The business has a verified license.
Licenses.
Authorized license users
Licenses that the licensing team was unable to verify.
SSN-less background checks
Account access disputes.
Reactivating accounts mistaken as being owned by minors.
Email Change Requests
Email change 
Account Take Over
Why
​​(return to index)
This queue allows us to keep users’ personal identifiable information (PII) secure by locking access to the queue/case type and by automatically deleting their files after 30 days. It also allows us to further promote safety on Thumbtack, by reviewing all requests and denying those with other unresolved issues on the account.
When
​​(return to index)
Once a user submits their request through our online intake form, a case is created and sent to our queue for review.
SLA for the ID Help queue is 72 hours and AHT is 12.6 minutes.
How
​​(return to index)
   Steps
   ​​(return to index)
Disclaimer: Any files downloaded MUST be deleted at the end of your shift. Documentation should never be saved, shared, emailed, etc. Downloading personal files is a data privacy concern and should be used only for their purpose then deleted.

GUIDELINE OVERVIEW
(return to index)
 

 ISSUE TYPE:
CHANGE IS ALLOWED:
REQUIRED DOCUMENTATION:
CHANGE IS DENIED:
Personal info change
Change account name or DOB if:
The person requesting it is the existing account owner.
The change matches their legal documents (legal name, correct date of birth).
Current government-issued ID
Proof of change (in some cases)
Don’t change personal info if:
They’re trying to change who owns the account.
Offer account transfer instead.
The change doesn’t match their legal documents.
License verification
Verify the license if:
License is active, belongs to the account holder, and matches one of the dropdown options.
Current government-issued ID
Professional license
Link to the state database (in some cases)
Don’t verify if:
We don’t verify that license type.
The license is expired.
The license owner doesn’t match the account owner.
We can’t find the license in online databases.
Account transfer
Transfer the account if the account owner:
Passed away.
Sold the company and all of its assets to a new owner.
Hired or changed the manager of a franchise location. 
Left the company, AND no other changes are being made to the business.
Is/was a family member of the account owner (and doesn’t own/partially own the business)
Current government-issued ID
Proof of the change (unless we find it online)
Ironclad Account Transfer Agreement
Don’t transfer the account if the account owner:
Didn’t provide documented proof of the change.
Hasn’t sold their business but wants someone else to run the account.
They can delegate an authorized user.
Sold the company, and the new owner is making drastic changes to the company, like:
Staff.
Company name.
Services provided.
Anything that would impact reviews. 
We requested a background check and haven’t received their submission yet.
SSN-less background check
Send the SSN-less link if:
The ID matches the account owner, and Au10tix results say “passed.”
Exception: ID expired within 18 months, and that’s the only reason it didn’t pass.
Current government-issued ID
Don’t send the SSN-less link if:
The ID doesn’t belong to the account owner.
Au10tix results aren’t “passed.”
Business name change
Remove verification if:
Requester is the account owner.
Business name is locked.
Current government-issued ID
Don’t remove verification if:
Requester isn’t the account owner.
Business name isn’t locked.
Authorized license user
Verify the license if:
The license owner verified that they are authorized.
The license owner and account owner both signed our form.
Current government-issued ID for license owner
Professional license
Ironclad agreement
Pros can’t display another individual’s license if:
They don’t have permission from the license owner.
We didn’t receive a form signed by both the license and account owner. 
They’re not legally authorized to work under the license. 
The license is expired.
The license owner revokes the authorization. 
Minor account
Reopen the account if:
The ID matches the account and shows that the owner is 18 or older.
Current government-issued ID
Don’t reopen the account if:
The ID doesn’t match the account.
The ID doesn’t show that they’re 18 or older.
Account access dispute
Delete the reported account if:
The reporter proves they own the business, and the account owner doesn’t match the reporter’s ID. 
Current government-issued ID
Proof of business ownership
Don’t take action if:
The reporter can’t prove they own the business.
The reporter and account owner are both owners of the business.
Email Change

Complete email change when
ID passes Au10tix 
ID matches the name and DOB on the account.
User’s account is deactivated due to an open issue (linked account Issue), and needs to change email to get communication from TT.
Current government-issued ID.
Don’t take action if:
ID submitted did not pass Au10tix. 	
If ID details (e.g., name) are different from the ones on Thumbtack account.

STARTING ID HELP CASES
​​(return to index)
Receive Case (auto-assigned through Omni).
Click Details on the right side of the case.
Find the Web Name and Web Email.

[Image: Screenshot 2023-11-29 at 7.52.51 AM.png]

Assign the Thumbtack User for new cases.Note: If the email used in the request does not show any Thumbtack account, send the email macro, Cant find Thumbtack account.
Click the Find User tab next to Details.
Use the Web Email from step 2 to search for an account.
Add the contact if it already exists in Salesforce, or create a new one if it doesn’t.
Existing contact:
Click the small box/image to the left of the name that appears, then click Confirm.
New contact:
Click Add New.
Fill out the fields with the user’s email and first and last name, then click Create.
Back under Details, find and read the Description for information on what the user needs.
Optional: copy and paste the description to the case feed to keep all the info in one place.

[Image: Screenshot 2023-11-29 at 7.54.19 AM.png]

Check the Files section on the left side of the case for the attached files.
The ID Help form requires files for all but the “authorized license user” flows.
All files are automatically deleted after 30 days to protect sensitive information.

[Image: Screenshot 2023-11-29 at 7.55.29 AM.png]

Check Case History by clicking on View All to search for duplicate cases. If there are duplicate cases, you may assign them to you and close them as "Duplicate."
Add notes: “Duplicate of case____” and respond to the pro using your original case.

[Image: Screenshot 2023-03-29 at 11.06.54 AM.png]
In the user’s admin, check:
The Account Status (directly under their name).
If it’s anything other than enabled, check why in Page Actions.
Blocklisted - check Blocklist Record.
Account Hold - check Account Hold Logs.
Disabled - check Deletion Logs.
If the deletion log says “user delete,” send the Update account - user delete macro and wait for their answer before moving forward.
If anything mentions linked users, check Show Linked Users.
This can help us make sure we’re working on the right account.
If there are violations that need to be resolved, the user must resolve them before we’ll continue with their ID Help case. Send them ID Help - Resolve account issue first and close the case.
The status of the user’s background check in Identity Status.
“Requires Background Check” means they need to take a background check.
“Requires Submission/Resubmission/New Submission” all mean they didn’t provide all data this can be resolved by updating verification data with the info on their ID.
If the user has been badged for background check, please check BGC report in Checkr and ensure the ID, Admin, and Checkr details (First name, last name and DOB) are the same to continue with the request. If it is not the same, here are the steps:
Scenario 1: If Checkr name and ID are the same but the TT admin name is different:
We only need to update the admin name and need not send BGC.
Scenario 2: If Admin name, Checkr name is different from ID name:
Verify that they own the business. (this applies if the name on the ID is totally different from what is on admin- we can skip this if the name on ID and admin are only different due to misspelled names or legal name change/marriage.)
Verify ID in Au10tix, if they pass, proceed with name change and send SSN-less link BGC on your email response.
Update User Identity information to match ID.
DELETE BGC existing badge and add the Reason: Updated Admin Name to match ID. Need to retake BGC with correct name/info.
Send email macro ID Help - Account Details are different from Checkr - Need to retake BGC. Add a line to explain why they need to retake BGC.
If the user has a Services section.
If they do, it’s a pro account. If they don’t, it’s a customer account.
The status of the user’s license under Licenses.
If you can’t find an admin account for the user, ask for the right account using the Can’t find account macro.
Use all the info you found to determine which issue type the user needs help with.
 
Note: Occasionally, we’ll receive cases that didn’t come from the ID Help form. You can usually skip steps 2-5 in that instance.
 
IDENTIFYING ISSUE TYPE
​​(return to index)
Before you attempt to identify the issue type, be sure to first follow all steps to prepare your ID help case and review the account.
Most issue types are easy to identify based on what the user chose in the form (what you see in Details):
Authorized license user if they stated they’re an authorized user of someone else’s license.
License verification if the user stated their license wasn’t verified and they included a business license.
Account access dispute if the user stated someone is accessing their account that shouldn’t be.
Minor account if they stated their account was removed because they’re believed to be under 18.
SSN-less background check if they chose “background check.”
You can double-check if this is the right path by checking if the user’s Identity Status says “requires background check." If they don’t have a case in the background check mismatch queue, it’s likely an SSN-less case.
To check cases, look under Thumbtack User and click View all to the right of Cases. Check for cases that say "mismatch."
If the user needs help with their personal or business info, an account transfer, or if they chose one of the above but the info doesn’t quite add up, they might need:
Account transfer
If the user is trying to change whose name is on the account (rather than correcting the existing name ), this is the process to follow regardless of what they chose on the form. 
Personal info change
If the user needs the account owner's name or date of birth corrected (but not changed to a different person’s info ), this is the process you should follow.
Business name change
This process is for changing the name of the business/service itself.
Email Change - If they chose any of the above but the Details state they would like to update their email address.
If you don’t have enough information to learn what the user needs, send ID Help - Unclear what user needs.
If you know what the user needs but none of the above (not an ID help concern), refer the pro to the team that should help with the issue using the macro ID Help - Resolve account issue first. (Edit the template if needed). We can transfer the case to MTS - General if it's a linked account dispute.
Under the Details tab, click on the “person” icon.
[Image: Screenshot 2024-06-20 at 2.11.38 PM.png]
Choose Queues.
Look for MTS General, then click on the Change Owner button. Make sure to leave notes on the case.
[Image: Screenshot 2024-06-20 at 2.12.15 PM.png]
[Image: Screenshot 2024-06-20 at 2.12.42 PM.png]
 
Note: If you have any doubt that what they chose was the right option, send them through the SSN-less process.
PERSONAL INFO CHANGE
​​(return to index)
Follow these steps to prep the case.
The reporting user should have already included:
Their ID.
Double-check that this is the current account owner asking for their name (or DOB) to be altered by comparing the ID with the user’s Verification Data.
Some of the verification data likely won’t match (that’s what they need help with). If enough matches that you believe it’s the same person, you can move forward.
If the ID doesn’t match/nearly match the account or it’s a different person wanting their name on the account, send them the ID Help - Personal info - name mismatch/misspelled macro and close the case.
Request additional documentation if needed using the ID Help - Need more info macro.
For misspelled names or users who want their middle name added, the ID may be enough.
For name changes, we need documentation of the change, such as:
Marriage license
Divorce decree
Legal name change petition
We require legal names on our accounts, so we’ll only make changes that match their legal documentation.
Send ID Help - Personal info - legal name if they want you to change their name to something other than their legal name.
If they can't provide the proof we need, send the Need documentation - closing macro and close the case.
If they’ve provided all the appropriate documentation, update their account name.
Note: If ID seems suspicious, upload ID in Au10tix for additional verification. If they pass, continue with the next step.
If not, click into the results to get more information and ask pro for documentation using ID Help - Need more info macro.
In the user’s admin, click Edit Identity Information on the top right side.
Add the info needed based on the info/documentation the user provided, then click Submit.
Send the ID Help - Successfully completed macro and close the case.
LICENSE VERIFICATION
​​(return to index)
Follow these steps to prep the case.
The reporting user should have already included their professional license or ID.
In admin, under the Licenses section, check the license verification request that matches the document submitted by the pro, (usually, it’s the most recent) and click Full License Check. 

[Image: Screenshot 2023-11-28 at 3.23.18 PM.png]
Verify the license information in the database and the submitted documents.
Identify the issue: 
License type: Check if we verify the license type under Licenses in admin.
If it is not a type we verify, send them the macro ID Help - License - can’t verify and close the case.
If the license type on the document is not listed in the drop-down options or in the admin but is related to an existing license type, escalate it to US License Verification POC through the License Type Clarification sheet.
Note: Check if it has been escalated before.
License Information: Compare the on the license to the Admin Verification Data.
See the License Verification Quickview and Match vs Mismatch criteria to determine if the license should be verified.
If the license does not belong to the account owner, send the ID Help - License - doesn’t match account macro and close the case.
If the name doesn’t match in admin but the submitted ID and DB are a match, send the ID Help - License - update name macro and close the case.
Once the pro sends in their ID, update the name, delete the background check badge, and require the user to retake a background check.
License not found:
Check if we have the right link to the database.
If it’s the wrong link, search the internet with the license type, state name, and the word “lookup.” (i.e., Contractor license TN lookup)
Look for any official licensing board or .gov websites that appear to match what you are looking for.
If you cannot find the correct website or the license on it, send ID Help - License - not found macro and close the case.
If Pro provided an alternative link where we verified his license, escalate it to US License Verification POC through the License Type Clarification sheet to check if we need to update the current link in admin. 
Expiration date: Take note of the issue date and expiration date.
If expired, delete the license, send ID Help - License - not found macro, and close the case.
If the submitted information would be considered a match, verify the license and notify the user using the ID Help - License - Verified macro and close the case.
If there is no license verification request in admin, wrong information, or it is already deleted, add license verification to the pro's profile.
Note: assign the generated License Verification Work Ticket to your name and process the work ticket.
 
ACCOUNT TRANSFER
​​(return to index)
Follow these steps to prep the case.
The reporting user should have already included:
Documentation proving their ownership of the business
Their ID
Identify if we will or won’t transfer the account.
If we won’t, send the macro ID Help - Account transfer - denied and close the case.
If we won’t, because the account owner needs to take a background check and they say they don’t have an SSN, follow the SSN-less steps to offer a SSN-less background check to the account owner.
You may need to send ID Help - Need more info to gather the account owner’s ID.
Verify the submitted ID of the new owner in Au10tix. 
If the ID passes, proceed with the next step. 
If the ID does not pass, ask for another copy of their government-issued ID using the macro that will be used in Step 5.
If the situation matches anything on the list below, and we don’t already have the info we need, ask for documentation using ID Help - Need more info (include the specific documentation type we need based on the list below).
Owner passed away.
Before you ask for documentation, do an internet search for the account owner’s obituary. If you can’t find it, then ask for a death certificate.
Be empathetic and sensitive.
Owner sold the company and all of its assets.
Proof of purchase (i.e., purchase contract).
Current email address for previous owner.
Owner hired or changed the manager of a franchise location.
Proof of franchise (i.e., contracts).
Current email address for previous owner.
Owner left the company (but no other changes are being made to the business).
Documentation showing the old account owner isn’t associated with the business.
Current email address for the previous owner.
Owner is/was an employee, and we're transferring to the business owner.
Documentation showing that the new account owner owns the business.
Owner is/was the spouse of the account owner (and doesn’t own/partially own the business).
Documentation showing that the new account owner owns the business and the current account owner doesn’t.
Current email address for the previous owner.
From your existing case, send the ID Help - Account Transfer - notify owner macro to the email address listed in admin.
We need to notify the user on the admin email, which could be different from the one on the case.
Leave the case open for 48 hours, and place the case into “Pending Thumbtack” status before following the next step.
If we hear back from the account owner that they didn’t authorize the account transfer, send the macro ID Help - Account transfer - denied and close the case.
Once you have the documentation, send the ID Help - Account transfer macro followed then send the Account Transfer Agreement - Multiple Parties form through Ironclad to the new and previous account owners (if the previous account owner’s email address has changed, the new account owner should provide it). If the previous account owner has passed away, send Account Transfer Agreement instead.
If the pro doesn’t send us everything we need, send them the macro Account Transfer - Need more info.
If the pro doesn’t qualify or clearly doesn’t own the business, send them the macro Account Transfer - Denied.
Once you’ve received the form back, update the account information.
Open the pro’s admin.
In Page Actions, click Add TOU accept from Docusign.
This name wasn’t updated when we switched away from Docusign.
Enter the case number in the notes and click Save. 
Back in Page Actions, click Edit Identity Information. Update all fields on this page with the info the user provided (including in their ID), then click Submit.
Remove any background check, license or other badges/credentials.
To remove the background check, open the pro’s admin, scroll to Verifications and click delete next to the section that says “Background checked” if it appears.
Reason: “Account transferred - new BGC required”
Update “Identity Status” to “Requires background check.” 
Delete all payment information on the account.
In the pro’s admin, click login as 000000000 under their name to impersonate the pro.
Once logged in, click the pro’s profile picture on the top right side, then click Payments.
Click on the card(s) under Payment method, then choose "Delete credit card."
Repeat until all cards are removed.
On the bottom right of your screen, click Admin then Last Admin to stop impersonating the pro.
Email the pro the ID Help - Account Transfer - approved macro and close the case .
 
 
Account Transfer for Data Privacy Deleted Accounts (ID help)
(return to index)
Identifying Account Deleted due to Data Privacy:
Accounts that have been deleted due to Data Privacy will show blank under deletion reason in the deletion logs in Admin. 
 

[Image: Screenshot 2023-11-07 at 12.28.46 PM.png]

 
We need to check the service profile (business introduction) in admin to determine if the account has gone through the data deletion team. 
 

[Image: Screenshot 2023-11-07 at 12.29.39 PM.png]

 
Once we have determined that the account was deleted through our data deletion team or was deleted due to Data Privacy, follow the steps below.
Steps: 
Review case details: The reporting user (new account owner) should have included the following information. 
Government-issued ID 
Documentation of the business ownership. 
If the user has or has not shared this information, send the email template, ID Help - Account Transfer for CCPA Deleted Account - Request email of the account owner. We need to ask for complete documentation and the email address of the current account owner. 
Once we receive the email address of the current account owner, we can create a Quick Case.
Create a Quick Case for the current owner
At the bottom of your Salesforce screen, click Quick Case.

[Image: Screenshot 2023-11-07 at 12.30.16 PM.png]

Fill out all Quick Case fields.
Subject: “Thumbtack Support: action needed.”
Click Submit.
The case will automatically be created for you.
Copy and paste the case number into your original case and paste the original case number onto the new one so anyone can find the related cases.
In your new case, email the current account owner with this template, ID Help - Account Transfer - Notify current owner. Make sure to ask for the government-issued ID of the current owner. 
In the original case, email the ID Help - Account Transfer (CCPA deleted) - expectations for new account owner.

​​(return to index)

If it matches,

ID HELP TRICKY SCENARIOS
(return to index)
 

QUESTION
EXAMPLE
ANSWER
 CATEGORY 
When dealing with multiple issues, what issue should I prioritize?
A user requested to transfer their account, but the account needs to undergo a BGC, as well.
For multiple issues, let's assist the user with more important issues first. In this case, BGC should be prioritized because account changes are restricted to those in good standing.
Account Transfer
When must a user undergo another BGC?
 
A fully verified user recently updated their marital status and now wants to change their account name.
If users request a name change due to a legal name alteration or to align with their license details, they must undergo another BGC.
 
Process the name change request following standard verification steps, remove their BGC badge, and instruct the user to undergo BGC using their new name.
Personal Information Change
How do we assist users who failed BGC or are linked to accounts that failed BGC?
1. If a Pro has failed a background check (BGC) or is linked to an account with a failed BGC (same person) and wishes to retake it.

 
2. If a Pro is linked to an account with a failed BGC (different person).
 
If the failed BGC is not recent (taken a year ago/ >12 mos), the Pro can retake it. However, if the failed BGC is recent (taken within the year/ <12 mos), we will not reconsider the request.
 
They need to resolve the linked issue before we can proceed with the BGC request.
 
Note: Failed BGC and Failed Identity Verification are two different account flags.
Background check
Can we allow a transfer of ownership for an account associated with a dissolved business and re-brand the account under a new LLC?
Dissolved business: ABC123 Photography
New business: JKL001 Productions
 
Category: Video editing, video production, video streaming, wedding and event photography
We can allow account transfer for rebranding as long as the nature of the business is still the same.
Account Transfer
Can we allow email changes for accounts with issues?
Accounts flagged due to Past Due balance, chargeback, open dispute, profile issues, etc.
To help users access their account to resolve their issues, we can proceed with the email change request. This may entail temporarily reinstating their account (removing account hold, undeleting, etc.) and then reimposing the sanction afterward.
Email Change
Can we proceed with the email change if the account is ghosted - spammy?
 
Once their ID is verified via au10tix, yes we can.
 
We would need to remove the account from the blocklist and unghost to update their email address.
Email Change
The supporting documents you received for an email change request does not match the details on the account. What should we do to proceed with the request?
Pro name: John Smith
ID name: Maddie Smith
We need to verify whether we are interacting with the account holder or a designated representative of the business. Therefore, it's essential for us to request identification from the owner and proof of business ownership.
Email Change
A user wishes to change their email address, but the address they wish to use is already linked to another user with a different name.
Main account: Dominic Roque
domroque123@gmail.com
 
Other account: David Licauco
dandnotaryservices_official@gmail.com
To ensure that the requester is authorized to take the email address from the other user, ask the requester to submit a photo ID of the account owner associated with the email address.
Email Change
Can we process email change for current and previous thumbtack employees? 
Thumbtack email johnsmith@thumbtack.com
No, we cannot change their email. Aside from Admin won’t allow it, accounts linked to TT email addresses are only valid for active employees.
Email Change
Pro claims someone used their information to open a Thumbtack account. How do we proceed?
 
Identify the particular account flagged for potential identity theft.
Request proof of identification from the individual who reported it.
Remove the BGC badge by deleting the account.
If further assistance is required in investigating the identity theft, direct them to the CS/Incidents Team.
Account Takeover
Pro claims someone is trying to change their email and someone changed the name on their account. Can we still proceed with the email change?
 
Yes, as long as the person reporting can prove their account ownership by submitting a photo ID and proof of business ownership. Make sure to offer email and password changes to secure the account.
Account Takeover
Pro claims that they have allowed a previous employee to access their account. Now, the employee is no longer part of the company, and Pro wants to regain control of the account. How do we proceed?
Account name: Ken Sean
 
Business owner: Barbie Carson
 
Business name: XYZ Handyman
We can treat this first as account transfer, and request the necessary documents. We can notify the former employee using the 'ID Help - Account Transfer - Notify current owner' macro using the email address associated with the account as part of the transfer process. If the former employee opposes, then we can switch to account access dispute and delete the account so that the business owner can create a new account.
Account Access Dispute
Pro claims that their account was hacked by their competitor and changed their business name. Confirmed non-ATO, and records show the account is still under the name of the user reporting. Can we help the user gain access to the account and change the business name? 
 
Request for a photo ID. If the ID is verified in au10tix, we can proceed with the request. Advise the Pro to change their business name back to the original once they gain access to their account.
Account Access Dispute
Pro’s account was disabled - flagged for being minor based on their service profile description. Account is under the father's name, BGC passed. Can we reactivate the account even though there's an explicit mention that a minor will be involved in the business?
Account name: Juan Garcia Sr
 
Service description: "Hey, My name is Juan Garcia. I am 17 years old. Me and my dad Juan Garcia Sr have a lawn care business together.”
We must ensure that we are communicating with the account owner of legal age by requesting them to provide their photo ID and evidence of business ownership.  
After verification, update their BL record from Minor User to Account Hold + BL (User needs coaching). Instruct the account owner to proceed with updating their service profile to lift the hold.
Minor
The ID provided is expired. Can this be considered?
 
As long as the expiration falls within the last 18 months, we can proceed with the next step.
All case types
The account is for BGC, and the status is Engaged (or other than the listed statuses on KA).
 
For statuses on Checkr (Consider, etc), send an inquiry to #bgc_idhelp_teams.
All case types
The ID was successfully verified by Au10tix but the name on the result is different from the  actual name on the ID because Au10tix misread it.
 
Proceed with the request using the correct information written on the ID. Some letters or numbers may not be clear on the ID that is why sometimes Au10tix misreads it.
All case types
What if the user’s name is a Mononym?
Name on ID: Michelangelo
 
Account name: NFN Michelangelo
If the pro has a government-issued ID with the name that is a mononym, we can use NFN (No first name) and then the monoym as their last name.
All case types
TT employee wants to undergo BGC on their pro account.
 
Escalate to #bgc_idhelp_teams. They have to decide whether or not the request can be allowed.
SSN-Less Background Check
User is requesting for a name change on their business account but the name on the account is Undefined..
 
Request for a photo ID and proof of business ownership. If the business details match the details on the account and if the ID is verified in au10tix, we can proceed with the request.
Personal Info Change
What if we are not sure if a license type is a TTDNV or not?
 
Check list of accepted licenses on Admin. If still unsure, Escalate to License Type Clarification tracker.
License Verification
What if the license on the DB is not showing the license of the pro but the pro was able to provide a link where to search for the license and shows that they are registered and valid?
 
Escalate to License Type Clarification tracker to check if the DB link needs updating.
License Verification
What if:
Name on Admin: John Roberts
Name on DB: John Roberts Smith
Also completed BGC/Badged: John Roberts
ID name: John Roberts Smith
 
Request their ID, conduct verification through Au10tix, update the account name accordingly, verify the license, remove the badge, and request the professional to retake BGC.

How issues come to Trust and Safety


How issues come to Trust and Safety
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
T&S Ops categorization
Incident automation
Details
Report origins
What
(return to index)
This article outlines how users report issues to Thumbtack, are transferred to Trust and Safety, and categorized.
Why
(return to index)
Knowing what users experience before our initial outreach helps specialists to modify our approach. The first contact method gives some insight into the best way to reach out and how long they’ve been waiting.
When
(return to index)
An incident is created when one or more of the following concerns have been reported:
Project disputes between users
Discrimination
Safety Concerns
Behavior Concerns
Account issues
Legal, Law enforcement, and Media
You can find more about what qualifies as a Trust and Safety issue here.

How
(return to index)
   Steps
   (return to index)
T&S OPS CATEGORIZATION
(return to index)
Once a report is sent to T&S, the Categorization (CAT) team reviews and triages the issue. Their team will work out of either case or dispute request record types.
When reviewing reports and potentially creating an incident, CAT will:
Confirm it’s a T&S issue (based on these standards)
Establish if it should be a case or incident
Determine the tier.
Assign to a queue.
Select the project/safety category(s)

INCIDENT AUTOMATION
(return to index)
After our Cat team reviews and triages reports to their corresponding queues, many incidents without specialization will go to the T&S Automation queue. This is where incidents will go through our incident email automation flows before being ready to be worked on by a specialist.

[Image: Screenshot 2023-06-22 at 11.18.31 AM.png]

There are two different paths depending on Amount in Dispute and Project Categories:
1, 2, close:
If the amount in dispute is $250 or less OR the amount in dispute is $500 or less, and the Project Category is either “Unsatisfactory Work” or “Other.”
If there is no response after two emails (4 days), the system will auto-close the incident.
Note: Because these are lower-risk incidents, additional follow-up prior to closing isn’t necessary.
If the customer responds at any time, the system sends the incident to the Unassigned queue for follow-up.
1, 2, escalate:
Customer:
If the amount in dispute is $501+ OR the amount in dispute is $251+, and the project category is "Work not complete", "Deposit no show", or "Property damage."
Pro:
If the amount in dispute is $251+ AND the Project Category is "Deposit no show."
The system will send the incident to the Unassigned queue when:
There is any response, OR
There is no response after two emails (4 days)
Note: Because these are higher-risk incidents, they’re escalated to the Unassigned queue for follow-up, even if they are unresponsive.

   Details
   (return to index)
REPORT ORIGINS
(return to index)
There are five ways that incidents are reported to us.
Users reporting through the Help Center.
Our Service and Support team receives phone, text, or email from a user. 
Pro reports directly from their Thumbtack account.
In-Product Scam Report (IPSR)
In-Product Refund Request (IPR)
A customer leaving a 1-2 star review about their experience or a 3-4 star review with private feedback to Thumbtack (Concerning Reviews).
Through other Thumbtack teams finding concerns. 
Social media team (Comments on Instagram/ Facebook, app reviews, etc.)
Marketing team (Pro Community page, etc.)
Sales

Help Center

Users can self-serve and report a concern through our Thumbtack Help Center. Once the user answers all the questions in the report flow, the report comes straight to our CAT team for review.
Service & Support

When a user calls, texts, or emails our Service and Support team and reports a T&S issue, they’ll escalate the issue to our team based on this guidance.
The transfer flow in Tack will walk the agent through a series of questions to get details about the issue, which our CAT team will review and use to determine their action and triage.
In-product

In-product reports are submitted through the Thumbtack product so pros can report issues or request a refund. Once they answer all the questions in the flow, a Work Ticket (WT) is created so our T&S Proactive Ops team can review and triage issues to the right place.
Concerning review

When customers leave a 1, or 2-star review OR a 3 or 4-star review with Private to Thumbtack feedback, a Work Ticket is triggered for review from our T&S Proactive Ops concerning reviews team.
If it’s a T&S concern, the customer is usually auto-emailed a link to the help center to report any concerns they’d like our assistance with. Sometimes, they reply to the email instead, but either way, they’re reviewed by the CAT team and can be worked as usual by the incident team.
Occasionally, an issue is determined to be a T&S concern but needs additional manual review from an incident specialist. In these cases, there’s no automation to the customer, and a specialist will review for appropriate action or follow-up.
Other Thumbtack teams

Sometimes other teams will receive reports from users through channels other than the ones mentioned already. This can include:
Sales calls
Social media posts/comments
App reviews
Pro Community
These teams don’t always have the same access and options to escalate T&S issues to our team. Though we should encourage users to utilize one of the reporting origins previously mentioned, we may need to be accommodative and create cases to escalate to T&S on their behalf for our CAT team to review and triage.
If the concern involves an issue for our Critical Escalations team, loop them in to determine the best follow-up method.


**Use the content request form to request an update or submit questions/concerns**

Handling Time and Service Level Agreement

Transactions or communications that trigger the creation of a ticket must be delayed to allow for MTS manual review. And because part of the Thumbtack value is connecting pros and customers real-time, each delay must be minimal in order not to adversely affect their Thumbtack experience. MTS specialists work in consideration of this delay and have two types of time-related considerations: Handling Time and Service Level Agreement.
HANDLING TIME (HT)
This is the MTS specialist's target time to completion. Completing the review and actioning the request/account (if needed) within this time minimizes any impact to experience the delay may cause.

SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT (SLA)
This is the prolonged but still acceptable delay in completing tickets. The listed durations have been assessed to not cause too much adverse impact to the pro/customer experience. If the tasks in queues with a 15 minute SLA are not completed within those 15 minutes, the contact/message/profile may be approved automatically, leading to potential exposure to violations that could have been caught otherwise.

What is the fraud investigation queue?
(return to Index)
Fraud Investigation (FI) is a queue where high-risk payment transactions are manually reviewed by the Trust and Safety proactive ops team to proactively identify and reduce fraudulent users on Thumbtack. There are multiple work ticket (WT) types triggered in this queue: 
Radar Risk Score Review
Radar Rules Review
Early Fraud Warning
Lost/Stolen/Pickup Decline Code Review
Payment Within 1 Hour
Why is the fraud investigation queue important?
(return to Index)
This queue was set up to identify and take action against fraudulent payment behavior and trends, which can help detect and prevent complex fraud schemes early.
When is the fraud investigation queue used?
 (return to Index)
A fraud investigation is conducted when Thumbtack's internal fraud detection systems have identified a risky transaction, triggering a WT in the Fraud Investigation queue.
The queue's Service Level Agreement (SLA) is 24 hours, and the Target Handle Time is 15 minutes.

(return to index)
Are you working on a case and can't find a Knowledge article with the steps? Do you have a new email template or talking point you think would be helpful? Have no fear; Trust and Safety content requests are here! If you'd like to get an update to an HC article, email template, Knowledge article, process, etc., please submit a content request.
How it works 
To submit a content request, you'll follow these steps:
Talk through your idea with your manager and let them know what you're thinking. Managers have good insight into behind-the-scenes updates, and they could agree that we need new content or guide you to the article you're looking for.
Once they approve of your idea, create an edit doc using Google Docs. (Follow the steps below)
For smaller updates, like updating a sentence in an article, there's no need to create a whole edit doc. You can put smaller changes right into the request form.
Submit a content request.
Your content request will go to our Operations Analysts, who will reach out to you with any questions.
Note: Each content request must be scoped and prioritized. We may not be able to get to it right away due to other projects that were prioritized prior. Please be patient and don't hesitate to reach out with any questions.
Creating an edit doc
Edit docs are helpful to show specifically what you need changed or to outline a process. Use the guidelines below to help outline your request:
Email templates
If you have an email template you'd like written, you can either:
Paste an example of an email you've sent in the past into a doc to be edited.
Summarize the kind of email you're needing and how it will help - we can write the rest.
If the email template exists already, paste the template into a doc and make edits to the template.

New Knowledge articles
If you'd like a new Knowledge Article created:
Create a doc with a title that matches the topic you're focusing on using this template (make a copy of the template).
Outline the process you need to create.
You don't need to write out tons of in-depth specifics, and we can write the nitty-gritty. However, we may not be aware of the process you need to be written down. So be sure to make it clear what agents should be doing.
If we have questions or need clarification, we'll reach out to you.
Paste the link to your edit doc into your content request.
Updates to an existing Knowledge article
If you'd like an existing Knowledge article updated:
Copy and paste the title and the content of the Knowledge article into a doc.
Paste (or hyperlink) the link to the article - this helps us find the exact article you need to be updated.
Make your changes to the Knowledge article using a different color, so your changes are easy to see.
Paste the link to your edit doc into your content request.

Fake Reviews
(Knowledge index)
INDEX

WHY

Scope and limitations
HOW

Process FlowChart
Related

What
(return to index)
Fake Reviews (FR) are inauthentic reviews of customer experiences with pros, including self-written or duplicate reviews created to artificially inflate a pro's rating.
TYPES OF FAKE REVIEW

Review Types
Fake Review Description
Pro-Cust Fake Reviews
The pro and customer accounts are linked by Device ID, Native ID, Smart ID, or credit card.
Cust-Cust Fake Reviews
Two customers review the same pro and their accounts are linked by Device ID, Native ID, Smart ID, or credit card, but they are not linked to the pro.
3 IP Fake Reviews
The request IP, customer signup IP, and Pro signup IP are identical.
Same Pro Different Service Fake Reviews
A customer leaves multiple reviews for the same pro but for different services and shares the same login IP address.
Short Interval Reviews
A customer submits a review claiming work completion within an unrealistically short time frame following their initial service request.

The Fake Reviews task includes investigating linked accounts, using specific criteria to audit and delete inauthentic reviews and taking action that aligns with Thumbtack's Terms of Use.

Why
(return to index)
Customers rely on authentic reviews to accurately represent the quality of pros on Thumbtack. To protect the integrity of Thumbtack's marketplace and the trust of its users, the Fake Reviews queue identifies and takes action on abuse of the review system. This ensures customers can select reliable pros and remain confident in the platform.
When
(return to index)
When a review is submitted, Thumbtack's internal system assesses it based on multiple rules. When a rule is triggered (such as device ID links, IP similarities, etc.), the system sends it for manual review, generating a Fake Review work ticket.
The SLA for this task is 48 hours, and the HT target is 6 minutes.
SCOPE AND LIMITATION
(return to index)
Target Positive Rating Focus (4-5): This Fake Reviews task addresses positive 4-5 star ratings to prevent artificial inflation of pro ratings and reputations.
Negative Ratings Exclusions (1-2): Negative star ratings, intended to discredit pros, are addressed in the Concerning Review queue.
How
(return to index)
   Steps
   (return to index)
GENERAL PRINCIPLES
(return to index)
Customers are limited to one review per completed job and have a single opportunity to update an existing review.
Reviews are inauthentic when the job request was created solely to leave a review and no actual job or project was performed.
Reviews are considered inauthentic when the customer has been identified as offering or selling fake reviews to inflate pro profiles, or has a close connection to someone engaged in such activities.

Deceptive practice identification

Deceptive practice identification
(Knowledge index)

What
(return to index)
Deceptive practices include: scams, platform abuse, and inauthentic leads. 

Scams: Using fake or misleading information to defraud users out of money or by acquiring their personal information.
Overpayment Scam: Scammers trick others into refunding or sending money that the scammer never actually paid.
Advanced Payment Scam: Scammers convince others to pay upfront for goods, services, or benefits that are never delivered.  
Platform Abuse: Gaming Thumbtack features in order to avoid fees or take unfair advantage of program incentives.
Customer Data Scraping: Bad actors create pro accounts to access the jobs feed to collect user details from Thumbtack customers.
Lead payment Circumvention: Bad actors create multiple accounts to place bids until their account is deleted due to past-due balance or being linked to a previously deleted account for the same violation.
Inauthentic Leads: Engaging in suspicious, repetitive behavior that negatively impacts pro-trust in lead quality but does not necessarily cause direct financial harm.
Fake Reviews: Users create fake accounts to leave bad reviews on their competitors’ profiles.
Fake Requests: Fake customer accounts create fake requests to damage TT’s reputation or exhaust competitors' funds.
Proactive Op specialists will review accounts for deceptive practice signals. If an account is found engaging in deceptive practices, their account may be ghosted, deleted, placed on account hold, and/or blocklisted. These actions prevent bad actors from returning to the platform. 
Why
(return to index)
Users who engage in deceptive practices cause negative experiences for other users, which violates our Terms of Use and ultimately decreases user trust in the Thumbtack Platform. The loss of trust in Thumbtack leads to a higher churn rate, which impacts the business and revenue. The purpose of this procedure is to outline the steps Proactive Ops specialists should take in order to identify and address users who engage in deceptive practices. 
When
(return to index)
Proactive Ops specialists review users for deceptive practices in the following queues: 
Contact Verification (CV)
Customer Message Review (CMR)
In-Product Reports (IPR & IPSR)
How
(return to index)
   Steps
   (return to index)
PROCESS OVERVIEW
(return to index)
Select View User to pull up their Admin page (if working CV, pull up the syndication portal as well).
Review the user details.
Review their account name.
Compare it to the list of known bad actors.
Review their email address.
If you don't recognize the email domain:
Google it to see if it’s a valid organization.
Check against https://check-mail.org/ to see if it’s a disposable email.
Check if it’s a domain from mail.com.
Review their phone number.
Search for the phone number using realvalidito.com and Spydialer.com.
Search the default phone number in Admin to check for linked accounts.
If reviewing the pro account, review the service profile. 
Profile content
If the service/business name seems familiar, compare it to the list of known bad actor service/business names. 
Review Projects (requests) for signals.

Request velocity (# of requests in a short period of time)
Request true IP location
Review Message History.
Message content
Review Login History.
If the location is blank, search the IP address in Whatismyipaddress.com.
Review Show Linked Users.
If there are linked users, check to see if the linked users are ghosted/deleted for deceptive practices.
If working IPR, review report content for signals. 
Reports of scam or phishing (user asking for SSN) attempts.
IDENTIFYING SIGNALS
(return to index)
Users may have one or more signals and still be considered a valid user. Be sure to compare signals found to the Admin action guide below in order to identify if there are enough to confirm they are deceptive.

SIGNALS
EXCEPTIONS

The user pushes to move the conversation off the platform.

N/A

1 device, 1 account name, but a high number of true IPs and input IPs. (The user could be requesting from an office where 1 IP is used by multiple computers)

DETERMINE ADMIN ACTION
(return to index)
The Admin action taken depends on the amount and/or combination of signals identified. 

ACTION
SIGNALS NEEDED
*ADMIN REASON & NOTES
Ghost or Delete & Blocklist
Any of the below scenarios:
Name AND either service description OR message behavior is similar to a previously identified bad actor.

The request/account has deceptive signals similar to a known modus operandi (MO)(make sure to explain the reasoning in the WT Internal Notes)

N/A

EXAMPLES

Automated Data Deletion Process Overview
Automated Data Deletion Transfer Notes
What
(return to index)
The Data retrieval and deletion case queue is for approving or denying user requests to permanently delete their data from Thumbtack and/or receive a copy of their personal information. This is in compliance with the Data Privacy Law in certain states.
Privacy Policies from different platforms and app providers have also given users the right to have their personal data deleted.
Thumbtack is legally required to fulfill deletion requests from all users, as permissible by law, and to provide a summary of personal information we collect, utilize, and share with vendors for business purposes when requested by users (customers and pros) from California. Thumbtack is also legally required to fulfill Summary Information requests for customers from:

California
Colorado
Connecticut
Delaware
Florida
Indiana
Iowa
Kentucky
Maryland
Minnesota
Montana
Nebraska
New Hampshire
New Jersey
Oregon
Rhode Island
Tennessee
Texas
Utah
Virginia
To comply with privacy laws, these requests must be completed within 45 calendar days. 
All accounts without Trust and Safety restrictions, incident history, WTs, cases, or outstanding balance greater than $20, currently go through the automated process workflow for Data Deletion Fulfillment. The remaining volume is manually reviewed by specialists. 
When
(return to index)
Users can submit a request by using our intake form, the Apple Thumbtack App, reaching out to Service & Support, or emailing dataprivacy@thumbtack.com.
The options listed in the intake form are:
Receive a copy of their personal information. 
Delete their personal information.
Delete and receive a copy of their personal information. 
Users may select one or both options.
Users logged into the Help Center are immediately authenticated and sent an acknowledgment email. If they’re not logged in, they’re considered unauthenticated, and they receive a confirmation request. 
The resulting cases are routed to the Data Disclosure Request-Automated queue to be reviewed and actioned by the Tack automated deletion script. All cases not actioned by the automation are routed to the Data Disclosure Request-New queue.
SLA for the Data retrieval and deletion queue is 30 days, and AHT is 2.5 minutes for deletions and 10 minutes for summaries.
Non-data privacy-related concerns are triaged and transferred as needed. 
How
(return to index)
    Steps
   (return to index)
PROCESS FLOWCHART
(return to index)

[Image: Screenshot 2024-04-17 at 9.38.50 AM.png]

Process overview for specialists
(return to index)
Take a case from the Data Disclosure Request-New list view.
Ensure that you select the subcategory assigned to you.
Personal Information Deletion
The Proactive ops team owns Information Deletion requests.
* Always pick the oldest case from the queue.
Personal Information Summary
 The Critical Escalations Data Privacy team owns Information Summary requests.
Personal Information Summary + Deletion
The Critical Escalations Data Privacy team owns requests, Information Summary + Deletion requests.
*Always pick the oldest case from the queue.
Review the Data Disclosure Auth Type.
[Image: rtaImage]
Validating Account Info
If the Data Disclosure Auth Request Type is “Authenticated”:
No account validation is needed.
If the Data Disclosure Auth Request Type is “Unauthenticated”:
Review the user’s reply to verify the email and zip code they provided match what’s in their Admin profile. 
If they didn’t provide the correct information:
Send a follow-up email for more info: 
Start with a new “_Blank lLtterhead" from the Select a Template dropdown. 
Follow the steps to update the data disclosure request for unresponsive users.  
If they provided the correct information, proceed with the request.
If Data Disclosure Auth Request Type is “Null” or case originated via Email:
If the email and name match the account, proceed with the request.
If we do not have enough information:
Send a follow-up email for more info: 
Start with a new “_Blank Letterhead" from the Select a Template dropdown.. 
Follow the steps to update the data disclosure request for unresponsive users.  
If they provided the correct information, proceed with the request.
Create a Data Disclosure Request
(return to index)

All cases for data retrieval and deletion requests need to have a disclosure request. As the majority of these are auto-created by the system, verify that no existing DDR case has been created by checking the ‘Related’ tab. If no case exists,  assign the case to yourself, and follow the steps below:
Go into the MTS Categorize/Status tab. Look at the Subcategory to determine the request type. It will be one of three:
Personal Information Deletion
Personal Information Summary
Personal Information Summary and Deletion
Open the Data Disclosure Request tab. 
Click the drop-down under the Data Disclosure Request type.
Select the request type that matches the Subcategory. 
Click Save.
Personal Information Deletion Request(
return to index)

Certain scenarios are currently not part of the automated script and are being routed to the Data Disclosure Request-New queue.
Unable to fulfill  scenarios. 
Personal Information Summary 
Personal Information Summary + Deletion

If it is determined that the request can be fulfilled, follow the steps below to complete the Data Deletion request. 
Click the data disclosure request hyperlink to go to the Data Disclosure Request tab within the case. 
Tip: This is the first activity that you will see on the case details. 

[Image: _IjnyCGbahXn9AybcikbP-U7jsahWi5bAFXo6BBW3Sc7CftyT0NmSuXH8C-wm1luB_mKmYYpJMsom8nEkBVxLZpFnOYam95Wu8wC8MnSQwPZ_eUPWwfg-n8rK-zx8hadNdEFkJg3vpWrofYd-4Rc3P0]

Update the Request Status to “In Progress.”
Click Save. 
Data Privacy | (Auto-Email) to vendors to delete users’ personal information is sent out to vendors.
Note: vendor emails will only be sent for customer requests.
Change the Data Disclosure Request Status to “Submit for Deletion.” 
Click Save. 
Refresh Tack to confirm the user information has been deleted. 
Most changes in Tack are only visible on customer accounts. See customer example below:

[Image: pSy9hXzc-GOSELVCo04SHsXg9keVAxjtX-ryhxVOX-L_6zHHfEBJ364e246ZQlc60He6IRZtub12n8XWpK0evv2F0dUN7di2rgz-evfR5b-bFUBcTzJzhZrckRatWSi5cmhG-xH39k5CdMbw1rbSHDo]

The visible change for Pro accounts is the Preferred Language field within the Contact Details. Preferred Language will have a “Blank” value. See pro example below:

[Image: 2bZfwix8LWQpkw4LFGeXCO_SNnseAnZ-UCMJxM-qOMTayDIU9nwG_zdv7IXezU-Z96DDbtzf_QM11HhKCXTB7t4VCfDXQxn5e8zkSVFFyfn1CgLeGdddJtS2tqAmjGcBwScYaLoJmOaQWnKaIYPPh7I]


For both Pro and Customers, the Account Status will go from “enabled” to “disabled.”
Return to the case view to email the user. 
Pro: Send Request to delete | Completed macro
Customer: Send macro: Data Privacy | 2nd email | Request to delete | Completed | Customer
Close the case. 
Case Status: Closed
Data Disclosure Request Status: Completed
Outcome: Completed in whole
*There may be instances where the user replies with a different concern other than Data Deletion. Create a new case for Service and Support and include the email response in the case notes for further handling.
Personal Information Summary Request
(return to index)
Once you’ve confirmed that the user qualifies and it’s clear the user wants a copy of the personal information we have on them, follow these steps:
Review the users open Cases for any duplicate Data Disclosure Requests. 
Go to the Related tab and click the data disclosure request hyperlink to go to the Data Disclosure Request tab within the case. 
Update the Request Status to “In Progress.”
Leave the Outcome blank.
Click Save. 
(Auto-email) to vendors to provide users’ personal information is sent out to vendors.
Click Information Request. 

[Image: rtaImage]

Click Build with Parameters on the left side of the page. Enter the user’s PKID in the box and click Build.
All the user’s data will be emailed to your work Gmail.

[Image: zTj4IygDbu-2BbXo-hlj3QwY96U-Tn9xJe-joehR_DcdoK07_IBBoEFg2WMJL28PNfF3rdMUm5qUj8_JNnE2dzS2dvS5vw524nAh2MYdLfoP385f_FVsZV3NjMc3cUy1PoWbsaz6Qh5puIHM6TQ4fiM]

Open the email containing the user’s information. Open with a Google Sheet.
The information must be presented to the user in an easy and readable manner, so remove unneeded data. See the example below: 

[Image: UCIKgZ4FugWBuBn9KziWmIdrpzA8LIeyDE747vkS_5Qs9KWkRgtuVlhhSJTsEUkfZ1Jie5W3BwBmZcUfj2uPXKzANvpuBErYKjZrh91i4l78YiWVn5CoxtNL6GBZAXHuC5kRH08RnPnOVcgLZrQCJAU]


[Image: OXkQS32PXmUC0TjZ-lRQVsDsBLsg_sRrYoyHcb6mMi8HPUnu2EiPjXvsohzq1pMtQKp-deyeeVLz6VBiEA7pUmxcdimiLj8FVdCX8Z2mrfol7af23Fq40Njy1DvdmXLqLFdqS3IByrgemHteWU773sk]

Once complete, change the page layout to Landscape and save the sheet as a PDF. 
Title the PDF as “Data summary request [user’s first and last initials].”
Upload to Adobe.
Upload Response Cover Letter
Upload PDF of users data
For the PDF of user’s data: Add ‘Left Footer Text’ to say “Confidential”, and ‘Right Footer Text’ by ‘Inserting Page Number’I
Encrypt the document.
Click Protect on the right-hand side of the screen. 
Click Advanced Options on top of the screen. 
Select “Encrypt with Password.” 
A pop-up screen will appear:
Select “Require a password to open the document.” 
Enter a password for the user.
Password format: user initials, year,! (ex. DT2022!)
Click Restrict Editing and Printing of the document. 
Printing is allowed. Select “High Resolution.”
Changes Allowed is “None.”
NOTE: “Change Permissions Password” is for you only. This password is required if you wish to edit/change the document. Users do not get this password. 
Select OK. 

[Image: Xg4A76_u0hcQAh9F-hzTQg5upfPHRxcaqc__MqaUIYuR54a5fg84d-KlrQs1NGiEvP2jOLMfdj46L4S-ZRyFA6ClaSgYzuZd9mINT6BLlGm2SwtrpJcGqG9T9ZitjyJ9UMTZBdD6ez3W38sqscpiIPM]

To save all encryption on the document, save to your computer as “Data summary request [user’s first and last initials].” 
Delete the Google Sheet that contains the personal information of the user.
Send the following applicable email, along with the summary document, and password confirmation email, to the user.
Summary only: Request to know | Completed
Summary & Deletion: Qualified for deletion: Data Privacy | Request to know & delete | Summary completed
Summary & Deletion: Conditionally qualified for deletion: Data Privacy | 2nd email | Request to know & delete | Won’t delete (conditional)
Summary & Deletion: Disqualified for deletion: Data Privacy | 2nd email | Request to know & delete | Won’t delete (will not reconsider)
Close the case. 
Case Status: Closed
Data Disclosure Request Status: Completed
Outcome: Completed in whole
* If the case Subcategory is Summary + Deletion, the Outcome should be “partially completed” until we have fulfilled the Deletion request. 
Jenkins Dashboard
(return to index) 

This dashboard shall be utilized to monitor the success/failure of the Tack automation script. Busapps shall review and re-run any potential failure to ensure legal compliance.
   Details
   (return to index)
UNABLE TO FULFILL REQUESTS
(return to index)
Any deletion-only cases are auto-triaged for “Unable to fulfill” reasons prior to being assigned to the Data deletion request-new queue. If it is authenticated and in the queue, you can assume there’s an “Unable to fulfill” reason, and you’ll identify it for the next steps.
Users involved in incidents
(return to index)

There are instances where a user has been involved in an incident. Regardless of whether the incident has been resolved or not, Thumbtack is legally allowed to retain their personal information to protect the integrity of our platform. 
Send the won't delete (will not reconsider) advising that the request cannot be fulfilled as allowed by law.
Fill out the Data Disclosure Request fields.
Close the case.
Case Status: Closed
Data Disclosure Request Status: Denied.
Outcome: Denied due to legal exception.
Invalid requests
(return to index)

There are instances when users would send an email to dataprivacy@thumbtack.com for reasons such as:
Service and Support related concerns such as but not limited to:
Opt-out requests
Deactivate account
Refund Request
Pro/customer concern (issues with the project)
Spam/Noise (Can be closed)
The user replied that the request was a mistake. (Can be closed)
Follow the steps below on how to transfer the case:
Go to All Cases view in Tack.

[Image: 6TQYt_AjWxtMVAYqJHUaYJClNBT4l2Fig1DUuwvQtkBcX48Ty_TzMw0-ajuq9iEHODgVFVYxBHAzwarfrUoPCB2aUKYS521Jz-Jan_0vtecD6uDYMvoVyZIb8TGxzMBSsHX9sLvxBzfFrIZLxItN_gY]

Click New.

[Image: V57F2VAgxqfGqWuDWXSYzFqMZE8kXmdJCxEu7SK_oOs6LskHZWLBWM_IEtBDtOe7NYl4e6itkp4l7dvSLz8qQomU3q4LUlmfuNoAUxonFIYXtI16XphS4_6qVCd_haw1J0iuuBCdz5AP-6dCq23I9ec]

Select “Customer Support,” then click Save.

[Image: ebqeVx5DWuArM_MfYBCCii5wlP_6bLP3p_HizNtKY9YqWONDeH5KizKaEO1YwK7XyWJyhCbfwz6Ebo1wzvmhevepb-BZZa-EkCTpEAJh84n6epAu9WsNj-6bTjcV6Lcgb4sS5ub66bIVRDqfnifPtCU]

Copy and paste the user’s email from the Data Disclosure case together with the note, “Not a Data Privacy Request. Please assist further.”

[Image: m0Wz2ECLT3Hp9MtpeUfRHFejDpzDDfkFU8evWNEYN_S5kFfiaNKqzgK0Mv9oDLMKgow6IwlaOlwe6eaNVXIFkUYqNzYcBvVClfka_biFp4HwERApHFUri4miJ6kFEyDbhqsDVUCyaQvcw9aD9xk4emE]

Transfer the case to the “Customer Support-Email” queue.

[Image: cRl6SW12AsdYPppTB3hWGfHwjEPWS9Po61jcZvv6DSw78-WNZ2d-e4gcTHHGo5wXmebAQl6sPgm3wBiCnn_ElOp0ywxfOjOKJd35MW_oVo6LQRvxANm1gio-qDFuyDYVr5kKCnluf7SzJLPepJYGmr0]
a

Close the Data Disclosure Request case.
Leave notes stating “(Case number) sent to Support Operations.”
No Thumbtack account
(return to index)
Using the account information provided, confirm that no account can be found in admin.
Send the Data Privacy | 2nd email | Non-TT user macro advising their request cannot be fulfilled.
If the user responds with info identifying an account, specialists will proceed as normal.
Fill out the Data Disclosure Request fields.
Close the case.
Case Status: Closed.
Data Disclosure Request Status: Denied.
Outcome: Denied due to legal exception.
Account is on hold/deleted due to T&S reasons
(return to index)
Always check the following fields in Admin and ensure that there are no active account holds/restrictions from Trust and Safety:
Account Hold Logs
Deletion Logs
Ghost Logs
If the account hold reasons are one of the following, proceed with the Personal Information Deletion.
Incomplete profile setup
Identity Data Stored
BGC Submission or Requires a BGC
Internal process
Chargebacks:
Accounts with chargeback level 1 (TT won)
Chargeback, which resulted in Early Fraud Warnings
Chargeback, which resulted in the charge being refunded by TT (no record in the CB dashboard, please check credit logs)
If any other account holds or deletions are found, either: 
Send the Won't delete (will not reconsider) advising that the request cannot be fulfilled as allowed by law (will not reconsider).
Send Data Privacy | Request to know & delete | Won’t delete (conditional), advising that the request cannot be fulfilled until the account deletion/hold has been lifted.
If the user replies about resolving their account issue, send it to the appropriate place for follow-up.
Send to Support. 
Attach to the incident. 
Fill out the Data Disclosure Request fields.
Close the case.

Outcome: Denied due to legal exception

(return to index)

If the scenario falls under any of the following, notify Lindsey Rice and wait for further instructions before taking any action on the account.
The account has been ghosted by incidents.
The account has been disabled and noted in the deletion log, "Do Not Discuss." 
Outstanding/remaining Thumbtack balance (pros)
(return to index)

Before deleting an account, we have to ensure that pros are able to fulfill their obligation to pay for their leads in Thumbtack. In addition, any remaining credit on their Thumbtack account is non-refundable as per our Terms of Use. 

[Image: xhKfRoQWb4gE389bmYV91jwH8VFjdlDiFxoOcwg1CbdNOz-DEB8B83BojwenZnTdl7QuC_S1fAUMrfXwMQfhHtuBwA7SpjunvXX6Mt7wcdRScK6T8JBnH6Cz0LHe3omq0jeGT1XH53WNYx5d96b-Hxc]

If the credit remaining is >=$20, send the Data Privacy | Request Confirmation | Pros with the remaining Thumbtack credit macro.
If the credit is less than $20, proceed with the deletion request.
If the balance is >=$20, send the Data Privacy | 2nd email | Request to delete | Won’t delete (outstanding balance) macro.
If the balance is <$20, proceed with the deletion request.
Fill out the Data Disclosure Request fields.
Close the case.

Data Disclosure Request Status: Denied
Outcome: Denied due to legal exception
Proceed with Personal Information Deletion if the pro replies and agrees to forfeit their remaining Thumbtack credit.
Request for Summary + Deletion | Not a CA or approved state resident
(return to index)

There are instances where users would dispute our decision to deny their request for a summary since our data shows that they are not a resident of an approved state. (Approved states: Pros in CA and Customers in CA, CO, CT, DE, FL, IA, IN, KY, MD, MN, MT, NE, NH, NJ, OR, RI, TN, TX, UT, and VA).
Follow these steps In order to give these users a chance to prove their state of residence:
Create and then deny disclosure requests.
Click to edit Outcome as “Not a California resident.”
Send the appropriate Request to know & delete | User is not a resident email.
Pro: Data Privacy | 2nd Email | Request to know & delete | User is not a resident | Pro
Customer: Data Privacy | 2nd Email | Request to know & delete | User is not a resident | Customer
Close the case.
Case Status: Closed
Data Disclosure Request Status: Denied
Outcome:
Pro: Not a California resident
Customer: Not a resident
The case reopens when the user replies.
If the user wants to proceed with deletion, then follow the Personal Information Deletion process.
If the user sends supporting documents proving that they are a resident of an approved state, transfer the case ownership to Lyndsie Patane.
If the user states they are from an approved state without providing additional proof, transfer the case to Lyndsie Patane for further processing.
Duplicate Cases
(return to index) 

Currently, users can send multiple requests using either the intake form or via dataprivacy@thumbtack.com. It is important to always check for duplicate cases and ensure that we do not process deletion requests if there’s a related Information Summary request found on the same account.

If a duplicate is found, close the case and select the “Duplicate” Outcome.
Follow these steps on how to check and action duplicate cases.
Reactivation Requests
Reactivation Request Received After Deletion Request
If the date and time of the reactivation request are later than the creation date and time of the deletion request:
Do not proceed with processing the deletion request.
Close the case.
Note the work ticket number for reactivation on the Personal Information Deletion request.
Reactivation Request Submitted by Pro via Email
If the Pro contacts us via email requesting account reactivation:
Reactivate the account by removing the “disabled” status under the Pro’s business service.
Send the macro: Data Privacy | Reactivation Confirmation | Pro.
Close the case.
SUPPORT OPS FAQ
(return to index)

QUESTION
ANSWER
“I did not submit this request/a request to delete my account/personal information.”
Every user goes through at least 4 prompts asking them to confirm their understanding of the request they’re submitting. Every deletion is authenticated when processed in the data deletion queue. 
 
We’ve also sent an email asking users to inform us if the request was a mistake. 
“Can the data deletion be reversed?”
No (for customer-only accounts) 
Customers will have to create a new account using a different email address. Their original email address can no longer be used in the platform 
Yes (For Pro or Pro and Customer accounts)
The account can be reactivated, and any data that we retained will be available to them again.
Service Profile will have some missing information, which they will need to redo.
If the account name is showing as “Thumbtack User,” their account can no longer be reactivated.
“I was not advised of this!”
Every user received an email confirming their request to delete their personal information has been completed upon completion. You can refer them back to their emails and restate that every request was authenticated prior to completion.
“I had a balance on my account and wanted those funds back!”
Reach out in the #ts-proactive-ops-questions Slack channel. 
“I thought my account was already disabled after I submitted the deletion request?”
Please note that we advised you in our acknowledgment email that we shall reach out to you once the request has been fulfilled. 

DEFINITIONS
(return to index)
Sub Categories (Request Type)
Personal Information Deletion: The user requested that all their personally identifiable information be deleted from our database.
Personal Information Summary: The user requests a copy of all their personally identifiable information in our database.
Personal Information Summary and Deletion: The user requested a copy of all their personally identifiable information that we have on our database and have them deleted at the same time.
Data Disclosure Request Authentication Type
Authenticated: The user is logged in when they fill out the intake form.
Unauthenticated: The user is not logged in when they fill out the intake form.
Null: Request came via dataprivacy@thumbtack.com, or the case has been transferred from another department, such as Service & Support.
Request Status
In progress: The request is currently being processed.
Completed: The request has been fulfilled, and there is no further action required.
Denied: The request cannot be fulfilled due to a specific reason.
New: The request has not yet been processed or started.
Data Disclosure Request Outcome
Identity could not be verified: The user failed to provide information that would allow us to authenticate/verify their account.
Partially completed: The specialist was not able to fulfill all requests. (used when the user requests Summary + Deletion, but the specialist can only fulfill one request)
Completed in whole: All requests have been fulfilled.
Not a California resident: The Pros is not in CA, and Customer is not in CA, CO, CT, DE, FL, IA, IN, KY, MD, MN, MT, NE, NH, NJ, OR, RI, TN, TX, UT, and VA.
Declined due to legal exception: The request was declined due to legal exception. (Account has T&S Restriction, User is not a resident from any approved states for account Information Summary, etc…)
Invalid third party request: Request came from 3rd party/ not the account holder.

New: 
Authenticated users: The case has not yet been assigned to a specialist.
Unauthenticated users/blank value: When a user reaches out to this queue and is unauthenticated, they receive an automated email requesting to verify some information. If the user never replies to that email,  the case will stay in “New” status, and the user will be considered unresponsive.
