articles.fullText:
Customer satisfaction payouts

Customer satisfaction payouts
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
No manager approval required
Manager approval required
Process a CSAT payout
Details
Pro contacts us after payout
Rehire eligibility
Emails
Forms
Payout forms
What
(return to index)
When customers don’t qualify for the Thumbtack Guarantee, Thumbtack may still be able to help with a Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) payout.

If there’s a lower dollar amount involved, Trust and Safety may offer this as a way to help users move on quickly.  If there’s a higher dollar amount, egregious concerns, or hardships involved, Trust and Safety may offer a CSAT to help make the customer whole while protecting and building trust in the Thumbtack brand. 
Why
(return to index)
Offering CSATs can save Trust and Safety time and money that would have been spent working on the incident. It can also help preserve or improve Thumbtack’s reputation and retain customers who might have otherwise stopped using the platform.
When
(return to index)
If a customer doesn’t qualify for the Thumbtack Guarantee, but special circumstances or serious risk factors suggest additional compensation may be appropriate, consider a CSAT payout.
As of January 2026, we’re including “rehire” situations to support Thumbtack’s  'My Team' feature and reward long-term pro-customer relationships.
How
(return to index)
   Steps
   (return to index)
NO MANAGER APPROVAL REQUIRED
(return to index)
Review the incident to determine if the customer is eligible for a CSAT payout. Use the criteria below:
The customer is ineligible for the Thumbtack Guarantee.
Guarantees should always be exhausted before offering CSAT payouts.
The job in question is not a rehire. (if it is a rehire, see below.
The potential payout amount is $250 or less (or the current expedited incident threshold determined by leadership).

If any of these criteria are not met, seek manager approval in Slack before moving forward.
MANAGER APPROVAL REQUIRED
(return to index)
For amounts in dispute above the expedited incident dollar amount, Specialists will need explicit manager approval to offer a CSAT payout. This also applies to customers who are eligible under the Thumbtack Guarantee and receive a payout for our cap, but the amount they would have been eligible for is above that cap.
CSAT payouts requiring manager approval should be considered when there are multiple or egregious risk factors. Review the incident to determine if this is something to discuss with a manager, based on the criteria and examples below:
Something particularly egregious or difficult to manage happened:
The user needs counseling.
The general public would think poorly of Thumbtack for not helping the user in this circumstance.
Sensitive parties are involved and severely impacted by what’s happened.
The user is on a fixed income and is struggling to make ends meet due to issues caused by a pro.
Thumbtack could be considered liable.
Evidence of fraud that was missed and should have been caught by T&S processes
The specialist manager has suggested it, or is needed to move the incident forward.
The specialist has spent a significant amount of time on the incident and doesn’t see a resolution happening soon.
Rehire Situation
The incident involves a qualifying rehire situation, and a payout is requested to resolve issues from the new project.

PROCESS A CSAT PAYOUT
(return to index)
Before taking this step, the Specialist should have already: 
Completed the steps for the incident through the Thumbtack Guarantee, collected any required documentation, and received the signed Thumbtack Guarantee submission form in Ironclad.
Determined whether manager approval is needed before moving forward with offering payment.
If required, a manager should leave a note on the incident before moving forward.

Once these steps are complete, follow the steps in the  KA to move forward with offering payment, then follow the steps belo.:
Once these steps are complete, follow the steps in the Navigating Payout requests KA to move forward with offering payment, then follow the steps below:
Flag the customer’s and pro’s accounts.
For payout situations where the pro was not required to resolve, use “Low dollar comp” flag type. 
Expedited payout customer: Grammarly snippet: EP flag CX (100c)
Expedited payout pro: Grammarly snippet EP pro flag (100p)
For payouts where the pro was required to resolve and didn’t, use “Other” flag type
Grammarly snippet CSAT flag (csatflag)
Close your incident.
   Details
   (return to index)
PRO CONTACTS US AFTER PAYOUT
(return to index)
Pros are only required to pay Thumbtack back if they were given the chance to address the concern and were removed because they didn’t. If the pro does reach out wanting to reactivate their account, follow the same steps you would if the pro reaches out after a payout through the Guarantee. 

REHIRE ELIGIBILITY 
(return to index)
A project is considered a “Rehire” when the Customer reengages the same Pro for work outside of the original project without submitting a new request. 
To qualify for CSAT consideration, the rehire must meet the following conditions.
On-platform / Documented Engagement: Rehires must be formally initiated on-platform via the Thumbtack messenger or through a documented transcript of an intermediary-recorded phone call between the users. If communication moves entirely off the platform without a Thumbtack message or an intermediated recorded call transcript, the project is ineligible.
In the same Category: Rehires must match the original project category. If the new project is completely unrelated to the original job type (I.e., Painting to Plumbing), they are not eligible. 
Eligibility window: 
Project Reset Policy: Every rehire is officially classified as a new project. This means the 30-day "Proof of Hire" window resets completely the moment a re-engagement message is sent.
Claim Filing Window (6 Months): The 6-month deadline to file a claim is now triggered by the New Proof of Hire date. The original project start date is no longer used to determine this window. 
Additional work: Work that is considered an "add-on" to an original, ongoing, documented agreement—such as undocumented amendments to the original agreement—is not covered.


DATE
REQUIREMENT
DETAILS
MECHANISM
Re-engagement (Request)
Must be after January 1, 2026
To be eligible, the rehire must have been initiated after the policy's effective date.
Manual 
Rehire Activation 
Must be On-Platform
The rehire must be "activated" via a new Thumbtack message or new project bid to maintain an audit trail.
Manual / On-Platform
Pro Hired
Must be within 30 days of the re-engagement message. 
The 30-day window to hire the pro resets. It starts from the moment of re-engagement, not the original request.
Manual
Problem Recognized
Within 45 days (MBG) / 14 days (PDG)
Date the customer noticed the issue with the new rehire work.
Manual
Date Reported
MBG: Must be within 45 days of Problem Recognized AND within six months of Pro Hired.
PDG: Must be within 14 days of Problem Recognized AND within six months of Pro Hired.
All date requirements are anchored to the new Rehire Proof of Hire date.
Manual
Documentation Deadline
Must be within 60 days of the Date Reported unless extended
All evidence for the rehire claim must be submitted within 60 days of the date reported.
Manual 
Scenario examples


Initial Project
Rehire (Eligible)
Add-on Work (Excluded)
Kitchen Faucet Repair
Two weeks after the project ends, the customer contacts the pro again through the Thumbtack messenger to fix a different leaky pipe.  Sending a re-engagement message on Thumbtack two weeks later to hire them for a different pipe.
While on-site to fix the pipe, they ask the pro to also fix another leaky pipe.  Asking the pro to also fix a different leaky pipe while they are already on-site.
Interior Painting (Living Room)
A month after the project is completed, the customer only contacts the pro through the Thumbtack messenger to paint another room. 
Halfway through painting the living room, the customer asks the pro to also paint the hallway. 
Lawn Mowing
After completing the work on the lawn, the customer reaches out through Thumbtack messenger to hire them for leaf removal. 
The customer requests that the pro "trim the hedges real quick" during their scheduled mowing visit.
If the specialist determines that the situation qualifies as a rehire payout, they should send the "Payout: Notify of rehire payout (customer)" email macro to inform the customer of the rehire coverage and continue with the standard payout process. 
For more information on the payout process, follow the steps in the Navigate a payout knowledge article.
   Emails
   (return to index)
Thumbtack Guarantee: Request submission: Send this to the customer to introduce the program and send them the form they have to fill out. This email tells them about the 10-day time frame they have.

Thumbtack Guarantee: Unresponsive Customer: Send this to the customer if they haven’t responded within 2 business days.

Payout: Notifying pro of expedited payout: Send this to the pro if we’re paying the customer out without removing the pro, and we want the pro to know.

Payout: Notify of rehire payout (customer): (PO: Notify cx of rehire):  Send this to the customer if we are sending payment related to a rehire project. 
FLAGS

EP pro flag (100p): Flag for the pro’s account. Use this in your flag notes.
EP flag CX (100c): Flag for the customer’s account. Use this in your flag notes.
CSAT flag (csatflag): Flag for the user after successful payout through our customer satisfaction payout process.
Rehire CSAT flag (rehirecsatflag): Flag the user after successful payout for a rehire situation.
 
  Forms
   (return to index)
PAYOUT FORMS
(return to index)
For all payout types, the users will be required to fill out forms before we send a payment to them. 
The “Thumbtack Guarantee Submission form” is required for all cases that are not considered an in-product payment.
The “Thumbtack Payment Agreement” is also required for:
All PDG payouts.
MBG and CSAT payouts $501+.
For payouts $12,001+, the “Wire Transfer Request Form” is also needed.
Note: Wire transfers are rare. Do not send before the payout is officially approved in Tack and by your manager.

What
(return to index)
Customer Message Review (CMR) is a queue where user messages on the platform are flagged for manual review. The Trust and Safety task is to evaluate if the message being sent is acceptable, following and actioning according to Thumbtack’s Terms of Services. 
Why
(return to index)
We review customer messages to protect the Thumbtack brand and the quality of our customers' and pros’ user experience. If the tickets aren’t processed promptly, they’ll be passed through and auto-verified within 15 minutes. Messages not evaluated within 15 minutes auto-pass and may expose pros to online abuse.
When
(return to index)
The Message Spam Model scores customer messages: 
A minimum score will automatically action and ghost the user's account, and the message will not be sent to the platform. A score below the minimum threshold will automatically be passed and sent to the platform.
Messages scored as "potentially spammy" will become a work ticket for manual review to verify acceptability. The bid link on the ticket reveals the full conversation between the users, which helps with gauging the broader context.
During the evaluation of CMR tickets, instructions found in the Deceptive Practice Identification procedure and the TOS Violations procedure should be followed.
SLA for the CMR queue is 15 minutes, and the HT target is 2.5 minutes.
How
(return to index)
   Steps
   (return to index)
PROCESS OVERVIEW
(return to index)

[Image: rtaImage]

Upon receiving the Customer Message Review (CMR) WT, check the Fides Rules to see what triggered the WT and collect more information.
Click each link found in the WT:
Request
Bid
Read the full conversation in the Bid Link and the details in the Request link for any deceptive behavior and/or TOS violations.
Refer to the Deceptive Practice Identification procedure and the Terms of Service Violations procedure for detailed steps and information.
Based on the investigation done:
If applicable, take action against the request and/or account.
Refer to the Quickview for the actions required for each violation.
On the Negotiation/Bid Page, use the dropdown next to each message to tag those marked “IN REVIEW”, whether they have a violation or not.
If there are no violations found, select Okay.

If there are multiple TOS violations in one message, select the most severe category from the picklist.

Note: For multiple violations  found in one message, tag all violations found in Salesforce.
Note: If a violation is found outside of the message itself (backend signals, linked accounts, etc.), there is no need to tag the message. Follow the steps for tagging the violation found in the WT.

Guiding Principle
The goal of CMR is to check for TOS violations by customers. However, there are times when Pros also violate our terms of service. It is important to call them out and take action on their account to protect our customers from potential abuse.
The actions taken depend on the type of TOS violation found. Refer to the tier chart in the Profile Review procedure for guidance on actioning pro accounts.

Critical Escalations

Critical Escalations
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps

Urgent Tier 6
Transfer the Incident
ProActive Operations
Urgent Tier 6

Proactive ops managers
Details
Helpful links
What
(return to index)
Critical Escalations Case Managers handle serious safety concerns, highly sensitive parties, and high-risk cases that may impact the Thumbtack brand.
It’s in our best interest to do everything we can to assess high-risk scenarios and prepare to reach a favorable outcome.

Why
(return to index)
High-risk and sensitive incidents need a higher level of care. The Critical Escalations team delivers a human-first, tailored approach to these matters. They maintain consistent, fair standards while thoughtfully managing risk.

When
(return to index)
Any high-risk or sensitive situation classified as a Tier 4-6 Trust and Safety issue should be escalated to the Critical Escalations team. 

How
(return to index)
   Steps
   (return to index)
IDENTIFY CRITICAL ESCALATIONS (Tier 4-6)
(return to index)


TIER
ISSUES UNDER THIS TIER
Tier 6
Urgent Scenarios: 

Specific, direct threats made by a user to another person, themselves, a Thumbtack employee, or a Thumbtack office. 
Threat of physical harm 
Threat of self-harm
Office threat 
These threats should have a location, method, and threat to happen imminently. 
Tier 6 is reserved exclusively for situations where Thumbtack's immediate intervention has the potential to save a life. If the user has contacted local authorities or law enforcement, or has already taken definitive action to secure their safety, the incident does not qualify as a Tier 6. Instead, such incidents should be prioritized as Tier 4, as the immediate urgency of the threat has been mitigated.

*Note: Tier 6 incidents are very serious and need immediate action. Follow steps under contacting Critical Escalations. 
Examples:
“I’m going to hills high school tomorrow at 10am and I’m going to start shooting everyone”
"I'm coming to your house after work and I'm going to (blow up your house) (stab/shoot/kill you)"
“I’m going to shoot myself tomorrow if I am not refunded for all my leads”
Tier 5
Safety Concerns:

Sexual reports where it's clear that it was in-person.
Do not investigate further 
Make sure the reported user is removed.
For the deletion log, select “Sexual Content”
Do NOT add additional details in the log.
Remove linked accounts as well.
(Click "show linked users" under "page actions" in admin, then remove accounts listed there.)
Serious injury or death resulting from a Thumbtack project.
Intentional physical harm or an attempt to physically harm. 
Ex. “The pro hit me,” “The dog sitter hit my dog,” etc., “He threw a drill towards me, barely missing” “He pulled a gun on us”
Non-consensual aggressive physical touch (pushing, shoving, etc.)
Non-consensual physical contact that excludes the specific actions listed in Tier 4 (taps on the shoulder, touched/grabbed arms/shoulder, touching of the leg below the knee, touching of feet, brushed up against, or hugged).
If the specific area touched is not specified it should be a Tier 5. 
Fires or disasters where a user is in danger.
Displaced user.
(i.e., no where to go tonight, unable to live at home, etc.)
Arrest or prosecution of any user in relation to the project.
Tier 4
Safety Concerns:

ANY sexual reports that weren't in person, including reports of inappropriate photos being sent, comments, soliciting sex, etc
Includes violations of explicit nudity and sexual content/pornography
Make sure the reported user is removed.
Remove linked accounts.
(click "show linked users" under "page actions" in admin, then remove accounts listed there).
If the project is in a sensitive category: 
Private Yoga
Personal training
House cleaning 
Boudoir photography
Video production 
Alternative healing 
1 on 1 project requests - ex. Piano lessons, Spanish lessons, etc
AND the user is uncomfortable and the following was reported: 
Non-consensual physical touch 
(taps on the shoulder, touched/grabbed arms/shoulder, touching of the leg below the knee, touching of feet, brushed up against, hugged)
All other reports of non-consensual inappropriate touching, including when the area touched is not specified, should default to T5.
Flirting
Romantic advances/gestures 
Staring/leering
Photos/videos taken
Information other user requested from them (i.e., photos, address)
Threats with an action plan but not considered urgent (i.e., no plan to happen imminently). Examples: 
"they told me if I showed up that I would be killed"
"When the pro told the customer he was on his way, he started cursing him and told him that he will beat him"
Concerns of human trafficking. 
"seems like human trafficking"
Missing or failure to return an animal
Highly Sensitive Parties or Project Concerns:

>=$25k in dispute.
Thumbtack employee is involved in dispute.
Known prominent figures.
(Celebrities, famous or influential figures)
High Risk to Thumbtack (Legal or Brand Risk):

Law enforcement inquiries or subpoenas.
Legal action has already been started against Thumbtack.
Contacts from lawyers/attorneys representing a user when legal action against Thumbtack is mentioned.
Contacts from licensing bodies or Attorney General offices.
User mentioned Attorney General and dispute is in NY or CA.
Known or imminent media involvement (that poses a significant risk to Thumbtack’s reputation).
Pro circumvented the blocklist and the linked pro was previously removed by Critical Escalations. 
DMCA (Digital Millennium Copyright Act) and trademark concerns.
(ie., using a business name/logo without trademark owner’s permission, using content such as images without the copyright owner’s permission, etc.)
NOTIFY CRITICAL ESCALATIONS
(return to index)

Notify Critical Escalations: Instructions for Incident Ops specialists: 
(return to index
For URGENT TIER 6
Scenarios that are considered URGENT (tier 6) are ones that have not yet happened.
They are specific, direct threats made by a user to another person, themselves, a Thumbtack employee, or a Thumbtack office. These threats should have a location, method, and threat to happen imminently. These are very serious scenarios that we would wake up our Critical Escalations team in the middle of the night for.
Examples:
“I’m going to hills high school and I’m going to start shooting everyone”
"I'm coming to your house after work and I'm going to (blow up your house) (stab/shoot/kill you)"
“I’m going to shoot myself tomorrow if I am not refunded for all my leads”
Non-Examples:
“I'm going to beat you up if you don't remove that review.”
“Pay me now or you will regret it, I know where you live.”
“The pro punched me before he left my house”
“If you don’t X,Y,Z I am going to kill myself”
What to do if you come across an urgent scenario:

Reach out directly to the Critical Escalations team via Slack in #escalation_questions.
Follow the workflows in the channel to submit an incident question through the 'Critical Escalations Workflow Button.'
Use the 'Urgent-Bypass button' if the Issue involves sexual reports, displaced users, threats of or confirmed physical harm, or confirmed legal/media threats (Attorney is currently involved/you have received something from the attorney or the court.
Only use this in rare instances where the Issue may not fit any of the current workflows.
If you’re on a call with a user and the Critical Escalations team is not able to take the transfer immediately, gather (and note) the users:
Name
Phone number
Admin links for the users involved
Let the user know they'll be contacted by our Trust and Safety team as soon as possible.
Follow the steps below to pass the TACK record on to the Critical Escalations team. 
If you don’t hear back from a Case Manager within 30 minutes, you can directly message Lisa Ronquillo, Ashlee Atkinson, Edgar Herrera Castaneda, or Erika Hager in Slack. If they’re unavailable, you can call or text them. For weekends or after regular business hours (8 AM - 5 PM MST), check the "Escalations Weekend Rotations" calendar to see who is available.
Lisa Ronquillo: 801-664-2467
Ashlee Atkinson: 801-450-2574
Edgar Herrera Castaneda: 562-314-5970
Erika Hager: (832) 546-6119

As a last resort, if you do not hear back from the on-call Case Manager, you can reach out to Rebecca Fitzsimmons: 440-862-0477. 
TRANSFER THE INCIDENT
(return to index)
Incident ops specialists
(return to index)
Review with your manager to confirm the Critical Escalations team should be involved. 
If the decision is "yes," move on to step 2.
If the decision is "no," handle as normal  with managers' guidance.
Go to the Details tab and change the “Owner” of the incident to “MTS Escalation.” Make sure the “Owner” is set to Queues by clicking on the carrot next to the image. This will transfer it to the team.

[Image: mtcP_NCsO4juy7bAZm3JhJHG9oDdEazu0RYp3J-hoSPNvC5-W44LLQFhQr6cxJSt_qCP0zzm0Mt0ol3tvvrfLGf0i0JdnuIzp5Q52TjawU4JxWlpEP9hHyz_iAeJddI6Q9_0f_oQYxfeUGDn9cSBhuc]


[Image: LHqI6Bh28WgipWLJHsgqiFfUOdN6djQF4XEcXBGhlCOgRfWKetvj38lpt0nheMljaXciKuXPgmGDbr8nZWXKJEq-16sOL19BdzK34-a6zMo_elDQGdq95I05JqSBurAo_0mQvJBufzM-LwuC2Gm3YRA]

Notify Critical Escalations: Instructions for Proactive Ops specialists:
For URGENT TIER 6
Scenarios that are considered URGENT (tier 6) are ones that have not yet happened.
They are specific, direct threats made by a user to another person, themselves, a Thumbtack employee, or a Thumbtack office. These threats should have a location, method, and threat to happen imminently. These are very serious scenarios that we would wake up our Critical Escalations team in the middle of the night for. 
Examples:

"I'm coming to your house after work, and I'm going to (blow up your house) (stab/shoot/kill you)"

Non-Examples:

“Pay me now or you will regret it, I know where you live.”
“The pro punched me before he left my house”
“If you don’t X,Y,Z I am going to kill myself”
What to do if you come across an urgent scenario:
During Business Hours (Monday-Friday 8am-5pm MST)
Slack the Critical Escalations team on #ts-incident-ops-questions, tag @escalations and ask a Case Manager to DM you for an urgent issue. Make sure to include the Work Ticket Number in your Slack message. 
After Business Hours (or company holidays)
Submit an Urgent Report in Salesforce.
From a  WT or DR: 
You will proceed as normal, categorizing the scenarios and creating an incident. Once the incident is created, you will go into the case of the user who is reporting the threat and fill out the Urgent Report flow following the steps below. 
From a Case:
Click Submit Urgent Report under the Email tab on the case. You may have to select More to see it in the drop-down. 
Choose the appropriate report type.
Office Threat
Threat of Physical Harm
Threat of Self harm
Click Next.
Answer all of the questions in the report flow, making sure to be detailed.
Once submitted, a Case Manager will take over the incident and case. They will reach out to you if they have further questions. 
You will also receive an email confirming your report was successfully submitted. 
Follow the steps belowd to pass the TACK record on to the Critical Escalations team.
CREATE AND TRANSFER THE CASE
(return to index)
Proactive ops specialists
(return to index)
Review with your manager to confirm the Critical Escalations team should be involved.
If confirmed, escalate the work ticket to a manager.
If you’re working a Concerning reviews or in-product report work ticket, follow the normal Outcomes and Outcome Details, and a case will be created automatically. No need to escalate to a manager.  
Add to Internal Notes that this was escalated to a manager. 
Update action fields in TACK. 
Proactive ops managers (if there is not a related incident):
(return to index)
Check to see if there is an open case.
If there is, follow the steps here to attach the case to the incident. 
If there is not, continue to step 2.  
Create a Quick Case.
Enter the violating user’s Full Name and Email Address.
The subject should be related to the report you’re sending.
Case Origin should be "email."

[Image: ZochTsHSvxG1Wiww3koLZvUSGG971RVBTJGWQzKuS1-h4wUjroNv5EXbvY6_KZ45QiAqvEqXqYXlQsF1lEgysu6lZQ1zjzeZ6kjvYZuHdnWI7o_Qv5eCKDTeNaUAL2rI6prQA6rjTGKy_NZIUDjXnnA]

Once the case is created, go to the Email + Action tab, click on the Post tab, and enter the following information:
Pro User Admin link

Work Ticket number
Service Request number
Reason for escalating - Copy and paste the message(s) that contain the violation(s). Censor explicit/abusive words (e.g., A**, F***).
Set the To field to “Thumbtack Only.”
Click Share.
Transfer the case to the Marketplace Integrity queue.

Open the case and check if there’s a related incident.[Image: pWhuxrfzf7OU-AEpWekIT-2K1zOxDK4rq6AZTgZbXRUDJHHo8uhBHJajQtqYbtEsL-cInLjK_yLDc1mDi1ab_qfNpYLqqdwRL5-ghzcJ6KFimgZbn1Ytd_Mnyex0dEVGNPuQjN1iS5kLBGOmCKfMRjo]
Review the incident, and once we confirm that it’s for the same pro and customer, copy the incident number, go back to the case, and go to the Details tab.[Image: WOzGl2TzaD6XE5qSiG5oWb26527Xg1sxN2hVOLzvZO4--mskePWgy0kARzt_PkVXc8iajVCBycL6oBVcVQeiljXny8vK63_wj3bbn2oKS3uNR4WXjrlvNPW4eE0biZwcqFO6uap3RJu3EaxVNQJgi9U]

articles.fullText:
Copyright or trademark

Copyright or trademark
(Copyright and Trademark issues are worked on by the critical escalations team. They should be notified when these issues are reported in an incident.) 
 (Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
Definitions
DMCA
Copyright
Trademark
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Reports of Copyright infringement
Third-party reports Copyright concern
Reports of Trademark infringement
Details
Copyright: Notices of infringement
Copyright: Counter-notice
Talking points
Pro is using my copyrighted content
Pro is using my trademark
Emails
Copyright: Email templates
Trademark: Email templates

What
(return to index)
DEFINITIONS
(return to index)
DMCA = Digital Millennium Copyright Act
(return to index)

The DMCA (Digital Millennium Copyright Act) is designed to govern copyright protection for digital content. It provides requirements for dealing with online copyright violations. Specific DMCA guidelines can be found in our Help Center under Copyright Policy.

Copyright
(return to index)

The Copyright Act protects the rights of individuals who create literary, dramatic, musical, artistic, and certain other intellectual works (such as history tests and software code, etc.).
Copyright infringement occurs when copyrighted media (images, text, video, literary and artistic work, or other intellectual property) is used without the explicit permission of the copyright owner.
Any reports of copyright infringement must be from the copyright holder themselves or their authorized representative. We cannot take action on a report from a third party alleging the use of someone else’s copyrighted material.
What isn't considered a copyright infringement?

If a Thumbtack customer reports a pro for posting pictures that the pro took of the project on the pro’s profile, this is not a copyright issue. We should encourage pros to be clear with customers about the photos they take and how they'll be used.

Trademark
(return to index)

Trademarks are all about identifying the source of something, which can include a company's name, product name, brand identity (like logos), and slogans.
A trademark complaint might occur when one user is using a competitor's business name, logo, or slogan/
Note: Trademark infringement is different from copyright infringement. Trademarks protect elements that help define a company brand, such as its logo or name, whereas copyrights protect original works that often consist of music, written text, photography, or other visual art.

Helpful links:
Thumbtack’s Copyright Policy - Help Center article
Thumbtack Terms of Use (User Content, Prohibitions, Copyright Policy)
USPTO - United States Patent and Trademark Office
TESS - Trademark Electronic Search System - allows you to search the USPTO database of registered trademarks. 
When
(return to index)
When a user contacts us regarding copyright infringement, trademark infringement, DMCA, or any other allegedly unauthorized use of that user’s intellectual property, this policy governs.
If the reported content is related to categories, search terms, or other content that is part of the Thumbtack website or uploaded by Thumbtack itself, please reach out to the Legal team.
 
How
(return to index)
   Steps
   (return to index)
REPORTS OF COPYRIGHT INFRINGEMENT
(return to index)
Note: Copyright and Trademark are only handled by the critical escalations team. They should be notified if these types of concerns are reported.
Before taking any action, we must receive a completed Copyright: Notice of infringement.
Verify all information is included in the Notice of Infringement.
If the claim provided is missing any of the required information, send the Legal - Copyright concerns macro so an official notice of infringement can be provided.
Once we receive a complete Notice of Infringement:
Review the information provided and locate the material at issue.
Confirm whether or not the reported material matches the original copyrighted work. 
If the reported material matches the original work, remove the infringing material.
 Note: If the infringing material is located on Thumbtacks' public-facing pages, work with the Legal team on the next steps.
Send the macro ​Legal - Copyright - Reply to official notice of infringement macro to the reporting party.
Notify the reported user of the infringement complaint.
Send the Legal - Copyright - Notify reported user of infringement macro to the reported user.
This informs the user that we’ve removed the claimed materials, that the copyright holder has the right to take legal action, and provides detailed steps on how they can provide an official counter-notice.
Handling an official counter-notice:
If the reported party provides an official counter-notice, you’ll send a copy of the counter-notice to the copyright holder who originally reported the infringement as an attachment to the macro Legal - Copyright - Notify of counter notice.
Set a follow-up on the incident for 10 days.
If we don't hear back from the original reporting copyright holder indicating their intent to seek a court order to prevent reinstatement within 10 days, we can reinstate the material on the reported user's account.
Send Legal - Copyright - Counter notice filed - No response notifying the reported user that the material has been reinstated.
If the reporting copyright holder notifies us that they’re taking action against the reported user, the material must remain removed.
Send the reported user Legal - Copyright - Counter notice filed notifying them the material cannot be reinstated until the matter is settled.

No Copyright concern located
If no content/media is located based on the official notice of infringement, send the reporting user Legal - Copyright - No violation found macro.
This will notify the reporter that we didn’t find any violation while allowing them an opportunity to provide additional information on the report.
REPORTS OF TRADEMARK INFRINGEMENT
(return to index)
Steps for Trademark Concerns
 
When a user reports unauthorized use of their registered trademark, send them the Legal: Trademark concern macro to request additional documentation.
If the reporting party provides documentation (i.e., trademark registration number), verify the trademark serial number by searching for it in the Trademark Electronic Search System (TESS). 
Review the reporter’s trademark information and compare it to the reported user’s account. Look for: 
Business name or logo similarity 
Registered trademark’s goods and service categories and whether they are similar to the reported party’s goods and services (i.e., are both parties providing similar goods or services?) 
 If the business name/logo and the goods and services are similar, remove the reported party's business name or logo in question.
Send the Legal - Trademark - Notify reported user of infringement macro to notify the reported party of the action we’ve taken.
This informs them that we have removed the claimed materials, that the registered trademark owner could take them to court, and provides steps on how they can respond to us to reconsider the removal.
Send Legal - Trademark - Reply to trademark infringement report to notify the reporting party of the action we have taken.
Set a follow-up on your case for 10 days.
If 10 days pass and we don’t receive a response from the reported party sharing relevant documentation that they own the materials, close the case.
If the reported party responds and provides documentation, review the documentation with the legal team to determine whether or not the reported account can be restored, and reach back out to both parties and inform them that they will need to resolve the issue amongst themselves via their own legal counsel. 
If the reporting trademark holder notifies us that they’re taking action against the reported user, then the material must remain off the site.
Send the reported user Legal - Trademark - Notify Reported User of Legal Action macro notifying them the material cannot be reinstated until the matter is settled.
Once a decision has been made through the courts, we will review and either reinstate or leave the material removed based on the outcome.
 
Unable to determine Trademark concern
If no content is located based on the trademark report, send the reporting user Legal - Trademark - Unable to Determine macro.
This will notify the reporter that we were not able to confirm any violation while allowing them an opportunity to provide additional information.
 
THIRD PARTY REPORTS COPYRIGHT CONCERNS: (For specialist use)
(return to index)
Customer or other parties reporting media on Pro's profile
If a customer or another party is reporting concerns with content/media that is not owned by them but may be related to projects they had completed, this is not a copyright concern as they are not the owners of the content in question.
If the reporting party is requesting the content be removed because they did not give the pro permission to post it, follow these steps:
Check the content in question for any potential safety risk concerns, such as personal identifiable information (PII). Note that PII may include anything that could identify the customer, such as showing the street name and house number in a photo, images of the customer’s face, text caption for a photo giving the customer’s name, etc.
If PII is found, remove the content and notify the pro with an explanation for the removal.
If no personally identifiable information is listed on the photos, advise the reporting party of the following:
We are not required to remove the content. However, we can follow-up with the pro and ask that they remove the content.
Coach the pro to ask for permission to move forward with customers prior to taking pictures of project-related work.
Pros Reporting Another Pro for Copyright Concerns

Review the information reported. If the content is clearly a match, such as copied pictures or text that is verbatim, follow the copyright infringement process.
Please note:
Text that is similar in formatting but not verbatim is not a copyright concern.
If the business name or logo is in question, see Trademark process.
 
   Details
   (return to index)
COPYRIGHT: NOTICE OF INFRINGEMENT
(return to index)
Most reports of copyright infringement won’t contain all of the necessary information to qualify as an official Notice of Infringement. However, we can move forward if the reporting party’s email has ALL of the following:
Identifies the copyrighted work they claim has been infringed. 
Identifies where the allegedly infringing content is located on Thumbtack 
Provides the reporting party’s mailing address, telephone number, and email address.
Include both of the following statements in the body of the notice:
“I hereby state that I have a good faith belief that the disputed use of the copyrighted material is not authorized by the copyright owner, its agent, or the law (e.g., as a fair use)."
"I hereby state that the information in this Notice is accurate and, under penalty of perjury, that I am the owner, or authorized to act on behalf of the owner, of the copyright or of an exclusive right under the copyright that is allegedly infringed."
Provides their full legal name and their electronic or physical signature.
COUNTER NOTICE
(return to index)
A counter-notice is a formal response in which an individual denies a report of copyright infringement and asserts ownership of the disputed material. It is more than just a statement from the reported party; we receive a physical counter-notice via email.
If we receive a counter-notice from the account accused of infringement, the contested materials will remain removed from the account for at least 10 days. This period allows the copyright holder to pursue legal action until the matter is resolved in court.
What must a counter-notice include?

A counter-notice must include all of the following:
The countering party’s physical or electronic signature.
The countering party’s name, address, and phone number.
Identification of the material and its location before it was removed.
A statement under penalty of perjury that the material was removed by mistake or misidentification.
The countering party’s consent to the jurisdiction of a federal court in the district where they live (if they are in the U.S.) or their consent to the jurisdiction of a federal court in the district where their service provider is located. (if they are not in the U.S.)
The countering party’s consent to accept service of process from the party who submitted the takedown notice.
 
   Talking points
   (return to index)
PRO IS USING MY COPYRIGHTED CONTENT
(return to index)
 

DO’S
DON’T
Do: Highlight your role:
 
Emphasize that you are not an attorney, and your purpose is to provide information only and not legal advice.
Don’t: Give advice: 
 
Provide information but do not offer personalized advice on legal matters.
Do: Provide General Information:
 
Offer clear explanations about copyright and trademark concepts without making definitive statements.
Don’t: Confirm infringement occurred:
 
Avoid stating whether something is or isn't infringement; instead, provide general information about what our requirements are for review.
Encourage pro/consumers to consult with an attorney for any legal advice or specific guidance on their copyright or trademark concerns.
Don’t: Give recommendations: 
Don't suggest specific actions that require legal expertise (i.e., Don't suggest that they get it registered. that is up to them.)
  
Optional responses:
 
“We understand how important it is that copyrighted content/material isn’t being used inappropriately. We appreciate you sharing these concerns with us, and we’d like to investigate further. If we can confirm this is copyright infringement, then we’ll remove the content.”
“I’ll send you an email with more information. To move forward, we’ll need appropriate documentation, like a complete Notice of Infringement and a list of what specific items you’re requesting be removed and where they’re located.”
PRO IS USING MY TRADEMARK
(return to index)
There’s a formal process you can go through to register a trademark. Have you done so?”
“No, I haven’t registered a trademark.”
“Since the trademark hasn’t been registered, we can’t force _______ to stop using the same name for their business. If you would like information on registering your trademark, a good place to start is the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office’s website, www.uspto.gov.”
 
“Yes, I’ve registered a trademark.”
 
“Great, thanks for letting us know! Unfortunately, we’re not in a position and don’t have enough information to make a determination about whether one person’s intellectual property is infringing on the rights of another. That’s up to a court to decide. If you have a court order or some sort of settlement agreement you’d like to share with us, we’d be happy to review the situation further.”
“Otherwise, we encourage you to take whatever actions you feel are Legal - Copyright - No Violationappropriate to pursue the situation further outside of Thumbtack.”
 
   Emails
   (return to index)
COPYRIGHT: EMAIL TEMPLATES
(return to index)
Legal: Copyright concerns: Use this macro to obtain the information we require in order to process a notice of infringement to the reported user.
Legal: Copyright - Reply to official notice of infringement: Use this macro when the required information has been provided by the copyright holder and to inform them that the material has been removed.
Legal - Copyright - No Violation Found: Send this macro to the reporting party if we are unable to locate the material they reported as an infringement to allow them to send additional information if they feel necessary.
Legal: Copyright - Notify reported user of infringement: Send this macro to the reported user to notify them that we have removed copyrighted material from their profile. Provides detailed steps as far as providing a counter-notice and potential legal action from the copyright holder.
Legal: Copyright - Counter notice request: Send this macro to obtain the missing information required to provide a counter-notice to the copyright holder/original reporting party.
Legal: Copyright - Notify of counter notice: Informs the copyright holder/reporting party that the infringing user is contesting the removal of the materials in question. Provides next steps for them to take to prevent the materials from being reinstated. ATTACH COUNTER NOTICE TO THIS EMAIL.
Legal: Copyright - Counter notice filed - No response: Send this macro to the “infringing” user if the original reporting party does not notify us within 10 business days that they are taking legal action to prevent the materials from being used. This informs the “infringing” user that they are free to repost the disputed materials.
Legal: Copyright - Notify reported user of legal action: Send this macro to the “infringing” user to notify them that the copyright holder has taken legal action against them to prevent the materials from being reinstated.
TRADEMARK: EMAIL TEMPLATES
(return to index)
Legal: Trademark - Unable to determine: Use this macro when someone is reporting a trademark violation without supplementary documentation.
Legal: Trademark - Reply to trademark infringement report: Use this macro when responding to a pro who has provided a formal letter requesting the takedown of infringed material.
Legal: Trademark - Notify reported user of infringement: Use this macro when notifying a pro we have received a Trademark infringement notification and we are removing the content in violation.
**Use the content request form to request an update or submit questions/concerns**

Contact Verification
(Knowledge index)

What
(return to index)
Contact Verification (CV) is a queue where customer requests are flagged for manual review. The Trust and Safety task is to evaluate if the request is acceptable, following and actioning according to Thumbtack’s Terms of Services.
Why
(return to index)
We review customer requests to protect the Thumbtack brand and the quality of our customer and pros’ user experience. If the tickets aren’t processed promptly, they’ll be passed through and syndicated within 15 minutes. Requests not evaluated within 15 minutes auto-pass and may expose pros to deceptive behavior.
When
(return to index)
The Request Spam Model scores request:
A minimum score will automatically action and ghost the user's account, and the request will not be sent to the Platform.
Requests with certain issues, such as being “potentially spammy” or those that contain certain words or signals, will trigger Salesforce to create a Work Ticket for manual evaluation. The syndication link in the WT Details provides comprehensive details of the user making the request.
During the evaluation of CV WT, instructions found in the Deceptive Practice Identification procedure and the TOS Violations procedure should be followed.
SLA for the CV queue is 15 minutes, and Target HT is 2.5 minutes.
How
(return to index)
   Steps
   (return to index)
PROCESS OVERVIEW
(return to index)
 
[Image: Screenshot 2024-06-27 at 2.01.49 PM.png]
Click the link under the Work Ticket Details. It will direct you to the Syndication Portal in Admin.
Review for any deceptive behavior and/or TOS violations.
Check the customer’s default phone number for banned linked accounts.
If strongly linked, mirror the banned account action. 
Refer to the Deceptive Practice Identification procedure and the Terms of Service Violations procedure for detailed steps and information. 
Based on the investigation done:
If applicable, take action against the account. 
Refer to the Quickview for the actions required for each violation.
Syndicate, ghost, or delete the request in the Syndication Portal.  
If the request is a legitimate contact, click Yes, Syndicate this Request.
If the request does not abide by our Terms of Use, it should not be syndicated.
If determined to be spam (meets the required signals), click No, Ghost Request.
If the request is likely spam (has 5+ signals but doesn’t meet ghosting criteria), click No, Delete Request and select Other Violation from the dropdown. Include any additional details about why the request was not syndicated in the notes.
If the request is determined to violate our Terms of Service, click No, Delete Request and select the corresponding violation from the dropdown. Include any additional details about why the request was not syndicated in the notes.
Note: If multiple violations are found, use the violation with the higher sanction in Admin, and then tag all violations found in Tack. If the same level of sanction applies in Admin, choose either of the violations and then tag all violations found in Tack.
Fill out the Outcome and Admin Actions sections in the WT.
Refer to the Quickview for the Outcome and Outcome Details required for each violation.
Under Admin Actions, choose the corresponding actions done in Admin.

Q: What to do when the language used in the creation of the service request is in a Foreign Language​​​​​

A: We are okay with customers using foreign languages as long as we can verify that the English translation doesn't reveal a different TOS violation.
If the English translation is found to have violated any of our other terms of service, the most egregious TOS violation should be used as a deletion reason.e.g. ¡Por favor, tocame! (Translation: Please touch me.)This should be tagged as Sexual. Therefore, we will delete and blocklist the user.

Chargebacks
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY

What
(return to index)
A chargeback occurs when a user contacts their bank or credit card company about a charge they disagree with or do not recognize and dispute a charge from Thumbtack. When a dispute is filed, the funds are immediately removed from Thumbtack’s account and given back to the cardholder while the investigation takes place.
The Chargeback queue aims to get chargebacks reversed by submitting the required documentation through Stripe.
Why
(return to index)
Chargebacks directly impact the profitability and success of Thumbtack. Responsive chargeback monitoring minimizes that risk. 

When
(return to index)
When a dispute is filed resulting in a chargeback to Thumbtack, a Work Ticket (WT) is generated for manual review. The creation of the WT is controlled by a becquerel view (managed by Payments Risk in GitHub) that is administered by BusApps. Currently, this view is refreshed daily between 7-8 am MST with data from Stripe and Salesforce.
SLA for the chargeback queues is 120 hours, and Target HT is 7 minutes.
How
(return to index)

(return to index)
Receive WT
Confirm the dispute type.

Submit the evidence packet.

Fill out the WT Outcome section.
Close WT

Customer Details
(return to index)
Open WT.
Pull an unassigned WT from the “Customer Chargeback - New” WT list view. 
Confirm what type of chargeback you're handling by looking to the right of Evidence Submission Info in the WT. 
C2P
TOD
Check if the dispute was already resolved. 
Click on the Dispute Link in the WT Details to open up the Stripe dispute page. 
Note: If you are getting an error when clicking on the Dispute Link, make sure you are logged into the correct version of Stripe (Marketplace for customers and Pro Payments for pros).
If the dispute was already resolved, the Stripe dispute page will display “won” or “lost” in the top right corner. If you see either of these, move on to step 9. 
Confirm if the dispute needs to be escalated to Payments Risk. The WT will need to be escalated if:

There is an Incident Number listed under Chargeback Work Ticket Details in the WT.

Customer Members can select a job type and schedule a service and pay their professional directly through the Thumbtack app. The Thumbtack platform only facilitates payments between Customer Members and Service Pro Members (“Marketplace Payments”) through our payment processing partner Stripe, but Thumbtack is not a party to any such Marketplace Payments and does not handle funds on behalf of its Members.

articles.fullText:
Blocklist Hits

Blocklist Hits
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Work ticket quick view
Confidence form
General process
Account investigation steps
Link analysis guide
Outcome: Accurate
Outcome: Indeterminate
Work ticket outcome and actions
Outcome: Inaccurate
Details
Utilizing override user link
Other BLH workflows
Inappropriate photos involving minors
Email
What
(return to index)
When an account is blocklisted or put on hold, we do not allow re-entry unless they have resolved all issues pertaining to the blocklist or hold status. However, pros sometimes circumvent this process by creating new accounts. Work tickets will then be created when information on an active account matches information on a blocklisted account.
Note: As long as the profile shows that the account is on hold, we'll consider it as such, even when there are no account hold logs.

Why
(return to index)
We want to ensure we are making fair and reasonable judgments on account deletions. If we do not have sufficient information linking the accounts, we should not take action.
You should feel empowered and confident to make the decision on work tickets, so escalation for additional review is not needed.
Be thorough in your review and answer the questions in the work ticket as completely as possible to provide an accurate confidence score (if using). Be sure to include notes on your findings.
When
(return to index)
First, an automatic re-entry check is completed at signup, and if a pro changes their email after signup. Checks are also triggered if blocklisted information is sent in a quote message or added to a profile. Based on the rules that are triggered, certain actions will be taken (deletion, manual review, or passing). If marked for manual review, these work tickets are created and sent to Salesforce via an internal API called “MI Salesforce Integration.”
There are 14 ways a work ticket can be triggered for this queue- the links will be outlined in the Name of the specific work ticket and can include one or a combination of the following links:
Profile: Phone -  Linked active user has a banned phone number on their profile.
Quote: Phone - Linked active user mentions banned phone number in quote message.
Quote: Email - Linked active user mentions banned email in quote message.
TMX: Fuzzy Device ID - The linked active user is using the same device as a deleted pro.
IP Address - A linked active user shares an IP address with a deleted pro.
Profile: Email - The user has changed their email to that of a banned user sometime after signup.
Same Address and Name or Signup IP - A linked active user shares an address and either name or Signup IP with a disabled user.
Same Name and at least 2 IP Addresses - A linked active user shares a name and more than 1 IP address with a disabled user.
Same Service Name, Category and City - A linked active user shares a service name, category, and city with a disabled user.
Same Images - Linked active users share at least 3 uploaded images with a disabled Pro.
Same License and State or Type - A linked active user shares a license number and state or license type with a disabled Pro.
Message: Phone - Linked active user mentions a banned phone number in the messenger.
Message: Email - A linked active user mentions a banned email in the messenger.
SLA for the Blocklist Hits (BLH) queue is 24 hours, and HT target is 6.5 minutes.
How
(return to index)
  Steps
   (return to index)
WORK TICKET QUICK VIEW
(return to index)
When your Routing Skills include "Blocklist Hits," you should automatically receive tickets like the one below.

[Image: Work Ticket.jpeg]

Type of link that triggered this ticket. For this example, it is Profile: Phone.
List of blocklisted accounts. Each link leads to the corresponding admin page.
The active account to be investigated. The View User button located on the right corner under the Thumbtack User section redirects to the account's admin page.
To the right corner, under the Outcome section, is where you'll tag according to your review.

[Image: outcome.jpeg]
Outcome: "Accurate," "Indeterminate," "Inaccurate," "Ticket is Duplicate."
Internal Notes: State if the active account was reinstated, linked to the account on hold, etc., as well as specialist's notes as to why accounts are strongly or weakly linked.

CONFIDENCE FORM
(return to index)
On the Work Ticket, you can find the Confidence Scoring Form and the Confidence Score. Use this form if you are unsure of the linkage between the accounts. You do not need to fill out the Confidence Form of the work ticket if you are confident that the two accounts are strongly linked. This tool is more useful for newer specialists to help them familiarize the investigative process.

[Image: confidence form.jpeg]

Account Holder Names Match - Does the name on the active account match that of the banned account?
Three options: "Yes," "No," "No, but they are similar."
Email Address Similarity - Are their email addresses similar?
Three options: "Contains the same/similar identifying name information," "Contains the same/similar identifying company information," and "Not similar."
Address Match - How similar are their physical addresses?
Five options: "Exact Match," "Same Zip Code," "Same City," "Same State," and "No Similarities."
Number of Phone Number Matches - How many similar phone numbers do they share?
Four options: "0," "1," "2," "3+."
Profile Pictures Match - Are their profile pictures similar?
Three options: "Yes," "No," "No, but they are similar."
Business/Service Name Match - Are their business/service profile names similar?
Three options: "Yes," "No," "No, but they are similar."
Service/Category Match - Do they offer at least one similar service/category?
Two options: "Yes," or "No"
Number of IP Matches - How many similar IP addresses do they share?
Account Creation Date - When was the active account created?
Original Account Creation Date - When was the banned account created?
Original Account Action Date - When was the banned account blocklisted or put on hold?
Phone Number Referenced - Is the banned user's phone number referenced in the quote (seen in the Tack ticket)?
Banned User Name Referenced - Is the banned user's name referenced in the quote message, quote template, or review?
Banned Company Name Referenced - Is the banned user's business/service name referenced in the quote message, quote template, or review?
Degrees of Link - What is the active account's degree of link to the banned account?
Three options: 1 (Linked directly to the original banned user), 2 (Linked to an account that was removed for being linked to a banned user), 3+ (Linked to 2 or more accounts before being linked to the original banned user)
Auditor Confidence - How confident are you that these accounts are linked to each other?
Two options: "Yes", "No"
Confidence Score - The total score is calculated based on your answers to the questions, so it is important that the form be filled out as completely as possible.
If the confidence score is 40% and above, the accounts are strongly linked to each other.
If the confidence score is below 40%, the accounts are not strongly linked to each other.
Confidence Form Limitations
The confidence form should not be treated as the end-all-be-all. There are other signals that are not taken into consideration by the form; therefore, you should still use your best judgment in determining the proper outcome.
GENERAL PROCESS
(return to index)
First, pull up the admins of both the originally blocklisted and linked active accounts to compare their information for the next step.
If the account is linked to more than one (1) blocklisted account, choose which one among the list you would use for comparison, especially when using the confidence form. It is recommended to choose the linked account closest to the active account.
Be sure to check the Deletion Logs on the active and blocklisted users to uncover any and all past actions taken (Quote Gating, resolved issues, background check requests, etc.) and any possible additional linked accounts.
If the active account is accurately linked to the banned account, manually link them in Admin using the Override User Link feature.
​​​Note: No need to override linked users already in the “Featured Linked Users” section.
Check for similarities - first names, last names, emails and email domains, profile pictures, addresses, phone numbers, service names, and even looking into quote messages for similarities is very insightful. If they have reviews, look for mentions of the other users.

ACCOUNT INVESTIGATION STEPS
(return to index)
Check if the accounts are linked by one or more phone numbers.
Identification as non-default phone numbers should be the least signal to assess when deciding. If we find that one of the phone numbers is non-default, then treat this as a weak signal.
Answer the confidence form properly first before taking the non-default phone number into consideration.
If they are linked by a junk phone number and no other links are found, delete the phone number from the active account so it does not pull a future Work Ticket.
You can typically recognize a “junk” phone number by repeating the same digit throughout the whole number, numbers like 123-456-7890, "555" phone numbers (reserved for use by TV and movies), etc.
Check the number of IP address matches between the accounts.
Check the Login History on the admin page. Be sure to click on Load Logins.

[Image: Screenshot 2024-03-11 at 12.54.55 PM.png]
For banned accounts, sometimes the Login history is no longer available. You can check the IP addresses used by the banned account on the Blocklist Record.

[Image: Screenshot 2024-03-11 at 12.55.54 PM.png]
On the Page Actions section, click on the View Blocklist Record.
On the Blocklist Record, you can see a list of IP addresses used by the banned account.
Note: Generally, IP is considered a weak signal by itself.
Check if the accounts have the same or similar physical address.
Use the address/es found in the user profile. Do not use the geolocation in the login history, as these are not reliable.
Check for other signals that could link these accounts.
Other signals or clues can be found in accounts that are not accounted for in the confidence form. Signals such as LADS (Linked Accounts Detection System), aka Linked Users page, information only mentioned on reviews or quote messages and templates that are not automatically flagged, profile pictures that don't match but contain business information, etc.
Outside resources should be the last resort in edge cases. We should rely first on the resources provided by Thumbtack to establish the confidence score.
In edge cases where we need more information, we consider non-Thumbtack sources as valid if they are updated and strongly show connection/non-connection.
If signals other than those that can be noted in the confidence form can be found by thoroughly reviewing the accounts involved or by searching for reliable information outside of Thumbtack for edge cases, then that can be the basis of auditor confidence as to whether accounts are linked or not.
Make sure to add additional findings to the internal notes field so that the thought process used in decision-making can be verified.
Check whether the accounts are part of a franchise or not.
For franchise accounts, unless they work in the same state, we should not take action on these franchises if their only similarity of information results from being part of the franchise.
e.g., Pro accounts for franchises of Off ****** ** Training always trigger BLH tickets since the accounts usually contain the company's main nationwide toll-free number (888) 413-0*** and their email domain@off********training.com.

LINK ANALYSIS GUIDE
(return to index)
We may use the chart below to determine if the Active account and Originally banned account are Strongly linked or not.
There are three groups with different sets of combinations that could help us decide if the accounts could be considered strongly linked.

Strong Signals - If the accounts have this combination we can already consider it as strongly linked.
Secondary Signals - If the accounts do not have Strong signals, they should have at least 2 Secondary Signals from the chart below, for us to be able to tag it as strongly linked.
Weak Signals - If these are the only signals we have, we cannot consider the accounts as strongly linked. Consider tagging it as indeterminate if the confidence score is below 40%
 
[Image: AD_4nXfa0L-v3Hnq53l_bhgDH8Qph18Q0V9TqbseEvMuacrQx-iALy7Vg2okgk0F0ZtKFKas3fS-ET25L4wHvTD5Xeroa_FvxHzhWf3ZOL7HPKkMz3Kbwu-85ociXIn2jVLVyhi2EWA7]


BLH PROCESS MAP
(return to index)

[Image: AD_4nXdEeTYJnFdIWz2rsEwizrBev-fK9o2uR55ZPmyjd3A_8JTehVXh0cm6-8eayKc7tv4li0FwxTc79IwQ_QArfSvFQpKyDzJkTktJuaACvdppKD9swXS5fHKUQaUHdLA3vntf_T10HA]

 
WORK TICKET OUTCOME AND ACTIONS
(return to index)

OUTCOME IN TACK
BRIEF DESCRIPTION
ACTION IN ADMIN
Accurate
The accounts are strongly linked.
Action the active account.
Manually link them using Override User Link if needed.
Indeterminate
The accounts are not strongly linked.
The active account has already been actioned.
The active or banned account has been reinstated.
No action or unblocklist accounts if needed.
Inaccurate
The accounts are linked by junk phone numbers.
The accounts are part of Thumbtack's Pre-building Profiles Project.
One of the accounts is owned by a Thumbtack employee.
No action or delete the junk phone number if needed.
Note: You may also refer to the BLH Summary of Admin Actions, a charted version of the guidelines for each outcome below, for a simplified view.
Outcome: Accurate
(return to index)

OUTCOME IN TACK
BRIEF DESCRIPTION
ACTION IN ADMIN
Accurate
The accounts are strongly linked.
Action the active account
The Outcome is "Accurate" if all of the following criteria are met:
The original banned account is still blocklisted.
The accounts share a strong link, or the confidence score is 40% and above, and.
The active account is not a managed account, has not been actioned beforehand, or the active account's previous issues are different from the banned account's issues.

Inclusions:
If the active account is a Pro and the originally banned account is disabled but NOT user deleted/requested by the user:
Delete the active account under Delete Reason: "(Pro) Linked to a previously banned account."
Paste the User PKID of the banned account under Linked User PKs.
Add user to the Blocklist using Reason: "Previously Banned," and add other info if applicable."
Note: If the active pro and previously banned users are linked through the quote phone number, input the phone number in the Phone Number Field in the Blocklist page in Admin.
If the active account is a Pro and the originally banned account is on hold but enabled or on hold and disabled by user deletion/requested by the user:
Delete the active account under Delete Reason: "(Pro) Linked to previously banned account."
Paste the User PKID of the banned account under Linked User PKs.
State in both the Deletion Notes and the ticket's Internal Notes: "Linked to Account on Hold #."
Note: If the originally banned account is on hold and disabled due to Internal Process or due to another violation, we should delete AND blocklist the active account. This “Disabled” status supersedes the "On Hold" status.
Note #2: If the active user is already on hold (Enabled/Hold/BL status) and is strongly linked to another Hold/BL account, we do not need to un-BL the "active user" for us to disable this account. Instead, click Admin Delete from the Page Actions directly and put the reason for deletion. This way, the BL status of the Hold flag will still remain.
Note #3: There may be times when there are other linked banned accounts that were blocklisted because:
The original banned account was also once deleted and blocklisted or
 The on-hold + BL status of the original banned account incorrectly triggered the system to automatically add them to the Blocklist.
If we encounter these linked banned accounts, we need to remove them from BL after confirming that the original banned account is only on hold + enabled or on hold + deleted by the user. Doing so will prevent these accounts from reentering the queue. The specialist should still tag this as Accurate and leave notes explaining why the linked accounts were removed from Blocklist.
The active account is strongly linked to a confirmed spam account:
If the active account is a pro, delete it using "Pro(Spammy)." If the active account is a customer, ghost using the Reason, “Spam Message: Manual Review.”
Paste the User PKID of the banned account under Linked User PKs.
Type "Linked to spammy user" in the Notes.
Add the user to the Blocklist using Reason: "Scam or Fake Requests" and add other info if applicable.
Note: Managed accounts should still follow the escalation process to a manager.
If the active account is a customer and the banned pro account is deleted and blocklisted:
Check the deletion reason for the banned pro account.
For background-related deletions and non-Trust and Safety violations, we should allow the customer account to remain active and tag this scenario as "Indeterminate."
For Trust and Safety violations, we should also action the customer account via the following steps:
Delete the account under Delete Reason: "Other."
Paste the User PKID of the banned account under Linked User PKs.
Type "Linked to banned user" in the Notes.
Add user to the Blocklist using Reason: "Previously Banned," and add other info if applicable."

UTILIZING OVERRIDE USER LINK
(return to index)
If you find a link to be accurate, but they aren’t found in the Feature Linked users section, manually link them through the Override User Link.  
Note: If the active user and banned user are linked via multiple link types, they should all be included in 1 entry to follow the existing format of LADS.
In Tack, click View User to access the active user admin profile.
On the active user admin profile, click Show Linked Users. Under the Feature Linked User's, make sure that the banned account to be linked is not found there.
Click the Override User Link on the Page Actions box.
Fill out the following fields, then click Confirm:

Override Type - choose User Link
User PK/s
Reason (format: BLH WT#xxxx - linked by [link type in the WT details, not title, e.g., profile phone], linked account name.)
For the Reason field, make sure to get the link type of the banned user you selected from the Details section of the WT. You may add additional link types (e.g., linked by profile phone, name, email).[Image: Screenshot 2022-12-15 at 3.35.14 PM.png]

OTHER BLH WORKFLOWS
(return to index)
Outside the BLH queue, we also review blocklist hits that come through soft links and pro messages. These workflows aren’t currently in Tack. However, if assigned these processes, reviewing the account links as accurate, indeterminate, or inaccurate is the same.
Soft Links

New data will be uploaded into the BLH- Soft links working sheet daily. Review columns C-J to investigate, and fill out K-O.

Pro Message

New data will be uploaded into BLH (pro message)- Phone and email working sheet daily. Review columns A-K to investigate, and fill out L-R and AB-AD.
Open the quote link in column K to review the entire conversation.
Ensure the flagged email or phone number is associated with the active pro. If the number is the customer’s and there are no other strong links between the active and banned accounts, do not action the pro.
Search the phone or email address in Admin under Users, and review all accounts that appear in the results to determine the link status.
Confirm the linked phone number isn’t already deleted from their profile. If it is deleted, the account link is inaccurate.
If the accounts are strongly linked, review the banned pro user’s deletion logs.
If the deletion logs show they were undeleted already, coordinate with the person who took that action to know more about the reason for undeleting.
If there’s information available on the deletion reason, such as case/WT number, search in tack before making a decision. If it wasn’t clear, proceed to coordinate with the person who undelete the account.
Action account according to the outcome
Accurate
Indeterminate
Inaccurate

If the flagged pro is currently enabled OR on an account hold due to fake reviews and was strongly linked to an enabled pro/customer account, don’t action the linked account.
If the flagged pro was strongly linked to a disabled account because the user deleted their account, then we won’t do anything to the enabled account.
If the pro that was flagged was strongly linked to an account on hold because of the quote gating process, then we won’t do anything to the enabled account.

INAPPROPRIATE PHOTOS INVOLVING MINORS
(return to index)
