BGC ID Mismatch

BGC ID Mismatch
(Knowledge index 
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Overview
Evaluate for a match
Close a case
Details
No Fiides info available
Hyphenated/Multiple names
Duplicate accounts
Emails
Related
What
(return to index)
The BGC ID mismatch queue reviews the details of the pro account and compares it with the results of the background check. All pros in this queue have passed a BGC but need to be reviewed to confirm the report is for the Thumbtack account owner. 

Why
(return to index)
This task ensures that the person who passed the BGC and the owner of the Thumbtack account are the same person. We need to confirm this before we add a badge to their account. 

When
(return to index)
A new case is triggered when BGC results come back “Clear,” but the information in Admin, like name and date of birth, does not match the Checkr report.
SLA for the BGC ID Mismatch queue is 48 hours, and handle time varies between 3 and 7 minutes.
How
(return to index)

[Image: t01IW3suNuojlcsYLDb6lKj_tdhJcmSqxKTinI7Kf-AFRa_N3kbQkgexsFWXkMPmbSBOPOPTqoMbnvhwSDs99zd0L1dt9cw82cq5fwTGyDcIr8Z3YgJI2Gd0xDRsiuhrxD0QenSa-8fOIL60jPOfPkM]

   Steps
   (return to index)
OVERVIEW
(return to index)
Receive Case via Omni.
Click on the Details tab [Image: rtaImage]
Scroll down to the Description section and review the details of the mismatch.
Fides name/DOB = What the pro provided as their name/date of birth when they signed up. 
Checkr name/DOB = What was submitted in Checkr on the BGC. 

[Image: qPT1Gu8mns_QZY9KGCkbcHqaLgunOq0MufZYlAC-dAhKMdD4_EBlMIfyOqa-ErtDbMbRkPOfCpAfvpbATuRk4AumFcfohBI4gSA5-r0RCLJ5synsuagb0ZE6XTShdQDrk_-KPEasQG-JPrVHMZLcw_Q]

Note: If case details are not showing (Fides name/Checkr name results), go to User Admin and click on “Show verification data.” Review the name and DOB submitted to Thumbtack vs. the one in Checkr.
Compare the details to evaluate for a match.
If it’s a match:
Apply the BGC badge in admin by clicking Add Checkr Verification on the right-hand side.
If the pro has an old badge from a previous BGC, delete it and update the badge with the most recent date. 
If a recent badge has already been applied, close the case.
                                                       
[Image: Screenshot 2023-09-26 at 2.38.57 PM.png]

Select the date the mismatch case was created in Tack for the Verification Date:
Ensure their name is spelled correctly and matches the pro’s Checkr results.
Check the box for “Is Good.”
Copy and enter the Checkr Report ID (found in the case details; otherwise, reach out to any ID help team member to get it).
Click Confirm.

[Image: Screenshot 2023-09-26 at 2.40.02 PM.png]

If you make an update to the name for a small correction, click on Edit Identity Information and enter the pro’s legal name and date of birth as listed on their Checkr BGC. 
You’ll need to input their address from the verification data as it was entered previously. If there is no address in the verification data, do not proceed with editing the identity information. These cases can be sent to ID help, where they will ask the user to send a photo of their government-issued ID. 

[Image: Screenshot 2023-09-26 at 2.40.48 PM.png]

If it’s NOT a match:
If you’re not sure that they’re the same person, send BGC ID Mismatch - Ask Pro to submit ID to ID help so we can verify their information to the Thumbtack account owner.
If it’s clear they’re not the same person, send BGC ID Mismatch - Notify pro account owner must submit BGC to the Thumbtack account owner.
Close the case.
EVALUATE FOR A MATCH
(return to index)
To determine if the pro is the same person, we need to verify that the information is a MATCH. Follow the guidance below to determine what is considered a match:
Date of Birth in Thumbtack platform/admin and Checkr are exact matches
First and Last Name in the Thumbtack platform/admin is a match, and Checkr results are a close match. (only one letter variation of either last name or first name) 
First Name in either of the reports are different but fall under a common nickname or name variations. For reference to name variations, you can click on this link.
Disabled accounts due to “user delete” or non-TOS violation reason (like “User has been escalated to Checkr by Fides”) — if user account is disabled in Thumbtack but passed the BGC, we apply the badge.
Note: DOB details should always match.

DECISION
NAME
DATE OF BIRTH
MATCH
Fides Name: Jhon Smith 
Checkr Name: John Smith
Fides DOB: 01/02/1985 
Checkr DOB: 01/02/1985
MATCH
Fides Name: Sam Smith 
Checkr Name: Samantha Smith
Fides DOB: 01/02/1985 
Checkr DOB: 01/02/1985
It is considered NOT A MATCH if:
The name matches, but the DOB is different. 
This can happen between family members. (Sr. and Jr.) 
Thumbtack account name is the business name, and Checkr results are under a business name. 
If there are uncertainties in determining whether the details are the same or if they are of the same person (e.g., Individuals with four names and report does not match our information in the Thumbtack platform).

DECISION
NAME
DATE OF BIRTH
NOT A MATCH
Fides Name: John Smith 
Checkr Name: John Smith
Fides DOB: 01/02/1985
Checkr DOB: 01/02/1963
NOT A MATCH
Fides Name: Housekeeping Services
Checkr Name: Housekeeping Services
Fides DOB: 01/02/1985
Checkr DOB: 01/02/1985
CLOSE A CASE
(return to index)
Go to MTS Categorize/Status tab.

[Image: yQ-jfuJp8aaXtoW2n4M3jUiF4aozjNmS2cbJc0F0T2ZvgmsDVLmQ_DeEmsPMWS8nKEKokb1FVH-sg0VuX57AisLE0uzPILEoj-rFG3Kxx88p9NIDVzYgQhrVVSsfvMzoCkH6_RTio0eh0LAHpYp1Dcw]

Look for the Status field, click on the pencil button, and choose the “Closed” option.

[Image: gTihaI5mgDcHDtsiB9gBFUuf34XHRiXSLfIdd9w7CalCoSZtMCh8BtmwVBdyeCRFr-t5ZHTODmYtlqh4JDzNa9KGVla87XB9laApluP0oo079clIyzLxuol6qIQsIpqjvZpxeXkMlr3TqnDr1Q0Us0Y]

In the Do Not Survey field, choose “Marketplace Integrity,” as we do not send surveys for these. 
Click on the Save button.

[Image: K2osvDIgI3jd4nUDlT0TF8AWNqcGNlM4v2EWy_p15eGkVfZT_Ma5kJiB7t8nVXq_q7idOJzw67g5cFO8HJpoHXXuyui6Vr6XdvpGGpyEwYl4ep6tZjdic4qMRuVTvZ6wNVcB8cTjHLrqwI5L9m3a3W4]

   Details
   (return to index)
NO FIDES INFO AVAILABLE
(return to index)
If information is unavailable in the Description section in Tack or cannot be verified in User Verification Data through Admin, have the user send a photo of their government-issued ID to ID Help.
So we can verify information, update the D.O.B. or information, and badge the account.

[Image: pKqW5z6xSUVjXKsUCvcRWAygUgP45DmXG_5rCQ-MXPawQEVvimFcnsQFvTXvE-zIl5YJzrHcCUZQp5GD3uGO9b1TZWLQb-W_L5yTYfjx8AEqafev2HSsuAkTKwvAMmqFQiaFN8pcIH0q_pAV_VLrOKo]

HYPHENATED/MULTIPLE NAMES
(return to index) 
For users with four names or hyphenated names where the information in Admin and Checkr results are not a match, have the user send a photo of their government-issued ID to ID Help.
We want to make sure Checkr results, Admin, and their ID are the same before we update and badge the account.
Sample:
Background check type: Voluntary
Thumbtack website name: Jane Smith-Jones
Fides name: Jane Smith
Fides DOB:  12/08/1984
Checkr name: Jane Smith-Jones
Checkr DOB:  1984-12-08
DUPLICATE ACCOUNTS
(return to index) 
Pros are allowed to have multiple accounts as long as they are not offering the same services in the same area on both accounts.
For true duplicate accounts offering the same services in the same area, we usually require the pro to keep the most established account. If they are all similarly established, we can let the pro decide which one they want to keep.
Look over each account, especially the reviews, to ensure the pro is not trying to avoid any negative reviews posted on the profile.


SCENARIO
DESCRIPTION
ACTIONS
Scenario 1
Old Account: Disabled, No BGC but with negative reviews.
 
New Account: Active and BGC Passed.
Action: Badge the old account and advise the user that we will delete the new one. 
 
​​Account Action: Delete the new account and add notes saying- “Do not reinstate-dup account-pro needs to use. (Enter admin number)”
 
Email: Send macro “BGC ID MISMATCH-  Pro has Duplicate Accounts- will badge the old account.”
Scenario 2
Old Account: Disabled, No BGC but with no negative review.
 
New Account: Active BGC Passed.
Action: Badge the new account.
Scenario 3
Old Account: Disabled, No BGC but with no negative review.
 
New Account: Disabled, BGC Passed.
Action: Badge the old account. -

   Emails
   (return to index)  
BGC ID Mismatch - Notify pro account owner must submit BGC: Results for BGC were not from the account owner. The user needs to resubmit in the account holder's name.
BGC ID Mismatch - Ask Pro to submit ID to ID help so we can verify their information: Information submitted through BGC needs to be verified. Asks user to submit information to ID help for verification.
BGC ID Mismatch -  Reopened Cases for additional concerns - Ask Pro to submit to IDhelp: User sent us information in reopened case (not secure). Requests the user to resubmit through the ID help form for further assistance.
BGC ID Mismatch -  Pro has Duplicate Accounts- will badge the old account: User submitted BGC under a recent duplicate account. Informs the user we’ve removed the duplicate account and badged the original.
BGC ID Mismatch - Admin name misspelled - Changed to match Checkr: BGC confirms the user name was misspelled at initial sign-up. Informs the user we’ve corrected the mistake and badged the account. 
   Related
   (return to index) 
Name Variations

What
​​(return to index)
The Better Business Bureau (BBB) is a platform that allows consumers to rate and review businesses and file complaints. The BBB grades businesses from A-F based on their responsiveness to customer complaints. Thumbtack reviews and responds to any submitted complaints to maintain an “A” rating on its site.
Why
​​(return to index)
To maintain Thumbtack’s public reputation and cultivate trust in the platform, it’s important we maintain an “A” rating with the BBB. Our rating is based on consistent timely responses to all complaints and rebuttals.
Since review responses are not factored into our rating, we don’t respond to posted reviews unless they report concerns.
When
​​(return to index)
When Thumbtack receives a complaint or rebuttal, it will appear in the dashboard on our BBB complaint portal.
The SLAs for responding:
BBB complaints - 9 days
BBB rebuttals - 6 days.
The AHTs:
Complaints - 10 minutes
Rebuttals - 5 minutes
How
​​(return to index)
   Steps
    (return to index) 
BBB PROCESS OVERVIEW
(return to index) 
Log in to the Better Business Bureau complaints dashboard.
Select a case that requires a response.
Review the complaint.
Add to the tracker if this is a new complaint, or update the tracker for rebuttals.
Investigate the user’s concern.
Respond.
BBB COMPLAINTS
(return to index)
Complaints dashboard
(return to index)

[Image: AD_4nXckMGjLFyJdnNeW2991POVCixjow5czvyAo2-ta4NsD79sD3GkmD_byW7_MwcQciEn7W3je65CPcTlMJPVXjLignInsmiph6ks6LkBxVbjrDEoKtjLnCjc27FyCG-Wl9Gik-okgWQMLA3E_e2UIHdtAFbQ]

Complaints requiring immediate attention, or those that are within 6 days of the deadline to respond.
All open complaints, including ones that are pending consumer responses.
All complaints awaiting a response from Thumbtack.
Unanswered complaints.
This should always be zero since a specialist will reply to every complaint before the deadline.
Complaint ID which allows specialists to click on the specific complaint, review the details, and submit a response.
INVESTIGATE A BBB COMPLAINT
(return to index)
Responses should address specific concerns, so while Specialists don’t need to become an expert on a consumer’s account with Thumbtack, it’s important to investigate enough to understand the context of the complaint.

Admin
Tack
Check the account status.
If the user has been actioned, review the action logs for notes on any relevant cases.
If relevant, review any linked accounts.
Search for the user account in Tack and check for the work ticket, case, or incident relevant to the complaint.
Support issue:
Review the most recent notes to determine what the outcome or next steps are for the user.
If the issue is ongoing and there are no clear next steps, feel free to reach out in the #xfnc_depts_help Slack channel.
T&S issue:
Review the incident or most recent notes to determine what the outcome or next steps are for the user
If something is unclear (payout status, eligibility, next steps, etc.), reach out to the agent assigned to the incident for details
RESPOND TO A BBB COMPLAINT
(return to index)
All complaints require a response, but the level of detail required in your response may vary depending on whether the consumer has already worked with a Thumbtack support agent or T&S specialist.
Remember that BBB complaints and responses are public. Do not include any sensitive or personally identifiable information.
Open/Pending issues
If an issue hasn’t been closed or resolved, or a Thumbtack representative is still working with the consumer:
Focus on the consumer’s next steps. 
Encourage them to follow up directly with the specialist or rep they’ve been working with for further assistance.
Reference the date and subject of the last contact they received.
Closed/Resolved issues
If an issue has already been handled and closed by a Thumbtack representative:
Repeat the information from the last contact the user received.
Encourage the reporter to follow up with the previous rep or specialist with any additional questions.
No previous TT contact
If the consumer hasn’t contacted Thumbtack about their issue:
Provide as much general information as you can to address their concern
If the consumer needs a specific resolution, encourage them to contact Service and Support or report a T&S concern. 
   Details 
    (return to index)
THUMBTACK’S BRAND VOICE
(return to index)
Specialists responding to the BBB represent Thumbtack, so it’s important they follow the Thumbtack Brand Voice expectations. The tone of every interaction should be relatable, grounded, and natural while also being helpful, instructive, and supportive with their answers. 

THINGS TO AVOID
PHRASES TO INCORPORATE
Overuse sympathy
Don’t start every message saying, “We apologize for the inconvenience.” 
Jargon (TT internal terms)
The royal “we”
We dug around and…
Let’s take a look
Let’s check this out
We checked it out
Glad you’re reaching out
We hear you
Thanks for letting us know.
That’s not the experience we want.
We want to help.
We’re listening
  Talking points
    ​​(return to index)
Reference BBB responses for snippets to incorporate.
   Troubleshooting 
    (return to index)
MULTIPLE REBUTTALS
Occasionally, the BBB may determine that more than one rebuttal is required.  This may be determined if: 
New information in consumer rejections
Status of the concern with the business
Our provided response is overly generic.
Less than a month has gone by since the initial submission.
If a second response is required from Thumbtack, the specialists should follow the same process listed above.
NOTE: If issues persist after attempting to troubleshoot, contact the T&S manager in charge of the BBB to contact the BBB account manager directly.

Background checks (incidents)


Background checks (incidents)
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT
WHY
WHEN
HOW
Steps
Request a pro take a background check
Process results
Details
Do’s and don’ts
Talking points
Emails
What
(return to index)
Background checks look into a user’s criminal history.
Quick info
Background checks are processed by specific team members - not everyone has access to them.
Background check results can take anywhere from an hour to 14 days to get back to us.
Publicly, we tell pros it could take 5-7 business days.
Determine the severity of charges listed based on the Removal Policy and Disposition Glossary.
Why
(return to index)
Thumbtack is constantly working to improve the safety and security of our marketplace by verifying the identity of all pros that advertise with us.
When
(return to index)
When signing up for Thumbtack, we do a verification of the personal info they enter. This verification may notify us of concerning info about that user, and we will request a background check that’s required to continue to use Thumbtack.
How
(return to index)
   Steps
   (return to index)
REQUEST A PRO TAKES A BACKGROUND CHECK
(return to index)
If you have a pro you feel should take a background check, you can request that they do so. Keep in mind that if they don't take the background check, they'll be removed from Thumbtack, which could impact whether they help your customer or not. If this is the case, you may want to wait until after they've resolved the issue to request they take the check.
Things to remember:
A pro has two days to take a background check once we've asked them to take one.
They'll remain "on hold" until they take the background check.
Only ask the owner of the account, not employees, to take a BGC.
In circumstances involving safety or public relations concerns, we may make an exception. Consult your manager before taking this step.
Request a background check
If you're ready to request a pro takes a background check, follow these steps:
Place the pro's account on hold.
Go to the pro's admin and change their identity status (on the left side of the admin page) to "required background check."
This puts a banner on the pro's account that will tell them to take the check before they can continue getting leads.
Note your incident to show we're asking the pro to take a background check and set a reminder to follow up on the account in 48 hours.
If the pro has taken the background check, the background check team will process the results and either remove the pro or give them a background check badge.
If the pro hasn't taken the background check, delete and blocklist the pro's account.
PROCESS RESULTS
(return to index)
To process a background check
Open the Checkr dashboard and filter for "consider results after 1/11/2019."
You can also use this link.
Review each charge. Information to consider are:
Disposition - The decision for the crime that was committed (dismissed or guilty).
Disposition date - The date the user was legally sentenced.
Charge - The type of crime the user committed.
Charge type - The degree of the crime they committed (misdemeanor, felony, etc.)
Determine whether the user will receive a background check badge or whether they'll be removed based on the results.
Refer to the Background Check Removal Policy and the BGC Glossary to determine if the charge would result in removal. (These documents shouldn't be available to the floor.)
If the user qualifies for a badge, select “Engage” on the report in Checkr. This means we’ve reviewed it and are taking action on it (applying the badge).
Add the badge on the user’s profile - make sure the name and DOB match Verification Data.
If the user will be removed based on the results, select “Pre Adverse Action” on the report in Checkr.
Select any guilty charges to be included in the email.
Review and send the BGC: Account Removal - Pre AA  - make sure the box is checked to “Auto send post-adverse action” in 7 days.
Go into the user’s account. If the pro has a positive balance, use "credit balance payout" to refund the appropriate amount back to their card.
Delete/blocklist with the note: “Pro failed BGC - Pre Adverse Action sent through Checkr.”
Make sure to check the BGC AA Unassigned queue in Tack for any replies to Pre-AA notices.
If the pro responds with additional information about their charges, we will accept any mitigating information about the charges and take this into consideration when making our decision.
Normally, our decision will remain the same, but we need to provide the option of correcting any errors.
If the user's BGC results change at any time, they can initiate a re-investigation with Checkr to dispute the results. We’ll always reconsider any new results provided.
The info the pro provided to Checkr is different than the account verification data:

The only person who can take the background check to get an account reinstated is the person whose information is in the verification data. Users can’t update this information, so another person can take the check.
Name is different:
We will email the pro and explain that only the person who signed up on the site is eligible to take the BGC/Receive the badge.
Email macro BGC: Mismatch - Submit.
If it’s possible the name is a typo, ask the pro to use this form to submit their ID so we can verify their identity.
Name is the same, but the Date of birth is vastly different (it could not be considered a typo):
Have the pro to use this form to submit their ID so we can verify their identity.
   Details
   (return to index)
DO'S AND DON'TS
(return to index)
Do make sure to send the appropriate macros to the pro:
BGC: Account Removal - Pre AA: Pre-AA to notify of our intentionsBGC: Account Removal - Post AA: Post-AA email finalizing our decision.
Do understand making the pro take a BGC too soon can negatively impact the outcome of your incident.
Don’t use your name on the emails you send - these are worked anonymously.
   Talking points
   (return to index)
Talking points for customers
Talking points for pros 
   Emails
   (return to index)
If you’re new to the background check team, refer to the Grammarly snippets doc to properly set up your TE with these necessary shortcuts.
BGC: Account Removal - Post AA: Send this to the account holder after taking adverse action on their account for not taking the BGC check.
BGC: Account Removal - Pre AA: Send this email to warn the account holder that we will take adverse action on their account if they don’t take the BGC.
BGC: Disable Account: Send to the account holder when  they haven’t completed the BGC we’ve removed their account.
BGC: Pro Upset - Account Removed: Sent to the account holder if they’re upset about their account being removed for not taking a BGC.
BGC: Request to take Background Check: Send to the account owner to request they take a BGC.
BGC: Response to Criminal Allegation (Customer): Send when a customer has reported a pro for Criminal allegations, and we’re letting them know that we’ll look into their concerns.
BGC: Response to external report: Send when a customer has reported concerns about a pro, but they’re not connected to the pro on Thumbtack.
BGC: Mismatch - Request ID : Send this to the account holder when the info on their info doesn’t match the BGC and we need them to submit their ID.
BGC: Email address - Request to verify: Send this to the account holder when we need them to verify the email address on their account. BGC: Verify information - no SSN: Send this to the account holder when we need to verify their information and they don’t have a SSN.
BGC: Name and BGC don’t match: Send to the account holder when the name on the account is different than the BGC submission. (not a mismatch)
GRAMMARLY ONLY
Link: Checkr General: Send this if the account holder needs to resubmit their information to Checkr.
Link: Checkr SSNless: Send this link if the account holder needs to submit a BGC but doesn’t have a SSN.
Link: Checkr status: Send this to the account holder when they want to check the status of their BGC through Checkr.
BGC: Slack questions: Use this when answering Slack questions about the BGC.

Anomaly Detection

Anomaly Detection
(Knowledge index)
INDEX
WHAT

What
(return to index)
The Anomaly Detection (AD) queue is designed to monitor networks of accounts and compare their behavior to previous fraud trends. If fraud is proven, AD risk analysts will add any new information in the fraud activity to the query rules to trigger review of related accounts. 
Why
(return to index)
Users who engage in deceptive practices cause negative experiences for other users, which violates our Terms of Use and ultimately decreases user trust in the Thumbtack Platform. The loss of trust in Thumbtack leads to higher churn rate, which impacts the business and revenue. Reviewing users account behavior allows us to capture recurring and new abuse and further improves the overall process.
When
(return to index)
The AD proactive ops team receives work from:
Work Tickets automatically assigned with the Anomaly Detection routing skill. 
Work Tickets from other queues where the customer was put on an account hold. 
Slacks from other frontline agents in the #anomaly_detection_global channel or the  #ts-incident-ops-questions channel. 
Assignments from AD risk analysts to monitor trends before moving the process into Salesforce Work Tickets. 
This procedure will focus on steps for reviewing the AD WTs. Each WT and reported case is reviewed by an AD ops specialist who will action the user's account(s), if applicable.
SLA is 24 hours and HT target is 12 minutes. 
How
(return to index)

Review ALL Message history. Look for:

Bad actor terms

If the location is blank, search IP address in Whatismyipaddress.com.
Review Show Linked Users.
If there are linked users, check to see if the linked users are ghosted/deleted for deceptive practices.
Review any Reviews Received.
Is the review text repeatedly used/templated reviews?
If you are working on a Trend Focused or Scammy Request Behavior WT, pull up the Reference Sheet, tab “AD Trend X Behavior Data Extract”, and search for the account you are reviewing.
Look for daily trends in name, email patterns, or TMX signals used and compare them to the account being reviewed. 
In the Reference Sheet, open the “AD Trend X Behavior Reference Repository” tab.
Check to see if the user has similar reported/historical behavior to that of previous bad actors by searching their name, email address and User PK.
Once enough signals have been collected, use them to determine the MO.
Action the user in Admin, if applicable.
Fill out the Outcome and Admin Actions section of the WT.

Close WT.

articles.fileName: SMS Verified Login (Customer) - internal - Support Ops - EN
articles.headings: SMS Verified Login (Customer)
articles.summary: This article explains how users can secure their accounts and access profiles by using text message codes for identity verification during the sign-in process.
articles.concepts: account security, two-factor authentication, mobile verification, text message login, login security, identity verification
articles.aliases: SMS = Short Message Service; 2FA = Two-Factor Authentication
articles.fullText:
SMS Verified Login (Customer)

Contents
 
1. Overview
a. How it works
b. Common issues and fixes
2. Talking points
3. Internal FAQs
4. Resources 
1. OVERVIEW
 
Our current login process for customers isn't the most seamless user experience, as it requires users to leave the app to check their email to complete logging in. To enhance the customer experience, we have introduced an alternative login option using phone numbers. This new SMS verified login option will provide users with a more convenient way of logging in.
It is important to note that not all phone numbers will be eligible for SMS verified login. Customers may be prompted to provide their phone number, but it may be unavailable for SMS verified logins, and they may need to log in a different way.
NOTE: SMS verified login is available for iOS and Android apps.
HOW IT WORKS
Customers using the Thumbtack app will have the following experience: 
 
Customers will open the Thumbtack app and click “I have an account.” 
Customers can also select “I’m new to Thumbtack,” either way we ask for a phone number. 

[Image: 9ydIIb6Oo05-uo-OuMmVkW4GGngPt1pn6CYQKnfha9Pqi1ey6GhJQOxYJHh-oWHg0O3Yk1wHeQwAXWNCq9_SbOaRMXvW1Xq6EajeGBV94u8WeNheJriEPtq_AIQOS-DYDAa67ouy-xzr323Dvv9q09M]

From there, customers are asked for their phone number so we can text them a code to verify their phone number. Customers can’t skip this step. 

[Image: 7jv_bpcvZHO9UnSmrKPm05WZzdGeBG5dyqJYMaTgB24TDRWoAeuFC4wlS7vx6eySE7pzB9ACOHJJhIgcVKD3gIHke0hQGS3QFIkaUKobuaw9VD-3en-bI7kZ37IR68wV4UYNtuC6y2pxHj5jk3Osee0]
=

Once the customer enters their number and clicks “Continue,” on the backend we search for accounts with that phone number. 
Account found - If there is one account with the customer's phone number – 
We will send the phone number a 6 digit code via SMS. This code expires after 10 minutes. (image below)
If the customer doesn’t receive the code, they can click “Resend.” Customers can resend a code after 30 seconds. 
If a customer resends a code numerous times, they could be timed out and have to wait 10 minutes before trying again.
Customers will enter the code and click “next” to be logged into their account on the app. 

[Image: qzrIpU4rgOcp106m1KSGDUp1rnqgdtRHLKRlc5YVvV2VsngIbnpRQ6t_fhA6ZIG7Rs6dgO-cMzk0NOT1obzKsszxk0wHCHKD-vzVfpnQZwHbrVbrdr7I3aVqJwfD1M1BLbVX4-YPJh_BWQMjzSRz9ig]

Once logged in, customers will see a “Your phone number has been verified” message. 

[Image: jNFONGh2T1FzBLgd8GnG22be3fCFvKo7YV78JbtDPeMI2cpz6ONE6jI2ohB-41uOggxBf2lTxCIAU37urUZRYkZTY4PbaYLwtiU_A2OjgI4Jrzlh9a0Ke671xkoIXU25JqLugCx1BavXLgmB3LR7fAQ]

Post SMS Verified login – Customers who log back into the app will have the SMS verified login option moving forward. Customers who log back into Thumbtack on a desktop will use their email address as SMS verified login isn’t available outside of the app.
No account or duplicate accounts – If there is more than one account with the phone number or the number isn’t valid –  customers are redirected to the usual login screen. (This is internal information only and should not be shared with customers. Use the talking points below to help navigate these conversations.) 

[Image: Tfvb9UrzlFElUaVM1rwYtExNZUx2v269cxXMcW3sslC7AWwtN8yeTC6TY70jwzyd_kiQiNQcM4FZ2A9bdDH4_-4eWML016TdHgayOegNSqgu4Bw1spkPWm2R6GLmR1nDShpqS1hgjz8PQKZCXzXV3kU]

 
Customers using a web browser will have the baseline experience, which asks the customer for their email address or to login using Facebook, Google, or Apple. Customers not eligible for SMS verified login will also login this way. 
COMMON ISSUES AND FIXES
“We encountered an error. Please try again” –  This error can be caused by a few reasons: 1) The customer tried sending too many codes, or tried to login too many times, they will have to wait ten minutes for it to reset. 2) The customer's account is deactivated. 
“Sorry we couldn’t find your account. Please try another method.”  – There is more than one account with the phone number or the number isn’t valid. Customers are redirected to login using email, Facebook, Google, or App. (Internal information only. Don’t share with customers.)
“Your code expired. Please try again” – Verification codes expire after 10 minutes. If the customer waits too long, the code expires, they will need to resend a new code. 
“Invalid phone format. Please try again.” – If the number entered isn’t a valid format, a code won’t be sent. 
ADDITIONAL TIPS
 
Double check the phone number you’re entering. The number they enter needs to be the number associated with their account.
Please note: If customers are unsure which number is associated with their account, they can login through the standard email and password process.
Wait 10-15 min and try again.
SMS login is not available to all customers. If they have tried multiple times and no troubleshooting methods work, it could mean that it is not possible. 
2. TALKING POINTS
Why are you asking me for a phone number?
We want to make sure you’re a real person and the number is a secondary method of contact for you.
¿Por qué me solicita un número de teléfono?
Deseamos asegurarnos de que sea una persona real y el número sea un método secundario de contacto para usted.

Why are we asking you to enter a code?
We need to verify your phone number to ensure it works with our system as certain areas or carriers may not be compatible.
¿Por qué le pedimos que ingrese un código?
Necesitamos verificar su número de teléfono para asegurarnos de que funcione con nuestro sistema, ya que ciertas áreas o proveedores pueden no ser compatibles.

Why is it directing me to email? I want to use my phone. 
Only some phone numbers are eligible for SMS verified login. If you see the screen, you may still not be able to log in using the code.
¿Por qué me redirige al correo electrónico? Quiero usar mi teléfono.
Solo algunos números de teléfono son elegibles para el inicio de sesión verificado por SMS. Si ve la pantalla, es posible que aún no pueda iniciar sesión utilizando el código.

Why am I not eligible? 
Some phone numbers are ineligible for a number of reasons, often due to geographic or carrier issues. I don’t have access to your specific reason due to privacy laws, but you may be able to do so in the future as we update and expand coverage.
¿Por qué no soy elegible?
Algunos números de teléfono son inelegibles por diversas razones, a menudo debido a problemas geográficos o con el proveedor. Yo no tengo acceso a el motivo específico debido a las leyes de privacidad, pero es posible que su número pueda ser elegible en el futuro a medida que actualicemos y ampliemos la cobertura.

How do you know my phone number?
When you enter your phone number for a pro to contact you, that number is added to your Thumbtack account. You can also view this in your profile page on the website to see what number is currently associated with your account. (“Profile-> Account Settings”)
¿Cómo saben mi número de teléfono?
Cuando ingresa su número de teléfono para que un profesional se comunique con usted, ese número se agrega a su cuenta de Thumbtack. También puede ver esto en su página de perfil en el sitio web para conocer el número actualmente asociado con su cuenta. ( Profile > Account Settings)
3. INTERNAL FAQ
Suppose a customer (who isn’t eligible) changes the phone number on their account. How long will it take for them to be eligible for SMS verified login (assuming they are eligible)?
No, it is almost real time, (5 seconds maybe?)
Is this available for Android and iOS users?
Both. It is currently available for Android devices, but please note that it is still in the experimental phase and not yet shipped final. (projected to make final decisions on this in around 3 weeks approximately).

Do customers need to create a password for their Thumbtack account to use SMS verified login? Or can they use SMS verified login without ever having a password for their account?
Correct, they are not required to have ever created a password before.
 
After a customer signs in for the first time, what is their experience like? Will they have to enter their phone number every time they log in, or will the process be different the next time they log in?
It's tied to their device ID (phone/app install). Once it's shipped, it will always be the same for them; if they get a new phone or reinstall the app, for now, they'll need to renter the number. If the login session expires, they'll need to go through the phone login again with the same number, but as long as they are using the app, they won't likely need to log in again as regular use keeps the login session active.
Can we remove phone numbers from an account to make a customer eligible?
Yes they can remove the numbers from the other associated accounts and try again with the account they would like to use, once the numbers are removed from the other accounts simply have them wait 5 minutes and it should work with their main account.
 
When a pro asks if we verify customer phone numbers, we tell them that we don't and can't guarantee the accuracy of the phone numbers provided by customers. However, since the customer experience includes a message that says, "Your phone number has been verified," pros may wonder if this will affect their experience. What should our frontline reps say if a pro inquires about this message?
Are you verifying customer phone numbers now with SMS verified login? OR I hear Thumbtack is verifying customer phone numbers now. Is that true? 
Not right now as we aren’t enforcing this yet across the customer base, however we will be enforcing verification for all customers who use sms login in the future, when we have a solid date for this we will update the policy and messaging
 
Will the How to log in – Thumbtack Help article be updated to reflect this experience?
Yes, we are planning on updating the help article.
4. RESOURCES
Customer  
Thumbtack Help

Direct links
N/A

articles.fullText:
Working with Spanish Support (Rep)

Contents

1. Overview
a. Who qualifies for Spanish support, and how to confirm
b. How to contact the Spanish support team
2. Process
a. Steps: How to identify and flag a user's language preference (Rep)
b. Steps: How to transfer a phone call (Rep)
c. Steps: How to transfer an SMS or chat
d. Steps: How to transfer an email (Rep)
3. Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article provides Support Reps with the process for handing off pros and customers who require help in Spanish. It covers how to identify qualifying users and the correct transfer procedures for phone, chat, text, and email.
The Service and Support team includes a dedicated Spanish team that assists pros and customers via the following channels:
Phone
Chat
Text
Email
For Spanish speaking help, pros and customers can call (866) -501-5809 and press 2, or email ayuda@thumbtack.com. 
Who qualifies for Spanish support, and how to confirm
Criteria to qualify for Spanish Support - In order to transfer pros and customers to the Spanish Support team, they must meet any of the following criteria:
They request Spanish assistance
Prefer language of Spanish on their account
Their account has “Preferred Language” of Spanish on their account 
To find the preferred language, go to the Details tab > look under Preferred Language
Their account has a “Spanish Support” user flag. See Tools: Salesforce  > User Flags
They show difficulty communicating outside of the Spanish language
The Support Rep determines that the user would benefit from Spanish support
The user mentions they do not speak English and speak Spanish
NOTE: Support Reps shouldn’t proactively bring up transferring a pro or customer to Spanish support except for the above reasons.
How to confirm user qualifies for Spanish Support - To confirm if a pro or customer qualifies for Spanish support, Support Reps can use the talking points below:
Does your business primarily operate in the Spanish language? 
Would you prefer help in Spanish?
Will we be working with anyone on your team who prefers help in Spanish? 
How to contact the Spanish support team
For questions or help, there are several ways to contact the Spanish support team. To confirm the Spanish Support team, frontline reps will follow these steps:
Support Reps can reach out in #service_global_help-and-escalations Slack channel. 
All other team members can post in #xfnc_depts_help Slack channel.
Tag the Spanish support team by adding @spanishsupport to your message.
2. Process
To ensure a smooth handoff to the Spanish Support team, Support Reps must follow the specific transfer process for each communication channel.
Steps: How to identify and flag a user's language preference (Rep)
To correctly identify and flag a user who may need Spanish support, Support Reps should follow these steps:
Check for a Spanish Support user flag in Salesforce. 
This is located under the Thumbtack User section of a case.. 
Check the user's preferred language in Salesforce.
In a Salesforce case, click on Details.
Or on the users Contact page > Details > Contact Preferences > Preferred Language 
Look under Preferred Language.
If not already completed, mark Spanish as the pro's or customer's primary language by clicking the [Image: i5jhcYFTtJh6n564wzRIePatWcVJhl1SkYDNlTfF4tQREAQHETnSjJ2STt9V7DDSncKTCG6UCfQw-dLu12pjypxWcT3RaUYyh1pWdPHuckD7ZiK6suwMSLVE6-bnoNa2MrIwXFpYDKZfoojbFj0O3JA] icon.
Talking Point: "I see you have Spanish as a preferred language on your account. Would you like to speak to a Spanish support agent?"
If Spanish is their preferred language, a Support Rep can transfer them to the applicable Spanish support queue.
Talking point: “We have a Spanish Support team that would be happy to assist you in Spanish. Please hold while I get you over to a Spanish representative.” 
Add the Spanish Support user flag. 
To add a user flag, see the internal Tools: Salesforce  KA > User Flags. 

[Image: G3eQjTN94RuXDwTU7o-trKqjx9tflLgZ7XjpItfeC8k2BdU6v-q6xf1txZAuA2L4iBbIIaOmFbpeEXGBUPAhMyJQ_gwWUQMw-XpNzgqxrBH87aEr4-W2JESLtnnMg8x5gyhzAiLU5vQkzhx9ZY2ANZs]

Steps: How to transfer a phone call (Rep) 
To transfer a user to the Spanish Support queue via phone, Support Reps will follow these steps:
Perform a warm transfer to the “Spanish Support” queue.
For steps on transferring a call, see the Transfer a call section of the internal Genesys Phone System KA.
This will transfer both the Support Rep and the user to the Spanish Support Queue. 
If the wait is over 90 seconds, ask the pro or customer if they’re okay with waiting on their own or would prefer an email follow-up.
Transfer the Salesforce case to the "Spanish Support" queue. Refer to the internal Salesforce |  Case Navigation And Management KA for steps. 
Mark Spanish as the primary language of the pro or customer in their contact information if this hasn't been done yet. To do so, follow the Steps: How to identify and flag a user's language preference (Rep) above.
Steps: How to transfer an SMS or chat
 
To transfer a user to the Spanish Support queue during an SMS or chat interaction, Support Reps should follow this step:
For steps detailed steps and guidelines, follow the (Rep) Steps: How to transfer an interaction on the Genesys | SMS & Chat KA.
Transfer the conversation to the Spanish Support Queue. 
To do this, type “Spanish Support Queue" in the field where a Support Rep's name would typically be entered for a transfer.
Steps: How to transfer an email (Rep)
 
The Spanish Support team has a dedicated queue and email address (ayuda@thumbtack.com). To transfer an email case to this queue, Support Reps should follow these steps:
In the case record, find the "Case Owner" field.
Click the edit icon [Image: JZAFeG_BLl05yfH2ywjcgeedHyCr8r7kjeg9BYYn3cy_gxbHO8U4ISpOVugjAXcPPHCCGfK5Bi-bd03QsTMzHr1jMsFbYWoHxNxG8o5U9eL1noZ_wDCdYM2QnAgzAvYLH6sKg3S7IhP9NWGoZUnHBmU]next to the current owner's name.
Select the option to transfer to "A Team (queue).

Welcome Discount for New Pros

Contents

Overview
Process

Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) outlines details for Frontline Reps regarding the new pro discount. Specifically, eligible pros receive 25% off their first 12 leads if they are received within the initial four-week period following the pro's  sign up.
All new pros who sign up on or after May 11, 2026 automatically receive a 25% welcome discount on their first 12 leads. The discount does not apply to opportunities. 
Discount start date: The discount starts when the pro receives their first lead.
Discount expiration date:  The offer expires four weeks after the pro's signup date. If the pro's first lead arrives after that window, the discount does not apply and they will not receive any notifications about it.
When a pro receives their first lead, they are notified about the discount in the following ways:
In-app pop-up: A one-time pop-up in the Jobs tab announcing the discount and its expiration date.
Persistent banner: A banner in the "Leads and bookings" section of the Jobs tab showing the discount and expiration date for the duration of the offer.
Lead details: Each of the first 12 discounted leads is marked with "You got 25% off this lead" directly in the lead details view.
Email: Pros receive an email for each of the 12 discounted leads. The first lead email announces the discount; leads 2–12 include a banner and footer reiterating the discount terms.
▶ What the in-app pop-up looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ What the email announcement looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

2. Process
Steps: How to check a pro's discounted lead balance (Rep) 

To check the status of a pro's welcome discount, go to the Discounts section in their Admin profile. This shows whether the discount is active, how many of the 12 leads have been used, and when the discount expires.

To find remaining leads, look at the free leads (total / redeemed) field and subtract the redeemed count from the total.

To view the contact IDs for all awarded or discounted leads, run the Lead Incentives Query and refer to the applied_contact_pks column in the results. All other columns from the query are already reflected in the Discounts section in Admin. For steps on running the query, refer to the internal Lead Incentives Query (Pro) KA

Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro)

Contents
Overview
Key points
Setting a budget 
Understanding Recommended Budgets
Understanding Unlimited Budgets
Unlimited Budget Discount Offer
Understanding Custom Budgets
Managing budget during the week(adjusting or hitting)
Updating budget during the week
Not hitting budget during the week
Hitting budget during the week

Overserved contact opt in
Budget increase incentives

Key points

Process
How to set or edit their budget (Pro)
How to accept the Unlimited Budget Discount offer (Pro)
Talking points
How weekly targeting budget works
How to control spending (Budget and Bid)
How to update budget
Understanding custom budget amounts
How budget is impacted with targeting paused
Limited availability tag for pros with low budgets 
Pro has concerns about setting a budget
Budget alert and recommendation card to update weekly budget (and show in search results)
How the unlimited budget discount offer works
Resource
1. Overview
Note on targeting terminology: You may see "Targeting" and "Job preferences" terms used interchangeably throughout our internal KA resources or in-product.
A pro's weekly targeting budget on Thumbtack is a tool that allows them to control their total weekly spending and runs from Monday to Sunday. It lets Thumbtack know how much a pro is willing to spend every week for leads across all of their services. 
Pros also set a lead price to control their spending on individual leads. The budget caps the total weekly spend, and the lead price sets a limit on the cost per lead. 
The budget does not impact a pro's ranking but can affect whether they show up in search results. Once a pro reaches their budget amount, they will stop getting leads and appearing in search results, and targeting (also known as "Job preferences") is paused. Pros might not reach their budget every week, depending on how many customers contact them from search results.
Reps can refer to the internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA to learn more.
Key points


Understanding these key points will empower reps to effectively help pros in managing their weekly targeting budget.
Budget vs. Lead Price: The budget is a weekly spending cap for all services, while the lead price controls the cost per individual lead.
Budget Flexibility: Pros can adjust their budget throughout the week.
Increases take effect immediately.
Decreases below current spending take effect on Monday.
Note that there are specific limits on setting a custom budget after the initial weekly budget has been spent.
Custom Budget Limits: Once a pro exhausts their weekly budget, they can only set a new custom budget amount one more time that week. If they spend that new amount, their remaining options until the Monday reset are to keep their budget as-is, increase to the recommended amount, or set an unlimited budget.
Budget options: 
Recommended: Thumbtack suggests a recommended budget amount based on a pro's market and lead price.
Unlimited: Pros get as many leads as possible within their lead price. Pros in under-supplied markets may be eligible for a 10% discount on direct leads with this option.
Custom: Pros set custom budgets but are limited in how often they can change them within a week to encourage effective budget usage.
Budget Notifications: Pros receive notifications when they're close to or have reached their budget limit.
Limited Availability Tag: Pros with low budgets may have this tag on their profile.
Budget Overserving: In low-supply markets, pros who've reached their budget may still appear in search results to meet customer demand. Remember: Reps should not explain the specifics of budget overserving to prevent pros from gaming the system.
Tracking Spending: Pros can track their spending through the Services tab, Performance Dashboard, and Payment History.
(Internal) Check budget in Admin: Frontline reps can check a pro’s budget history for the past four weeks, including the pro’s existing budget for their business, changes made and updates resulting from accepting a BOSUP offer. See internal Budget Oversering Upsell KA to learn more.
Setting budget on Thumbtack
Pros should think about how many customers they want to find their business each week on Thumbtack and use that to set their lead price (How to set my lead prices – Thumbtack Help). Thumbtack will tell the pro how far that amount could go and recommend a good budget for them. Reps can refer to the internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA. 
Pros then set their budget (How to edit my budget – Thumbtack Help) to control the total amount they’ll spend in a week on Thumbtack. Pros budget is one spending limit for all their services on Thumbtack and is found on the services tab. 
When setting a budget, pros can either set their budget to: 
The recommended amount 
An unlimited budget to get as many customers as possible (and potentially get a dicount)
A custom budgets. Pros have to set a minimum budget amount.  
Reminder: Pros may experience limits on how they can update their budget once they've reached it in a week. Reps can refer to Hitting budget during the week section to learn more. 
▶ A screenshot that provides an in-product view of a pro's weekly budget page on the app

[Image: image.png]

Reminder: When unlimited is selected, pros will not see the recommended amount option when editing their budget amount. 

[Image: image.png]

NOTE: Once a pro sets or adjusts their lead prices, it’s a good idea to adjust their budget to ensure they can get enough leads for their business.
Understanding Recommended Budgets

Based on a pro's market and lead price settings, Thumbtack will recommend a budget to help them reach their business goals. Pros also have the option to set an unlimited budget to get the most leads possible within their lead prices.
Pros will only see a recommended amount if it's higher than their current budget. If a recommended budget isn't available and they want leads, they must set their budget to unlimited. If they don't want leads or an unlimited budget, they can keep their budget as is, hide their business, or pause targeting.
▶ What the Recommended budget looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Internal note: As of June 22, 2026, Thumbtack has updated the recommended budget amount that pros see — about 40% higher. A pro's current budget remains the same. The update changes only the recommended budget amounts for pros not currently using a recommended budget. NDFP pros are excluded from this update and use different recommendation logic.]
The recommended budget option looks higher than what I've seen in the past. Why?
Thumbtack periodically updates the budget recommendations it shows pros to better reflect current demand in your area. You're always in control of your own budget — you can set it to any amount that works for you.
What is a recommended budget?
Thumbtack recommends a budget based on the demand for your services in your market. Setting your budget at or above the recommended amount helps you get more leads when customers are searching for what you offer. You can always choose to set your own amount instead.
Do I have to increase my budget to the recommended amount?
No. The recommended budget is a suggestion based on the demand for your services in your market. You can set your budget to any amount you choose.
Understanding Unlimited Budgets 

An unlimited budget opens pros to any leads that come in through the rest of the week.
When unlimited is selected, pros will not see the recommended amount option when editing their budget amount. This means the purple "Recommended" pill, which would otherwise appear next to the suggested budget amount (e.g., "Set to $X per week"), will not be displayed.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Unlimited Budget Discount Offer
Pros in underserved markets may be eligible for a 10% discount on leads if they set an unlimited budget. 
Where to claim: Pros will see this special offer on their Services, Budget, and BOSUP offer pages. To see how a pro claims the discount, reps can refer to Steps: How to accept the unlimited budget discount offer (Pro) below.
When pro claims special offer: If the pro confirms the switch to an unlimited budget, the discount is applied to all leads and remains active as long as they stay on an unlimited budget. 
Discount removed: The discount is removed immediately if a pro switches back to a fixed budget (recommended or custom budget). If a pro attempts to switch back to a fixed budget, they will see an alert warning them that the discount will be removed instantly. 
Lead type: The discount does not apply to opportunities, claimable jobs (fixed-price jobs), or other lead types. 
Availability: This offer may not always appear in a pros account. Thumbtack may modify or end this promotion at any time. If the promotion ends, Thumbtack will notify pros on the unlimited budget offer in advance. 
How reps see if pro has an active discount offer: The Discounts section on the User Admin page displays "Unlimited Budget 10% Off". 
Excluded pros: The unlimited budget discount offers will not be shown to pros who have: 
Not been active in the past 7 days OR
0 lifetime verified reviews OR
0 contacts in the last 30 days
NOTE: Pros who qualified for the original experiment's 20% discount will keep that higher rate for leads as long as they maintain an unlimited budget.
▶ What the special offer looks like on the budget budget

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ What the warning looks like if a pro changes from unlimited
Warning alert: “You’ll lose your 10% discount if you switch back to a fixed budget.”

[Image: rtaImage]

Unlimited budget offer with free lead offer 
Pros may be eligible for both the unlimited budget discount and a budget overserving upsell (BOSUP) offer simultaneously. In this case, switching to an unlimited budget allows them to unlock both the 10% discount on leads AND a set number of free leads (subject to a maintenance period).
▶ What both offers look like on the budget page

[Image: rtaImage]

Reps can refer to the internal Budget Increase Incentive (BOSUP & SOBU) (Pro) KA to learn more. 
 Understanding Custom Budgets

When setting a custom amount, pros have to set a minimum budget amount. Additionally, Thumbtack limits the number of custom budgets a pro can set in a week to ensure they're using their budget effectively. While a custom budget may give pros flexibility to control their spending, consistently running out of budget risks missing out on potential customers.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Pros can always set a new custom budget when their budget resets on Monday.
▶ Once a pro has used up their budget for the week, they can only set a new custom budget amount once before Monday. A pros budget page will say “You used up your budget this week and can only set a new custom amount once before Monday.”

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ If, after setting a custom amount, the pro hits their budget again, they won’t be able to set another custom amount. The pro will see a yellow banner that says “You can’t set a new custom amount until Monday. Select another option.”  After that, pros can 1) keep budget as is, 2) increase to recommended amount (if available), or 3) set unlimited budget.

[Image: rtaImage]

Managing budget during the week (adjusting or hitting budget)
Updating budget during the week
Before reaching their budget amount, pros can update their budget throughout the week as usual. 
If a pro lowers or increases their budget during the week, the changes will take effect right away. If the pro decreases their budget below the amount they've spent on leads for the week, they will receive new leads once the budget resets on Monday. 

Not hitting budget during the week (and wants more leads)
Pro’s not hitting their weekly budget each week and wants more leads, they can try increasing their lead prices for the services that matter most to them. That way, the pro will be more competitive for their desired jobs. Reps can refer to the internal Lead Prices (Pro)  KA to learn more. 

Hitting budget during the week (and wants more leads)
If a pro is hitting their budget each week and wants more customers, they should consider increasing their budget. The pro may need to set their budget higher to meet the demand for their services in their area.
Pro’s hitting their budget during the week have a few options:
Keep budget as it is. Pros won't appear in search results until their budget resets on Monday. [Internal note to reps: However, they may still get leads if they're in a market with a low supply of pros. Reps refer to overserving section.  
Increase budget to recommended amount. Thumbtack will recommend a budget based on the pros market and lead price settings to help them reach their business goals.
Increase budget to unlimited. An unlimited budget will make the pro eligible for any leads that come in through the rest of the week.
Increase budget to custom amount. When setting a custom amount, pros have to set a minimum budget amount. Once they've used up their budget for the week, they can only set a new custom budget amount once before Monday. After that, pros can 1) keep budget as is, 2) increase to recommended amount (if available), or 3) set unlimited budget. 
Increases take effect immediately, so pros won't miss out on customers seeing them in search results.
Reasons a pro would be notified about their budget (budget alerts and recommendations)
Pros will be notified about their weekly targeting budget when they: 
Are close to hitting their budget
Hit their budget
Need to increase their budget to reply to a new lead
Have targeting turned off in all categories (this disables their budget)
Pros are filtered out of search results when they don't have enough budget to cover the cost of leads (known internally as 'budget throttling’). NOTE: Budget throttling is an internal term and should not be used when speaking with pros or customers.
Pros may see a budget alert on their services page and a recommendation card on their leads page to update their weekly budget when they have either reached their weekly spending limit or are close to reaching it.
The alert will show on the services page when the pro has been budget throttled at least 10 times in the previous week. This alert is only displayed if other budget alerts aren’t present (almost out of budget, hit your budget). This alert goes away once the pro increases their budget.
Budget alert notifications can also be sent via email, push, or SMS depending on how the pro has their notifications set up. Reps can refer to Notifications (Pro) KA to learn more about notifications. 
▶ Email sent to pro if they hit their budget

[Image: AD_4nXdScRVtdAmVidyds9cahGjRUrxDCQ4QrSEIlGBNu6t1zh9o5hd2OcmylZXzxtUsnjsO79dbWRWYllSpEO3jHQr6ULV9PRLN499gTbzLDkB7mLdsXBDE67bELQuCTWKAmxFrN7US9w]

▶ Budget alert and recommendation card when pro has been budget throttled at least 10 times in the previous week

[Image: AD_4nXcpHJfPibuo52onVAYzkKDde4vJkjZ5N8eRABg3fZO8NfpdW19YOHy8A_yYaswu2hnDQ93tv7NW1_Ru8jiwwxDOZMQQEHPD6kXAlm1eVzG1jDelZxjdUgfbRAI4Kt5ilqkhpXRW8A]
[Image: AD_4nXfSuNCs3JAGDiKThMseE7onG456DwMyS44POSGb6M3JJFo5WLkt9jQE57soqvAH9Jz4RS_DBEnTjXf84LaG62sdcgvWdaTc-8x0HsihC-q6r4b7xRNrrFtGK1nk9GPD4ZYVPEesNA]

Reasons pros who have reached their budget may still appear in search results (Overserving) 
Sometimes, Thumbtack doesn’t have enough pros in a certain area to meet customer demand. To ensure customers see a good number of options, Thumbtack might show pros in search results even if they've already used up their weekly budget. This is known internally as overserving. When this happens, pros may be eligible for different types of incentives or offers, such as:
An Overserved Contact Opt-In,
A Budget Overserving Upsell (BOSUP) offer,
A Seasonal Overserving Budget Upsell (SOBU) offer
Eligibility for Overserving:

Thumbtack may show eligible pros who have reached their weekly spending limit in search results if:
Low Supply Market: The pro's category and zip code have fewer than four eligible pros.
Targeting On: The pro has their targeting preferences turned on.
Search Visibility: The pro would normally appear in search results for a given request.
Important Note for Frontline Reps: Don't explain or share the qualifications for free leads or opt in contacts as this could encourage pros to try to game the system.
Key Takeaway: Overserving helps ensure a positive customer experience in low-supply markets.
Overserved Contact Opt in

Thumbtack may let pros who have hit their budget for the week know when a customer contacts them. This is known internally as an overserved contact opt in. 
Important reminder: Thumbtack wants to avoid overserving pros when possible and frontline reps should not explain what qualifies pros for opt in contacts. 
Pros see details explaining that the customer contacted them after they exceeded their budget and that if they accept the contact, they will be automatically charged. Opt-in contact can be found in the Jobs tab under “Leads” with an “Accept by” pill with a date.
For a closer look, reps can refer to Overserved Contact Opt In (Pro) KA. 
NOTE: Pros earning free leads from an active BOSUP offer will not be affected by the overserved contact opt in experience. The overserved contact is granted as free until their free lead balance is gone (instead of receiving the contact as opt in).
Budget increase incentives

Thumbtack offers pros two types of free lead upsell offers, the Budget Overserving Upsell (BOSUP) and the Seasonal Overserving Budget Upsell (SOBU), both designed to increase a pro's budget during specific scenarios. IMPORTANT: These offers are not visible to pros beforehand to prevent overserving and frontline rep should NOT explain the specific criteria that qualify pros for free leads. 
BOSUP offers free leads to pros who exhaust their budget in low-supply markets. 
SOBU offers free leads during peak seasons to encourage pros to increase their budget.
To qualify for these free leads, pros must:
Accept the offer on their Services page under “Activity this week.” Increasing their budget independently will not qualify them for the free leads.
Maintain the increased budget for a specific duration:
BOSUP offers require a 2-week commitment.
SOBU offers require a 6-week commitment.
Pros receiving free leads from an active BOSUP offer are not affected by the overserved contact opt-in experience. Instead, the overserved contact is granted as free until their free lead balance is depleted.
For more detailed information, including how pros accept offers and how to view a pro’s budget and offer status, reps can refer to the internal Budget Increase Incentive (Budget Overserve Upsell or BOSUP) (Pro) KA.
Pro has reached weekly budget and has a "Limited availability" tag in search results 
IMPORTANT: The following section covers internal Thumbtack information only and should not be shared with pros. If frontline reps receive questions from a pro about this tag, use the Limited availability tag talking points below.
In some low-supply markets, Thumbtack may still show pros in search results even if they have reached their weekly budget (known as overserving) to meet customer demand. This can lead to a bad customer experience if these overserved pros are less likely to respond. To help mitigate this, Thumbtack informs customers that these pros in the pro list have "limited availability." This may make customers less likely to contact these pros and more likely to contact another pro who still has a budget available for additional leads.
▶ What the limited availability tag looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Important Note for Frontline Reps:
Thumbtack does not want pros to know that they can still receive contacts after exhausting their budget, as this could encourage gaming behavior. Therefore, if you receive questions from pros about this tag, be careful about how you discuss it. Focus on the pro's ability to increase their weekly budget to remove the "Limited Availability" tag and become eligible for more leads. 
Use the Limited availability tag for pros with low budgets talking points below.
How to control spending
The budget is not the only factor that controls a pro’s spending and lead volume on Thumbtack; that is controlled by both a pros budget and lead price, but in different ways.
Their lead prices control what the pro spends per lead and gives an estimate on how many. 
How to set my lead prices – Thumbtack Help
Their budget controls their total weekly spending. 
They work together to ultimately give pros more control over how much they spend and what they spend it on. 
Reps can refer to the internal Lead Prices (Pro)  KA to learn more. 
How to track weekly spending
Pros need to know that we’re looking out for them when it comes to their budget. Be sure to explain what we do to help pros track their spending. Pros can track their spending themselves three ways: 
▶ 1. Going to their Services to view their spending for the week
Pros can check their Services to see a breakdown of their activity and spending for the week. The spending tracker resets to $0 every Monday morning (12:01 am PT). 
Activity this week: Shows the number of profile views and the number of leads and bookings received that week. 
Spending this week: is divided into two parts:
1. Budget spent: How much was spent on leads, bookings and overserved contacts if pro selected “Accept & adjust budget
2. Additional spent: How much they’ve paid for opt-in contacts, including all opportunities and any overserved contacts the pro selected “Accept only this lead.” (Charges for overserved contacts where the pro selected “Accept & adjust budget” will appear under Budget spent).
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Additional things to note: 
Unlimited budget: The leads will be grayed out if a pro doesn't have a budget set up. When a pro has an unlimited budget set, they'll see "$0 / unlimited budget". 
Targeting off: When a pro doesn't have targeting on for any of their services, this is grayed out and says "Your targeting budget is disabled for all services. You won’t be charged for additional leads."
▶ 2. Using their Performance Dashboard for another breakdown.

T o see a pros activity in more detail, frontline reps can view the pros  Performance Dashboard by clicking on each individual service. The reports break down the pro's activity over four weeks and show how they compare to the pro's competition.
Reps can refer to the Business and Performance Dashboard (Market Level Insights) KA. 
▶ 3. Visiting their payment history
Pros can go to their Payments page to see a breakdown of their charges. They'll see the cost of each lead and any refunds issued.
Reps can refer to the Payment Methods (Pro) KA
Factors that impact the budget
On Thumbtack, various factors influence a pro's budget. To determine which actions impact the pro's budget and what doesn't, Frontline reps can refer to the information provided below:
▶ Does impact budget
Leads: Pros auto-pay whenever a customer contacts a pro that's an exact match to a pro's targeting preferences. Frontline reps can refer to the internal Leads (Pro) KA for more information.
Overserved opt-in contacts ("Accept & adjust budget"): When a pro receives an overserved contact and chooses the "Accept & adjust budget" option, the charge counts against and reduces the pro's weekly budget. Frontline reps can refer to the internal Overserved Contact Opt In (Pro)  KA to learn more.
Refunds for leads from the current week: If a lead that was charged during the current budget week (Monday-Sunday) is refunded, that amount is credited back to the pro's available weekly budget. This applies to all refund types, including both in-policy refunds and Promotional Balance Increases (PBIs), also known as courtesy credits.
* For example, if a pro has a $100 budget, spends $20 on a lead, and then receives a $20 refund for that same lead within the same week, their available budget returns to $100. 
▶ Does NOT impact budget
Claimable jobs: Pros don't pay for the lead, instead Thumbtacks pays the pro for the job. Frontline reps can refer to the internal Claimable Jobs (Pro) KA for more information.
Opportunities: If a pro is looking to pick up extra jobs, they can check out Opportunities. If a customer responds to the pro, the cost is separate from the pro's budget. That way, pros don't have to worry about how it factors into their budget. Frontline reps can refer to the internal Opportunities (Pro) KA for more information.
Overserved opt-in contacts ("Accept only this lead"): When a pro receives an overserved contact and chooses the "Accept only this lead" option, the charge does not count against the pro's weekly budget and is instead tracked in the "Additional spent" section of their Services page. Frontline reps can refer to the internal Overserved Contact Opt In (Pro) KA to learn more.
Partial match opt in leads (Accept & Pay):  Partial match opt-in leads, also known as expanded matches, impact a pro's budget with a one-off charge only if the pro chooses to "Accept & Pay." Unlike overserved opt-in contacts, these leads are determined by the Matchmaker AI to be relevant based on the pro's profile and job history, even though they don't perfectly align with the pro's specific job preferences. Reps can refer to the internal Partial Match Opt-In Leads (Pro) KA.
Refunds from previous weeks: No adjustments are made to a pro's budget for refunds on leads they were charged for from previous weeks.
For example, if a pro's budget is $20 and they receive a refund for a lead they were charged for two weeks ago, their budget stays at $20. The refund goes to the pro's Thumbtack balance instead.
Frontline reps can refer to the internal Lead Refunds (Pro) KA to learn more.
Manual billing: If a pro is on manual billing it doesn't affect their budget (this is used by National accounts). Frontline reps can refer to the internal Managed Accounts KA to learn more.
Pre-loadable balance: The pre-loadable balance and weekly targeting budget are different. The weekly targeting budget lets Thumbtack know how much the pro is willing to spend each week. Pre-loadable balances make sure the pro always has funds available so they don't miss out on leads. Frontline reps can refer to the internal Payment Methods (Pro) KA to learn more.
Overserved opt-in contacts ("Accept only this lead"): When a pro receives an overserved contact and chooses the "Accept only this lead" option, the charge does not count against the pro's weekly budget and is instead tracked in the "Additional spent" section of their Services page. Frontline reps can refer to the internal Overserved Contact Opt In (Pro) KA to learn more.

2. Admin tools to investigate a pro’s budget (Rep) 
This section provides a guide to understanding a pro's budget and promotional offers. 
The Admin tool offers the most convenient way to access a pro's complete BOSUP and SOBU offer history and status, with real-time data updates (meaning each time you refresh the page, the data updates instantly). 
This gives reps all the necessary details without needing to run complex queries. On the Business Admin Page:
Business-level Budget: Shows a pro's existing, real-time budget for that business.
Business Budget History: Provides a detailed log of every change the pro has made to their budget.
Reminder: When looking at timestamps, reps should remember the time zone difference (Admin uses the local device's time zone, while the query (BIgQuery) uses UTC).
Where to view a pros current weekly budget (Business-level Budget Admin section)
The Business-level budget section in Admin provides a real-time snapshot of the pro's current weekly budget. The section displays fields for a Desired Limit, Hard Limit, and Current Spend. 
▶ What the section looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Screenshot of Business-Level Budget field: The image shows the “Desired Limit” as $50.00, the “Hard Limit” as $50.00 and “Current Spend” as $31.18. Meaning, the pro has spent $31.18 of their $50 budget
The below table shows what each field means and how to use it.

Admin Field
What It Means
How reps can use it
Desired limit
The pro’s current weekly targeting budget for their business. This should always be the same as the Hard Limit.
Use this to confirm the pro's current, active budget setting.
Hard Limit
The maximum amount the pro is willing to spend per week. This should match the Desired Limit.
This is the definitive weekly budget cap set by the pro.
Current spend
The amount of the weekly budget the pro has spent so far in the current week.
Check this to see how close the pro is to exhausting their weekly budget.
"N/A" means the pro has an unlimited budget selected. This is important for confirming when a pro has accepted a BOSUP offer by choosing the "Unlimited" option.
Where to view a pro’s budget changes from the past 4 weeks (Business Budget History in Admin)
The Business Budget History section in Admin provides a complete log of every change a pro has made to their budget for the past four weeks. This data appears in a table with several columns, where the most recent changes are shown at the top.
This is the most critical tool for confirming if a pro met the offer's requirements.
