Steps: How to view a pro's budget history in Admin (Rep)
Frontline reps can check a pro's budget history in Admin from the Business page. Reps may need to review this information to troubleshoot issues or answer questions about spending.
In Admin, navigate to the "Business" tab, which is located under the "Models" section.
Search for the pro: Enter the pro's Business PK or business name into the search bar and click "Search Businesses."
Finding the Business PK: If needed, locate the pro's Business PK by going to their main user page and finding the "Businesses / Services" field.
View business details: Scroll down to the relevant section on the Business page to find the information you need.
Business-level Budget: Shows a pro's existing, real-time budget for that business.
Business Budget History: Provides a detailed log of every change the pro has made to their budget.
BOSUP Discount Offers: Lists all budget increase incentives the pro has received and their current status. 
If a pro says they did not receive free leads after accepting a budget incentive offer, look at the "BOSUP Discount Offers" section to see what happened with the offer. For more detailed information and steps, frontline reps should refer to the internal Budget Overserving Upsell KA. This article provides additional context and guidance on how to navigate these Admin sections.
3. Process
How to set or edit budget (Pro)
Pro steps: To set or adjust their weekly targeting budget, pros will follow the steps in the How to edit my budget – Thumbtack Help article 
Pros set a weekly limit so they can control their spending. Their budget is all about finding the right balance of customers and cost.
Pros can update their weekly budget anytime. If they hit their budget, and decide to increase it, the pro will be eligible to receive new leads right away. If they decrease it below the amount they’ve spent on leads for the week, they won’t receive any new leads until their budget resets on Monday. 
​​NOTE: The amount the pro selects will cover leads for all their services. Pros can control which service they want more or less of by setting a higher or lower lead price. Frontline reps can refer to the internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA to learn more. 
How to accept the unlimited budget discount offer (Pro)
Reps can refer to the Unlimited Budget Discount Offer section above to learn more about this special offer. 
Pros in underserved markets may be eligible for a 10% discount on leads if they set an unlimited budget. Pros will see this special offer on their Services and Budget pages. To accept the unlimited budget discount, the pro will follow these steps:
From the Services page, select "View special offer" (or go to the Budget page).
Select the "Don't limit my budget" option.
Click "Save weekly budget" to switch to an unlimited budget and activate the discount.
Review the offer term details. (Details include: Pros get 10% off all leads while maintaining an unlimited budget, if they switch back to a limited budget, the discount will end immediately). 
Click “Got it.” 
To remain eligible for the discount, pros must keep their budget set to "unlimited." If they change to a custom or recommended budget, the discount is removed.

4. Talking points
This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros about their weekly targeting budget. Use these talking points to ensure consistent and accurate messaging.

For additional talking points, frontline reps can refer to the following KAs: Payment Methods(Pro) , Lead Prices (Pro), and Lead (Pro).
How weekly targeting budget works
This section provides frontline reps with talking points to explain how the weekly targeting budget functions to pros, directly addressing common questions they might have.

English FAQs
Spanish FAQs
Why do I need to set a weekly targeting budget?
¿Por qué debo establecer un límite de gasto semanal?
You set a weekly limit so you can control your spending. Your weekly targeting budget is all about finding the right balance of customers and cost.
Establece un límite semanal para que pueda controlar sus gastos. Su límite de gasto semanal se trata de encontrar el equilibrio adecuado entre clientes y costos.
What if I don’t want to limit the number of leads I am getting each week? 
¿Qué pasa si no quiero limitar la cantidad de prospectos que recibo cada semana?
You can skip setting a limit if you just want to get as many leads as possible. To do this you can select the “Unlimited” option on the Weekly Targeting Budget page.
Usted puede omitir el establecimiento de un límite si solo desea obtener tantos prospectos como sea posible. Para hacer esto, usted puede seleccionar la opción “Ilimitado” en la página de Presupuesto de Enfoque Semanal.
Is the weekly spend limit a subscription fee?
¿El límite de gasto semanal es un cobro de suscripción?
No. You can adjust the amount you spend from week to week and you aren’t locked in to anything long-term. And depending on how many leads you get in a week, you might spend less than the budget amount you set. We want you to use this tool to find the customers you’re looking for, while staying within your spending limits.
No. Puede ajustar la cantidad que gasta de una semana a otra y no está limitado a nada a largo plazo. Dependiendo de la cantidad de prospectos que obtenga en una semana, es posible que gaste menos del presupuesto que estableció. Queremos que utilice esta herramienta para encontrar los clientes que está buscando, mientras se mantiene dentro de sus límites de gasto.
Why does my budget sometimes change when I get a refund, but not​​ on all refunds?
¿Por qué a veces cambia mi presupuesto cuando recibo un reembolso, pero no con todos los reembolsos?
I can definitely help clarify when a refund impacts your weekly budget while other refunds don't. To keep things simple and consistent, any refund you receive—whether it's an automatic refund or a courtesy credit—for a lead that you were charged for in the same week will be added back to your weekly budget. This gives you more budget to continue connecting with customers that week.
However, if a refund is for a lead from a previous week, that amount is returned to your overall Thumbtack balance instead of your current weekly budget. Your current week's budget will not be affected in that case.
Puedo ayudarle a aclarar cuándo un reembolso impacta su presupuesto semanal y cuándo no. Para mantenerlo simple y consistente, cualquier reembolso que reciba, ya sea un reembolso automático o un crédito de cortesía, por un prospecto cobrado en esa misma semana, se agregará nuevamente a su presupuesto semanal. Esto le da más presupuesto para seguir conectando con clientes durante esa semana.

Sin embargo, si el reembolso corresponde a un prospecto de una semana anterior, ese monto se devuelve a su saldo general de Thumbtack en lugar de a su presupuesto semanal actual. En ese caso, el presupuesto de la semana en curso no se verá afectado.
How to control spending (budget and bid)
This section provides frontline reps with talking points to explain to pros how they can control their spending using both budget and bid, offering clear distinctions between the two.

English FAQs
Spanish FAQs
Q: What’s the difference between my budget and lead price?
Q: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre mi presupuesto y el precio por prospecto?
A: Your Budget is the total amount you're willing to spend in a week; it controls how many leads you can get. Your Lead Price is the exact price you'll pay for one lead. Think of it as your lead price being the price of a single item, and your budget being your total weekly shopping allowance.
A: Su presupuesto es el monto total que está dispuesto a gastar en una semana; controla cuántos prospectos puede recibir.
Su precio por prospecto es el precio exacto que pagará por un solo prospecto.
Piense en el precio por prospecto como el costo de un solo artículo, y en su presupuesto como su gasto total semanal.
How do I control how many leads I am getting each week? 
¿Cómo controlo cuántos prospectos recibo cada semana?
You set a weekly limit so you can control your spending. Your weekly targeting budget is all about finding the right balance of customers and cost. We also recommend reviewing your targeting preferences to make sure that you are only targeting the leads you are willing to pay for. 
Usted establece un límite semanal para poder controlar sus gastos. Su presupuesto de enfoque semanal se trata de encontrar el equilibrio adecuado entre clientes y costo. También recomendamos revisar sus preferencias de enfoque para asegurarse de que solo se está enfocando en los prospectos por los que está dispuesto a pagar.
How to update budget
​​This section provides frontline reps with talking points to explain to pros how they can update their budget, including when changes take effect.

English FAQs
Spanish FAQs
Can I edit my budget?
¿Puedo editar mi presupuesto?
You can update your weekly budget anytime. If you’ve already hit your budget, and decide to increase it, you’ll be eligible to receive new leads right away. If you decrease your budget below the amount you’ve spent on leads for the week, you won’t receive any new leads until your budget resets on Monday. 
Usted puede actualizar su presupuesto semanal en cualquier momento. Si ya ha alcanzado su presupuesto y decide aumentarlo, podrá recibir nuevos prospectos de inmediato. Si disminuye su presupuesto por debajo del monto que ha gastado en prospectos durante la semana, no recibirá nuevos prospectos hasta que su presupuesto se restablezca el lunes.
How do I modify my budget?
¿Cómo puedo modificar mi presupuesto?
To modify your budget, go to the Service tab and choose “edit weekly targeting budget.” From there, you can adjust it to the max you’ll auto-pay for leads each week, for all of your services.
Para modificar su presupuesto, vaya a la pestaña Services (“Servicios”) y seleccione Edit weekly targeting budget (“Editar preferencias del presupuesto semanal”). Desde ahí, puede ajustar el máximo que se cobrará automáticamente por prospectos cada semana, para todos sus servicios.
How do I check what my weekly budget is set at?
¿Cómo puedo revisar en cuánto está configurado mi presupuesto semanal?
To check your weekly targeting budget, go to your Services tab and choose "Manage your budget." We’ll also let you know what your new weekly targeting budget will be in an email prior to it going into effect.
Para revisar sus preferencias de su presupuesto semanal, vaya a la pestaña Services (“Servicios”) y seleccione Manage your budget (“Administrar su presupuesto”). También le informaremos cuáles serán sus nuevas preferencias de su presupuesto semanal en un correo electrónico antes de que entren en vigor.
Understanding custom budget amounts
This section provides frontline reps with talking points to explain to pros the details of custom budget amounts, including limitations and available options.

English FAQs
Spanish FAQs
Why am I limited to how many times I can set a custom budget per week? 
¿Por qué tengo un límite de cuántas veces puedo establecer un presupuesto personalizado por semana?
If you’re running out of budget multiple times each week, you’re putting yourself at risk of not showing up in search results and missing out on potential new customers.
Based on your market and lead price settings, we have a recommended budget to help you reach your business goals, we also give you the option to set an unlimited budget which allows you to get the most leads possible within the lead prices you have set.
While a custom budget may give you additional flexibility to control your spending, consistently running out of budget puts you at risk of missing out on potential customers, which is why in certain scenarios we may limit the number of custom budgets you can set in one week. You will always be able to set a new custom budget when your budget resets on Monday.
Si usted se queda sin presupuesto varias veces por semana, corre el riesgo de no aparecer en los resultados de búsqueda y perder posibles clientes nuevos.
Según su mercado y la configuración de sus precios de los prospectos, le recomendamos un presupuesto para ayudarle a alcanzar sus metas de negocio. También le damos la opción de establecer un presupuesto ilimitado, que le permite recibir la mayor cantidad posible de prospectos dentro de los precios de prospectos que usted haya configurado.
Aunque un presupuesto personalizado puede darle más flexibilidad para controlar sus gastos, quedarse sin presupuesto con frecuencia aumenta el riesgo de perder posibles clientes. Por eso, en algunas situaciones, podemos limitar la cantidad de presupuestos personalizados que usted puede establecer en una semana.
Usted siempre podrá establecer un nuevo presupuesto personalizado cuando su presupuesto se reinicie el lunes.
I’ve already changed my budget to a custom amount once this week. What are my options now?
Ya he cambiado mi presupuesto a una cantidad personalizada una vez esta semana. ¿Cuáles son mis opciones ahora?
Once you’ve hit your custom budget limit for the week, you can: 
Leave it where it is currently set. This means you won’t get new leads until the new week.
Set it to the recommended amount (if available).
Set your budget to unlimited, to open yourself to any leads that come in through the rest of the week. 

Head to your budget to see the options available to you. 
Una vez que haya alcanzado su límite de presupuesto personalizado para la semana, puede: 
Dejarlo como está actualmente configurado. Esto significa que no obtendrá nuevos prospectos hasta la nueva semana. 
Establecerlo en una cantidad recomendada. 
Establecer su presupuesto en ilimitado, para abrirse a cualquier prospecto que llegue durante el resto de la semana. 
Diríjase a su presupuesto para ver las opciones disponibles.
Why is 'Unlimited' the only other budget option I can select?
¿Por qué 'Ilimitado' es la única otra opción de presupuesto que puedo seleccionar?
Consistently running out of budget puts you at risk of missing out on potential customers, which is why in certain scenarios we may limit the number of custom budgets you can set in one week. The best way to ensure you aren’t missing out on potential customers is by setting an unlimited budget. In the meantime, if you would no longer like to receive leads this week you can consider hiding your business or pausing targeting. You will always be able to set a new custom budget when your budget resets on Monday.
Quedarse sin presupuesto de forma constante lo expone al riesgo de perder clientes potenciales, razón por la cual, en determinados escenarios, podríamos limitar la cantidad de presupuestos personalizados que usted puede establecer en una semana. La mejor manera de asegurarse de que no está perdiendo clientes potenciales es estableciendo un presupuesto ilimitado. Mientras tanto, si ya no desea recibir prospectos esta semana, usted puede considerar ocultar su negocio o pausar sus preferencias de enfoque. Usted siempre podrá establecer un nuevo presupuesto personalizado cuando su presupuesto se restablezca el lunes.
How budget is impacted with targeting paused
This section provides frontline reps with talking points to explain to pros how their budget is impacted when targeting is paused.

English FAQs
Spanish FAQs
If I turn targeting off for a service, how will my budget change?
Si desactivo las preferencias para un servicio, ¿cómo cambiará mi presupuesto?
If you turn targeting off, your budget will remain the same, but you will no longer receive targeted leads for that service. Please check your budget to make sure it reflects the total amount you want to spend on leads for each week.
Si usted desactiva las preferencias, su presupuesto seguirá siendo el mismo, pero ya no recibirá prospectos dirigidos para ese servicio. Revise su presupuesto para asegurarse de que refleje el monto total que usted quiere gastar cada semana en prospectos.

1. Overview
▶ KA summary
This article explains how Thumbtack pros can set up webhooks to send Thumbtack data to external tools such as CRMs, automation platforms, or other software.
Webhooks allow pros to connect Thumbtack to external software (e.g. CRMs, Zapier, proprietary systems) that support webhooks. These webhooks send information from Thumbtack to another system automatically using a unique endpoint URL.
Thumbtack has the following available endpoints: 
Leads: Triggered when a customer contacts a pro. This contains the customer’s contact info and job details.
Messages: Triggered when a customer sends a new message within Thumbtack. Read-only in external tool) 
Review: Triggered when a customer submits a new review on the pro’s profile.
The endpoints above are one-way connections where Thumbtack pushes data to the external tool, but the pros must still log into Thumbtack to respond to leads, messages, or reviews. 
Webhooks are set up per business profile. This means if a pro wants data from all their Thumbtack business profiles to flow to their software,  they will need to set up the webhook for each individual profile. The same endpoint URL can be used for multiple webhook setups.
Webhooks require technical familiarity with integrations. If a pro doesn’t understand how webhooks or endpoint URLs work, this setup may not be appropriate. 
Key points

Frontline reps can use these as quick reminders when helping a pro with webhooks:

A receiving tool is required before setup. Pros must already have a CRM or tool that can accept webhook data and provide an endpoint URL. If they don’t have this, they cannot complete setup.
Webhook must be enabled to send data.  Thumbtack only sends data when the webhook status is set to Enabled.
Webhooks are created per business profile. Each business must have its own webhook setup. If a pro has multiple businesses, confirm which one they’re working on.
Technical familiarity is required. If a pro does not understand how endpoint URLs or webhook setup works, this integration may not be the right fit. In these cases, suggest using a Thumbtack partner integration instead. 
Webhooks are one-way only.  Thumbtack sends data to the external tool, but pros must log into Thumbtack to respond to leads, messages, or reviews.
Testing confirms the connection is working.  Pros can use “Test this webhook” to send a test lead and verify the setup. Always direct pros to check ”recent deliveries” after testing.
“Recent deliveries” is the source of truth for issues.  If a pro reports a problem, guide them to:  Manage webhook → Recent deliveries → Failed row → Responses tab.  This shows exactly why the webhook failed.
Setup: Created and fully managed by the pro directly within Thumbtack
Neutrality on External Tools: Reps should not push or recommend specific third-party tools, nor should they suggest one category of tool is superior to another. If a pro has access to a partner tool, reps can recommend they use it. 
Case Themes: When logging case themes, reps should use the following: P>Partnerships>Pro integrations (supply)>Existing integrations>Webhooks
▶ When to use this article (Rep)
This article is a resource for both Support and Sales teams when a pro inquires about connecting Thumbtack to a software via webhooks. 
▶ For Support and Sales teams
Language Neutrality: Do not use "CRM" as a blanket term. Refer to the pro’s setup as their "external tool" or "receiving system." A pro might be using an automation bridge (like Zapier), a custom database, or a simple communication app.
Tool Neutrality: Don’t push specific third-party tools or suggest one category of tool is superior to another (e.g., do not suggest a connector like Zapier is "better" than a standalone CRM).
Reps should: Confirm Thumbtack’s ability to send data to any valid endpoint URL. The internal setup and choice of that tool are the pro's sole responsibility.
Different integration types: If the pro is using a tool that is already integrated with Thumbtack but wants to build a secondary custom connection via webhook, use this article. If they are having trouble with the Partner's native connection, switch to the Thumbtack Partners: Activation And Troubleshooting KA.
▶ For Support reps
Use this article when:
A pro mentions:
webhooks
endpoint
Automation tool like Zapier / Make / Workato
custom CRM
A pro needs help: 
Navigating, testing, or troubleshooting a webhook. 
The pro says:
“I want leads sent to my webhook”
“I have my own webhook. How do I set it up?”
“My webhook isn’t working. How do I troubleshoot?”
Case Themes: When logging case themes, reps should use the following: P>Partnerships>Pro integrations (supply)>Existing integrations>Webhooks
▶ For Sales Reps
Use this article when a pro: 
Uses or wants to use a software that is NOT a partner tool.
Wants to build a secondary connection via webhook
Has questions around Thumbtack webhook or integration capabilities
 For a list of partner tools, reps can refer to the How to link your Thumbtack account with partner platforms Thumbtack Help article. 
When a pro can use a webhook

Pros can use a webhook when:
The tool they want to connect to is not already integrated with Thumbtack 
They want Thumbtack data sent automatically to another system
They have a receiving endpoint URL for the software they want to connect to
The pros software tool might be:
A Customer Relationship Manager (CRM) like HubSpot, Salesforce, or Zoho
An automation tool like Zapier, Make, Workato, Microsoft Power Automate, Tray.AI , N8N, etc
A proprietary internal system
Any other software that can receive a webhook 
The receiving system must already be set up to accept webhook data. If the pro does not understand how webhooks or endpoint URLs work, this setup may not be appropriate. Webhooks require technical familiarity with integrations.
Common Integration Issues and How to Help (Rep)

Pro reports their webhook endpoint URL isn’t receiving data

When a pro contacts Support reporting that their webhook endpoint URL isn’t receiving data, frontline reps will follow these steps: 

1. Verifying the Endpoint URL 
If a pro says their webhook isn't receiving data, the first step is to check the structure of their link.
How to check: Guide the pro to the Endpoint URL field in their settings. 
Go to Integrations  > Locate and click on the specific webhook.
What to look for: A valid URL must be "specific," not "generic." It should contain a unique string of numbers or letters at the end.
❌ Wrong (Generic): https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/catch/
Rep talking point: "I noticed the link you entered is a bit too general. Webhooks require a unique, specific URL from your tool. Make sure you've copied the entire address provided by your CRM or automation tool."
✅ Right (Specific): https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/catch/7383229/bvadzm3/
Rep Action: If the URL is generic, the pro must go back to their external tool, copy the complete unique Hook URL, and paste it into Thumbtack. If it’s specific, move to step 2.

2. Enabling and Disabling the Webhook 
Sometimes a connection needs a "refresh" to trigger properly.
Who does it: The pro must do this within their Thumbtack account. (Reps can view the status in Admin but should guide the pro to take the action).
How the pro does it: 
Go to Integrations  > Locate and click on the specific webhook.
Toggle the webhook to OFF. 
Wait 5 seconds, then toggle it back to ON.
When to do this: Use this as a first-line "reset" if a pro has updated their URL or if they just resolved a billing/setup issue with their external tool.
3. Sending a Test Lead 
This is the only way to verify a connection without waiting for a real customer to reach out.
Who does it: The pro (via the Thumbtack App/Web).
How the pro does it: Click the "Test this webhook" button.
How the Rep helps: 
After the pro sends a test lead,  tell the pro to check their Recent deliveries for a new "test lead" entry to confirm the fix.
If they don’t see it, transfer the case to the Partnership Support team.

Transferring to the Partnership Support Team

If the pro has followed the three steps above (Correct URL, Refresh Toggle, and Test Lead) and they still don’t receive lead data, OR if they have a question not covered in this KA, support reps will transfer the case to the Partnership Support queue.

To transfer a case to the Partnership Support team, reps will follow these steps: 
Before you transfer the case in Salesforce, add notes to the outcome box that includes the following:
Business/service_pk impacted 
What the core issue is
Error code(s) if provided 
What software tool the pro is using
To transfer the case, lick Next in the case flow.
Select A Team (Queue).
Choose Partnership Support from the dropdown.
Click Next.
Let the pro know that Partnership Support will follow up via email within 1-3 business days for the initial response.
NOTE:  When logging case themes, reps should use the following: P>Partnerships>Pro integrations (supply)>Existing integrations>Webhooks
▶ Common questions from pros and how to help (Rep)

This is not an extensive list of commonly asked questions. For additional talking points, reps should refer to the talking points section at the bottom of this KA.
 
Pro asks: “Where can I find information webhooks?”
Rep action: Share the How to create a custom lead integration Thumbtack help article
Rep response: We have a comprehensive guide in our Help Center that walks you through the entire process from start to finish. It includes step-by-step instructions on how to create, update and test a webhook. It also goes over how troubleshooting steps and common reasons a webhook may fail. You can find all the information you need in the How to create a custom lead integration Thumbtack help article. 

Pro asks: "Is my software compatible with Thumbtack webhooks?"
Rep action: Explain that pros can set up webhooks for any integration tool that provides an endpoint URL and support webhooks. 
Rep response: Thumbtack webhooks work with any external tool that can provide a receiving endpoint URL. This includes most modern CRMs, automation tools (like Zapier), and custom databases. It is independent of the pro's operating system (Mac/PC/Mobile).
Note to rep: Avoid recommending one specific tool. 
 
Pro asks: "How can I be sure the connection is working?"
 
Rep action: Instruct the pro to send a test lead and then check their recent deliveries log. 
Rep response: To confirm the connection is active without waiting for an actual customer request, you can use the "Test this webhook" feature. This action triggers a dummy lead, clearly identified as a "test lead" within the recent deliveries log. After sending a test lead, check your Recent deliveries log. If you see a red "Failure" notice, click on it and look at the Responses tab—that will tell you exactly why your system isn't accepting the data.  If you see a green “Success” notice, that confirms the external tool received the data.
For steps on how to send a test lead, check out the How to create a custom lead integration Thumbtack help article.
2. How pros setup and managing webhooks (Pro)


How webhook set up works

To create a webhook, pros will navigate to the Integrations page by clicking their profile picture and then selecting “Integrations.”  Pros can follow the steps outlined in the https://help.thumbtack.com/article/how-to-create-a-webhook Thumbtack Help article. 
What pros should have before setting up a webhook
To ensure a smooth integration, pros should have the following ready before starting the setup in Thumbtack:
A receiving tool: A software tool that supports webhooks and ready to accept data. 
An endpoint URL: The unique "digital address" provided by the external system to receive Thumbtack's data.

What details a pro enters when creating a webhook
During setup, the pro will need to complete the following fields on the creation page:
Endpoint URL: Paste the URL from the external tool here. This is mandatory to proceed.
Authorization Type:  Only needed if the pro understands it (majority of tools will not need this)
Authorization options:
None: No authentication is required. Recommended if unsure.  
Basic: Allows the pro to create a username and password for the webhook. This protects the webhook from unauthorized requests.
Custom: Allows the pro to create a custom header. Only use this if the receiving system requires it.
Business profile selection: Select the Thumbtack profile they want to connect their tool to. If they need all webhooks to be set up, they need to set it up individually.  The same endpoint URL can be used for multiple webhook setup.
Event types: Select the data types (Leads, Messages, or Reviews) to be pushed to the software tool.
Leads → new leads
Messages → customer messages
Reviews → customer reviews
Status toggle: Defines the current state of the webhook  
Enabled: Actively sending date with no delivery failures recorded in the last 7 days.
Disabled: The setup is complete, but the connection is inactive.
Error: Connection is active but deliveries are failing. Pros should review the Recent deliveries section to identify specific problems.
▶ What the Create a webhook page looks like on desktop

[Image: rtaImage]


How to manage webhooks
Pros can access their webhooks from Integrations > Manage Webhooks  page on a desktop. This page allows them to:

Create: Set up new endpoints for Leads, Messages, or Reviews.
Monitor: View the "Recent deliveries" log to confirm data is flowing.
Edit/Delete: Update endpoint URLs or remove inactive connections.
Troubleshoot: Identify specific failure reasons via the Responses tab. 
For steps on how to manage their webhooks, pros will refer to the How to create a custom lead integration Thumbtack help article. 

NOTE: Although pros can access their webhooks on the app, it’s best that pros use a desktop for full features. 

▶ What the Webhooks page looks like on desktop

[Image: rtaImage]


Steps: How to help a pro setup or navigate their webhook (Rep)

When a pro needs help navigating or configuring their webhook, frontline reps will guide them through these steps:

Access the dashboard: 
Log into their Thumbtack account on a desktop.
Click the Calendar
Click Connect partner tools 
Click Manage webhooks.
From there, pros can: 
Create: Set up new endpoints for Leads, Messages, or Reviews.
Monitor: View the "Recent deliveries" log to confirm data is flowing.
Edit/Delete: Update endpoint URLs or remove inactive connections.
Troubleshoot: Identify specific failure reasons via the Responses tab.
Self-serve resources: Share the How to create a custom lead integration Thumbtack help article for steps on: 
Creating or deleting a webhook.
Updating an existing endpoint URL.
Generating a URL via Zapier.
For issues a pro may have with their software, reps will follow the steps in the + Troubleshooting: Pro reports their webhook endpoint URL isn’t receiving data + section above. 
How pros can test and troubleshoot webhooks
Pros are encouraged to verify their webhook connections upon creation, after any settings updates, or as a primary step in troubleshooting.
Sending a test lead to check webhook connection (Pro)
To confirm the connection is active without waiting for an actual customer request, pros can use the "Test this webhook" feature. This action triggers a dummy lead, clearly identified as a "test lead" within the recent deliveries tab. Reviewing these logs allows pros to confirm successful data transmission, validate their tests, or pinpoint specific errors.
For steps on how to send a test lead, pros will follow the steps in the How to create a custom lead integration Thumbtack help article
Troubleshoot issues from the recent deliveries log (Pro)
A delivery is an attempt by Thumbtack to send data to the pros webhook. Pros can check the Recent deliveries tab to:
confirm data was sent
verify tests
investigate errors.
Here are the general steps a pro takes to review a webhook delivery: 
Go to the Manage webhooks page.
Click the webhook they want to inspect.
Open the Recent deliveries tab.
The deliveries table displays: 
Success (green): Confirms the external tool received the data.
Failure (red): Confirms there is an error. From the Responses tab, pros will see a specific error code and explanation.
3. Talking points

General Overview & Capability


English talking point
Spanish talking point 
Q: What information can be sent to my webhook?

A: Thumbtack supports three primary data categories for webhooks:

Leads (real-time job details), 
Messages (incoming customer texts)
Reviews (new customer feedback)

Webhooks function as a one-way bridge, pushing data from Thumbtack to your system. To engage with customers—such as replying to messages, responding to reviews, or managing lead statuses—you must still use your Thumbtack account directly.

Q: Can I respond to messages or reviews using webhooks?

A: No. Webhooks are a one-way connection from Thumbtack to your tool. You must still log into Thumbtack to respond to leads, messages, or reviews.

Q: If I connect my CRM, will it automatically message my customers? 

A: No, since this is a one-way integration, Thumbtack doesn't send the message for you and your webhook-integrated tool cannot send a reply message to the customer in Thumbtack.  Functionality outside of that is outside TT purview.

Q: What kind of webhooks can I use on Thumbtack?

A: You can set up a webhook for any integration tool that provides an endpoint URL and support webhooks. 

Q: Can I use webhooks with a partner tool?

A: Yes, only if the partner tool supports webhook integration 

Q: Can I connect Thumbtack with Zapier?
Q: ¿Puedo conectar Thumbtack con Zapier?
Yes. Zapier lets you automatically send your Thumbtack leads into thousands of other apps using webhooks.

It’s best if you’re already familiar with Zapier.
Zapier only supports leads (not messaging).
Step-by-step Zapier instructions are available in our How to create a custom lead integration – Thumbtack Help article. 
Sí. Zapier le permite enviar automáticamente sus prospectos de Thumbtack a miles de otras aplicaciones mediante webhooks.

Es recomendable que ya esté familiarizado con Zapier.
Zapier solo admite prospectos (no mensajes ni disponibilidad).
Las instrucciones paso a paso están disponibles en nuestro artículo de ayuda Cómo crear una integración personalizada de prospectos.
Setup and Management 


English talking point
Spanish talking point 
Q: What do I need to set up a webhook on Thumbtack?

A: You need a receiving tool (like a CRM) that is already configured to accept data and a generated endpoint URL from that system.

Q: How do I create a webhook on Thumbtack?

A: On a desktop, go to “integrations” in the dropdown menu and select your business profile. From there, click Create webhook, paste your endpoint URL, and choose the data types you want to send.

Q: I’m already using a customer management tool that uses webhooks. How do I connect it to Thumbtack?

A: Thumbtack’s self-service webhook capability allows you to integrate your existing webhook-enabled software directly through your Thumbtack account.

To begin, verify that your current tool is set up to receive data and has a generated endpoint URL ready for use.

Follow these steps once you have obtained your endpoint URL:

Sign in to Thumbtack on a desktop computer and head to the Calendar section.
Select “Connect partner tools” and then choose “Manage webhooks”.
Click on Create webhook. Here, you will paste your endpoint URL, pick the relevant business profile, and indicate which data types you wish to transmit.

Q: How do I access and manage my webhooks?

A: You can view and manage your webhooks directly through your Thumbtack account on a desktop computer.

To view and manage your webhooks:

Sign in to Thumbtack on a desktop and navigate to “integrations” in the dropdown menu.
To filter by business: If you have multiple business with webhooks, use the business selection dropdown menu at the top of the page. 
Select a specific business profile to see its unique connections.
Select "All businesses" to see every webhook active across your entire account.
To edit or review: Click on the specific webhook you want to manage.
From the "Manage this webhook" page, you can:
Update your Endpoint URLs.
Enable or Disable the connection.
Monitor data flow via the Recent deliveries log.
Send a test lead to verify the connection.
Delete the webhook entirely.

Q: How do I delete a webhook?

A: You can remove connections directly from your Webhooks dashboard on a desktop. 

On a desktop, sign in to Thumbtack and navigate to the Calendar section.
Click on “Connect partner tools” and select “Manage webhooks”.
Locate and click on the specific webhook you intend to remove.
On the management page, you can either toggle the status to disable it or select “Delete webhook” and confirm to remove it permanently.


Managing multiple business profiles


English talking point
Spanish talking point 
Q: Do I have to set up webhooks for each of my business profiles individually?

A: Yes. Webhook connections are profile-specific. If you want data from all your businesses to flow to your CRM, you will need to create and connect a webhook for each individual profile.

Q: How can I view the webhooks for my different businesses?

A: On the "Manage webhooks" page, use the business selection dropdown to filter your view. You can choose a specific business or select "All businesses" to see every active connection in your account.

Click on the specific webhook you want to manage. From the "Manage this webhook" page, you can:
Update your Endpoint URLs.
Enable or Disable the connection.
Monitor data flow via the Recent deliveries log.
Send a test lead to verify the connection.
Delete the webhook entirely.


Troubleshoot Webhook 


English talking point
Spanish talking point 
Q: I set up a custom integration but I’m not seeing any leads in my CRM. What should I do?

A: First, check your Recent deliveries log in Thumbtack. If you see a red "Failure" notice, click on it and look at the Responses tab—that will tell you exactly why your system isn't accepting the data. If you don't see any deliveries at all, it likely means you haven't received a new lead yet. You can also send a Test Lead to confirm the setup.

Q: Why did my webhook fail?

A: The best way to find out is to check your Recent deliveries log, click on the Failed row, and look at the Responses tab. This shows the exact error code and explanation provided by your system. Common issues include mistyped URLs or using a URL meant for a different platform.

Q: How can I test my webhook?

A: Once set up, scroll to the bottom of your webhook settings and click Test a webhook. This sends a "dummy" lead to your system so you can verify the connection in your Recent deliveries log.

Q: My webhook shows a "Disabled" status and I don't know why.

A: A webhook may be automatically disabled by Thumbtack after repeated delivery failures. You will receive an email notification if this happens, including the error type that caused the disconnect.

Q: My webhook shows an "Error" status. What does that mean?

A: An "Error" status means your connection is active, but deliveries are currently failing. You should review the Recent deliveries section to identify the specific technical problem your system is reporting.

Q: I got an email saying my webhook "isn't connecting." What do I do?

A: That email means Thumbtack tried to send you a lead, but your CRM rejected it. Your webhook is still active, but you should check your Recent deliveries log to see the error code. If you don't fix it, the system may eventually disable your connection entirely.

Q: I got an email saying my webhook "is disabled." Why?

A: Our system automatically disables a webhook if it fails too many times in a row or if your CRM tells us the URL is 'Gone' (Error 410). This protects your data. To fix this, you’ll need to resolve the error in your CRM, then go to your Manage webhook page in Thumbtack and manually toggle the status back to Enabled.

4. Resources

Related resources for PROS

Direct links
Resources for FRONTLINE REPS

Other

articles.fullText:
Visible Back-End Price Caps (Lead Pricing) (Pro)

Contents

Overview
Price capped categories
Known bug in a few categories
Process
Steps: Helping pros frustrated about pricing
Talking points
Resources
1. Overview
Price caps are caps that set a maximum limit on lead prices, preventing pros from bidding higher than what we consider a reasonable price.
Pros who are targeting services in price capped categories will notice the lead price will stop increasing at some point as they move the slider to the right (so they don’t go past the maximum accounts set by Thumbtack). Reps can refer to the internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA to learn more about the competitiveness slider and setting lead prices.
Price caps mainly impact booking prices. However, there are a few service categories with price caps that impact leads. Learn more in the Price capped categories section.
Note: Price caps do not change or impact actual prices.
Note: With the rollback of Instant Book, the majority of pros in price capped categories won’t see caps. That’s because price caps mainly addressed the high booking prices. However, there are three categories with price caps enabled. Some dimensions may have the same lead value as the lowest lead price setting. This means the lead price in those categories won’t change at all for some prices as the slider moves. 
Price capped categories
Price caps mainly impact booking prices.¹ However, there are a few service categories with price end caps that impact leads, which include: Lawn Mowing and Trimming, House Cleaning, and Full Service Lawn Care.²
Appliance Repair or Maintenance
Central Air Conditioning Repair or Maintenance
Duct and Vent Cleaning
Electrical and Wiring Repair
Full Service Lawn Care²
Furniture Assembly
Furniture Moving and Heavy Lifting
Garage Door Repair
Handyman
House Cleaning²
Junk Removal
Lawn Mowing and Trimming²
Local Moving (under 50 miles)
Lock Installation and Repair
Plumbing Drain Repair
Plumbing Pipe Repair
Sprinkler and Irrigation System Repair and Maintenance
Toilet Repair
TV Mounting

²These three service categories (in some markets) have back-end price caps with the same value as the lowest lead price setting. This means the price for those service categories won’t change at all for some prices as the slider moves.
▶ Known bug for a few categories
Thumbtack has found that in some markets for House Cleaning, Lawn Mowing and Trimming, and Full Service Lawn Care, the back-end price cap for some dimensions (i.e 3 bedroom house cleaning) is the same value as the lowest lead price setting. This means the leads price won’t change at all for some prices as the slider moves. 
Thumbtack will work to address this in the coming weeks. Only about 3% of pros may actually experience this. ​​​​​​
Talking point - how to talk to a pro about this

English talking points
Spanish talking points
In order to avoid charging unreasonable prices, we have set maximum amounts that we charge for leads in some categories. The price for some leads won’t change once you hit the maximum. In this case, the minimum setting is also the maximum setting for this category in your market.
Para evitar cobrar precios poco razonables, hemos establecido montos máximos que cobramos por los prospectos en algunas categorías. El precio de algunos prospectos no cambiará una vez que usted alcance el máximo. En este caso, el ajuste mínimo también es el ajuste máximo para esta categoría en su mercado.
2. Process
Steps: Helping pro frustrated about pricing (Rep)
Pros may contact support for several reasons, including high prices, costs exceeding what they would charge a customer, and negative return on investment (ROI) after expenses. 
If a frustrated pro contacts Support, frontline reps should follow these steps:
Acknowledge the pro's feedback and mention that Thumbtack is actively working to address unreasonable pricing. 
▶ Talking point
English talking points
Spanish talking points
We hear your feedback and are actively working on solutions to avoid unreasonable pricing. One solution that we have recently implemented is setting maximum amounts that we charge for certain types of leads as we continue improving our pricing system. Your lead prices for certain types of leads will not increase even as you move the slider higher.
Hemos recibido sus comentarios y estamos trabajando activamente en soluciones para evitar precios poco razonables. Una solución que hemos implementado recientemente es establecer montos máximos que cobramos por ciertos tipos de prospectos, mientras seguimos mejorando nuestro sistema de precios. Sus precios de los prospectos para ciertos tipos de prospectos no aumentarán, incluso si usted mueve el control deslizante a un valor más alto.
Submit the pro’s feedback in Salesforce following the steps in the internal Product Feedback KA.
3. Talking points

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Why does my booking prices for some categories stop increasing at one end while others do not?
¿Por qué mis precios de reserva en algunas categorías dejan de aumentar, pero en otras no?
In order to avoid charging unreasonable prices, we have set maximum amounts that we charge for certain leads. The price for leads will remain the same once you hit the maximum. 
Para evitar cobrar precios poco razonables, hemos establecido montos máximos que cobramos por ciertos prospectos. El precio de los prospectos se mantendrá igual una vez que usted alcance el máximo.
The price of leads on my lead prices is so high!
¡El precio de los prospectos en mis precios de prospectos es demasiado alto!
We hear your feedback and are actively working on solutions to avoid unreasonable pricing. One solution that we have recently implemented is setting maximum amounts that we charge for certain types of leads as we continue improving our pricing system. While you will still be able to increase your lead prices for leads, for certain types of leads the amount will not increase even as you move the slider higher.
Hemos recibido sus comentarios y estamos trabajando activamente en soluciones para evitar precios poco razonables. Una solución que hemos implementado recientemente es establecer montos máximos que cobramos por ciertos tipos de prospectos, mientras seguimos mejorando nuestro sistema de precios. Aunque usted todavía podrá aumentar sus precios de los prospectos, para ciertos tipos de prospectos el monto no aumentará, incluso si usted mueve el control deslizante a un valor más alto.

articles.summary: Internal guidelines for verifying a user's identity before making account changes, including voice and name verification methods.
articles.concepts: account verification, identity confirmation, name verification, voice verification, security check
articles.fullText:
Verify Account Information (Pro) (Customer)

Contents
Overview
Updates
Maven voice verification
Name verification for Maven SMS and chat transfers 
Verification guidelines (when to verify vs not)
Verification IS required
Verification NOT required
Information used to verify an account
Additional verification information
Process
Steps: How to verify an account when working with account owner (Rep)
Steps: How to verify an account when working with an authorized user (Rep)
Steps: How to verify an account from a Maven transfer (SMS and Chat) (Rep)
Steps: How to verify an account for email cases (Rep)
Steps: How to handle interactions rerouted due to technical issues (Rep) 
Steps: How to help an unauthorized users (Rep) 
Steps: How to add security code flag or authorized user flag in Salesforce (Rep)
Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) outlines the mandatory processes for frontline reps to verify a user's (pro or customer) identity before providing account details or making any changes. It details when verification is and isn't required, the specific information to be used for verification (including primary and additional details), and the steps for handling account owners, authorized users, rerouted interactions, and unauthorized users. The goal is to ensure the security and privacy of sensitive account information.
To protect our users' (pros or customers) sensitive information, frontline reps are required to verify the identity of the person they are speaking with before providing account-specific details or making any account changes. Only the Account Owner or an Authorized User may approve changes to an account.

Account Owner: The person whose name is on the account. They have complete access to all account information and are the only person who can grant Authorized User status.
Authorized User: A person explicitly given permission by the Account Owner to access the account, request specific account information, and approve changes. Accounts with an Authorized User will have a specific flag in Salesforce.

Reps must strictly adhere to the verification guidelines and process prior to disclosing any account-specific details or approving changes. Sensitive account information is defined in the internal Sensitive Account Information Handling Guidelines (Pro) (Customer) (Rep) KA. 
Updates
May 1, 2026: Maven voice verification
Thumbtack's AI assistant is now being piloted on the phone channel as of May 1, 2026 (soft launch). This is a limited pilot and is not yet fully rolled out — not all calls will be handled by Maven Voice during this phase.
Verification is still required on every Maven Voice transfer — the same as any other inbound phone call. Maven does not verify users on phone calls.
For full details on how Maven Voice works and how to handle transferred calls, see the Thumbtack’s AI Assistant (Maven) (Rep) KA.
April 27, 2026: Name Verification for Maven chat and SMS transfers 

The process for handling name verification on Maven transfers has been updated to ensure legal compliance. This update affects the Verification IS Required and Verification NOT Required sections, as well as the Information Used to Verify an Account section.

What changed:
Previously, reps were told that if Maven displayed a VERIFIED status, they only needed to ask for the user's name to address them — not for identity matching or re-verification.
Effective April 27, 2026, reps must always ask for the user's name and confirm it matches the name on the Thumbtack account, regardless of Maven's verification status. A VERIFIED status means Maven confirmed the user's credentials (login or phone number) — it does not confirm who is actually on the other end of the interaction.
For full steps, see Steps: How to verify an account from a Maven transfer (SMS and Chat) (Rep) below. 
Verification guidelines (when to verify)

To ensure the security of our users, it’s important that frontline reps follow the verification guidelines listed below.
▶ Verification IS required
Support reps must verify the account in the following situations:
New interaction: Every time an interaction has ended in Genesys and the pro or customer contacts support again. Even if the pro or customer contacted support within 24 hours, verification must occur.
Maven Voice transfers: Maven does not verify users on phone calls. There is no verification status or 24-hour window for voice. Full verification is required on every Maven Voice transfer, the same as any other inbound phone call.
Maven Chat and SMS transfers: A conversation is transferred from Thumbtack’s AI assistant with the status:
VERIFIED: Ask the user for their name to verify it matches the account name. If it’s a mismatch, follow the full verification process.
UNVERIFIED (or blank): Follow the full verification process.
Same interaction, different account: In situations where a user passes the interact (phone, chat, SMS) to someone else during the interaction, reps must verify the second account before helping the user.
Email case, different email: If a pro or customer is emailing from a different address than what’s on their Thumbtack account, reps can ask them to verify an additional three items under “Additional verification information" and ask for specifics about their requests.
Outbound phone calls: When making an outbound call, reps must verify they’re speaking with the account owner before making any changes or sharing any account information. If the rep reaches the account owner by dialing the phone number on the account, they can consider the phone number verified, but must still verify two other pieces  of information. 
Advanced Service takes case: Advanced Service is required to repeat the verification process even though the previous rep already completed it.
▶ Verification NOT required
Support reps do NOT need to verify the account in the following situations:
Email case, same email address: If the pro or customer is emailing us from the email on their account, they are verified, and reps can make their requested changes.
Technical issues reroutes interaction (SMS/Chat only): If a previous teammate experiences technical issues, a rep may receive a contact from the original rep they were working with. If the conversation in Genesys has not ended, follow the Steps: Handling rerouted interaction due to technical issues.
Department transfers: If a user has already completed or started the verification process with another department before being transferred. Follow Steps: How to handle departmental transfers or interactions rerouted due to technical issues (Rep).
Information used to verify an account 
This section outlines the specific pieces of information that can be used to confirm a user's identity and their authorization to access or make changes to an account.
Frontline reps must verify the identity of the person they are speaking with. When verifying a user, reps will have the user provide the following information: 
Full name: The name of the person on the call, chat, or SMS, confirmed against the name on the Thumbtack account. 
Ask open-ended questions only:
✅ "Can I have your full name?"
✅ "Can I have your first and last name?"
Do not ask leading questions:
❌ "Can you confirm that I'm speaking with John Doe?"
❌ "Can I have the first and last name listed on the account?
▶ Acceptable name variations:
The legal name of the user
An acceptable nickname (abbreviated form or a commonly recognized variation).
▶ Common Nickname Variations include:
Bill → William
Joey → Joseph
Bob → Robert
Peggy → Margaret
Chuck → Charles
▶ Common Abbreviated Forms include:
Dan → Daniel
Ed → Edward
Mike → Michael
Liz → Elizabeth
Nich → Nicholas
Note: Name extensions such as Sr., Jr., and III must still be verified even when a nickname is accepted.
▶ Email address: The email address associated with the Thumbtack account.
Chat interactions: If Maven status is VERIFIED, email is already confirmed via login.
▶ Phone number: The phone number associated with the Thumbtack account
Inbound calls (voice): Phone number must be verified on every call.
Outbound calls: If the rep reaches the user by dialing the phone number on the account, phone number verification is considered complete. 
SMS interactions: If Maven status is VERIFIED, phone number is already confirmed via Maven. No need to ask again.
▶ Security code flag (if applicable): Check for a security flag under the "Thumbtack User" field in Salesforce:
Security code: When a security code is on the account, the rep must ask the user to provide it as part of verification.
▶ Authorized user: Flag added by the account owner to grant a specific person permission to access the account, request account-specific information, and approve changes.
Account has authorized user flag → follow Steps: How to verify an account when working with an authorized user (Rep)
Account owner wants to add an authorized user → follow Steps: How to add security code flag or authorized user flag
Security Code flags are visible under the “Thumbtack User” field in Salesforce
[Image: rtaImage]
For complete steps, see Steps: Verify an account (account owner). 
Additional verification information (when applicable)
When the primary verification details (full name, email, and phone number) cannot fully confirm a user's (pro or customer) identity or access to an account, additional details may be required. 
This section outlines the supplementary information that can be used for verification when necessary.
Physical address associated with the account
Last 4 digits of the card used on the account (payment method)
Recent project details (for customer accounts that don’t have a phone number or address), such as: 
Zip code
Type of service requested
2. Process
Steps: How to verify an account when working with account owner (Rep)
To provide account-specific details or help with making account changes, Pros and customers must successfully verify a minimum of two pieces of information, excluding their name, the name on the account, and the security code (if one is set).
(See Internal Making Account Changes on Behalf of Pro or Customer (Impersonation Guidelines) (Rep) KA KA for a list of items reps can and cannot change on behalf of the user.)
Support reps must complete the verification process when starting a new interaction by following these steps:
Verify the full name on the account.
▶ If the name provided doesn’t match the one on the Thumbtack account:
Check the security flag to determine if you are speaking to an Authorized User. 
If yes: Follow Steps: Verify an account (authorized user)
No: Follow Steps: Handling unauthorized users (Rep)
Verify the email address.**
Verify the phone number.**
Security code (if one is set).
▶ If the security code cannot be verified:
Ask the pro to verify at least one item under the "additional info to verify" (on top of the initial 2 verification items). 
Once verified, ask them to change or remove the existing security code.
IMPORTANT

**If the email address or phone number cannot be verified, rep can have them verify any items from the Additional verification informationsection. A minimum of 2 items excluding name must still be successfully verified.
If the pro or customer is unable to verify the required items, follow Steps: Handling unauthorized users (Rep)
Steps: How to verify an account when working with an authorized user (Rep)
To provide account-specific details or help with making account changes, Pros and customers must successfully verify a minimum of two pieces of information, excluding their name, the name on the account, and the security code (if one is set).
(See Internal Making Account Changes on Behalf of Pro or Customer (Impersonation Guidelines) (Rep) KA KA for a list of items reps can and cannot change on behalf of the user.)
When a frontline rep receives a new interaction with a security code flag for an authorized user on their account, frontline reps must complete verification by following these steps: 
Verify the name of the person on the line or chat
Verify the full name on the account
Verify the email address**
Verify the phone number**
Verify the authorized user’s relationship to the account owner
Verify the security code (if one is set).
▶ If the security code cannot be verified:
We can’t share any account-specific information or make any changes. 
You can offer non-account related help like providing general Thumbtack information or processes documented in the Help Center. 
If the user insists on getting account related help, tell them to have the account owner reach out to update to the security code.

IMPORTANT

**If the email address or phone number cannot be verified, rep can have them verify any items from the Additional verification information section.
If the pro or customer is unable to verify the required items, follow Steps: Handling unauthorized users (Rep)
Steps: How to verify an account from a Maven transfer (Chat and SMS)
When receiving a chat or SMS interaction transferred from Thumbtack's AI assistant (Maven), the user has already gone through system verification before being transferred. 
Support reps will review the prior conversation, confirm who they are speaking with, and complete any remaining verification before proceeding. Maven behavior is identical for both chat and SMS — the only difference is which credential Maven used to verify the user.
Part 1: Before You Start
Check the # VERIFICATION STATUS field in the interaction window:
VERIFIED: Maven successfully verified the user.
UNVERIFIED or blank: Maven was unable to verify the user after two attempts. Full verification will be required.
Review the AI assistant summary and scroll up to view the full conversation history.
The user is labeled "Visitor" and the AI assistant is labeled "Maven bot" in the log.
Do not ask the user for any information they already provided to Maven — this will result in a QA markdown during Case and Account Review.
Part 2: Verify the Account
Ask for the user's full name (regardless of verification status):
"Can I have your full name?"
Confirm the name matches the name on the Thumbtack account in Salesforce.
Name matches → continue to step 2.
Name does not match, check for a Security Flag in Salesforce under the "Thumbtack User" field for an authorized user listed:
If yes, follow Steps: How to verify an account when working with an authorized user (Rep)
If no, follow Steps: How to help an unauthorized users (Rep)
The # VERIFICATION STATUS field in the interaction window will determine if further verification is needed:
If status is VERIFIED: Verification is complete. Proceed with the interaction.
If status is UNVERIFIED, follow the standard verification process starting on step 2 > Steps: How to verify an account when working with account owner (Rep) 
Note: If a user was verified by Maven and contacts support again within 24 hours via the same channel, they will automatically be flagged as Verified. Reps must still confirm the user's name in step 1.
Steps: How to verify an account for email cases 
When a pro or customer emails Thumbtack support from the email address listed on their Thumbtack account, they are considered verified. Support reps will confirm the sender email matches the account before responding.
Confirm the email address the message was sent from matches the email address on the Thumbtack account in Salesforce.
Matches → Verification is complete. 
Does not match, move to step 2. 
Ask the user:
To verify 3 items from the Additional verification information list AND
For specifics about their requests.
All items verified → verification is complete. Proceed with the interaction.
If the user is unable to verify the required information → follow Steps: Handling unauthorized users (Rep).

Steps: How to handle departmental transfers or interactions that were rerouted due to technical issues (Rep)
If a previous teammate experiences technical issues, a new rep may receive a contact from the user the previous rep was working with. If the conversation in Genesys has not ended, the rep who received the new interaction will follow the steps below:
You don’t need to verify their identity again.
To continue the conversation, proceed with a proper introduction:
▶ Rerouted due to technical disconnection“Hi [user]! This is [advocate name] from the [team name]  Team. I apologize for the disconnection. It looks like your account has already been verified by the previous rep, so I can pick up right where you left off and help you with [concern].
For a department transfer: 
▶ Departmental transfer — user already fully verified:“Hi [user name]! This is [advocate name] from the [team name] Team. Your conversation was transferred to me by our Customer Support Team. I can see that the account verification has been completed already, I’d be more than happy to take over and help you with [concern].
▶ Departmental transfer — some verification still needed“Hi [User Name], this is [Your Name] from the Thumbtack Support Team. I've received your transferred conversation from [team name] Team. It looks like we just need a bit more verification; could you please provide [Missing Verification Details]?
IMPORTANT
Failure to review prior conversations, resulting in repeated requests for information already shared, is considered a markdown in Case and Account Review. 
The objective is to streamline the user experience by minimizing the need for users to reiterate information already verified in earlier interactions.
Steps: How to help an authorized user (Rep)
Policy on Sharing Account-Specific Information: Under no circumstances should a rep make any changes or share any account-specific information if the user cannot verify the account or claims they are not the account owner or an authorized user. In such situations, encourage the user to have the account owner contact Thumbtack to authorize their access to the account. Thumbtack can add a security flag to the account for added safety.
Permissible General Information: Frontline reps can provide general Thumbtack information to the user, such as how Thumbtack works or how to reset a password, even if they haven't verified their information. Reps can refer to the internal Sensitive Account Information Handling Guidelines (Pro) (Customer) (Rep) KA for information on what they can and cannot share.
Frontline reps will follow these steps if the pro or customer is unable to verify the required items: 
Inform the user that they are not listed on the account.
Ask if the account owner is with them and if they are available to talk or chat
If the account owner is available ("yes"):
Ask the account owner to verify their account by following Steps: Verify an account (account owner). 
Ask the account owner if they want to add an authorized user to their account, which grants them permission to authorize changes and receive account-specific information.
If they agree to add an authorized user ("yes"):
Follow Steps: Add security code flag or authorized user (Rep). 
Continue the conversations as usual with the authorized user.
If they decline to add an authorized user ("no"):
Ask the account owner if they grant one-time authorization to the current person.
If they grant one-time authorization ("yes"):
Continue the conversations as usual with the temporary authorized user.
If they refuse one-time authorization ("no")
Continue the conversations with the account owner.
If the account owner is not available ("no"): Proceed to Step 3.
Offer non-account-related help only, such as providing general Thumbtack information or process details found in the Help Center.
If the user insists on account-related help, advise them that the account owner must reach out to add them as an authorized user.
Steps: How to add a security code flag or authorized user flag to account in Salesforce (Rep)
Pros and customers can add a security flag to their account for increased security. The flag, known as a security code, is added to the user's account in Salesforce for two main reasons: 
Security code: A custom code or password set by the account owner as an extra layer of account protection. 
Authorized user flag: A flag added by the account owner to grant a specific person permission to access the account, request account-specific information, and approve changes. The flag includes the authorized user's name and their relationship to the account owner.
Frontline reps from voice and non-voice channels can add an authorized user to an account, or a security code flag as long as the rep is working with the account owner. 
Follow these steps to add a flag to the account in Salesforce: 
First, verify you are working with the account owner by following the “Steps: How to verify an account when working with account owner (Rep)”
From Salesforce from the case, select the plus sign located under the "Thumbtack user" section.
For steps and visuals, see internal Salesforce: Case Navigation and Management (Rep)
Under “Flag”, type “Security Code”.
In the notes field, include the following details: 
▶ If adding a security code only:
Who requested the flag (should always be the account owner)
The security code the account owner wants to set
▶ If adding an authorized user (with or without a security code):
Who requested the flag (should always be the account owner)
The authorized user's full name
The authorized user's relationship to the account owner or company
Security code (if the account owner wants to add one)
Any helpful context for future reps (if applicable)
Click Save. The flag is added immediately after clicking save.  
Confirm with the account owner:
Security code added: "I've added the security code to your account. You'll be asked to provide this code when contacting us in the future."
Authorized user added: "I've added [authorized user's name] to your account. They will now be able to access account information and approve changes when contacting us.

This internal knowledge article provides guidance for Frontline Reps on handling inquiries related to Thumbtack's user research, including surveys and interviews. It outlines processes for helping pros or customers with past survey questions, survey rewards, and the monthly economic survey, and provides contact information for the User Research Team and relevant Slack channels for support.
Thumbtack regularly email pros and customers asking if they would like to participate in user research sessions, this could be interviews or surveys. 
Frontline reps can stay up-to-date on user research by joining the #experience-research Slack channel.
Reminder to frontline reps: All metrics and statistics shared externally must be approved by Legal.
2. Process
(Rep) Steps: How to help pro or customer with user research queries 
This subsection outlines the specific process for addressing inquiries related to previous Thumbtack surveys. It includes instructions for gathering information from the inquiring party, relaying the request to the appropriate team, and ensuring follow-up.
Most of these pros and customers should respond to the email directly, but if a pro or customer contacts us mentioning "user research" (or something similar), frontline reps will follow these steps:
Contact the User Research Team:
Send an email to userresearch@thumbtack.com with the subject "User research inquiry."
▶ Use the following email template:Hi User Research Team,I have a [PRO/CUSTOMER] asking about the user research sessions. Here's their admin link: [ADMIN LINK][INCLUDE ANY PRO/CUSTOMER QUESTIONS]Let me know the next steps.Thanks,[NAME]
Close the Loop with the Pro/Customer:
Once you’ve received a response from userresearch@thumbtack.com, follow up with the pro or customer.
Let them know what steps they should take to participate.
Steps: How to handle questions about previous Thumbtack surveys (Rep) 
This subsection outlines the specific process for addressing inquiries related to previous Thumbtack surveys. It includes instructions for gathering information from the inquiring party, relaying the request to the appropriate team, and ensuring follow-up.
If a pro or customer contacts you to discuss a past Thumbtack survey, the frontline rep will need to gather the key details and connect with the right team for follow-up.
Gather the user's information.
The person's name and contact information.
The reason for their request (if they’ve provided it).
Any other helpful details about the survey.
Acknowledge and forward the request. Let the pro or customer know you'll forward their inquiry to the appropriate team.
Post the details in Slack. Share the information you gathered in the #experience-research Slack channel.
If you know the survey's owner (like a category manager or user researcher), reach out to them directly.
Confirm follow-up. Let the user know that the team will review the information and follow up with them.
NOTE: To avoid sending too many, Thumbtack only surveys pros who haven't received a survey in the last 30 days.

Contact Ian Hall on Slack. Send a direct message to Ian Hall with the pro's inquiry.

The date the survey was completed.
