Unresponsive Inbox Cues (Customer)

Contents

Overview
Customer experience
Inbox badge triggers
Inbox message sorting
(Customer) Steps: How to update an unresponsive inbox cue
Pro experience
Talking points
Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article provides Frontline Reps with information on customer inbox cues when unresponsive.It focuses on how it impacts customers and pros on Thumbtack. It details the changes to the customer experience, the pro experience based on customer actions, and provides talking points for reps to use when addressing customer inquiries about the updated inbox sorting and messaging prompts.
Thumbtack actively prompts all customers to respond to pros by making unread messages and unresponsive conversations more prominent in their inbox. 
For more details on the customer app experience, refer to the internal App Experience | Home Profile, Plan, Team (Customer) KA.
Customer experience
For Frontline Reps, the following section details the customer's experience as part of the unresponsive inbox cues experience. 
Unresponsive inbox cues consist of two main changes to the customer’s experience: inbox badge triggers and inbox message sorting.
▶ Inbox badge triggers
If a customer doesn’t read a pro’s message after 24 hours then it will receive inbox badge triggers. These triggers include an unread indicator, nudge text, and an inbox notification.
Unread indicator: A blue dot will appear for any unread messages in the customer’s inbox and will remain until the customer clicks into the pro’s message again.
[Image: AD_4nXfFbaQb7qcDB3ibGnQBK2R9q9quBH1lT3dvMX6sE9HEiTUXdMD3YjJ_p0ig0iOCTOaZobxCIZOjrxbTkv6zBunUjDPJ6d85y9RfqrAau_Cz4ooIezlxQklRkFT6jkljawSkEdVJHA]
Nudge text: This blue text will say “Sent X days ago. Reply?” The nudge text will remain visible for 14 days, unless the customer takes an action by either responding to the pro, making a hiring selection, or leaving a review.
[Image: AD_4nXciaP3j8vy4nXEpzhXngOBFftGPOIaQ5kMYqyKx79cgey0FYhflxune5SLB4Upxglxj6M6nkU0bSVuqnnX6OmUOkJ3U4KPxLBwj0O8GneB3TDc6IbLG6160BGH2YI6NtRr2eHb3ZA]
Inbox notification: When a pro’s message is left unread, it will be added to the customer’s inbox notifications.  On both desktop and mobile, it will show a red indicator dot on the inbox. On the app, the red inbox notification count will decrease after the customer clicks into the message again.
App
 [Image: AD_4nXdQBiSK7Hz7IzWY6bN-wY-gPGyLS15lFXYlLlPDiIa5_NDZbgtgK90_YSXL7cY-sqTt9rvtGoZ1qiuaxP_NszCBkQzsRh3lGMRiaUKTHIzMrwaKXiedcY29Jx8o-88lB1l8euEwxQ]
Web: 
[Image: AD_4nXcET8GU0CqkS_7AAkWGue9CXMB-ygk3qPanMbOhIRQBIQ_IvlW-66JYnWm4r14LymPIBiwWXyYUe7WKD-tBS96yUK-ZAllHUez_bCFtWtBYpnQrXbhD_iBu4yeaeNActP9X76kjPw]
▶ Inbox message sorting

To help improve the likelihood of customers responding to unread messages from pros, the customer’s inbox will be sorted in the following order:
Priority 1: Unread message without a nudge
Priority 2: Unread message with a nudge.
Priority 3: Read messages with a nudge.
Priority 4: Read messages.

Definitions:
Unread message: A message in the customer's inbox that they have not yet opened or clicked on.
Read message: A message in the customer's inbox that they have opened or clicked on.
Nudge: A prompt displayed to the customer, such as the blue text "Sent X days ago. Reply?". Nudges appear for unread messages after 24 hours.

The following image illustrates the Thumbtack customer inbox message sorting. The messages are ordered to prioritize unread conversations and those with a 'nudge' to encourage customer response.

[Image: AD_4nXcSOWb95cK-0O21vTnyuwrAXEjQFPOOhjNCzQOp5CM-HRi1WDmoyitaTyxtuMLxMa-F8NWVOhXg3SOo9RM6t8z8ttB9gDXsxHutEZtmOiCpes9bhDk8iuFW8va1K80x4R5rHiIO]

Customer (Steps): How to update an unresponsive inbox cue
For Frontline Reps, the following section details the process and steps customers will use to update an unresponsive inbox cue within the Thumbtack platform.

When a customer clicks an unread message, a prompt will appear in the messenger asking if they hired the pro. This prompt is visible for 14 days if the customer hasn't responded. The customer can choose one of three status updates:
Customer selects “Yes, I’ve hired this pro”
Condition: Only one pro was contacted
Outcome: The customer sees the message: “You indicated that you hired this pro.”
Condition: More than one pro was contacted
Outcome: The customer sees the message: “We let other pros you contacted know that they weren’t hired.”
Customer selects “No, I’m going with someone else”
Outcome: The customer sees the message: “We let the pro know that you hired someone else.”
Customer selects “I’m not pursuing this project”
Condition: Only one pro contacted
Outcome: The customer sees the message: “We’ve let the pro know that you’re not pursuing this project.”
Condition: More than one pro was contacted
Outcome: The customer sees the message: “We’ve let this pro and all others you contacted know that you’re not pursuing this project.”

The following screenshot displays the Thumbtack customer messaging interface. When the customer opens an unread message from a pro, a modal appears with the text 'Did you hire this pro?' Three buttons are presented for the customer to select: 'Yes, I've hired this pro', 'No, I'm going with someone else,' or 'I'm not pursuing this project’

[Image: rtaImage]

Pro experience

This section provides Frontline Reps with information on the pro’s experience with the unresponsive inbox cue.

If a customer receives an unresponsive inbox cue, then the corresponding pros will see an update based on the customer’s reply. And the job status pill will also be updated automatically based on the customer’s selection.

If customer selects “Yes, I’ve hired this pro”:
Condition: Only one pro contacted. Outcome: Job status updates to “Scheduled”. System message in thread: “[Customer name] let us know they hired you.”
Condition: More than one pro contacted. Outcome: Job status for other pros updates to “No hire.” System message in their threads: “[Customer name] let us know they hired someone else.”

If customer selects “No, I’m going with someone else”:
Outcome: Job status updates to “No hire.” System message in thread: “[Customer name] let us know they hired someone else.”

If customer selects “I’m not pursuing this project”:
Outcome: Job status for all pros in the project updates to “No hire.” System message in all their threads: “[Customer name] let us know they are no longer pursuing this project.”
2. Talking points
This section provides Frontline Reps with externally approved talking points to use when navigating conversations with customers regarding unresponsive inbox cues.

English talking point 
Spanish talking point 
Why are my messages sorted differently now? 
To help you see messages you haven't read, we're sorting your inbox. Unread messages will appear at the top, so you won't miss them. This helps you connect with pros who have responded to your request.

What does it mean when a message is marked as "unread"? 
It means we've noticed you haven't replied to the pro's message yet. We're highlighting it to make sure you see it and can respond if you're still interested.

How long will a message be marked as "unread"? 
The message will be marked as "unread" until you click on it again. The nudge text will stay visible for up to 14 days, or until you respond to the pro, make a hiring selection, or leave a review.

What if I'm not interested in a pro anymore?
If you're no longer interested, you can respond to the pro to let them know (the best route in most cases) or you can decline the pro. We're also working on ways to make it easier to close conversations you're no longer interested in.

Why are you doing this? 
We want to make sure you have the best experience on Thumbtack. We've heard from both customers and pros that unanswered messages can be frustrating. This update helps improve communication and makes it easier for you to focus on finding the right pro for your project.

What if I don't like this feature? 
We're always looking for feedback! If you have any suggestions or concerns, please let us know, we're here to help.

Will this affect all my messages? 
This applies to messages from pros you've contacted. We're focusing on helping you see responses you might have missed.

3. Resources
Resources for FRONTLINE REPS

Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal Knowledge Article (KA) (Unprofessional Behavior, Support Abuse, & Discrimination (Rep)) provides guidance to Thumbtack Support reps and Advanced Service on handling various user interactions related to unprofessional behavior, support abuse, and discrimination from users. It covers the appropriate processes for de-escalation, warning, and disconnecting interactions, and addressing different types of discriminatory behavior and service abuse, along with identifying when to escalate critical situations to the Trust & Safety Team.
Support reps may encounter challenging interactions, including unprofessional behavior, service abuse, and discrimination. Processes are provided for de-escalation, issuing warnings, disconnecting interactions, and escalating critical situations to the Trust & Safety Team. 
Ending Interactions When Users Refuse Resolution (Not unprofessional behavior): Provides steps for concluding conversations professionally when users are resistant to a resolution but not behaving unprofessionally.
Unprofessional behavior: Direct or indirect behavior toward Support rep by user: Outlines how to handle direct or indirect unprofessional conduct, including de-escalation techniques, issuing warnings, and disconnecting interactions.
Service abuse: Details the process for addressing misuse of Thumbtack support channels, including a warning system and potential removal from the platform.
Discriminatory behavior: Explains how to manage situations involving discrimination, including what reps should and should not do, and when to escalate to the Trust & Safety Team.
Reps will find information on how to effectively managing difficult interactions with pros and customers, such as: 
De-escalation: Techniques for calming situations where users are exhibiting unprofessional behavior.
Issuing Warnings: How and when to give verbal or written warnings to users for unprofessional conduct or service abuse, depending on their flag history.
Disconnecting Interactions: When and how to professionally end calls, chats, or SMS conversations when users continue to be unprofessional or refuse resolution.
Escalating Critical Situations: Identifying when to escalate serious allegations, potential safety risks, or severe discriminatory behavior to the Trust & Safety Team.
Pro has account manager reminder: Support reps should not add any unprofessional flags or send any warning emails for professionalism and/or phone support abuse if the pro has an account manager. Reps will handle the case as usual and then send a Slack message directly to their pros Account Manager to update them.
Definitions: Unprofessional Behavior, Discrimination, and Support Abuse

To help Support Reps and the Advanced Service team identify and respond to user conduct, this section defines the key terms used throughout this article.

Key term
Definition 
Direct Unprofessional Behavior
Personal attacks, including profanity, name-calling, or other abusive language directed at the support reps.
Indirect Unprofessional Behavior
Disrespectful conduct that hinders effective communication, such as yelling, constant interruptions, condescending language, refusing to allow the agent to speak, or excessive profanity directed at Thumbtack or its policies.
Discrimination
Unjust or prejudicial treatment based on protected characteristics, including age, disability, gender identity, marital status, medical condition, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or other legally protected categories.
Support Abuse
Misuse of Thumbtack support channels, including excessive contact regarding previously resolved issues or repeated escalation of the same issue.
Non-Discrimination Policy Violations
Thumbtack wants everyone—no matter their race, religion, gender, age, sexual orientation, etc.—to feel safe using the platform and ensure customers and pros have equal opportunity to hire or be hired for projects.
Thumbtack doesn’t allow discrimination based on age, disability, gender identity, marital status, medical condition, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, or sexual orientation.
This means Thumbtack doesn’t allow:
Discrimination of any form, regardless of the parties’ intentions or word choice.
Refusing to provide/receive services for discriminatory reasons outlined in our policy.
Vulgarity, slurs, name-calling, insults, etc.
Passing comments or generalizations
Offering or charging different pricing for discriminatory reasons outlined in our policy.
For more details, reps and users can refer to the Non-Discrimination Policy – Thumbtack Help article. 
Thumbtack's Non-Discrimination Policy
Below is Thumbtack’s Non-Discrimination Policy as outlined in the Non-Discrimination Policy – Thumbtack Help article. 
“At Thumbtack, our goal is to enable anyone to find the right professional to accomplish any project, anywhere, at any time. Thumbtack therefore prohibits discrimination against professionals or customers based on age, disability, gender identity, marital status, medical condition, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or other improper basis. Prohibited discrimination includes refusing to provide or accept pro services offered through the platform because of any of these characteristics, offering different pricing based on any of these characteristics, or any other conduct that improperly takes into account any of these characteristics. Along with our Content and Review Policy, this prohibition also applies to the posting of content, such as reviews or profiles, on Thumbtack.
Any pro or customer who believes they have been discriminated against in violation of this policy should report their concern here. A pro or customer found to have violated this prohibition may lose access to Thumbtack.”

Trust and Safety​​ will review the discrimination report to determine if the discrimination was intentional and if there is proof. They work to keep Thumbtack’s platform a fair and safe space for our users. To do this, they:

3. Unprofessional behavior: Direct or indirect behavior toward Support rep by user
Steps: How to Handle Direct or Indirect Unprofessional Behavior by Pro or Customer (Rep) 
These steps help support reps manage situations where a pro or customer is behaving unprofessionally. Reps will follow: 1) de-escalation, 2) warning the pro or customer, 3) disconnecting and then 4) post disconnect action. 
▶ 1. De-escalation:
The first step is to de-escalate the situation by letting the individual vent their frustrations without interruption, unless their behavior becomes abusive or threatening*. Give them space to express themselves can often help them calm down. To do this, Support reps will: 
Active Listening: Active listening is crucial for understanding the other person's perspective and effectively addressing their concerns.
Use these techniques:
Attentiveness: Focus on what they're saying, not on what you're going to say next.
Open-ended Questions: Ask questions that encourage them to elaborate (e.g., "Can you tell me more about that?").
Probing Questions: Ask targeted questions to uncover the root cause of their frustration.
Clarification: Don't hesitate to ask for clarification if you're unsure about something.
Paraphrasing: Restate their points in your own words to confirm your understanding and demonstrate that you're listening.
Reflecting Feelings: Acknowledge their emotions with brief phrases like, "I hear you," or "That sounds frustrating."
Summarizing: Summarize their key points to ensure you're both on the same page.
Empathy vs. Sympathy: It's important to show empathy (understanding their feelings) rather than sympathy (feeling pity).
Empathy helps you connect with the individual and work towards a resolution.
*NOTE: If their behavior becomes abusive or threatening, see Situations Handled by the T&S Critical Escalations Team section. 

▶ 2. Warning the pro or customer
To determine the appropriate response, review the user's account in Salesforce for any existing unprofessional behavior flags. The handling of the interaction will depend on the number of previous flags.
Support reps will issue warnings to encourage respectful and professional communication to de-escalate the situation for pros and customers who have not been flagged for unprofessional behavior. 
Review Account Status
Review the user's account (pro or customer) for existing unprofessional behavior flags in Salesforce to determine the number of warnings to issue.
NOTE: If the pro has an Account Manager, do not issue a warning or add an unprofessional flag. Instead, handle the case as usual and immediately send a Slack message to the Account Manager with an update.
Determine Warning Protocol
O previous unprofessional flags: If the pro or customer has 0 previous unprofessional flags, support reps will deliver a first warning and, if behavior continues, a second (Final) warning (two verbal (phone) or written (chat/SMS) warnings).
1 or 2 previous unprofessional flags: If the pro or customer has one or two previous unprofessional flags, support reps will deliver one warning. (one verbal (phone) or written (chat/SMS) warning).
Deliver the Warning
Choose an appropriate scripted warning from the available "Warning talking points" that best suits the communication style and the specific situation. The advocate must choose from the provided scripted warnings.
If a second warning is required (for users with 0 flags), it must be a different talking point than the first.
Conclude or Escalate
If the user heeds the warning and communicates respectfully, continue with the service interaction.
If the user does not heed the warning (and all allowed warnings have been delivered) and continues to be unprofessional, move to the Disconnecting steps below.

Additional Disconnecting Guidelines 
Acknowledge the previous warnings: Mentioning that you've already given warnings reinforces that this isn't a sudden decision.
State the reason for disconnecting: Clearly explain that it's due to the continued unprofessional behavior.
Keep it brief: Avoid getting into further arguments or justifications.
Maintain a professional tone: Even while disconnecting, remain calm and polite (though firm).
Option to reconnect (sometimes): Offering the option to reconnect later if they can communicate respectfully can be helpful, but it's not always necessary, especially if the behavior was very severe. Use your judgment.

5. Discrimination: Discriminatory behavior and policy violations
Do's and don'ts when dealing with discrimination
 
Frontline support reps should follow these guidelines any time they are dealing with discrimination: 
Don't ignore passing comments or generalizations. 
Do remind users of our policy and hold them accountable.
Don't share your personal opinion on the matter, whether that is agreeing or disagreeing with the user. 
Do remain neutral and stick to our policy.
Don't be rude or aggressive to the user. 
Do understand some of these matters are sensitive and users may not realize what they're saying.
Don't challenge a person’s core beliefs; that's not our role.
Steps: How to handle users reporting discrimination (via any channel) (Rep)
 
If a user reports discrimination through any channel (chat, email, text, phone, etc.), frontline reps  will follow these steps: 
Be empathetic to the situation. Thank them for contacting us about the concern and explain our Non-Discrimination Policy.
▶ English and Spanish talking point:
“Thumbtack doesn’t allow discrimination and we’re glad you came to us about this. I’m sorry to hear you had this experience. Can you tell me what happened?”
Thumbtack no permite la discriminación y nos complace que nos haya contactado al respecto. Lamento escuchar que tuvo esta experiencia. ¿Me puede decir que es lo que paso?
Gather relevant information such as: 
How did the interaction take place? In person? Text? Email?
Let the user know Trust and Safety will review the case and follow up with them.
Escalate the case to the T&S queue for review by the NDP team. Refer to the internal Trust and Safety Incidents KA for steps.
Upon review, Trust and Safety will take appropriate action.
Important guidelines when handling these situations: 
Don't tell the user that Thumbtack will remove the other party. We can't guarantee this until Trust and Safety has reviewed the details.
Don't make any other determinations about the situation such as: “It doesn’t sound like discrimination. Just move on to other projects.” or "If you don't have documentation, we can't take any action."

For emails, see email template “Guidelines: non-discrimination policy warning.”
After explaining the policy, you can continue the conversation as usual.
Gather relevant information such as: 
How did the interaction take place? In person? Text? Email?
Escalate the case to the Trust and Safety queue for review by the NDP team. Refer to the internal Trust and Safety Incidents KA for steps.
Reps should not tell the user you’re sending a case to T&S. 
Steps: How to handle discrimination in content or reviews on Thumbtack (Rep)
Discrimination in reviews, review responses, profile content, messaging, and any other interactions on the site will be treated similarly. The review will be deleted because it violates Thumbtack's Content and Review Policy – Thumbtack Help  and the user will be warned or removed.
Discrimination will not be allowed anywhere on Thumbtack, even if no one involved reported the concern.

If frontline reps come across discriminatory content in a review, they should follow these steps: 
 
Escalate the review to Trust and Safety. Steps on Reviews (Pro) KA. 
When notified the review was removed, the rep will place a Non-Discrimination Policy Notice flag on the account. Steps on Salesforce: Case Navigation and Management (Rep) KA. 
If this is their first flag  – Reach out to the user to explain why the review was removed and warn them about using discriminatory language
If the user is reporting another user's discriminatory behavior through the review, escalate to T&S. Steps on Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA for follow-up.
If this is their second flag – escalate the case to Trusty and Safety to remove the account. Steps on Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA for follow-up.
[If applicable] Send email template Review Disputes: Customer wants to know why their review was removed.

If a wedding officiant declines a wedding request for religious or moral reasons (e.g., I don’t officiate same-sex weddings or I only officiate Christian weddings), we won’t remove their account unless the officiant was rude or offensive in doing so. 
If you think a wedding officiant may be discriminating against a user, explain our non-discrimination policy to the user by letting them know we don’t tolerate discrimination on Thumbtack

Steps: How to handle users saying you are discriminating again them (Rep)
If a user accuses you of discriminating against them while you’re helping them (on chat, email, text, phone, etc.), frontline reps should: 1) let them know we take concerns of discrimination very seriously and 2) while you’re abiding by the guidelines Thumbtack has set, you will be forwarding their concern and the interaction on to our non-discrimination team for review. 
Examples of what this might look like:
“What’s your race? I don’t believe you can relate to me.”

“You’re not helping me because I am [blank] “
“Just because I’m old, doesn’t mean you can’t help me with my account.”
When a user says you are discriminating against them, Support reps will take the following steps:
Politely state our Non-Discrimination policy and let them know it pertains to customers, pros, and employees. See talking points below.
▶ Talking points
“Thumbtack doesn’t allow discrimination of any kind on our platform or by employees. I assure you I am following a consistent process as outlined for our team to follow. If you would like to continue working with me, I can help you with your concerns. However, if you are uncomfortable, I can/will forward your concern to another team for review.”
“Thumbtack doesn’t allow discrimination on their platform or by their employees. I’m sorry you’re frustrated with our ____ policy, I would like to try and help you.”
Ask the pro or customer if they would like to continue the conversation.
If they are willing, continue with the conversation based on our policies. For example: If they don’t qualify for a refund, don’t grant it at this time.
If they are not willing to continue speaking with you, let them know that you will end the call and that you will be sending their concerns to our non-discrimination team for review. Move to step 3.
Let the pro or customer know that you will need to disconnect the call or end the chat/SMS. You may then disconnect. 
Fill out Non-Discrimination/Unprofessional Report for Service form.
Fill out the "Global Help Others" request type in the Assist app.
Comment on the report thread letting the AS Team know that you filled out the form.
Leave the case open. 
The responding OC will put the case in their name and notate the case. The OC will action the case (deactivate, blocklist, block from phones, send business decision email, and add unprofessional flag) and then close it.
Refuses to Work With You Based on Your Location, Gender, Etc.
This section outlines what support reps will do when encountering discriminatory behavior or location-based bias from users (pros or customers). 
Examples of Discriminatory Remarks include:
I don't want to talk to you because you don't speak English.
I want you to transfer me to someone in America right now.
I don’t talk to foreigners. Get me someone in the U.S.
IMPORTANT: Thumbtack frontline reps' priority is to provide excellent support to our pros and customers while maintaining a respectful and inclusive environment. Frontline reps are empowered to set healthy boundaries and address inappropriate conduct. 
Steps: How to handle user says something discriminatory towards you (Rep)
If a user makes discriminatory remarks to you based on religion, gender, race, etc. (e.g., insults, name-calling, generalizations, or expresses bias), follow these steps.
If the user's discriminatory remarks are about your location, follow the steps in "(Rep) Steps: How to handle user asking about your location (location-based bias)."
State Policy:
Clearly state Thumbtack’s Non-Discrimination Policy.
"Thumbtack's Non-Discrimination Policy clearly states that discrimination or bias based on personal attributes or location is not tolerated on our platform. We strive to create an inclusive environment for everyone."
Emphasize that discrimination or bias based on personal attributes or location is not tolerated.
"Our policy ensures that all customers and pros receive equal service regardless of [mention the discriminatory factor]."
Disconnect (If Necessary): 
Your well-being is paramount. If the user continues the discriminatory behavior after the warning, you are authorized to disconnect the call or end the chat/SMS. 
Before disconnecting, please let the pro know that you will be disconnecting. 
“As I've mentioned, we require all communication to be professional. Because the conversation hasn't changed, I'm going to disconnect this [ call/chat ] now. Thank you for your time.”
Report the Incident to the AS Team: 
Fill out the Non-Discrimination/Unprofessional Report for Service form.
Fill out the "Global Help Others" request type in the Assist app.
Comment on the report thread, letting the AS Team know that you filled out the form.
Leave the case open.
The responding AS will put the case in their name and take any necessary action. See III. Support>For Operations Consultants.
Steps: How to handle users asking about your location (Location-based bias) (Rep) 
If a user refuses to speak with you based on your location or demands to be transferred to someone in the United States, follow these steps:
Acknowledge and Redirect: Politely acknowledge the user's request, but emphasize your ability to help them.
▶ Talking points:
"We're located in one of Thumbtack's support centers in the Philippines. I'm more than happy to help you today. Can you tell me more about your situation so I can look into your account?"
"I'm trained to help with your concerns. Let's chat more about your situation so I can take a look."
“Our advocates are required to speak fluent English to do the job, regardless of whether they’re based in North America or in the Philippines.” 
Offer Help: Focus on addressing their actual concern. Attempt to redirect the conversation to the issue they are experiencing.
Reinforce Training: If the user insists on speaking with someone from the United States, reassure them that all Support Advocates, regardless of location, receive the same comprehensive training and are equipped to handle their concerns.
▶ Talking point
Talking Point 1: "I understand you prefer to speak with someone from the U.S. Every Thumbtack support advocate receives the same training globally. And that means every advocate will give you the same level of care, regardless of where they’re located. I’m happy to look into your account. Let’s talk more about your situation."
Escalate (If Necessary): If the user persists in their location-based bias:
Explain Thumbtack's non-discrimination policy. Reiterate that we do not tolerate discrimination on our platform.
▶ Talking points to use:
Talking Point 2: "As a reminder, Thumbtack doesn’t allow this type of behavior because of our non-discrimination policy. Continuing with such behavior may impact your standing with Thumbtack. Let’s work on your concerns together. Tell me more details about why you reached out, and I’ll take a look into your account?"
Talking Point 3: "Thumbtack doesn’t allow this kind of behavior. I can send you our non-discrimination policy if you’d like to take a look. I’m happy to help you, but if you don’t let me, I’ll have to end this conversation. If this happens, we may also reevaluate your standing on Thumbtack."
Disconnect and Report: If the user continues to be discriminatory after the policy explanation, let the pro or customer know that you will need to disconnect the call or end the chat/SMS. You may then disconnect. 
Fill out this form.
Fill out the "Global Help Others" request type in the Assist app.
Comment on the report thread letting the AS Team know that you filled out the form.

1. Overview
On March 30, 2026, Thumbtack expanded the discovery points for the 10% Unlimited Budget Discount (UBD). While the 10% discount on leads for maintaining an unlimited budget remains structurally the same, this experiment introduced a dedicated "Special Offer" page and unified messaging for pros eligible for both UBD and BOSUP into a single "Get Free Leads” value proposition. This experiment shipped to baseline around June 23, 2026.
Eligible pros will now see the offer across multiple high-intent surfaces including the services tab, recommendation cards, and lifecycle communications (email/push). If a pro is eligible for both BOSUP and UBD, the app will now show a unified "Combined State" experience rather than competing banners. 
If a pro asks: “Why should I set an unlimited budget?”
Rep talking point: Setting your budget to  unlimited helps you get more leads at your level of competition while paying less per lead. Keeping your budget unlimited allows you to keep saving and continue getting the most leads possible.
Key points
Experiment details: 
Pros eligible for both BOSUP and the Unlimited Budget Discount (UBD) will no longer see competing banners. Instead, they see a unified "Get X free leads + 10% off the rest" headline
Clicking these new entry points leads to a dedicated full-screen "Special Offer" page designed for one-tap enrollment.
Unlimited Budget Discount terms
To keep the discount, pros must maintain an unlimited budget. If they switch back to a fixed (custom or recommended) budget, the discount is revoked immediately.
UBD only applies to leads, (Exclusions: opportunities, claimable jobs, or opt in leads or contacts)
Combined BOSUP + UBD terms
Remind pros that while the UBD persists as long as they are unlimited, BOSUP free leads require the pro to keep their increased budget for a specific commitment period (2 weeks).
The UBD is 10%. The number of free leads a pro gets varies.

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) explains Thumbtack's "Enforcing Minimum Requirements" (EMR), which dictates the steps new pros must take to become active and visible on the platform. It outlines different EMR versions, the associated requirements (like targeting setup and getting reviews), and how frontline teams can identify a pro's EMR status. This ensures new pros meet certain criteria to enhance their success and customer experience.
To ensure a positive customer experience and help new pros succeed, certain requirements must be met before they become fully visible in search results and can receive customer contacts.These requirements are known internally as "enforcing minimum requirements (EMR). These activation requirements vary depending on the pro's assigned version, which is based on their market and sign-up date.
New pros are defined as those who created their accounts on or after March 22, 2020, at 12:20 PM PST, when the activation requirements were implemented for all new accounts. Pros with accounts created before this date are not subject to these requirements. Once a new pro completes the required activation steps, they are permanently considered active and will have full access to Thumbtack's features.
The goal of these activation requirements is to ensure that new pros are ready to engage with customers and provide quality service, ultimately leading to their success on Thumbtack.
NOTE on terminology:
Targeting terminology: You may see "Targeting" and "Job preferences" terms used interchangeably throughout our internal KA resources or in-product.
"Enforcing Minimum Requirements (EMR)" is an internal term and must not be used when communicating with pros.
Updates
▶ Accelerated profile in onboarding
Starting sometime soon, Thumbtack will test a faster way for new pros to build their profile during onboarding. Pros will be able enter their business website, and Thumbtack will scrape it to pre-fill parts of their profile — which the pro then reviews and edits before confirming.
Launch date: TBD
Who's included: New pros signing up after the launch date
Markets: All
Priority: P1
Everything about EMR itself — job preferences, reviews, background check — works exactly the same. The only change is how some pros get through the business-profile step of onboarding. 
How it will work: 
Draft profile using website: Pros who enter a website see the option to have their profile drafted using their website. They can select:
Build my profile — starts the automated build below. (Move to step 2)
Enter info manually — continues through the standard flow, same as any pro without a website. (Skips to Select your business (prebuilt profile match) section below)
Scanning the website and auto-generate profile details. When a pro clicks Build my profile, Thumbtack will scan the pro’s website for business information.
Review and refine profile: The pro will review what Thumbtack found from their website and fill in anything missing or make edits as needed.
Continue onboarding: Pros will then move to the next step in onboarding.  
The Build my profile flow consolidates into this one review canvas — pros who use it don't see the individual prebuilt-profile-match, photo, or description screens separately.

▶ Go Live with “Activate Profile”
To help new pros understand when they start receiving and paying for leads, Thumbtack introduced an explicit activation step for pros on EMR versions 7 and 8 (launched August 28, 2025). V7 and V8 are the Go Live versions of V5 and V6 respectively — they carry the same requirements but add the activation step described below.
How go live works depends on where the pro is when they pass EMR:
If the pro passes EMR during onboarding:  They go live immediately and automatically. No activation step is required and no 24-hour window applies.
If the pro passes EMR after exiting onboarding (completed requirements via the finish setup checklist): Their profile does not go live automatically. Instead:
The pro receives an email with the subject line "Activate your profile so customers can find you today" prompting them to activate. From there:
Their profile will automatically go live 24 hours after passing EMR
They can go live immediately by clicking Activate profile now in the email or on their finish setup checklist
If the pro clicks "Activate profile now": They are taken to a confirmation screen: "You're now showing up in customer searches." This screen shows their active services, locations, days of the week, weekly budget, and the credit card on file for auto-pay — so the pro has full visibility into what they'll be charged for.
If the pro takes no action: Their profile activates automatically after 24 hours. When they return to the app, the confirmation screen appears.
Communications the pro receives (post-onboarding path only):
Email at EMR pass: "Activate your profile so customers can find you today" — with "Activate profile now" and "Review profile" CTAs
12-hour reminder (if not yet activated): Email and push notification — "Your profile will go live in 12 hours" — with a CTA to activate now
Confirmation email (once live): "You're now showing up in customer searches"
This distinction ensures pros who complete setup outside of onboarding have clear expectations about their visibility and when they'll start being charged for leads.

Versions: Enforcing minimum requirements (EMR)
To help Frontline Reps understand the different activation requirements, pros will experience different EMRs depending on their market and when they signed up for a pro account.

Older app builds: If a pro signed up after March 22, 2022 on an older Android or iOS build of the Thumbtack app (downloaded but never used to sign up), they may not be subject to EMR requirements, because not all EMR components were present in that build.
Requirements for activation (Pro)
Pros need to complete a few requirements before they show up on search results or get any contacts. An important thing to note is that requirements vary based on the pro's EMR version. They can be completed in any order.
Complete business profile
Pros must fill out their profile with:
Business name 
Basic personal information (first and last name, birthdate and address)
Profile picture
Business introduction 
Smarter lead matching: 
Pros onboarding in smarter lead matching will also set up their availability and travel area during the profile-building phase rather than later during job preference setup. Both are set at the business level and apply across all of a pro's trades, not per trade.
Set up job preferences
Baseline experience: 
Pros can select multiple service categories during onboarding and will pick one to set up. Pros must have at least one service category set up in the same business where the review(s) will be received. All EMR versions (excluding V0) require targeting set up for 1 category.
Job preferences switch on automatically, ensuring that once a pro fulfills EMR, they become visible in search results and eligible for leads. 
Pros can pause their job preferences at any point—either before or after passing EMR requirements. 
Visibility in search results and lead generation will start for all unpaused services as soon as all EMR requirements are met
Note: Because pros can pause (turn off) their job preferences at any time, the in-product phrasing is "Set up job preferences" (not "Turn on job preferences") for this reason.
See the internal Targeting Preference KA for more detail.
Smarter lead matching:
Pros onboarding in smarter lead matching don’t set job preference the way the baseline experience does. However, onboarding screens still refer to this as job preferences (or targeting), same as baseline. This requirement includes:
Reviewing recommended job types (auto-generated via AI based on the pro's trade, editable by the pro)
Setting a weekly budget (so charges don't exceed what the pro wants to spend)
Adding a card (payment method) (so Thumbtack can actually charge them). 
Similar to the baseline experience, job preferences switch on automatically, ensuring that once a pro fulfills EMR, they become visible in search results and eligible for leads. Pros can pause a specific trade at any point—either prior to or following the completion of EMR requirements. They do this on their Services page and select Pause next to that trade. Visibility in search results and lead generation will start for all unpaused trades as soon as all EMR requirements are met
Get reviews
Depending on the EMR version a pro is assigned, they may be required to get reviews.  Review requirements by EMR version: 
0 reviews: V0, V4, V6, and V8. 
1+ reviews: V1.5, V3, V5, and V7. 
3 reviews: V1  and V2 
NOTE: Pros onboarding in smarter lead matching are assigned EMR Version 8, which doesn't require a review.
Pros can get reviews by:
Requesting them directly from past customers, or
Importing from Google
Import an average star rating (when claiming a prebuilt profile). Pros who import a review rating (without the actual review text) instantly meet the requirement for having at least one review, which can speed up their activation.
See the internal Reviews (Pro) KA for more detail.
Complete a background check (BGC)
Pros must complete and pass the mandatory background check. The pro submits their name, date of birth, address and either their SSN or a live image capture of a government-issued ID (no SSN).
BGC submitted: Once the BGC is submitted and all other EMR requirements are met, pros can start getting leads even if the check has not yet been approved. 
Failed BGC: In the rare case that the pro fails the BGC, they will be blocked from the platform, and a refund will be processed for unused funds. The pro does not need to submit a refund request.
See the internal Background Checks KA for more detail.
Onboarding differences between baseline and smarter lead matching
The table below provides a breakdown of how the standard onboarding path compares to the smarter lead matching onboarding route, which applies to 50% of all new pros.

Profile review
Thumbtack automatically runs a profile quality check in the background whenever a pro's profile is created or edited. The pro is not notified unless action is taken as a result.
When profile review is triggered:
Profile creation — fires when a pro's business profile is first created
Profile edits — fires whenever a pro modifies their business introduction or Q&A section
Four possible outcomes:

Outcome
What triggers it
Automatically passed
No violations detected
Profile placed on hold
Content issues (e.g. "test" or gibberish text, non-US location, contact avoidance, mismatched category)
Profile deleted
Serious content violations (e.g. inappropriate language, service not offered, third-party marketing)
Profile deleted + account blocklisted
Most serious violations (e.g. sexual content, illegal content, discriminatory content, user is a minor, scam activity)
Why this matters: A pro can complete all EMR requirements and still not appear in search results if their profile is on hold or under manual review. If a rep cannot identify another reason a pro isn't appearing, checking for a profile hold is a key troubleshooting step. This can happen at any point — not just during initial onboarding — any time the pro edits their introduction or Q&A.
For profile holds and how to help pros resolve them, see the Account Holds (Pro) KA. For profile deletions and permanent removals, see the Removed or Banned Users (Pro) (Customer)  KA.

2. Pro onboarding (Baseline experience): Signing up to going live 
Existing customer accounts
If a customer wants to become a pro on an existing account, they should create a password if they haven't already, log in, then click Sign up on the landing page and follow the prompts. 
After selecting their service and zip code and clicking Sign up for free, a Set up your business profile modal appears with their email pre-filled (since they're already logged in) and a Phone number field to fill in. 
Tapping Continue prompts a verification code screen. Once verified, the pro moves into the "Tell us more about your business" survey.
Account creation
Step 1 — Pre-sign-up: category, zip, and services

Before creating an account, the pro tells Thumbtack what they do.
Landing screen 
The pro taps Sign up from the Thumbtack pro landing screen (thumbtack.com/pro) or Thumbtack app.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Category and zip code 
The pro searches for the service or trade they offer and enters their business zip code. 
▶ What the "Tell us what you do" / "Enter your business zip." screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Services 

The pro selects all service categories they want to offer. They'll show up in customer search results and get leads for every service they set up. During onboarding, they set up one service. They can add or remove services later. 
▶ What the "Select the services you offer." looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Sign-up method 

The pro sees a screen confirming demand in their area (e.g. "New customers are waiting. There were 2,183 Plumber jobs on Thumbtack last month in San Jose, CA") and chooses how to sign up:
Sign up with email
Sign up with Google
Sign up with Apple (iOS only)
Sign up with Facebook
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]


Rep note: The sign-up method a pro chooses becomes their login method. Pros who sign up with Google, Apple, or Facebook log in using that account going forward. Pros who sign up with email can update their email address after creating their account. For steps on updating account information, see the Account Information: Manage Account Settings and Status (Pro) KA.
Step 2 — Create account and survey
Create your account (email sign-up only) 

The pro enters their email, creates a password, and provides their phone number. They can opt in to text messages. Password requirements are shown in-product. They can opt in to text messages via two toggles:
Enable texts for account and job updates (checked by default)
Enable texts to help you succeed on Thumbtack (unchecked by default)
Tapping Sign up creates the account. On web and mobile web, Thumbtack sends a verification code after account creation, which the pro must enter to verify their phone number. On the app, there is no verification code step — the phone number is submitted but not verified at sign-up.
▶ NOTE: New pros signing up on mobile web in a home category
New pros signing up on mobile web, in a home category, see a non-skippable "Continue on the app" screen pushing them to download the Thumbtack app, directing them to the App Store. Once installed, the pro continues into the survey.
Workaround: Pros can get around this hard gate by leaving the page — closing the browser or hitting back — then logging back in. The prompt won't reappear once they do this, and they can continue onboarding on mobile web. See Thumbtack App (Pro) KA to learn more. 
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Survey 

Thumbtack collects internal data about the pro. This information is not shared publicly. The survey asks:
▶ What's your name?
Rep note — Name field: Thumbtack requires pros to use their legal name when signing up. The person listed on the account should be the business owner. The name on the account can only be changed if it’s misspelled or legally changed. Because pros are required to take a background check, the name on the account must match the name submitted for the BGC. If there is a name mismatch, the BGC process may be affected. For more detail, see the Background Checks (Pro) KA.
How much do you spend each month on online marketing?
What's your preferred language?
What's your business goal?
What type of business do you represent?
How big is your business?
▶ Do you use any of the following software? (asks about apps)
Rep note — Software app question: If a pro selects a CRM or software app during the survey, they will see an entry point on desktop only during onboarding (after the availability screen) where they can choose "Email me instructions" to receive setup steps, or skip it. For full detail, see the CRM in Onboarding (Great Integrations) KA.
▶ What the "Tell us more about your business." survey screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Rep note: Survey responses are for Thumbtack's internal use only and do not affect the pro's account, EMR status, or search visibility.
Business profile
Step 3 — Build a winning profile
Build a winning profile 
After the survey, the pro enters the profile-building phase of onboarding. An interstitial screen shows the two-phase flow:
Build a winning profile (active)
Add your preferences (grayed out — comes next)
▶ What the screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Business name 

The pro enters their business name and taps Next. 
If a pro is in the experiment, they will see the optional business website field. Refer to the Accelerated profile in onboarding (experiment) section above 
Business name fallback:
If a pro doesn't enter a business name, Thumbtack automatically creates one using their account name. The pro can update it at any time.(Note: Name field is locked if the pro has a verified business or has a verified license. They must submit the ID Help form).  
Their business name appears in search results, on their profile, and in messages to customers.
For more info, see the Account Information: Manage Account Settings and Status (Pro) KA and ID Help Guide (Pro) (Customer) KA.  
▶ What the "Stand out to customers."  screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]



Select your business (prebuilt profile match) 
Thumbtack searches for a matching prebuilt profile based on the business name entered. The pro sees a list of potential matches and either selects theirs or taps "My business isn't shown here" to proceed manually. See Prebuilt Profiles and Importing Reviews From Other Sites (Pro) KA for full detail. 
▶ What the "Select your business" screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ Prebuilt profile review rating (if a match exists)
After the main review step, if a prebuilt profile with a review rating was found, the pro is shown a second screen: "We found recent ratings for your business." They choose either "Add rating" to import the aggregate rating, or "Don't add" to skip it.
Rep note: Importing a rating instantly satisfies the "at least one review" EMR requirement (where applicable).  Once a rating is imported, it cannot be removed. If a pro skips this step during onboarding, they can still import their rating later by clicking "Import reviews from other sites" on their reviews page. For full detail on how imported ratings work and what's displayed on the profile, see the Prebuilt Profiles and Importing Reviews From Other Sites (Pro) KA.

[Image: rtaImage]

Set up your business profile 
The pro confirms or manually fills in (pre-filled if a prebuilt match was claimed):
Business name
Year founded
Number of employees
Business address (optional)
By tapping Next, the pro confirms the information is correct and that they are the business's authorized representative.
▶ What the "Set up your business profile" screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

For details on how the business address is used, see the Business details info section on the Profile (Pro) KA. 
Profile photo 
The pro uploads a profile photo or logo. In-product guidance notes that customers prefer pros with a clear profile photo, and example images from top pros are shown for reference.
Rep note:
Profile photos are shared across all of a pro's business profiles.
Photos should be square and 400x400 pixels for best quality. For photo tips and troubleshooting upload issues, see the Profile (Pro) KA.
Profile photos cannot have contact information in them. To learn what happens if a photo has contact information, see Profile review section above 
▶ What the profile photo screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]


Get reviews / import review ratings

The pro is shown options for requesting reviews from past customers. Options and behavior differ by platform.
▶ App (3 options):
Import from Google — launches the Google import flow; on completion, the pro is directed back to the review screen with the Google option shown as completed
Email past customers — opens the device's email app with pre-populated content
Text past customers — opens the device's text app with pre-populated content
Other sharing options — opens the device's share sheet
The screen auto-advances after the pro completes an action.

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ Web (3 options):
Import from Google — launches the Google import flow; on completion, the pro is directed back to the review screen with the Google option shown as completed
Email past customers — opens a modal where the pro enters past customers' email addresses and sends requests; on completion, the pro is directed back to the review screen with the email option shown as completed
Copy link — copies a shareable review request link to clipboard
The pro can also tap/click "Do it later" to skip and return to this from their setup checklist.
Rep note: For full detail on review types, importing from Google, and how reviews affect a pro's profile and EMR status, see the Reviews (Pro) KA.

▶ Prebuilt profile review rating (if a match exists)
After the main review step, if a prebuilt profile with a review rating was found, the pro is shown a second screen: "We found recent ratings for your business." They choose either "Add rating" to import the aggregate rating, or "Don't add" to skip it.
Rep note: Importing a rating instantly satisfies the "at least one review" EMR requirement (where applicable).  Once a rating is imported, it cannot be removed. If a pro skips this step during onboarding, they can still import their rating later by clicking "Import reviews from other sites" on their reviews page. For full detail on how imported ratings work and what's displayed on the profile, see the Prebuilt Profiles and Importing Reviews From Other Sites (Pro)  KA.

[Image: rtaImage]

Business description 
The pro writes a description of at least 40 characters explaining what makes their business stand out. Example introductions are shown in-product. When a pro clicks Next, our AI will strengthen their intro by rewriting it. The pro can either click Undo, Edit, or Use this version.
There are a few things pro cannot put in their business description. To learn what those are, see Profile review section above 
Rep note: Reps should not write the pro's introduction for them — they can offer tips but the pro must write it themselves. For coaching guidance, see the Profile (Pro) KA.

[Image: rtaImage]


Turn on notifications

For pros onboarding on the Thumbtack pro app: The pro is prompted to enable push notifications. The screen explains that pressing and holding notifications lets pros view job details and reply instantly, and that faster replies increase their chances of getting hired. The pro taps Turn on notifications to enable them or dismisses the screen to skip.
Enabling notifications is optional but recommended — pros who respond quickly to leads are more likely to get hired. If a pro asks about updating their notification settings later, they can do so from their account settings. Refer to the Notifications (Pro) KA to learn more about the different notifications a pro can receive. 
▶ What the "Add notifications and get hired more" screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]
Job preferences
Step 4 — Add preferences 
Add your preferences 
After building their profile, the pro moves into the targeting setup phase. An interstitial screen shows the updated flow:
Build a winning profile (completed — checkmark shown)
Add your preferences (active) "Tell us about your availability, ideal job types, and work areas so you show up in the right customer searches."
Job preferences intro screen "Control where, when, and how you work." Explains that leads will exactly match the pro's availability, work areas, and other preferences. The pro can tap "See an example lead" to preview what a matched lead looks like before continuing.
▶ What the intro screens for job preferences look like

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

Availability 
The pro sets their hours — either any open day or time, or specific business hours with a lead time setting. They'll auto-pay for jobs during these times when they match their preferences. 
▶ What the "Set your hours" screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Pros must have a minimum of 12 hours of total availability per week to appear in search results. 
Business hours are set at the profile level and apply to all service categories under that profile. 
For full detail on availability settings, calendar blocking, and how customer timelines affect matching, see the Availability: Business Hours, Calendar, and Hide a Business (Pro) KA.
Note: On desktop only, if the pro selected a CRM or software integration during the survey, they will see an additional screen after availability prompting them to connect that integration. The pro can choose "Email me instructions" to receive setup instructions, or skip it. Pros who skip during onboarding will see prompts later on their leads tab, messages tab, and calendar tab. For full detail, see the CRM in Onboarding (Great Integrations) KA.
Pick a service to set up first 

The pro selects which of their services to set up job preferences for first. During onboarding, they only set up one service category. They can set up additional services later.
▶ What the "Pick a service to set up first" screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Pricing (quote sheets)
The pro enters their base price per job type. Average prices are shown for reference. This step can be skipped.
▶ What the "How much do you charge for [service] jobs?

[Image: rtaImage]


Setting prices during onboarding is optional but strongly encouraged — pros who post prices rank better in search results and attract more qualified leads. Key things to know:
Thumbtack may pre-fill default prices to help new pros get started, but pros should enter their own rates since they know their business best
All prices are estimates and can be adjusted based on job details
Prices can be updated or hidden at any time from the Services tab
Pricing options vary by service category (base price, hourly rate, price range, add-ons, on-site evaluation fee, minimums for variable price categories)
For full detail on pricing types, what customers see in search results, and talking points, see the Pro Pricing: How Pros Price Their Services (Quote sheets) KA.
Job types 

The pro answers questions specific to their service category (e.g. grass lengths, property types, customer requirements) known as job types. These answers determine which jobs they auto-pay for. For full detail on how job type preferences work, see the Targeting: Job Types and Travel Preferences (Pro) KA.
▶ What the "Tell us more about your work" screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Travel area 

The pro sets their service areas, either by specific areas or by distance. They'll auto-pay for leads that match these areas. They can fine-tune this later. For full detail on how travel preferences work, see the Targeting: Job Types and Travel Preferences (Pro) KA.
If a pro sets their travel area by distance, their business address is the center of their travel radius.  For details on business address, see Account Information: Manage Account Settings and Status (Pro) KA.
▶ What the "Choose where you'll work" screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]


Weekly budget 

The weekly budget intro explains that the weekly budget is the maximum the pro will spend in a week. Thumbtack sends leads matching their preferences until the budget runs out. When the pro clicks Next, the pro will select from a recommended budget, unlimited budget, or sets a custom amount. 
▶ What the budget screens look like

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]


Rep note: New pros do not qualify for the unlimited budget discount offer. For full detail on budget options, see the Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro) KA. 
Payment 
The pro enters their card details. The screen explains:
They won't be charged right now
They only auto-pay when a lead exactly matches their preferences
The card is secured via Stripe
▶ What the "Add a card to pay for future leads." screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Adding a payment card is required to complete job preferences setup.
The card must be linked to a valid bank or credit card account and becomes the default payment method on the account.
For full detail on payment methods and billing, see the Charges on Thumbtack: Payment Methods and Billing (Pro) KA.
Background check (BGC) 

The pro submits their BGC using either their SSN or a no-SSN option. When the pro clicks Next, they will see a  page to provide details like their name and address. After submitting their check, the pro sees a  "Your background check is processing." The pro is told it usually takes 24 hours or less, but can occasionally take longer. They will receive an email once the status of their background check changes. 
The BGC is run through Checkr and is free for the pro. The pro can submit using their SSN or a government-issued ID (no SSN required)
Results typically take 5–7 business days; the pro can check status at applicant.checkr.com
Once submitted and all other EMR requirements are met, the pro can start getting leads even if the BGC is still processing. 
NOTE: Even after activation, a pro must have a "clear" BGC to remain in search results. If a pro fails their BGC, they are blocked from the platform. If a pro is blocked due to a BGC failure, Thumbtack automatically refunds any unused funds. The pro does not need to ask for this refund; it is handled by the system.
For full detail on BGC statuses and talking points, see the Background Checks (Pro) KA. 

[Image: rtaImage]

Step 7 —Onboarding complete  (three possible paths)
A pro’s journey during onboarding varies based on their EMR status and whether they complete all setup steps during the initial flow.
If the pro passes EMR during onboarding:

If a pro completes targeting setup during onboarding, already has a qualifying review, and has submitted their background check, they pass EMR. They go live immediately and automatically — no activation step required. 
They see a "You're now showing up in customer search results for [service]!" confirmation. This screen explains where leads show up (under Jobs), when they are charged(when customers contact them), and where to adjust their preferences (under Services). 
▶ What the screen looks lik

[Image: rtaImage]

If the pro completes onboarding but hasn't yet passed EMR 
If a pro gets to the gets to the of onboarding but hasn’t completed all EMR requirements, (e.g., targeting setup for 1 service, has submitted their background check, BUT does NOT have a qualifying review), they see a targeting confirmation screen: "Targeting is on — now you just need 1 review." They are then shown the finish setup banner with their remaining checklist items. 
▶ What the screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Move to Step 6 — Finish the setup checklist (EMR)  below.
If the pro closes out of onboarding before finishing 
If a pro exits without completing all requirements, when they access their Thumbtack account again, they will see a banner on their Jobs tab telling them they have [number] of setup tasks left before they can start getting leads with a Finish setup button. 
▶ What the "Finish setup" screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Move to Step 6 — Finish the setup checklist (EMR)  below.
Step 6 — Finish the setup checklist (EMR)
Once a pro exits onboarding, any incomplete requirements appear in a finish setup checklist. Pros can access this checklist by clicking Finish setup on their Jobs tab. At the top of the checklist, pros see: "You aren't showing in search results yet — finish X setup tasks to start getting leads."
▶ What the "Finish setup" screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Checklist items include: 
[Image: unchecked]Fill out your business profile
[Image: unchecked]Set your job preferences
[Image: unchecked]Set your budget
[Image: unchecked]Add one past customer review
[Image: unchecked]Get a background check
The items will appear with green checkmarks as each is completed. Pros can complete items in any order. The checklist updates in real time.
When all checklist items are complete, the pro's EMR status updates in Admin:
Is Complete → True
Completion Time → stamped with date and time
At this point the pro is eligible to appear in search results, assuming no profile hold or other block is present. From the checklist pros can click Activate profile to go live immediately. Move to Step 7 – Activate profile and go live below. 
Step 7 — Activate profile and go live
This step applies to pros who exited onboarding before passing EMR and completed their requirements via the finish setup checklist.
After passing EMR, the pro sees a pop-up: "Ready to start getting leads?"  This pop-up explains two things:
Their profile will automatically go live in 24 hours
They can go live immediately by clicking Activate profile
If the pro clicks "Activate profile" before 24 hours: They see a brief "Adding you to search results" screen, followed by a confirmation: "Congrats! You're now showing up in customer searches." 
If the pro takes no action: Their profile activates automatically after 24 hours. When they return to Thumbtack, a confirmation pop-up appears: "Congrats! You're now showing up in customer searches.

[Image: rtaImage]

Communications the pro receives:
12-hour reminder (if they haven't activated yet): Email and push notification with the subject line "Your profile will go live in 12 hours" and a CTA to activate immediately.
Confirmation email (when live): Subject line "You're now showing up in customer searches."
After going live — what new pros can expect
Welcome discount on first leads
New pros who sign up on or after May 11, 2026 automatically receive a 25% discount on their first 12 leads. Key things to know:
The discount does not apply to opportunities
It starts when the pro receives their first lead
The offer expires four weeks after the pro's signup date — if their first lead arrives after that window, the discount does not apply
Pros are notified about the discount via an in-app pop-up, a persistent banner in their Jobs tab, lead details, and email
For full detail on how the discount works, eligibility, and communications, see the Welcome Discount for New Pros KA.
Lead prices
Lead prices are not set during onboarding. Once onboarding is complete, the pro needs to visit the Lead Prices section on their Services page to set their price range. Pros are nudged to do this via a post-onboarding welcome email that directs them to the Lead Prices page.
The lead price is initially set at a system-generated default. These defaults are a starting point only. Pros should review and update their lead prices after onboarding. 
For full detail on how lead prices work, see the Lead Prices (Pro) KA.

Account creation
Step 1 — Pre-sign-up: category, zip, and services

Before creating an account, the pro tells Thumbtack what they do.
Landing screen 
The pro taps Sign up from the Thumbtack pro landing screen (thumbtack.com/pro) or Thumbtack app.

Trade selection

Create your account (email sign-up only) 

The pro enters their email, creates a password, and provides their phone number. Password requirements are shown in-product. They can opt in to text messages via two toggles:
Enable texts for account and job updates (checked by default)
Enable texts to help you succeed on Thumbtack (unchecked by default)
Tapping Sign up creates the account. On web and mobile web, Thumbtack sends a verification code after account creation, which the pro must enter to verify their phone number. On the app, there is no verification code step — the phone number is submitted but not verified at sign-up.

Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA summary:
This internal knowledge article (KA) provides Sales Reps with a reference guide to help pros with a variety of Trust and Safety-related issues. It includes information on contacting the Trust and Safety team, an overview of account holds and actions, and guidance for handling cases and reports.

This knowledge article provides an overview of multiple Trust and Safety processes. It will link to multiple related knowledge articles. Please visit the related knowledge article for full steps and process details. This article is merely a quick reference. 
Understanding the Trust and Safety teams 
Incident Operation:
This team primarily handles disputes and reports of discrimination. They often directly communicate with users via incidents and cases.
Critical Escalations:
Critical Escalations Case Managers handle serious safety concerns, highly sensitive parties, and high-risk cases that may impact the Thumbtack brand. This team is responsible for handling issues involving violence, threats, sexual misconduct, and other highly sensitive topics.
Proactive Operations:
Proactive Operations is a team of Specialists who primarily work to resolve potential issues before they impact pros and customers. This team is responsible for handling issues like scam requests, profile review, and inauthentic reviews
Risk Analytics:
Risk Analytics is a small team of analysts who are experts in detecting and dealing with issues such as scams, coordinated malicious accounts, and fraud trends.
Reps can refer to the internal Trust and Safety Department Overview (Rep) KA learn more about the Trust and Safety department. 
Understanding account holds
▶ Summary:
This section explains account holds, how to identify a hold, and what actions a pro can still take while on hold. 
Pros with an unresolved T&S issue and pros who haven't completed the full sign-up process may have a hold on their account. 
If the pro has an account hold, they can still:
Log in to their account. 
View previous messages they’ve sent. 
Access their account settings. 
Update their profile.
They’ll also see a banner at the top of their profile, letting them know they need to make updates. 
▶ Example 1:

[Image: rtaImage]

Image description: The image above shows the banner that appears when a user has an incident. It says, “Heads up: You’re not appearing in search results. A customer opened with you in the Thumbtack Solution Center. Find a resolution.”
▶ Example: 2

[Image: rtaImage]

Image description: The image above shows the banner that appears when a user has an incident. It says, “Heads up: you can’t accept leads until you resolve a payment error.”
Reps should refer to the internal Account Holds (Pro) KA for more information about account holds. 
Understanding account deletions 
▶ Summary:
This section explains the deletion logs in detail. What each log note means and when it’s used.
If a user's account is deleted, Sales reps should review the Admin deletion log to see if the issue can be resolved and the account reinstated, or if the removal is permanent (there are no appeals). 

Deletion log type
Deletion log description
Issue can be reviewed
Unresolved customer concern
Request to take a background check
Identity mismatch
Disputed card charges
Linked accounts (only some)
Account Hold; User has:…
Open dispute (TSC)
Past due balance
Resubmission
General issues or needs coaching
Issue will not be reconsidered. (no appeals)
Failed background check
Reports of sexual misconduct
Reported credit card fraud
Business decision | Will not reconsider
Discrimination 

Reps should refer to the internal Removed and banned users (Pro) (Customer) KA for additional information.

2. Process
▶ Summary:
This section explains the steps Sales reps would use to handle Urgent reports, how to contact T&S depending on the issue, transferring a case to T&S, non-discrimination, inappropriate behavior, ID help form submissions, linked accounts and business verification.
Steps: How to handle urgent reports (Sales)  
▶ Summary:
This section explains how Sales reps handle reports involving sexual misconduct, weapons, or confirmed legal or media action being taken against Thumbtack, or serious threats of violence towards themselves, Thumbtack locations, Thumbtack reps, etc. 
For urgent safety concerns (sexual misconduct, serious threats of violence, weapons, or confirmed legal/media action against Thumbtack), reps should: 
Immediately tag the Critical Escalations Team with @escalations in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channel.
Refer to the internal knowledge article: Identifying and Responding to Threats (Reps).
For threats of physical bodily harm (directed at self, another pro, customer, or rep, or harm to any Thumbtack library), Reps should: 
Follow the steps in the internal knowledge article: Identifying and Responding to Threats (Reps).

Reps can refer to the related internal KAs:  Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) and Removed or Banned Users (Pro) (Customer).
Steps: How to contact the Trust and Safety team 
▶ Summary:
This section details the T&S Slack channels and what they are used for. 
If you have questions for the Trust and Safety team, use the applicable Slack channels listed in the internal Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA.
NOTE: If Sales reps have any user concerns that involve violence, weapons, sexual misconduct, legal/media action against Thumbtack, or serious unprofessional behavior, they should tag Critical Escalations directly with @escalations in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channels.
NOTE: Sales reps should reach out to their manager with any questions they have. Managers will direct reps to the channel that’s better for the situation. See internal Slack and Common Support Channels (Rep) KA for additional channels commonly used. 
NOTE: If Sales reps have any concerns that are serious in nature, unprofessional or inappropriate, please tag escalations directly with @escalations in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channel. See related internal Identifying and Responding to Threats (Reps), Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer), and Removed or Banned Users (Pro) (Customer) KA. 
Steps: How to transfer a case to Trust and Safety (Sales)
▶ Summary:
This section explains the steps for a Sales rep to create a quick case and submit a case to T&S. 
If the Sales rep has a Trust and Safety concern and needs to send the case to T&S, they should create a Quick case and follow the steps in the internal Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA.
If the rep is unsure if a case should be created or sent to T&S, reach out in #ts-incident-ops-questions.
If you are unable to create a quick case, please reach out in #ts-incident-ops-questions to have the case/incident report created for you.
Steps: How to use the Id Help form
▶ Summary:
This section explains the ID help form and when a pro may need to help a pro use it.
For concerns requiring additional information or documentation, Sales reps should direct pros to the ID Help form for help. Examples of when to use the Id Help form include:
License concerns:
Verifying a license: When pros have an issue adding or verifying a license.
Adding an authorized license: When a business needs help adding a license they are authorized to use, but they aren’t the owner of. 
Account transfers: When a business has been purchased or the previous account owner is deceased.
Background check issues: 
BGC ID mismatch: Used when the pro is having issues with the BGC and needs to verify information to continue.
SSNless BGC submission: Used for pros who need to complete the BGC process but don’t have a SSN. 
Sales reps should refer to the internal ID Help Guide (Pro) (Customer)  KA for more information. 
Steps: How to handle requests for business verification (Sales)
▶ Summary:
This section explains how a Sales rep can handle requests for business verification.
When working with a business that would like to have Business Verification completed, Sales reps should review the verification requirements and submit their requests using the form found in the internal Business Verification (Verified Business) (Pro) KA
NOTE: Before submitting a request, Sales reps should be sure the business name is correct.
Steps: How to handle Discrimination towards users (Sales)
▶ Summary:
This section explains how Sales reps should handle reports from a user of discrimination against them.
If any user accuses a Sales rep of being discriminatory towards them for any reason during a phone call, chat, or email, the rep will need to complete the Report of Discrimination During User Interaction form. The report will be reviewed to ensure reps are following Thumbtack policies and procedures.
Steps: How to handle inappropriate content (Sales)
▶ Summary:
This section explains how sales reps handle situations involving inappropriate content.
If you are working with a pro or come across a pro with inappropriate content (profile picture, service profile description, or uploaded photos), follow these steps:
Do not reach out in Slack. 
Submit the admin to be reviewed by a T&S Case Manager through the Pro Review form.
Steps: How to handle linked accounts
▶ Summary:
This section explains how a sales rep should handle linked account issues and disputed links.
If the business has a linked account question or wants to see if it can be unlinked, Sales reps should submit a request through the Pro Review Survey.
See the internal Removed or Banned Users (Pro) (Customer) KA. 
Steps: How to handle unprofessional behavior from users (Sales)
▶ Summary:
This section explains how a sales rep should handle users showing unprofessional behavior. 
If a Sales rep is working with a user who is extremely unprofessional towards them (e.g., cursing at the rep, name-calling, threats, etc), they should follow these steps: 
Discuss the details with a manager.
Submit a report of the behavior using the Unprofessional Behavior Towards Agents Escalation Form.
If the user is being unprofessional (e.g., cursing/upset about the situation), but the behavior isn’t directed towards the rep, they should follow these steps: 
Reach out to a manager to review the details. They will determine if the user should be coached, flagged, and/or blocked from calling/texting/chatting with Thumbtack. This type of behavior may also lead to the removal of the user's account.
NOTE: To protect Sales reps from interactions outside of Thumbtack, they are encouraged to update their social media privacy settings. Reps should follow these instructions to ensure their social media presence is private.
See the related internal KAs: Identifying and Responding to Threats (Reps), Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer), and Removed or Banned Users (Pro) (Customer) for more information.
