1. Overview
This KA is frontline reps go-to resource for understanding and handling Trust and Safety (T&S) issues at Thumbtack. It’s designed to empower frontline reps to effectively handle Trust and Safety incidents, ensuring the security and integrity of the Thumbtack platform. 
In this KA, frontline reps will find essential information to help them:
Identify Trust and Safety Issues: The KA provides various scenarios that may require escalation to the T&S team, including account issues, behavior concerns, discrimination reports, Legal matters, Project disputes, Safety concerns and Thumbtack product or policy reports.
Determine When to Escalate: Reps will learn clear "Escalate to T&S if" and "Do NOT escalate if" criteria for each type of issue, enabling them to quickly determine the appropriate action.
Handle Sensitive Situations: The KA provides guidance on handling particularly sensitive issues, such as reports of harm, sexual contact/assault, credit card fraud, and mentions of lawsuits or legal proceedings.
Escalate Efficiently: Reps will learn the process for reporting new incidents, following up on existing T&S cases, and report suspicious activity.
Understand the Thumbtack Solution Center (TSC): Explain how the TSC works, its different statuses, and how to help customers and pros navigate it.
Use Helpful Talking Points: Talking point for sensitive conversations, such as those involving credit card fraud or disputes.
By using this KA, frontline reps are prepared to confidently identify, assess, and escalate Trust and Safety incidents.
NOTE: If a report should be handled by Support, T&S will send a case to the CS queue. The case will be noted with details about the Solution Center and a list of questions we asked the customer — so the Support rep can help from there. 
Trust and Safety Team: What they handle and how to reach them
Trust and Safety team 
Trust and Safety (T&S) is a specialized team dedicated to proactively identifying malicious behavior, enforcing the Thumbtack User Guidelines, and helping customers and pros to resolve disputes. Their goal is to protect both customers and pros by preventing things from going wrong, and working hard to make it right when they do. The team works on a very specific set of case types and situations. 
The types of issues T&S handles include:
Account issues: Account transfer, authorized license user, update verified business info and related issues.
Behavior concerns: Reports of illegal activity, harassment, threats, and other inappropriate conduct.
Investigative Report (also known as a Good Samaritan Report): A report of serious concerns about a user from someone who has not interacted with them on Thumbtack. See the full definition and steps below."
Discrimination reports: Instances of unfair treatment based on protected characteristics.
Legal matters: Legal inquiries, involvement of law enforcement, and media-related issues.
Project disputes: Disagreements between pros and customers regarding project completion, payment, or other project-related matters.
Safety concerns: Reports of users feeling threatened, unsafe, or in danger.
Thumbtack product or policy
If a user (customer, pro, or non-Thumbtack user) contacts a frontline rep to report an issue, the rep should look at the relevant section of this KA to determine whether the issue needs to be escalated to Trust & Safety.
Availability and Contacting T&S
The Trust and Safety team is usually available to answer questions via Slack and take cases from frontline reps Monday - Friday, 7 am to 6 pm Mountain Time. Responses to Slack inquiries and T&S cases on weekends or outside these times may be delayed. 

While T&S does not take calls directly from pros or customers, a T&S specialist assigned to an open case may be able to accept a live transfer if they are available during these operating hours.
Slack Channels for T&S Inquiries
If frontline reps have questions for the Trust and Safety team, use the applicable Slack channels below. Use the applicable Slack channels outlined in the internal Slack and Common Support Channels (Rep) KA. Reps should review available resources BEFORE reaching out in Slack.
For more information on T&S managed Slack channels and what they handle, reps can refer to the internal Trust and Safety Department Overview (Rep) KA .

2. When to escalate reported issues to Trust and Safety
Sometimes users (Thumbtack customers and pros or non-Thumbtack users) may contact Thumbtack with various issues they would like to report. Some issues need to be escalated to the Trust and Safety (T&S) team, while others don't. 
Frontline reps helping these users should refer to the following guidelines to determine if an issue needs to be escalated to the Trust & Safety team.
▶ Account issues
Account issues that require escalation to the Trust and Safety team include copyright or trademark concerns, such as using a business name or logo without permission or using trademarked content without permission, as well as ID Help issues, such as account transfer and authorized license user.
Frontline reps can resolve some account issues reported by users (customer, pro or non-Thumbtack user). Other issues will need to be escalated to the Trust and Safety team. To determine when an account issue requires escalation, reps should consult the following list.
If the user reports these issues, escalate to T&S if: 
Copyright or trademark concerns. Includes using business name/logo without permission, using trademarked content without permission, etc.
ID Help issues. Includes account transfer, authorized license user, updating business info (when the business is verified or has verified licenses), and updating or verifying personal information/identity.
ID Help Guide | Article # 000012565 
Non-US IP address.
Users disputing their link to another account
Removed or Banned Users (pro) (customer) | Article number 000007660 
Do NOT escalate to T&S if the user reports these issues:
Inauthentic reviews. 
Removed or Banned Users (pro) (customer) | Article number 000007660 
Pro avoided paying for leads or asked the customer to pay for their lead. 
Contact Avoidance (Pro)  | Article #000013627
Questions about background checks. 
Removed or Banned Users | Article number 000007660
▶ Behavior concerns
Behavior concern issues can include reports of criminal history, illegal activity, theft, harassment, stalking, drug or alcohol use, and credit card fraud.
Frontline reps can resolve some behavior concerns reported by users (customer, pro or non-Thumbtack user). Other issues will need to be escalated to the Trust and Safety team. To determine when a behavior concern requires escalation, reps should consult the following list.
If the user reports these issues, escalate to T&S if: 
User reports criminal history.
User reports illegal activity. Does NOT include illegal requests where there are no safety risks, such as “they’re asking me to paint a copyrighted character, which is illegal.”
Theft (reports of a user stealing property, reports of theft occurring between users). Includes when customers agreed to give their possession(s) to pros while they work on it, but now can’t retrieve the possession(s).
Harassment or unprofessional communication, when: Thumbtack might remove the user, Thumbtack needs to investigate further, or Thumbtack may need to communicate back-and-forth.
Stalking (following someone home, showing up uninvited with no business purpose).
User saw the presence, use, or dealing of illegal substances. Includes marijuana - T&S will look at local laws.
Alcohol use that could endanger users. Includes when driving was involved, or user became belligerent, etc.
Credit card fraud. Includes when someone reports that their credit card has been used on Thumbtack and they don’t recognize the charges.
Early fraud warning. Includes when Thumbtack puts a hold on a pro’s account and emailed them because they contacted their bank about a charge on the card on their account.
Do NOT escalate to T&S if the user reports these issues:
Minor issues that can be resolved by one contact / coaching. This includes behavior that wouldn’t result in account removal, isn’t a pattern for the user based on prior flags, etc. 
Mild harassment or unprofessional behavior. Includes late night contacts that aren’t sexual, posting negative reviews on other user’s online profiles, excessive contacts, swearing (when we’re not considering removing the user).
Non-illegal substance use (when it doesn’t endanger users). Includes when user is reporting that it was unprofessional for other user to drink on the job, but they weren’t endangered by it. Except for marijuana - T&S will look at local laws.
Illegal substances mentioned (“they smelled like pot,” “I think they were on something”), but didn’t specify they saw the presence, use, or dealing of illegal substances.
Illegal requests where there are no safety risks. Includes statements like “they’re asking me to paint a copyrighted character, which is illegal.”
Users didn’t follow safety standards (when it’s not causing physical harm to users). Includes not wearing harness on roof, not wearing protective eye gear, etc.
Only concern reported is that user may not be properly licensed.
Users used words indicative of an T&S issue, but didn’t describe a T&S issue (for vague reports, ask for more information to see if a T&S issue is actually involved).
“Stalking” or “stalker” mentioned, but didn’t describe someone physically following them or showing up uninvited with no business purpose.
“Thief,” “theft,” or “steal” mentioned, but didn't describe their property being stolen by a user.
Undefined threats like “they threatened me,” “threats were made,” or “I feel threatened.” Reps should gather more info on whether the threat is violent. If we can’t gather more info but you believe the threat is violent, send to T&S.
Non-violent threats like “I’ll report you to the BBB” or “if you don’t respond to me, I’ll cancel payment.” Includes when the only concern reported is that users will take legal action against each other.
Reps can refer to the internal Identifying and Responding to Threats (Reps) KA to learn more.
Investigative Reports | (Rep) Steps: How to handle reports of
Note: The term "Good Samaritan Report" is a common phrase used externally for the types of issues described below. Internally, Thumbtack refers to these as Investigative Reports. Please use this internal terminology when discussing these cases.
An Investigative Report is used when someone reports serious concerns about a pro or customer, and there is no record of interaction between them on Thumbtack (e.g., no quote, no hire, no message). If they have worked with each other through Thumbtack, it should be handled as a regular incident, not an investigative report
.
Reports can come from a Thumbtack user who found a pro but didn't hire them, or from a non-user who is concerned about a pro or customer on our site.
When to file an Investigative Report:
The person reporting must have specific reasons and, ideally, supporting evidence for their concern. A vague feeling is not enough to submit a report.
Examples of valid concerns:
Licensing concerns: The pro is advertising services they are not licensed to perform.
Criminal background: The user has knowledge of a criminal history that would violate our terms of service.
Quality concerns: The user can point to a poor BBB rating or a pattern of negative reviews on other websites.
Any other information that calls into question whether the pro or customer should be on our platform.
Steps for Handling an Investigative Report:
If a user shares one of the concerns above (or another serious concern), follow these steps:
Thank them for bringing their concerns to our attention.
▶ Talking point:
“Thank you for letting us know about this. We take reports like this very seriously.”
Gather information. Ask probing questions to get as much specific detail as possible.
Manage expectations. Inform them that we will review the information and take appropriate action.
▶ Talking point:
“I've documented the information you've shared. We will review this and take the appropriate action based on what we find to maintain the trust and safety of our marketplace.”
Handle requests for anonymity. If the user doesn't want us to contact the pro on their behalf, or they wish to remain anonymous:
▶ Talking point:
“We are happy to respect your wishes and consider your report anonymous. From here, we will make a note of your concerns and take appropriate action on our end, including reviewing their account to determine if this is someone we want doing business on our site moving forward."
Escalate the report to the Trust & Safety (T&S) team for investigation.
▶ Discrimination
Frontline reps should reference the internal Identifying and Responding to Threats (Reps) KA  for steps on how to navigate these reports, talking points and additional information. Non-Discrimination Policy – Thumbtack Help is also a helpful reference. 
To determine when these issues require escalation, frontline reps should consult the following list.
Escalate to T&S if: 
User stated they were discriminated against. Includes using words such as “racist,” “sexist,” “ableist,” “trans-phobic,” “anti-semitic,” etc.
User discriminated against or used discriminatory language towards a Thumbtack employee.
User expressed a preference towards a certain race, gender, minority group, age, etc. to employee or user.
User was exposed to discriminatory content. 
Thumbtack found discriminatory content that users weren’t exposed to.
Do NOT escalate if: 
User reported that they were discriminated against, but they’re not describing one of Thumbtack's protected characteristics. Includes when user feels pro discriminated against their job/house because it was too messy or the job was larger than expected.
▶ Legal, law enforcement, and media
Legal, law enforcement, or media concerns reported by users (customer, pro or non-Thumbtack user) can sometimes be resolved by frontline reps. If they are unable to help, they will escalate to the Trust and Safety team. Use the following list to determine when a legal issue needs to be escalated.
Escalate to T&S if: 
Official contacts:
From law enforcement or government entities.
From an attorney where they're representing a user and legal action against Thumbtack is mentioned.
About current legal action against Thumbtack.
Threats of legal action against Thumbtack when there’s a T&S issue or concern about user or work quality. Includes when there’s an open incident related to the person stating they’ll take legal action.
Media or news were involved and there’s a T&S issue or concern about user or work quality.
If you receive a subpoena
Mentions of lawsuits or legal processing. If a user reaches out about a project in a risky category and mentions a lawsuit or legal proceeding but does NOT want to submit a report through Thumbtack. Risky Categories include: 
Boudoir Photography
House cleaning
Massage Therapy
Personal Training
Pet Category
Private Yoga
Video Production
Do NOT escalate if: 
Law enforcement professional, government official, or attorney needs help using Thumbtack.
User states they’ll take legal action against Thumbtack but no T&S issue is involved.
NOTE: If the user threatens to sue, take legal action against or report Thumbtack, frontline reps should refer to the internal Sensitive Account Information Handling Guidelines (Pro) (Customer) (Rep) KA for guidelines and steps. This includes if a pro or customer threatens legal action (saying they’ll contact a lawyer, file a lawsuit, or register a complaint with the BBB).
▶ Project disputes between users
Project disputes reported by users (customer, pro or non-Thumbtack user) can sometimes be resolved by frontline reps. If they are unable to help, they will escalate to the Trust and Safety team. Use the following list to determine when a project dispute needs to be escalated.
Escalate to T&S if: 
User reached out/provided updates about an existing T&S incident.
Customer reports they want help with any of the following:
Payment was exchanged or the project was started, and: 
The pro didn’t show up (deposit no show).
The work is unsatisfactory.
The work isn’t complete.
Their property was damaged.
Payment wasn’t exchanged, but additional work or expenses are now necessary. Includes when they need to pay new pro to demolish concrete, city has fined them, etc.
Pro reports they want help because they weren’t paid or were only partially paid for work they completed.
A lien was placed or user stated a lien would be placed.
User reports that pro charged too much for the work during/following a natural disaster.
Do NOT escalate if: 
No money exchanged and no work completed.
Pro reported their customer has concerns with the project or damage.
Customer reported they didn’t pay the pro.
T&S concern was resolved before an incident was created.
Only concern is that a receipt wasn’t provided to the customer. 
Refer to the internal Projects (Customer) KA for steps.
Reps can refer to the internal Thumbtack Pay (In-Product Payments) KA to learn more about payments between a pro and customer on Thumbtack.
▶ Safety concerns
User reports of safety concerns, including physical harm, sexual harm, or misconduct, from customers, pros, or non-Thumbtack users, should be escalated by frontline reps to the Trust and Safety team.
Frontline reps should use the following list to determine when to escalate to the Trust and Safety team.
Escalate to T&S if:
Physical harm
Has occurred to human or animal.
Threats to/concerns about physical safety of self, others, or animals (includes when a request for harm is submitted). Includes threats of self-harm, statements about harming users or Thumbtack employees, reports of animal abuse, requests for mercenary services, etc.
Violent intimidation has been reported. Includes threats to damage property/undo work, language like “or else” or “I know where you live.”
User reported they’re uncomfortable or scared.
User reports of non-consensual physical touch (even if not sexual).
Sexual harm or misconduct
Sexual contact or sexual assault occurred.
Nudity or sexual content that involves a minor (do not investigate).
User was exposed to sexual or sexually suggestive content.
User reports that a pro is on sex offender registry.
User reported they’re concerned or uncomfortable about flirting, romantic advances/gestures, staring/leering, request details, photos/videos taken, or information other user requested from them (i.e. photos, address).
Do NOT escalate if: 
See “behavior concerns” section of this KA.
For additional information regarding threats between pros and customers, self-harm threats, bodily harm or sexual contact/assault reports, immediate danger processes, and emergency call routing processes, reps can refer to the Threats | Article #000007664.
▶ Thumbtack product or policy
Frontline reps will use the following list to determine when a Thumbtack product or policy concerns needs to be escalated.
Escalate to T&S if: 
Concerns about discrimination within Thumbtack product or policy. 
NOTE: These should NOT be sent as cases. Frontline reps should instead submit the Unprofessional Behavior Towards Agents Escalation Form.
Review disputes.
Reviews (Pro) | Article #000007721
Do NOT escalate if: 
Questions or assistance with Thumbtack product or policy, including:
Refund requests (with no related T&S concern).
Lead Refunds (Pro) | Article #000007615
Questions about the guarantee when there isn’t a project concern or other T&S issue.
 The Thumbtack Guarantee | Article #000007665
Refund gaming, unless a secondary safety concern is present. 
These are handled by the Advanced Service Team (AST) through the #service_global_help-and-escalations Slack workflow. See “Steps: How to handle suspected refund gaming (Rep)” in the internal Lead Refunds (Pro) KA for more information.

3. Other issues to escalate
Harm, sexual contact and assault
This section outlines content and service types related to harm, sexual contact, and assault that are strictly prohibited on the Thumbtack platform. 
Thumbtack doesn’t allow customers to post jobs with inappropriate language (sexual, profane language) or pros who provide inappropriate services, including:
Nudity or erotic photography (exceptions for female nipples in breastfeeding contexts and suggestive, non-explicit photography in boudoir services)Any references to massage services, including sexual massages or massage therapy
Nude or erotic photography (except for boudoir photography
Any services that explicitly sell sex
A job that includes coded messages or insinuations leaning towards sexual acts or prostitution (i.e., contains the words “escorts”, “discreet”, “personalized,” “personal service”, “showgirls”, “exotic”, “adult entertainment”, “go-go dancers”, “burlesque dancers”, ”nude models”)
Sexually inappropriate requests | (Rep) Steps: How to handle reports of
This section outlines the steps for frontline representatives to handle reports of sexually inappropriate requests made by either a pro or a customer on the platform. Frontline reps can refer to the  + "Harm, sexual contact and assault" + section above to understand what constitutes a sexually inappropriate request.
If a frontline rep receives a report with any inappropriate requests, please follow the instructions below:
Reps should deactivate the reported user’s account immediately using the drop-down "sexual content", but no added details in the notes field.
Don’t delete any of the content, this includes any/all photos. If it is super sensitive the agent can delete the request only, but not the content.
Don’t post a link to the request or admin in Slack - these are sensitive cases.
Don’t email or issue refunds to any users involved.
Don’t provide a refund or reach out any further to the reporting party or reported party. The Escalations team will take care of all further actions.
Do escalate the case to the Trust and Safety team. The Escalations team needs to be able to review all info and will take appropriate actions.
Slack the Critical Escalations team in #ts-incident-ops-questions using the @escalations tag and ask a Case Manager to DM you for an urgent issue. 
If the issue occurs outside of business hours (8am - 5pm MST), and you do not hear back from a Case Manager on Slack within 30 minutes:
Reach out to the on-call Case Manager using Genesys. (See Genesys Phone System KA to learn more).
Check the “Escalations Weekend Rotations” calendar to see who is available.
Lisa Ronquillo: 801-664-2467
Ashlee Atkinson: 801-450-2574
Edgar Herrera Castaneda: 562-314-5970
Erika Hager: (832) 546-6119
If you do not have access to Genesys, escalate the issue to your manager, and they will get in contact with Critical Escalations.
As a last resort, if you do not hear back from the on-call Case Manager within 30 minutes, you can reach out to Rebecca Fitzsimmons: 440-862-0477.
Once a Case Manager has agreed to take your urgent issue, they will handle the Salesforce record (by creating a quick case or transferring the current case to themselves).  
If this was reported to you by a user, thank them for bringing this to our attention and let them know we’ll be reviewing the concerns and follow up with them as soon as possible.
Bodily harm, threats to physical safety, or sexual contact or assault | (Rep) Steps: How to handle reports of
This section provides critical steps for frontline reps to follow when handling reports of bodily harm, threats to physical safety, or sexual contact or assault involving pros or customers on the platform, as defined in the 'Harm, sexual contact and assault' section.
If a frontline rep has any cases where a customer/pro reports bodily harm, threats to physical safety, or a sexual contact or assault, these are to be taken very seriously.
If a frontline rep receives a report related to these concerns, follow the steps below:
Make sure the person you’re in contact with is safe and that they are calling from a safe location.
Let them explain what happened. 
Do: Be very sensitive to the victim’s feelings and very careful in how you refer to their incident.
Do: The rep should focus on letting them know that Thumbtack takes this very seriously and are here to help them.
Do: Use empathetic statements like “I’m very sorry you’re going through this.”
Don’t: Reps should avoid probing for additional details unless there is something that Thumbtack needs to know.
Don’t: Even if the rep has been through something similar, don’t try to imply you can understand how they feel or what they are going through.
Take notes on the case and reach out to the Critical Escalations team by following the procedure outlined in the Identifying and Responding to Threats (Reps) KA.
Let the user know they'll be contacted by a Trust and Safety Case Manager as soon as possible.
Unless otherwise specified by leadership, remove the reported user from the site, using deletion reason: T&S Deletion - T&S Review.
(Rep) Steps: How to escalate the case for bodily harm, threats to physical safety, or sexual contact or assault)
After following the steps above, Frontline reps will escalate the case by following these steps: 
Reach out to Lisa Ronquillo or Ashlee Atkinson via Slack.
If they weren’t available to take the transfer immediately, gather (and note) the user's:
Name
Phone number
Admin links for the user's involved
Let the user know they'll be contacted by an T&S Case Manager as soon as possible.
Unless otherwise specified by leadership, remove the reported user from off of the site, using deletion reason: T&S Deletion - T&S Review.
 
NOTE: If a frontline rep has any concerns that are serious in nature, unprofessional or inappropriate, please tag Critical Escalations directly with @escalations in Slack. For weekends or after regular business hours, check the "T&S Escalations Weekend" calendar in Google Calendar to see who should be available.
Child endangerment or exploitation | (Rep) Steps: How to handle reports
This section provides crucial steps for frontline reps to follow when handling any reports or identifying any signs of child endangerment or exploitation involving pros or customers on the Thumbtack platform.
Potential signs of endangerment can be any of the following (in pictures or messaging):
Tattoos (or branding) related to money or ownership
Sending links to other websites to “see more about their services”
Language within messaging could include:
The life/game — term used by survivors, but also used to explain the culture
Daddy, the family, folks — “daddy” is a term used to explain perpetrator
Wifey/wife in law- women - victims refer to each other as wifey or wife in law
Stroll/Track — places trafficking is happening
Bottom — the person closest to the trafficker - often recruits
Stable — the whole group (trafficker/victims)
Quota — how much money the victim has to earn that night
Renegade — a girl choosing to go to another trafficker
Choosing up — choosing to leave “the stable” and go to another
Out of pocket — working outside the trafficker's umbrella
Square — people outside of the industry
Trick — another name for a buyer
NOTE: These words can seem harmless, depending on the context of the message.
Example: A pro in the house cleaning category may often use the word “square” to describe measurements of a room or a way they accept payment (the Square platform), but it would be uncommon for them to use the words “the game” or “wifey.”
If a frontline rep sees any of the signs mentioned above (or has any interactions with a user that's concerning), follow these steps:  
Slack the Critical Escalations team in  using the @escalations tag and ask a Case Manager to DM you for an urgent issue. 
If the issue occurs outside of business hours (8am - 5pm MST), and you do not hear back from a Case Manager on Slack within 30 minutes:
Reach out to the on-call Case Manager using Genesys. (See Genesys Phone System KA to learn more).
Check the “Escalations Weekend Rotations” calendar to see who is available.
Lisa Ronquillo: 801-664-2467
Ashlee Atkinson: 801-450-2574
Edgar Herrera Castaneda: 562-314-5970
Erika Hager: (832) 546-6119
If you do not have access to Genesys, escalate the issue to your manager, and they will get in contact with Critical Escalations.
As a last resort, if you do not hear back from the on-call Case Manager within 30 minutes, you can reach out to Rebecca Fitzsimmons: 440-862-0477.
Once a Case Manager has agreed to take your urgent issue, they will handle the Salesforce record (by creating a quick case or transferring the current case to themselves).
Credit card fraud | Steps: How to handle credit card fraud reports (Rep) 
 
This section outlines the process for frontline reps to handle reports of credit card fraud from cardholders or pros on the Thumbtack platform. Credit card fraud, in this context, refers to instances where a credit or debit card is used for unauthorized transactions on the Thumbtack platform, typically reported by the cardholder who does not recognize the charge, or by a pro whose account has been impacted by such activity.
If contacted by someone claiming their card is being used fraudulently, follow the steps below.
Before transferring the case to T&S — Payments, we must know if the caller has an account on Thumbtack or, if they don’t have an account, how they found out about Thumbtack. 
The caller doesn’t have an account — Ask how they found out about Thumbtack, and note this in the case with as much detail as possible.
The caller has an account — Review their account activity. 
Check for linked users or references to the pro they are reporting, like quotes with their name on them. If you find anything, paste the link to the messages in the case. 
Submit a request to the Advanced Service Team (so they can look up the last 4 digits of the card to find the account the card was used on) using the Atlassian Assist app in Slack:
Navigate to the #service_global_help-and-escalations Slack channel.
Use a keyword like “Help Stripe” or “Stripe” to trigger the Assist app workflow.
Select the "Global Help Stripe" request type and fill out the form with all necessary details.
Ask the caller if they know (or have any relationship) to the business who used the card.
Never give the individual the pro's full name (unless the pro's business name is their full name) to avoid compliance issues.
If they know the pro, note the relationship in the case.
If they don't know the pro, ask if they've recently received services related to the business categories associated with the pro's account and note their answer
Ask the card owner for the following information to transfer the case. If needed, they can email their credit card statement to us:
Their name and email address
The last four digits (and only the last four) of their card
Card expiration date
Their zip code associated with the card
The date of the charge(s)
The exact amount(s) that was charged on the card
Their phone number (to include for the T&S transfer)
The card type (Visa, Mastercard etc) 
Whether it's a debit or credit card
Let the card owner know you will be forwarding their report to the appropriate team, and they'll receive an update within 2 business days. ▶ Talking pointforward this information to our Trust and Safety team. They’ll conduct a thorough review of the charge(s) and reach out to you with updates as soon as they can. Please allow 1 to 2 business days for our team to investigate the issue.
Escalate the case to the Trust and Safety team in the “T&S — Payments” queue, selecting credit card or payment fraud as the transfer reason.

For recommended talking points when discussing credit card fraud with cardholders or pros, reps can refer to the Credit card fraud – cardholder and Credit card fraud – pro sections below.
4. Process: How to escalate a case to T&S
Reporting a new Trust and Safety incident to the T&S team  | (Rep) Steps: How to handle new incident reports
NOTE: Reps should keep the user (pro, customer, or non-Thumbtack user) on the phone/chat/text to gather all necessary information. 
When a user (customer, pro, or non-Thumbtack user) reports an issue, reps should review the “When to escalate reported issues to Trust and Safety” to see if it should be escalated to the Trust and Safety team. 
If one of the concerns above (or another serious concern) is shared, frontline reps should report the concern to Trust and Safety by following the steps below.
Acknowledge the user's concern. Thank the user (customer, pro, or non-Thumbtack user) for letting Thumbtack know.
Talking point: Thank you for bringing this to our attention, [Customer/Pro Name]. I understand this must be concerning.
Gather information using the T&S transfer flow in Salesforce. Gather as much information as you can about their concerns while following the T&S transfer flow.
Talking point: We have a team that handles concerns like this one. To get your report over to them, I’ll need to go through a few questions with you.
*The T&S flow will guide you through questions about the issue, including who’s reporting, the nature of the concern, and relevant PKID numbers from Admin (Customer PKID, Pro PKID).
Enter the T&S flow in Salesforce. 
▶ In the top left of the case, where it says “Current owner,” click “Next.”[Image: AD_4nXcmsxDeCqLDak9bWNMe_7hqo00Xtbxe2vI2kEyD1MYyIWT2nj9Ao11BkMBURAI8Nq1im20dO6-xbYHH8ZF85bi9q0T8RFwnkFxeR4km5Mj25J9GBppkcqETiyAQ5PrK8mT4ZmRuiQ]
▶ In the “Transfer To” choices, select “A Team (Queue).”[Image: AD_4nXdArON_ygIqH6x312xdhaCYhSem7ckU7JQ_d9G0TJE73p3r5G9mOQDcT_utq_BBDXxOqEiak0otuhoQRXY1NYuTP5DbfrUH6mpGkmISe_jcBh9gJz2dM8iTQtWvHD2yyiYlMLvNjg]
▶ In the “Select the Team” dropdown, select “Marketplace Integrity."[Image: AD_4nXdArON_ygIqH6x312xdhaCYhSem7ckU7JQ_d9G0TJE73p3r5G9mOQDcT_utq_BBDXxOqEiak0otuhoQRXY1NYuTP5DbfrUH6mpGkmISe_jcBh9gJz2dM8iTQtWvHD2yyiYlMLvNjg]
While filling out the flow, confirm that you have the correct PK IDs (if unsure, note that).
Reassure the user. Let them know Thumbtack take reports like this very seriously. We'll review the information they have shared with us and take appropriate action based on what we find.
Talking point: Thank you again for bringing this to our attention. We take reports like this very seriously. Our Trust and Safety team will review the information you have shared and and follow up with you within 2-3 business days. Look out for an email from our team."
*If they have questions about what Thumbtack will do, explain that "We have a variety of actions we can take in cases like this, and we'll take the appropriate action to best maintain the trust and safety of our marketplace."
Follow up with the customer using email template "Trust and Safety escalations: Customer had a bad experience."
Case Closure: The transfer flow will let you know if you will keep the case or not.
If you don't keep the case: Exit the tab without closing the case itself.
If you keep the case: Close the case as "T&S related concern > complaint about a pro."*Once the case is closed, you will see a note on the case that says "Dispute Request created."
Follow-up on existing incident | (Rep) Steps: How to handle contacts with open Trust and Safety case
Sometimes a pro or customer with an open T&S case may contact support. T&S does not take calls directly, but the agent assigned to the case may be able to take a live transfer if they’re available. 
Frontline reps will follow the steps below to check if a Trust and Safety specialist is available:
In Salesforce, look for who owns the most recent open T&S case.
If the owner is a queue name (i.e.,“T&S General”), no one currently owns the incident.
Leave notes on your case and/or transfer to T&S for follow-up.
Check if the T&S specialist is available by tagging them in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channel.
If the specialist is available, transfer the call.
If the specialist isn’t available (or it’s not a live transfer), leave notes on the case and let the customer know they can expect a follow-up from the Trust and Safety team within one to two business days.
If the customer/pro pushes for a call with their T&S agent or requests a supervisor, find the specialist who owns the incident on the T&S Team Info sheet and share their Call Scheduling link with the customer.
Let the user know that they can schedule a call with the T&S specialist using the provided Call Scheduling link.
Support reps should not use the Call Scheduling links to book meetings with T&S specialists on behalf of the customer/pro.
Transfer the case to T&S by following +  (Rep) Steps: How to handle new incident reports + starting on step 3. 
If you received a screen-pop to the T&S case instead of a new case, simply write notes and exit out of the tab.
When transferring the case, you'll be asked if this is a new or existing concern. Choose "existing."
Never transfer directly to a T&S agent (they don’t work out of the case view and may not see there is an update).
Note: If the customer has an urgent concern (i.e., they're in danger or are displaced with nowhere to go), follow the applicable steps in the Threats KA. Otherwise, reach out to the T&S team in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channel.
Note: If a customer mentions the Thumbtack Solution Center (TSC), you can help them with sign-up or troubleshooting using the internal Thumbtack Solution Center KA (Service and Support) doc.
Report suspicious activity
Reports are an important part of Thumbtack's trust and safety efforts and help Thumbtack keep track of behavior that isn’t allowed on the site. 
Pro steps: To report something, pros can go to messenger with the customer and click report. For full steps, pros will follow these steps in the How to report suspicious activity – Thumbtack Help 
Thumbtack will review the report within 24 hours and share an update with them on any next steps we took.
Frontline reps can refer to the Fake or Scammy Leads (Pro) KA for steps on how to help a pro concerned a lead is fake and for more info. 

How to handle pros and customers involved with Trust and Safety issues, asking for a manager (Reps)
Customers and pros involved with T&S-related concerns may ask to speak to a manager. Frontline reps should note that the Advanced Service team does not take escalations for Trust and Safety-related concerns, including:
Thumbtack Solution Center
Active disputes
Linked accounts
Background checks
Profile issues
Chargebacks
Removed reviews
For questions or talking points for working with escalated users, reps should submit a request to the Advanced Service Team using the Atlassian Assist app in Slack:
Navigate to the #service_global_help-and-escalations Slack channel.
Use a keyword like “Help others” or “Others” to trigger the Assist app workflow.
Select the "Global Help Others" request type and fill out the form with all necessary details.
5. The Thumbtack Solution Center (TSC)
This section provides an overview of the Thumbtack Solution Center (TSC) and guides frontline reps on how to help customers and pros with their disputes. For recommended talking points when navigating conversations related to the Thumbtack Solution Center, reps can refer to the Thumbtack Solution Center (TSC) - Customer and Thumbtack Solution Center (TSC) - Pro sections below. 
The Thumbtack Solution Center is where customers can work with a pro to find a solution. This is not a platform for pros to file complaints about their customers.
In the Thumbtack Solution Center, customers and pros can:
Action in TSC
What it means 
Suggest or counter a solution
Both customers and pros can suggest a solution to the problem. If either party thinks the solution is unreasonable, they can counter and provide another suggestion.
Accept a solution
If they’ve found a solution they can agree to, they should click Accept and work out the final details together.
Upload documentation
They can upload documentation to support their solution.
Get help
Customers and pros can click Get Help to find articles about how to use the Solution Center and more.

Note: Do not coach the pro on what they should do or say. We’re a neutral party in disputes and shouldn’t appear to be on one side or the other. Encourage them to use the TSC.
How the TSC works
If the T&S specialist working the customers incident determines they’re a good fit, they may have theire concerns put into the
Users can access their dispute in the Solution Center by going to their homepage.
If the pro doesn’t sign up, or stops responding,  the Trust and Safety Specialists working the incident may put the pro’s account on hold.. The Specialist will work with the pro to determine when the account hold will be lifted. This typically happens once the pro has started responding or reached an agreement with their customer. (they reached the deadline to agree on a solution).
If a frontline rep is contacted by a customer or pro trying to view their dispute, reps can guide them to https://help.thumbtack.com/solutioncenter.
Note:  If a customer mentions the Thumbtack Solution Center, reps can walk through sign up and troubleshooting using the internal: Thumbtack Solution Center KA (Service and Support) doc. Additionally, reps can use the internal doc to help pros sign up or troubleshoot. 
TSC homepage and dispute statuses
The Homepage for the Thumbtack Solution Center (TSC) is a quick reference for current and past disputes. Each dispute will display one of the statuses below. Frontline reps cannot access the TSC but can use the following information to help pros and customers. 
Users can click View Dispute to see the Thumbtack Solution Center. 
If the dispute has not yet been reviewed by Thumbtack, they can click View Details to see what’s been submitted.

Dispute status
What it means 
Under Review
Thumbtack is currently reviewing the dispute and no action is required by either party. 
The status usually changes in 2-3 business days.
Transferred
The Thumbtack Solution Center may not be a good fit for this dispute, so Thumbtack has transferred to a different process. 
Thumbtack will reach out within 2-3 business days.
In Progress
The dispute is in progress and action may be needed from either party.
They should click View Dispute to see more.
Agreement Made
Either the customer or pro clicked Accept within the Thumbtack Solution Center to make an agreement. 
More information can be found if they click View Dispute.
Closed
The dispute has been closed. This doesn’t always mean the concern has been resolved. 
Thumbtack usually emails before taking this step, so the customer and pro should check for emails from Thumbtack if they don’t know why the dispute was closed.
Steps: How to help customer or pro with dispute in TSC (Rep) 
If a customer or pro contacts Thumbtack about a dispute in the Solution Center, Frontline reps can help them by following these guidelines:
Help them find the introduction email from no-reply-tsc@thumbtack.com with the link to their dispute.
If they can’t find the email, guide them to their spam folder.
They can also find their dispute at help.thumbtack.com/solutioncenter
Tell them to log in to the Solution Center using their Thumbtack login information (they may need to reset the password if they never made one or don’t remember).
Tell them to confirm the details of their dispute.
Reps can refer to the internal Thumbtack Solution Center KA (Service and Support) doc for customer and pro steps to sign up for and troubleshoot the TSC.
Note: The Solution Center can’t be accessed through Thumbtack Help, only by the link in their email.
Steps: How to help pro or customer troubleshoot error in TSC (Rep) 
If the customer or pro sees an error screen when trying to log into the Thumbtack Solution Center, first ask what the error says. 
If the error says “Time ran out,” let them know a specialist will reach out to them soon. For anything else, help them with the following troubleshooting below:
Have them go to help.thumbtack.com/solutioncenter
If they don’t see the dispute there, they are probably logged into the wrong account.
Note: Links to the Thumbtack Solution Center will never work for Thumbtack agents. Trying to use the link yourself should not be part of troubleshooting.
Make sure they're using their Thumbtack login information. 
If they're using a different email address than the one on their account, they won't be able to log in.
Tell them to use a different browser or clear cache and cookies.
If possible, have them try a different device.
If none of these steps fix it – Take notes and send it to the T&S agent 
It may be an error on our end that we need to fix. Try to get screenshots from the user if possible, as this is essential to fixing any problems they see.
6. Talking points
Credit card fraud - Cardholder Reporting Unauthorized Charges
This section provides frontline reps with talking points to address concerns and questions from cardholders reporting unauthorized credit card charges on the Thumbtack platform, whether they have a Thumbtack account or not.
I have a charge from Thumbtack on my bank statement, but I’m not on Thumbtack?
I’d like to gather more information about the charge(s) so we can look into this. I’ll need the following information:
Your first and last name, email address, and phone number (so we can contact you with any updates in our investigation).
The last four digits of the card, the expiration date, and the zip code associated with your card (so we can locate the card in our system).
The date and exact amount of the charge(s) so we can locate the charge(s) in our system.
The card type (Visa, Mastercard, etc) and whether it is a debit or credit card 

I’ll forward this information to our Trust and Safety team to review. They’ll reach out with an update within 1 to 2 business days.
¿Tengo un cargo de Thumbtack en mi extracto bancario, pero no estoy en Thumbtack?
Me gustaría recopilar más información sobre los cargos para que lo podamos investigar. Necesitaré la siguiente información:
Su nombre y apellido, correo electrónico y número de teléfono (para que podamos contactarlo con cualquier actualización de nuestra investigación).
Los últimos cuatro números de su tarjeta, la fecha de vencimiento y el código postal asociado a su tarjeta (para que podamos localizar la tarjeta en nuestro sistema).

1. Overview
This internal knowledge article (KA) provides frontline reps with a quick reference guide to the Trust and Safety Department. 
It outlines the department's structure, functions, and the four key operations teams: 
Trust & Safety Incident Operations
Trust & Safety Critical Escalations
Trust and Safety Proactive Operations
Trust and Safety Risk Analytics
Processes for connecting with the Trust & Safety team via Slack channels and escalating cases
Understanding account deletion processes. 
List of internal and external resources related to Trust and Safety processes.
Reps should refer to the related knowledge articles linked in this KA for full processes and details.
Key points
Here are key points for Frontline Reps to remember when helping customers and pros with Trust and safety-related issues:
T&S has four main teams: Know which team handles what.
Incident ops (direct user contact, specific case types)
Critical Escalations (physical harm, sexual misconduct, legal issues)
Proactive ops (reviewing service profiles, user messages, linked accounts)
Risk Analytics (harm detection and automated filtering). 
Deletion log is your friend: For account deletions, always check the deletion log first to see if it's temporary/reinstatable or permanent/no appeal.
Permanent deletions are final: If a reason for deletion is listed as permanent (e.g., failed background check, sexual misconduct, discrimination), there are no appeals.
Allow time for BGCs: Remind pros that background check results typically take 5 - 7 business days.
Escalate serious concerns immediately: Use @escalations in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack Channel for issues involving sexual misconduct, violence, weapons, serious unprofessional conduct, or confirmed legal/media action against Thumbtack.
When in doubt, consult internal KAs: Don't guess! Refer to the detailed internal KAs for "Trust & Safety," "Removed or Banned Users," and "Background Checks" for escalation steps, specific issues, and more in-depth information.
The Advanced Service team is a resource: If you're unsure about the best channel or process, ask Advanced Service. Refer to the internal Requesting Help from the Advanced Service Team (Rep) KA.
Slack channels are key for quick help: 
#idhelp-questions: Used for all ID Help inquiries including account transfers, authorized license use, license submission, name changes, DOB changes, email changes, SSN-less BGC concerns, and account takeovers.
#background-check-questions: For anything related to background checks.
#ts-incident-ops-questions: For account status, holds, deletions, reinstatements, and general T&S concerns.
Understanding the Trust and Safety Department (Rep)
This section offers Frontline Reps a clear overview of the Trust and Safety Department's structure and functions, highlighting how each team contributes to safeguarding our platform.
The Trust and Safety Department consists of four operations teams dedicated to protecting both pros and customers, preventing issues, and resolving them effectively. 
Trust & Safety Incident Operations:
Primary Function: This team actively safeguards users by addressing and resolving issues as they arise. They also work proactively to prevent potential problems.
Specific Case Types: This team handles a specific set of issues requiring manual intervention and direct user contact through incidents and cases. This includes:
Project Disputes
Customer/Pro Payment Issues
Discrimination
Behavioral Concerns
Internal Resources: Frontline reps can find detailed information on escalating issues to this team in the internal  Trust & Safety incidents (pro) (customer) Knowledge Article (KA).
Trust & Safety Critical Escalations:

Primary Function: Critical Escalations is a team of case managers and specialists who primarily deal with issues escalated by other operations teams.
Specific Case Types: Case Managers handle serious safety concerns, highly sensitive parties, and high-risk cases that may impact the Thumbtack brand. This includes:
Physical violence and threats
Sexual Misconduct
Serious Harassment and Stalking
Sensitive Media or Legal Issues
Disputes with High Monetary Value
Internal Resources: Frontline reps can find detailed information on escalating issues to this team in the internal Identifying and Responding to Threats Knowledge Article (KA).
Trust and Safety Proactive Operations: 
Primary Function: This team of specialists primarily works to resolve potential issues before they impact pros and customers.
Specific Case Types: This team handles issues automatically routed through work tickets and queues, impacting user accounts, messages, images, reviews, and in-product reports/refunds. Their responsibilities also include:
Linked Accounts
Inaccurately Ghosted Accounts
Non-US IP reports
Fake reviews
Contact Avoidance
Scammy Users
Internal Resources: Frontline reps can find detailed information on these case types in the following knowledge articles: 
Removed or Banned Users (Pro) (Customers)
Contact Avoidance (Pro)
Account Holds (Customer) 
Fake or Scammy Leads (Pro) 
Trust and Safety Risk Analytics:
Primary Function: This small team of risk analysts are experts in proactively detecting and mitigating harmful behavior. Risk Analytics supports the Proactive Operations team by improving proactive harm detection and work ticket quality.
Internal Resources: Frontline reps can find steps on how to contact the Proactive team for help in the internal Removed or Banned Users (Pro) (Customers) KA, specifically by following the "Asking the Proactive Team for help" steps.
Understanding account deletions and how to handle them (Rep)

When a user's (pro or customer) account is deleted, Frontline reps should consult the deletion log to determine if the issue can be resolved and the account reinstated, or if the deletion is final with no appeal options. For steps on how to check a deletion log, reps can refer to the internal Removed or Banned Users (Pro) (Customers) KA. 
The following table outlines various reasons for account or user removal, categorized by whether the removal is temporary or permanent.



Removal Type
Action type
Reasons for Removal
Temporary
Account hold
Unresolved customer concern
Request to take Background Checks
Identity Mismatch ID Help Guide
Disputed card charges
Linked accounts (only some)
Account Hold, User has:
Open dispute (TSC)
Past due balance
Resubmission
General issues or needs coaching
Permanent (no appeals)
Deactivated and blocklisted
Failed Background Checks
Reports of sexual misconduct
Reported credit card fraud
Business decision | Will not reconsider
Discrimination

articles.fullText:
Trust and Safety (T&S) issues overview

Trust and Safety (T&S) issues overview
Index
T&S Vision and Mission
When T&S Should be consulted
What the T&S Support Ops team handles
Project disputes between users
Safety concerns
Discrimination
Behavior concerns
Account issues
Legal, law enforcement, and media
Thumbtack product and policy
What the T&S Proactive team handles
T&S Vision and Mission
T&S Vision
People trust us. For projects big or small, they know they can count on us.
T&S Mission
We protect both pros and customers. We work hard to keep things from going wrong and - in the rare event that anything happens - we work hard to make it right.
When T&S should be consulted
User safety.
Spam/scams.
Payment fraud.
Discrimination.
Thumbtack Guarantee.
User credentials.
Background checks.
Licensing.
T&S reporting flows.
In-product scam report/In-product refund request.
Concerning Reviews.
Help Center intake forms.
What T&S Support Ops handles
Issues that should be manually sent to the T&S Support Ops team. (This team has direct contact with users via incidents and cases).
T&S issues: quick view
Use the table below for quick summaries of what this team handles. Click the links for more information.
Project disputes

Project disputes between users who want our help.
Physical safety concerns
Physical harm is possible or has occurred.
Sexual safety concerns
Sexual harm is possible or has occurred, user reported or was exposed to sexual content.
Discrimination
 
User or employee was discriminated against, or discriminatory content was reported/found.
Behavior concerns
 
Behavior concerns that need further investigation, require back-and-forth communication, or may lead to account removal.
Account issues
 
Account issues related to verified accounts or licenses, copyright or trademark concerns, links to other accounts, or credentials.
Legal and law enforcement
 
Official contacts from law enforcement, government officials, and attorneys.
Media
 
Media or news involved in a concern about a user or their quality.
Project disputes between users
SEND TO T&S:
User reached out/provided updates about an existing T&S incident.
Customer reports they want help with any of the following:
Payment was exchanged or the project was started and: 
The pro didn’t show up (deposit no show).
The work is unsatisfactory.
The work isn’t complete.
Their property was damaged.
Payment wasn’t exchanged, but additional work or expenses are now necessary.
Includes when they need to pay new pro to demolish concrete, city has fined them, etc.
Pro reports they want help because they weren’t paid or were only partially paid for work they completed.
A lien was placed or user stated a lien would be placed.
User reports that pro charged too much for the work during/following a natural disaster.
DON’T SEND TO T&S:
No money exchanged and no work completed.
Pro reported their customer has concerns with the project or damage.
Customer reported they didn’t pay the pro.
T&S concern was resolved before an incident was created.
Only concern is that a receipt wasn’t provided to the customer.
Safety concerns
SEND TO T&S:
Physical harm
Has occurred to human or animal.
Threats to/concerns about physical safety of self, others, or animals (includes when a request for harm is submitted).
Includes threats of self-harm, statements about harming users or Thumbtack employees, reports of animal abuse, requests for mercenary services, etc.
Violent intimidation has been reported.
Includes threats to damage property/undo work, language like “or else” or “I know where you live.”
If vague (“they seemed violent,” “they were trying to scare me”), try to gather more information first.
User reported they’re uncomfortable or scared.
Gather more information and check if their concern is actually about something listed here as “don’t send to T&S.” If you can’t gather info, send to T&S.
User reports of non-consensual physical touch (even if not sexual).
Sexual harm or misconduct
Sexual contact or sexual assault occurred.
Nudity or sexual content that involves a minor (do not investigate).
User was exposed to sexual or sexually suggestive content.
User reports that a pro is on sex offender registry.
User reported they’re concerned or uncomfortable about flirting, romantic advances/gestures, staring/leering, request details, photos/videos taken, or information other user requested from them (i.e. photos, address).
Gather more information and check if their concern is actually about something listed here as “don’t send to T&S.” If you can’t gather info, send to T&S.
DON’T SEND TO T&S:
Sexual or suggestive content that users weren’t exposed to.
If a minor is involved, always send to T&S without further investigation. 
Discrimination
SEND TO T&S:
User stated they were discriminated against. 
Includes using words such as “racist,” “sexist,” “ableist,” “trans-phobic,” “anti-semitic,” etc.
User discriminated against or used discriminatory language towards Thumbtack employee.
User expressed a preference towards a certain race, gender, minority group, age, etc. to employee or user.
User was exposed to discriminatory content. 
We found discriminatory content that users weren’t exposed to.
DON’T SEND TO T&S:
N/A - send all discrimination concerns to T&S.
Behavior concerns
SEND TO T&S:
User reports criminal history.
User reports illegal activity.
Doesn’t include illegal requests where there are no safety risks such as “they’re asking me to paint a copyrighted character, which is illegal.”
Theft (reports of a user stealing property, reports of theft occurring between users).
Includes when customers agreed to give their possession(s) to pros while they work on it, but now can’t retrieve the possession(s).
Harassment or unprofessional communication, when:
We might remove the user.
We need to investigate further.
We may need to communicate back-and-forth.
Stalking (following someone home, showing up uninvited with no business purpose).
User saw the presence, use, or dealing of illegal substances.
Includes marijuana - T&S will look at local laws.
Alcohol use that could endanger users.
Includes when driving was involved, or user became belligerent, etc.
Credit card fraud.
Includes when someone reports that their credit card has been used on Thumbtack and they don’t recognize the charges.
Early fraud warning.
Includes when we put a hold on a pro’s account and emailed them because they contacted their bank about a charge on the card on their account.
DON’T SEND TO T&S:
Issues that we won’t remove the reported user for, and can be resolved by one contact/coaching.
Only concern reported is that user may not be properly licensed.
Mild harassment or unprofessional behavior.
Includes late night contacts that aren’t sexual, posting negative reviews on other user’s online profiles, excessive contacts, swearing (when we’re not considering removing the user).
Non-illegal substance use (when it doesn’t endanger users).
Includes when user is reporting that it was unprofessional for other user to drink on the job, but they weren’t endangered by it.
Except for marijuana - T&S will look at local laws.
Illegal requests where there are no safety risks.
Includes statements like “they’re asking me to paint a copyrighted character, which is illegal.”
Users didn’t follow safety standards (when it’s not causing physical harm to users).
Includes not wearing harness on roof, not wearing protective eye gear, etc.
Includes accusations of infecting others with illness.
Users used words indicative of an T&S issue, but didn’t describe a T&S issue (for vague reports, ask for more information to see if a T&S issue is actually involved).
“Stalking” or “stalker” mentioned, but:
Didn’t describe someone physically following them or showing up uninvited with no business purpose.
“Thief,” “theft,” or “steal” mentioned, but:
Didn't describe their property being stolen by a user.
Illegal substances mentioned (“they smelled like pot,” “I think they were on something”), but:
Didn’t specify they saw the presence, use, or dealing of illegal substances.
Undefined threats like “they threatened me,” “threats were made,” or “I feel threatened.”
Gather more info on whether the threat is violent.
If we can't gather more info, but you believe the threat is violent, send to T&S.
Non-violent threats like “I’ll report you to the BBB” or “if you don’t respond to me, I’ll cancel payment.”
Includes when the only concern reported is that users will take legal action against each other.
Account issues
SEND TO T&S:
Copyright or trademark concerns.
Includes using business name/logo without permission, using trademarked content without permission, etc.
ID Help issues:
Includes account transfer, authorized license user, updating business info (when the business is verified or has verified licenses), and updating or verifying personal information/identity.
Non-US IP address.
Users disputing their link to another account.
DON’T SEND TO T&S:
Inauthentic reviews.
Pro avoided paying for leads or asked the customer to pay for their lead.
Questions about background checks. 
Legal, law enforcement, and media
SEND TO T&S:
Official contacts:
From law enforcement or government entities.
From an attorney where they're representing a user and legal action against Thumbtack is mentioned.
About current legal action against Thumbtack.
Threats of legal action against Thumbtack when there’s a T&S issue or concern about user or work quality.
Includes when there’s an open incident related to the person stating they’ll take legal action.
Media or news were involved and there’s a T&S issue or concern about user or work quality.
DON’T SEND TO T&S:
Law enforcement professional needs help using Thumbtack.
Government official needs help using Thumbtack.
User states they’ll take legal action against Thumbtack but no T&S issue is involved.
Thumbtack product or policy
SEND TO T&S:
Concerns about discrimination within Thumbtack product or policy.
Submit here.
DON’T SEND TO T&S:
Questions or assistance with Thumbtack product or policy.
Includes Review disputes.
If related to an existing T&S incident, resolve the review question first then send the case to T&S for visibility.
Includes Refund requests (with no related T&S concern).
Includes questions about the guarantee when there isn’t a project concern or other T&S issue.
What Proactive T&S handles
Issues that are automatically sent to the T&S Proactive team. (This team impacts users’ accounts, messages, images, reviews, and in-product reports/refunds via work tickets and queues).
Queues worked by Proactive T&S:
Anomaly Detection 
Blocklist hits.
Purpose: Review accounts to determine if they’re linked to accounts they appear to match.
Actions: Delete and/or blocklist accounts.
BGC Mismatch Case Queue 
Chargebacks.
Purpose: Action pro accounts and respond when pros submit chargebacks.
Actions: Create and submit evidence packets, create receipts, action accounts.
Customer Chargebacks.
Purpose: Action customer accounts and respond when customers submit chargebacks.
Actions: Create and submit evidence packets, create receipts, action accounts.
Concerning reviews.
Purpose: Check for T&S issues within reviews.
Actions: Escalate issues that should go to the T&S Support Ops team.
Contact verification.
Purpose: Check potentially abusive requests before they’re sent to pros.
Actions: Ghost, delete, or syndicate requests, delete and blocklist accounts.
Data Disclosure Requests Case Queue 
Fake reviews.
Purpose: Check potentially inauthentic reviews for authenticity.
Actions: Remove reviews.
Fraud Investigation
ID Help Case Queue
Image Review.
Purpose: Review images uploaded by pros and photos in customer reviews for nudity, inappropriate/suggestive content, violence or gore, or being legally questionable.
Actions: Delete images, delete and blocklist accounts, delete reviews. 
Incentive and Referral Fraud 
In-product scam reports and in-product refunds.
Purpose: Check for T&S and Service and Support issues within In-product reports and refunds.
Actions: Escalate issues that should go to the T&S Support Ops team or the Service and Support team.
License verification.
Purpose: Verify the validity of licenses submitted by pros.
Actions: Approve or reject licenses.
Customer Message Review.
Purpose: Check potentially abusive customer messages before they’re sent to pros.
Actions: Ghost or delete and blocklist accounts, delete requests.
T&S Payments Case Queue
Pro Abuse Investigation.
Purpose: Review pro accounts for deceptive practices. 
Actions: Delete, and/or blocklist accounts.
Proactive MI Case Queue
Profile review.
Purpose: Screen specific sections of pro’s service profile for TOS violations when profile is created and when edits are made.
Actions: Add account hold, delete, and/or blocklist accounts.
Survey Triage 
T&S Categorization.
Purpose: Categorize all cases and dispute requests sent to the MTS team.
Actions: Create, categorize, and choose queue for incidents, transfer cases.
Terms of Service (TOS) violations
Within various queues, contacts, messaging, and profiles are reviewed for the following TOS violations:
Barter or free service
Competitor contact abuse
Competitor service
Contact avoidance
Discrimination
Harassment
Identity theft
Illegal activity
Inappropriate content/language
Minor user
Minor users
Mismatched category
Non-US service location
Not a service
Questionable names
Seeking employment or partnership
Severely unprofessional conduct
Sexual content
Spammy/scammy behavior
Test posts
Threats to physical safety
