Pro In Product Chat Experience
Pro Experience: Start An In Product Chat
Where to access the chat feature by chat type
Thumbtack's AI Assistant
Thumbtack's Automated Assistant
Process
(Rep) Steps: How to handle chat conversations from start to end
Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Overview
This internal KA is a guide for frontline reps to gain a better understanding of both the pro and customer experience with the chat feature. It also provides support on how to navigate the user journey, manage different scenarios, and when to transfer chats as needed.
For steps on how to use the chat window, transfer a chat, manage chat interactions, and other technical details within Genesys, frontline rep should refer to the internal Genesys | SMS & Chat KA.
Thumbtack offers chat support to help pros and customers get answers quickly. This support is powered by a few main resources: Thumbtack’s AI assistant, Thumbtack’s automated assistant, and our live support reps.
The chat feature is a convenient way for users (pros and customers) to get help with their questions or issues in real-time, without having to switch to a different communication channel, like email or phone.
Thumbtack’s AI assistant: 
Powered by Maven. Maven uses natural language processing to resolve common questions before transferring to a rep if needed.
External name:  When speaking with users, reps refer to this as Thumbtack’s AI assistant. 
Chat entry points: 
Thumbtack Help: Chats from the help center (https://help.thumbtack.com/)  (user must be logged in).
Pro Services Page: Web-only chats from the pro’s Services page (pro must be logged in).
User experience
The chatbot asks the user what kind of help they need. The AI can understand a wide range of common service questions. However, if a user’s issue is complex or requires personalized attention, the AI assistant will recognize these needs and transfer the interaction to Support. 
Reps can learn more about Thumbtack’s AI Assistant in the internal Thumbtack’s AI Assistant (Maven) (Rep)  KA. 

Thumbtack’s automated assistant 
Powered by Genesys. These interactions typically use standard routing or menu-based bots (predefined questions).
External name:  When speaking with users, reps refer to this as Thumbtack's automated assistant. 
Chat entry points: 
The Thumbtack landing page (thumbtack.com).
App-only chats from the pro’s Services page (pro must be logged in).
User experience: 
Home Category Pros: 
Home category pros are routed directly to the Sales queue - PRT SDR. 
If the pro is not eligible for a sales package, they are transferred to the "Service In-App Chat" queue.
Non-Home Category Pros: 
Non-home category pros will interact with a bot that can answer predefined questions and provide basic help..
If the bot cannot resolve the issue or the pro requests it, they will be able to request to chat with a live rep. These pros are routed to the Service In-App Support queue. 
Customers
The chatbot asks the customer what kind of help they need and will try to provide answers (to predefined questions) and suggest helpful articles.
If the bot cannot resolve the issue or the pro requests it, they will be able to request to chat with a live rep. They are routed to the Customer Chat Support queue. 
Key points
Here are some helpful points for support reps to keep in mind when working with chat interactions: 
Chat Support Hours: Available Monday - Friday, 6 am - 6 pm MT.
Access chat: Chat support is available to all pros and customers who are logged into their Thumbtack accounts.
Inbound Chat Limits (Pros/Customers):
Character limit: 4,089 characters
Image attachment limit: 10MB or smaller
Rep Chat Message Limit: 1,999 characters
User Blockage: If a user is blocked, the chat interaction will end abruptly with no message to the user.
Chat Termination (User Side):
Users cannot manually end an in-product  chat from their end.
If a user refreshes the page, it can disrupt the chat, and your responses may not be delivered. See troubleshooting red triangle error. 
Even if the user appears to be gone, you must still officially close the interaction in your system (e.g., Genesys).
Wrap-Up Codes:
Every chat interaction requires a wrap-up code for completion.
Using wrap-up codes prevents interactions from getting stuck, which can hinder your ability to receive new chats.
Click "End Messages" and select the appropriate wrap-up code from the available options.
Complete the interaction by clicking the "Done" button after selecting the wrap-up code.
Bot Interaction:
Thumbtack’s AI assistant on help.thumbtack.com will attempt to provide help using natural language processing.
The in-product chatbot primarily provides answers to predefined questions.
If the bot or AI assistant encounters an error or cannot understand the user's input, it will escalate the chat to a live rep.
Chat Transcript Interaction Logs, Queues, and Routing

Chat Routing and queues
Chats from home category pros will be automatically routed to the Sales queue. Support reps will handle non-home category chats in the "Service In-App Support" queue.
If a sales rep determines the pro is “non-sellable” or is unable to help the pro with their inquiry, they’ll transfer the chat to the “Service In-App Support” queue.  
If a support rep determines the conversation is sales-related, transfer the pro to the "PRT SDR" queue.
Chat queues 
Here is a list of chat queues to be aware of: 

Queue
Purpose
PRT SDR
Handling sales-related inquiries from Home category pros.
Service In-App Support
Handling support requests from Non-Home category pros. 
Customer Chat Support:
Handling support requests from customers.
Pro Chat Support
Handling support requests from pros.
▶ Handling Transferred Chats from Sales: Non-Sellable Home Pros
This section helps frontline reps understand why and how Home pros might be transferred to the "Service In-App Chat" queue from Sales, specifically when they are identified as "non-sellable."
Why a Support Rep May Receive These Transfers:
Home Pros Routed to Sales: Home category pros who initiate in-product  chats are initially routed to the Sales team.
Identifying Non-Sellable Pros: Sales reps are instructed to identify pros who are not eligible for sales packages ("non-sellable") and transfer them to the "Service In-App Chat" queue.
Definition of Non-Sellable: A "non-sellable" pro is an active pro who meets any of the following criteria:
Maxed their activation date
Already spent more than $200
Started accepting jobs without their knowledge
Been disabled or Blocklisted
Interaction transcript logs

Transcript interaction logs provide a record of conversations. An interaction log will display all conversations that occurred within 72 hours. If the user contacts us after 72 hours have passed, a new interaction log will be created.
 Interaction logs are saved at the task level (case or lead). To access transcripts: 
Salesforce: To access the interaction log in Genesys from Salesforce, navigate to the associated call task record, find it under 'Activity History,' and click the Interaction URL under 'Contact Center Information.'
Genesys: Alternatively, access the log via the Genesys web browser by navigating to Genesys in Okta, clicking 'Performance,' selecting 'Workspace,' then the interaction row and the 'Transcript' tab. 
Note that permissions for interaction logs are still being worked on, so you may encounter an error message.
For additional details, reps can reference the internal Genesys | SMS & Chat KA. 
Troubleshooting Red Triangle error
▶ Red Triangle Error While Sending Messages
This error usually means that the customer or pro has closed their chat window or browser, ending the session and making it impossible to deliver messages. If you've tried sending a message multiple times unsuccessfully, close the conversation.

[Image: AD_4nXfb65Qee06GqVfkDtpjUP6KwJRyqKRtpKvJQXnR4Ox-kKCgi1Sxm8L__F2ryyfiolcwn4FuAj2SBzJUiq-aKqcCx4V2me-3JH2DP0xfYW6OdtQjSlFCShKlDMODFD_SMJaDR8OxcQ]

▶ Red Triangle Error While Receiving Messages

Hover over the alert to view the error. If it says "one or more unsupported media attachments have been removed," the attachment was too large. Ask the user what they were trying to send and let them know that it didn't come through.

[Image: AD_4nXcrpU1lSknbXjjrR-Tok-Au7LivDagfGxDUNb7QgBQHAnohFxxpUk91-YBy0s54LCD5V2DHH1D6BUFRDEDrRtUx5ZFP6pBFicR58N2Or4qq3wTOkPnJRsUZKyN-NiQLMYD1tbI6Cg]

Example Talking Point:
"I noticed that your last message came through as blank. Can you please let me know what you were trying to send? It's possible that there was a character or size limit that caused the issue."
2. Pro in-product chat experience 
This section outlines the chat experience for both Thumbtack pros and customers.
Pro Experience: Start An In-Product Chat
Pros can start an in product chat from the following entries: 
Thumbtack land page: Pros can initiate a chat with Thumbtack's automated assistant from the landing page at https://www.thumbtack.com/pro. A pro will find a blue bubble with a black chat icon in the lower right corner of the page. Clicking this icon opens the chat window.
Thumbtack app: Pros can initiate an in-app chat from the Thumbtack pro app's Services page by clicking the blue circle icon containing a chat bubble. 
When a pro initiates a chat from these entry points, the chat window's automated assistant greets the pro with: "👋 I'm Thumbtack's automated assistant. Are you a pro who's new to Thumbtack? We’re here to answer your questions and help you get started. First, select which type of services you provide."
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

The chat experience the pro receives is based on their selection. 
Home Category Pros: 
Home category pros are routed directly to the Sales queue - PRT SDR. 
If the pro is not eligible for a sales package, they are transferred to the "Service In-App Chat" queue.
Non-Home Category Pros: 
Non-home category pros will interact with a bot that can answer predefined questions and provide basic help.
If the bot cannot resolve the issue or the pro requests it, they will be able to request to chat with a live rep. These pros are routed to the Service In-App Support queue. 
▶ Walkthrough of pro using in product chat
Initiate Chat: The pro opens the in-app chat feature.
▶ Screenshot of chat
[Image: AD_4nXc73bTAREdMAbbbGBlzcNLXEJGQRFdUP_uGOfZzhjBmYlx-1ORJv8dypgliIcyKehUkowVw2cS613JqbCy33Jrokq7cKEONRBINziej_Oi4cdMNMsMiKXK2kAAEANMq-fJrEmKS]
Category Selection: The pro selects the category of their service.
Bot Interaction:
For home categories, the pro is routed to a Sales rep (SDR). The Sales rep will transfer to Service In-App Support for non-prepaid package concerns.
For non-home categories, the pro interacts with a bot that provides predefined questions and answers.
If the user fails to interact with the bot, Thumbtack sends them a nudge. If they do not respond, we disconnect the chat 3 minutes later if there is no activity for three minutes.
Support Rep Request: If needed, the pro can request to chat with a live Support rep.

Live Support from Rep: Once connected, the pro receives real-time support from a live rep.
Where to access the chat feature by chat type 
Thumbtack’s Automated Assistant 
Thumbtack’s automated assistant is powered by Genesys. These interactions typically use standard routing or menu-based bots (predefined questions). Entry points include: 
The Thumbtack landing page (thumbtack.com).
App-only chats from the pro’s Services page (pro must be logged in).
▶ Web chat from the pro landing page
 Pros can initiate a chat with Thumbtack's automated assistant from the landing page at https://www.thumbtack.com/pro. A pro will find a blue bubble with a black chat icon in the lower right corner of the page. Clicking this icon opens the chat window.
Automated Assistant Greeting: The automated assistant greets the user with: "👋 I'm Thumbtack's automated assistant. Are you a pro who's new to Thumbtack? We’re here to answer your questions and help you get started. First, select which type of services you provide:”
Chat Options and Fields: Below the greeting, the pro can select their service category (e.g., Home, Events, Wellness) or choose "End chat." They can also type their questions into the "type your message her" field at the bottom. The chat window also includes a paperclip icon (lower left) for attachments and a gray send arrow (lower right) to submit the message.

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

▶ Services page from the app
▶ Pros can initiate an in-app chat from the Thumbtack pro app's Services page by clicking the blue circle icon containing a chat bubble (Image 1 below).

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ Clicking this icon opens a separate webpage with a "Welcome, We're here to help. Start a conversation" message, a "[Message us]" button, and a "What are you looking for?" section with a search bar. This action effectively opens the chat window.

[Image: rtaImage]

Automated Assistant Greeting: The chat window's automated assistant greets the pro with: "👋 I'm Thumbtack's automated assistant. Are you a pro who's new to Thumbtack? We’re here to answer your questions and help you get started. First, select which type of services you provide:"
Chat Options and Fields: Below the greeting, the pro can:
Select their service category (e.g., Home, Events, Wellness) or choose "End chat." They can also type their questions in the "type your message here" field at the bottom. The chat window includes a paperclip icon (lower left) for attachments and a gray send arrow (lower right) to submit the message.
▶ Clicking the search bar under "What are you looking for?" opens a page with categories that link to articles in the Help Center.

[Image: rtaImage]


Thumbtack’s AI Assistant 
Thumbtack’s AI assistant is powered by Maven.  Maven uses natural language processing to resolve common questions before transferring to a rep if needed. Entry points include: 
Thumbtack Help: Chats from the help center (https://help.thumbtack.com/)  (user must be logged in).
Pro Services Page: Web-only chats from the pro’s Services page (pro must be logged in).
▶ Web chat from the Thumbtack Help page
Users can access Thumbtack's chat support via the blue "Get help" icon located in the lower right corner of the Thumbtack Help page. Users must be logged in to access this chat. 
Clicking this icon opens a chat window where Thumbtack's AI assistant greets you with: "👋 I’m Thumbtack’s AI assistant. How can I help you today?" Users can type their questions into the "ask a question…" field at the bottom. A paperclip icon is available next to the blue send arrow for attaching files.

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

3. Process
(Rep) Steps: How to handle chat conversations from start to end
▶ 1. Chat Arrival and Initial Assessment
When a support rep receives a new chat in Genesys, it is important to assess the user type and route the chat appropriately to ensure they receive the correct support and avoid delays. Follow these steps to identify and route the chat accurately.
1.1 Chat Notification: A new chat interaction will trigger a notification within Genesys.
1.2 Case Creation: Salesforce automatically creates a new case for each incoming chat.
If the user is logged in, their account details should populate the case.
If the user is not logged in or no contact information is found, the case will appear with a blank contact field.
1.3 Category Identification: Immediately identify the user type:
1.3.1 Pro in Home Category:
If the chat has not been automatically routed to the "PRT SDR" (Sales) queue, transfer the chat to that queue.
Inform the pro why they are being transferred. 
Example: "Since you are a home category pro, I'm transferring you to our Sales team who can best help you."
1.3.2 Pro in Non-Home Category:
If the chat is from a non-home category pro, the chat should be routed to the "Service In-App Support" queue.
Proceed with helping the pro.
1.3.3 Customer:
Customer chats should be routed to the "Customer Chat Support" queue. If a Pro Support rep receives a customer chat, they should help the customer directly rather than transfer the chat.
▶ 2. Chat Initiation and Greeting
Once the chat is routed and identified, a prompt and professional greeting is essential to establish a positive connection with the user and set the stage for a helpful interaction. Support reps will follow these steps to initiate the chat with a proper greeting.
2.1 Initial Messages: The chat will begin with two messages from the user:
Chats powered by Genesys: The chat will begin with two messages from the user: 
Message 1: Includes the user's initial question or concern and their account information (if available).
Message 2: Contains only the user's initial question or concern.
Chats powered by Maven: 
Thumbtack AI assistant transferred interactions will display a summary followed by the transcript history. Review the AI Assistant summary to understand the user's request and check for any information already provided.
2.2. Review the interaction:
Reps must view the chat history to understand the user's request and check for any information already provided. Reminder: Logs retain history for 72 hours. 
When reviewing the log from Maven transfers, users are labeled as “Visitor” and “Maven bot” is the AI assistant. 
Do not ask for information already provided to Maven. This results in a QA markdown.
2.3 Greeting and Introduction: Start with a professional and friendly greeting:
Example 1: "Hi, I'm [Your Name] with Thumbtack Support. How can I help you today?"
Example 2: "Hey there, this is [Your Name]. I'm here to help you with your Thumbtack inquiry."
▶ 3. User verification
To ensure security and provide accurate help, support reps will verify the user's identity. Follow these guidelines to effectively verify the user.
3.1. Check the Verification Status. Look for “# VERIFICATION STATUS” in the interaction window (This only applies to chats from Thumbtack’s AI Assistant (powered by Maven).
If the chat indicates VERIFIED, ask the user for their name to ensure it matches the account name. If it’s a mismatch, follow the full verification steps. 
If the chat indicates UNVERIFIED or is blank, verify the full verification steps.
Note: Mandatory steps for full verification are on the internal Verify Account Information (Pro) (Customer) KA.
To learn more about Maven, see the internal KA Thumbtack’s AI Assistant (Maven) (Rep) KA. 
▶ 4. Addressing user inactivity
Maintaining engagement and addressing user inactivity is important to provide timely support and prevent users from feeling ignored. Support reps will follow these steps to manage user inactivity and ensure a positive chat experience.
4.1 Monitoring: Keep an eye on the chat for user inactivity.
4.2 First Inactivity Message (after 3 minutes): If the user does not respond for three minutes, send a courtesy message:
4.2.1 If the user's concern is unknown:
Example: ""I noticed you might be busy. Feel free to check out our Help Center at [link] or reach out again when you're ready."
Example 2: ""No rush at all. I'll be here if you have any more questions."
Example 3: ""[User's Name], are we still connected?"
4.2.2 If the user's concern is known:
Example: "It seems like you might be away for a moment. I'll remain available. In the meantime, you can find more information about [topic] here: [link]."
4.3 Second Inactivity Handling (after 2 more minutes): If there is still no response after an additional two minutes, proceed with the chat closing procedure (see step 5.3).
▶ 5. Chat resolution and closing
Effectively resolving the user's issue and properly closing the chat is crucial for successful interaction and accurate record-keeping. Support reps follow these steps to ensure the issue is fully addressed and the interaction is correctly documented and completed.
5.1 Issue Resolution: Once the user's issue is resolved, confirm with them.
5.2 Active User Closing: If the user is still active and the issue is resolved:
Example 1: "Thanks for reaching out today! Have a great day!"
Example 2: "It was a pleasure assisting you. Have a wonderful night!"
Example 3: "Have we addressed all of your questions or is there anything else I can help you with?"
5.3 User Leaves the Conversation:
5.3.1 If the issue was resolved:
End the chat in Genesys.
Send a follow-up email summarizing the interaction.
5.3.2 If the issue was unresolved:
Before closing the interaction, provide the pro or customer with a resolution or any additional information. 
End the chat in Genesys. 
5.4 Chat Termination (User Side): 
Users cannot manually end an in-product chat from their end.
If a user refreshes the page, it can disrupt the chat, and your responses may not be delivered. See Troubleshooting Red Triangle error section.
Even if the user appears to be gone, you must still officially close the interaction in Genesys.
5.5 Wrap-Up Codes and Interaction Completion:
Every chat interaction requires a wrap-up code for completion.
Using wrap-up codes prevents interactions from getting stuck, which can hinder your ability to receive new chats.
To apply a wrap-up code:
Click "End Messages".
Select the appropriate wrap-up code from the available options.
Complete the interaction by clicking the "Done" button after selecting the wrap-up code.
▶ 6. Case notes and closure
Accurate case documentation is essential for maintaining records, tracking trends, and ensuring a seamless handover if further help is needed. Support reps must follow these steps to document the interaction properly and close the case effectively.
6.1 Detailed Notes: While auto summaries should capture interaction details, reps can add any internal Thumbtack notes as needed. 
6.2 Case Categorization: Categorize the case by choosing one but no more than two themes that accurately reflect the main reason for the interaction.
6.3 Case Closure: Close the case in Salesforce.

1. OVERVIEW
▶ 🤖 Background notes
[AI Context]: (KA Summary) This internal knowledge article provides Frontline Reps with information on the features and benefits of the Thumbtack Pro app, focusing on its use for managing leads and messages.

The Thumbtack Pro app gives pros access to their leads and messages from anywhere. 
Customers appreciate prompt responses, and this app helps pros achieve that. If pros cannot be at their computers, the app ensures they are still alerted to new leads and messages through push notifications, allowing for immediate responses.
Note: As of November 13, Thumbtack no longer supports Android 8.1 and lower versions in the Android Apps. Thumbtack only provides support for devices running Android 9.0 or higher. Any users currently using Android 8.1 or lower will still be able to use the Thumbtack app and reinstall it, but users won't be able to upgrade to any of Thumbtack’s newer releases of the Thumbtack app. 
Key Points
▶ 🤖 Background notes
[AI Context]: This section provides Frontline Reps with a bulleted list of key points to remember when assisting pros with the Thumbtack Pro app, including topics like app access, push notifications, and response speed, aimed at ensuring customer satisfaction.

Here are key points for Frontline Reps to remember when helping pros with the Thumbtack Pro app:
Pros can access leads and messages anywhere they are.
Push notifications alert pros to new customer inquiries.
Pros can respond directly from their mobile devices.
Responding quickly is crucial for customer satisfaction.
Prompt to download the Thumbtack Pro app (on mobile web for home pros)
▶ 🤖 Background notes
[AI Context]: This section explains for Frontline Reps the different prompts pros receive when signing up for Thumbtack on the mobile web, specifically detailing the "hard" gating experience for pros in home service categories, and how it differs from pros in non-home categories.

Pros who sign up for Thumbtack on the mobile web in home categories are prompted to download the app (commonly referred to as “hard” gating pros). Pros in home categories can get around the hard gate by leaving the page (close browser, hit back), then logging back in.  

Pros in non-home categories are given the option to download the app but can skip this step. 
The following table shows the differences in the sign up process for home pros signing up on the mobile web versus non-home pros sign up process on the mobile web:

This is the sign-up process that new pros in home service categories experience on the Thumbtack mobile web:
Mobile web pros in home categories will start creating their account and completing phone verification. 
From there, the pro will see the push to download the app and be directed to the app store. Once installed, pros will continue the onboarding flow.

2. Process
▶ 🤖 Background notes
[AI Context]: This section details the process for downloading and updating the Thumbtack Pro app on both Apple (iOS) and Google (Android) platforms, as well as how to find the app version and provide app reviews. It provides step-by-step instructions for Frontline Reps to guide pros through these processes, ensuring pros can access and use the app effectively. This section also includes specific information regarding compatibility with different Android versions.

(Rep) Steps: How to download the iOS Thumbtack app from Apple’s app store
▶ 🤖 Background notes
[AI Context]: This section outlines step-by-step instructions for Frontline Reps to assist pros in downloading the Thumbtack Pro app from the Apple App Store, including a direct download link and guidance on app identification and push notification settings.
Frontline reps can send the pro the following link to download the Thumbtack Pro app: https://thumbtackpro.app.link/bv5vQuCQ8Z

Or Frontline reps can walk the pro through the following steps to help the pro download the iOS Thumbtack Pro app from Apple’s App store: 
Go to the App store  and search for "Thumbtack." 
Two Thumbtack app options should appear: 
Thumbtack pros should install the "Thumbtack for Professionals" app with the black logo.     
When the app finishes downloading, pros can set their push notification settings, and begin using Thumbtack.​​​​

For additional information on how to download the Thumbtack Pro app, see the external How to download our pro app Help article.
(Rep) Steps: How to download the Android app from Google Play 
▶ 🤖 Background notes
[AI Context]: This section details how Frontline Reps can guide pros to download the Thumbtack Pro app from the Google Play Store, including a direct download link and instructions for identification and push notification settings, with a specific note regarding supported Android versions.

Frontline reps can send the following link to pros so they can download the Thumbtack Pro app: https://thumbtackpro.app.link/bv5vQuCQ8Z
Or Frontline reps can walk the pro through the following steps to download the Android Thumbtack Pro app in the Google Play store:
Go to the Google Play store and search for "Thumbtack." 
Two Thumbtack app options should appear: 
Thumbtack pros should install the "Thumbtack for Professionals" app with the black logo.
After clicking Install, the Thumbtack app will start to download.
When the app finishes downloading, pros can set their push notification settings, and begin using Thumbtack.
For additional information on how to download the Thumbtack Pro app, see the external How to download our pro app Help article.

NOTE: The Android version on the pro's device needs to be 9.0 (or newer) to download the Thumbtack app. If it's older than 8.1, the pro will need to update their device to a newer software version.
Steps: How to turn on auto-updates for iOS apps
▶ 🤖 Background notes
[AI Context]: This section provides step-by-step instructions for pros on how to turn on automatic app updates for the Thumbtack Pro app on iOS devices.
Pros can turn on auto-updates for their Thumbtack Pro app on iOS by following these steps:
Open the Settings app.
Tap App Store.
Toggle the "App Updates" switch on. 
(Pro) Steps: How to turn on auto-updates for Android apps
▶ 🤖 Background notes
[AI Context]: This section provides step-by-step instructions for pros on how to turn on automatic app updates for the Thumbtack Pro app on Android devices via the Google Play Store settings.

Pros can turn on auto-updates for their Thumbtack Pro app on Android by following these steps:
Open the Google Play Store app.
Tap on the profile icon (top right corner).
Tap Settings.
Tap Network preferences.
Select Auto-update apps.
Choose the desired setting:
Don't auto-update apps.
Auto-update apps at any time. 
Auto-update apps over Wi-Fi only.
Benefits of turning on auto-updates for apps
▶ 🤖 Background notes
[AI Context]: This section outlines the key advantages for pros who enable automatic app updates for the Thumbtack Pro app on their devices, which Frontline Reps can communicate to pros to encourage a better app experience.
It’s beneficial for pros to turn on auto-updates for their Thumbtack Pro app, here’s why:
Security: Updates often include security patches, which help protect the device from malware and vulnerabilities.
Performance: Updates can improve app performance.
New features: Updates often introduce new features and functionalities to apps. 
(Pro) Steps: How to review the Android Thumbtack app in Google Play
▶ 🤖 Background notes
[AI Context]: This section outlines how Frontline Reps can guide pros in leaving a review for the Thumbtack Pro app in the Google Play Store, detailing the steps from opening the Play Store to posting the review.
If a pro wants to review the Android Thumbtack Pro app, Frontline reps can help pros follow these steps: 
Open the Google Play store on the Android device. 
At the top of the page, search for the right version of the app:
Professionals use "Thumbtack for Professionals" (with the black Thumbtack icon).
Scroll down to the reviews section.
Select a star rating (and tap Write a review to add more).
Follow the prompts to write a review and add details.
Tap Post.

To find the version of the iOS Thumbtack Pro app, pros should follow these steps:

Open the pro app.
Tap Profile in the bottom right.
Tap the settings gear icon in the top right of the screen.
Scroll down to see the “Version” listed at the bottom.

Spanish FAQs
What features does the app have?
¿Qué características tiene la aplicación?
All of the key features that you have access to on the desktop version of Thumbtack are also available on the app. In addition, you have more filters to fine-tune how you look for open opportunities in the “Opportunities” section of your Leads tab, as well as push notifications to help you stay on top of your messages and new leads.

La aplicación móvil de Thumbtack es el mejor lugar para conectarse con profesionales para prácticamente cualquier cosa. En la aplicación, tiene toda la información que necesita al alcance de su mano y puede buscar profesionales, responder mensajes y administrar sus proyectos desde cualquier lugar.

1. Overview ​​​​
With Thumbtack’s all-in-one app, customers will be on top of their to-do list. The Thumbtack app puts hundreds of local professionals right at customers' fingertips.Thumbtack customers should install the Thumbtack app with the blue Thumbtack logo. The Thumbtack app with the black icon is for pros. 
Here are a list of reasons why customers should download the Thumbtack customer app:
On-the-go access. Life doesn’t always happen on schedule. Use the app to create a project whenever and wherever customers need to.
Quick messaging. Make phone tag a thing of the past. The Thumbtack customer app lets customers send and receive messages instantly and get their projects handled quickly.
Customizable notifications. Mobile notifications keep customers current on their projects. If a pro reaches out, asks a question or finishes a job, customers will be the first to know.
Personalized home guidance. Customers can create their home profile and get a personalized plan and browse guides with recommended projects based on their unique home and goals. 
Easy project management. Customers can prioritize tasks, set reminders, and manage all of their projects in one place.
Building a team. Thumbtack will save the pros that the customer has contacted, so customers can easily message or re-book the pros they trust.
NOTE: For steps on troubleshooting the iOS or Android app (e.g., updating app, uninstall + reinstall app), refer to the Basic Troubleshooting App and Web (Pro) (Customer) KA.
Difference between the Thumbtack app versus using Thumbtack on mobile web
Mobile web is the browser on a mobile device that customers can use to navigate to Thumbtack’s website. While customers can still access many of Thumbtack’s features through mobile web, it's highly recommended to download the Thumbtack app to have access to Thumbtack’s full features and information. 
Thumbtack believes that the app offers customers the best experience. With the app, customers always have their messages and projects right at their fingertips. The Thumbtack app experience is streamlined to fit right into customers' busy lives, letting them manage their projects easily on the go.
Key Points
Here are key points for Frontline Reps to remember when assisting customers with the Thumbtack customer app:
The Thumbtack app with the blue Thumbtack logo is for customers.  The Thumbtack app with the black icon is for pros.
Customers using Android will show as Punk = Android customer app in Admin. 
Customers using iOS will show as Bowtie = iOS customer app in Admin. 
Android versions below 9.0 are no longer supported for app upgrades (as of November 13, 2023). Thumbtack only provides support for devices running Android 9.0 or higher. Any users currently using Android 8.1 or lower will still be able to use the Thumbtack app and reinstall it, but users won't be able to upgrade to any of Thumbtack’s newer releases of the Thumbtack app. 
To learn more about app features, reps can refer to the Customer App Features: Home Profile, Plan Tab and Team Tab (Customer) KA. 
2. Process

Steps: How to see if the customer is using Android or iOS in Admin (Rep)
 ​​​​

When filing a bug report, helping a customer find the app version they’re using or to see which app the customer is trying to log in to, support reps will follow these steps: 
Go to the customer’s Admin page.
Scroll to the Login History section.  This log of all events when the customer signed into their account. Covers all platforms (web, mobile, etc) and methods (password, Google, Facebook, etc).
Check the Type column to see their login attempts which tells you which app the customer is using.
If you see the “Bowtie app” the customer is using an iOS (iphone).  
If you see the “Punk app” the customer is using an Android phone.
▶ What the Login History section looks like in Admin:

[Image: rtaImage]

Download the app 
 ​​​​
Steps: How to help a customer download the Thumbtack app on Android (Rep) ​​​​
To download the Thumbtack customer app on an Android device (Google Play store), support reps can follow these steps:
Send the customer a link to download the Thumbtack customer app: https://thumbtack.app.link/t1UC9dER8Z
Or can walk the customer through these steps to download the Thumbtack app on Android:
Go to the Google Play store and search for "Thumbtack." 
Two Thumbtack app options will appear. Thumbtack customers should install the "Thumbtack: Hire Service Pros" app with the blue  logo. 
After clicking Install, the Thumbtack app will start to download.
When the app finishes downloading, customers can set their push notification settings, and begin using Thumbtack.
Steps: How to help a customer download the Thumbtack app on iOS (Rep)
To help a customer download the Thumbtack customer app on iOS (Apple App store), support reps will follow these steps:
Send the customer a link to download the Thumbtack customer app: : https://thumbtack.app.link/t1UC9dER8Z
Or walk the customer through these steps in order to download the Thumbtack customer app on iOS:  
Go to the App store and search for "Thumbtack." 
Two Thumbtack app options will appear. Thumbtack customers should install the "Thumbtack: Hire local pros" app with the blue logo. 
After clicking Install, the Thumbtack app will start to download.
When the app finishes downloading, customers can set their push notification settings and begin using Thumbtack.
Auto-updates
Benefits of turning on auto-updates for the Thumbtack customer app
It’s beneficial for customers to turn on auto-updates for their Thumbtack customer app, here’s why:
Security: Updates often include security patches, which help protect the device from malware and vulnerabilities.
Performance: Updates can improve app performance.
New features: Updates often introduce new features and functionalities to apps. 
Steps: How to turn on auto-updates for the Thumbtack Android app (Customer)
Customers can turn on auto-updates for their Thumbtack customer app on Android by following these steps:
Open the Google Play Store app.
Tap on the profile icon (top right corner).
Tap Settings.
Tap Network preferences.
Select Auto-update apps.
Choose the desired setting:
Don't auto-update apps.
Auto-update apps at any time. 
Auto-update apps over Wi-Fi only.
Steps: How to turn on auto-updates for the Thumbtack iOS app (Customer)
Customers can turn on auto-updates for their Thumbtack customer app on iOS by following these steps:
Open the Settings app.
Tap App Store.
Toggle the "App Updates" on. 
Review the app
Steps: How to review the Thumbtack app on Android (Customer)
To review the Thumbtack customer app on the Google Play Store, customers can follow these steps:
Open the Google Play store on the Android device. 
At the top of the page, search for the right version of the app:
Customers use "Thumbtack: Book local pros for home repair, events" (with the blue Thumbtack icon). 
Scroll down to the reviews section.
Select a star rating (customers can also tap Write a review if they want to add details).
Follow the prompts to write a review and add details.
Tap Post.
Find the app version


Steps: How to find the Thumbtack app version for an Android device (Customer)
 ​​​​ 

To find the version of the Thumbtack app on Android, customers should follow these steps:
Open the “Apps,” "Applications," and/or "Application Manager" section. (The option they see may vary based on their phone.)
Tap on the app to select it.
Scroll down to see the version number. 

▶ What it looks like

The following image shows the page where customers can see the Thumbtack app version on an Android:

[Image: rtaImage]

Steps: How to find the Thumbtack app version for an iOS device (Customer) ​​​​ 
To find the version of the Thumbtack app on iOS, customers should follow these steps:
After logging in to the iOS customer app, tap on the avatar at the top of the screen.
Scroll down to the bottom of the screen to see the app version.
The following gif shows how customers can find their version of the Thumbtack app on iOS:

3. Talking points  ​​​
This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with customers about the Thumbtack Customer App. Use these talking points to ensure consistent and accurate messaging, ultimately helping customers by providing clear and helpful support.

articles.fullText:
Thumbtack Acronyms, Systems and Terminology (Rep)

Contents
1. Overview
a. Common internal acronyms and terminology
b. Internal tools and company platforms terminology
c. Internal teams, roles, and acronyms terminology
d. Pro and customer terminology
2. Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This article is a centralized glossary of current and historical Thumbtack acronyms, internal systems, teams, and user-facing terminology. Frontline Reps can use this guide to quickly look up and understand unfamiliar terms.
Thumbtack's language has evolved, resulting in many acronyms, systems, and terms. This article serves as a centralized guide to help Frontline Reps navigate this terminology. The following tables define terms used both today and in the past.
▶ Common internal acronyms and terminology
The following table defines common internal business acronyms and operational terms for Frontline Reps. These terms are for internal use only and should not be used when communicating with pros or customers.
T erm or Acronym
Definition
A/B Test
Test that determines what effects a change has on certain metrics. Name comes from serving version "A" to some people and version "B" to others, using data to determine the winning version.
ACW
After call work
Allowlist
This references zip codes and means these are the only zip codes allowed for quoting. Formerly called "whitelist”.
AP
Action plan
Becquerel
Read only API that allows Salesforce to access product data. You can see emails, SMS, and instant book information via becquerel's  Becquerel types: becquerel__email_send_event, becquerel__sms_send_event, becquerel__instant_book_service
Blocklist
An account restriction where an account is unable to send quotes. MTS takes action to shut the account down. This is indicated in Admin. Formerly called "blacklist”.
BoB
Book of business
BP
Business partner
BOY
Balance of Year
BR
Bug Report. See the internal Bugs (Rep) KA to learn more. 
C2PP or CTPP
Customer To Pro Payment, initiated by customer or pro after they have started a conversation.See Thumbtack Pay (In-Product Payments) (Pro) (Customer) KA.
#CBB
Could be better.
CDC
Custom Direct Contacts, subset of opt-in contacts
CLV
Customer Lifetime Value
DEI
Diversity, Equity and Inclusion, join #inclusion in Slack.
EAS
Experiment Assignment Service, Reference: Experiments Infrastructure
EFW
EFW (the term has been deprecated) Agents may see it mentioned in older cases but its meaning is the same as Payment Dispute and Chargeback – simply an early notification Thumbtack receives from the users's bank or credit card company letting us know that the customer has indicated they do not recognize a charge or they intend to dispute a payment to Thumbtack. We do not receive these notifications from all banks or for all disputed transactions. See the Disputes section in internal Removed or Banned Users (KA) to learn more.
EM
Exact Match, contact type
EMR
Eligible Minimum Requirement, also known as onboarding activation.
ERG
Employee Resource Group Space within the workplace that fosters belonging and safety | ERG Wiki Page
Front Door
SEO-optimized pro list. Example: https://www.thumbtack.com/ca/san-francisco/djs/
GTM
Go To Market
L3M
Last three months
LP
Landing Page, special type of SEO-designed pages to capture traffic from search engines e.g. search for "San Francisco House Cleaner San Francisco". URL looks like: http://www.thumbtack.com/ca/san-francisco/painting/
LTC 
Likelihood To Continue, score used by CS to determine how likely it is that a pro who received assistance will stay on Thumbtack. See the internal CSAT KA to learn more. 
Macro
Another name for an email template within Salesforce. 
MBT
Market-Based Test
Mode
Data analysis platform that’s connected to our data platform which allows us to run and share analyses. Many of our key Managed Accounts dashboards and tools live here. SQL editor that provides basic dashboarding capabilities. Useful for analytics.
N2K
Need to Know, Weekly round up of news and highlights from across the company sent out every Monday, as opposed to the old practice of teams sending out their full meeting notes to everyone
NPS
Net Promoter Score, methodology used to measure pro or customer sentiment and satisfaction
NPV
Net Present Value
OKR
Objective and Key Result. Formally known as Get Stuff/Sh!t Done (GSD). This is the way Thumbtack talks about our goals. Goals for the quarter, year or other time period.
ONB
Onboarding
OOO
Out of office
Organic
SEO traffic
PBI
Promotional Balance Increase, discretionary promo credits that support agents can grant to pros up to a certain limit. See the internal Credits, Returns and Grants KA to learn more. 
PK ID, and Legacy ID
Admin terms, all of these are ways to identify a pro or customer (legacy ID being the oldest way, and PK being the newest way). 
PK ID = Primary Key Identification 
PL
Pro List, refers to Browser View (filter_view) page which shows list of pros.
PoC
Point of Contact
PRD
Problem Requirements Document defining the “why” and is generally the first step toward an RFC (though not always).
RFC
Request For Comment, a document outlining a proposed change or feature that is requesting for others to review and comment on | RFC template
RFS
Request Form Service
SOP
Standard Operating Procedure
SOT or SSOT
Source of Truth / Single Source of Truth
SR or IR
Search results (SR), the results generated after a search on TT. Known internally as Instant Results (IR) so don’t use it when talking to pros. Refer to the SR section for more details.
Thumbtack Classic
An internal term that refers to the previous business model of Thumbtack, where all pros would pay to create and send their own quotes.
TToD
Thumbtack on Demand (internally), known as claimable jobs for pros and On-Demand bookings for customers. See the internal Claimable Jobs (Pro) KA for more details.
Users
Often used to refer to the people who submit requests through Thumbtack. Sometimes referred to as 'customers’. Service pros can also be considered users, but Thumbtack commonly refers to them as service pros (or just pros).
WIP
Work in progress
WoW or w/w
Week over Week
WT
Work ticket 
YoY or  y/y
Year over Year 
▶ Internal tools and company platforms terminology
This section defines the various systems Frontline Reps may encounter. The list includes a mix of internal Thumbtack tools (like Admin), third-party software (like Slack), and internal codenames for mobile apps (like Wingtip).
Term or Acronym
Definition
Admin
The tool Thumbtack reps use to search the accounts of all Thumbtack users. Reps will find information about specific requests and quotes, details about a user’s activity, and even log in to the pro or customer’s account (Reps must be careful, because they are clicking around in the user's actual account and can make changes). Providers superuser capabilities to manipulate the website application www.thumbtack.com/admin or d.thumbtack.com/admin
Big Query
The interface in which Thumtack pull information from our data platform. See the internal Big Query KA lo learn more.
Bowtie, BT
Our internal name for the iOS customer app. “Thumbtack: Find Local Pros” in the App Store. See also: Wingtip.
Daft
Our internal name for the Android pro app. Thumbtack for Professionals” in the Google Play Store. See also: Punk.
CHECKR
Thumbtack uses CHECKR, a vendor, to run background checks.
Dog Food
The dogfood page on the staging site allows for more specific user actions than fishfood. Wiki page
Fides
Service responsible for user verification process (e.g., blocklist checks, Chekr) 
Fishfood
Dev rollout/testing environment. Fishfood is more general user actions. (fishfood)
Front Door
SEO-optimized pro list. Example: https://www.thumbtack.com/ca/san-francisco/djs/
Gmail
The email service Thumbtack uses. TSL and TSF emails end in @thumbtack.com, and TPH emails end in @ttc.thumbtack.com.
Google Drive
The platform Thumbtack uses to store documents, spreadsheets, and presentations.
KA or Knowledge article 
Knowledge articles or Lightning Knowledge The knowledge management system for frontline agents. The go-to spot and source of truth for the playbook, processes, etc.  These can be found in the knowledge tab in Salesforce (Reps have to toggle from the lightning app to classic). Here, you’ll find information about the product, troubleshooting and other processes. See the internal Knowledge Navigation KA to learn more. 
Lessonly or eLearning 
The app Thumbtack uses to train employees, especially for product updates. Lessonly has weekly updates, deep dives, features and experiment courses. Also known as eLearnings. https://thumbtack.lessonly.com/learn
Mode
Data analysis platform that’s connected Thumtack's data platform which allows it to run and share analyses. Many of their key Managed Accounts dashboards and tools live here. SQL editor that provides basic dashboarding capabilities. Useful for analytics.
Native (App)
Mobile app. See Punk, Daft, Bowtie, Wingtip. 
Okta
Thumbtack's main single sign-on authentication system. It acts as a password manager for a lot of programs we use. It’s also how IT manages a user’s access to these programs. 
ProNexis
A fully integrated business solution that gives professionals tools they need to generate leads, detailed reporting by a lead source, and a trained and professional customer service team that converts those leads into appointments. For some of Thumbtack's accounts, Thumbtack partners with ProNexis to handle communication from a Thumbtack customer to then schedule an estimate for a pro. The pro simply waits for an appointment to pop up on their calendar.
Punk
Our internal name for the Android customer app. Thumbtack: Find Local Pros” in the Google Play Store. See Daft
Slack
The team-collaboration tool used company wide. Use this to communicate with coworkers, groups of coworkers, other groups and teams, and follow channels of interest (both work related and for fun). A great place to go to see what things are happening on topics you care about. See the internal Slack Channels (Reps) KA to learn more. 
Stripe
Thumbtack uses Stripe to process its payments, who stores this info. Stripe is a certified PCI Service Provider Level 1, which is the most stringent level of certification available in the payments industry. All card numbers are encrypted. You can read more about security at Stripe here.
Tableau
Connects to Thumbtack's data platform and allows for the creation of useful data visualizations. Many of our key Managed Accounts dashboards and tools live here.
Salesforce
Thumbtack's customer relationship management tool (CRM). Salesforce is used to support pros and customers across all communication channels (e.g., phone, email, web, live chat, community).
Q&A
Questions and answers. 
Wiki
The go-to source of information for teams within the company, including Thumbtack policies, company-wide goals, and more. (go/wiki) 
Wingtip , WT 
Our internal term for the iOS pro app (“Thumbtack for Professionals” in the App Store). See also: Bowtie.
YCBM
Youcanbook.me
Zoom
The video conferencing platform we use.

Contents
c. Teams
d. External terms
II. Resources
▶ Internal teams, roles, and acronyms terminology
To help Frontline Reps understand the company's structure, this section defines the various internal teams, roles, and department acronyms at Thumbtack.
Term or Acronym
Definition
AE
Account Executive
AM
Account manager
BusOps / BizOps
Business Operations
CM / CatMan
Category Management This team learns as much as they can about pros and customers in each category, and then implements that knowledge to make Thumbtack better. Wiki page #categorymanagement
CS
Service and Support was formally known as CS or Customer Support. This team answers calls from pros and customers. They’re made up of managers, team leads, and support specialists. See the internal Support Ops Guide KA to learn more.  Wiki page
CSM
Customer Success Manager
CX
Customer eXperience
ELT
Extended leadership team 
Eng 
Engineering Department. Pro Growth - The product team specifically focused on growing the number of successful pros Thumbtack has on its platform. Wiki page. Storefront - (They call themselves “Pro StoreFurrront”). The product team focused on giving pros the tools they need in-product to succeed on Thumbtack. Wiki page
EPAD 
Engineering, Product, and Design, Focused on developing the vision for, developing, and designing the Thumbtack product, as well as maintaining the health of the site. See the full list of teams to learn more about what they’re working on (Wiki page)
FDS Ops
Front Desk Service Operations agent (FDS Ops). Front Desk Service is an in-house messaging service that allows pros to optimize their business on Thumbtack. By having a dedicated Front Desk team ready to quickly respond to customers, pros can spend less time at the computer and more time making money. See the internal FDS and Front Desk (Pro) KA to learn more.
GTM Teams
Go To Market) Cross-functional teams that identify pros that either a) we want on Thumbtack or b) who are already on Thumbtack and significantly affect growth. Once identified, other teams work to bring them on (Sales and Onboarding teams), help them understand how to use Thumbtack effectively (Intercom and Activation), or help them grow (CSMs and Account Management).
IT
Internal Tools Wiki page, Information Technology Wiki Page
MA
Managed Accounts
MTS or MI or T&S 
Trust and Safety team that has T&S specialists. This team creates policies to increase trust in our site. They have teams in TSF and TSL. The TSL branch works with pros and customers to resolve escalated issues. Formerly “Marketplace Trust and Safety” or “MTS” , and “Marketplace Integrity” or “MI”. 
AST
Advance Service Team, formerly Ops Consultants or formerly Advanced Support Advocates.
People
Reps who have questions about their benefits or Thumbtack perks should send them to the People Team. This team includes Recruiting, Internal Comms, Learning & Development, and Workplace Experience. Join #people in Slack. 
PM or PMM
Product Manager, Product Marketing Manager 
ProdOps
Product Ops is a key link between product teams and the pros and customers. They share feedback, solve technical issues for customers, and help track and alert Salt Lake of product updates as they roll out. Wiki page.
SAM
Sales and Managed Account Wiki page
SLT
Senior Leadership Team
Technical Program Management
This team builds and manages our operational infrastructure, such as the Salesforce CRM, the Help Center, and the MTS Solution Center (where pros and customers can resolve any disagreements). Wiki page. Formerly called “Business Applications”, “BizApps”,  and “Systems”.
TPH
Thumbtack Philippines
TSF
Thumbtack San Francisco, Thumbtack Head Quarter 
TSL
Thumbtack Salt Lake City
TT
Thumbtack
TTO
Thumbtack Toronto, Ontario, Canada
QA
Quality Assurance / Assessment 
XFN
Cross-functional
▶ Pro and customer terminology
This section defines terms and product features that Frontline Reps will use when communicating with Pros and Customers. Using this shared language ensures clear and consistent conversations
Term or Acronym
Definition
Account hold
When a pro can’t quote anymore for various reasons, ie. blocklisted, allowlisted, spamming, etc. This could also refer to any new pros who haven’t set up the basics of their account completely yet and aren’t able to quote until they do. Formerly called "quote gating”. Wiki
Account vs Service vs Profile
When a pro signs up on Thumbtack, they create an account. Within their account, they can add a business profile for each of their businesses as needed (for example, if a chef has two businesses, catering and cooking lessons, and wants to keep them separate, they’d make two profiles). Within each profile, a pro can offer multiple services. Services are the actual skills offered. See related term(s) .
API
An application programming interface (API) is a messenger that processes requests and ensures seamless functioning of enterprise systems. API enables interaction between data, applications, and devices. See the internal Partnerships and API Integrations KA to learn more. 
BGC
Background Check. See the internal Background Checks (Pro) KA to learn more.
Bids vs Quotes
Quote provided by service pros in response to request. Essentially the same entity. Pros and customers see the term ‘quotes’. Historically known as Bid, engineers will often say “Bid” as that is the internal name in the codebase. See related term(s).
Categories vs Services
The general types of projects that consumers can use to hire pros on Thumbtack. See related term(s) .
CBSA
Core-based statistical area, a geographical region that's commonly used to define a Thumbtack "market" e.g. a metropolitan area, geo
CMS
Construction Management Software (CMS) provides pre-sale tools including built-in customer relationship management (CRM) systems, bid requests, project proposals, payment integrations, and more. See the internal Partnerships and API Integrations KA to learn more.
Contact vs Lead
Essentially the same entity.  Formerly known as contacts. Pros are charged for leads, which is the first time a customer messages them to learn more, calls, books an appointment, or hires them. Customers make a contact while pros see leads. Pros aren’t charged when the customer’s first response is “no thanks” or “not interested.” See related term(s).
Credits
Thumbtack's currency used by pros to pay for quotes.
CRM
Customer Relationship Management (CRM) is a software platform that contains large amounts of customer data to help maintain and grow your business. See the internal Partnerships and API Integrations KA to learn more.
Disabled
When a pro shuts down their own account. This is indicated in Admin.
DNC
Do Not Call/Contact. See the internal Notifications (Pro) KA to learn more.
Enabled
When a pro has an active account. This is indicated in Admin.
Enrolled
An account is considered "enrolled" once the enrollment app/onboarding has been completed for an account.
FSM
Field Service Management (FSM) is a software platform that enables business tracking, recording, and optimization of pros field operations. FSM’s help pros with scheduling projects, invoicing clients, payment processing, and can also contain many of the same sales components of a CRM. See the internal Partnerships and API Integrations KA to learn more.
FDS
Front Desk Services (FDS). See the internal FDS Ops and Front Desk KA to learn more. 
IB
Instant Book. See the internal Instant Book KA to learn more.
IPR
In-Product Refund. See how to request a refund. 
JDNB
Jobs Done Near Me
JF
Job Feed
JTBD
Job To Be Done
Matching, Ranking
The ranking of search results. See the internal Search Results And Rank KA to learn more. 
NLE / NLD
New Lead Experience / New Lead Details
Opportunities
After a customer has contacted a pro through search results, the other pros on the search results page who weren’t contacted might see that customer’s job in the "Opportunities" section of their Leads tab. From here, pros can reach out to customers to show they’re interested in the open opportunity. If the customer responds to the pro, the pro is automatically charged for the lead at full price (even if the pro has targeting preferences turned on). That's because the pro initially reached out to the customer to say they're interested. See the internal Opportunities KA to learn more.
ROI
Return On Investment
SD
Supply Demand
SEO
Search Engine Optimization
SLA
Service level agreement. 
SR
This feature is similar to using filters to narrow down search results on a retail website. Search results allow customers to find pros that could work with them. Instant Results is another internal only name for search results, so don’t use it when talking to pros. See Instant Results
Thumbtack Help (Help Center)
Our help center resources to help pros and customers find answers to their questions. https://help.thumbtack.com/
ToU
Terms of Use. https://www.thumbtack.com/terms/ 
VHC
Virtual / Video Home Consult
WTP 
Known externally as max lead prices. See Max Lead Prices (Manual Bidding) KA. Internally as manual bidding, and willingness to pay (WTP).

articles.fullText:
The Thumbtack Guarantee (Customer)

Contents
Overview
Thumbtack Guarantee Claim Process
Dos and don’ts
Navigating the Money-Back Guarantee Process
How the Money-Back Guarantee Helps Customers
Money-Back Guarantee Eligibility Criteria (Customer)
What to do when a customer does qualify for the Money-back guarantee (Rep)
What to do when a customer doesn't qualify for the Money-back guarantee (Rep)
Navigating the Property-Damage Guarantee Process
Property-Damage Eligibility Criteria (Rep)

Service Categories Specifically Excluded from Coverage (Rep)

Talking Points (Customer
General questions about the money-back guarantee and eligibility from customers (Customer)

Talking points (Pro)
General Inquiries around the Thumbtack Guarantee and Eligibility (Pro)
Questions about the Money-Back Guarantee (Pro)
Resources
1. Overview
▶ AI Context:
This section provides a high-level overview of the Thumbtack Guarantee, explaining its dual components (Money-Back and Property Damage), the proper terminology to use, and guidance on handling customer inquiries and eligibility discussions.
The Thumbtack Guarantee has two parts: the Money-Back Guarantee (MBG) and the Property Damage Guarantee (PDG). Both should be referred to as the Thumbtack Guarantee.
Frontline reps should help customers who are interested in learning more about the Thumbtack Guarantee by sending them the Guarantee Terms and Conditions. Frontline reps can also let the customer know that they can send the case to the Trust and Safety team, and that team will reach out to the customer about the claim, or the customer can submit the concerns themselves by filling out the Contact Thumbtack Support form found on the Guarantee – Thumbtack landing page.
Frontline reps should NOT make assumptions about whether a customer is eligible for the Thumbtack Guarantee. — The Trust and Safety team will handle all conversations about eligibility.
Thumbtack Guarantee Claim Process
▶ AI Context:
This section outlines the step-by-step process of a Thumbtack Guarantee claim, from initial submission through potential payout, including considerations for Property Damage Guarantee (PDG) cases involving third-party investigations.
Frontline reps should direct customers to the Help Center article, The Thumbtack Guarantee. Frontline reps can find a summary of the Thumbtack Guarantee process below.
Submit a project concern – If a customer has concerns about a project, they should submit them to Thumbtack by using the Contact Thumbtack Support form found in the Guarantee – Thumbtack landing page.   . Frontline Reps can also submit the concerns on behalf of the customer by escalating the case to T&S. (For steps on how to escalate the case, Frontline Reps should refer to the Trust and Safety Incidents KA.
Dispute resolution – Thumbtack will connect the customer and the pro in a neutral environment (Thumbtack Solution Center, etc.) to discuss the Issue and the customer's desired outcome.
Determine eligibility – If the customer and the pro are unable to resolve the dispute and the customer appears to be eligible for the Thumbtack Guarantee, the Trust and Safety team will begin a final eligibility review.
Review—The Trust and Safety team will review the request and the customer's supporting documentation and notify the customer whether the request has been approved.
Payment – Following approval, the Trust and Safety team will contact the customer to initiate a Thumbtack Guarantee Payout. Thumbtack’s goal is to ensure that all payments are received within 30 days of approval, but this will not always be the case.
NOTE: For extreme or high-dollar PDG cases, Thumbtack may use Crawford, a third-party vendor, to conduct an on-site investigation of the damages.
Crawford is one of the largest claims management providers in the world, and Thumbtack uses its experience and industry expertise (home in particular) to help process high-value claims. Crawford's expertise includes activities ranging from on-the-ground investigations and damage valuation to remote reviews of photographs and estimates provided as part of a claim.
Dos and don’ts
▶ AI Context:
This section outlines the key "Dos and Don’ts" when communicating with customers about The Thumbtack Guarantee, focusing on accurate terminology, eligibility discussions, and avoiding misrepresenting it as insurance.
Frontline Reps should adhere to the following do's and don'ts when communicating with customers and pros about the Thumbtack Guarantee.. Following these guidelines will help the pro or customer by providing clear expectations for the Thumbtack Guarantee process.  .
Do refer to both the Property Damage and Money-Back Guarantees as The Thumbtack Guarantee - both guarantee types  fall under the term.
Don't tell a customer whether or not they qualify for the Thumbtack Guarantee. Guarantee eligibility conversations should be had with the Trust and Safety team.
Frontline Reps should gather the details and escalate the case to the Trust and Safety team for review. Frontline Reps should then inform the customer that the Trust and Safety team will contact them within 1 to 2 business days. For steps on how to escalate the case, Frontline Reps should refer to the Trust and Safety Incidents KA.
Don't refer to the Thumbtack guarantee as insurance, even by comparison. 
The insurance industry is heavily regulated and has strict requirements that the Thumbtack Guarantee does not meet. 
Presenting the Thumbtack Guarantee as insurance is a legal misrepresentation.
2. Navigating the Money-Back Guarantee Process
▶ AI Context:
This section provides a detailed overview of the Money-Back Guarantee, including what it covers, the eligibility criteria, and alternative support options for customers who do not qualify, along with instructions for escalating cases to the Trust and Safety team.
How the Money-Back Guarantee Helps Customers
▶ AI Context:
The following section outlines the scope of coverage for the Money-Back Guarantee, explaining what is covered for customers and providing next steps for further inquiries.
The Money-Back Guarantee covers projects that weren’t finished or were completed in a way that’s considerably different from what was outlined in the agreement. If the customer is eligible, Thumbtack will cover either the cost to finish the project or the amount the customer paid the pro, whichever amount is less (up to $2500). 
The Money-Back Guarantee also helps customers recover lost deposits of up to $2500 if the pro takes a deposit and never shows up for the job, and the customer's project qualifies according to the Thumbtack Guarantee terms and Conditions.
Customers interested in learning more can refer to the Thumbtack Guarantee landing page. 

Money-Back Guarantee Eligibility Criteria (Customer)
▶ AI Context:
This section outlines the specific criteria used to validate Money-Back Guarantee claims, including required documentation and timelines, along with instructions for frontline reps to escalate potentially eligible cases to the Trust and Safety team for review.
When the Trust and Safety (T&S) team reviews a claim, they look at a few different factors. These factors include a project request being submitted through Thumbtack, and the work wasn't added to the original project request. The T&S team will verify the following information with the customer:
The customer placed the request and hired the pro through Thumbtack.
The customer has a contract or document showing the terms of the agreement.
The customer hired the pro within 30 days of placing the request.
The customer discovered the problem within 6 months of the pro being hired and notified us within 45 days of noticing the issue.
The customer has made efforts to resolve the situation with the pro directly. 
What to do when a customer does qualify for the Money-back guarantee (Rep)
▶ AI Context:
This section provides guidance to offer customers whose issues may meet the eligibility criteria for the Money-Back Guarantee, emphasizing escalation to Trust and Safety.
When Frontline Reps encounter a customer situation that might be eligible for the Thumbtack Guarantee, the Frontline Reps should gather the details, provide the customer with information about the Guarantee by sharing help center resources, and then escalate the case to the Trust and Safety team for review. Frontline Reps should then inform the customer that the Trust and Safety team will contact them within 1 to 2 business days. For steps on how to escalate the case, Frontline Reps should refer to the Trust and Safety Incidents KA.
What to do when a customer doesn't qualify for the Money-back guarantee (Rep)
▶ AI Context:
This section provides guidance on alternative support and resolution options for customers whose issues do not meet the eligibility criteria for the Money-Back Guarantee. It emphasizes escalation to Trust and Safety, utilization of the review system, and submission of product feedback.
Not all customers will qualify for the Thumbtack Guarantee, but Frontline reps should let customers know they still have options:
If, after escalating the case, the Trust and Safety team determines that a customer's situation does not qualify for the Thumbtack Guarantee, Frontline Reps can provide several alternative support options.
Is the concern a Trust and Safety issue?
Direct the customer to reach back out to the Trust and Safety specialist in charge of the incident for further help.
Does the customer know about the Thumbtack review system? 
Reviews are a great way for customers to let others know about their experience. 
Customers can also let the pro know there’s a problem, so the pro can offer to help.
Frontline reps can offer to submit product feedback on the customer's concerns. 
Thumbtack appreciates feedback from customers and is always looking for ways to make Thumbtack better. 
Customer feedback is important to improve the Money-Back Guarantee.
3. Navigating the Property-Damage Guarantee Process
▶ AI Context:
This section provides a comprehensive overview of the Property Damage Guarantee (PDG), including eligibility requirements, specific exclusions for property and service categories, and guidelines for frontline reps handling customer inquiries and escalating cases to the Trust and Safety team.
Property-Damage Eligibility Criteria (Rep) (Customer)
▶ AI Context:
This section outlines the initial eligibility requirements for the Property-Damage Guarantee (PDG) and provides specific instructions to escalate a case to the Trust and Safety team, while emphasizing the importance of not making direct qualification determinations with customers.
The Property-Damage Guarantee has certain requirements that need to be met initially to determine eligibility. When Frontline Reps encounter a customer situation that might be eligible for the Thumbtack Guarantee, the rep should gather the details and escalate the case to the Trust and Safety team for review. The Rep should then inform the customer that the Trust and Safety team will contact them within 1 to 2 business days. For steps on how to escalate the case, Frontline Reps should refer to the internal Trust and Safety Incidents KA.
To qualify for the PDG, the customer must meet the following requirements:
The customer must provide proof they hired the pro within 30 days of finding the pro on Thumbtack.
Damages must be reported within six months of the initial request on Thumbtack.
The customer must report the damage to Thumbtack within 14 business days of discovering the damage.
Property Types Specifically Excluded from Coverage (Rep) (Customer)
▶ AI Context:
This section details the specific categories of property that are explicitly excluded from coverage under the Property Damage Guarantee, clarifies the exclusion of "property in transit," and provides guidelines for handling uncertain or potentially ineligible cases by escalating them to the Trust and Safety team.
There are several types of excluded property that are not covered by the Thumbtack Guarantee, including: 
jewelry, antiques, 
automobiles, 
watercraft, 
precious metals, 
and animals. 
The Thumbtack Guarantee also does not cover “property in transit.” This term refers to items that are being actively moved or shipped from one location to another, such as belongings being transported by a moving company or a shipping service. 
Frontline reps shouldn’t have any conversations with the customer about eligibility. Instead, the rep should gather the details and escalate the case to the Trust and Safety team for review. Frontline Reps should then inform the customer that the Trust and Safety team will contact them within 1 to 2 business days. For steps on how to escalate the case, Frontline Reps should refer to the Trust and Safety Incidents KA.


Service Categories Specifically Excluded from Coverage (Reps) 
▶ AI Context:
This section provides a definitive list of service categories that are categorically excluded from the Thumbtack Guarantee due to inherent risk factors, along with a clarifying note that unlisted services are not automatically covered and must still meet all guarantee requirements.
Certain services are universally excluded from the Guarantee as a result of the types of risk they represent. These services are:
Architectural Services
Land Surveyor
SUV Limousine Rental
Stretch Limousine Rental
Wedding Limousine Rental
Limousine Rental
Party Bus Rental
Town Car Rental
Driving Lessons
Charter Bus Rental
Mini Bus Charter
Corporate Bus Charter
Data Recovery Service
NOTE: If a dispute involves a service not listed above, that doesn't mean it qualifies for the Thumbtack Guarantee. All requirements for the Thumbtack Guarantee still need to be met.
Frontline reps shouldn’t discuss eligibility with customers; instead, they should gather the details and escalate the case to the Trust and Safety team for review. The rep should then inform the customer that the Trust and Safety team will contact them within 1 to 2 business days. For steps on how to escalate the case, Frontline Reps should refer to the Trust and Safety Incidents KA.

English talking points
Spanish talking points
The Guarantee Terms were updated recently. Will my project still qualify? (customer)
Los términos de garantía se han actualizado recientemente, ¿seguirá siendo elegible mi proyecto? (Cliente)
Let me gather some information about your situation so I can have our Trust & Safety team follow up with you. They specialize in handling these types of situations and can give you the guidance you need.
Permítanme recopilar información sobre su situación para que nuestro equipo de confianza y seguridad pueda realizar un seguimiento con usted. Se especializan en el manejo de este tipo de situaciones y pueden darle la información que usted necesita.
Should I try to resolve my issue with the pro directly first?
¿Debo de intentar resolver mi problema con el profesional directamente primero?
The Thumbtack Guarantee claim process relies heavily on resolution processes. We ask customers to try to work with the pro to resolve the concern before we begin the claim process.
El proceso de reclamo dela Garantía de devolución de dinero (Thumbtack Guarantee) se basa en gran medida en los procesos de resolución. Pedimos a los clientes que intenten trabajar con el profesional para resolver la inquietud antes de comenzar el proceso de reclamo.
If I already have homeowners' or renters' insurance, how does the Thumbtack Guarantee work for me?
Sí ya tengo seguro de propietario o inquilino, ¿cómo funciona la Garantía Thumbtack para mí?
The Thumbtack Guarantee is separate from your current insurance. Depending on the details of the situation, you may need to file a claim with your insurance first. Note: the Thumbtack Guarantee is not gap insurance.
La Garantía Thumbtack es independiente de su seguro actual. Dependiendo de los detalles de la situación, es posible que deba presentar un reclamo con su seguro primero. Nota: la Garantía Thumbtack no es un seguro gap.
I’m unsatisfied with the end result of my project. Am I covered under the Money-Back Guarantee? [Money-Back Guarantee Specific Inquiries (Customer)]
No estoy satisfecho con el resultado final de mi proyecto. ¿Estoy cubierto por la Garantía de devolución de dinero?
Our Money-Back Guarantee covers projects that weren’t completed as outlined in the original scope of work. If your project’s end result is vastly different than what was agreed upon and you have the original agreement in writing, you may be eligible for the Thumbtack Guarantee. You can learn more about eligibility qualifications in the Thumbtack Guarantee Terms and Conditions.
Nuestra garantía de devolución de dinero cubre los proyectos que no se completaron como se describe en la cuota de trabajo original. Si el resultado final de su proyecto es muy diferente de lo acordado y tiene el acuerdo original por escrito, puede ser elegible para la Garantía de Thumbtack.
Puede obtener más información sobre las calificaciones de elegibilidad en los Términos y condiciones de la Garantía Thumbtack.

Why did you launch the Thumbtack Guarantee for customers? What about pros?
¿Por qué Thumbtack lanzó la garantía para los clientes? ¿Y los profesionales?
We care about both our pros and our customers, and this Guarantee is meant to provide benefits to both groups by building trust on our platform. The more customers trust Thumbtack, the more likely they are to hire pros on Thumbtack. That means more business for pros like you.
Nos preocupamos tanto por nuestros profesionales como por nuestros clientes y esta Garantía fue creada para proporcionar beneficios a ambos grupos mediante la creación de confianza en nuestra plataforma. Cuanto más confíen los clientes en Thumbtack, más probabilidades tendrán de contratar profesionales en Thumbtack. Eso significa más negocios para profesionales como usted.

La garantía de Thumbtack no reemplaza su seguro. Sin embargo, el proceso de garantía tiene un enfoque significativo en la resolución de disputas, por lo que puede ser capaz de resolver las cosas con el cliente sin necesidad de utilizar su seguro.
