1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article, "Targeting Preferences", provides Frontline Reps with comprehensive information on how Thumbtack pros use targeting preferences (job types, travel areas, and availability) to control their visibility in search results and manage lead acquisition. It details the benefits of effective targeting, outlines step-by-step processes for pros to manage their preferences, and addresses common questions and troubleshooting scenarios related to leads and payments. The article's purpose is to equip Frontline Reps to effectively guide pros in optimizing their targeting for successful lead generation and to resolve related inquiries.
Note on targeting terminology: You may see "Targeting" and "Job preferences" terms used interchangeably throughout our internal KA resources or in-product.
What targeting preferences are
A pro’s targeting preferences (also known as "Job preferences") tell us when to show their business in search results (which helps us do a better job of matching customers to the right pros). With targeting preferences, pros tell us for each service they offer: 
Where: (Travel preferences) Pros pick their own travel radius and areas, even down to the neighborhood. 
When: (Availability) Pros choose their own hours. They set the days and the times and new jobs fit within their schedule. 
What: (Job types) This is where pros get really specific about the jobs they always want (and the jobs they don’t want). Job preferences 
NOTE: Effective as of March 19, 2020, new pros will be gated from appearing in search results until they meet minimum onboarding requirements. This is known internally as enforcing minimum requirements (EMR). Reps can see the internal New Pro Activation and EMR KA to learn more.
Service categories
A service category (often referred to as a 'service') is the broad type of work a pro offers, such as "Handyman," "Wedding Photographer," or "Plumbing." Each service represents a distinct area of expertise that pros can list on their profile to attract relevant customers. A pro can offer multiple services on their Thumbtack profile.
Setting up a service (turn on targeting)
Adding and setting up services is essential for pros to appear in search results. For each service a pro offers, they can set specific targeting preferences to control what jobs they get. Here are three major things to know:
1. Targeting preferences help pros show up in the right search results for the specific services they offer.
2. Pros auto-pay for leads that exactly match their preferences for each service.
3. The Quality Commitment applies to exact matches.
By setting preferences for their services (job, travel, and availability), pros agree to pay automatically for leads that match. Because pros auto-pay for exact matches, pros should make sure they only target jobs they really want and are always willing to pay for.
However, keep in mind that pros can’t filter out flexible preferences in eligible request forms because these aren’t options available to adjust in targeting preferences. These flexible preferences indicate that the customer is open to the options, and includes “I’m flexible” and “I’m not sure” type of answers. Frontline reps can learn more in the internal Flexible Request Form (Pro) (Customer) Knowledge Article (KA).
If a pro doesn't want to turn on targeting, they can still look for jobs on their opportunities tab. (Reps can see the internal Opportunities (Pro) KA to learn more). 
What targeting preferences are

Within a pro's profile, they will set preferences to let Thumbtack know which jobs they are looking for. These preferences are called targeting. 
To fully set up and turn on targeting, pros first need to define the services they offer. Once services are added, pros will set their preferences for each, including:
Job types: Job types are part of a pro’s targeting preferences and allow pros to get specific about the kind of work they do within a particular service. Each service has unique preferences.
Travel areas: Pros can select a distance they are willing to travel or select areas they can serve. Travel preferences are only available for pros who have targeting preferences enabled. 
Availability: Pros determine when they are able to work. They can set specific business hours or indicate they're able to work whenever the customer requests it. Frontline reps can see the internal Availability: Business Hours, Calendar, and Hide a Business (Pro) KA for more details.
Pros should also review these following preferences:
Lead prices: Pros choose how much they pay for each lead by setting their lead price. Their targeting preferences tell us what their ideal job looks like and their lead price tells us the amount they’re willing to pay for that ideal job. Reps can see the internalLead Prices (Pro) KA to learn more.
Budget: Pros set an amount they are willing to pay for leads each week. They will stop appearing in searches when their budget is met. Reps can see the internal Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro) KA to learn more.
Pricing (where applicable): Pros can set base pricing to establish accurate expectations. Pros can hide prices whenever they’d like. Reps can see the internal Pro Pricing KA to learn more.
Job types: Targeting preferences 
Job types are part of a pro’s targeting preferences and allow pros to get specific about the kind of work they do. Each service has unique preferences. 
Note: However, flexible options on eligible request forms are not available for pros to adjust in their targeting preferences. These flexible preferences indicate that the customer is open to options, and include “I’m flexible” and “I’m not sure” type of answers. Frontline reps should advise pros to still engage with these customers, and if the lead genuinely turns out to be a mismatch, pros can follow the usual refund process. Learn more in the internal Flexible Request Form (Pro) (Customer) Knowledge Article.
Why they’re important: Pros can use their job types to help control how often they appear in search results.
To appear in more search results (and meet more customers): Pros can open up their job types to take on a wider variety of jobs.
To appear in fewer search results (and meet fewer customers): Pros can focus on specific types of jobs and narrow their preferences.

Job types also tell Thumbtack which leads the pro wants to automatically accept and pay for.

Pro resource: How to manage my job types – Thumbtack Help 
Travel areas: Targeting preferences 
Travel preferences are only available for pros who have targeting preferences enabled. That’s because pros who have targeting preferences enabled automatically accept (and pay for) leads that match their preferences. Pros who don't set preferences don't have the same control over the location of their leads.
Here are the three travel options available on Thumbtack:
Travel to customers – “I travel to my customers” (specific areas or distance)
Have customers travel to you – “my customers travel to me ”
Work remotely (depending on their service) – “I work remotely (phone or internet) ”

NOTE: Pros will only see the options that make sense for their business. For example, a handyman can’t repair a closet over the phone or internet, and the customer can’t bring that closet to the pro. So handymen only have the "I travel to my customers" option.
▶ I travel to my customers: Travel area settings
When a pro selects "I travel to my customers" they specify where they travel to by either:
Specific areas: Selecting specific counties, cities, towns, or zip codes in an area. (Sew what it looks like below.)▶ What it looks like[Image: AD_4nXcRp0XIfWCJwx-P7LGRY8UCfZkQ3RVZpAmyk2n1cQGzCMarazVJNNRSXxMRWWfgNy4GsNCiAI9HZ3moDpXPQSO4ZoM_5ZkKL5-IbWEN0CyTGnTON9Fn85NF4De1daUMz_GuKDPZqaGqRKp11SF6CENS7Oeo]
Distance (the slider): Choosing a travel radius. (See what it looks like below)▶ What it looks like[Image: AD_4nXcocQdXSNeSBmrs8mXQYfeNi0U071cLQ-soqYKm8ZqetUuMP2tJclmvZjep_Rqg972hKu9WCIQPwgqHhDiqk7gYbbFe9LUpYJ3C2b6YtduGnq9O0cMijS6gNdkQYNU60M1HpyxiXPDstuxrLIeLS_haGpY]
NOTE: Travel distance/radius is calculated as air distance, aka "as the crow flies," not via road miles. What distance a pro sees on Google maps may not be the same as the outlined purple area on the map on Thumbtack within their Travel Preferences.
Pros can appear in search results for customers up to 150 miles outside of their location.
If a pro changes their travel areas from specific areas to distance (the slider), they will lose specific areas that they manually added or removed. Pros will be notified of this before their preferences are fully saved. After selecting a travel radius, the pro can add or remove areas to their travel area by selecting them from the list. 
If a pro sets their travel area by distance, their business address is the center of their travel radius. Pros can update their address in the “Business Info” section of their profile.
▶ My customers travel to me: Travel area settings
A pro can choose to have customers travel to them by selecting "My customers travel to me"
When this is selected, the pro can set how far customers can travel to meet them. This way, pros only get exact match leads that fall inside the area they specified — so they don’t have to worry about paying automatically for leads that are farther away than they want.
Note: Zip code level targeting only applies to areas a pro will travel to for work. Pros cannot pick specific areas for how far a customer travels to work with them. 
▶ Pro works remotely (phone or internet): Travel area settings
Pros can receive requests for remote work by selecting the "I work remotely (phone or internet) " option. 
Keep in mind that this will open up jobs nationwide for the pro. Only the "I travel to my customers" option allows pros to select different specific areas.

Benefits of targeting their services

There are many benefits to setting up targeting and making sure it is accurate. Not only will the pro appear more often and higher in search results, but these pros will also:
Get contacted more
Have higher conversation rates
Have better pro response rates
Higher customer response rates
Targeting tips for pros
Frontline reps can provide pros with the following targeting tips:
Respond to the customer quickly, or click “Can’t do it.” Remember, these leads can’t be refunded, even if the pro isn’t interested.
Pro resource: How to respond to leads and bookings – Thumbtack Help
Reps can see the Internal Messaging and Responsiveness KA for more details.
Update preferences regularly. Since pros are automatically charged for these leads, accurate preferences are important. 
Pay automatically for the jobs the pro wants. Those exact matches will qualify for The Quality Commitment. Pros can always adjust their preferences to fit their business needs.
Reps can see the internal Thumbtack's Quality Commitment KA for more details.
Build an engaging profile. Targeting preferences help pros appear in the right search results. But the pro’s profile is what draws the customer in. 
Pro resource: Here's a guide to your Thumbtack profile — Thumbtack Help article
Reps can see the internal Profile (Pro) KA for more details.
Don't forget about the weekly spend limit. Pros miss out on leads if they hit their budget before the end of the week.
Pro resource: How to edit my budget – Thumbtack Help article
Reps can see the internal Weekly Targeting Budget KA for more details.

Pro resource: Here’s a guide to your job preferences.  
Targeting paused automatically due to charge or payment issue
A pro’s targeting preferences are only paused if there is a charge or payment issue (for example, if the pro removed their credit card or has a negative balance).
Once the pro fixes their payment method (by adding a credit card or paying off the negative balance), their targeting preferences will automatically turn back on.
NOTE: Pros who pause targeting or have targeting paused due to a payment issue will void any budget increase incentive offer they accepted and they won't get free leads. Reps can learn more by referencing the internal Budget Increase Incentive (BOSUP & SOBU) (Pro) KA. 
Reps can see the internal Payment Methods KA for additional info and talking points 
Leads and targeting 
A lead is a new customer who has seen what a pro offers (most commonly in search results) and wants to learn more about working with them. Reps can refer to the internal Leads KA to learn more.
When a customer reaches out to a pro about a job that matches all their targeting preferences (travel area, job types, and availability), the pro auto-pays for the lead (even if the pro decides they’re not interested in a particular lead later). 
Pros can select “Can’t do it” on a lead that exactly matches their preferences and are given an optional survey asking them why they turned down the lead. If the job is outside of the pros preferences, see the “Job Outside of Preferences” section of the internal Lead Refunds KA to help navigate these conversations.
Frontline reps can help the pro fix their preferences so they’re accurate and remind the pro to review their preferences regularly through their Services tab.
NOTE: Opportunities are priced separately. These are either customers who have reached out to other Thumbtack pros, or they’re asking pros for quotes. Pros can let these customers know if they’re interested in the job, and they only pay if the customer responds to the pro. Reps can refer to the internal Opportunities KA for more details.

2. Process
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: The "Process" section of this article guides Frontline Reps on assisting pros with their targeting preferences. It covers step-by-step instructions for turning targeting on/off, adding/removing services, and updating job types and travel areas. This section also provides guidance on troubleshooting common issues like incorrect location data or lead volume discrepancies.
Steps: How to help a pro set their targeting preferences (Rep)
Frontline reps should follow these guidelines when helping a pro set their targeting preferences: 
Tell the pro what to expect: Search results will only show pros who set targeting preferences. Let pros know they don't have to have targeting preferences set up for all of their services, just the ones they want to appear on search results.
Set targeting preferences: Show the pro how to set targeting preferences.
"Look me up" tool: Walk the pro through the customer search demo, so they better understand how customers find pros on Thumbtack.
Explain targeting preferences: Explain what happens when they set targeting preferences (automatically pay for exact matches; Thumbtack's Quality Commitment covers exact matches; etc.)
Explain what an exact match is: A lead that matches their job, travel, and availability preferences.
Weekly targeting budget: Make sure they understand how to set up and adjust their budget.
Product feedback: Do gather feedback from pros about things they find appealing or don’t like. Let pros know that Thumbtack is listening and wants to know what does and doesn’t work for pros.
Steps: How to turn targeting on (Pro)

Pros can use the steps found in the  How to turn your job preferences on or off – Thumbtack Help article to turn targeting on. If a pro offers more than one service, they need to set targeting preferences for each one individually. 
Process reference: Pause (turn off) targeting (Pro) 
Pros manage their job preferences (targeting) within the Services page and tapping "Pause" under the Job Preferences section. For full step, see the How to turn your job preferences on or off – Thumbtack Help article
Note: 
Saved preferences: A pros preferences will be saved so it’s easy for them to turn targeting back on when they're ready.
Vacation/Temporary Pausing: If a pro is going on vacation, they should hide their business instead of pausing targeting to maintain their settings. 
See the How to pause leads by hiding your business – Thumbtack Help article for steps 
Reps can refer to the internal Availability: Business Hours, Calendar, and Hide a Business (Pro) KA for additional context.
Incentives & Billing: If a pro pauses targeting (manually or due to a payment issue), they will void any budget increase incentive offers and lose access to free leads.
Reps can refer to the Targeting paused automatically due to charge or payment issues section above for details on charge and payment issues. 
Reps can refer to the internal Budget Increase Incentive (BOSUP & SOBU) (Pro) KA additional context on these types of offers. 
Process Reference: Add a new service category to business profile (Pro)
Pros can add a new service category to an existing business profile from their account settings page. For full steps, see the How to add or remove a service — Thumbtack Help article. 
Adding a new service made easy
Adding new services is made easy because they are partially set up based on how a pro has set up other services. However, pros should check and change these settings if they want the new service to work differently.
The benefits of adding a new service are:
The more services pros add, the more potential business they can get
Not having to manage another business profile
Customers will be able to see reviews for all services within a business 
Getting notifications for all services to the same email address 
Adding back a previous service
If a pro had targeting turned on for a service when they removed it, and then they add it back, they will be asked to set their lead prices for that service. Pros will go to the Services and tap lead prices. This happens after they set their location preferences and before the budget page.
Reps can refer to the internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA for details on setting leads prices.
If lead targeting was paused for the service when they removed it, adding it back will keep it paused, and the pro won't need to go through the targeting setup.
When to create a new business profile
Pros can create a new business to keep services that aren’t related on separate profiles. 
See steps on the How to add or remove a business profile – Thumbtack Help article. 
Frontline Reps can see the internal Profile (Pro) ) KA for details on pros creating a new business profile.  
Steps: How to remove a service category (Pro)
Pros can follow the steps in the How to add or remove a service — Thumbtack Help article to remove a new service.
Steps: How to update job types (Pro)
Pros can follow the steps in the How to manage my job types — Thumbtack Help article to update their job types.
When a pro selects their job types, they tell us exactly which jobs they want. Pros auto-pay for leads that match their targeting preferences (including their job types, travel area, and availability).
Steps: How to update travel areas (Pro)
Pros can follow the steps in the How to manage my travel areas – Thumbtack Help article to update their travel areas.
Travel: Pros can choose specific locations to work in (zip codes) or they can have a more general travel area set by distance (radius). If a pro changes their travel areas from specific areas to distance (the slider), they will lose specific areas that they manually added or removed. Pros will be notified of this before their preferences are fully saved.
Remote: If a pros service can be offered over the internet or phone, they’ll see the option to work remotely. This means pros can get leads from customers from all over the country. If they don’t see this option when setting up their travel area, it means remote work isn’t available for the service.
Note: There are three travel options available on Thumbtack, but pros will only see the options that make sense for their business. So the pro may not have all travel options.
Steps: How to set where a pro travels to by uploading CSV of zip codes (Pro)
Guidelines for formatting a CSV
Frontline reps and pros should keep these guidelines in mind when it comes to uploading a CSV of zip codes in their travel preferences:
All zip codes must be in one column
No headings
Must be on web to upload (Pros won’t see the advanced option on the app)
▶ Zip codes are five digits. Leading zeros must be includedWhen saving as CSV in Excel or Google Sheets, leading zeros may be removed. Pros should confirm leading zeros are included in the zip codes before uploading the CSV file. Failure to do so may result in the file not uploading or could lead to an error. For example, zip code 00123. CVS can’t say 123.
Zip code level targeting only applies to areas a pro will travel to for work ("I travel to my customers”). Pros cannot pick specific areas for how far a customer travels to work with them. Once the list of zip codes are uploaded, the new list will override any old travel areas the pro had set for where they want to work.
Pros can upload a CSV file to quickly add a list of zip codes they work in by following these steps on desktop: 
Go to Services.
Tap the service to edit.
Tap the Travel areas option.
Tab the Advanced tab. (See what it looks like below.)▶ What it looks like[Image: AD_4nXfWve1hDJq9jGEjlScNrqaBomaO8BUXdxygrY1SXzshjwREaNAIrsw2wrl6lxBpb1uryY_PYG2AZY9rSEO9gYo8Gdmyd3kSRXRImKYPE84EPxPm79U8LH5OL9zsT2U-PvPBVnABGTjqcvnSBr3TaevMGd4]
For a successful upload, the CSV should have the zip codes in one column and no headers.
Click Upload. 
Once uploaded, the new list overrides the pro previous travel areas for where they want to work.

Steps: Correcting incorrect zip code, address, or city (Rep)
If a pro needs to adjust their address, they can follow the steps in the How to update personal information as a pro — Thumbtack Help article.
After confirming the address has been correct, if the issue continues, submit a Bug with “incorrect zip code - city matching” as the bug description. For a workaround, suggest that the pro use a nearby zip code and test this out until a desired or acceptable city is displayed.
NOTE: Regardless of city name, the pro will appear in search results and get leads based on zip code and the travel radius selected.  
Steps: How to help a pro whose leads don’t match their preferences (Rep)
To learn more, Frontline reps can see the internal Lead Refunds (Pro) KA to under the section: "Refund policy for Job outside of preferences (Job is unreasonable)"
▶ Troubleshooting steps for reps to take:
Make sure the pro’s travel preferences match what the pro wants.
Ask the pro for the name(s) of the customer(s) who didn't match their travel preferences.
Find the lead(s) in Admin and check the "Travel" section of the request. 
If the customer selected:
This can be done over phone or internet - the pro's location doesn't matter, so that's why the pro received the lead.
I will travel to the pro - check the distance (straight line distance, not driving distance) between the zip code on the lead and the pro's zip code.
Compare it to the radius the pro set in their "Distance customers travel to you" travel preferences. 
If the distance is less than the radius, the lead matches the pro's preferences.
Professional must travel to my address - compare the zip code on the lead to the pro's zip code whitelist in Admin
From the lead Admin, click the pro's service name.
Scroll to "Zip Code Travel Preferences (Strict White-list)" section.
Choose the service category of the disputed lead (next to "Showing whitelist zip codes for").
Use COMMAND + F to search the list for the zip code on the lead.
If the zip code is there, the lead does match the pro's preferences.
If the rep finds that the lead does not match the pro’s travel preferences, the pro may have changed their preferences after the lead was created.
Ask the pro if they updated their preferences recently.
If they say no, ask the Advanced Service team to run a query to verify that.
Submit a request to the Advanced Service Team (AST) in Slack.
Navigate to the #service_global_help-and-escalations Slack channel. 
Use keyword Global Help BQ to trigger the Assist app workflow.
Fill out the form with all necessary details. 
If it's confirmed that the pro didn’t change their preferences, the rep can submit a bug report. Steps on internal Bugs and Bug Reports (Rep) KA. 

3. Talking points
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros about their targeting preferences. Use these talking points to ensure consistent and accurate messaging.
Getting started with targeting preferences

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Why am I required to turn on targeting?
¿Por qué se me exige activar las preferencias de enfoque?
Without turning on your targeting preferences, we won’t know which jobs you want to do. When you set your preferences, it tells us when to show you in search results — so we can get you in front of the right customers.
Sin activar sus preferencias de enfoque, no sabremos qué trabajos desea realizar. Al configurar sus preferencias, usted nos indica cuándo mostrarlo en los resultados de búsqueda, de modo que podamos presentarlo a los clientes adecuados.
Do I have to turn on targeting preferences? 
¿Tengo que activar las preferencias de enfoque? 
No, whether or not you set targeting preferences is completely up to you. If you’re not sure, I’d recommend trying it for a week and seeing if helps more of the right customers find you.
No, el establecimiento de preferencias de enfoque depende completamente de usted. Si no está seguro, le recomiendo probarlo durante una semana y ver si ayuda a que más clientes adecuados lo encuentren.
Why should I turn on targeting preferences?
¿Por qué debería activar las preferencias de enfoque?
Your preferences tell us the exact jobs you want so we show your business to the right customers. 
Sus preferencias nos dicen los trabajos exactos que desea para que podamos mostrar su negocio a los clientes adecuados.
I’m concerned about auto-paying for leads.
Me preocupa el pago automático de prospectos.
You only auto-pay for leads when they’re an exact match to your preferences. You control your preferences so that means you also control what leads you pay for. 
It’s ultimately your decision whether you want to turn on targeting preferences or not, but if you’re not sure, I’d recommend trying it for a week to see how it goes. Start small (since you will still see leads you aren't targeting in your opportunities tab) and then add more job types as you see fit.  There is less risk, and you can get a good idea of which leads work best for you.

Solo paga automáticamente los prospectos cuando coinciden exactamente con sus preferencias. Usted controla sus preferencias, lo que significa que también controla los prospectos por los que paga. 
Últimamente, es su decisión si desea activar las preferencias de enfoque o no, pero si no está seguro, le recomiendo que lo pruebe durante una semana para ver cómo funciona.
How does setting targeting preferences help me get the right leads?
¿Cómo me ayuda la configuración de preferencias de enfoque para obtener los prospectos adecuados?
Your targeting preferences tell us exactly what leads you want. When it comes to search results, it helps us understand when to show your business so the right customers find you. It also means that you only auto-pay for leads that exactly match your preferences. The preferences you set are in your control, and that means you control what leads you auto-pay for. 
Sus preferencias de enfoque nos dicen exactamente cuáles prospectos desea. Cuando se trata de resultados de búsqueda, nos ayuda a comprender cuándo mostrar su empresa para que los clientes adecuados lo encuentren. También significa que solo paga automáticamente los prospectos que coincidan exactamente con sus preferencias. Las preferencias que establezca están bajo su control, y eso significa que usted controla por qué prospectos paga automáticamente.
Availability and targeting

For more talking points, Frontline reps can see the internal Availability (Pro) KA.

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
How often should I update my calendar?
¿Con qué frecuencia debo actualizar mi calendario?
It’s a good idea to update your calendar regularly to make sure your availability is accurate. For example, you can set a regular reminder on your phone every month to make sure you’ve blocked off any times you’re booked or won’t be working.
Es una buena idea actualizar su calendario con regularidad para asegurarse de que su disponibilidad sea precisa. Por ejemplo, puede configurar un recordatorio regular en su teléfono todos los meses para asegurarse de haber bloqueado cualquier horario en el que haya reservado o no esté disponible.
When I block off a date, does that mean I won't see leads for jobs with that date?
Cuando bloqueo una fecha, ¿eso significa que no veré prospectos para trabajos con esa fecha?
That's right. There's still a chance a customer could contact you about a job for that date, but as long as you've blocked it off on your calendar and set specific business hours, you won't be charged for leads that fall on that day.
Así es. Todavía existe la posibilidad de que un cliente se comunique con usted sobre un trabajo para esa fecha, pero siempre que lo haya bloqueado en su calendario y establezca un horario comercial específico, no se le cobrará por los prospectos que caigan ese día.
What if a customer says they’re flexible or not sure about their project details?
¿Qué sucede si un cliente dice que es flexible o no está seguro acerca de los detalles de su proyecto?
These flexible preferences indicate that the customer is open to options or would like your advice. We recommend that you communicate with these customers and help them decide on the job details. And if the project turns out to be a mismatch after finalizing the details, you can request a refund.
Estas preferencias de enfoque flexibles indican que el cliente está abierto a opciones o le gustaría recibir su asesoramiento. Le recomendamos que se comunique con estos clientes y les ayude a decidir los detalles del trabajo. Y si el proyecto resulta no ser adecuado después de finalizar los detalles, usted puede solicitar un reembolso.
What if a customer says their project date is flexible?
¿Qué sucede si un cliente indica que la fecha de su proyecto es flexible?
Your unavailable dates only apply to jobs that include a specific date. So you’ll still see jobs that:
List a flexible date
Begin on an available day, but end on your unavailable date
When customer does not specify a date needed

If a customer selects multiple time slots (for example, Saturday, Sunday and weekday mornings), you do not have to be available for all of them to receive the lead.
Sus fechas no disponibles solo se aplican a trabajos que incluyen una fecha específica. Por lo tanto, usted seguirá viendo trabajos que:

Indican una fecha flexible.
Comienzan en un día disponible, pero terminan en una fecha no disponible para usted.
El cliente no especifica una fecha necesaria.

Si un cliente selecciona múltiples franjas horarias (por ejemplo, sábado, domingo y mañanas de lunes a viernes), usted no tiene que estar disponible para todas ellas para recibir el prospecto.
Lead doesn't match preferences

For more info on Thumbtack's refund policy, Frontline reps can see the internal Lead Refunds KA. 

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Why am I seeing jobs outside of my travel area? (customer travels to pro)
¿Por qué veo trabajos fuera de mi área de viaje? (el cliente viaja a pro)
These jobs are actually from customers who have told us they’re willing to travel this distance to you. If you don’t mind customers traveling to you, feel free to leave the option on and see what kinds of jobs you get. Otherwise, it’s easy to turn off the “My customers travel to me” option for any service in your travel preferences. 
Estos trabajos son en realidad de clientes que nos han dicho que están dispuestos a viajar esta distancia hasta usted. Si le gustaría que los clientes viajen a usted, no dude en dejar la opción activada y ver qué tipo de trabajos obtiene. De lo contrario, es fácil desactivar la opción "Mis clientes viajan a mí" para cualquier servicio en sus preferencias de viaje.
Targeting paused due to failed payment

For more information on failed payments, Frontline reps can see the internal Payment methods (Pro) KA. 

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Why did you turn off or pause my targeting preferences?
¿Por qué desactivó o pausó mis preferencias de enfoque?
It looks like we just need you to update your payment information. Once you do that, your targeting preferences will turn back on. 
Parece que solo necesitamos que actualice su información de pago. Una vez que lo haga, sus preferencias de enfoque se volverán a activar.
Travel preferences

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
How far from my location can I get leads?
¿A qué distancia de mi ubicación puedo obtener prospectos?
You’ll appear in search results for customers up to 150 miles outside of your location.
When you set travel preferences, you have more control over what leads you pay for. You decide what areas you work in and when a job matches you automatically pay for the lead.
Aparecerá en los resultados de búsqueda de clientes que se encuentren hasta 150 millas fuera de su ubicación. Cuando establece las preferencias de viaje, tiene más control sobre los prospectos por los que paga. Usted decide en qué áreas trabaja y cuando un trabajo coincide, paga automáticamente por el prospecto.
How do you verify my location?
¿Cómo verificar mi ubicación?
We verify your address using Google Maps and will display the city that Google Maps lists under that zip code. Since some cities are considered part of a larger, nearby city, that larger city may be displayed instead of the city you expected. As long as your zip code is correct, you’ll still appear in search results and get leads based on the preferences you set for your business.
Verificamos su dirección usando Google Maps y mostraremos la ciudad que Google Maps enumera bajo ese código postal. Dado que algunas ciudades se consideran parte de una ciudad cercana más grande, esa ciudad más grande puede mostrarse en lugar de la ciudad que esperaba. Mientras su código postal sea correcto, seguirá apareciendo en los resultados de búsqueda y obtendrá prospectos según las preferencias que establezca para su empresa.
Can I set how far customers can travel to me?
¿Puedo establecer qué tan lejos pueden viajar los clientes hasta mí?
Yes! When you set your travel preferences, you can select how far customers can travel to you. That means you’ll only pay automatically for leads from customers within the distance you set.
¡Si! Cuando configura sus preferencias de viaje, puede seleccionar qué tan lejos pueden viajar los clientes hacia usted. Eso significa que solo pagará automáticamente por prospectos de clientes dentro de la distancia que establezca.
What does “Customers travel to me” mean in my travel preferences?
¿Qué significa "Los clientes viajan a mí" en mis preferencias de viaje?
You set preferences to target specific jobs. This is one way you tell us what customers you want to work with. Some pros prefer to work with customers who travel within a certain distance or area, like personal trainers at a specific gym. So that’s why we give you the option to set your travel preferences this way.
Establece preferencias para enfocarse a trabajos específicos. Esta es una forma en que nos dice con qué clientes desea trabajar. Algunos profesionales prefieren trabajar con clientes que viajan dentro de una cierta distancia o área, como entrenadores personales en un gimnasio específico. Por eso le damos la opción de establecer sus preferencias de viaje de esta manera.
Do I have to use zip codes for travel preferences? 
¿Tengo que usar códigos postales para mis preferencias de enfoque en viajes?
No, you don’t have to. You can still target the way you were previously. This is just an additional option if you would like to get more specific with where you’d like to target using zip codes instead of areas or a distance from your business. 
No, no es necesario. Puede seguir enfocándose de la misma manera que lo hacía antes. Esta es solo una opción adicional si desea ser más específico con el lugar al que desea dirigirse utilizando códigos postales en lugar de áreas o una distancia desde su negocio.
How do I add the zip codes that I want to target?
¿Cómo añado los códigos postales a los que quiero dirigirme?
You will go to the services tab and select the service you want to add zip codes to target. Scroll down and select travel areas. You will see an option to select by area and zip code. From there you will select the area you want to update and select the zip codes within that area that you want to target

If you are on the app you will see zip code options when you click in the “select by area list" option and click into the individual areas to see zip code options. 
Vaya a la pestaña de servicios y seleccione el servicio al que desea añadir códigos postales para enfocarse. Desplácese hacia abajo y seleccione áreas de enfoque en viajes. Verá una opción para seleccionar por área y código postal. A partir de ahí, seleccione el área que desea actualizar y seleccione los códigos postales dentro de esa área a los que desea dirigirse.

Si está en la aplicación, verá opciones de código postal cuando haga clic en la opción "seleccionar por lista de áreas" y haga clic en las áreas individuales para ver las opciones de código postal.
I already called in to have someone set my zip codes for me. Do I have to go in and set them myself now? 
Ya llamé para que alguien configurara mis códigos postales por mí. ¿Tengo que entrar y configurarlos yo mismo ahora?
No, your preferences will remain the same until you decide to make any changes. If you are happy with the zip codes that you had someone from Thumbtack set up for you, you don’t need to make any changes. If you would like to make any updates you can now go in and do that yourself in the Travel Areas section of your service preferences page. 
No, sus preferencias permanecerán igual hasta que usted decida hacer algún cambio. Si está satisfecho con los códigos postales que alguien de Thumbtack configuró para usted, no necesita hacer ningún cambio. Si desea realizar alguna actualización, ahora puede hacerlo usted mismo en la sección Áreas de Enfoque en Viajes de la página de preferencias de su servicio.
Once I set these are they now permanent? 
Una vez que los configure, ¿son permanentes?
No, you can go in and make adjustments at any time. 
No, puede entrar y hacer ajustes en cualquier momento.
I would prefer to just upload a CSV. of the zip codes I would like to target. Can I do that? 
¿Puedo simplemente cargar un archivo CSV con los códigos postales a los que deseo dirigirme?
Yes, if you would like to do that you will have to go on the web version of Thumbtack and go to your travel preferences. There you will see an advanced option. By clicking on that option you will be able to upload a CSV. Just make sure that all the zip codes are in one column and there are no headings. Once uploaded this will override any previous targeting preferences you had set.
Sí, si desea hacerlo, tendrá que ir a la versión web de Thumbtack y dirigirse a sus preferencias de viaje. Allí verá una opción avanzada. Al hacer clic en esa opción, podrá cargar un archivo CSV. Solo asegúrese de que todos los códigos postales estén en una columna y que no haya encabezados. Una vez cargado, esto anulará cualquier preferencia de enfoque anterior que usted haya configurado.
Turning targeting on or off 

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
How can I turn my targeting preferences off?
¿Cómo puedo desactivar mis preferencias?
You can pause your targeting preferences at any time. To turn off targeting preferences:

Go to Services.
Click the name of the service.
Scroll down to where it says ”Job preferences” and select the option to pause the service.
Puede pausar sus preferencias de trabajo en cualquier momento. Para desactivar sus preferencias de trabajo:
Vaya a Services (“Servicios”).
Seleccione el nombre del servicio.
Desplácese hacia abajo hasta donde dice Job preferences (“Preferencias de trabajo”) y seleccione la opción para pausar el servicio.
Can I change my targeting preferences?
¿Puedo cambiar mis preferencias de segmentación?
Yes! You can adjust your targeting preferences at any time. After you see what leads you get, you should continue to adjust your preferences to get more of the leads you want.
Si! Puede ajustar sus preferencias de enfoque en cualquier momento. Después de ver cuales prospectos obtiene, debe continuar ajustando sus preferencias para obtener más de los clientes potenciales que desea.

articles.summary: This article explains how Thumbtack automatically pauses a service provider's targeting preferences when they fail to respond to incoming customer messages.
articles.concepts: targeting preferences, unresponsive professionals, lead responsiveness, account pause, lead settings
articles.fullText:
Targeting Paused for Unresponsive Pros (Pro) (Experiment)

Contents

Overview
Experiment details
Pro experience
Baseline [manual action] experience
Experiment [targeting paused] experience
Process
Steps: How to handle questions about paused targeting due to inactivity (Rep)
Talking points
Warning email
Targeting turned off
Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) outlines the Inactive Pro Chargeback Experiment, designed to reduce chargebacks by automatically pausing targeting for pros who do not respond to consecutive leads. Frontline Reps can use this article to understand the new automated triggers, the difference between the baseline and experiment experiences, and how to communicate these changes to affected pros.
What
Starting December 15, 2025, Thumbtack will launch an experiment to automatically turn off targeting for pros who meet specific inactivity criteria (consecutive unresponsive leads). This system replaces the current manual process with an automated one to prevent inactive pros from receiving and being charged for unwanted leads.
Why
Internal why: To enhance the pro experience and reduce disputes, this experiment aims to ensure that only actively engaged professionals receive relevant leads. This approach protects pros from unwanted charges and confusion while preserving their control over their business activity. By preventing inactive pros from receiving leads, we anticipate a decrease in disputes, which will help stabilize chargeback rates in advance of the Visa policy change scheduled for April 2026. Ultimately, this creates a more transparent and frustration-free experience for Pros.
External pro facing why: We’re introducing an update designed to protect pros from unwanted charges and improve control over their Thumbtack activity. When a pro repeatedly ignores leads, it often means they’re not actively managing their business on the platform. This can lead to confusion, unexpected costs, and even disputes. To help prevent this, Thumbtack will temporarily turn off targeting for pros who haven't responded to several consecutive leads. This pause ensures pros aren’t charged for leads they aren’t engaging with.
How
Currently, Thumbtack manually identifies pros who are inactive (fail to respond to a specific number of consecutive leads). For these identified pros, their payment methods are manually removed by Trust and Safety to prevent future charges and prevent chargebacks.
Instead of the manual removal of payment methods by Trust & Safety, this experiment will automatically pause targeting for pros who consistently ignore incoming leads.
Trigger and Action:
Pros who fail to respond to a specific number of consecutive leads defined as 5, 7, or 15 unresponsive leads (with no responses in the past 7 days) across all platforms will trigger an action.
Process:
Educational Warnings: Thumbtack will send educational warnings to pros after they ignore a defined number of consecutive leads.
Targeting Paused: If the pro remains unresponsive, the system will automatically turn off their targeting.
Notification and Charges: The pro will be notified via email that their targeting has been paused. Thumbtack will stop charging the pro until they choose to reactivate their targeting.
Experiment details
This section provides details about the Targeting Pause for Unresponsive Pros experiment, including assignment, launch and end date, and impacted users.
Launch date: December 15, 2025
Anticipated end date: ~ February 27, 2026
Important Note: This is a target date. Experiment timelines are fluid and may be extended, concluded early, or shipped permanently based on results. Details will be shared closer to this date.
Impacted users: All pros who meet the “inactive” definition criteria
Inactive trigger condition:
First streak of consecutive 5 leads without a response and no response in any leads in last 7 days
First streak of consecutive 7 leads without a response and no response in any leads in last 7d
First streak of consecutive 15 leads without a response
Excluded users: 
Large, National pros (managed accounts) are excluded. 
Pros with integrations connected to their account are excluded.
Pro experience
This section details the differences between the baseline experience and the experiment experience for pros regarding unresponsive leads.
Baseline [manual action] experience (Pro)
Under the baseline experience, Thumbtack relies on a manual process to identify inactive pros. Pros identified as inactive may have their payment methods removed manually to stop charges. 
Inactive pro: Pros are removed  from search results if they've been unresponsive to leads for a specific amount of time. However, logging back in resets their "last activity time" and returns them to search results. This exposes these pros to new leads and charges, even if they still do not intend to respond, leading to a recurring problem of unwanted charges and subsequent disputes.
No Notifications: Pros who are inactive and do not respond to leads do not typically receive any specific notifications about their inactivity. However, pros will receive push, SMS, or email notifications based on their settings whenever they get a lead or a message from a customer.
Manual Intervention: When a pro meets an inactive criteria, Trust & Safety runs a manual process to remove their payment method (default card on file) to stop chargebacks. 
Outcome: Removing the payment method stops new charges, but the action is manual, unscalable, and provides the pro with no control or visibility. Furthermore, the core flaw—that a simple login can re-expose the pro to charges—remains.
Experiment [targeting paused] experience (Pro)
In this experiment, Thumbtack uses an automated process that tracks streaks of non-response to take specific actions,  rather than having their payment methods removed by Trust & Safety.
Inactive pro: If a pro reaches a specific streak of unanswered leads (Lead #7 or #15), their targeting is automatically turned OFF. For this experiment, a "non-response" or "unresponsive lead" means they did not reply or  decline the lead. This effectively stops new leads and charges until the pro explicitly chooses to turn targeting back on, preventing the cycle of unwanted charges.
Email Notifications: Unlike the baseline, pros in the experiment receive proactive communication.
Lead #5 (Warning): 
Trigger: The pro has not responded to 5 consecutive leads.
Action: The pro receives a warning email. This email explicitly educates them that "You are charged even if you don’t respond" and warns that their targeting will be turned off if they continue to be unresponsive.
Lead #7:
Trigger: The pro has not responded to 7 consecutive leads.
Logic Check: The system checks the pro's history.
If the pro has a 0% response rate in the last 7 days: The system determines the pro is inactive. Targeting is Automatically Turned OFF. The pro receives an email notification stating targeting has been turned off with instructions on how to turn it back on.
If the pro has responded to other leads in the last 7 days (Response rate > 0%): The system determines the pro is still active. No action is taken, and targeting remains on.
Lead #15: 
Trigger: The pro has not responded to 15 consecutive leads.
Action: Targeting is Automatically Turned OFF regardless of recent activity. The pro receives an email notification with instructions on how to turn targeting back on.
Automated Intervention: This process replaces the manual removal of payment cards with a scalable, automated solution. It provides a consistent experience that gives pros control to reactivate their business when they are ready, rather than having their payment methods removed by Trust & Safety
Outcome: When targeting is turned off, the pro is removed from search results and will not receive (or be charged for) new leads until they manually reactivate their targeting preferences.
2. Process
Steps: How to handle questions about paused targeting due to inactivity (Rep) 
To help pros who have received a warning or had their targeting paused due to this experiment, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:
Verify the Pro's Status: Check the "Experiment assignments" section in Admin to confirm if the pro is in the Inactive Pro Chargeback Experiment.
Check targeting status: Check to see if the pros targeting was paused. 

[Image: rtaImage]

Confirm the Trigger: Review the pro's recent lead history to verify consecutive non-responses (streaks of 5, 7, or 15 leads without a response).
Explain the Action: Use the approved talking points to explain that targeting was paused to protect them from paying for leads they are not engaging with.
Guide Reactivation: If the pro wishes to receive leads again, guide them to their targeting preferences to turn targeting back on.
Pro resource: How to turn your targeting preferences on or off – Thumbtack Help 
Rep internal KA resource: Targeting: Job Types and Travel Preferences (Pro)
3. Talking points
This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros who are part of the Targeting Pause for Unresponsive Pros experiment about their account status. Use these talking points to ensure consistent and accurate messaging.
Warning email 
This section provides frontline reps with talking points for pros whose targeting was automatically turned off due to consecutive unresponsive leads.

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: I received a warning message about not responding (to leads and targeting may be paused). What does this mean? 
Q: Recibí un mensaje de advertencia sobre no responder (a los prospectos) y que mi enfoque podría pausarse. ¿Qué significa esto?
A: Thanks for reaching out. I’m happy to clarify what that message means.

We sent you a warning because we noticed you haven’t responded to several recent leads. When that happens, we want to make sure you're aware that you’re still charged for leads even if you don’t respond. Sometimes our users get busy or step away from the platform for a bit, and we want to prevent unwanted charges from piling up.

The warning is simply a heads-up so you remain in control of your business activity. If you start responding again, nothing else happens—your account will continue running normally.

However, if the system sees continued inactivity, your targeting may be paused automatically to protect you from paying for leads you’re not engaging with. You’ll always be notified before anything changes, and you can turn targeting back on anytime.
A: Gracias por contactarnos. Con gusto le explico qué significa ese mensaje.
Le enviamos una advertencia porque notamos que no ha respondido a varios prospectos recientes. Cuando eso ocurre, queremos asegurarnos de que sepa que se le cobra por los prospectos incluso si no responde. A veces nuestros usuarios se ocupan o se alejan de la plataforma por un tiempo, y queremos evitar que se acumulen cargos no deseados.
La advertencia es solo un recordatorio para que usted mantenga el control de la actividad de su negocio. Si vuelve a responder, no sucede nada más: su cuenta seguirá funcionando con normalidad.
Sin embargo, si el sistema detecta inactividad continua, su enfoque (“targeting”) podría pausarse automáticamente para protegerlo de pagar por prospectos con los que no está interactuando. Siempre le notificaremos antes de que ocurra cualquier cambio, y usted puede volver a activar su enfoque cuando quiera.
Targeting turned off
This section provides frontline reps with talking points for pros whose targeting was automatically turned off due to consecutive unresponsive leads.


English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: Why was my targeting turned off (due to inactivity)?
Q: ¿Por qué se desactivó mi enfoque (“targeting”) por inactividad?
A: I’m happy to explain what happened and how to get your account active again.

Your targeting was automatically turned off because we noticed you hadn’t responded to several consecutive leads. This pause is designed to protect you from being charged for leads you’re not currently able to take on. Nothing has been removed or changed about your account—you just won’t receive new leads until you choose to turn targeting back on.

This approach helps prevent accidental charges and ensures that you only pay for leads when they’re actively available to connect with customers.

If you’re ready to start getting leads again, you can turn targeting back on in just a few taps. I’m happy to walk you through it or help review your preferences so you get the right types of leads moving forward.
A: Con gusto le explico lo que ocurrió y cómo volver a activar su cuenta.

Su enfoque se desactivó automáticamente porque notamos que no había respondido a varios prospectos consecutivos. Esta pausa está diseñada para protegerlo de cargos por prospectos que, en este momento, no puede atender. No se eliminó ni cambió nada en su cuenta: simplemente no recibirá nuevos prospectos hasta que decida activar nuevamente su enfoque.

Esto ayuda a evitar cargos accidentales y garantiza que solo pague por prospectos cuando esté disponible para conectarse con los clientes.

Si está listo para comenzar a recibir prospectos otra vez, puede activar su targeting (“enfoque”) con solo unos pasos. Con gusto puedo guiarlo en los pasos o ayudarle a revisar sus preferencias para que reciba los tipos correctos de prospectos en adelante.

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article introduces Frontline Reps to the "Request Pay Support" Slack workflow for submitting inquiries about Stripe investigations and customer-to-pro payments. It explains when to use this process, how it works, and answers frequently asked questions. 
Frontline Reps must understand how customer-to-pro payments work and be aware of how to resolve any issues that may arise. To support this, information is available across several Knowledge Articles (KAs) covering payment features. While frontline reps should always rely on these applicable KAs and other internal resources first, there are times when a complex payment situation requires additional help.
When reps need help with a payment issue that cannot be resolved using available documentation, their escalation path is to first, seek help from the Advanced Service team by posting in their designated Slack channels. Steps on internal Requesting Help from the Advanced Service Team (Rep) KA.
In the event that Advanced Service cannot provide a resolution, you will connect with the Pay team using the "Request Pay Support" Slack workflow. This centralized workflow is accessed in the #marketplace-pay-support Slack channel. The Pay team established this process to streamline support for complex issues, which directly helps them improve the product, enhance educational materials, and boost support tool capabilities.
Dos and don’ts
Frontline reps will follow these guidelines when requesting help for a payment related situations: 
DO:
Utilize all resources (KAs, Help Center) before request help. 
Direct Deposit and Stripe (Pro)
Instant Deposits (Pro)
Claimable Jobs (Pro)
On-Demand Bookings (Customer)
Report bugs following the usual process. Steps on internal Bugs and Bug Reports (Rep) KA.
Fill out the "Request Pay Support" form as completely as possible.
Follow up on the Slack thread and check the "also send to marketplace-pay-support" box to alert the engineer on call if urgent and no update within 24 hours.
DO NOT: 
Submit bugs using the "Request Pay Support" workflow.
Submit an inquiry to the Pay team before checking internal resources AND consulting Advanced Service
Post in #customer-to-pro-payments or use the old Tracker.
Create duplicate requests; search for the case number or pro/customer
Steps: How to request support for a pay related situations (Rep) 
Before submitting a payment inquiry related to customer to pro payments (Thumbtack page) and a Stripe investigation, Frontline Reps must follow a clear escalation path, starting with self-service resources. Reps will do this by following the steps below: 
Before posting in Slack, Frontline Reps must utilize the available resources like KAs, Help Center, and any other training materials. 
Payment-related KAs include:
Direct Deposit and Stripe (Pro)
Instant Deposits (Pro)
Claimable Jobs (Pro)
On-Demand Bookings (Customer)
If Frontline Reps cannot find the answer in the above resources, they should ask Advanced Service for help. Steps in internal Requesting Help from the Advanced Service Team (Rep) KA
If Advanced Service cannot answer your payment question, submit a report to the Pay team using the process workflow below.
Navigate to the #marketplace-pay-support slack channel.
▶ Hover over the channel name to show the channel options and select Request Pay Support.
[Image: Screenshot 2024-06-21 at 11.29.23 AM.png]
▶ In the next window, select Start Workflow[Image: Screenshot 2024-06-21 at 11.30.46 AM.png]
NOTE: If this is the rep's first time using workflow automation in Slack, they may need to connect their Google account by selecting Connect.
Fill out the form as completely as possible. Scroll down to complete the full form.
Click Submit.
NOTE: Bugs should not be submitted here. They should be reported following the usual process. See the internal Bugs KA for steps. 
An engineer on call will be notified and will follow up with the rep on the thread if needed.
Once the request has been addressed, the submission will show as “Mark as Resolved.”
Steps: How to check the status and follow-up on a payment inquiry (Rep)
To check the status of a request and see if the Pay Team has responded, the Frontline Rep should:
Check the Workflow comment thread. 
If there are no updates and the request is urgent and has not been addressed within 24 hours, the rep can: 
Follow up on the thread and check the “also send to marketplace-pay-support“ box on their reply to alert the current engineer on call. 
[Internal note: Requests are considered urgent when:]
There is a risk of a large or national pro churning due to an unresolved issue.
A large or national pro is blocked from paying for leads or receiving large earnings deposits.
