1. Overview
▶ KA summary
This internal knowledge article provides guidance for Frontline Reps regarding the acquisition of StreetFair by Thumbtack and the upcoming launch of "Thumbtack Neighbors." It covers the wind-down of StreetFair platforms by May 15, 2026, and outlines specific talking points for helping StreetFair pros and customers during the transition to the Thumbtack app.
StreetFair is joining Thumbtack to help build Thumbtack Neighborhoods, a community-centric experience designed to help homeowners find the local pros their neighbors trust and join together on services. StreetFair has proven successful in driving increased projects per user and lowering acquisition costs through neighborhood-based referrals.
To focus on this new chapter, StreetFair’s current app and website were sunset on May 15, 2026.
Reps can check out the internal Thumbtack Neighborhoods V1 (Pro) (Customer) (Pilot) KA to learn more.
Key points

This section provides frontline reps with a high-level "cheat sheet" of the most critical facts regarding the StreetFair acquisition. 
Critical Dates:
April 22, 2026: StreetFair users received emails about the acquisition and what to expect..
May 15, 2026: StreetFair apps and website were fully decommissioned.
External Awareness (Thumbtack Neighbors): 
StreetFair Users: Only StreetFair pros and customers have been notified about Thumbtack Neighbors via brief "teasers" in their email communications.
Thumbtack Users: There has been no nationwide announcement to existing Thumbtack pros or customers. Do not proactively mention the acquisition or "Neighbors" feature to Thumbtack users.
Pro Data: StreetFair automatically emailed a CSV of customer information to all pros on May 15, 2026.
No Automatic Migration: Accounts, reviews, and project histories did not move automatically. Pros and customers must choose to join Thumbtack and create new profiles. 
Reviews & History: Thumbtack is actively working on a solution to help pros showcase their established reputation on Thumbtack.
2. What is Thumbtack Neighbors?
[Internal information ONLY: 
It is a re-imagined "neighborhood marketplace" experience within the Thumbtack app. While StreetFair successfully drove neighborhood referrals, Thumbtack Neighbors scales this technology to a nationwide audience.
Upcoming Service Visits (USVs): A feed where homeowners can see services scheduled by their neighbors and "join in" on those visits. 
Social Proof: Showing exactly how many neighbors have hired a specific pro or are participating in a group service.
Group Discounts: Enabling pros to offer lower rates when multiple neighbors book services in the same geographic area.
Reps should refer to the internal Thumbtack Neighborhoods V1 (Pro) (Customer) (Pilot) KA to learn more about the experience. 
Evolution: From StreetFair to Thumbtack Neighbors

While StreetFair successfully drove neighborhood referrals, Thumbtack Neighborhoods scales this technology to a nationwide audience. Building on StreetFair’s foundation, Thumbtack Neighborhoods adds:
Unmatched Scale: Access to Thumbtack’s massive customer base across 500+ categories that were not available on the StreetFair platform.
Automated Visibility: Moving from manual "Nudges" to an API-driven experience that automatically shares pros' presence on a street when their CRM is linked.
Consolidated Management: The ability to manage neighborhood-based "route density" alongside standard Thumbtack leads in one professional dashboard.
End of internal only info]
What StreetFair users know about Thumbtack Neighbors
The comms sent to StreetFair pros and customers on April 22, 2026, mention Thumbtack Neighbors at a high level. 
StreetFair pro email: 
Introduces Thumbtack Neighbors, a "re-imagined" experience coming to Thumbtack later this year that incorporates StreetFair’s community-driven trust features.
StreetFair customer email: 
"Teases" the July 1st launch of the Thumbtack Neighbors experience, promising a better way to join group deals and see neighborhood-verified reviews.
Speaking with StreetFair pros about Thumbtack Neighbors
Focus 
Talking Point
The Evolution of Growth
Thumbtack Neighbors takes the route density you built on StreetFair and scales it. You aren't just winning a neighborhood; you're gaining access to the millions of customers who use Thumbtack every day.
Reputation & Migration
Our teams are actively developing a solution to help you showcase your established StreetFair reputation on Thumbtack. By joining now, you secure your spot as an early adopter in our pilot markets 
Integration & Automation
Thumbtack is working on developing similar integration and automation enhancements that were available at StreetFair to share your upcoming jobs to the neighborhood , helping you cluster jobs more efficiently than ever.
Speaking with StreetFair customers about Thumbtack Neighbors
Focus 
Talking Point
Category Expansion
Building on StreetFair’s foundation, Thumbtack Neighbors adds the ability to see who your neighbors trust for every home project—from the lawn care you had on StreetFair to plumbers, electricians, and more.
Pilot launch:
The re-imagined experience launches later this summer in select pilot communities.. We recommend downloading the Thumbtack app now so you’re ready to see neighbor-verified pros the moment we go live in your area.
What Thumbtack users know about Thumbtack Neighbors or the acquisition
Thumbtack customers or pros will not receive a nationwide announcement on April 22, 2026 about the StreetFair acquisition or Thumbtack Neighbors. Frontline reps should not proactively mention the acquisition or "Neighbors" feature to Thumbtack users.
When speaking with existing Thumbtack customers and pros who inquire about the StreetFair acquisition, Frontline reps should follow these guidelines: 
For both customers and pros 
The Vision: Explain that StreetFair joined Thumbtack to help build Thumbtack Neighbors, an experience centered on neighborhood trust and seeing which pros your neighbors use.
No Immediate Changes: Reassure users that there are no immediate changes to their current Thumbtack experience or account settings today.
NOTE: Thumbtack Neighbors will NOT be communicated externally. The only external users informed about Thumbtack Neighbors are brief teasers StreetFair users received in email comms on April 22, 2026. 
3. Timelines and Comms
Use this chronological roadmap to track the wind-down of the StreetFair platform and the subsequent launch of Thumbtack Neighbors. This section is vital for managing user expectations regarding when specific features will disappear and when the new experience will become available.
Timeline: Wind-Down & Notification (April – May 2026)

This timeline outlines the specific dates for user notifications, billing pauses, and the final decommissioning of the StreetFair app and website. 
April 22: Notification Date. Emails sent to all StreetFair pros and customers (Subject: "A new chapter for StreetFair").
In-product pop-up modals appear in the StreetFair app.
StreetFair Pro mailers and "Neighborhood Nudges" (subscriptions) are officially paused (as of March 31st). 
Late April: Final invoices sent to StreetFair pros for work completed in April.
May 15: Sunset Date.  The StreetFair consumer app, pro app, and website are fully decommissioned.
Last day for pros to access the Provider Portal.
Last day for customers to use existing StreetFair credits for completed jobs.
Comms to StreetFair users (April 22, 2026)
A formal email announcement is scheduled for April 22, 2026 (providing approximately three weeks' notice). Separate emails will be sent to StreetFair customers and pros, along with in-product popups (in StreetFair app) for returning sessions until the shutdown date.
Comms to StreetFair pros
On April 22nd, all StreetFair pros (referred to as "Providers") will receive an email and in-product notification titled "A new chapter for StreetFair" announcing the acquisition and the upcoming wind-down of the StreetFair platform.
The communication includes the following key information:
Platform Sunset: The StreetFair app and website will be fully decommissioned on May 15th, 2026.
Thumbtack Neighbors: The email introduces Thumbtack Neighbors, a "re-imagined" experience coming to Thumbtack later this year that incorporates StreetFair’s community-driven trust features.
Portal and Data: Pros will maintain access to their Provider Portal until May 15th. StreetFair will then export and send you your StreetFair customer information via email.
Data Migration: StreetFair data (verified work history, reviews, etc.) will not move to Thumbtack automatically
Billing and Charges:
Pros will receive a final invoice for work completed during April.
All recurring charges for StreetFair Pro customers, including mailers and Neighborhood Nudges, have been paused.
Onboarding Help: Pros not currently on Thumbtack are encouraged to list their services and can reply directly to the email for help getting set up for the future Neighbors experience
NOTE to rep: The email is sent from an @Streetfair.com email address. If a pro replies directly from the email, Blake will handle the response and direct them to the proper Thumbtack channel. 
Comms to StreetFair Customers
On April 22nd, StreetFair customers will be notified via email and in-product pop-ups regarding the transition to Thumbtack. The communication is designed to be positive, focusing on the "upgrade" to the Thumbtack platform while providing clear deadlines for the current StreetFair experience.
The communication includes the following key information:
The Big News The email announces that StreetFair has been acquired by Thumbtack to build Thumbtack Neighbors. The narrative focuses on the fact that homeowners make better decisions when they see who their neighbors trust and that joining Thumbtack allows this vision to scale.
The Wind-Down Timeline
Shutdown Date: The StreetFair app and website will be fully decommissioned on May 15th, 2026.
Ongoing Projects: Customers are advised that any active projects or conversations with pros will not be accessible after May 15, 2026. They are encouraged to save pro contact information (phone/email).
Financials (Credits & Refunds)
Existing Credits: All StreetFair credits must be used for services completed by the May 15, 2026 deadline.
Unused Credits: The email explains that any credits not used by the shutdown date will be lost.
The Transition to Thumbtack
Call to Action (CTA): Customers are encouraged to download the Thumbtack app.
Teasing "Neighbors": The email "teases" the July 1st launch of the Thumbtack Neighbors experience, promising a better way to join group deals and see neighborhood-verified reviews

4. Pro Experience


Experience Comparison: StreetFair vs Thumbtack

This side-by-side comparison highlights the fundamental differences between the legacy StreetFair model and the future Thumbtack experience. Use this table to explain shifts in billing, lead pricing, and geographic availability to pros moving between platforms.


Feature
StreetFair Experience (Legacy)
Thumbtack Experience (Current/Future)
Service Locations
Limited Markets: Only available in Charlotte & Raleigh, NC; Dallas/Fort Worth, TX;  and Nashville, TN.
Nationwide: Available across the USA. Note: The new "Neighbors" pilot is launching only in select communities for the initial pilot.
Lead Pricing
$0 Upfront Cost: Pros do not pay to receive leads or for profile setup.
Exact Lead Prices: Pros set the exact amount they will pay for a specific lead type. 
Billing & Revenue Model
Success-Based (Commission): Pros pay a 6–10% "take rate" only on closed jobs. Invoiced after work is completed. Subscriptions for nudges/mailers.
Lead-Based (Upfront): Pros pay for the lead immediately. Billing via Weekly Batches ($1,000+ spend) or immediate charges ($1-$999 spend).
Customer Reach
Neighborhood Feed: Upcoming service visits (USVs) are shown to neighbors to encourage "joining" a job, creating multiple jobs in one neighborhood to save travel overhead.
Thumbtack Neighbors 
Current: Driven by search results and matching preferences
Future: A similar community-centric experience launching in pilot markets  later this summer.
Lead Distribution
Direct Requests: Customers submit a request directly to one specific pro.
Direct & Shared: Customers can reach out directly to one or more pros..
Data & History
Auto Export: SF will auto-email a CSV backup on 5/15.
Review/history migration is currently under review by product teams.
New Profile: Pros must create a Thumbtack profile. 
CRM / FSM Integrations
Direct Sync: Integrations with Jobber, ServiceTitan, etc., used to populate "Upcoming Service Visits."
New Connection: Existing SF integrations will not cross over. Pros must re-link their tool to Thumbtack to enable Neighbor features.
Contracts & Terms
SF Service Agreement: Legacy agreements governed the commission structure.
Thumbtack Terms of Service: Pros must agree to Thumbtack's terms to list services; legacy SF agreements will not be honored.
Coverage Area
Set by specific, hyper-local Neighborhoods.
Set by travel radius (up to 150 miles) or specific ZIP codes.
Social Proof
Verified reviews organized by neighborhood and proximity.
Star ratings and reviews from Thumbtack and non-Thumbtack customers. 

StreetFair Experience (Legacy)

This section describes the original tools and services available to StreetFair Providers. 

Provider Portal: Where pros manage their leads, view neighborhood job density, and handle billing.
Neighborhood Nudges & Subscriptions: 
Automated alerts for neighbors to join scheduled services. 
These and mailer subscriptions were paused (on March 31, 2026) and no further charges will occur. 
A final invoice for April work will be issued before the shutdown.
Data: StreetFair will export and email a CSV of customer information to pros on May 15, 2026.
Transition to Thumbtack

This section focuses on the logistical "Evolution" of a Pro’s business from StreetFair to Thumbtack. It provides the narrative for why this transition is an upgrade and outlines the status of account and review migration.

Why move to Thumbtack? StreetFair pros are moving to access Thumbtack’s massive customer base while keeping the "neighborhood" benefits. By joining Thumbtack now, pros can be among the first in their neighborhood to establish their presence. We are actively working on solutions to help pros showcase their StreetFair history on their new Thumbtack profile so they can maintain the trust they've built
Data migration: 
Account: Accounts do not transfer. Pros must create a Thumbtack profile to access a larger customer base and future "route density" features. Pros are encouraged to download the Thumbtack pro app. 
Integrations: Existing syncs (Jobber, ServiceTitan) will not cross over. Pros must re-link their tools within their new Thumbtack account.
Reviews & History: Verified work history and reviews do not migrate automatically. Solutions to showcase reputation on Thumbtack are under development.
Billing: A final invoice for April work will be issued prior to the May 15 shutdown.

Guidelines: Helping StreetFair pros (Rep)

Here is the guide for what frontline reps should and should not share specifically with StreetFair providers.


DO Share
DON’T Share
The "New Chapter": Share that StreetFair and Thumbtack are joining forces to build Thumbtack Neighbors, a higher-scale version of the neighborhood referral model they already love. 
The "Shutdown" Focus: Avoid framing this as StreetFair being "shut down" or "deleted." Focus on the team and technology moving to a larger platform.
Data: StreetFair will email a CSV file of all their StreetFair customer information. 
Account Migration: Do not tell them their accounts, reviews, or project history will automatically appear on Thumbtack. They must choose to join Thumbtack and set up a new profile.
Trust Signals: Share that Thumbtack is working on ways to highlight their existing reputation through neighborhood-verified reviews.
Account Migration: Do not tell them their reviews will automatically appear on Thumbtack. 
Billing: Confirm that all StreetFair Pro subscriptions (mailers and Neighborhood Nudges) have been paused and no further charges will occur.
Refunds: Applicable pros received a refund from StreetFair proactively on April 2, 2026. Pros received email comms. 

Discounts: Do not discuss future "take rate" models or potential group discount percentages for the Neighbors feature, as these are still being tested
Thumbtack Benefits: Encourage them to list their business on Thumbtack now so they can be "early adopters" when Neighbors launches in pilot markets later this summer..
Internal Jargon: Do not use technical terms like "USV" (Upcoming Service Visit) or "Route Density." Instead, talk about "clustering jobs" or "neighborhood visibility".
Future Benefits: Mention that the new "Neighbors" experience aims to help pros build "Route Density"—the ability to book multiple jobs in the same neighborhood to save on travel time and overhead.

5. Customer experience

StreetFair Experience (Legacy)

This overview covers the core features homeowners valued on StreetFair, such as Social Trust and Group Deals. Understanding these legacy benefits helps reps frame the Thumbtack "Neighbors" transition as a continuation of those values.

Social Trust: Customers used StreetFair specifically to see "Who did my neighbor use for their lawn?"
Group Deals: The core draw was the ability to join a "Group Service" to unlock a lower price because the pro was already in the neighborhood.
Customer experience: 
Find and join their neighborhood.
Browse and book services recommended by their neighbors or join already scheduled services.
Share reviews on completed services to help their neighbors make informed choices.

Transition to Thumbtack Experience

This section outlines the journey for StreetFair homeowners moving to Thumbtack. 

Timeline: Customers lose access to the StreetFair app on May 15, 2026. They must use any remaining credits by this date for completed jobs..
StreetFair customer accounts will not automatically move to Thumbtack. They must choose to join Thumbtack.
Future changes
The re-imagined experience launches later this year (pilot starts in the summer). 
Customers should download the Thumbtack app so they’re ready to see neighbor-verified pros the moment the experience launches in their area. 

Guidelines: Helping StreetFair customers (Rep)

Here is the guide for what frontline reps should and should not share specifically with StreetFair customers.


DO Share
DON’T Share
Access Deadline: Clearly state that the StreetFair app and website will be fully decommissioned on May 15, 2026.
Long-term Support: Do not suggest they will be able to log in to StreetFair "just to check a phone number" after May 15, 2026. Access will be completely cut off.
Ongoing Projects: Advise them to save their pro's phone number and email immediately to continue any projects currently in progress.
Liability for Projects: Do not imply that Thumbtack is taking over the management or guarantee of active StreetFair projects.
Credit Usage: Remind them that any existing StreetFair credits must be used for services completed by May 15, 2026.
Credit Transfer: Do not tell customers their StreetFair credits will transfer to the Thumbtack app. Explain that any credits will be lost if not used on the SF platform by May 15, 2026.
The Future Experience: Invite them to download the Thumbtack app to see "who your neighbors trust" once the Neighbors feature launches in their area. Thumbtack Help article: How to download the Thumbtack app 
Exact Pilot Dates: Do not promise that the "Neighbors" tab will be available in their specific ZIP code. While the target launch is July 1, 2026, it is limited to pilot markets.

Internal Terminology: Do not use internal project names like Upcoming Service Visit. Instead, use customer-friendly terms like "scheduled neighborhood visits" or "the Neighbors feed".
6. Talking points
General
These high-level responses address the "Big Picture" of the acquisition. Use these to explain the overall vision of StreetFair joining Thumbtack to users who are curious about the corporate change.
English talking point
What is happening to StreetFair? 
StreetFair is joining Thumbtack to help build Thumbtack Neighbors. This is a re-imagined way for users to find the local pros their neighbors trust. To focus on this new chapter, the StreetFair customer and pro apps will be decommissioned by May 15th.
StreetFair customer talking points 

These talking points are to help frontline reps handle homeowner inquiries regarding app closure, credit usage, and the move to the Thumbtack app. They focus on maintaining customer trust during the transition.
English talking point
Why is the StreetFair app closing? 
StreetFair has joined Thumbtack to build an even better neighborhood experience called 'Thumbtack Neighbors.' To focus on building this new feature inside the Thumbtack app, the original StreetFair app will be closing on May 15th.
What happens to ongoing projects or credits?
Projects: Ongoing requests and projects are not affected; users should save pro contact information directly.
Credits: Any StreetFair credits must be used for services completed by May 15th.
How can users stay involved?
Users are encouraged to download the Thumbtack app to stay informed. Thumbtack Neighbors is expected to launch in select communities later this year
What happens to my service pro's information?
You'll have access to the StreetFair app until May 15th. We recommend reaching out to your pro now and saving their phone number or email address so you can stay in touch for your ongoing projects after the app closes.
Will my StreetFair account move to Thumbtack?
There isn't an automatic move for your account. We'd love for you to download the Thumbtack app and create a new profile so you're ready when our new 'Neighbors' feature launches in your area this summer!
Q: What is Thumbtack?
A: Thumbtack matches you with local pros. You tell us what’s next on your to-do list and we show you a list of nearby pros who fit the job. With the Thumbtack app, you can compare pro profiles and prices, chat with the pros you like, and (last but not least) check availability and hire pros who fit your projects.
What are the benefits of downloading the Thumbtack app?  
Whether you’ve been using Thumbtack for years or you’re just starting out, our app is all you need to care for your home throughout the year. Download the app for:
On-the-go access. Life doesn’t always happen on schedule. Use the app to create a project whenever and wherever you need to.
Quick messaging. Make phone tag a thing of the past. The app lets you send and receive messages instantly and get your projects handled quickly.
Customizable notifications. Mobile notifications keep you current on your projects. If a pro reaches out, asks a question or finishes a job, you’ll be the first to know.
Personalized home guidance. Create your home profile and get a personalized plan and browse guides with recommended projects based on your unique home and goals. 
Easy project management. Prioritize tasks, set reminders, and manage all of your projects in one place.
Building your team. We’ll save the pros you’ve contacted, so you can easily message  or re-book the pros you trust.
StreetFair pro talking points 
Use these value-driven talking points to help pros with technical questions regarding agreements, CRM integrations, and the evolution of "route density" on the Thumbtack platform.
English talking point
How do I get my customer information before the shutdown?
StreetFair will automatically export and email your customer information to you in a CSV file on May 15th.
What happens to StreetFair Pro subscriptions and billing?
Billing: You will receive a final April invoice for work completed on StreetFair.
Subscriptions: All "Neighborhood Nudges" and mailers have been paused. There will be no further charges for StreetFair Pro customers.
Can I bring my StreetFair recommendations and reviews to Thumbtack?
Currently, verified work history and reviews do not move automatically. However, our teams are actively working on a solution to help you showcase your established reputation on the new platform.
Will my CRM/FSM integration (like Jobber or ServiceTitan) automatically move to Thumbtack?
No, existing StreetFair integrations will not cross over. We recommend connecting your Thumbtack profile to your preferred system now so you are better positioned to share your work with neighborhoods as we roll out new features.
Will Thumbtack honor my existing StreetFair Service Provider agreement?
No. To list your services on Thumbtack and prepare for the Neighbors experience, you will need to review and agree to Thumbtack’s specific Terms of Service.
How can StreetFair Pros join Thumbtack?
If you’re not currently using Thumbtack, we encourage you to download the app and create a profile to list your services. You can also reply directly to the announcement email for help getting set up on the upcoming Thumbtack Neighbors experience.
How do I share my upcoming jobs with neighborhoods on Thumbtack?
Thumbtack is working on developing similar integration and automation enhancements that were available at StreetFair to share your upcoming jobs to the neighborhood. In the meantime,we recommend connecting your CRM (like Jobber or ServiceTitan) to your Thumbtack profile today. We currently have several active partnerships and by connecting now, you ensure your scheduled jobs can be automatically shared with local neighborhoods to help you win more work on the same street. To see partner tools, check out Thumbtack’s Marketplace.  
What is Thumbtack Neighbors?
Thumbtack Neighbors will be a very similar experience for customers and pros to StreetFair, allowing customers to join their neighborhood and request services based on your established reputation there.
Where / When will Thumbtack Neighbors be launched?
We will pilot the Neighbors experience in select communities later this summer. While Thumbtack is available nationwide, we plan to gradually roll out these community features to additional markets following the initial testing phase,.

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) provides Frontline Reps with comprehensive guidance on managing challenging interactions with pros and customers, including de-escalation techniques and the escalation process. It outlines steps for handling various forms of unprofessional conduct and details the unified process for escalating cases to the Advanced Service Team. The KA also covers specialized escalation types, such as executive and social media requests, and provides standardized talking points and resources for Frontline Reps.
Working with users (pros and customers) who are upset can be difficult, as their frustration, fear, or feeling of being unheard can often make interactions feel personal. It's crucial for Support reps to step back during these interactions and remember that the user's frustration is typically directed at the situation or issue impacting their business and livelihood, rather than at the rep personally. 
This knowledge article provides guidance on managing these challenging interactions, including de-escalation techniques, the escalation process, and effective communication strategies. 
Note: Support reps who need help in handling a situation or require additional talking points should contact Advanced Service for support and insight. Steps on internal Requesting Help from the Advanced Service Team (Rep) KA. 
Key points
Support reps should keep the following in mind when handling escalation requests: 
De-escalate First: Always attempt to de-escalate the situation once before escalating to a supervisor/manager. This involves actively listening, empathizing, and using de-escalation techniques as outlined in this KA.
Don't Be Afraid of Tough Conversations: Support Reps have the same authority as Advanced Service in many situations. Do not shy away from addressing difficult issues or setting boundaries.
No Callbacks (Without Approval): Supervisors (Advanced Service) primarily reach out via email. Do not promise a callback. If a pro or customer requests a callback, inform them that any follow-up will likely be via email, but you will note their request.
Phone Call Requests: Note all phone call requests in the case notes. Advanced Service will determine if a call is necessary. Do not promise a callback. If a callback is deemed necessary, a YCBM link will be sent via email to the pro or customer to schedule the call.
Case Notes: Always document all actions, communication, and relevant details in the case notes. Include specific details about the issue, the user’s concerns, and any steps you've taken. 
Empathy is Key: Remember that users may be frustrated, scared, or feeling unheard. Approaching interactions with empathy can significantly improve the situation. Try to understand their perspective and acknowledge their feelings.
Take a Step Back: If a user is upset, remind yourself that their frustration is not directed at you personally. It's about the situation or the issue they're experiencing.
Utilize Slack: If you need help handling a situation, don't hesitate to contact Advanced Service in Slack for talking points, advice, or insights from other team members. Steps on internal Requesting Help from the Advanced Service Team (Rep) KA.
Stay Professional: Maintain a professional demeanor at all times, even when dealing with challenging or upset pros and customers.
Be Mindful of Language: Choose your words carefully and avoid language that could escalate the situation further. Use positive, reassuring language and focus on finding a resolution.
Know When to Disconnect: If a conversation becomes unproductive or abusive, and you've provided all possible help, know when it's appropriate to end the interaction politely and professionally. Steps on internal Unprofessional Behavior, Support Abuse, & Discrimination (Rep) KA.
Navigate Challenging Interactions: How to De-escalate and Work Towards Solution
When dealing with a pro or customer expressing frustration, it’s important for Support reps to allow them to vent without interrupting or assuming. This approach helps users calm down and increases the likelihood that they will listen to a rep's suggestions. 
While these techniques are crucial for de-escalating challenging, frustrated, or upset interactions, they are also highly beneficial for most conversations to foster understanding and positive outcomes. 
To better understand a user's concerns, there are several techniques Support reps can use during the conversation, including:
Empathize: Understand and share user feelings to effectively assist them. Imagine yourself in their situation. Refer to "Empathy: Connecting with User Feelings" for specific talking points.
Be Attentive: Be fully present and avoid distractions. Focus on what the user is saying without thinking about your next response.
Ask Open-Ended Questions: Demonstrate interest in the user's perspective and identify underlying issues. Use probing questions to gain deeper insights. Refer to "Follow-Up / Probing Questions: Gathering More Information" for specific talking points.
Request Clarification: Ensure a clear understanding of the customer's viewpoint. Ask questions to confirm you've grasped their message. Refer to "Follow-Up / Probing Questions: Gathering More Information" for specific talking points.
Paraphrase: Restate user concerns in different words to help them feel heard and understood. Use verbal affirmations like "I hear you" to build rapport. Refer to "Empathy: Connecting with User Feelings" for specific talking points.
Summarize: Confirm your understanding of user concerns to ensure they feel heard and understood, then guide the conversation toward a resolution. Refer to "Resolution: Guiding Towards Solutions" for specific talking points.
Effective Communication Strategies: Talking Points for Various Interactions
While these phrases are particularly helpful when navigating challenging conversations with frustrated users, the following talking points are versatile and can be applied in many other situations to foster positive interactions, build rapport, gather information, and guide conversations toward productive outcomes. These strategies are beneficial for:
Building strong customer and pro relationships
Providing clear and concise information
Resolving inquiries and concerns
Managing expectations effectively
Enhancing overall communication efficiency

▶ Resolution: Guiding Towards Solution

2. Process

Steps: Escalate a case to a supervisor / manager (Rep)
This section details how Support reps handle escalation requests from pros or customers who ask to speak to a supervisor/manager. It also details how to handle escalations from social media, executive requests, and Escalation abuse. 
To address a customer or pro escalation, frontline reps will follow these steps, regardless of the channel (phone, email, or chat):
Assess the situation. Identify the user's core issue and emotional state. Determine if the issue can be resolved with existing knowledge or requires a handoff.
Inform the user. Clearly and empathetically explain that the issue requires specialized support and that their case is being escalated to the appropriate team.
Document the case. In Salesforce, create or update the case with all relevant information, including a detailed summary of the user's request, the conversation history, and the reason for escalation.
Route the case. Use the appropriate internal tools to escalate the case to the Advanced Services (AS) team.
Confirm the handoff. Acknowledge to the user that the case has been successfully handed off and provide any next steps or a timeframe for a follow-up.
Steps: User asks for a supervisor (1st time)
The first time a customer or pro asks for a manager, Support reps should use these de-escalation tactics. Keep in mind that this is one attempt at de-escalation. If the User asks for a manager a second time, Frontline reps should follow the steps in the “Second Request for Escalation” section.
Support reps should be knowledgeable and confident to show the user they can move forward with them towards a resolution.▶ Talking points:
Focus
English talking points
Spanish talking points 
Express confidence in your ability to help
“All our agents are trained to resolve even the toughest of issues. I would love a chance to be able to assist you and resolve this situation
Todos nuestros agentes están entrenados para resolver los problemas más difíciles. Me encantaría tener la oportunidad de poder ayudarlo y resolver esta situación
Acknowledge request for  supervisor while offering help
I am happy to see if a supervisor is available. I know your time is valuable so while we wait to see if a supervisor is available, let me see if there is anything I can help you with or pull up for them.
Con gusto puedo ver si hay un supervisor disponible. Sé que su tiempo es valioso, así que mientras esperamos un supervisor disponible, permíteme ver si hay algo en lo que pueda ayudarlo o buscarles".

▶ Use the de-escalation talking points in the tables below to help you navigate these conversations.
This section outlines talking points designed to help frontline reps move forward and work toward a resolution.
▶ Focus on Understanding and Validating the User
To move towards a resolution, these talking points offer concrete actions, demonstrate commitment, suggest teamwork, and ensure a solution by actively involving the user and taking ownership of the issue.

Focus
Talking Point
Acknowledge request and offer help
"I understand you need to escalate, and I'm here to help find a solution."
"I understand you've reached a point where you feel you need to escalate this, and I want to assure you that I'm here to help and find a resolution that works for you."
Acknowledge feelings and offer to help
"I recognize your frustration and want to help understand and solve this issue."
"I recognize that you've experienced frustration with this issue, and I want to personally work with you to understand the full scope of the problem and find a solution."
Express empathy and listen
"This sounds difficult. I'm here to listen and fully understand your concerns."
"I can see that this situation has been difficult for you, and I want to take the time to fully understand your concerns."
Validate experience and offer help
"I see this has been inconvenient. I want to help get this resolved for you."
"It's clear that this issue has caused you considerable inconvenience, and I want to personally intervene to help get it resolved."
▶ Focus on Action and Collaboration with User
To move towards a resolution, these talking points offer concrete actions, demonstrate commitment, suggest teamwork, and ensure a solution by actively involving the user and taking ownership of the issue.

Focus
Talking Point
Offer concrete action
"Let's look at this together and find all possible solutions."
"I'd like to take a closer look at your situation and work with you directly to explore all available options for resolution."
Show commitment and request information

"I'm committed to finding a satisfactory outcome for you. Could you please provide me with [specific information or details] so I can better help you?"
Suggest teamwork
"Let's work together on this. I'd like to discuss this with you directly."
"Let's work together to address this. I'd like to schedule a time to discuss this further with you directly."
Ensure resolution
"I'll ensure this is resolved. I need more information to work with you on next steps."
"I want to personally ensure that this matter is resolved to your satisfaction. To do that, I'd like to gather more information and collaborate with you on the next steps."
Take ownership
"I'll take ownership and find a solution. To do this, I need to..."
"I am going to take ownership of this issue, and will work to find a solution. In order to do this effectively, I would like to..."
▶ Focusing on Empathy and Taking Responsibility to Resolve Matter
These talking points provide phrases to apologize for difficulties, show understanding, express remorse, and demonstrate a willingness to personally investigate and resolve the matter, reinforcing a sense of responsibility and care.

Description
Talking Point
Apologize and offer help
"I apologize for the difficulties. I want to personally help you."
"I sincerely apologize for the difficulties you've experienced. I want to personally help resolve this matter for you."
Show understanding and commitment
"I understand, and I will investigate and find a solution."
"I understand what you’re saying, and I want to assure you that I will personally investigate this matter and work diligently to find a solution."
Express remorse and willingness to help
"I'm sorry about this. I'll do everything I can to help."
"I am sorry this has been your experience, I am going to do everything I can to help resolve this for you."
For additional talking points, frontline reps can reference the User asks for a supervisor (1st time) talking points below.

User asks for a supervisor (2nd time) 

The second time a user asks for a supervisor, Frontline reps should follow the steps below:
Submit a request to the Advanced Service Team (AST) in Slack.
Navigate to the #service_global_help-and-escalations Slack channel.
Use the applicable keywords below to trigger the workflow.
Escalations (All Escal options)
Escalation Refunds
Escalation Reviews
Escalation Others
Fill out the form with all necessary details.
Note: Reps should refer to the internal < Requesting Help from the Advanced Service Team (Rep) > KA for guidance on the applicable workflows.
Let the user know that a supervisor will contact them via email within 24 business hours. 
Do not promise a callback: Supervisors will always reach out via email. If the pro is specifically requesting a phone call, please note that request in the case notes. The Advanced Service team will determine if it’s a situation where a phone call is necessary. 
Do not make any promises: Let the user know that the supervisor knows they prefer a phone call. If Advanced Service decides a phone call is appropriate, the user will receive an email with a YCBM link, so they will still want to watch for an email.
Before transferring the case to the Ops Consultant Case Queue:
Notate the account.
Save your notes and leave the case open
Transfer the case to the Advanced Service queue. (Steps on the internal Salesforce: Case Navigation and Management (Rep) KA)
Advanced Service will contact the pro or customer via email within 24 business hours.
Steps: Handling Executive Escalations
)
 
Occasionally, a user will reach out to a Thumbtack executive directly through email, LinkedIn or other forms of social media. Executive escalations specifically refer to situations where a user contacts a Thumbtack executive (senior leadership) directly. Executives' roles may include: Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Chief People Officer (CPO), Chief Product Officer (CPO), Chief Technology Offer (CTO), Chief Legal Officer (CLO), Chief Marketing Officer (CMO), Chief Commercial Officer (CCO), and Chief Financial Officer (CFO).
If contacted by a pro requesting to speak to an executive directly, reps will follow these steps:
Send Kiko Cabantug or Zaida Cortez a direct Slack message explaining the situation.
Include the case number, the name of the user you are speaking with, and any other helpful information related to the interaction.
These cases will be assigned to an Advanced Service team member to contact the user directly. 
Steps: Social Media Escalations
)
A user may post on a Thumbtack social media page, such as Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, or LinkedIn, which should be escalated. These escalations can stem from upset pros or customers regarding issues like a public complaint, dissatisfaction with an initial resolution, a viral complaint, or a perceived unfairness. 
Most of the time, these cases will go directly to the Trust and Safety Social media team. If a user contacts support with this type of concern, Frontline reps should reach out in the #xfnc_depts_help for help.
Steps: Other escalation types
)
Beyond standard escalations to supervisors or managers, there are specific processes for handling other types of escalations related to Trust & Safety incidents, potential threats, website or Admin outages, and urgent bugs. This section outlines where to find the appropriate resources and guidance for each of these situations, ensuring that Support reps can direct these issues to the correct teams for resolution.
For Trust and Safety (T&S) escalations and incidents, see the internal Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA
For any instance where a user states they’ll cause physical harm, damage, intimidation, or any other hostile actions towards you, a Thumbtack office, or an employee of Thumbtack, see the internal Identifying and Responding to Threats (Reps) KA.
For website or Admin outage escalations, see the internal Bugs KA.
For urgent bug escalations, see the internal Bugs KA. 

Steps: How to document a completed escalation (Advanced Service)

To ensure proper documentation of a completed escalation, Advanced Service will follow these steps:
Add notes in Salesforce. Add detailed notes to the Salesforce case with the specific theme: P>Ops>Support>Escalations>Escalations Support.
Copy notes to the tracker. Copy the case notes and paste them into the 2025 So_Global Escalation tracker.
Add a checkmark emoji. Place a checkmark emoji (✅) on the original Slack thread to indicate that the case has been completed.
Steps: How to handle Escalation Abuse (Advanced Service)
IMPORTANT: This process is exclusively for Advanced Service. The email templates and processes should not be followed by Support reps.
This section outlines the process for handling escalation abuse, which occurs when a user repeatedly tries to escalate a topic to a different supervisor or team after it has already been addressed by the Advanced Services (AS) team, or is an issue that cannot be escalated (See internal Trust and Safety incidents (pro) (customer).
To handle a case of escalation abuse, Advanced Service will follow these steps:
Assess the user's intent. Confirm that the user is attempting to re-escalate an issue that the Advanced Services (AS) team has already addressed and provided a final decision on.
Determine if a flag is appropriate. Only apply a service abuse flag in cases where the user is trying to get a different outcome on a closed issue. Do not apply the flag if the user is simply frustrated or if a final decision has not been reached by the AS team.
Apply the service abuse flag. If the situation meets the criteria, apply the service abuse flag to the user's account in the internal system.
Document the case. Record any actions taken and the reason for applying the flag in the case notes, adhering to the internal documentation process.
3. Talking points
)
User asks for a supervisor (1st time)
)
▶ Summary:
This section outlines talking points for the first time a user asks for a supervisor. on body...
When a user asks to speak with a supervisor or manager for the first time, Frontline reps can use the following talking points: 

Focus
English talking point
Spanish talking point
Manage expectations about a supervisor's ability to provide a different answer
"I'm happy to see if someone is available. However, I want to be upfront that they will provide the same answer I have. Would you still like me to see who is available?"

"I understand you'd like to speak with a supervisor. I can certainly connect you, but I want to be transparent and let you know that they will follow the same process and policies that I have. I'm fully equipped to help you with this issue, and I'd be happy to go over it with you again to see if we can find a solution together."
“Entiendo que desea hablar con un supervisor. Con gusto puedo ponerle en contacto; sin embargo, quiero ser transparente y avisarle que seguirán el mismo proceso y las mismas políticas que yo. Yo tengo las herramientas necesarias para ayudarle con este caso y, si le parece, puedo revisarlo nuevamente para ver si encontramos una solución en conjunto.

To offer to forward the email thread to a supervisor if the user still wishes to proceed after clarification.

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) outlines the Smart Match program, where pros receive and are auto-charged for leads outside their exact preferences that our lead matching system predicts are a strong fit. It details the experiment specifics, the pro experience for opting out and requesting refunds, and provides talking points for Frontline Reps.
IMPORTANT: Smart Match has rolled out nationwide. It began as a market-based test in Detroit (V1), expanded to the top 300 markets (V2), and is now available to eligible pros in all markets as of June 17, 2026. See the Updates section for the full rollout history.
What are smart match leads
Smart matching automatically sends and charges pros for leads that fall slightly outside their defined job type preferences when Thumbtack’s lead matching system predicts a strong fit. These are called “smart match” leads.

To maintain quality, Thumbtack ensures that most of the leads a pro receives will still match their job preferences (targeting). [Internal note: 80% or more of a pro's total leads will still be exact matches. Reps must not share this specific number with pros or customers, as the real percentage can change.]
Why did Thumbtack launch smart match nationwide
Internal why: The goal is to help pros get more jobs and better leads by looking beyond their specific targeting preferences.  It aims to test automatic charging for expanded matches paired with a generous refund policy to improve match quality over time. Additionally, Thumbtack uses pro feedback on these matches to improve future targeting.
External pro facing why: More leads, smarter targeting. Starting [x], you may get leads outside of your exact preferences through our AI-powered matching when we predict there is a strong fit. And if we get it wrong, we’ll refund you.
How smart match leads work
Eligible pros are automatically opted in to receive smart match leads and charged for these expanded matches, whose settings default to off and must be manually turned on.
Multi-business accounts are excluded from the program and will not see the Smart Match toggle.
Pros can decline these leads for a refund if the job type is not a fit and can opt out of the program at any time.
[Internal note: These leads are auto-charged but are priced at a 50% discount for their request category and market. To build trust during the launch phase, Thumbtack is operating in a high-trust mode. If a pro claims a lead is not a fit for their business and did not follow the refund flow in product, reps with refund access will approve all refund requests for “Not what I do.” ] 
Updates
Smart Match nationwide launch
As of June 17, 2026, Smart Match is available to eligible pros nationwide. Previously the program was limited to Detroit (V1) and the top 300 markets (V2). 
Eligibility rules are unchanged: 
standard pros are auto-opted in
single-business managed, national, and integrated pros default to off
multi-business accounts are excluded.
Naming details: 
External name: Smart Match program, Smart matching or “smart match” leads. 
Internal name: Smart Match aka ‘Carrot’ or Smart charging 
What this means for rep support
A pro in any market may now be in Smart Match. Don't assume a pro is excluded based on location.
Continue to confirm a lead is a Smart Match using the Admin fields in How to identify a smart match lead in Admin before applying Smart Match refund guidance.
The refund experience is unchanged from V2 (see Refunds for smart match leads below).
Rollout history (V1 → V2 → nationwide)
V1 — Jan 20, 2026 (Detroit): Launched to ~1,775 pros in Detroit. Comms sent Dec 18, 2025.
Comms — April 2, 2026: Comms sent to V2 markets (and nationwide)
V2 — May 4, 2026 (Detroit): V1 ended and transitioned to V2 in Detroit.
V2 — May 11, 2026 (top 300 markets): Expanded to the top 300 markets nationwide, including Detroit. Comms sent April 2, 2026.
Nationwide —  June 17, 2026: Available to eligible pros in all markets.
▶ Comms sent for V2 and nationwide launches (April 2, 2026)
Thumbtack sent email communications to in-market pros (V2 in the top 300 markets) regarding this program on April 2, 2026.
[Internal note: Not all pros who received the email will see the expanded matches.]
▶ Email sent to standard pros (auto-opted in)
Image below: An email sent to pros letting them know they can get more leads with refund protection. The email explains:
Starting in May 2026, pros may get leads outside their exact preferences when AI predicts a strong fit,
The refund guarantee for incorrect matches.

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ Email sent to national, managed, and integrated pros (option to opt in)
Image below: An email sent to pros letting them know they can turn Smart Matches on in their services page. The email explains:
Starting in May 2026, pros will have a new setting that can help them get more leads outside of their exact preferences when Thumbtack sees a strong fit for the pro’s business. 
The refund guarantee for incorrect matches.

[Image: rtaImage]

How smart match is different from Smarter lead matching

Smart match leads and Smarter lead matching (NDFP) are easy to confuse because both use AI to match leads, but they are fundamentally different programs targeting different problems:


Smart Match
Smarter Lead Matching
What it does
Sends pros leads slightly outside their existing targeting preferences when AI predicts a strong fit
Replaces category-based targeting entirely with AI-learned preferences at the trade level
Who it applies to
Pros nationwide
Pros in the Baltimore, Maryland DMA and Washington, D.C. (Hagerstown) DMA only
How pros are matched
Pro keeps their existing targeting — Smart Match just expands slightly beyond it
Pro no longer manages categories — AI learns preferences from activity and feedback
Pricing
Standard exact lead prices with 50% discount on Smart Match leads
Existing pros: Opt-out flow at bottom of Services page requiring feedback
New pros: No opt out option
Opt out
Toggle on Services page
Opt-out flow at bottom of Services page requiring feedback
Refunds
Automatic when pro declines and selects Not what I do
Automatic when pro declines and selects Not what I do
Performance insights
Available
Not available
How to identify a Smart Match lead in Admin
Reps can verify whether a lead is a Smart Match using two different pages in Admin depending on what they are investigating. 
Negotiations page: Use the Negotiations page syndication type when investigating whether a lead was a Smart Match.
Refund request details page: For reps with refund access, use the Refund Request Details page when processing a refund to confirm the lead qualifies for Smart Match refund treatment.
On the Negotiations page
Check the Syndication type field: 

Syndication type
What it means
TARGETING_V2_NOT_ENROLLED_AUTO_CHARGE
Smart Match lead — auto-charged expanded match
▶ Expand to see what it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

On the Refund Request Details page
Check the “Is smart charge bid? (aka carrot test)” field:
Yes — this is a Smart Match lead and the refund should be approved if the pro selected Not what I do
No — this is a standard lead and standard refund policy applies
▶ Expand to see what it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Frontline reps can use the Negotiations page to confirm whether a lead was a Smart Match. For reps with refund access, use the Refund Request Details page when processing a refund to confirm the lead qualifies for Smart Match refund treatment.
[Internal note: If a pro mentions "Smart Match," reps should ensure they're speaking about the correct experience. Do not confuse this experiment with "New Deal for Pros: Smarter Lead Matching (Pro)" For a detailed comparison between Smart Match leads and other active AI initiatives, reps should refer to the internal centralized Active AI Matching Experiments (Rep) KA.] 

How to share pro feedback about smart matching 

Submit all feedback related to the Smart Match experience using the existing feedback item in Salesforce: [Targeting] User Feedback Regarding Smart Match Leads

Talking point: “Your feedback is crucial in helping us build a smarter system. Do you mind sharing details about what you do or don't like about the feature?"
2. Pro experience
The following section details the differences between the baseline experience and the Smart Match experiment experience for pros.
Benefits of Smart Match leads
Frontline reps can use the following benefits when a pro asks why they are receiving Smart Match leads or needs reassurance about the experience.
More opportunities a pro might have missed
Our smart matching system looks beyond your current targeting settings and considers your full profile, past work, and experience to find jobs that are a strong fit for your business — even if they fall slightly outside the categories you have selected. This means you could win jobs you would never have seen otherwise.
Pros are protected if it is not a fit
Even though these leads are automatically charged, you are not stuck paying for jobs that are not right for you. If you receive a Smart Match lead that is not something you do, just decline it and select Not what I do — we will refund you and use your feedback to send you better matches going forward.
Pros stay in control
If you decide Smart Matching is not right for your business, you can turn it off anytime from your Services page. You are always in control of whether you want these leads.
How smart matching works 
Before Smart Match, pros only received leads that exactly matched their defined job type preferences and were automatically charged for them.
With Smart Match, pros still receive mostly exact match leads.* The difference is that pros may also receive a small number of leads that fall slightly outside their defined job type preferences when the lead matching system predicts a strong fit based on their profile, past work, and experience. Pros are and are auto-charged for these “smart match” leads. To maintain quality, the system ensures that most of a pro's leads will still be exact matches.
* [Internal note: At least 80% of a pro's total leads will still be exact matches. Do not share this specific percentage with pros or customers — the actual percentage can change over time]
Rep note — pro list order: Pros appear in customer search results in a stratified order: Exact Match pros are listed first, followed by Smart match (expanded match) pros, then Budget Overserve pros. 
Who receives smart match leads 
Most pros are automatically opted in to Smart matching and will be auto-charged for smart match leads. However, enrollment works differently depending on the pro's account type:

Account type
Default
Can change?
Standard single-business pros
On — auto-charged
Can opt out anytime
Pros with an app integration, managed account, or national account working with a managed account
Off
Must manually opt in
Multi-business accounts
Excluded
Cannot participate at this time.

How pros manage smart matching
Pros control smart match leads through the “Smart matching” toggle on their Services page:
Toggle on — pro receives smart match leads and is auto-charged for them
Toggle off — pro no longer receives smart match leads
Pros can turn this toggle on or off at any time. Reps should only suggest opting out as a last resort — the preferred path for a mismatched lead is to decline it and select Not what I do to get a refund and help the system learn.
▶ What the Smart matching toggle looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

What the pro sees when they click "Learn more."

[Image: rtaImage]

How pros know it's a smart match lead 
Pros can identify a smart match lead in two places:
In the Jobs tab (lead card)
The lead card shows a purple Smart match pill alongside other lead details like "Only picked you" and the respond-by timer. This is how the pro first sees that a lead is a Smart Match before opening it.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

In the job details page
When the pro opens the lead they see a purple Smart match banner at the top with the message: "We think you're a good fit for this job. If not, just decline the lead and we'll refund you. If you don't want these types of leads anymore, opt out in services."
Below the job details the pro also sees a "Not the right fit? View options" link which is one of two ways to start the refund flow — see the Automatic refund flow section below.
▶ What the banner details look like

[Image: rtaImage]

Rep note — app integrations: Pros managing leads through a third-party app integration cannot see the Smart Match pill or banner in their external platform. They must log into the Thumbtack app directly to view it and to request a refund for a mismatched lead.
How the AI learns from lead activity
If a pro accepts a Smart Match lead and completes the job, the system does not automatically update their job type preferences. Preferences are only updated when the pro selects Not what I do as their decline reason and confirm the AI-generated preference suggestion.
Refer to the Automated Refund Flow above to learn more.
3. Refund policy on smart match leads
Smart Match leads are auto-charged, but pros can receive a refund if a lead is for a job type outside their skillset. 
There are two paths to a refund: automatic and manual.
Automatic refunds (primary path)
Automatic refunds for smart match leads are available only before the pro replies. Once the pro clicks Reply, the decline option is removed and the manual path applies instead.
The pro selects Decline → Yes, decline lead → Not what I do → briefly explains why the job type is not something their business does → answers AI clarifying questions. The refund is issued automatically when the flow is complete. See the full flow below. 
[Internal note: Smart Match leads are processed as exact match leads, meaning Front Desk (FD) will auto-respond to them using the pro's custom Initial Response message. However, the pro remains eligible for a refund if they decline the lead as 'Not what I do,' regardless of whether FD has auto-responded.]
[Internal note: These refunds are different from LLM automated refunds, where the pro submitted a refund request for a Job Outside Preferences or Not hired, and unresponsive customers. Refer to the Lead Refunds (Pro) KA to learn more.]
Automated refund flow: Pro declines lead that isn’t the right fit 
When a pro receives a Smart Match lead that is not a good fit for their skill set, declining it and selecting “Not what I do” does two things:
A refund is issued automatically and
our smart matching system learns what kinds of jobs are not a fit for that pro, improving future matches over time.
Here’s what that workflow looks like: 
Enter refund flow: On the lead, the pro either clicks Reply or Decline. 
▶ Confirm decline: Tapping Declined opens a “Decline this job?” where the pro clicks Yes, decline lead.[Image: rtaImage]
▶ Select decline reason: On the "Why did you decline?" screen, the pros select Not what I do (lead that doesn’t fit their job types.). The screen notes: "This private feedback is used to learn what types of leads you want in the future."[Image: rtaImage]
Rep note: Only Not what I do triggers the Smart Match refund and AI learning flow. If the pro selects "Location" or "Not available," they will be given options to update their travel areas or availability instead of the refund flow below.
Explain why: After selecting Not what I do a text field appears. The pro is required to explain why the job type is not something their business does — minimum 10 characters. The pro taps Next. 
▶ AI clarifying questions: Based on the pro's explanation the AI generates specific yes/no clarifying question(s). The screen notes: "This private feedback is used to learn what types of leads you want in the future." The pro answers and taps Next.[Image: rtaImage]
▶ Confirm preference: The AI generates a preference statement based on the pro's explanation and clarifying answer — for example: "Does not do garbage disposal installs." The screen reads: "We'll save this job detail and refund the lead you just declined." The pro taps Yes or No.[Image: rtaImage]
▶ Yes — the job detail is saved to help the system learn what types of leads to avoid sending in the future, and the refund is issued automatically.[Image: rtaImage]
No — job details are not saved. The system displays "Thanks for sharing. You may also be eligible for a refund."
Manual review approvals 
If the automatic path was not completed — for example because the pro already replied to the customer before realizing the job was not a fit — the pro can contact support to request a refund. Reps with refund access must approve the request if the pro is indicating the Smart Match lead was for a job type outside their skillset, including when:
The pro selects "Not what I do" but leaves a blank, short, or vague written explanation (e.g., just typing "Appliances").
The pro submits a refund request under Job Outside Preferences (JOP) without further explanation.
The pro says they don't offer the service in their refund request details, even if they chose a different reason like “Other.”
The pro realized the job was a mismatch after talking or messaging the customer (automatic refunds do not occur post-reply, so these must be manually approved).
The pro provides mixed feedback (e.g., complaining about the lead price but also noting the job was not a fit).
Non-Eligible Reasons
When a pro enters the refund flow by clicking “Decline” they are asked why they are declining. If the pro selects "Location" or "Not available," they will be given options to update their travel areas or availability instead of the refund flow below.
The Smart Match refund policy covers job type mismatches only (“ Not what I do”). Declining for any other reason, like the following do not qualify for Smart Match refunds and follow standard refund policies:
Travel area issues (location)
Schedule conflicts (not available)
Price concerns (low job value)
Customer unresponsiveness
Not being hired
Refer to the Lead Refunds (Pro)  KA to learn more

4. Process
Steps: How to turn the Smart matching setting on or off (Pro) 
Pro steps: To turn off smart matching, pros will follow the steps in the What are Smart Match leads? – Thumbtack Help article.
Pros have the ability to turn off and on the Smart matching toggle on their Services page at any time and only receive exact match leads.
Reps note: refer to the Who receives smart match leads section above to learn more about who is auto opted in.
▶ What the “Smart matching” toggle looks like:
The banner says “AI-powered matching that gets smarter over time. Get refunds for job types you don’t do.” 
What the pro sees when they click Learn More.
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
Steps: How to request a refund for a Smart Match lead (Pro)
A pro can request a refund for a Smart Match lead that is not a fit for their business (e.g., they don't perform that specific job type).  When a pro declines a lead for “Not what I do”, they'll answer a quick survey to provide feedback. This feedback helps Thumbtack understand the types of jobs the pro does want, which is then used to adjust their Smart Matching preferences for future leads.
Pro steps: If a Smart Match lead is not a good fit because it’s not what they do, pros will follow the steps in the What are Smart Match leads? – Thumbtack Help article to decline the lead and request a refund.
Steps: How to help a pro with Smart match leads (Rep)
To handle complaints or concerns about Smart Match leads, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:
Acknowledge and validate: Use empathy to address the pro's concern about receiving leads outside their targeting. Keep in mind that most leads will still match the pro’s targeting preferences.
▶ Talking point“I understand how frustrating it is to get leads that don’t match what you selected.”
Investigate the lead: On the Negotiations page in Admin, check the Syndication type field.
If it shows TARGETING_V2_NOT_ENROLLED_AUTO_CHARGE — this is a Smart Match lead. Continue with the steps below.
If it shows anything else — this is not a Smart Match lead. Investigate other potential targeting issues.
▶ See what it looks like below:

[Image: rtaImage]

Explain the feature: Tell the pro that Thumbtack may occasionally send leads outside their preferences if our lead matching system predicts a strong fit based on the pro’s experience, profile, and past work.
▶ Talking point“We recently introduced Smart Matching, which looks beyond your targeting and considers your overall experience, profile, and past work to find relevant opportunities you might not have seen otherwise.”
Help the pro get a refund if the lead isn't a fit: 
If the pro has not yet replied to the customer (hasn’t already clicked Reply), guide them to decline the lead and select Not what I do to receive an automatic refund. (See Steps: How to request a refund for a smart match lead (Pro) for more details).
▶ Talking point“If the lead isn’t something you do, you can decline it and select “Not what I do” — the refund will be approved automatically. You’re not stuck paying for leads that aren’t a fit.”
If the pro already replied to the customer or the automatic refund did not issue: The automatic refund flow is only available before the pro replies. if the pro already clicked  “Reply” on the lead  or the refund went to manual review, reps with refund access should manually process the refund:
Navigate to the “Refund Request Details” page.
Confirm that “Is smart charge bid? (aka carrot test)” shows Yes.
Manually approve the refund if the pro indicates the job isn’t a good fit ("Not what I do")  — regardless of the refund request reasons. Always give the pro the benefit of the doubt during the launch phase. Reps can refer to the ”Not what I do” refund requests (launch-phase manual override rules) section above for more details.]
Offer opt-out (last resort): If the pro is still frustrated and and does not want to continue requesting refunds for these leads, walk them through how to turn off the Smart Match toggle in their Services page. 
▶ Talking point“The goal is to provide you with more opportunities without adding risk — you stay in control. But, if you’re getting too many leads that don’t fit your needs, and no longer want to request refunds for them, you can turn Smart Matching off anytime in your Services page.”
Capture feedback: Submit all feedback related to the Smart Match experience using the existing feedback item in Salesforce: [Targeting] User Feedback Regarding Smart Match Leads
▶ Talking point"Your feedback is crucial in helping us build a smarter system. Do you mind sharing details about what you don't like about the feature?"
4. Talking points

This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros in the Smart Match experiment about their leads and refunds. Use these talking points to ensure consistent and accurate messaging.

General Smart match inquiries


English talking point
Spanish talking point 
Q: Why am I getting charged for leads outside of my job preferences?
Q: ¿Por qué se me cobra por prospectos que están fuera de mis preferencias de trabajo?
A: You’re receiving these leads because you’re part of our Smart Match program. To help you get more of the jobs you want, our smart matching system looks beyond your job preferences to find customers that we believe are still a strong fit for your business. 
[If the pro expresses frustration]: I understand how frustrating it is to get leads that don’t match what you selected. We recently introduced Smart Matching to help find more jobs for you based on your profile and past work, even if they fall outside your targeting.
If a Smart Match lead isn't a fit for what you do, you can request a refund and it will be approved. You aren't stuck paying for leads that aren't a fit.
A: Usted recibe estos prospectos porque forma parte de nuestro programa Smart Match. Para ayudarle a conseguir más de los trabajos que quiere, nuestro sistema de emparejamiento inteligente busca más allá de sus preferencias de trabajo para encontrar clientes que creemos que todavía son una buena opción para su negocio.
[If the pro expresses frustration]: Entiendo lo frustrante que es recibir prospectos que no coinciden con lo que usted seleccionó. Hace poco presentamos Smart Match para ayudarle a encontrar más trabajos basados en su perfil y trabajos anteriores, incluso si están fuera de sus preferencias. 
Si un prospecto de Smart Match no es adecuado para lo que usted hace, puede solicitar un reembolso y este será aprobado. Usted no tiene que pagar por prospectos que no sean adecuados.    
Q: I don't recall being told about this smart match program! Did you notify pros about this experiment?
Q: No recuerdo que me hayan dicho sobre este programa de Smart Match. ¿Les avisaron a los profesionales?
A:
V1 (Detroit): Yes, we sent an email on December 18, 2025 with the subject line "You’re in: Smart Match beta program. More leads, less work." The email explained that you might receive leads outside your exact preferences when our AI predicts a strong fit, and that these leads are refundable if they aren't a match.
V2 (Detroit & Top 300 Markets): Yes, we sent an email on April 2, 2026. The email explained that you might receive leads outside your exact preferences when our AI predicts a strong fit, and that these leads are refundable if they aren't a match.

Más prospectos, menos trabajo"). El correo explicaba que usted podría recibir prospectos fuera de sus preferencias de trabajo exactas cuando nuestra IA prediga una gran compatibilidad, y que estos prospectos son reembolsables si no coinciden.

Q: Will this change my budget?
Q: ¿Esto va a cambiar mi presupuesto?
A: No, your weekly budget and lead prices will stay the same.

Job type preferences and refunds 


English talking point

Q: Can I get a refund for these leads?
Q: ¿Puedo recibir un reembolso por estos prospectos?
A: Yes. If our smart matching system sends you a lead that doesn't fit your skill set, decline the lead and tell us why. We’ll refund you and use your feedback to find the right jobs for your business.

Q: How can I tell Thumbtack that I don't want a Smart Match lead?
Q: ¿Cómo le digo a Thumbtack que no quiero un prospecto de Smart Match?
A: When you receive a new smart match lead that isn't a fit for your skill set, you can indicate that you can’t do the job. If you decline the job and select ‘Not what I do’, the system will trigger clarifying questions. This confirms the job type is a mismatch for you, and we’ll refund the lead you just declined.

Si rechaza el trabajo y selecciona Not what I do ("No es lo que hago"), el sistema activará preguntas de aclaración. Esto confirma que el tipo de trabajo no es el adecuado para usted y le reembolsaremos el prospecto que acaba de rechazar.
Q: I didn't change my job preferences. Why does it say I do [Job Type]?
Q: Yo no cambié mis preferencias de trabajo. ¿Por qué dice que yo hago [tipo de trabajo]?
A: This can happen when you decline a smart match lead and select "Not what I do." If you answer the follow-up questions and confirm a suggestion, our smart matching system saves that detail for future leads. It’s constantly learning about what types of leads to send you (or not send you).
You can always review and update your smart matches at any time from your Services page.

El sistema aprende constantemente qué tipos de prospectos enviarle (o no enviarle).

Usted siempre puede revisar y actualizar sus preferencias de Smart Match en cualquier momento desde su página de Services (“Servicios”).

Opt out of smart match 


English talking point
Spanish talking point 
Q: I don't like the smart match feature, can I opt out?
Q: No me gusta Smart Match. ¿Puedo salirme?
A: Our goal is to give you more opportunities without adding risk — you stay in control through our easy refund process. However, if you'd prefer to stop receiving these altogether, you can turn this feature off anytime in your Services page.

[Reps should ask the pro]: "Your feedback is crucial in helping us build a smarter system that truly understands the work you do. Do you mind sharing details about what you don't like about the feature?"

Slack and Common Support Channels (Rep)

Contents
Overview
