Resources
1. Overview
Slack is a team-collaboration tool. Frontline reps at Thumbtack use Slack to connect with coworkers, stay informed about company happenings, engage in active conversations outside of meetings, and participate in local communities, ERGs, and other groups.
This Knowledge Article serves as a guide for frontline rep on effectively using Slack, outlining available channels, distinguishing between public and private channels, and providing best practices for communication. It also details how frontline reps can get help in Slack, including using Slack Workflows and the Assist app for Jira ticketing.
Dos and Don’ts
Frontline reps should follow Slack these best practices:
Do use threads as much as possible. Threads are especially helpful for organizing comments in busy channels. Frontline reps can post in a thread by clicking the “Reply in thread” icon. 
Do find the right channel for a message. Check a channel's history to see if it’s the right fit for your question.
Don’t use @here, @[group], @[channel]. Using the tags above will notify everyone in a particular channel and should only be used for smaller group conversations.
Don’t @here to remind people to come to a meeting
Don’t @here to ask advice or share something personal
Don’t use @here, @channel, or @group unless it’s an emergency

Frontline reps should review Slack’s official etiquette guide for more information.
Public vs. Private Channels
Slack channels can be set as public channels or private channels. Public channels are typically company wide and private channels are typically for team chats, department level channels, etc. 
Anything posted in a public channel is visible and searchable by everyone at Thumbtack. These channels have a pound sign # next to it. Thumbtack employees can join or leave public channels whenever they choose. 
Private channels (also known as locked channels) are for sensitive or exclusive conversations and are marked with a padlock symbol 🔒. To join a private channel, you’ll need to be added by someone in that private channel. 
The table below lists Slack channels commonly used by frontline reps.
2. Slack Channels 
This section outlines commonly used Slack channels by Frontline Reps. Each channel is referenced through internal knowledge articles, with links provided for easy access. Reps should always consult these related articles before posting in the channels to ensure adherence to guidelines and best practices.
IT help Channel:
#helpdesk: This channel should be used rarely.
Channel purpose:  
For immediate help with internal tools, network access, or lockout issues. 
For non-urgent issues, submit a ticket via the  TackIT Help Desk Portal.
Used by: Everyone
Bugs Channel:
#bugs:
Channel purpose:  For TSL and TPH to flag urgent bugs and get help with bug reports.
Used by: All frontline reps
Internal knowledge article: Bugs and Bug Reports (Rep)
Research Channels:
#research-incentives-questions:
Purpose: To ask questions about participant incentives or gift cards.
Used by: All frontline reps
#experience-research:
Purpose: To keep the organization updated on new research findings, trending updates, and important research events.
Used by: All frontline reps
Internal knowledge article: User Research (Pro) (Customer)
Product Channels:
#product_ops:
Channel purpose: Open channel to coordinate anything with the product ops team. Open to all XFN partners and most non-private product ops coordination encouraged in this channel.
Used by: Everyone
#product-updates:
Channel purpose:  Product Ops to communicate product changes, timelines, resources, and news from the Product Marketing Managers (PMM) team regarding product experiments and rollouts.
Used by: Everyone
Internal knowledge article: Current running experiments (Rep) 
Partnerships and Front Desk Channels:
#partnerships-global:
Channel purpose: For general updates and Q&A on partnerships (supply integrations, Thumbtack partner integrations). Not for credit grant requests.
Used by: All frontline reps
Internal knowledge article
Supply API Integration Partnerships
Supply Integration Activation And Troubleshooting (Rep) ( Pro)
#front-desk-support:
Channel purpose: To submit Front Desk requests and inquiries.
Used by: Everyone
Internal knowledge article:  Front Desk (Pro) 
Refunds and Payments Channels:
#refundsflex-tph-tsl:
Channel purpose: For following up on existing refund work tickets. Reps are welcome to check this channel first if disputes or appeals can still be reversed. However, the channel's authority is limited. If not, reps should reach out through #service_global_help-and-escalation
Used by: Support reps
Internal knowledge article: Lead Refunds (Pro) 
#marketplace-pay-support:
Channel purpose: For submitting inquiries about customer-to-pro payments and Stripe investigations through the "Request Pay Support" Slack workflow.
Used by: Support reps
Internal knowledge article: Support for Payment Related Inquiries
Sales Channels:
#sales_am_inbound:
Purpose: For transfer requests and questions for Sales. 
CS to Sales Handoff 
Sales Callback Request Form 
Note: The #sales_am_inbound Slack channel should not be used to contact the managed accounts team. Frontline reps will Slack the pro’s account manager directly. 
Used by: Everyone
Internal knowledge article: 
Sales and Prepaid Packages (Pro)
Managed Accounts (Pro)
Support & Cross-Functional Help Channels:
#service_global_help-and-escalations (private channel)
Channel purpose: For general questions about refunds, reviews, Big Query lookups, Stripe lookups, and other help-related issues when other resources are insufficient, or to escalate cases to the Advanced Service team
Used by: Support reps
Internal knowledge article:
Requesting Help from the Advanced Service Team (Rep)
#xfnc_depts_help:
Channel purpose: Ask the Advanced Service team questions, including for failed or blocked payment issues.
Used by: Other departments (Sales, Success, etc.)
#service_unprofessional_and_ndp_reports: Report incidents of unprofessional behavior, support abuse, or discrimination from users, and to manage the follow-up actions related to these reports.
Used by: Support reps
Internal knowledge article: Unprofessional Behavior, Support Abuse, & Discrimination (Rep)
Trust and Safety Channels:
Frontline reps can use dedicated Slack channels to connect with the Trust and Safety team for various inquiries. These channels include:
#idhelp-questions:
Channel purpose: For questions related to ID help, licensing, and name changes.
Internal knowledge articles:
ID Help questions: Internal ID Help Guide (Pro) (Customer) KA
Licensing questions: Internal License Credentials (Pro) KA
Name change questions: 
Internal Account Information: Manage Account Settings and Status (Pro) KA
Internal Account Info (Customer) KA
#background-check-questions:
Channel purpose: For questions related to background checks.
Internal knowledge article: Background Checks KA 
#ts-incident-ops-questions:
Channel purpose: For inquiries about account status, holds, deletions, reinstatements, and general Trust and Safety concerns.
Internal knowledge article: Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) 
#ts-proactive-ops-questions:
Channel purpose: For questions concerning proactive operations. 
Internal knowledge article: 
Contact Avoidance (Pro) KA 
Removed or Banned Users (Pro) (Customer) KA
For detailed information and guidance on when to use each channel, reps should refer to the internal Trust and Safety Department Overview (Rep) KA. NOTE: It is important for reps to refer to the relevant resources within that KA before posting in these channels.

3. Steps: How to get help in Slack 
Many teams at Thumbtack use specific tools within their help channels to manage and track requests. Before posting your question, always do your own research first. When you enter a help channel, look for a pinned post or check the channel description to see which of the following methods you should use.
Using Slack Workflows
Some teams use built-in forms called "Workflows" to gather specific information for requests.  Channels that use workflows include #marketplace-pay-support and the majority of T&S channels. 
Reps can typically find and start a workflow in one of these ways:
Look for a button in the message bar: Many channels have a prominent button directly in the message bar for the most common action (e.g., ▷ Review Disputes). This is the quickest way to open the form.
Click the 'Workflows' tab: At the top of the channel, next to 'Messages' and 'Files', you can click the 'Workflows' tab. This will take you to a page showing all "Featured" and "Bookmarked" workflows for that channel.
Use the plus icon (+): To the left of the message bar, click the plus icon (+) and select 'Workflow' from the menu that appears to see a list of available workflow forms.
Once you select the correct workflow for your request, fill out the form and click Send.
Using Assist App
Some teams, like the Advanced Service Team (AST) and Sales Operations use the Atlassian Assist app to create official Jira tickets for requests which allow for more formal tracking. The Sales Ops team has you navigate to the Assist app to trigger the flow, while the Advanced Service Team has you navigate to the specific channel to raise your request. 
Support reps and cross-functions teams like Sales, can refer to the internal Requesting Help from the Advanced Service Team (Rep) KA for steps on how to ask the Advanced Service Team questions using the Assist app. 
To create tickets manually through the Assist app in Slack, which also serves as a central hub for reviewing all submitted requests.
Navigate to Assist under the "Apps" section in your Slack sidebar. 
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

In the app's Home tab, click the green "Raise a request" button.
You can also type a request command (keyword) in any message field to open this menu. Some workflows require you to add a forward slash to trigger the Assist app, while others don’t. 
For “Select a site:” choose https://thumbtack.atlassian.net
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

For “What team do you need help from?:”choose the appropriate team from the dropdown
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

For “What do you need help with?:” choose the appropriate request type from the dropdown.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Fill out all the required fields in the “Create a work item” form with as much detail as possible.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Click Submit
How to View Your Submitted Requests
In Slack:
Go to the Assist app (under "Apps" in your sidebar).
In the Home tab, click the "View your requests" button to see all your tickets.
In Jira:
Log in to Okta and open the TackIt (Helpdesk) application.
Click your profile picture in the top-right corner, then select "Requests".
Use the filters to search for a specific request, and quickly locate relevant tickets.
Post Message Directly In A Channel 
If a channel does not use a Workflow or the Assist app, it is likely an open channel for general questions. In this case, you can simply post your inquiry as a message directly in the channel. Always check the channel's topic or pinned posts for any specific formatting guidelines.

Sherwin-Williams x Thumbtack Pilot

Contents

Overview
Pilot details
Incentives structure 
Stage 1
Stage 2
Pro experience
How pros sign up
Partner benefits
Customer experience
Process
Steps: How to confirm a pro receives their SW incentive credit (Rep)
Steps: How to help a pro with an uncredited SW incentive (Rep)
Talking points
Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) provides information regarding the Sherwin-Williams pilot. It covers the specialized incentive structure for painting contractors and the marketing channels used to acquire these new pros.

[Image: rtaImage]

What is this partnership? 
Starting June 1, 2026, Thumbtack is launching a partnership with Sherwin-Williams (SW) to acquire new professional painting contractors via co-branded marketing and in-store placements. This article equips Frontline Reps with everything needed to support pros who join Thumbtack through this pilot.
Sherwin-Williams is the largest paint manufacturer in the U.S. and a premium brand widely used by professional painting contractors. Through their Digital Alliance program, SW is providing painting pros with access to additional digital business tools — including Thumbtack — to help grow their businesses.
Why it matters (internal info)
The goal of this partnership is to leverage Sherwin-Williams' position as a premium paint brand to drive high-quality supply to the Thumbtack platform. 
How the partnership works
New pros sign up via a co-branded landing page  or in-store QR code and receive a total of $400 in incentives: an initial $150 credit and a subsequent 25% discount on leads up to $250.
NOTE: Pros who signed up via the SW landing page will NOT receive the standard new pro discount. 
For a closer look at the user experience, refer to the Pro experience and Customer experience sections below. 
Pilot details
This section provides details about the Sherwin-Williams pilot experiment, including launch dates and store locations.
Launch date: June 1, 2026
Anticipated End Date: Approximately X [Internal note: Subject to change based on performance.]
Eligible pros: New professional painting contractors only — no existing Thumbtack account
Eligibility requirements:
New pros only: Pros who already have an existing Thumbtack account are NOT eligible. They must be brand new to Thumbtack.
Sign-up channel matters: The pro must sign up through the co-branded landing page or in-store QR code. Sign-ups through other channels do not qualify.
Pilot market: The pro must be in one of the pilot markets. 
Pilot Markets: 
Atlanta, GA
Washington, DC metro area
Los Angeles, CA
Incentive structure
Eligible pros can receive a total maximum value of $400 in free lead credits, unlocked in two stages. The incentive is structured this way to ensure pros are active and set up for success before receiving the full benefit.
All promotional credits during the SW pilot are managed and issued manually and will appear in the pro’s Credit Log. Credits are reviewed and issued on a bi-weekly basis by the ops team.
Stage 1 - $150 Signup Credit

When the pro signs up through the co-branded landing page or QR code and completes all activation requirements, they receive $150 in free lead credits added to their Thumbtack balance. The activation requirements (EMR) are as follows: 
Set up job preferences (targeting) for at least one service category
Add a valid payment method
Add at least one review (imported Google reviews or star rating from other sites)
Submit a background check (BGC)
Once all activation steps are complete, the $150 credit is issued to the pro’s Thumbtack balance within 2 weeks.
Stage 2 Trigger
Once the pro is live on the platform and receiving leads, they become eligible to earn additional free lead credits in batches as they spend on leads.
What the landing page says:  “After receiving 2-requests, pro will receive 25%-off their leads until they hit the next $250 in discounted leads.”
How it actually works
Stage 2 credits are not a live percentage discount applied at the time of each lead charge. They are free lead credits issued in batches by the ops team as the pro spends on leads. The mechanics are:
The pro must have received their first 2 leads to become eligible.
After that, the pro earns up to $65 in free lead credits for every $250 they spend on leads — up to $250 in total. The last credit value will be $55.
Credits are issued manually by the ops team — they are not applied automatically.
Stage 2 credits appear in the pro’s Credit Log, not in the Discounts section in Admin.
Batch breakdown
Use this table to quickly calculate where a pro stands and when their next batch is expected. Cross-reference with the Total Spend field in the Credits section on the pro's main user page in Admin.

Track Stage 2 progress and identify billing issues.
To find the Total Spend and gauge when the next batch of credits should be issued:
Go to the pro's main user page in Admin.
Locate the Credits section.
Check the Total Spend field to see how much the pro has spent on leads to date.
Compare against the batch thresholds in the table above to determine which batches have been issued and when the next one is expected.
Pro experience

How pros sign up
Pros can enter the Thumbtack funnel through the following SW-branded touchpoints:

Channel
Details
In-Store QA codes
Printed materials placed in ~200 pilot stores. Separate QR codes for pros and homeowners (customers).
SW Sales Rep Texts
3,500 SW sales reps send text messages with a direct sign-up link to their local pro contacts.
Co-Branded Email
SW communicates with ~1.7M pros and ~32M homeowners (customers) via their existing email newsletter program.
Co-Branded Landing Page
Dedicated Thumbtack landing page presenting the $400 incentive offer and explaining the sign-up flow. 
Pro sign-up flow
Once a pro scans the QR code or visits the co-branded landing page, the flow is:
Scan QR code or visit co-branded landing page. 
Sign up as a new Thumbtack pro. 
Complete activation (EMR): job preferences, payment, review, background check.
$150 credit is applied to their Thumbtack balance
Pro begins appearing in search results and receiving leads.
After receiving their first 2 leads, the pro becomes eligible for Stage 2 credits.
Ops team issues free lead credits in batches as the pro spends on leads — up to $65 per $250 spent, up to $250 total.
Partner Benefits
In addition to the Thumbtack incentive, pros who sign up through this partnership receive access to two additional resources: 
Sherwin-Williams Pro+ business Tools 
Pros gain access to SW’s Pros+ suite of business tools and resources:
sherwin-williams.com/painting-contractors/pro-plus/business-tools
Thumbtack Growth Guide  —  “Scale with Confidence”
Pros who visit the SW co-branded landing page can access a free downloadable Thumbtack growth guide: “Scale with Confidence: Insider growth strategies from Thumbtack's highest-performing businesses.' 
How to access: 
Visit the co-branded pro landing page
Click “Get success tips” → opens the guide landing page.
Click “Get this guide” or enter their email address to have it emailed to them. 
Customer experience
The partnership also includes a homeowner-facing component to help SW customers quickly find and hire local painters after purchasing paint in store.
How It Works for Customers
Customers scan a homeowner-specific QR code in-store (separate from the pro QR code).
They are directed to a Thumbtack landing page where they can find, review, and compare local painting pros.
They hire a pro who is ready to complete their project.
Note for reps: If a homeowner contacts support after scanning an in-store QR code, guide them through the standard Thumbtack customer flow. There is no special homeowner incentive associated with this pilot.
2. Process

Steps: How to confirm a pro received their SW incentive credit (Rep)
Support reps will use this process when a pro asks whether their credit has been applied, or when a pro says they were charged for a lead but expected it to be free.
NOTE: Pros do NOT receive an in-app or email notification when the credit is added to their account. The credit is automatically applied to lead charges before their card on file is charged. Pros with frequent leads may not notice the credit was used. This is expected behavior — not a bug.
To confirm the credit was issued, reps will follow these steps: 
In Admin, go to the pro’s Credit Log.
Scroll down and look for a row matching ALL of the following:
Transaction type: Promotional Credit (Admin grant)
Admin Reason: Promotional (Special Projects/Marketing)
Note:  SW - [specific text]
Amount: $150.00 (Stage 1) or up to $65.00 (Stage 2 batch)
If the row is present, the credit was issued. Share the date and amount with the pro.
If no matching row is found, the credit has not yet been issued. Follow the steps below to flag it.
To confirm the credit has been used (and what leads it was used on), reps will follow these steps: 
In the Credit Log, find the row where the promotional credit was granted (using the steps above).
Look for the next row above the grant row that has a “Payment [receipt link]” in the transaction type column.
Click “Rebuild receipt” to view the receipt. This shows the leads that used the credit before the pro’s card was charged again.
Steps: How to help a pro with an uncredited SW incentive (rep)
Support reps will use this process when a pro has met the eligibility requirements but the credit has not yet appeared in their Credit Log.
Before flagging a missing credit, reps should first check whether the pro is within the normal issuance window. SW promotional credits are reviewed and issued on a bi-weekly basis by the ops team — it is normal for a credit to take up to 2 weeks to appear after the pro has met the requirements. If the pro completed activation recently, the credit may still be on its way.
If the pro has been waiting longer than 2 weeks and the credit is still not visible in the Credit Log, follow the steps below to flag it for the ops team.
Verify the pro completed all four EMR activation steps (job preferences, payment method, review, background check). See the Understanding and Completing Activation Requirements (Pro) KA to check EMR status.
Check the Credit Log to confirm the credit is actually missing — not just unnoticed (see Steps above).
Check whether the pro is within the normal 2-week issuance window before submitting a request. If the pro completed activation less than 2 weeks ago, let them know the credit is still within the expected timeframe and to check back if it hasn't appeared after 2 weeks.
If the pro has been waiting longer than 2 weeks, submit a request for the ops team to investigate:
​​​​​​​Open the Atlassian Assist app in Slack.
Select Raise a request.
For “What team do you need help from?,” choose Sales Operations (SOPS).
For “What do you need help with?,” select Compensation. 
Under “Incentives,” select Bugs.
Fill out the form with all necessary details.
Click Submit.
Once submitted, let the pro know that they should see the credit in their Thumbtack balance within 2 weeks or less.
Talking point: “I’ve let our team know you are missing $[X] in credits. They should be added to your Thumbtack balance with 2 weeks or less. Once added, the credit will automatically apply to your next lead charges before your card is charged.”
3. Talking points
This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros about the Sherwin-Williams pilot. Use these talking points to ensure consistent messaging.

English talking point
Spanish talking point
Q: How do I get my $400 credit?

The $400 is unlocked in two stages. First, complete all activation steps — set up job preferences, add a payment method, add a review, and submit a background check. This is also what makes you visible in search results so customers can find you. Once activation is complete, you’ll receive $150 in free lead credits. After receiving your first 2 leads, you’ll start earning up to $65 in free lead credits for every $250 you spend on leads, up to $250 in total additional credits.

Q: I signed up via QR code in a Sherwin-Williams store. Why haven't I received my credit yet?

The $150 credit requires all four activation steps to be complete: job preferences, payment method, review, and background check. Completing these steps also gets your profile live so you start showing up in search results. Once all four are done, the credit will be applied to your Thumbtack balance.

Q: How will I know when my credit has been added?

You will not receive an in-app or email notification when the credit is added. The credit will automatically be applied to your lead charges before your card on file is charged. If you want to confirm it was applied, check your messenger — leads covered by a credit will be marked as free.

Q: Can I use the credit for any service category?

Yes. Once your credit is added to your Thumbtack balance, it can be applied to leads in any category, not just painting. 

Q: When does the 25% discount kick in?

After you receive your first 2 leads through Thumbtack, you become eligible to earn up to $65 in free lead credits for every $250 you spend on leads — up to $250 in additional credits total. These are added to your account in batches as you spend. Note: the last batch may be slightly less than $65.

Q: I didn't sign up through the Sherwin-Williams QR code or landing page. Am I still eligible?

No. Eligibility requires signing up specifically through the co-branded Sherwin-Williams landing page or in-store QR code. Pros who signed up through a different channel are not eligible for this promotion.

Q: I already have a Thumbtack account. Can I still get the $400?

No. This promotion is only available to new Thumbtack pros. Painting contractors who already have an existing Thumbtack account are not eligible.

4. Resources

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article provides guidelines for Frontline Reps on handling sensitive account information for Thumbtack users. It outlines processes for securely managing, sharing, and removing data, as well as adhering to data privacy regulations. The article covers topics such as account status inquiries, password management, payment information security, and legal considerations.
For security purposes and to keep Thumbtack as safe and secure as possible, it’s essential that frontline reps follow each process exactly when it comes to sensitive account information. Thumbtack is cautious about the account information shared.
This article provides guidelines for handling sensitive account information for Thumbtack users (pros and customers). It outlines processes for sharing, removing, and managing such data, including adherence to privacy laws.
Frontline reps can use this article to understand how to respond to inquiries about account status, payment details, personal information, and project-related data while maintaining security. Following these guidelines is crucial to protect sensitive account information and maintain user trust. Thumbtack is committed to data security and regulatory compliance; these processes ensure that reps handle information responsibly and consistently.
2. Handling sensitive account information
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: This section provides comprehensive guidelines for Frontline Reps on how to handle sensitive account information for Thumbtack users. It covers various scenarios including account status inquiries, password management, payment information security, and personal data protection. The aim is to ensure secure and compliant handling of user data while addressing common support requests.
Account status inquiries
If a user contacts support requesting information about another person's account, frontline reps must follow these guidelines:
For privacy and security reasons, frontline reps must never share specific details about another user’s account with anyone other than the account owner. This includes:
Account status of a pro or customer
Their standing on Thumbtack
Specific spending amounts of a pro who was referred to Thumbtack. Learn more in the internal Pro Thumbtack Pro Referral Program (Pro) KA.
Any past Trust and Safety incidents or information regarding claims made against them on Thumbtack.
*The only exception is when Thumbtack receives information in writing from a user’s attorney. Refer to + required documentation from third-party requesters +. 

Important: Support reps must always follow the verification guidelines before disclosing account-specific details to a user about their own account. See the internal Verify Account Information | Article #000007658 KA for more details.
Steps: How to handle user requests for another person's account information (Rep)
If a Frontline rep receives a contact from someone asking about a user's account status, follow these steps: 
DON’T share specific details about a customer or pro's account status or standing on Thumbtack. 
DO explain that, for privacy reasons, we can't share personal information about another person's account. However, you can help them by trying to identify the concern the pro or customer wants to be addressed.
Talking Point: “For privacy reasons, I'm unable to share details about another person's account. Is there something specific you have questions about that I can help you with?
Por razones de privacidad, no puedo compartir detalles sobre la cuenta de otra persona. ¿Hay algo específico sobre su pregunta con lo que le pueda ayudar?
Steps: How to handle user requests for another person’s T&S case history (Rep)
A user may contact Thumbtack to request information about another person’s account, such as their account standing on Thumbtack, history of any past Trust and Safety incident cases or information regarding claims made against the account on Thumbtack.
If a frontline rep receives a contact from someone asking about another user’s claim or previous Trusty and Safety cases, follow these steps: 
DON’T share any information about the claims Thumbtack has received against a customer or pro on the site and details about previous Trust and Safety issues with anyone. The only exception is when Thumbtack receives +information in writing + from a customer or pro's attorney. Reps can share the Guidelines for third party information requests – Thumbtack Help with them.
DO let the interested person know that Thumbtack is researching the issue and working with the pro or customer (and others who are directly involved) on the next steps.
▶ Talking points to explain this:
English talking point
Spanish talking point 
If there was a concern brought to our attention, we'll investigate the issue and work directly with the account owner (and anyone else involved) to figure out the next steps we should take.”
Si se nos comunicó una inquietud, investigaremos el problema y trabajaremos directamente con el propietario de la cuenta (y cualquier otra persona involucrada) para determinar los próximos pasos que debemos tomar.
Password management
Frontline reps must never take a pro or customer’s password over the phone, during a chat or SMS interaction, or in an email. 
Steps: How to handle password-sharing situations (Rep)
The Frontline rep should follow the applicable steps in the internal Account Information (Pro) or Account Information (Customer) KAs on how to help a pro or customer reset their Thumbtack password.
Payment information security
For security reasons, pros and customers should avoid sharing any payment information (including credit card, debit card, or other banking info) through Thumbtack Messenger. 
Additionally, frontline reps must never take credit card numbers over the phone, during a chat or SMS interaction, or in an email. If contacted by a user (pro, customer, or non-Thumbtack user), reps must follow the guidelines in the table below. 
Steps: How to handle sensitive payment information (Rep)
Customer asks how they should send payment
When a customer inquires about the appropriate method for sending payment to a pro, it's crucial that frontline reps guide them toward secure and approved channels while advising against insecure alternatives. Frontline reps should not tell the user to send payment info over text or email (or any other specific service). Thumbtack can’t guarantee these are secure.
Reps can share the Safety tips for paying a pro – Thumbtack Help article with customers. 
If the rep needs to verify a credit card
In instances where a frontline rep needs to verify a credit card, strict security protocols must be followed to protect sensitive payment information. Frontline reps must follow these guidelines: 
Reps must only ask for the last 4 digits. 
If the user (pro or customer) provides more information before the rep can stop them, ensure the recording is deleted by following the steps in the Removing sensitive information section above.

Pro needs help making a purchase with a credit card
When a pro requires help with making a purchase using a credit card, the frontline reps role is to guide them through the self-service process on Thumbtack, rather than directly handling their card details. Reps will follow these steps: 
Don't run the card for them. 
Walk them through the process on Thumbtack.
Reps can share the How to add or remove a credit card Thumbtack Help article with the pro as well. 
Explain to user why we can’t take their credit card info 
▶ Talking points to explain this:
English talking point
Spanish talking point 
For security reasons, we cannot take credit card information over the phone or email. But if you'd like, I'm happy to walk you through the steps on our site.
Por razones de seguridad, no podemos recibir información de su tarjeta de crédito por teléfono o por correo electrónico. Pero si lo desea, con gusto lo guiaré con los pasos en nuestro sitio.
Reps can refer to the internal Payment Methods (Pro) KA for steps. 
Personal information protection
A user may contact Support asking for another user's personal information, such as their contact information, email address, and other sensitive user information. It’s important that frontline reps never share a user's personal information with another user.* 
*Information can only be shared if it has been previously and explicitly provided voluntarily by the customer or pro (e.g., a customer voluntarily shared their phone number in the messenger).
A user’s personal information includes: 
Phone number
Full name
When referring to users, frontline reps should only use the person's first name and last initial (e.g., Mary H.).
Email address
Physical address
Contact details 
Any other personal information (Unless it has already been provided voluntarily by the customer or pro.) (e.g., A customer provided their phone number in the messenger with a pro)
Project-related information sharing
Pros sometimes ask about the status of a customer's project, such as contact info, request details, and more. It’s important that frontline reps follow the project-related information guidelines below. 
Project details reps CAN share with pros
Project details reps must NEVER share with pros
Request details. Any job details the customer included in their request
This information is visible in the messenger with the customer. 
Number of pros customer contacted. Whether a customer has reached out to other pros or not
This information is visible next to the pro's messages with the customer and other details about the lead.
Read receipt. If a pro can already see the “read” checkmark, then the rep can reiterate that the customer has seen the pro’s message.
Contact pro info. Which other pros a customer has reached out to
Hire status. Whether the customer has already hired another pro
Read receipt. If a pro can already see the “read” checkmark, then the rep can reiterate that the customer has seen the pro’s message. But the rep should not give the pro details about what time the customer read their message or any other data about the customer viewing their message.
Steps: How to handle pro requests for customer project details (Rep)
If a frontline rep is contacted by a pro who wants to know more about a customer project, it’s important the guidelines below are followed: 
Confirm that the information the pro is asking for can be shared by referring to the table below. 
If yes, Thumbtack can tell the pro any information they already have access to in their account. Reps can direct the pro to where they can find that information themselves, so they can easily find it in the future. 
If no, reps should encourage the pro to follow up directly with the customer to find out if they're still interested.
▶ Talking point to encourage pro:
English talking point
Spanish talking point 
We care a lot about protecting your information on Thumbtack. That's why we leave it up to each pro and customer to decide if and when to share their personal information. If the person you're curious about has already shared this information, I'd be happy to relay it. Otherwise, try following up with another message to chat about those details
Nos preocupamos mucho por proteger su información en Thumbtack. Por eso dejamos que cada profesional y cliente decida si desea compartir su información personal. Si la persona por la que se está comunicando ya ha compartido esta información, con gusto se la transmitiré. De lo contrario, puede intentar con otro mensaje para recibir esos detalles.
Third-party information requests
Thumbtack does not share account information with anyone outside of Thumbtack without the required documentation. If contacted by someone requesting information about an account, the frontline rep will follow these steps: 
Direct third parties to Guidelines for third-party information requests to learn our current policy on how to obtain information or records from Thumbtack.
▶ Talking points to direct users:
English talking point
Spanish talking point 
We're very careful about the personal information we share. Unless I have proof that the pro/customer has shared that information with you already, I won’t be able to give you any of their personal information. I can direct you to our current policy on how to officially obtain information or records from Thumbtack.”
Somos muy cuidadosos con la información personal que compartimos. A menos que tenga pruebas de que el profesional/cliente ya ha compartido esa información con usted, no podré darle ninguna información personal. Puedo dirigirle a nuestra póliza actual sobre cómo obtener oficialmente información o registros de Thumbtack.
Helpful resources reps can share with users: 
Non-law enforcement requests: Guidelines for third party information requests – Thumbtack Help.
Law enforcement requests: Guidelines for law enforcement information requests – Thumbtack Help

Reps can direct users to Thumbtack’s current policies on how to officially obtain information or records from Thumbtack.
Thumbtack employee contact information
Salespeople and vendors often try to contact different Thumbtack team members through support. (i.e., contacting Thumbtack’s IT team to try to sell or pitch them a product.)
NOTE: Established partners and vendors will already have the contact info they need. They should never contact support to ask for another employee's information.
If asked for a Thumbtack employees info, frontline reps will follow these steps:
Never give out another Thumbtack employee's email address or phone number.
Encourage the person to use the contact information they may already have  (I.e., a text from a recruiter, a phone number on an invoice, etc.)
If you’re unsure the request is legitimate:
Submit a request to the Advanced Service Team using the Assist app in Slack for help in determining next steps.
Navigate to #service_global_help-and-escalations.
Type Help others (or Others) to trigger the Assist workflow.
Select the "Global Help Others" request type. (If you selected the wrong type, click Cancel and start over.)
Click Open in new window.
Complete all required fields, including:
The requester’s name, company, and role (if provided).
The Thumbtack employee’s name or the team the person is trying to reach.
Why the person is trying to contact the employee (one sentence).
Click Submit.
A manager may choose to forward the person’s contact info to the employee if appropriate; this should be rare.
Don’t promise the person that they’ll receive an email or call back.

3. Removing sensitive information
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: This section details the procedures for Frontline Reps to remove sensitive user information from Thumbtack's systems. It covers the removal of data from Genesys (call recordings, chats, and SMS) and Salesforce (emails, screenshots, and conversations). Adhering to these steps ensures the protection of user privacy and compliance with data security regulations.
Steps: How to remove sensitive information from Genesys (call recordings chats, SMS) (Rep)
To remove information from a phone call, chat or SMS, frontline reps will follow the steps below. The recording and transcript will be removed in its entirety.
Navigate to the associated call task record.
From a Salesforce case, click Related.
Scroll down to “Activity History” and click the call (Click view all, if needed). 
Look under the "Task Information" section.
Obtain the following information:
Conversation ID
If phone call include the ANI (see what it looks like below)▶ What it looks like:[Image: AD_4nXceDmEiyY5qZkuIwYM5yoT3xKw0e0Wz0WGQgIUuvCS4hSLlXMuzSMYb7sOSa1hQ7RkvHdlNvGjwMMYdxDuatu5PpeaRSu7TDMhndOYL57uwYobXPy3B-HH03UrH-QvaSI1YWYk9dmR49XUVfr7RiqpPtXc]
If SMS/ Chat, include the interaction type (e.g., (Voice, SMS, chat)
Agent Name
Date and time
Submit a Helpdesk ticket requesting that the call recording be removed. Reps can access the Helpdesk through Okta.
In Salesforce, add a note to the case detailing the Helpdesk request and ticket number.
Reps should receive a reply in 1-2 business days confirming that the information has been removed.
Steps: How to remove sensitive information from Salesforce (emails, screenshots, conversations) (Rep)
Pros or customers may unintentionally send us personal information, like their credit card details or passwords. To ensure Thumbtack protects our pros’ sensitive information and complies with regulations, it must be removed from Salesforce.
To request the removal of sensitive information from Salesforce, frontline reps will follow these steps: 
In Salesforce, identify the email or part of the conversation that contains the sensitive information.
Submit a Helpdesk ticket requesting that the screenshot or email be removed. Reps can access the Helpdesk through Okta.
In Salesforce, add a note to the case detailing the Helpdesk request and ticket number.

Reps should receive a reply in 1-2 business days confirming that the information has been removed.
4. Collecting, sharing, and deleting information (Data privacy regulations and user requests)
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: This section outlines how Frontline Reps should handle user requests concerning data privacy, including collecting, sharing, and deleting personal information. It details user rights under U.S. State Data Privacy Laws, such as the right to know, delete, correct, and opt-out of data sale or sharing. Reps will learn the proper procedures for assisting users with these requests while ensuring compliance with relevant regulations.
Data privacy regulations are laws that give people rights over their personal information — such as viewing it, correcting it, deleting it, or controlling how it’s shared. These rights are designed to give users more control over their data and how businesses use it.
In the U.S., these rights depend on where the user lives. Some states, like California, have strong privacy laws (e.g., the California Consumer Privacy Act), while others do not. Many states have recently passed similar laws, each with specific rules (see U.S. state data privacy laws section below). Some apply to customers only, while others also apply to pros.
The full details of Thumbtack’s data collection, use, storage, and sharing are available in our external articles:
Privacy Policy - Thumbtack:  Explains what information we collect (including from pros, customers, and other users), how we use it, when and to whom we disclose it, and the rights users may have under applicable laws.
Terms of Use - Thumbtack: Sets the rules for using the Thumbtack platform and includes privacy-related provisions and references to the Privacy Policy.
Whenever a user asks about data privacy rights, direct them to these articles for the full legal details. Frontline reps can refer to the table below for a list of states with current data privacy laws.
User rights and requests (Access, deletion, opt out) U.S. State Data Privacy Laws
A privacy rights request is when a user asks Thumbtack to take action on their personal information — such as viewing it, correcting it, deleting it, or limiting how it is shared.
Under U.S. state data privacy laws  (such as the California Consumer Privacy Act and similar laws in other states), users may have the following rights:
Right to Know / Access – Receive a copy of the personal information Thumbtack has on file about them.
Right to Delete – Request that Thumbtack delete their personal information that we have stored about them..
Right to Correct – Fix inaccuracies in their personal information.
Right to Opt-Out of Sale – Applicable privacy laws may provide individuals with the right to opt out of  (stop) Thumbtacks’ disclosure of their personal information to third parties for the third parties’ own purposes.)
Right to Opt-Out of Sharing – Applicable privacy laws may provide individuals with the right to opt out of (stop) Thumbtack sharing that individuals’ personal information to third parties for behavioral targeted advertisement purposes. 
Right to Appeal – Challenge Thumbtack’s decision if a request is denied (in whole or in part) their data rights request in accordance with applicable laws.
Right to Non-Discrimination – Not have Thumbtack discriminate against individuals because they exercised any of the above rights
Important: Not every user has all of these rights. What we can do depends on:
The type of request.
Where the user lives. Some rights are only available in certain states with active privacy laws.
Understanding User Data Privacy Requests

Frontline Reps should understand the types of requests that can be universally processed versus those limited by state-specific privacy laws:
Request to delete or opt out: Thumbtack processes qualifying “requests to delete” and “requests to opt-out” for all users, regardless of their state of residence
Requests to know: For requests to know, state privacy laws currently only apply to:
Pros in CA 
Customers in the following states:  CA, CO, CT, DE FL, IA OR, MT, NE, NH, NJ, TX, UT, and VA as of Jan. 2025, with more states becoming effective later this year and beyond
If a customer requests a copy of their personal information and they are NOT from one of the states listed above*, they are NOT eligible, and the request will not be completed. *Exception: In California, both customers and pros can request this documentation.

Users can find more details about Thumbtack’s data handling practices and privacy rights requests in Privacy Policy - Thumbtack  and Terms of Use – Thumbtack articles.

Privacy Rights Requests: What Thumbtack Accepts and Who It Applies To


Type of Request
Accepted?
Who It Applies To
Notes
Delete Data / Account
✅ Yes (if qualifying)
All users (pros + customers, all states)
Requests must be verified (account owner or authorized agent). Can take up to 45 days to process. Recommend Deactivate account if user doesn’t want leads during this time. If deleted, the user must create a new account with a different email to continue using Thumbtack.
Opt-Out of Sale of Data
✅ Yes (if qualifying)
All users (pros + customers, all states)
Processed through the Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information form. Requires email verification. Opting out may limit Thumbtack’s ability to connect users with additional pros.
Opt-Out of Sharing Data (for targeted ads)
✅ Yes (if qualifying)
All users (pros + customers, all states)
Processed through the same opt-out flow. Requires email verification. Opting out means data will not be shared with third parties for behavioral/targeted ads.
Right to Know / Access (copy of data)
✅ Yes, but limited
- Pros: only in California 

- Customers: in CA, CO, CT, DE, FL, IA, OR, MD, MT, NE, NH, NJ, TX, UT, VA (as of Jan 2025; more states added later)
Denied if the user lives in a state without an active privacy law. Requests must be verified.
Right to Correct
✅ Yes, if law applies
Users in states with privacy laws
Some info can be updated directly in Account Settings. Legal name/business info requires submitting the Account Information and Licensing – Thumbtack Help form. Requests must be verified.
Right to Appeal a Denial
✅ Yes, if law applies
Users in states with privacy laws
User may appeal if Thumbtack denies a request in whole or part.
Right to Non-Discrimination
✅ Yes, if law applies
Users in states with privacy laws
Thumbtack cannot treat users differently for exercising privacy rights.
Requests from Non-Regulated States
⚠️ Partial
All users in states without active privacy laws (refer to the U.S. State Data Protection States, Laws, and Effective Date table above)
Thumbtack will still process delete and opt-out requests. Thumbtack will not process “Right to Know.” Use approved talking points to explain.
GDPR Requests
❌ No
Not applicable
General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) does not apply to Thumbtack.
Data Privacy Request Processing Timeline
This section outlines the standard processing times and communication protocols for data privacy requests submitted to Thumbtack.
Timeline: It can take up to 45 days for Thumbtack to process an initial request under applicable privacy laws. 
Extend timeline: Thumbtack can extend that period, if we have a reason and provide that reason to the user.
Communicate with requestor: After a customer submits a request, Thumbtack will, in compliance with applicable privacy laws, reach out to communicate the next step(s). This communication may vary depending on the nature of the request.
Frontline reps should make pros aware that the process may take up to 45 days and that they should use the “Deactivate account” option if they don’t want to receive leads during that time. 
Reasons for Data Privacy Request Denials
This section provides frontline reps with a list of reasons a user's Data Privacy Request might be denied by Thumbtack: 
The user does not live in a state with an active privacy law (for “Right to Know” requests). (most common reason for denial) 
Thumbtack cannot verify that the requestor is the account owner or an authorized representative.
Other legal reasons under applicable privacy laws*
* If a request is denied for other legal reasons under applicable privacy laws, Thumbtack will follow up with the requestor to explain the reason for the denial.
Do’s and don’ts when helping with data privacy regulations and user requests 
Frontline reps should keep the following do’s and don’ts in mind when helping users with data privacy regulations and user requests: 
Do ask customers to fill out the Data Retrieval or Deletion Request intake form.
Do make pros aware that the process may take up to 45 days and that they should use the “Deactivate account” option if they don’t want to receive leads during that time.  
Don’t promise residents from states that do not have a current state privacy law in place that they can exercise the rights described under state privacy laws.
Don’t promise users they can speak with the agent who will be reviewing their request.
▶ Key points
A privacy rights request is when a user asks Thumbtack to take action on their personal information in a way that’s covered by a privacy law (for example, “I want to see all my data” or “Delete my information”).
What Thumbtack can do depends on:
The type of request (view, delete, correct, opt out, etc.).
Where the user lives (some rights only apply in certain states).
Some rights are available to all users (pros and customers), while others are limited to residents of specific states.
Some requests are not applicable to Thumbtack at all (e.g., General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) rights).
Steps: How to help a user's inquiries for privacy rights requests (Rep)
If a user wants to make a privacy rights request to view or delete their personal data, or to opt-out of Thumbtack selling and/or sharing their personal data, frontline reps will guide them to through these steps:
Step 1 
First, reps should direct the users to the Privacy Policy - Thumbtack article to better understand their rights. 
Step 2 
Requests to know and/or delete:
Advise them to fill out the following form: Submit a request to know or a request to delete your personal information
Requests to opt-out of selling or sharing:
Have them submit the Do not Sell or Share my Personal Information form. 
After submitting their request, Thumbtack sends a verification email to the email address they provided. 
The user needs to click the link in the email to finish opting out.
Requests to correct inaccurate personal data:
Users  can update certain information themselves by logging into their Thumbtack account and navigating to the Settings  page.
For legal name or any other personal or business information, they’ll need to submit a request for review through the Account information and licensing – Thumbtack Help form. 
Steps: How to submit an authorized agent submit a Privacy Rights Request on users behalf (Rep)
 
Some data privacy laws allow users to appoint an authorized agent to submit rights requests on their behalf, including requests for data deletion. 
 
If someone contacts Thumbtack as an authorized agent, frontline reps should follow these steps: 
Inform them that the request must be submitted to dataprivacy@thumbtack.com.
Explain that they may need to provide written authorization or a power of attorney signed by the user they represent.
 
NOTE: Thumbtack may require the user to verify their identity directly before their request is processed. 
Steps: How to troubleshoot issues with the privacy rights request opt-out flow (Rep)
The opt out page form is found on the Personal information rights requests – Thumbtack Help article.  If the user contacts Thumbtack about the opt-out flow not working, reps can help them by submitting the information for them.
 
To help the user opt out of Thumbtack sharing or selling their information, frontline reps will follow these steps: 
Go to the Syndication Opt-out portal
Have the user confirm the email address on their account and the last zip code they submitted a request in.
Confirm they'd like to opt out of selling and sharing.
Inform them that if they opt out of the sale, then Thumbtack won't share their information with any pros outside of the pros they choose themselves. As such, it will make finding the right pros for their project harder.
Inform them that if they opt out of sharing, then we won’t share their information with third parties for behavioral targeted advertising purposes.
On the form, enter the email address the customer verified and click the "Opt out" button.
Ask the user to check their email and confirm they've received an email from Thumbtack about processing their request.
Ask the user to select the opt-out button in the email to finish their portion of the opt-out process.  
Steps: How to handle requests from residents of non-regulated states (no privacy laws in effect) 
This section provides guidance for Frontline Reps on how to handle data privacy requests from users residing in states where specific data privacy laws are not yet in effect. It clarifies which types of requests can be processed for all users, regardless of their state of residence, and how to respond to requests that fall under current state-specific regulations.
Thumbtack processes qualifying requests to delete and requests to opt-out for all users in all states. For requests to know, state privacy laws currently only apply to:
Pros in CA
Customers in CA, CO, CT, DE, FL, IA, OR, MT, NE, NH, NJ, TX, UT, and VA as of Jan. 2025. More states will be added later this year and beyond. Reps can refer to the U.S. State data protection laws table above.
If a frontline rep receives a request from a customer or pro in a state without an effective privacy law to access their information (i.e., to receive a copy of their information, or to receive a copy and then delete it), follow these steps:
Explain to them that their request falls under applicable privacy laws, which only apply to certain users in states with current data protection laws (More states are becoming effective later this year (2025) and beyond) 
▶ Talking point
English talking point 
“Thanks for reaching out about your account. While you’re not a resident of the states where the right to information summary is applicable, we have [insert approved action taken. Example: ‘deactivated your account in line with your request.’]”

5. Legal threats and inquiries
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: This section guides Frontline Reps on handling cases with legal implications or "red flags." It details when and how to escalate such issues, including user appeals regarding data deletion denials, threats of media involvement, and direct contact from lawyers. The aim is to ensure proper procedure and escalate to appropriate teams like Trust and Safety when legal concerns arise.
Cases with legal implications or red flags

Most of these cases won't require further review from the data privacy team. However, it's essential for frontline reps to escalate each case involving the reasons below.  
When to escalate a case to the Trust and Safety team: 
The user wants to appeal the data deletion denial (in whole or in part).
Certain data privacy laws include the right of an individual to appeal the denial (in whole or in part) of the privacy rights request to the business if the individual is not satisfied.
A negative response to the standard actions Thumbtack takes. e.g., the user contacts Thumbtack a second time because they're angry after our standard response.
Lawyers (Attorneys)
Threats to get the media involved
Any other signals that Legal should be involved
Reps can refer to the “Legal, law enforcement, and media“ section of the internal Trust and Safety Incidents  KA for more information.
If the user has already submitted their request through the Data Retrieval or Deletion Request intake form and they’re reaching out separately, frontline reps should:
Encourage them to reply to the email they already received. 
If the user needs help finding the email, reach out to #ts-incident-ops-questions for help. 
If they’re unable to do so, escalate the case to the Trust and Safety team. 
Steps: How to handle inquiries from lawyers (Rep) 
If a user's lawyer contacts Thumbtack on behalf of the user, frontline reps will follow these steps:
Verify that the call or email is coming from a lawyer. (Do a quick Google search to see if there is an affiliated law firm or legal practice)
Let the user’s lawyer (attorney) know that they’ll get a call back from a manager — don’t specify who that manager will be.
▶ Talking points to use:
English talking point
Spanish talking point 
Thanks for taking the time to reach out to us. I'm sharing your information with a manager who can help you with this.
​​Gracias por tomar el tiempo para comunicarse con nosotros. Estoy compartiendo su información con un gerente que puede ayudarlo con esto.
Slack the Trust and Safety Critical Escalation team in #ts-incident-ops-questions using the @escalations tag and ask a Case Manager to DM you for an urgent issue. 
Mentions of lawsuits or legal proceedings

This section provides guidelines for Frontline Reps on how to handle user threats of legal action against Thumbtack, including lawsuits or reports to organizations like the BBB. It outlines steps for de-escalating the situation, resolving the issue if possible, and escalating to the Advanced Service team or Trust and Safety when necessary. The aim is to ensure proper handling and escalation of legal threats.
Steps: How to handle threats of legal action (sue, take legal action against or report Thumbtack) (Rep) 
Someone threatening legal action against Thumbtack could like the user (pro, customer, or non-Thumbtack user) saying they’ll contact a lawyer or file a lawsuit against Thumbtack. Additionally, users could also say they will report Thumbtack by registering a complaint with the BBB.
If a user threatens legal action against Thumbtack, frontline reps should follow these steps: 
Try to de-escalate the situation and take care of their issue. Reps should refer to the internal < Standard Escalations and De-escalation Guidelines (Rep) > KA for de-escalation techniques and talking points for guidance. 
Issue requires follow-up: If a follow up is needed to fully resolve their problem, the rep should be clear about when and how that follow-up will happen.
Issue can be resolved: If the rep can fix the issue together, ensure they feel good about the solution, then check if there’s anything else they need help with.
Issue cannot be resolved: If the issue can’t be resolved and the user continues to threaten legal action:
Submit a request to the Advanced Service Team using the Assist app in Slack for help in determining next steps.
Navigate to #service_global_help-and-escalations.
Type Help others (or Others) to trigger the Assist workflow.
Select the "Global Help Others" request type. (If you selected the wrong type, click Cancel and start over.)
Click Open in new window.
Complete all required fields, including:
Summary of the situation and what has been tried.
Exact legal threat (lawsuit/BBB/media) and any deadlines given.
Links to the Salesforce case and any supporting screenshots.
Click Submit.
Issue cannot be resolved and in risky category: If the issue can’t be resolved and the user is threatening legal action and it's in a risky category, the rep will escalate the case to Trust and Safety. Follow steps in the internal Trust and Safety Incidents KA.
If they’d like to get in contact with Thumbtack’s legal department, frontline reps can refer to the internal  External Inquiries | Employment, Law Enforcement, Legal, Marketing, Press, Sales (Reps) KA for steps.
Steps: Manager escalation protocol for threats of legal action (Advanced Service)
Managers handling issues that can’t be resolved and the user keeps threatening legal action will follow these steps: 
Follow regular escalation procedures.
If the user continues to threaten legal action and it's in a risky category, the Advanced Service rep will review the Legal, Law Enforcement, and Media section of the internal Trust and Safety Incidents KA.
 6. Talking points
▶ 🤖Background notes
AI context: This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros and customers about sensitive account handling topics. Use these talking points to ensure consistent and accurate messaging.
California consumer privacy act (CCPA) and other similar laws.
English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Q: What is the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA)?
Q: ¿Qué es la Ley de Privacidad del Consumidor de California (CCPA)?
A: The CCPA is a California law that introduces broad rights for California consumers around how businesses collect, use, store, delete, and share their personal information. Many other states have enacted similar policies.  See U.S. state data protection laws in order of effective date. 
La CCPA es una ley de California que introduce amplios derechos para los consumidores de California sobre cómo las empresas recopilan, usan, almacenan, eliminan y comparten su información personal. Muchos otros estados han promulgado políticas similares. Consulte las leyes de protección de datos estatales de EE. UU. en orden de fecha de entrada en vigor.
Q: I am a resident of a state with data privacy law in effect. What rights do I have?
Q: Soy residente de un estado con una ley de privacidad de datos en vigor. ¿Qué derechos tengo?
A: If you are a pro that resides in California (not a pro of other states) or a customer of Thumbtack and live in a state with data privacy laws, you have the right to:
Receive a copy of the personal information Thumbtack has collected about you. (Right to know/Access)
Request that Thumbtack delete your personal information (Right to Delete).
Right to correct your personal information (Right to Correct).
Opt out of a business selling your personal information (Right to Opt Out of Sale).
Opt out of a business sharing your personal information for targeted advertising purposes (Right to Opt-out of Sharing)
If you are a customer and/or a pro that resides within California, then you also have the same rights. 
A: Si usted es un profesional que reside en California (no un profesional en otros estados) o un cliente de Thumbtack y vive en un estado con leyes de privacidad de datos, tiene derecho a:

Recibir una copia de la información personal que Thumbtack ha recopilado sobre usted (Derecho a Saber/Acceder).
Solicitar que Thumbtack elimine su información personal (Derecho a Eliminar).
Derecho a corregir su información personal (Derecho a Corregir).
Optar por que una empresa no venda su información personal (Derecho a Optar por Excluirse de la Venta).
Optar por que una empresa no comparta su información personal para fines de publicidad dirigida (Derecho a Optar por Excluirse del Uso Compartido).
Si usted es un cliente y/o un profesional que reside en California, también tiene los mismos derechos.
Q: Why does this only apply to residents of states with data privacy laws?
Q: ¿Por qué esto solo se aplica a los residentes de estados con leyes de privacidad de datos?
A: These states have data privacy laws that govern how businesses handle the data of their residents. While Thumbtack strives to be transparent with its policies regarding personal information, only residents of states where these laws have been passed and are effective can make specific requests under these regulations. 
A: Estos estados tienen leyes de privacidad de datos que rigen cómo las empresas manejan los datos de sus residentes. Aunque Thumbtack se esfuerza por ser transparente con sus políticas sobre información personal, solo los residentes de los estados donde estas leyes han sido aprobadas y están en vigor pueden hacer solicitudes específicas bajo estas regulaciones.
Q: Will these changes affect how I use Thumbtack?
Q: ¿Estos cambios afectarán cómo uso Thumbtack?
If you choose to opt out of what these states may consider a sale of your personal information, you may be unable to find professionals to complete your job. If you choose to delete your personal information, you'll need to create a new customer account using a different email address to continue using Thumbtack.
A: Si elige optar por excluirse de lo que estos estados pueden considerar una venta de su información personal, es posible que no pueda encontrar profesionales para completar su trabajo. Si elige eliminar su información personal, necesitará crear una nueva cuenta de cliente con una dirección de correo electrónico diferente para continuar usando Thumbtack.
Q: How do I request to view/correct/delete my information, or to opt out of allowing Thumbtack to sell and/or share my information?
¿Cómo solicito ver/corregir/eliminar mi información, u optar por no permitir que Thumbtack venda y/o comparta mi información?
A: If you are a resident of a state with a data privacy law in effect, then you can follow the links in our Privacy Policy about data privacy, go to Thumbtack's data protection and information privacy page, or email dataprivacy@thumbtack.com to submit a request.
Si usted es residente de un estado con una ley de privacidad de datos en vigor, puede seguir los enlaces en nuestra Política de Privacidad sobre privacidad de datos, ir a la página de protección de datos y privacidad de la información de Thumbtack, o enviar un correo electrónico a dataprivacy@thumbtack.com para presentar una solicitud.
Q: What personal information has Thumbtack collected about me?
¿Qué información personal ha recopilado Thumbtack sobre mí?
Thumbtack typically collects personal information that we need to help match you with pros to complete your project. For a list of personal information that we may collect from our customers, see our Privacy Policy or, if you are a resident of a state with privacy laws you can request your information by emailing us at dataprivacy@thumbtack.com or submitting your request through our data protection and information privacy page, which can be found by following the relevant links in our privacy policy.
Thumbtack generalmente recopila la información personal que necesitamos para ayudarle a encontrar profesionales para completar su proyecto. Para obtener una lista de la información personal que podemos recopilar de nuestros clientes, consulte nuestra Política de Privacidad o, si es residente de un estado con leyes de privacidad, puede solicitar su información enviándonos un correo electrónico a dataprivacy@thumbtack.com o presentando su solicitud a través de nuestra página de protección de datos y privacidad de la información, que puede encontrar siguiendo los enlaces pertinentes en nuestra política de privacidad.
Q: Does Thumbtack sell or share my information?
¿Thumbtack vende o comparte mi información?
A: When you start a project on Thumbtack, part of how we find you the right pro is by showing your project to additional pros in your area who may be able to help. These pros can reach out to you through Thumbtack. Some states consider this a sale of personal information.
If you have questions or want more details about how Thumbtack uses your personal information, please review our Privacy Policy.
Cuando inicia un proyecto en Thumbtack, parte de cómo le encontramos el profesional adecuado es mostrando su proyecto a profesionales adicionales en su área que podrían ayudarle. Estos profesionales pueden contactarle a través de Thumbtack. Algunos estados consideran esto una venta de información personal.

Si tiene preguntas o desea más detalles sobre cómo Thumbtack utiliza su información personal, por favor revise nuestra Política de Privacidad.
