1. Overview
▶ KA summary
This internal KA provides comprehensive inform
ation for Frontline Reps about search results and ranking on Thumbtack. The following topics are covered in this KA:
Understanding Search Results: How customer searches lead to pro listings and rankings.
Ranking Factors: The primary factors influencing pro rank, including lead prices and quality (responsiveness, reviews, profile completeness, etc.).
Tools and Resources: How pros can use the search results tool, performance dashboards, and other resources to check their ranking and improve visibility.
Process and Steps: Detailed steps for reps to help pros see their ranking, improve it, and address issues where pros are not appearing in search results.
Talking Points: Guidance on how to discuss ranking factors, budgets, availability, and other related topics with pros.
Badges and Tags: Explanation of the various badges and tags that appear on pro profiles and search results, and how they are determined.
Troubleshooting: Common issues and solutions for when pros are not appearing in search results or are receiving unwanted leads.
This KA is designed to equip Frontline Reps with the knowledge and tools to effectively support and advise pros on optimizing their presence and performance on the Thumbtack platform.
Note on targeting terminology: You may see "Targeting" and "Job preferences" terms used interchangeably throughout our internal KA resources or in-product.

When customers search for pros on Thumbtack, they see a list of pros in search results. The order in which those pros show up is determined by their rank. The number of pros a customer sees depends on two things: their area and what they’re searching for. A pro may rank differently depending on how closely they match different search filters customers set. 
Rank is just one part of finding success on Thumbtack. It can take time to improve, but it comes along with offering great service — and that’s something pros can control. 
To appear in a customer's search results, a pro must set their targeting preferences (also known as "Job preferences") and complete onboarding requirements. Search results are determined by the service level, so a pro doesn't need to have targeting preferences set for every service, just the ones they want to appear on search results for. 
Pro resources: Here’s a guide to how customers find you and What are search results?
Search Results Ranking Factors
Rank is determined by how competitive a pros lead price is and their overall quality. 
Each factor's impact can change over time and vary by market. Thus, a pro's rank is likely to change as their market conditions change. Because of this, we shouldn't go into how important one factor may be compared to another when speaking to pros. 
When reviewing a pros ranking, it does not matter whether you tackle quality or lead price first, as both play an impactful role in ranking. Improving all of these things will help pros be considered higher quality. 
To rank higher, pros should focus on both their quality or lead price, keeping in mind that improvement takes time and is achieved by providing great customer experiences. And keep in mind that improving rank doesn’t happen overnight. A better rank usually comes as pros focus on providing great customer experiences.
▶ Important reminders to frontline reps
We should not tell pros whether one factor is more important than the other. They're both important. Knowing the weights isn't actionable, and it can change over time.
Higher-quality pros will be able to be more competitive at similar prices than pros whose quality isn’t as high. However, we can't tell a pro that they will always rank above some other pro.
Low-quality pros won’t achieve top ranking on lead price alone.
▶ Talking point: most important factor impacting ranking

English FAQ with answer
Spanish FAQ with answer
What is the most important factor impacting ranking?
¿Cuál es el factor más importante que afecta su posición en los resultados?
Both your lead price and quality play impactful roles in how you’re ranked. Where other pros in your market set their prices will have an impact on whether the prices you set will comparatively be more or less competitive. Another factor is your overall quality. Being a higher quality pro means that you will be able to be more competitive at similar prices than pros who’s quality isn’t as high. When considering quality we look at things like profile completeness, response time and rate, number of reviews and review rating. Improving all of these things will help you be considered higher quality and help you improve your overall competitiveness.
Tanto el precio de sus prospectos como su calidad influyen en su posición en los resultados. Los precios que otros profesionales establecen en su mercado afectan si los precios que usted establece serán más o menos competitivos en comparación. Otro factor es su calidad general. Si usted es un profesional de mayor calidad, puede ser más competitivo con precios similares que otros profesionales cuya calidad no sea tan alta. Para evaluar la calidad, consideramos cosas como qué tan completo está su perfil, su tiempo de respuesta y su tasa de respuesta, la cantidad de reseñas y la calificación de sus reseñas. Mejorar estos puntos ayuda a que se le considere de mayor calidad y a mejorar su competitividad general.
▶ Quality factors
Be responsive: Communicating quickly and helpfully with customers can help a pros rank. And a fast response rate also helps improve their odds of getting hired by responding quickly. 
Targeting on: Pros need to set targeting preferences to show up in search results. Expanding targeting preferences (zip codes, job types, availability) can impact the frequency of customer contacts since they're more likely to reach more customers, which can help improve ranking.
Get reviews. Pro's review rating and the number of reviews on their profile are factored into their ranking. Pros should remember that great reviews follow great service, so they shouldn't focus too much on the numbers. Pros can increase the number of reviews they have by making it a habit of asking customers for reviews  after completing jobs 
Add prices. If they have the option, pros can set prices for their services. This helps to improve their rank (note: this should NOT be proactively communicated to pros unless a pro asks). Pros should also post accurate pricing for their services that are competitive for their market. One thing reps should note is that customers will no longer see a pro’s pricing on Thumbtack (effective August 10, 2026). Refer to the Pro Pricing KA to learn more.
Profile completeness (engaging profile). A pro's profile is the first impression they make on customers. Over time, the pro ranks better in results as customers engage with their profile.
Have an engaging profile. 
Customer engagement is an important factor in a pro's overall quality. Customers click based on what they see in search results, making it one of our best predictors, though not the only one. Customer engagement includes the click-through rate (how often customers click on a pro from search results in the last 90 days) and the contact rate (how often customers contact the pro from search results that've been viewed in the last 30 days). 
A pro’s Performance Dashboard will show pros the number of profile views the pro received from search results and the number of interested customers that have reached out to them. Pros can also see additional views from customers who have found their public profile outside of Thumbtack search results. For example, they might have found the pros profile by searching on Google.
▶ Budget and Lead Price factors
Set lead prices: Pros set their lead price as the exact amount they are willing to pay per lead. The pro's lead price combined with their overall quality (e.g., reviews, responsiveness), determines their competitiveness level against other pros in their market. This competitiveness level is what directly influences their ranking and visibility in customer search results. 
Setting a higher lead price can help pros be more competitive against similar pros in their market. 
Lowering lead prices can negatively impact ranking while increasing them can boost rank.
Budget: A pro’s weekly spend limit does NOT impact where a pro ranks. However, it can impact if a pro shows up in search results at all.
How pro see where they rank (see how you rank tool) 

Pros can look themselves up in search results with the search results tool. This will show them what customers see before they contact them, where they rank, and the other pros in their market. Seeing Thumbtack from this perspective gives pros a better understanding of how to be successful. To use the tool, see Steps: See where a pro ranks.
Thumbtack tries to surface pros who can fulfill all of the customer’s needs, so results constantly change when a customer comes to Thumbtack with a job that needs to be done and the services the pros have indicated they want through targeting. If a pro is in a highly competitive area with lots of pros, they might not see their profile.

[Image: VYtCqdga9yKMjKAKxCA6nAs9ZZmaQCbqZ4CWXtjrswrukLL5MEcoZbzyNw5ZZZNvJGz3GhhsLWfuaWhad_cvO_aIRFbw9DyQf_eCbev_EvyjFvWYKOgE6BJuRiMfzPKZFpQoTX4LOmCgRp30Goa-kq0]
 

NOTE: Pros must complete their account setup* before they have access to the "look yourself up" tool. When clicking on the tool, they will see a "Finish setting up your account" message. *See Onboarding and activation requirements (EMR) (Pro) KA to learn more.
▶ Other performance tools
Additionally, pros can regularly check their performance using the tools listed below:
Profile strength: A pro’s profile strength tracks improvements to their profile, and gives actionable tips. The score is dynamic and relative to other pros, so it could go up or down as a pro's market changes. Following the tips will help pros stay more competitive in their market. See internal Profile (Pro) KA to learn more.
Performance recommendations. In the performance module below the lead prices table on each service, pros will see personalized recommendations on how to get more leads based on their current quality score and lead prices. See internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA to learn more.
Performance dashboard. The dashboard gives pros insight into how they are performing, what the market conditions look like, how they compare to competitors, and what they can do to improve. See internal Market Level Insights (Performance Dashboard) KA to learn more. 
Badged on search results and pro profile 

Some pros have a tag next to their listing in search results. Badges change often and help customers find the pro that matches their priorities for a particular project. Pros can't request specific badges, and they can have no more than three badges at a time. As long as they have a strong profile, great reviews, and quick response times they’re doing everything they should be.
Frontline reps may hear "badges" also referred to as “pills” or “tags.”

The "Process" section of this internal KA provides a guide for Frontline Reps on how to help pros with their search ranking and visibility concerns. This section is crucial when a pro contacts support about their visibility, asks for guidance on improving their ranking, or during proactive outreach to those who might be experiencing issues.
This section is broken down into three key subsections to guide you through various scenarios:
Steps: See where a pro ranks: This subsection is to be followed anytime a pro inquires about their search result placement, as an initial step in troubleshooting visibility problems, to demonstrate the "See how you rank" tool, or to verify a pro's self-reported ranking issues.
Steps: Help pro improve their ranking: This subsection comes into play when a pro wants to boost their ranking, after assessing their current rank, when their performance metrics show room for improvement, or to proactively coach them on best practices. 
This subsection includes specific sub-points such as Responsiveness, Preferences, Weekly budget,Lead prices, Location, Reviews, Prices, and Profile completeness, each to be addressed when a pro has particular issues or questions related to that area.
Steps: Pro not appearing in some or any results: This subsection is essential when a pro reports complete invisibility in search results, when the "See how you rank" tool confirms this, when troubleshooting severe visibility issues, and before escalating the problem to higher support levels.
By adhering to these steps, Frontline Reps can guide and support pros in optimizing their visibility in search results.

(Responsiveness) Improving Pro Ranking: Optimizing Responsiveness to Customer Contacts
▶ Details about responsiveness
Communicating quickly and helpfully with customers can help a pros rank. As pros consistently accept and respond to new leads, we’ll take the hint. Pros responding quickly tell us they’re available and looking for more work. And a fast response rate also helps — pros up their odds of getting hired by responding quickly. 
When it comes to responsiveness, pros should: 
Aim to respond within 4 hours (between 8 am - 8 pm local time) and if they can’t, try to stay under 24 hours.
Keep up with new messages with push notifications from the app.
Make a habit of responding to exact matches first.
Write customized messages that make a clear path forward for the customer.

(Weekly targeting budget) Improving Pro Ranking: Managing Weekly Targeting Budget for Visibility
▶ Details about weekly targeting budget
A pro’s weekly spend limit doesn’t impact where a pro ranks. However, it can impact if a pro shows up in search results at all. That’s because if they reach their spend limit within the week, they’ll no longer show up in searches. Every lead and booking a pro gets counts toward their budget.
Pros should think about how many customers they want to find their business each week on Thumbtack and use that to set their lead price (How to set my lead prices – Thumbtack Help) . We’ll tell the pro how far that amount could go and recommend a good budget for them.
NOTE: Pros with a low budget have a limited availability tag added to their profile so they won’t get more leads than what they’ve indicated they’re available to receive. We let customers know that these pros have limited availability, making customers less likely to contact these pros and more likely to contact another pro that still has budget available for additional leads. Pros can increase their weekly budget so that more customers will be able to contact them.

(Lead prices) Improving Pro Ranking: Adjusting Lead Prices for Competitiveness
▶ Details about lead prices
A pros lead prices will influence where they show up in search results (and the cost of the lead).
When reviewing a pros ranking, the sequencing of whether to tackle quality or bid first does not matter because both play an impactful role in ranking (and their competitiveness).
Pros do not have to set their competitiveness level to "more competitive" to appear in search results. However, setting a higher lead price could help pros be more competitive against similar pros in their market, which impacts their ranking.
We’ll show eligible pros recommendations for increases that will have a significant impact on their leads/booking volume with a relatively small increase in their lead prices. The recommendations we show are the ones we think will have the biggest impact based on their market.

(Availability) Improving Pro Ranking: Ensuring Accurate and Sufficient Availability Settings

▶ Details about pro availability on Thumbtack
It’s important that pros tell us when they are available, so they only get contacted for jobs that fit their schedule.
Setting up business hours is required. However, using the calendar is optional. Pros must meet all availability requirements or they won’t appear in search results and receive leads. 
Availability requirements (minimum availability window) are as follows: 
Pros must have at least 12 business hours of availability in the next 7 days. 
Note: This only pertains to their business hours, and doesn’t take into account any blocked off time on their calendar.
The maximum amount of notice pros can require before a job is 7 days
Customers must be able to book pros starting at least 14 days in advance
Pros must have any availability within the next 14 days
Keep the following in mind when working with a pros availability: 
A pros availability applies to all jobs
Availability requirements include business hours, and any date(s)blocked off on their calendar.
Pros who don’t meet all availability requirements won’t appear in search results.
Business hours and the calendar are set at a business profile level and apply only to the services on the business profile. This means pros with multiple business profiles will have to manage separate calendars and business hours for each business.
Pro resources: How to manage my availability – Thumbtack Help
To help pros improve their ranking through their availability, Frontline Reps will guide them on:
Check the pro’s calendar and business hours. 
Pros must be available to be scheduled for a minimum window (availability requirements) to prevent pros from setting up their availability in ways that don't allow them to be scheduled. 
To appear in more results, pros can increase their availability by asking for less advanced notice or making themselves available for more time. Decreasing their availability below the required window will cause them to not appear in search results. 
Note: Availability requirements includes business hours, and any time blocked off on their calendar.
If a pros business hours don’t meet the four requirements, they won’t appear in search results or receive any leads. 
▶ [Explain availability requirements]
For your business to show up in search results, you need to have at least 12 business hours of availability. Additionally, your maximum amount of notice can be no more than one week. For example, if you choose “2 days notice”, a customer could book you on Monday for a job that starts Wednesday. If you’re a pro who doesn’t need much notice before starting a job, you can choose “same-day” and receive bookings with as little as four hours notice. And you’re required to be able to fill your calendar with bookings up to two weeks out.If you’re fine with customers booking you further out than that, you can adjust that timeframe further. 
Para que su negocio aparezca en los resultados de búsqueda, necesita tener por lo menos 12 horas de disponibilidad. Además, su aviso máximo no puede ser de más de una semana. Por ejemplo, si usted elige “aviso de 2 días”, un cliente podría reservarle el lunes para un trabajo que empiece el miércoles. Si usted es un profesional que no necesita mucho aviso antes de empezar un trabajo, puede elegir “mismo día” y recibir reservas con tan solo cuatro horas de aviso. También debe poder aceptar reservas en su calendario con hasta dos semanas de anticipación. Si le parece bien que los clientes le reserven con más anticipación, puede ajustar ese periodo.
If a pro’s availability is limited, they’ll show up in fewer search results. That’s because pros with open availability are more likely to find an appointment time that works with the customer’s schedule.
▶ [Calendar has many blocked dates]
English: Only mark off days you know you won’t be able to work, and keep everything else open. If you end up being available for a day you blocked, click the date on your calendar and select Unblock this time. Additionally, it’s a good idea to update your calendar regularly to make sure your availability is accurate. For example, you can set a regular reminder on your phone every month to make sure you’ve blocked off any dates you’re fully booked or won’t be working.
Spanish: Solo marque los días en los que sepa que no podrá trabajar y mantenga el resto del tiempo disponible. Si resulta que está disponible un día que bloqueó, haga clic en la fecha en su calendario y seleccione Unblock this time ("Desbloquear este tiempo"). Además, es una buena idea actualizar su calendario con regularidad para asegurarse de que su disponibilidad sea exacta. Por ejemplo, puede configurar un recordatorio mensual en su teléfono para asegurarse de haber bloqueado los días en los que ya esté totalmente reservado o no vaya a trabajar.
See  Availability KA for additional info and talking points.
(Location) Improving Pro Ranking: Verifying and Updating Location (Address) Information
▶ Details about a pro location information and search
All pros add their location to their profile. 
When a pro sets up their profile, they tell us details like their location and basics about their business. We use this information to make sure the pros business shows up in the right market and for the right customers. The business info section of a pros profile is where they update their address.
Travel preferences are only available for pros who have targeting preferences enabled. By setting targeting preferences, pros can target the right jobs based on more specific factors — like how far they’ll travel to meet customers.

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary:
This internal knowledge article outlines the Samsung Thumbtack on Demand (TToD) Partnership that launched  June 24, 2025. The experience connects pros with out-of-warranty Samsung appliance owners for repair jobs. It summarizes key details of the program, including experience details, pro and customer experiences, communications, and payment processes. This resource provides frontline reps with essential information and talking points to help both pros and customers involved in the partnership.

[Image: rtaImage]


The Samsung X Thumbtack partnership launched on Jun 24, 2025. Through this experience, appliance repair pros can connect with Samsung owners whose washer, dryer, dishwasher, or stove top / oven are no longer under warranty to facilitate necessary repairs.
How it works
Customers seeking repairs for their Samsung washer, dryer, dishwasher, or stove top / oven first reach out to Samsung. During the evaluation of these service requests, Samsung agents determine the warranty status of the appliance. For units no longer under warranty, agents guide customers to a dedicated Samsung x Thumbtack landing page. From there, the customer can schedule a service call, where a pro performs an assessment and provides an estimate for the necessary repairs.

[Image: rtaImage]

Experience details
This section provides details about the Samsung Thumbtack on Demand (TToD) program.
Experience launched: June 24, 2025
Locations: 
New York 
New Jersey
California
Pennsylvania
Audience:
Customers who own a Samsung washer, dryer, dishwasher, or stove top / oven
Eligible Appliance Repair pros with at least a 4.5-star rating, 3+ reviews, background check) 
Samsung Service Call Workflow: From Booking to Job Complete 

This section provides frontline reps with a high-level look at the flow of Samsung jobs:
 
Customer books the service call
Triage: Samsung determines the appliance (washer, dryer, dishwasher, or stove top / oven) is out-of-warranty and sends the customer a unique booking link.
Booking: The customer uses the link to access the co-branded landing page. They provide job details and select a date and time.
Payment: The customer provides a credit card for the fixed diagnostic fee ($95). A temporary hold is placed, but the customer is not charged until the service call is marked complete.
Pro claims the job
Matching: The job is pushed to the “For you” tab of eligible pros (4.5+ star rating, background checked).
Claiming: Pros see a flat payout of $75 and the job details (including Samsung symptom codes). There are no lead fees for the pro.
Service call and diagnosis
Arrival: The pro arrives at the customer's home to inspect and diagnose the appliance.
The Quote: The pro provides a formal quote for the necessary repairs. If additional parts or labor are needed, the pro informs the customer of these extra costs on-site.
Follow-up: If the customer approves the quote, the pro may complete the repair on the spot or schedule a follow-up visit. 
Repairs and parts: Any repair work or part orders beyond the initial diagnosis are handled directly between the pro and customer outside of the Thumbtack platform.
Job completion and payment
Marking Done: To trigger payment, the pro must update the job status to “Job done” in the Thumbtack app and answer the outcome survey (e.g., "Was the repair completed?").
Payout Logic: Pros are paid the flat diagnostic fee regardless of whether the repair was completed or declined, as long as the service call was performed.
Earnings Transfer: Once marked done, earnings are transferred via direct deposit. It typically takes 3–4 business days for the funds to appear in the pro's bank account.
Key points

Frontline reps must adhere to these guidelines when handling Samsung inquiries. These points help differentiate between Thumbtack-owned processes and Samsung-owned responsibilities.
Samsung Unique Link Logic: 
Accessing the Form: Customers must use the specific link emailed by Samsung to book. 
Duplicate Prevention: Once a request is submitted, clicking the link again will not open a new form. Instead, it shows: "You've already submitted a booking request. Review your project details."
OrderID Errors: If the page displays "We can't find your Samsung ticket number," the OrderID does not match our records. The customer must refer back to their Samsung email or contact Samsung for a corrected link.
Rebooking cancelled job: If the job is canceled by Thumbtack, the customer, or the pro (not Samsung), the customer can use the same original Samsung link to rebook. If the link no longer works, they must contact Samsung for a new one.
Fees and payouts: Customers pay $75 (or $125 in CA). The pro is paid $75 or ($100). 
No Free Diagnostics: Thumbtack never provides free diagnostic visits. If Samsung has offered to cover the cost of the visit, the customer must book through a Samsung-authorized provider and NOT through Thumbtack.
Follow-up Repairs: Payments for repairs/parts after the initial diagnosis are handled directly between the pro and customer and are not tracked in the Thumbtack app.
Cancellation Policy: To cancel a service call, customers must do so via their Thumbtack account  or through the link in their confirmation email. Reps should guide customers to these self-service options.
Misdiagnosis: If a customer claims a misdiagnosis (the pro identified the wrong issue or caused further damage), do not attempt to troubleshoot. Immediately escalate the case to Trust & Safety (T&S).
Customer experience
This section outlines the general customer experience for Samsung appliance repair jobs.
Customer Journey: From Samsung Triage to Repair
This section helps frontline reps understand exactly what the customer sees and does to secure a service call.
Frontline reps should understand this flow to help customers identify where they are in the process.
Triage & Redirection (Samsung Owned)
The customer contacts Samsung for a washer or dryer repair.
Samsung determines the unit is out-of-warranty.
The Samsung agent sends a notification/email to the customer with a unique booking link.
Booking the Service Call (Thumbtack Landing Page)
The customer clicks the link to visit the co-branded Samsung x Thumbtack landing page.
Form Fill: The customers Samsung ticket number will prefill some of the form out:
Prefilled: Appliance type (washer, dryer, dishwasher, or stove top / oven)), Brand, Property type, and Zip code.
Manual: Name, Email, Physical Address, and Phone Number.
Scheduling: The customer selects a preferred date and time. The earliest available slot is 48 hours out.
Payment Authorization: The customer adds payment info to secure the booking. They are only charged after a successful service call (the pro marks the job as done. The fee is non-refundable, even if they decline the repair quote.
Matching and Managing Booking*
The Match: The customer is matched with a pro within 1–2 business days. They receive a Thumbtack confirmation email with the pro's details.
Self-Service: Customers manage the booking via their Plan Page under the "Booked" tab. Here, they can click the job to see a "Reschedule" or "Cancel" button.
The Service Call Appointment
Arrival: The pro arrives within the 3-hour window to diagnose the unit. 
Diagnosis: The pro inspects the appliance.
Decision: The customer decides on next steps: 
Repair completed on the spot. The pro has the necessary parts and completes the fix during the visit. The customer pays the pro directly for the additional labor/parts.
Quote provided, follow-up needed. The pro provides a quote, but parts must be ordered. The pro and customer schedule a follow-up visit outside of the Thumbtack platform.
Quote provided, customer declines. The customer receives the repair estimate but chooses not to proceed. The customer is still charged the diagnostic fee for the pro's time and travel.
Appliance is unrepairable. The pro inspects the unit and determines it cannot be fixed (or is not cost-effective to fix). The pro provides guidance on replacement. The diagnostic fee still applies.
Payment: The $95 ($125 in CA) diagnostic fee is processed through Thumbtack. Any additional repair costs are paid directly to the pro.
*If a job remains unclaimed for 6 business hours (8 am–8 pm PT), the specialized TToD team will begin manual outreach to find a pro. If the job remains unfulfilled after manual attempts, the request is marked unsuccessful, the customer's payment authorization is dropped (not charged), and the customer is referred back to Samsung for alternative options.
Customer Eligibility
Warranty Status: Unit must be confirmed as Out-of-Warranty by Samsung.
Appliance Type: Limited to washer, dryer, dishwasher, or stove top / oven only.
Location: Must be within the service areas (currently CA, NJ, NY, PA).
Booking Method: Must have a valid Samsung Ticket Number or unique booking link. 
Customer service call fee

The service call is for a diagnostic visit only, not the final repair.
Standard Markets: $95 diagnostic fee.
California (CA): $125 diagnostic fee.
Repairs: Any repair work is quoted separately by the pro after the diagnosis.
Payment Authorization: The customer adds payment info to secure the booking. They are only charged after a successful service call (the pro marks the job as done. The fee is non-refundable, even if they decline the repair quote.
 The diagnostic fee still applies when: 
The repair completed on the spot. The customer pays the pro directly for the additional labor/parts.  The diagnostic fee still applies.
Quote provided, customer declines. The customer is still charged the diagnostic fee for the pro's time and travel.
Appliance is unrepairable. The diagnostic fee still applies.
Payment: Diagnostic fee is processed through Thumbtack. Any additional repair costs are paid directly to the pro.
Customer Rescheduling, Cancellations, and No-Shows
Rescheduling: To reschedule, the customer can do so directly in the Thumbtack app. They will find the booking on their Plans tab under “Booked.” Customers receive a confirmation email when Thumbtack reschedules the installation.
Cancellations: If cancelled less than 24 hours before the job, the customer will be charged a $15 late cancellation fee. 
No-Show: If the pro reports that the customer was a no-show, they’ll be charged a $15 penalty.

Access link and booking details 

Customers must use the specific link emailed by Samsung to book. Once a request is submitted, the customers can view their service call details in three ways:
The Samsung Link: Clicking the original link again will show a button: "Review your project details."
Confirmation Email: Using the "View Project" link in the Thumbtack confirmation email.
Thumbtack App: Under the "Booked" tab on the Plan Page.

Thumbtack cannot generate or resend this link.
NOTE: 
Ticket Number Errors: If a customer sees "We can't find your Samsung ticket number," it means the OrderID does not match our records. The customer must refer back to their original Samsung email or contact Samsung for a corrected link.
Duplicate Prevention: Once a customer has submitted a request, clicking their link again will not open a new booking form. They will see: "You've already submitted a booking request. Review your project details."
Rebooking cancelled job: If the job is canceled, the customer can use the same original Samsung link to rebook.
Pro experience 

Pro Eligibility
To be eligible for Samsung appliance repair jobs, pros must meet the following criteria:
Be targeting in Applicable Repair service category 
Be targeting the zipcode of the job (Currently CA, NJ, NY, PA)
3+ reviews with a 4.5+ star rating
Background check completed by account holder.
Although not an eligibility requirement, pros must have direct deposit setup to receive payment.
Pro Journey: From Claiming to Payout
This section helps frontline reps understand exactly what happens for the pro after a Samsung request is generated.
Notification
Notification: Qualified pros (4.5+ stars) receive a push notification, SMS, and email.
▶ What one of the notifications looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

The Listing: The pros see “Samsung Appliance Service Call" in the For you tab. Unlike standard leads, these are preset jobs with a fixed payout and no lead fee.
Visible Details: Pros see the appliance type, zip code, and the Samsung Symptom Code (e.g., "Washer - Not Spinning") with notes from the Samsung agent.
▶ What the job details look like

[Image: rtaImage]

Claiming the Job
Acceptance: The first eligible pro to click "Claim" gets the job. The status immediately moves to "Job Confirmed."
[Internal Only] Manual Fulfillment: If a job sits unclaimed for 6 business hours, the Specialized TToD Team will manually call pros to ask them to take the job.
▶ What the pro sees after claiming the job

[Image: rtaImage]

Before the Job (Preparation)
Direct Deposit Setup: Pros are prompted in-app to ensure their Stripe account is linked to be paid.
Customer Outreach: Pros are expected to use Thumbtack Messenger to introduce themselves and confirm the specific arrival time within the customer's selected window.
On-Site: The Service Call
The Visit: The pro arrives and performs the diagnosis.
The Quote: The pro provides the customer with a formal quote for the repair.
Three Possible Outcomes
Diagnosis only (Repair declined or part needed later).
Same-day repair (Repair accepted, pro has parts and completes the fix).
Non-repairable (Pro provides guidance that the unit should be replaced).
After the Job: Marking "Done" & Survey
Completion Requirement: To get paid, the pro must click the job status and select "Yes, service call done."
Mandatory Survey: The pro must answer: "Did you repair the appliance during the service call?"
If No: They select a reason (e.g., "Follow-up scheduled" or "Appliance not repairable").
If Yes: They see the confirmation screen: "Your earnings are on the way."
Payout Tracking
Timeline: It typically takes 3-4 business days for the deposit to hit their bank account.
Tracking: Pros track this in their Earnings Tab.
Transactions Tab: Shows the "Claimed Job" record for the fixed $75 ($100 for CA).
Deposits Tab: Shows the status of the transfer to their bank.
Pro Rescheduling, Cancellations, and No-Shows

Action
Policy
Penalty / Result
Reschedule
Pros cannot reschedule claimed jobs.
If the date/time no longer works, the pro must cancel the booking.
Pro Cancellation (within 48 hours of job)
Pro cancels the job via the Thumbtack app.
The pro is charged a $15 penalty. The customer is notified.
Pro No-Show
Customer reports the pro did not arrive.
The pro is charged a $15 penalty.
Customer Late Cancel
Customer cancels <24 hours before the job.
The pro is credited $15 to their Thumbtack balance.
Customer No-Show
Pro reports the customer was a no-show. 
The pro will receive a $15 Thumbtack credit. 
Pro Earnings & Payouts
Pros are paid a guaranteed flat fee for the diagnostic service call.
Flat Fee Payout: Pros earn $75 (or $100 in CA) per completed service call.
Lead Fees: Pros do not pay a lead fee when claiming these jobs. 
Payout visibility: Pros can view the Earnings page to see the payment and payout. 
The Transactions Tab shows the individual payment and will be listed with the status 'Claimed job'. 
The Deposits Tab details the actual payout sent to your bank, showing the status and expected arrival date. 
payout, these funds typically arrive in 3-4 business days.
Non-Adjustable Rates: The service call fee is fixed and cannot be adjusted in the product.
Additional Work: Payments for any extra services or repairs outside the initial diagnosis must be handled independently and outside the Thumbtack platform.
2. Process
Steps: How to Schedule a service call with a pro (Customer) 
After the customer follows the link to the Samsung Thumbtack landing page, they will follow the following steps to schedule a service call. 
The customer will fill out a form either manually or by using the Samsung ticket number to prefill the form’s details, including:
The appliance type (washer, dryer, dishwasher, or stove top / oven)
The appliance brand 
The property type (residential/commercial)
Zip code
Customers will always manually enter their:
Email address
Name
Physical address
Phone number
The customer will pick a date and time to schedule their appointment.
The customer will add their payment information before confirming the booking, but they are only charged after a successful service call completion. 
Internal only: The fee is non-refundable, even if the customer decides not to proceed with the repair after getting a quote.
Steps: What to do after claiming a Samsung TToD job (Pro)
After claiming the job on the Thumbtack app, pros will receive the full service call details and confirmation with the customer. The pro should chat with the customer in the Thumbtack messenger as they finalize any other details and complete the job.
Once the service call is completed, the pro will:
Mark the job as Done in the Thumbtack app.
On the next screen, the pro will answer if they “completed the repair work during the service call?”. Pro is paid regardless of what option they choose:
If no, the pro selects which option applies to the job:
Made a follow-up appointment to complete the repair
The appliance is not repairable
The appliance is repairable, but the customer chose to replace it
Other
If yes, the pro moves to the next screen to complete payment.
Internal only: To receive payment, the pro must have Direct deposit set up on their account. For information, frontline reps should follow the steps in the internal Direct Deposit and Stripe (Pro) KA.

3. Talking points 
Pro talking points
General questions (Pros)
Support reps can use the following talkings points to address general inquiries from pros regarding their eligibility, payment methods, and notification for Samsung jobs.

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Q: How do I know it's a Samsung job?

A: You'll see it listed in your Opportunities as a 'Samsung Appliance Service Call.' It will also show a fixed payout amount and have a $0 cost to claim.

Q: How will I be notified about these new Samsung service call jobs?
Q: ¿Cómo se me notificará sobre estos nuevos trabajos de servicio técnico de Samsung?
A: If you’re qualified for the job, you’ll be notified through push notification, text, and email the moment a job becomes available.
A: Si usted califica para el trabajo, recibirá una notificación por mensaje emergente (push), mensaje de texto y correo electrónico.
Q: What are the eligibility requirements for these service calls?

A: Pros must have 3+ reviews, a 4.5+ average rating, have targeting turned on in the eligible category, and the account holder must pass a background check to be eligible. 

Q: How / when do I receive payment? 

A: To receive payment, you must set up direct deposit. After you finish the service call, you’ll be able to mark the job as complete. Once you mark the job as complete, we’ll begin the transfer to your bank account. It typically takes 3-5 days to see the money in your bank account.

Repairs and payouts


Support reps can use the following talkings points to clarify details for pros regarding the guaranteed flat payout, lead fees, and payments for repairs related to Samsung jobs.
English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Q: Am I being charged a lead fee?

A: No. For these specific Samsung service call jobs, there is no lead fee. You receive a guaranteed flat payout for the diagnostic visit. 

Q: Do I get paid if I can't fix it?

A: Yes. The payout is for the service call and diagnosis. You are paid for your time even if the appliance isn't repairable or the customer declines the repair quote.

Q: What if I repaired it on the spot?

A: The payout you see in the app is for the diagnostic service call only. Any payments for the actual repair work should be collected directly from the customer outside of Thumbtack.

Q: Why haven't I been paid yet?

A Please ensure the job is marked 'Done' in the app and that your Direct Deposit is active in your account settings. Payments are triggered once the service call is finalized.

Q: What if I have to order a part?

A: You will still mark the initial service call as done to receive your $[75/100] diagnostic fee. Any follow-up repair work and payments for parts are handled directly between you and the customer outside of the Thumbtack platform.

Q: Where do I see the payment and track the deposit after I mark a claimed job as done? 

A: You can find all payment information on your Earnings page, which is divided into two helpful tabs:
Transactions Tab: This shows individual records for every payment you've received. Look for entries labeled "Claimed job" to see payments from your Samsung service calls.
Deposits Tab: This tab details the actual payouts sent to your bank. It shows the current status and the expected arrival date for your funds.

Reschedule, cancel, no-shows (Pro)

Support reps can use the following talkings points to explain the policies and associated penalties for pros regarding rescheduling, cancellations, and no-shows for claimed Samsung jobs.

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Q: What if the customer cancels?
Q: ¿Qué pasa si el cliente decide cancelar su cita?
A: Customers can cancel more than 24 hours in advance without a fee. If the customer cancels less than 24 hours before your appointment, we'll charge them a fee and you'll receive this in your earnings.
A: Los clientes pueden cancelar con más de 24 horas de anticipación sin cargo. Si el cliente cancela con menos de 24 horas de antelación, se le cobrará una tarifa, y usted recibirá ese monto en sus ganancias.
Am I compensated if the customer doesn't show?

Yes, if the customer doesn’t show, report it within 24 hours, and we’ll add a credit of $15 to your Thumbtack balance to compensate for your time.

Am I compensated if the customer cancels?

If the customer cancels within 24 hours of the job, we’ll add a credit of $15 to your Thumbtack balance to compensate for your time.

Q: Why was I charged $15?

A: "Claimed Samsung jobs cannot be rescheduled. Cancellations or no-shows within 48 hours of the appointment result in a $15 fee to cover the administrative costs of re-assigning the request."

Q: What if I need to cancel the job? 

A: If you need to cancel the job, please try to give Thumbtack as much notice as possible. To cancel the job, you can either go to the messenger and click on the 3 dots in the right-hand corner of the confirmation bubble. You can also go straight to your calendar, click on the event and choose “manage booking.”
If the cancellation occurs greater than 48 hours before the job start time: We will not charge you a cancellation fee since there’s still time to try and match the customer with another pro. 
If the cancellation occurs less than 48 hours before the job start time: Unfortunately, because there’s not enough time to match the customer with another pro, you will be charged a $15 cancellation fee. 

What happens if I don’t show up for the job?

If you don’t show up for the job, you’ll be charged a $15 fee.

What if I need to reschedule? 

Unfortunately, claimed jobs can’t be rescheduled. If the set date and time no longer works, please cancel the job in-product. 

Customer talking points
How service calls works (Customers)
Support reps can use the following talkings points to explain to customers how the Samsung service call process works, including what an inspection covers and how pros are qualified for Samsung jobs.

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Q: How does it work to have Thumbtack match me with a pro?

A: Thumbtack is an online marketplace that connects homeowners with independent home service professionals. For select services through our partners, Thumbtack helps simplify the process by matching you with a top-rated pro. Just choose the service, share a few details about the job, and pick a date and time that works for you.

Q: Is the service call a repair or an inspection?
Q: ¿La visita de servicio es una reparación o una inspección?
A: It’s a service call. A service call is a visit where a pro inspects and diagnoses your appliance. You'll get a repair estimate, and if you approve, the repair may be completed on the spot or a follow-up will be scheduled if parts are needed.
A: Es una visita de servicio o inspección, lo que significa que el profesional revisará su electrodoméstico y le dará una cotización para cualquier reparación.
Q: How do I know the pro is qualified?

A: Every pro in this program must maintain at least a 4.5-star rating and pass a background check."

Q: Is the pro I hire employed by Thumbtack?

A: No, when you book a job through this service, you’re booking with an independent service professional. Thumbtack does not provide the booked service and is simply facilitating your relationship with the independent service professional you are matched with.

Q: How do I see my service call booking?

A: You have a few easy ways to see your details. You can click the original link Samsung emailed you and select 'Review your project details,' check your Thumbtack confirmation email, or log into the Thumbtack app and look under the 'Plan' tab.


Diagnostic fee and payment authorization

Support reps can use the following talkings points to clarify the customer's options for hiring a pro for the actual repair, including payment methods and why the diagnostic fee is charged regardless of whether the customer accepts the repair quote for Samsung jobs.

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Q: How much does it cost?

A: A Samsung appliance service call is a set price of $95 ($125 for California). Your card will be charged after the service call is complete."

Q: What is included in the $95 price?

A: The fee covers the pro's visit and the diagnosis of your appliance. The cost of actual repair work (labor and parts) will be provided as a separate quote by the pro during the visit.

Q: Why doesn't the $95 cover the repair?

A: The diagnostic fee is separate from the repair. It covers the professional’s time and travel to provide an expert assessment of your appliance.

Q: Why is there a hold on my card?

A: When you book, a temporary authorization hold is placed to secure the pro's time. You won't be officially charged until the pro completes the diagnostic visit.

Hiring pro and paying for repair (Customers)

Support reps can use the following talkings points to clarify the customer's options for hiring a pro for the actual repair, including payment methods and why the diagnostic fee is charged regardless of whether the customer accepts the repair quote for Samsung jobs.

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Q: Can I hire the pro for the repair?

A: Yes. You can choose to hire the pro for the quoted repairs and arrange that payment directly with them outside of Thumbtack.

Q: What if I decide not to use the pro for the repair?
Q: ¿Qué pasa si decido no contratar al profesional para la reparación?
A: You can choose not to use the pro to complete your repair. However, the service fee is non-refundable as it covers the pro's time and travel for the diagnosis.. 
A: Puede decidir no contratar al profesional para realizar la reparación. Sin embargo, la tarifa por la visita de servicio no es reembolsable.
Q: What if I don't want to pay for the repair quote?

A: You are under no obligation to hire the pro for the repair work. However, the initial diagnostic fee is non-refundable as it covers the cost of the pro coming to your home to assess the appliance."

Q: How do I pay for the actual repair?

A: The $95 fee handled by Thumbtack is for the diagnosis only. If you choose to move forward with the repair, you will pay the pro directly for those additional costs using their preferred payment method.

Q: What if the pro says it can't be fixed?

A: The service call fee covers the pro's time and expertise to travel to your home and provide a professional diagnosis. Even if the unit is unrepairable, the diagnostic fee is required for the inspection performed.

Reschedule, cancel, no-shows (Customers)
Support reps can use the following talkings points to inform customers about the policies, fees, and procedures for rescheduling, canceling, or dealing with no-shows for Samsung jobs.

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Q: What if I need to reschedule?

A: Life happens. If the set date and time no longer works, you can reschedule by going to your projects page and clicking “Reschedule” on the project you want to reschedule.

Q. Can I cancel my appointment?
Q: ¿Qué pasa si decido no completar la visita de servicio?
A: You can cancel for free as long as it's at least 24 hours before the appointment. Cancellations within 24 hours incur a small fee to compensate the pro for the held time slot
A: Puede cancelar sin costo si lo hace con más de 24 horas de anticipación. Sin embargo, se le cobrará una pequeña tarifa si cancela con menos de 24 horas de antelación.
What if I need to cancel? Is there a fee?

You can cancel your project in-product or by contacting support.
Cancellation occurs greater than 24 hours before scheduled job time: You won’t be charged anything additional.
Cancellation occurs less than 24 hours before scheduled job time: You’ll be charged a $15 cancellation fee, and you’ll be refunded the rest of your payment.

What if the pro cancels the job?

Cancellation occurs greater than 48 hours before the scheduled job time: We’ll work to find another pro to do your job. If no one else is available to do the job, we’ll cancel your booking.
Cancellation occurs less than 48  hours before the scheduled job time: Unfortunately at this time we won’t be able to find another pro to do your job.

1. Overview
This internal article guides Service Reps on using Salesforce to navigate and manage cases, including their statuses, flags, themes, and processes for different situations.
Salesforce is Thumbtack's central internal tool for managing communication with users (pros and customers). It supports Thumbtack’s pros and customers across all communication channels (phone, email, web, live chat, and community). Support reps primarily manage "cases" in Salesforce, which are records used to track, solve, and understand customer and pro issues, questions, and inquiries.
Salesforce integrates with several tools to provide its full range of capabilities: consists of multiple 3rd party applications that can be configured, extended, and integrated. The main applications included:
Salesforce: Manages customer information and cases.
Genesys: Handles phone calls, texts, and chats.
Qualtrics: Used for surveys.
Each department within Operations (e.g., Support, Trust and Safety, Account Management, Sales) has its own application in Salesforce customized to the department's needs. Support reps primarily use cases in Salesforce to:
Submit and track feedback and bug reports from pros and customers.
Record interactions, noting actions, outcomes, and themes discussed.
View user flags (e.g., "Do Not Call").
Case origins
Salesforce automatically creates a case whenever a pro or customer reaches out through official Thumbtack contact channels. These auto-generated cases represent inbound interactions across channels. These cases are distinct from quick cases that reps create manually when system automation or workflow needs require intervention.
You can see which channel a case originated from by checking the Case Origin field at the top of the case:
Inbound phone: Generated when a pro or customer calls Thumbtack support
Email: Generated from an email sent to Thumbtack support
Live chat: Generated from a pro or customer initiated chat session
Text Messages: Generated from incoming text support requests to Thumbtack support
Web: Generated when a pro or customer fills out a contact form on Thumbtack's website
Case generation: Automatic vs manual 
Whenever a pro or customer reaches out through official channels, you will encounter one of two case types in your queue:
Auto-generated cases: Created automatically by Salesforce when a user contacts Thumbtack or when an active (non-closed) case is recycled to you by the system.
Quick cases: Cases created manually by a rep when you need to intervene.
NOTE: If you receive a case without an assigned user, follow Steps: How to find and assign a user to case in this KA.
Technical Logic: How cases reach you
Salesforce uses the current case status to determine routing:
Active statuses (New, Pending): If a case is already in an "Active" state, the system will recycle that case to you to ensure service continuity.
Finalized status (Closed): If the previous case is "Closed," the system generates a new case
Important: If the system recycles a case (active or finalized) but the user is reaching out about an unrelated, new issue, you must manually create a quick case to maintain documentation and survey integrity.
When to create a quick cases
A quick case is a case manually created by a rep. While Salesforce attempts to automate case creation, reps must manually intervene and create a create a quick case in these scenarios:
Missing auto-generated case: No case was automatically created for the interaction.
Trust and Safety (T&S) banner conflicts: Required when an existing case has a T&S banner but the user needs help unrelated to that enforcement, or the rep needs to send a follow-up unrelated to the action.
Language or department transfers (Recycled Case): If a recycled case appears that was previously handled by a different rep who provided the user with help. 
Refund gaming warnings (Advanced Service team only): Required to ensure clean documentation and proper survey triggering.
To create a quick case, follow the (Rep) Steps: How to create a quick case in this KA.
Important: Failure to create a quick case when required is subject to the performance infractions outlined under “Policy and guidelines” in the Reps Survey Dispute (Rep) KA.
When to keep a recycled case

Support reps may continue working a recycled case only if: 
Routing errors: The case was incorrectly routed by the automated system (e.g., wrong language or department). 
Established escalations: The case was transferred to Advanced Support as part of a formal escalation or callback workflow. 
No prior help: The previous case owner did not provide any help during the prior interaction.
Case navigation
In Support Ops, reps work from cases. Cases are used to track and solve Thumbtack's pro and customers’ issues or questions. Cases originate from phone calls, emails, chat, and SMS.
Cases have the following features and tabs: 
Case flags provide real-time visibility to cases requiring responses to pros or customers and can be found under “Case Details” in Salesforce.
Case status represents the state that the case is in. There are four case statuses.
User flags appear on a user's Salesforce account to provide important information for Thumbtack staff. There are two types of flags: There are system generated flags and user-submitted flags.
Case notes (auto summaries): Automatically generated notes from each conversation.
Themes tab is where reps record interactions by noting actions and outcomes and logging themes discussed. Internal feedback is also recorded here.
Bug Search tab is where Frontline reps can submit bug reports. See Bugs KA to learn more. 
Feedback Report tab is where Frontline reps can submit pro and customer feedback and bug reports. See Product Feedback KA to learn more. 
Capture interaction details

AI Agent Summary 
The AI Agent Summary automatically handles note-taking for phone, chat, and SMS interactions, significantly reducing the need for manual entries. AI summaries are posted almost in real-time immediately after the conversation ends and can be found in the case feed. If you experience a delay, try logging out and back into Salesforce. AI summaries generically use the label "Customer." 
Guidelines reps must follow: 
To ensure the AI summary captures everything, reps must ensure all key details are spoken or typed within the conversation. For example, explicitly state the user's name, refund amounts, and specific reasons for requests. 
If a summary is incomplete or incorrect,Support reps should report it to the Gen AI team. Reps should not manually add notes to the summary. QAs will identify and report inaccuracies or incomplete notes directly to the Gen AI team during audits. 
Manual notes
While the AI summary handles most note-taking, reps may need to occasionally add notes manually. Manual notes are still mandatory in the following scenarios to provide clarity and context:
Channels: Spanish Support or email cases. 
Pending Status: Updating a case status to a "Pending" status. Document the specific reason and justification for the status.
Related and duplicate cases: Note multiple related cases for the same user to avoid duplicate work and indicate the primary case.
Transfers: When transferring a case to a different person or team, provide context on why it is being transferred and what actions have been taken.
Additional context: For any internal details or context. Typically added when an AI summary misses something (rare), a process states specific notes must be added, or for future reference to help other reps.
To add manual notes to a case, use the Outcomes/Notes freeform text box and click Save.
Classification

For steps on how to classify a case, see “Steps: Classify case with themes.”
After helping a user, Support reps will use themes to classify the case. Reps should select 1 primary theme and 1 secondary theme, if applicable, to best represent the main reason for the contact. This helps Thumbtack analyze the data and make better decisions about the product and platform.  See the Theme Taxonomy section below for a closer look.
▶ Here’s what the Theme tab shows and how to navigate it:


1. Theme tab: where support reps classify the case.
2. Theme menu: click the arrow for a view of a full list of primary and secondary themes for each user type by specific product areas.Double-clicking a theme will add it to the case. 
3. Status: Represents the state that the case is in. Thumbtack has four case statuses (New, pending customer, pending Thumbtack, closed).
4. Search for themes search bar: enter keywords to see auto-populated results to quickly find a theme. Clicking the result will add it to the case. 
5. Outcomes/Notes freeform text box: add relevant notes that are not fully captured in the 1-2 selected themes but may be helpful to future Frontline reps who may need to support the user in the future. (e.g., related case #, work tickets, etc)
6. Theme box: shows all selected themes. Select the Priority field next to the theme that best fits the main reason for the conversation. Click the trash can to remove a theme. 
7. Save: save selected themes and outcome notes by clicking Save. Selected Actions will show in the case feed at the bottom.

8. AI Agent Summary: The AI summary notes after the conversation ends.

▶ Theme taxonomy structure breakdown
Themes follow a taxonomy and are like tags that describe the topics discussed during an interaction. Theme taxonomy is broken down by: 
User type: Who you are talking to (Pro or customer)
Product lane: Team or product lane over area* 
Product area: Major product area 
Primary theme: Feature or theme impacted 
Secondary theme: Specific issue with feature
* Product lanes are only visible in the auto-populated results from the search bar. Reps are not expected to be knowledgeable about these teams. However, if you want to learn more about these teams/lanes, refer to the Component Ownership wiki page.

Case status


The case status represents the state that the case is in. You can see which status a case is from in the Case status field at the top of the case. The status of a case determines whether a returning user's contact is surfaced as a new or recycled case.
The table below outlines when a status is used: 

Case Status
When it’s used
New
Automatically appears when a Frontline rep accepts or creates a case.
Pending Customer
 - Used only when a rep is actively waiting for a reply from the pro or customer (e.g., rep asked for missing information like screenshots). 
 - Case notes must be added to document what the rep is waiting for. 
 - If no update is provided, the case must be closed within 24 hours.
Pending Thumbtack
- Used when a rep is waiting for an internal team's response after a case has been escalated (e.g., to Trust & Safety or RDT). 
- Case notes must be added to document what the rep is waiting for. 
- If no update is provided, the case must be closed within 24 hours. 
Closed
- Used to mark when an action in the case has been completed (I.e., email response sent). 
- In general, by the end of a Frontline rep's shift, all cases should be closed.
NOTE: Reps should NOT use "Pending Customer” or “Pending Thumbtack" to delay a survey, to seek a second opinion, or because a call disconnected. To manage cases in pending status, see Steps: How to handle your pending cases in this KA.

User flags are designed to provide quick, at-a-glance information about a user that might impact how Thumbtack reps interact with them.  A user flag appears on a user's Salesforce account.
