2. Process

Frontline reps should follow the applicable workflow below to manage cases in Salesforce. 
Steps: How to handle a newly popped case (Rep)
When a new case appears in the reps queue (from a phone call, chat, SMS) or taking a case from the queue, support reps will: 
Identify the concern that needs to be addressed.
Gather and review information related to the concern. Check the AI Agent Summary for initial context and key interaction details.
Determine whether the case can be resolved, needs more information from the pro or customer, or requires insight from another team. 
To do this, the frontline reps will follow these steps: 
Check the case history. 
Click “ View All” next to cases under “Thumbtack Users” to see if there are any related or recent cases. This helps reps: 
Address all of the user’s needs at once. 
Avoid duplicate work. 
Provide more seamless experiences.  
Review case origin: Determine how the case was created: 
 "Case Origin: Web" means the email came through the Webform. 
Subject: "Thumbtack Support Message" indicates that it went through Thumbtack’s email automation software (currently Forethought).
Subject: "Thumbtack Support Team Message" indicates that it went through Thumbtack’s Support teams (the email was handled manually). 
Asses case status: Check for cases that have a status of ‘New’ or ‘Pending’ or any recent ‘Closed’ cases. If there are, see how the case(s) relate to your case and follow the applicable steps below.
▶ “New:” The case is new and needs immediate attention.
Assign all cases to yourself and try to condense all cases into one email response to the pro or customer.
Add notes to each related case, referencing the primary case you're working from (e.g., "Emailed pro on case 012345678 addressing all concerns.")
If another rep has a related “new” case, reach out via Slack and see if they’ve already started working on the case or not (this could occur if agents take a case at the same time). Transfer the case if necessary and provide handover notes. 
For example: Hey, I have another case from [pro name]. If you haven't started working on your case, transfer your case to me, and I'll take care of them.
▶ “Pending:” The case is awaiting further action.
If the pending case is with an L3 team (e.g., Advanced Service Team (AST), OB/Follow-Up Team, T&S, or RDT):
Add notes to the case.
Transfer your new case to that L3 queue. Do not work the case.
Slack the rep to let them know you’ve transferred a related case they’ve been working on it.
If the pending case is with another support rep: Do not transfer the case. You are empowered to own and resolve the issue in your new case.
Review the pending case for context, but handle the resolution on the new interaction
▶ “Closed:” The case was closed.
Review the closed case(s) for context.
Own and resolve the user’s current concern in the new case. This includes re-explaining a resolution, handling a challenge or appeal, or gathering new information.
Do not simply email the pro to say the issue was already handled.
When finished, close your new case
Check the themes of the ‘Closed’ case. 
If it applies to your current case (case is similar), review the closed case to see if the concerns were resolved.
Resolve case: Provide the resolution to the pro or customer. End your email with “Contact us at support@thumbtack.com for any further concerns.” to encourage pros and customers to submit a new email ticket to us instead of replying.
Log and update: Follow Complete standard case wrap-up steps. 
(Rep) Steps: How to complete standard case wrap-up
Follow these steps whenever a process tells you to "complete standard case wrap-up." This is the default — if a specific process gives you its own wrap-up instructions instead, follow those.
Add manual case notes, if applicable.
Classify the case by selecting the applicable theme(s). see Classification above.
Submit any feedback, or bug reports as needed. (See Product Feedback (Rep) and Bugs and Bug Reports (Rep) KAs for steps. 
Set the case status. Close, set to Pending, or Transfer the case, depending on the outcome. See Case status section above for guidelines on when to put a case into which status.

(Rep) Steps: How to handle a closed case with same or new issue 
A closed case is a case with an issue history that has already been resolved. To encourage pros and customers to submit a new email ticket instead of replying to an old case, Support reps should end old email cases with “Contact us at support@thumbtack.com for any further concerns.” 

▶ Closed cases with new issue
Support reps should follow these steps when receiving an old case with a new issue from a contact:
Rep should create a quick case using the Steps: When and how to create a quick case.
Resolve the new issue from the pro or customer accordingly.
End the email with: “Contact us at support@thumbtack.com for any further concerns.”
Document the previous case number on the new case.
▶ Closed cases with same issue
A recontact is not a duplicate, even if it is about the same issue. Support reps are empowered to own and resolve any repeat concerns from the same user, regardless of the channel or prior contact.
Support reps should follow these steps when receiving an old case with the same issue from a contact:
Own the case. Review the previous case history for context.
Resolve the issue. Treat this as a new interaction. This may include: 
Providing clarification if the pro was confused by the first resolution. 
Handling their challenge or appeal of the prior resolution.
If the issue is complex or has been appealed multiple times: 
Follow the standard escalation process to Advanced Service. For steps, refer to the internal Standard Escalations and De-escalation Guidelines (Rep) KA. 
Do not simply stop replying.
End the email with: “Contact us at support@thumbtack.com for any further concerns.”

NOTE: There would not be any escalation or transfer back to the high priority queue as this is strictly reserved for inbound queue segmentation purposes only.


(Rep) Steps: How to handle cases that need more info to close case
Need more info from pro or customer
When there isn't enough info to get started on the user's issue or the Support rep is unable to address the issue due to missing info (e.g., rep asked for missing information or screenshots), reps will follow these steps: 
Ask for the necessary information from the pro or customer.
Change the case status to “Pending Customer.” 
Add a case note documenting the specific information that’s being waited on. 
Select the theme combo: Routing > Non-voice > Not enough info as the priority theme.
Once the rep has the info:  
Provide the resolution to the pro or customer.
Select the applicable theme that matches the user’s main reason for contacting and make it the “Priority."
Provide the resolution to the pro or customer.
If it’s been over 24 hours with no update, close this case. (Follow Complete standard case wrap-up steps)
Need more info from another department or team
If a Frontline rep is unable to resolve an issue because they require more information from another department/team (for example, Trust and Safety), they should follow these steps:
Contact the other Thumbtack team and ask for help resolving the concern.
Change the case status to “Pending Thumbtack” and wait for the team’s response.
Add a case note documenting the details that are being waited on. 
Send a follow-up to the Thumbtack team if you don’t receive a response within two business days.
Once you receive the information you need, provide the resolution to the user and complete standard case wrap-up steps.
(Rep) Steps: How to manage your pending cases
Support reps are responsible for managing their own pending cases daily. The required action reps take depends on the "Pending" status type.
Handling "Pending Customer" Cases:
These cases are waiting for a reply from the pro or customer. 
Reps must review and close these cases within 24 hours if no update is provided by the user.
Handling "Pending Thumbtack" Cases:  
These cases are waiting for a response from an internal team.
Review daily: Check if the internal team has responded. 
If no response after 2 business days: Send a follow-up to the assigned team. 
If no response after 2+ business days: Seek help from your team leader to follow up with the assigned team.
Daily Workflow:
Frontline reps should follow these steps when handling their pending cases:
Review all cases in your "Pending" queue. Pay close attention to the case notes to understand the reason for the "Pending" status.
For "Pending Customer" cases: If the case is 24 hours old and has no user reply, close the case.
For "Pending Thumbtack" cases: Check the case age. If it is 2 business days old, follow up with the internal team. Add case notes for any updates and explain why the case is still pending. 
If a new response is received (from a customer or internal team), take the necessary action to resolve the case and change the case status to Closed. 
Repeat the above steps until you’ve checked all your open cases.

▶ (Team manager) Steps: How to identify cases that need to be actioned/prioritized
Team managers should follow these steps when handling pending cases:
Open the sheet for Open/Pending Cases at start of business
Select the data for your team
Identify cases that need to be actioned / prioritized
Aging cases (more than 2 business days)
Cases on Pending Thumbtack outside SLA
Cases on Pending Thumbtack due to be actioned
Reach out to the agents on your team with open cases.
If the agent is available, ask the agent to check for an update on their open case(s).
If the agent is not available, distribute their open cases to other teammates.
Team managers can also do the scrubbing if in case no one is available to do so
Email cases
(Rep) Steps: How to handle related or duplicate cases (email cases only)
This section goes over how email reps only use the “Duplicate of” field for related or duplicate cases. 
IMPORTANT: Restriction on "Duplicate" Function (Effective Oct 27, 2025)
The "Duplicate Of" field is not to be used for all live, inbound cases (Voice, Chat, and SMS). Failure to follow this process is considered a critical offense under QA guidelines.

[Image: rtaImage]

Who CAN Use This: The “Duplicate of” field should only be used by assigned email reps (e.g., back-office teams like the Refund Dispute Team) . 
Who CANNOT Use This: Reps handling live interactions (Phone, Chat, SMS) must not use the “Duplicate of” field. 
A recontact from a pro is  NOT a duplicate. Support reps on live channels are empowered to own and resolve any repeat concerns from the same user, regardless of the channel or prior contact.
The following steps for marking a case as a duplicate apply only to assigned email advocates:
Instead of transferring the case to the previous case owner, Support reps handling email cases are responsible for handling the cases assigned to them, together with any existing cases currently owned by another rep.
Once the case has been closed or handled, the next advocate will take over any new or ongoing cases.
Reps should only use “duplicate of” if the case is in “pending” status, or if it is still “open” but owned by another rep.
Marking cases as duplicates helps cut down on unnecessary survey emails. There are only a few scenarios that are considered duplicates. Refer to the Duplicate case guidelines table below. 
Duplicate guidelines
What qualifies as a duplicate case
Description and scenarios
Duplicate cases are
The same questions were emailed multiple times, referring to the exact concern (i.e., a refund request for the same customer). 
The case needs to have been created before the original case was responded to in order to count as a duplicate.
The user emailed screenshots or supporting documents related to an existing “pending” case.
Duplicate cases are NOT
Cases where the user reached out, was helped, and then reached out again about the same issue. We should still help these pros or customers as usual.
Cases related to another case, outside the guidelines above.
A prior resolution was already communicated, and the user is challenging or appealing it.
The call or chat was disconnected, and the user is recontacting for a continuation of the conversation.
Reps can learn more about survey exemption guides on the Reps Survey Dispute (Rep) KA.
As a back-office team, the Refund Disputes team (RDT) will continue to use a modified form of case duplication for efficiency. The RDT will consolidate multiple individual refund disputes from a single pro into a single ongoing case or a linked set of cases.
To handle related or duplicate cases, Support reps working on email cases ONLY will follow these steps:
When an RDT advocate identifies multiple incoming emails from the same pro regarding different leads, they should:
Create the primary case for the first dispute.
For subsequent, related disputes, create new cases but immediately tag them as 'Duplicate - Pro Consolidation'.
Link these new "duplicate" cases to the primary user case. The rep handling the primary case will then be responsible for managing all linked cases.
Check previous cases: Check the previous cases to determine if a new case is a duplicate or not.
Click “ View All” next to cases under “Thumbtack Users.”
Cases are only considered duplicates if they meet the guidelines for Duplicate Cases.
All cases that do not fall under the Duplicate case category should be handled by the assigned rep.
Take case ownership: Review previous transactions as it can provide context to the current issue of the pro or customer.
Take ownership by assigning yourself the case. 
Attempt to resolve the users concerns based on the information you’ve gathered. 
When connecting with the user, introduce yourself and explain that you’ll be helping them with their concern moving forward. 
Reassign case: If the user insists on working with the previous rep, the email rep can relay the request to the original / previous rep who handled the concern. 
Leave notes on the case explaining why you’re transferring the case to the previous rep. 
Transfer the case to the previous rep by assigning the case to the previous rep.
Send the previous rep a Slack message to notify them about the new case ownership. Include the reps manager in the Slack message.

(Rep) Steps: How to handle an email case with a Google voicemail
Sometimes Thumbtack gets Google voicemails. These voicemails are transcribed and forwarded to the email queue. Frontline reps should follow these steps when handling an email case with a Google voicemail:
Read the transcript (or click “Play Message” to listen to the recording).
Answer the pro or customer’s questions via email. Your email introduction should start with:
▶ English email introduction template:Thanks for reaching out. Your voicemail was recorded on a phone line we don’t use anymore. To contact us in the future, visit our Help Center and select Contact Thumbtack Support at the bottom of any article. To answer your question, [CONTINUE WITH YOUR EMAIL]
▶ Spanish email introduction template:Gracias por contactarnos. Su mensaje de voz se grabó en una línea telefónica que ya no usamos. Para ponerse en contacto con nosotros en el futuro, visite nuestro Centro de ayuda y seleccione Contactar apoyo de Thumbtack en la parte inferior de cualquier artículo. Para responder a su pregunta, [CONTINÚE CON SU CORREO ELECTRÓNICO]
Send the email and finish the case as usual. (Follow Complete standard case wrap-up steps) 
(Rep) Steps: How to handle an email case with a callback request


Support reps will evaluate the pro or customer’s concerns to identify if they can be addressed via the connected channel or if it would be easier to handle the situation over the phone. 
Most situations can and should be addressed via email. The Support rep will explain to the pro or customer that they can help and ask/answer what they need. It should be rare that Frontline reps are setting up a callback for them.
Support reps should follow these steps when handling an email case requesting a callback:
Read the email to find the pro or customer’s needs.
If pro or customer can call support, send template Pro requests phone support (“call me!”)
If pro or customer can’t call support, send template Pro requests phone support (“call me!”) (Blocked)
Manage the case status for the shift. 
Keep the case open until the end of your shift.
Close case if you still have it at the end of your shift.
If you receive a reply and feel their concerns would be better addressed via phone, reach out to Advanced Service queue to confirm this. (Only if a pro is blocked from calling)
Submit a request to the Advanced Service Team (AST) in Slack. (For steps, see Requesting Help from the Advanced Service Team (Rep) KA)
Wait for Advanced Service to confirm a phone call is appropriate.
▶ If Advanced Service agrees this is a better fit for a phone call:
Send template Callback request- transferred to OCQ for courtesy phone call
Transfer the case to the Advanced Service Case queue
NOTE: Once the Advanced Service team receives the case, they‘ll have preferred times to contact the pro or customer and add it to their calendar. Advanced Service should email the pro or customer to confirm their call and include their you can book me (YCBM) link in the event they need to reschedule
▶ If Advanced Service disagrees:
Reply to their email with template Callback Request - Push Back
Continue to work with the pro or customer on their concerns.
General email steps

(Rep) Steps: How to insert an email template
Email templates allow you to send emails quickly without writing them from scratch. To insert an email template, follow these steps: 
 
Navigate to the case feed.  Click to expand the Email action.
Verify the "To" address.  Add any additional Cc's or Bcc's as needed.
Select the email template icon () in the bottom left hand corner of the email editor.
Select the appropriate folder.
Select the appropriate template.
Review the template for any manual prompts and make the necessary edits.  
Manual prompts will be displayed similar to this: [***MANUAL PROMPT HERE]
Make sure to edit the formatting to remove the bold red text prior to sending the email
TIP: To save a copy of the email as a draft, click "Save Draft" next to the Send Email button. This allows you to save your draft if you need to come back later to finish the correspondence.  Your edits are not automatically saved.
Click Send Email (   ) when ready. Verify that the email sent successfully.
Complete standard case wrap-up steps.
(Rep) Steps: How to send bulk emails
 NOTE: To use bulk macros, you must be given the proper permissions from the System Administrators.
Frontline reps with proper permissions will follow these steps when sending bulk emails:
In a case list view, select the cases you wish to run macros on by clicking the box to the left of each case. This will check the box. Be careful to only check the boxes of cases you wish to run the macro on.
Click the Macros button at the bottom of the service console to open the macro selection interface.
Find the macro you wish to run.
The macro must have a green icon next to it. That indicates the macro can be run in bulk.
Click the play icon.
Confirm that you want to run the macro for all the cases selected by clicking OK.
(Rep) Steps: How to classify case with themes

Support reps use theme taxonomy on cases to categorize interactions, including internal system feedback (e.g., Admin, BigQuery, Genesys, Salesforce, and Slack). Reps should select 1-2 themes that reflect the main reason the pro or customer reached out to support. Thumbtack’s Product Operations team also uses these themes to categorize bug reports and Salesforce feedback. 
Auto summary notes generated from the interaction itself (call recording, SMS, or Cha) are separate from the theme selection process. The summary automatically labels all users as 'Customer,' reps must choose the correct theme under 'Pro' or 'Customer' to clarify the user type.
Steps: 
From a Salesforce case, Frontline reps will select 1-2 themes applicable to the case by following these steps:
To quickly locate and select a theme combo, use the search bar under “Search for theme” and search using key terms. If that doesn’t work, search by product area or feature. 
You can also click through the column dropdowns to the left. To do this:
Select the Themes tab.
Select the applicable user (Pro or Customer).
Click the drop downs under each theme to the applicable themes.
Double click the theme to add it to the case. 
Hover over the last level (usually secondary theme) for the “use case” (definition). 
Reps must choose the correct theme under ‘pro’ or ‘customer’ to clarify the user type.
Add any secondary themes, if applicable, and if it helps clarify the main reason for contact.
Choose the priority theme that the customer or pro cared the most about by checking the “Priority” bullet under Themes. Select the theme that best reflects the main reason the pro or customer reached out to support. 
This may not always be the first issue they mention during the interaction. Sometimes, they may start with minor issues before moving on to the main reason they contacted you for a resolution.
After each interaction, the auto summary will capture what was discussed. In the freeform “Outcome/case notes” box, add any internal Thumbtack notes that would be helpful for future.
There are a few reps who need to leave notes on a case: 1) Spanish support reps will still need to add case notes for Spanish interactions, 2) reps will also leave case notes for email cases. 
Select a case status from the drop-down menu.
Click Save.
▶ THEME TAXONOMY TIPS
Navigate to the Searchable Themes List in Salesforce for a full list of themes with definitions.
Shift away from thinking about actions completed and focus on the main feature or product area that the pro or customer is contacting Thumbtack about. Ask yourself: 
What is the main Thumbtack product area and feature(s) this issue or question is about? 
What specific feedback, question or issue related to their main concern do they have?? 
Use the search bar to quickly locate and select the appropriate themes. Search for key terms first. If that doesn’t work, search by the product area or feature. 
To see a description, hover over the last level (usually secondary theme). 
If reps can’t find 1-2 themes needed to classify a case, they should notify their manager. Managers will work with Support & Product Op managers to determine what needs to be added. Reps should choose the most closely related available theme combo in these instances.
▶ Can't find the theme you need?
Frontline reps should follow these steps if they can’t find the right theme combo:
Select the most closely related available theme combo. 
Notify your manager about the missing theme combo. Managers will work with Product Op teams to determine what needs to be added.
(Rep) Steps: How to create a quick case 
Quick cases let Frontline reps quickly and conveniently create a new case, while assigning an account to the case. For guidelines on when to create a quick case, see the When to create a quick cases section above
A Frontline rep should follow these steps to create a quick case:
At the bottom of your Salesforce screen, click + Quick Case.
Fill out all fields with the user's information:
Full name
Email address
Subject for your case and email message
i.e., Follow-up From Thumbtack Support
Select the case origin from the drop-down list. (email, phone, etc)
Click Submit. The case will automatically be created for you. 
This image shows what creating a quick case will look like:

[Image: AD_4nXfz4v3niS6soLT_HetbgYvtyzRFIRVQtolFryCFCzsgo-Ldp5eyXi34TE2exwrvh77I7FTrfF6WYAJa5WBRywx-M6lftEVgfR8kFt-_zXWtad2mMIWlSIwzqKws4T9gtmH45BUJXBxNq8INEy0vCyxfZ2lB]


(Rep) Steps: How to transfer a case
Sometimes, it’s necessary to transfer a case to a different team or Support rep. This ensures that the right person handles the issue, leading to faster and more effective resolutions for our pros and customers. Here are a few common reasons why a Frontline rep might transfer a case:
Escalating a case to Advanced Service 
Reporting a Trust and Safety incident or 
The case is closely related to another case being handled by a different rep, and consolidating them would be more efficient. 
NOTE: When reporting a T&S incident, follow the transfer steps in the Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA. 
Frontline reps should follow these steps to transfer a case to a different person or team:
Add notes and the reason for the transfer.
Look for “Current Owner” in top left corner
Click Next
Select the person or team you want to transfer the case to.
Depending on the transfer flow, you may ask for additional details before the case can be transferred (e.g., the T&S incidents flow)
Click Update to finish the transfer flow.  
After transferring a case in Salesforce, it’s helpful to inform that person the case was sent to. Reps can Slack the rep (or tag them in the case using “post” if they aren't on Slack) to let them know it's in their open cases.

(Rep) Steps: How to add a user flag 
User flags are designed to provide quick, at-a-glance information about a user that might impact how Thumbtack reps interact with them. Support reps can add “user-submitted” flags, which are added manually by Thumbtack reps.These include: 
Name / Pronoun
Non-Discrimination Policy Notice
Security Code
Spanish Support
Unprofessional Behavior
For more information on the user flags that can be manually added to a user's Salesforce account, refer to the User flags table above. To learn more about adding a security code (or authorized user flag), see Verify Account Information KA.
To add a user flag, Frontline reps should follow these steps: 
Click the plus sign in the ‘Thumbtack User’ section
[Image: rtaImage]
In the Related To section, fill you:
Your case Number
Check the “pro / customer Warned’ box if you warned the user about flagging their account.  
In the Flag section, fill out:
Flag Type by searching for the requested flag
Flag Explanation with why you are requesting the flag
Refer to User flags table for required notes.
Click Save to add the flag 
 NOTE: If an unprofessional behavior flag should be added to a user's account, escalate the case to Advanced Service to handle and add any flags accordingly. See Escalations and Unprofessional or Abusive Interactions KA for steps. 
(Rep) Steps: How to find and assign a user to case (no user on case)
Frontline reps may receive a case without an assigned user. Frontline reps should follow these steps to find a user to attach to the case:
On a Salesforce case, select the “Find User” button.

1. Overview
Thumbtack's Sales team plays a crucial role in acquiring new pros and introducing them to the platform through prepaid packages. These packages are designed to help pros start on Thumbtack with an initial investment, providing a set number of leads upfront. This strategy aims to secure a certain level of engagement from pros and encourage them to view their lead generation as an ongoing investment.
What are Prepaid Packages?
Prepaid packages are bundles of leads, success materials, and sometimes premium support, sold by the Sales team to new or existing pros. By purchasing these packages in advance, pros pre-pay for a set number of potential customer leads and other resources designed to help them succeed on the platform. These packages encourage a higher level of engagement from pros and secure a commitment to using Thumbtack's lead generation services.
What This Knowledge Article Covers:
This article provides a guide for frontline support reps who help pros with inquiries related to Sales prepaid packages. It details the various types of prepaid packages offered by the Sales team, including their benefits, eligibility criteria, and the specific details of the Plus, Premium, and Enterprise Packages, which include Free Front Desk services for a limited time and Service Level Agreements (SLAs). The article also outlines the Demand Guarantee policy, sales processes, and provides talking points to help support reps effectively address pro inquiries and facilitate seamless interactions with the Sales team.
Specifically, this KA will help frontline reps help pros with questions about:
Eligibility for specific packages
Understanding package benefits and terms, including SLAs
Navigating questions about Front Desk access 
Understanding the Demand Guarantee and refund process
Connecting with the Sales team for further inquiries
Updates

Sales Team Prepaid Package Offerings
Thumbtack's Sales teams offer various prepaid packages tailored to different types of pros:
Outbound Sales: For pros who have never used Thumbtack 
Inbound Sales: For pros who have recently signed up.
National Sales: For franchise owners or pros operating in more than one state.
Spanish Sales: For Spanish-speaking pros.
Packages
Thumbtack now offers four Sales packages for pros to select from.

For information on lead credit, see the Service level agreement section below.
Dormant pro prepaid package details
For pros who have been inactive for over 180 days, known internally as dormant pros, a zero-down package option may be available. This package is similar to the standard Sales packages but has the following key differences:
Upfront cost: $0
Success guide
No money required upfront
No Thumbtack lead credit
No signed agreement required
Demand guarantee included in packages 
Sales prepaid packages come with a Demand Guarantee. By purchasing a package and signing a contract that includes the Demand Guarantee, pros are assured of getting the maximum value out of their investment.
This guarantee represents Thumbtack's commitment that pros will utilize 100% of their purchased credit within 12 months of activation. Should there be any unused balance remaining after this period, Thumbtack will refund their unused balance automatically. 
Qualifications criteria for demand guarantee 
To qualify for the guarantee, pros must:
Complete all activation requirements for their Thumbtack account. 
Reps can refer to the internal “Understanding and Completing Activation Requirements (Pro) KA for a list.
Have targeting turned on for at least 80% of the time within 12 months
Have a conversation with their Account Executive (AE) after four months of their package purchase if they haven't spent 50% of their credits by then
After meeting the above criteria, they have unspent credit from their purchase (have not spent 100% of their paid credit)
How the Demand Guarantee works for pros 
Here's a step-by-step explanation of how the Demand Guarantee works:
Purchase and Agreement: The pro buys a Sales Prepaid Package from their Account Executive (AE) and signs a contract that includes the Demand Guarantee. This guarantee ensures they get the most out of their investment.
Four-Month Check-In: If the pro hasn't used at least 50% of their package credit within the first four months,Thumbtack will send them an automated email.
Key Action: The pro needs to schedule a phone call with their AE within three weeks of receiving this email. This is a required step to stay eligible for the guarantee.
Consultation with Account Executive: During the call, the AE will review the pro's Thumbtack profile. The AE will provide suggestions on how to improve their profile to attract more leads. This helps the pro make the most of their remaining credit.
Remaining Eight Months: After the call, the pro has eight more months to use the rest of their credit. This adds up to a total of 12 months from the original purchase date.
Refund Eligibility:
If, after these 12 months, the pro has:
Not used 100% of their credit, and
Kept their targeting turned on for at least 80% of the time
Then, they will be eligible for a refund of the remaining unused credit.
Note: Currently, refunds are processed manually by the refunds team, but Thumbtack plans to automate this in the future.
Refund Notification: Once the refund is processed, the pro will receive an email notification.
Key Points to Emphasize to Pros:
Below are some key points about the Demand Guarantee that Frontline reps should know. However, in most cases, reps should refer the pro back to their AE with any questions.
Activating Their Account: They must complete their account activation to qualify (refer to the "Activation Requirements (Pro)" KA for details).
Targeting: They need to keep their targeting turned on for at least 80% of the time within those 12 months.
The Four-Month Call: This call is mandatory if they haven't used 50% of their credit. They must schedule it within three weeks of the email notification.
Automatic Refunds: Eligible refunds are automatically processed after the 12-month period.

Prepaid package refund requests 
Prepaid package sales are final and non-refundable. However, exceptions may be approved in certain situations. For the complete process on handling these requests, review the applicable KA referenced below: 
Package refund request: There are certain situations where an exception would be made, and a refund would be approved. 
Frontline reps will refer to the internal Prepaid Package Refunds (Pro) KA for additional information and steps. 
Lead refund request: If they use that package to pay for a lead, and that lead qualifies for a refund, they'll get the cost of the lead refunded to their Thumbtack balance to use on future leads. 
Frontline reps will refer to the internal Lead Refunds (Pro) for information on lead refund requests. 
2. Package details and features


Core package details
This section outlines the fundamental components and benefits included in all Sales Prepaid Packages, such as the Thumbtack Success Guide and the Demand Guarantee, ensuring pros have a strong foundation for success on the platform.
Success guide
Prepaid packages come with the Thumbtack Success Guide. This guide is designed to help pros hit the ground running by providing an onboarding guide and a checklist to help them in running their business on Thumbtack.
Pros receive the Thumbtack Success Guide, along with any other relevant information and links, via the email address they used to sign up for their Thumbtack account at the time of their prepaid package purchase. The guide is a PDF.

Plus, Premium, and Enterprise packages and Details 
The Plus, Premium, and Enterprise packages are specialized offerings designed to provide pros with enhanced tools and support to maximize their success on Thumbtack. They include a combination of standard benefits found in the Basic package, plus exclusive features.
Here's a breakdown of what the Plus, Premium, and Enterprise packages include: 
The Plus, Premium, and Enterprise packages include:
 
Thumbtack success guide: Access to onboarding materials and best practices.
28 days of priority phone support: Expedited help from Thumbtack's support team. (See Thumbtack Service Channels to learn more. 
 
In addition to the features above, the table below outlines the package specific benefits only included in all Plus, Premium, and Enterprise packages.

Account executive support (premium feature)
Businesses will have access to phone support from an Account Executive for a limited amount of time. This time will depend on the plan that was purchased.

Access to AE support includes expertise and focus on:
Setting up the pro's budget (and setting up a preloaded balance)

Explaining the value of lead prices and budget
Top Pro status coaching: What it is and how to get it
Service level agreement (SLA) (premium feature)
The Plus, Premium, and Enterprise packages include lead credit incentives for pros who meet specific performance standards during an initial 30-day term. This agreement is locked in for the first month of the package.

30-day commitment requirements
To qualify for lead credits, pros must adhere to the following requirements for the duration of the 30-day term:
Weekly budget: Maintain an unlimited budget.
Job preferences (targeting): Keep targeting enabled at least 80% of the time.
Response time: Respond to at least 80% of initial customer messages within 30 minutes (between 8 am and 8 pm local time).

Lead credit and fulfillment 
Pros who successfully meet the SLA requirements will receive a one-time lead credit applied to their Thumbtack balance. The credit amount is determined by the purchased package:

Fulfillment Timeline: If these Service Level Agreement (SLA) commitments are met, pros will receive lead credits which will be applied to their account within 7 business days after the 30-day term ends. If these commitments are not met, pros will not receive the free Lead credits from their package.
Front Desk trial (premium feature)
The Plus, Premium, and Enterprise packages include a limited Front Desk trial. Front Desk is a service Thumbtack offers that allows pros to get back time in their day while Thumbtack’s dedicated team of agents responds to their customer messages. 
Prepaid package
Front desk trial period
Plus
30 days
Premium
60 days
Enterprise
90 days
The pro’s free Front Desk trial begins the day they sign the agreement. The trail is a limited version of Front Desk, not the full paid service. Here’s how the trail version works:
Auto-Responder: A single, standardized message is automatically sent to leads within two minutes of receipt, 24/7.
Trial end and auto-renewal: The trial ends on the Monday following 30/60/90 days after the agreement start date (depending on the package that was purchased). Unless the pro opts-out, Front Desk will automatically renew to a full paid subscription.
Reps can refer to the internal Front Desk (Pro) KA for information on the paid version. 
IMPORTANT: The following are important notes for frontline reps to keep in mind: 
Auto-renewal: Highlight the auto-renewal aspects of both the Front Desk trial and the SLA agreement.
Opt-out options: Inform pros about how to opt out of Front Desk auto-renewal or terminate the SLA agreement (within the given timeframe).
Front Desk trail end date approaching

The pro’s access to the Front Desk trail stops responding to customers the Monday following the 30/60/90 days after their agreement start date (depending on the package that was purchased).

When a pros end date approaches, here’s what happens: 

Email notification: Pros are sent an email before the end of the trial with the Front Desk Update Form.  
Cancel (Opt Out): To cancel Front Desk, they should submit the form before they get charged.
Continue: To continue with Front Desk, the pro will automatically be charged (unless they opt-out). 
Thumbtack will charge the card on file.  
After the free period, Front Desk will continue with monthly payments of $60.
When upgrading, pros will be charged a one-time fee for the difference in the base price between the original plan and the new plan, and all subsequent charges will be billed at the new plan’s rate.
For any changes to a pro's Front Desk plan, or to cancel, they can reach out to support or submit the Front Desk Update Form. Ops updates the auto-responder twice a day. 7 am, 2 pm.
3. How the Sales team works with pros 
Sales team roles and how they interact with pros
The Sales team has Account Executives (AE) who reach out to new, high-value pros in markets with high customer demand and not enough pros.
The AEs ask these pros to add a prepaid package to their Thumbtack accounts (to be used on future leads), and in exchange, they'll get to work with a Thumbtack coach (an Account Executive). This coach will help them get ahead of the learning curve and get set up for success from the beginning. 
Pro Commitments and Responsibilities During Sales Onboarding
This section outlines the commitments and responsibilities that pros agree to uphold when engaging with Thumbtack's Sales team and purchasing a prepaid package. These commitments are crucial for ensuring a successful onboarding experience and maximizing the benefits of their investment on Thumbtack.
In addition to the credit upfront, Thumbtack asks pros to agree to the following:
Be willing and able to take and pass a background check. Reps can refer to the internal Background Check KA. 
Don’t take jobs on Thumbtack during onboarding.
Be responsive during the onboarding process.
Complete all activation requirements for their Thumbtack account setup before Thumbtack put the credit on their Thumbtack account.
Reps can refer to the internal Understanding and Completing Activation Requirements (Pro) KA for a list.
New pro onboarding flow and Sales contact points 
This section details the onboarding journey for new pros who have purchased a prepaid package, outlining the various contact points available to them to connect with Thumbtack's Sales and Success teams for support and guidance during their initial experience on the platform.
During the onboarding flow, new pros can quickly contact Sales and Success Teams through a Call Us entry point (button).
Click to call is available on the app and web via computer. The click-to-call button is available during the duration of the prepaid package offer.
Pros press the “Call us” button in the top right corner during the onboarding flow. 
Outside of onboarding, “click to call” is available in the packages screen, reachable by email or pro tip.
Push +1(855) 696-8868 in blue which will open up the call on your phone, on web only the phone number will be  displayed as web make a phone call.
After the call is complete, you will land back on the same screen, press X to dismiss and continue to the next step of the onboarding flow.
Pros can click to call a Thumbtack rep during the designated available hours, Monday-Friday: 9 am-7 pm (ET). 
If they call outside of those hours, they will be connected to voicemail and leave a message.
After call completion, pros will land in the phone number screen, X out of the screen to continue the onboarding flow. 
NOTE: If a pro contacts Support because they can't reach a Sales or Onboarding rep, the frontline rep should let the pro know the hours of operation (Monday-Friday: 9 am-7 pm (ET)) and encourage them to leave a voicemail so they can get a call back the next business day.
4. Processes
(Rep) Steps: How to transfer pro inquiries to the sales team
When a pro inquires about sales charges, the sales process, or requests to speak with a Sales team member, frontline support reps should follow these detailed steps to ensure a smooth and efficient transfer:
Identify the Pro's Sales Rep
Ask the Pro: Begin by politely asking the pro if they know the name of their assigned sales rep or account executive (AE). This is the quickest way to connect them directly.
Check the Contact Page in Tack: If the pro doesn't know, navigate to the pro's contact page within the Tack system.
Review Activity Log: Examine the activity log or notes section on the contact page for any mentions of a specific sales rep. This often includes names or contact information from previous interactions.
Direct Contact If Sales Rep Is Known
Initiate Contact: If you have the name of the sales rep, reach out to them directly, informing them of the pro's request and providing any relevant context or details of the pro's inquiry.
Document the Interaction: Make sure to note the interaction and the transfer in the pro's case notes for future reference and move to step 4. 
Help When Sales Rep Is Unknown
Use the Designated Slack Channel: If you are unable to identify the pro's sales rep, go to #sales_am_inbound. 
Provide Detailed Information: When posting in the Slack channel, provide the following information:
The pro's name and Admin link
A brief summary of the pro's inquiry or request.
Any relevant details or context that might help the Sales team.
Monitor for Response: Keep an eye on the Slack channel for a response from a sales team member who can help the pro.
Update the Pro: Once a sales team member has claimed the inquiry, update the pro with any next steps.
Closing the Case
Record Details: Record all relevant details of the transfer in the pro's case notes, including the name of the sales rep (if known) or the Slack channel interaction.
Close the Case: Close the support case with an appropriate resolution status.
(Rep) Steps: How to help a pro asking about their SLA or Lead credit 
To learn more about the SLA and lead credit, reps shoulder refer to the Premium Feature: Service Level Agreement (SLA) section above.
If a frontline rep receives a call from a pro asking about their SLAs or credit, reps will follow these steps:
Search the pro's PK ID in Tack.
Access the pro's Contacts Page.
Look for the "Opportunities" Section: To the right, look for an "[Image: rtaImage]Opportunities" section. 
If it's not visible, click "Show More" on the left side panel to expand the relevant Tack objects, then click on "Opportunities."
Check Opportunities: Click on the relevant opportunity. 
Verify:
Pay $150 (Base)
Pay $300 (Plus: $50)
Pay $600 (Premium: $100)
$1000+ (Enterprise: $250)
For credit questions, reps can explain the credit criteria and application timeline: If these Service Level Agreement (SLA) commitments are met, pros will receive lead credits which will be applied to their account within 7 business days after the 30-day term ends. If these commitments are not met, pros will not receive the free Lead credits from their package.

5. Talking points
This section provides frontline reps with  talking points to effectively communicate with pros regarding their prepaid packages, addressing common inquiries and explaining important details.
General prepaid package inquiries
Eligibility and purchase

This section provides frontline reps with talking points related to pros' eligibility to purchase prepaid packages and the initial sign-up process.

English Talking Point
Spanish Talking Point
After I sign up, can I start meeting customers immediately?
Después de registrarme, ¿puedo empezar a reunirme con los clientes de inmediato?
Before you start meeting customers, you need to tell us which jobs you’re interested in. You’ll do that by setting targeting preferences. You’ll also need to add a few things to your profile (like a profile photo and a review). Once your targeting preferences and profile are set up, you can start meeting customers.
Antes de comenzar a conocer clientes, debe indicarnos qué trabajos le interesan. Para ello, configure las preferencias de enfoque. También deberá agregar algunas cosas a su perfil (como una foto de perfil y una evaluación). Una vez que haya configurado sus preferencias de enfoque y su perfil, puede comenzar a conocer clientes.
Can I buy another pack from you?
¿Puedo comprar otro paquete?
We only offer these packs during your initial sign-up.
Solo ofrecemos estos paquetes durante su registro inicial.
I didn’t buy the pack when I signed up — can I buy it now?
No compré el paquete cuando me inscribí, ¿puedo comprarlo ahora?
No, the prepaid credit packs are only available during sign-up.
No, los paquetes de crédito prepagados solo están disponibles durante el registro inicial.
Where can I see the receipt for the pack I bought?
¿Dónde puedo ver el recibo del paquete que compré?
The receipt was sent to the email you used to sign up for your Thumbtack account. You can also check your Thumbtack balance on your Payments page to see how much credit you still have available.
El recibo se envió al correo electrónico que usó para registrarse en su cuenta de Thumbtack. También puede verificar su saldo de Thumbtack en su página de Pagos para ver cuánto crédito aún tiene disponible.

Credit and budget
This section provides frontline reps with talking points for common questions regarding how pros can use their package credits and manage their budgets on the Thumbtack platform.

English Talking Point
Spanish Talking Point
Are the leads that I purchase with my credit eligible for other discounts?
¿Los prospectos que compro con mi crédito califican para otros descuentos?
Yes, any discounts you qualify for will still apply.
Sí, se aplicarán todos los descuentos para los que califique.
Can I set a weekly budget with my credit pack?
¿Puedo establecer un presupuesto semanal con mi paquete de créditos?
Yes, you can use your weekly spend limit to budget for how many leads you want each week. It’ll work the same with and without the credit. Can I show you how to adjust that?
Sí, puede usar su límite de gasto semanal para presupuestar la cantidad de clientes potenciales que desea cada semana. Funcionará igual con y sin crédito. ¿Puedo mostrarte cómo ajustar eso?
Will my credit pack expire?
¿Mi paquete de créditos expirará?
Your lead credits won’t expire. But the best way to get an idea of what Thumbtack can really do is by regularly talking to customers. Let me give you a few tips on making the most of the credit pack you purchased. 

[COACH PRO ON RELEVANT ISSUES (targeting preferences, profile, messaging customers, etc.)]
Su paquete de créditos no expirará. Pero la mejor manera de tener una idea de cómo realmente funciona Thumbtack es hablando regularmente con los clientes. Permítame darle algunos consejos sobre cómo aprovechar al máximo el paquete de crédito que compró. 

[Educa al PRO EN CUESTIONES RELEVANTES (preferencias de enfoque, perfil, como responder a los prospectos, etc.)]
Refunds and issues
This section provides frontline reps with talking points for addressing pros' questions and concerns about package refunds and other related issues.

English Talking Point
Spanish Talking Point
I’m not getting hired — I want a refund for this pack!
No me contratan - ¡quiero un reembolso por este paquete!
I understand it can be frustrating when customers go with another option. Unfortunately, this credit pack is nonrefundable. It might help to think of Thumbtack the way you’d think of traditional advertising — like a billboard. Every person who sees the billboard won’t automatically become a customer, but several will. You’ve invested in Thumbtack to get your business in front of potential customers, so let’s figure out how to make it work for you. I can give you some tips that might help you connect with more customers. 
[COACH PRO ON RELEVANT ISSUES (profile, messaging customers, etc.)]
Entiendo que puede ser frustrante cuando los clientes siguen adelante con otra opción. Lamentablemente, este paquete de créditos no es reembolsable. Podría ser útil pensar en Thumbtack de la forma en que pensaría en la publicidad tradicional, como una valla publicitaria. Todas las personas que vean la valla publicitaria no se convertirán automáticamente en clientes, pero varios lo harán. Ha invertido en Thumbtack para mostrar su negocio a clientes potenciales, así que descubramos cómo hacer que funcione para usted. Puedo dar algunos consejos que podrían ayudarle a conectarse con más clientes. 
Educa al PRO EN CUESTIONES RELEVANTES (preferencias de enfoque, perfil, como responder a los prospectos, etc.)]


Success materials and other resources sent to pros
This section provides frontline reps with talking points for guiding pros on where to locate and utilize the success materials and other resources included with their prepaid packages.

English Talking Point
Spanish Talking Point
Where can I find my success guide and other resources that came with my package?
¿Dónde puedo encontrar mi guía de éxito y otros recursos que vienen con mi paquete?
We sent links and any information you need to the email address you used to sign up for your Thumbtack account. Head to your email to see how to get started.
Enviamos enlaces y cualquier información que necesite a la dirección de correo electrónico que utilizó para registrarse en su cuenta Thumbtack. Diríjase a su correo electrónico para ver cómo empezar.
Plus, Premium, and Enterprise package specifics

Agreements and renewals

This section provides frontline reps with talking points for discussing the agreements associated with the Plus, Premium, and Enterprise packages, including information on SLA tracking and renewal processes.

English Talking Point
Spanish Talking Point
When will I receive my earned credit?
¿Cuándo recibiré el crédito que he ganado? o ¿Cuánto ganaré?
At the end of your 30-day commitment, we will apply the Lead credits to your account, within 7 business days of your term end date.
Si está inscrito en Front Desk al finalizar su compromiso de 3 meses, se aplicará un crédito del 15% de todos los dólares gastados dentro de los 7 días hábiles posteriores a la fecha de finalización de su término. Si no está inscrito en Front Desk al finalizar su compromiso de 3 meses, aplicaremos un crédito del 10% de todos los dólares gastados dentro de los 7 días hábiles posteriores a la fecha de finalización de tu término.
How do I renew?
¿Cómo renuevo?
We do not offer renewals at this time. 
Después de los primeros tres meses, se autorenovara en el mismo acuerdo que durará un año, y le acreditaremos los créditos del acuerdo de nivel de servicio cada tres meses a partir de entonces. Como Thumbtack, podemos decidir que un profesional no es adecuado para el acuerdo y podemos rescindir su contrato con previo aviso por escrito.
Can I terminate the agreement?
¿Puedo rescindir el contrato?
No, you cannot. If you have questions, you can respond to the email you received from our Sales team. If you don’t achieve the service level agreement, you simply won’t receive credit back.
No, no puede. Si no desea renovar, puede responder al correo electrónico que recibió de nuestro equipo de ventas indic
Front desk trail



English Talking Point
Spanish Talking Point
What is Front Desk?
¿Qué es?
Front Desk is a service Thumbtack offers that allows pros to get back time in their day while our dedicated team of agents responds to your customer messages. 
Pros who use Front Desk can keep their response time under two minutes by setting up responses and messaging strategies for the Front Desk team to work with. 
Front Desk es un servicio que ofrece Thumbtack que permite a los profesionales recuperar el tiempo de su día, mientras nuestro equipo dedicado de agentes responde a los mensajes de los clientes de nuestros profesionales. 

Los profesionales que usan Front Desk pueden mantener su tiempo de respuesta por debajo de los dos minutos configurando respuestas personalizadas y estrategias de mensajería para que le equipo de Front Desk trabaje. 
When does my Front Desk trial begin and end?
¿Cuándo comienza y termina mi prueba de Front Desk?
It begins the day you sign the agreement and ends the Monday following your initial trial period. The trial period depends on the package you purchased. 
Comienza el día en que firma el acuerdo y finaliza el lunes siguiente a 30 días después de la fecha de inicio de su acuerdo.
What impact can it make on my business?
¿Qué impacto puede tener en mi negocio? 
This service has also helped free up countless hours of time, allowing pros to focus on running their businesses while ensuring their leads are engaged with and converted at high rates. 
Pros have seen average response times of under two minutes and increases in lead conversion by 20%. Customers are happy too -- reporting 26% higher satisfaction scores (LTC and NPS) when working with pros who use Front Desk. 
Este servicio también ha ayudado a liberar incontables horas de tiempo para que los profesionales se centren en dirigir sus negocios, al mismo tiempo que aseguran que sus prospectos estén comprometidos y se aumente la tasa de conversión. 

Los profesionales han visto tiempos promedio de respuesta de menos de 2 minutos y aumentos en la conversión de prospectos del 20%. Los clientes también están contentos – informan de un 26% de satisfacción más alta (LTC y NPS) al trabajar con profesionales que utilizan Front Desk.
After my 30-day free Front Desk access, what are my options?
Después de mi prueba gratuita de Front Desk de 30 días, ¿cuáles son mis opciones?
You can continue with Front Desk to support you in achieving your response service level agreement. This will occur automatically, unless you opt out. We will charge the card on file. You can fill out our Front Desk Update Request Form to cancel your Front Desk service.
Usted puede continuar con Front Desk para que lo apoye en el cumplimiento de su acuerdo de nivel de servicio de respuesta. Esto ocurrirá automáticamente, a menos que cancele el servicio. Nosotros cobraremos en la tarjeta que esté guardada. Usted puede completar nuestro Formulario de Solicitud de Actualización de Front Desk para cancelar su servicio de Front Desk.
Can I cancel my Front Desk service?
¿Puedo cancelar mi servicio de Recepción?
You can reach out to support@thumbtack.com or fill out our Front Desk Update Request Form to cancel your Front Desk service. You can cancel at any point, but we require a notice of 2 business days ahead of a new billing month to ensure you aren't charged for the next month.
Puede comunicarse con nosotros a través de support@thumbtack.com o completar nuestro Formulario de Solicitud de Actualización de Front Desk para cancelar su servicio. Usted puede cancelar en cualquier momento, pero requerimos un aviso de 2 días hábiles antes de un nuevo mes de facturación para asegurarnos de que no se le cobre el próximo mes.
Can I upgrade my Front Desk trail?
¿Puedo ascender de categoría mi prueba de Front Desk?
Yes, you can upgrade your Front Desk trial to a plan by contacting support@thumbtack.com or filling out our Front Desk Update Request Form. When upgrading, you will be charged a one-time fee for the difference in the base price between the original plan and the new plan, and all subsequent charges will be billed at the new plan’s rate.
Sí, usted puede ascender de categoría su prueba de Front Desk a un plan poniéndose en contacto con support@thumbtack.com o llenando nuestro Formulario de Solicitud de Actualización de Front Desk. Al mejorar, se le cobrará una tarifa única por la diferencia en el precio base entre el plan original y el nuevo plan, y todos los cargos subsiguientes se facturarán a la tarifa del nuevo plan.
How quickly will the auto-responder be turned on?
¿Con qué rapidez se activará el contestador automático?
The auto-responder updates twice a day. 7am, 2pm.
El contestador automático se actualiza dos veces al día: a las 7 a. m. y a las 2 p. m.

6. Internal FAQ for frontline reps
This section provides answers to frequently asked internal questions about Sales prepaid packages, offering clear and concise information to help them in their support role. This section is for Internal Thumbtack use only. 
Can a pro sign up for a $0 agreement in product?
No, this is an exclusive Sales offer.
Does a pro need to commit to an Unlimited weekly budget?
No, all benefits for the Premium Package are optional. If the pro would like to work to achieve the Lead credits, then they need to accomplish the following:
Unlimited weekly budget minimum*
80% of leads are responded to w/in 30 mins
Targeting is enabled 80% of the time 
*The budget is not a requirement of this package nor commissions and we cannot describe it as such. All of the benefits that come with this package are optional and are not required.
How long do pros get support from an Account Executive and premium phone support?? 
Businesses get access to an Account Executive for a limited amount of time, depending on the package that was purchaced.
Plus: 30 days
Premium: 60 days
Enterprise: 90 days
Any sales or in-product package gets 60 days of premier support post-sale/purchase.
What should a pro do if they have questions about Front Desk?
The pro can reach out to Premier Support.
When are the pros charged for the prepaid package?
Thumbtack charges pros within 24 hours of them signing our terms of service (ToS) and agreeing to the charge.
NOTE: The credit won’t show up on the account until after completing their activation requirements.
Who is eligible for the Dormant pro agreement?
Only dormant pros who have been inactive for over 180 days are eligible.

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article, "Background Checks (Pro)," serves as a comprehensive guide for Thumbtack Frontline Support Agents on handling Pro background check inquiries. It covers the background check process, common talking points for Pros, and various resources for agents.
Background checks (BGC) helps keep Thumbtack a safe platform for users, and build trust with customers.
All pro account owners are required to take and pass a background check. The background checks are always free for the pro (Thumbtack covers the cost). The background check looks for criminal activity linked to a pros name and verifies their identity. The background check requires basic information like the pros name, date of birth, zip code, and social security number.
Background check results can take anywhere from an hour to 14 days to get back to Thumbtack. Publicly, Thumbtack tells pros results typically take around 5 - 7 business days to be processed.
To qualify for Thumbtack Pro Rewards, pros need to take a background check. Reps can refer to the internal Thumbtack Pro Rewards (Pro KA to learn more. 
Name on background check  

When a pro is asked to take a background check, Thumbtack populates the background check form with the name from their account. This means the name on the background check will always match the name on the account.
If a pro contacts Thumbtack saying they need to update the name on their account to take a background check: Frontline reps can direct them to fill out the ID Help Intake Form or use the Salesforce email template ‘Ask pro to send info to ID Help’. 
If the name on their account was spelled wrong, a pro may be unable to complete a background check. If this is the case: Frontline reps can direct them to fill out the ID Help Intake Form. 
Internal note: The name on a pro’s account cannot be changed to anything other than the original account owner’s to complete a background check.
Frontline reps can refer to the internal ID Help Guide KA for more info, along with the internal Account Information (Pro) KA. 
Checkr
Thumbtack uses Checkr, a vendor, to run background checks. Frontline reps should not mention any other vendors or screening methods Thumbtack uses.
Checkr is an accredited third-party background check provider that searches national and state criminal databases (though databases vary by state).
What the BGC looks for: 
In the check, they review the criminal history of the pro with a focus on convictions related to felonies, violent misdemeanors, and theft-related offenses. 
It reviews from when they were 18 until now and will not pull any removed/dismissed charges. It doesn’t pull a credit report.
Thumbtack looks at results on a case-by-case basis. 
Timeline on results: 
Background check results can take anywhere from an hour to 14 days to get back to us. 
Publicly, Thumbtack tells pros results typically take around 5 - 7 business days to be processed. 
Contact Checker about BGC results: 
Due to the sensitive nature of BGCs, Thumbtack cannot reach out to Checkr on behalf of the pro or discuss the results with the pro. 
Any pro who has questions about Checkr can reach out to them directly at (844)824-3257 or support@checkr.com.
Pros can also read about Checkr security (Privacy Policy | Checkr Legal) and check out their FAQs (Candidate Background Check Status and FAQ) on their website.
Mandatory background check

 
▶ INTERNAL THUMBTACK INFORMATION ONLY ABOUT MANDATORY BACKGROUND CHECKS
The following information is only for internal Thumbtack information only and should not be shared with external users. Frontline reps should use the approved talking points in this KA to navigate these conversations.
Trust and Safety can request a pro take a background check at any time, even if one was taken. The pros account may be placed on hold until the background check is taken.
Reps can refer to the internal Removed or Banned Users (Pro) (Customer) and Account Holds (Pro) KAs to learn more. 
If a pro is asked to take a background check it’s required and must be completed to use Thumbtack, new pros included. Here’s how it works: 
Email to take BGC: The pro will receive an email with a link to submit their information to the Checkr system. 
Frontline reps can direct the pro to the email that was sent to submit their information. 
They can try searching their inbox for "Action required: Take a free background check"). 
If they can’t find the email, first make sure the pro is required to take one. To resend the email, follow the Steps: How to resend BGC invite email to pro (Rep) below.
Account hold: The pro’s account will be on hold until they pass the background check. This applies for new pros as well. 
If the pro is being asked to complete a check, their account may be closed under the reason “Escalated to Checkr by Fides.”
Thumbtack’s terms of use
In December (2018), Thumbtack updated its Terms of Use to state we can process background checks for pros throughout their use of Thumbtack. Thumbtack made this update to ensure the safety of the platform and keep records up-to-date.
If a pro decides they'd like to remove their account because of this, let them know it could take up to 35 days to be removed from this process.

When to escalate to Trust and Safety (T&S)
 

There may be times Frontline reps will escalate a case to Trust and Safety (T&S) because: 
There is a concern or report of a pro that may have a criminal background.
A pro is asking about background checks, and after you've asked a few probing questions, feel that there may be a potential criminal background we should investigate.
To escalate, reps will follow the report incident steps on the internal Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA. Don’t escalate if the pro is just upset about their results or has questions about why they were removed from the site due to a background check.
Background check results and timeline 

Background check results can take anywhere from an hour to 14 days to get back to us. Publicly, we tell pros results typically take around 5 - 7 business days to be processed.
If a pro calls about their background check before seven days have passed:
Do tell the pro Thumbtack will wait to see the results of their background check before making any decisions.
Don't bring up specific results or crimes with the pro or engage in “what if” scenarios or tell the pro if specific results will be okay or not.
Direct them to https://applicant.checkr.com. 
From there, they can check the status of their check and request copies of their results. 

Internal note: Due to the sensitive nature of BGCs, Thumbtack cannot reach out to Checkr on behalf of the pro or discuss the results with the pro. Any pro who has questions about Checkr can reach out to them directly at (844)824-3257 or support@checkr.com.
Pro passed background check (BGC meets Thumbtack requirements)
If the pro’s results do meet Thumbtack's requirements, the pro will receive the background check badge in the “Credentials” section on their profile. If the account was disabled, it will be reactivated.

Do direct pros to their results for more details or applicant.checkr.com for more details.
Pro failed background check (BGC doesn’t meet Thumbtack requirements)
If the pro’s results don't meet Thumbtack's requirements, the pro is removed from Thumbtack.
Pros who have been removed from Thumbtack because of background check results won’t be added back. However, sometimes it’s possible to have charges removed from the pro's record. Frontline reps can refer to the section below to learn more. 
Additionally, if the pro was removed (and Thumbtack will not reconsider their account), the Trust and Safety team will refund the pro's credit balance to the card on their account. Frontline reps can see the refund section below to learn more. 
A few things to note: 
Thumbtack doesn't make these decisions lightly. Careful consideration has been given to how Thumbtack handles background checks. 
Thumbtacks standards regarding background checks apply to all pros, with no exceptions. 
Thumbtack’s decision wasn’t made because of them specifically or because of their specific background. Any pro with these same results would have the same action taken.

Internal note: Frontline reps should not reactivate any accounts closed for background check results or bring up their specific results or crimes.
Dispute results | Pro has charged removed or results change
The pro has seven days to dispute the convictions with Checkr before Thumbtack takes action. If the seven days pass, and Thumbtack doesn't hear anything, action is taken.
The pro will need to contact Checkr [email support@checkr.com or call (844)824-3257] to dispute their background check results. Checkr will help the pro get their information updated.
If, in the future, the pro says there are changes to their background check results, they can resubmit for an updated background check. Thumbtack will determine the pro's eligibility based on the most recent background check results on file.
Thumbtack balance returned to removed pros card 

 
If a pro was removed (and Thumbtack will not reconsider their account), the Trust and Safety team will refund the pro's credit balance to the card on their account.
Internal note: Only in-policy refunds will be processed back to the original form of payment. Thumbtack won't provide refunds for any past quotes or promotional (unpaid for) credits. Reps can refer to the internal Transfer Pros Cashable Balance Back To Card KA to learn more. 
Steps: How to help a removed pro who hasn’t received their funds (Rep)
If pro says they haven’t received the funds, Support reps will follow these steps:
Go to the pro's admin.
Check their credits to see if a refund was processed
If it's already been processed, let the pro know they should see the refund on their card within 7 - 10 business days.
If they weren't refunded, post in the #background-check-questions Slack channel for a Trust and Safety specialist to review the case. 
Once a refund has been processed, let the pro know they should typically see the refund on their card within 7 - 10 business days.

Import reviews from Google or other sites to Thumbtack profile 
Thumbtack offers two main ways to import reviews from outside sources to enrich their profile: Google Reviews and Other Site Reviews (Aggregated Ratings). Understanding the differences between these options is key.
▶ General Important Considerations for All Imported Reviews
Regardless of whether a pro imports Google reviews or an aggregated rating from other sites, frontline reps should note the following:
Verification Status: Imported reviews are not considered "verified" by Thumbtack.
Top Pro Status: While imported reviews contribute to a pros overall star rating, they do not count toward Top Pro status (for Pro Rewards). Top Pro status is calculated from verified reviews from Thumbtack customers.
Permanence: Once imported, these reviews or ratings cannot be edited or removed by the pro. However, Google reviews can be refreshed to display the most recent reviews. If the reviews violate the Content and Review Policy Thumbtack will remove them. 
No Ranking Factor: Imported reviews or ratings do not directly factor into ranking in Thumbtack search results.
Facebook Reviews: Importing Facebook reviews is not supported at this time.
▶ Import reviews from other sites (Aggregated Ratings)
Importing reviews from other sites allows pros to import an aggregated star rating from other online platforms where their business is listed. This feature is particularly helpful for new pros and is now available on-demand, not just during initial onboarding.
Frontline reps can refer to the internal Prebuilt Profiles and Importing Reviews From Other Sites (Pro) KA 
for talking points and to learn more. 
▶ What is Imported:
Only the overall aggregated star rating is imported.
No review text is imported from these other sites.
The aggregated number of reviews will show up as a number only (e.g., "4.5 stars based on 50 reviews").
Why We Offer This: We calculate the pros average rating from publicly available reviews to make signing up on Thumbtack easier. This helps pros quickly establish a reputation and meet the 1 review requirement for profile activation, getting them closer to growing their business on Thumbtack.
▶ How review imports from other sites work
Access Point: On the web, the option to import reviews from other sites is available from the pro's profile page, not from their general reviews page. It may also be presented during onboarding.
Business Information Match: Pros will go through a flow similar to prebuilt profiles where they select their business information.
If your business is found: Pros can select their business name and claim the available information. If multiple records are found, they will all be displayed. Pros can then choose "Add rating" or "Don't add."
If your business is NOT found: Pros will see "My business isn't shown here." If they click this, they'll be taken to a screen suggesting "We couldn't find any online reviews for your business." Pros will then have the option to "See other options," which takes them back to their reviews page to explore importing Google reviews or contacting past customers.
▶ Specific Notes for Other Site Reviews (Aggregated Ratings):
Profile Activation: For new pros using prebuilt profiles, importing an aggregated rating helps you instantly meet the 1+ review requirement for profile activation, allowing you to get started quicker.
Impact on Thumbtack Rating: Your imported average review rating impacts your overall Thumbtack review rating with the same weight as reviews you get on Thumbtack. As you receive more reviews from Thumbtack customers, they will be factored into your total review rating.
Business Name Change: The third-party review rating will be removed if you change your business name on Thumbtack.
Reps should refer to the General Important Considerations for All Imported Reviews section above for additional key details. 
▶ Google review imports
Pros can import their Google reviews to enhance their Thumbtack profile with more customer reviews. This feature allows pros to import up to 100 of their most recent Google reviews. Pros can update their imported Google reviews to feature their most recent reviews by clicking the 'Update' button in the 'Reviews' section of their Profile tab.
▶ What is imported
Thumbtack only imports reviews that have the following: 
Reviewer name
Date
Rating
Review text
No other information will be pulled over in the import — just the review info. Pros don't get to choose which reviews are imported. And once imported, pros cannot delete these reviews.
▶ Specific Notes for Google Review:
Initial Import and Refresh: Pros can initially import up to 100 of their most recent Google reviews once. However, they can then manually refresh these imported reviews at any time to reflect their newest Google reviews.
Update Imported Reviews: Pros can update their Google reviews to feature their most recent reviews by clicking the 'Update' button in the 'Reviews' section of their Profile tab."
No Selection: Pros cannot choose which specific Google reviews to import; the system pulls their most recent ones up to the 100-review limit.
Refresh from a different Google business account: Pros can now also refresh their Google reviews from a different google business account, as long as that google business account is not yet tied to another Thumbtack business profile.
No Automatic Updates: Imported Google reviews on Thumbtack will not automatically update if the original reviews on Google are changed. However, pros can manually refresh them.
Responses to Imported Reviews: If a pro has responded to an imported Google review on their profile and then refreshes their Google reviews, their response may be removed if the original review is no longer among the 100 most recent reviews imported. Pros should be aware that refreshing can alter the set of displayed reviews and their associated responses.
Reps should refer to the General important considerations for all imported reviews section above for additional key details.

Steps: How to help pro with issues importing their Google reviews (Rep) 
If a pro encounters problems while importing their Google reviews, frontline reps should guide them through the following checks:
Google My Business (GMB) Visibility: Confirm that the pro can see their business listed in Google My Business (GMB), which is Google's location manager dashboard.
GMB and Search Consistency: Verify that the business displayed in GMB is the same as the one visible in Google Maps and search results.
Login Email Match: Ensure the pro is logging into Google with the identical email address used for their GMB account when attempting to import reviews.
Street Address Requirement: Confirm that their Google business location has a physical street address.
Address Visibility: Check that their business's address is not hidden within GMB settings.
