3. How pros respond to reviews
Steps: How to respond to a review (Pro) 

It’s a good idea for pros to post personalized review responses to show customers a pro cares. Pros can respond to each customer review on their profile, and the response will be shown alongside the review. Responses (like reviews) can’t be edited. Pros can respond once to each review and updated review. 

Frontline reps should remind pros that their review response will be public, so they should be polite and professional.
Pro steps: When a pro has their response ready to post, they can follow the steps on the How to respond to reviews – Thumbtack Help article.
Responding to a negative review 

Pros with negative reviews will sometimes contact Thumbtack Support looking for help or asking for the review to be removed. Thumbtack doesn’t allow pros to delete and then re-create their account just to remove the negative reviews. Instead, reps should encourage them to respond to the reviews.
Responding to a negative review allows the pro to provide additional context and lessons learned for other customers to see. Reps can coach pros on how to respond in a way that builds trust with customers.
Responding to a negative review allows the pro to provide additional context and lessons learned for other customers to see. Here are a few ways to respond to negative reviews: 
Thank the customer for their feedback.
Tell the customer that you’d like to find a compromise and offer some suggestions.
Say you’re sorry the customer wasn’t pleased with the work.
Let the customer know you’ll reach out so you can fix the situation.
Explain that you’ll keep their feedback in mind for future jobs.
Guidelines for helping pros respond to reviews (Rep) 
If the pro needs help writing their response, frontline reps must follow these guidelines:
Do coach the pro on how to respond and suggest what to include. ​
Don’t publish (or write) review responses for pros, the pro needs to actually post the review.
Do review the details to help uncover constructive feedback for future projects and customer interactions (i.e., work on not being late, etc.)​
Do probe. This means asking questions, figuring out why this review was left.
Don’t advise pros to send follow-up messages to customers to resolve the issue. They’re welcome to do this, but we want to be consistent and encourage them to send a public response.
Offer tips to help pros respond to reviews in a way that builds trust with customers (Rep) 
When coaching the pro on how to respond to a review, frontline reps can offer the tips below:
Thank the customer for their feedback.
Keep it direct and to the point.
Say sorry the customer wasn’t pleased with the work.
Provide additional context.
​For example, the customer might say that a project cost more than the pro initially quoted. The pro could explain why that would be and provide additional insight the customer (and future customers) may not have considered or know
Address concerns by sharing lessons learned.
For example, a customer might point out it was hard to get a hold of the pro.
Pro response example: "I'm sorry you felt like it was hard to get a hold of us. We'll be sure to increase how often we're checking our messages to make sure all our customers feel like they're able to reach us when they need to."
If the pro doesn’t like the photos the customer uploaded, encourage them to add any photos they have to their image gallery. Pros can’t include photos in review responses. 
4. Review ranking and rating   
Review order  

Reviews are ordered slightly differently depending on where you’re looking at them and what factors are considered.  
Customers like to see the work pros do, so the most complete and recent review will appear first. After that, the review order is determined by:
Reviews that have one or more of the keywords a customer searched for.
Reviews for the service a customer is looking for.
Verified reviews
Reviews with at least one media item
Reviews containing between 52 – 675 characters
Reviews that have been updated recently
For example, a recent verified review with a photo of the job will appear higher than an older unverified review without an image.
In search results, the customer sees the pro’s overall review rating and how many reviews they have. Once the customer clicks into a profile, the customer can see all of the pros' reviews.
NOTE: Use the Review ranking/order talking points to help navigate these conversations. 
Review ranking on a pro’s profile: How it works  
When a customer views a profile’s profile, the reviews on the profile will be ranked in the following order: 
Customers review: If the customer is viewing the profile of a pro they've already reviewed, their review will appear first.
Keyword: Reviews that contain all or some of the keywords the customer searched for
The service / category: Customers want to see reviews for the service they're looking for specifically
Verified reviews: Customers trust reviews from other Thumbtack customers
Media items: Attaching media (like a photo) to a review adds accuracy
Text length (within 52 to 675 characters): These reviews are usually more detailed and helpful to customers than shorter reviews (i.e., “She did a great job!”)
Timestamp: Experiences can change, so recent reviews are more relevant to new customers
Review ranking in messenger: How it works  
In the messenger, the review order is slightly different from on the profile (not as many factors are considered).

Here's how reviews are ranked in Messenger:
Customer Reviews: If a customer has already reviewed a pro, their review is prioritized and displayed first.
Verified Reviews: Verified reviews are prioritized, with the most recent verified reviews appearing first.
Media Content: Reviews that include images are ranked higher.
Text Length: Longer reviews are ranked higher than shorter reviews.
Recency: Recently updated reviews are ranked higher than older reviews.
Review rating calculation   
Frontline reps can utilize a review calculator to:
Determine how many five-star reviews a pro needs to reach a desired review rating.
Calculate a pro’s current average review rating
Note: When calculating for Pro Rewards, reps should only count verified reviews within the specified time period. While imported reviews contribute to a pros overall star rating, they do not count toward Top Pro status (for Pro Rewards). Top Pro status is calculated from verified reviews from Thumbtack customers.
Review calculator sheets (internal only): 
Reviews Calculator
Reviews Calculator
Note to reps: Don’t make a copy of the sheets above.

5. Thumbtack’s content and review policy   
In order to preserve the integrity of the reviews, Thumbtack’s Content and Review Policy. is that Thumbtack rarely ever removes reviews or updates reviews. Keep in mind that content on Thumbtack’s site may be disagreeable to pros without being in violation of this policy — a negative review alone is not grounds for removal.
If Thumbtack considers removing a review, it will first be reviewed by the Trust and Safety team who will consider if the review violates Thumbtack's Content and Review Policy. If you are uncertain whether a review qualifies for removal, or the pro remains insistent after receiving a clear policy explanation, always submit a dispute. Trust and Safety will review the case and email the pro with a final decision. Do not make this determination yourself — that is T&S's role.
Pros and customers can refer to the public-facing Content and Review Policy – Thumbtack Help for more information.
Reviews removed automatically versus manually 
  
There are two ways a review can be removed from Thumbtack:
Automatically: Thumbtack's systems proactively flag and remove reviews that violate the Content and Review Policy or Terms of Use — most commonly inauthentic reviews. See Inauthentic (fake) reviews section below for details.
Manually: The Trust and Safety team reviews and removes content flagged by reps or reported by pros and customers. Pros may contact Support requesting that a review be removed. Thumbtack will consider manually removing a review if it violates the Content and Review Policy.
For full criteria, see Does this review qualify for removal? Below.
Inauthentic (fake) reviews   
Important note to frontline reps: When discussing inauthentic reviews with pros, always use the term "inauthentic" —never "fake" or "fraudulent."
Thumbtack monitors pro accounts to ensure they aren't posting inauthentic reviews to their profile. This is done automatically by Fides, Thumbtack's internal system, and manually by the Trust and Safety Proactive team. Reps should refer to internal Removed or Banned Users (Pro) (Customer) KA> Inauthentic/fake reviews for additional information. 
Reps should be aware of the following when handling inauthentic review cases:
Transparency & Confidentiality: Thumbtack does not disclose the specific reasons why a review was flagged to the pro or customer. Reps can only inform them that it violated Thumbtack’s Terms of Use. Reps can use the review deletion reasons in the table below to determine why a review was removed. Do not share these specific reasons with the pro.
Communication: Explain that Thumbtack takes the legitimacy of reviews very seriously and will not reconsider this decision. Use the talking points in this KA to help navigate these conversations. 
▶ Inauthentic review deletion reasons
The table below describes the internal deletion reasons Trust and Safety uses when removing inauthentic reviews. These reasons are for internal rep use only — do not share them with the pro. Use them to understand why a review was removed and to determine next steps.
Deletion Reason
What it means
Next steps 
3 IP Match
The pros signup IP, the customer’s signup IP and the review IP all match. Because of this, Thumbtack is very confident that these reviews are inauthentic
Thumbtack won’t reconsider these reviews.
Cust — Cust Device Match
The customer who left the review is linked (by device) to another customer who left a review for the pro. Since the link is a device match, Thumbtack considers the two customers to be the same person and only let the pro keep the oldest review.
Thumbtack won’t reconsider these reviews.
Fake Verified Review — Manual Review
Thumbtack either found a device link between the pro and customer, or the time from initial contact to review was suspiciously short. Thumbtack looks at both the review text and messaging between the pro and customer and if there’s doubt that the work wasn’t completed, the review is removed.
If the rep believes the review was actioned improperly, they’ll follow the steps below.
Pro — Cust Device Match
The pro and the customer share the same device.
Thumbtack won’t reconsider these reviews.
Same Pro Different Service — IP Match
A customer left a second (or more) review for a pro, but for a different service. The customer and pro also share the same login IP address. Thumbtack wants reviews to be one review for one job.
Thumbtack won’t reconsider these reviews.
▶ Steps: How to help a pro disputing an inauthentic (fake) review removal (Rep)
Thumbtack’s Proactive team (in Trust and Safety) only removes reviews (and accounts) when they're sure the pro left the review themselves. Frontline reps can use the talking points in this KA to help navigate these conversations. 
If a pro disputes a review that was removed for being inauthentic (fake) with the deletion reason Fake Verified Review — Manual Review, frontline reps will follow these steps:
If a rep sees that the review was posted close to initial contact or has doubt that the work wasn’t completed, inform them that we (Thumbtack) will investigate further.
To escalate a case, frontline reps will submit a report to the Proactive queue by following the steps on the internal Trust and Safety Incidents KA and include the following information on the case: 
Detailed notes
Timeframes of reviews posted
Does the request qualify for removal?   
Thumbtack does not edit reviews or review responses. A review or response may only be removed if it violates our Content & Review Policy, Non-discrimination Policy or Thumbtack’s Terms of Use. If a review does not meet any of the criteria below, it does not qualify for removal.
Timeline requirements: 
To dispute a review, the pro or customer must contact Thumbtack within 30 days of the review being posted. 
Removal exceptions (typo, gibberish, unwanted text, personal information) must be requested within 24 hours provided an identical duplicate review exists, proving the user's intent to leave a single, authentic review.

IMPORTANT: While frontline reps are equipped to handle many review-related inquiries, some situations require the expertise and authority of the Tr

1. Overview
▶ KA summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) is for frontline reps to help customers with questions about leaving, updating, or removing reviews on Thumbtack.
Reviews help customers get to know pros, check their reputation, and build trust to move forward and hire them. 
In search results, the customer sees the pro’s overall review rating and how many reviews they have. Once the customer clicks into a profile, the customer can see all of the pro’s reviews. 
NOTE: This internal KA does not outline all review content. For information on our Content and Review Policy, along with how to dispute a review and review removal reasons, see Reviews (Pro) KA. 
Leaving a review as a customer 
This subsection explains the process of customers leaving a customer review, including how customer reviews are verified, timeframes for posting, and the option to add photos.
Customers can leave a review for a Thumbtack pro either through their Thumbtack inbox or by using the pro's link if provided. Reviews from customers who contacted the pro through Thumbtack are considered verified and will be displayed on the pro's profile as "Verified" or "Hired on Thumbtack."
Reviews must be posted within six months after the last interaction between the customer and the pro or within one year of the last day the pro worked on the project. After submitting their review, customers will be asked to provide the cost of the job, but this step is optional.
Customers have the option to add photos when leaving a review. Each photo should be less than 10 megabytes and a jpg or png file. 
For steps, see (Customer) Steps: How to leave a review below.
▶ Customer asked for job cost when posting a review
This section clarifies why customers are asked for job costs after submitting a customer review and assures that this information is not published.
After a customer submits their review, they’re asked how much the job cost. Thumbtack collects project costs from customers when they submit a review on both the website and app.
They can select between:
Total cost
Per hour
Per session 
or decide to skip this step.  
The cost won’t be published. Thumbtack uses this information to help future customers get accurate estimates. To learn more about estimates (and starting costs), see the Projects (Customer) KA > Starting cost and estimated cost.
To update the project cost after submitting a review, customers can follow the update review steps  to make changes. 
▶ What the job cost page looks like

[Image: AD_4nXer_JggvPIbTQ5eqRXj2-dkI_Qfyc8LsBanBdCYGY_9nhXjVfj6RbT99LZpppUM-0LMHTfLKRa0j1FP9zwvSuRAjFOshOEJySWLFHhqFfndWoLkGDkHDibWpsepP4wV_0pMt-fAKI3m8gvbnA954M6p3cBr]

Internal Thumbtack info ONLY
Other customers can’t see the cost they provided once their review is posted. 
The cost of the project is not visible in Admin, or for reps to view. 
The data is being used for analysis and data sources so that we can surface for accurate upfront pricing (which is related to the "estimated cost").
Job cost data will be used to inform other monetization initiatives like a better understanding of how much we should be charging pros for leads and bookings.


▶ Ways to talk about it with customers (translations coming soon)
Why do you ask me for the cost of the job? 
Giving customers like you the ability to add information about the cost of the job helps us better understand how much this job will cost for future customers. This information will make price estimates more accurate and help customers have a better estimation of what the job will cost when searching for a pro. 
Can I edit the project cost I submitted with my review?
Yes. If your review is verified (meaning you contacted the pro through Thumbtack), you can update it once. After submitting the updated review, you’ll be asked to add the project cost again – this is where you can make your changes. To update a review, head to Thumbtack.com on a web browser (not the app).

Updating a review as a customer
This subsection details how and when customers can update a customer review, emphasizing that updates can only be made once to verified customer reviews.

If a customer wants to remove, change, or finish a posted review or didn't include text with their rating, they can update their review. 

To update a review, it must be verified (review from a customer who contacted the pro through Thumbtack). Customers can only add an update once. Reps should tell customers to read over their review for accuracy and typos before submitting. 

Thumbtack’s policy is to keep reviews even if the pro has reached out to make the situation right afterward. This is also true if a customer has an initially positive experience that later becomes negative after they've left the review. 

If the customer is being harassed or threatened by the pro, frontline reps should escalate the case by following the steps on the  Trust & Safety Incidents KA.
For steps on updating review, see (Customer) Steps: How to update review
▶ Reasons a customer would not see the option to update a review
This section outlines common reasons why a customer might not see the option to update their customer review, such as having already updated it or the customer review not being verified.
If the customer doesn’t see the option to update their review, it could mean they’ve already made an update to their original review, the review isn’t verified, or they aren’t on the app.
Reviews can only be updated once. Customers who’ve already updated their review won’t be able to make any other changes to it.
Only verified reviews can be updated. Verified reviews are from customers who connected with the pro through Thumbtack. If the review isn’t verified and the customer thinks it should be, they should contact us for help. 
Reviews can’t be updated on the Thumbtack app. To update a review, customers need to be logged into their Thumbtack account using a mobile or web browser. 
Customer requests to remove their review
This subsection explains Thumbtack's policy on customer review removal, highlighting the rarity of removals and the process involved.
In order to preserve the integrity of the reviews, Thumbtack’s review policy is that we rarely ever remove reviews or update reviews. Additionally, keep in mind that content on our site (Thumbtack) may be disagreeable to customers without being in violation of this policy.
A few things to note include: 
If Thumbtack considers removing a review, it will first be reviewed by the Trust and Safety team, who will consider if the review violates Thumbtack's Content and Review Policy.
To dispute a review, the customer must contact us within 30 days of the review being posted.
Updated reviews follow the same process as regular reviews for edits, disputes, and escalations. To learn more, see the internal Reviews (Pro) KA. 
If a customer is being harassed or threatened by the pro, frontline reps should escalate the case by following the steps on the internal Trust & Safety Incidents KA.
If a customer contacts Support requesting their review be removed, Support reps will follow the steps on the internal Reviews (Pro) KA.
Why customer reviews may be flagged and removed on Thumbtack
This subsection describes specific reasons why a customer's review might be flagged and removed, such as being outside the valid time frame or deemed inauthentic.
Thumbtack may flag a customer's review and remove it from their profile. Below are a couple of reasons a review would be removed. 
Time frame (Customer review removed for being outside a reasonable time): Thumbtack only allows reviews posted within a reasonable time frame of the project itself. If the customer's job was submitted over a year ago, their review will be removed. If the customer has more details about when their project took place, reps can look into it further.
Inauthenticity (Fake Reviews): Thumbtack strives to maintain an honest review system. Reviews found to be inauthentic (fake) will be removed. Thumbtack does not disclose its process when determining review authenticity.  When speaking about these types of reviews, do refer to them as “inauthentic,” don’t call them “fake” or “fraudulent”. 
Reps will follow the (Rep) Steps: How to help a customer requesting their review be removed
Other reasons: For other reasons for may be review removal, reps can refer to the internal Reviews (Pro) KA.
Note: For steps on how to dispute a review and review removal reasons, Support reps should reference the internal Reviews (Pro) KA.
Key points 
Frontline reps should keep the following key points in mind when helping customers with reviews:
Reviews and responses to reviews are each limited to 10,000 characters.
Each review and its responses are limited to 20 photos total.
Photos in reviews should be less than 10 megabytes and is a jpg or png file. 
Reviews must be posted within six months after the last interaction between the customer and the pro, or within one year of the last day the pro worked on the project.
Reviews can only be updated once, only verified reviews can be updated, and reviews can’t be updated on the Thumbtack app.
As of January 24, 2018, customers can no longer leave anonymous reviews. Any anonymous reviews submitted before this date will not be removed and will remain anonymous.
To dispute a review, the customer must contact us within 30 days of the review being posted.
After a customer submits their review, they’re asked how much the job costs. See Job cost below to learn more. 
2. Process
This section outlines the steps for customers to leave and update customer reviews, and for frontline reps to help customers with customer review removal requests.
 Steps: How to leave a review (Customer)
This subsection guides customers on how to submit a customer review for a Thumbtack pro.
Customers can leave a Thumbtack pro by going to their Inbox and finding and clicking on the pro they want to review. After a customer submits their review, they’re asked how much the job costs. Customers can skip this step. Reps can refer to the job cost section above to learn more.
Customer steps: Customers can leave a review for a Thumbtack pro by following the steps in the How to review a pro – Thumbtack help article. 

[Image: Thumbtack customers can click "Review" in the top left corner of the messenger with the pro they want to review or click the star icon on the lower left.]

▶ In product view of leaving a review flow

[Image: AD_4nXdxhwDKIWe59Q9CYUazO_ZDaHqIjljPyGtNvO6X35Lk463uX7il97D_UYL6gEe_bkwfe3D8XK0qwQeinBEGtOE8BGDawQjyE26zY16GtHBRdEKw02GIQjd5tmESHHuj9y7B4kHNFNjT6Xndk_J_yi9MuKdd]

 Steps: How to update a review (Customer)
This subsection provides steps for customers who wish to modify or complete an existing customer review.
Customers who want to remove, change, or finish a posted review or didn't include text with their rating can update their review once (and it must be a verified review).  NOTE: If the customer is being harassed or threatened by the pro, frontline reps will escalate the case by following the steps on the internal Trust & Safety Incidents KA.
Customer steps: Customers can go to their customer profile to see the option to update their review or refer to the How to update my review – Thumbtack Help article. Customers can’t update reviews through the app and will need to use a web browser or mobile browser. 
Steps: How to help a customer requesting their review be removed (Reps)

This subsection details the steps for frontline reps when a customer asks to have their customer review removed.
Thumbtack’s policy is to keep reviews even if the pro has reached out to make the situation right afterward. 
If Thumbtack considers removing a review, it will first be reviewed by the Trust and Safety team who will consider if the review violates our Content and Review Policy. Additionally, to dispute a review, the customer must contact Thumbtack within 30 days of the review being posted.
When a customer contacts support requesting their review be removed, frontline reps will follow these steps: 
Explain that Thumbtack’s policy is to not delete reviews (both verified and unverified). 
In order to preserve the integrity of the reviews, Thumbtack’s review policy is that we rarely ever remove reviews or update reviews. 
Ask the customer why they would like the review removed.
Note ti reos: Keep in mind that content on our site (Thumbtack) may be disagreeable to customers without being in violation of this policy.
Review the table under “Potential Removal Reasons” in the internal Reviews (Pro) KA.
Rep should not make any promises that we’ll remove the review.
Transfer the case to Trust and Safety by using the “Steps: How to escalate a review dispute to Trust and Safety (Rep),” section in the internal Reviews (pro) KA.

3. Talking points
This section provides talking points for frontline reps to use when addressing common customer questions and concerns related to reviews.
▶ Timeline for leaving a review for a pro
This section provides reps with talking points and general responses to common customer inquiries about the timeframes for leaving customer reviews.
Is there a time limit for leaving a review?
Reviews must be posted within six months after the last interaction between you and the pro, or within one year of the last day the pro worked on the project.
¿Existe un plazo para dejar una reseña?
Las reseñas deben publicarse dentro de los seis meses posteriores a la última interacción con el profesional, o dentro de un año desde el último día en que trabajó en el proyecto.
▶ How customers add photos to their review
This subsection offers guidance on how customers can include photos with their reviews.
How do I add photos to my review?
You’ll see the option to add photos when you’re leaving your review. You can add up to 20 photos per review., To get technical, just make sure each photo is less than 10 megabytes and is a jpg or png file. And if you use the Thumbtack app, you can upload photos straight from your phone.
¿Cómo agrego fotos a mi reseña?
Usted verá la opción para agregar fotos cuando deje su reseña. Puede agregar tantas fotos como desee. Para ser técnico, solo asegúrese de que cada foto tenga menos de 10 megabytes y sea un archivo jpg o png y si usa la aplicación de Thumbtack, puede cargar fotos directamente desde su teléfono.
▶ How customers edit or update their review
This section provides reps with talking points and information, and answers related to editing or updating existing customer reviews.
How many updates can I leave? 
You can only add an update once, so make sure to read it over for accuracy and typos before submitting. 
¿Cuántas actualizaciones puedo dejar?
Solo puede agregar una actualización una vez, así que asegúrese de leerla con detenimiento para verificar su precisión y corregir posibles errores antes de enviarla.
Can I edit the project cost I submitted with my review?
Yes. If your review is verified (meaning you contacted the pro through Thumbtack), you can update it once. After submitting the updated review, you’ll be asked to add the project cost again – this is where you can make your changes. To update a review, head to Thumbtack.com on a web browser (not the app).
¿Puedo editar el costo del proyecto enviado con mi reseña?
Sí. Si su reseña es verificada (es decir, contactó al profesional a través de Thumbtack), puede actualizarla una vez. Tras enviar la reseña actualizada, se le pedirá que agregue nuevamente el costo del proyecto, donde podrá realizar los cambios. Para actualizar una reseña, visite Thumbtack.com en un navegador web (no en la aplicación).
Why can only verified reviews be updated? 
It helps us ensure the review and the update come from the same person. We aren’t able to verify the authenticity of reviews from customers outside of Thumbtack.
¿Por qué solo se pueden actualizar las reseñas verificadas?
Esto nos ayuda a garantizar que la reseña y la actualización vengan de la misma persona. No podemos verificar la autenticidad de las reseñas de los clientes fuera de Thumbtack.
If the pro fixed the situation, can I change the review I left them?
I realize the pro helped improve the situation after you left a review, and it’s great that they took care of the problem. However, we think your initial review is still valid and could be useful for customers to know about.
If you haven't already, you can leave an update to your review. I’d also recommend encouraging the pro to respond to your review about how they made things right.
Si el profesional arregló la situación, ¿puedo cambiar la evaluación que les dejé?
Tengo en cuenta que el profesional mejoró la situación después de que usted le dejó una evaluación, y es genial que se hayan ocupado del problema. Sin embargo, creemos que su evaluación inicial sigue siendo válida y podría ser útil que los clientes lo miren.
Si aún no lo ha hecho, puede dejar una actualización de su evaluación. También recomendaría alentar al profesional a responder a su evaluación sobre cómo mejoraron la situación.
Will you delete the review I left a pro?
In order to preserve the integrity of the reviews, our policy is to not edit or remove reviews. Reviews help other customers make informed decisions when hiring.
¿Eliminarás la evaluación que le dejé a un profesional?
Para preservar la integridad de las evaluaciones, nuestra política es no editar ni eliminar evaluaciones. Las evaluaciones ayudan a otros clientes a tomar decisiones informadas al contratar.
Can I edit the review I wrote for a pro?
Because we want to maintain an environment of honesty, our policy is to not edit reviews. While you can’t edit your review, you can add an update to any verified review you’ve left on Thumbtack. You can use the update to add new details about your experience. We’ll post the updated review along with your original review for future customers to see. Visit Thumbtack Help to learn more about leaving reviews.
¿Puedo editar la evaluación que escribí para un profesional?
Debido a que queremos mantener un ambiente de honestidad, nuestra póliza es de no editar las evaluaciones. No puede editar su evaluación, pero puede agregar una actualización a cualquier evaluación verificada que haya dejado en Thumbtack. Puede usar la actualización para agregar nuevos detalles sobre su experiencia. Publicaremos la evaluación actualizada junto con su evaluación original para que la vean los futuros clientes. Visite la página de Ayuda en Thumbtack para obtener más información sobre cómo dejar evaluaciones.
▶ Customer having trouble leaving a review
This section provides reps with talking points and offers solutions and advice for customers encountering difficulties while trying to leave a customer review.
Why don’t I see an update option? (review is unverified)
If there’s no update option when you follow the steps above, it means your review isn’t verified. You can only add updates to verified reviews. 
¿Por qué no veo una opción de actualización? (review is unverified)
Si no hay una opción de actualización cuando sigue los pasos anteriores, significa que su reseña no está verificada. Solo puedes agregar actualizaciones a reseñas verificadas.
I’m having trouble leaving a review, what should I do?
If you’re getting an error, check your internet connection (wifi is best). If it’s not your internet, try our troubleshooting tips.
Tengo problemas para dejar una reseña, ¿qué debo hacer?
Si recibe un error, verifique su conexión a Internet (wifi es lo mejor). Si no es su Internet, pruebe nuestros consejos para solucionar problemas.
▶ Customer review not verified
This section provides reps with talking points and explains why a customer's review might not be marked as verified and what steps can be taken.
Why isn’t my review verified?
Only reviews from Thumbtack customers are marked as verified. While it doesn’t happen often, reviews from Thumbtack customers might not be verified due to review link issues or because it’s been over a year since you worked with the pro. Reviews are incredibly important for building trust on Thumbtack, so contact us if a review isn't verified, but should be.
¿Por qué no está verificada mi reseña?
Solo las reseñas de los clientes de Thumbtack están marcadas como verificadas. Si bien no sucede con frecuencia, es posible que no se verifiquen las reseñas de los clientes de Thumbtack debido a problemas con el enlace de la reseña, o porque ha pasado más de un año desde que trabajó con el profesional.
▶ Customer review was removed
This section provides reps with talking points and explanations for why a customer's review might have been removed from Thumbtack.
(Review removed - general answer) 
Why was my review removed for violating the Content and Review Policy? 
Our site flagged the review, which is why it's no longer on your profile. I'd be happy to go over our Content and Review Policy with you if you have more questions.
¿Por qué se eliminó mi evaluación por violar la Política de Contenido y Evaluación?
Nuestro sistema marcó la evaluación, por lo que ya no está en su perfil. Me complacerá repasar nuestra Póliza de contenido y evaluación con usted si tiene más preguntas.

(Review removed for being posted outside reasonable time) 
Why can't I keep the review I just left for a pro I hired more than a year ago? 
We appreciate the time you took to leave a review, but we only allow reviews posted within a reasonable time frame of the project itself. It looks like your job was submitted over a year ago, which is why the review was removed. If you have more details about when your project took place, I’d be happy to look into it further.
¿Por qué no puedo conservar la evaluación que acabo de dejar para un profesional que contraté hace más de un año?
Agradecemos el tiempo que se tomó para dejar una evaluación, pero sólo permitimos que las evaluaciones se publiquen dentro de un plazo razonable del proyecto. Parece que su trabajo fue creado hace más de un año, por lo que se eliminó la evaluación. Si tiene más detalles sobre cuándo se llevó a cabo su proyecto, estaré encantado de investigarlo más a fondo.
(Review removed for being fake) 
Why was my review removed?
We want to make sure our review system is honest and we've found this review to be inauthentic. We won't be reconsidering this action and this review will remain removed.
 ¿Por qué se eliminó mi evaluación?
Queremos asegurarnos de que nuestro sistema de evaluación sea honesto y hemos encontrado que esta evaluación no es auténtica. No reconsideraremos esta acción y esta evaluación permanecerá eliminada.
What process do you use to determine this? 
While we can’t disclose our processes, our team makes sure we only remove inauthentic reviews.
¿Qué proceso utiliza para determinar esto?
Aunque no podemos revelar nuestros procesos, nuestro equipo se asegura de que sólo eliminamos las evaluaciones que no son auténticas.
That is not fair, put my review back!
We understand your reviews are important, but we won't be reconsidering this action and this review will remain removed. 
Eso no es justo, ¡vuelva a poner mi evaluación!
Entendemos que sus evaluaciones son importantes, pero no reconsideraremos esta acción y esta evaluación se eliminará.

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) guides Frontline Reps on how to effectively request help from the Advanced Service Team (AST) by submitting inquiries through the Atlassian Assist app in Slack. It covers the purpose of the AST, best practices for submitting requests, step for creating and tracking tickets, and what to expect during the resolution process. 
The Advanced Service Team (AST) manages several Slack channels (like #service_global_help-and-escalations) where Frontline Reps can ask questions and get help.
They handle a wide range of requests, including:
Global Help: For general questions, refunds, reviews, Stripe issues, bugs, Big Query help, and Trust & Safety concerns.
Escalations: For cases requiring a manager, such as refunds, reviews, and other escalation scenarios.
Cross-functional Help: For inquiries from other departments like Sales or Success.
To ensure all requests are tracked and resolved efficiently, frontline reps must submit all inquiries for the AST through the Atlassian Assist app in Slack. This creates a formal Jira ticket.
This internal knowledge article will cover:
When and why to contact the AST.
Best practices for submitting requests.
Step-by-step instructions for creating a ticket via Slack or the Web Portal.
How to track your ticket and what to expect.
The AST is available Monday through Friday, from 6am. to 6pm. MST.
Do's and Don'ts 
To ensure your request is handled quickly and effectively, frontline reps should follow these best practices:
Do provide as much detail as possible in your request.
Do conduct your own research in the Knowledge Base before submitting a ticket.
Do use the official channels and workflows to submit your request.
Don’t send requests via Direct Message (DM) to the AST.
Don’t reopen a ticket that has been marked as "Done." Instead, submit a new ticket for new questions.
Key points
Here is a some helpful key points for frontline reps to know when requesting help  from the Advanced Service Team (AST):
How to Contact AST:
All inquiries to the AST must be submitted through the Atlassian Assist App in Slack.
Reps should navigate to the relevant Slack channel and use a keyword to trigger the Assist App workflow, then select the appropriate request type
Ticket Management:
After submission, a confirmation is posted in Slack, serving as a live ticket.
Tickets progress through statuses: To Do, In Progress, Waiting for Customer, Waiting for Support, and Done.
Reps receive notifications in Slack as the ticket status changes.
All communication related to the ticket should occur within the ticket's thread in Slack or Jira.
Resolving & Closing Tickets:
Reps must confirm the resolution before a ticket is marked "Done."
Do not reopen "Done" tickets; submit a new ticket for new questions.
Provide feedback via the optional survey after a ticket is closed.
Help Channels and When to Contact the AST
Frontline reps can initiate requests in the following channels for issues related to an active case when KAs are insufficient:
#service_global_help-and-escalations: For Support reps needing help with general questions, refund requests, query lookups, Stripe payment issues, or to escalate cases to the Advanced Service team.
#xfnc_depts_help: This channel is for other departments (like Sales and Success) to ask the Advanced Service Team questions.
Note: This flow does not include the #service_unprofessional_and_ndp_reports Slack channel.

2. Process: Asking the Advanced Service Team for Help
This section outlines the steps for Frontline Reps to request help from the Advanced Service Team (AST) using the Atlassian Assist app in Slack. It details how to submit inquiries, manage and track tickets, and what to expect throughout the resolution process, ensuring efficient communication and timely support.
Steps: How to submit a request to AST (Rep) 
Frontline Reps are required to use the official Assist App process to submit all inquiries to the Advanced Service Team, rather than sending a message in Slack. To contact the Advanced Service team, frontline reps will follow these steps: 
Navigate to the Slack channel that is most relevant to your question (e.g., #service_global_help). 
In the message box, type in keywords to trigger the Assist app (like Help or Refunds). For a list of keywords, refer to the Assist Request Types table above. 
From the menu that appears, select the specific request type that best matches your issue.
Important Note: Once the "Create a work item" form appears, you cannot go back to select a different request type. If you chose the wrong one, you must click "Cancel" and start the process over from step 2.
When the form opens, click the "Open in new window" [Image: rtaImage]icon in the top-right corner to prevent your work from being lost. 
Fill out all the required fields in the “Create a work item” form with as much detail as possible.
Click Submit.
The Assist app will post a confirmation of your ticket in the channel. You can now communicate with the Advanced Service Team in the thread of that message.
▶ What the “Create a work ticket” form looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Screenshot: The image above shows the “Create a work item” form that was triggered after following steps 1 - 4 in the “Steps: How to Submit a Request to AST (Rep)” above.  
Steps: How to Manage and Track your Tickets (Rep)
After you submit a request using the Assist App, a confirmation will be posted directly in the Slack channel, serving as your live ticket. You will receive notifications in Slack as its status changes. The Advanced Service Team follows a structured process to ensure efficient resolution, and reps are responsible for managing and confirming the resolution of their tickets.
Here’s what the process looks like: 
Submission & Triage (To Do): Your ticket is successfully submitted, enters the AST's queue, and is reviewed to ensure all necessary information is present. It is then in the queue for the next available AST rep.
Assignment & Investigation (In Progress): Your ticket is assigned to an available AST rep who takes ownership. The AST will actively investigate the issue, potentially reaching out for clarification. You will receive a notification when this happens.
Communication & Pending States:
Waiting for Customer: If the AST needs more information from you, they will clearly state what is required in a comment in the ticket's thread. Please respond promptly to ensure your issue is resolved as quickly as possible.
Waiting for Support: If the AST is waiting for input from another internal team, the AST rep will set an expectation with you on timing. All updates are logged in the Jira ticket to maintain a clear record.
Resolution & Closure (Done): Once the issue is complete, the request has been resolved. 
Before a ticket is marked as Done, reps should confirm that the solution provided resolved the issue. 
The AST will then provide a final update in the ticket and close it. 
You will receive a final notification when the AST has resolved your issue, and the Assist App will add a final comment to the thread stating, "This request was closed."
Post-Closure Actions:
Do Not Reopen "Done" Tickets: Once a ticket's status is "Done," do not comment on it or try to reopen it. If new questions arise, submit a new ticket and reference the original ticket number if needed. This ensures that every new issue is tracked properly.
Provide Feedback: After a ticket is closed, reps will receive an optional survey. The AST encourages you to submit your feedback to help the team improve its service.
How the Advanced Service Team Processes Your Ticket 
For transparency, here’s a brief look at what happens on the AST's end after you submit a request:
Ticket Triage: Your ticket enters the AST's queue and is reviewed to ensure it contains all necessary information.
Assignment: The ticket is assigned to an available AST rep who takes ownership of the issue.
Investigation and Resolution: The assigned rep will investigate your request, potentially reaching out via the Jira ticket or Slack for clarification.
Communication: All updates are logged in the Jira ticket to maintain a clear record.
Closure: Once resolved, the rep will provide a final update in the ticket and close it.
Steps: How to View Your Request in Slack (Rep) 
Frontline Reps can easily monitor their submitted requests directly within Slack, ensuring they stay informed about the resolution status.
In Slack, go to the Assist app (under "Apps" in your sidebar).
In the Home tab, click the "View your requests" button to see all your tickets.
▶ What it looks like
Screenshot: The image below shows the Slack window with “Assist” selected and the Home page showing the "View your request" button.

[Image: rtaImage]

Steps: How to View Your Tickets In Jira (Rep)
Frontline Reps can also track their submitted requests through the Jira platform, providing a comprehensive view of all their tickets. To view a request you’ve submitted to the ASTH from the web portal, reps will follow these steps: 
Log in to Okta.
Open the TackIt (Helpdesk) application.
Click your profile picture in the top-right corner.
Select "Requests".
From this page, use the filters at the top to search for a specific request.
Note: This shows you all your submitted tickets like IT. 
The filter “Request type” will help you locate the ticket quickly. Type “Advanced Service Team Helpdesk” in the search bar. 
▶ What it looks like:
Screenshot: Image shows the https://thumbtack.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/user/requests page with all the users submitted requests with the “Request type” dropdown and “Advanced” typed out showing the ASTH request types.

[Image: rtaImage]


3. Process: Advanced Service Team (AST) 
This section outlines the process for the Advanced Service Team when handling all incoming requests via the Jira Service Management helpdesk. The goal of this process is to ensure consistency, efficiency, and clear communication from ticket creation to resolution.
Step 1: Ticket Triage and Assignment 
For the Advanced Service Team, the first step is to promptly acknowledge and assign all new tickets to ensure they are handled within the 6-minute SLA, as leaving tickets unacknowledged in the queue risks SLA breaches.
Review the Queue: Monitor the Advanced Service Team Helpdesk queue in Jira or the #asth channel in Slack for all new incoming tickets. Prioritize any that are approaching or have exceeded the SLA.
Assign the Ticket:
In Jira: Open the ticket (ASTH-###), and in the "Details" section, assign the ticket to yourself.
In Slack: On the ticket notification in the #asth channel, click the “Take it” button.
Set the Status: Immediately after assigning the ticket, change its status to “In progress”. This action notifies the rep that their request is actively being worked on.
Step 2: Ticket Investigation and Documentation
Before acting, it is essential for the Advanced Service Team to fully understand the issue, always keeping communication transparent and tracked within the appropriate platform.
Understand the Issue: Carefully review the ticket's summary, description, SGH link, and any attachments to get a complete picture of the request.
Communicate Visibly: All communication must be kept within the ticket's thread to ensure a clear record. Do not use side chats or DMs.
In Jira: Use the “Reply to Customer” field in the "Activity" section to respond. Be sure to click "Save" to post the reply.
In Slack: Respond directly in the ticket's thread.
Manage Pending States: If you cannot proceed, update the ticket status accordingly:
Waiting for Customer: Use this status when you need more information from the rep. 
Clearly state what is required in your reply.
Waiting for Support: Use this status when you are waiting for input from another internal team or for a technical issue to be resolved. 
Tag the relevant team if possible, set clear expectations, and follow up within SLA.
Step 3: Collaborating vs. Moving a Ticket
It's important for the Advanced Service Team to know when to ask another team for help versus when to move a ticket to their queue entirely.
Collaborating (Tagging a Team): Use this method when you own the ticket but need input or help from another team.
In your Jira comment or Slack reply, tag the appropriate team (e.g., @eng-team).
Clearly state what information you need and set an expectation for a follow-up.
Change the ticket's status to “Waiting for Support”. This indicates that you are waiting for an internal team's input.
Moving a Miscategorized Ticket: Use this method only when a ticket was created in the AST queue by mistake and belongs entirely to another team.
Inside the open Jira ticket, click the three dots (...) in the upper right corner and select “Move”.
Choose the correct project/category to move the ticket to and complete any required fields.
Step 4: Resolution and Closure
Before closing any ticket, the Advanced Service Team must confirm the resolution with the rep and capture key data for reporting and process improvement.
Confirm Resolution: Always check with the rep to ensure the solution provided has fully resolved their issue before proceeding to close the ticket.
Capture Before Closing: Do not close a ticket without documenting the outcome. This data is critical for reporting.
In Jira: Fill out the fields in the “Details” section of the ticket:
Reason
Outcome
Agent Opportunity
Policy Driven Opportunities
Product Related Opportunities
In Slack: Click “Edit” on the ticket to open the form and fill out the same fields listed above.
Close the Ticket:
Set the ticket's status to “Done”.
If the rep raises a new, unrelated issue during the conversation, advise them to open a new ticket. Do not bundle new issues into an existing one.

Steps: How to dispute a survey for removal (Rep)
Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) outlines the specific and limited reasons a Customer Satisfaction Score (CSAT) survey can be disputed by a Support rep (also known as "Advocate"). It also details the required process for submitting a dispute for review and explains which scenarios are not eligible for dispute.
Customer Satisfaction Score (CSAT) is the key performance indicator used by Thumbtack to assess overall customer or pro satisfaction and how likely they are to recommend Thumbtack to a peer or colleague. This metric is a measure of the overall satisfaction of the customer or pro with Thumbtack’s service and product experience.
Support reps are responsible for keeping pros and customers on the site, and reps should take ownership of their interactions with pros and customers.
While rare, there are a few instances where Thumbtack will remove a CSAT survey response or not send a CSAT survey. 
▶ Allowed Survey Dispute Reasons
Disputes will be reviewed for the following reasons (these are considered valid grounds for survey removal):
Abusive behavior 
Agent feedback
Blocklisted pro or customer
Duplicate survey
Escalations
Expired survey return
Foreign language speaker
Meant for another rep
Negative survey threat
Noise interactions
Unable to assist due to technology issues
▶ Reasons NOT Allowed for Survey Disputes
Disputes will not be approved for the following reasons (these are not considered valid grounds for survey removal)
Comments about the product or process: Frontline reps are expected to communicate negative information about the product or process constructively and positively. A customer's dissatisfaction with the product or process should not negatively impact the level of service provided.
Mismatched scoring between CSAT and NPS (unless another reason from the Allowed list applies).
General "overall experience" comments (e.g., regarding segmentation, requests for phone support, or wait times).
Survey offer resulting from a rep’s error: If a support reps action leads to an incorrect survey offer (e.g., selecting a surveyable theme instead of "Not Surveyable," etc.), this is not valid grounds for survey removal.
Internal note: By default, any dispute filed that does not fall within the allowed dispute categories will only be considered if discussed by leadership and approved by the Director of Support and Head of Quality Analytics (QA).
Dispute Reasons and Exemptions 

This section explains the very specific and limited reasons why a Customer Satisfaction Score (CSAT) survey can be challenged and removed from a support rep's performance review, or why a case is automatically not included in the survey process.
Allowed survey dispute reasons
The following sections below are the only reasons for which a Frontline rep can dispute a CSAT survey.
Abusive behavior 
Survey dispute reason: Escalations (Abusive behavior is not a selectable reason in Salesforce — use Escalations). 
When it applies: When the pro or customer continued abusive, hostile, discriminatory, or inappropriate behavior after the rep gave the appropriate warning(s), case notes or interaction details show this.
What reps should do during the interaction: Follow the “Steps: How to Handle Direct or Indirect Unprofessional Behavior by Pro or Customer (Rep)”  steps in the Unprofessional Behavior, Support Abuse, & Discrimination (Rep) KA.
Submitting the dispute: 
Reps can submit a survey dispute if a related negative survey is received. Reps should: 
Check the case notes or interaction details to confirm the required documentation is there. 
Once confirmed, submit the dispute (Steps below). 
In the dispute comments field, add: 
what the pro or customer said or did (with a timestamp)
the warning(s) given
the resolution or outcome provided.
When it does NOT apply: 
The rep didn't follow the warning steps in the Unprofessional Behavior, Support Abuse, & Discrimination (Rep) KA.
The behavior stopped after a warning was given.
The incident isn't clearly documented in the case notes.
Agent feedback
Survey dispute reason: Agent feedback
When it applies: A survey can be disputed and removed from a support rep's performance evaluation if the feedback explicitly states the rep's positive performance (e.g., "The agent was very helpful," "The representative provided excellent service," etc.).
Note: Neutral comments, such as "the agent was okay," are not grounds for a dispute.
Score Adjustments by the QA Team:
If a pro or customer provides one of the following Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) scores, the QA Team will make adjustments:
A CSAT score of 1 will be adjusted to 5.
A CSAT score of 2 will be adjusted to 4.
A CSAT score of 3 remains unchanged and is not eligible for dispute.
Blocklisted accounts tor Trust and Safety transfers
Survey dispute reason: Escalation (Blocklisted pro or customer is not a selectable reason in Salesforce — use Escalation)
When it applies: A survey can be disputed and removed for cases 
Will-not-reconsider accounts: The account is blocklisted and has been confirmed as not eligible for reactivation. 
Trust & Safety transfers: The case required a transfer to T&S, regardless of whether the account may eventually be reactivated.*
Because the rep cannot offer a resolution on accounts that won’t be reconsidered or T&S-handled cases, the survey can be disputed.
* Important — mixed-issue cases: If a case had a T&S banner but the user also needed help with something unrelated, a quick case is required per case handling guidelines for the unrelated issue. Only the T&S case is eligible for this dispute. See Salesforce: Case Navigation and Management (Rep) KA for quick case guidelines. 
Before submitting, verify: Confirm the account is will-not-reconsider or that a T&S transfer occurred. If neither applies, the dispute will not be approved.
When it does NOT apply: 
Situations that can still be handled by Support reps are eligible for a survey and are not disputable. These include account hold situation like: 
Need to take a background check
User has profile issues 
Past due balance
Reminder: Accounts put on hold will also have a blocklist, but that doesn’t mean they won’t be reconsidered. Reps must confirm the user will not be reconsidered. If a user contacts support about an account hold, the rep can give users next steps to resolve account holds and many will auto-resolve once the user completes what's needed. Because the rep has an opportunity to help, the survey remains valid.
Duplicate surveys

Survey dispute reason: Duplicate survey
When it applies: This applies to cases where multiple surveys were offered and answered for the same interaction. For a dispute to be valid, the duplicate survey must occur within the same case, typically due to a system error.
Note: Disputes will not be approved if there are interactions on separate cases with similar issues. In the case of a duplicate, Thumbtack will keep the first response and remove others.
Escalations
Survey dispute reason: Escalations
When it applies: The survey is reassigned or retained based on the user's comments and contact handling.
If the survey was offered and answered after an escalation was received, the survey will be assigned to the rep who handled the escalation.
If "Meant for another Support Rep” rules apply, the escalation rep may dispute the survey, and it will be transferred to the original rep.
If there is no contact between Advanced Service and the customer or pro, the survey will be returned to the rep who escalated the contact.
If the customer or pro states they have not heard back from Advanced Service, the dispute can be approved and the survey assigned to the original rep, provided Advanced Service has already called, left a voicemail, and sent an email.
Note: Escalated cases should be reassigned to the last rep who handled the contact.
Expired survey return

Survey dispute reason: Expired Survey Return
When it applies: This applies to cases where a customer or pro responds to a survey offer that was sent more than 30 days ago.
Note: This dispute reason will only be used in instances where a system glitch allowed the customer or pro to reply to an offer that should have expired.
Foreign language speaker
Survey dispute reason: Foreign language speaker
When it applies
A survey may be disputed when a language barrier prevents mutual understanding and resolution, provided the rep handled the interaction according to policy.
Eligibility is determined by the language involved and proper documentation in the case notes.
 
1. Language Barriers Involving English (ENG) or Spanish (ESP)
A dispute may be approved if the case notes clearly document one of the following criteria:
▶ A. Reasonable Attempt
The rep made a reasonable attempt to help, but mutual understanding was not possible due to the language barrier.
A reasonable attempt includes:
The rep identified the language mismatch early in the interaction.
The rep attempted basic clarification in their supported language.
The rep clearly documented the confirmed language barrier in the case notes 
Required documentation:  Case notes must show that the rep:
Identified the barrier
Attempted clarification
Documented the outcome
▶ B. Explicit Queue Request
The user explicitly requested a transfer to the English (ENG) or Spanish (ESP) queue, and no help was provided.
Required documentation: Case notes must clearly state that the user requested transfer to the ENG or ESP queue.

2. Languages Other Than English or Spanish
A dispute may be approved only if the rep made a documented attempt to help and mutual understanding was not possible due to the language barrier.
Documented attempts include:
Suggesting the use of a translator.
Offering alternative communication channels such as chat or email.
Required Documentation: Case notes must show the attempt made and that the language barrier prevented resolution
▶ Critical Adherence and Automatic Denial
Requirement when submitting a surrey dispute:
 Reps must select “Foreign language speaker.”
 Do not use “Meant for another rep” for language barrier cases.
Automatic denial:
Disputes will be denied if the incorrect category is selected, OR if the case notes do not clearly show:
A reasonable attempt was made (for ENG/ESP cases), OR
A documented attempt to assist was made (for other languages), OR
An explicit ENG/ESP transfer request was made by the user
Meant for another rep


Survey dispute reason: Meant for another rep

When it applies: This applies to surveyed cases where the survey comments are about an interaction with a different rep.
The rep's name must be explicitly mentioned in the survey verbatim.
Dispute notes must reference the rep and case to which the dispute should be transferred.
We can reassign the survey to the correct support rep if:
The other support rep had no direct interaction with the user such as a disconnected call.
The other support rep did not provide any help.
The other support rep does not have their own survey offer.
The survey will not be disputable if:
A different issue is mentioned on the verbatim but no other rep's name was alluded to by the customer or pro.
The verbatim mentions dissatisfaction with another team or rep in a different department outside of Support.
Note: If two support reps worked on the same case and the survey owner had no direct interaction with the user, this category also applies. See + Survey reassignment: two advocates on the same case + under Noise Interactions for details.
Negative survey threat 
Survey dispute reason: Escalations (Negative survey threat is not a selectable reason in Salesforce — use Escalations). 
When it applies: The pro or customer threatened to leave a negative Thumbtack survey or CSAT response unless they received a specific outcome, exception, or special treatment, and case notes or interaction details show this.
Important: Threats to leave a negative review on the Better Business Bureau (BBB), social media, app stores, or other public platforms do not qualify for this dispute reason unless the pro or customer also threatened the Thumbtack survey or CSAT response.
What reps should do during the interaction:
Stay professional and continue handling the issue according to policy. Refer to the Standard Escalations and De-Escalation Guidelines (Rep) KA for tips on navigating challenge interactions.
Do not change the resolution because of the threat. 
Submitting the dispute: 
Reps can submit a survey dispute if a related negative survey is received. Reps should: 
Check the case notes or interaction details to confirm the required documentation is there. 
Once confirmed, submit the dispute (Steps below). 
In the dispute comments field, add: 
what the pro or customer said or did (with a timestamp)
any warning given (if applicable) 
the action or resolution provided.
When it does NOT apply: 
General dissatisfaction with no explicit threat toward the Thumbtack survey or CSAT response.
The threat targeted only a public review platform and did not also threaten the Thumbtack survey or CSAT response.
The rep changed the resolution because of the threat.
The behavior isn't clearly documented in the case notes.
Note: This process is specific to survey threats and is separate from the escalation processes in the Identifying and Responding to Threats (Reps)  KA, which covers physical harm, facility threats, and similar safety concerns.
Noise interactions 
Survey dispute reason: Noise Interactions
When it applies: This applies to the following scenarios where no meaningful interaction took place and no help was provided:
Email: When a pro or customer responds to an automated "do-not-reply" email from Thumbtack (e.g., Trust and Safety messages related to inauthentic reviews).
Voice and SMS: When the user was unresponsive or disconnected before any meaningful exchange occurred and no help was provided.
Note: If the interaction got disconnected due to a technology issue after an exchange had begun, that falls under + Unable to assist due to technology issues +, not Noise Interactions.
When it does NOT apply — Email
The following situations do not qualify for this dispute reason:
Pro replying to a Thumbtack lead notification, advertisement, or current Service issue that is being handled.
There is a response from the pro that requires the rep to reply and classify the case properly.
If there is no written response from the user, the rep should reply and categorize the case as Pro/Customer > Ops > Routing > General > Not enough information, and a survey should only be sent if there is clear context for the user's issue. If they then reply, categorize appropriately.
Cases where a rep responded to a Help Center inquiry via email and the user did not reply.
When it applies — Voice and SMS (with exceptions)
Use the table below to determine whether a Voice or SMS noise dispute will be approved:

Scenario
Outcome
Why
No valid interaction occurred and no help was provided (including cases where the user was unresponsive or disconnected before any meaningful exchange)
Dispute approved — survey removed
No meaningful interaction occurred and no help was provided
A second case is created within a few minutes of the first, handled by the same support rep, and the rep successfully helps the user in that second case
Not disputable — survey on the first case remains valid; if a survey was triggered on the second case it will be removed as a duplicate
The feedback reflects the actual completed interaction in the second case, even if the survey is attached to the first case
The user contacts again within a few hours, is helped by a different support rep, and the survey is completed after that second interaction
Not disputable — survey assigned to the second rep
The survey was completed after the second interaction, so it reflects that reps help, not the first
Survey reassignment — two advocates on the same case
If two advocates worked on the same case and the survey owner had no opportunity to help the user, the survey will be reassigned to the advocate who directly supported the user. This scenario is classified as Meant for another representative.
Note: Under normal case handling guidelines, if the first support rep provided help, the second support rep should have created a Quick Case for any new or continued interaction. Two reps on the same case without a quick case is only expected when the first rep provided no help during the prior interaction. If a quick case was required but not created, this does not affect the survey reassignment — the survey will still follow the rep who directly helped the user.
These guidelines protect survey integrity and ensure feedback reflects the user’s true experience. Removing surveys solely due to unresponsiveness, disconnection, or an initial failed contact — when a later interaction resulted in actual help — would distort performance measurement and produce inaccurate scoring.
Unable to assist due to technology issues
Survey dispute reason: Unable to assist due to technology issues 
When it applies: This applies to surveyed cases where the interaction got disconnected due to a technology issue and NO information or resolution was provided to the pro or customer as a result. Examples include dropped calls, dropped chats, and SMS message failures..
Support reps must follow the appropriate process for their channel before submitting a dispute:
Phone: Follow the disconnected call process. See Phone Call Support Interaction Guide (Rep) for steps on handling connection issues or disconnected calls.
Chat and SMS:  Follow the connectivity issues process. See Non-Voice Interactions: Writing and Conversation Etiquette (Rep)  KA for steps on connectivity issues and message failures.
When it does NOT apply:
The support rep provided any information or resolution before the disconnection — even partial help disqualifies the dispute.
The user became inactive after the rep provided a resolution or information. If the user stopped responding after receiving help, the survey remains valid and is not disputable.
The support rep sent a follow-up email that addressed the user's concern — this counts as information or resolution being provided.
Note: Cases where the user was unresponsive or disconnected before any meaningful exchange occurred with no technology failure involved fall under + Noise Interactions + .
These guidelines protect survey integrity and ensure feedback reflects the support rep's actual opportunity to help. Removing surveys when information or resolution was provided — even if the user later became inactive — would distort performance measurement and produce inaccurate scoring.
Survey exemption guide

All conversations with pros and customers must be documented in Salesforce. Each conversation should be classified based on what occurred during the conversation.
 There are two main reasons for a CSAT survey exemption:
No contact
Duplicate
To learn more about classifying cases, reps should refer to the internal Salesforce: Case Navigation and Management (Rep) KA.
No contact
Exemption Reason: No contact (no account or contact info provided)
When it applies: Use this classification if:
The customer or pro refused to provide any contact information.
The conversation ended or was disconnected before contact information could be shared.
Someone contacted Thumbtack, but they don’t have a Thumbtack account.
The email address provided doesn’t pull up an account in Admin.
Note: All other scenarios should have contact information associated with the case.
Duplicate
Exemption Reason: Duplicate
When it applies: This survey exemption applies only to Assigned Email Reps (e.g., RDT) who are using the "Duplicate" function as part of their specific workflow (e.g., 'Duplicate - Pro Consolidation'). An exemption is granted if:
The case refers to the exact same concern (e.g., multiple refund disputes from one pro) and is being consolidated into a primary case.
The case only contains attachments as a follow-up to a previous, pending concern.
Note: The manager must contact OPS to have the survey removed from the original support rep.
IMPORTANT: "Duplicate" Function Restriction (Effective Oct 27, 2025)
The "Duplicate Of" function is strictly prohibited for all live, inbound cases (Voice, Chat, and SMS). 
A recontact from a pro or customer is considered a repeat contact, not a duplicate, and must be handled as a new interaction. Live reps are empowered to own and resolve the issue. Failure to follow this process is a critical offense under QA guidelines.
Here’s how reps should handle these situations: 
When a rep receives a case with an issue that a pro or customer has already received help with (regardless of the channel), the rep should still offer additional help. This is considered a repeat contact, not a duplicate. 
Even if follow-up conversations occur within 24 hours, they should be handled as normal and not tagged as a duplicate.
Policy & Guidelines
Support reps must adhere to the following mandatory guidelines when submitting a CSAT survey dispute, covering manager approval, required documentation, and the critical submission timeline.
Survey avoidance
Frontline reps must never engage in "survey avoidance," which is any action taken to intentionally prevent a Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) survey from triggering.
Prohibited survey avoidance behaviors:
Reusing recycled cases: Continuing work on a recycled case from a different interaction specifically to suppress a new survey.
Mismatched issue handling: Documenting a new, unrelated problem on an existing case to avoid CSAT attribution.
Case status: Keeping a case on pending status without a valid reason.
Case ownership: Continuing work on a case with the wrong owner to avoid CSAT attribution.
Reps should refer to the internal Salesforce: Case Navigation and Management (Rep) for information on recycled cases and case handling. 
Classification of Infraction
Survey avoidance is treated as a violation per the TPH Corrective Action Policy. 
Integrity: Intentional survey avoidance results in immediate dismissal.
Reliability : Failing to follow proper Quick Case creation steps (unintentional) is a documentation error subject to standard corrective action.
QA review standards:
The Quality Analytics (QA) team reviews case notes, interaction details, and survey feedback against the Service | Cx/Pro Support - Current QA Rubric  before approving or denying a dispute.
General dispute guidelines
Support reps must adhere to the following guidelines when submitting a CSAT survey dispute:
Approval and Documentation:
All disputes must be reviewed and approved by the Support reps manager before submission.
When submitting a manager-approved dispute, Support reps must provide detailed notes in the dispute comments section.
Special Circumstances:
Any unique situations require discussion with and approval from both the Director or Support and the Head of Quality Analytics (QA).
Only after receiving this explicit approval should the dispute be forwarded to the survey disputes queue.
Deadline for Submission:
To maintain accurate reporting, disputes must be submitted within 5 business days of the survey response date. Submissions received after this deadline will not be considered.
Dispute decision timeline
The Quality Analytics (QA) team reviews the survey dispute queue every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday* to ensure prompt handling and provide Support reps with current information regarding their Customer Satisfaction score (CSAT).
*Note: Disputes submitted on Fridays and Saturdays will be addressed on Sunday evenings (US).
To prevent delays, reps are strongly encouraged to submit disputes as soon as they are identified, rather than sending them in batches.
2. Process
Steps: How to dispute a survey for removal (Rep)
While managers should check for non-surveyable categories, Support reps can still submit disputes for review if they believe a survey qualifies.  
Important: Before submitting, support reps should review the General dispute guidelines above to ensure compliance.
To dispute a CSAT survey, Support reps can follow these steps:
Start the Dispute in Salesforce:
Click the drop-down button in Salesforce.
Select Survey Offers.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Locate the Survey:
Under “Survey Offers,” click the drop-down menu to filter for the desired survey (e.g., "My Surveys - This week").
Choose the relevant Case Number to view the CSAT score.
Submit the Dispute Details:
Find the Survey Offer Dispute sections.
Select a Dispute reason form the dropdown list. 
Fill out the Dispute comments with detailed notes. 
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

Notify Your Manager: 
Notify your manager (via Slack or email) which CSAT surveys are being disputed, as the system does not do this automatically.
Review Process:
Manager Review (Step 1): Your manager will review the interaction and either approve the dispute for QA review or decline it, providing reasons for the decision.
QA Team Final Review (Step 2): If approved by the manager, the QA Team performs the final review. The QA team member will provide a written decision and make any necessary changes to the case if they agree with the dispute.
Check the Decision:
To read the outcome, open the case.
Select the "Related" tab and navigate to Survey Offers.
Scroll down to "Survey Offer Dispute" to read the sections titled "Review Team Decision" and "Review Team Comments."
3. Resources
Frontline reps will find a collection of resources in this section, including links to internal knowledge articles, and other relevant resources. These resources may be referenced in the article or provide additional, related information.
Resources for REPS:
Related internal knowledge articles
Phone Call Support Interaction Guide (Rep)
Non-Voice Interactions: Writing and Conversation Etiquette (Rep)
Salesforce: Case Navigation and Management (Rep) 
Other
Support QA Bulletin
Service | Cx/Pro Support - Current QA Rubric
TPH Corrective Action Policy
