1. Overview
▶ KA Summary:
This internal KA outlines guidelines for Frontline reps regarding user account removals and bans. It details reasons for removal, including violations of user guidelines, payment issues, and other concerns like background check failures or linked accounts. The KA also provides steps for reps to check account statuses, handle deleted requests, and communicate removal reasons to users. It emphasizes that certain removals, such as those for sexual content or comprehensive business decisions, are final and not subject to reconsideration.
Users, like pros and customers, have to abide by Thumbtack user guidelines in order to use Thumbtack. Pros and customers will be removed from the platform if they violate Thumbtack’s guidelines. These guidelines are crucial for maintaining a trustworthy community and a seamless experience. 
The content in this article outlines the reasons for user account removals and bans, detailing violations of these guidelines, payment issues, and other concerns. Frontline reps should use the guidelines below to understand why a user may have been removed. Reps can also send pros or customers the User Guidelines if they'd like to review it on the website, by sharing the Thumbtack user guidelines, and the Thumbtack's Terms of Use article.
Key aspects of Thumbtack’s User Guidelines include:
Account Creation:
Users must be at least 18 years old and located in the United States.
Provide real and accurate information (name, contact details).
Prohibited: Bartering for services, creating test accounts, and making/receiving payments in anything other than U.S. dollars.
For Customers (when submitting a job request):
Use appropriate language and provide accurate information.
Avoid requesting:
Sexual or illegal services.
Full-time jobs / internships.
Advertising their own services.
Services not offered on Thumbtack.
For Pros (when building a business on Thumbtack):
Use appropriate language in messages and profiles.
Offer legitimate services and provide accurate account information.
Ensure business details are primarily in English.
Services must be offered within the United States or a U.S. territory.
Be legally qualified to perform services.
Prohibited: Offering products (unless accompanying services), lending services, or services not listed on Thumbtack.
Work directly with customers (no referral or third-party services).
Avoid asking customers to use external apps or duplicate forms.
Do not offer duplicate services.
Understand and take full responsibility for how Thumbtack charges work.
Common Trust and Safety internal terms 
The table below has a few internal terms that Frontline reps may hear referenced. 
▶ Account holdDefinition: A hold on a pro or customer account. It prevents pros from appearing in search results and customers from accessing their accounts. Pros or customers with an unresolved Trust & Safety (T&S) issue and pros who haven't completed the full sign-up process may have a hold on their account until they either resolve the issue or complete certain steps in the sign-up process.For additional information on account holds, see the internal Account Holds (Pro) and Account Holds (Customer) KAs for more details.
▶ BlocklistedBlocklisting an account is only available when the pro or customer account is already deactivated. The blocklisting feature is predominantly used only by the T&S team. If reps are to blocklist a user, the steps they follow will make that very clear.Trust and Safety is the point of contact for any accounts that are blocklisted. 
▶ FidesFides uses identity information from multiple sources to determine whether a user should be allowed to access our site. Sources include our internal blocklists and third-party services. It detects undesirable users who are either previously known bad users signing up as a new user (linked accounts), or those who might fail a background check. This is done automatically by Fides. Reps may see deletion logs that say “Deleted by Fides” for a variety of reasons, see below.
Incorrect or fake user information
Linked accounts
Repeat fraud reviews detected by Fides. See Inauthentic/fake reviews
User has been auto-escalated to Checkr by Fides. See Background checks
▶ Ghosted"Ghosted Account" or "Inaccurately Actioned Account” means a customer's account was flagged for suspicious activity, preventing their requests or messages from reaching pros. Customers are unaware their account is flagged and will not receive quotes.For additional details, refer to the internal Account Holds (Customer KA.
Key points 
Frontline reps should keep the following key points in mind when handling removed or banned user accounts:
Accounts are removed for violating the user guidelines (Thumbtack user guidelines) (e.g., spam/scams, harassment, sexual content).
Refer pros and customers to the Thumbtack user guidelines - Thumbtack Help article  if they'd like to review it
Background check failures, linked accounts, inauthentic reviews, and profile issues can lead to account removal.
Accounts can also be removed for outstanding balances or payment disputes.
The Chargeback Dashboard provides information on chargeback levels and status.
Removals for sexual or inappropriate content, or business decisions, are final.
Avoid using internal terminology with pros and customers.
"Account Hold" prevents users from appearing in search results or accessing their accounts due to unresolved issues.
"Blocklisted" accounts are deactivated for Trust & Safety reasons.
"Fides" is an internal system that automatically detects undesirable users.
Do not blocklist users without Trust & Safety approval.
Steps: How to handle a removed or on-hold user who is asking for a manager (Reps)
Pros and customers with account holds or removals may ask to speak to a manager. Frontline reps should note that the Advanced Service team does not take escalations for account removals, holds, or other Trust and Safety issues.
If Frontline reps have questions or need talking points for working with escalated users, reps should submit a request to the Advanced Service team using the Atlassian Assist app in Slack:
Navigate to the #service_global_help-and-escalations Slack channel.
Use a keyword like “Help others” or “Others” to trigger the Assist app workflow.
Select the "Global Help Others" request type and fill out the form with all necessary details.
2. Checking account statuses and handling deleted requests  
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: This section guides Frontline reps on how to investigate and manage user accounts that have been deleted or put on hold. It details steps for checking deletion and account logs, identifying blocklist statuses, and reviewing reasons for account holds. The section also outlines how Thumbtack handles projects that violate guidelines, including helping customers with deleted projects and undeleting requests.
Steps: How to check deletion and account logs (Rep)

When a pro or customer contacts Thumbtack about their deleted account, Frontline reps will follow the steps below to better understand what has happened:
Verify the user's identity. As usual, reps must verify the identity of the customer or pro by following the steps in the internal Verify Account Information KA. 
NOTE: Account information, including deletion actions and reasons, can only be shared with the Account Holder. 
Check for a Trust & Safety Blocklist. Check if the account has been blocklisted by the Trust and Safety team by looking under the “Banned Status” section of the main user’s Admin page
Internal note: The Blocklist record does not need to be accessed. Only confirm if that status is listed on the account. 
Investigate Account Holds. To see why an account is on hold, check the “Identity Status” and “Account Hold flags” section of the main user’s Admin page. If the hold reason is not directly shown in the fields mentioned above, click on “Account Hold Logs”  under Actions for additional information that may be available. 
Review Deletion Reasons. To see why an account is disabled, click “Deletion and Ghost Logs” under Actions.
Match the Issue to This Article. After reading the deletion/hold log reason, notes, and other details, look through the list of reasons for the account action in this article, and find one that best fits the situation
Seek Help if Needed. If a Frontline rep has any questions, submit a request to the Advanced Service Team using the Atlassian Assist app in Slack by following these steps:
Navigate to the #service_global_help-and-escalations Slack channel.
Use a keyword like “Help others” or “Others” to trigger the Assist app workflow.
Select the "Global Help Others" request type and fill out the form with all necessary details.
How Thumbtack handles projects that violate guidelines
Project Removal: Requests that don't follow Thumbtack's guidelines are removed (deleted) and won't be sent to pros (syndicated).
Customer Notification:  Depending on the guideline violation, the customer may receive an email notification to let them know their project was removed. However, some violations won’t notify a customer.
Steps: How to help a customer whose project was deleted for violating guidelines (Rep)
If a customer reaches out about their deleted project for violating guidelines, Frontline reps will follow these steps: 
Look at the request in Admin (and the guidelines in this KA) to find the reason for deletion.
For violations involving explicit or inappropriate content: reps should simply state that the project was removed for "violating our terms of use." Do not provide any further details. It’s important to remember that this type of content is a "do not discuss" topic, even if the customer’s account was also removed for the same reason.
For email interactions, send the “Customer guidelines: explicit or inappropriate messages” email template.
For bartering for services, see Bartering for services below.
For questionable/fake info, see Incorrect or fake user information below.
For internship or full-time employment, see Jobs offering internships or full-time employment below.
For outsources or plagiarize writing jobs, see Plagiarized academic writing jobs below.
For other violations: reps can provide specific details and clarify how Thumbtack works. For example, if the project was a third-party job, reps can explain that Thumbtack doesn’t allow third-party requests. Or if the customer was looking to apply for a job, reps can explain that Thumbtack is not for job seeking.
Provide the customer with suggestions on how they can resubmit their project by following Thumbtack’s user guidelines. (Frontline reps can’t resubmit a project for the customer if the project was deleted for a guideline violation.)
If the rep believes the customer’s project was deleted in error: post in the #ts-proactive-ops-questions channel about the situation. The T&S team can review and make a final decision (they may undelete the project if they deem it was deleted by error).
For email interactions, reps can send and personalize one of the “Customer guideline templates” explaining why the customer’s request was removed. Templates include: 
Customer guidelines: Questionable Name
Customer Guidelines: Full-Time Job Request
Customer Guidelines: Charity Requests
Customer Guidelines: Test job 
Customer Guidelines: Academic Writing
Customer guidelines: third party job 
Customer guidelines: job from a minor
Internal note: Frontline reps can’t resubmit a project for the customer if the project was deleted for a guideline violation. 

3. User guideline violations
Users have to abide by Thumbtack’s user guidelines in order to use Thumbtack. Frontline reps should use the guidelines below to understand why a user may have been sanctioned and send pros or customers the User Guidelines if they'd like to review it on the website. They can find the guidelines on the  Thumbtack user guidelines article. 
The violation reasons below are ordered alphabetically. 
Bartering for services (Pro) (Customer) 
Bartering is the exchange (goods or services) for other goods or services without using money.
Thumbtack doesn't allow trade or bartering requests on Thumbtack. Users cannot exchange goods, labor, objects, etc., for services. 
Thumbtack customers: Thumbtack only allows requests from customers who are willing to pay monetarily, and services offered by pros are willing to receive payment monetarily.  
Thumbtack pros: Thumbtack only allows pros to accept U.S. dollars when they offer their services on Thumbtack.
Thumbtack removes the customer’s project or the pro’s account if it notices they’re looking to trade or barter for services. 
Actions Taken by Trust & Safety: 
Customer Projects: Thumbtack will delete the customer’s project and send an automated email to notify the customer of the violation.
Pro Accounts: T&S will place the pro’s account on hold and send an automated email to inform them of the account hold. See Account Holds (Pro) KA
How Support reps can help customers
If a Frontline rep is contacted by a customer about a bartering violation, they should follow these steps:
Investigate: Review the account and project status to confirm T&S has removed (deleted) the project for bartering.
Tell the customer: If they would like to use Thumbtack to hire a pro for a specific project using monetary payment, they can submit a new request. 
▶ Send Template: Send the Customer Guidelines | Barter Request email template below.Subject: An update about your Thumbtack projectHi {{{Case.ContactFirstName__c}}},Thanks for reaching out to us about your recent search for a [TYPE OF SERVICE] pro. We removed your project because we noticed you were looking to trade or barter for [TYPE OF SERVICE].While we’d like to help you find a [TYPE OF PROFESSIONAL], we don't allow trade or bartering requests on Thumbtack. If you decide you’d like to offer monetary payment for [SERVICE], you’re welcome to start a new search so we can help.{{{Case.EmailMessageSignature__c}}}
How Support reps can help pros
If a Support rep is contacted by a pro with an account hold due to bartering, they should follow the steps under User has profile issues on the  Account Holds (Pro) KA.
Duplicate services (Pro)  
Pros cannot have duplicates of a service they already offer in the same area. However, they can provide their services in multiple locations as long as there is no overlap.
If a pro has duplicate services, Thumbtack can activate one service and deactivate the other based on the pro's preference. Alternatively, the pro can modify their profiles to represent different types of services.
Steps: How to handle duplicate service violations (Rep)

If a Frontline rep identifies a pro with duplicate services, the rep should follow these steps:
Deactivate the duplicate service (not the account). 
Explain to the pro why their account was removed.
Talking point: “​​After reviewing your profile, it looks like you already have a similar service listed on our site. According to your account details, the original profile was created on [DATE]. Is that the service you’d like to keep? We can activate that service (and then deactivate the other one) based on your preference. If you'd prefer, you can edit your profiles so they're for different types of services.”
Or send email template: "Pro Guidelines: Duplicate Service" 
Incorrect or fake user information (Customer)
Occasionally, customers use incorrect or fake user information when they don't genuinely need help with a project. Incorrect or fake user information could include fake phone numbers and fake or questionable account names.
For information on invalid numbers, reps can refer to the Lead Refunds (Pro) KA. 
The following are some examples of fake names that Thumbtack doesn’t allow:
Mickey Mouse
Amy Skkdkdkdk
Amy Amy
Amy Test
Amy's Maid Service
Other fake names could be:
Names of popular celebrities, fictional characters, or political figures that can't be names of real people (i.e., Bat Man, Scooby Doo, or Lady Gaga)
Vague names (li.e., Friend of the bride)
Profane or inappropriate names
Dummy names (i.e., Firstname Angeles)
First/last names with the word "Test" that don't seem real (i.e., Test Test)
Names that are websites, social media handles, or email addresses
Nonsensical names (i.e., None None or Blah Blah)
Random letters or numbers in the first name
First and last names that make up a phrase (i.e.,Heart Breaker or Ano Nymous)
Steps: How to handle fake phone number in an account (Rep)

If Frontline reps see the phone number on an account is fake, they should:
Explain Thumbtack’s policies for phone numbers.
Help the customer update their phone number. Reps can refer to the internal Account Information (Customer) KA for more information.
Steps: How to handle fake name in an account (Rep)

* When a Frontline rep encounters a customer account with a potentially questionable name, the rep should take the following steps:
Determine if the account is fake by reviewing other information on the customer's profile.
Internal note: Reps should be cautious when making this determination based solely on the name.
Escalate the case to the Proactive team as a Fraud Report by following the steps outlined in the internal Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA.
Steps: How to handle a fake name on a removed project (Rep)

Frontline rep contacted by a customer whose project was removed for a potentially questionable name should take the following steps:
Explain the following to the customer (or use the talking point below):
Since pros pay to connect with customers on Thumbtack, Thumbtack reviews every job to ensure it complies with its guidelines before forwarding it to pros. Because of this, the name on the project was flagged.
Talking point: “​​I'm sorry you had trouble meeting [TYPE OF SERVICE] pros. That's because the name [CUSTOMER'S NAME] was flagged. To give you background on why this happened, sometimes customers use fake names when they're not actually looking for help with a project. Because professionals pay to meet customers on Thumbtack, we review each job to make sure it meets our guidelines before sending it on to pros. That said, I can see we made a mistake here and I apologize that we kept you from finding a [TYPE OF SERVICE] pro. I’ll re-submitted your job so you can reach out to any [TYPE OF SERVICE]  pros you're interested in working with.”
Follow the steps in the "How to help customer whose project was deleted for violating guidelines" section above.
Reps can also use the email template: “Customer guidelines: Questionable Name.”
Jobs offering internships or full-time employment (Customer)

Thumbtack doesn’t allow jobs from customers looking to fill full-time employment or internships. A customer’s project will be removed if Thumbtack notices they’re looking to hire for a full-time position.
Steps: How to handle internship or employment violation from customer (Rep)

If a Frontline rep finds that a customer is recruiting pros, the rep should follow these steps:
Report the lead to T&S.
T&S will review the customers project. If it's confirmed as a true internship or employment job, T&S will delete the project. Any affected pros will be automatically refunded.

Related email template: "Customer Guidelines: Full-Time Job Request"

If the customer would like to use Thumbtack to hire a pro for a specific project, they can submit another request.
Jobs or services not offered (Pro) (Customer)
Thumbtack doesn’t allow jobs for services that aren’t offered on Thumbtack.  For a list of services, see Thumbtack Services. Thumbtack may make an exception if the job requires a service that can be offered independently. Frontline reps can refer to the table below.

Services not allowed
Exceptions
Advertising or Promotion Services exclusively dedicated to driving traffic to specific websites, customer referrals, etc.
Caregiver Services such as babysitting, childcare, senior care, etc.
Hotels, B&Bs, or other lodging
Lending Services offering debt consolidation, mortgages, foreclosure assistance, loans, refinancing, credit card repair, etc.
Any massage-related services (Massage therapy was removed from Thumbtack in October 2022)
Medical Services including dental care, veterinary care, and doctor visits. 
Service that offers or sells stand-alone products (makeup, auto insurance, nutritional products, host-a-party events, etc.)
Sexual Coaching, including pick-up artistry services or advice on seduction.
Sexual Photography or Videography, including nude photoshoots, or photos/videos of sex acts.
Alternative Healing or Life Coaching
Boudoir Photography that may incorporate sexual themes is allowed if the service is listed specifically under boudoir.
Boutique services that also provide invitations, announcements, event accessories, and personalized gifts
Custom handmade jewelry
Food trucks for catering purposes
Life coaching or finance planning that may involve advice on debt consolidation, loans, etc. as a secondary service.
Pro Referrals for related projects or services that the pro cannot fulfill themselves (e.g. a plumber recommending a separate drywall specialist on the same job)
If a Trust and Safety Specialist finds a user violating this guideline, they will deactivate the service or account, depending on the severity and send an automatic email to notify the user.
Steps: How to handle job or services not offered violation (Rep)
If the user contacts Service, send the user the applicable email template:
“Customer Guidelines: Charity Requests”
“Customer Guidelines: Test job” 
“Job types: Pro wants to add a service not offered on Thumbtack”
Located outside of the United States

To be on Thumbtack, a pro’s business must be located in the United States. Businesses cannot operate outside the United States on Thumbtack — including services that can be done remotely over the phone or Internet. 
Pros with an IP address outside the U.S. will be automatically removed by T&S without warning. Internal note: Frontline reps should not tell pros that Thumbtack uses their IP address to figure out where they are.
Steps: How to handle located outside of USA violation (Rep)

Frontline reps will follow these steps if contacted by a pro removed for being outside of the United States, and they are not permanently located there, such as with travel:
Tell pros why they were removed but shouldn’t tell them Thumbtack uses their IP address to figure out where they are.
Let them know they’ll need to email Thumbtack a business license or a public tax form.
Once the pro provides the necessary documents, escalate the case to the Trust & Safety team by following the steps in the internal Trust and Safety Incidents KA.
Let the pro know they’ll hear back from the Trust and Safety team within 1-2 business days.
Reps can also send the pro email template: “Pro Guidelines: Located outside of the US”
Outsourced or plagiarized academic writing jobs
Customers cannot outsource or plagiarize academic assignments or homework.  Customers are not permitted to request projects for writing portions of school assignments. However, they can submit projects for editing services. When Thumbtack identifies a potential academic or school writing request, it's flagged to safeguard pros' writing integrity. 
If a T&S Specialist encounters a customer project that violates the academic writing guidelines, the following steps will be taken:
T&S will identify exact homework specifications such as:
"I need a narrative essay about World War II. It has to be 500-1200 words, 12pt. Times New Roman font, 1 inch margins."
"I need a five-page paper summarizing XYZ."
"Should be written at a high school student level."
T&S will take action and delete the request. 
Steps: How to handle an outsourced or plagiarized writing violation (Rep)
If the Support rep finds any request that references the above specifications:
Send the email template titled "Customer Guidelines: Academic Writing" to the customer.
If the pro wasn't automatically refunded, submit an IPR for the refunds team to review the lead. See < Lead Refunds (Pro) KA for steps.
Referral or third-party services
Thumbtack requires pros to work directly with customers and don't allow third-party services. Pros offering a referral or third-party service or customers looking to hire a pro as a referral or third-party service is not allowed on Thumbtack. 
Thumbtack doesn’t allow any referral services or services offering monthly subscriptions, free referral services, or directory services/listings.
Example: A pro's profile on Thumbtack advertising where to find a local ceremony wedding officiant to perform the perfect wedding or vow renewal ceremony.
Businesses with multiple pros can use Thumbtack if they work directly with and collect payment from the customer. The customer must transact with the business sending the quote and pay them directly, not the pro.
To learn more about what is and is not a third party request, Frontline reps can refer to the internal Lead Refunds (Pro) KA.
If a service fits the descriptions above, T&S Specialists will deactivate the service or account, depending on the severity and send an automatic email notification that the account or service was deleted.
Steps: How to handle referral or third party services violation (Rep)
If the user contacts Service, send the applicable email template: 
“Pro Guidelines: Referral/Third-Party” 
“Customer guidelines: third party job”
▶ (Customer) Talking point: The customer submitted a third party request

A pro let us know you might be looking to hire a professional for a third party. We require Thumbtack pros to work directly with their customers as part of our Terms of Use, so we're reaching out to you for more information about your job.
Spanish talking point: Un profesional nos hizo saber que podría estar buscando contratar a un profesional para un tercero. Requerimos que los profesionales de Thumbtack trabajen directamente con sus clientes como parte de nuestros Términos de uso, por lo que nos comunicamos con usted para obtener más información sobre su trabajo.
Services or jobs in languages other than English 
Thumbtack currently operates primarily in English. Thumbtack requires service profiles to be at least partially in English so that customers as a whole can receive a clear understanding of the businesses on the site.
Steps: How to handle services or jobs in languages other than English (Rep)
If a service profile is entirely written in another language, Frontline reps will follow these steps:
Ask the pro to rewrite their service profiles to have an English translation.
Send the applicable email template: “Pro guidelines: Profile isn’t in English”
Services sending customers to another platform

Pros shouldn’t ask customers to download additional apps or complete forms with information customers have already shared.
Steps: How to handle a pro sending customers to another platform violation (Rep)
If a Frontline rep finds a pro asking customers to use another platform or app to hire them, the rep should follow these steps:
Escalate the case to T&S. Steps on Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer)
T&S will determine if the pro’s service profile or account should be deleted.
If the pro reaches out to Service for help, inform them of Thumbtack’s policy
User is a minor (under 18 years old)

Thumbtack’s Terms require customers to be over 18 when they submit a project. Thumbback services are not designed for minors under 18.
It’s important to note that the steps T&S Specialists take depend on the age of the user mentioned in the deletion log. Deletion reasons a rep may see include: 
(Customer) Minor requester Salesforce case
(Pro) Minor

Steps: How to handle user is minor (under 18) violation

If a Frontline rep finds a pro asking customers to use another platform or app to hire them, the rep should follow these steps:
▶ Minor is 12 years old and under
Frontline reps will reach out to T&S immediately for a T&S Specialist to deactivate and blocklist the account. Follow these steps exactly if the minor is 12 years old and under: 
Escalate to T&S for review immediately. Steps on Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer)
Do not notify the account owner that their account will be deactivated. Thumbtack cannot reach out to these users.
▶ Minor is 13-17 years old
If the minor is 13 to 17 years old, Frontline reps will reach out to T&S immediately for a T&S Specialist to deactivate their account and send an automatic email notification. Follow these steps if the minor is 13 to 17 years old: 
Escalate the account to T&S immediately. Steps on Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer)
If the user writes in to Service, send the applicable email template 
Pro Guidelines: Pro is a Minor 
Customer guidelines: job from a minor 
If a user claims to be 18 years or older: 
Tell them to fill out the ID Help Intake Form. Reps can refer to the internal ID Help Guide (Pro) (Customer) KA for more details. 
If they’re concerned about the security of their personal information, Frontline reps can let them know that the email address has restricted access, so their ID info will be secure.
Let them know they can expect a response within 2 - 3 business days.
Steps: How to deactivate and blocklist a user (Rep) 

Before Frontline reps must reach out to Trust and Safety for approval to blocklist an account. To do this, follow the Asking the proactive team for help steps. After receiving approval from Trust and Safety, reps will follow these steps: 
In order to blocklist an account, the account must be deactivated. To deactivate in Admin, click “Admin Delete” under the Account Status section of the Actions field (in the top right corner).
Once an account has been deactivated, the option to “Add user to Blocklist” can be found under the Trust and Safety section of the Actions field (in the top right corner).
Fill out the fields on the Blocklist page and click “Add User to Blocklist.”​​​​​

▶ fContents
Payment related removals
Can’t collect payment (outstanding or past due balance)
Chargebacks (Payment disputes)
Chargeback dashboard
Actions taken based on chargeback level
(Rep) Steps: How to help a user with chargebacks
Customer removed for unresolved payment issue (pro not paid)
4. Payment related removals and holds 
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: The "Payment related removals" section details why Thumbtack users might be removed due to financial issues, such as an outstanding balance or payment disputes (chargebacks). It explains the chargeback process, how to use the Chargeback Dashboard, and the actions taken by Thumbtack based on different chargeback levels. The section also covers customer removals for unresolved payment issues with a pro.
Can’t collect payment (outstanding or past due balance)   
 
Pros removed because “Past due balance” means they have a negative balance large enough to have their account removed from Thumbtack, OR the unpaid balance has been past due for 45 days. On day 45 of payment failure, the pros account is placed on hold for the past due balance (PDB). If the PDB is $50 or more, they are also added to the blocklist, and any linked accounts will also be deleted. 
The inability to collect payment may be due to an expired credit card, an invalid card, insufficient funds, or a declined card on their account. 
Steps: How to help pros with an outstanding balance (Rep)

When helping a pro whose Thumbtack account has an outstanding balance, Frontline reps will follow these steps:
Inform the pro that Thumbtack has placed a hold on their account because of a negative balance.
Check the Details section in Admin to confirm the pro has a "User has a past due balance" flag in the "Pro account hold flags" section.
Check the Credits section in Admin to confirm the pro's Thumbtack Balance.
▶ Example of the Credits section with a past due balance
[Image: rtaImage]
Let the pro know they will not be able to use Thumbtack until the amount is paid, (their balance is greater than $0).
If the pro claims they were not notified of a past due balance, follow the steps in the “The inability to collect payment may be due” section of the < Charges on internal Thumbtack: Payment Methods and Billing (Pro) KA>.
If a pro reached out to reactivate their account and their Thumbtack balance is exactly $0, select Remove Past-Due Balance Hold under Actions in Admin.
Enter Notes stating why the hold is being removed (e.g., “Thumbtack balance is paid off”) and click Confirm.
Hold status and blocklist rules
If a pro has multiple holds on their account, removing the PDB hold won’t enable their account. The pro must resolve the other concerns first. If the pro is on hold and on the blocklist for PDB only, lifting the hold will automatically remove them from the blocklist.
Handling Linked Accounts 
Frontline reps should never undelete accounts that have been removed because they’re linked to an account with a PDB. Only the main account with the PDB hold should be enabled. Escalate linked accounts to the Trust and Safety team through the transfer flow in Salesforce (select Marketplace Integrity).
When Manual Hold Removal is Required
PDB holds typically lift automatically when a balance is paid. However, reps will need to manually remove the hold if: 
The balance reached $0 via a credit or refund
A manual PDB hold was placed
Payment disputes (Chargebacks)  
Payment disputes and chargebacks are terms that refer to when a user disputes a charge from Thumbtack with their bank or credit card company. Reasons for disputes can include unrecognized charges or disagreements about the service.
Account hold reasons: 
User has chargebacks
May also see: ‘User has early fraud warnings’
Deletion log reasons: 
Other Violation
Notes: Level 4  chargebacks.
▶ Here’s a closer look at how the chargeback process works:
Dispute Filed: The user contacts their bank or credit card company to dispute a Thumbtack charge.
Funds Reversed: The bank or credit card company immediately reverses the disputed amount from Thumbtack’s account and returns it to the user.
Bank Dispute Notification: The bank or credit card company sends Thumbtack a notice of the chargeback, including the reason provided by the user.
Evidence Submission: Thumbtack provides evidence to the bank or credit card company to show the charge was valid.
Hold Level Assigned: Thumbtack assigns the user a hold level (1-4) based on the dollar amount of all chargebacks that have occurred in their account or the amount of chargebacks submitted up until that point.
Email Notification: Thumbtack sends an automated email to the user about the chargeback based on their hold level. Reps can refer to the internal Pro Chargeback Auto Emails doc for what the email says)
Account holds: Account holds will be placed on accounts with levels 2-4. 
Bank Review and Resolution: The bank reviews the evidence from Thumbtack to determine if the dispute is valid.
Thumbtack Wins: Funds are returned to Thumbtack. (The bank rules in favor of Thumbtack)
Thumbtack Loses: The user keeps the funds. (The bank rules in favor of the pro, and Thumbtack has permanently lost the funds)
▶ Chargeback dashboard
The Chargeback Dashboard in Tableau provides details about chargebacks. Frontline reps can use it to determine:
Chargeback hold levels: 
Levels are assigned based on the total dispute amount or number of chargebacks. Higher levels may result in account holds or closures. Levels are assigned when the chargeback(s) are received and processed by Thumbtack. 
Status of disputed charges: 
Pending: The user needs to contact their bank to resolve the dispute.
Won: Thumbtack won the dispute; funds are returned.
Lost: Thumbtack lost the dispute; the user keeps the funds.
Combination: A mix of pending, won, and/or lost chargebacks.
If repayment is required: 
Users with pending chargebacks must resolve those disputes with their bank before any further action can be taken. (Repayment is only possible if there are no pending chargebacks.
▶ Chargeback status and actions

Frontline reps will use the chargeback status as a guide on what to tell the user. 

Chargeback Status
Meaning
Action Required
Pending*
The user has disputed the charge with their bank.
- User needs to contact their bank to drop the chargeback. 
- Levels 1-2, it’s the honor system, and the user does not need to send in the documentation. 
- Levels 3-4 need to send documentation of this by replying to the chargeback email they received. 
Won
Thumbtack won the dispute. 
Funds are returned to Thumbtack.
Check chargeback level for next steps.
Lost
Thumbtack lost the dispute. 
The user keeps the funds.
Check chargeback level for next steps.
Combination of statuses
A mix of pending, won, and/or lost chargebacks.
- All pending chargebacks must be dropped with the bank. 
- Levels 3-4 require documentation showing chargebacks were dropped before being reconsidered. 
*Repayment can only be made if there are NO pending chargebacks. If there are chargebacks pending, the customer must close those disputes with their bank before proceeding.
▶ Actions taken based on chargeback level
The table below shows the actions the Trust and Safety team takes on the user’s account based on the chargeback level assigned. 

Hold Levels
Total payment disputes or chargebacks
Actions
Level 1
< $150
Total chargebacks are < $150 (pro) or total chargebacks submitted = 1 (customer)
- Level 1 warning auto email sent. 
- No hold is placed on the account.*
*Reps may see a Level 1 with a hold. These are typically leftover holds that were placed before the changes were made.
Level 2
Total payment disputes are $150 - $299.99 (pro) or total chargebacks submitted = 2 (customer)
- Level 2 warning auto email is sent. 
- Account hold placed.
Level 3
Total payment disputes are $300 - $799.99 (pro) or total chargebacks submitted ≥ 3 (customer)
- Level 3 warning auto email sent. 
- Account hold is placed and action is needed. 
- Possible partial repayment due if disputes were lost.
Level 4
Total payment disputes are ≥> $800 (pro) or ≥ $3500 customer
- Level 4 warning auto email sent. 
- Account is put on hold and closed. 
- Account will need to be reviewed by T&S-Payments before a decision is made on whether or not the user is allowed back on the platform. 
- Repayment will be required if disputes were lost and we decide to allow the user back on the platform.

▶ Chargeback warning emails
Thumbtack sends an automated email to the user about the chargeback based on their hold level. (Reps can refer to the Pro Chargeback Auto Emails to see what those emails look like.)
When a user responds to the warning email, it will be sent to the T&S-Payment queue for processing.  If the user sends their response to Support, Support reps should transfer to the Trust and Safety queue for it to be triaged to T&S-Payments.
If the pro did not receive an email or cannot find it, the Trust and Safety team can resend it. Frontline reps can post in #ts-proactive-ops-questions for help resending the email. 
Steps: How to help a user with chargebacks (Rep)  
If a user reaches out about a chargeback email they received  or their account being on hold (and the rep confirm its for chargebacks), Frontline reps will follow these steps:  
Check the dashboard: Review the Chargeback Dashboard in Tableau for the user’s level and chargeback status. 
Follow instructions: Follow ALL instructions listed under “Steps to take before posting in ts_global_questions”
Request hold removal (if applicable): If there is a hold on the account that needs to be removed, escalate the case to Trust and Safety by following the steps in the internal Trust and Safety incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA.
Customer removed for unresolved payment issue (Pro not paid) 
 
When a pro notifies us that a customer didn't pay them for a service they performed, Thumbtack’s Trust and Safety team will do their best to contact the customer and prompt them to work with the pro to reach a payment resolution.
If the customer was unresponsive or refuses to pay without a reasonable justification, their account will be removed. The goal is to prevent pros from being hired by customers who shouldn’t be on the site. 
If a customer seems suspicious, has multiple instances of not paying, or there is anything else concerning about them, they shouldn’t be reinstated.
Steps: How to help customer removed for unresolved payment issue with pro (Rep)

If Frontline reps see an account removed for an unresolved payment issue with a pro, they will follow these steps:
Check the case notes to learn more about the situation. 
If possible, reach out to the rep who deleted the account to get more information.
Let the customer know exactly why their account was deleted.
If necessary, reference the date and subject of the email Thumbtack sent notifying them about their account. Encourage the customer to respond to those emails.
Listen to the customer and add notes to the case if the customer has any updates.
If there are issues with the pro or the work (like damages or poor quality), escalate the case to Trust and Safety by following the steps in the internal Trust & Safety. KA. 
If there aren't issues with the work, encourage them to reach out to the pro to reach a solution.

5. Other removal reasons 
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: The "Other removal reasons" section outlines various additional causes for user account removal on Thumbtack. These include issues with background checks, accounts linked to previously banned users, and concerns regarding inauthentic or low-quality reviews. The section also covers profile issues identified during quality checks, and unresolved customer complaints.
Background checks 
When new pro accounts are created, or pros make changes to their account information, Thumbtack automatically reviews the changes to determine if the pro should complete a background check. 
Reps can refer to the internal Background Checks (Pro) KA to learn more. 
Frontline reps can refer to the deletion log reasons in the table below to see what the pro needs to do. 

Deletion log reasons
What it means
User has been auto-escalated to Checkr by Fides 
Pro needs to take and pass background check (BGC) before Thumbtack can reconsider
Background check email 
Pro needs to take and pass BGC before Thumbtack can reconsider
MTS Delete, Pro did not submit ID As requested
Pro needs to re-submit their BGC
Need to upload ID to Checkr
Pro needs to re-submit their BGC
(Pro) Failed background check — Failed BGC — Notice sent to pro through Checkr
Thumbtack made a final decision, and the decision won’t be reconsidered. These emails are sent from Checkr, not from Thumbtack. Reps won’t see a case for privacy reasons. 
Three Name Authentic Criminal Hit 
Pro is required to submit a new BGC. Pro may need to reach out to submit the ID Help Intake Form with a photo of their government ID. 
Reps can refer to the internal ID Help Guide KA to learn more.
Linked account to banned user 
A linked account user is an individual whose new or existing account has been identified as associated with an account Thumbtack previously blocklisted and removed. Thumbtack's policy is to remove all accounts found to be associated with a previously removed user.
When a user contacts support about being linked to an account, some links can be overturned if the reason the account was blocklisted can be remedied, while others mean the link and removal will remain.
Important: When speaking with the user who is linked, reps cannot share why the original account has been blocklisted, unless they have verified they are speaking to the owner of the original account in question.
▶ How Accounts are Linked
Accounts are linked through shared account data, which can include:
Phone numbers
Emails
Device ID
Credit card numbers
Native device and/or Fingerprint device
Crucial Note for Reps: For security and privacy reasons, the specific information used to tie one account to another is internal information only that cannot be shared with the user. The Trust & Safety team reviews and verifies this information before any action is taken.
▶ Consequences of Being Linked to a Banned User
When an account is flagged as "linked to a banned user," it is typically removed or placed on hold. The linked account cannot be reactivated unless the original, banned user resolves the issues that led to their removal. This measure prevents previously removed individuals or businesses from circumventing their ban and regaining access to the platform.
The removal reason for the original banned account(s) can vary (e.g., failed background check, past-due balances, user guideline violations, business decision). The ability to overturn a linked account removal depends on whether the original blocklist reason can be remedied.
The Trust & Safety teams are responsible for reviewing and potentially reactivating accounts removed for "Linked Accounts," provided the user resolves the underlying issue or the removal is determined to be inaccurate.
▶ Common Admin Deletion Reasons for Linked Accounts
When reviewing the Admin deletion log for a removed pro or customer, if the log indicates the user is "linked to a banned user," the reason will include one of the following:
Linked to previously blocklisted pros 
Linked accounts
has_blocklist_native_device_id Linked to
Has_blocklist_tmx_device_id Linked to
Has_blocklisted_credit_card Linked to
Deleted by Fides
duplicate acct 02563793
Internal note: If a pro resolves their past-due balance, any linked accounts that were deactivated are NOT automatically reactivated. Frontline reps should never manually undelete these linked accounts. Always escalate linked accounts to the Trust and Safety team using the steps below. 

▶ What Frontline Reps CAN and CANNOT Share
When a Thumbtack pro or customer contacts Support about an account removal, they won’t know it’s due to a linked account. Reps' responses must be clear, protective of Thumbtack's internal information, and focused on the necessary steps for resolution.
What frontline reps CANNOT share (Do not disclose):
Linking Information: You must not share the specific types of data Thumbtack uses to identify a link (e.g., email address, phone number, device ID) or explain how the link was discovered.
Specific Reason for Removal (Non-Matching Names): If the names on the new account and the original banned account are different, do not disclose the specific reason the original account was deleted.

articles.fullText:
Refund Request Flow (Pro)

Contents

Overview
Key points
Do’s and Don’ts 
Process
Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
[start of summary]
This internal knowledge article (KA) provides Frontline Reps with information regarding the refund request form used by pros to submit refund inquiries.
[end of summary]
The in-product refund request form is the primary method for pros to submit refund requests for leads and bookings.
Submitting requests directly through this self-service tool is significantly faster and more efficient for pros. Frontline Reps can use this KA to help pros navigate the "Request a refund" workflow and understand the specific interface elements and guidance banners they encounter on the form.
In October 2025, Thumbtack A/B tested a more visible entry point for refund requests and simplified the refund request flow for pros. In January 2026, that flow was launched to all pros.
Key changes to the entrypoint and flow:
Direct Access (Entrypoint): Pros no longer need to select "Report" to find the refund option. "Request a refund" is now a top-level action in the conversation menu.
Renamed Reporting (Entrypoint): The legacy "Report" button has been renamed to "Report an issue" to clearly distinguish Trust & Safety reporting from the refund flow.
Unified Submission Page (Flow): The previous multi-step questionnaire has been consolidated into a single, unified page to streamline the submission process.
Instant Policy Guidance (Flow): Blue informational banners now appear immediately when a pro selects a refund reason (e.g., Location, Job Type), providing real-time feedback on eligibility before they submit.
Key details
Frontline Reps should keep these points in mind when helping pros with the refund request form:
The form is the primary method for pros to request refunds for leads or bookings.
There are two ways to enter the refund request flow - from the customer contact message (udpated in 2026) and from the payment tab.
In-product requests are usually faster and more efficient for pros than manual outreach.
Pros must submit the form within the required timeframe to be eligible for review.
Frontline Reps can refer to the internal < Lead Refunds (Pro) > KA for specific eligibility criteria.
Do's and Dont's
Frontline Reps must strictly adhere to the following guidelines when helping pros with refund requests:
Do guide pros to use the in-product refund request form for all standard lead and booking refund inquiries.
Do remind pros to provide detailed information and any relevant evidence when completing the form to prevent processing delays.
Don't submit the refund request form on behalf of a pro.
Don't guarantee a refund or specify a decision outcome during the initial conversation with the pro.

2. Process

Frontline Reps should use the following steps to guide pros through the self-service refund request flow.
Pros can request a refund in two ways:
Payments page (fastest)
From the customer thread, clicking the three dots,  → Report → Select Request a refund, then follow the prompts.
Steps: How to request a refund (Pro)

Access the Refund Refund Form: Pros can initiate a refund request in three ways:
Payments page (fastest)
Go to Payments →
On the Activity tab, click on the specific charge
Select “Request a refund.” 
Note: If it's been over 45 days, the Request a refund button won’t appear
Messenger conversation menu
Open the conversation with the specific customer
Click the three dots menu in the top right corner
Select Request a refund from the dropdown menu. 
Note: The “Report” option is now labeled “Report an issue” and is separate from the refund flow. 
Completing the submission form: The pro will be asked why they are requesting a refund.
Select a reason and review guidance: The pro selects a refund reason. Immediately upon selection, a blue banner appears on the same page providing specific policy guidance relevant to that reason. 
Here’s what the pro can select and the guidance they will be given: 
Location (not in my service area) - “If you were auto-charged for a job in an area where you don’t provide services, we’ll credit your Thumbtack balance.”
Timing (outside my availability) - “If you were auto-charged for a job that doesn’t match your calendar availability preferences, we’ll credit your Thumbtack balance.”
Job type  (not in my line of work) - “If you were auto-charged for a job and don’t provide that type of work, we’ll credit your Thumbtack balance.”
Charged twice (duplicate job) - "If a customer contacts you for two identical jobs within 45 days, we’ll refund you for the repeated lead.”
Phone disconnected or out of service - “We verify phone numbers; if a number is disconnected/invalid, we’ll credit your balance.”
Reason not listed
▶ What it looks like
Provide explanation and evidence: Pro will type a short explanation, upload images.
Tell us why: The pro should enter a short explanation of the issue in the free-text field. 
Add images: The pro may optionally upload screenshots or images (up to 6) to support their request.

articles.fullText:
Pros Who Are A Close Match (Customer)

Contents

Overview
Experiment details
How "close match" pros are ranked and displayed
Criteria for “Close Match”
Factors Determining Pro Ranking
Prioritizing Pros by Ranking Tiers
The Role of Mismatches and CMP in Ranking
Near Match Scenarios
Example 1: Pro who is NOT a “close match” due to too many mismatch reasons or excluded reasons
Example 2: Pro who IS a “close match” and would be shown to the customer
Customer search experience
Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) provides Frontline Reps with details about the Near Match Pros experience. It outlines the new customer experience and provides talking points for navigating conversations related to this feature.
In August 2025, Thumbtack ran an experiment to improve the customer experience by adding back 'near match' pros when search results yielded few or zero options. On October 28, 2025, the 'Pros who are a close match' feature was fully launched.
This feature ensures customers can still find relevant pros to get their jobs done, even if those pros were initially filtered out by specific answers on the request form.
Customers will see pros who are a close match ("near match" pros) added to their pro list in search results, with clear explanations of why these pros were initially filtered. 

[Image: AD_4nXdDR3c_wJrRT_3lvEJ9MxrZiXxxeGo9MJ7otBHYibhE_z5MqTO3Fle6brpqszaHaK8K23ugS-OyJx68DA5Fk5INLiORic3KOb6rdi3JsD0QzyFzUvM3PScQ2STylf2nHgq6yFaOHw]

More detailed information about this experience is provided in the Customer experience section below.
HoRanking and display logic for close match pros
The goal is to show customers between 1 and 10 relevant pros, even if they aren't a perfect match for all project details. This is done by filtering out pros with certain mismatch reasons and then ranking the rest based on a specific hierarchy.
Eligibility criteria for close match 
A pro is eligible to appear as a 'close match' if they meet the following conditions:
Filter Status: They were initially filtered out from the main pro list.
Mismatch Count: They have a maximum of two reasons for not matching the customer's request.
Mismatch Type: The mismatch reasons are unrelated to travel preferences (e.g., 'Where will the work be done?') or scheduling (e.g., 'When do you need this job to start?').
Ranking factors
Once deemed eligible as a 'close match'‘, pros are ranked based on the following hierarchy:
Number of Mismatch Reasons: Professionals with fewer mismatches (e.g., 1 vs. 2) are ranked higher.
Category Management Priority (CMP): Professionals matching internal business priorities (e.g., high-demand services) are ranked higher.
Quality Score: This score is used as a tie-breaker for pros within the same tier.
Ranking tiers (internal only)
The following section details the backend logic used to prioritize 'close match' pros.
Pros are categorized into priority tiers based on their mismatch count and alignment with Category Management Priorities (CMP), with higher tiers appearing first in the results:
1 mismatch reason & 1 CMP: Pros with only one mismatch reason and one CatMgmt Priority match are considered the highest priority.
2 mismatch reasons & 2 CMP: These pros have two eligible mismatch reasons (not related to travel or scheduling) and satisfy two CatMgmt Priority criteria, making them a high-priority suggestion. Acceptable mismatch reasons could come from questions about add-on services, who is buying materials, or specific scheduling types.
2 mismatch reasons & 1 CMP: Pros with two eligible mismatch reasons and one CatMgmt Priority match.
1 mismatch reason & 0 CMP: Pros with only one mismatch reason but no CatMgmt Priority matches.
2 mismatch reasons & 0 CMP: Pros with two eligible mismatch reasons and no CatMgmt Priority matches.
The Role of Mismatches and CMP in Ranking 
The ranking system for "close match" pros prioritizes a crucial balance between minor mismatches and alignment with Thumbtack's business objectives (CMP). This ensures that even if a pro doesn't perfectly match every customer detail, their overall relevance and business value make them a valuable suggestion.
▶ Close Match Scenarios
To further illustrate how pros are categorized as "close match" and how the ranking criteria are applied, the following examples provide specific scenarios. These examples clarify which pros would or would not be shown to a customer based on their mismatch reasons and other eligibility factors.
▶ Scenario: Pro disqualified due to conflicts
Pro who is NOT a “close match” due to too many mismatch reasons or excluded reasons 
This example illustrates a scenario where a pro is not considered a "close match" and therefore would not be displayed to the customer. This can happen if the pro has too many mismatch reasons or if any of the mismatch reasons are related to excluded categories like travel preferences or scheduling conflicts.
A customer is searching for a house cleaning pro and provides the following details:
Request Form Question: "How often do you want the house cleaned?"
Customer's Answer: "Just once"
Pro's Preference: The pro offers "Once a month," "every week," and "every 2 weeks," but not "Just once." (This is one mismatch reason.)
Request Form Question: "Is there anything else you need?"
Customer's Answer: "Baseboard cleaning"
Pro's Preference: The pro does not offer "Baseboard cleaning." (This is a second mismatch reason.)
Request Form Question: "When do you need this job to start?"
Customer's Answer: "Within 48 hours"
Pro's Availability: The pro is blocked for the next three days, so they are not available. (This is a scheduling conflict.)
Outcome: This pro will not be shown to the customer as a "close match" because they have more than two mismatch reasons and a scheduling conflict, which are criteria for exclusion.
▶ Scenario: Pro qualified as close match
Pro who IS a “close match” and would be shown to the customer  
This example demonstrates a scenario where a pro is considered a "close match" and would be shown to the customer. This occurs when the pro has an acceptable number of mismatch reasons, and none of those reasons fall into the excluded categories of travel preferences or scheduling conflicts.
A customer is searching for a house cleaning pro and provides the following details:
Request Form Question: "How often do you want the house cleaned?"
Customer's Answer: "Just once"
Pro's Preference: The pro offers "Once a month," "every week," and "every 2 weeks," but not "Just once." (This is one mismatch reason.)
Request Form Question: "Is there anything else you need?"
Customer's Answer: "Baseboard cleaning"
Pro's Preference: The pro offers "Baseboard cleaning" and all other options in this section. (This is not a mismatch.)
Request Form Question: "When do you need this job to start?"
Customer's Answer: "Within 48 hours"
Pro's Availability: The pro has open availability and no scheduling conflicts.
Outcome: This pro will be shown to the customer as a "close match" because they have only one mismatch reason and no scheduling or travel preference conflicts, which are the criteria for inclusion.
Customer search experience 
When a customer's search results yield few or zero exact matches, the system automatically displays the 'Pros who are a close match' carousel to provide additional options.
Customers who see few or zero pros on their list will have additional "pros who are a close match" added, with a clear explanation of why they were previously filtered out. The experience will differ depending on whether the initial pro list is small or empty.
Pro List in Search Results is Empty:
If the initial list is empty, a message will appear that says "we are currently short on pros who match all of your needs".
Below this message, the same "pros who are a close match" carousel will be displayed.
Warning messages include “Doesn’t offer: [service not offered]
▶ What it looks like:[Image: AD_4nXfwgAtPQEZxcU2Bs2ROS4UpvrNBYYXC4xUiKuaOssMvNkxG11Kexg5sHg85zRBgKSvBBJcHR_Pwj0Y4YQGBF4j48fJW6RoH07he0sMOYD7P-tWVmqsdMOEp226fNAyZj_pVyCG0Hw]
Few Pros in Search Results
If a customer sees a small list of pros, a "pros who are a close match" carousel will be displayed at the bottom.
The carousel will show cards for filtered pros, along with a note explaining the reason for the filter, such as “Doesn’t offer: Laundry”
An "edit project details" button will be available below the carousel, allowing the customer to go back and adjust their answers to potentially make the filtered pros available. 
▶ What it looks like:[Image: AD_4nXcie1U4CXcrGAm9S0y2pF6djpJIpnbGtLLCWtzkEHL4oRDa-odms9Rdzi1jruqSbvoBTfuS5kvyoheNGYaRqrcYpJq6Z4tuzAYiPbZBGo6UtoEtGLFqZ14tYYsWlWa-qgZnR32Z]
Pro Profile Page
If a customer clicks on the profile of a filtered pro, a yellow warning box will appear in the "your project" section, explaining why the pro was filtered. 
Warning messages include: "Not offered by this pro." Clicking the information icon explains “If you’re flexible on these details, this pro could get the job done too.” 
▶ What it looks like:[Image: AD_4nXdyXD1c6OzGISoSVb-oVgf1D3hz4CLPJKPlla6qT7wIad7-Y9PW-xp_eLfw922aPG8eFGbUaO9osWCO6xIgmijDAiATXA8bU0HdNWQCNp_DvZ3U6YpT3xRUcCfOJgNe6X7oIjw06w]
Request flow warning:
If a customer revisits the request flow for a filtered pro, the request form will have two warnings:
"This pro doesn’t offer some of your choices. Continue if you're flexible or see other pros" directly on the selection option that the pro does not offer.
“Not offered by this pro” under option will be grayed out and can't be checked to reflect that a pro doesn't offer a specific preference or service. This prompts the customer to be flexible.
These warnings ensure customers are fully aware of any mismatches before they finalize their request, allowing them to make an informed decision and increasing the likelihood of a successful match.
If a customer decides they aren’t flexible, they can click “See other pros” in the warning at the top. 
▶ What it looks like:[Image: AD_4nXeUHkMKrvK6LfkVhSGXxcaWJgnAkqF1gY81sQJlx7av1YB0RwimUfyw_nNC_-Ee7BQs2NQJ9eZwaTIJO-S8CFSwJMfewuP-Opqrvg9JPZ_Uz4njeBU21l-5VQqpMq9xBJSBdJ72CA]

Property Ownership Question Expansion: H1 '26 Request Flow & Targeting updates (Pro) (Customer)

Contents

Overview
Impacted categories
Expansion details
Comms and timeline
Pro experience
Before March 18, 2026
On and after March 18, 2026
How pros can opt out of these job types
Pro has business hidden during launch
Refund policy

Key points
Talking points
Resources
1. Overview
What is happening?: 
Thumbtack is expanding the "Property ownership" preference question to 48 additional service categories to improve lead quality and ensure pros have the necessary permissions before starting a job. 
The mandatory question to the customer request form is: "Are you the owner, renter, or property manager?" 

[Image: rtaImage]

Before submitting their request, customers must select one of five options, including:
Owner
Renter, with owner’s permission to do this job
Renter, haven’t discussed job yet with owner
Buyer under contract
Property manager
Why is the "Property ownership" preference expanding?
[Internal why: The goal of this update is to provide pros with critical context regarding property authority before they pay for a lead. High-revenue categories like Interior Painting and Roofing often require owner consent; by capturing this upfront, Thumbtack reduces friction and potential cancellations caused by unauthorized renters or buyers.]

How will it happen? 
When customers submit a project in an impacted category, the request form will ask them a mandatory question about property ownership. Pros will see the customer's response within the project details, allowing them to prioritize owners or authorized managers as part of their targeting preferences.
Pros in the 48 affected categories will be automatically opted in to receive job requests from all ownership types (Owner, Renter, Property Manager, etc.).
Impacted categories
The "Property ownership" preference expansion update affects 48 categories, including top revenue drivers like Interior Painting, Roof Installation or Replacement, Electrical and Wiring Repair, Floor Installation or Replacement, and Bathroom Remodel. Here is the full list of categories broken down by occupation in alphabetical order:: 
Decks, Fences, & Outdoor Structures

Floor Repair

Central Air Conditioning Repair or Maintenance

Duct and Vent Repair
Heating System Installation or Replacement
Heating System Repair or Maintenance
Window, Wall, or Portable AC Repair or Maintenance
Painting
Exterior Painting
Interior Painting
Plumbing & Water Systems
Plumbing Inspection
Water Damage Cleanup and Restoration
Water Feature Repair and Maintenance
Water Heater Repair or Maintenance
Remodeling & General Contracting

Bathroom Remodel

General Contracting

Structural & Exterior Finishes

Stucco Repair

Expansion details
Implementation date 
March 4, 2026 (Pro job preferences): Pros in the 48 impacted categories will see the new job type option in their job preferences.. They can adjust these preferences before the request form changes launch. 
March 18, 2026 (Request forms): Customers submitting projects in the 48 impacted categories will be asked the mandatory question about property ownership. 
Launch type: Full launch to product
Comms and timeline
We want to give pros a heads-up in advance of the change that is coming, what they should expect, and what to do once the change is implemented. The following comms will be sent out. 
2-weeks pre-launch (March 4, 2026): Email and push announcement informing pros of upcoming changes and the automatic opt-in.
1-week pre-launch (March 11, 2026): In-product banner launches on impacted pro accounts (persists until launch date). Clicking the banner directs the pro to their Service page to update preferences.
Reminder (March 17, 2026): Email and push reminder sent to pros regarding the update going live the following day.
Launch Date (March 18, 2026): Final email follow-up confirming the preferences are live. Pros begin receiving leads containing property ownership data.
Pro experience
Pros can check out the How to set my property ownership preferences – Thumbtack Help article to learn more.
Before March 18, 2026:
On March 4, 2026, pros who offer the service categories listed above in the + impacted categories + section will:
Receive an announcement email informing them of the upcoming changes to their job types. 
See the new job types in their preferences and can update them to prioritize owners or authorized managers as part of their targeting preferences. 
On and after March 18, 2026:
Customers will see the new job types on the request form in those 48 categories.
Pros will start receiving leads for the new job types (based on their adjusted preferences).
How pros can opt out of these job types

Pros are automatically opted into these new job types. 
No action: If the pro offers these services, there’s no action they need to take. 
Action to take: If the pro does NOT offer these services, they should opt out of these new job types (by updating their targeting preferences) before March 17, 2026 to avoid receiving these types of jobs. Pros can also update their job types anytime before or after launch. 

Pro has business hidden during launch

Pros with hidden businesses will only receive jobs for these new preferences once their business goes live. They can opt out of these jobs by updating their preferences.

Refund policy

No special refund policy will be applied since pros will clearly see the notification that they need to review the targeting preferences. However, a one-time courtesy refund (Approved_Courtesy_Refund) can be applied by the Refund Dispute team if a pro disputes  a denied refund explaining that they were unaware of this update.

Support reps working with a pro who disputes a denied refund for preference mismatches related to the new job types should follow these steps to direct them to the Refund Disputes Team:

If the pro has not yet requested a refund, direct them to submit a refund request in-product (How to request a refund – Thumbtack Help).
If the pro has received a denied refund decision, direct them to follow the dispute process:
The pro should contact the Refunds team at refunddisputes@thumbtack.com for help.
The pro should include the customer’s name and any screenshots, information, context, or additional details, that were not already shared in the original request, to help the Refund Disputes team help the pro in the best way possible.
Pro’s should receive a response within 1 business day.
Walk the pro through how to manage their job types for services they are targeting (How to manage my job types – Thumbtack Help). Reps can refer to the internal < Targeting: Job Types and Travel Preferences (Pro) > KA for more info on job types.
Do not promise that the pro will receive a refund.

Reps can learn more about refund requests and refund disputes in the internal < Lead Refunds (Pro) > KA.
Standard Refund Policy for Job Outside of Preferences (Job is Unreasonable)
Thumbtack only provides in-policy refunds for property ownership issues if the pro's job types were specifically set to avoid that job type at the time the customer submitted the request.
Eligibility for In-Policy Refunds: A lead is only eligible for an in-policy refund if "owner" was included in the pro's targeting preferences, but the lead received was from a non-owner (e.g., a renter).
Ineligibility: If the pro did not have "owner" selected in their preferences, Thumbtack does not offer an in-policy refund. This is because the pro still had the opportunity to win the job.

NOTE: Pros may request a refund and the Refund Ops team will look into it. Frontline reps MUST not promise that the pro will receive a refund.
Customer experience
In the baseline experience, the property ownership question already exists for several categories on Thumbtack where customers are required to specify their relationship to the property. However, for the 48 categories included in this update, customers previously were not required to provide this information during the request flow.
Prior to March 18, 2026, customers will not be asked the property ownership question in those 48 impacted categories.
On and after March 18, 2026, customers must answer “Are you the owner, renter, or property manager?" “ by selecting one of the following options when submitting their project in those categories.
Owner
Renter, with owner’s permission to do this job
Renter, haven’t discussed job yet with owner
Buyer under contract
Property manager
Key points
Key takeaways for reps regarding the property ownership expansion:
All pros will be auto-enrolled into the new job types (unless they opt-out before March 18, 2026). 
Pros can update their preferences as early as March 4, 2026. 
Pros won’t receive leads with these new job types until March 18, 2026.
Pros with hidden businesses will only receive jobs for these new preferences once their business goes live. They can opt out of these jobs by updating their preferences.
Customers won’t see these new job types on the request form until March 18, 2026.
2. Talking points

Q: Are my lead prices changing?
A: No. These leads will come at the same prices as what you would pay for similar leads, and as always, you can make adjustments to your lead prices at any time. We are adding this to your preferences and to the customer request form so that you can get more of these jobs that are in high demand. If you don’t want to receive these leads you can always opt out of this option in your job preferences.

Q: Will I get leads for this new job type right away?
A: You'll be able to get leads for this new job type in about two weeks. This gives you time to adjust your job preferences before they are visible customer options on the customer request form. After this two week period you will then be able to get leads for this new job type preference. 

Q: Why is Thumbtack making this change? 
A: There's increasing demand for these new job types and services, and pros have told us they would like to target these new preferences.
