1. Overview
▶ 🤖 Background notes
[AI Context]: Provides frontline teams with comprehensive information on the customer project lifecycle, covering how customers search, hire pros, and manage payments. It outlines essential processes for starting and canceling projects, and offers guidance for frontline reps to troubleshoot common issues, including phone number verification during submission.
Customers can fill out a request form and submit their projects on Thumbtack. Pros appear in a customer's search results based on a couple of factors, such as their review rating, if they’ve built an engaging profile, how quickly they respond to customers, and how well they match a customer’s project details. 
Here’s a high level view of the customer hiring journey: 
Search. Customers browse pro profiles and read verified reviews in search results.
Chat. Once they submit their project, they can chat about their project with the pros they selected (customers can contact up to five pros in the first four hours). They can also upload and view videos or documents within the messenger to help pros understand the project. 
Hire. Customers hire a pro for their project right in the app.
Customer resources: How It Works Thumbtack landing page and How to find a pro on Thumbtack article. 

Hiring methods
There are different ways a customer can hire a pro depending on how a customer schedule, pay, and work with them:
Contacting a pro: Customers choose which pro they want to reach out to. After they reach out, the customer and the pro decide on a date and time to get started, and the cost. 
On-demand booking: Thumbtack matches customers with a pro at a set price and scheduled date and time. On-demand bookings require customers to pay upfront. 
Customers can refer to the What are On-Demand bookings? – Thumbtack Help article.  

Services on Thumbtack 
Thumbtack offers about 500 different services. If the customer doesn't see the service they’re looking for, they should try different keywords. If it still doesn’t appear, then Thumbtack likely doesn’t offer that service at this time. 

Go to the Thumbtack Services landing page to see all services available on Thumbtack. 
For reps, they can refer to the internal Request Category List page under Category Management in Admin. 
Updates
Customer Journey: From project initiation to contacting pros 
This section outlines the standard, baseline customer journey from initiating a project to communicating with pros they’ve contacted. 
Project initiation flow
Project details: The journey begins with a project request form. Customers answer targeted questions to help pros understand their specific needs and provide accurate quotes.
Matching: Once details are provided, customers see filtered search results based on a mix of two match types:
Exact Match: Pros who strictly target the specific category.
Expanded Match: Pros relevant based on AI predictions/job history but who do not explicitly target the category.
Note: This distinction is invisible to the customer; they see one unified list.
If there are enough pros:
Top 3 Best Matches: Customers are presented with a curated top 3 matches featuring highly-rated pros at the top of their search results. 
Contact the 3 best matches: Customers can click "Get 3 quotes" to send their project details to all three curated pros simultaneously, allowing customers to gather multiple quotes. 
All pros list: Below the top three pros, the customer can browse additional pros in the pro list. This list also contains both exact and expanded (partial match) pros.
Refer to the Top Three Pros in Search Results (Customer) KA to learn more.
If there aren’t enough pros: 
The customer will see the standard pro list without the "Top 3" module.
Submitting the project
Contacting pros: After reviewing search results, customers select the specific pro they wish to reach out to or use the “Get 3 quotes” button.
Mismatch handling (Preventing Contact): 
Job preference block: If a customer's request form answers conflict with the pro's job preferences, the system displays: "This pro doesn't match your project needs - they don't offer [service]".
Availability block: Customers are always blocked from contacting any pro (exact or expanded) if the project timeline does not align with the pro’s availability (unless the customer has the flexibility toggle turn on).
No block: If a customer’s project details are deemed relevant based on the pros profile and job history by the matchmaker engine, the system removes the standard "mismatch" block. Customers will not see an error message if the pro doesn't explicitly target the service category.
Additional pro upsell: If a customer contacts only one pro, the system may ask, "Want to send your project to additional pros?" to help them gather more quotes.
Mismatch Handling (if applicable): When selecting additional pros, if a selected pro doesn't meet the project's specific needs, the system will display an error like "This pro doesn't match your project needs - they don't offer [what they don't offer based on customer's request form details]." 
Customers can then select other pros and click "Send project to selected pros."
Home address: Customers without a saved address will be prompted to add one to their Home Profile. They can skip this by clicking the “X” in the top right. 
After the customer completes the address page and clicks Next, the flow continues.
Customers with a saved address won’t see this step.
Phone Number Verification: After the customer has filled out all project details and is ready to hit "Submit,"  the system validates the customer's identity. 
Backend Match: Thumbtack attempts to automatically verify the name and phone number provided.
SMS Validation: If the automatic check cannot confirm the identity (a "mismatch"), the customer must enter a 6-digit verification code sent via text message before the project is officially posted.
Device Limits: To prevent spam, a single phone number can only be associated with a maximum of three customer accounts.
Troubleshooting and more info: Reps should refer to the internal Enhanced Lead Quality Commitment (Customer Phone Number Verification Code Validation) (Pro) (Customer) KA.
Project Details Sent (Success Screen): After successfully sending project details to one or more pros, the customer sees a confirmation.
The 4-Hour Contact Limit: Customers are limited to contacting five pros within the first four hours to ensure they are making intentional hiring decisions.
Project Access and Management
Project details: Once a project is submitted, the core details cannot be changed or edited. Customers should message pros directly if minor updates are needed.
Communicating with pros: After submitting the project, customers can respond to new messages from pros by going to their Inbox.
To learn more about the inbox, reps should refer to the internalCustomer App Features: Home Profile, Plan Tab and Team Tab (Customer) KA. 
NOTE: When a customer starts a search or submits a project on Thumbtack, they may not be required to set up a password. They can access their account and view project details using Magic Login (a link sent to their email) or by clicking the links in the project emails Thumbtack sends them. Reps can refer to the Account Information (Customer) KA for more info on login and password. 
Searching and matching logic
Before a customer ever sends a message to a pro, Thumbtack’s matching engine works behind the scenes to align customer needs with pro preferences. This section explains the logic and AI-driven features that power those initial recommendations.
Home Profile: Personalized Recommendations

The Home Profile acts as the foundation for a customized user experience. By capturing specific data points about a customer’s property, the platform moves from generic results to high-intent matching.
Data Capture: Customers provide their address, home type (e.g., single-family, condo), and specific features (e.g., roof material, lawn size).
The Logic: This data powers "Personalized Guides." For example, if a customer adds that they have a shingle roof, the system will prioritize "Roof Maintenance" guides and suggest pros who specialize in that specific material.
Customer Value: Instead of searching from scratch, the Home Profile allows the app to surface "Next Steps" for home maintenance based on the season and the home's unique attributes.
NOTE: Customers without a saved address will be prompted to add one to their Home Profile when submitting a project request.
To learn more about home profiles, reps should refer to the internal Customer App Features: Home Profile, Plan Tab and Team Tab (Customer) KA. 
AI-Powered and Recent Search Functionality
Thumbtack’s AI and search history features make it easier for homeowners to find pros by interpreting intent and providing shortcuts to previous searches.
Natural Language Matching: Customers can describe their problem in the search bar (e.g., “need help with my leaky sink” or "house cleaning after construction”).
The Logic: The AI interprets the intent behind the description and maps it to the correct service category (e.g., "Plumbing" or "House cleaning").
Rep Action: If a customer is struggling to find a category, encourage them to describe the problem in the search bar as if they were talking to a person.
Recent Search Logic: For returning customers, the "Search" tab stores recent intent to reduce friction. If a customer previously searched for a service but didn't hire, the system saves their previous questionnaire answers.
Seamless Sync: These searches sync across mobile and desktop, allowing users to pick up exactly where they left off without re-entering project details.
▶ What the search looks like when tapping on search in the app
The image below shows the search bar and the customers zip code. Below that shows “Planned projects” if the customer has any, recent searches from returning customers, and popular services. 

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ What a search looks like when using natural language
The image shows a customer searching for someone to watch their pet while out of town. The search surfaces related categories with animal boarding being first in the list. 

[Image: rtaImage]

Project timeline and search filtering
When customers search for a pro, they are asked about their project timeline ("What's your timeline?"). Once they’ve selected a pro, they will confirm their project timeline on the request form ("When do you need this job to start?").
▶ Here’s what customers see in search results and the request form around their timeline

Search results: ”What’s your timeline?”
Request form: “When do you need this job to start?”

[Image: rtaImage]


[Image: rtaImage]

Search results filter: The customer's selection filters search results to show only available pros (customers don’t see a pros individual calendar). Pros will not appear in search results if the customer filters for a day the pro is not available.
The following table provides detailed information on customers project timeline options, how pros are filtered, and the logic used for matching:

Search result options

Request form ONLY: The request form has a "I can work with the pro’s schedule if they aren’t available in the time I chose" toggle. 
Default State: The toggle is ON by default for all timeline options, indicating the customer is open to other dates. Customers can manually turn it off if their timeline is firm.
One thing to note is that customers will be blocked from contacting a pro if the project timeline does not align with the pro’s availability (unless they have the flexibility toggle turn on).
To learn more about pro matching based on project timelines, reps should refer to the internal Availability: Business Hours, Calendar, and Hide a Business (Pro) KA. 
Blocking a pro on a project 
This section guides customers on how to block a pro on desktop if they experience unprofessional behavior.
Steps: How to block a pro on desktop if they’ve become unprofessional (Customer)
If a customer feels that a pro’s messages made them feel uncomfortable, acted unprofessionally or crossed a line (e.g., offensive or inappropriate content), the customer has the option to block the pro. This feature is exclusively available on a desktop browser. Customers can access the blocking option within the messenger with the specific pro by clicking “Block pro” in the lower right corner.  After blocking a pro, the messenger will say “You  have flagged the pro.” and the customer will no longer receive messages from the pro.
Here’s what it looks like from the customer’s perspective:

[Image: rtaImage]

Once a pro is blocked, the customer will no longer receive new messages from them. However, past messages will remain visible in the conversation. It's important to note that the pro will not be notified that they have been blocked and will still be able to send messages, although these will not be received by the customer.
When initiating a block, customers are prompted to select a reason from the following options:
Inappropriate or spam content
Pro messages or calls me too much
I want to report a sensitive or urgent issue
All reports of blocked pros are tracked by the Trust and Safety team. This data helps monitor and address potential issues.
Internal only information Important to reps: Frontline reps can refer to the Trust and Safety Report Handling Section of the internal Unprofessional Behavior, Support Abuse, & Discrimination (Rep) KA for details on further steps.
Cost estimates (average price for services) 
Thumbtack’s Cost Estimates for Home Projects, Events and More page show the national average price for different services on Thumbtack. 
For most services, customers can go to the cost estimates page to see a national average. For a more comprehensive guide to the cost of a specific service, they’ll click on a service. Cost guides typically include the following: 
Cost Overview: Information about the national average cost for the service.
Factors Impacting Price: Details on various elements that influence the service's cost, such as home size, type of issue, location of infestation, scope of damage, and tools needed.
Hiring a Pro vs. DIY: A comparison of the pros and cons of hiring a pro versus attempting a do-it-yourself solution.
Prevention Tips: Advice on how to prevent future occurrences of the problem.
How to Choose and Hire a Professional: Guidance on selecting and hiring a qualified service provider.
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs): Answers to common questions related to the service.
Customers can refer to the Cost Estimates for Home Projects, Events and More - Thumbtack page. Thumbtack hopes giving the customer a general idea of cost will provide them with a good starting point and understand how much a project might cost.
Key points
Customers should add as many details as they can to help pros understand what they need.
Customers can only contact up to five pros in the first four hours of their search. 
The request form has a "I can work with the pro’s schedule if they aren’t available in the time I chose" toggle. When turned on, it indicates the customer is open to other dates. 
Customers without a saved address will be prompted to add one to their Home Profile (to skip click the “X” in the top right). 
Once a customer taps “submit” on their project, they can’t change or edit these details.
After the customer has filled out all project details and is ready to hit "Submit,"  their name and phone number will be verified. 
If the phone number and name match, the customer's request is submitted and shared with relevant pros. 
If a mismatch happens, the customer must enter a 6-digit verification code sent via text message before the project is officially posted.
Customers can’t reopen a canceled project, but they'll be able to see the previous messages they sent.
Customers who haven’t set a password can access their account and view project details using Magic Login (a link sent to their email) or by clicking the links in the project emails Thumbtack sends them.
2. Process
Steps: How to start a project (Customer)
Customer steps: Customers can follow the steps in the How to Find a Pro on Thumbtack article to start their project search.  
Customers can only contact up to five pros in the first four hours of their search. Thumbtack wants to make sure the customer finds the right pro, so if it doesn’t work out with those pros in those first four hours, the customer can contact more pros afterward.
After submitting a project, customers can respond to new messages from pros. Customers can also upload and view videos or documents within the messenger to help pros understand the project.
Thumbtack's inbox features actively prompt customers to respond to unread messages through visual cues and sorting, making it easier for customers to see and engage with pro messages.
[Internal note: If a customer views a video in an older app version, it may appear as an "empty bubble." Encourage the customer to update to the latest app version.]
Steps: How to cancel a project (Customer)
When a customer cancels their project it will be moved to the Done section of their plan page. Customers won't be able to reopen a canceled project, but they'll be able to see the previous messages they sent.
Customer steps: To cancel a project, customers can follow the steps on How to continue or cancel my project – Thumbtack Help. 
If a customer wants to remove a project from their plan, see “Steps: Remove project from plan” on the Customer App Experience KA.
Steps: Customer reports an issue with a pro they are working with (Rep)
If a customer reports an issue with a pro they are working with, frontline reps should escalate the case to the Trust and Safety team by following the applicable steps in the internal Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA. 
Customers can also Report a concern from the Help Center.
Steps: How to help a customer with their project (Rep)
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: This section provides guidelines for Frontline Reps on how to help customers with their projects, including submitting projects on behalf of customers and handling handoffs to the Boost team.
Note: If a customer encounters an error or their project is not visible due to phone number policy issues, Frontline Reps should refer to the internal Enhanced Lead Quality Commitment (Customer Phone Number Verification) KA for detailed troubleshooting steps. This includes:
Errors during submission: If a customer sees an error like 'This phone number can't be used on your account' due to the 3-user limit.
Projects not visible after submission: If a customer's project was silently deleted after submission due to a blocklisted phone number.
Inbound Voice Support Rep
These reps ARE able to help customers submit their project, if requested. Before submitting a project on the customer’s behalf, read the guidelines in the internal Making Account Changes on Behalf of Pro or Customer (Impersonation Guidelines) KA.
Non-Voice Support Reps
There reps will need to hand off to the Boost team if the customer needs help submitting a project: 
Note:
If the customer does not have access to the account, even if they have completed verification, Non-Voice Support Reps need to address any login issues the customer may be experiencing or encourage them to set up a new account first.
After the customer gains access to their account, Non-Voice Support Reps will complete the handoff to the Boost Team. This way, Boost reps can guide the customer through submitting their project. a request.
▶ Steps to hand off to Boost team:
Let the customer know that you’ll send their project details over to our specialist's team and that you need to gather their name, phone number, email address, and project details.
▶ Talking point
"Thanks for contacting Thumbtack. We're happy to help you with your project. To get things moving, I’m going to pass your project request to our specialized team. They're experts at matching customers with pros. Before I send those details over, can I get your phone number and some project details from you?”
Once you have those details, let the customer know when they can expect to hear back from the team
▶ Talking point:
"Thanks for those details. Our team will check out your project and contact you within 1-2 business days to chat about what you need. Just keep an eye out for a call or email from them."
Submit those details by filling out the Boost Handoff workflow with the following details: 
Customer Name
Phone Number
Job Category
Zip Code
Admin Link (optional) 
Customer email address 
Case Number
Other Details (optional) 
Complete the case as usual.
Once the workflow form is submitted, a request is automatically added to the Boost Handoff Tracker. 
Steps: How to help a customer ask a pro for a receipt for their project (Rep)
If a customer is concerned they didn’t get a receipt from a pro, frontline reps will follow these steps: 
NOTE: Thumbtack doesn’t have receipt requirements, so our goal is to get the users back in contact with each other.
Let the customer know that we’ll reach out to the pro as a reminder, and that we encourage them to contact the pro directly if they haven’t already.
If you’re emailing the customer, your email can include: 
▶ Email suggestion:
My name is {{{Sender.FirstName}}} with Thumbtack Support. We’re sorry you haven’t received a receipt for your project yet. While we’re not part of [PRO'S NAME/BUSINESS NAME]’s business and can’t provide the receipt ourselves, we’ll reach out to them as a reminder to send it to you.
We encourage you to continue to contact them directly to request this information. Let us know if you have any questions, we’re happy to help.
Create a quick case to email the pro.
▶ Email suggestion:
We received a report from [CUSTOMER’S NAME] that they haven’t received a receipt for their payment to you. Please reach out to them to discuss this further.
Let us know if you have any questions, we’re happy to help.
If the pro pushes back, ask them to discuss further with their customer. 
Complete the case as usual. 

3. Talking points
Customer wants to update their project details
This section addresses customer inquiries about updating project details after submission and offers guidance on how reps can respond.
My project has changed. How can I update the details?
Once you send a pro your project, the details can’t be changed. If the details have changed substantially, we recommend starting a new project. But if you’ve already started chatting with pros, tell them about the changes in case one of them can help. Our team is working on adding a way to edit and update project details in the near future.
Mi proyecto ha cambiado. ¿Cómo puedo actualizar los detalles?
Una vez que envía su proyecto a un profesional, los detalles no se pueden cambiar. Si los detalles han cambiado sustancialmente, recomendamos comenzar un nuevo proyecto. Pero si ya ha comenzado a hablar con profesionales, comparta los cambios en caso de que alguno de ellos pueda ayudar. Nuestro equipo está trabajando para agregar una forma de editar y actualizar los detalles del proyecto en un futuro cercano.
4. Resources

▶ Rep Processes
(Rep) Steps: How to coach pro on profile photos and videos
(Rep) Steps: How to troubleshoot social media link errors on pro profile

(Rep) Steps: How to help pro create widget for their multiple businesses
(Rep) Steps: How to help a pro resize their photos
(Rep) Steps: How to help pro with issues uploading a photo
▶ Talking Points
Business info details

Customer view
Feature projects
Customer review as featured project
Introduction
Add another business profile 
Profile photo
Profile strength
Review widget
Widgets no longer available 
Resources
1.Overview
The pro’s profile is like their online storefront. It’s how pros capture a customer's interest, give an idea of what it's like to work with them, and how they stand out from the other pros in search results. 
▶ A pro's profile can include:
Business details info, including their profile photo
Service details (depending on the category)
Credentials (background check and professional licenses)
Photo and videos
Social media links
Payment methods accepted
Introduction (business description)
Featured projects (only available for some services)
Reviews
Location
Business hours
FAQs (Questions and answers)
▶ A pro’s profile can not include:
Contact information
Verbiage sharing how pros pay for leads,
Verbiage telling customers to not contact them on Thumbtack.
NOTE: Pro’s who try to include contact information in their description or FAQ section, it will be automatically redacted and replaced by asterisks (this is known internally as contact avoidance). The pro is notified the information has been removed and warns them about further contact avoidance. Reps can refer to Contact Avoidance (Pro) KA to learn more.
Reminder: In order for new pros to meet customers on Thumbtack: 
Provide a business name
Fill out basic personal information (including birth date and address)
Upload a profile photo
Ask for at least one review
Reps can refer to internal Onboarding and activation requirements (EMR) (Pro) KA to learn more. 
Key points
Here is a list of help key points for frontline reps to note when helping pros with their profiles: 
Changes to profile: Any changes a pro makes to their public profile may take up to 24 hours to reflect. 
Contact Information: Pros are not allowed to add their contact information (address, phone number, website, and social media) to any section of their profile except the business details info section.
Business name: Once a business license is verified, the business name can not be edited by the pro. 
Profile photo: The profile photo is shared across all of a pro's profiles. (e.g., if a pro has 2 service profiles under 1 account, both profiles will show the same profile photos). The photo should be 400x400 pixels, and pros should rotate photos before uploading them.
Introduction: Reps should encourage the pro to write their own introduction, keep it short, and use it to stand out from competition.
Credentials: Pro's profile can display up to two licenses. Pros can only enter the "no social security number" background check flow through their profile. Pro profiles can have a background check badge and/or licenses badge. 
Featured projects: These are only available for some services and must include at least one photo. Pro’s can make verified reviews a featured project as well. 
Reviews: Reviews are on the service level and do not transfe racross profiles.
Profile strength: This score is dynamic and relative to other pros, so it can go up or down. The score is not visible to customers.
Widgets: Only the Reviews Widget is currently offered.
Photo and videos: These show customers what the pro can do and should only be used for photos that are not for specific featured projects.
Videos: Videos must be uploaded to YouTube or Vimeo to be added to a profile.
Business profiles: There’s no limit to the number of profiles on an account. Pros can add another business profile to keep services that aren’t related on separate profiles. 
Additionally, frontline reps should follow these guidelines when helping pros with their profile: 
Do tell the pro to pay extra attention to their profile photo, business name, review rating, and Introduction since these are the first parts of the profile the customer sees.
Do encourage pros to be detailed in their profile and add examples. This adds another layer of trust when a customer is checking out a profile.
Don't write the pro's introduction for them. Support reps can give tips, but they need to do the writing themselves.
Do encourage pros to use their introduction section to stand out from the competition.
Do encourage pros to keep their Introduction short and add other details to their Questions and Answers section.
Do explain how customers see the Introduction, to emphasize how important it is.
Don’t use the terms “profile score” or “profile points” with pros when talking about profile strength.
Do tell new pros that before they can meet customers on Thumbtack, they have to fill out their:
Business name
Basic personal information (including birth date and address)
Profile picture
Ask for at least one review
Reps can refer to the internal Onboarding and activation requirements (EMR) (Pro) KA to learn more. 
Profile elements


Service details on the pro’s profile (Displayed services the pro offers)

When a customer finds a pro in search results, they can see a preview of the pro's profile in search results in the Thumbtack customer app. When a customer clicks “View Profile,” they can browse the pro’s full profile. Customers see the pro’s profile photo, business name, star rating, and other details they may have added about their business (like number of employees).
The Services offered section is where pros outline the specifics of their service. And depending on the service, this section looks different (or a pro won't have it at all).
Pros can choose the types of services they offer and the types of customers they work with. This information is important because:
It helps customers choose the right pro for their job (so pros want to make sure this is completely filled out)
It's how Thumbtack determines what jobs are relevant to pros who don't set preferences 
Pro’s can look themselves up in search results with the search results tool. This shows the pro what customers see before they contact them, where they rank, and the other pros in their market. Keep in mind, if the pro is in in a highly competitive area with lots of pros, they might not see their profile. Reps can refer to the internal Search Results and Rank KA to learn more. 

[Image: rtaImage]

Business details info (basic business details: contact info, address, etc.)
When a pro sets up their profile, they tell Thumbtack things like their location and other basics about their business. The “Business Info” section is where pros provide those basic business details such as:
Year the business was founded
Number of employees
▶ Business Address
If a pro sets their travel area by distance (targeting preference), their business address is the center of their travel radius. Pros can update their address in the “Business Info” section of their profile. 
Pros may notice that the zip code, address, or city displayed on their profile is incorrect.Frontline reps can help pros by following the “Correcting incorrect zip code, address, or city” steps in the internal Targeting Preferences KA. 
▶ Phone numberOne thing to note is that the phone number on the profile page and the phone number in notifications are separate. This means that updating one does not update the other.
If a pro needs to update the phone number (or address) on their profile, the pros will go to the business info section of their profile. 
Pro steps (to change address or phone number on profile): How to edit my business profile – Thumbtack Help article. 
If a pro needs to update the phone number they’re receiving text notifications, pros will go to Notification settings and click Edit next to their phone number (located below the text messages section). 
Pro steps (to change phone number for notification): How to update notifications – Thumbtack Help
Website
▶ Payment methods acceptedPros can select which payment methods they accept on their profile under the “Payment methods accepted.” Options include Credit Card, Cash, Venmo, Paypal, Square, Cash App, Check, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Zelle, Samsung Pay, and Stripe. 
▶ Social mediaThe social media section on a pro profile allows them to add their Facebook, Instagram, or Twitter accounts to their profile. Before adding the social media URL the pro must:
Ensure that they copied the shareable link and not the link from a private account dashboard or analytics view.
Remove the extra parameters or redirect routes that Thumbtack cannot recognize (e.g., ?utm_source=, session IDs, or mobile preview links)
From search results, customers can select View profile to see the pro's social media links listed under the pro's Introduction section. The customer may need to select "View all details" to see the links. 
NOTE: Pros cannot include contact information in their business profiles. Any contact information is automatically removed and replaced by asterisks, and the pro is sent an email warning them about future contact avoidance behavior. Reps can refer to Contact Avoidance (Pro) KA to learn more. 
▶ What the business info section looks like
Customer facing view
Pro edit view
Customer facing view image description:  Customer view of a Thumbtack pro profile showing "Overview" with business details and "Payment methods". (Image below is from the Android Pro app)

[Image: AD_4nXcVubA1oRJ2Um8hmfgSRFDCksOz7PGzMy-hmA8e2cDm2t3zSUwQ901py3IVAien1Eif6tVZkXIkbEIQMJf8Vhs2kXj99Pze9G_jRCtGBl7BcEuqjtXVe5ImGa1kZYahB_dnw5eEc7YwX28nMDc-9IDFjJoh]

Pro edit view image description: Thumbtack pro profile showing the "Business info" section where pros can edit details like contact information and payment methods.
[Image: rtaImage]
Business name

Customers see a pro’s business name in search results, when they view a pro’s profile, and when the pro sends them messages. If a business name is not added by the pro, Thumbtack will use their account name. Some pro's profiles will also show "Verified business".
Pro's can update their business name at anytime, but this is not possible once their license is verified or they have a verified business. This is because the licensee and business name on their license must match the information on Thumbtack in order for their license to be verified. This is so customers can trust the "verified" information shown by Thumbtack.
If a pro with a verified business (or license) wants to change their business name, they should submit the  ID Help form. The response time for this process is 2 - 3 business days.
Reps can learn more about verified businesses in the Account Information (Pro) KA and about the ID help process in the ID Help Guide KA.
Credentials

For pros, the “Credentials” section of their profile is where they can take a  background check, add or update any professional or occupational licenses they may have, and a certification of insurance (COI). This helps pros build credibility and trust with customers, and it gives them the opportunity to showcase their training and credentials.
NOTE: Insurance credentials are not variable to customers at this time. See Insurance Credentials (Pro) to learn more.
For customers, the "Credentials" section of a pro's profile allows customers to view a pro's background check and license badges, showing that the pro has completed a background check and has a professional or occupational license. 

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ Background check
Pro’s don’t need a social security number (SSN) to take a BGC. Pro’s can only enter the SSN-less flow through their profile. 
If the pro passes the BGC, a badge will be automatically added to their profile so customers can see that they’ve completed and passed the check.
Reps can refer to the Background Checks (Pro) KA to learn more.
▶ Licenses
Pros can display up to two license on their profile.

Introduction (business description) guidelines + tips 
The introduction is a free-form section of the pro’s profile, which gives pros the creative space to highlight themselves however is best for them. 
Their introduction should share details about their business and why customers should hire them. Here are some tips pro’s can use when writing their introduction:
Say some kind of hello.
Point out the details that make them different from other services (like if the pro has worked in their field for a long time, or has any specialties).
If the pro loves what they do, say so! Passion is a powerful thing.
Answer the questions customers commonly ask them.
Invite the customer to reach out to learn more about working with them.
Pros only have the customer’s attention for a few sentences, so the Introduction should propel the customer to keep reading or to contact the pro for the next steps.
When a customer clicks on a pro’s profile, they’ll see the pro’s Introduction under the pro's profile photo and business name.  The pros introduction section may be called “about this pro.” 
Pro steps: Pro can update the business introduction section of their Thumbtack profile by following the “How to update your profile” on the How to edit my business profile – Thumbtack Help article.  Pros can also refer to the How to improve my profile – Thumbtack Help guide. 
 A few reminders to frontline reps when helping a pro with their introduction: 
Don't write the pro's introduction for them. Support reps can give tips, but they need to do the writing themselves.
Do encourage pros to use this section to stand out from the competition.
Do encourage pros to keep their Introduction short and add other details to their Questions and Answers section.
Do explain how customers see the Introduction, to emphasize how important it is.

Profile photo guidelines + tips
A pro’s profile photo is the first photo customers see in search results. Here are a few tips for a great profile photo: 
Their photo should give customers a glimpse of them (or their team) so they know who they’d be working with. 
A smiling photo gives the customer a positive first impression and helps the pro connect with the customer. 
For lighting, it’s best to use natural lighting. Try taking the photo outside or standing near a window.
For best quality, profile photos should be square and 400x400 pixels.

Profile photos are shared across profiles (e.g., if a pro has 2 service profiles under 1 account, both profiles will show the same profile photos).

Profile strength: How pros can level up their profile 
A pro’s profile strength tracks improvements to their profile and gives actionable tips. The score is dynamic and relative to other pros, so it could go up or down as a pro's market changes. As the pro completes more of the suggested items, their profile strength will go up.
Their profile strength is only visible to the pro and not to customers. Following the tips will help pros stay more competitive in their market. 
Pro’s will see one of four strengths: 
Needs Work: Pros will start here. They should focus on adding photos, getting reviews, and writing a good introduction first.
Good Start : After pros have the basics, coach them on things like adding their license or completing a background check.
Looking Good: When pros reach this level, it’s time for them to fill out their profile even more by adding things like featured projects.
Super Strong: This is the final level where pros can polish their profile by adding things like payment methods or social media links.

(Rep) Steps: How to coach pro on their profile media
Frontline reps can help a pro improve their profile by giving them tips on their profile (media (photos and videos). 
For example, reps can check to see if the pro has uploaded relevant media. This could look like actors or entertainers adding videos of their performances, and wedding planners could add photos of their events.
To do so, reps will follow these steps: 
First, internally review the pro's current media. When reviewing the pro’s photos and videos, ask yourself these questions to identify areas for improvement:
Does it sell the customer on hiring them?
If you were the customer, would you hire the pro based on their media content?
Is it good quality and professional?
Is it competitive with what pros with similar services have uploaded?
Then, use these coaching points to help the pro. Based on your review, encourage the pro to do the following:
Have a picture of themselves, their team, or their logo. It helps customers feel more comfortable hiring the pro and makes the business feel more personal.
Show their experience instead of just telling. Pictures, especially before-and-after photos, show customers what pros can do.
Upload relevant media. For example, house cleaners could add before and after photos of their cleaning jobs, and entertainers like musicians or costumed characters can upload videos of their performances. 
Add captions to tell their story whenever they can. This helps customers understand the photo and why it was included.

Steps: How to troubleshoot social media links on pro profile (Rep)
If a pro reports being unable to add a social media link to their profile, it may not be a bug. Often, the problem is with the format of the link.
Common Causes:
The pro copied a non-shareable link (e.g., from a private account dashboard or analytics view instead of their public profile).
The link contains extra parameters or redirect routes that Thumbtack cannot recognize (e.g., ?utm_source=, session IDs, or mobile preview links).
▶ Rep talking point: Why do I need to update my social media link in order to save it to my profile?
If a pro asks why they need to edit the social media link in order to save it, frontline reps can explain:
"When you use the 'Share' button in an app like Instagram, or copy a link from Facebook, it often adds extra text to the URL. This can be tracking codes (like ?igsh=...) after your username, or extra words (like /people/) after the '.com'. These are used by the social media apps for their own analytics.
Our system, however, is built to recognize only the direct, clean URL for your profile (like facebook.com/Username). This extra text prevents our system from recognizing the link. You just need to delete those extra parts to get the clean link, and it should save correctly.”
Troubleshooting Steps:
Ask the pro to confirm that they’re using the direct, public URL to their social media profile.
If they haven’t or aren’t sure, explain that they should remove any string of numbers, letters or symbols after “.com” and after their username. 
Without removing them from the URL, pros will see an error: “Invalid Facebook URL,” “Invalid Twitter URL.,” or “Invalid Instagram URL.” 
See examples of what accepted links look like below. 
If the link includes extra text or parameters, have the pro remove everything after the main profile URL, excluding their username. See examples below.
Ask the pro to paste the cleaned-up link into the social media field on their Thumbtack profile and try saving again.
If issues persist, reps should test the link in a browser while logged out of the social media website to ensure it’s accessible publicly.
Example links
Facebook
✅ Accepted format: https://www.facebook.com/Username 
❌ Not accepted: https://www.facebook.com/people/Username/3367884412864/ 
Instagram 
✅ Accepted format:https://www.instagram.com/Username   
❌ Not accepted: https://www.instagram.com/Username?igsh=eHlpnmc4NzE4PGhu  
The bold text in the "Not accepted" links above highlights the text or parameters that must be removed for the link to be saved on their Thumbtack profile.

Spanish
How are the service details in my profile different from my targeting preferences?
¿En qué se diferencian los detalles del servicio en mi perfil de mis preferencias de enfoque?
Your profile shows details about your business that don’t usually change much, like location and information about the type of work you do. By setting targeting preferences, you can target the right jobs based on more specific factors — like how far you’ll travel to meet customers, or how large of an event you’ll cater. Your service details and targeting preferences will vary depending on the type of business you have.
Su perfil muestra detalles sobre su empresa que generalmente no cambian mucho, como la ubicación y la información sobre el tipo de trabajo que realiza. Al establecer las preferencias de enfoque, puede enfocarse en los trabajos adecuados en función de factores más específicos, como la distancia que viajará para conocer a los clientes o la magnitud de un evento que ofrecerá. Los detalles de su servicio y las preferencias de enfoque variarán según el tipo de negocio que tenga.
Business name
Frontline reps can use these talking points to guide conversations with pros about their business name on their profiles.

English
Spanish
Why can’t I change my business name on my profile? It’s blocked out.
¿Por qué no puedo modificar el nombre de mi empresa en mi perfil? Aparece bloqueado.
Once your business license is verified, you can't edit your business name. That's so customers can trust the information we show as “verified.” If you’d like to update your business name, fill out the form at ID Help Intake Form.
Una vez verificada su licencia comercial, no es posible editar el nombre de su empresa. Esto garantiza que los clientes confíen en la información que se muestra como "verificada". Si desea actualizar el nombre de su empresa, complete el formulario en el Formulario de admisión de ayuda de identificación.
 Customer view
Frontline reps can use these talking points to guide conversations with pros about how customers see their Thumbtack profile. 

English
Spanish
Can I see what my profile looks like to customers?
¿Puedo ver cómo ven mi perfil los clientes?
Yes. When you’re editing your profile, click View as customer. It’s a good idea to check it from time to time to make sure it looks right. Keep in mind we may vary how we show your profile to customers. Customers will also see a snapshot of your profile from search results. In the app, customers see your profile photo, business name, star rating, and other details you may have added about your business (like pricing or number of employees).
Sí. Cuando esté editando su perfil, seleccione “View as Customer” (Ver como cliente). Es una buena idea revisarlo de vez en cuando para asegurarse de que se vea bien. Tome en cuenta que podemos variar la forma en que mostramos su perfil a los clientes. Los clientes también verán un resumen de su perfil en los resultados de búsqueda. En la aplicación, los clientes ven la foto de su perfil, el nombre de la empresa, la calificación de estrellas y otros detalles que puede haber agregado sobre su empresa (como el precio o la cantidad de empleados).
How does my profile help the right customers find me?
¿Cómo ayuda mi perfil a que los clientes adecuados me encuentren?
When you set up your profile, you tell us things like your location and other basics about your business — things that won’t change day to day. We use this information to make sure your business shows up in the right market and for the right customers.
Cuando configura su perfil, nos dice cosas como su ubicación y otros aspectos básicos sobre su negocio, cosas que no cambiarán día a día. Usamos esta información para asegurarnos de que su negocio aparezca en el mercado adecuado y para los clientes adecuados.
Featured projects
Frontline reps can use these talking points to guide conversations with pros about the featured projects in their profiles.


English
Spanish
I noticed featured projects on my profile. What is this?
Noté proyectos destacados en mi perfil. ¿Qué es esto?
Pros told us they wanted a better way to feature their past work. Now, you can add details about a job you’ve completed to your profile.
And if you’ve gotten a review from a Thumbtack customer, you can turn their review into a featured project, too.
Los profesionales nos dijeron que querían una mejor manera de presentar su trabajo pasado. Ahora puede agregar detalles sobre un trabajo que ha completado a su perfil.

Si ha recibido una evaluación de un cliente de Thumbtack también puede convertir su evaluación en un proyecto destacado.
Why can't I add featured projects for all my services?
¿Por qué no puedo agregar proyectos destacados para todos mis servicios?
Featured projects are only available for certain services (where we felt it made the most sense and added a lot of value). We may add featured projects to more services. I'm happy to pass on your feedback on which services you'd like to see featured projects for.
Los proyectos destacados solo están disponibles para ciertos servicios (donde sentimos que tenía más sentido y agregaba mucho valor). Podemos agregar proyectos destacados a más servicios y me complace compartir sus comentarios sobre los servicios que le gustaría ver los proyectos destacados.
Can I still add to the Photos and Videos section of my profile now that I have Featured Projects?
¿Puedo añadir a la sección Fotos y vídeos de mi perfil ahora que tengo proyectos destacados?
Yes. You can continue to add photos and videos like normal, but you don’t need to add photos to both places. Your photos and videos section should be used for photos that aren’t for specific featured projects.
Sí. Puede continuar agregando fotos y vídeos como normal, pero

Product Feedback (Rep)

Process

Resources
1. Overview
▶ 🤖Background notes
[AI Context]: This article provides Frontline Reps with a comprehensive guide to submitting product feedback from pros and customers using Salesforce Feedback in Salesforce. It covers the importance of feedback, best practices for submission, and the process for how that feedback is used by Thumbtack's Product teams.
Frontline Reps collect feedback from pros and customers about their experience using Thumbtack’s. This feedback is important because it helps improve how Thumbtack serves users. All feedback is submitted through Salesforce Feedback in Salesforce.
Salesforce Feedback, helps Frontline Reps share feedback with Thumbtack’s Product teams quicky and easy. It also helps track feedback submitted by a specific pro or customer, including the feedback’s current status.
How Feedback Shapes the Thumbtack Platform
Collecting feedback from pros and customers is crucial for improving Thumbtack and guiding the product roadmap.
Thumbtack makes strategic changes to the platform, each aimed at improving the user experience. Feedback helps us understand the pro and customer experience, which drives the product roadmap and influences action. 
It's more than just numbers — it's about how pros and customers feel about a change. These changes could be small (like a color scheme) or larger (like how the budget works).
Any feedback is valuable, even if it's positive. Positive feedback could include what users are happy with, what features they love, or product updates that have improved their experience.
Other feedback could point to product areas that need improvement, such as new categories, user wish lists, or suggestions for overall process enhancements.
Frontline Reps play a key role in capturing feedback and ensuring it reaches the appropriate teams for action.
Do’s and don'ts of Submitting Feedback
In this section, Frontline Reps will find a list of important do’s and don’ts for submitting product feedback. Following these guidelines ensures that feedback is detailed, actionable, and valuable for Thumbtack's Product Operations team.
To ensure all submitted reports are detailed and effective, Frontline Reps can follow these guidelines:
Do:
Submit detailed and actionable feedback. 
Quality feedback allows the Product Ops team to address the root cause. Include specific details such as:
User type (pro or customer)
Lead type
Reason for feedback
Blockers
Costs
Other relevant details 
This additional information will gives the Product Ops team a starting point and allows them to make more effective changes in the future. However, don’t submit feedback if there’s no feedback from the user. See the Quality feedback best practices section in this KA below for more info and feedback examples.
Capture user feedback verbatim.
Feedback should be specific to the user. Capture the user's feedback word-for-word. This will provide valuable insight into how the feedback impacts them, help our teams prioritize and act on the feedback, and capture additional feedback not currently mentioned in existing reports.
See the Quality feedback best practices section in this KA below for guiding questions.
Use keyword search to check for existing feedback.
Before adding a new feedback item, search for existing feedback using keywords. This ensures duplicate feedback isn’t being submitted on separate reports.
See the How to submit feedback section in this KA below for steps.
Carefully read an existing feedback item’s description.
Before adding feedback to an existing report, carefully read the description of the feedback item. This ensures an accurate count of reports per item.
Submit one report per feedback item.
Submit one item per feedback report, even if the feedback is from the same pro or customer. Doing so allows us to correctly gauge volume, identify patterns, and follow the progress of the different feedback. Grouped feedback may get lost or overlooked. 
Respond to Product Ops within 48 hours.
If Product Ops has questions about your report when triaging the feedback, you should respond within 48 hours to avoid delays.
Submit all feedback reports, even positive feedback.
Don’t submit multiple feedback items on single report. Any feedback is valuable feedback, even if it's positive. This can include what they're happy with, what features they love, recent product updates that have improved their experience, and so on.
Check for Duplicate Feedback Reports
Frontline Reps should always check for duplicate feedback reports to ensure accuracy of feedback items.
Submit user feedback in the feedback flow.
Don’t submit potential bugs using the feedback flow. The feedback flow should only be used for submitting feedback. If the user encounters unexpected platform behaviors (errors, lags, etc), you should investigate/troubleshoot the issue, and submit a bug report if necessary. Reps can refer to the internal Basic Troubleshooting KA and Bugs KA to learn more.
Don’t:
Don’t submit a feedback report if there’s no feedback
Frontline Reps should not submit a feedback report if there’s no feedback from the user.
Unexpected app behaviors as feedback; investigate and report to the correct channel: bug or feedback
Frontline Reps should not submit feedback for reports wherein the app is not working as intended (errors, lags, etc.) as it could be a bug that needs immediate attention. 
Don’t copy and paste
Frontline Reps should avoid copy-pasting the feedback item name or description to the feedback report details field, as we want to be as verbatim as possible.
Don’t submit multiple feedback per report
Frontline Reps should submit one feedback report per feedback to ensure accuracy of feedback items.
Processing and Utilizing User Feedback

After a Frontline Rep submits a feedback report, the Product Ops team reviews, categorizes, and uses the feedback to help prioritize improvements to the Thumbtack platform.
Product Ops uses feedback to:
Help prioritize the product roadmap
Guide feedback roundtable discussions
Improve the user experience to attract, engage, and retain our pros and customers
After a Frontline Rep submits feedback, it's sent to the Product Ops team. They will review, categorize, and classify it. If it's new feedback, they will create a theme for it. If it falls under an existing theme, they will add the rep’s submission to that theme. 
The Product Ops team monitors feedback and themes, reviewing how often it has been reported, how frequently it comes up, how easy it is to implement, the impact it has on users, and other factors to prioritize the feedback. They work closely with the product teams to get the highest priority feedback added to the product roadmap and, in turn, improve our platform.
When to Submit a Feedback Report
A Frontline Rep should submit a feedback report when they receive comments about the Thumbtack platform or have suggestions for internal policies, processes, and tools.
Feedback should be submitted for the following reasons:
Feedback about Thumbtack from pros and customers
When Frontline Rep hears of a product experience that should be changed or improved to better support our pros’ and customers’ needs
Feedback from Frontline reps about Thumbtack policy, process and tools. (not related to a specific pro or customer)

NOTE: Frontline Reps should make sure to submit both positive and negative feedback.
Navigating the Salesforce Feedback Report Layout

Salesforce feedback has been structured to make it efficient for Frontline Reps to quickly search and submit feedback. Depending on how Frontline Reps use Salesforce, they will access the form under the Feedback Report tab under Cases, Contacts, Maintain Records, Opportunities, and Work Tickets. Here are a few things to keep in mind when submitting any feedback.
Feedback title taxonomy
Once feedback is submitted, Product Ops will review, classify, and name the feedback. To make locating existing feedback quick and easy, Product Ops will name the feedback. 

Feedback titles are in the following format: 
[Product area] + detailed feedback sentence that includes user type

Example
[Booking form] Pro requires square footage information to define pricing

Below is a breakdown of what each means: 
Product area: If the feedback can be clearly mapped to a specific product, Product Ops will add a product area label . If not, this label will not be added. 
Detailed feedback sentence: This is a detailed summary of the feedback. See feedback examples and feedback best practices.  
Feedback report fields

When submitting a feedback report, Frontline Reps will complete the following fields in the Salesforce Feedback form:
Agent Sense of Urgency - Select the urgency of your feedback. See the table below to identify the urgency. 
Job Category - Add the job category for your feedback.
NOTE: There should always be a category tied to the account, this is still added as input even if the feedback is not category-specific as we want to identify pros in which categories appear to be impacted.
For feedback on new category, 'new job category' option can be selected from the drop down menu.
Feedback Details - Add any details that will help the Product Ops team understand the feedback better. Follow feedback best practices to leave quality feedback. 
NOTE: More info is better. Check out the following sections for more resources: Do’s and don’ts and feedback examples. 

[Image: Khw1fI5CPaCGm0Ht9_bzLKor2zNtGLCY5trBjPCxOXDxkpGTR8V1nXHMBw7L4yqLuvpvcCe2zONmdWg0zUUtb1dnJizTHXAyCCQWyQQRffkh-PYULI2jMobUKKSLnJVVLlPpaZryEbuCR_HtnQ-KGrU]

Image description: A screenshot of the 'Feedback Report' form in Salesforce. It shows the 'Feedback Report Flow'. It contains three required fields: a dropdown for 'Agent Sense of Urgency', a dropdown for 'Job Category', and a text box for 'Feedback Details'.
Agents' sense of urgency: Assessing feedback urgency levels
When Frontline Reps submit a feedback report, they must select an urgency level to help Thumbtack prioritize the issue.
Although the pro or customer may feel that their issue is urgent, Thumbtack rates urgency from Thumbtack's viewpoint.

Urgency Level
Definition
High
Instances that require our utmost priority and may put the business at risk.
These include process roadblocks or challenges, and issues that have damaging effects on our business operations or cause many users to leave our platform. 
This can include things like TToD payment issues, or Instant Book leads where the pros' lead price is above the job cost estimate shown to the customer.
Medium
Instances where the product is working as intended but causes minor inconveniences, or instances that slow the completion of certain actions but do not block our business operations.
This can include things like targeting geo preferences, profile updates, lead or project management, etc. 
Category improvements are also deemed medium urgency unless supported by extremely high feedback volume/revenue impact.
Low
Instances that do not block or slow down the overall flow of business operations nor impact the user experience in a negative way. 
This can include ideas for new categories, user wish lists, positive user feedback, or general process improvement recommendations.
How to Write Impactful Product Feedback  
Writing actionable and specific feedback reports helps the Product Ops team act on feedback quickly. Frontline Reps can use these best practices to improve the quality of their submissions.
For Frontline Reps, the key to leaving quality feedback is to make it actionable, specific, and solution-focused. Providing specific details helps the Product team understand the "why" behind the feedback, which allows them to identify trends and solutions faster. 
Submitting feedback on existing reports, when applicable, is also a best practice that helps teams prioritize issues affecting a large number of users.

To ensure feedback is high quality, Frontline Reps should include the following information in the Feedback Details field:
Who is being affected – Pro or Customer
What is the user's sentiment – How the customer or pro felt when they contacted support.
What is the core issue – What issue does the customer or pro have with the product? (E.g., Pro understands how to set a weekly spend limit but is not sure why it's required to move forward). 
What is causing the issue - Describe the specific product behavior or missing information that is creating the problem for the user.
What is the projected impact of the issue if no product improvement is made (why it's important) – What actions has the customer or pro taken due to the issue? Have they stopped quoting? Have they lowered their weekly spending limit?
Possible solutions or suggestions – Detail what the customer or pro thinks Thumbtack can do to improve the experience, or what product improvements they would like to see.
NOTE:​​​​​​ ​​More information is always better. For example, instead of saying pricing is too expensive, explain how and why by including the actual costs of jobs and leads, etc. This additional info will give us a starting point and allow us to make more effective changes to lead prices. Err on the side of too detailed.
Feedback examples
The following examples show Frontline Reps how to turn vague feedback into actionable, high-quality submissions.
✍  
Could be better
Better
Love it
Example 1
Went over how the weekly spend limit works.
Pro wanted to know average price of contacts to set an appropriate budget
HC & Commercial cleaner had set a weekly spend limit but was confused why they kept seeing the pop-up "Pay and Send" when trying to send quotes. Wasn't clear to the pro that they still needed to add a credit card on file. Pro wanted to know average price of leads to set an appropriate spending limit. Will add card next week when they have money.
Example 2
Pro is confused about setting up a custom spend limit
Pro understands how to set a weekly spend limit, but is not sure why it's required to move forward and quote and wants to know if he is still able to pay as you go and quote?
Pro understands how to set a weekly spend limit, but is not sure why it's required to move forward and quote and wants to know if he is still able to pay-as-you-go. Pro has stopped responding to leads until he receives an answer.
2. Process
Submitting and tracking feedback follows a clear, structured process within Salesforce. Frontline Reps can use the following steps to ensure feedback is recorded correctly and its status can be monitored.
Where to submit feedback
All pro and customer feedback will be submitted using Salesforce Feedback in Salesforce. The entry points for submitting feedback vary depending on which Salesforce app a Frontline Rep uses. 
Feedback entry points are found on the following Salesforce pages: Case, Contact, Opportunity, Work Tickets, and Maintain (for Intercept users). See the images below for a visual of each entry point. 
NOTE: If a Frontline Rep does not have Salesforce access to submit feedback, they can use the Thumbtack Product Feedback Form to share their feedback. 
▶ Case

Steps: How to submit customer and pro feedback (Rep)
Before a Frontline Rep submits a new report, they should check if the feedback has already been reported. To search for existing feedback items, follow these steps: 
From the feedback entry point, click on the “Feedback Report” tab.
Searching for feedback using Salesforce's main search bar can produce feedback that is outdated or used by other teams. Be sure to only search for feedback from within the “Feedback Report” tab to make sure you are seeing current feedback.
NOTE:​​ Be sure to open the “Feedback Report” tab from within the case, work ticket, or account of the user who provides the feedback because it will automatically be attached to that user.  
For ease of searching, type general keyword search terms like travel preferences, pro or customer, or the name of the product area.
Click "Search Feedback."

[Image: AD_4nXeO5L9QZmXZWAvtiWXQZOaZ5dlEZwR8YMAAAw6aQrW8AqL6FylZa6z62cfUcfVKOkH5oCoL06lm6UBJv04Lyros_RdiDRp2zy8QKzKRn25LGgVt-l_8NfpXs2BpAQ_JZm4euJsF0yE8Vhh9bwZ2Ird2Tus]

Review the feedback search results.
If an existing feedback item appears to match, click the item's name to review the details. 

[Image: AD_4nXeodA2l9QiwNM1qvR-Sd4V45ozCMowkht73eH-pAQzRm4VULxalljN0UDfU4NeikKkIA2AaGIhIOla5r0Qr-_0cTIdxYZqKTPoS2EXNI_M9NPDckK3aq0olC73SBV7kfN3VcKS8wOtpRFtZkt1kcuMHX00]

If the feedback matches, click the blue “+”to add the report under the existing feedback.
If no existing feedback matches, submit new feedback by clicking the “Feedback not found? Create New”  button.

[Image: AD_4nXcXU_m-hyH_VLpp30dbtKwdJm8ORgG_e1QmLimUW-Lxz7ys0E1ch0b_ol4v7cOZNOR2N-0GkPNTcZYHaPYVd3gPDyLFhX7foYO0FJS4qsTfinPbKtmOGWRN_E3p2fP1HwdbAyJEBbdfHsXeJCMdPQCZRww]

Once it is determined if the feedback is new or existing, fill out the required fields. 
Agent Sense of Urgency - Select the urgency of the feedback.
This field is optional when adding to an existing feedback item.
Job Category - Add the job category for the feedback. 
NOTE: There should always be a category tied to the account; this is still added as input even though the feedback is not category-specific, as the Product Ops team wants to identify pros in which categories appear to be impacted.  
For feedback on a new category, 'new job category' option can be selected from the drop-down menu
Feedback Details - Add any details that will help the Product Ops team understand the feedback better. Follow feedback best practices to leave quality feedback. 
NOTE: More info is better. For example, instead of saying pricing is too expensive, tell us how orwhy. Include actual costs of jobs and leads, etc. Having this additional info will give us a starting point and allow us to make more effective changes to lead prices. Err on the side of being too detailed.
If adding existing feedback (you clicked the '+'), this section is required; add additional details to add clarifications and/or have information not yet mentioned in the main description..

[Image: AD_4nXckMq-M3cUFdya_vM7SmiNL0URdK5rknsBA4ilOWhm8rDbS595QPsmTqP6KiUMhyr9boKfKHgu7VOCRAwPini64t1CS4c4JDOx0DXG7XRT1NQuOWbDYh8HMznEycCXiP0Eb8njNyJcZuDmxCdQxYYIGYIvW]

Click the Next button to finalize and submit the report. 
NOTE: If a user gives a Frontline Rep more than one piece of feedback, submit separate feedback for each item, which will allow the Product Ops team to correctly gauge volume, identify patterns, and follow the progress of the other feedback items. Grouped feedback can easily get lost or overlooked.
For feedback and questions about the Salesforce Feedback experience, post in the #product_ops Slack channel. 
Steps: How to check feedback statuses (Rep)
To check the status of a submitted feedback report, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:
Navigate to the feedback report and click on it to view its details.
In the Associated Feedback field, click the link to open the feedback ticket.

[Image: Click to enlarge]

Review the Chatter section on the right-hand side of the ticket for any status updates from the Product Ops team.

[Image: AD_4nXfQFbZw0e0LEkTk47DNIOSNPvMcHR42x8ulspIcN1EYi6JHYzJcepdQWy8M2V1rKAz-KKtqtNWSWIqom5XH8WtjNjVUjxUv-RL837QYLmENE4TsgE_eRU81wVS7SYNUYD9LSJiFesWj4cTQWpuxpqiMWLgy]


NOTE:​​​​ The chatter field is only for asking about the status of that specific feedback item, not for general product questions. Reps should be aware that responses in this feed may not be immediate.
Steps: How to submit internal feedback (Rep)
Internal feedback is submitted through case taxonomy under “internal”  and not through the usual feedback process. Frontline reps can choose between Process, Policy, or Tools when submitting this type of feedback.

NOTE: Internal feedback can be submitted on any open case, even if it’s unrelated.
3. Talking points
This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros and customers about their feedback. Use these talking points to ensure consistent and accurate messaging.

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Thank you for helping us find issues on our site and how we can make Thumbtack better for our customers and pros. I have shared your comments with our product team to review as they work on improvements. 
Le agradecemos por ayudarnos a encontrar problemas en nuestro sitio y por indicarnos cómo podemos mejorar Thumbtack para nuestros clientes y profesionales. He compartido sus comentarios con nuestro equipo de producto para que los revisen mientras trabajan en las mejoras.

Pro Rewards Bonus Points (Pro) (Experiment)

Contents
Overview
Experiment details
Pro experience
Process
Steps: How to verify experiment variant and eligibility (Rep)
Steps: How to verify push notification eligibility (Rep)
Talking points

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) provides Frontline Reps with information about the Pro Rewards Bonus Points experiment for new pros. It explains how new pros earn points for successful behaviors, identifies the differences between experiment variants, and provides instructions for reps to identify and help impacted pros.
What
Starting April 27, 2026, Thumbtack will launch an experiment that gives newer pros additional pro rewards, including bonus points. These new milestone rewards are to incentivize new pros to take action that will set them up for success.
This experiment has two variants.
Variant 1: Earns points
Variant 2: Earns points and a lead credit
Why
Thumbtack is running this experiment to help new pros learn the best ways to succeed on the platform. The goal is to increase the number of pros who stay on Thumbtack by rewarding actions that lead to more hires.
How
Pros in the experiment see special notifications in the app and receive emails about the new ways pros can earn reward points. These new milestone rewards include: 
Getting 5+ reviews
Responding to their first five leads within 60 minutes
Turning on push notifications.
Experiment details

This section lists the specific dates, impacted users, and variant types for the Pro Rewards Bonus Points experiment.
Launch date: April 29, 2026
Anticipated end date: 4–8 weeks after launch
Important Note: This is a target date. Experiment timelines are fluid and may change based on results.
Impacted users:  All newer pros (App and desktop)
How to identify pros in the experiment
Frontline reps can identify pros in this experiment by checking the Experiment assignments section in Admin. Reps should search for the experiment name: Pro Rewards Bonus Points.
The Bucket column in Admin identifies the specific group:
Baseline or blank: Pro is not in the experiment.
Variant 1: Pro earns bonus points for actions.
Variant 2: Pro earns bonus points and a $25 lead credit added to their balance. 
Feedback Theme Tagging: Reps should use the feedback item:
[Experiment][Pro Rewards] Feedback on bonus points/credit for 30-day milestones.
Pro experience

This section compares the standard Pro Rewards program to the experience for pros in the bonus points experiment.
Baseline pro rewards experience
Response points: Pros earn 100 points per lead or opportunity response.
Review points: Pros earn points based on the total number of reviews from the last 12 months.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Image description: A screenshot of a pro's account interface displaying the "Your path to Top Pro" and "Business info" sections. The top section features a progress tracker UI showing the pro's current status tier, along with primary buttons to see their rank and view their profile as a customer. The bottom "Business info" section includes an "Edit" link and structured data fields containing the pro's contact and company details, specifically their phone number field, website URL, physical address, year founded, and number of employees.  
To learn more, reps can refer to the internal Thumbtack Pro Rewards (Pro) KA. 
Pro rewards bonus points experience
Variant 1
This experience applies to pros who are part of the experiment. They receive the following bonus points and incentives on top of the Baseline experience:
Review points: Pros earn extra points for reaching the 5-review milestone.
New pros: Awarded once reaching 5+ reviews within their first 30 days
Existing pros: Awarded once reaching 5+ reviews within 30 days from experiment launch
Bonus points awarded: 200
Response points: Pros earn extra points for responding to the first five leads within 60 minutes.
New pros: Awarded for responding within 1 hour to the first 3 leads within the first 30 days
Existing pros: Awarded for responding within 1 hour to the first 3 leads within 30 days from the experiment launch
Bonus points awarded: 200
Engagement Points: Pros earn points for turning on push notifications.
New Pros: Awarded if push notifications remain enabled per each Pro Rewards period
Internal note: To earn these points, the pro must enable notifications at the device level (iOS or Android system settings). This happens when the pro selects "Allow" in the system pop-up during app installation, or manually turns on notifications for the "Thumbtack for Pros" app in their phone's settings menu.
Existing Pros: Awarded if push notifications remain enabled per each Pro Rewards period
Bonus Points awarded: 100
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Image description: A screenshot from a pro’s mobile app interface detailing their progress in the rewards program. The top section, titled "Your Pro Rewards progress," features a visual progress bar displaying four status tier badges and a link to view details. Below this is a section titled "Earn rewards points faster" which lists specific actionable tasks—such as enabling push notifications, gathering reviews, and responding quickly to leads—alongside their potential bonus point values. The bottom portion of the screen displays three expandable accordions for different tier levels (e.g., Silver, Gold, Platinum). One accordion is expanded, revealing tabs for requirements and rewards. Under the requirements tab, distinct line items show progress for points earned, star rating status, and profile photo completion using numerical fields or green checkmark icons.
Internal note: Bonus points do not roll over across pro rewards periods or quarters, and this offer does not reset. 
Variant 2
Pros in Variant 2 receive all the bonus points and incentives offered in Variant 1, plus a $25 lead credit added to their Thumbtack balance.
2. Process

Steps: How to verify experiment variant and eligibility (Rep)
Frontline Reps must follow these steps to see if a pro is in the experiment and if the pro met the goals:
Open the pro account in Admin.
Scroll down to the Experiment assignments section.
Search for "Pro Rewards Bonus Points" to find the bucket (Variant 1 or 2).
Once the experiment variant is verified:
Check the Reviews Received section in Admin to see if the pro reached 5 reviews.
To see the pro's exact Response time, log in as the pro and check the competition insights.
Ask the pro what kind of push notifications they have enabled.
Steps: How to verify push notification eligibility (Rep)
Ask the pro if they have the Thumbtack for Pros app installed.
If they don’t have it installed, ask them to download the app and select “Allow” when asked to confirm push notifications.
Ask the pro to check their phone's system settings (not the Thumbtack app settings).
iOS: Settings > Notifications > Thumbtack for Pros > Ensure "Allow Notifications" is toggled ON.
Android: Settings > Apps > Thumbtack for Pros > Notifications > Ensure "Show notifications" is toggled ON.
3. Talking points

This section provides approved messages for Frontline Reps to use when talking to pros about bonus points.

English talking point
Spanish talking point
Q: Why should I care about bonus points?
Q: ¿Por qué deberían importarme los puntos de bonificación?
A: These bonus points help you reach a higher rewards tier faster. Reaching a higher tier unlocks badges and perks that can help you grow your business on Thumbtack.
A: Estos puntos de bonificación le ayudan a alcanzar un nivel de recompensas más alto con mayor rapidez. Alcanzar un nivel más alto desbloquea insignias y beneficios que pueden ayudarle a hacer crecer su negocio en Thumbtack.
Q: When will the $25 credit appear on my account? (Variant 2 only)
Q: ¿Cuándo aparecerá el crédito de $25 en mi cuenta? (Solo variante 2)
A: Thumbtack tracks your progress for 30 days, and credits are added once the qualification period ends. 

Internal note: For new pros, this is 30 days from sign-up; for existing pros, this is 30 days from the date of the experiment launch.
A: Thumbtack realiza un seguimiento de su progreso durante 30 días y los créditos se agregan una vez que finaliza el periodo de calificación.

Internal note: For new pros, this is 30 days from sign-up; for existing pros, this is 30 days from the date of the experiment launch.

This section contains links to other articles that help reps understand the Pro Rewards program.

What's changing
