1. Overview
Pros can post their prices (known internally as quote sheets) for their services. Depending on the type of service, a pro will have different options for adding their prices to Thumbtack. Pros can post their pricing with or without targeting on.
Thumbtack adds automated default prices to help new pros understand better where to start. Pro’s should add their own pricing, since they know their business best. 
Pros should always enter prices that reflect their typical rates to set accurate expectations, keeping in mind that all prices are estimates and can be adjusted based on specific job details. 
Pros have the flexibility to hide or update their prices at any time. 
Pros can learn about pricing their services by referring to the  How to price my services – Thumbtack Help article.   
Important updates
Customers not longer see pro pricing
Starting August 10, 2026, customers will no longer see a pro’s pricing on Thumbtack. See Pricing areas that have been removed section below. 
What is changing:
Remove all upfront customer-facing pricing (powered by pro quote sheets) in the customer experience. This does not include aggregate pricing banners. 
All CHX flows on native that haven’t been converted to NCX will continue to show pricing (All entry points except for the search box and search tab are still CHX)
What’s not changing: 
Pro-side pricing settings — pros can still set, update, and hide prices normally 
Plan tab (cost estimates): Customers see project-level cost estimates on the Plan tab and within the Project Details page (“Your project” tab). Plan tab cost estimates are unrelated to pro-specific quote sheet pricing. 
Pricing on near-me SEO landing pages. (E.g., https://www.thumbtack.com/k/handyman/near-me) 
▶ Customers can see pro pricing in the messenger after contacting the pro.[Image: rtaImage]
There is no direct change to ranking (e.g.,  posting prices still helps a pros ranking in search results). 
Thumbtack doesn't refund leads where the customer is asking about the pro’s pricing.
If a pro adds pricing info to their profile's Business FAQs section, that's still visible to any customer who views the profile.
Why Thumbtack is making this change
[Internal Background: We are removing all upfront customer-facing prices powered by pro quote sheets from the user experience. Thumbtack plans to prioritize a new end-to-end NHX solution for customer-facing pricing and price alignment spanning NCX, NDFP, and IC/Post-Contact. Currently, the smarter lead matching (NDFP) architecture does not support our legacy quote sheets, especially for fixed price (FP) and select variable price (VP) categories where quote sheets depend heavily on request for quote answers and legacy targeting preferences.]
Pro-facing why: Thumbtack is updating how pricing appears while customers browse pros. Upfront estimates do not always reflect the full scope of a project. By allowing customers to first consider factors such as experience, reviews, availability, and overall project fit, customers can have a more informed pricing conversation with a pro after sharing the details of their project.
Pricing areas that have been removed
Customers no longer see a pro's pricing in the following areas:
Search results: Pricing summary above filters is hidden. Individual pro pricing (starting price / estimated cost) is hidden for all pros.
Pro profile: Pricing shown in the action card is hidden.
Mismatch gate & mismatch gate SP: When a customer’s request form answers don’t match a pro’s job preferences or availability, they hit the mismatch gate. Pricing is hidden.
Additional pro upsell: After a customer contacts a pro, the APU appears at the end of the request flow encouraging them to reach out to additional pros. Pricing is hidden.
Post Contact Pricing List (PCPL): After submitting a project, customers see a pro list on the Projects tab. Pricing on pro cards is hidden.
Near-me SEO landing pages. (E.g., https://www.thumbtack.com/k/handyman/near-me)
Dos and don'ts: How to help pros with this change: 
DOs:
Let pros know they can explain their pricing in their profile using their Introduction or Q&A section, especially for services requiring in-person estimates.
Advise realistic pricing and remind pros that prices are estimates.
Use the feedback theme [Pricing] User has complaints about the removal of customer facing pricing when a pro has feedback about pricing changes.
If a pro asks whether to keep pricing up to date, use the approved talking points below.
If a pro specifically asks about ranking, be direct: tell them that the changes to pricing visibility do not impact their ranking or search visibility. Do NOT bring this up proactively. (See talking point below)
If speaking with customers about pro pricing refer to the How Thumbtack Works (Customer) KA for talking points.
DON'Ts:
Don't tell pros pricing helps them rank better, unless directly asked by the pro. 
Don't imply pricing is being removed as a pro-facing feature — pros can still set, update, and hide pricing.
Don't over-encourage posting pricing on the profile beyond the approved talking point. 
Pro feedback on removing pricing
When speaking with pros who have feedback about this update, reps should use the following feedback theme: 
[Pricing] User has complaints about the removal of customer facing pricing
Refer to the internal Product Feedback (Rep) KA for steps submitting feedback.  
▶ Talking points: Pro concerns about posting prices
English talking point
Q: Why can't customers see my upfront prices anymore?
A: Thumbtack is updating how pricing appears in the customer experience, and upfront pricing may no longer be shown while customers browse pros. 

Every project can vary based on its scope, timing, location, and the customer's specific needs. Removing the upfront estimate gives customers an opportunity to learn more about a pro and their expertise to have a more informed discussion about what goes into pricing and discuss their project details before evaluating a final price. 

Once a customer has contacted you, you can share pricing details — and any pricing you've added to your profile's Business FAQs section is still visible to customers who visit it.
Q: Why did Thumbtack make this change?
A: We're updating the way pricing is presented as part of broader work to create a more consistent pricing experience throughout the customer journey. An upfront estimate is only one part of a customer's decision and may not always reflect what their project will ultimately require. This update encourages customers to also consider factors such as a pro's experience, reviews, expertise, availability, and overall fit before deciding who to contact.
Q: How will customers know what I charge?
A: Customers can discuss pricing with you after they reach out and share more information about their project. 

This gives you an opportunity to understand what the customer needs, ask any necessary questions, and provide pricing that reflects the actual scope of the work rather than an estimate based on limited information. You can also fill out the Business FAQs section of your profile to add any additional information about pricing you would like customers to know when they review your business profile on Thumbtack
Q: How will customers decide which pro to contact without seeing prices?
A: Customers will still see information that helps them evaluate pros, including reviews, photos, business details, experience, and other profile content. 

The goal is to help customers consider the overall fit for their project rather than making their initial decision based primarily on an upfront estimate.
Q: Does this mean I'll get more leads from customers who are just comparing prices?
A: We understand why you may be concerned about how this change could affect lead quality and the value you receive. 

This update helps customers look beyond an initial price and engage with pros who may be a strong fit for their project. Hiding rates within the pro list creates an opportunity for you to educate clients on the value behind your pricing after they connect with you. This prevents initial cost from being the sole determining factor when they choose a service provider.
Q: Will upfront pricing come back?
A: Thumbtack is continuing to evaluate how pricing should be presented across the full customer and pro experience. We're also working toward a stronger and more consistent approach to pricing throughout the customer journey. 

We don't have additional details or a timeline to share right now, but we'll communicate any relevant updates as they become available.
Q: Should I still update my prices?
A: Yes — keeping your pricing accurate is still worthwhile. While customers won't see your pricing while browsing pros, having it up to date helps you give a faster, more informed answer once a customer reaches out, and it's used to calculate the pricing breakdown they see in the messenger after they contact you.
Q: So should I post pricing information on my profile?
A: That's up to you. If you choose to include pricing on your profile, consider sharing general pricing or starting rates rather than treating them as fixed quotes. Because every project is different, discussing the details with a customer is often the best way to provide accurate pricing.
Does my pricing affect my ranking? (only answer if asked directly)
Yes, pricing is still one of the factors that can affect your ranking on Thumbtack.
What customers see in search results 
Customers no longer see a pro's pricing on Thumbtack. Refer to the Important Update section above to learn more. 
Pricing options
Depending on the type of service, a pro will have different options for adding their prices to Thumbtack. When a customer sees the pro’s service in search results, they can see a starting price in the app based on the pricing details the pro shared. 
To see what pricing is available for a pro, frontline reps can log in as the pro through Admin.
Pricing options include:
A base price 
A price range (by square footage or hourly, for example)
Add-on prices 
Pricing differences depending on whether the job is on a weekday or weekend  
Discounts (e.g., recurring jobs, new customers)
Travel fees
On-site estimate fees 
Upfront pricing minimums (for variable price categories)
Base price
A pro's base price is the fundamental cost for their service, which can be structured differently depending on the service category. 
For example, a pro's base price could be: 
A base price by job type:
▶ For house cleaning, a housecleaner might have one flat fee for 2-bedroom, 1-bathroom homes and charge a higher flat fee for larger homes with three or more bedrooms. This gives the customer a starting price and then an estimated price once they enter in job details.[Image: rtaImage]
For floor cleaning, this could be based on flooring type (e.g., tile, concrete, vinyl) and charged by square foot or hourly.
An hourly rate: ($X/hour Base price)
Price per square footage: ($X/Sq ft)
A price range: For services like concrete removal, a pro might set a minimum to maximum number for a job by square feet (e.g., $100-300).
▶ By session: (e.g., $120/session) for services like reiki healing.[Image: rtaImage]
An on-site estimate fee: (e.g., $50/on-site estimate, waived if hired
A minimum upfront price: Pros can set this if in a variable price category like handyman or local moving (e.g., for a minimum of hours, $100/hour 2 hour minimum.​​
For more in-depth information on each base price type, reps can navigate to the relevant sections below. 
Price ranges
Pros in some “unpriceable” services can add price ranges. Depending on the service the pro offers, they’ll have options for filling out their prices as a range.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Add-on pricing (what pros charge extra for) 
In some service categories, pros can also include add-ons. For services like house cleaning, add-ons could include laundry, fridge cleaning, oven cleaning, etc. 
 Examples of add on prices include: 
A DJ might set an hourly fee as a base price, and could offer add-ons like a fog machine at an extra cost.
A housecleaner might have one flat fee for 2-bedroom, 1-bathroom homes and charge a higher flat fee for larger homes with three or more bedrooms.
Pros can either check a box to "Include in base price,” enter a price, or enter $0 if they don't want to include a price for an add-on.
If a pro checks the box to "Include in base price": The add-on is considered part of the base job and its cost is incorporated into the overall base price. It's not an additional charge but rather a service bundled within the initial price.
If a pro enters $0 for an add-on: Pros who entered $0 for the price, the customer will see the add-on but it won’t change the price estimate. The customer will see the add-on listed as $0.
If a pro enters a price for an add-on: When the customer sees the pro's price, they will see this add-on price included in the total price estimate.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Discount prices by sessions, recurrence and new customers 
Pros in select categories can include a discount with their price estimate. There are two different discounts available in select services. See the table below for price details.

Pros can offer a percentage discount for recurring jobs (e.g., every week, every 2 weeks, etc)
Pros will scroll to "Discounts for first-time customers" or "Discount for session packages" and enter a percentage amount when adding discount prices. 
The pro can discount a percentage from their base price and the customer would see the pro's standard price and discounted price.
If a pro sets a discount, it applies to all requests for that service. If a pro doesn’t offer discounts they can enter $0 during setup. 
NOTE: Thumbtack doesn't refund for leads asking about discounts (even if the discount is included in the pro's price estimate).

Upfront pricing minimums (Variable price categories)
Minimum upfront pricing gives pros in variable price categories the option to set a minimum hourly or dollar amount for their services, providing customers with upfront pricing. 
Variable pricing categories are typically hourly rate jobs. Floor cleaning is the only variable price (VP) category that charges per square footage instead of an hourly rate. Variable price categories include the following:
Barbecue and grill services
Floor cleaning*
Furniture delivery
Furniture moving and heavy lifting
Handyman
Holiday lighting installation
Home organizing
Hot tub moving
Land surveying
Local moving (under 50 miles)
Long distance moving
Office moving
Packing and unpacking
Picture hanging and art installation
Play equipment construction
Pool table repair services
Tree planting
Wardrobe consulting
In search results, when a customer looks for a pro in a variable price category only, they will see one of four cost options based on what the pro has decided: 
Base price with no minimum
Hourly or dollar amount with a minimum of hours at their standard rate
▶ Hourly or dollar amount with a minimum of hours at a different rate (expand for what it looks like)[Image: GTqMKUkAkWDCVEkKmKwKQJ4tMxYiaRMqvdgt7QnyPzcDK0qRZffXr0oil4tuiJ7-94j7btov0M_OOiSv9zEMixtMeSV5TVBBvXaRrfNXh2k4CvbOSQz0uXCmCf_7qZYe8e6W3GOjefedhY_yBKfKkyU]
Hourly or dollar amount with a minimum dollar amount
Customers will see minimum pricing in the following places:
Pro’s profile
Project details page
Booking confirmation email
NOTE: At this time, customers will only see the pro’s standard rate (no minimum) on the search results list view. 
Minimum pricing options
When minimum prices are toggled off, pros choose to set a standard base price. ($X/hour Base price). When the toggle is turned on, pros choose to set one of the following options for their VP categories, as detailed in the following table:

Pros will only the minimum dollar amount option will be shown when minimums are toggled on. 
Pros can enter decimal point values (two decimal points) in the $/sq ft fields for floor cleaning quote sheets (instead of a whole dollar amount)

On-site evaluation fee 
Pros can set on-site estimates or service call fees around what they charge for an onsite evaluation, not the total job cost. Pros can waive the fee they charged for the initial evaluation by clicking the “I will wave this fee if hired for the job.” 

▶ On-site estimates: For services like Deck or Porch Removal or Addition, pros can charge per estimate and waive the fee if hired.

[Image: rtaImage]


▶ Service calls: For services like Appliance Repair, the rate charged will be per service call and pros will have the option to waive the fee if hired.

[Image: rtaImage]

Thumbtack's cost estimates guides by service 
Thumbtack’s Cost Estimates for Home Projects, Events and More page show average prices for different services on Thumbtack. 
For most services, pros and customers can go to the cost estimates page to see a national average for a service. For a more comprehensive guide to the cost of a specific service, they’ll click on a service. Cost guides typically include a cost overview, factors impacting price, and more. 
The price estimates are based on a large number of customer requests and pro quotes for that service in their area. This gives customers a general idea of the cost, providing them with a good starting point, which can discourage them from reaching out to a pro only to understand how much a project might cost. 
That said, Thumbtack wants to make sure to share the right information with customers and set the right expectations. If a pro feels the price is significantly different, gather their feedback and thank them for their feedback. 
Pros can check out the How to price my services – Thumbtack Help article. Both pros and customers can refer to the Cost Estimates for Home Projects, Events and More - Thumbtack page. 
2. Process
(Pro) Steps: How to set up, post or hide pricing 

Pro steps: Pros can set up or update their pricing by following the steps on the How to price my services – Thumbtack Help article. 
Pros posting prices for the first time will see “Post prices,” while pros updating their prices will see “Update prices.” To remove their prices from their profile they will select “Hide Prices.”Any changes pros make to their pricing will be updated immediately. 
Steps: How to set and edit minimum prices for variable price categories (Pro) 
Pros can set and edit their upfront prices (minimums) for all variable price categories by following these steps:
From the pros prices page, pros will toggle on the "Minimum Required" at the bottom of the page. (See what it looks like below.)▶ What it looks like[Image: AD_4nXc2MQ3cwLbYgP3Cu-jhNW1T-z_6iC1vR5kd7FNgxln5FIvFCy1ijsWamU4nWBMVFuuZDxzQdzD72VlKEq31KOlHaRzOo6hj2AapL12yNhd_NcdJ0V9htRssVNKCXNBajMleEqLkjL1FZ3VaUi2HOTwFxm7Q]
Tap a pricing option and enter the minimum price details. 
Number of hours (at standard rate)
Number of hours (at a different rate)
Specific dollar amount
Tap Next to save and set minimums for another variable price category.
Steps: How to hide minimum prices for variable price categories (Pro)

Pros won’t see the toggle on booking details until they set their minimums (the toggle is off by default). Pros can hide their minimum prices by following these steps:

From booking details, pros will turn off the “include minimum” toggle which puts a strikethrough through the text, and their minimum pricing info won’t be sent to the customer. 
Tap Send to share the pricing and message the customer, 

Note: Turning off the 'Include minimums' toggle on booking details only means that their minimums change the pro's overall minimum settings for that specific category. (See what it looks like below.)

[Image: AD_4nXeOZF9tcjiWm0LXCqiyy0MwIylhK1_Tyt_BkjVeWTCxrCBRn0rCynQKdePSM7pjwrZlRN_knY6KxoYA39-MhK3zqINdaEsayhtiz5wf7-pHjtWEQVqRD579MqM7_C5hExcHtWgvMSNlXxwnHfcqevWr_wDn]

(Reps) Steps: Pro has feedback about pricing options 
If a pro says they don't have the right pricing options for their service, Frontline reps should:
Submit the pro’s feedback following the usual feedback process. Reps can refer to the internal Product Feedback KA for steps. 
Let them know that they can explain their pricing in their profile (using their Introduction or Q&A). 

3. Talking points

Understanding pro pricing on Thumbtack
This section provides talking points for frontline reps to help pros understand how pricing works on Thumbtack.

English talking point
Spanish talking point 
Q: Do I need to set up my pricing? 
Q: ¿Necesito configurar mis precios?
A: Setting up your pricing is optional. If you choose to add pricing, enter prices that reflect your typical rates. But remember, any prices you set are just estimates. You can always adjust them based on the job details.
A: Configurar los precios es opcional, pero lo recomiendo altamente porque los precios pueden ayudar a los clientes a elegir a qué profesional contactar cuando usan la aplicación. Los profesionales que establecen sus propios precios pueden atraer a más clientes y tienen más probabilidades de evitar prospectos de clientes que solo están comparando precios.
Ingrese precios que reflejen sus precios típicos para asegurarse de establecer las expectativas correctas con los clientes. Pero recuerde, los precios que establezca son solo estimaciones. Siempre puede ajustarlos según los detalles del trabajo.
Q: Do I have to turn on targeting preferences to post my pricing?
Q: ¿Tengo que activar las preferencias de enfoque para publicar mis precios?
A: No. You can post your pricing for businesses without targeting preferences on, and you can also set your targeting preferences for a business without posting your pricing. 
A: No. Puede publicar sus precios para empresas sin preferencias de enfoque activadas y también puede establecer sus preferencias de enfoque para una empresa sin publicar sus precios.
How to post prices and what to include
This section provides talking points for frontline reps to guide pros on how to post their prices and what information to include.

English talking point
Spanish talking point 
Q: What should I include in my pricing?
Q: ¿Qué debo incluir en mi precio?
A: In your pricing, you can include your base price, any discounts you’d like to offer, and the price of any add-ons to your service. We’ll do the math for you and update your overall price estimate for future leads based upon the itemized costs you include (previous leads and quotes won’t be impacted by this). We’ll save your pricing details in your Services tab, where you can also come back to edit them.
A: En su precio, puede incluir su precio base, los descuentos que le gustaría ofrecer y el precio de los complementos de su servicio. Haremos los cálculos por usted y actualizaremos su precio estimado general para prospectos futuros en función de los costos detallados que incluya (los prospectos y las cotizaciones anteriores no se verán afectados por esto). Guardaremos los detalles de los precios en la pestaña Servicios, donde también puede volver para editarlos.
Q: What if one of the add-ons listed is already included in my base price?
Q: ¿Qué pasa si uno de los servicios adicionales ya está incluido en mi precio base?
A: Great question. Just enter a zero when you’re asked to provide a price for this specific add-on. 
A: Buena pregunta. Simplemente ingrese un cero cuando se le solicite que proporcione un precio para este servicio complementario en específico.
Q: How can I use my profile to clarify my price range?
Q: ¿Cómo puedo usar mi perfil para aclarar mi rango de precios?
A: You can add your pricing details in the Q&A section, or you can mention it in your introduction. Keep in mind, shorter introductions are more impactful, so keep it brief.
A: Puede agregar los detalles de sus precios en la sección de preguntas y respuestas, o puede mencionarlos en su introducción. Tenga en cuenta que las presentaciones más breves tienen más impacto, así que sea breve.
Q:  Do I have to use the automated default prices Thumbtack added, or can I enter my own pricing?
Q: ¿Tengo que usar los precios predeterminados automáticos que agregó Thumbtack, o puedo ingresar mis propios precios?
A: Please add your own pricing, since you know your business best. We only add these automated default prices to help new pros understand better where to start.
A: Agregue sus propios precios, ya que usted conoce mejor su negocio. Solo agregamos estos precios predeterminados automatizados para ayudar a los nuevos profesionales a comprender mejor por dónde empezar.
Q: I'm setting up my pricing. What's the travel fee?
Q: Estoy configurando mi precio. ¿Qué es Tarifa de viaje (Travel fee)?
A: The travel fee is optional. You can cover your travel costs by adding an amount to your pricing. Pros told us they like to include fees to cover travel costs, so that’s why we added the new travel fee option in your pricing settings. If you don’t have a travel fee, just deselect the option and continue setting up your pricing.
A: La  sección de “Travel Fee” es opcional. Puede cubrir sus costos de viaje agregando una cantidad a su precio. Los profesionales nos dijeron que les gusta incluir tarifas para cubrir los costos de viaje, por eso agregamos la nueva opción de tarifa de viaje en su configuración de precios. Si no tiene una tarifa de viaje, simplemente anule la selección de la opción y continúe configurando su precio.

Pro and Customer Case Studies (Rep)

Contents
Overview
Identifying and meeting case study candidate requirements 
Process
Steps: How to submit a case study referral (Rep)
What happens after a rep submits a case study referral
Internal FAQ
Resources
I. OVERVIEW
Thumbtack uses case studies to highlight who we are, what we do, and how our pros and customers benefit from using Thumbtack.
Aside from general success stories, case studies span over more focus areas, can be from pros or customers, and will be used for a variety of purposes (i.e., sales collateral, landing page content, social proof for product/feature adoption, etc.). Thumbtack wants to ensure that each study is focused on a particular topic and that the user represents the incredible diversity that we have on Thumbtack.
All employees are eligible to submit a case study and have a chance to earn a $50 gift card in the process. This process helps Thumbtack collect diversified case studies and use them strategically to accomplish marketing and DEI goals. 
Case studies can include pros and customers 
Our criteria has diversity and marketplace health in mind.
Case study referrals are accepted from all employees who've had contact with a pro or customer, whether through work or Thumbtack bucks benefits.
IDENTIFYING AND MEETING CASE STUDY CANDIDATE REQUIREMENTS 
To help Thumbtack identify and secure ideal case study candidates, frontline reps can follow the guidelines below, which outline the characteristics of a strong candidate and the general requirements for participation in case studies.
A useful voice: This refers to a case study candidate who:
Represents an in-demand category or geography.
Has a unique perspective or identity.
A specific connection to Thumbtack: This describes a candidate who has a clear and demonstrable link to Thumbtack, such as: 
Highlights a specific feature (TToD, APIs, Front Desk, etc.).
Has used a Thumbtack resource (community, workshops, etc.).
Has successfully started or grown their business using Thumbtack.
Captures the difference between Thumbtack and our competitors.
The candidate: This outlines the general eligibility requirements for a case study participant: 
Can’t be a personal connection (family, friend, etc.).
Must represent Thumbtack in some way (business owner, homeowner).
Available between 9 am - 5 pm MST for an interview via phone or Zoom and is willing and able to share enough personal information to warrant a case study (must sign a release form if we plan to use their content).
Needs to be active on Thumbtack, not disabled or blocklisted, with spend in the last 60 days (if a pro).
For a full list of requirements, reps can refer to the internal Case Study Candidate Qualifications doc. The qualification criteria are likely to update quarterly with new primary focuses. 

TIP: Frontline res can bookmark the Case Study Intake & Management form to have it readily available.
II. PROCESS 
STEPS: HOW TO SUBMIT A CASE STUDY REFERRAL (REP)
This section outlines the steps frontline reps should follow to submit a case study referral.
If a frontline rep knows a pro or customer who meets the case study requirements and thinks they’ll be a good fit for a case study, submit the referral form. Even if they don’t meet all of the requirements, the content team would love to review your submission.
A few things steps should know: 
Its essential frontline reps provide accurate, complete information. This will increase the likelihood your candidate will be selected. 
All questions on the form are required. 
The case study team will take your answers and determine if they can move forward. 
Do fill out the form even if you’re not sure. 
The form takes ~3-5 minutes to complete. 
To submit a case study referral, reps will follow these steps: 
Gather the following details to complete the referral form:
User PK ID
Focus area (category, market, diversity, etc.)
Data classification (qualitative, quantitative) 
Enter the details into the Case Study Intake & Management form
The form links to the internal Case Study Candidate Qualifications doc that includes information about what questions are on the form and what the case study team is looking for. 

NOTE: Checking “testimonial candidate” in Salesforce no longer flags a user as a candidate. 
WHAT HAPPENS AFTER A REP SUBMITS A CASE STUDY REFERRAL 
This section outlines the process and next steps after a frontline rep submits a case study referral.
If a frontline reps case study referral is selected, they’’ll be contacted by the Case Study Content Team. The team will contact the referral to set up and conduct an interview via Zoom.
After the candidate completed the interview the rep will receive a $50 digital gift card via email. If the rep doesn't hear back from the team within 2-3 business days, it’s likely the referral wasn’t selected. 
NOTE:  Contact Cailee Markosian via slack if you have questions. 
III. INTERNAL FAQ
This section addresses frequently asked questions from reps regarding the case study referral process.
How do I (a rep) refer a pro for a case study?
First, you will want to bookmark this Case Study Intake & Management form so you have quick access to it whenever you encounter a great case study candidate. It should take 3-5 mins to fill out. The more information on the user you provide, the more likely we will be able to move forward with an interview. If the user shows for an interview, we will email you a $50 digital gift card!
Who can refer a case study candidate?
Any employee who has had contact with a pro or customer that would meet certain case study needs and qualifications. Teams who are most likely to have these user interactions would be Sales, Success, Service & Support, and Experience Research, as they speak with our users on a regular basis. However, if you meet a great pro through the TT bucks programs that meet some of the qualification criteria, refer away.
Can I (a rep) still check the “testimonial candidate” box on a Salesforce contact to refer a pro?
This system is no longer being used. By filling out the Case Study Intake & Management form with as much detail as you can (should take 3-5 mins), we can better keep track of and prioritize candidate referrals for building case studies. 
How do I (a rep) know if my case study referral will be interviewed? 
We will reach out to you directly over slack or email to gather more details on that user’s preferred contact info if we do not have that already. If we do not reach out within 2-3 business days, your referral did not meet the needed criteria. Please reach out to Cailee Markosian if there are any questions.
How do I (a rep) win a $50 digital gift card?
​​After you submit your pro/customer referral to this Case Study Intake & Management form, we will review the content to decide if the user meets the current needs for case studies. If they do, we will invite them to complete a zoom interview. After they complete the interview, you will be awarded a $50 digital gift card, sent to your Thumbtack email. 
IV. RESOURCES
This section provides helpful resources for frontline reps, including internal forms and documents related to case studies.
Resources for frontline reps 
Internal form
 Case Study Intake & Management form 
Internal doc
Case Study Candidate Qualifications

Prepaid Package Refunds (Pro)

Contents
Overview
Updates
Process
Steps: How to determine the prepaid package purchase method (Rep)
Steps: How to handle Sales package refund requests (Rep)
Steps: How to handle an in-product package refund request (Rep)
In-Product Prepaid Package Refund Eligibility
Steps: Check for accidental duplicate charge for preloadable balance 
Steps: Handling pro who has received 0 leads in first 90 days since purchase 
Steps: Handling packages purchased on duplicate account
Steps: How to process in-package purchase refunds (Advanced Service ONLY)
Talking points
Package receipt and expiration
Explain how refunds on leads paid for using package works
Pro is not eligible for a prepaid package refund
Pro is not eligible for a refund on their pre-loaded balance
Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article guides Frontline Reps on processing refunds for prepaid packages. It outlines how to determine package type (sales vs. in-product), the specific refund processes for each, and the eligibility criteria for various refund reasons. The article also provides talking points for communicating with pros about refund decisions.
While the option for pros to purchase in product packages was removed in April 2023, pros can still purchase prepaid packages directly from the Sales team. Additionally, pros have the ability to preload their Thumbtack balance by adding funds to their account.* 
Credit package purchases are final and non-refundable. However, there are certain situations where an exception may be made and a refund could be approved. These situations are outlined in the processes below.
* Important for reps: When a pro preloads their balance, this transaction is displayed in Admin as a “prepaid package” purchase. Therefore, this article covers refund procedures for both Sales-purchased packages and preloaded balances.
If a package is eligible for a refund, the process for refunding a prepaid package begins with the Frontline rep, who will identify the package type and escalate the request to the appropriate team. The Advanced Service team (for in-product packages) or the GTM (Sales) operations team will then use a new refund tool in the New Admin interface to process the refund for the specific package.
Lead refunds and returns
If a pro uses their package balance to pay for a lead and that lead qualifies for a refund, the cost is returned to their Thumbtack balance to use on future leads. For details on this process, reps should refer to the internal Lead Refunds (Pro) KA. If the pro then requests to have that refunded lead credit transferred from their Thumbtack balance back to their original payment method, reps must follow the steps in the Transfer Cashable Balance Back To Card (Pro) KA.
Updates

2. Process
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: This section outlines the process for Frontline Reps to handle prepaid package refund requests. It details how to determine if a package was sold by a sales representative or purchased in-product, and the subsequent steps for processing refunds based on the package type, including eligibility criteria.
Steps: How to determine the package type (Rep)
If a pro requests a refund on a package purchase, the rep will first want to identify if the package was sold by a Sales rep. 
Frontline reps can follow these steps to determine if Sales sold the package to the pro: 
Search the pro's PK ID in Salesforce.
Access the pro's Contacts Page.
Look for the "Opportunities" Section: To the right, look for an "[Image: rtaImage]Opportunities" section. 
If it's not visible, click "Show More" on the left side panel to expand the relevant Salesforce objects, then click on "Opportunities."
Check the "Close Date" in Opportunities: Click on the Opportunities and look at the “Close Date.” 
If an Opportunity with a Close Date that equals the date of purchase is found, the package was sold by a Sales rep. Support reps will follow the Steps: How to handle Sales package refund requests (Rep). 
No Opportunity Found: If there’s no Opportunity found, that means the package was not sold by a Sales rep. Reps will proceed to the Steps: How to handle an in-product package refund request (Rep). 

[Image: rtaImage]

Screenshot: The image above shows the Opportunities page with a prepaid package purchased on June 13, 2025. The pro paid $200 for a one-time package. 
Steps: How to handle a Sales package refund request (Rep)
For prepaid packages purchased from the Sales team, Support reps will submit a refund request for review. Once Sales Operations has reviewed the request (typically within 1-2 business days for initial response, and 5-7 business days for cases requiring additional review), the decision will be communicated to the rep, who will then inform the pro.
Support reps should follow these steps when a pro requests a refund on a Sales team prepaid package: 
Contact the Sales Manager: Reach out to the Sales rep's manager about the refund request to make sure it’s valid and needs to be processed.
In Slack, search for the Sales Rep and open their Slack profile.
Scroll to the People section where their manager will be noted.
Click on the manager's profile picture or name to open a Slack message with them.
Submit a request using the Assist App:
​​​​​​​Open the Atlassian Assist app in Slack.
Select Raise a request.
For “What team do you need help from?,” choose Sales Operations (SOPS).
For “What do you need help with?,” select Compensation. 
Under “Incentives,” select Refunds.
Fill out the form with all necessary details.
Click Submit.
Set Case Status to Pending Thumbtack: After submitting the request to Sales Operations, change the case status in Salesforce to "Pending Thumbtack." This indicates that the case is awaiting a response from another Thumbtack team (Sales Operations).
Await Sales Ops Response: Sales Ops will respond to the rep (requestor) within 1-2 business days, confirming receipt of the ticket and outlining the next steps in the refund process.
Investigation and Review (if applicable): Depending on the refund reason, a deeper investigation may be necessary.
Refund reasons without deeper investigation: 
Trust and Safety triggered refunds (A failed background check or pro was blocklisted).  
An incorrect pro account was charged
Refund reasons requiring additional review (5-7 business days):
Sales Ops and QA will review the initial sales call before issuing a refund. It can take 5 to 7 business days to process the request.
Reasons include:
Pro asserts sales call was misleading
Prospect did not have authority to purchase
Pro is not a market fit for Thumbtack
Pro was unaware they would be charged
Other reasons
Sales Ops Notification: Sales Ops will notify the manager and AE about the request.
Refund Decision Notification: After any necessary investigation, Sales Ops will notify the rep (requestor), sales rep, and their respective managers of the refund decision.
Communicate with the pro: The rep (requestor) will email the pro the details of the refund outcome.
Close the Case: Once the pro has been informed of the refund outcome, close the case in Salesforce.
Steps: How to handle an in-product package refund request (Rep)
Before following the below steps, support reps will first follow the "Steps: How to determine the prepaid package purchase method (Rep)" to confirm the package was an in-product purchase.
If a pro purchased a package in-product or added funds to their Thumbtack balance by using the preload feature and is requesting a refund, the Frontline rep will first check the eligibility criteria. Based on the eligibility, the reps will then follow the appropriate steps to process the refund or communicate the decision to the pro.
Support reps will follow these steps:
Check Eligibility: Review the package refund eligibility in the "In-Product Prepaid Package Refund Eligibility" table below.
If Ineligible:
Communicate the decision to the pro, reiterating that package sales are final and non-refundable, as stated on their package receipt. 
Coach the pro on how to utilize and succeed with Thumbtack.
To view or download a receipt, click the "receipt link" under the package purchase in the credit logs.
If a pro is not eligible for an in-product package refund and they dispute the outcome, stand firm on why the package isn’t refundable. Reps can use the Talking points below and follow the de-escalation techniques in the Standard Escalations and De-escalation Guidelines (Rep)  as needed.
If Eligible (or pro disputes outcome):
Submit a request to the Advanced Service Team using the Atlassian Assist app in Slack.
Navigate to the #service_global_help-and-escalations Slack channel.
Use a keyword like Help refunds or Refunds to trigger the Assist app workflow.
Select the "Global Help Refunds" request type and fill out the form with all necessary details. 
Advanced Service Review: The AST will review the case and confirm if the pro is eligible for a refund. If they determine the pro is eligible, they will process the refund.
If AST refunds the package: 
Once the refund has been processed, let the pro know they will receive a refund within 5-7 business days.
Send a confirmation email to the pro confirming the refund. No refund receipt will populate in Admin.
In-product prepaid package and pre-loadable balance refund eligibility
This table outlines the eligibility criteria for in-product prepaid package refunds, detailing various refund request reasons and whether they qualify for a refund.

Refund request reasons
Eligible for a refund? 
Account is Blocklisted
(linked to banned user or account hold)
Yes

Yes

Yes (see steps below)

Or

▶ Examples:
Boat Detailing: Yes 
Commercial tile installation:” No (can be targeted specifically under Tile Installation, removing Residential as a targeted job)
Pro Claims They Were Unaware Of Charge
No
Pro doesn’t want to use Thumbtack anymore
No

No
Pro Has Received Zero (0) Leads In First 90 Days Since Purchase
Maybe (see steps below)
Purchased package on a duplicate account
Maybe (see steps below) 
Steps: Accidental duplicate charge for preloaded balance

To check for accidental double-charges, reps will:
Go to the Journal Entries table in Admin.
In New Admin, navigate to the pro's user page.
In the Actions column to the right, under the Payments section, click the "Pro-Payment Summary" link. 
On the Pro-Payment Summary Page, locate the "Journal Entries" table.
Look for two "PREPAID_CREDIT_PURCHASE" entries with the same amount and nearly the same timestamps.
▶ Example of duplicate charges

[Image: rtaImage]

If a duplicate charge is confirmed, the pro is eligible for a refund for the extra amount.
Steps: Pro Has Received Zero (0) Leads In First 90 Days Since Purchase
Reps will follow these steps to determine refund eligibility:
Work with the pro on their profile and targeting set up. 
If improvements have been made and the pro still has not received leads, a refund may be reconsidered.
Steps: Purchased package on a duplicate account
Reps will follow these steps to determine refund eligibility:
A refund will only be processed if the pro can prove they do have a duplicate account. Here's how to check:
Determine who added the package:
If the Sales Team added the package:
The rep will submit a request to the Sales Ops team using the Assist App to request a refund and recharge to the correct account. Follow the Steps: How to handle Sales package refund requests (Rep) to do this.
If the pro purchased an in-product package:
The rep reaches out to the Advanced Service Team to process the refund.
Once the refund is processed, the pro can preload refunds to their account. For steps, pros can refer to the How to preload my balance – Thumbtack Help article.
Steps: How to process in-product package refunds (Advanced Service ONLY) 
This process is only for use by the Advanced Service after receiving an escalated refund request. Support reps should not follow this process. It outlines how to issue a refund for a specific prepaid package, including those from preloaded balances, directly back to a pro's original form of payment using the New Admin interface.
Important Note: If the pro has already disputed the prepaid package charge with their bank, they will need to wait for an outcome from their bank. Reps can learn more about payment disputes in the internal Removed or Banned Users (Pro) (Customers) KA.
Advanced Services reps should follow these steps: 
If the Pro is NOT Eligible for a Refund: 
Inform the Support rep that the pro is not eligible for a refund on their prepaid package. 
Instruct the rep to: 
Coach the pro on how to utilize and succeed with Thumbtack.
Reference the package receipt that states sales are final and non-refundable if needed.
If the Pro IS Eligible for a Refund: 
Follow the steps below for processing a prepaid package refund in Admin and then return back to these steps. 
Once the refund has been processed, inform the support rep that the pro know they will receive the refund in 5-7 business days from the date of approval.
To process a prepaid package or pre-loaded balance refund in Admin, the Advanced Service team will follow these steps:
Navigate to the Pro's Payment Summary
From the pro's user page in New Admin, scroll down to the Payments section.
Click the “Pro-Payment Summary” link. This will take you to the main dashboard for the pro's financial account.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Access the Prepaid Package List
On the Pro-Payment Summary page, click the “Prepaid Package List” link to view all active and past packages the pro has purchased.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Identify and Refund the Correct Package
Review the package details (purchase date, initial amount, and remaining balance) to identify the correct one for the refund.
If a package has a remaining paid balance and is eligible for a refund, a “Refund to credit card” button will be visible.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Confirm the Refund Action
Click the “Refund to credit card” button for the desired package.
A confirmation pop-up modal will appear asking, "Are you sure you want to refund this prepaid package?"
Click “OK” to confirm and submit the refund for processing.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Verify the Refund was Processed
Initial Confirmation: Upon success, a green banner will appear at the top of the page with the message: "Success! Prepaid package refunded successfully."
Final Verification: Refresh the "Prepaid Package List" page. The “Refund to credit card” button for the package you just refunded will no longer be visible. This confirms the action is complete and cannot be repeated.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

(Optional) Review the Transaction in the Journal
To see the detailed accounting of the refund, navigate back to the "Pro-Payment Summary" page.
In the "Journal Entries" table, you will now see a new line item.
The Type for this transaction will be REFUND_CREDIT_PURCHASE, and the Amount will show a negative value, reflecting the refunded amount. Clicking on this entry will take you to the detailed "Pro-Payment Journal" page for the complete transaction record (as shown in the image below).
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]


3. Talking points
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros about prepaid package refunds. Use these talking points to ensure consistent and accurate messaging.
Package receipt and expiration
This section provides support reps with talking points to address common questions about where to find package receipts and whether credit packages expire. It clarifies that receipts are sent to the registered email and credits do not expire, offering an opportunity to coach pros on maximizing their Thumbtack experience.


English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Q: Where can I see the receipt for the pack I bought?
Q: ¿Dónde puedo ver el recibo del paquete que compré?
A: The receipt was sent to the email you used to sign up for your Thumbtack account. You can also check your Thumbtack balance on your Payments page to see how much credit you still have available.
A: El recibo se envió al correo electrónico que usó para registrarse en su cuenta de Thumbtack. También puede verificar su saldo de Thumbtack en su página de Pagos para ver cuánto crédito aún tiene disponible.
Q: Will my credit pack expire?
Q: ¿Mi paquete de créditos expirará?
A: Your lead credits won’t expire. But the best way to get an idea of what Thumbtack can really do is by regularly talking to customers. Let me give you a few tips on making the most of the credit pack you purchased. 
[COACH PRO ON RELEVANT ISSUES (targeting preferences, profile, messaging customers, etc.)]
A: Su paquete de créditos no expirará. Pero la mejor manera de tener una idea de cómo realmente funciona Thumbtack es hablando regularmente con los clientes. Permítame darle algunos consejos sobre cómo aprovechar al máximo el paquete de crédito que compró. 

[Educa al PRO EN CUESTIONES RELEVANTES (preferencias de enfoque, perfil, como responder a los prospectos, etc.)]

Explaining refunds on leads paid for using package
This section provides support reps with talking points to explain that while credit packages are generally non-refundable, if a lead paid for with a package qualifies for a refund, the cost of that lead will be returned to the pro's Thumbtack balance for future use.


English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Q: Can I get a refund for the credit package I purchased?
Q: ¿Puedo obtener un reembolso por el paquete de créditos que compré?
A: If you prepaid for leads by purchasing a credit package, the credit package isn't refundable. But if you use that package to pay for a lead, and that lead qualifies for a refund, you'll get the cost of the lead refunded to your Thumbtack balance to use on future leads.
[Support rep: Salesforce email template titled: “Sales Package Refund Request”]
A: Si usted pagó por adelantado los prospectos mediante la compra de un paquete de créditos, dicho paquete no es reembolsable. Sin embargo, si utiliza ese paquete para pagar un prospecto y este califica para un reembolso, se le reembolsará el costo del prospecto en su saldo de Thumbtack para usarlo en futuros prospectos.

Pro is not eligible for a prepaid package refund
This section provides support reps with talking points for situations where a pro is not eligible for a prepaid package refund, such as when they are not getting hired. It guides reps on how to explain that credit packs are non-refundable and offers strategies to help pros make the most of their investment in Thumbtack.


English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Q: I'm not getting hired — I want a refund for this pack! 
(Pro is not eligible for a refund)
No me contratan - ¡quiero un reembolso por este paquete! 
(Pro is not eligible for a refund)
A: I understand it can be frustrating when customers go with another option. Unfortunately, this credit pack is nonrefundable.
It might help to think of Thumbtack the way you'd think of traditional advertising — like a billboard. Every person who sees the billboard won't automatically become a customer, but several will. You've invested in Thumbtack to get your business in front of potential customers, so let's figure out how to make it work for you.  
I can give you some tips that might help you connect with more customers. 
[COACH PRO ON RELEVANT ISSUES (profile, messaging customers, etc.)]
Entiendo que puede ser frustrante cuando los clientes siguen adelante con otra opción. Lamentablemente, este paquete de créditos no es reembolsable. 
Podría ser útil pensar en Thumbtack de la forma en que pensaría en la publicidad tradicional, como una valla publicitaria. Todas las personas que vean la valla publicitaria no se convertirán automáticamente en clientes, pero varios lo harán. Ha invertido en Thumbtack para mostrar su negocio a clientes potenciales, así que descubramos cómo hacer que funcione para usted. 
Puedo dar algunos consejos que podrían ayudarle a conectarse con más clientes. [Educa al PRO EN CUESTIONES RELEVANTES (preferencias de enfoque, perfil, como responder a los prospectos, etc.)]
Pro is not eligible for a refund on their pre-loaded balance
This section provides support reps with talking points for when a pro inquires about a refund for their preloaded Thumbtack balance. 

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Q: Can I get a refund on the funds I added to my account? 
(Pro preloaded their Thumbtack balance, not eligible for refund)
Q: ¿Puedo obtener un reembolso de los fondos que agregué a mi cuenta?
(Pro preloaded their Thumbtack balance, not eligible for refund)
A: Once you've preloaded funds to your Thumbtack balance, it's non-refundable. However, your balance never expires, so you can use it for any future leads. You can turn off auto-refill at any time by editing your Billing settings.
A: Una vez que usted haya precargado fondos a su saldo de Thumbtack, el dinero no es reembolsable. Sin embargo, su saldo nunca vence, así que puede usarlo para futuros prospectos. Usted puede desactivar la recarga automática en cualquier momento desde su configuración de Facturación.

Prebuilt Profiles and Importing Reviews From Other Sites (Pro)

Contents
Overview
Claiming Business Profile and Importing Review Ratings
How Imported Review Ratings Work
Pro experience: How pro claims their business profile
Onboarding Flow (for reference)
Process
Steps: How to help pro report that another pro claimed their business information (Rep)

Talking points
How imported review rating works
How pro claims their business profile
How imported review rating works with other reviews on Thumbtack
Verification of business and business owner
What customers see on the pro’s profile
Pro wants to know where Thumbtack gets the imported information
Pro wants to change or remove their imported review rating
Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal Knowledge Article (KA) details how Thumbtack's "Prebuilt Profiles" feature allows pros to claim and import business information and review ratings from other public websites. It explains the process for both new and existing pros (as the feature is now available on-demand), how the imported information is used on Thumbtack profiles, and provides guidance for frontline reps on addressing pro inquiries and concerns, including how to handle situations where a pro reports another pro claiming their information.
New and existing pros have the option to claim available pieces of information about their business, including "Import reviews from other sites." This feature is now available on-demand, not just in the initial sign-up flow. This allows pros to enter their business name and zip code to be almost instantly matched with a profile Thumbtack scrubbed from credible sites that pros advertise their business on. 
▶ Internal Info Only: Where Thumbtack Gets Information
Thumbtack scrubs information from websites where pros advertise their services, including Yelp, HomeAdvisor, Angie's List, Google, and others. Frontline rep must follow these guidelines when discussing prebuilt profiles: 
Don’t: Frontline reps should NOT tell pros where Thumbtack scrubs their profile info from. 
Do: Frontline reps can let pros know they have the choice to claim the profile or not and that we only scrape from reputable sources. 
Do: Frontline reps should refer to the provided talking points below to help navigate these conversations with pros. 
Claiming business profile and importing review ratings(aggregate rating) 
This section explains how Thumbtack uses publicly available online information to help pros quickly set up their profiles and import existing review ratings.
Here’s how Thumbtack uses existing online information to:
Quick Matching: When a pro enters their business name and zip code, Thumbtack quickly finds public details such as:
Year founded
Website
Phone number
Address
Number of employees
Business address
Importing Review Ratings: If reviews are found on other sites, pros can choose to import their overall review rating. This helps potential Thumbtack customers see their value upfront.
Visible Profile Info: Once live, customers can see the pro's years in business, number of employees, and imported review ratings. Pros can update these details anytime on their profile.
How Imported Review Ratings Work

This section details the specifics of how imported review ratings function on Thumbtack, including what information is displayed and how these ratings interact with Thumbtack's review system.
Pros who import a review rating (without the actual review text) instantly meet the requirement for having at least one review, which can speed up their activation. (Reps can refer to the internal Understanding and Completing Activation Requirements KA).
Only the numerical aggregate rating shows up.
Only reviews written directly on Thumbtack will have their text displayed.
If a pro changes their business name on Thumbtack, the third-party review rating is removed.
These imported ratings do not directly affect Thumbtack's internal ranking system.
Frontline reps should refer to the internal Reviews (Pro) KA to learn more.
Pro experience: How pro claims their business profile

This section outlines the process pros follow to claim their business profile and import review ratings, both during initial setup and on-demand.
Pros can now claim their business information whenever they want, not just when they first sign up. Here's how it works:
Enter Business Name: Pros type in their business name. Most searches are super fast, taking less than 5 seconds.
Select or Skip:
If Thumbtack finds their business, the pro can choose it to claim the available information. If multiple businesses match, they'll see all of them.
If their business isn't listed, they can click "My business isn't shown here." This will take them to a screen where they can manually enter their information.
Confirm Information: The pro checks if the auto-filled information is correct and clicks "Next." If it's not their business, they can click "Not your business?" to enter details themselves.
Import Review Ratings: If Thumbtack found existing reviews for their business, the pro will have the option to "Add rating" to import their overall review rating, or "Don't add" to skip it.
Important for Thumbtack reps: Never fill in profile information for a pro. They must confirm ownership of any details themselves.
If a pro didn't select a profile during initial setup:
They can still do so by clicking "Import reviews from other sites" on their reviews page.
If a pro clicks "My business isn't shown here" and no online reviews are found, they'll see a message like "We couldn’t find any online reviews from your business." They can then click "See other options" to go back to their reviews page and explore other ways to get reviews, such as importing Google reviews or emailing past customers.
Frontline reps should refer to the internal Reviews (Pro) KA to learn more. 
▶ Onboarding Flow (for reference):

This section provides a brief overview of the business profile claiming process as it appears during a pro's initial onboarding experience.
At the beginning of the onboarding, pros can claim their business information. Here’s what the flow looks like: 
Pro enters their business name.

2. Process
This section outlines the steps and procedures for frontline reps to effectively manage common scenarios related to prebuilt profiles and imported reviews. It covers how to address pro concerns, escalate issues, and ensure accurate information handling.
(Rep) Steps: How to help pro report that another pro claimed their business information

If a frontline rep is contacted by a pro reporting that someone signed up on Thumbtack with their company’s information, the rep will follow these steps: 
Thank the pro for reaching out and let them know you’re going to send the details over to Trust and Safety for further investigation. 
Escalate to Trust & Safety by following the applicable steps on Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA. 

(Rep) Steps: How to handle situations where pro continuously asks for which specific sites Thumbtack gets information from

If the pro continuously asks for which specific sites Thumbtack gets our information from, frontline reps will follow these steps: 
Reach out to Cass Abernathy on Slack for guidance. 
If Cass is out of office, reach out to legal@thumbtack.com.
NOTE: If pro says they recognize this info and says they are going to talk to that site about this, frontline reps should: 
Let the know you’ll look into this for them. 
▶ Talking point:"While I know this is all public information, I’m not certain exactly where it comes from. Let me look into this for you."
Immediately start a Slack conversation with Cass Abernathy (if she's out of office, reach out to legal@thumbtack.com instead) and your manager and include the following in your message:
Pro's name
Pro admin
Which details they recognized from the pre-built profile 
The site the pro said they came from 
3. Talking points
This section provides frontline reps with clear and concise talking points for various pro inquiries about prebuilt profiles and imported review ratings. These responses are designed to be easily digestible and help reps confidently communicate key information to pros.
▶ How imported review rating works
This section provides frontline reps with talking points to explain how Thumbtack calculates and displays imported review ratings, and how they integrate with reviews received directly on the platform.

English talking point
Spanish talking point 
How did you get this review rating for my Thumbtack profile?
¿Cómo se calculó la calificación de evaluaciones en mi perfil de Thumbtack?
We calculated your average rating from certain reviews that were publicly available on the internet. It’s one way we try to make signing up on Thumbtack easier for you, so you can get right to growing your business. It’s up to you whether you’d like to claim your public review rating, or start from scratch. Either way, reviews are important, so when you’re setting up your account, we’ll help you ask your past customers for reviews.
Calculamos su calificación promedio a partir de sus evaluaciones disponibles públicamente en Internet. Es una de las formas en que intentamos facilitar el registro en Thumbtack, para que pueda comenzar a hacer crecer su negocio. Depende de usted si desea reclamar su calificación de evaluación pública o comenzar desde cero. De cualquier manera, las evaluaciones son importantes, por lo que cuando configure su cuenta, lo ayudaremos a solicitar evaluaciones a sus clientes anteriores.
Frontline rep note: If the pro continuously asks for which specific sites Thumbtack gets our information from, frontline reps should reach out to Cass Abernathy on Slack for guidance. If Cass is out of office, reach out to legal@thumbtack.com.
▶ How pro claims their business profile
Frontline reps can use these talking points to guide pros through the process of claiming their business profile, including what content is imported and options for inaccurate matches.

English talking point
Spanish talking point 
What kind of content is imported when I claim my business profile? 

We scrub real-time content from credible sites that you advertise your business on. By entering your business name and zip code, we can quickly pull your business details like your year founded, website, phone number, address, number of employees, and business address in a matter of seconds. 

If you have reviews on the sites we were able to find your info, you have the option to import your review ratings so new customers on Thumbtack can see your value upfront. 

What happens if the profile match is not the right profile? 

You do not have to claim the profile. Simply click, “my business isn’t shown here” to move forward to the next step where you can fill out your accurate business info. 

▶ How imported review rating works with other reviews on Thumbtack
This section equips frontline reps with talking points to clarify how imported review ratings integrate with reviews obtained directly on Thumbtack, including their impact on overall ratings and Top Pro status.

English talking point
Spanish talking point 
How does this average review rating work with reviews I’ll get on Thumbtack?
¿Cómo funciona esta calificación de evaluación promedio con las evaluaciones que obtendré en Thumbtack?
Your average review rating impacts your Thumbtack review rating with as much weight as reviews you get on Thumbtack. So if your review rating was based on one five-star review, and you get another five-star review from a Thumbtack customer, those two reviews would impact your overall rating equally.
Su calificación promedio de evaluaciones impacta su calificación de evaluación de Thumbtack con tanto peso como las evaluaciones que obtiene en Thumbtack. Entonces, si su calificación de evaluación se basó en una evaluación de cinco estrellas y obtiene otra evaluación de cinco estrellas de un cliente de Thumbtack, esas dos evaluaciones afectarían su calificación general por igual.
How long will this review rating stay on my Thumbtack profile?
¿Cuánto tiempo permanecerá esta calificación de evaluaciones en mi perfil de Thumbtack?
Once you have a review rating on your profile, that becomes part of the equation for your reviews on Thumbtack. As you get reviews from Thumbtack customers, we’ll add those ratings into the mix to come up with your total review rating.
Una vez que tenga una calificación de evaluación en su perfil, eso se convierte en parte de la ecuación para sus evaluaciones en Thumbtack. A medida que reciba evaluaciones de los clientes de Thumbtack, agregaremos esas calificaciones a la combinación para obtener su calificación total de evaluaciones.
Will this rating go towards my Top Pro status?
¿Esta calificación irá hacia mi estado de Top Pro?
Top Pro status is calculated from verified reviews from Thumbtack customers. Since this star rating is based on reviews outside of Thumbtack, they won’t count toward Top Pro.
El estado de Top Pro se calcula a partir de evaluaciones verificadas de clientes de Thumbtack. Dado que esta calificación de estrellas se basa en evaluaciones fuera de Thumbtack, no se tomarán en cuenta para el estado Top Pro.
▶ Verification of business and business owner
Here, frontline reps will find talking points to address pros' concerns about security and verification, ensuring them that Thumbtack has processes in place to confirm legitimate business ownership.

English talking point
Spanish talking point 
What keeps a random pro from claiming someone else’s business details and review rating?
¿Qué evita que un profesional cualquiera reclame los detalles de la empresa y la calificación de evaluaciones de otra persona?
We have teams and processes in place to verify businesses and make sure they are who they say they are. So even though it feels super simple to set up a business on Thumbtack, there are people here working to make sure everything runs smoothly.
Contamos con equipos y procesos para verificar las empresas y asegurarnos de que sean quienes dicen ser. Entonces, aunque se siente muy simple configurar un negocio en Thumbtack, hay personas aquí trabajando para asegurarse de que todo funcione sin problemas.
▶ What customers see on the pro’s profile
This section offers talking points for frontline reps to explain clearly what specific business details and review information customers can see on a pro's Thumbtack profile after claiming their business and importing ratings.

English talking point
Spanish talking point 
What can customers see? 

Customers can see your years in business, number of employees, and review ratings after your business is live. You can always go back to your profile to update your business details. 

▶ Pro wants to know where Thumbtack gets the imported information
This section provides frontline reps with talking points to respond to pros' questions about the sources of imported business information and review ratings, emphasizing the use of public internet data.

English talking point
Spanish talking point 
Where are you getting the information from for this Thumbtack profile?
¿De dónde obtiene la información para este perfil de Thumbtack?
Across public internet sources. I’d love to share our profile guide with you. It shows you how to stand out to customers. Can I send that to the email address on your account?
A través de fuentes públicas de Internet. Me encantaría compartir con usted nuestra guía de perfiles. Le muestra cómo destacar ante los clientes. ¿Puedo enviarlo a la dirección de correo electrónico de su cuenta?
I recognize this info, it comes from [specific website]. I’m going to talk to that site about this. **
Reconozco esta información, proviene de [sitio web específico]. Voy a hablar con ese sitio sobre esto.
While I know this is all public information, I’m not certain exactly where it comes from. Let me look into this for you.
Si bien sé que toda esta es información pública, no estoy seguro de dónde proviene exactamente. Déjame ver esto por usted.
This review rating looks like it came directly from [other website].
Parece que esta calificación de evaluación proviene directamente de [otro sitio web].
The average review rating is intended to reflect your reviews from across the internet, but I don’t have a way to see exactly which sites your reviews have come from. 
La calificación promedio de evaluaciones está destinada a reflejar sus evaluaciones de Internet, pero no tengo una forma de ver exactamente de qué sitios provienen sus evaluaciones. 
** IMPORTANT STEPS FOR REP: Immediately start a Slack conversation with Cass Abernathy (if she's out of office, reach out to legal@thumbtack.com instead) and your manager and include the following in your message:
Pro's name
Pro admin
Which details they recognized from the pre-built profile 
The site the pro said they came from **
▶ Pro wants to change or remove their imported review rating
Frontline reps will find talking points here to address pros who wish to modify or remove their imported review ratings, explaining the limitations and alternative options for gathering reviews.

English talking point
Spanish talking point 
My review rating is better on a different site, can I use that instead?
Mi calificación de revisión es mejor en un sitio diferente, ¿puedo usar eso en su lugar?
The review rating is based on public reviews, and we’ve included it as an option in case that helps you get a jumpstart meeting customers. We can’t change the rating, but if the review rating you’re seeing doesn’t feel accurate or representative of your work, you don’t have to claim the review rating. I can talk you through some other easy ways to add reviews to your profile. To start, do you have any reviews on Google?
La calificación de las evaluaciones se basa en evaluaciones públicas, y la hemos incluido como una opción en caso de que lo ayude a comenzar a conocer clientes. No podemos cambiar la calificación, pero si la calificación de revisión que está viendo no se siente precisa o representativa de su trabajo, no tiene que reclamar la calificación de evaluación. Puedo compartir otras formas sencillas de agregar evaluaciones a su perfil. Para empezar, ¿tiene alguna evaluación en Google?
I added a review rating to my Thumbtack profile, but now I don’t want it. Can I remove it?
Agregué una calificación de evaluación a mi perfil de Thumbtack, pero ahora no la quiero. ¿Puedo quitarlo?
Just like the reviews you received from Thumbtack customers, this review rating can’t be removed. Reviews are a major factor in being successful and getting hired on Thumbtack. So this review rating helps future customers get to know your past customer’s experience.
Al igual que las evaluaciones que recibió de los clientes de Thumbtack, esta calificación de evaluaciones no se puede eliminar. Las evaluaciones son un factor importante para tener éxito y ser contratado en Thumbtack. Por lo tanto, esta calificación de revisión ayuda a los futuros clientes a conocer la experiencia de sus clientes anteriores.
4. Resources
Frontline Reps will find a collection of resources in this section, including links to internal knowledge articles, and other relevant resources. Reps can share any external Help Center articles with pros to help them as needed. These resources may be referenced in the article or provide additional, related information.

1. Overview 
This internal KA has steps and details on how frontline reps connect their Salesforce account to the Admin tool. Connecting them allows reps to utilize the new functionality to validate and set User PKs on Contacts, Accounts, and Leads.
To improve the efficiency of data pulls and automate admin functionality within Salesforce, Salesforce has been integrated with the Admin platform. This update streamlines the "Find Thumbtack User" process by switching the data source from BigQuery to Admin for real-time data. 
Access to edit PKID fields (contact, account, lead) will be limited.
A new component has been added to facilitate PKID edits and updates on Salesforce records.
This update impacts workflows that involve PKID updates, particularly for the Boost, Sales, Support, and Trust and Safety teams. 
Frontline reps will need to follow specific steps to utilize this new functionality.
The Find Thumbtack User functionality is the same across the Contact, Account, and Lead pages.
Note: For any issues with the connection or functionality, submit a Helpdesk ticket.
2. Process
The Find Thumbtack User process involves two main parts: establishing the connection between Salesforce and Admin and then utilizing the Find TT User tool.
(Rep) Initial Setup: Establishing the Salesforce and Admin Connection
Frontline reps must first establish a connection between their Salesforce account and the Admin tool. This setup is required to utilize the Find Thumbtack User functionality. 
Follow these steps to establish the connection:
Log in to Salesforce.
Access Settings: Click on your profile icon in the top right corner and select "Settings".

Authorize in Okta: You will be redirected to Okta to authorize Thumbtack Admin. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the authorization.

(Rep) Using the Find TT User Tool: Locating Users and Managing PKID Information
(Return to contents)
Once the connection is established, frontline reps can use the Find Thumbtack User tool to locate users and manage their PKID information on the Contact, Account, and Lead pages.
From these pages, frontline reps can validate and set User PKIDs on the Contact, Account, and Lead pages.
Follow these steps to utilize the Find Thumbtack User tool:
Read-only Field: The PKID field is read-only on the record pages.
Locate the Component: To enter the PKID on the Contact, Account, or Lead page, a component is available on the right-hand side.
Enter and Search: Enter the PKID in the provided field and click "Search".

(Rep) PKID Update Confirmation and Error Handling: Understanding Validation Messages
The system will provide feedback to confirm the PKID update or indicate any issues.
Success: If the PKID is valid and not used on any other record, a success message will appear: "User PK has been updated for this Contact. You may need to refresh the page."
PKID Already Exists: If the PKID is already associated with another record, an error message will display the ID of the existing record (e.g., "Warning: PK already exists on a Contact with the following Id: 003WE00000LqmUHYAZ").
If Reps encounter this issue they should search for the record using the PKID in Salesforce and continue the workflow from the existing record.
Invalid PKID: If the PKID is invalid, you'll receive an error message: "Please enter a Valid PK ID."
