Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This KA outlines phone support etiquette and resources for Thumbtack's Support team. It details procedures for handling various call scenarios, including connection issues, callback requests, and three-way calls. The guide also covers outbound call protocols, call recording policies, and provides resources for reps, pros, and customers. This internal knowledge article aims to ensure consistent and effective phone support operations while adhering to legal requirements and company policies.

The Support team is available to help customers and pros from Monday through Friday. The phone support hours are 6am to 6pm MT on weekdays.
Frontline reps can refer to the Thumbtack Service Channels: Pro and Customer Support (Rep) KA for more info on support channels and hours of operation.
How access to phone support works
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section outlines how access to phone support is structured for both pros and customers, including priority levels and routing procedures.

(Frontline reps may hear this called ‘user experience assignment’ or ‘phone segmentation’ internally)

Both pros and customers have access to phone support. Pros and customers are segmented, which allows them to be routed to the appropriate team. However, segmentation no longer determines the type of support they receive.

Access to phone support is set by prioritization for pros
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section explains how and why Thumbtack prioritizes phone support access for pro users, detailing the criteria and implications for call routing.

When pros reach out for support, the level of priority their call is received will vary. The calls routed to Frontline reps are based on the skill level the rep is assigned to.
Priority: ideal pros are always be at the top of the queue and first to be helped by the next available rep. (Premier Pro Support queue - Priority)
Regular: All other pros are helped on a first-come, first-served basis. (Pro Support queue - Regular)
For a pro to be considered an ideal pro, they must meet the following criteria:
+1 activated service* for at least 14 days in the past 30 days.
Passed a background check.
Vacation mode on less than 14 days in the past 30 days.
*An active service refers to having targeting turned on and completing Enforced Minimum Requirements (EMR). This includes pros in their first 28 days after a purchase of a Sales Prepaid Package. Frontline reps can see the internal New Pro Activation and EMR to learn more about EMR. 
Frontline reps can see the internal Thumbtack Service Channels: Pro and Customer Support (Rep) KA to learn more about the different types of support Service offers.
Priority access to phone support for pros is updated within 24 hours 
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section clarifies the timeframe for changes to pro users' priority access to phone support, detailing how updates are processed and reflected in the system within a 24-hour period.
If an ideal pro no longer meets the criteria above, then the pro's priority routing will change to regular within 24 hours. Pros would no longer meet the criteria if they hide their business or turn targeting off for at least 14 out of the preceding 30 days.
If a pro becomes active, they will have access to phone support within 24 hours. If pros become inactive by turning off targeting, they will remain active until they have been inactive for 30 days.  

The Business Applications team can’t manually adjust an individual user’s experience to include phone support.  
NOTE: The "User Experience Assignment" in Salesforce does not determine the level of support a user is entitled to. Phone access is not determined by loyalty status. To verify a pro's loyalty status, Frontline reps must validate the information in Admin next to “Pro Loyalty Member Status.” Salesforce is no longer accurate. Don’t submit a Help Desk ticket about a loyalty program change unless it is incorrect in Admin.
2. Process
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section details various common phone call scenarios and provides specific steps and talking points to handle each situation effectively, ensuring a consistent and professional support experience.

Frontline reps should follow the applicable process below when working with a pro or customer via phone support. 
(Rep) Steps: How to handle a blocked user calling support
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section provides a step-by-step guide on how to properly handle support calls from users who are currently blocked from accessing phone support, ensuring consistent procedures are followed.

If a pro or customer who is blocked from phone support calls from a different phone number, Frontline reps should submit a request to the Advanced Service Team (using the Atlassian Assist app in Slack) to update the pro or customer contact info in Salesforce:
Navigate to the #service_global_help-and-escalations Slack channel.
Use a keyword like “Help others” or “Others” to trigger the Assist app workflow.
Select the "Global Help Others" request type and fill out the form with all necessary details. 
(Rep) Steps: How to handle a pro calling support through the customer queue
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section outlines the specific steps to take when a pro user mistakenly contacts support through the customer queue, ensuring they are appropriately rerouted and receive the correct level of assistance.

Frontline reps should follow the below steps if a pro calls support through the customer queue:

Let the pro know they’ve reached the customer queue and ask if they’d like to be transferred to the pro support team. 
▶ Talking point"I'm sorry, but you've reached our customer support line, and I'm unable to help you with your professional account. Would you like me to transfer you to our professional support team?
If the pro says yes, move to step 5.
If the pro says no, ask them if they have a customer account they’d like help with. 
▶ Talking point
"Do you have a Thumbtack customer account you'd like me to help you with?"
If the pro says no tell the pro they'll be transferred to the pro queue and move to step 5.
Talking point: "I'm sorry, but you've reached our customer support line, and I'm unable to help you with your professional account. Since you don't have a customer account. please hold one moment while I transfer you to our professional support team." 
If the pro says they can't get to support through the pro line:
▶ Talking point"One moment, and I'll transfer you to the professional line. When you select "pro," the phone system will offer to help you start a conversation. Thank you for calling."
Transfer the pro to the pro queue. See the internal Genesys | SMS & Chat (Rep) KA for more information. 
If the pro asks how they can be a part of the sales commitment program, offer to transfer the pro to a sales rep – don’t solve their problems. Frontline reps can follow the steps on the internal Sales and Prepaid Packages (Pro) KA.
(Rep) Steps: How to handle connection issues or disconnected calls
 
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section outlines the specific steps and procedures to follow when encountering connection issues or disconnected calls with pros or customers, ensuring a consistent and professional resolution process.

Frontline reps should follow these steps if unable to hear the caller or the call disconnected after receiving a call: 
Repeat the greeting and wait a few moments to see if the caller responds.
Ask again if the caller is still on the line: "Unfortunately, I can't hear you. If you can hear me, I’m going to disconnect this call and call you right back. Speak with you soon."
End the call.
Search for the phone number in Admin to see if there's an account tied to that number.
If an account exists add the user to Salesforce and use the phone number in Admin to call the user back.
▶ If the caller answersProvide the recorded call disclaimer and continue where the conversation left off.
Talking point: “This is (agent name) calling on a recorded line” or
Talking point: "I would like to let you know that this call is monitored or recorded for quality and training purposes"
▶ If the caller doesn't answer
Leave a voicemail (if the voicemail box is set up) letting them know that a follow-up email will be sent.
Send email template "General: phone connection issues."  
Send a follow-up email to the caller and address as much of the conversation as possible. Let the caller know that they can continue the conversation through email or call back in.
Add notes to the case.
Classify and close the case.
If an account doesn't exist in Salesforce or Admin, don’t attempt to call back. Close the case and classify the case as Pro or Customer > Ops > Routing > Phone > Disconnected [Call didn't go through or was dropped, unable to reach pro. (dead air, didn’t talk or another connection issue)]
(Rep) Steps: How to handle a callback requestor who doesn't answer
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section outlines the specific steps and procedures to follow when attempting to return a callback and the requester does not answer, ensuring appropriate documentation and follow-up actions are taken.

If a call comes in as a callback but the caller doesn’t answer, Frontline reps should follow these steps: 
 
Leave a voicemail (if the voicemail box is set up).
Search for the phone number in Admin to see if there's an account tied to that number.
If an account exists 
Add the user to Salesforce and send the template "Caller didn’t answer callback request."
If no user is found in Salesforce or Admin
Close the case and classify the case as Pro or Customer > Ops > Routing > Phone > Disconnected [Call didn't go through or was dropped, unable to reach pro. (dead air, didn’t talk or another connection issue)]
If the case is still there at the end of a shift, close the case and classify it as Pro or Customer > Ops > Routing > Phone > Disconnected [Call didn't go through or was dropped, unable to reach pro. (dead air, didn’t talk or another connection issue)]


(Rep) Steps: What to do if the caller says they're driving
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section provides the procedure for handling interactions when a caller informs them that they are currently driving, ensuring safety and efficient information delivery.

If a call comes in and the caller says they’re driving, Frontline reps should follow these steps:
Offer to send the caller an email with the information they're requesting, rather than explaining while they're driving.
Talking Point: "For your safety, I will send an email with information to use when you're in a safe place."


(Rep) Steps: How to handle frequent callers
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section provides a detailed guide on how to effectively manage interactions with frequent callers, outlining strategies to address recurring issues and encourage self-service.

If a pro or customer continuously calls Thumbtack about the same issues, Frontline reps should empower the caller to do things independently or direct them to another channel like email or chat.
Frontline reps should follow these steps when handling a frequent caller:
Take a minute to review the call history. 
Identify the frequency of calls, any repeated issues, and call notes.
Be sure to solve the caller's larger issues. For example:
If the caller has called in about adding media 10 times in the past, ask: “I noticed that you called in a few times about adding photos. Can we talk through how to do it together so next time you’ll be able to do it on your own?”
If the pro frequently calls for refunds, stick to the refund policy and make no exceptions. Frontline reps can also direct the caller to email or chat to request refunds instead.
Suggest the caller uses Thumbtack Help to find answers to their questions in the future. 
Share any helpful articles with the caller in a follow-up email.


(Rep) Steps: How to place a caller on hold
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section provides guidelines for effectively placing callers on hold during phone interactions, ensuring a positive customer experience and adherence to established hold time limits.

Frontline reps must follow these guidelines when placing a pro or customer on a hold: 
Phone Support: Hold time should be within two minute. 
If Frontline reps need more time, check in with the pro or customer before placing them on another hold. 
Non-Voice: Hold time and idle time should be within three minutes before checking in with the customer/pro. This is unless the agent advised of a specific time the hold would be.
 
To view the steps on how to place a call on hold or mute the mic, Frontline reps can follow the steps in the internal Genesys Phone System (Rep) KA > Steps: How to mute your mic and place a caller on hold.

When placing a caller on hold, Frontline reps can use the following talking points:
“I would love to investigate this further. I will place you on a brief hold, and check in with you shortly.”
“Permítame un momento en espera, con gusto puedo revisar más en detalle. Estaré con usted pronto.”
“I would love to investigate this further. I will need about three minutes to do so, and I will be back shortly.” 
“Permítame aproximadamente 3 minutos, con gusto puedo revisar en más detalle. En seguida regreso con usted.
(Rep) Steps: How to handle long wait times
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section provides guidance on how to address and manage caller concerns related to long wait times, including talking points and alternative resource suggestions to offer a positive support experience.

Frontline reps should not proactively address wait times. If a caller is upset about longer wait times, Frontline reps can use the following talking point and provide the resources listed below. 

Talking point for long wait times: "We apologize that you have experienced a long wait time, we are still committed to your success and growth. I'd be happy to share some resources you can use that wouldn't require waiting on the phone."
The following resources can be provided to pro or customer callers who don’t want to wait for phone support.
Pros and customers can contact Thumbtack support through chat or other contact methods instead.
Pros and customers can access Thumbtack's help articles and videos within the Help Center.
Pros and customers can self-submit bug reports and feedback.
Pros can attend workshops, webinars, and Community events.
Pros can check for Thumbtack's monthly Pro Newsletter with tips and FAQs. Pros should check their notifications settings to ensure they don’t miss out.

Resources
(Rep) How to handle transferring a call
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section details procedures for transferring calls, including both blind (cold) and consult (warm) transfers, to ensure efficient and accurate routing to other reps, skill groups, or internal/external parties.

Calls can be transferred to other reps, skill groups, campaigns, and internal or external parties. There are two methods of transferring:
Type of transfer
How it works
Blind transfer 
(cold transfer)
Frontline reps should rarely use this option. The call will be transferred to the receiving rep right away without speaking to the new recipient first. Frontline reps can also choose whether the call returns to them or if it's routed to the receiving agent’s voicemail if they don’t accept the transfer.
Consult transfer 
(warm transfer)
Consult transfers are best practice and should be used most often. Before transferring the call, Frontline reps should talk to the new rep and offer background details about the caller’s problem. 
NOTE: Frontline reps can transfer a call on any interaction. Frontline reps should do a consult (warm) transfer most of the time. 
Frontline reps should go to the internal Genesys Phone System (Rep) KA for the steps on how to transfer a call. 
For steps on transferring to the Spanish team, Frontline reps can see the internal Spanish Support Handoff | Service and Support.
(Rep) Steps: How to handle three-way calls
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section provides clear guidelines and procedures for managing phone interactions that involve a third party, ensuring a professional and effective resolution process while maintaining Thumbtack's policies.

When speaking with a pro or customer, Frontline reps may be asked to speak with multiple people on the line. 
NOTE: Frontline reps should never end a call because there’s a third party on the line. Instead, focus on giving both parties the best experience possible.
Situations
Steps to take
Talking points
Caller asks Frontline rep to initiate a three-way call
Help the caller as much as possible, but don’t add the third party to the phone call. 
Encourage the two parties to work out the details together.
Instead of adding them to this call, I’ll reach out to [name] after you and I are done talking. That way I can give you my full attention while I’ve got you on the phone. Let’s spend our time figuring out how I can help you with [topic of call].
I appreciate that you want to include [name]’s point of view. I’ll reach out to them individually so I can spend the full time on this call hearing your side of the story.
Caller wants to add another person during the call
Tell the caller it’s not necessary.
Thumbtack will reach out to the third party privately if a follow up is needed.
Instead of adding them to this call, I’ll reach out to [name] after you and I are done talking. That way I can give you my full attention while I’ve got you on the phone. Let’s spend our time figuring out how I can help you with [topic of call].
I appreciate that you want to include [name]’s point of view. I’ll reach out to them individually so I can spend the full time on this call hearing your side of the story.
Call is connected with both parties already on the line
Take the call as normal. 
Stay objective and encourage the two parties to work it out together. Remember, Thumbtack doesn’t take sides. 

Caller adds another person during the call
If the caller adds a third party to the call without warning, follow steps as if both parties had originally been on the call. 
Stay objective and encourage the two parties to work it out together.

(Rep) Steps: How to end an interaction and give the survey awareness spiel
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section details the proper procedures for concluding a phone interaction, including when to share survey information and the steps to finalize call handling, ensuring consistent and professional closing practices.

Once the caller’s issue has been handled and the call is over, Frontline reps should follow these steps:
Ask if there’s anything else the caller needs.
If the caller says yes, help them with their inquiry. 
If the caller says no, thank them for calling and make the caller aware of the survey Thumbtack will send out after the interaction (if applicable).
Talking point: “You may receive a survey within an hour. We’d appreciate it if you could tell us how we’re doing and how we’ve assisted you today.” OR 
Talking point:  “You may receive a short survey via email. It would be great if you could let us know how we did today.” 
Allow the caller to end the call or disconnect first. 
If they don't hang up in 10 seconds, the Frontline rep can disconnect the call.
Disconnect the call. See internal Genesys Phone System (Rep) KA for more information.
Should the Frontline rep say the survey awareness spiel?
Scenario details
DO say the survey awareness spiel if:
No pending action needed on the case 
Don’t say the survey awareness spiel if:
Account is on hold
Account was deactivated by Thumbtack
There's an issue for Trust & Safety
The caller is being transferred to another department (other than Sales)
The caller is in a hurry (Voice channel).
However, the Frontline rep can send a follow-up email to continue with the standard add value and survey spiel. 
If the current case was reopened and the previous rep already provided the survey awareness spiel. 
All cases that are Pending Thumbtack and Pending Customer Status. 
NOTE: Deliver the survey spiel after making any follow-up contacts. (e.g., mention this during callback or when sending follow-up email/sms).
3. Outbound calls
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section outlines the procedures for making outbound calls to pros and customers, including when these calls are necessary, how to properly initiate them, and the legal requirements for disclosing call recording.
(Rep) Steps: When to make an outbound call
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section clearly defines the specific scenarios and circumstances under which making an outbound call to a pro or customer is required to effectively resolve their support needs.

There are times when a Frontline rep is required to make an outbound call to a pro or customer to resolve their concerns. These are the situations where an outbound call would be made: 
The phone call line got disconnected
The pro or customer requested phone support
Review the user's experience assignment to confirm they qualify for phone support.
Escalation or supervisor callback. See the internal Standard Escalations and De-Escalation Guidelines (Rep) KA for steps

NOTE: When making an outbound call, Frontline reps must tell the customer or pro that the call is being recorded. This is a legal requirement and can't be forgotten.

For steps on how to make an outbound call, Frontline reps should follow the steps found in the internal Genesys Phone System (Rep) KA.
4. Call recordings
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section outlines the procedures for handling calls in which recording is discussed or requested, detailing both Thumbtack's policies and the steps to take in various recording-related scenarios.
Depending on the call recording situation, Frontline Reps will take the following steps:

Steps: How to handle situations where the caller wants to record the call themselves

Tell the caller: “I don’t consent to be recorded, but I’d like to continue this conversation and see how we can resolve this concern. Can you confirm that you've stopped the recording so we can continue?”
Listen for the caller's explicit verbal confirmation that the recording has stopped. Reps must hear the caller say this out loud. 
Important note: Silence, a topic change, or hesitation does not count as confirmation 
Once they confirm, continue the call and document the confirmation. (See documentation section below for what to log.)
If the caller refuses to confirm or hesitates: Disconnect the call. 
Tell the caller: "I want to help, but without confirmation that the recording is stopped, I cannot proceed, so I'll need to end the call here. Would you like to reach us by email, text, or chat instead?" Then follow the steps below to share the right contact info before ending the call."
If at any point during the call the rep suspects the recording is still active (e.g., active beeping or verbal slip-up): Disconnect the call.
Tell the caller: "It sounds like the recording is still active. As mentioned, I cannot proceed while recorded, so I'll need to end the call here. Would you like to reach us by email, text, or chat instead?"
Offer alternate channel options before disconnecting:
If a frontline rep needs to disconnect a call, they should ensure the caller is aware of other ways to contact support and how to do so. Use the internal Thumbtack Service Channels: Pro and Customer Support (Rep) KA for more information about these options.

If the caller asks why Thumbtack has this policy:
Frontline reps can explain: “Our policy does not permit callers to record agents. This is for privacy and security reasons.” 

Steps: How to handle call recording situations (Rep)
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For Frontline reps, this section details the specific procedures and guidelines for handling various scenarios involving call recording, including customer requests, refusal to be recorded, and requests for transcripts, to ensure compliance with legal requirements and company policies.
The caller doesn’t want to be recorded
If the caller asks about their privacy rights or wants more details on the recording policy: Direct the caller to Thumbtack's Privacy Policy (https://www.thumbtack.com/privacy).
If the caller doesn't want to continue, given the recording policy, tell the caller they can reach Thumbtack by email, text, or chat instead.
Steps: How to handle a caller asking for a transcript or recording of the call
When a caller asks for a transcript or recording of the call, frontline reps will follow these steps:
If the caller has a subpoena or court order: Escalate to the Trust and Safety Team.
If the caller doesn't have a subpoena or court order:
Let the caller know that Thumbtack records calls for quality assurance, and the recordings can't be released.
If they continue to ask about a recording, reiterate that recordings can't be released outside a formal legal process.

Guidelines: Requests for call recordings
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: For internal use by Frontline reps only, this section details Thumbtack's specific procedures and legal considerations regarding the release of call recordings, including when and why recordings are not shared.
INFORMATION IN THIS SECTION IS FOR INTERNAL ONLY
Thumbtack doesn’t release call recordings or chat and text transcripts without a subpoena or court order, even if the request is for a caller's own conversations. That's because Thumbtack doesn’t want call recordings or transcripts of specialists floating around in public. 
Thumbtack assumes every Frontline rep is doing a great job on calls, texts, and chats. But statements can be taken out of context to misinterpret a situation, and it's safer that Thumbtack doesn’t give out call recordings or transcripts.
See internal External Inquiries | Employment, Law Enforcement, Legal, Marketing, Press, Sales (Reps) KA for more information.

Perplexity Rebate Program (Customer)

Contents
Overview
Rebate terms and conditions
Program details
Customer experience
Do’s and don’ts
Process
Customer Steps: How to claim Perplexity rebate
Customer steps: How to claim payment in Hyperwallet
Talking points
Resources 
1. Overview

[Image: AD_4nXe1ZYomJHzRNpeGuui6DGejBU7ofSlyq1zCoWOJYotMmrHxOBDc8k_H2eEO4HlbwkiPQz-l6b0zhBofgsyyoIUnuv3qIOLx-x1X-vkJnscdam3gSmKP8Ox9PfeIDS5wLjCApsIAnQ]

Tl;dr: Thumbtack customers with a Perplexity Pro account can get rebates on Thumbtack projects.  
What: Thumbtack customers who also have a Perplexity Pro account are eligible for a one-time $50 rebate and nine (9) subsequent $25 rebates. 
Perplexity Pro is a paid subscription service that gives users access to the Perplexity AI search engine, which utilizes a large language model to process search queries and generate answers based on web search results. Similar AI search engines include ChatGPT and Google Gemini.

Why: Perplexity would like to add value to their Pro membership offering by giving their users discounted access to Thumbtack services.
How: To get the rebate, customers hire a pro through Thumbtack, pay them, get a receipt, and submit the Thumbtack x Perplexity rebate request form within 30 days of payment.
Once a rebate is approved, Thumbtack will send the customer the cost of their project, up to $50 for the first project and $25 for each of the following 9 projects, via our partner, Hyperwallet, to the customer's preferred payment method.
Rebate terms and conditions

User must have a Perplexity Pro account.
User must have a Thumbtack account in good standing.
The promo code is only valid for a maximum of ten uses and cannot be used if it has already been redeemed ten times.
Each rebate can only be used on one project.
If your rebate is approved, you’ll get the full $50 rebate (for the first rebate) if your project costs $50 or more (including tax and tip).
If your total project cost is less than $50, you’ll get a rebate for the cost of your project and lose the remaining amount.
This limit also applies to the later $25 rebates, where the project must cost $25 or more (including tax and tip).
The Thumbtack Pro who completes this project must have an active profile on Thumbtack and must have been contacted by them through Thumbtack.
User must submit the rebate request form with their receipt within 30 days of paying for the project.
This rebate cannot be combined with any other discount. Only one discount can be used per project. If you have multiple discounts available on your Thumbtack account, the Thumbtack x Perplexity rebate will be used first.
On-Demand bookings are not eligible for this rebate.
Thumbtack can end or cancel a discount, rebate, or promotion at any time. 
This rebate is subject to Thumbtack’s Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Customers can refer to the Thumbtack x Perplexity rebate terms and conditions article.
Program details

Launch Date: April 14, 2025
End Date: ~ March 31, 2026 
Rebate Details:
Thumbtack customers with a Perplexity Pro account are eligible for a one-time $50 rebate and nine (9) subsequent $25 rebates.  
Perplexity Pro users  will see the rebate offer starting April 14, 2025
Rebates must be applied to separate projects and cannot be stacked.  
Customers must submit the rebate request form within 30 days of payment.  
Impacted Users: Thumbtack customers who also have a Perplexity Pro account.  
Identify Impacted Users: The user will mention the Perplexity Pro rebate program or provide a Perplexity promo code.
Customer experience
There are two main entry points to the Thumbtack offer on the Perplexity platform for Perplexity Pro members:
Relevant search results about a potential Thumbtack project
Pro membership benefits page
Do’s and Don’ts (Rep)
When helping Thumbtack customers with a Perplexity rebate, support reps should follow these guidelines: 
Do direct them to the help center link for help with any questions.
Do explain how Thumbtack works and help the customer book a pro.
Don’t mention the rebate to customers who haven’t asked about it first.
2. Process

(Customer) Steps: How to claim Perplexity rebate
Customers with Perplexity Pro accounts will follow these steps to redeem their Perplexity rebate:
Hire a pro through Thumbtack and pay them. (Pay the pro through Thumbtack or use a payment method outside of Thumbtack if preferred.)
Get a receipt from your pro, as you’ll need a receipt to claim your rebate.
Go to the rebate request form within 30 days of payment and fill in the required information.
First name *
Last name *
Email used with their Thumbtack account *
Perplexity promo code *
Email address on their Perplexity's platform *
Pro business name who completed the project *
Total project cost *
Address where the work was completed *
Receipt * (file download)
Once the claim is approved, we’ll send the rebate through Hyperwallet. It may take up to one week for a rebate to be approved. 
The customer will get an email from Hyperwallet with instructions on how to create an account and choose how to receive their rebate. 
Important details about claiming a rebate
When requesting a rebate, customers must do the following: 
Complete the project and pay the pro (before claiming the rebate).
Submit the Thumbtack x Perplexity rebate request form with an attached receipt within 30 days of paying for the project

(Customer) Steps: How to claim payment in Hyperwallet
Once the customer’s claim is approved, Thumbtack will send funds to Hyperwallet to issue the customer's rebate as a payment.
Hyperwallet will send an email to the email on file. The email includes a Claim Payment button.
Clicking “Claim Payment” from the email, they will enter the Hyperwallet redemption flow. 
Hyperwallet will need details in order to send the payment. The customer will need to:
Select a payment option (PayPal, Venmo, etc.)
Provide profile details
Add account info
After claiming their rebate the customer can track their payment and will receive an email once their payment has been processed. 
Customers are sent a final email once the payment has been processed. The rebate will appear in the account the customer provided. The customer should reach out to Hyperwallet with any concerns or questions.
3. Talking points 
Frequently asked questions (FAQs) and answers for frontline reps.

English FAQ with answer
Spanish FAQ with answer
How do I claim my rebate?
¿Cómo reclamo mi reembolso?
Once you’ve completed a project and paid the pro, you’re ready to claim your rebate.
Submit proof of your project payment using this form. 
Once your claim is approved, we’ll send your rebate through our partner, Hyperwallet.
Follow the instructions in the email from Hyperwallet to create an account and choose how to receive your rebate. 
You can also check out our help article on how to claim your rebate to learn more.
Una vez que haya completado un proyecto y pagado al profesional, estará listo para reclamar su reembolso.
Envíe el comprobante de pago de su proyecto utilizando este formulario. 
Una vez que su reclamación sea aprobada, le enviaremos su reembolso a través de nuestro socio, Hyperwallet. 
Siga las instrucciones en el correo electrónico de Hyperwallet para crear una cuenta y elegir cómo recibir su reembolso.

También puede consultar nuestro artículo de ayuda sobre cómo reclamar su reembolso para obtener más información.
How will I know when my rebate is approved?
¿Cómo sabré cuándo se aprueba mi reembolso?
It may take up to a week for a rebate to be approved. Once it’s approved you’ll get an email from Hyperwallet.
La aprobación de un reembolso puede tardar hasta una semana. Una vez que se apruebe, recibirá un correo electrónico de Hyperwallet.
Does this offer expire? 
¿Esta oferta tiene fecha de vencimiento?
No, the offer does not expire.
No, la oferta no tiene fecha de vencimiento.
Can the offer be converted into cash value?
Se puede convertir la oferta en dinero en efectivo?
No, this offer cannot be converted into cash value.
No, esta oferta no se puede convertir en dinero en effective.
Do I have to use my credit on Thumbtack?
¿Tengo que utilizar mi crédito en Thumbtack?
Yes, this rebate is only available on Thumbtack. However, you’re free to choose whatever project and pro you’re interested in using for your project as long as it falls within the terms and conditions.
Sí, este reembolso solo está disponible en Thumbtack. Sin embargo, usted es libre de elegir cualquier proyecto y profesional que le interese para su proyecto, siempre que cumpla con los términos y condiciones.
Will I see my credits in the Thumbtack app?
¿Veré mis créditos en la aplicación Thumbtack?
No. This isn’t a credit you will see on your account. Instead, you’ll need to complete a project and submit your receipt for reimbursement. You can check out our help article on how to claim your rebate to learn more
No. Este no es un crédito que verá en su cuenta. En su lugar, deberá completar un proyecto y enviar su recibo para obtener el reembolso. Puede consultar nuestro artículo de ayuda sobre cómo reclamar su reembolso para obtener más información.
Is there a cost to sign up or use Thumbtack?
¿Hay algún costo por registrarse o utilizar Thumbtack?
There is no cost to sign up for Thumbtack or use Thumbtack. Pricing for projects will vary by category and depending on the pricing the pro sets.
No hay ningún costo por registrarse en Thumbtack ni por utilizar Thumbtack. Los precios de los proyectos varían según la categoría y los precios establecidos por el profesional.

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article provides Frontline Reps with information about the Performance dashboard (Market Level Insights) for pros. It outlines how pros can access the dashboard on both desktop and mobile, describes the various data points and insights available (such as performance summaries, budget summaries, lead information, and search results), and explains how pros can take action and provide feedback. This internal Knowledge Article ensures Frontline Reps are equipped to effectively guide pros in utilizing the Performance dashboard to grow their business.
The Performance dashboard (also referred to as  "Market Level Insights"), is a centralized data hub that provides pros with real-time analytics and market trends to drive business growth. This tool allows pros to move beyond high-level summaries and access granular data to refine their business strategies. 
Its primary functions are:
Performance Tracking: Monitoring key metrics (visibility, ranking, profile views, leads).
Data Exporting: Downloading lead-level performance data for custom offline analysis.
Market Analysis: Reviewing local customer search trends to understand demand.
Competitive Analysis: Comparing their business ranking against market competitors.
Growth Opportunities: Identifying geographic "sweet spots" with high-demand and low-competition.
Budget Management: Tracking weekly spending against allocated limits.
Pros can access the dashboard on desktop computers and laptops via the Performance tab for the best experience. It is also available on mobile web and the app by selecting "View Business Insights" on the Services page.
Updates
Starting April 6, 2026, some eligible newer pros may see an experiment in the Performance Dashboard. This experiment adds more educational guidance and reorganizes insights to help newer pros understand how Thumbtack works, what to focus on, and which actions may improve results during their first 14 days on Thumbtack.
For eligible pros:
Intro guidance remains through day 7 after activation.
After day 7, guidance updates weekly using the past 30 days of data.
The dashboard may prioritize guidance related to search coverage, visibility, response behavior, and lead spend.
Benefits of the Performance dashboard

The Performance dashboard offers several significant benefits for pros:
Data-driven decision making: By providing clear and detailed data, the dashboard enables pros to make informed decisions about their services, pricing, targeting, and overall business strategy.
Granular performance tracking: With the ability to download lead-level data, pros can perform custom offline analysis to track individual lead costs, customer details, and ROI.
Improved visibility: Pros can see where they appear in customer searches and understand how visible they are in their market.
Optimized budget management: The dashboard helps pros track their spending against their budget, allowing for adjustments to maximize return on investment (ROI).
Increased lead generation: By identifying high opportunity areas and recommended services, pros can focus their efforts to generate more leads.
Enhanced search ranking: Personalized recommendations help pros improve their ranking in search results, making them more discoverable to potential customers.
Actionable insights: The dashboard not only provides data but also actionable suggestions and the ability to make changes directly from the dashboard, such as adjusting lead prices or targeting preferences.
Feedback loop: Pros can share direct feedback about the dashboard, contributing to its continuous improvement and ensuring it meets their needs.
Essentially, the Performance dashboard serves as a centralized hub of information and tools that pros can use to gain a competitive edge, optimize their operations, and drive business growth on Thumbtack.
Performance Dashboard: Breakdown by section
The Performance Dashboard is organized into distinct sections, each providing targeted insights for Pros. This breakdown ensures Frontline Reps have a comprehensive understanding of the data points and filters available to effectively support Pros.
Performance summary
This section details the performance summary within the Performance dashboard, and explains the key data points and filter options that Frontline Reps can use to help pros understand their overall performance.

[Image: AD_4nXeHxiE0GDaovVCx_0t9XcXdTRJqv3QUvLzhyW8W-jrUXrqwGnQIsHaVaXeqYCM8ZKLsd4SWUp2LTjMwSRjeFTRbvRhP4FvSfhcgNngwNzD0mDMwUzFUNR0Zp9eLToQUFB6awDyA]

The "Your Performance Summary" provides a concise, high-level overview of the pro's performance.
Purpose for Reps: Use this to help pros understand key performance indicators and compare them across different timeframes and locations.
The Your Performance Summary is broken down into five key metrics:
Total searches in your market: The total number of customer searches in the pro's market for services they offer.
Searches you appear in: The count of times the pro appeared in customer search results for their services.
Profile views: The number of times a pro's profile was viewed by customers.
Leads: The total number of leads the pro received during the selected time period.
Hires: The number of times the pro was hired, as confirmed by both the pro and their customers.
Filtering Options
Located below the "Your Performance Summary," dropdown filters allow pros to adjust the data view by:
Business (if the pro manages multiple businesses)
Service category or all services
Timeframe (Last 7 days, Last month, Last 6 months)
Location
Download Lead Data
The “Download Lead Data” feature allows pros to export granular, lead-level performance details into a customizable CSV file for offline business analysis. This functionality is designed for pros who need to perform advanced reporting and analyze performance outside of the TT platform. This feature is web-only and not available in the app at this time.
▶ Pros can also access this feature from the Messages tabs by clicking Lead details under "Tools" in the left-hand column.

[Image: rtaImage]

Purpose for Reps: Use this section to guide pros who want to see a line-item breakdown of their leads, including customer names, phone numbers, and specific lead costs.

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ What the "Download lead details" screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ Information included in the CSV file
Pros have the ability to generate a CSV file containing granular lead information. The file includes:
Customer names
Customer number
Contact date
Business name
Category
Zip code
Contact link (navigates to messages)
▶ Lead cost**The “lead cost” export only provides the total amount paid (does not break down sales tax or discounts).If a pro wants a detailed breakdown of lead price, sales tax (if applicable), or discounts, they should still download their Receipts from their Payments page (Steps in the How to track my spending – Thumbtack Help article).Receipts include charges, credits, discounts, and refunds. Reps can refer to the internal Charges on Thumbtack: Payment Methods and Billing (Pro) KA for more details.
Refunded cost
Data Limits: Each CSV file is limited to a maximum of one year's worth of data, requiring a separate download for each year. 
Steps: How to download lead data (Pro)
To download a CSV of their lead performance data, pros will follow these steps:
Navigate to the Performance dashboard tab. 
Click Download lead details.
Choose a specific business or all businesses (if managing multiple).
Select a calendar year or custom date range.
Note: Date ranges are limited to a maximum of one year per download. To get two years of data, pros will run two separate downloads.
Click Download CSV to save the file to the device.
Once clicked, a banner will appear stating "Lead details downloaded." The file will be named "thumbtack_lead_data". 

Pros can also access this feature from the Messages tabs by clicking Lead details under "Tools" in the left-hand column.
Budget summary
This section explains the budget summary within the Performance dashboard, and shows how pros can view their weekly budget and the amount they spent each week, for the past six weeks. 

[Image: AD_4nXcMfrrWy3ICa6maK257EPSro_bLOoiLu2jZHXX4UV0islBGOuGtNQ1BU9OxAIrilD9kVGYKEdKzwc9ekKsIT5IGXbCAMNwf5TEKi-2vb-KvpQlwb9B8x_QVjs39qNgTd4sXFrRwtedG7-UlvR63d1Gm3F4]

The "Budget and amount spent each week" section of the Performance dashboard offers a budget summary detailing a pro's weekly budget and total spending over the last six weeks.
Purpose for Reps: Help pros assess if they are consistently hitting their budget and guide them on whether they should adjust it for optimal lead flow.
The Budget summary provides a graph comparing:
Your budget: The pro's allocated budget for that week.
Total dollars spent: The total amount of money the pro spent during that week.
Filtering Options:
Below the "Budget and amount spent each week" view, pros can refine the data using dropdown filters based on:
Business (for pros with multiple businesses).
Service category or all services combined.

Frontline reps can refer to the internal Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro) KA to learn more.
Leads and average cost per lead summary
This section details the Leads and average cost per lead summary on the Performance dashboard, showing pros their lead volume and average price per lead over the last six months. Frontline reps can use this to help pros assess the competitiveness of their lead prices.

[Image: rtaImage]

The "Number of leads you received, and average lead price per month" section provides pros with their lead volume and average price per lead over the last six months. 
Purpose for Reps: Use this to help pros assess the competitiveness of their lead prices.
The Leads and average cost per lead summary provides a graph comparing:
Number of leads: Number of leads the pro received per month (past 6 months)
Average lead price: The average cost per lead per month (past 6 months)
Filtering Options:
Below the "Leads and average cost per lead summary " header, pros can refine the data using dropdown filters by:
Business (if the pro has more than one)
Service category
Location
Frontline reps can refer to the internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA to learn more. 

Search results summary
The “Customer searches in your market” section of the Performance dashboard offers a clear breakdown of market demand versus the pros visibility, showing the "size of the pie" (total demand) compared to their "slice" (how often they are seen).
Purpose for Reps: Use this when helping pros to validate market demand and identify visibility gaps.

[Image: rtaImage]

This section provides a graph comparing market demand vs. pro visibility, specifically: 
Total customer searches in your market (Light colored bars): The total number of customers searching for the services the pro offers within their designated area.
Total searches you appeared in (Dark colored bars): The number of times the pros profile actually appeared in search results for those customers.
Pro stat: A summary percentage of relevant searches the pro appeared in over the last 6 months (e.g., 8%). For example: “You showed up in [#]% of searches for your services in your market in the last 6 months. Here are some ways to get seen more:.”
Actionable Steps to Improve
Thumbtack provides three specific suggestions in this section to help the pro bridge the gap between the "Total searches" and the "Searches you appeared in", which may include: 
Expand travel preferences: Increase their service radius to cover more geographic areas. (Clicking this brings the pro down to the Opportunity areas map on the dashboard)
Add more job categories: List additional services they are qualified to perform. (Clicking this takes the pro to their service page)
Increase budget: Adjust spending to ensure their profile continues to show up after daily or weekly limits are hit. (Clicking this takes the pro to their budget page)
Filtering Options:
Below the "Customer searches in your market " header, pros can refine the data using dropdown filters by:
Business (if the pro has more than one)
Service category
Timeframe
Location
Frontline reps can refer to the following KAs to learn more: 
Search Results Ranking Factors and Pro Visibility (Pro)
Targeting: Job Types and Travel Preferences (Pro) 
Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro) 
Ranking summary
The "How often you rank in the top 3 search results" section measures the pros' visibility in the most valuable search positions—the first three profiles a customer sees.
Purpose for Reps: Use this when helping pros to diagnose performance issues and prescribe specific behavioral changes.

[Image: rtaImage]

This section provides the pro with a ranking chart and key metrics that influence the pros search ranking: 
The pros visibility score: The percentage of time their profile appeared in the top 3 slots during customer searches over the last 30 days
Review Rating: The pros average star rating compared to top pros (Clicking “Get more reviews” takes pros to their reviews page)
Your Lead Prices: How competitive their pricing is (e.g., "Most competitive"). (Clicking “Adjust lead prices” takes the pro to their lead prices page)
Response Time: How quickly the pro replies to customers (Clicking “Improve response time” takes the pro the Here's a guide to getting hired with your messages – Thumbtack Help article”) 
Your Pro Rewards Status: Tracks the pros and how close they are to reaching the next level of recognition. (Clicking “See more about pro status” takes the pro to the “Pro Rewards” page)
Filtering Options:
Below the "How often you rank in the top 3 search results " header, pros can refine the data using dropdown filters by:
Business (if the pro has more than one)
Service category
Location
Frontline reps can refer to the following KAs to learn more: 
Search Results Ranking Factors and Pro Visibility (Pro)
Profile (Pro)
Reviews (Pro)
Lead Prices (Pro) 
Messaging Customers and Pro Responsiveness (Pro) 
Thumbtack Pro Rewards (Pro)
Opportunity areas
The "Opportunity areas" section of the Performance dashboard helps pros identify geographic "sweet spots" where they are most likely to win work.
Purpose for Reps: Use this when helping pros to visually encourage expansion and smarter targeting.

[Image: rtaImage]
It highlights locations where customer demand is high, but competition from other pros is low. The data is based on activity from the last 30 days and refreshes every Monday, ensuring the pro is making decisions based on current market trends.
Reading the Map
Purple Shading (Opportunity Level): The map uses color to show potential value. 
Darker purple areas indicate "Excellent" opportunities—places with many customer searches but fewer pros competing for them. 
Lighter purple indicates "Good" opportunities.
Yellow Blocks (Pros travel preferences): The yellow areas represent "Your current travel areas," showing exactly where their profile is currently set to show up for in search results. 
Performance Snapshot: A summary box evaluates the pros current coverage (e.g., You take jobs in 100% of high-demand areas in your market, for the service you have selected. Select another service to view opportunity areas.)
Interactive Features & Filters OptionsPros can click directly on the map to add new areas to their travel preferences, allowing them to quickly target those high-value purple zones.
In the “Opportunity areas” section, pros can refine the data using dropdown filters by:
Business (if the pro has more than one)
Service category
Frontline reps can refer to the internal Targeting: Job Types and Travel Preferences (Pro) KA to learn more. 
Other Performance and Recommendation Tools
In addition to the Performance Dashboard, pros may see several other recommendation and alert tools on their account to help them manage their business, spending, and lead flow. Frontline Reps should be aware of these tools to provide a complete picture of pro performance guidance.
Recommendation Cards (Carousel)
Summary for Reps: Pros may see these cards based on current market supply gaps. They encourage pros to complete an action (e.g., add a new service category, expand targeting preferences, improve response rate, or get more reviews). Sometimes these actions are for incentives like free leads or as a non-incentivized suggestion.
Internal KA for Details: Incentivized Recommendation Cards (Pro) 
Lead Price Recommendations (Carousel)
Summary for Reps: Eligible pros see personalized recommendations on how to get more leads. These are found on the service pages as a recommendation card. They are based on the pro's current quality score and their Lead Prices (bids). Pros may need to click "How to get more customers" to view them.
Internal KA for Details: Lead Prices (Pro)
Weekly Budget Recommendations
Summary for Reps: Pros are notified about their weekly budget through alerts and recommendations that appear on their services and leads pages. These appear when a pro is close to hitting their budget, has hit their budget, or needs to increase it to respond to a new lead.
Internal KA for Details: Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro)
Profile Strength
Summary for Reps: This is a dynamic score (not visible to customers) that tracks a pro's profile improvements and gives actionable tips on how to level up their profile. Following these tips helps pros stay more competitive in their market.
Internal KA for Details: Profile (Pro) | Article # 000007613
Key points
Here are the key points for Frontline Reps when helping pros with the Performance dashboard, with a specific focus on what each section is used for:
Overall Dashboard Purpose: The Performance Dashboard (or "Market Level Insights") is a centralized hub to give Pros data and analytics about their business and market to empower them to make informed decisions for growth.
Access: Pros can access the dashboard on desktop via the Performance tab or on mobile (app and web) by selecting "View Business Insights" on the Services page. Pros will have the best experience with the Performance dashboard on desktop, as the Opportunity area map is view-only on mobile web.
Filter options: Pros can use different filters in each section of the dashboard to adjust the data. Some have filters by Business, Service category, Timeframe, and Location.
The different sections of the Performance dashboard: 
Performance summary: Reps should use this section to help pros understand key performance indicators (like total searches, profile views, leads, and hires) and compare them across different timeframes and locations.
Lead Data Downloads: Pros can now export granular CSV files containing customer names, contact info, lead costs, and refund data. This is accessible via the Performance Dashboard or the Messages tab.
Budget summary: This section helps pros assess if they are consistently hitting their weekly budget and guides them on whether they should adjust it for optimal lead flow.
Leads and average cost per lead summary: Reps should use this to help pros assess the competitiveness of their lead prices by reviewing their lead volume and average price per lead over the last six months.
Search results summary: This section is used to help pros validate market demand and identify visibility gaps by comparing the total customer searches in their market (demand) against how often they are seen (visibility).
Ranking summary: This section provides tailored recommendations to Pros to improve their search ranking by showing comparisons to top Pros in their market (e.g., review ratings, response time) and their current rank status.
Opportunity areas: These sections help Pros identify growth opportunities by showing recommended geographic expansion areas and high opportunity service categories (based on customer searches and lead volume) within their market.
The dashboard is updated daily. Pros can see the last update timestamp at the bottom of the dashboard.
 Important Note: Starting April 6, 2026, some eligible newer pros may see an experiment in the Performance Dashboard.
The experiment adds more educational guidance to help newer pros understand how Thumbtack works and what actions to take early on.
Insights may be reorganized to reinforce where the pro should focus in their first 14 days.
Intro guidance remains through day 7 after activation.
After day 7, guidance updates weekly using the past 30 days of data.
The experience may prioritize guidance related to search coverage, visibility, response behavior, and lead spend.

2. Process
This section details the sections within the Performance dashboard. Frontline Reps can use this information to understand how pros navigate and utilize the dashboard, enabling them to provide effective support and guidance.
Steps: How to can access the Performance dashboard (Pro)
The Performance dashboard allows pros to gain insights and provides guidance on how they can grow their business. Pros can find their Performance Dashboard using these methods:
Desktop: Navigate to the Performance tab. 
Mobile (web or app): Tap Business insights in the Services tab.
Important Note: While the Performance Dashboard is accessible via mobile web browsers and the pro app, it is designed for the best experience on a desktop computer or laptop. Mobile users will see a message stating, "For the best experience, try viewing these insights on a laptop or other computer." Additionally, on mobile devices, the Opportunity area map is limited to view-only.

▶ What the “View business insights” looks like from the Services tab
The image below illustrates the mobile access point, showing a section of the Pro app's Services page. Under the “Activity this week” header, the button labeled "Business insights" is the gateway to the Performance Dashboard.

[Image: rtaImage]

 
Steps: How to take action on the Performance dashboard (Pro)
This section details the direct actions pros can take using the data and features within the Performance Dashboard. Frontline Reps can use this information to effectively guide pros on how to optimize their settings directly from the dashboard.
Recommendation to adjust lead prices: 
In the lead price summary or "Number of lead you received, and average lead price per month" section of the dashboard, the pro is shown how competitive their lead prices are. There's a call-to-action button to adjust their lead prices, letting pros easily adjust their prices.
Section in this KA: Leads and average cost per lead summary
Recommendations to help with search visibility:
In the search summary or "Customer searches in your market" section of the dashboard, pros will see recommendations on how they can be seen more in customers' searches. Pros can click on the personalized tips to be taken to adjust their settings in their account. For example: expand travel preferences, add more job categories, or increase budget.
Section in this KA: Search results summary
Recommendations to help with their overall ranking:
In the ranking summary or "How often you rank in the top 3 search results" section of the dashboard, pros can see how competitive they are with their reviews, lead prices, response time, and pro rewards status. The pro will see call-to-action buttons for each of these, which navigates the pro to the applicable page to complete an action or learn more. For example: edit lead prices, get more reviews, etc.
Section in this KA: Ranking summary
Add opportunity areas to targeting preferences:
The Opportunity areas map is clickable, letting pros add the area to their targeting settings for the service. However, the map is view-only on mobile.
Section in this KA: Opportunity areas
Steps: How to share feedback on the Performance dashboard (Pro)
 This section explains how pros can submit feedback on the Performance dashboard. Collecting feedback from pros is important for continually improving the Performance dashboard.
It is essential to collect feedback from pros to continuously enhance the Performance dashboard. Pros are encouraged to share their opinions on the features they find most valuable and what they hope to see added in the future.
Pros can submit their feedback directly through the Performance dashboard . At the bottom of the page, they will find a "Let us know" prompt. Clicking this leads to a feedback form.


[Image: rtaImage]

2. Talking points
This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros about the Performance dashboard (Market Level Insights). Use these talking points to ensure consistent and accurate messaging regarding its features and benefits.
Overview of the Performance dashboard

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
What’s the performance dashboard? 
¿Qué es el Performance Dashboard ("Panel de rendimiento")?
The Performance Dashboard is a tool designed to provide you with the market insights and lead-level data necessary to make informed decisions and grow your business on Thumbtack.

Customer search data. See what services customers are searching for and where your business shows up so you can tailor your offerings and business profile. 
Lead insights and average price. Understand which months have more lead competition and how much you’ve spent for leads over a period of time. 
Downloadable lead data: Export your specific lead details, including customer contact info and lead costs, into a CSV file for your own offline analysis.
High opportunity areas: Identify market areas with high customer demand and low competition to strategically expand your reach.
Search improvement recommendations: Receive tailored recommendations to improve your search ranking and see how you compare to competitors. 
Leave feedback on the dashboard: Share your thoughts directly through the dashboard to help us build the features that matter most to your business
El Panel de rendimiento es una herramienta diseñada para darle información del mercado y datos a nivel de prospecto para que usted pueda tomar decisiones informadas y hacer crecer su negocio en Thumbtack.
Datos de búsqueda de clientes. Vea qué servicios buscan los clientes y en qué lugar aparece su negocio, para que usted pueda ajustar sus servicios y el perfil de su negocio.
Información de prospectos y precio promedio. Entienda en qué meses hay más competencia por prospectos y cuánto ha gastado en prospectos durante un periodo.
Datos de prospectos descargables. Exporte los detalles de sus prospectos, incluida la información de contacto del cliente y el costo del prospecto, en un archivo CSV para su propio análisis fuera de Thumbtack.
Áreas con alta oportunidad. Identifique áreas del mercado con alta demanda de clientes y baja competencia para ampliar su alcance de forma estratégica.
Recomendaciones para mejorar la búsqueda. Reciba recomendaciones personalizadas para mejorar su posición en los resultados de búsqueda y vea cómo se compara con otros profesionales.
Deje comentarios sobre el panel. Comparta sus comentarios directamente desde el panel para ayudarnos a crear las funciones que más le importan a su negocio.
Performance Dashboard experiment update
This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros about the Download Lead Details feature. 

English talking point
Spanish talking point 
Q: Why does my Performance Dashboard look different?
Q: ¿Por qué mi panel de rendimiento se ve diferente?
A: Thumbtack may test updates to the Performance Dashboard for some newer pros. In this experiment, the dashboard may add more educational guidance and reorganize insights to help pros understand how Thumbtack works, what to focus on, and what actions may improve results in their first 14 days.
A: Thumbtack puede probar actualizaciones del panel de rendimiento para algunos profesionales nuevos. En este experimento, el panel puede agregar más orientación educativa y reorganizar la información para ayudar a los profesionales a entender cómo funciona Thumbtack, en qué enfocarse y qué acciones podrían mejorar sus resultados durante sus primeros 14 días.
Download lead data
This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros about the Download Lead Details feature. 

English talking point
Spanish talking point 
Q: Why should I use the lead data download?
¿Por qué debería usar la descarga de datos de prospectos?
A: This tool allows you to download granular data for every lead, making it easier to analyze your performance and integrate Thumbtack data into your own business workflows.
Esta herramienta le permite descargar datos detallados de cada prospecto, lo que facilita analizar su rendimiento e integrar los datos de Thumbtack en sus propios procesos de trabajo.
Q: What information is included in the CSV file and what are the limits?
¿Qué información incluye el archivo CSV y cuáles son los límites?
A: When you download your lead data, the file includes customer details like names and phone numbers, the date they contacted you, the specific lead cost, and any refunded amounts. You can customize the report for a specific business or all your businesses. One thing to note is while you can select a calendar year or custom range, each export is limited to a maximum of one year of data.
Cuando usted descarga sus datos de prospectos, el archivo incluye datos del cliente, como nombres y números de teléfono, la fecha en que se comunicaron con usted, el costo específico del prospecto y cualquier monto reembolsado. Usted puede personalizar el reporte para un negocio específico o para todos sus negocios. Tenga en cuenta que, aunque puede elegir un año calendario o un rango personalizado, cada exportación está limitada a un máximo de un año de datos.
Q: How do I download my lead data?
¿Cómo descargo mis datos de prospectos?
A: To download your lead data, you can use either the Performance Dashboard or your Messages tab, depending on which view you prefer.
From the Performance Dashboard: Go to the Performance tab, click Download lead details and select a calendar year or custom range.
From the Messages Tab: Navigate to your Messages, click Lead Details, and select a calendar year or custom range.
Puede descargar sus datos de prospectos desde el Panel de rendimiento o desde la pestaña Mensajes, según la vista que usted prefiera.
Desde el Panel de rendimiento: Vaya a la pestaña Performance, seleccione Download lead details ("Descargar detalles de prospectos") y elija un año calendario o un rango personalizado.
Desde la pestaña Mensajes: Vaya a Messages ("Mensajes"), seleccione Lead Details ("Detalles del prospecto") y elija un año calendario o un rango personalizado.
Q: Can I download multiple years of lead data? 
¿Puedo descargar varios años de datos de prospectos?
A: Yes, you can download data from multiple years. However, each download is limited to a maximum of a one-year date range. To download multiple years, you'll  run a separate download for each year.
Sí, usted puede descargar datos de varios años. Sin embargo, cada descarga está limitada a un rango de fechas de un máximo de un año. Para descargar varios años, haga una descarga por cada año.
Q: What if I want a full breakdown of lead cost that the export doesn’t provide?
¿Qué pasa si quiero un desglose completo del costo del prospecto que la exportación no incluye?
A: The lead data export provides a high-level view of your lead costs and customer details. If you need a more granular, line-item breakdown of every transaction and fee, I recommend visiting the Payments tab in your account, where you can view and download receipts. I appreciate you sharing what data is most useful for your business; I will be sure to share this feedback with our product team. If you have additional thoughts in the future, you can submit them directly through the "Let us know" link at the bottom of your Performance Dashboard.
La exportación de datos de prospectos ofrece una vista general de sus costos de prospectos y de los detalles del cliente. Si usted necesita un desglose más detallado, por concepto, de cada transacción y tarifa, le recomiendo ir a la pestaña Payments ("Pagos") en su cuenta. Ahí puede ver y descargar recibos.
Gracias por compartir qué datos son más útiles para su negocio. Compartiré estos comentarios con nuestro equipo de producto. Si usted tiene más ideas en el futuro, también puede enviarlas directamente con el enlace Let us know en la parte de abajo de su Panel de rendimiento.
Update Frequency of dashboard Stats

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
How often are the stats on the performance dashboard updated?
¿Con qué frecuencia se actualizan las estadísticas en el panel de rendimiento?
The dashboard is updated daily. You can see the last time it was updated at the very bottom of the dashboard. 
El panel se actualiza diariamente. Puede ver la última vez que se actualizó en la parte inferior del panel.
