1. Overview
▶ KA summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) provides a comprehensive overview of the "Earnings" page for pros, detailing how customer payments are processed, displayed, and deposited into the pros bank accounts. 
This KA is designed to help frontline reps:
Quickly understand and explain a pro's payout experience when pros contact support. 
Foundational understanding of how this page helps pros track their incoming funds, review customer payments, and monitor deposit statuses.
The Earnings page is a pro's central hub for all money the pro receives from claimable jobs (and Thumbtack pay before feature was removed). It provides transparency into a pro's incoming funds, showing a clear history of customer payments and their deposit statuses.
The Earnings page is divided into a few main sections:
Deposit account: This section displays the deposit accounts (bank account and debit card) a pro has linked to their Thumbtack account and their setup status.
Transactions Tab: This tab provides a detailed list of individual payments received from customers.
Deposits Tab: This tab details the actual payouts (collections of one or more customer payments) sent to the pro's bank account, including their status and expected arrival dates.

[Image: AD_4nXdz0ilMof-gwJDbF6ixOSrHEtFMZ9hTia6SSIwxHoeFdNH0tQIxY_pBqD3LSXOyakzhTCLtkGPEsTKRP9Qms7ChDuFo8PJWda7hEIezaYtwtHbOPD8CMwp5JUgFABQJXPM-hae-jg]

(Image above: A screenshot of a pro's Earnings page on the web, showing both the "Transactions" and "Deposits" tabs, along with the "Deposit accounts" section at the top, which displays the linked bank account and debit card for deposits.)
Standard payouts and Instant Payouts

Frontline Reps can explain the differences between standard and instant payouts to pros by referring to the comparison  provided in this section. Understanding these distinctions will help pros choose the most suitable payout method for their needs.
The table below provides a comparison of standard payouts (the default option) and instant payouts.

Payout structures
Standard Payout
Instant Payout
Fee
No fee (free)
1% fee
Payout speed
3-4 business days
30 minutes (or less, depending on bank)
Payout window
Available after the 24 hour instant deposit window
Thumbtack will initiate payment processing as soon as the prepaid job is marked "done." Available only within 24 hours. If not selected within this window, or once the pro's bank starts processing the payment (typically 24 hours after), the payment automatically transitions to a standard payout.
Destination
Bank Account
Debit Card
Requirements
Must have direct deposit set up
Must have direct deposit set up. 
Must meet eligibility requirements and add a debit card
Minimum Amount
N/A
$50
 
Thumbtack uses Stripe as its trusted payment partner to process both standard and instant payouts. Reps can learn more in the General payment information section below.
General Payment Information: Security and Confirmation
Thumbtack uses Stripe to process payments, a secure site that keeps bank routing and account numbers encrypted and confidential. Thumbtack does not store pros' sensitive banking information directly. Stripe is a certified PCI Service Provider Level 1, which is the most stringent level of certification available in the payments industry. All card numbers are encrypted. Pros can find more information on the Security at Stripe article. 
Confirming Payment Success: When a customer pays, Thumbtack sends the pro an email receipt. Thumbtack also sends notifications in their account to let them know the payment has been sent and when funds are ready for use. If there are any concerns with a payment or the pro's direct deposit account or debit card, Thumbtack will notify the pro directly.
Deposit account statuses 
The Deposit accounts section of the Earnings page indicates the setup status of the pro's direct deposit. Setting up direct deposit is required for the pro to receive payment for a claimed job. This section is also where pros can manage their linked deposit accounts, including their bank account for standard direct deposits and their debit card for instant deposits.
Reps may see the following statuses under the "Deposits accounts" section of the Earnings  page when helping pros:

Status
Deposit accounts message
Details
In product view
Verified accounts
No message. It shows the pros of deposit accounts.
The pro's direct deposit account (bank account) and instant deposit account (debit card) is verified and ready to receive payments.

[Image: AD_4nXdLjzL8nNoj2rc4xuzhM588_01VzX9eBaAGi-RkZdVL2xaEn58yUnBFW6aHI016te6yf0qE_fwa-xjprTdnHeAnf72_o7iAHsVSy0HCTGDHjCc0H0MiyUqQPvxKrdzZISB1jTzpTg]

No bank account linked
“No account linked. Add your bank to get paid through Thumbtack”
The pro needs to add their bank information. This often means the pro exited the direct deposit setup process early.

[Image: AD_4nXf9-NbsROW1415fqN-zhnslTzqgWaUqFM4Yr5IDIUZMLQ7ROWgj6GCMYpDpIoG3Pk9NggqPjcGHBYGVCWCDdA9IuY6g-qJPXA6v_7jken0rI_WDg4E1ZRxwSLVnVmG6XBpBd10a]

Bank account pending verification
“Pending verification. We’re verifying your information and will let you know once it’s complete. 
The account information the pro submitted is currently under review by Stripe (Thumbtack's payment processing partner). This typically takes 1-3 business days.

[Image: AD_4nXf4d5b94yiof1mBnLxD31C3t0Ow4tGjlW_puoQElB4hM10X6AF0Rw9UHPj7u1dAawGIVJwWZwuWlLXWlvbBSgOwK3QXF2bLqrZi9ck1Wku7tK7qKmtlSTpAUpEJ8j840nTlKzbTKQ]

Bank account issues
“There’s an issue with this account. Please update your bank.”
There is a problem with the bank account information the pro entered. This could be due to incorrect routing/account numbers, or a broader issue with the pro's bank. The pro may need to update their bank details or contact their bank directly.

[Image: AD_4nXchJop4P3IokNE5PInElAxYxnbHsSg_XGvPk8HQ22nsqgLrTGtdEjGRsu-WraN7qd6yvEAiM1JY5Oj_PJOUIRLpya93JghebKtwNkAE5fOFtF0AoHujh7tELRGbIgByXgVmS0i8iA]

Debit card issue
“There’s an issue with this account. Please update your debit card.” 
There is a problem with the debit card information the pro entered. This could be due various reasons. The pro may need to update their bank details or contact their bank directly.

[Image: AD_4nXdl8iWvd9I1D2t-u7RpsKyCwmzhxrk4wRUXvY43Wirxlb90Dpgq3gCIbm2lQIwk0OfznxCxekDnD4Rd9ZqiXxdsXy3kDd4xda3c2mQuKG51zmZWHU45FDr_NQlqXVswW0DcaSXdwA]

Pros seeking to update their deposit accounts can find guidance in the How to set up direct deposit – Thumbtack Help article for bank accounts (standard deposits) and the What is instant deposit? – Thumbtack Help article for debit cards (instant deposits).
For detailed setup, update, or troubleshooting verification issues related to direct deposits, reps should refer to the internal Direct Deposit and Stripe KA.
Transactions Tab: Customer payment)
The "Transactions" tab on the Earnings  page provides a comprehensive list of all individual payments a pro has received, seen in the image below. 
▶ What the transactions tab looks like:

[Image: AD_4nXdiIIX9TDDAH6aFP0j_2OQ9Zxv6BFZawHn6ooE3Fktdwp35JUkClVjAOVjtuADEPliTvq9E3hIqMEOJhk_NG7AQbIOxKgNlyA3y2yKTabR-9D_pRLrUXWiXDRDautlx6ixYaRi0GQ]

Claimable job payments show up here (Thumbtack Pay transactions also showed up here prior feature removal). Payments typically take 2-3 business days to process, unless using instant deposits. Each entry represents a single payment, providing individual records of customer activity. The individual records include details such as the: 
Customer's name
Service provided
Amount paid.
Payment initiation date (not pending or completed statuses)
Clicking on an individual records brings the pro to the messenger with that customer as seen in the image below. These transactions are then grouped and sent as deposits to the pro's bank account. See Deposits Tab (Payout Statuses below.
▶ What individual payments look like in the messenger
These transactions are then grouped and sent as deposits to the pro's bank account (see +Understanding the Deposits Tab (Payout Statuses)+ below).

[Image: rtaImage]

One thing to note is that pros and customers don’t receive a detailed invoice for any payments exchanges. However, both will receive receipt of payment via email. Pros can see a record of payments on their Earnings tab.  
Transaction statuses
This table outlines the various statuses a transaction can have on the Earnings page's "Transactions" tab, along with a brief explanation of what each status means for the pro.

Transaction status
Status meaning 
Claimed job
The pro has been paid for a job the pro claimed and marked as done. 
Customer refund
Funds were returned to the customer, resulting in a debit from the pro's account.
If you see “Customer payment,” this was a customer who paid the pro through Thumbtack Pay prior to the feature being removed. Reps can refer to the internal Thumbtack Pay (In-Product Payments) KA. 
For claimable jobs, reps should refer to the internal Claimable Jobs (Pro) KA. 
Deposits Tab (Payout Statuses)
The Deposits tab on the Earnings  page shows the actual payouts (collections of one or more customer payments) that have been sent to the pro's linked bank account. This is where a pro can track the status and expected arrival of their funds.
Deposits may be grouped together: Stripe, Thumbtack's payment processing partner, tends to batch payouts on a daily basis, resulting in some payments being batched as a single deposit even if they originate from multiple individual customer payments. 
Additionally, to qualify for instant deposits, a pro needs a history of receiving at least three separate payouts. Pros can learn more on the What is instant deposit? – Thumbtack Help article.
▶ What the Deposits tab looks like

[Image: AD_4nXfDn9oylrWAdX8eNJo_2d7lnnzerfQ4e4ghNms8sgZyDQsG9U4Dj1-h2jakLbRAArOKZrpu5q8ZM1SQ3HCFuHCz6cP2sdN7GRHewYueNPNSgKpaQ4qRN6eChS5Oo4UcbCwOD8aWGg]

Deposit payout icons and status meanings
Here’s a breakdown of the different deposit payout status icons a pro might see, along with their meanings and descriptions: 

Deposit Icon
Deposit Status
Deposit Description 

[Image: AD_4nXdAMU2VE75NKsEK4SnYQbiwLizoz5ey9DnQUSlJA1aYl6aDoPONDIafnX65qcsSdM8GYvUDhM8JxK1VfAn2VhEp4UiCMjV4S4FOnBKvA7sY9oCg0pRl8CCZ2RIdiwrVrjheADuC]

Pending
This indicates the anticipated date the pro's funds will be available in their bank account for a pending deposit. Standard deposits typically arrive within 3-4 business days

[Image: AD_4nXcDtl8-M8fxc58roomM0-lWjA_Wb7DIl3qlKR85lLtmvvahMsYJ32-6yU8l3YRgpgMjwaSXup7rGEVHaXbmOC9_qGabKksx746V5bS5hfysv0Q0fnLV1fdoTAZgAgxwZALo-JoiGA]

Standard Deposit 
A standard deposit has been sent to the pro's bank account. These funds typically take 3-4 business days to appear. This icon is used for standard deposits.

[Image: AD_4nXcxVMKGNs80O8QDhrb0KLWpKhjKDXBoYRyN0eg8IBGQHRJUgsS4sAZfxjtc4YPQ-b-1mJxu8HklGAis-URPB4pDXmJBkBAGssfXs2aZ62fXnkv3q0J2qSd6V_3Z0Zm0ud0GFosg6g]

Issue with Deposit
The standard deposit could not be completed and the funds were not sent to the pros bank account. A specific reason for the failure will be displayed next to this status. Common reasons are detailed in the Failed Deposit Reasons table below.

[Image: AD_4nXfDoIFNwoN87FiKMNe_RGEYvTTso9I7r5HhEddFjogyXFixITH-slSe1K-XnZYKsA-yIAmB5uOnLjzy2zWrStb4olGIRANxKN1J0crV__GE0k8KWIQofzEZBPk3ko7mdFhsgKejWA]

Negative payouts
(Withdrawal)
This indicates a negative payout has occurred, meaning funds were debited from the pro's account, often for a refund or adjustment.

[Image: AD_4nXdzBjbxpTWF2kAAforT6r_AnzeXnKEWTIG5eGaF9Q7srfDuIJ7AiRLXWvW_YMy-UMkt3vi0NXQum5YO-KobM_89jmhlHVj9QoWFUyKowb223UYUhrRpPlHFVBzCukO_iPj0hym8cg]

Instant Deposits 
An instant deposit has been successfully sent to the pro's debit card. These funds typically appear within 30 minutes. This icon is used for instant deposits.

[Image: AD_4nXcqxuiBDLZ_NGrypn2UhdCNa3X5Q7dBxh6AU5yPSFC0bYuQ4zn3u_tnSiWLy5PuudO0TGrFSHBlPviMvEJXwWg_W6IQIlzc8697Q0lbl6A4b4PYnqFtvj_yi7CxJRxCWQIOEHUO]

Instant Deposit failed 
The instant deposit could not be completed and the funds were not sent to the pros debit card. A specific reason for the failure will be displayed next to this status. Common reasons are detailed in the Failed Deposit Reasons table below.
If a deposit has any issues, reps can refer to the Failed Deposit Reasons below. 

Payout Window Clarity:
Pros can request instant deposits soon after a customer pays them, and they have 24 hours to select an instant deposit. Once the pro's bank starts processing the payment (typically 24 hours after the customer pays the pro), instant deposits are no longer available. The green banner on their Earnings tab will be replaced with a grey one informing them that funds cannot be instantly deposited. This means the deposit is now processing as a standard payout.
Failed Deposit Reasons:
When a standard deposit or an instant deposit fails, a specific reason for the failure will be displayed next to that status icon. Listed below are common reasons a deposit may fail and how to help the pro: 
▶ The card used has been reported lost or stolen
Error message: "The card used has been reported lost or stolen. Please contact the issuing bank for clarification.
Description: This indicates that the debit card linked for the pro's Instant Deposit has been flagged by their issuing bank for security reasons.
Action for pro: The pro should contact their issuing bank for clarification and resolution regarding their card's status.
Talking point for reps if a pro says: “My payout showed my card was reported lost or stolen, but that's not true!” 
"I understand why you would be concerned seeing that message. This status is provided directly by your issuing bank for security reasons. Thumbtack does not have further details on why your bank flagged this. The most important step for you is to contact your bank to clarify the status of your card and resolve the issue. They can provide you with the most accurate information."
▶ The card used was invalid
Error message: "The card used was invalid. This usually means the card number is invalid or the account has been closed. Please verify card details before retrying."
Description: The card details linked for the pro's Instant Deposit are either incorrect or the associated account has been closed.
Action for pro: The pro should double-check the card number, CVC, and expiration date in their settings. If details appear correct, the pro should contact their bank to verify the account's status.
Talking point for reps if a pro says: “My deposit failed, and it says the card used was invalid.” 
"When a deposit fails because the card used was invalid, it usually means there's a small error in the card details linked for your Instant Deposit, or the account connected to that card might be closed. Please double-check your card number, the CVC (security code), and the expiration date you have on file in your Earnings pages. If everything looks correct, please contact your bank directly to verify the account's status."
▶ Bank account details on file are probably incorrect. No bank account could be located
Error message: "The bank account details on file are probably incorrect. No bank account could be located with those details.",
Description: This indicates that the bank account information on file for the pro's direct deposit may be incorrect, or their bank could not be located using the details provided.
Action for pro: The pro should carefully review and update their bank account details in their Earnings settings. If they are sure the details are correct, the pro should contact their bank to confirm their account details and ensure it's active and able to receive transfers.
Talking point for reps if a pro says: “My deposit failed, and it says the bank account details on file are probably incorrect. No bank account could be located with those details.”
 "This message indicates that the bank account information on file for your direct deposit may be incorrect, or your bank could not be located using the details provided. This can happen if there's a typo in the routing or account number, or if the account is no longer active. Please carefully review and update your bank account details in your Earnings pages. If you're sure they are correct, contact your bank to confirm your account details and ensure it's active and able to receive transfers."
▶ The bank no longer supports transfers to this card
Error message: "The bank no longer supports transfers to this card."
Description: The pro's bank has declined the attempt to send the pro's funds. This is a general decline and can be due to various reasons (e.g., security flags, temporary holds, transaction limits).
Action for pro: The pro should contact their bank directly to understand why this policy exists and if alternative solutions are available.
Talking point for reps if a pro says: “My deposit failed, and it says the bank no longer supports transfers to this card.”
"This message typically indicates a specific policy from your bank regarding transfers to that particular card. It's not an issue with Thumbtack's processing, but rather a decision by your bank. To understand why this policy exists and if there are alternative solutions, you will need to contact your bank directly."
▶ The bank has declined this transfer
Error message: "The bank has declined this transfer. Please contact the bank before retrying."
Description: The pro's bank has declined the attempt to send the pro's funds. This is a general decline and can be due to various reasons (e.g., security flags, temporary holds, transaction limits).
Action for pro: The pro should contact their bank directly to understand why this policy exists and if alternative solutions are available.
Talking point for reps if a pro says: “My deposit failed, and it says the bank has declined this transfer.”
"When your bank declines a transfer, it means they've blocked the funds from being sent to your account. This can happen for various reasons, such as security flags, temporary holds, or transaction limits. Thumbtack does not receive the specific reason for the decline. The best way to resolve this is to contact your bank directly and ask them for the exact reason for the decline."
▶ The pro's account has insufficient funds to cover the transfer
Error message: “Your account has insufficient funds to cover the transfer."
Description: This occurs when Thumbtack attempts to debit funds from the pro's account (e.g., to process a customer refund that was previously sent to the pro), and there are not enough funds available.
Action for pro: The pro should ensure sufficient funds are in their account if a debit is expected for a refund or other adjustment.
Talking point for reps if a pro says: “My deposit failed, and it says my account has insufficient funds to cover the transfer.”
 "This specific 'Failed deposit' message means that Thumbtack attempted to debit funds from your account, and there weren't enough funds available to cover the transfer. This typically occurs when we need to recover a payment, for example, to process a customer refund that was previously sent to your account. Please check your bank account balance to ensure you have sufficient funds for any expected debits."
Transition from Instant to Standard Payout
If a pro does not select Instant Deposit within the 24-hour window (or if their bank begins processing the payment), the funds will automatically transition to a standard payout. The pro's Earnings tab will show the payment as "Pending" (replacing any "Available for Instant Deposit" banner), indicating it is now being processed for a standard direct deposit.
▶ Banner: Available for instant deposits

[Image: AD_4nXc202TDGplInXkQHgYk6js9jcWrC2k02MDg-jZ3Mx7BERBK2kiDhO5XwablIsflnl5HkxOHSSYY8AktYDR9Aer8t1d9TwMCNaMpswXbo0Jfr2NAvja38RM9_PxUX5YbZMBzv7y8]

The image above depicts the green banner that says “Available for instant deposit. Get paid in minutes for a 1% fee” with a “Deposit” button. 
▶ Banner: No earnings available to instant deposits

[Image: AD_4nXch_0nBPNFoy-usubzoKHCInYwohjEjWi2SHEoqOJbJo72mbTjoi66jTgiwVXw5vAFTp5pp77rUYxD-b6p33s0qm8EzOwqAPb2KiJUbzJS_4HKP2SJBnNZ8trlGUXUCySU5MuGg]

The image above depicts the gray banner that says “No earrings available for instant deposits. The next time you get paid, check here to deposit your earnings instantly for a 1% fee.”
Pos can refer to the What is instant deposit? – Thumbtack Help article to learn more about instant deposits. For full details on Instant Deposit eligibility, fees, and the process to initiate them, reps can reference the internal Instant Deposits (Pro) KA.  
2. Process
Steps: How to troubleshoot issues with payouts and deposits (Rep)
This section outlines how to help pros who contact support with questions or issues regarding their payouts or deposits. Frontline reps should follow these steps to effectively troubleshoot and guide them toward a resolution.
When a pro reports an issue with a payout or deposit, reps should first understand what kind of issue the pro is having: 
For setup or account-level issues: Reps can refer to the internal Direct Deposit and Stripe  KA for troubleshooting account verification statuses.
For transactional payout failures: Reps will first follow the steps below to troubleshoot the failure. If unable to, reps will contact Advanced Service for them to review detailed Stripe decline codes in the internal Direct Deposit and Stripe KA.
To help a pro troubleshoot a payout issue, frontline reps will follow these steps: 
Check the in-product Earnings > Deposits tab: Reps should always start by logging in as the pro and checking the in-product Earnings > Deposits tab. The "Failed deposit" status and its accompanying reason are often the most direct indicator of the problem. Reps can refer to the Failed Deposit Reasons for more information on error messages a pro may see.
Advise Pro to contact their Bank: For most "Failed deposit" reasons, the primary action for the pro is to contact their issuing bank or card provider with the specific reason displayed. Thumbtack generally cannot resolve these bank-level issues directly.
Review Admin View (for internal troubleshooting): If the in-product message is insufficient, reps can review the Thumbtack payment logs in Admin. Reps should use these logs to understand what happened within Thumbtack's internal system regarding the payment flow. Reps can find these transaction logs on the quote/bid page for a specific project in Admin.
For a thorough understanding of the Payment logs, reps should reference the internal Thumbtack Pay (Pro) (Customer) (Sunset Jun 30, 2026) KA. 
Request Stripe Review from Advanced Service: If the in-product message is insufficient and the pro has contacted their bank or card holder and their bank told them to contact Thumbtack, reps can reach out to Advanced Service in #service_global_help-and-escalations. 
Only Advanced Service can review detailed Stripe information for further investigation. Advanced Services will use Stripe to understand why an external payment or payout failed, getting the precise reason from Stripe.*
Only Advanced Service can review detailed Stripe information for further investigation. Advanced Service will use Stripe to understand why an external payment or payout failed, getting the precise reason from Stripe.*
Submit a request to the Advanced Service Team (AST) in Slack.
Navigate to the #service_global_help-and-escalations Slack channel.
Uses keywords Global Help Stripe to trigger the workflow.
Post a clear and concise summary of the issue, including the pro's name, relevant project ID, the exact "Failed deposit" reason from the Earnings page, and what troubleshooting steps have already been taken.
Specify that you are requesting Advanced Service to review Stripe details for further investigation.
*Important Note for Reps: Reps should note that these granular details cannot always be shared with pros in an effort to prevent fraudulent activity. It's best for reps to redirect pros to contact their bank or card holder for specific bank-level details.
General Advice for Pros:
Reps should have the pro check their deposit account information on file is accurate and up-to-date.
If a pro is receiving multiple failed deposits, reps should encourage them to proactively contact their bank.
3. Talking points
This section provides frontline reps with approved, conversational talking points to use when explaining payout statuses to pros who contact support.

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Q: What do the different payout statuses on my Deposits tab mean?
Q: ¿Qué significan los diferentes estados de pago en la pestaña Depósitos?
Your Deposits tab is designed to give you a clear overview of the money being sent to your account. Here's what each payout status means:
Pending: This means your payment is on its way and processing. You will see an estimated arrival date next to it, so you know when to expect the funds in your bank account.
Deposit: This means a standard deposit has been sent to your bank account and should arrive within 3-4 business days.
Instant deposit: This means an instant deposit has been successfully sent to your debit card and should arrive within 30 minutes.
Failed Deposit: Your deposit could not be processed. Next to 'Failed Deposit,' you will see a specific reason provided by Thumbtack's payment processor, such as 'The bank has declined this transfer' or 'The card used was reported lost or stolen.' For detailed troubleshooting, you should contact your bank directly with this specific reason.
Withdrawal: This indicates a negative payout has occurred, meaning funds were debited from your account, often for a refund or adjustment.
La pestaña Depósitos está diseñada para brindarle una visión clara del dinero que se está enviando a su cuenta. A continuación se explica qué significa cada estado de pago:
Pendiente: Esto indica que su pago está en proceso. Verá una fecha estimada de llegada junto a este estado, para que sepa cuándo esperar los fondos en su cuenta bancaria.
Depósito: Esto significa que se ha enviado un depósito estándar a su cuenta bancaria, y debería reflejarse en un plazo de 3 a 4 días hábiles.
Depósito instantáneo: Esto significa que se ha enviado correctamente un depósito instantáneo a su tarjeta de débito, y debería reflejarse en un plazo de 30 minutos.
Depósito fallido: No se pudo procesar su depósito. Junto a la etiqueta "Depósito fallido", verá una razón específica proporcionada por el procesador de pagos de Thumbtack, como por ejemplo “El banco rechazó esta transferencia” o “La tarjeta utilizada fue reportada como perdida o robada”. Para obtener asistencia más detallada, le recomendamos comunicarse directamente con su banco y proporcionar la razón específica indicada.
Retiro: Esto indica que se ha producido un pago negativo, lo cual significa que se descontaron fondos de su cuenta. Esto suele deberse a un reembolso o ajuste.
Why don't I see the option to instantly deposit my earnings, or why did my instant deposit fail? 
¿Por qué no veo la opción de depósito instantáneo de mis ingresos, o por qué falló el depósito instantáneo?
You might not see the option because the funds have passed the 24-hour instant deposit window and will now process as a standard deposit. 
If your instant deposit failed, you will see a specific reason on your Deposits tab, such as ''The card used was invalid.' We recommend acting quickly and checking your Earnings tab shortly after receiving a customer's payment to see what funds are available for instant deposit. 
If a deposit fails, you should consult the reason provided on the Deposits tab and contact your bank for further details.
Es posible que no vea la opción porque los fondos ya superaron la ventana de 24 horas disponible para depósitos instantáneos, y por ello se procesarán como un depósito estándar.
Si su depósito instantáneo falló, verá una razón específica en la pestaña Depósitos, como por ejemplo “La tarjeta utilizada no es válida”. Le recomendamos actuar con rapidez y consultar su pestaña Ingresos poco después de recibir el pago de un cliente, para ver qué fondos están disponibles para depósito instantáneo.
Si un depósito falla, debe consultar la razón indicada en la pestaña Depósitos y comunicarse con su banco para obtener más información.
How does Thumbtack notify me if a deposit fails, and how specific are the reasons provided? 
¿Cómo me notifica Thumbtack si un depósito falla y qué tan específicas son las razones proporcionadas?
Thumbtack will notify you directly via email and in-app notifications if a deposit fails. The in-app 'Deposits' tab will display a specific reason for the failure, such as 'The card used was invalid.' While these reasons come directly from our payment processor, Stripe, or your bank, for the most information and specific details about the failure, you should always contact your bank or card holder directly. They will have more insight into the exact reasoning for the decline.
Thumbtack le notificará directamente por correo electrónico y mediante notificaciones dentro de la aplicación si un depósito falla. La pestaña Depósitos dentro de la aplicación mostrará una razón específica del fallo, como por ejemplo “La tarjeta utilizada no es válida”. Aunque estas razones provienen directamente de nuestro procesador de pagos, Stripe, o de su banco, para obtener más información y detalles específicos sobre el fallo, le recomendamos comunicarse directamente con su banco o emisor de la tarjeta. Ellos podrán ofrecerle una explicación más precisa sobre el motivo del rechazo.
4. Resources

Opt-In Leads (Pro)

Contents

Overview
Comparison: Opt-In lead types
Why do pros receive opt in leads?
Benefits of opt in leads
Do's and Don'ts
Key points
Pro experience
Overserved opt in ledas

How overserved opt in and partial match leads wor

What is matchmaker and how does it work?
Resources
1. Overview
IMPORTANT: Around July 16, 2026, partial match opt in leads were turned off. Pros won't receive these opt-in leads moving forward. 
As a frontline rep, you may hear from pros who are seeing leads that don't seem to follow their standard budget rules. These are Opt-In Leads—high-value opportunities provided to pros in specific scenarios to ensure they never miss a potential job, while still maintaining full control over their spending.
Understanding the mechanics of these leads will help you explain the "why" behind these notifications and help pros in managing their budgets effectively.
Comparison: Opt-In Lead Types

Reps can reference this table to distinguish between the two primary types of opt-in leads.

Feature
Partial Match Opt-In Lead 
(Matchmaker AI)
Overserved Opt-In lead 
(out of budget)
Status

Nationwide
Opt-in contact type

How it works

Accept and pay and within 24 hours or decline at no charge 
Pricing and offer
‘Accept & pay’ 
"Accept & adjust budget,” (discounted price 
“Accept only this lead" (standard price)
Track spending

Response Time

Does NOT impact response time.
Expiration

Syndication type
targeting_v2_not_enrolled_contact_optin

[INTERNAL Note about budget throttling: For partial match leads, pros may have received them even if they were low on funds. The system may have offered a "Hard Budget Discount" to fit the lead within their remaining balance to keep the pro visible. Reps should not share this information with pros.]
Why do pros receive opt-in leads?
While most leads are exact matches based on a pro’s job preferences and are auto-charged, the system generates opt-in leads for two main reasons:
To bridge the gap in low-supply markets: Ensuring customers find help even when local pros are out of budget for the week.
To surface relevant opportunities: Using AI to find jobs that are a strong fit for a pro’s skills, even if they fall slightly outside their current job preferences (targeting).
Benefits of opt-in leads
Regardless of the type, all opt-in leads share pro-first logic:
Zero Risk: Pros are never auto-charged. They must manually review and select "Accept & pay" to initiate the contact.
No Penalty: Ignoring or declining these leads has no impact on a pro’s responsiveness.
Control: Leads expire after 24 hours if no action is taken, ensuring the pro's inbox stays current.
Do’s and Dont’s
Reps must follow these rules when discussing opt-in leads with pros: 
Overserved Opt-In Leads
🚫 DO NOT use the term "Overserved": This is internal jargon. Externally, refer to these as leads.
Correct: "This lead was sent to you because you reached your weekly budget, but the customer still wanted to reach out."
Incorrect: "This is an overserved contact."
🚫 DO NOT explain qualification: Do not go into detail about "low supply markets" or specific system triggers that qualify a pro for these leads. Keep the focus on the value to the pro.
✅ DO coach on Budgeting: If a pro is getting these leads because they are out of budget (Overserved), use it as an opportunity to recommend a budget increase so they don't have to manually opt-in to high-quality jobs.
Key points
Here are key points for Frontline Reps to remember when discussing opt-in leads with pros:
If the pro doesn’t accept an opt in lead within 24 hours of receiving the contact, it will be removed from the Jobs tab. 
Responding or declining an opt in lead does not count towards a pros responsiveness.
An overserved opt-in lead is when a customer contacts a  pro who has already reached their weekly budget limit. These pros only show in search results in markets where there is a low supply of pros. 
An overserved opt-in lead does not count against a pro's budget limit, unless the pro chooses “Accept and adjust their weekly budget”.
Pros earning free leads from an active BOSUP offer will not be affected by the overserved contact opt in experience. Opt in leads, just like exact match leads, are granted as free until their free lead balance is gone (instead of receiving the lead as an opt in).
2. Pro experience: Opt-in leads 
When a lead falls outside of a pro’s standard settings—either due to a job preference mismatch or a depleted budget—the experience shifts from auto-charge to an opt-In flow.
While both experiences look similar to the pro, the specific prompts and banners they see will depend on the type of lead received.  In both cases, they have 24 hours to act before the lead expires.
Overserved Opt-In Leads 
These leads occur when a pro’s weekly budget is already exhausted, but they are a match for a customer in a low-supply market.
Where they appear: In the Jobs  tab under "For you" with an "Accept by" date.
Incentive: Pros see: "The customer contacted you after you hit your budget… If you increase your budget, you’ll also get a discount on the price of this lead.”  
Pro Actions: When a pro clicks “See options,” they have three distinct choices:
Accept & adjust budget: Increases their weekly budget cap to accommodate this lead (and future ones) at a discounted price.
Accept only this lead: The pro pays for this contact as a one-time purchase at the standard price.
Decline this lead: Removes the request at no cost.
Budget Impact: 
If they adjust their budget, the cost is deducted from the Weekly Budget. This does not count as a "custom budget change.
If they choose a one-off purchase, it appears under "Additional spent."
▶ What an overserved opt in lead looks like

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

The first image above shows a: "Save $X on this lead - pay $X. To get this job, you must accept by XX:XX am/pm” with a “See options” button..
The second image above shows the pop-up after the pro taps “See options", which says: "The customer contacted you after you hit your budget, so you haven't been charged for this lead. If you accept, you'll be automatically charged. If you increase your budget, you'll also get a discount on the price of this lead.
Here’s an overview of the overserved opt-in lead flow: 
The pro has reached their weekly budget limit but is shown in search results when there’s a low supply of pros. 
The customer finds the pro in their search results and contacts them.
The pro sees the new lead in the “For you” section of their Jobs tab.
From the job details page, pros will see a "Save $X on this lead - pay $X” label.
The pro can either:
Accept & adjust budget: They are charged for the lead at a discounted price, and their weekly budget is immediately increased by that amount. Pros see a "You paid $X for this lead and adjusted your budget to $X". 
Accept only this lead: They pay the standard price (no discount) as a one-off purchase, which does not affect their weekly budget. Pros see a "You paid $X outside of your budget for this lead.” 
Decline this lead: This removes the lead at no cost and lets the customer know.
If the pro accepts the lead and replies to the customer, the conversation moves to the Messages tab.
3. Customer experience
The distinction between lead types is not visible to customers. Reps should not communicate these internal distinctions to customers.
Search Results: Customers see a mix of "exact match" and "expanded match" (partial match) pros. This often includes the Top 3 Best Matches carousel, which uses an active auction to display the most relevant pros.
Mismatch Blocks:
Exact Match Pros: Standard mismatch logic applies. If a customer's request doesn't match a pros job preferences or availability, they are blocked from contact.
The system will display an error like "This pro doesn't match your project needs - they don't offer [what they don't offer based on customer's request form details]." 
Customers can then select other pros and click "Send project to selected pros.
Expanded Match Pros: Job preference (job type, travel area) mismatch errors are removed. Customers are only blocked if the project timeline conflicts with the pros' availability.
Unresponsive Flow: If pros do not respond or they decline the request, customers receive an automated email 24 hours after the initial request.
▶ What the automated email looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

4. Process
Steps: How to identify an opt-in lead type in Admin (Rep)
When troubleshooting with a pro, you can identify which experience they encountered by checking the syndication type on the Negotiations page in Admin. 
Search for the pro: Access the User Admin page by searching for the pro using their email, phone number, or PK ID.
Locate the Negotiation: Scroll to the Negotiations (fka Quotes/Bids) section to find the specific lead in question.
Access Negotiation details: Click the ID link for that specific lead to open its Negotiations page.
Check the Syndication type: Look at the 'Syndication type' field within the main Negotiation header.
By reviewing the value in the Syndication type field, you can confirm exactly why the pro received an opt-in request:
Partial match leads (turned off): 
Look for targeting_v2_not_enrolled_contact_optin. 
This indicates the lead was relevant based on AI but fell outside the pro's strict targeting.
Overserved Contacts: 
Look for: instant_results_promote_converted_optin_contact_instant
This confirms the pro was out of budget, but the lead was served anyway due to low pro supply in that market
Refer to the internal Admin Tool (Rep) KA for all syndication types and meanings.
Steps: How to check a pro's budget history after accepting an opt-in lead (Rep)
When a pro has questions about their budget after accepting an overserved opt-in lead, frontline reps should check a pro's budget history in Admin from the Business page. 
For details and steps on Admin tools to investigate a pro’s budget and steps, reps should refer to the Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro) KA. 
5. Talking points 
This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with Pros about the Matchmaker Test Expansion. Use these talking points to ensure consistent and accurate messaging.
How overserved opt in leads work

English talking point
Spanish talking point 
Do I have to pay for these leads? / Are they auto-charged?
¿Tengo que pagar por estos prospectos? / ¿Se cobran automáticamente?
You are never automatically charged for these leads. They are 'opt-in' opportunities, meaning you have 24 hours to review the details. You only pay if you select 'Accept.' If you do nothing or decline, you are not charged.
Nunca se le cobrará automáticamente por estos prospectos. Son oportunidades de tipo "opt-in" (opcionales), lo que significa que tiene 24 horas para revisar los detalles. Usted solo paga si selecciona "Aceptar". Si no realiza ninguna acción o si los rechaza, no se le cobrará.
What happens if I decline or ignore these leads?
¿Qué sucede si rechazo o ignoro estos prospectos?
There is no penalty. Declining or ignoring these leads does not impact your response time, responsiveness score, or search ranking. They simply expire after 24 hours."
No hay ninguna penalización. Rechazar o ignorar estos prospectos no afecta su tiempo de respuesta, su calificación de capacidad de respuesta ni su clasificación en los resultados de búsqueda. Simplemente vencen después de 24 horas.
How do I stop getting these?
¿Cómo dejo de recibir estos prospectos?
There is no direct 'off' switch for opt-in leads. However, they are designed to be low-friction; since they don't impact your metrics and require manual approval to charge you, you can simply ignore the ones that don't fit your current needs."
No hay un botón de apagado directo para los prospectos opcionales. Sin embargo, están diseñados para que el proceso sea sencillo; ya que no afectan sus métricas y requieren de su aprobación manual para que se le cobre, simplemente puede ignorar los que no se ajusten a sus necesidades actuales.
Overserved opt-in leads and budget 

English talking point
Spanish talking point 
Q: What happens if I don’t want to increase my budget after accepting an opt-in lead after I hit my budget? 
Q: ¿Qué pasa si no quiero aumentar mi presupuesto? 
A: Nothing changes for you. You can still accept the lead for its listed price without adjusting your budget, or you can decline it, just like before. 
A: Nada cambia para usted. Todavía puede aceptar el prospecto por el precio indicado sin ajustar su presupuesto, o puede rechazarlo, igual que antes.
Q: Why should I increase my budget after accepting an opt-in lead after I hit my budget ?
Q: ¿Por qué debería aumentar mi presupuesto usando esta opción? 
A: A good way to think about this is that by adding the cost of this lead to your weekly budget, you’re helping yourself get more consistent leads in the future. It helps keep your budget aligned with the demand we're seeing in your area, so you can stay competitive. Plus, in this case, you'd also be saving some money on this specific lead with the discount being offered.
A: Una buena forma de verlo es que, al agregar el costo de este prospecto a su presupuesto semanal, podrá recibir prospectos de manera más constante en el futuro. Esto mantiene su presupuesto alineado con la demanda que vemos en su área, para que pueda seguir siendo competitivo. Además, en este caso, también estaría ahorrando dinero en este prospecto específico gracias al descuento que se le ofrece.
Q: What happens if I accept the opt-in lead and adjust my budget?
Q: ¿Qué pasa si acepto el prospecto opcional y ajusto mi presupuesto?
A: When you choose to accept the lead and adjust your budget, that amount is immediately added to your weekly budget. Your budget will stay at this new, higher amount. You can always review and adjust your budget at any time by going to the Service tab and selecting “edit weekly targeting budget. This is a great way to make sure you're staying in a good budget range to get leads more consistently in the coming weeks.
A: Cuando elige aceptar el prospecto opcional y ajustar su presupuesto, ese monto se agrega de inmediato a su presupuesto semanal. Su presupuesto permanecerá en esta nueva cantidad más alta. Siempre puede revisar y ajustar su presupuesto en cualquier momento yendo a la pestaña Services (“Servicios”) y seleccionando edit weekly targeting budget (“editar presupuesto semanal”). Esta es una excelente manera de asegurarse de mantenerse en un rango de presupuesto adecuado para recibir prospectos de manera más constante en las próximas semanas.
Q: How can I track my spending if I accept an opt in contact and adjust my budget?
Q: ¿Cómo puedo hacer un seguimiento de mis gastos si acepto un prospecto opcional y ajusto mi presupuesto?
A: If you choose to accept the contact and adjust your budget, you'll see that charge reflected in the 'Budget spent' section of your Services page. It's treated just like any other lead that's part of your regular weekly budget."
A: Si elige aceptar el prospecto opcional y ajustar su presupuesto, verá ese cargo reflejado en la sección Budget spent (“Presupuesto gastado”) de su página de Servicios. Este se trata igual que cualquier otro prospecto que forma parte de su presupuesto semanal.
Q: How can I track my spending if I accept an opt in contact and DON'T adjust my budget?
Q: ¿Cómo puedo hacer un seguimiento de mis gastos si acepto un prospecto opcional y NO ajusto mi presupuesto?
A: If you decide to accept the contact as a one-off purchase without adjusting your budget, that charge will appear in the 'Additional spent' section of your Services page. It's kept separate from your weekly budget spending.
A: Si decide aceptar el prospecto opcional como una compra única sin ajustar su presupuesto, ese cargo aparecerá en la sección Additional spent (“Gasto adicional”) de su página de Servicios. Este se mantiene separado de los gastos de su presupuesto semanal.
6. Internal FAQs
What is Matchmaker and how does it work? 
Matchmaker: An AI-Powered Matching Engine
Matchmaker is an AI engine that enhances search results by using a broad range of pro data—including profile details and job history—to find relevant matches beyond strict targeting selections. Before sending a lead, Matchmaker predicts the likelihood of the pro accepting based on project details and job preferences to ensure quality.
How "Partial Match" Leads are Determined
Matchmaker predicts a pro's likelihood of accepting a job based on project details and the pro's job preferences before sending a "Partial match" lead. This prediction benefits:
Customers: By seeing pros more likely to take the job, lead quality and the overall customer experience are improved.
Pros: They receive fewer leads they are unlikely to accept.
Generating Partial Matches in Search Results
In the standard search experience, customers are usually prevented from contacting a pro if their project details don't strictly align with the pro’s job preferences.
The Matchmaker engine removes this "mismatch" block* for pros deemed relevant by the system based on their profile and job history, even if they aren't directly targeting that service category. As a result, customers will see a mix of "exact match" and "expanded match" pros in their search results.
* Important Note on Contact Blocks: Customers will still be blocked from contacting a pro if the project's timeline doesn't match the pro’s availability. For "exact match pros," the standard mismatch logic remains, meaning mismatched Request Form answers about services can prevent contact.
Ensuring Adequate Pro Supply
To ensure customers always have enough pros to choose from, search results may include pros who have exceeded their budget if there is a low supply of pros in that specific market and "Exact Match" pros are limited.
Enrollment and Exclusions
As of March 16, 2026, these leads are a baseline feature nationwide. However, some pros are excluded:
Excluded Markets: Currently, pros in four specific markets are excluded from the Matchmaker partial match experience.
Specific Service Categories: Certain high-risk or highly specialized categories may be excluded from the AI matching engine to maintain quality.
Customer experience with Matchmaker
When a customer submits a project request, they are presented with a list of pros. This list includes a mix of "exact match" pros (who strictly target the requested service category) and "expanded match" pros (pros who are relevant but may not have specifically targeted the exact category). This distinction is NOT visible to the customer and reps should not communicate this to customers.
Pro Curation:
The results typically feature a "Top 3 Best Matches" module (also known as the Pro Curation Carousel or PCC) highlighting curated, high-performing pros, followed by a list of "All pros" who match the specific request details. The PCC uses an active auction to display the top three most relevant pros, including Expanded Match pros*.*If eligible and in the top 3. 

Mismatch Flows (Preventing Contact):
The system only prevents a customer from contacting a pro in specific mismatch scenarios:
Exact Match Pros: For "exact match pros," mismatch logic still applies. A mismatch on Request Form answers (e.g., regarding specific services or details) or on availability can prevent contact. The system will display an error like "This pro doesn't match your project needs - they don't offer [what they don't offer based on customer's request form details]." Customers can then select other pros and click "Send project to selected pros.
Expanded Pros (partial matches): When a customer contacts an "expanded pro" (who does not target the category), they will NOT see the standard mismatch error regarding services offered. They will only see mismatch flows if the project's timeline doesn't match the pro’s availability.
7. Resources
Frontline Reps will find a collection of valuable resources in this section, including links to internal knowledge articles, external Help Center articles, and other relevant documentation. These resources may be referenced in the article or provide additional, related information.

articles.fullText:
Opportunities (Pro)

Contents
Overview
Key points
Updates
Thumbtack numbers on opportunities

Opportunity creation and initial notification
Four hour follow up
Opportunity availability window
Payment timeline
Customer reply = phone number unmasked
Differences between leads and opportunities

Viewing project details and expressing interest
Passing on Opportunties

Budget and spending

(Pro) Steps: How to reach out to a customer on an opportunity
Talking Points
General understanding of opportunities
How long opportunities are available
Notifications on opportunties
Competition considerations on opportunities
Customer phone number on opportunities
Cost, charges, and pricing for opportunties
Resources
1. Overview 
▶ KA summary
This internal knowledge article equips Frontline reps to guide pros on Opportunities. Reps will learn to differentiate Opportunities from Leads, understand their workflow and pricing, and address common Pro questions. 
Key takeaways include: 
How Opportunity costs differ from regular leads, 
Why notifications aren't sent for all Opportunities, 
How timelines work (especially weekend exceptions), and 
How payment is triggered. 
This knowledge helps reps effectively support Pros, troubleshoot issues, and maximize Opportunity success.
In the Jobs section, pros can switch between the For you tab, where they’ll find Leads and Claimable jobs, and the Opportunities tab.

Opportunities (found in the Opportunities tab) are a pros chance to get in front of customers who haven’t hired someone yet. These are customers who have reached out to a few Thumbtack pros and they’re asking for quotes. Simply put - these are leads that went to other pros first. 
Each Opportunity will show how many pros the customer has contacted and how many pros have already responded to them. Even though a pro might not be the first pro the customer contacted, that pro could be the first pro that the customer hears back from.
Pros can learn more in the What are Opportunities? – Thumbtack Help article.
Key points
Frontline reps should keep the following in mind when helping pros with opportunities:
Pros should not expect to be sent notifications for all opportunities, or even for very many. 
Pros are notified for opportunities within 25 miles.
Pros are NOT notified for opportunities in categories where targeting (also known as "Job preferences") is on.
Once a quote is sent, pros can no longer edit the pricing. They can use the messenger if they want to update the price.
When a pro clicks “pass” on an opportunity, a small "Undo" message will appear. The pro can then restore the opportunity to their list if they change their mind
Frontline reps should follow these guidelines:
Don’t promise the customer will see a pro’s message.  
Do explain that if a customer responds, the pro pays the price shown on the opportunity. Since opportunities are priced separately from exact match leads, they may exceed the lead price set by the pro. Reps can refer to the internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA.
Do emphasize that the customer has already contacted at least one different pro, and might only respond if their first plan doesn’t work out.
Updates
Opportunities now include a Thumbtack number 
Opportunities now come with a Thumbtack number, the same as exact match leads. When the customer replies to a pro's quote and the pro replies back, the number that unlocks is a Thumbtack number — a dedicated number routed to the customer's verified phone — not the customer's personal phone number. The pro can call or text the customer through it, and the customer's personal number stays private until they choose to share it.
The timing for opportunities hasn't changed: the number still unlocks only after the customer replies to the quote and the pro replies back. What's changed is which number the pro receives at that point.
Excluded services: Certain services are not assigned a Thumbtack number. Opportunities in those categories won't include one. For the full list of excluded services and how Thumbtack numbers work, see the internal Thumbtack numbers (Pro) (Customer) KA.
Timelines for Opportunities
Understanding the timeline of an Opportunity helps frontline reps manage pro expectations and prioritize effectively. Here’s a breakdown of the key stages:
1. Opportunity Creation & Initial Notification:
As soon as a customer submits their project request, the Opportunity is created.
Thumbtack's system identifies pros who might be a good fit and sends out initial notifications.
Important: Pros will only be notified for select opportunities. See more details on why not all opportunities are shown.
If the job is within 25 miles or not in a targeted category, the pro will receive a notification.
2. Four-Hour Follow-Up:
If the customer has not received any positive responses (e.g., messages, chats) within four hours of the Opportunity being created, Thumbtack send reminder emails to pros about the customer’s job to help the customer's project move forward.
This is to help the customer get the help they need and to provide more chances for pros to connect.
3. Opportunity Availability Window:
Each Opportunity remains active and available for pros to express interest for a limited time, specifically until one of the following occurs:
48 Hours Pass: The Opportunity closes exactly 48 hours after creation. However, if the request is created on a weekend (Saturday or Sunday), the Opportunity will close around 5 PM on the following Tuesday (instead of 48 hours after creation).
Five Pros Express Interest: If five different pros express interest (by sending a quote) before the 48 hours are up, the Opportunity will close.
Customer Cancels: If the customer cancels the job request for any reason, the Opportunity will close immediately.
4. Payment Timeline:
When a pro expresses interest in an Opportunity, they are not immediately charged.
They will only be charged if the customer responds to their message within 30 days, including weekends.
The pro isn't charged if the customer does not respond or responds after the 30-day window.
5. Customer Reply = Phone Number Unlocked:
For Opportunities, pros will only get to the customer's Thumbtack number after the customer replies directly to their message. This is different from leads.
Differences between leads and opportunities
 Below is a table comparing Leads and Opportunities to help frontline reps quickly grasp their main distinctions.



Leads
Opportunities
What they are
Leads are initiated by customers who found the pro in search results and contact them directly. The primary goal is to connect customers actively searching for their specific services based on the pro's preferences
Opportunities are customers who have already contacted other pros, but haven’t chosen anyone yet. Pros initiate contact by expressing interest by sending a quote.
When a pro is notified 
Pros are notified that they’ve received a lead (based on their job preferences).
Pros are not notified for all opportunities.

Pros are notified for opportunities within 25 miles or if the opportunity is not in a category they are targeting. 
How they make the pros job preferences (targeting)
Pros get leads by setting their job preferences 
Thumbtack may show pros jobs from outside of their job preferences (just in case they need more jobs to browse)
How they impact a pros budget 
Does use a pro's weekly budget, found under “Budget spent.”
Does not use a pro's weekly budget; found under “Additional spent.”
When a pro pays
Pros pay when the lead contacts them.
Pros pay only if the customer responds to their message within 30 days of the pro reaching out. 
No charge if the customer doesn't respond, or responds after 30 days (including weekends).
If the customer’s first message to the pro is a clear no, the pro can request a refund. Refer to internal Lead Refunds (Pro) KA. 
When pro receives customer Thumbtack number
Received after the pro pays for the lead or booking.
Available after the customer replies directly to the pro's quote, and the pro replies back.
Where they are found
Found under the "For you" tab in the Jobs section
Found under the "Opportunities" tab in the Jobs section.
How Opportunities work
A customer searches for pros, and reaches out to a pro through their search results. Once the customers project details have been submitted, the project is automatically assigned to the Opportunities tab of local pros who might be a good fit. Here's how opportunities work for pros:
Thumbtack only notifies pros of opportunities we believe are particularly suitable for them.
Pros will be notified of an opportunity if it's within 25 miles
Thumbtack does not send notifications for opportunities in targeted categories
Pros should not expect to be sent notifications for all opportunities, or even for very many. 
Talking point: "We only notify pros of the opportunities we think they're particularly suited for."
If a pro wasn't contacted by the customer but has been sent the opportunity, the job details of the customer will be automatically assigned to the Opportunities tab in the Jobs section for the pros that aren't contacted. Notifications of the opportunity are sent as soon as the project request is created.
Then, if the customer hasn’t received any positive responses (e.g., chatting with a pro) at the four-hour mark, we send reminder emails to pros about the customer’s job to help the customer's project move forward. 
Job details will remain under the Opportunities tab until one of the following happens:
48 hours have passed. (If a request is created on a weekend, it closes at around 5pm on Tuesday instead of 48 hours after creation)
Five pros have already expressed interest in the job.
The customer cancels the job.
If a pro is interested, they can quote on the opportunity and introduce themselves. Quotes will appear in the “Sent Quotes” folder in the Messages tab before the customer replies. 
If a pro passes on an Opportunity, it can’t be undone.
Once a quote is sent, pros can no longer edit the pricing. They can use the messenger if they want to update the price.
If a customer replies to the pro’s quote it shows up as a new message in the Messages tab and the pro will be notified they have a new message.
When a pro reaches out on opportunity, they're only charged if the customer responds to their message (within 30 days [including weekends]). If the customer’s first message to the pro is a clear no, the pro can request a refund and we'll look into it.
The pro does NOT pay if the customer:
Doesn't contact the pro
Contacts the pro more than 30 days (including weekends) after the pro reaches out.
Opportunities tab and project details
Utilize open leads
Pros should focus on leads first. If a pro wants to fill their calendar with more work, they can see what’s available in the "Opportunities" tab in the Jobs section. These are open leads with customers who are still deciding on a pro to hire. For help understanding the differences between lead types, pros can click “Learn more” at the top of the tab.
▶ What the “Learn more” sheet looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Viewing project details and expressing interest
When a pro is interested in an Opportunity, they select "View details" to access the Project details page. This page shows all essential job, location, pricing, and competition information:
Job & Location Details: The page includes the job type (e.g., Appliance repair or maintenance), the customer's zip code, the specific details the customer answered on the request form, when the work should be done, any message from the customer, their travel preferences (e.g., pro must travel to my address), and a map of where the lead is located.
Pricing & Competition: Pros see competition data, including the number of pros the customer has contacted and the number of pros who have already responded to them. The page also displays the amount of time before the job expires. A fee banner clearly shows the cost of the lead and explains that the pro only pays if the customer responds.
Customer Contact Information: Under "Phone number," it explains that the customer's number is available only after they contact the pro directly in response to the quote. This would be the customer's Thumbtack number.
To express interest, the pro uses the direct "Message [Customer Name]" button (which has replaced the old "I'm interested" button). Both the Pass and Message actions now appear together at the bottom of the page.
▶ What the Opportunities tab, Project details page, and quoting on an opportunity looks like

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

Passing on Opportunities
If a pro decides to pass on an Opportunity, they can tap “Pass” from the Opportunities tab or from the project details page. When a pro clicks “pass”, a small "Undo" message will appear. The pro can then restore the lead to their list if they change their mind. (This option is new and was not available previously.)
Relevance and filtering
Opportunities showing at the top of the list are likely the best fit for pros — usually, they’re the most relevant and close by. The further down the list, the less relevant they become. Thumbtack may show pros jobs from outside of their preferences (just in case they need more jobs to browse). They’re able to adjust the distance and relevance filters from their Opportunities tab.
Pros can refine their view using the filters on the Opportunities tab:
Sort by: Most Relevant, Most Recent, or Closest to Expiry.
Business: Pros with more than one business on Thumbtack can filter opportunities either for all their businesses or for each individual business.
Distance: Within 5, 25, 50, 100, 150 miles.
Categories: All categories or limit the view to only the categories where the pro has job preferences set.
▶ What the filters look like on the app

[Image: rtaImage]

Cost, charges, and pricing on Opportunities
Cost and charge point
Opportunities are priced separately from other leads and may exceed the lead price set by the pro. The cost of a lead is determined by the specifics of the job details and supply and demand.  Pros can view the cost by clicking “View details” from the Opportunities tab to open the job details. The cost is what they paid if the customer responds to their quote.
A pro is only charged this cost if the customer responds to their quote (within 30 days, including weekends. 

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

Budget and spending
A pro’s weekly budget will NOT be used for Opportunities. Instead, pros will pay for the opportunity using their default payment method when the customer they reached out to responds. To track their spending on Opportunities, pros can view the “Additional spent” under the “Spending this week” on their Services page.  
Non-charges and refunds 
Pro is not charged for an opportunity if the customer:
Doesn't contact the pro OR
Contacts the pro more than 30 days (including weekends) after the pro reaches out
If the customer’s first message to the pro is a clear "no," the pro can request a refund. Reps can refer to the internal Lead Refunds (Pro) KA > Customers first contact is “No thank you” to learn more. 
2. Process

(Pro) Steps: How to reach out to a customer on an Opportunity

Pros can look at their Opportunities tab from their Jobs section when looking for extra work. These customers have reached out to other pros but haven’t hired someone and you may still be a great fit for their job.
Pro steps: Pros can follow the steps on the How to reach out to Opportunities – Thumbtack Help when they see an Opportunity they’re interested in. 
Opportunities are priced separately from other leads. Pros will always see the price upfront. If they quote on an opportunity, they’re only charged if the customer responds to their message. Pros can learn more about paying for leads. How much do I pay for leads and opportunities? – Thumbtack Help article.  

NOTE: Pros can type up to 1,000 characters when quoting (expressing interest) on an Opportunity.

3. Talking points
General understanding of opportunities
English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
What’s the difference between leads and opportunities?
¿Cuál es la diferencia entre prospectos y oportunidades?
Leads are customers who saw you in their search results and decided to reach out to you directly. You get leads by setting targeting preferences and telling us the types of jobs you want.

Opportunities are your chance to get in front of customers who haven’t hired someone yet. These are customers who have reached out to a few Thumbtack pros and they’re asking for quotes.
Los prospectos directos son clientes que lo vieron en sus resultados de búsqueda y decidieron contactarlo directamente. Usted obtiene prospectos configurando sus preferencias de enfoque y diciéndonos los tipos de trabajos que desea.

Las oportunidades son su oportunidad de presentarse ante clientes que aún no han contratado a alguien. Estos son clientes que se han comunicado con algunos profesionales de Thumbtack y están solicitando presupuestos.
Which Opportunity is the best fit for me?
¿Qué oportunidad se ajusta mejor a mí?
Opportunities showing at the top of the list are likely the best fit for you — usually, they’re the most relevant and close by. The further down the list, the less relevant they become. 

We may show you jobs from outside of your preferences (just in case you need more jobs to browse). You're able to adjust the distance and relevance filters from your Opportunities tab.
Las oportunidades que se muestran en la parte superior de la lista son probablemente las que mejor se adaptan a usted; por lo general, son las más relevantes y cercanas. Cuanto más abajo en la lista, menos relevantes se vuelven.
Es posible que le mostremos trabajos fuera de sus preferencias (en caso de que necesite más trabajos para explorar). Usted puede ajustar los filtros de distancia y relevancia desde su pestaña de Oportunidades.
When I reach out about an opportunity, how does the customer see my message?
Cuando me comunico con un cliente en oportunidades, ¿cómo ve el cliente mi mensaje?
When these customers see you in their search results, we’ll let them know you’re interested in the job. Then the customer will contact you if they want to learn more about you or hire you.
Cuando estos clientes lo vean en sus resultados de búsqueda, les haremos saber que está interesado en el trabajo. Entonces el cliente se pondrá en contacto con usted si quiere saber más de usted o contratarle.
How long Opportunities are available

How long is an Opportunity available for?
¿Cuánto tiempo está disponible una oportunidad?
An Opportunity is no longer available to quote on if :

48 hours have passed.
Five pros have already expressed interest in the job.
The customer cancels the job.
Una oportunidad ya no está disponible para cotizar si:

Han pasado 48 horas.
Cinco profesionales ya han expresado interés en el trabajo.
El cliente cancela el trabajo.
Notifications on opportunities

Why don’t you notify me when an opportunity matches my targeting preferences?
¿Por qué no me notifica cuando una oportunidad coincide con mis preferencias de enfoque?
If an open opportunity matches your preferences exactly, there’s a good chance the customer already saw you in their search results. Since they didn’t reach out to you in their initial search, they might not think you’re the right fit for their job. Rather than email you about these uninterested customers, we’ll email you when you get a new lead, or send you opportunities where the customer might not have seen you in their first search.
Si una oportunidad abierta coincide exactamente con sus preferencias, es muy probable que el cliente ya lo había visto en los resultados de búsqueda. Dado que no se comunicaron con usted en su búsqueda inicial, es posible que pensaron que no es la persona indicada para este proyecto. En lugar de enviarle un correo electrónico sobre estos clientes desinteresados, le enviaremos un correo electrónico cuando obtiene un nuevo prospecto o le enviaremos oportunidades en las que el cliente podría no haberlo visto en su primera búsqueda.
Competition considerations on opportunities

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Has the customer already been in contact with other pros?
¿El cliente ya ha estado en contacto con otros profesionales?
Each Opportunity will show how many pros the customer has contacted and how many pros have already responded to them. You can find this information by clicking View details.

Even though you might not be the first pro the customer contacted, you could be the first pro that they hear back from. If the customer hasn’t heard back from any pros yet, you’ll see “Be the first” on the opportunity.
Cada Oportunidad le mostrará cuántos profesionales ha contactado el cliente y cuántos profesionales ya le han respondido. Usted puede encontrar esta información haciendo clic en Ver detalles.

Aunque puede que usted no sea el primer profesional con el que el cliente se ha puesto en contacto, podría ser el primero del que reciba respuesta. Si el cliente aún no ha recibido respuesta de ningún profesional, verá "Sea el primero" en la oportunidad.
If the customer already contacted pros, why would I want to reach out about the opportunity?
Si el cliente ya se puso en contacto con los profesionales, ¿por qué querría informarme sobre la oportunidad?
Customers can reach out to a pro at any point in their search. That means they could possibly reach out to a pro for a day the pro is already booked, or maybe the pro just isn’t interested. If this happens, the customer will come back to Thumbtack to look for another pro — and you might be the pro they’re looking for.
Los clientes pueden comunicarse con un profesional en cualquier momento de su búsqueda. Eso significa que posiblemente podrían comunicarse con un profesional por un día que el profesional ya está reservado, o tal vez el profesional simplemente no esté interesado. Si esto sucede, el cliente volverá a Thumbtack para buscar otro profesional, y es posible que usted sea el profesional que está buscando.
Customer phone number on opportunities

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Why does it say “The customer's number is available after they contact you directly in reply to your quote”?
¿Por qué dice "El número del cliente está disponible después de que se ponga en contacto con usted directamente en respuesta a su presupuesto"?
For all leads on Thumbtack, you’ll receive the phone number after you pay for the booking or lead. For opportunities, since you reach out to the customer first, you won’t receive the phone number until the customer replies directly to you, and you reply back. 
To protect the safety and privacy of customers and pros, contact details are hidden until a customer decides to move forward with a pro and the pro pays for the lead or booking. Because opportunities have a few more steps than leads, it takes longer to get the phone number because they have to reply back to your quote.
En todos los prospectos de Thumbtack, usted recibirá el número de teléfono después de pagar por la reserva o el prospecto. En el caso de las oportunidades, dado que usted se pone en contacto primero con el cliente, no recibirá el número de teléfono hasta que el cliente le responda directamente y usted le responda.

Para proteger la seguridad y privacidad de los clientes y los profesionales, los datos de contacto se ocultan hasta que un cliente decide seguir adelante con un profesional y el profesional paga por el prospecto o la reserva. Debido a que las oportunidades tienen unos cuantos pasos más que los prospectos, toma más tiempo obtener el número de teléfono porque el cliente tiene que responder a su presupuesto.
Can I find the customer’s phone number on the Opportunities tab?
¿Puedo encontrar el número de teléfono del cliente en la pestaña de Oportunidades?
No, the customer’s phone number will not appear on the Opportunities tab. You’ll only get their phone number when the customer reaches out to you directly.
No, el número de teléfono del cliente no aparecerá en la pestaña Oportunidades. Solo obtendrá su número de teléfono cuando el cliente se comunique con usted directamente.
Cost, charges, and pricing on opportunities


English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
How much do Opportunities cost?
¿Cuánto cuestan las Oportunidades?
Opportunities are priced separately from other leads. To see how much it costs if a customer responds to you, open the job details and select View price.

When you reach out to an opportunity, you're only charged if the customer responds to your message. Learn more about paying for leads.

Your weekly budget won’t be used for Opportunities. Instead, you’ll pay for the Opportunity using your payment method when you reach out to the customer.
Las Oportunidades tienen un precio independiente de otros prospectos. Para ver cuánto cuesta si un cliente le responde, abra los detalles del trabajo y seleccione Ver precio.

Cuando usted se comunica con una oportunidad, solo se le cobra si el cliente responde a su mensaje. Conozca más sobre el pago de prospectos.

Su presupuesto semanal no se utilizará para las Oportunidades. En su lugar, usted pagará por la Oportunidad utilizando su método de pago cuando se comunique con el cliente.
Why does this opportunity cost more than the Lead Price I set?
¿Por qué esta oportunidad cuesta más que el Lead Price ("Precio del prospecto") que configuré?
Opportunities are priced separately, and may cost more. The cost of the Opportunity is determined by the specifications of the job, so it is possible that it can cost more than the lead price you set.
Las oportunidades se cobran por separado y pueden costar más. El costo de la oportunidad depende de las especificaciones del trabajo, así que puede costar más que el precio por prospecto que usted estableció.
Why was I automatically charged for this lead?
¿Por qué se me cobró automáticamente por este prospecto?
You were charged for this lead because you reached out to the customer through the “Opportunities” section of your Jobs tab. When you reach out about an opportunity, you let the customer (and Thumbtack) know you’re interested. So if the customer responds to you for those jobs, you pay for the lead.
Se le cobró por este prospecto porque se comunicó con el cliente a través de la sección de "Oportunidades" de la pestaña Jobs (Trabajos). Cuando se comunique con una oportunidad, le hace saber al cliente (y a Thumbtack) que está interesado. Entonces, si el cliente le responde por esos trabajos, usted paga por el cliente potencial.

Process
