1. Overview
▶ KA UPDATE (April 2025)
Note to reps: This internal article has been updated to remove talking points and information related to specific situations, such as ranking and search results, unresponsive customers, trust and safety concerns, targeting, refunds, reviews, ranking in search results, and escalations. This content has been removed for those specific scenarios to eliminate redundancy and ensure clarity for both users and AI systems. 
For example, for information regarding ranking in search results, reps should refer to the dedicated "Ranking and Search Results" knowledge article. 
This article now focuses on general writing tips, best practices, and conversation etiquette, such as initiating and concluding text conversations, and handling transfers. Please refer to the dedicated internal articles for detailed information on specific situations.
▶ KA summary
This internal KA provides guidelines and best practices for Service reps when communicating with pros and customers via non-voice channels (chat and SMS). 
Each conversation with a pro or customer is a new one. However, this article will outline general best practices and typing points for non-voice channels (chat and SMS). 
2. Written Communications: General Tips and Best Practices
This section is designed for Support reps who communicate with pros and customers through non-voice channels, such as chat or email. It provides key principles and practical advice to ensure effective and professional written communication.
The below section you’ll find general best practices and typing points for:  
Add a human touch
Consultative service
Conversation control
Check grammar and spelling
Empathy and ownership
Partnering
Positive positioning 
Probing
Soften facts by adding a question
Terms to avoid
Add a human touch
In all written communications, support reps should remember that they are interacting with real people. Injecting personality and warmth into messages can significantly enhance the pro or customer experience. Reps can apply this in every message to make interactions more personal and engaging.
By adding one of the phrases below, it can help create a human response: 
Absolutely! Happy to help.
Alright, glad I could help.
Anytime!
Awesome! That’s great to hear.
Hmm, let me look into this.
No problem.
Perfect, one moment while I pull this up.
Tell me what you see as your choices here.
When we have the latest update about [xyz]

Reflect feelings by using brief verbal affirmations like,  “I see,” or “I understand.”

For additional expressions and phrases, see internal KA Escalations and De-escalation Tools  > Empathize. 
Consultative service
As a Support Rep, your role extends beyond simply answering questions. Providing valuable insights and guidance beyond just answering questions helps establish trust and build stronger relationships. 
Generally, if someone is reaching out via text, they want a quick conversation. However, we want to be as consultative as possible. Reps are giving the pro or customer what they want (quick answers) while keeping in mind what the business needs–for the pro or customer to be fully educated. 

Support Reps should refer to the Internal Consultative Conversations: A Guide for Support Reps KA for guidance, talking points and steps on how to have consultative conversations.
Conversation control
Effectively managing the flow of the conversation ensures clarity, efficiency, and a positive interaction. Use these techniques in interactions to keep the conversation on track and address all pro or customer needs.
When a support rep needs a moment to investigate, they can let the pro or customer know.
Talking point: I can absolutely look into this for you. Just one moment while I do that.
Talking point: Pulling up your account now. One moment while I dig in.
Be sure to follow the hold times guidelines 

Non-Voice: Hold time and idle time should be within three minutes before checking in with the customer / pro. This is unless the advocate advised of a specific time the hold would be.
Check grammar and spelling
Another part of conversation control is “Gives clear responses avoiding grammar and spelling slips that affect comprehensibility.” 
Quickly double check for grammatical mistakes before sending. 
Capitalize or place quotations around product names (i.e., “On-Demand bookings”).
Add Language Tool as a Chrome extension to help resolve grammar slips.
Empathy and ownership
Showing empathy is putting yourself in the shoes of another. It’s different from sympathy. Sympathy means feeling compassion, sorrow, or pity for another person's hardships.
Showing empathy for upset pros and customers will help you be in a position of support to truly help address their concerns.
Showing empathy and ownership can look like the following:
Admits mistakes and takes ownership of less-than-ideal experiences.
Apologize when appropriate while not over-apologizing.
This is particularly important when writing. We don't want to look back and see every message start with "I'm sorry."
Empathizes as appropriate. There's a fine line between too much and too little.
If we provide too much, it could read as if we're against Thumbtack.
If we provide too little, we seem robotic or uninvested.
Takes ownership of the issue and the resolution of the issue.
Move forward with an action. We want to touch on empathy while not lingering.
​​NOTE: For additional expressions and phrases, see Escalations and De-escalation Tools > Empathize or Phrases/Words for Empathy and Rapport doc. 
Partnering
Follow the below best practices to partner with a pro during a conversation. 
Expresses partnership and a desire for the user to be successful.
Celebrates successes and commends the pro for milestones. 
Did they write something about a wedding? Congratulate them! 
Did they get their first review? Let them know how great that is!
Encourages the pro to improve on areas that they could do better at. This means having tough conversations sometimes.
Be champions for Thumbtack and highlight the benefits of features, processes and product updates. 
Positive positioning
Positive positioning doesn't necessarily have to be revolving around a positive situation. Generally, it's actually about taking a negative situation and making it seem better than it is. 
Negative positioning
Positive positioning
This is not refundable
The reason you were charged for this is because…
We don’t delete reviews.
Unless a review violates our guidelines, it will remain on your profile.
  
The examples above take away triggering words such as “don’t”, “can’t”, or “won’t” and flip it to what can be done.

Below are positive words and phrases to you:
Fantastic!
For the quickest resolution, I would suggest for you to [xyz]
Great!
I appreciate the points you're making, but would you mind if we got back to the subject at hand?
I can fix that.
I think you’ll find it’s much easier if you do [xyz].
Personally, I would recommend you to [xyz]
That’s awesome / great!
That’s good to hear.
We have a few options available, the best one for you is [xyz]
Wonderful!
Would you like to try [xyz]
You can consider [xyz]
You might find [xyz] helpful.
Probing
Probing is a great way to get more context and helps with time management. 
If you ask them to provide more detail, you’ll have more time to form your answer, answer another text, dig into their account, etc.
Can you tell me a little more about it, please?
I really want to help here. Do you mind if I ask you a few more questions?
I want to make sure that I really have an understanding of what you’re telling me. I’m hearing that [xyz]
If I skip anything important, please stop me and let me know.
If I’m understanding you correctly [xyz]
Is there anything I can do for you today?
Please tell me more about your situation.
Tell me what you see as your choices here.
When we have the latest update about [xyz]
Soften facts by adding a question
This is another excellent way to create tone in your writing. 
As employees, we know the facts - we have the answers - and we’re ready to state them. However, adding a question at the end can create a partnering effect.  
Additionally, it’ll stop the pro or customer from feeling like we are saying, “Duh, the answer is right there!”
Example
Instead of
Let’s try
Customer says “I haven’t heard back from any pros."
“I see two pros have messaged you.”
“I see two pros have messaged you. Do you know how to find those messages?”
Pro says “I was charged for 2 leads this past week but I clicked the decline option because I’m already booked those days.”
“There’s a calendar feature to stop this from happening.”
“There’s a calendar feature to stop this from happening. Do you know where to find that?”
In conclusion – state the facts and include a question.
Terms to avoid
“You” can come off as blaming or accusatory. We can take Ownership by restructuring the sentence. When we see ourselves writing a sentence with “You” (especially if it’s the first word in the sentence), let’s try to rewrite it by placing the focus elsewhere. 
Instead of
Let’s try
I’m sorry if you felt my email was condescending - that was not my intention.”
“I’m sorry if my email came off as condescending - that was not my intention.”
The above example shifts the focus (which can come off as blame) from YOU (the pro) to the email.
If we find ourselves writing “You,” this could be a sign we’re trying to defend ourselves or Thumbtack. This is a valid human reaction if we’re feeling the heat of angry pros or customers. However, let’s take a step back.
Additional words or phrases which can be triggering:
Instead of 
Let’s try
Actually
But
However
So 
Well
Unfortunately 
As I mentioned 
As I said
As I wrote in my previous email [message]

3. Conversation etiquette
3. Navigating Non-Voice Converstions: Etiquette and processes 
This section of the internal KA provides general best practices for:  
Starting SMS convo
User goes inactive
Ending SMS convo
Transferred convo
Connectivity issues

Related internal KA: Genesys | SMS & Chat
(Rep) Steps: How to start an SMS conversation
An SMS generally starts with the pro or customer stating their concern. An automated message will pop-up asking the pro or customer to share their email and first and last name. 
In the reps first message, they’ll need to share their name.
Talking point: Hello, my name is [name], and I’m with Thumbtack Service and Support. May I get your full name and email address so I am able to better assist you? 
Talking point: Morning, my name is [name] with Thumbtack support. [Continue with message].
Talking point: Hey there, this is [name]. [Continue with message].
Have the customer or pro verify their information:
Email - The automated first message will ask for their email, but the pro or customer may not respond with it. 
Full name – Don’t ask for the account holder or owner's name. 
Three piece verification – If a rep is making any changes to the account, we’ll verify a third piece of information such as the address.  
Reps can refer to the internal Verify Account Information KA for steps. 
Reps can refer to the internal Account Information (Pro) and Account Information (Customer) | Article #000007604 for guidelines on changes reps can and cannot make for the user. 
(Rep) Steps: Addressing User Inactivity (user goes inactive)
Reps can reference the internal Thumbtack Chat Support (Customer) (Pro) KA > 4. Addressing User Activity for processes around inactivity from the user. 
Reps can reference the internal Genesys | SMS & Chat | Article #000012582 for processes on using Genesys and ending conversations. 
If a pro or customer goes inactive and the advocate has not resolved their concern, follow the below steps:  
After 3 minutes with no response, send a courtesy SMS or chat to remind the user that we are still there to help. 
Talking points:
If concern is unknown:
I can see you’re busy and not able to respond right now. If you have further questions, don’t hesitate to check out our help center or reach out again.
No rush, but it seems like you have stepped away. I’m here to help when you are ready. 
[Pro / cust name], I’m just checking to see if we are still connected. 
If concern is known: 
Looks like you may be busy right now. Whenever you’re ready, I’ll be here to help. You can also learn more about [topic] here: [insert appropriate help center link] 
This not only provides a consultative service but it may prevent a future contact
If reps do not receive any response after 2 minutes, they are required to deliver the recommended plus one, closing and survey spiel then manage the case and documentation accordingly.
Talking point: Ending a SMS conversation
Reps can reference the internal Genesys | SMS & Chat | Article #000012582 for processes on using Genesys to end conversations. 
If a pro or customer is still active and the rep has resolved their concern, the rep can use the following talking point:
Have a great day. 
Thanks for chatting with me, and I hope you have a great evening. 
Glad I was able to help you today, and thank you for partnering with Thumbtack. You may receive a short survey and I would appreciate your feedback about our interaction today. If you have any other questions, visit our help center https://help.thumbtack.com/ 
Talking point: Introduction when taking a transferred conversation
Reps can reference the internal Genesys | SMS & Chat | Article #000012582 for processes on using Genesys and transferring conversations. 
Example: Hello, my name is [name], and I’m with Thumbtack Service and Support, the conversation was transferred to me. Please give me a moment to review the previous conversation to better assist you. 
(Rep) Steps: Navigating Connectivity Issues (Message failures)
Reps can reference the internal Genesys | SMS & Chat | Article #000012582 to learn more about message failures and Genesys. 
There may be times where we have a connectivity issue and your message won’t be sent to the customer or pro. If this happens, follow these steps: 
Send a final message to the customer or pro. This is for cases where your message does get through to set expectations. 
Example: It seems like my messages are not getting through to you. I will send you a follow up email to offer other forms of assistance. [If pro has phone support] You can also give us a call at (866)-501-5809.)]  I’m sorry for any inconvenience.
Report the problem to your manager. 
Submit a help desk ticket with any information you can provide, including screenshots. CC your manager on the help desk ticket. 
Send the customer or pro a follow up email detailing what had happened so far in the conversation, offer solutions if possible, and always give them other options in which they can contact us. 
Email template below: 
Hey [pros name],
I am sorry we were unable to finish our conversation. There was a technical malfunction with our messaging tool. 
Here is a summary of what we have talked about already. [Summarize conversation].
Based on the conversation, here are some solutions that may help the situation. [Explain steps and solutions].
Please feel free to contact us through this channel at a later time. [If pro has phone support (You can also give us a call at (866)-501-5809 during our hours of operation or reply to this email and I will be happy to continue helping you.]
Thank you for your understanding. I hope to hear from you soon. 
[Advocate Name]

articles.fullText:
New Pro Bundled Enrollment (Pro) (Experiment)

Contents

Overview
Experiment details
Pro experience
Comparison between baseline and experiment experience
Experiment experience for new pros
Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article details the New Pro Bundled Enrollment experiment, which introduces a streamlined onboarding flow for new pros in six occupations (Auto Mechanic, Cleaner, Handyman, Electrician, Landscaper, Plumber)..
What
Starting January 28, 2026, Thumbtack will test a new way to onboard new pros in five specific occupations: Auto Mechanic, Cleaner, Handyman, Electrician, Landscaper, and Plumber.  
Note: This experiment is an expansion of the previous Bundled categories experiment from H1 2025. The previous experiment covered Electrician, Handyman, Landscaper, General Contractor, and Plumber, and is now being re-tested with an expanded list of categories. 
Why
By allowing for quicker activation through this bundled enrollment, Thumbtack aims to address pros' feedback that managing numerous individual categories, decreasing the need for pros to go into the services tab and activate each job type one by one.The ultimate goal is to accelerate onboarding, improve lead quality, and thereby enhance pros' overall success on Thumbtack.
How
Currently, new pros select individual categories for the services they offer. During this experiment, new pros will experience a streamlined targeting setup that uses category bundles instead of individual categories.
Here’s a glance of the new onboarding flow for new pros in the affected occupations:
Bundled Category Enrollment: While pros already select services in bundles, the key change in this experiment is that the targeting preferences defined during onboarding will now be applied to all selected job types, instead of requiring individual targeting setup post-onboarding.
Occupational Level Preferences: Pros will answer targeting questions once in the onboarding flow.
Automatic Activation: The targeting answers (including budget) will be applied to all selected job types. Passing EMR (Eligibility, Membership, and Risk) will automatically activate the pro in all selected job types.
A new post-onboarding message/visual will be shown to pros, clearly stating that they are set up to receive leads for all job types selected during onboarding, and they can refine their targeting preferences by going to the Services tab.

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

Experiment details
This section provides details about the Next Gen Targeting experiment. 
Launch date: January 28, 2026
End date: TBD
Impacted users: Randomly triggered for 50% of the visitors to the new pro onboarding page for five occupations nationwide. 
Auto Mechanic
Cleaner
Handyman
Electrician
Landscaper
Plumber
Rollout: This is an experiment. Roughly 50% of new pros in these occupations will be randomly assigned to the new experience, and 50% will have the current experience. This will allow us to measure the impact of the changes.
Platform: This change affects web and app (iOS and Android) pros.
Pro experience
Comparison of Baseline and Experiment Experiences
To further illustrate the differences between the current onboarding experience and the new experiment variant, the following table provides a high-level comparison. 

Baseline Experience
Experiment Variant Experience (New)
Baseline pros select individual categories (e.g., Faucet Repair, Toilet Installation, Pipe Leak Repair).
The targeting defined in onboarding will be applied to all job types selected (instead of just one, requiring post-onboarding setup). 
Pros targeting selection only applies to one of the job types selected
Auto-enrollment is applied only for the job types selected. The difference is how the targeting applies to multiple job types.
Preferences for baseline pros are set per category
Occupational level preferences for variant pros apply across all job types per job category 
Experiment experience for new pros
For new pros in the experiment, the onboarding experience will be as follows: 
Faster Onboarding: During the onboarding process, new pros in the Auto Mechanic, Cleaner, Handyman, Electrician, Landscaper, and Plumber occupations can target multiple job types in onboarding.
Example: Instead of selecting ‘Faucet Repair’ and ‘Toilet Installation’ and only defining targeting for ‘Faucet Repair’ in onboarding (baseline), a plumber selecting those services will have targeting applied for both in onboarding (variant).
Auto-enrollment: New pros will automatically have their targeting implemented for the selected services in onboarding. They can later adjust/fine-tune their preferences in their settings. 
Activation: Passing EMR automatically activates the pro in all job types selected during onboarding.
Impact: New pros will likely receive a wider variety of leads as they are initially enrolled in broader categories. This should lead to more overall contacts and hires per pro. Pros have the ability to refine their targeting preferences in their settings.
Wider Lead Variety (Initially): New pros may initially receive a wider variety of leads as they are automatically enrolled in broader targeting for their selected services . This should lead to more overall contacts and hires per pro
Control: Pros will still have the ability to refine their targeting preferences in their settings after onboarding. 

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

If a pro ends up with a lead that doesn't quite match their preferences, they should request a refund as usual.

1. Overview
▶ KA summary
This internal knowledge article provides frontline reps with details to support pros enrolled in Smarter Lead Matching. This KA covers how the experience works, how pros manage their job preferences and lead prices, and how reps can support them. For historical context on the Beta pilot that preceded Smarter Lead Matching, see the Beta pilot reference section at the bottom of this KA.
What smarter lead matching is
Smarter lead matching is Thumbtack's AI-powered lead matching experience for some existing pros and 50% of new pros. It replaces the rigid, category-based targeting system with a smarter, more responsive experience that learns a pro's job preferences over time based on their activity and feedback.
Instead of managing preferences for individual service categories, pros target broader trades and let the AI refine their matches. The system gets smarter the more a pro engages — every time a pro declines a lead, requests a refund, or adjusts their preferences, the AI updates its understanding of what jobs are a good fit.
Smarter lead matching is not a pilot or a limited-time offering. It is an improved experience that will continue to expand.
Why Thumbtack launched smarter lead matching

Internal why: Existing pros feel the current targeting system does not reflect the full scope of work they can do. Rigid, checkbox-based preferences limit the quality and quantity of matches. This initiative moves Thumbtack toward more and better matches while unlocking latent supply in the marketplace.
External pro facing why (Existing pros): Your current preferences don't show the full picture of the work you can do. Smarter lead matching uses AI to learn your specific preferences so you get more of the leads you want.
How smarter lead matching works
The system learns and updates a pro's preferences based on three key signals:
Pro declines: Selecting "Can't do it" on a new lead
Refunds: Requesting a refund because a job did not align with their skill set
Continuous feedback: Adjusting learned matches directly in their account
Preference tune ups (batched feedback): Pros are periodically asked to review recent leads in bulk and tell us which job types that want more (or less) of
Reps may share the (unsearchable) What is smarter lead matching? - Thumbtack Help article with existing pros in this experience. For new pros, reps can share the (searchable) What is smarter lead matching? — Thumbtack Help article.
Enhanced refund protections:
Skill-set mismatch: When a pro declines a lead by selecting "Not what I do," the system asks clarifying questions, generates a new preference, and issues a refund for that lead automatically
Duplicate customers: When a pro requests a refund for duplicate customer contact, refunds are granted, even if the jobs are different.
To learn more, pros can refer to the Refund policy for smarter lead matching article. 
Updates
These updates are listed by newest updates first. For the full Beta pricing timeline in chronological order, see the Beta pricing transition entry below.

▶ NDFP Pricing V2 rolled out: Aug 3, 2026

Starting August 3, 2026, Thumbtack is rolling out NDFP Pricing v2, a backend update to how lead prices are calculated in smarter lead matching. Pros do not need to change anything — pricing v2 only changes how Thumbtack calculates where a lead lands inside a pro's existing price range. 
[Internal note: Do not refer to "pricing v1" or "pricing v2" with pros. There is no pro-facing name for this change — pros simply experience updated lead pricing.] 
What's different: 
Pricing v1 (the original MVP pricing): priced leads at a broad, trade-wide level. 
Pricing v2: 
prices each lead based on the specific job type within a trade more accurately (for example, a water heater installation vs. a faucet repair within Plumbing), anchored to what pros have historically paid for that specific type of job. This corrects some starting prices that were set too low under v1. 
The bottom of a pro's price range is now a "soft" floor rather than a hard minimum. Some lower-value leads may be priced below the minimum shown on the Lead prices page. 
NOTE: Leads are still never priced above the maximum, on either v1 or v2. 
See How lead pricing works in smarter lead matching and How the final lead price is determined below. 
Who this applies to:  Pricing v2 is applied per trade, not per pro: 
A pro newly onboarding into smarter lead matching on or after Aug 3, 2026 — their trades start on v2. 
A new trade added by an existing pro on or after Aug 3, 2026 — that new trade is priced on v2. 
A pro's trades that were already active in smarter lead matching before Aug 3, 2026 stay on v1 until a separate, later migration (timing TBD).  
A single pro can have some trades on v1 and others on v2 at the same time. 
[Internal note: Do not refer to "pricing v1" or "pricing v2" with pros. There is no pro-facing name for this change — pros simply experience updated lead pricing.] 
The one visible change for pros:
For some lower-value jobs, the lead may be priced below the minimum. This is intentional and means the pro is paying a price that matches a smaller job. When a lead is priced below the minimum, the “what you paid” section on the lead view will say: “Occasionally, lead prices may be lower than your range, but they'll never exceed the maximum you set.". 

▶ Smarter lead matching expanded to new pros
New pros signing up are automatically onboarded into smarter lead matching during sign-up. They do not go through the same enrollment flow as existing pros and can’t opt out of the experience.
Washington D.C. and Baltimore markets on or after June 2, 2026
50% of all new pros on or after August 3, 2026 (See How to check a pro's smarter lead matching eligibility and enrollment status)
Here is what reps need to know:
New pros are automatically onboarded into NDFP MVP during sign-up and cannot opt out, unlike existing pros who can opt out at any time.
New pros set a single bid price range at the occupation level instead of managing individual service-category prices.
Business and performance insights are currently unavailable.
To learn how AI generated preferences work for new pros, refer to the New pro onboarding section below. 
For the pro onboarding flow, see the Onboarding and activation requirements (EMR) (Pro) KA
Trades and job types
Before supporting a pro in this experience, reps should understand how services are organized in smarter lead matching. This is different from the category-based system most pros are familiar with.

Term
What it means
Example
Trade
(known internally as occupation)
The broadest level of work a pro targets. Replaces individual service categories.
Plumber, Handyman, House Cleaner
Job types
The specific types of work within a trade that the AI uses to refine matching.
Fixtures, Pipes, Drains & sewer
When an existing pro enrolls, their existing service categories are automatically converted into trades. The AI generates an initial set of job type preferences based on the pro's profile, settings, and job history. Pros can remove any preferences that do not apply.
For new pros, there is no prior profile history or job history to draw from. Instead, a tag recommendations model generates their initial job type preferences based on data collected during onboarding — including the service name they enter, their service introduction, and any reviews. These are shown as editable suggestions on the job type preferences screen during sign-up
Pilot details
This section provides reps with the key details about the current smarter lead matching experience and the Beta pilot that preceded it. Use this section to quickly identify which experience a pro is on and confirm whether they are eligible.

Smarter lead matching (MVP)
Status: Active
Launch date: Week of April 20, 2026
Comms date: March 30, 2026
External term: Smarter lead matching
DO refer to smarter lead matching as an improved experience.
DON'T Refer to smarter lead matching as a "pilot" or "experiment.”
Internal term: New deal for pros MVP or Hybrid preferences
Target markets: 
Baltimore, Maryland 
Washington, D.C. (Hagerstown) 
50% of all new pros nationwide
▶ * Definition: DMA (Designated Market Area)
A DMA (Designated Market Area) is a regional geographic grouping used in the United States. It covers a broader area than a single city. For example, the Washington, D.C. (Hagerstown) DMA includes not just Washington, D.C. but also surrounding areas. This means a pro may be eligible for Smarter Lead Matching even if they are not located in Baltimore city or Washington, D.C. city specifically.

Audience
Who is included
Who is excluded
Existing pros
Existing pros in the Baltimore DMA and Washington, D.C. (Hagerstown) DMA with >75% of recent contacts within targeted markets.
Managed account pros
Pros with integrations connected to their Thumbtack account
Pros who have not completed EMR
Pros who have not accepted any contacts
New pros
New pros signing up in the target markets are automatically onboarded into smarter lead matching:
June 2, 2026: D.C./Baltimore market
August 3, 2026: 50% of all new pros
Pros signing up outside the D.C./Baltimore market
Pros who integrate with Housecall Pro, Workiz, Jobber, GoSite, or ServiceTitan — pros who select an integration during the onboarding survey 
Do’s and Don’ts
The following table includes guidelines for reps to follow when contacted by a pro who is participating in the New Deal for Pros experience.

Category
Do's (Your Action)
Don'ts (Actions to Avoid)
Resources
DO Share the help article with eligible pros in the MVP experience: What is smarter lead matching? — Thumbtack Help.
For new pros, share this article with them:  What is smarter lead matching? — Thumbtack Help. 
Don't Use internal content to directly explain personalized preferences to a pro. Refer them to the dedicated support resources. 
Terminology
DO Refer to smarter lead matching as an improved experience
DON'T Refer to smarter lead matching as a "pilot" or "experiment"
Preference management expectations
DO Explain that preferences help signal which jobs are a good fit.
DON'T Describe preferences as a strict "allowlist" or "blocklist."
Pricing disputes or history
DO check the pro's chronological price ranges, saved lead prices, and competitiveness estimates in Admin to resolve disputes. Refer to the Occupation Bid Setting History (NDFP) Admin section below
DON'T manually edit or override a pro's trade-level lead price ranges in Admin, as pros must adjust these settings themselves in their account.
Competition
DO Inform smarter lead matching pros they follow the standard competition factors (same as baseline). See Thumbtack's Quality Commitment (Pro) KA.
DON'T Promise a limit of only two other pros for smarter lead matching.
Insights
DO Let pros know that performance insights are not available in the smarter lead matching experience.
DON'T Attempt to troubleshoot missing business insights for smarter lead matching pros.
Travel
DO Explain that travel preferences now apply globally to all trades and can be found on the pro's profile.
DON'T Look for travel settings within individual service or trade pages.
Opt-out (existing pros)
DO explain to existing pros that they can opt out at any time from the bottom of their Services page, and can re-enroll at any time after opting out.
DON'T imply opt-out is unavailable to existing pros.
Opt-out (new pros)
DO answer questions about the experience factually based on what the pro is seeing in their account.
DON'T tell new pros they are in a different experience from "baseline" or that any other experience exists. Explain that their account is set up with the current lead matching experience and leave it at that.
 How to check a pro's smarter lead matching eligibility and enrollment status
Frontline reps can check whether a pro is eligible for smarter lead matching (internally: NDFP MVP) and confirm their current enrollment status from the main User page in Admin under Occupation Targeting.
IMPORTANT: Reps should NOT use the “Disable” or “Enable” button. 
▶ New pros in NDFP MVP
New pros signing up in the Washington D.C. and Baltimore markets on or after June 2, 2026 are automatically onboarded into Smarter Lead Matching during sign-up. They cannot opt out of the experience. 50% of new pros are also onboarded into smarter lead matching starting August 3, 2026.
In Admin, the Occupation Targeting field will display: 
Not Eligible for Occupation Targeting MVP
This user is not eligible for MVP
MVP is enabled
Enrolled: timestamp of when they signed up 

[Image: rtaImage]

The “not eligible” terminology should be disregarded here. 
▶ Existing pros in NDFP MVP
Starting April 20, 2026, existing pros in the Baltimore, Maryland DMA and Washington, D.C. (Hagerstown) DMA were made eligible to enroll in Smarter Lead Matching. They can opt out of the experience and back in.
In Admin, the Occupation Targeting field will display: 
Not Eligible for Occupation Targeting Alpha/Beta
This user is eligible for MVP
MVP is enabled
Enrolled: A timestamp of the pro's most recent enrollment action 

[Image: rtaImage]

NOTE: If you see, “MVP Is disabled” - the pro is either: 1) is eligible but has not enrolled OR 2) enrolled but has it turned OFF. (Reps can use the New Deal for Pros (NDFP) MVP opt-in / opt-out history query to see when a pro opted out)
How to check when a pro was enrolled in or opted out of smarter lead matching
Reps can see if a pro is eligible for or has enrolled into the smarter lead matching experience using the Occupation Targeting section on the main User Admin page. However, to see exactly when a pro enrolled or opted out, reps can use the New Deal for Pros (NDFP) MVP opt-in / opt-out history query. 
Common use cases:
A pro disputes a lead charge and you need to confirm whether they were enrolled in NDFP MVP at the exact time of the charge, since NDFP MVP pricing (min/max range) and baseline pricing work differently
A pro's experience or pricing seems inconsistent and you need to confirm whether their enrollment status changed around the time in question
Any investigation where knowing the exact timing of a pro's enrollment or opt-out is relevant
Where to find the query: The query is in the S&S SQL Queries sheet, row 22: New Deal for Pro (NDFP) MVP opt in / opt out history on the Queries: Pro Settings tab.
Reading the query results: Once the query runs, focus on the status and event_timestamp columns to answer the enrollment timing question. Note that the query will sort the timestamps so that the latest (newest) one is at the top. 
▶ What the results look like

[Image: rtaImage]

For general guidance on running BigQuery queries — including how to enter parameters, read results, and handle errors — refer to the internal Big Query (Run Support Query) (Rep) KA.
How to see whether a lead was from smarter lead matching on the Negotiations page
When investigating a specific lead, reps can confirm whether it came in while the pro was enrolled in NDFP MVP by checking the Contact Price Details section on the Negotiations page in Admin.
If the lead was received while the pro was enrolled in NDFP MVP, the following fields will appear under Contact Price Details:
price_min_at_setting
price_max_at_setting
price_single_at_setting
▶ What it looks like in Admin

[Image: rtaImage]


These fields are specific to NDFP contacts and will not appear for non-NDFP leads. The values shown next to these fields can be ignored — their presence or absence is what matters. 

Rep note: This is particularly useful when investigating a pricing dispute for a pro who has since opted out of NDFP. Even if their enrollment status has changed, the presence of these fields on a specific lead confirms that NDFP pricing was in effect at the time of that charge. Use this alongside the Occupation Bid Settings History and the NDFP opt-in / opt-out BigQuery query for a complete picture.
2. New pro onboarding 
New pros are automatically onboarded into smarter lead matching during sign-up: 
Washington D.C. and Baltimore markets on or after June 2, 2026
50% of new pros on or after August 3, 2026
To see if a new pro is onboarded into smarter lead matching, refer to the How to check a pro's smarter lead matching eligibility and enrollment status section above. 
For the full onboarding flow, see the Onboarding and activation requirements (EMR) (Pro) KA. It covers the complete step-by-step experience for all new pros, including those onboarding into smarter lead matching. 
Two things specific to smarter lead matching to note:
Job types are AI-generated, not pulled from history. Unlike existing pros whose initial job types come from their profile history and past activity, new pros have no prior Thumbtack history to draw from. Instead, a tag recommendations model generates their initial preferences based on data collected during onboarding itself — including the business name they enter, their business introduction, and any reviews. These are surfaced as editable recommendations, and pros can delete anything that doesn't apply before continuing. 
Lead prices aren't set during onboarding. New pros aren't prompted to set a price range as part of sign-up. Once onboarding is complete, they need to visit the Lead Prices section on their Services page to set their range themselves. They're nudged to do this via a post-onboarding welcome email.

2. Enrollment for existing pros
Existing pros in the Baltimore, Maryland DMA and Washington, D.C. (Hagerstown) DMA are made eligible to enroll in smarter lead matching. When they open the app or visit the website they will see a full-screen enrollment flow that walks them through setup. Pros must complete this flow to enroll — it is not automatic.
Pros can snooze the enrollment screen for up to three days by tapping Remind me later. After three days the screen returns and cannot be dismissed until the pro completes enrollment. Pros can opt out at any time after enrolling.
Note: The enrollment flow below ONLY applies to existing pros in the Baltimore and Washington D.C. markets. 
Introduction: The pro sees a full-screen introduction to three changes: simplified matching, simplified pricing controls, and simplified refunds. The pro taps Get started to begin enrollment or Remind me later to snooze.
Rep note: "Remind me later" is a snooze, not an opt-out. If a pro says they tapped it and think they are not enrolled, clarify that enrollment is still pending and the screen will return within three days.
Confirm your trades: The pro sees their AI-generated trades and job types, pulled from their profile, settings, and history. The pro taps Edit trades to make changes or Looks good to confirm and continue.
Rep note: If a pro says their trades look wrong at this step, they can tap Edit trades to correct them before continuing. They can also add or remove trades after enrollment from the What you do section on their Services page.
Review job types: For each trade the pro reviews two AI-generated lists: Get more like these and Get less like these. The pro taps X to remove a job type from either list. If they remove something by mistake they can tap Undo to restore it. The pro taps Looks good to continue.
Rep note: These lists are not a strict allowlist or blocklist. They are signals the AI uses to learn what is a good fit over time. Do not describe them to pros as a guarantee of "only this" or "never this."
Set lead price ranges: The pro sets a min/max lead price range for each trade using a slider. The screen explains that leads for smaller, simpler jobs cost less and leads for complex, higher-value jobs cost more. The pro taps Next to continue.
Rep note: If a pro moves through this step without adjusting the slider their range stays at the system-generated default. They will see a warning on their Services page after enrolling prompting them to update it.
Refunds introduction: The pro sees an explanation of the updated refund experience — if they get a lead for a job type that does not match what they do, they can decline it and Thumbtack will refund them right away. The pro taps Done to complete enrollment.
After enrollment confirmation: The pro sees a confirmation that smarter lead matching is live. The modal lists two things that still need their attention:
Update your lead prices — trade price ranges are currently set at a default amount
Refine your lead matches — review and add job types to get tailored leads faster

3. Navigating the Services page
The Services page looks and works differently for pros enrolled in smarter lead matching compared to the baseline experience. Reps should be familiar with this layout so they can orient a pro quickly when they call in confused about what they are seeing.
▶ What the Services page looks like
Image 1: Services page with warning banners
Image 2: Services page with banner to review recent leads

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

Review recent leads: Pros may see a banner along the top of their services page prompting them to review their recent leads to keep their preferences up to date. See the + preference tune up + section below to learn more. 
Lead prices: Shows the pro's current trade-level lead price range. 
Warning alert: After enrollment this section shows a warning: "Set to default amounts — please update prices." This warning means the pro's price range was automatically set to a system-generated starting point when they enrolled and they have not yet updated it. Direct them to tap Lead prices to review and set their own range. 
What you do: Lists each of the pro's trades. For each trade the pro sees:
Their most frequent job type — for example "Your most frequent job is faucet repair"
A Pause or Resume option to stop or restart receiving leads for that trade
A Refine your matches link to manage job type preferences. Tapping Refine your matches for any trade opens the preferences page for that trade. This is where the pro manages which job types they want more or less of. For full detail on how this works see the Managing preferences and matches section of this KA.
Warning alert: Some trades may show a warning: "We pulled in past preferences — please review." This means the AI automatically migrated the pro's existing category-level targeting into the new trade structure when they enrolled. The pro should tap Refine your matches for that trade and remove any job types that no longer apply.
Performance: Detailed business performance insights are not available in smarter lead matching. If a pro asks why their performance dashboard looks different or data they used to see is missing, Support rep will: 
Let them know this is expected and that detailed insights are not part of this experience. 
NOT attempt to troubleshoot missing business insights for smarter lead matching pros.
Opt-out: At the very bottom of the Services page FOR EXISTING PROS ONLY, below all other content: "Not loving the new lead system? If you no longer want to participate, you can revert to your prior targeting experience after sharing final feedback." This option is intentionally understated and requires the pro to share feedback before reverting. 
Do not proactively direct pros toward it. 
If a pro asks how to opt out, direct them to the What is smarter lead matching? Help article for steps.
NOTE: New pros in the Washington D.C. and Baltimore markets who signed up on or after June 2, 2026 are automatically onboarded into smarter lead matching and cannot opt out of the experience.
4. Managing preferences and matches
After enrolling pros have two ways to refine what leads they receive — through their activity on leads and directly through their Services page.
How the AI learns from lead activity
The AI continuously updates a pro's preferences based on how the pro responds to leads. The two key signals are:
Declining a lead and selecting "Not what I do" — triggers the full decline and refund flow below
Requesting a refund because a job did not align with their skill set
Batch feedback: Pros are periodically asked to review their recent leads and tell us which job types they want more or less of. 
Declining leads 
When a pro receives a lead that is not a good fit they can decline it from the lead view by tapping Can't do it. This is the most important feedback signal in smarter lead matching — when a pro selects Not what I do as their reason, the system learns from it, updates their preferences, and issues a refund automatically.
Reps should understand this flow well because it is the primary way the AI improves over time and the primary way pros get refunds for mismatched leads.
Initiate the decline: The pro taps Can't do it on the lead.  
Rep note: Can't do it is only available if the pro has not yet replied to the customer. If a pro already replied and then realized the job is not a fit, they need to request a refund through the standard refund process instead. The decline flow and its automatic refund are not available at that point.
Select a reason: The pro chooses why they are declining. Reason options include location, not available, low job value, duplicate job, too much competition, and Not what I do.
Rep note: Only Not what I do triggers the preference update and automatic refund. All other reasons decline the lead without updating preferences or issuing a refund. This is the most common source of confusion when a pro says they declined a lead but did not get a refund — ask which reason they selected.
Explain why: If the pro selects Not what I do a required text field appears asking them to explain. The response must be at least 10 characters. The pro taps Next to continue.
Rep note: The explanation the pro enters here is what the AI uses to generate clarifying questions in the next step. Encourage pros to be specific — a vague explanation may result in less useful clarifying questions and a less accurate preference being generated.
AI clarifying questions: The AI processes the pro's explanation and asks one or more follow-up questions to better understand the preference. Questions are dynamically generated based on the pro's trade and the specific job they declined, so they will look different every time. 
Rep note: If a pro asks why they were asked a specific question, explain that the AI generates questions based on the job they declined and their trade. Reps will not be able to predict or explain the specific questions in advance.
Preference suggestion: Based on the pro's answers the AI generates a new preference and asks the pro to confirm it. The preference is shown as a plain language statement — for example: "Does not do commercial jobs." The pro confirms with Yes or rejects with No.
Two important things about this step:
If the pro taps Yes, the preference is applied to future leads and the refund is issued. The preference cannot be edited for 45 days.
If the pro taps No, the preference is not applied and a refund request is submitted for the Refund Ops team to review.
Rep note: If a pro confirmed a preference and now wants to change it, let them know it will be editable after 45 days. In the meantime they can manage other job types from Refine your matches on their Services page. If a pro rejected a preference and wants to add it manually, direct them to Refine your matches where they can add it to Get less like these.
Confirmation: The pro sees a confirmation that the new preference will be applied to future leads and the declined lead will be refunded. The pro taps Done to close the flow. The refund is issued automatically at this point. The pro does not need to take any further action to receive it.
Rep note: If a pro says they completed the decline flow but did not receive a refund, confirm they selected Not what I do as their reason and tapped Yes on the preference suggestion. If they did both and the refund has not appeared, escalate through the standard refund process

Refining matches
Pros can manage their job preferences directly from the What you do section on their Services page without going through the decline flow. Tapping Refine your matches for any trade opens the preferences page for that trade.
Preferences are organized into two lists:
Get more like these — job types the pro wants more of
Get less like these — job types the pro wants less of
Preferences the AI generated are marked with a sparkle icon
[Image: rtaImage]
. Pros can edit these the same way they edit manually added preferences. 

▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

REP NOTE: These lists are not a strict allowlist or blocklist. They are signals that help the AI learn over time. Do not describe them as a guarantee of "only this" or "never this." If a pro asks why they are still receiving a job type they added to Get less like these, explain that preferences inform the AI but do not hard-block specific job types.
▶ Adding a job type
The pro taps Add next to either list and searches the catalog for job types to add. They can select multiple job types before saving. The pro taps + to select and Add to save.  After saving a confirmation toast appears at the bottom of the screen.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

What adding to each list tells the AI:
Get more like these: Adding this job type signals to the AI that this type of work is an excellent fit for the pro's business. The AI will prioritize sending related leads but does not guarantee the pro will only receive that type of work
Get less like these: Adding this job type signals to the AI that it should try to avoid sending these jobs in the future. The AI will deprioritize related leads and does not block it entirely.
These are signals to the AI, not hard rules: If a pro asks why they are still receiving a job type they added to Get less like these, explain that the AI uses these preferences to inform matching over time but does not hard-block specific job types.
Things reps should know about the add flow:
Job type already in the same or opposite list: Pro cannot have the same job type in both lists at the same time. Shows "Already in More/Less like these"
Search term not in catalog: Shows "Not a known job type"
▶ Missing job type and adding feedback
If a pro cannot find a job type they are looking for, they can tap Can't find the job type you need? Tell us at the bottom of the search sheet. This opens a short survey where the pro can describe the missing job type and tap Submit feedback for Thumbtack's review. Their suggestion has been received but will not be added immediately.
NOTE: There is no way for reps to add job types on a pro's behalf.
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

▶ Removing a job type

Pros can refine their matches by removing job types from their preferences. The pro taps X next to any job type. After saving a confirmation toast appears at the bottom of the screen.
What removing from each list tells the AI:
Get more like these: Removing a job type tells the AI to stop prioritizing related leads. The AI will no longer treat this as a signal that the work is a good fit.
Get less like these: Removing a job type tells the AI to stop deprioritizing related leads. The AI will no longer treat this as a signal to avoid this type of work.
When removing from Get more like these the pro has two options:
Yes, remove job — removes the job type from the list only
Remove & add to "Less like these" — moves it to the opposite list in one step▶ What it looks like[Image: rtaImage]
When removing from Get less like these the pro has two options:
Yes, remove job — removes the job type from the list only
Remove & add to "More like these" — moves it to the opposite list in one step▶ What it looks like[Image: rtaImage]

Rep note: If a pro wants to move a job type from one list to the other, the quickest path is tapping X and selecting the move option rather than removing it and then adding it manually to the other list. This also ensures the AI signal is updated correctly in one action rather than having a gap between the removal and the re-add. 
Preference tune up (Batch feedback)

Periodically, pros are prompted to do a preference tune up — a chance to review their recent leads in bulk and tell us how well each job type is matching their business.. Pros with a connected app (e.g., HouseCallPro, Jobber, Workiz, etc.) can earn a lead credit (see step 5 below). Non-integrated pros see the same flow but aren't eligible for the credit.

A preference tune up is triggered on a 7-day rolling cadence — 10 or more leads received in the past 7 days, or at least 5 leads at the 14-day mark for lower-volume pros. It won't trigger if the pro's business is hidden, all trades are paused, or they've already adjusted preferences in the last 30 days.

Job types on the preference tune up screen only covers leads received in the review window — it doesn't include Opportunities or other job types, and any paused or removed trades are excluded entirely. Leads that already have a refund request tied to them are also excluded from the pool, so a pro can't earn credit and a refund on the same lead.

How it works 
Pros are prompted through an Insights email, or banners on their For You and Services pages. All three stay active for up to a week or until the pro completes the review. 
When a pro clicks Review recent leads from a banner (or "No, not a good fit" from the email), they're taken to the Preference Tune Up page. Here, they see one trade with up to 10 job types and how many recent leads came in for each. Pros with more than one trade review each trade on its own screen, tapping Next to move to the next one.
For each job type, the pro uses a slider to tell us whether they want more or fewer leads like it, with an expandable list of recent leads shown for context. They don't have to adjust every slider, but it's recommended to keep their preferences updated and get leads that fit.
On the last trade, the button changes from Next to Update preferences. Tapping it submits the pro's answers.
Integrated pros who move at least one slider earn a Thumbtack credit when they submit. The amount is based on the median lead price for their trade. If they have more than one trade, they get credit for whichever trade pays the most, not both combined. Pros can only earn this credit once every 30 days.


[Image: rtaImage]

Travel areas and out-of-market leads

Travel preferences in smarter lead matching work differently from the standard experience and are a common source of confusion. There are two separate things reps should understand: how travel areas are set, and how to identify an out-of-market lead in historical data — this was more common earlier in NDFP's rollout and isn't expected to happen with current leads.
How travel areas work
Travel preferences now apply globally across all of a pro's trades and are managed from the pro's profile — not from the Services page. Any change a pro makes to their travel area applies to all trades at once. 
▶ Historical context: out-of-market leads
Earlier in NDFP's rollout, a pro's legacy category targeting settings could still be active for areas outside the test market. When a lead came in from outside the market and matched via those legacy settings, it was free — the pro wasn't charged. This isn't expected to occur with current leads, but reps may still see it referenced when investigating older pricing questions.
The AI learns and refines job type preferences based on the pro's activity. It does not adjust travel area — that's always controlled by the pro manually from their profile.
How to identify the lead type in Admin

When investigating a lead charge on the Negotiation page in Admin, the syndication type confirms how the lead was matched and whether a charge applies.

Scenarios
Syndication type
What it means
Charge?
Lead from within Baltimore or D.C. (Hagerstown) DMA, matched via NDFP targeting
INSTANT_RESULTS_DIRECT_CONTACT_INSTANT
Standard lead matched through the pro's smarter lead matching preferences. This is the most common syndication type for NDFP pros.

TARGETING_V2_NOT_ENROLLED_CONTACT_FREE

Rep note: If a pro asks about a past lead from outside their area, explain that targeting settings may have still been active outside the Baltimore/D.C. DMAs earlier in the rollout — this isn't expected for current leads. If a pro asks why an older lead was free, use the table above.
Rep note — AI and travel: If a pro asks whether the AI will learn their travel preferences the same way it learns job preferences, clarify that it does not. The AI only refines job type matching based on the pro's activity and feedback. Travel area is a separate setting the pro controls manually from their profile — it does not change automatically and is not influenced by the leads a pro accepts or declines.

5. Lead price ranges and competition
How lead pricing works in smarter lead matching 
Smarter lead matching changes how pros manage their lead costs and how reps support them. Instead of setting an exact lead price for each service category, pros enrolled in smarter lead matching set one lead price range per trade. Note that some trades show a single lead price rather than a range — this is expected and not all trades use range pricing.
Using the slider on the lead prices page, the pro sets their range — which determines the minimum and maximum they are willing to pay for any single lead within that trade. 
Moving the slider shifts the entire range up or down. 
The minimum of a pro's range is set based on their trade and market to help ensure pros are competitive in their market. 
For trades on pricing v1, pros cannot be charged below this minimum. 
For trades on pricing v2 (see the NDFP Pricing V2 rollout entry above), the minimum shown is a display guide rather than a hard floor. A low-value lead in that trade may be priced below it. 
The maximum is always a hard cap on both v1 and v2: a lead is never priced above it.
The range covers all service categories under that trade. For example, a Plumber's range can apply to fixtures, pipes, drain and sewer, sump pump, septic, gas line, and so on. The pro does not set a separate price for each of these — one range covers all of them.
Lead prices page: Where pros set their ranges 
The lead prices page is where pros manage their pricing. Each trade has its own card on the page. Pros with multiple trades see all of them on the same page, each with its own slider.
▶ What the Lead Prices page looks like
Image 1: What the lead pricing page looks like
Image 2: Screen after clicking how it works” 
Image 3: Screen after clicking “why do lead prices vary”

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

Each trade card shows:
Lead price range and slider: The pro's current min - max range. 
Moving the slider shifts the entire range up or down — it does not change the width of the range, just where it sits. 
Moving right increases the range and moves toward more leads. 
Moving left decreases the range and moves toward fewer leads.
How you compare: The pro's current competitiveness level. This is an estimate of how well a pro competes against other pros in customer search results.
Estimated leads: An estimate of how many leads a pro will get based on their current pricing settings. This is a forecast, not a guarantee.
Performance: Past 30 days showing total leads and average lead price per trade.
Current weekly budget: Shown at the bottom of the page across all trades.
How the final lead price is determined
The exact amount a pro pays for any given lead is not fixed — it is determined in real time based on the estimated value of the customer's specific job. The pro's lead price range sets the boundaries for what they can be charged, and the job value determines where within that range the price lands.
Pricing updates (August 3, 2026)
For trades on pricing v2, this job-value estimate is anchored to the specific job type within the trade (for example, water heater installation vs. faucet repair within Plumbing) rather than a broad trade-wide average. This is meant to make prices track more closely with what pros have historically been willing to pay for that specific type of work. Trades still on pricing v1 continue to use the broad, trade-wide estimate. See  NDFP Pricing V2 rollout  in the Updates section for which trades are affected and when.
Smaller, simpler jobs land closer to the lower end of the range
Larger, more complex jobs land closer to the higher end
The pro is never charged above their maximum

The price charged for any given lead is determined solely by the pro's price range setting and the estimated size of the customer's job. Competitiveness level, profile quality, and other ranking factors do not affect what the pro is charged — they only affect how often the pro receives leads.
Default price range amounts

When a pro enrolls or onboards into smarter lead matching their price range is initially set at a system-generated default. These are a starting point only. Pros should review and update their range after enrolling.
Pros who have not updated from defaults may receive a push notification: "Important! Update your default prices — Your prices for the new lead matching system are still set to default amounts. Learn about the new system and make pricing updates ASAP." They may also see a warning on their Services page: "Set to default amounts — please update prices." If a pro contacts support after receiving this notification or seeing this warning, direct them to Lead prices on their Services page to review and update their range. 
▶ What the warning on the services page looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

If a pro questions when their defaults were set or whether they have updated their pricing, reps can check the Occupation Bid Settings History in Admin. When a pro's range is initialized at enrollment the Source column will show System set. Once the pro manually updates their pricing it will show Pro set. This is a quick way to confirm whether a pro has reviewed and updated their range or is still on defaults.
How competitiveness works

Competitiveness works the same way in Smarter Lead Matching as it does in the baseline experience. However, the one difference to note for pros enrolled in Smarter Lead Matching: competitiveness is based on the pro's trade-level price range rather than a per-category price. Otherwise the four levels — Less competitive, Competitive, More competitive, and Most competitive — and the factors that determine them (price, business performance, and demand) are the same.
For full details on competitiveness levels, how they are determined, and talking points for pros, see the internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA.
Lead price range vs. weekly budget

The weekly budget works the same way in Smarter Lead Matching as it does in the baseline experience. However, the one thing specific to Smarter Lead Matching: the lead price control is a trade-level range rather than a per-category price. The budget still works as a weekly spending cap across all trades combined.
For full details see the internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA and the Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro) KA.
Where pros can see the cost of a specific lead 
Pros can see the pricing details for any lead directly in their lead view. After receiving a lead the pro can see:
Lead price — Cost of the lead (based on the value of the job)
Total — the exact amount charged for that lead (after discounts when applicable) 
Price range — their lead price range for that trade at the time the lead came in, for example: Your lead price range for [trade] was $11–$120 when this lead came in at $100." 
Below-range note (pricing v2 trades only) — if the lead is priced below the bottom of the pro's range, the lead details page shows: "Occasionally, lead prices may be lower than your range, but they'll never exceed the maximum you set." This only appears when a lead actually prices below the minimum; it does not show on every lead.
Manage lead costs — a link that takes the pro directly to their lead prices page to review or update their range
▶ What the “What you paid” section looks like with a discount

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ What the “What you paid” section looks like when price was lower than the minimum

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ What it looks like in product
[Image: rtaImage]
Rep note: If a pro disputes a charge or says they were charged more than expected, direct them to the lead view first. In most cases seeing the total charged alongside their price range at the time resolves the question. If the charge still looks incorrect after they review, reps can use the Occupation Bid Settings History in Admin to investigate further.
How to help smarter lead matchings pro with questions or disputes around lead pricing (Rep)
When a pro has questions or disputes regarding their lead prices or past changes to their ranges, support reps can use the Occupation Bid Settings History (NDFP) section within the Admin Tool. This section includes these key details:
Bid history: Chronicled changes to the pro's bids, grouped by occupation.
Saved lead prices: The lead prices or price ranges that were displayed to the pro when the bids were saved.
Competitiveness: The estimated competitiveness and lead volumes when the bids were saved.

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
Beginning June 23, 2025, Thumbtack will pilot a partnership with Moen to install their smart water sensors. Pre-qualified plumbing professionals in Las Vegas will handle the service. This article outlines the operational details for Frontline Reps, covering the customer and pro experience, including communication protocols, job assignment types (manual vs. automated), and how to address common questions.
What
On June 23, 2025, Thumbtack launched a pilot partnership with Moen and the Moen Flo, a smart water sensor and valve. In the partnership, pre-qualified plumbing pros in Las Vegas will install these water sensors. 
The Moen Flo is a smart water sensor and valve designed to protect homes from floods, leaks, and other water-related issues. It continuously monitors a home's water system for anomalies. If a problem is detected, it can automatically shut off the water supply to prevent damage. The device also provides insights into water usage and can be controlled remotely via a smartphone app.

[Image: AD_4nXfGUffHnBhHMt6RVFduAM_gdehXAmzK1eVNi1pY-L-97i1cbtu3U7F4qbl50s3RzMb_tv2IWqUfVcMoaF10EpfjlsWxr_vpTG9TGcSDyw19jgjlM87sklY3IzHXwxD7terPqHzF_A]

Why
This pilot program focuses on customer satisfaction, successful installation rates, and pro acceptance rates to ensure a sufficient number of qualified pros are available for Moen installations. This partnership benefits Thumbtack by building brand awareness, offers a valuable service to customers, and provides plumbing pros with job opportunities
How
Moen bundles the Moen Flo device and installation services for a flat, nationwide cost, partnering with Farmers Insurance. 
Thumbtack will pilot an offering to facilitate these installations with minor changes to the existing preset job infrastructure. 
These installations will be handled with Thumbtack’s network of qualified pros. 
The Moen Flo requires installation by a licensed plumber, which Thumbtack can provide. 
Here’s a brief look at how this pilot works for users:
Customers: Customers are likely new to Thumbtack and are sources from Moen’s existing customer base. The Thumbtack Operations team will manually manage customer information and job details, contacting customers to create Thumbtack accounts (with consent) and scheduling installations. 
Pros: Pre-qualified plumbing pros in Las Vegas will be contacted by the Thumbtack Ops team with preset job offers. Pros will charge based on the installation type and receive payment from Thumbtack only after submitting documentation of the completed job. 
Reps can refer to the Customer experience and Pro experience  sections below for more details 
Pilot details
This section provides Frontline Reps with specific details about the Moen Flo Partnership Pilot, including its launch date, end date, expected impact, and processes.
Pilot launch date: June 23, 2025
Pilot end date: TBD
Impacted users: Pre-qualified plumbing pros in Las Vegas
Scope:  Single market (Las Vegas), single trade (plumbing), single job type (Moen Flo installation)
Key points
Here are key points about the customer and pro experience in the pilot for frontline reps:
Customers are New to Thumbtack & Sourced by Moen:
Most customers in this pilot will be new to Thumbtack, as they are sourced from Moen's existing customer base (those who recently bought a Moen Flo device).
Installation Payment Handled by Moen: 
Customers do not pay Thumbtack for the installation at the point of service; it's included in their initial Moen device purchase. 
Pros are paid by Thumbtack after submitting job completion documentation.
Communication is Off-App:
All direct communication between pros and customers for this pilot must occur via phone or text, not through the Thumbtack app.
Pro Job Acceptance & Resources: 
Pros receive preset job offers from Thumbtack Ops and can accept or decline. 
Frontline reps can direct pros to a dedicated Help Center article with training resources for Moen Flo installations.
Pro experience 
This section describes the experience for variant pros in the Moen Flo Pilot program.
As a Thumbtack pro, they can claim a Moen installation and receive payment for a completed installation through Thumbtack.
Here’s how the pros experience in the pilot will work: 
Thumbtack contacts pro: The Thumbtack Ops team will contact qualified pros with a preset job offer. Thumbtack matches pros with jobs in two ways:
Automated Claiming: Jobs are made available for pros to claim through an automated system. If no pro claims the job within six hours, sales reps will begin calling pros for the job (manual assignment). 
Manual Assignment: Sales Reps manually call pros from a list to claim jobs.
Notification: If the pro chooses to accept, they’ll receive an email with the details of the job and the customer’s information.
Working with customers: All communication the pro has with the customers during the pilot must happen through phone or text, not through the Thumbtack app.
Charge: Pros will charge depending on the type of installation the job requires. 
Receive payment: Pros will receive payment only after they submit documentation of the completed job to Thumbtack.  
Customer experience
This section details the customer journey within the Moen Flo Partnership Pilot, from initial intake to scheduling and reminders.
Here’s how the customer experience during this pilot will work: 
Thumbtack contacts customer: Customers are sourced from Moen's existing customer base (e.g., those who recently purchased a Moen Flo device). These customers are likely new to Thumbtack. The Thumbtack Operations team will manually manage customer information and job details.
Initial intake: Thumbtack Ops will contact Moen customers, create Thumbtack accounts on their behalf (with consent), gather job details and manage the scheduling and coordination of installation between the Moen customer and the Thumbtack pros. 
Payment: During the pilot, installation is included in the initial cost of the Moen device. This means customers will not be paying through the Thumbtack platform at the point of installation.
Communication: All communication with the pro during this pilot must happen through phone or text, not through the Thumbtack app.
2. Process
Steps: How to help customers with questions (Frontline Rep) 
This section provides Frontline Reps with information on how to help customers with questions about the Moen Flo partnership.
If contacted by a Moen customer, frontline reps will follow these steps: 
When they purchase the Moen Flo product, the customer receives an initial email with information. Frontline reps should direct customers to that email for help. 
If they still need help, frontline reps can post in the #moen-samsung-training Slack channel for next steps. 
Steps: How to help pros with questions (Frontline Rep) 
This section provides Frontline Reps with information on how to help customers with questions about the Moen Flo partnership.
If pros have questions about the Moen Smart partnership or how to handle the Moen Smart Flo Device installation, frontline reps will:  
Send them to the help center article How Moen Flo Installation jobs work – Thumbtack Help article.
