articles.fullText:
Midea air conditioning recall repair program (timed partnership) (Pro)

Contents

Overview
Key points
Program details
Pro experience
Customer experience
Process
Steps: How to participate in Midea recall repair jobs (pro)
Steps: How to get compensated if they’re unable to complete the job (pro)
Resources
1. Overview 
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article for reps explains the partnership between Midea and Thumbtack, where Midea customers can hire Thumbtack pros to fix recalled air conditioning units. The partnership was piloted starting June 20, 2025, in the New York area (Manhattan and Brooklyn). On July 23, 2025, we added select zip codes in SD, RI, ND, KS, TX, MO, NM, WY, ME, and VT. The full partnership is only expected to last about 5 weeks, which is how long the demand for pros is expected. [ end of summary]
What
Starting June 20, 2025, Thumbtack pros can be hired to repair Midea air conditioning units impacted by a recall. The partnership between Thumbtack and Midea was initially piloted for pros in the New York area (Manhattan and Brooklyn), and expanded to select zip codes in SD, RI, ND, KS, TX, MO, NM, WY, ME, and VT. We plan to launch it nationwide if successful. The recall program is expected to run until the end of July.
Why
Some versions of Midea air conditioning units (Midea U and U+ Window Air Conditioners) retain water, causing mold issues. Midea needs pros who can repair the recalled units for their customers.
How
Customers: Midea’s customers can either request a refund through Midea, or hire a pro through Midea’s partnership with Thumbtack to repair the unit. Customers who want to repair their AC unit will receive a link that allows them to book a pro directly through Thumbtack. Customers are not responsible for payment for these recall repairs.

Pros: Eligible pros must sign up in order to receive these leads. Once the job is completed, Midea will send the pro $150 per repair. 
Key points
Here’s a list of important details that frontline reps should be aware of when working with pros or customers and the Midea air conditioning recall repair program:
What it is: A timed partnership between Midea and Thumbtack to repair recalled Midea air conditioning units.
Who it's for: Thumbtack pros who opt-in.
How it works: Midea customers with recalled units can hire Thumbtack pros directly through a special link provided by Midea. Pros are paid $150 per completed repair by Midea.
Affected Locations: Initially New York (Manhattan and Brooklyn), expanded to select zip codes in SD, RI, ND, KS, TX, MO, NM, WY, ME, and VT.
Pro Responsibilities: Pros must opt-in via a form, receive parts from Midea, use provided training materials, collect Midea case and unit serial numbers, and email Midea for payment. They are also responsible for other necessary supplies.
Pro Compensation: Pros receive $150 per repair directly from Midea via Zelle or PayPal. Compensation of $75 is also available if the job cannot be completed due to customer unavailability or unit inaccessibility.
Customer Payment: Customers are not responsible for payment for these recall repairs; pros will be paid directly by Midea.
Customer Experience: Midea customers with recalled units choose between a refund or a repair. Those choosing repair are directed to Thumbtack pros. Customers do not pay the pros for these repairs.
Program details
This section outlines the specific dates and affected users for the Midea air conditioning recall repair program.
Launch date: The Midea air conditioning recall repair program launched June 20, 2025. 
End date: The Midea air conditioning recall repair program ends approximately at the end of July, 2025 (when repair requests are expected to stop). 
Impacted users: Eligible pros who opt-in. 
Available currently in:
The New York area (Manhattan and Brooklyn) 
Select zip codes in SD, RI, ND, KS, TX, MO, NM, WY, ME, and VT.
Identify impacted users: Information is not available in Admin. Impacted pros will mention the Midea air conditioning recall during interactions
Pro experience
This section provides key details about the Midea recall program for pros, including how they sign up and what they do.
Here’s a general overview of how the pro experience works in the Midea air conditioning recall repair program: 
Opting in: 
Eligible pros will learn about the program through a Thumbtack email. 
If they're interested, they'll complete an opt-in form.
Receiving parts and training: 
Midea will send the pro the parts they need to make the repairs. 
The pros will use the provided training materials (PDFs and a YouTube video) to learn how to repair the air conditioning units. 
Certificate of Insurance: 
Pros working in multi-family units, condos, or large buildings may be required by building management to supply a Certificate of Insurance (COI). 
They should check with their customer to see if their building requires COI.
Getting Paid: 
Pros will earn $150 for each completed repair job.
Pros will be paid directly by Midea through Zelle or PayPal. 
To get paid, pros need to: 
Collect the Midea case number
Collect the unit's serial number
Email Midea's team. 
Important: Customers are NOT responsible for payment for these recall repairs. 
Customer experience
This section explains what Midea’s customers experience when working with a Thumbtack pro for this recall program. 
Midea recently recalled nearly 1.7 million air conditioning units. They’re contacting impacted customers to ask if they’d prefer a refund on their unit (and they dispose of it themselves), or if they’d like a repair. 
For Midea customers who want their unit repaired, Midea will send them a link. This link will connect them to book with Thumbtack pros who have opted in to take these repair appointments. 
Here’s what the customer views from the link:

[Image: AD_4nXduMHj4dJR4Sjzn0Skuizesid3D9EDLIOw2LjXc1ng8HhiTRq3vO6FaOtsPNvLqDDUm-V-lHP__fnP5AStXjJy6M0YGmV-zhjiM8WnFKdRK7qpQ-uAH-wVFPjLPACuBPLHjWgyq]

2. Process
This section provides steps for pros on how to participate in and get paid for Midea recall repair jobs.
Steps: How to participate in Midea recall repair jobs (pro)
This section provides steps for pros on how to participate in and get paid for Midea recall repair jobs.
To participate in these repair jobs, pros will follow the steps listed in the help center article Midea U and U+ AC recall repairs.
Steps How to get compensated if they’re unable to complete the job (pro)
​This section explains the conditions under which pros can receive compensation for uncompleted Midea recall repair jobs and how to request it.
Compensation requirements: 
Midea will compensate pros $75 if they’re unable to complete the job due to:
The customer isn’t home or doesn’t answer the door, and isn’t reachable by phone at the scheduled appointment.
The pro arrives at the scheduled appointment and the customer’s unit is installed in a wall, a locked window, or is otherwise inaccessible.
Request compensation: 
To request compensation, pros can contact Midea at repairs@midea.com or by calling 1 (866) 629-9261. 

These pros can also request a refund by submitting an in-product refund request by following the usual steps in the How to request a refund – Thumbtack Help article.

 1. Overview 
(Table of content)
▶ KA summary
This internal KA provides pros with guidelines and information on effectively using Thumbtack's messaging features and the importance of quick responsiveness to customer inquiries. It covers response time expectations, message tab functionalities, tips for engaging with customers, and how to share media attachments like videos and documents to communicate project needs.

When a customer finds a pro in search results and reaches out, it’s up to the pro to respond quickly. A response is any time a pro responds to a customer’s initial contact. This could be replying to a customer's first message, accepting a booking request, or declining a lead.
When it comes to responsiveness, pros should: 
Aim to respond within 4 hours (between 8 am - 8 pm local time) and if they can’t, try to stay under 24 hours.
Keep up with new messages with push notifications from the app.
Make a habit of responding to exact matches first.
Write customized messages that make a clear path forward for the customer

2. Responsiveness
(Table of content) 
A pros response rate is based on the percentage of new leads they get and respond to between 8 am-8 pm local time. If the pro offers more than one service, their percentage includes all the leads they get. 
A pros responsiveness score impacts where they appear in search results. Pros who are more responsive will rank better in search results. Additionally, the score is used to calculate their Pro Rewards. To learn more about qualifications, frontline reps can refer to the internal Thumbtack Pro Rewards (Pro) KA. 
Pros can check their responsiveness score in the performance dashboard. Reps can refer to the internal Performance Dashboard: Market Level Insights (Pro) KA.  
Here's why it's important.
Search results rank: A pros responsiveness score impacts where they appear in search results. Pros who are more responsive will rank better in search results. Additionally, the score is used to calculate their Pro Rewards.
More likely to get hired: A quick response could show the customer that the pro will provide a great experience. And customers may be more likely to hire pros when they respond quickly.
What counts towards responsiveness 
(Table of content)
A response is any time a pro responds to a customer’s initial contact. This could be replying to a customer's first message, accepting a booking request, or declining a direct lead (either an exact match or partial match).
If the pro doesn’t want the job, they need to let the customer know to avoid hurting their responsiveness. Once a pro turns down a lead, they won’t be able to access it again, unless they’ve set their preferences.
▶ Does count towards responsiveness
Here’s a list of what does count towards a pro's responsiveness: 
Any time a pro gets a new lead from search results they need to respond.
Accepting a job (and replying)
Saying the pro can’t do a job they paid for
Declining a job that doesn’t match their preferences
Accepting a booking request (and suggesting new times)
Any time a customer replies from the "Opportunities" section of the Jobs tab, the pro needs to respond. Pros can send messages to any open opportunities and if the customer responds, it becomes a new lead. 
▶ Does NOT count towards responsiveness
Here’s a list of what does not count towards a pro's responsiveness: 
A pro calling a customer. The pro's ability to call the customer is enabled only after the pro sends their first message on a lead.
Selecting “reply” but not sending an actual reply in the messenger.
Refunded leads
A pro's initial message to a customer from the "Opportunities" section of the Jobs tab. We only look at how long it takes the pro to respond once the customer has reached out and it’s become a new lead.
A pro passes on an open opportunity in the "Opportunities" section.
3. Competition insights 
(Table of content)
Competition Insights is a tool for pros to benchmark their response time and performance against direct competitors on a specific lead and their local market average. 
Unlike the performance dashboard, which provides pros with their average response time compared to top pros (e.g., You 59 mins, Top pros 48 Minutes), Competition Insights shows specific response times and data for a specific lead. This provides a direct comparison to competitors for that specific job. 
Reps should use this information to coach pros on the importance of speed, competitive pricing, and profile quality.

What pros see in competition insights:
(Table of content)
The data in competition insights helps pros understand what they need to optimize to win the job.
Immediate competitive metrics (Response time and price): Pros can see their own response time (e.g., "Responded in 11 minutes") and pricing position (e.g., "Lowest price" or "Highest price") directly compared to other pros the customer contacted. This feature makes the impact of slow response time and uncompetitive pricing immediately visible.
Market benchmarks: Pros can compare their performance metrics (star rating, review count, and average response time) against the local average for their occupation (e.g., "Avg. mover 4.9 (five star) (27) Responds in 3 hours"). Reps should highlight this to drive improvement in overall profile health.
Customer view: Pros have the option to "view all [occupation] as a customer," which redirects them to the search results page to see exactly how they and their competition appear to a customer.

4. Messages 
(Table of content)
Messaging quality is a critical step in winning the job. Reps should coach pros that a great message must reduce customer uncertainty and create forward momentum in the conversation.
Sending a message to a customer
(Table of content)
To message a customer, pros will navigate to the Messages tab and find the customer they want to message (or search for the customer by name).
When messaging customers, pros can: 
Send a message with 1,000 characters per message. 
Send and receive various media formats within the messenger. Depending on the specific file type, these attachments can either be played and viewed directly in the chat or downloaded to the pro's device for later use.
Use a quick reply to respond to customers faster.
How leads land in the messages page various on the lead type: 
New Leads: New (exact match) leads initially appear in the “Leads” section of the pro’s Job tab. Once a pro responds, the conversation moves to the Messages tab.
Opportunities: Messages initiated from Opportunities appear directly in the Messages tab.
Sending media attachments in message
(Table of content)
Pros can add attachments to their messages and receive attachments from customers. Depending on the specific file type, these attachments can either be played and viewed directly in the chat or downloaded to the pro's device for later use.
NOTE: Attachments are not available for quick replies. 
The following list outlines the various media formats that pros can send to customers (or receive), along with specific use cases for each to improve project communication:
Images and GIFs: Ideal for providing visual updates, such as "before and after" photos, showcasing past project results, or sharing quick reactions during a conversation.
Videos: Highly effective for introducing the business, performing site walkthroughs, or explaining technical repairs. Creative pros like videographers can also use this to share portfolio highlights.
Audio files: Useful for sending voice notes to explain complex issues or for diagnosing mechanical problems based on sounds provided by the customer. DJs and musicians can share brief audio samples of their style.
Documents (PDF, DOCX, etc.): Necessary for exchanging professional paperwork like contracts, estimates, invoices and receipts. They are also used for sending resume examples, cleaning checklists, or maintenance schedules.
Archives (ZIP): Best for bundling multiple files, such as a comprehensive collection of blueprints or legal documents, into a single, manageable attachment.

Privacy and Security
(Table of content)
Links are now private which means only the involved customer and pro can view them.They require a login to view and expire automatically to protect sensitive information.

While Thumbtack messenger links are secure and require a login to view, once a file is downloaded to a personal device, it is no longer protected by Thumbtack’s security settings. Users should use caution when downloading and storing sensitive documents on shared or public devices.
Troubleshooting Media Attachments
(Table of content) 
If a pro is having trouble uploading or viewing attachments in the messenger, use the following troubleshooting steps to help them resolve the issue.
▶ General Requirements (Check these first for ALL files)
Size Check: Is the file 26MB or smaller?
Quantity Check: Is the user trying to send more than 20 files in one message? Only 20 files per message. If they are at the limit, they’ll need to send a separate message.
Network Check: If size and type are correct, ask the user to check their internet connection or try switching from Wi-Fi to cellular data.
Network Check:  Is the user on a strong Wi-Fi or cellular data connection? If size and type are correct, they can check their internet connection or try switching from Wi-Fi to cellular data.
App Version: Is the user on the latest version of the Thumbtack app? (Crucial for video and viewing new file types).
▶ Video Troubleshooting
Format: Is it an MP4, MOV, M4V, 3GP, WebM, or MPEG-TS?
iOS: MP4, M4V, and MOV
Android: MP4, 3GP, WebM, MPEG-TS
Playback Issue: If a customer sees an "empty bubble," they must update their app.
Length: If the file is too big, suggest the pro trim the video or lower the resolution in their phone settings before re-uploading.
▶ Document Troubleshooting
Login Check: Is the user logged into their Thumbtack account? (Links are secure and won't open if they aren't logged in).
Link Expiration: If the link doesn't work, it may have expired for security. Ask the sender to re-upload the document to generate a fresh link.
Mobile Access: Note that iOS users can currently only upload from their camera roll; they may need to use a desktop to upload saved PDFs or Word docs
▶ Audio Troubleshooting
Format: Is it an MP3, WAV, or M4A?
Playback Method: Remind the user that audio will not play inside the messenger.
Download Step: Did the user tap to download the file to their device first?
▶ Image & GIF Troubleshooting
Format: Is it a JPG, PNG, GIF, BMP, or TIFF?
GIF Animation: If a GIF isn't moving "inline" (in the chat bubble), the user likely needs an app update.
Image Quality: If the image is blurry, ensure it wasn't compressed too much before uploading.
▶ Archive (ZIP) Troubleshooting
Content Check: Is the user aware they need to download and extract the ZIP file on a computer or compatible mobile device to see the individual files?
Upload Limit: Even if it’s a ZIP, the total folder size must still be under 26MB.

Sending follow-up messages when a convo drops off  
(Table of content)
It's a good idea to send customers another message if the conversation drops off. Pros can let the customer know that they're still interested and suggest a next step to get things moving again.
If a customer has not responded to the pros initial message within 24-48 hours, a follow-up is appropriate. However, sometimes customers' plans change. Pros can skip the follow-up message if they see a note that the project was canceled or that they went with another option.
Examples of follow-up messages: 
Example 1: "Hi [Customer Name], I wanted to follow up on my previous message about your [Job Type] project. I'm still very interested in helping you and wanted to see if you had any other questions or if you'd like to schedule a quick call to discuss the details further."
Example 2: "Hello [Customer Name], Just checking in regarding your inquiry about [Job Type]. If you're still looking for a professional, I'm available and would love to provide a quote. Let me know if you'd like to chat!"
Coaching pros on message quality (Rep)
(Table of content) 
Reps should emphasize that customers consistently favor responses that make it easy to continue, not necessarily the shortest or most polished ones. The strongest pattern is "just enough detail + a clear next step".
Key Coaching Points:
Acknowledge and Listen (Build Trust):
Pros must read the customer's message and job details carefully to fully understand their needs. This careful acknowledgment is the strongest trust signal.
They should personalize their response by addressing the customer by name and showing interest in their specific project.
Show You Understood: Demonstrate comprehension by answering their questions and addressing the specifics of their job to reduce uncertainty.
Set a Clear Next Step (Drive Momentum):
Make it easy for the customer to move forward. 
Proactively suggest a clear, easy path forward, such as scheduling a quick call or an in-person meeting to discuss the project in more detail.
Address Pricing: 
If the pro's pricing isn't clear, they should explain how their pricing works and why they need more information to provide an accurate estimate.
If the pro doesn’t have pricing set and it’s clear, they can add their pricing to set accurate expectations.
Review and Send Quickly: 
Before hitting send, proofread messages to ensure it's clear, error-free, and conveys their intended message. 
Remind pros that while their messages should be clear, they should also prioritize speed. Pros can make quick replies to  save time from typing a new message each time.
Messaging tools to respond quickly
Thumbtack offers several tools and features to help pros respond to customers faster, stay organized, and win more jobs. From built-in shortcuts to fully automated services, pros can choose what works best for how they run their business.

Quick replies
 (Table of content)
Quick replies let pros save responses to common questions to reuse for future customers. We want to help pros respond to customers faster and more often. 
A few things to note: 
Saved replies have a 500-character limit each.
Pros can save up to 100 replies and all 100 saved replies should show on the app.
Attachments are not available for quick replies. 
Descriptive titles for quick replies make them easier to find again.
Since quick replies go out to multiple customers, pros should proofread their replies thoroughly to make sure they are accurate and error-free. 
Additionally, encourage pros to check their performance dashboard to see how quick replies are impacting their response rate and response time.
Pros can check out the How to use quick replies – Thumbtack Help article for more info.
Front Desk
Front Desk is Thumbtack's automated lead response service that helps pros manage customer messaging and stay competitive without being tied to their phone.
What it does: Automatically sends the pro's first message to every new lead, 24/7, with an average response time of under 2 minutes.
Customization: Pros set their own message to represent their business — whether that's gathering project details, scheduling estimates, highlighting promotions, or outlining next steps.
Performance impact: Responding to customers quickly can increase conversion rates, and Front Desk handles that automatically on the pro's behalf.
Apps: Front Desk works alongside other apps for more efficient workflow management.
For full details on plans, billing, setup, and how to make changes, reps can refer to the internal Front Desk (Pro) KA.
NOTE: Front Desk+ is an AI-powered receptionist service currently available to a very small group of pros as part of a limited pilot.
Apps
Pros can connect their Thumbtack account to third-party tools to help them respond faster and stay on top of new leads. Depending on the tool, the connection may include the following endpoints:
Lead notifications: Thumbtack sends lead data — including customer contact info and job details — to the pro's tool so they're notified of new leads without having to check the Thumbtack app.
Message notifications: Thumbtack sends new customer messages to the pro's tool so they can stay on top of conversations in one place. Some tools also allow pros to message customers back directly from within the platform.
Some tools support both endpoints; others support leads only. 
Pros can set this up through a Thumbtack partner integration or a webhook. Reps can refer to the internal Thumbtack Partner Integrations (Pro) KA for the full list of partners and their supported endpoints. For webhooks, reps can refer to the internal Webhooks (Pro) KA.
Messages tab: Manage messages by type and job status
(Table of content)
The Messages tab allows pros to search for a customer by name, or filter by the message type (e.g., Unread, archived) or job status (e.g., scheduled, job done). Here is a list of filter options the pro has: 
Message type: 
Unread. New messages the pro hasn't checked yet.
Archived. Messages they have archived because they don’t need them anymore.
Sent quotes. Messages they have sent about an open opportunity if the customer hasn’t responded yet.
Starred. Messages they have starred (because they’re important, or the pro wants to come back to them).
Job status: 
Not scheduled yet. The pro is still trying to win the customer and negotiating details.
Scheduled. The customer and pro have decided to work together.
Job done. The pro has finished the job.
No hire. The pro didn’t get hired, and the lead didn’t work out.
For more information on job statuses, refer to the Leads (Pro) KA. 
To access the filters on the app, the pro will click the three dot menu in the top right corner. On the desktop, pros will see the filters on the left hand column.

(Rep) Steps: How to help a pro with their response time
(Table of content)
Show the pro where to find their responsiveness score in their performance dashboard. (KA: Performance Dashboard: Market Level Insights (Pro))
Encourage the pro to turn on their notifications so they know when a new lead comes in. (KA: Notifications (Pro))
Recommend the pro downloads the Thumbtack for Professionals app to get push notifications. (KA: Thumbtack App (Pro))
Coach pros to respond to all the leads they get within four response hours, whether or not they're interested in the job. "Response hours" (formerly business hours) means between 8 am - 8 pm local time. Remind pros that acting on each lead impacts their responsiveness score.
(Pro) Steps: How to send a message to a customer
(Table of content)
Go to your Messages tab.
Find the customer you want to message (you can search their name or use a filter).
Click the customer to open the messenger.
Type your message. You can also use a saved reply and add attachments.
Select Send.

NOTE: Pros can also send a saved reply whenever they're responding to a customer's message by clicking the bookmark icon in the messenger and select the quick reply they want to send.
(Rep) Steps: How to help pros write engaging messages to customers
(Table of content)
What pros include in their response is up to them, but we can give them ideas. 
Coach pros to make sure their messages are clear and error-free before they send them, but remind them of the importance of responding quickly. 
Read the customer’s message first. Before responding, review the job details and read the customers whole message so the pro knows what the customer is looking for.
Make it personal. Greet the customer by name and express interest in working with the customer.
Show you’re listening. Answer any questions the customer might have and talk about their specific job.
Invite the customer to take the next step. Suggest setting up a time to discuss the customer’s project in detail (either in person or on the phone), making it easy for them to continue moving forward with the pro. 
Explain you’re price (if they didn't already see it). Tell the customers how your pricing works and why you need to learn more about the job before you can give an estimate. 
Reps can refer to the internal Pro Pricing: How Pros Price Their Services (Quote sheets) KA to learn more. 
Proofread. Do a last-minute check for spelling and to make sure it covers what you want to say before you send it off.

Response time
(Table of content)

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Why is responding quickly so important?
¿Por qué es tan importante responder rápidamente?
It’s what customers want (and Thumbtack expects) as a part of a good experience. When you’re quick to reply to customers, you give them exactly what they want. This tells us you’re a pro who is likely to provide that great experience customers are looking for.
Es lo que los clientes quieren (y Thumbtack espera) como parte de una buena experiencia. Cuando responde rápidamente a los clientes, les da exactamente lo que quieren. Esto nos dice que eres un profesional que probablemente brindará la gran experiencia que buscan los clientes.
What is my responsiveness score?
¿Qué es mi “responsiveness score”?
Your responsiveness score shows how quickly you respond to your new customers. Specifically, it counts the percentage of new customers you respond to within four business hours of getting the lead. You can check your responsiveness score in your performance dashboard.
Remember, this score impacts where you appear in search results (and it’s one of the criteria for Pro Rewards), so it’s a good idea to check it often. I recommend downloading the Thumbtack app and turning on your push notifications so you know right when new leads come in.
Su “responsiveness score” es su calificación de respuestas. Demuestra la rapidez en que responde a sus nuevos clientes. Específicamente, cuenta el porcentaje de nuevos clientes a los que responde dentro de las cuatro horas laborales después que obtiene el cliente potencial. Puede revisar su “responsiveness score” en sus “Performance Dashboard.”
Recuerde, esta calificación afecta dónde aparece en los resultados de búsqueda (y es uno de los criterios para Top Pro), y es una buena idea revisarla con frecuencia. Recomiendo descargar la aplicación Thumbtack y activar las notificaciones automáticas para saber cuándo entran nuevos clientes potenciales.
I don’t have the time to respond quickly every time. What can I do?
No tengo tiempo para responder rápidamente cada vez. ¿Que puedo hacer?
Responding to customers fast is an important step to take to get hired more often. It’s how you make the most of every lead. But we know you’re busy. I recommend setting a goal to respond to each customer within four business hours as often as you can. See how this works for you and in a couple weeks, re-evaluate and set a new goal if it makes sense.
Responder a los clientes con rapidez es un paso importante que se debe tomar para ser contratado con más frecuencia. Así se puede aprovechar de cada prospecto al máximo. Pero sabemos que está ocupado. Recomiendo establecer una meta para responder a cada cliente dentro de las cuatro horas laborales con la mayor frecuencia posible. Vea cómo funciona esto para usted y, en un par de semanas, vuelva a evaluar y establezca una nueva meta si tiene sentido.
I'm too busy to respond in four business hours!
¡Estoy demasiado ocupado para responder en cuatro horas laborales!
We understand you’re busy, but customers are too. We’ve found that after a few hours, some customers will move on and look for other pros if they haven’t heard back from you. If you’re too busy to reply with a detailed message, you can still reply with a brief note and let the customer know you’re interested and you’ll provide more details when you have more time. This way, the customer knows what’s going on and your responsiveness score is not negatively impacted
Entendemos que está ocupado, pero los clientes también están ocupados. Descubrimos que después de unas horas, algunos clientes seguirán adelante y buscarán otros profesionales si no han recibido una respuesta suya. Si está demasiado ocupado para responder con un mensaje detallado, aún puede responder con una nota breve e informarle al cliente que está interesado y brindará más detalles cuando tenga más tiempo. De esta forma, el cliente sabe lo que está pasando y su “responsiveness score” no se ve afectada negativamente. 
(Su “responsiveness score” es su calificación de respuestas. Demuestra la rapidez en que responde a sus nuevos clientes.)
I got a lead I’m not interested in. Why can’t I ignore it?
Tengo un prospecto que no me interesa. ¿Por qué no puedo ignorarlo?
Ignoring a lead isn’t helpful for you or the customer. If you ever see a lead you’re not interested in, always let the customer know. This keeps your response time quick and allows us to tell the customer to keep looking.
Ignorar un prospecto no es útil para usted ni para el cliente. Si encuentre un prospecto que no le interesa, siempre avisé al cliente. Al poder hacer esto, mantiene su calificación de respuesta alta y nos permite decirle al cliente que siga buscando otras opciones.

What happened to quick replies?

What are saved replies?

Saved replies let you reuse your answers to common questions so you don’t have to rewrite the same response every time. This can save you time and help you get in touch with customers faster when you’re busy.
Las respuestas guardadas le permiten reutilizar sus respuestas a preguntas comunes para que no tenga que volver a escribir la misma respuesta cada vez. Esto puede ahorrarle tiempo y ayudarlo a comunicarse con los clientes más rápido cuando esté ocupado.
What should I include in my quick reply?

What you write is up to you, but your response should get the customer excited about working with you. You should answer the customer’s question upfront and guide them toward the next step. Saved replies are meant to save you time, but you’ll still want to personalize them so they’re meaningful and engaging to the customer.
Lo que escriba depende de usted, pero su respuesta debe entusiasmar al cliente por trabajar con usted. Reconozca cualquier pregunta y guíe al cliente a tomar el siguiente paso. Las respuestas guardadas están destinadas a ahorrarle tiempo, pero aún querrá personalizarlas para que sean significativas y atractivas para el cliente.

Q: How secure is it to send attachments like contracts or private photos in the Thumbtack messenger?"
Q: ¿Qué tan seguro es enviar archivos adjuntos como contratos o fotos privadas en el messenger de Thumbtack?
A: It’s very secure. We’ve updated our system so that every attachment link is private and requires you to be logged into your account to see it. We also use temporary links that expire automatically, so your documents and videos stay protected and are only accessible to you and the person you’re messaging.
A: Es muy seguro. Hemos actualizado nuestro sistema para que cada enlace de archivos adjuntos sea privado y requiera que usted haya iniciado sesión en su cuenta para verlo. También utilizamos enlaces temporales que vencen automáticamente, de modo que sus documentos y videos permanecen protegidos y solo son accesibles para usted y la persona con la que se comunica.
Q: Why should I use Thumbtack's messenger instead of just texting?
Q: ¿Por qué debería usar el messenger de Thumbtack en lugar de simplemente enviar mensajes de texto?
A: Using the Thumbtack messenger for your videos and documents makes your life easier and keeps your business safer.

Everything in one place: You don't have to search through your emails or texts to find a contract or a video of a leaky pipe—it's all right there in the project thread.
Privacy: Unlike regular text links, our attachment links are private and expire, so your documents aren't floating around the public web.
Professionalism: Sending a professional estimate or a video walkthrough directly through the app shows customers you're organized and ready to work.
A: Usar el messenger de Thumbtack para sus videos y documentos le facilita la vida y mantiene su negocio más seguro.

Todo en un mismo lugar: No tiene que buscar en sus correos electrónicos o mensajes de texto para encontrar un contrato o el video de una tubería con goteras; todo está allí mismo, en el hilo del proyecto.
Privacidad: A diferencia de los enlaces de texto normales, nuestros enlaces de archivos adjuntos son privados y vencen, por lo que sus documentos no quedan circulando por la web pública.
Profesionalismo: Enviar una cotización aproximada profesional o un video del recorrido directamente a través de la aplicación les muestra a los clientes que usted es organizado y que está listo para trabajar.
Image attachments
(Table of content)
English talking points
Spanish talking points
Why would I send customers images or GIFs in the messenger? 
¿Por qué enviaría imágenes o GIFs a los clientes a través del messenger?
You can send photos (JPG, PNG) to show your work. If you use a GIF, it will play automatically right in the messenger. This is a perfect way to show a quick 'before and after' or a time-lapse of your progress without the customer having to click anything.
Usted puede enviar fotos (JPG, PNG) para mostrar su trabajo. Si utiliza un GIF, este se reproducirá automáticamente directamente en el messenger. Esta es una forma perfecta de mostrar un "antes y después" rápido o un video acelerado de su progreso sin que el cliente tenga que hacer clic en nada.
Audio attachments
(Table of content)
English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: I received an audio file, but I can't hear it," OR 
"The customer says they can't listen to the audio file I sent them. Why is that?
Q: Recibí un archivo de audio, pero no puedo escucharlo, O BIEN: 
"El cliente dice que no puede escuchar el archivo de audio que le envié. ¿A qué se debe esto?"
A: Currently, our messenger doesn't have a built-in player for audio files. To listen to a recording, you or the customer will need to download the file to your device first. Once it’s saved, you can play it using your phone or computer's standard media player.
A: Actualmente, nuestro messenger no tiene un reproductor de audio integrado. Para escuchar una grabación, usted o el cliente deberán descargar primero el archivo en su dispositivo. Una vez que esté guardado, puede reproducirlo utilizando el reproductor multimedia estándar de su teléfono o computadora.
Q: How do audio attachments work? 
Q: ¿Cómo funcionan los archivos de audio adjuntos?
A: You can send and receive voice notes or audio files. Just keep in mind that the Thumbtack app doesn't have a 'play' button for audio yet. You’ll just need to download the file to your phone or computer first to listen to it.
A: Usted puede enviar y recibir notas de voz o archivos de audio. Solo tenga en cuenta que la aplicación de Thumbtack aún no tiene un botón de "reproducir" para el audio. Simplemente necesitará descargar primero el archivo en su teléfono o computadora para escucharlo.
Video attachments
(Table of content)
English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: The customer said the video I sent isn't playing (or is an empty bubble).
Q: El cliente dijo que el video que envié no se reproduce (o aparece como una burbuja vacía).
A: I’m sorry they’re having trouble seeing that. Usually, this happens if someone is using an older version of the app. Please ask your customer to update their Thumbtack app to the latest version. Once they do, the video should play right in the message for them.
A: Lamentamos que tengan problemas para verlo. Por lo general, esto sucede si alguien está utilizando una versión anterior de la aplicación. Por favor, pídale a su cliente que actualice su aplicación de Thumbtack a la versión más reciente. Una vez que lo haga, el video debería reproducirse directamente en el mensaje para ellos.
Q: My video isn’t uploading and I don’t understand why!
Q: ¡Mi video no se sube y no entiendo por qué!
A: I’m happy to help you get that video uploaded. There are usually two main things to check: the file size and the file type.

Check the size: Each video needs to be 26MB or smaller. If your video is longer or high-definition, it might be too large to send in one go.
Check the format: Our messenger supports the most common video types, like MP4, MOV, and M4V. If your video is in a different format, it might not upload correctly.

Pro Tip: If your video is too big, try shortening the clip or sending it as a ZIP file. Our messenger now supports ZIP files, which can help compress the size so it fits.
A: Con gusto le ayudaré a subir ese video. Generalmente hay dos cosas principales que debe revisar: el tamaño del archivo y el tipo de archivo.

Verifique el tamaño: Cada video debe ser de 26 MB o menos. Si su video es más largo o de alta definición, es posible que sea demasiado grande para enviarlo de una sola vez.
Verifique el formato: Nuestro messenger es compatible con los tipos de video más comunes, como MP4, MOV y M4V. Si su video tiene un formato diferente, es posible que no se suba correctamente.

Pro Tip: Si su video es demasiado grande, intente acortar el clip o enviarlo como un archivo ZIP. Nuestro messenger ahora es compatible con archivos ZIP, lo que puede ayudar a comprimir el tamaño para que quepa.
FiIe and ZIP attachments 
(Table of content)
English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: Can I send sensitive docs through the messenger? 
Q: ¿Puedo enviar documentos confidenciales por el messenger?
You can send all your professional documents directly through the chat. Whether it's a PDF contract or an Excel estimate, it’s all supported. Plus, these links are secure and private—only you and your customer can see them, and you have to be logged in to open them.
Usted puede enviar todos sus documentos profesionales directamente a través del chat. Ya sea un contrato en PDF o una cotización aproximada en Excel, todos son compatibles. Además, estos enlaces son seguros y privados: solo usted y su cliente pueden verlos, y debe haber iniciado sesión para abrirlos.
Q: What kinds of files can I send, and how big can they be?
Q: Qué tipo de archivos puedo enviar y qué tan grandes pueden ser?
A: You can send most standard files, including videos (like MP4 or MOV), documents (like PDFs or Word docs), and photos. You can attach up to 20 files at a time, and each file can be as large as 26MB. If you’re sending a GIF, it will even play automatically right in the chat. 
Usted puede enviar la mayoría de los archivos estándar, incluidos videos (como MP4 o MOV), documentos (como PDF o archivos de Word) y fotos. Puede adjuntar hasta 20 archivos a la vez, y cada archivo puede tener un tamaño de hasta 26 MB. Si envía un GIF, incluso se reproducirá automáticamente directamente en el chat.
Q: I am having issues uploading my files to the chat.
Q: Tengo problemas para subir mis archivos al chat.
A: Let's check a few things to get that fixed. First, make sure the file is under 26MB. If it’s a document, check that it’s a standard type like a PDF or Word doc. Also, the messenger can take up to 20 files at a time—if you have more than that, try sending them in a second message.
A: Revisemos algunas cosas para solucionar esto. Primero, asegúrese de que el archivo pese menos de 26 MB. Si es un documento, verifique que sea de un tipo estándar como PDF o un archivo de Word. Además, el messenger puede recibir hasta 20 archivos a la vez; si tiene más que eso, intente enviarlos en un segundo mensaje.
Q: Can I attach a folder with multiple files/images,etc? 
Q: ¿Puedo adjuntar una carpeta con varios archivos, imágenes, etc.?
A: If you have a lot of files to share—like a dozen photos or several different contracts—you can bundle them into a ZIP file. Our messenger supports uploading and downloading ZIP files, so you can send everything in one go. It’s a great way to stay organized and keep the chat from getting cluttered.
A: Si tiene muchos archivos para compartir, como una docena de fotos o varios contratos diferentes, puede agruparlos en un archivo ZIP. Nuestro messenger permite subir y descargar archivos ZIP, para que pueda enviar todo de una sola vez. Es una excelente manera de mantenerse organizado y evitar que el chat se desordene.
Q: The ZIP file I sent is empty
Q: El archivo ZIP que envié está vacío.
A: A ZIP file is like a digital folder. If it's appearing empty, it might be because the files inside are in a format we don't support. Make sure you're only 'zipping' standard files like PDFs, JPEGs, or Word docs. Also, ensure the total size of that ZIP folder is under 26MB.
A: Un archivo ZIP es como una carpeta digital. Si aparece vacío, podría ser porque los archivos que contiene tienen un formato que no es compatible. Asegúrese de incluir solo archivos estándar como PDF, JPEG o archivos de Word. Además, verifique que el tamaño total de esa carpeta ZIP sea inferior a 26 MB.

Managed Accounts: Pros with Account Managers (Pro)

Contents
Overview
Do's and don'ts
Process
Steps: How to identify and help Managed Account Pros (Rep)
Steps: When and how to transfer a pro interaction to their account manager (Rep)
Steps: How to handle referrals to managed accounts (Rep)
Identifying a Potential Managed Account Pro
Referring a Potential Managed Account Pro
After Referring a Pro
Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA summary
This internal knowledge article provides guidance for frontline reps on helping pros with managed accounts. It covers how to identify managed accounts, the process for helping these pros, including when and how to transfer interactions to their account managers, and guidelines for referring potential new managed accounts. The purpose is to ensure consistent and effective service and support for Thumbtack's high-revenue pros.
Managed Accounts are a core component of Thumbtack's Enterprise program, designed to provide an "above and beyond" experience for high-revenue pros. These pros are invited to join the program based on qualifications established by the National team, including business success, revenue, and geographical reach.
Upon joining, a Managed Accounts pro is assigned a dedicated account manager who offers one-on-one guidance, overseeing their account to ensure continued success.
Important: This exclusive program isn't available to all pros, making it crucial for frontline reps to understand the key guidelines for helping these high-value accounts.
Managed Accounts are large accounts with dedicated account managers. They'll be assigned an account manager on the National team, who oversees their account and ensures the pro continues to be successful.
▶ Internal note:
The #sales_am_inbound Slack channel should not be used to contact the managed accounts team. Frontline reps will Slack the pro’s account manager directly.
Do's and Don'ts
To help pros with managed accounts, frontline reps should adhere to the following guidelines, which detail both recommended actions and those to avoid.
Do’s
Slack the pro’s account manager any time Support Reps work with one of these pros—whether Support Reps resolve their issue or not. The pro’s account manager will want to know about the situation.
Help pros with basic support issues (like updating a password).
Have Managed Accounts answer any questions about the program or tell pros how it works. 
Don’ts
Do not promise interested pros that Thumbtack will accept them into Managed Accounts, or that Managed Accounts will contact them.
Do not change a pro’s phone number, email address, or add any services to their account. These issues should be escalated to Managed Accounts.
Do not mention Managed Accounts, because pros may not know this term.
Do not say, “It looks like you’re with Managed Accounts.”
Do say, “I’m going to transfer you to your account manager.”
2. Process
Steps: How to identify and help Managed Account Pros (Rep) 
 
To help a Managed Accounts pro who reaches out for help, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:
Locate the pro’s account manager’s name from the Salesforce case or on the pro’s contact page. 
 From the case in Salesforce: Look for the account manager's name in the "Thumbtack user" field.  See what it looks like below.)
▶ What it looks like in Salesforce case[Image: AD_4nXd1xNAjjx1XLPa51LMUoxmPIMa-_OBocG3vcuUPkGQX4nWPVitDglGDGmiuBlIk3Fgngx94NkaUCEA18fX-4bd1KY3L9nbY0u6Oc26s7CEbFuYSL2a-BHaQvZWqRL7QuEtdVovfuL7WPCmXcVbCS-k9Svr0]This screenshot of a Thumbtack user profile highlights the 'Managed account' tag, which appears directly below the pro’s name in the profile header, indicating that the pro is part of the Managed Accounts program
From the pros contact page: There will be a banner that says “National Managed Account.”.Under the Contact Information section, reps will see the “Account Manager Name” field with their name. (See what it looks like below.)
▶ What it looks like on the pro's contact page[Image: AD_4nXfyrzzja76Nb9Cc0jawUbg8rVo8dHU4wlwLSCMuL7YP8467uXo9BaVz11O-MVoEYRiBnGZ7l862x9P6r7Mh5wfDVMKEyoRt5ovmK_jOwqR8SFdMSVprJ1Ynd8q5tFgVp4tmBtcpYlwOFOAfvxQuLtJiMVQX]
Determine if the pro has an assigned account manager by following step 1 above. 
If a pro does not have an assigned account manager, Support Reps should handle the pro’s issues and close the case as usual.
If the pro has an assigned account manager, ask them to email their account manager. Account managers typically respond within 48 hours.
If the pro cannot email their account manager, email the account manager directly. Details to Include in Email:
Pro Admin link
Summary of the issue
Best time and number to call the pro back.
If the pro needs immediate help (and cannot wait 24 hours to hear back), reach out to the #sales_am_inbound Slack channel to see if anyone is available.
Keep the case assigned to you, the rep,  and close it after the account manager confirms they talked to the pro.
Steps: When and how to transfer a pro interaction to their account manager (Rep) 
The following drop downs outline reasons a frontline rep would contact Managed Accounts:
▶ General reasons
Add a services
Change their contact information
Question or issue related to Managed Accounts
▶ Urgent reasons
Pro's account was shut off
Pro stopped seeing any activity in their account when they should be
Pro stopped getting notifications
Frontline Reps will transfer calls to Managed Accounts when a Managed Accounts pro needs anything other than basic customer support.
▶ Frontline reps can use the following talking point to let the pro know you'll transfer them:
It looks like you’ve been working with an account manager. They know your business inside and out, so they’ll be able to offer you the best support. Let me see if they're available to help.
How to transfer a pro interaction 
Frontline reps will follow these steps to transfer a pro with an account manager: 
Determine if the reason for contact is a General or Urgent transfer reason, as outlined above.
Send the account manager a direct message in Slack to let them know about the transfer.
Keep the case open until the account manager confirms they’ve reached out to the pro.
Close the case as Department Inquiry > Managed Account.
Important reminder to rep: Do not give out any employee's personal phone number. Reps can reference the Sensitive Account Information Handling Guidelines (Pro) (Customer) (Rep) for more guidelines and details. 
Steps: How to handle referrals to managed accounts (Rep)
This section outlines how Frontline Reps can identify pros who may be a good fit for Managed Accounts and the steps to refer them.
▶ Identifying a Potential Managed Account Pro:
To determine if a pro could be a good candidate for Managed Accounts, Frontline Reps should consider the following criteria and ask the pro these qualifying questions:
Confirm the pro is not already a managed account. (See + Steps: How to help a managed account pro (Rep) + for details on identification.)Ask the pro the following questions to assess their business structure and reach: ▶ Questions for Pros:
Are you part of a Franchise?
Do you do business in multiple states?
Consider additional factors that indicate a strong fit for Managed Accounts, such as
The pro's name and contact information.
The pro's business name.
Whether they have 15 or more employees.
Whether they have a dedicated marketing person.
Whether they are a franchise, regional, or national company.
Whether they have locations in multiple states.
▶ Referring a Potential Managed Account Pro:
If, after identification, Frontline Reps believe a pro is a good fit for Managed Accounts, follow these steps to submit the referral:
Do not promise pros that Thumbtack will accept them into Managed Accounts or that Managed Accounts will contact them. 
▶ English Talking Point:“Thumbtack will send your information over to the account managers. If they think you’re a good fit for the program and if they have the availability, they’ll reach out to you. Is there anything else Thumbtack can help you with?” 
▶ Talking point (Spanish):Enviaré su información a los administradores de cuentas. Si creen que eres un buen candidato para el programa y si tienen la disponibilidad, se comunicarán con usted. ¿Hay algo más en lo que pueda ayudar?”
If the pro answers “Yes” to the qualifying questions and is not a managed account already, Slack Yael Emmerich and she will review the account. Details to Include in Slack Message:
Pro’s name and contact information
Business name
Do they have 15 or more employees?
Do they have a dedicated marketing person?
Are they a franchise, regional, or national company?
Do they have locations in multiple states?
Add any additional details.
▶ After Referring a Pro:
Managed Accounts will email the agent to confirm if they will take action with the pro.
If accepted: Managed Accounts will reach out to the pro, and no further action is required by the frontline rep.
If declined and Frontline Reps have promised to follow up with the pro, Frontline Reps must reach back out. Managed Accounts will not contact any pro that is declined.

This section provides a centralized hub for relevant internal and external links and additional helpful documentation related to Managed Accounts.

Making Account Changes on Behalf of Pro or Customer (Impersonation Guidelines) (Rep)

Contents
Overview
Key points
Impersonating Pros
Guidelines: Changes Frontline Reps can make on behalf of pro

Steps: How to make changes to a pro account (Rep)
Impersonating Customers

Process
Steps: How to log in as a pro or customer and impersonate them (Rep)
Steps: How to switch between impersonating pro and customer accounts (Rep)
Steps: How to log out as a pro or customer and stop impersonating (Rep)
Resources
1. Overview 
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: This internal Knowledge Article (KA) provides Frontline Reps with instructions on how to log in as pros and customers for troubleshooting and support purposes. It outlines how to impersonate a pro or customer, how to switch between impersonating a pro or customer account, and how to stop impersonating the pro or customer. 
Not everything Frontline Reps need to do can be done in Salesforce, Admin, or other tools. Sometimes, the only way to complete a given task is to log in as the pro or customer to either see what they’re seeing or to do something on their behalf in their account. In these cases, this KA will go over how Frontline Reps can impersonate a pro or customer, switch between a pro and customer account, and how to stop impersonating a pro or customer.  
The ability to impersonate a pro or customer can be useful, but it comes with an increased risk of a negative outcome if something goes wrong. So, this KA (Making Account Changes On Behalf of Pro or Customer) also explores what Frontline Reps can do on behalf of a pro or customer versus what not to do to ensure Thumbtack isn’t put at risk of legal issues.
Key points
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: This section provides a list of key points for Frontline reps to keep in mind when impersonating a pro or customer.
Here are key points for Frontline Reps to remember when impersonating a pro or customer:
Guideline Compliance: Reps must strictly follow the authorized and restricted action guidelines when making account changes on behalf of a pro or customer.
Impersonation Purpose: Pro and customer impersonation is for troubleshooting and support only, not personal use.
Verification: Verify the pro or customer’s identity, offer guidance, and ensure requested changes are approved before impersonating a pro or customer to make changes.
Account Switching: Frontline Reps can switch between pro and customer accounts while impersonating them. The black Thumbtack logo at the top left is for pro accounts, while the blue Thumbtack logo is for customer accounts.
"Impersonating" Bar: A red bar indicates when a rep is impersonating a pro or customer, with the pro or customer’s name and PKID.
Proper Logout: Frontline Reps must log out correctly after impersonating a pro or customer to avoid account issues; use the Feedback toolbar and "Stop Impersonating."
Email Confirmations: Send confirmation emails (CC changes@thumbtack.com) after any changes made while impersonating the pro or customer.
User: Anytime “user” is mentioned in this internal KA, it’s referring to either the pro or customer (or both if they have both accounts).
Impersonating Pros

Guidelines: Changes Frontline reps CAN make on behalf of pro 
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: This section guides Frontline Reps on the authorized actions they can take within a pro's Thumbtack account while impersonating them, focusing on troubleshooting, account management, and providing necessary support.
Frontline Reps should encourage pros to edit their account info themselves. With this in mind, if the account owner or authorized user requests a change to their account or profile, and they insist the rep do it for them, Frontline Reps must follow these guidelines exactly to ensure compliance and proper account security.
For detailed steps and specific guidelines related to each of the following actions in this section, refer to the linked internal Knowledge Articles (KAs) below.
The following list explains what Frontline Reps CAN do when logged in as a pro, if requested by the account owner:
View the pro’s account to troubleshoot issues: If the Frontline Rep is NOT making changes to the pro’s account, they can impersonate (log in as) the pro to see what they’re seeing. 
This is especially useful when the pro is experiencing a bug, to check that the pro’s targeting preferences are set up correctly, or to walk the pro through a feature (like setting targeting preferences, requesting reviews, or attaching images).
Make approved changes to an account or profile: If the authorized pro requests a change to their account, these are the edits Frontline Reps are allowed to make on behalf of the pro:
Account status: Reactivate or deactivate an account (Steps on internal Account Information: Manage Account Settings and Status (Pro) KA).
Calendar: Adjust availability (Steps on internal Availability: Business Hours, Calendar, and Hide a Business (Pro) KA).
Notifications: Turn notifications on or off (Steps on internal Notifications (Pro) KA).
Targeting: Adjust Targeting preferences (Steps on internal Targeting: Job Types and Travel Preferences (Pro) KA).
Budge: Adjust lead spend (Steps on internal Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro) KA)
Lead price: Adjust lead spend (Steps on internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA)
Quote sheet: Adjust pro’s pricing (Steps on internal Pro Pricing: How Pros Price Their Services (Quote sheets) KA).
Profile: Edit social media, photos, intro, FAQs, and featured projects on the pro’s profile (Steps on internal Profile (Pro) KA)
Registered phone numbers: Add numbers to a pros registered numbers list (for Thumbtack Numbers Pilot for pros in Atlanta)
This is different from a pro's primary phone number on their profile (which cannot be changed by a rep). (Steps on internal Thumbtack Numbers Pilot (Atlanta Pro) (Customer) KA)
Guidelines: Changes Frontline reps CANNOT make on behalf of pro
▶ 🤖 Background notes
AI Context: To ensure compliance and prevent errors, this section outlines the specific actions Frontline Reps are restricted from performing within a pro's Thumbtack account while impersonating them, even if the pro requests it.
Frontline Reps should encourage pros to edit their account info themselves. To ensure compliance and proper account security, Frontline Reps are strictly prohibited from performing the following actions on a pro's account or profile, even if the account owner or authorized user requests or insists upon the change.
For detailed steps and specific guidelines related to each of the following actions in this section, refer to the linked internal Knowledge Articles (KAs) below.
Here is a list of the things Frontline reps cannot do when logged in as a pro, even if the pro requests it:
Edit profile details
Business name (Steps on internal Account Information (Pro) KA.
Business address (Steps on internal Account Information (Pro) KA).
Background check (Steps on internal Background Checks (Pro) KA).
Licenses (Steps on internal Licenses (Pro) KA).
Edit account details
Account ownership (Steps on internal Account Information (Pro) KA).
Credit card number (Steps on internal Payment Methods (Pro) KA).
Email address (Steps on internal Account Information (Pro) KA).
Legal name (Steps on internal Account Information (Pro) KA).
Password (Steps on internal Account Information (Pro) KA).
(Primary) Phone number: This is the main number on a pros profile used for account verification, security, and communication from Thumbtack. Steps on internal Account Information (Pro) KA. This is different from pros registered phone numbers.
Write*, edit, or send a message to a customer
Frontline reps can give tips and suggestions, but the pro needs to do the writing and submitting themselves.
Steps on internal Messaging Customers and Pro Responsiveness (Pro) KA.
Write*, edit, or publish a response to a review
Frontline reps can give tips and suggestions, but the pro needs to do the writing and submitting themselves.
Steps on internal Reviews (Pro) KA.
Submit a refund request
There are some expectations and a few exceptions for when a Frontline Rep can help the pro with submitting a refund request. Steps on internal Lead Refunds (Pro) KA.
*NOTE: With any writing, Frontline Reps can give tips and suggestions to pros, but pros need to do the writing and posting themselves. This applies to review responses, messaging customers, and so on. 
Steps: How to make changes to a pro account (Rep)

The following steps must be followed by Frontline Reps:
Encourage Self-Service First. Frontline Reps should encourage pros to edit their account info themselves, as this is the primary and most secure method. However, Frontline Reps are here to make it as easy as possible for the pro to use Thumbtack. If the account owner or authorized user requests that a Frontline Rep make changes to their account or profile, and they insist the rep do it for them, proceed with the following steps.
Review the Guidelines. Review the Changes Frontline Reps can make and Changes Frontline Reps cannot make lists to confirm the requested change is authorized.

NOTE: Do not make any changes or share any account information if the customer or pro can't verify the account or states they're not the account owner. See the internal Sensitive Account Information Handling (Pro) (Customer) (Rep) KA for more information.

Email the account owner any time a change is made on their behalf, regardless of whether there’s a "Do not email" tag in Tack.
Use the template: “Changes made to account - Confirmation email to account owner.”
List out all changes made to the account on behalf of the pro in the email.

AI Context: This section outlines the authorized actions Frontline Reps can take within a customer's Thumbtack account while impersonating them, focusing on account management, troubleshooting, and fulfilling specific customer requests, all while maintaining Thumbtack's policies.
Frontline Reps should encourage customers to edit their account info themselves. With this in mind, if the account owner or authorized user requests a change to their account or profile, and they insist the rep do it for them, Frontline Reps must follow these guidelines exactly to ensure compliance and proper account security.
For detailed steps and specific guidelines related to each of the following actions in this section, refer to the linked internal Knowledge Articles (KAs). 
The following list explains what Frontline reps can do when logged in as a customer, if requested by the account owner:
View the account to troubleshoot issues
If the Frontline Rep isn’t making changes to the customer’s account, they can impersonate the customer to see what they’re seeing. This can be useful when the customer is experiencing a bug or to walk the customer through steps in their account.
Reactivate or deactivate an account (Steps on internal Account Information (Customer) KA).
Edit method and number of notifications (Steps on internal Notifications (Customers) KA).
Submit a project (see non-voice or inbound voice for guidelines)
▶ Non-voice Support Reps will transfer to Boost. Learn more:
Non-voice Support Reps will want to transfer to Boost as usual, see the internal Projects (Customer) KA for more details on transferring to Boost
However, if the customer does not have access to the account, even if they have completed verification, Non-Voice Support Reps need to address any login issues the customer may be experiencing or encourage them to set up a new account first. After the customer gains access to their account, Non-Voice Support Reps will complete the handoff to the Boost Team. This way, Boost reps can guide the customer through submitting their project.
▶ Inbound Voice Support Reps can help the customer. Learn more:
Inbound Voice Support Reps are now able to help customers in submitting their project and finding new pros, if requested. Learn more in the internal Projects (Customer) KA.
When submitting a project for a customer, Voice Support Reps should follow these guidelines to avoid putting Thumbtack at risk:
Only submit a project if the customer explicitly asks for it.
Always explain that customers can book pros online through the website or app, and offer to walk the customer through how to do it before submitting.
Only fill out the request form based on the information the customer provides.
Help choose a pro who is a good fit for what is known about the customer's needs. Be sure to share the pro's business name with the customer and explain why that pro is a good fit (skills, ratings, availability).
Only send the request if the customer agrees with the pro that was chosen.
Submit the request to one pro unless the customer wants the request shared with multiple pros. Frontline Reps can ask if the customer wants to share the request with additional pros, but should never pressure the customer to do so.
Once the project is submitted, Frontline Reps should share the confirmation details (business name, contact info as appropriate, profile link, etc.), and give clear instructions on how the customer should follow up with the pro.
Send an email to the customer confirming the details of the pro and their project.

▶ Learn more (create account):

Using an incognito window, go to Thumbtack.com. 
Search for a pro and go through the booking process. Be sure to use the customer's name and email to complete the booking. 
After completing the booking, the customer will show up in Admin so the Frontline Rep can impersonate them.
The customer can then access their account and set up their password.

Major Rocket Rebate Program (Customer)

Contents
Overview
Rebate terms and conditions
Program details
Customer experience
Do’s and don’ts
Process
Steps: How to claim Major Rocket rebate (Customer)
Steps: How to set up a Hyperwallet account and select rebate payment method (Customer)
Talking points
Resources 
1. Overview
Major Rocket Rebate Program for Customers
Customers who are Major Rocket members—including those with accounts on Launchingdeals.com  or participating discount programs—are eligible to receive two separate rebates of up to $30 each per 12-month calendar year. These rebates apply to jobs booked through the Major Rocket partnership with Thumbtack.
Major Rocket is a major technology and benefits partner, operating as the US's largest employee perk plan, serving over 160 million clients. They leverage an extensive network to provide unique discounts.
Why Thumbtack is partnering with Major Rocket 
This partnership aims to establish a featured partner relationship between Thumbtack and Major Rocket, one of the largest employee benefit programs in the US.
How it works 
To get the rebate, customers hire a pro through Thumbtack, pay them, get a receipt, and submit the Major Rocket Rebate Claim Form within 30 days of payment. 
Once the rebate is approved, Thumbtack will send the customer the project cost, up to $30 for each of two separate projects per 12-month calendar year. The payment will be made via our partner, Hyperwallet, to the customer's preferred method (e.g., PayPal, Venmo, or bank account).
Rebate terms and conditions
The rebate is two separate $30 rebates each year.
Each rebate must be for a different job. You cannot use both on one job.
The total cost of the job must be $30 or more for the full rebate.
The claim must be sent with a receipt in 30 days of paying.
The client's Thumbtack account must be fine.
You cannot mix this rebate with any other deal.
The pro must have an active profile. The client must have found them on Thumbtack.
The $30 offer is only two times per calendar year (Jan 1 - Dec 31).
Thumbtack can end or revoke the promo.

Reps can refer customers to the Thumbtack x Major Rocket rebate terms and conditions Thumbtack article for more details. 
Program details
Launch Date: December 2025
End Date: TBD (The 2 rebates reset every 12 months)
Rebate Details: 
Two separate $30 rebates. 
Rebates must be for separate projects and cannot be stacked. 
Project cost must be $30 or more to claim the full rebate.
Impacted Users: Thumbtack customers who also have an account with Major Rocket, Launchingdeals.com, or are part of a participating employee or member-based discount program.
Identify Impacted Users: The customer will mention the Major Rocket rebate or the customer journey starts from the Major Rocket platform
Customer experience
Customers find Thumbtack from Major Rocket's marketplaces, or through seasonal, category-specific emails.
The marketplace links to Thumbtack’s website.
On the Thumbtack page, the Call to Action (CTA) is split into two buttons:
“Hire a pro today!” which links to the pro list search experience.
“Claim your $30 rebate” which links to the landing page with redemption instructions.
Customers will follow instructions on the landing page to claim the rebate using the Major Rocket Rebate Claim Form.
Do’s and Don’ts (Rep)
When helping Thumbtack customers with a Perplexity rebate, support reps should follow these guidelines: 
Do direct the customer to the help page/T&Cs for detailed questions. Thumbtack x Major Rocket rebate terms and conditions 
Do explain how Thumbtack works and help the customer book a pro. How to find a pro on Thumbtack 
Don’t mention the rebate to customers who haven’t asked about it first.
2. Process
Steps: How to claim Major Rocket rebate (Customer)
Customers with Major Rocket, Launchingdeals.com, or are part of a participating employee or member-based discount program will follow these steps to redeem their Major Rocket rebate:
Hire a pro through Thumbtack and pay them. 
Get a receipt from the pro (they will need this for their claim).
Go to the Major Rocket Rebate Claim Form within 30 days of payment and fill in the required information.
First name *
Last name *
Email used with their Thumbtack account *
Pro business name who completed the project *
Total project cost *
Address where the work was completed *
Receipt * (file upload)
If the claim is approved, Thumbtack will send the rebate through Hyperwallet. It may take up to one week for a rebate to be approved. 
The customer will get an email from Hyperwallet with instructions on how to create an account and choose how to receive their $30 rebate (PayPal, Venmo, bank account, or another method).
Important details about claiming a rebate
When requesting a rebate, customers must do the following: 
Complete the project and pay the pro (before claiming the rebate).
Submit the Major Rocket Rebate Claim Form with an attached receipt within 30 days of paying for the project
Steps: How to set up a Hyperwallet account and select rebate payment method (Customer)
Once the customer’s claim is approved, Thumbtack will send funds to Hyperwallet to issue the customer's rebate as a payment.
Hyperwallet will send an email to the email on file. The email includes a Claim Payment button.
Clicking “Claim Payment” from the email, they will enter the Hyperwallet redemption flow. 
Hyperwallet will need details in order to send the payment. The customer will need to:
Select a payment option (PayPal, Venmo, etc.)
Provide profile details
After claiming their rebate, the customer can track their payment and will receive an email once their payment has been processed. 
Customers are sent a final email once the payment has been processed. The rebate will appear in the account the customer provided. The customer should reach out to Hyperwallet with any concerns or questions.
3. Talking points 
Frequently asked questions (FAQs) and answers for frontline reps.

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: How many times can I use this $30 Major Rocket rebate? 
Q: 
A: You can submit up to 2 claims, for a maximum of $30 each, per 12-month calendar year.
A: 
Q: Do I have to claim all $30 at once for the Major Rocket rebate?

A: Yes. You can submit a claim for the cost of one project, up to $30. The project cost must be $30 or more to receive the full $30 rebate.

Q: Can I use both of my Major Rocket rebates for the same job?

A: No, only one rebate can be used per job.

Q: How will I know when my Major Rocket rebate is approved?
¿Cómo sabré cuándo se aprueba mi reembolso?
A: It may take up to a week for a rebate to be approved. Once approved, you'll get an email from Hyperwallet with next steps.
La aprobación de un reembolso puede tardar hasta una semana. Una vez que se apruebe, recibirá un correo electrónico de Hyperwallet.
Q: What payment methods can I use to get my Major Rocket rebate?

Your rebate is sent through our partner, Hyperwallet, and you can choose to receive it via PayPal, Venmo, bank account, or another method of your choice.

Q: Does my Major Rocket rebate offer expire?

The offer to get $30 back is limited to two times (2) within a calendar year (Jan 1 - Dec 31). However, you must submit your request within 30 days of paying your Pro.

Can the Major Rocket rebate offer be converted into cash value?
Se puede convertir la oferta en dinero en efectivo?
No, this offer cannot be converted into cash value.
No, esta oferta no se puede convertir en dinero en effective.
Is there a cost to sign up or use Thumbtack?
¿Hay algún costo por registrarse o utilizar Thumbtack?
There is no cost to sign up for Thumbtack or use Thumbtack. Pricing for projects will vary by category and depending on the pricing the pro sets.
No hay ningún costo por registrarse en Thumbtack ni por utilizar Thumbtack. Los precios de los proyectos varían según la categoría y los precios establecidos por el profesional.

▶ KA summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) provides Frontline reps with high-level details regarding Lowe’s installation jobs. It also outlines the specific workflows and transfer processes that Support reps must follow when helping customers or pros with active Lowe’s jobs.  
 
[Image: rtaImage]

Thumbtack and Lowe's have teamed up to enable installation bookings directly through Lowes.com and select in-store locations for plumbing and electrical jobs. This partnership helps Lowe's customers move from buying products—like sinks, toilets, fans, and light fixtures—to finishing their home projects faster by connecting them with local, qualified professionals.
Why is Thumbtack teaming up with Lowes? 
This experience improves the overall customer experience by providing:
Easier Project Completion: Connects customers who lack the skills or time for DIY with pros who can finish the job.
Trusted Local Pros: Customers hire with confidence knowing they are being matched with pros who meet specific standards including: 
Verified licensing: Pros must have a valid license on file for plumbing or electrical jobs (if the pros location requires it). 
Comprehensive screening: Mandatory background checks for the account owner and all on-site technicians. 
Proven quality: Only pros who maintain high-performance ratings on Thumbtack are selected to fulfill these installations. 
Convenience and Speed: Customers book their installation at checkout and can communicate directly with their pro.
Updates
Types of Lowe’s installation jobs
Lowe’s customers can request professional installation for Plumbing and Electrical projects.
 
[Image: rtaImage]

A single Lowe's order can contain multiple installation items. See Multiproduct Jobs for details on how bundled orders work.  Eligible pros can claim “simple jobs” directly in product. Complex jobs (sink measurements, sink installations, toilets, and disconnect/reconnect) will continue to be manually fulfilled.

Overview of installation job workflow
This section provides frontline reps with a high level look at the flow of Lowe’s jobs: 
Customer purchases the job
The customer purchases eligible products and the installation services from Lowe's (online or in-store).
Lowe's is the merchant of record; they manage the financial transaction and initial order.
Thumbtack will send the customer an email to schedule their installation by selecting a date and time (a 3-hr arrival window).
Pro accepts the job
Thumbtack matches the customer's job with a Thumbtack pro.
Eligible pros (Plumbers or Electricians): Must have a verified license and passed BGC, plus a 4.0+ star average rating if reviews exist. Pros must also sign the Lowe’s one-time subcontractor contract to qualify.
For complex jobs: Thumbtack will call eligible pros to fulfill the job.
For simple jobs: Pros can claim the job from their “For you” tab. 
Job completion and payment
If additional labor or parts are needed for the job, the pro must call Lowe's Support at (888) 516-1010 for approval before starting the extra work.
After the job is complete (and after the scheduled start time), the pro marks the job as "Job done" in the Thumbtack app.
Payouts are sent once the following conditions are met:
Pro assigns technicians to the claimed job 
Pro uploaded required permits or document (if applicable)
Pro marked job as done
Once these conditions are met, earnings are transferred via direct deposit within 4–5 business days.
Multi-product Jobs
 
A single Lowe's order can include multiple installation services. When this happens, all items are bundled into one claimable job rather than separate jobs.
Job classification
The job type is determined by the most complex item in the bundle. If all items are simple, the job is eligible for in-product claiming. If any item in the order is complex — such as a toilet, sink, or disconnect/reconnect — the entire order defaults to the manual (complex) workflow and is fulfilled by the TToD team. 
Customer experience 
The scheduling and booking flow is the same as a single-item job — the customer schedules once for all items in the order. The customer's confirmation and pro details emails will reflect all items included.
Pro experience 
Before claiming, the pro sees:
Total number of installations (e.g. "3 total")
Each installation type listed individually with a "View requirements" link
A list of all items to install with a "View item details" link for each
Combined flat payout for all items

Marking a multi-product job as done 
Pros should only mark the job as done once all items in the bundle have been installed. If a pro plans to return to complete remaining items, they should wait until everything is finished before marking the job as done — this is the simplest path to getting paid in full.
