1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) (Leads (Pro)) provides guidance for frontline reps on how pros manage leads within the Thumbtack platform. It details various lead types, payment structures, and processes for how pros respond to and decline leads. Additionally, it offers troubleshooting steps for lead volume issues, addresses questionable behavior, and provides essential talking points and resources for effective pro support.
Customers come to Thumbtack with work to be done, answer a few questions, and then browse pros in their area. If a customer is interested in learning more about a pro or hiring a pro right away, they’ll reach out. Pros will get the customer's message along with the job details. This first message is a lead, which appears in the pro's "Jobs" tab.
There are a few different types of leads or jobs on Thumbtack, like:
▶ Leads
What they are:
Leads are customers who saw a pros profile in their search results and reached out to the pro.
These leads match pro's targeting preferences (also known as "Job preferences"). Pros will find these under the “For you” tab.
When a pro pays: Because they match a pros preferences, they pay for these leads automatically.
Pro resource:  What are leads, claimable jobs, and opportunities? – Thumbtack Help
▶ Opportunities
What they are:
Opportunities are customers who haven’t hired a pro yet and are still looking for quotes.
Pros can reach out to these customers to let them know they’re interested in their job.
The customer can hire the pro if they think the pro is a good fit.
These are leads pros take on if they have some gaps to fill in their schedule, or simply want more leads. 
Pros will find them in the “Opportunities” tab on the Jobs page.
When a pro pays: Pros only pay if the customer responds to them.
Resource: 
Pro: What are Opportunities? – Thumbtack Help 
Rep: internal Opportunities (Pro) KA
▶ Claimable jobs
What they are:
Claimable jobs are jobs where the customer already scheduled the date and time. 
They match a pro's preferences and all the pro needs to do is claim it. 
These jobs are available to pros that offer specific service types and meet certain criteria (like having 3 or more reviews). 
Pro will find them in their “For you" tab, where they can browse the details and claim the jobs that are a good fit for them.
When a pro pays:
Thumbtack takes a percentage of the customer's payment, rather than having the pro pay for the lead up front.
Pros will see how much they'll earn for the job before they claim it.
Once the pro marks the job as completed (and sets up direct deposit), they’ll get paid. 
Resource: 
Pro: What are claimable jobs? – Thumbtack Help 
Rep: Internal Claimable Jobs (Pro) 
▶ Opt-in Leads
Rep: Internal Opt-In Leads KA
Updates and experiments
Leads (exact matches)
Leads come from customers who searched for a pro, saw a pros profile, and reached out to the pro directly. These leads perfectly match a pro’s targeting preferences and are covered by The Thumbtack Quality Commitment (What is Thumbtack’s Quality Commitment?).
Pros agree to auto-pay when a lead exactly matches their preferences, even if they decide they’re not interested in a particular lead later.
Pros will find these in the "For you" section of their Jobs tab. Pros should respond to all exact matches. They pay for the lead regardless, and it keeps up their response rate (which impacts rank). Reps can refer to the internal Messaging Customers and Pro Responsiveness (Pro) KA to learn more. 
If a pro finds they’re getting exact matches they’re not interested in, they should update their targeting preferences. Reps can refer to the internal Targeting: Job Types and Travel Preferences (Pro) KA to learn more.
Here’s an overview of the lead flow: 
The customer finds the pro in (or right after) their search results and contacts them.
The pro sees the new lead in the “For you” section of their Jobs tab.
The pro can either "Reply" or select "Can’t do it" to let the customer know.
Once the pro replies to the customer, the conversation moves to the Messages tab.
NOTE: The “Can’t do it” button will not show if the pro clicks “Reply”, then leaves the page without sending a message. At that point, they've already accepted the lead and need to follow through with sending the message. "Can't do it" is no longer an option. 
Important lead timelines to keep in mind: 
If the pro replies later than 48 hours or not at all, the response time for that contact is treated as 48 hours.
If a pro doesn't take action (reply or accept) a lead within 30 days, it will be removed from the pros "For you" tab and will no longer have access to it after 30 days, regardless if they've viewed the lead or not.
Reps can use the Leads (exact match) talking points below to help navigate these conversations. 
Being charges for (exact match) leads 
Pros automatically pay for exact match leads because these leads are generated based on the preferences the pro has set.
Pros can see the cost of each lead (and whether it's a paid or pending charge) by going to their Payments. 
Charged
Pros are charged for leads. A lead is the first time a customer reaches out to the pro. This can mean the customer messages, calls, books an appointment, or hires the pro. 
To learn more about lead pricing, frontline reps can refer to the internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA.
 Not charged
Pros aren't charged for any follow-up chats, jobs, or referrals from that customer. 
To track spending and other ways to see lead cost, frontline reps can refer to the internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA. For details about the payments page, frontline reps can refer to the internal Charges on Thumbtack: Payment Methods and Billing (Pro) KA. 
Labels on leads 
To highlight important information, leads may have different labels on them. 

[Image: rtaImage]

The table below details some of the labels a pro might see on a lead within the "For you Leads" tab of the Jobs page. The labels are listed in alphabetical order.


Label on lead
What the label means
Canceled
Thumbtack or the customer deleted the request or the customer account
Exact match
The details of the lead exactly match the pro’s preferences (includes availability)
Free
The pro gets the lead for free
High value job 
The job’s value is higher than 70% of other jobs
Near you
The lead is within a certain amount of miles from the pro’s travel preferences (distance varies depending on Thumbtack's market assessment)
New
A lead the pro has not seen yet.
Only picked you 
The customer hasn’t contacted any other pros yet, which means it’s a good chance for the pro. The “Only picked you” pill will show on leads if the pro viewed the lead before the customer reached out to more pros. *Reps should compare the timestamp of the quotes in the project admin.
Paid
The pro already paid for this lead
Photos
The customer added photos to the request
Recurring job
The customer is looking for a pro to help with a recurring job
Reduced price
The pro got a discount for any number of reasons
Refunded
Pro was refunded for this lead
+
If there are more labels than can be displayed on the lead, pros will see + and the number of labels hidden
Managing new leads: Respond or declined (exact matches) 
When a pro receives a new lead, they’ll see it in the “For you” section of their Jobs tab. To learn more about a lead, they’ll click View details. The pro can either Reply or select Can’t do it to let the customer know.
Responding to a New Lead (When the Pro is Interested)
Customers come to Thumbtack looking for a pro, and pros that fit the customer’s needs show up in search results. When a pro receives a new lead (exact match), it means the customer saw the pro in their search results and reached out to learn more about them. They should follow these steps to engage with the customer and potentially secure the job:
Locate the Lead: All new leads will appear in the "For you" section of the pro's Jobs tab. 
Review Details (Optional but Recommended): To gain a deeper understanding of the customer's request, the pro can click "View details." This will provide additional context that can help the pro tailor their response.
Initiate the Response: If the pro is interested in pursuing the lead, they should select the "Reply" option..
Craft the Message: The pro should write a clear and professional message to the customer. The pro has the flexibility to:
Compose a custom message from scratch.
Utilize a "quick reply" for common scenarios, saving the pro time.
A few other helpful things a pro can include in their message: 
Personalize the response by using the customer's name.
Answer any questions the customer asks.
Suggest a next step, like a phone call or in-person meeting.
Attach relevant files or images to the message, such as a portfolio or a detailed service breakdown.
Send the Message: Once the message is complete and the pro is satisfied with its content, they should click "Send."
Conversation Continues in Messages: After the pro sends a response, the entire conversation with that customer will automatically move to the pro's Messages tab. This keeps all ongoing communications organized in one place.
Declining an Exact Match Lead (When the Pro is Not Interested)
Even if a lead is an "exact match" (meaning it perfectly aligns with the pro's targeting preferences), there might be instances where the pro is unable or unwilling to take on the job. Here's how the pro can decline such leads while managing their profile effectively:
Locate the Lead: As with all new leads, the pro will find the exact match in the "For you" section of their Jobs tab.
Take Decline Action: If the pro is not interested in the lead, they should select the "Can't do it" option to let the customer know.
Crucial Note: The “Can’t do it” button will not show if the pro clicks “Reply,” then leaves the page without sending a message. At that point, the pro has already accepted the lead and needs to follow through with sending the message. "Can't do it" is no longer an option.
Complete the Optional Survey: After a pro selects "Can't do it" for a lead that exactly matches their preferences, an optional survey will appear. This survey asks for the pro's reason for declining the lead.
Adjust Preferences (If Applicable): If the pro indicates that they weren't interested due to an inaccurate preference, the survey will guide them on how to adjust those preferences. This is a vital step to ensure that future leads better align with the pro's desired work, helping them maintain control over the types of jobs they receive and pay for.
Key points for managing leads: 
Prompt Action is Key: Whether the pro is responding or declining, acting on leads quickly is crucial. The pro's responsiveness directly impacts their ranking in search results and informs customers to continue their search if the pro is unavailable.
Refunds for Exact Matches: It's important to understand that pros automatically pay for exact match leads because these leads are generated based on the preferences the pro has set. Therefore, refunds are generally not issued for declining exact matches. Maintaining accurate targeting preferences is paramount to avoid receiving and paying for unwanted leads.
Lead Expiration: If a pro does not take any action (either reply or accept) on a lead within 30 days, it will be automatically removed from their Jobs tab. After this 30-day period, the pro will no longer have access to that lead, regardless of whether they had previously viewed it.
Handling Mismatched Preferences (for Reps): If a pro is receiving leads that don't match their preferences, support reps should first check if the pro has targeting preferences turned on for that service. Then, they should follow the steps on the internal  Targeting Preferences (Pro) KA. 
Flexible preferences: However, reps should keep in mind that pros cannot filter out flexible preferences in eligible request forms because these aren’t options available to adjust in their targeting preferences. These flexible preferences indicate that the customer is open to options, and includes “I’m flexible” and “I’m not sure” type of answers. Reps can learn more in the internal Flexible Request Form (Pro) (Customer) Knowledge Article.
Updating Job Status on a Lead
Pros can track the progress of their leads by updating the job status. This helps them manage their workflow and can trigger important actions on Thumbtack.
A job's status can be updated in two ways:
Manually by the pro: A pro can open their messages with a customer and use the drop-down menu to select the status that best fits
Automatically by the customer: If a customer hasn't responded to a message, they will be prompted to update the status of their project. The job status will then automatically update for the pro based on the customer's selection.
Manually by the pro: 
Pros have four options when updating the job status on a lead:
Not scheduled yet: The pro is still trying to win the customer and negotiating details.
Scheduled: The customer and pro have decided to work together.
Job done: The pro has finished the job.
No hire: The pro didn’t get hired, and the lead didn’t work out.
▶ What the “update job status” screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Impact of Status Updates:
When a pro updates the status to "Scheduled" or "Job Done," Thumbtack will ask the customer to write a review for the pro.
The hire count on the pro's profile will increase when the customer leaves a review or when they tell Thumbtack how their project is going in response to an auto-generated email.
Pros can filter their messages by job status to get a quick view of which jobs turned into hires.
Automatic updates from customers:
If a customer selects...
“Yes, I’ve hired this pro”: 
If the customer only contacted one pro:
The job status updates to “Scheduled”
The messenger will update to say:  “[Customer name] let us know they hired you.”
If the customer contacted more than one pro:
The job status for other pros updates to “No hire”
The messenger will update to say: “[Customer name] let us know they hired someone else.”
“No, I’m going with someone else”: 
The job status updates to “No hire”. 
The messenger will update to say: “[Customer name] let us know they hired someone else.”
“I’m not pursuing this project”: 
The job status for all contacted pros updates to “No hire”
The messenger will update to say: “[Customer name] let us know they are no longer pursuing this project.”

2. Process
Steps: How to respond to leads (Pro)

To respond to leads, pros should follow the steps outlined in the How to respond to leads – Thumbtack Help article. This involves carefully reading customer messages and job details, personalizing responses, answering questions, and suggesting next steps. Pros can also use Quick Replies to respond faster to common questions.
To learn more about messaging customers and quick replies reps can refer to the internal Messaging Customers and Pro Responsiveness (Pro) KA.
Steps: How to update the job status on a lead (Pro) 
Pros can update the job status on a lead by following the steps in the How to keep track of my hires – Thumbtack Help article. This allows them to track the progress of their leads, manage their workflow, and trigger important actions on Thumbtack, such as prompting customers to write a review when a job is marked as "Scheduled" or "Job Done."
(Rep) Steps: How to help pros can get more leads
There are a lot of things pros can do to meet more customers. To help a pro get more leads, support reps can: 
Look at their targeting preferences: When those are set, pros have a better chance of getting seen in search results for the jobs they really want. And exact matches qualify for additional discounts and refunds with The Thumbtack Quality Commitment.
Reps can refer to the following internal KAs: 
Targeting: Job Types and Travel Preferences (Pro)
Thumbtack’s Quality Commitment (Pro)
Check their budget: If they hit their budget by Tuesday or Wednesday, they could be missing out on leads that show up near the end of the week.
Reps can refer to the internal Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro) to learn more. 
Adjust notifications: Pros can get an email, text, or phone alert when interested customers reach out or if there are new opportunities they might want to express interest in.
Reps can refer to the internal Notifications (Pro) to learn more. 
Check out the “Opportunities” section of the Jobs tab – That’s where pros can meet more customers. Pros can also use this to get a better idea of what type of work customers in their area need help with — and then update their services and preferences to better match those opportunities.
Reps can refer to the internal Opportunities (Pro) to learn more.

A quick overview of opportunities 
If pros want to fill their calendar with more work, they can see what’s available in the "Opportunities" section of their Jobs tab. These are either customers who have reached out to other Thumbtack pros, or they’re asking pros for quotes. Pros can let these customers know if they’re interested in the job, and they only pay if the customer responds to the pro. Opportunities are priced separately, and targeting preferences aren’t tied to how the pro is charged.
(Rep) Steps: How to help pros who aren't winning or hearing back from customers
There are many reasons why a pro might not get hired by Thumbtack customers. There are also specific actions a customer can take if they aren’t interested in hiring a pro, like canceling a project or declining a pro. 
If a pro contacts support say they aren’t winning jobs or hearing back from customers, support reps can follow these steps: 
Pull up the pro's account: It can be discouraging to put work into their Thumbtack account and not hear back from customers. It can be a number of factors, so make sure to pull up the pro's account and give them honest feedback.
Pro resources: 
Here's a guide to your Thumbtack profile.
How to improve my profile – Thumbtack Help
▶ Talking Point
English talking points
Spanish talking points
If you have time, I’d love to go over your profile with you and give you tips to stand out in customer’s search results.
Si tiene tiempo, me encantaría revisar su perfil con usted y darle consejos para que resalte en los resultados de búsqueda de los clientes.
Reviews: Encourage pros to put some work into their reviews by reaching out to past customers and responding professionally (to both negative and positive reviews.)
Pro resource:
How to ask for reviews – Thumbtack Help 
How to respond to reviews – Thumbtack Help 
Rep resources: Reviews (Pro)
▶ Talking Point:
English talking points
Spanish talking points
Pros with more reviews get hired more often. That’s because customers want to know what it would be like to work with you. Do you know how to find your review link to send to your customers outside of Thumbtack?
Los profesionales con más reseñas son contratados con más frecuencia. Eso es porque los clientes quieren saber cómo sería trabajar con usted. ¿Sabe cómo encontrar su enlace de reseñas para enviar a sus clientes fuera de Thumbtack
Being responsive: Response rate can impact where a pro shows up in search results. It’s important they respond to leads and messages quickly.
Pro resource:  
Here's a guide to getting hired with your messages – Thumbtack Help
How to respond to leads – Thumbtack Help  
Rep resources: Messaging Customers and Pro Responsiveness (Pro)
▶ Talking Point:
English talking points
Spanish talking points
When a customer reaches out to you, responding quickly is key. If you’re too busy to reply with a detailed message right away, you can send a brief note to let the customer know you’re interested and you’ll provide more details soon. Also, make sure to decline leads quickly if you’re unavailable
Cuando un cliente se comunica con usted, responder rápidamente es clave. Si está demasiado ocupado para responder con un mensaje detallado de inmediato, puede enviar una breve nota para que el cliente sepa que está interesado y pronto brindará más detalles. Además, asegúrese de rechazar clientes potenciales rápidamente si no está disponible.
NOTE: Depending on the situation, reps can use the Not getting hired talking points to address their concern.
(Rep) Steps: How to help pros who aren't getting enough leads (troubleshooting)
If a pro says they’re not getting enough leads, Support reps should follow these troubleshooting steps:
Check the pro’s job types: Are their job types correct? (Pros can take another look at their job types and see if there are any other kinds of jobs they can add.)
Rep resource: internal Targeting: Job Types and Travel Preferences (Pro) KA
Check the pro’s travel preferences: Is their travel area set up correctly? (Pros can expand their travel area to meet more customers.)
Rep resource: internal Targeting: Job Types and Travel Preferences (Pro) KA
Check the pro’s availability: Make sure that the pro’s calendar and availability settings are correct.
Rep resource: internal  Availability: Business Hours, Calendar, and Hide a Business (Pro)
Check the pro’s Performance dashboard: Check the pro’s Performance dashboard for market and competition insights.
Rep resource: internal Performance Dashboard: Market Level Insights (Pro) KA
Check the pro's quality: Check for profile completeness, responsiveness, and reviews.
Check the pro’s account status: Does the pro have a hold on their account that's preventing them from appearing in search results?
Rep resource: internal Account Holds (Pro) KA
If the Frontline rep completes all the above troubleshooting steps and still thinks the pro should be receiving more leads, the Frontline rep should submit a bug report and make sure to include as many details as possible in the report. Reps will follow the steps in the internal Bugs and Bug Reports (Rep) KA. 
NOTE: ​​As long as the pro is in search results, it is not considered a bug and you should not submit a bug report. Not getting any or enough leads means that customers are not choosing the pro. 
In the meantime, pros can check for open opportunities in the "Opportunities" section of their Jobs tab to supplement lead volume.
(Rep) Steps: How to help pro get fewer leads (pro is getting too many leads) 
If the pro says they are getting too many leads than they need (and have targeting preferences on) pros can:
Job types: Narrow their job types to only the jobs they want the most.
Travel preferences: Make their travel area smaller.
For more info on preferences, reps should refer to the internal Targeting: Job Types and Travel Preferences (Pro) KA.
4. "Questionable" behavior on lead 
How Thumbtack handles competitor contact abuse (Pro pretended to be a customer)
Thumbtack monitors when pros pretend to be customers and reach out to their competitors on Thumbtack (or themselves). They might do this for several reasons:
to gauge competitors’ prices
to fake a hire on Thumbtack
to leave a fake verified review. 
Here are the actions Thumbtack takes when a pro is caught: 
First warning: If Thumbtack catches a pro doing this, Thumbtack deletes the request (which refunds any pros who were contacted) and give the offending pro a warning.
Second warning: If the pro does it again, we give them a second warning.
Third warning: If the pro continues and does it a third time, Thumbtack put their account on hold for three business days. 
Fourth warning: On the fourth offense, the pro’s account is deleted.
Support reps should not share any details with the pro around how Thumbtack discovered their fake requests (which often comes down to pros using the same devices, internet connections, and credit card info associated with their account).
(Rep) Steps: How to help a pro who received a warning for competitor contact abuse 
Pros may contact Thumbtack after receiving one of these warnings, or after their account was suspended or deleted. Support reps will follow these steps: 
Let them know when Thumbtack sends out warnings, and we’re confident in our actions. Account holds and deletions will not be lifted.
If they explain the situation and you feel the warning was sent incorrectly, please escalate the case to the Trust and Safety team.  For steps, reps will refer to the internal Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA. 

3. Talking points
▶ 🤖 Background notes
[AI Context]: This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with Pros and Customers regarding lead management. Use these talking points to ensure consistent and accurate messaging, ultimately helping both Pros and Customers by providing clear and helpful guidance on leads.
Leads (exact match)
English FAQs
Spanish FAQs
What does “exact match” mean?
¿Qué significa "coincidencia exacta"?
An exact match is a lead that matches all of your targeting preferences. You automatically pay for leads when they match your preferences because these are the jobs you told us you want. These leads are also covered by The Thumbtack Quality Commitment.
Un prospecto exacto es un prospecto que coincide con todas sus preferencias de enfoque. Usted paga automáticamente por los prospectos cuando coinciden con sus preferencias porque estos son los trabajos que nos dijo que deseaba. Estos prospectos también están cubiertos por nuestra Garantía de Precio.
How do I know if I’ve already paid for a lead?
¿Cómo sé si ya pagué por un prospecto?
It will be labeled “Paid.” If you haven’t already paid, that means you can choose to accept the lead and pay, or you can decline it at no charge. Either way, it’s important to respond to these leads quickly because your response time impacts where you appear in future search results.
Se etiqueta como "Pagado". Si aún no ha pagado, eso significa que puede optar por aceptar el prospecto y pagar, o puede rechazarlo sin cargo. De cualquier manera, es importante responder a estos prospectos rápidamente porque su tiempo de respuesta afecta dónde aparece en futuros resultados de búsqueda.
Customer cancelled or declines
English FAQs
Spanish FAQs
Why did this customer cancel their job?
¿Por qué este cliente canceló su trabajo?
There are a lot of different reasons customers cancel jobs. They may have decided not to complete the job, or chosen to do it themselves. I know it’s frustrating when a customer’s plans change, but as long as you’ve been helpful and professional, you’ve done your best to keep the door open in case they come back to do this project.
Hay muchas razones diferentes por las que los clientes cancelan trabajos. Es posible que hayan decidido no completar el trabajo o hayan optado por hacerlo ellos mismos. Sé que es frustrante cuando los planes de un cliente cambian, pero siempre que haya sido útil y profesional, habrá hecho todo lo posible para mantener la puerta abierta en caso de que regresen para hacer este proyecto.
Why did the customer decline after they contacted me?
¿Por qué declinó el cliente después de contactarme?
Once a customer contacts you, it’s up to you to work out the details with the customer and (hopefully) get hired. In this case, the customer let us know they went another direction and didn’t want to receive further messages.
Una vez que un cliente se pone en contacto con usted, depende de usted resolver los detalles con el cliente y (con suerte) ser contratado. En este caso, el cliente nos hizo saber que tomó otra dirección y no quería recibir más mensajes.
Why can’t I message a customer who canceled their job / declined?
¿Por qué no puedo enviar un mensaje a un cliente que canceló o rechazó su trabajo?
Customers don’t get notifications on canceled jobs, so you won’t be able to message them once a job is canceled. When customers’ plans change, it’s best to focus on providing great service to the active customers you’re chatting with. 
Los clientes no reciben notificaciones sobre trabajos cancelados, por lo que no podrá enviarles mensajes una vez que se cancele un trabajo. Cuando cambian los planes de los clientes, es mejor concentrarse en brindar un excelente servicio a los clientes activos con los que está hablando.
Pros says they're not getting hired 
NOTE: There are many reasons why a pro might not get hired by Thumbtack customers. There are also specific actions a customer can take if they aren’t interested in hiring a pro, like canceling a project or declining a pro. 
English FAQs
Spanish FAQs
Why aren’t I getting hired / leads? (in general)  
¿Por qué no me contratan / prospectos? (en general)
Great question. There are a lot of things you can do to increase the likelihood of a customer reaching out to you. I recommend focusing on what the customer sees in search results: your overall profile, reviews, and photos for example. And once a customer has contacted you, being as responsive as you can. If you can respond to customers within five minutes, you’re 50% more likely to hear back. 
Buena pregunta. Hay muchas cosas que puede hacer para aumentar la probabilidad de que un cliente se comunique con usted. Recomiendo centrarse en lo que el cliente ve en los resultados de búsqueda: su perfil general, evaluaciones y fotos, por ejemplo. Una vez que un cliente se haya puesto en contacto con usted, sea lo más receptivo posible. Si puede responder a los clientes en cinco minutos, es un 50% más probable que reciba una respuesta.
4. Resources

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
Purpose: The Lead Refunds (Pro) internal Knowledge article (KA) provides information for Thumbtack Frontline Service Reps regarding the Lead Refund Policy for pros. It details various refund types, processes for requesting and disputing refunds, and guidance for handling related inquiries from Pros.
Target Audience: Thumbtack Frontline Service RepsThis KA will help reps understand:
Refund Types: Automatic refunds versus case-by-case refunds, including specific reasons and eligibility criteria.
Refund Process: The steps pros take to request and check refund status, as well as how to dispute a refund decision.
Courtesy Credits: Information on Promotional Balance Increases (PBIs) and when they may be issued.
Talking Points: Guidance for reps on communicating refund information and addressing common pro questions.

Here's a quick overview of what reps will find:
Overview: Detailed explanation of the refund policy, types of refunds, and eligibility requirements.
Process: Step-by-step instructions for pros and reps related to refund requests, status checks, and disputes.

Refunds for certain situations are automatically given and others are given on a case-by-case basis and are usually based on Terms of Use violations and the refund policy. Pros must dispute a charge within 45 days of payment and have proof to support the pro’s reason for disputing the charge.
Lead refunds are returned to a pros Thumbtack balance, not to their original form of payment. Credit packages are not refundable but individual leads or bookings purchased with the credit can be disputed, and if approved, will be credited to a pros Thumbtack balance.
If a pro is asking about a lead that was free due to a promotional discount or incentive offer, standard refund policy does not apply in the same way. For guidance on free lead refund policy and complimentary credits, see the Investigate Free Leads and Discounts in Admin (Rep) KA.

Do's and Don'ts
Frontline Reps should adhere to the following do's and don'ts when helping with refund requests. Following these guidelines will help pros by ensuring consistent and accurate handling of their refund issues.
Frontline reps should follow these do’s and don’ts when helping pros with refunds: 
DO: 
Be positive about refund requests being done in product. Help the pro understand how this will help them use their business time more efficiently and this is the fastest way to get their request processed.
Remind pros they must dispute charges within 45 days to qualify for our refund policy. 
Review talking points to help pros understand why they qualify for a refund or not. 
Encourage pros to request future refunds through the Thumbtack website or app (do not process the request if they contacted us)
Help pro with additional questions they may have while letting them know they'll typically receive a response within 24-48 hours. If a situation requires future review, a response may take up to 96 hours (4 day).
Direct the pro to email refunddisputes@thumbtack.com if they have questions about a refund or want to dispute a decision. The pro should hear back within 1 business day. 
DON'T 
Check or process refund requests unless the pro meets one of the exceptions.
Check a refund request decision unless the pro contacts support disputing the decision. 
Immediately promise that the pro will receive a refund.
Be afraid to say no. Sticking to our refund policy sets the right expectations going forward for the pro (and helps other advocates do the same).
Grant a refund or courtesy credit to yourself, your family members, your friends, another Thumbtack employee’s pro account, or to a friend/relative of a Thumbtack employee. Direct them through the regular refund process. To ensure IPO readiness, Thumbtack has new tracking in place to monitor and prevent these types of transactions. Pros should hear back within 1 business day.
Key points
Here are key points for Frontline reps to remember when helping pros with refunds. Understanding these points will help pros by ensuring they receive timely and correct information and help. 
Frontline reps should keep the following key points in mind when helping pros with refunds: 
Don’t check or process refund requests. 
Don’t check a refund request decision unless the pro contacts support disputing the decision. 
Refund eligibility: Refunds are possible for issues that fall within Thumbtack’s refund policy. Pros must dispute charges within 45 days to qualify for Thumbtack's refund policy.
Refund status: Most refunds usually take 24-48 hours. If a situation requires future review, a response may take up to 96 hours (4 day). Pros can check the status on their Payments page or in the messenger with the customer.
Refunds and the pro's Thumbtack balance: Refunds are returned to the pro's Thumbtack balance by default, not the original payment method.
Refunds and the weekly budget: Refunds for leads charged in the current week (Monday-Sunday) are credited back to the pro's weekly budget. Refunds for leads from previous weeks are credited to the pro's overall Thumbtack balance.
Refunds back to pros original form of payment: Refunds can be returned back to a pros card if eligible. Reps can refer to the Transfer Pros Cashable Balance Back To Card KA. 
Case-by-Case refunds: These require a review by Thumbtack. 
Automatic refunds: Issued without a pro needing to request them (such as leads flagged as Trust and Safety violations).
In-Policy refunds: These are granted for issues within Thumbtack’s refund policy.
Courtesy credits (PBIs): Discretionary refunds for situations outside the refund policy, like unresponsive customers or not getting hired.
Refund decision disputes: If they disagree with a refund decision (pro’s refund was denied), they should email refunddisputes@thumbtack.com. Pros should include the customer’s name, and provide any additional information, context, or documentation that supports their dispute. Pros should hear back within 1 business day.
Free leads: If a pro is asking for a free lead to be refunded and the lead that was free due to a promotional discount, refer to the internal Investigate Free Leads and Discounts in Admin (Rep) KA .

Thumbtack's refund policy for leads
This section contains some information for internal use only, outlining situations where Thumbtack allows refunds for leads.
When speaking with pros, Frontline Reps should refer to the Explain Thumbtack's Refund Policy  talking points in this KA or share the Refund policy for pros – Thumbtack Help article with pros.
Thumbtack allows refunds in the following situations:

Availability issues: When a flexible lead ("allow pros to suggest alternative dates" or no service date provided) turns out to not be flexible after the pro offers alternative dates.
Duplicate job: Customer requests the same job twice (within 45 days of each other), and pro pays for both leads
Job details changed: Job details changed significantly from the original lead details. 
Questionable job: Pro gets a lead with unusual or suspicious details or activity
Scam job / against Terms of Use: Customer violates Terms of Use or other guidelines
Job is from a minor: Pro gets a lead from someone under 18 years of age
Job is from a third party: Customer is hiring full-time employees
Job doesn't match preferences (job is unreasonable): If a pro receives a lead that does not match with their set targeting preferences (also known as "job preferences") at the time of the request created, Thumbtack will provide an In-Policy Refund under job doesn’t match preferences. 
For businesses with targeting preferences turned on, the policy allows refund in these situations:
Bugs
Customers first contact is “no thanks” (opportunities only)
Refunds for leads and bookings are allowed in certain situations, as long as: 

The pro disputes the charge within 45 days of payment.
There’s proof to support the pro’s reason for disputing the charge.
Thumbtack recommends pros have a conversation with the customer within the Thumbtack messenger and explain the details of their dispute.
Pros also have the ability to attach proof to their refund request such as screenshots of their SMS conversation.

How Approved Refunds Are Applied
When a pro receives a refund (in-policy and courtesy credits), the lead amount is always returned to the pro's overall Thumbtack balance. The impact on the weekly budget depends on when the original lead was charged:
If the lead was from the current week (Mon-Sun): The refunded amount is credited to the pro's Thumbtack balance, and their available weekly budget is also replenished by that same amount.
If the lead was from a previous week: The refunded amount is credited to the pro's Thumbtack balance, but it does not impact their current weekly budget.

For more details on budget management, reps can refer to the internal Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro) KA. 
2. Lead refund types
This section defines and differentiates between automatic refunds and case-by-case refunds. Knowing the refund types enables Frontline Reps to quickly assess refund eligibility and explain it to pros.
In some circumstances, Thumbtack automatically issues a refund back to a pro's Thumbtack balance (or to their weekly budget if the lead was refunded in the same week as it was charged) without the pro having to request a refund. For all other circumstances, Thumbtack requires a review of the situation before a refund decision can be made. 
Reps can refer to the sections below for a closer look at each refund type. 
Automatic refunds
Automatic refunds are issued by Thumbtack back to a pro's Thumbtack balance without them contacting us or requesting a refund. The automatic credit should process immediately. 
If a pro believes an automatic refund should have been issued but it has not appeared after 2–3 business days, they should submit an in-product refund (IPR) request to be reviewed by the Refund team.
Completely unresponsive customers
Pros with Thumbtack numbers may qualify for an automatic refund if a customer is completely unresponsive — meaning the customer did not reply to any pro on the project within 72 hours of project creation. The refund is issued automatically when all criteria are met; pros do not need to submit a request.
Note: Pros in excluded service categories are not assigned Thumbtack numbers and are not eligible for this refund. Refer to the Thumbtack Numbers (Pro) (Customer) KA for the full list of excluded services.
For full details on eligibility criteria, how tracking works, and how to check eligibility in Admin, reps should refer to the internal Completely unresponsiveness customer refunds (Pro) KA.
NOTE: If a pro manually submits a refund request under "Reason not listed" for an unresponsive customer, the LLM automated process will evaluate it and deny the in-policy refund. Refer to the LLM Automation section for details.

IMPORTANT: Specific timing criteria should NOT be shared with pros.

LLM Automation
Thumbtack uses an LLM-powered (AI) automation system to evaluate and process refund requests for:
Job Outside Preferences (category mismatch or preference mismatch)
Not hired, and unresponsive customers (pros are selecting “Reason not provided” on refund request form). 
NOTE: This system is internal-only and designed to provide faster, more accurate, and more consistent refund decisions.
How it Works:
A pro still submits a refund request for one of these two reasons (just like any other "Case by case" request).
After the request is submitted, the LLM automation system automatically reviews it instead of the Refund Ops team.
This is different from the "Automatic refunds" (like for rapid cancellations) which are processed proactively without a pro needing to submit a request.
▶ What This Means for You (The Rep):
No Process Change: Your day-to-day process for handling refund inquiries does not change.
What You May Notice: When reviewing a pro's refund history in Admin, you may see new decision notes. The system follows a three-step evaluation process:
Handling Disputes for LLM Decisions: The LLM is highly accurate but not perfect; it may make a mistake or miss context (like details from the message thread).
If a pro contacts support to dispute a denied refund that was processed by the LLM, follow the standard Steps: How to help pro disputing a refund request decision (Rep). You will review their dispute, check the messages for new context, and use your judgment to either issue a PBI or uphold the denial, just as you would for a decision made by a human reviewer
CRITICAL: DO NOT MENTION AUTOMATION TO PROS. Do NOT mention the "LLM," "AI," "AutoReferee," or "automation" to pros. This is an internal-only process with no pro-facing changes. If a rep is handling a dispute for an LLM-processed request, handle it exactly as you would any other disputed request.
▶ LLM Evaluation Process & Admin Notes:
The system utilizes the following evaluation workflow to process requests.
Initial Screening & Routing: The system follows a tiered approach to ensure safety and accuracy before proceeding to policy evaluation.
Trust And Safety Triage: Every request is scanned for Terms of Use violations. Critical issues are immediately routed to the specialized Trust and Safety team for priority handling. 
Escalation Check: The system triggers a manual review by human reps if: 
The request includes any attachments (the system cannot “read” or interpret images and files)
The complexity exceeds automated parameters (e.g., specific service mismatches,  not hired or unresponsive customers requiring nuance). 
In-Policy Refund Check: If no immediate escalation is required, the system evaluates the request based on specific eligibility criteria.
Data sources: The determine eligibility, the system reviews the following: 
Customer’s job requests details
In-product conversations between the pro and customer 
Pro’s job preferences (targeting)
Limitations regarding visual media: What the system does not review: 
Refund attachments: Any files attached to a refund request are not reviewed. These are automatically escalated to human reps. 
In-app files: While the system recognizes that a file exists within the job details or chat history, it cannot view the content. In these instances, the system may escalate the case or grant an in-policy refund by giving the “benefit of the doubt” to the pro. 
Evaluation steps: 
Reason filtering: Requests related to “Unresponsive customer” or “Not hired” are automatically eligible for an in-policy refund. 
If the request is related to unresponsive customer or not hired, it will deny the in-policy refund. 
Service mismatch analysis: For service mismatch claims, the system cross-references the customer’s request against the pros profile and our 400+ service categories.
Step 1: Category mismatch: Was the job submitted in the wrong category? 
Step 2: Preference mismatch: If the category is correct, do the job details conflict with the pro’s established job preferences? 
PBI (Courtesy Credit) Check: If the in-policy refund is denied, the system then automatically evaluates for PBI eligibility.
If PBI is approved: A credit is issued. 
▶ Example for Denied Service Mismatch request:
AUTO_PROCESS - Lead matches: walls/basement insulation, rigid foam ('other'), no negative prefs violated.- Granted PBI
AUTO_PROCESS - Lead matches pro's preferences: 1 stump (1-2 ft), haul-away, home - no conflicts.- Granted PBI
▶ Example for Non-hires or unresponsive customer:
AUTO_PROCESS - Refund request reason(s) identified not eligible: NO_HIRE
If PBI is denied: The request is fully denied. 
Admin Notes: When the LLM-powered automation processes a request, it will leave automated notes. The Admin note follows this structure: AUTO-PROCESS -  [ai summary of reason].

Case by case refunds

This section lists the specific scenarios requiring a review before a refund decision can be made. Frontline Reps can use this to understand specific triggers for case by case refunds, and what information is required for review.
Case by case refunds are for all other circumstances where Thumbtack requires a review of the situation before a refund decision can be made. Thumbtack reviews the reason for the pro's dispute and the details (and attachments) they submit with their request. This process usually takes 24-48 hours. If a situation requires future review, a response may take up to 96 hours (4 day).

See the sections below for a closer look at each case-by-case refund type.
▶ Refund policy: Job request conflicts with pro's calendar availability
This section outlines situations where a Job Request might not align with a pro’s Thumbtack calendar, potentially impacting eligibility for a case-by-case refund. 
Thumbtack’s commitment: Pros don't pay for a lead for a specific date that isn't flexible, and the pro has blocked off that date on both their Thumbtack calendar and business hours. Pros can learn more on the How to manage my availability – Thumbtack Help article.
Lead types: Leads, and opportunities
How it happens: If a customer indicates that they are flexible on timing by selecting "I can work with the pro’s schedule if they aren’t available in the time I chose” or doesn't provide a date of service requested (for example., “flexible on timeline” or “I haven’t decided yet”), pros can be matched with these leads with service dates  outside of their specific calendar preferences. 
Refund Policy: 
Thumbtack does grant in-policy refunds when pros' suggestions for alternative dates (that are not blocked off by their calendars) were clearly rejected by the customer. (e.g., the pro suggests meeting on Monday, and the customer doesn’t respond or says no.). 
Thumbtack does not offer refunds to pros who do not offer alternative dates or respond to the customer when leads fall outside their calendar preferences.
Refund Process: If a customer requests a time when the pro is unavailable, the pro should offer alternative dates. If the pro can't find a time that works for both of them, they can refund a request.
Definition of a lead for a specific date that isn't flexible includes: 
A lead for a specific date that isn't flexible [e.g., planned celebrations (weddings) or deadline-specific projects (a move)]
Flexible leads with "open to other dates" feature that turned out not to be flexible on the dates. 
Flexible leads that don't specify an exact date that turned out not to be flexible on the dates.
For info on customer project timeline options and pro availability, reps refer to internal Availability: Business Hours, Calendar, and Hide a Business (Pro) KA to learn more.

▶ Refund policy: Duplicate leads or paid twice
This section provides details about whether a pro may have received duplicate leads or been charged twice for the same job, which might lead to a case-by-case refund consideration. 
Thumbtack’s Commitment: Pros don't pay twice for an identical job from the same customer within 45 days.
Definition of duplicate leads: Identical or similar job requests within the same or similar job category as the original lead created by the same customer (regardless of user PKs) within 45 days.
Lead Types: Leads, Opportunities (includes claimable jobs).
How it happens: Thumbtack’s system automatically screens for and prevents customers from creating identical requests. However, sometimes customers slightly modify the preferences in the new request form or use different Thumbtack accounts to submit the same request. (For example, if there is any difference, like 3 bedrooms to 4 bedrooms, the screening will let it go through.)
Refund Policy: Thumbtack issues a refund for duplicate leads that didn’t get picked up by our screening process. Duplicate leads are not cases where a customer reaches out twice in 45 days about different jobs. Pros should only submit a refund request for duplicate leads submitted within 45 days. 
Any duplicate leads over 45 days from the first requests are not eligible for in-policy refunds and may be PBI eligible.  
Any duplicate leads over 45 days from the first requests are not considered for courtesy credits (PBI) eligibility.
When the same customer creates a new request under a new user profile within 45 days, it is in-policy refund eligible.
If a related party (such as a bride and a groom) contacts the same pro within 45 days, it may be in-policy refund eligible if there is a strong signal that both requests refer to a single job / event (same customer IP address, etc).

▶ Refund policy: Customer provided an invalid phone number

This section covers situations where a customer provided an invalid phone number, which could be a reason for a case-by-case refund review. Frontline Reps can guide pros on how Thumbtack verifies phone numbers and what steps to take if they encounter an invalid number.
Thumbtack’s Commitment: As part of Thumbtacks Quality Commitment, pros will always get the customer’s phone number when they pay for a booking or lead — and Thumbtack limits the competition so they're more likely to be hired.
Lead types: Leads, Opportunities
How it works: Phone numbers will only be shown after the pro pays for the booking or lead. Opportunities will also have phone numbers, but the phone number will only show if the pro replies to a customer's initial message.
Refund Policy: Thumbtack issues refunds for:
Phone numbers identified as invalid or disconnected, based on RealPhoneValidation results.
When the customer name in the request form either does not match what’s in the RealPhoneValidation result or is not available, AND the phone number is not SMS-verified. (Meaning the numbers were verified upstream by the identity-matching process but were not flagged.)
When a refund request is submitted as "Invalid phone number," the system automatically checks the phone number in the background and populates the status in Salesforce. If a refund request is submitted under other refund reasons, the Refund Ops team will change the refund reason in Salesforce to “invalid phone number” to get the customer phone number validated by RealPhoneValidation.
While Thumbtack works to ensure that customer contact information is verified, Thumbtack can’t guarantee that customers will answer when a pro calls them.
Definition of Invalid Phone Numbers: Invalid phone numbers are those that return a disconnected or invalid status according to RealPhoneValidation. These numbers are considered non-working if they are fake, inactive, disconnected, or not currently in use.
Refund Process: When a pro requests a refund by selecting “Invalid phone number” for a lead, the Refund Ops team checks the “Real Validation Phone Info” section of the work ticket in Salesforce to see what RealPhoneValidation returned. The system triggers the phone number check in the background and populates it into Salesforce. Reps can open the work ticket to see if the phone number is valid and connected.

▶ Understanding RealPhoneValidation and Invalid Phone Numbers (INTERNAL INFO ONLY)
This 'Understanding RealPhoneValidation and Invalid Phone Numbers' section is for internal Thumbtack Frontline Service Rep use only. The information contained within these FAQs is strictly for internal knowledge and should not be shared with pros. Frontline Reps should utilize the 'Explaining Refund Process For Leads With Invalid Customer Phone Numbers' talking points when communicating with pros about this topic.

Phone Number Validity Inquiry
Internal Process Explanation (not to be shared externally)
What is RealPhoneValidation?
Thumbtack uses RealPhoneValidation API to check if the phone numbers associated with refund requests for invalid phone numbers are valid and active. 
The tool uses real-time carrier data and proprietary AI analysis to accurately validate phone numbers while complying with TCPA regulations. Using the integrated API, Thumbtack can confirm the authenticity and activity of phone numbers and identify the carrier name and line type.
RealPhoneValidation offers various services, and Thumbaack utilizes their most advanced service, Turbo V3. This service provides data for each phone number, including connection status, carrier name, phone type (landline, mobile, or VoIP), subscriber name (if available), and subscriber type (business or consumer).
What does RealPhoneValidation do?
RealPhoneValidation will check the phone number in question and return the results related to that phone number. Each phone number returns results with the following:
Status (Invalid, Connected, Disconnected, etc.)
Thumbtack will only utilize the “Status” information for refund requests. 
Phone Type (landline, mobile, or VoIP)
Caller Name
Carrier Name
Customer phone verification screens for any invalid or disconnected phone numbers. 
Does RealPhoneValidation confirm that the number belongs to the customer?
No, Thumbtack does not use RealPhoneValidation to verify that the phone number belongs to the customer since Thumbtack’s upstream identity-match customer verification system ensures that the number belongs to the customer. 
However, Thumbtack uses RealPhoneValidation mainly to detect any disconnected or invalid phone numbers that slipped through our upstream customer phone number verification. 
What do pros do if they believe that they received a NON-WORKING phone number?
Currently, Thumbtack does not automatically refund leads with invalid or disconnected phone numbers. 
For a pro to get refunded, they need to reach out and ask for a refund for a lead with a invalid or disconnected phone number. 
Upon request, the Refund Ops team checks the RealPhoneValidation data. The data is found on the refund request work ticket under the Request User Field in Salesforce. 
If Thumbtack confirms that the phone number is indeed an invalid or disconnected phone number,  or a connected number that lacks a reasonably matching subscriber name and SMS verification, Thumbtack will provide in-policy refunds. 
Why does Thumbtack still get invalid or disconnected phone numbers?
Thumbtack’s identity-matching process first checks if the phone number entered in the request form matches with the name of the customer by using Twilio’s identity match service which checks the number against their records.  

If the name does not match with the phone number, Thumbtack will send SMS verifications to the customer to confirm they are who they say they are and they are the one who submitted the request. Reps can refer to the internal Enhanced Lead Quality Commitment KA to learn more. 

However, while it is extremely unlikely, occasionally the scam phone numbers may get through the process. For example, a phone number entered by a potential competitor slipped through Thumbtack’s verification system, but was flagged by RealPhoneValidation as a potentially risky number.
▶ Refund policy: Job details changed significantly
How it works: Job details changes are very significant and affect the pro’s ability to do the job. Example: Customer changes the location, and it's outside of the pros travel area.
Refund Policy: In order for a pro to receive an in-policy refund for ‘job details changed with proof’ scenarios, Thumbtack must be able to see proof that the job details changed, such as a message exchange between the pro and customer. 
Thumbtack recommends pros message the customer through the Thumbtack app to confirm the change. The customer must then reply to confirm the change for refund approval. For example, the pro could message the customer saying something like: 
"As we discussed, it looks like you're actually looking for <xxxx>, which I don’t offer. Could you please confirm so I can update my record?  thanks in advance."
Refund Process: If a customer contacts a pro about a job that’s drastically different from the original lead, pros should request a refund and include what changed in their request. They can also include additional documentation from outside of Thumbtack as attachments to further support their refund request. 
▶ Refund policy: Job is from a minor

This details Thumbtack's policy regarding refunds for leads from minors (under 18). Frontline Reps can readily identify and act upon situations that involve minors.
Refund Policy: Thumbtack refunds pros if they pay for a lead from someone under 18, because it's against our Terms of Use. 
Refund Process:  If a pro gets a lead that doesn’t meet our Terms of Use, they should report the customer to request a refund. For steps, pros can follow the steps on the How to report suspicious activity – Thumbtack Help article.
Reminder: Reps can reference the internal Removed or Banned Users KA  > User guideline removal > User is a minor for more information.
▶ Refund policy: Job is from a third-party (or subcontractor)



This section outlines the rules for refunds when the job request is from a third party rather than the end customer. Frontline Reps can use this section to identify violations of terms around third party requests. 
How it works:  Customers looking to hire a pro as a referral or third-party service is not allowed on Thumbtack. However, subcontracting is permitted under specific conditions. 
The rule is: the customer (the person contacting pros on Thumbtack) is the one paying the pro, is actively involved in the project and should be able to leave a first-hand account of their experience working with the pro.
▶ Understanding key terms
Contracting Work (Direct Customer Relationship): This is the typical scenario on Thumbtack where a customer hires a pro directly for a service. The customer initiates the request, engages with the pro, and pays the pro directly for the work performed. 
Subcontracting Work (Customer Hires a Manager): This is when a customer hires a "manager" (like a property manager, wedding planner, or general contractor) who then hires other pros to fulfill specific parts of the overall project.
Refund Policy: If a job is from a third party, such as a company hiring full-time employees, Thumbtack will refund the charge because it's against Thumbtack's Terms of Use.  
Refund Process: If a pro gets a lead that doesn’t meet Thumbtack’s Terms of Use, they should report the customer to request a refund.
Reminder to reps: If the customer submitted a third party request, support reps should follow the steps under Referral or Third-party services on the internal Removed or Banned Users KA.  
▶ 👍 NOT a Third-Party Job (Permitted)
The table below will help frontline reps quickly understand permitted scenarios and understand how the examples relate to each one. 

Permitted Scenario
Explanation
Example
The customer on Thumbtack is responsible for paying the pro, even if the service is for someone else.  
Subcontractor work where the customer on Thumbtack is paying the pro and actively involved in the project.
A wedding planner (customer) hires a bartender. The wedding planner pays the bartender, not the couple getting married.
A property manager hires a carpet cleaner.
A wedding planner hires a bartender.
A general contractor hires a roofer.
The customer submits a job on behalf of a family member or friend, as a convenience, and not as outsourcing.
When this happens, it's usually because the family member or friend is being helpful and not because they are outsourcing work.
An assistant submits a request for their employer to find a tailor.
A renter submits a request for the property owner to find a handyman for repair work at the rental property.


▶ 🚫 Third-Party Job (NOT Permitted)
The table below will help frontline reps quickly understand and identify these violations.

Not Permitted Scenario
Explanation/Example
A company hiring a pro for full-time employment through Thumbtack
Thumbtack is designed for project-based work and not for facilitating full-time employment arrangements.
A customer on Thumbtack hires a pro on behalf of someone else and is NOT responsible for paying the pro
This is the central identifying factor of a prohibited third-party situation. The person contacting the pro must also be the one responsible for payment.
-  Referral services
-  Monthly subscription services
-  Free referral services
-  Directory services/listings
These business models do not align with Thumbtack's core principle of direct customer-pro engagement. Examples include: 
Find a local wedding officiant in our vendor directory.
A promotion team of four DJs, with different genres of music specialties and talent to cover all your occasions.

▶ Refund policy: Job is questionable
This describes what constitutes a “questionable” job and how it impacts refund eligibility. Frontline Reps can refer to this when assessing whether a pro’s request falls into a “questionable” category.
Pro gets a lead with unusual or suspicious details or activity. Reps can reference the internal Trust & Safety KA > Escalating to T&S  > Reporting suspicious activity for more information. 

Refund Process: If a pro gets a lead that doesn’t meet our Terms of Use, they should report the customer to request a refund. NOTE: Frontline reps can refer to the internal Fake or Scammy Leads (Pro) KA to learn more about this process. 
A job is questionable if one or more of the following occurs:
The customer is looking to get hired by the pro, or competitor testing out the site or checking how other pros are pricing.
The customer submitted multiple, seemingly unrelated jobs within a few minutes or days—particularly if the jobs have different locations (cities/states).
The customer submitted a job from a questionable IP address ou
