articles.fullText:
Knowledge Article Navigation (Rep)

Contents
Overview
Understanding the Knowledge Article (KA) Layout
Staying Up-to-Date with Knowledge Articles
Powerful Searching: Finding What You Need, Fast
Einstein Search: Your Smart Assistant
Global Search Bar: Quick & Precise
Knowledge Widget: Browse and Discover
Search or Browse: Choosing the Right Tool
"No Records Found"? Troubleshooting Tips
Smart Shortcuts for Efficiency
Favoriting Articles: Your Personal Library
Pinning Tabs: Keep Important KAs Handy
Keyboard Shortcuts
Resources
1. Overview
This internal knowledge article is a comprehensive guide for navigating Knowledge Articles (KAs) within Salesforce, Thumbtack’s internal cloud-based CRM software, also known as Salesforce. Salesforce is a frontline reps central hub for managing customer and pro interactions, accessing vital information, and utilizing various resources.
Within Salesforce, frontline reps will find Lightning Knowledge, commonly referred to as knowledge articles (KAs). Think of Lightning Knowledge as Thumbtack's "filing cabinet," containing all the necessary information for both pro and customer-facing teams. KAs provide step-by-step processes, procedures, policies, talking points, and other helpful resources. This empowers you to confidently and accurately assist our pros and customers.
Since KAs are a crucial part of a frontline rep's daily work, understanding how to navigate them effectively is key.
What KAs are (and aren't):
KAs ARE: Step-by-step guides for processes and procedures you can follow while working with a pro or customer. They include topic overviews, processes, talking points, and resources. KAs are ideal for quickly searching for content during interactions.
KAs ARE NOT: A place for videos, audio clips, or interactive training. They are updated frequently, but reps will not be automatically notified of every change..
2. Understanding the Knowledge Article (KA) Layout

Understanding the structure of a Knowledge Article will help frontline reps quickly find the information they need.
Here are the key sections found in each KA:
Article Info: Provides essential details about the specific article you're viewing, including its unique Article Number, Validation Status (valid or not), Version Number, Publication Status (draft, published, or archived), and the Last Published Date.
Information Section: Contains additional article information and, depending on your permissions, a link to the article's URL.
Article Details: This is the main body of the article, containing the core content you are looking for.
Properties: Shows who created the article (Created By) and who last modified it (Last Modified By), along with the Created Date, Last Modified Date, and its modification status. You'll also see the URL Name and if it's Visible in Internal App.
Topics: These are helpful tags (e.g., Resource, experiment, pro, customer) that act as keywords to quickly locate an article. They appear in the Knowledge Widget under the "Articles" field.
Rating: Use this section to provide feedback on an article's helpfulness.
Categories: This section indicates the category and subcategory the article belongs to. This helps you determine if a KA is specific to a certain team:
Go To Market: Used by Sales, Partnership, and Managed Account teams.
Support Ops: Used by Service teams.
Trust and Safety: Used by Trust and Safety teams.
Favorites: You can click the star icon (☆) while in an article to add it to your personal favorites list for quick access. You can have up to 200 favorites.
[Image: AD_4nXdPGzHSW9jXinC68Um3MzTAbRJGethilsRKqKPnA7Hs_MT2cEkTx_iew-5SIJP_upQfy0fhD457_0As4W5j897uocHtn57UXgKYwphuqvvPJpodTTRKEglmiv_uqBqklSWJuO3b]
3. Staying Up-to-Date with Knowledge Articles
Knowledge Articles (KAs) are frequently updated to ensure frontline reps have the most accurate information. It's crucial to always refer to the most current version of an article.
How to Identify and Access the Latest Version:
Outdated Version Alert: When viewing an outdated version of a KA, there will be a prominent orange banner at the top of the article.
This banner says “You are viewing an outdated version of this article. Please review the most recent published version.:
Check Last Published Date: Reps should check the "Last Published Date" in the "Article Info" section at the top of the article to see when it was last modified.
Accessing Newer Versions: Every time a KA is updated, it's assigned a new version number. To get to the most current version:
Click the "Versions" tab within the article.
Select the newest version (this will typically be the article listed at the top) by clicking the number hyperlink under the "Version" column.

[Image: AD_4nXd94hJaViUIv2FmEQhX7dJvmk_2ju1rEvttSy0jE3M4BJJlNpdo-CmHzA3p-t6oVoSvNDJBzZBX780U8HUFfNxZx0fPpZx_rP0gE7EtMbRwyszDmjV1ds1zgLCfStr7dYfogrAY7Q]

Important Notes on Updates:
Frontline reps will not be automatically notified when a KA is updated. 
4. Powerful Searching: Finding What You Need, Fast
 
Knowledge search is available in two main locations within Salesforce: the Global Search box at the top of every page and the Knowledge Widget located at the bottom of  the screen. Using these effectively will help frontline reps quickly find the information they need to help customers and pros.
Einstein Search: Your Smart Assistant
Salesforce utilizes Einstein Search, an AI-powered feature designed to help reps find records much faster. Einstein Search is used in the Global Search bar. 
Intelligent Suggestions: When reps click into the search bar, Einstein will suggest records, reports, dashboards, and list views based on the reps past search history.
Learns Your Habits: Einstein learns the reps specific search habits and adjusts results to better match what they’re looking for.
Prioritizes What You Use: As reps continue to search, Einstein Search will shift results based on the objects they interact with most. For example, if the rep frequently searches for and clicks on Knowledge articles, Einstein will start to display KAs higher in their search results.
Searching Specific Contacts or Accounts: When reps search for a contact or account, Einstein will show them all related information. Reps can hover over a specific object in the results to see other related objects, or click to drill deeper into additional records. Frontline reps can also manually enter any search term, and Einstein will provide closely matching records.
Global Search Bar: Quick & Precise
The Global Search bar is ideal when reps have a good idea of what they're looking for and need results quickly.
How to Use Global Search Effectively:
Filter by Knowledge (Recommended): To narrow down results and avoid too many irrelevant entries, click "All ▼" to the left of the search bar and select "Knowledge" from the dropdown list.
▶ Salesforce screenshot of filter dropdown[Image: AD_4nXfiXCYIDS6KnNAG8VlTmdDeuwM246oiHFKcQY74RE1xPXEdiUOxOkRGWPoS5jD7APtry7gB5BIszqJQNg8qKFhSigVzyIDI_EqrByjywLHTVaPzXhJJfHzRMhkcJE_eEHy4pRCBIQ]
Apply Filters: Click "Filters" to the right of the search bar to access advanced search options. Here you can pre-filter your results by criteria like publishing status, validation status, record type, or data category group. The filters you apply will affect instant suggestions, but not list views.
▶ Salesforce screenshot of filter dropdown[Image: AD_4nXcsbrGuRPJep5p2wZDQCSEn71UbFiYY0j7drErTp92la8DP9fUz9HN6i_HIqhinUYaA3U3v8OwlwrSEKdQMANs_YmLI4FXMZA2A0REKKdQzdLM31O1B4MwRPiDGRTnTBjA3gEd5]
Enter Search Terms: Type the search terms into the search bar at the top center of the Salesforce page.
Be Specific: The more specific the terms, the better the results. For example, instead of a full sentence, enter a feature name or action.
Check Spelling: Ensure the spelling is correct and that the complete term has been entered.
Avoid Wildcards: Do not use partial terms (e.g., "claim" for Claimable jobs).
Limit to Object: Limit the search to a specific object for more precise results.
Review Results: Press Enter to run the search or click “Apply.” Look through the results and click the article title to open it in a new Salesforce tab. Global Search also searches within the articles, so reps don't need to know the exact article title.
Filtering and Sorting Global Search Results: Global search can return many results, but they can be filtered and sorted to quickly find what you’re looking for.
Top Results Page: This page displays the best matches across Salesforce for the objects you use most. It's what reps see when they don't specify an object in their search. Click "View More" in the top right to see additional results for an object.
▶ Salesforce screenshot of Top Results Page with “Top Results” highlighted[Image: AD_4nXew0MNOtkp50AD062vfejcF2BsPlx3mSe9DJ2A0YyuFLOVghbMJOEBYaVTvPzK6897InS2RlTQ-pRZ_l60f7rbKGUasGZZAwbvVF5OvVqf0MgU5oM8uK2R0eV8MKpx52U4x8ib9zQ]
Specific Object Results: To view results for a particular object, click its name in the “Search Results” sidebar to the left of the search results page. If an object isn't listed, select "Show More" to see all searchable objects alphabetically.
▶ Salesforce screenshot of Search Results with the Results Results column highlighted[Image: AD_4nXdzGvl88QrRUMNf96Zg5tMKN031zpBv4g47MRBdZXKawab3n-UlB8ebtLjD12kK4YXKDeh2eC11ksdBI9dOuPgGqqa0R76hUVGGB_ygTYJTRrsrLTd7VXz0Bv9zNFrkRB2l4iI5_w]
Applying Filters: You can filter search results for various objects including Knowledge articles, accounts, cases, contacts, and more.
Click the object's name in the sidebar to see filtering options.
Search results will update as you apply filters.
To remove a filter, click "Restore Defaults".
The available filter fields are determined by your admin's search results layout for that object.
▶ Salesforce screenshot of Search results column highlighted with a filter field dropdown selected[Image: AD_4nXdeZcAsrZNg7-HUt7SVscQguoGgs_dfj_05IkH1DqjHt4RrLpJ7Py7pSYT6SXnqrGSeWE_vE4xnch6VMZbo5vWpyfO_4-U-mrE9pit2ybMI9cmWhA0s9hd0LcncJLfKhvyNuglscA]
How Results are Sorted (Relevance): Salesforce prioritizes article relevance based on factors like term frequency, how often an article is viewed, proximity of keywords, and exact matches. By default, articles are sorted by relevance. In the top right, you can click “Relevance” to sort by relevance, article title, and publication status. 
▶ Salesforce screenshot highlighting the “Sort by” dropdown option
Knowledge Widget: Browse and Discover
The Knowledge Widget is useful when you're unsure where to start your search or want to explore a topic broadly. It's structured like a filing cabinet, allowing you to browse through categories and subcategories.
Understanding the Knowledge Widget Structure:
Knowledge Widget: This is the main "cabinet" that holds all the knowledge folders. You'll find it on the bottom toolbar in Salesforce under "Knowledge".
Categories: These are your main "folders," organized by team:
Go To Market: For Sales, Managed Accounts, and Partnership teams.
Support Ops: For Service teams.
Trust and Safety: For Trust and Safety teams.
Subfolders: Within each category, you'll find subfolders that group knowledge about related topics.
Subsubfolders: Some subfolders may contain further subsubfolders to break down specific topics even more.
Articles: The "Articles" column displays all the KAs located within a specific folder.
Topic Tags: These are keywords or short phrases associated with the KA content, found in the "Articles" column dropdown, helping you quickly locate what you need. You can also use tags for searching by typing # followed by the tag name.
How to Use the Knowledge Widget:
Click "Knowledge" on the bottom toolbar of your Salesforce window to open the widget.
Under "Categories" on the left side, click your applicable team (Go To Market, Support Ops, or Trust and Safety).
Browse through the subcategories and click to open the relevant one.
Look through the list of articles on the right side of the widget, or use the search box on the left to search for an article by its name.
Once you find the article you need, you can click "Preview" to read it directly within the widget, or click the article title to open it as a new Salesforce tab.
Note: The knowledge categories and articles you can access depend on your team permissions.

[Image: WcZHqbzpeB_FJ9Bq8Jgx4hjABLOd-85KDiudbnnFIR4AtmIPLcsvEoI5jRVaROfRD4CRgdb4WVfwKjDTeJZ2Dva2gwaC-NDm3ctrkOFkyqVgimlX2gO0IaaZ_stOnxJsPT0_3VQxDdWsP62pvzgmYYI]

Search or Browse: Choosing the Right Tool
Here’s a quick comparison to help you decide when to use the Global Search bar versus the Knowledge Widget:

Feature
Pros
Cons
Global Search
Easy to search with specific terms.
Gives better results the more specific you are.Allows for advanced filtering to narrow results.
You can't see knowledge collections or related articles directly.
You can't preview the article without clicking into it.
Knowledge Widget
Great for browsing categories and getting familiar with content organization.
Allows you to see multiple similar articles at once.
Can be popped out of the Salesforce window for flexible viewing.
Allows you to preview articles before opening them.
Primarily searches by article title only.
Cannot search using keywords other than the article title.
"No Records Found"? Troubleshooting Tips
If you search in Salesforce and can't find the record or article you're looking for, consider these steps:
Recent Updates: If you recently created or updated the record, wait a few minutes for it to become searchable. If it's still not appearing after 15 minutes, contact your admin.
Permissions: You will only see records that you have access to. If you suspect permission issues are preventing you from seeing a record, submit a help desk ticket to your admin.
Search Terms: Ensure you checked your spelling and entered the complete search term.
Searchable Fields: Note that not all fields on a record are searchable.

5. Smart Shortcuts for Efficiency
Salesforce offers several shortcuts to help you work more efficiently and quickly access the information you need.
Favoriting Articles: Your Personal Library
"Favorites" in Salesforce function similarly to bookmarks in a web browser, allowing you to quickly access important records, lists, groups, and frequently used pages, including KAs. You can have up to 200 favorites.
How to Favorite an Article:
Open the Knowledge Article or any other tab you wish to add to your favorites.
Click the star (☆) icon located near the top of your Salesforce window.
A highlighted star indicates that the current page is already a favorite. Click a highlighted star to remove it from your favorites.
To view your favorites: Click the dropdown (▼) arrow next to the star icon. Each favorite entry will display its name and record type.
Your three most frequently used favorites will appear in the navigation bar's dropdown menu for certain objects. The "My Favorites" list is especially helpful when you have many favorites and want to filter them by a specific object.
To organize your favorites (add items, reorder the list, or rename entries), click "Edit Favorites".
Important Note: You can only favorite specific versions of Knowledge Articles. This means it's essential to regularly check the article's version to ensure you are always viewing the most up-to-date information.
Pinning Tabs: Keep Important KAs Handy
If you have a Knowledge Article or any other tab you want to keep open and easily accessible, you can "pin" it.
How to Pin a Tab:
Open the article or tab you wish to pin.
Click the dropdown (▼) arrow on the tab itself.
Select "Pin Tab" from the menu.
The tab will shrink and remain pinned in your Salesforce window until you unpin it.
To remove a pinned tab, follow the same steps and select "Unpin Tab".
Keyboard Shortcuts
Salesforce also offers a range of keyboard shortcuts to speed up your workflow. Shortcuts help you navigate and work with records faster and without using your mouse. Keyboard shortcuts are enabled by default.
To access a list of shortcuts, click the “?” in the top right of Salesforce and then select “ View Keyboard Shortcuts.” 
Some helpful shortcuts include: 

Shortcut action
Shortcut code
Close all tabs
⇧+w
Close workspace tab
⇧+x
Refresh tab
⇧+r
Search
/
Show this menu
⌘+/
Copy URL for active tab
⌘+c, then s
Copy URL for active workspace tab and subtabs
⌘+c, then w
For shortcuts that specify “then,” release the first key, or key combo, before typing the next key. The comma isn’t part of the shortcut.

articles.fullText:
Job Request Forms (Customer)

Contents
Overview
How customers submit a job request
General request form questions
Job requests from partner platforms
Resources
1. OVERVIEW
▶ KA overview
This internal KA provides Support reps with an overview of how job request forms function on Thumbtack. It explains how customers submit requests and the importance of accurate form completion for both customers and pros, aiding support reps in helping users with the job request process. The KA also covers common request form questions and available resources for further help.
When customers come to Thumbtack to hire a pro, they will submit a project request form. To start, Thumbtack will ask the customer a few questions about their project, and they should add as many details as possible to help pros understand what they need to find the best pro for their project.
However, for eligible request forms, If the customer doesn’t know the answer to a question or doesn’t have a preference, they can select a flexible option (like “I’m not sure” or “I’m flexible”). This allows customers to still submit their request even if they don’t know all the finalized details yet or if they’d like the pro’s advice. Learn more in the internal Flexible Request Form (Pro) (Customer) knowledge article.
The project request form is essential for the following reasons:
It's needed to begin the lead / booking process
How Thumbtack informs pros of the customer's project and what to expect 
A determining factor in job and lead cost
Selecting the Right Service Category
Accurately filling out the request form is crucial. This ensures the accuracy of the project and lead cost and ​​creates a positive experience for both the pro and the customer. Customers should submit their projects under the best fitting service. 
Some jobs exist in multiple categories, (e.g., if a customer needs their lawn mowed, they could select Lawn Mowing and Trimming or Full Service Lawn Care, but not Outdoor Landscaping and Design). Filling out the job request form will help customers know if they have selected the right category. 
Thumbtack offers about 500 different services. If customers don’t see the service they’re looking for, they should try different keywords or browse the comprehensive Thumbtack Services directory page, which allows users to search for or browse a list of services across various categories. If it still doesn’t appear, then Thumbtack likely doesn’t offer that service at this time. 
HOW CUSTOMERS SUBMIT A JOB REQUEST
To start a project and find a pro, customers will follow the steps in the How to find a pro on Thumbtack article. 
Frontline reps can refer to related internal Knowledge Articles: Projects (Customer) and App Experience | Home Profile, Plan, Team (Customer) to learn more. 
GENERAL REQUEST FORM QUESTIONS
​​When customers submit a project request, they will encounter a series of questions. This section outlines the general questions commonly found across most service request forms to help customers provide essential project details.

The questions below are asked on most request forms.
Dates: Customers select a general timeline for their project rather than a specific time of day. They can choose from the following options:
I haven’t decided yet. 
Within 48 hours: Shows pros available in the next 48 hours.
Within a week: Shows pros available in the next seven days.
Further out.
Select specific dates: (Customers can select up to seven dates)
Flexibility toggle: By default, the toggle "I can work with the pro’s schedule if they aren’t available in the time I chose" is turned on. Customers can turn this off if their dates are firm.

▶ What it looks likeScreenshot: Image shows the “When do you need this job to start?” question. [Image: rtaImage]
Photos: Customers are asked if they’d like to add photos with the option to upload images to their project. 
▶ What it looks likeScreenshot: Image shows “Would you like to add photos to describe your project?” with an “+ add photos” button[Image: rtaImage]
Additional details: Customers have the option to add additional details to help pros provide the right recommendations, prices, and service in a freeform box.
▶ What it looks likeScreenshot: images show “What other info should we pass along? “ with a free form box. [Image: rtaImage]
Location: Customers will enter their zip code.On iOS and web, logged-in customers without a saved home address will be asked to add one during the request form. 
▶ What it looks likeScreenshot: images shows “Please confirm where you need the [service occupation]. “ with a box to enter zip code.[Image: rtaImage]
Contact information: Customers will enter their phone number and can check the “Text me updates” box to stay in the loop with text messages from Thumbtack. They will then hit “Submit” to finish the request form, or click “Back” to make any edits to the details they’ve provided. 
▶ What it looks likeScreenshot: Images shows “Let’s get your contact info. “ with a box to add phone number.[Image: rtaImage]
Enter home address
After a customer contacts a pro, the additional pro upsell (APU) page appears at the end of the request flow encouraging them to reach out to additional pros. Logged-in customers without a saved Home Profile address are asked to add a home address during the request form. This step appears after the additional pro upsell (APU) page. If the customer already has an address saved, they won’t see this step. 
▶ What the page looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Customers can skip this step by clicking the 'X' icon in the top right corner of the screen.
After the customer completes the address page and clicks Next, the flow continues, and the final page confirms: "Your project details were sent to X pros!"
Job requests from partner platforms
When customers come to Thumbtack through a third-party platform, the job request experience may look different from the standard flow described in this article. Thumbtack has integrations with demand partners — businesses that surface Thumbtack pros and services on their own platforms — and the way customers submit a request varies depending on how that partner is set up.
There are two patterns reps should be aware of:
Embedded request forms — Some partner platforms (like Nextdoor, Realtor.com, and OfferUp) embed the Thumbtack request form directly on their site. The form appears as a pop-up labeled "Powered by Thumbtack," and the customer fills it out without leaving the partner's platform. The questions and flow mirror the standard Thumbtack request form. Once submitted, the request and any resulting contacts appear in Thumbtack just like any other customer request.
▶ How the embedded request from works:
When a customer on [demand platform] clicks on a Thumbtack pro,  a request form pop-up opens. The pop-up will say ““Powered by Thumbtack” along the top.
They’ll follow the prompts to add their project details, zip code, and email address.
The email address screen will include a “Submitting your email creates a Thumbtack account.” message to tell the user they’re creating a TT account and click “Next.”
After clicking Next the experience will differ if the user is new to Thumbtack. 
Existing users are asked for their password
New users are asked for their first and last name 
After they’ve logged in or created a new account, they’ll provide their phone number, have the option to contact other pros, and submit their project.
Once the project is submitted, new and existing customers will receive a confirmation email. (new customers will still need to create a password)
They can close out the module and continue on the demand platform as usual. 
Partner-specific flows that differ from the standard form —  Some partnerships use a different request model entirely. Lowe's is the primary example, see the table below for details. Thumbtack.
The table below summarizes the known partner flows and how they relate to the standard request form.

Partner
Standard request form?
Key differences
More info
Nextdoor, Realtor.com, OfferUp, and other embedded partners
Yes — embedded as a pop-up, labeled "Powered by Thumbtack"
Customer stays on partner platform; form mirrors standard TT flow; contacts appear like all other Thumbtack contacts
Demand Partnerships (Customer)
ChatGPT
Yes — standard form, may be pre-filled
Customer answers clarifying questions in ChatGPT first; answers carry over to the Thumbtack RFQ; customer must complete sign-up and submit on Thumbtack to hire
ChatGPT + Thumbtack Partnership (Customer)
Lowe’s
No — request is created automatically
Customer purchases installation at Lowe's checkout; Thumbtack creates the account and project automatically; customer schedules via a link sent by email or SMS; no standard request form questions
Lowe’s Installation Jobs (Customer) (Pro)

1. Overview
▶ KA summary
This internal knowledge article provides Frontline Reps with information on the Invoices and Estimates tool for pros on Thumbtack. It details the tool's features, including sending professional estimates and invoices through Thumbtack Messenger, and outlines the process for pros to create, manage, and track these transactions. The article also provides key points and approved talking points for both pros and customers to help navigate conversations.
The Invoices and Estimates tool allows pros to send professional estimates and invoices directly to customers through Thumbtack Messenger. This tool is designed to simplfy the pro's workflow by helping them handle transactions and organize job details in one place.
Estimates allow pros to show customers the ins and outs of what their pricing includes before the work begins. 
Invoices allow pros to request payment for completed work or deposits.
Why it matters:
For Pros: It provides a professional way to outline costs, enables digital payments (via 3rd party like Venmo or Zelle), and helps close leads.
For Customers: It offers a transparent breakdown of costs, easy payment options, and a clear record of the transaction.
Pro benefits: Invoices and estimates
Simplify Workflow. Create and send professional estimates and invoices directly through Thumbtack Messenger, keeping all communication and payment tracking in one place .
Get Paid Faster. Send invoices with clear due dates and automated payment reminders to customers, helping ensure timely payments.
Flexible Payments. Easily link to your preferred payment methods like Venmo, Zelle, or Check directly on the invoice.
Professionalism. Customize documents with line items, taxes, discounts, and your specific terms of service to present a polished image to customers.
Organized History. Access a complete history of all your estimates, invoices, and payment statuses in the dedicated "Invoices and Estimates" section.
Customer benefits: Invoices and estimates 
Transparent Pricing. Receive a clear, itemized breakdown of costs for services, making it easy to understand exactly what you are paying for.
Easy Payment Options. View all accepted payment methods in one place and choose the option that works best for you (e.g., Venmo, Zelle) .
Helpful Reminders. Get automated notifications when a new invoice is sent and reminders when a payment is due, so you never miss a deadline.
Secure Record. Keep a permanent digital record of all estimates and invoices within your Thumbtack message thread for easy reference.
Details on invoices or estimates
When pros create an invoice or estimate within Thumbtack Messenger, the document is prefilled with details. The following information is automatically prefilled and cannot be changed by the pro:
Job category
Creation date
Customer details (name and email address) 
Pro details (name, phone number, and email address)
The invoice or estimate also has customizable fields the pro will fill out and select. Refer to the section below for those fields.  
Customizable fields of an invoice or estimate
When creating an Estimate or an Invoice within the Thumbtack Messenger, pros can customize the following fields:
“Choose type”: Dropdown to select either "Estimate" or "Invoice." (Defaults to “Estimate”)
Due Date (Invoices Only): Specify the payment deadline. (Defaults to one week from the creation date if pro doesn’t add one)
Line Items: 
Item (name of item or service)
Quantity (Defaults to 1)
Price
Discounts: Apply a dollar amount deduction to the total cost.
Tax: Apply sales tax to the invoice or estimate. 
Note: Thumbtack does not provide tax advice; the pro is responsible for determining and applying the correct sales tax.
Message to Customer: Add a personalized note or comment for the customer.
Terms & Conditions: Add details about the pros policies.
Payment Methods Accepted (Invoices Only): Select and provide links to accepted payment methods. Refer to the Payment methods accepted (invoice only) section below. 
NOTE: Anything the pro does not add will not be displayed in the invoice.
▶ What the estimate or invoice form looks like
NOTE: The images below do not fully reflect the experience. Only the customers name and email address are visible (not their phone number).

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

Payment Methods Accepted (Invoices Only)
The invoicing tool allows pros to offer customers flexible payment options, which they select when creating an invoice.
Thumbtack does not process these payments directly. Instead, the tool provides customers with the pro's direct links or necessary instructions for completing the transaction through external third-party apps and platforms.
The table below outlines the external payment methods a pro can choose to display on an invoice, detailing the required input and the corresponding experience for the customer.

Payment Method
Required Input from pro
Customer Action/Experience
Venmo
Venmo handle
A button appears with the text: "Open Venmo"
Zelle
Email address or phone number associated with the Zelle account
A button appears with the text: "Open Zelle"
Paypal
Paypal email or phone number
A button appears with the text: "Open Paypal"
Square
Square payment link
A button appears with the text: "Open Square"
Check
Name or business name to whom the check should be made payable
A button appears with the text: "Next". Clicking this button displays the instruction: "Make your check payable to [Name or business name]"
Once the pro adds their payment method details, they are saved for future use.
Important Notes:
Thumbtack Pay is not an available option on invoices. Customers must complete the payment using one of the third-party payment options provided by the pro (e.g., Venmo, Zelle, Square, Check). Pros can, however, still use Thumbtack Pay to request payment from customers separately from the invoice.
Thumbtack does not process or handle the money for third-party payments. The tool provides the customer with the pro's direct links or instructions (e.g., for Venmo or Check) to complete the transaction outside of the Thumbtack platform.
The payment method fields are not automatically added from the pro’s profile settings.
Managing invoices and estimates
Pros can efficiently manage, organize, and track all their estimates and invoices including payment status and complete history within the dedicated Invoices and Estimates section, which is accessed from the Messages tab.
▶ How to access the Invoices and Estimates section from the Messages tab
The image below displays the Messages tab with the "Invoices & Estimates" button on the Android app. .

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ Pro view of sent invoices & estimates and the actions they can take
When a pro selects a sent invoice or estimate, they have these options: 
Estimate Actions: From an estimate, pros have the ability to "duplicate and edit" or "convert to invoice."
Invoice Actions: From an invoice, pros can choose to "cancel invoice," "duplicate and edit," or "mark as paid."
The first image displays an Estimate and the second image shows a sent invoice.

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

▶ Customer view of invoices & estimates and the actions they can take
When a customer views an estimate, they will see:
A price breakdown by line item
Subtotal, applied discounts, and taxes
The total due
A message from the pro
Any included terms and conditions
An invoice includes all the same details as an estimate, but also adds a payment due date and the option for the customer to "pay" the invoice.
Note: These details vary based on what the pro adds to the invoice or estimate.
IMPORTANT: The images below do not fully reflect the customer experience. Customers will not see a “Download as PDF” button, and only their name and email address are visible (not their phone number).

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

Statues on invoices and estimates

The following table outlines the Thumbtack-specific statuses pros will see in the Invoices and Estimates section to help them track the payment journey of their estimates and invoices. 
▶ What the Invoices and Estimates page looks like with various statuses
The image below that shows the Invoices and Estimates page, listing estimates and invoices across various statuses.

[Image: rtaImage]


Status
Status Definition
Draft
The invoice or estimate has been created but not yet sent to the customer.
Estimate sent
The estimate has been successfully delivered to the customer.
Invoice sent
The invoice has been successfully delivered to the customer. Payment is pending and is not overdue..
Invoice paid
Pro marked invoice as paid 
Invoice canceled
The invoice has been canceled by the pro.
Invoice past due
This status applies automatically if a set payment due date has passed without the customer making a payment (sent on day 3 past due).
Invoice or estimate notifications and reminders
This section outlines when pros and customers receive notifications regarding estimates and invoices to help Frontline Reps manage expectations about communication flows.
Pro Notifications
Pros receive in-app messages and updates regarding their estimates and invoices at these key moments:
Invoice sent: A message confirming the invoice was sent and that automated follow-ups will occur
Invoice paid: A notification when a customer pays
Status Updates: Visual updates in the messenger (e.g., "Invoice sent," "Invoice paid")
Customer Notifications
Customers receive notifications via their Messages tab, email, and/or text/push notifications in the following scenarios:
Estimate or invoice sent: When a pro sends a new estimate or invoice
Invoice payment due: On the invoice's scheduled due date
Invoice payment Overdue: A reminder sent if the invoice remains unpaid past the due date
Invoice paid: A confirmation when the pro marks the invoice as paid. The email links to the updated “Paid” invoice in the messenger thread. 
▶ What the invoice sent email looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ What the invoice overdue email looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Key points
Here are key points for Frontline Reps to remember when helping customers or pros with invoices and estimates. 
Pro
Accessibility: Pros can create and send estimates and invoices through both the Thumbtack app and the web platform.
Availability: These tools are available to all pros across nationwide and all categories (pro must be on the most up-to-date app)?
Payment Method: Thumbtack does not process payments directly. Instead, the invoicing tool provides links or instructions for external payment through third-party apps and platforms (e.g., Venmo, Zelle, Square, Check) that the pro links. Direct payment via a Thumbtack Pay feature is not available for this feature.
Autosave: Any estimate or invoice a pro starts to create will automatically be saved as a draft, allowing them to return to it later.
Preview Option: Before sending an estimate or invoice, pros can use the "preview" function to see exactly what the customer will receive.
Managing Drafts: Pros can delete a draft before it is sent by clicking the three dots in the top right-hand corner of a new estimate or invoice.
Customer Notifications: Customers receive both a push notification and an email when a new or updated estimate or invoice is available.
Sent documents cannot be changed: Once an estimate or invoice has been sent to a customer, that specific version cannot be altered. To make changes, the pro must select "Duplicate and edit" to create a new version, or "Cancel invoice" to void the original.
Conversions: Estimates can be easily converted into invoices.
History Access: Pros can review past estimates given to a specific customer within the Messenger interface.
Managing payments: A dedicated "Invoices and Estimates" section allows professionals to manage, organize, and view their complete history of transactions.
Customer: 
Notification and Access: Customers receive a notification in their Messages tab when a pro sends an invoice and can view the invoice details directly within the Thumbtack Messenger. (Customers must be on the most up-to-date app)
Easy Payment: Customers can complete payment by clicking the invoice notification and following the payment prompts. They will see all the payment methods the pro accepts and can choose the one that works best for them.
Payment Reminders: Thumbtack provides automated payment reminders as the due date approaches or if it passes.
History: Once the pro marks the invoice as paid, customers receive an email notification that links to the updated “Paid” invoice in the messenger thread. To keep a record of the paid invoice, customers can take a screenshot or, on the web, save the webpage. They can also view past invoices at any time within the message thread with the pro.

2. Process
Steps: How to create an estimate or invoice (Pro)
This section outlines the steps for Thumbtack pros to create invoices and estimates on both the Thumbtack app and desktop. 
Pro steps: 
Pros can create an invoice or an estimate from the app or web. They will fill out the customizable fields on the page, including: 
Invoice creation: 
Pros should follow the steps in the Thumbtack Help article,  How to create an invoice on Thumbtack– Thumbtack Help to create an invoice.
Once an invoice is sent, the messenger will display an "Invoice sent" box with a "View details" option and the customer will be notified. 
Clicking "View details" allows the pro to cancel the invoice, duplicate it, or mark it as paid.
Estimate creation: 
Pros should follow the steps in the Thumbtack Help article, How to create an estimate – Thumbtack Help, to create an estimate.
After sending, the messenger shows an “Estimate” box with the option to “View details.” This is when customers are notified. 
Clicking "View details" provides options to duplicate the estimate or convert it to an invoice. 
Pros can click “Preview” before sending to see how the customer will view the invoice or estimate. If a pro begins creating an invoice or estimate but doesn't send it, it is autosaved as a draft. Once finalized, the pro must hit “Send” to share it with the customer.
Steps: How to send customer an updated invoice (Pro)
Once an invoice has been sent to a customer, it cannot be directly edited. To make updates, the pro will need to duplicate the invoice, make the necessary edits and send it back to the customer. 
To update an existing invoice, pros will follow these steps: 
Navigate to the Messages tab.
Find the customer's message thread.
Find the box for the newest sent invoice in the thread.
Click the three dots in the corner of the invoice box.
Select Duplicate and edit.
Make the necessary changes (e.g., adjust line items, add discounts). A new version number will be automatically generated.
Click Send.
Duplicating and editing creates and sends a new version to the customer. The original invoice remains unchanged, but a note will appear on it: “Note: This is not the newest invoice.” For better tracking, the pro can manually update the status of the previous version to "canceled" or "paid."
The customer will receive a notification about the update. However, the pro should also personally inform the customer that a new version has been sent and clearly explain the revisions made.
Note: Pros can also access, duplicate, and edit all their invoices from the Invoices and Estimates page of the Messages tab.
Steps: How to send customer an updated estimate (Pro)
Once an estimate has been sent to a customer, it cannot be directly edited. To make updates, the pro will need to duplicate the estimate, make the necessary edits and send it back to the customer. 
To update an existing estimate, pros will follow these steps: 
Navigate to the Messages tab.
Find the customer's message thread.
Find the box for the newest sent estimate in the thread.
Click the three dots in the corner of the estimate box.
Select Duplicate and edit.
Make the necessary changes (e.g., adjust line items, add discounts). A new version number will be automatically generated.
Click Send.
When a pro duplicates and edits an estimate, it creates and sends a new version to the customer. The original estimate remains unchanged, but a note will appear on it: “Note: This is not the newest estimate.”
The customer will receive a notification about the update. However, the pro should also personally inform the customer that a new version of the estimate has been sent and clearly explain the revisions made.
Note: Pros can also access all their estimates from the Invoices and Estimates page of the Messages tab.
Steps: How to cancel or mark an invoice as paid (Pro)
When a customer pays a pro or when a pro needs to cancel a sent invoice, the pro must manually update the invoice's status. This section details the steps pros can take to efficiently manage their records by canceling a sent invoice or marking it as paid.
To Cancel an Invoice:
If a pro needs to cancel a sent invoice and update its status for both their records and the customer's view, follow these steps:
Navigate to the Messages tab.
Find the customer's message thread.
Find the box for the invoice to cancel.
Click the three dots in the corner of the invoice box (or click “View details”).
Select Cancel invoice. The invoice will be marked as canceled for both the pro and the customer.
The original invoice will say:  “CANCELED” with “Note: This is not the newest invoice.” along the top. The customer won’t see the option to pay.
To Mark an Invoice as Paid:
When the customer pays the pro, the pro must manually select “Mark as paid” on the invoice, which triggers an "invoice paid" confirmation in the messenger and notifies the customer. To mark an invoice as paid, pros will follow these steps: 
Navigate to the Messages tab.
Find the customer's message thread.
Find the box for the invoice to mark as paid).
Click the three dots in the corner of the invoice box (or click “View details”).
Select Mark as paid. This will update the invoice status and send an email confirmation to the customer.
Note: Pros can also mark an invoice as paid from the Invoices and Estimates page within the Messages tab. To do so, select the applicable invoice from this page.
Steps: How to convert an estimate to an invoice (Pro)
Pros can easily convert an sent estimate into an invoice by following these steps: 
Navigate to the Messages tab.
Find the customer's message thread.
Find the box for the newest sent estimate in the thread.
Click the three dots in the corner of the estimate box (or click “View details”).. 
Select Convert to invoice.
Review the filled in invoice template.
Fill in any required invoice-specific fields (like Due Date and Payment Methods), and make any final edits.
Click Send.
Note: Pros can also make an estimate into an invoice from the Invoices and Estimates page, within the Messages tab. To do so, select the applicable estimate from this page.
Steps: How to access all invoices and estimates (Pro)
Pros can manage, organize, and track all their estimates and invoices including payment status and complete history within the dedicated Invoices and Estimates page.
To access this page: 
On the app:
Navigate to the Messages tab.
Tap the three-dot menu in the top-left corner within the Messages tab.
Select "Invoices and Estimates."
On the web:
Navigate to the Messages tab.
Click "Invoices and Estimates" under the Tools menu in the left column.
From here, pros can see all invoices and estimates they’ve drafted, sent, canceled, and so on. When a pro selects a sent invoice or estimate, they have various options: 
From an estimate, pros have the ability to "duplicate and edit" or "convert to invoice."
From an invoice, pros can choose to "cancel invoice," "duplicate and edit," or "mark as paid."
Steps: How to pay an invoice (Customer)
Customers can view and pay invoices from pros directly in the Thumbtack Messenger.
To pay an invoice received from a pro, customers will follow these steps :
Notification: Customers receive a notification in their Messages tab (plus email and text) when an invoice is sent.
The email notification gives the customer the option to select “View patent methods” and “I already paid this.” 
Customers will receive reminders as the due date approaches or if it passes.
View Details: Click “View invoice details” to see the full invoice.
Select Payment: The customer sees a list of all payment methods the pro accepts and selects the one that works best for them. 
Complete Transaction: In most cases (unless using Thumbtack Pay), tThe customer is taken to the third-partyparent site/app (e.g., PayPal, Venmo) to make the payment or instructions for payment by Check.
View paid invoice: After the pro marks an invoice as paid, the customer will receive an email notification that says, "Your invoice was paid. the [business name] marked your invoice as paid. View invoice details." The customer can then view the paid invoice by selecting "View details" within the message thread. 
NOTE: Customers don’t have the option to download a receipt. However, to save a copy, customers can take a screenshot or, when viewing on the web, right-click and "save as" to save the webpage.
Steps: How to view and keep record of an invoice or estimate (Customer)
Customers can view and save estimates and invoices they’ve been sent by a pro by following these methods:
Go to the Messages tab.
Find the message thread with the pro who sent the invoice or estimate.
Locate the invoice or estimate within the message thread.
Select "View details."
Note: Customers can’t download a copy/receipt of an estimate or invoice directly from the Thumbtack app. To keep a personal record on the web or app, customers can take a screenshot. On the web, they can also right-click and select "save as" to save the webpage (webpage complete, single file, or HTML only).
Customers can return to the messenger at any time to view and save a record of any estimates or invoices from the pro.
3. Talking points 
This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros and customers about the invoicing and estimates tool. Use these talking points to make sure messaging is consistent and accurate.
Pro talking points
Tool Overview & Benefits  (Pro)
This section provides frontline reps with talking points to explain the purpose, benefits, availability, and payment flexibility of the invoicing and estimates tool to pros.

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: What is the invoice tool?

A: It’s a feature that allows you to create and send professional invoices directly through Thumbtack Messenger. It helps streamline your workflow and keep track of payments all in one place.
Coming soon
Q: What are the benefits of using the invoicing tool?

A: It helps you organize your transactions, simplifies payment tracking, provides automatic payment reminders for customers, and keeps all communication and payment history within Thumbtack.
Coming soon
Q: How is the invoicing different from how I used to invoice customers?

A: This tool integrates invoicing directly into the Thumbtack platform, offering a more seamless experience to both customers and pros. You can customize templates, track payment status, and send reminders automatically.
Coming soon
Q: Is this available on both the app and the desktop version?

A: Yes, the invoice feature works the same way on both the app and the desktop version.
Coming soon
Q: Can I still use my own invoicing system?

A: We encourage you to use the new tool. However, we know you may have existing workflows. We welcome your feedback on how it fits with your usual practices.
Coming soon
Q: Can customers pay me using Thumbtack Pay or why can't I select Thumbtack Pay as a payment method on invoices?

A: Currently, the tool does not require the use of Thumbtack payments. A: Customer payments are currently handled entirely through the external payment methods you provide (like Venmo, Zelle, or Square). The option for customers to pay using Thumbtack Pay on the invoice is not an available feature. 

However, you can still use Thumbtack Pay to request payment from customers separately from the invoice.
Coming soon
Q: What payment methods can I enter on an invoice?

A: You can provide customers with links or information for external payment methods, including Venmo, Zelle, PayPal, Square, or instructions for payment by Check. 
Coming soon
Creating & Accessing (Pro)
This section provides frontline reps with talking points on how pros can access the tool, the steps for creating new estimates and invoices, and the types of details they can include.

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: How do I access the invoicing tool?

A: When you mark a job as “scheduled” in Messages, a prompt will appear to create an invoice. You can also find all your invoices under the 'Estimates and Invoices' tab on the left side of the Messages page.
Coming soon
Q: How do I create a new estimate? 

A: You can create a new estimate by clicking the 3 dots in the right-hand corner of the Messenger and choosing “create an estimate.” You can also click the floating “Create an estimate” pill in the Messenger
Coming soon
Q: Why is the Invoice triggered by selecting “scheduled” and not “done?”

A: The intent is to help you get payment set up before completing the job, ensuring everything is agreed upon and ready. It also helps customers know what to expect and can help manage expectations.
Coming soon
Q: What information can I include on the invoice?

A: You can include line items, discounts, comments, terms of service, and links to your preferred payment methods.
Coming soon
Manage Estimates (Pro)
This section provides frontline reps with talking points detailing how pros can manage sent estimates, including how to update them by creating a new version and how to convert an estimate into an invoice.

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: How do I update an existing estimate?

A: Once an estimate has been sent to a customer, that version can’t be changed. If you want to send an updated estimate, you will need to create a new version #. 
To create a new version #, click into the most recent estimate and click the 3 dots in the top right-hand corner.  Choose “duplicate and edit.” 
From here a new version # will be auto-generated and you can update the estimate. Once you save it as a new estimate, it will appear in the messenger for the customer to see with the new version #.
[NOTE: Pros can never update an existing estimate without creating a new version #.]
Coming soon
Q: Can I make an estimate into an invoice?

A: Yes. Open the estimate you sent to the customer and select "Convert to invoice." This will pull the estimate details into an invoice template that you can review and send.
Coming soon
Manage Invoices & Payments (Pro)
This section provides frontline reps with talking points on how pros can manage invoices after they've been sent, specifically how to manually or automatically mark them as paid and the process for canceling a sent invoice.

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: How do I mark an invoice as paid?

A: You'll need to open the invoice and manually select "Mark as paid" to update your records.  You can do this in one of two ways: 
From the customer message thread: Click the three dots in the corner of the invoice box (or click “View details”), and select "Mark as paid."
From the Invoices and Estimates section: Navigate to the "Invoices and Estimates" page from the Messages tab, select the applicable invoice, and select "Mark as paid."
This will change the invoice status to "Invoice paid," and trigger an email confirmation to the customer.
Coming soon
Q: What if the customer pays me in cash?

A: You can open the invoice in your message thread and select "Mark as paid" to keep your records up to date.
Coming soon
Q: How do I cancel an invoice?

A: Find the invoice in your "Invoices and Estimates" tab or in the customer message thread, and select "Cancel invoice." This will mark it as void for both you and the customer.
Coming soon
History & Transparency (Pro)
This section provides frontline reps with talking points when speaking with pros about the history, visibility, and transparency of estimates and invoices, including where to find past documents and who can view them.

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: Where can I see the history of my invoices and payments?

A: You can view your invoice and payment history in the 'Invoices and Estimates' section of your Messages page.
Coming soon
Q: Can I go back and view the estimates I’ve given out?

A: Yes, you’ll always be able to go back into the Messenger to view the past estimates you’ve given out
Coming soon
Q: Can customers receive estimates from more than one pro?

A: Yes, customers can receive estimates from more than pro. However, customers can only contact up to five pros from search results in 4 hours, so the number of estimates they can receive will be limited.
Coming soon
Q: Can I see the estimates that other pros are giving customers?

A: No, you’ll only be able to see the estimates that you give out. You’ll never be able to view the estimates that other pros are giving customers.
Coming soon
Support and feedback (Pro)
This section provides frontline reps with talking points to direct pros to the support team for issues or to submit valuable feedback about the new invoicing tool.

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: What if I encounter issues or have feedback about the new invoicing tool?

A: Please contact our support team, and we'll be happy to assist. Your feedback is very valuable to us as we develop this feature.

Q: What if a customer says they can't view the invoice?

A: The most common reason a customer can't view an invoice is that their Thumbtack app is outdated. Please ask your customer to check their app store and ensure they are running the most up-to-date version.

Customer talking points
Invoice Overview (Customer) 
This section provides frontline reps with talking points to explain to customers what the invoice is when they receive it from a pro.

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: What is this invoice I received from a pro through Thumbtack?
Q: 
A: Your pro has used Thumbtack's invoicing feature to send you a detailed invoice for the services provided.
A: 
Q: I can't view the invoice the pro sent me.

A: If you're having trouble viewing an estimate or invoice, please ensure your Thumbtack app is fully updated. The invoicing feature requires the most recent app version to display correctly.

Payment & Receipts (Customer)
This section provides frontline reps with talking points to guide customers through the process of paying an invoice and obtaining a receipt.

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: How do I pay the invoice a pro sent me through Thumbtack?

A: You can view the invoice within your Messages page. Just click on the invoice notification and follow the payment prompts. You'll be shown all the methods of payment the pro accepts and can choose the one that works best for you.

Q: How do I keep record of paid invoices?

A: When the pro marks the invoice as paid, the invoice in your message thread will show as paid, and you will receive an email notification linking you to it. 

[If a customer wants to download a receipt] To keep a record, you can take a screenshot, or if viewing on the web, you can right-click and 'save as' to save the webpage. You can also typically find a receipt in the external payment app or platform you used (e.g., Venmo, Zelle).

History & Reminders (Customer)
This section provides frontline reps with talking points to inform customers about where they can view past invoices and what to expect regarding payment reminders.

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: Can I view past invoices?

A: Yes, you can view past invoices with the pro at any time by selecting "View details" on the invoice in your message thread.

Q: What happens if I don't pay the invoice that the pro send me on Thumbtack on time?

A: Thumbtack will send you payment reminders of the invoice the pro sent you. However, payment terms are ultimately between you and the pro.

Questions about invoice (Customer)
This section provides frontline reps with talking points to instruct customers on the appropriate next steps for asking questions or resolving a dispute about an invoice with a pro.

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: What if I have a question about the invoice a pro sent me on Thumbtack?

A: Please contact the pro directly to discuss any questions regarding the invoice.

4. Resources
Frontline Reps will find a collection of valuable resources in this section, including links to internal knowledge articles, external Help Center articles, and other relevant documentation. These resources may be referenced in the article or provide additional, related information.

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) covers how to use the Lead Incentives Query in BigQuery to investigate free lead and discount incentives for a pro. It is a fallback tool — most incentive questions can be resolved using the Discounts section in User Admin without running a query. Use this KA when you need the specific contact PKs for leads a free lead or discount was applied to, or when Admin doesn't provide enough detail to resolve the pro's question.
The lead incentives query is a BigQuery tool that gives reps a detailed view of a pro's incentive history, including the contact PKs for every lead a free lead or discount was applied to. It is a fallback tool — most free lead and discount questions can be answered using the Discounts section in User Admin without running a query.
Do not use the query as a first step. Always check the Discounts section in Admin on the User page first. For most questions — how many free leads a pro received, how many they've used, and when they expire — Admin is sufficient and faster.
For full guidance on when to use Admin vs. the query, and how to investigate free lead and discount questions, see the Investigating Free Leads and Discounts in Admin (Rep) KA.
Updates
How to use this KA
 
This article covers one specific process: running the Lead Incentives Query in BigQuery to view a pro's incentive history and identify the specific leads a free lead or discount was applied to.
For general troubleshooting, Admin investigation steps, and guidance on when to use the query vs. Admin, see the Investigate Free Leads and Discounts in Admin (Rep) KA.
For talking points and program-specific details, see:
Budget Increase Incentive (BOSUP & SOBU) (Pro) KA
Incentivized Recommendation Cards (Pro) KA
For guidance on running other queries in BigQuery, see the Big Query (Run Support Query) (Rep) KA.
Key points
Support rep should keep these key points in mind when running the lead incentives query:
What the query provides: The lead incentives query shows a pro's full incentive history including the contact PKs for every lead a free lead or discount was applied to, offer dates, acceptance dates, grant dates, expiration dates, offer status, and the number of free leads given. This level of detail is not available in Admin.
All data from the results can be shared with the pro upon request. Support reps should not share screenshots from the query with pros.
Support reps should refer to the KAs dedicated to specific incentives for details and talking points. 
If a rep need help running a query, reps should refer to the internal Big Query (Run Support Query) KA.
2. Process

You need to identify the specific leads a free lead or discount was applied to (contact PKs)

You need to match a specific lead to a specific offer
Always check the Discounts section in User Admin first — most free lead and discount questions can be answered there without running a query. Use this process only when you need contact PKs or details that aren't available in Admin.

Run the query: Click the "RUN" button. (Do not click "SAVE QUERY")

Process

Steps: How to help a pro who disputes using their free leads
Steps: How to troubleshoot why a lead wasn't free
Steps: How to request a complimentary credit on a free lead
Steps: How to report an issue with free leads
Resources
1. Overview
Thumbtack offers free leads and discounts on leads to eligible pros across multiple programs. These incentives are designed to encourage specific pro actions — such as increasing their budget, expanding their targeting preferences, or adding new service categories — that help address supply gaps in the marketplace.
Because free lead and discount content is spread across multiple programs, this article is the single starting point for reps before going deeper into a specific KA. It covers:
How to check incentive status in Admin and troubleshoot common issues
How free leads work — how they're applied, tracked, and confirmed
The types of discounts a pro may receive on leads
Reasons an offer is voided and talking points for each scenario
Refund and complimentary credit policy for free leads
For full program details, pro experience journeys, and complete talking points for specific offers, reps should refer to the dedicated KAs linked throughout this article:
Budget Increase Incentive (BOSUP & SOBU) (Pro) KA
Incentivized Recommendation Cards (Pro) KA
Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro) KA
Welcome Discount for New Pros KA
Investigating Lead Incentives in BigQuery (Pro) KA
Key points

Here are some key things every rep should know before using this article:

Free leads and discounts are system-generated — reps cannot manually issue, reinstate, or extend them
Pros have no designated place to view their free lead balance in-product — reps use the Discounts section in User Admin
Free leads apply to auto-charged leads only, with one exception for BOSUP overserved contacts (covered in Section 4)
Only one discount is applied per lead — the one with the highest value and earliest expiration date
Internal terms like "overserving," "BOSUP," "SOBU," "budget throttling," and "hard budget limit discount" are for internal use only and should never be used with pros.
Admin tools overview 

This section covers how to use Admin tools to investigate free lead and discount offers. There are two primary tools reps will use — they track different phases of the same process and are both needed for a complete picture. 
For free leads, always check both. 
For discounts like the Unlimited Budget Discount, the Discounts section on the User Admin page is sufficient.

Reminder: When looking at timestamps, Admin uses the local device's time zone.
Tool
Where to find it
What it tracks
BOSUP Discount Offers table
Business Admin page
The earning phase — offer history, maintenance period progress, and whether the pro met the requirements to earn free leads. 

BOSUP and SOBU only.
Discounts section
User Admin page
The redemption phase — all active and past discounts and free lead offers, how many leads have been used, balance remaining, expiration date, and discount type. 

Covers all offer types including BOSUP, recommendation offers, Unlimited Budget Discount, and other discounts.
Important: Recommendation offers are separate from BOSUP. They do not appear in the BOSUP Discount Offers table on the Business Admin page. They only appear in the Discounts section on the User Admin page.
Common scenarios: Where to look in Admin
Use this table to quickly identify which Admin tool answers the question at hand.
What you need to know
