 1. Overview

▶ KA summary
This internal Knowledge Article (KA) outlines how Frontline Reps should identify and respond to various types of threats to ensure the safety of both Thumbtack employees and users. It covers:
Types of threats: This section details different kinds of threats, including personal threats, threats to Thumbtack facilities, threats between pros and customers, and threats of self-harm.
Steps for responding: This section provides step-by-step procedures for handling threats received via phone, chat, email, or text, as well as reports from third parties.
Escalation resources: This section explains when and how to escalate urgent safety concerns, including contacting the crisis hotline and internal teams, and lists internal and external support resources.
The KA emphasizes prioritizing safety, active listening, remaining calm, gathering key information, and thorough documentation when dealing with any threat.
A threat is any instance where a user states they will cause physical harm, damage, intimidation, or any other hostile actions towards a Thumbtack office or a Thumbtack employee. This article outlines how Frontline Reps should handle various types of threats to ensure the safety of both Frontline Reps and users.
Threats can be made in person, by phone, email, text, social media, or through other channels.
Note: This KA covers threats to physical safety — harm to a person, property, or a Thumbtack facility. If a pro or customer threatens to leave a negative Thumbtack survey unless they receive a specific outcome, refer to the internal Reps Survey Disputes (Rep) KA instead.
General guidelines for handling threats

Frontline Reps can refer to the following general guidelines when handling any threat interaction. 
Reps must refer to the applicable process below for detailed, scenario-specific steps. 

Prioritize safety first: Thumbtack employee (Frontline Reps) safety and the safety of the customer or pro is most important. If Frontline Reps feel unsafe, they should leave the interaction and seek help.
Active listening: Pay close attention to the description of the threat. Details matter.
Remain calm and empathetic: A calm demeanor can de-escalate the situation and reassure the individual. Acknowledge the pro's or customer's distress.
Gather key information: Swiftly learn the who, what, when, where, and how (if relevant) regarding the threat.
Assess urgency: Determine if immediate intervention is required.
Refer to processes: Know and follow established company processes for threats to safety.
Documentation is crucial. Ensure that all relevant details, including time, date, individuals involved, and actions taken, are documented accurately and thoroughly.
Don't promise what you can't deliver: Be realistic about the scope of help Thumbtack can provide.
Escalate appropriately: If the threat is serious or a rep is unsure how to proceed, escalate to a manager or designated team immediately.
Protect confidentiality: Handle sensitive information with the utmost discretion.
Dos and Don’ts

Frontline Reps should adhere to the following guidelines when handling threats:
Do stay calm: It's vital to remain calm when receiving a threat.
Do prioritize safety: Thumbtack employees, including frontline reps, safety is the most important thing to Thumbtack. Reps do not have to continue interacting with a user if they feel unsafe.
Do document details: Do your best to remember the user's words as much as possible. Write down the threat word-for-word if you can. Note the time of the threat and as many details as you remember, such as the user's gender, voice, temperament, background noises, etc.
Don’t handle alone: No Thumback teams or employees should attempt to handle threats on their own.
Types of threats to report (rep)


This section outlines the types of threats Frontline Reps should report:
Threats of physical harm to an employee(s).
Threats to Thumbtack facilities.
Threats made by one employee to another employee.
Threats of an unwanted visitor arriving at the office.
Threats made towards an employee by a stranger, spouse, partner, friend, or family member of an employee, which create a feeling of danger at the workplace.
Acts of intimidation.
2. Addressing urgent safety concerns (Reps)

This section focuses on immediate and critical threats that require swift action to ensure safety. 
An urgent issue is whenever Thumbtack receives:
A report of immediate danger
An office threat (a physical threat made towards the office)
A threat of physical harm
A threat of self-harm

Steps: How to handle urgent safety concerns (Reps)

To handle interactions with urgent safety concerns, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:
Notify a manager.
Escalate the case to the Critical Escalations team by tagging @escalations in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channel.
3. Threats outside business hours

Steps: How to handle after-hours threats (Reps)


This section explains the process for addressing threats that occur outside of standard business operating hours.
Thumbtack's business hours are 8 am to 5 pm MST mountain standard time. 
To handle threats that occur outside those business hours, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:
If you do not hear back from a Case Manager on Slack within 30 minutes:
Refer to the Internal Emergency Contacts (for Frontline Reps/Managers Only) section and, 
Reach out to the on-call Case Manager using Genesys. (See internal Genesys Phone System (Rep) KA to learn more.)
If you do not have access to Genesys, escalate the issue to your manager, and they will contact Critical Escalations.
As a last resort, if you do not hear back from the on-call Case Manager within 30 minutes, you can contact Rebecca Fitzsimmons (contact in Internal Emergency Contacts (for Frontline Reps/Managers Only section).
Once a Case Manager agrees to take your urgent issue, they will handle the Salesforce case.
4. Supporting displaced users (Reps)

Steps: How to handle users in urgent need of basic living necessities (Reps)
This section outlines how to help users who are in urgent need of basic living necessities due to unforeseen circumstances.
A displaced user is anyone who is in a situation where their home (or other essential living necessities) is no longer available to them. They are currently unable to go home, have no food or water, or they are stranded somewhere.
Frontline reps will follow these steps when handling this types of situation:
Reps should ask the user if they have:
A place they can go to at the moment, or if there is nothing available to them.
Frontline reps should not tell the user they are displaced.
▶ Internal only:
A user is not displaced if they are able to go to a hotel or other accommodation.
Already contacted someone who can help (e.g., the police, a family member) – this is to make sure they’re currently safe.
Reach out to the manager on duty in person or through Slack.
Thank them for contacting us.
Slack Case Managers on #ts-incident-ops-questions using the @escalations tag and ask one of them to Slack you directly due to a sensitive issue. This will notify the appropriate people who can provide further assistance.
When tagging @escalations, make sure you’re available to talk about the situation.
5. Threats to Thumbtack or an employee 
Steps: How to handle threats of a personal nature (Reps)

This section provides guidelines for managing threats directed at Thumbtack employees from sources outside of direct Thumbtack cases.
These threats are made toward a Thumbtack employee by a stranger, another employee, a spouse or partner, a friend, or a family member of an employee, which creates a feeling of danger at the workplace. This category covers threats outside of a direct Thumbtack case. 
To handle threats of a personal nature, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:
If the threat is harmful or imminent, message the Critical Escalations team in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channel using the @escalations tag and ask a Case Manager to Slack you directly due to an urgent Issue.
Wait to hear from a Case Manager for the next steps. 
Steps: How to handle threats to Thumbtack facilities or locations (Frontline Reps)

This section details the process for responding to threats aimed at Thumbtack's physical locations or property.
This includes threats of an unwanted visitor arriving at the office or threats to harm (e.g., a bomb threat or threat to bring a weapon) at a Thumbtack facility.
To handle threats to Thumbtack facilities or locations, Frontline Reps will follow the steps below, depending on whether the threat is happening soon or is currently in progress.
If the threat is harmful or imminent (happening soon):
To handle threats that are harmful, about to happen or likely to happen soon, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:
Message the Critical Escalations team in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channel using the @escalations tag and ask a Case Manager to Slack you directly for an urgent Issue.
Wait to hear from a Case Manager for next steps.
If the User is in immediate danger, encourage them to contact 911.
If the threat is active (in progress):
To handle threats that are actively happening, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:
Message the Critical Escalations team in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channel using the @escalations tag and ask a Case Manager to Slack you directly due to an urgent Issue.
When tagging @escalations, make sure you’re available to talk about the situation.
5. Threats between pro and customer
Steps: How to handle threats between pros and customers (Reps)

This section describes how to address situations where a threat is reported between a Thumbtack pro and a customer.
A customer may report they were threatened by a pro, or a pro might claim a customer threatened them after a job.
To address a report of a threat between a pro and a customer, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:
Encourage them to call their local law enforcement immediately.
If the situation is urgent or life-threatening, encourage the customer or pro to call 911
Escalate the case to the Trust & Safety team for follow-up and review. Refer to the internal Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA for steps.
6. Threats of self-harm (Reps)

This section provides guidelines for Frontline Reps on how to respond when a customer or pro expresses an intent to harm or kill themselves.
Any time a customer or pro says they intend to hurt or kill themselves, regardless of whether or not they seem serious, this is considered a threat of self-harm.

Steps: How to handle threats of self-harm over the phone (Reps)

This section outlines the specific actions Frontline Reps should take when a user communicates a threat of self-harm during a phone call.
The steps a frontline rep will take depend on whether the caller is actively harming themself or threatening to. 
The caller is actively hurting themselves
If the caller is actively hurting themselves while on the phone with you, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:
Unless otherwise requested, stay on the line to help if any questions come up.
▶ Internal note:
While speaking with the caller, do not place them on hold.
After the call, send the user an email with information for the Suicide Prevention National Crisis Hotline – http://suicidepreventionlifeline.org/talk-to-someone-now/ (they have a chat option) or the phone number (800) 273-8255.
Message the Case Managers in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack Channel using the @escalations tag and ask one of them to DM you for an urgent issue.

The caller is threatening to hurt themselves
This sub-section describes the process for Frontline Reps when a caller expresses an intent to harm themselves but is not actively doing so.
To handle a caller threatening to hurt themselves, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:
Keep them on the line and notify your manager.
Frontline Reps are not trained mental health professionals, so be thoughtful and careful not to use triggering language. Often, just listening is enough.
Try to transfer the caller to the National Suicide Crisis Line (1-800-273-8255) as quickly as possible. The crisis line is staffed by specialists trained to deal with these situations and has numerous resources available 24/7.
Limit hold time, as this increases the likelihood they will hang up.
If the caller asks about the crisis line, tell them this resource is not a law enforcement agency and is designed to help anyone in any situation.
If they disconnect or if transferring to the crisis line isn’t available:
 Slack the Case Managers in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channel using the @escalations tag and ask one of them to DM you for an urgent issue.
You should also stay on the line with the crisis line worker to help give them details about the situation.
They will typically try to call the user back.
Slack the  Case Managers in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channel using the @escalations tag and ask one of them to DM you for an urgent issue.
When tagging @escalations, make sure you’re available to talk about the situation.

Steps: How to handle threats of self-harm through chat, email, or text (Reps)

User is actively hurting themselves (chat, email, or text)
This sub-section describes the process for Frontline Reps when a user expresses an intent to harm themselves but is not actively doing so.
If the user is actively hurting themselves while in communication with you, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:
Send them a link to the suicide hotline.
Try to get these details:
Their current location.
The type of danger they’re in.
The people involved.
Reach out to the manager on duty through Slack.
Slack Case Managers on #ts-incident-ops-questions using the @escalations tag and ask one of them to DM you for an urgent issue.
Internal note: Case Managers will use the information you gathered about the situation to locate and contact the proper authorities.

User is threatening to hurt themselves (chat, email, or text)
This sub-section details the immediate steps to take if a caller is actively engaging in self-harm while on the phone with a Frontline Rep.
To handle a user threatening to hurt themselves via chat, email, or text, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:
Tell the customer or pro that there is a resource available to help them and that Thumbtack will not be able to fully help them.
Provide them with the link to the National Crisis Line – http://suicidepreventionlifeline.org/talk-to-someone-now/ (they have a chat option) or the phone number (800) 273-8255.
Talking Point: “I understand you’re going through a difficult time. We care about your well-being and want to make sure your needs are met. To help, I’m going to transfer you to a specialist with the Crisis Line who is specifically trained to help in times like this.”
Reach out to a manager and relay the details you have about the situation.
Slack the Case Managers in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channel. Use the @escalations tag and ask one of them to DM you for an urgent issue.

Steps: How to handle reports of self-harm from a third party (Reps)

If someone contacts Thumbtack to report a person they know is threatening to hurt themselves, that is a third-party report about self-harm. This means the caller on the phone isn’t in danger, but someone they know may be. 
To handle reports of self-harm from a third party, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:
Encourage the caller to report the situation to their local law enforcement for help, as the police are better equipped to handle these situations.
7. Sensitive situations requiring immediate escalation
Steps: How to handle reports of bodily harm, sexual contact, or assault (Frontline Reps)

These are sensitive situations requiring immediate escalation to Thumbtack’s specialized team. To handle reports of bodily harm, sexual contact, or assault, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:
Encourage the caller to report the situation to their local law enforcement for help, as the police are better equipped to handle these situations.
Send a message in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channel and tag @escalations to notify the Critical Escalations team. A Case Manager will take the transfer.
If this is a sensitive situation (e.g., any sexual assault), instead of sharing details in a public channel, ask for a Trust and Safety Case Manager to message you directly
▶ Example:"I have a sensitive issue I need to speak with Critical Escalations about; please DM me."
Do NOT include details in your Slack message. You will work directly with Trust and Safety to share those details.
Reach out to your manager and relay the details you noted, letting them know you transferred a case to Trust and Safety.
If there were no Trust and Safety Case Managers available to take the transfer, gather (and note) the user's:
Name
Phone number
Admin links for the users involved
Let the user know they will be contacted by a Trust and Safety Case Manager as soon as possible.

8. Reports of immediate danger (Reps)

Immediate danger is any instance where a customer or pro tells Thumbtack they are in danger that could result in severe physical injury or loss of life at that moment. It’s a situation where they feel there’s an immediate threat. Thumbtack’s goal is for the caller to contact their local authorities on their own. These calls can be difficult, but Frontline Reps should remember to remain calm and keep these key points in mind:
Direct the caller to reach out to their local authorities (911). 
Do NOT disconnect a call or place a caller on hold, but encourage the caller to disconnect and call 911 for themselves.
Calls should be ended by the caller.
Steps: How to handle reports of immediate danger on the phone  (Reps)


To handle reports of immediate danger over the phone, Frontline Reps will ask the caller if they can contact the authorities for help.
If the caller can contact the authorities:
Encourage them to contact the authorities and wait for them to disconnect the call.
Do NOT disconnect the call yourself.
Once they've disconnected the call, Slack the Critical Escalations team in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channel using the @escalations tag and ask a Case Manager to DM you for an urgent issue.

Steps: How to handle threats of immediate danger over chat, email, and texts (Reps)

To handle threats of immediate danger through chat, email, or text, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:

If the threat occurs during Thumbtack business hours, follow these steps:
Try to get the following details:
The user’s location
Type of danger they’re in
Who’s involved.
Remain in contact with the user.
Advise them to contact their local authorities.
If they haven't done so within 10 min, message the  Critical Escalation team in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channel using the @escalation tag. Let that team know you have an urgent issue.
Reach out to the manager on duty through Slack.
Slack Case Managers in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channel using the @escalations tag and ask one of them to DM you for an urgent issue.
If the threat occurs after Thumbtack business hours, follow these steps:
If the issue occurs outside of business hours (8am – 5pm MST), and you do not hear back from a Case Manager on Slack within 30 minutes, refer to the contact in the Internal Emergency Contacts (for Frontline Reps/Managers Only) section and reach out to the on-call Case Manager using Genesys.
If you do not have access to Genesys, escalate the issue to your manager, and they will contact the Critical Escalations team.
As a last resort, if you do not hear back from the on-call Case Manager within 30 minutes, you can reach out to Rebecca Fitzsimmons using the contact in the Internal Emergency Contacts (for Frontline Reps/Managers Only section.
Once a Case Manager agrees to take your urgent issue, they will handle the Salesforce case.
9. What to do after an interaction involving a threat or immediate danger (Reps)

Once Frontline Reps are finished with the interaction, they will follow these steps:
Add basic, high-level notes to the case about the call.
You only need to note the basics. Trust and Safety use your notes to get a general understanding of the situation.
Notify your manager of the call and transfer the case to them.
Slack the Case Managers in the #ts-incident-ops-questions Slack channel using the @escalations tag and ask one of them to DM you for an urgent issue.
10. Critical escalations threat assessment (Reps)

Managers will review the incident to determine the immediacy, severity, and level of the threat made. All threats will be taken seriously, regardless of tone or intent to follow through. 
If immediate action is required, a Case manager should be notified as soon as possible. After-hours notification is approved in these instances. They will screen the threat and make proper law enforcement notification.
Guidelines for threats that involve immediate attention:
If the threat requires immediate attention, and reaching out to Critical Escalations would put others at increased risk due to the delay, managers should reach out to the appropriate law enforcement agency as soon as possible.
 Frontline reps will follow the steps under Steps: How to handle urgent safety concerns (Reps) above. 

11. Emergency contacts for Thumbtack employees (for Frontline Reps or managers only)


Internal note: The phone numbers mentioned in this article are only for internal use during an emergency and should NOT be shared externally.
Critical Escalation Case Managers’ personal phone number:
Lisa Ronquillo: (801) 664-2467
Ashlee Atkinson: (801) 450-2574
Edgar Herrera Castaneda: (562) 314-5970
Erika Hager: (832) 546-6119
Rebecca Fitzsimmons: (440) 862-0477 (Team manager) 
12. Talking Points
Frontline Reps can use the following talking points to navigate conversations with users about threats.

The caller feels threatened by a pro or a customer


When a user expresses feeling threatened or endangered by a Thumbtack pro or customer and requests help, Frontline Reps should refer to these talking points. This guidance helps prioritize the caller's safety and outlines the appropriate actions to take


English talking point
Spanish talking point
Caller says: “I feel threatened or endangered by a Thumbtack pro or customer. Please call the police.”

Frontline Rep responds: “I understand you feel you are in danger. Can you hang up and call 911 right now?

If the caller says, “No”:

Frontline Rep responds: "I want you to know that I am not an official police dispatcher, but I'm here to support you. For your safety, it's important that you hang up and call 911 directly and immediately. This is the fastest way to get help to you. I won't disconnect with you until you ask me to.Please know that I am not an official police dispatcher, but I will help as best as I can to contact your local authorities. I will not disconnect unless you tell me to." 
Caller says: "Me siento amenazado o en peligro por un profesional o cliente de Thumbtack. Por favor llame a la policía."

Frontline Rep responds: "Entiendo que siente que está en peligro. ¿Puede colgar y llamar al 911 en este momento?"

If the caller says, “No”:

Frontline Rep responds: "Por favor, sepa que no soy un oficial de policía, pero ayudaré lo mejor que pueda a contactar a sus autoridades locales. No me desconectaré a menos que me lo indique."
The caller threatens self-harm

When a caller communicates an intent to harm themselves, Frontline Reps must handle the situation with extreme care. These talking points provide critical protocols to ensure the caller receives immediate and appropriate support for self-harm threats.


English talking points
Spanish talking points
Frontline Rep says: "I want you to know that I am not an official police dispatcher, but I'm here to support you. For your safety, it's important that you hang up and call 911 directly and immediately. This is the fastest way to get help to you. I won't disconnect with you until you ask me to." 
Frontline Rep says: “Quiero que sepa que no soy un operador oficial del 911, pero estoy aquí para apoyarle. Por su seguridad, es muy importante que cuelgue y llame directamente al 911 de inmediato. Esa es la manera más rápida de obtener ayuda. No finalizaré esta llamada hasta que usted me lo indique.”
 13. Resources

This section provides a centralized hub for relevant internal and external links and additional helpful documentation related to handling threats.

External Resources (for Pros and Customers)
National Crisis Line (Online Chat Option): http://suicidepreventionlifeline.org/talk-to-someone-now/
National Suicide Crisis Line (Phone): 1 (800) 273-8255
Local Law Enforcement: Encourage users to call 911 or their local emergency services directly.
The emergency services to which a call is routed depend on the caller's location, which is why frontline reps can’t reach out on behalf of the caller.

Overview
An ideal pro (V3)

1. Overview
An Ideal Pro is a high quality pro on Thumbtack who consistently provides excellent service, leading to high customer satisfaction and repeat business. These pros are key to Thumbtack's success and help ensure customers have positive experiences.
Thumbtack launched a refined definition of the Ideal Pro on August 8, 2024 (v3) to clearly identify, target, and grow this segment. Frontline reps are essential in helping pros meet these standards.
▶ An ideal pro (V3)
To be considered an ‘ideal pro,’ at least one of the pros' services must meet the current measurements that have been set internally.
The parameters of what makes an ideal pro will continue to evolve and be more granular. Currently, we are at v3 of ideal pro definition, and what makes an ideal pro is an accumulative score impacted by the following:
High Quality Pro (score >= 70/100)
Response_rate_1hr >50%
Has_actively_set_bid = True
Num_reviews >= 10
[Internal only] “Responsiveness” review tag volume  > 34%
[Internal only] “Professionalism” review tag volume > 33%
[Internal only] “Work quality” review tag volume > 50%
Has quote sheet
AND
Passed BGC
AND
High Capacity Pro (at least one of the following)
[Internal only] Large (10+ employees) OR managed account
Unlimited budget
Monetizable budget exceeds $83 (75th percentile)
High Quality pro + Passed BGC + High Capacity pro = ideal pro
⚠️ Internal Information Only
'Ideal pro' and 'aggregated score' are internal terms only and must not be shared with pros.
Coaching Language: When speaking with pros, reps should describe the goal as 'recommended ways the pro can stand out to customers, get hired more, and how they can maintain/improve their ranking on search results.'
Do not discuss a pro's 'score' or how scoring/weighting works.
How to identify and coach a pro (Rep)
Frontline reps can identify an Ideal Pro by the black “Ideal Pro” flag on the pro's account in Salesforce (visible in the "Thumbtack User" field from a case view).

[Image: AD_4nXfDurJxmOymgQK9vrqyTdb8z5CLTYyvLJvfvQ8w_LZS-8bRELv1SswBVdbEKHYjkOUj9Mz6WltImsguRKZShNuDj6CGk1OZNCr7DUrUPmS0v3gfkH4Fa3R_BxxISz1uI0gmJVCWBjj5VEBmd-VJ_Jz6TMeY]


If a pro does not have an ideal pro pill, use the table below to guide them on how to meet the qualification criteria: Follow the steps under Steps: Help pro without ‘ideal pro’ flag in tack. 

Pro Issue (Unmet Criteria)
Action to Take (Guidance to Pro)
Pro has less than 5 reviews
Ask for reviews
Pro has a response rate over 1 hour
Respond to customers within a 1-hour time frame
Pro doesn’t have payment info
Add a payment method
Pro doesn’t have lead prices set
Set lead prices in at least 1 category
Pro doesn’t have a quote sheet
Add pro pricing
Pro has 10+ employees and is NOT a national/franchise account
Set an unlimited budget or increase budget
How to use this KA (Rep)
This article is here to help reps make a pro into an ideal pro in the easiest way possible. 
Use the talking points below to blend recommendations into your conversations with pros easily. 
The order of recommendations should depend on where the pro misses the mark.
The talking points and other details in this KA have been pulled from related KAs. For more information or talking points on a recommendation, check out the related KA mentioned below.

When helping a pro without the ‘ideal pro’ flag in Salesforce, reps should follow these steps:
Review the pro's account to identify where they have any unmet requirements.
Recommend ways the pro can stand out to customers. 
To start the convo, ask the pro if they have time for you go over their profile to help them stand out.

Background check

It looks like you haven’t completed a background check yet. We require all pro account holders to take and pass a background check on Thumbtack.They increase customer trust and build credibility, which helps you get hired. That’s because, for customers, finding a pro they can trust is at the top of their list.
Background checks are completely free, and with Checkr, our background check partner, it’s effortless too. All you need is your Social Security number (SSN) or a photo ID, like a passport or driver's license. 
To start a background check, you can:

Talking point for rep to use: 

English talking point: 

One of the best ways to control your spending is by setting your own lead prices, which puts you in control of what you pay. On your 'Lead Prices' page, you set the exact price you are willing to pay for a lead for each service. This gives you full transparency—the price you set is the price you pay—and makes your costs predictable. You can adjust your prices anytime to meet your business goals and still manage your total spending with your weekly budget

Spanish talking point: Una de las mejores formas de controlar sus gastos es establecer sus propios precios de los prospectos, lo que le permite controlar lo que usted paga. En su página de Lead Prices (“Precios de prospectos”), usted establece el precio exacto que está dispuesto a pagar por un prospecto para cada servicio. Esto le da total claridad: el precio que usted establece es el precio que usted paga, y hace que sus costos sean más predecibles. Usted puede ajustar sus precios en cualquier momento para cumplir sus metas de negocio y, a la vez, controlar su gasto total con su presupuesto semanal.

Set unlimited budget
Pro Issue (Unmet Criteria): 
Pro has 10+ employees and is NOT a national/franchise account
Action to recommendation (Guidance to Pro):
Reps can recommend an unlimited budget for pros who have 10 or fewer employees and are not classified as a national or franchise account.
Talking point for rep to use: 

English talking point: We recommend an unlimited budget for pros that are looking to increase lead volume and continuously show up in customer searches. 

Having an unlimited budget is the best way to help you get as many leads as possible. An unlimited budget will also ensure that you are never dropping out of search results due to your weekly budget running out. 

You are still in control of your lead prices and you can always adjust your budget as needed to make sure it makes sense for you and your business goals.
Spanish talking point: Recomendamos un presupuesto ilimitado para los profesionales que buscan aumentar el volumen de prospectos y aparecer de forma continua en las búsquedas de los clientes.Tener un presupuesto ilimitado es la mejor manera de ayudarle a recibir la mayor cantidad posible de prospectos. Un presupuesto ilimitado también asegura que usted nunca deje de aparecer en los resultados de búsqueda porque se le haya agotado su presupuesto semanal.Usted aún controla sus precios de los prospectos y siempre puede ajustar su presupuesto según sea necesario, para asegurarse de que tenga sentido para usted y sus metas de negocio.
Resources:
Pro resource: Here’s a guide to spending on Thumbtack. 
Rep: Internal Weekly Targeting Budget KA
3. Internal FAQs (Rep)
(Internal Use Only: This section contains information for Thumbtack Frontline Reps only. Do not share this information with externally)

What is an ideal pro?
An ideal pro is a cohort of pros that passes the benchmark of criterias defined internally by TT.
What makes them an ideal pro? 
The parameters of what makes an ideal pro will continue to evolve and be more granular. Currently, we are at v3 of ideal pro definition, and what makes an ideal pro is an accumulative score impacted by the following parameters:
High Quality Pro (score >= 70/100)
Response_rate_1hr >50%
Has_actively_set_bid = True
Num_reviews >= 10
[Internal only] “Responsiveness” review tag volume  > 34%
[Internal only] “Professionalism” review tag volume > 33%
[Internal only] “Work quality” review tag volume > 50%
Has quote sheet
AND
Passed BGC
AND
High Capacity Pro (at least one of the following)
[Internal only] Large (10+ employees) OR managed account
Unlimited budget
Monetizable budget exceeds $83 (75th percentile)
So, to summarize: High Quality pro + Passed BGC + High Capacity pro = ideal pro

If we can’t tell pros they’re ideal or not ideal, how is this info useful to us?
This definition serves as a guidance to how to prioritize recommendations/actions to give to pros to ensure success in our platform.  This then also contributes to increasing ‘ideal pro’ volume within TT by guiding them to grow into the ideal pro state.

What is the ‘ideal pro’ badge on the pro's Salesforce account?
It is a Salesforce flag that signals that a pro provides a good customer experience through their adoption of Thumbtack in helping them grow and manage their business. These are pros who have stood out in a number of areas of excellence that Thumbtack can confidently recommend as a good choice for the customer. 
How will the Salesforce flag impact the pro?
There is no impact to pros with the internal flag. However, pros without the internal flag will be a reminder to frontline reps to offer pros recommendations to help them stand out to customers, get hired more, and how they can maintain or improve their ranking on search results.’
How long does the pros account keep the internal flag?
How we measure what makes an ideal pro will continue to change over time as the product evolves, and we gather more data. Adjusting the measurements could result in a loss of ideal pro status, but this won't be communicated to the pro as this is an internal tool for Thumbtack only.
The specific metrics on this KA are for internal guidance only and should not be shared with pros.
Can I tell pros about how we score or how close they are to being considered “ideal pro?”
Don’t talk about pros having a ‘score’ or discuss how things are scored/weighted. 
To preserve the integrity of this system, we're not able to share what precise areas we are measuring to qualify. It’s important to note that being an “ideal pro” is only known internally. The best way pros can give themselves a chance, is to build a strong profile and take great care of their customers.
When offering recommendations, you can speak to this as ‘recommendations to help them stand out to customers, get hired more, and how they can maintain or improve their ranking on search results.’
Will we know what their exact score is to know how close they are to reaching ideal pro?
No. We don't have the integration necessary to share the exact score.  Reps can tell by how many of the recommendations they’ve completed.

1. Overview
▶ KA summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) serves as a guide for Frontline reps on the ID Help process. It outlines the various reasons users (pros and customers) might submit an ID Help form, details the required information and acceptable documentation types for each scenario, and provides key talking points for reps to address common user questions. The article aims to equip reps with the necessary information to efficiently guide users through identity verification and related account issues. 
[end of summary]
The ID Help process is a secure method for users to update or verify critical information on their Thumbtack account. It's crucial for maintaining the integrity and security of our platform. 
The ID Help form is a crucial tool used by both pros and customers to facilitate secure and verified updates to their Thumbtack accounts. Users submit this form primarily for requests that require verification of their identity or specific account details, ensuring the integrity and security of their profiles. 
Users can find the ID Help form from the following link: https://help.thumbtack.com/id-help (Account information and licensing – Thumbtack Help).
Pros and customers will typically submit the ID Help Form for the following reasons:
Email Address Changes: If a pro or customer cannot access the email address currently associated with their Thumbtack account, and needs to update it. This is a crucial step before they can reset their password if they're locked out.
Account Ownership Information: This includes situations like resolving disputes over account ownership, transferring account ownership, or reactivating an account if it was mistakenly flagged as belonging to a minor.
Background Checks (BGC): For submitting initial background checks, especially for SSN-less background checks, if the option isn't available directly within the product. Pros also use it if their name is misspelled on their account, preventing a background check.
Professional Licenses: If a pro needs to verify a professional license, add an authorized license user, or address issues with a license that failed verification. This applies if their name on Thumbtack doesn't match their license, or if they're authorized to work under someone else's license , or if there's a mistake in their license details.
Personal or Business Information Updates: This covers corrections to an account owner's name (e.g., misspelled name, legal name change ) or changes to a business name, particularly for verified businesses.
Important note: For all ID Help requests, users can expect a response within 2 - 3 business days. 
For ID Help questions, Frontline reps can post in the #idhelp-questions Slack channel. Questions will be answered as soon as possible, but answers may not be immediate. Before posting your questions, Frontline reps must review the applicable knowledge article to help answer your question.
Updates
▶ Update: Password Reset
Frontline reps should no longer provide temporary passwords for reset requests. Instead, Thumbtack will always send a password reset email to the email on the pro's Thumbtack account, allowing them to update their password. If a pro cannot access the email associated with their Thumbtack account, the pro must request an email change before resetting their password.
Users are not allowed to create a new account if their original account is on hold/blocklisted, deleted by Thumbtack, or if they are trying to avoid negative reviews.
Pros can change their email address by submitting the ID Help Form, including a photo of their ID. Once the Trust and Safety team updates the email address, pros can reset their password and access their account. Frontline reps should follow the applicable process outlined in the Account Information: Manage Account Settings and Status (Pro) KA and internal Account Info (Customer) KA.
Key Points
Frontline reps should remember the following key points regarding the ID Help process:
Timeline: Users can expect a response for ID Help requests within 2 - 3 business days.
Secure Handling of Personal Information: Reassure users that the ID Help queue has restricted access, and Thumbtack automatically deletes all submitted documentation after 30 days.
30-Day Resubmission Policy: If a user contacts Thumbtack stating they submitted information over 30 days ago, they must resubmit the ID Help form as their previous data is no longer available.
Password Reset Process: Frontline reps should not provide temporary passwords. Thumbtack sends password reset emails directly to the pro's account email. If a pro cannot access their email, they must request an email change first.
Image Submission Quality: When submitting documentation, photos and documents must be clear, capture the entire ID/document, and have no sides cut off. High-quality photos minimize delays.
Slack Channel for Questions: For all ID Help questions, Frontline reps can post in the #idhelp-questions Slack channel. Review applicable KAs before posting.
Dos and Don’ts
This section outlines strict guidelines for Frontline Reps regarding the ID Help process.
Do direct pros and customers to submit the requests using the ID help Form.
Do post ID Help questions in the #idhelp-questions Slack channel.
Do review applicable knowledge articles before posting questions in the Slack channel.
Do not provide temporary passwords for reset requests; Thumbtack will send password reset emails directly to the pro's account email.
Do not encourage users to create new accounts if their original account is on hold/blocklisted, was deleted by Thumbtack, or if they are trying to avoid negative reviews.
2. Accessing and Navigating the ID Help Form
This section guides Frontline reps on how users access the ID Help Form and the initial information they will be asked to provide.
How to access the form 
Users can access the ID Help Form in a few ways. The form is titled "Account information and licensing." In the Thumbtack Help Center, any article that addresses a topic requiring an ID Help Form submission will mention and link to the form directly. 
For direct access, users can find the ID Help form at the following link: https://help.thumbtack.com/id-help (Account information and licensing – Thumbtack Help). Frontline reps should direct users to this specific form when required.
Initial Form Fields
When a pro or customer opens the ID Help Form, they will first encounter a series of general fields that are crucial for initiating their request. These fields gather basic identifying information before diving into the specifics of their issue.
The initial fields users will see are:
Your name: The user's full name.
Email address: The user's email address. It is critical that users enter the email address currently associated with their Thumbtack account, even if they no longer have access to it.
I need to update or verify my: This is a key selection point where users choose the broad category of their request. The options provided on the form are:
Background check (For SSN-Less Background Check)
Account information update (For email and account information/ownership changes)
License (For issues with license verification)
Business name change (For issues updating business information)
Account that was removed because I'm believed to be under 18
Someone is accessing my account that shouldn't be
Once the user selects one of these main categories, the form will then dynamically present additional questions specific to their chosen issue. They will also encounter a free-form text box asking, "Is there anything else we should know?" where they can provide further context.
Acceptable Documentation Types
Depending on the reason the customer or pro is reaching out, the documentation required will vary.
When pros and customers submit documentation, photos and documents must be clear and capture the entire ID or document, with no sides cut off. Thumbtack's validation tool is sensitive, so providing a high-quality photo will improve the pro experience and minimize the need for multiple submission attempts.

3. Reasons to Submit the ID Help Form
This section details the specific scenarios where a pro or customer must submit the ID Help Form. Frontline reps should always ensure preliminary troubleshooting steps, as outlined in relevant knowledge articles, are completed before directing users to this form. Each entry outlines the specific reason, target audience, corresponding form selection, required documentation, key details, and relevant internal resources.
Background Checks

Pros should submit the ID Help Form for background check issues when they need to submit a background check and encounter issues related to their name, or the option to take a background check without a Social Security Number (SSN) is unavailable.
User who submits for this reason: Pro.
Form Option to Select: "Background check (For SSN-Less Background Check).
Documentation Needed: A clear photo of a government-issued ID of the account owner.
Key Details:
Used when the pro does not see the SSN-less option within the product for background checks. In such cases, they can either submit an SSN-less background check through the product or use the ID Help form, which will then direct them to submit the background check through the same link.
After ID verification by the ID Help team, a link will be sent via email for them to complete the background check. Pros must use this specific link to avoid prolonging the background check process.
While the ID Help team's response time is typically 2 - 3 business days, the overall background check process itself usually requires 5 - 7 business days.

Key Details:
The original Thumbtack account owner must first take and pass a background check.
Only after the current account owner passes the background check can the other person set up a new Thumbtack account and submit a transfer request through ID Help, if their situation qualifies.
Users should understand that transferring ownership means they give up the right to make any changes or access the account.
Reasons Thumbtack allows account transfers include the account owner passing away, selling the company, changing the manager of a franchise location, or leaving the company without other business changes.

Pros and customers should submit the ID Help Form for an email address change when they cannot access the email currently on file for their Thumbtack account. This is often a prerequisite for a password reset if they are locked out of their email.

Key Details:
Users must indicate their old and new email addresses in the free-form text box on the form.
If the desired new email address is already associated with a different Thumbtack account, the user should confirm if they want to transfer that email and deactivate the original account.
Once the Trust and Safety (T&S) team updates the email, the user can then proceed with a password reset and access their account.
Frontline reps must not advise users to create a new account to bypass this process, especially if their original account is on hold, blocklisted, or deleted by Thumbtack, or if they are trying to avoid negative reviews.

"The account owner's name was legally changed."
"Account information update (For email and account information/ownership changes)".
The account owner's name is misspelled
The account owner's name was legally changed
Documentation Needed: A clear photo of a government-issued ID of the account owner.
Key Details:
Pros are required to use their legal name on Thumbtack to help build trust and credibility with customers and verify that the pro is a real person.
If a pro's name is misspelled on their account and it is preventing them from taking a background check, submitting the ID Help form is the necessary first step to fix it. After the name is corrected, they can then submit their background check to get it updated.
Note for Customers: Customers can change the name on their account directly. They do not need to submit the ID Help Form or share their ID. Customers can change their name by following the steps in the How to update personal information as a customer – Thumbtack Help article.
Related Internal Knowledge Articles:
Internal Account Information: Manage Account Settings and Status (Pro) KA
Internal Account Info (Customer) KA
Account Information Update: Date of Birth Correction

Pros should submit the ID Help Form for a date of birth correction when they need to update an incorrect date of birth listed on their Thumbtack account.
User who submits for this reason: Pro.
Form Options to Selection:
Select "Account information update (For email and account information / ownership changes)"
Then, select "The account owner's date of birth is incorrect."
"Account information update (For email and account information/ownership changes)".
The account owner's date of birth is incorrect
Documentation Needed: A clear photo of a government-issued ID of the account owner.
Related Internal Knowledge Articles:
Internal Account Information: Manage Account Settings and Status (Pro) KA
Internal Account Info (Customer) KA
Licenses: Authorized user / license wasn't verified 
Pros should submit the ID Help Form for professional license issues when dealing with name discrepancies, authorized users, or problems with license verification.
User who submits for this reason: Pro.
Form Options to Selection:
Select "License” (For issues with license verification)
Then, choose one of the following:
"My license is not verified."
"Someone authorized me to use their license for my business."
“License (For issues with license verification)
My license is not verified
Someone authorized me to use their license for my business
Documentation Needed:
A clear photo of a government-issued ID of the license owner.
A photo of the professional license itself.
Key Details:
The form is used if the pro's name or business name is on Thumbtack does not match what's on their license.
In this case, the pro should indicate the email address of the license owner in the details section of the form.
It is also used if the pro is an authorized user of someone else's license (e.g., an employee authorized to use a business license).
If so, the pro should fill out the form with the license holder's name, phone number, email address, and an explanation for the request.
Used if there's a mistake in their license details (e.g., it's not supposed to be expired) or other license problems not relating to reinstating an expired license.
Used if the license verification failed because our team was unable to find a public database or website to verify the information, or if the name on the license did not match the Thumbtack account.
If a pro's license or authorized license user was rejected but is valid, they should reply to the email they received and send a copy of the license to the ID Help team for further assistance. They should not resubmit the ID Help form in this specific scenario.
Related Internal Knowledge Articles:
Internal License Credentials (Pro) KA
Business Name Change

Pros should submit the ID Help Form for a business name change when they need to update the business name associated with their Thumbtack account, particularly if it is a verified business.
User who submits for this reason: Pro.
Form Option to Selection: "Business name change (For issues updating business information)".
Documentation Needed:
A clear photo of a government-issued ID of the account owner.
Proof of business ownership (e.g., Articles of Incorporation, a doing business as (DBA) filing, business registration information, or any other documentation showing business ownership).
Key Details:
If the pro has a verified business and/or a verified license on the account, these credentials (profile badges) will be removed upon approval of the name change.
After the name change is processed, the pro will need to resubmit their license and business verification with the new business name to regain these credentials.
The expected response time for this process is 2 - 3 business days.
The ID Help team will verify the submitted documents before allowing the business name change.
Related Internal Knowledge Articles:
Internal Account Information: Manage Account Settings and Status (Pro) KA
Account that was removed because I'm believed to be under 18

Pros and customers should submit the ID Help Form for age verification when their account was removed because they were believed to be underage, and they wish to prove they are 18 years or older to reactivate their account.
User who submits for this reason: Pro, Customer.
Form Option to Selection: "Account that was removed because I'm believed to be under 18".
Documentation Needed: A clear photo of a government-issued ID of the account owner.
Key Details:
This process is specifically for reactivating accounts mistakenly flagged as belonging to minors (under 18).
Related Internal Knowledge Articles:
Internal Removed or Banned Users (Pro) (Customer) KA
Someone is accessing my account that shouldn't be

Pros and customers should submit the ID Help Form to dispute account access when they believe someone is accessing their account without authorization or there is a dispute over who legitimately owns the account.
User who submits for this reason: Pro, Customer.
Form Option to Selection: "Someone is accessing my account that shouldn't be.
Documentation Needed: A clear photo of a government-issued ID of the account owner.
Key Details:
Thumbtack prioritizes account security and verifies the identity of the legitimate account owner in such cases.
3. Talking points
General ID Help Questions
Frontline reps will use these talking points when addressing general questions about ID Help from customers or pros.

English Talking Points
Spanish Talking Points
“I’m concerned about the security of my info.”
“Me preocupa la seguridad de mi información.”
We care about your security. Rest assured, the queue has restricted access, and Thumbtack automatically deletes all documentation after 30 days.
Su seguridad es importante para nosotros. Puede estar tranquilo, el acceso a la cola es restringido y Thumbtack elimina automáticamente toda la documentación después de 30 días.
“I submitted my info over a month ago, and I haven’t heard back. What are the next steps?”
“Envié mi información hace más de un mes y no he recibido respuesta. ¿Cuáles son los siguientes pasos?”
For security reasons, Thumbtack only keeps documents for 30 days, and then they are automatically deleted. You will need to resubmit the ID Help form.
Por motivos de seguridad, Thumbtack solo conserva los documentos durante 30 días y luego se eliminan automáticamente. Necesitará volver a enviar el formulario “ID Help form” de Ayuda con la Identificación.
Background Check and Account Transfer Questions
Frontline Reps will use these talking points to guide conversations related specifically to background checks and account transfers. Reps can refer to the internal Account Information: Manage Account Settings and Status (Pro) KA for more on account transfers.

English Talking Points
Spanish Talking Points
Can I have a business partner take the background check instead of me?
¿Puede mi socio comercial realizar la verificación de antecedentes en mi lugar? 
No, only you can take the background check on your account.
No, solo usted puede realizar la verificación de antecedentes de su cuenta.
Can I transfer the ownership of my account to my business partner, so they can take the Background check?
¿Puedo transferir la propiedad de mi cuenta a mi socio comercial para que él pueda realizar la verificación de antecedentes? 
No. Your business partner can create their own account, but you will still need to submit a background check. If the situation qualifies, and both parties have taken and passed the background check, both parties may be eligible for the account transfer process.
No. Su socio comercial puede crear su propia cuenta, pero usted aún deberá pasar por una verificación de antecedentes. Si la situación lo amerita, y ambas partes han realizado y aprobado la verificación de antecedentes, ambos podrían ser elegibles para el proceso de transferencia de cuenta.

Background Checks without Social Security Numbers (SNN)
Frontline Reps will use this section’s talking points when handling questions about background checks for those without Social Security Numbers (SSN). Reps can refer to the internal Background Check (Pro) KA for more talking points and details. 

English Talking Points
Spanish Talking Points
I don’t have a Social Security Number (SSN), can I still submit for a Background check (BGC)? 
No tengo un Número de Seguro Social (SSN), ¿aún así puedo solicitar una verificación de antecedentes (BGC)? 
Yes, you can submit for a social security number (SSN)-less background check (BGC) through the Thumbtack app or by using the ID Help form to submit your ID.

After verifying the pro's ID, we will email you a link to start the background check. Make sure you use that link to avoid any further delays. The background check process should take 5 - 7 business days after using the link.
Sí, puede solicitar una verificación de antecedentes (BGC) sin número de seguro social (SSN) a través de la aplicación de Thumbtack o usando el formulario “ID Help form”.
Después de verificar la identificación del profesional, le enviaremos un enlace por correo electrónico para iniciar la verificación de antecedentes. Asegúrese de usar ese enlace para evitar más demoras. El proceso de BGC debería tomar de 5 a 7 días después de usar el enlace.
What do I need to start my SSN-less BGC through the ID help form?
¿Qué necesito para iniciar mi BGC sin SSN a través del formulario de ayuda con la identificación? 
To submit, you’ll need your government-issued ID. When submitting the photo ID, it must be clear and capture the entire ID, with no sides cut off. Our validation tool is sensitive, so providing a high-quality photo will help the process go smoothly, with no need for multiple attempts.
Para enviarla, necesitará su identificación emitida por el gobierno. Al enviar la foto de la identificación, esta debe ser clara y capturar la identificación completa, sin que se corten los lados. Nuestra herramienta de validación es sensible, por lo que proporcionar una foto de alta calidad ayudará a que el proceso se realice sin problemas y sin necesidad de múltiples intentos.
General License questions 
Frontline Reps will use these talking points when addressing general questions about licenses and their verification process. Reps can refer to the internal Licenses (Pro) KA for more talking points and details. 

English Talking Points
Spanish Talking Points
I’m trying to get this license verified, but it belongs to my business partner and doesn’t match the name on my account.
Estoy intentando verificar esta licencia, pero pertenece a mi socio comercial y no coincide con el nombre de mi cuenta. 
To continue, you will need to submit the license to the ID Help form request. Make sure to include the email address of the license owner in the details section of the form. 
Para continuar, deberá enviar la licencia al formulario de “ID Help form” Ayuda con la Identificación. Asegúrese de incluir la dirección de correo electrónico del propietario de la licencia en la sección de detalles del formulario.
Why was my license rejected?
¿Por qué se rechazó mi licencia?
You should have received an email about your license. To continue, please reply to that email and send a copy of the license you are trying to verify.
Debería haber recibido un correo electrónico sobre su licencia. Para continuar, por favor responda a ese correo electrónico y envíe una copia de la licencia que está intentando verificar.
Questions about updating the name on a pro account
Frontline Reps will use the following talking points when a user has questions about updating the name associated with their account. Reps can refer to the Account Information: Manage Account Settings and Status (Pro) for more talking points and details about name changes on a pro account.

English Talking Points
Spanish Talking Points
My name is misspelled on my account, and it’s stopping me from taking a background check (BGC). What can I do to fix it?"
Mi nombre está mal escrito en mi cuenta y eso me impide realizar una verificación de antecedentes (BGC). ¿Qué puedo hacer para corregirlo? 
Use the ID Help form to submit your ID for verification. Once the error has been fixed, you’ll be able to submit your Background check..
Use el formulario de Ayuda “ID Help form” con la Identificación para enviar su ID para verificación. Una vez que se haya corregido el error, podrá solicitar su verificación de antecedentes.

articles.fullText:
How Thumbtack Works (Pro)

Contents
Overview
Benefits of Thumbtack for new pros 
Types of leads
Actions to complete to show up in search results 
<Thumbtack Quality Commitment basics 
Pricing and lead cost basics 
Purchasing a credit pack for new pros
Key points
Sign up and get started
Pro guidance: Sign up as a new pro
Steps: How to help a new pro find success on Thumbtack (Rep)
Steps: How to help a pro's chance of getting contacted (tips for pros)
Talking points
Resources
1. Overview
Note on targeting terminology: You may see "Targeting" and "Job preferences" terms used interchangeably throughout our internal KA resources or in-product.
This internal knowledge article (KA) explains how Thumbtack works for pros, and what a new pro needs to do to sign up, get set up, and start getting leads.

How Thumbtack works
Thumbtack introduces pros to customers looking for the pros services. 

When a pro signs up, they create a profile page where customers go to learn about their business, see photos of their work, and read reviews. When a customer needs a job done, they come to Thumbtack and search. Customers see search results in real time, with pro profiles, reviews, ratings, and more.

Customers choose the pros they like and reach out. This contact is called a lead — it's the pro's moment to respond and win the job. If the job matches the pro's job preferences (how the pro tells Thumbtack what jobs they're interested in), the pro pays for the lead. The pro gets the lead in the "Jobs" section of their For You tab.

Reps can share the How Thumbtack works and Your guide to your first two weeks on Thumbtack help article with new pros. 

NOTE: Thumbtack helps customers find pros for their projects, but pros don't work for Thumbtack. Pros contract directly with their customers.
Benefits of Thumbtack for new pros (pro)
Frontline reps can share the following benefits of Thumbtack with new pros:
Customers are moving online. Setting up a business profile on Thumbtack is easy to do and we’ll introduce you to interested customers in your area who are online and ready to move forward.
We're a great partner. We helped pros like you complete over one billion dollars in business last year. We want to make it easier for you to find new customers and easier for customers to find you. And we’re here to help you where you need it along the way. 
​You only pay for interested customers. They can see your profile in the app and they're expressing interest. Think of it like a billboard. You don’t pay for every customer who passes by and sees your business on the billboard.  Just the ones who are interested enough to contact you.  
Targeting the right customers. We’ll show you more often to customers because you’ve told us you always want these jobs, so we know you’ll give the customer a good experience. When you get a lead that exactly matches your targeting preferences, those exact matches will be covered by The Quality Commitment.
Shareable resource: Here’s a guide to why you should choose Thumbtack and Here’s a guide to your job preferences
Types of leads (pro)
Frontline Reps can use these details to explain what a lead is, and the types of leads on Thumbtack.
A lead is a new customer who has seen what a pro offers (most commonly in search results) and wants to learn more about working with them.
Thumbtack offers different types of leads and bookings: 
Leads are customers who saw a pro in their search results and decided to reach out to the pro directly. Pros get leads by setting targeting preferences and telling us the types of jobs they want. The pro will get the lead in the "For you" section of their Jobs tab. See internal Leads (Pro) KA
Opportunities are a pro's chance to get in front of customers who haven’t hired someone yet. These are customers who have reached out to a few Thumbtack pros and they’re asking for quotes. Pros can express interest in any open opportunity listed in the "Opportunities" section of their Leads tab. If the customer responds, the pro is charged for the lead. See internal Opportunities (pro) KA.
With preset jobs, pros never pay for leads. Pros choose the types of jobs they want and fit their schedule, complete the work, and get paid.
Shareable resource: What are leads, preset jobs, and opportunities? – Thumbtack Help
Actions to complete to show up in search results

Before a pro can appear in customer search results and start getting leads, they must complete three requirements. This is known internally as enforcing minimum requirements (EMR), effective for pros who signed up on or after March 19, 2020.
Set up job preferences for at least one service — this tells Thumbtack which jobs the pro wants to be matched with.
Get at least one review — without a review, a pro won't be surfaced in search results; more reviews help a pro rank higher.
Complete profile basics — name and address that match the pro's ID (used for verification), plus a profile picture.
Complete  a background check.
Once a pro meets all of these, they can start getting contacted. 
For more detail, see internal Onboarding and activation requirements (EMR) (Pro) KA, internal Search Results Ranking Factors and Pro Visibility (Pro) KA and Background Checks (Pro) KA.
Thumbtack Quality Commitment basics (Pro)
Every lead and booking a pro gets on Thumbtack comes with the Thumbtack Quality Commitment:
Phone number guarantee - Pros will always get the customer’s contact info when they pay for a lead and booking.
Limited competition - We limit the number of pros that customers can contact from search results within the first few hours of starting their project. 
See What is Thumbtack's Quality Commitment? – Thumbtack Help and internal Thumbtack's Quality Commitment (Pro) KA.
Pricing and lead cost basics (pro)
Pros pay for leads — new customers who reach out to learn more about working with them. If a job is an exact match to a pro's job preferences and the customer contacts them, the pro is charged automatically.
Lead prices vary because a job's value changes based on things like project size, pro availability, and market. Pros set the amount they're willing to pay per lead (their lead prices). 
See internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA and internal Targeting: Job Types and Travel Preferences (Pro) KA. 
Sharable resources: How much do I pay for leads and opportunities? – Thumbtack Help, Here's a guide to spending on Thumbtack – Thumbtack Help 
Purchasing a credit pack for new pros (pro)
New pros can purchase a credit pack (prepaid package) to pay for their first leads.. After the credit pack is used up, leads will be charged to the default credit card on the pros account. 
NOTE: Prepaid Packages are only sold by the Sales team and are not available for purchase in product. See  internal Sales and Prepaid Packages (Pro) KA. 
Key points
Frontline reps should keep these tips and items in mind when they're helping new pros:
Use the pro dashboard in Salesforce to get an overview of how the pro is doing on Thumbtack
Share relevant Thumbtack help articles with pros. https://help.thumbtack.com/ 
If they signed up after March 19, 2020, they must set up targeting for one of their services and get at least one review before they can appear in search results.
Pros must complete activation requirements before they can appear in search results, 

Do’s and don’ts
Don’t write any profile information for the pro. 
Do check EMR status before troubleshooting why a pro isn't getting leads.
2. Signing up and getting started
Pro guidance: Sign up as a new pro (pro) 
To create a Thumbtack account, a pro will follow these steps, also covered in How to sign up as a pro – Thumbtack Help:
During onboarding, pros have the option to claim available pieces of information about their business, including importing reviews from other sites. This allows pros to enter their business name and zip code to be almost instantly matched with a profile Thumbtack scrubbed from credible sites that pros advertise their business on. To learn more, see internal Prebuilt Profiles and Importing Reviews From Other Sites (Pro) KA
During onboarding, pros will be asked to:
Add business name and write business introduction. 
Add their basic personal information, including birthdate and address. 
Upload a profile picture
Get at least one review.
Set up job preferences for at least one service.
For an in-depth look at the onboarding flow and activation requirements, see the Understanding and Completing Activation Requirements (Pro) KA. 
Steps: How to help a new pro find success on Thumbtack (Rep)
Frontline Reps can use this process to research a pro's situation and steer the conversation before offering guidance.
Research the pro's account. Use thepro dashboard in Salesforce (accessed from the pro's Salesforce contact) or the pro's Performance dashboard to see how they're doing on Thumbtack.
▶ What to find the pro snapshot

[Image: rtaImage]

Image description: A screenshot of the pro's contact in Salesforce, with the tab titled "Pro Snapshot" circled.
Ask questions to understand the pro's situation:
What's the pro's experience so far on Thumbtack?
Why is the pro reaching out?
Are they new and trying to understand the experience, or have they been on Thumbtack a while without quite figuring it out?
Assess what the pro understands, in three areas:
How Thumbtack works overall — what do they know, or want to know?
Features and options available to them — do they understand targeting preferences and how to use them?
The value of partnering with Thumbtack — what are they hoping to gain, and do they understand how to get it?
Check EMR status. To see if a pro has completed all activation requirements, you can check the pros EMR status in Admin. For steps, see Understanding and Completing Activation Requirements (Pro)  KA .
Steer the conversation using the talking points  below, and emphasize that a good customer experience matters to the pro's own success — satisfied customers keep coming back to Thumbtack to meet other pros.
Steps: How to help a pro's change of getting contacted (tips for pros)
Frontline reps can share the following tips to help increase the pro's chances of getting contacted. Pros should:
Make sure their profile represents their business well. The best way to do this is by building a high-quality profile with great reviews. Shareable resources: Here's a guide to your Thumbtack profile. and What is a profile? – Thumbtack Help. See internal Profile (Pro) KA. 
Set job preferences. That way they can focus on the right jobs and appear in the right searches. Shareable resource: Here's a guide to your targeting preferences - Thumbtack Help. See internal Targeting: Job Types and Travel Preferences (Pro)  KA. 
Respond quickly to show they're interested. Customers are more likely to engage with pros who respond right away. Shareable resource Here's a guide to getting hired with your messages - Thumbtack Help. See internal Messaging customers: Response rate, tools, and best practices (Pro) KA.

3. Talking points

Frontline Reps can use the following externally approved talking points when navigating conversations with new pros.
After I sign up, can I start meeting customers immediately?
Before you start meeting customers, you need to tell us which jobs you’re interested in. You’ll do that by setting job preferences. You’ll also need to add a few things to your profile (like a profile photo and a review). Once your targeting preferences and profile are set up, you can start meeting customers. 
I want to become a pro on Thumbtack, but I already have an account. How do I sign up?
If you already have a Thumbtack account, log in and follow the steps above to start meeting customers. When you’re asked to verify your email address during setup, enter the email address linked to your current account. If you don’t remember your password, or need to set one, click here.
I'm part of a larger business or franchise. Whose name and informations should be on the account?
To help keep your account secure, the owner of the business or franchise should sign up and be listed on the account.

Do pros work for Thumbtack?
No. We help customers find pros for their projects, but pros don’t work for Thumbtack. Instead, pros on Thumbtack set their own prices for their services and contract directly with their customers.

What do I pay for?
You pay for leads. When an interested customer first reaches out to you, that’s a lead. The customer can send you a message, request a call or estimate, or ask for your availability.
¿Por qué pago?
Usted paga por prospectos. Cuando un cliente interesado se comunica con usted por primera vez, es un prospecto. El cliente puede enviarle un mensaje, solicitar una llamada o presupuesto, o preguntar por su disponibilidad.

How can I get a review from a customer if I’m a new pro?
The review doesn’t need to be a Thumbtack customer. You can email any past customers or associates that can speak to your skills. You can add up to 10 of these reviews from your past customers.
Customers are more likely to hire pros with reviews, so getting at least one is the first step in showing customers you do great work.
¿Cómo puedo obtener una evaluación de un cliente si soy un nuevo profesional?
No es necesario que la evaluación sea de un cliente de Thumbtack. Puede enviar un correo electrónico a cualquier cliente o asociado anterior que pueda hablar sobre sus habilidades. Puede agregar hasta 10 de estas evaluaciones de sus clientes anteriores.
Es más probable que los clientes contraten a profesionales con evaluaciones, por lo que obtener al menos una es el primer paso para mostrarles que hace un buen trabajo.

Why am I required to turn on targeting?
When you set targeting preferences, we know when to show you in search results so you get in front of the right customers. As a new pro, targeting preferences are a huge part of Thumbtack and we believe they’ll help you meet the customers you’re looking for.  
¿Por qué debo activar el enfoque?
Cuando establece las preferencias de enfoque, sabemos cuándo mostrar su negocio en los resultados de búsqueda para que pueda estar frente a los clientes adecuados. Como nuevo profesional, las preferencias de enfoque son una gran parte de Thumbtack y creemos que lo ayudarán a encontrar los clientes que está buscando.

What if I turn targeting off later?
You can do that. We just ask that you give it a try while you get started on Thumbtack. You have the ability to update your preferences at any time so if you’re not getting the right jobs, it’s an easy fix.
¿Qué pasa si desactivo el enfoque más tarde?
Usted puede hacer eso. Solo le pedimos que lo pruebe mientras comienza con Thumbtack. Tiene la capacidad de actualizar sus preferencias en cualquier momento, por lo que si no obtiene los trabajos correctos, lo puede solucionar fácilmente.

I never sent my estimate, so how did this customer contact me?
Customers come to Thumbtack looking for a pro, and pros that fit the customer’s needs show up in search results. This customer saw you in their search results and reached out to learn more about you. Make sure to quickly decline or respond to these customers.
Nunca envié mi presupuesto, entonces, ¿cómo se comunicó conmigo este cliente?
Los clientes acuden a Thumbtack en busca de un profesional, y los profesionales que se adaptan a las necesidades del cliente aparecen en los resultados de búsqueda. Este cliente lo vio en sus resultados de búsqueda y se comunicó para obtener más información sobre usted. Asegúrese de rechazar o responder rápidamente a estos clientes.
4. RESOURCES

This section provides Frontline Reps with a list of relevant external articles and direct links for pros, and internal knowledge articles that reps can use to effectively help new pros learn about Thumbtack.
