1. Overview
NOTE: Customers no longer see pro pricing. For full details, refer to the Pro Pricing KA. For talking points for customers, refer to the Customer asks about pricing for their project section below.
Thumbtack helps customers find exactly what they're looking for. Customers are able to get things done without guesswork. Thumbtack matches customers with local pros who fit their project. 
Search – Customers browse a list of pro’s profiles, and use filters to find pros who match their project.
Chat – Customers can contact the pros they’d like to discuss their project details with.
Hire – Customers can check pros availability and book pros right in the Thumbtack app.
Key points
Here are key points for Frontline Reps to remember when helping customers with how Thumbtack works:
Customer Search Process: Customers can find pros by typing their needs and zip code, then filtering results.
Connecting with Pros: Customers can chat with pros and respond to messages from various pros.
Pro Account as a Customer: Existing pros can easily switch to a customer account within the app to find services.
Post-Contact Search Results: After contacting a pro, customers see a prioritized list of pros, including those they contacted, those who showed confirmed interest, and other potential fits.
Managing Interactions: All customer-pro messages are in the inbox, and customers can revisit search results from their Projects page if they don't hear back.
Finding and hiring a Pro
This section details the core process a customer follows to find, contact, and hire a professional on Thumbtack.
Search for a Pro 
The customer journey begins when they submit a project request form. Thumbtack's AI-powered search makes it easy for customers to find the right pros by simply describing their project or problem in their own words. 
To start, a customer searches for their project. Thumbtack's AI-powered search makes it easy for customers to find the right pros by simply describing their project or problem in their own words. They can enter a service category (e.g., "House Cleaning") or describe their project in their own words in the search bar (e.g., "need help with my leaky sink"). Thumbtack will then match the customer with relevant pros and display a list of them on the search results page.
List of pros in search results 
Pros let us know which types of jobs they want by setting up their account preferences. If a customer's project details match a pro's preferences, that pro will appear in their search results.
If a customer has answered at least one question on the request form, they will see a curated pros section at the top of the search results, highlighting the top three pros for the job. The order that pros appear in search results is based on several factors, including how well their services match the project details, their review rating, how quickly they respond to customers, and how engaging their profile is.
Viewing a pro's profile
From the search results, a customer can see a preview of each pro's profile. By clicking on a pro card from the pro list, they can browse the full profile. Customers see the pro's profile photo, business name, star rating, and other details the pro may have added about their business (like pricing or number of employees).  
In some categories, customers may see a “Licensed” pill on a pro’s profile when their license is verified. Refer to the internal Home Care and Routine Maintenance Resources (Customer)  for details licensing and permits.
The customer can contact the pro by clicking “Request estimate” at the top of their profile, and “Message” or "Request a call."
Contacting Pros
There are different ways for a customer to contact and hire a pro on Thumbtack. 
Contacting a pro: Customers can choose which pro they want to contact directly from their profile page. After they reach out, the customer and pro decide on the final cost, date, and time. 
On-Demand Booking: For some services, Thumbtack can match a customer with a pro at a set price for a scheduled date and time. These are called On-Demand Bookings and require customers to pay upfront through Thumbtack.
NOTE: Customers can only contact up to five pros within the first four hours of their search. This ensures the customer finds the right pro without being overwhelmed. If it doesn't work out with the first set of pros, the customer can contact more pros after the four-hour period. 
Submitting their project
When a customer is ready to contact a pro, they will finish the request form about their project by following this flow: 
Answer project questions: The customer will first be asked to provide more details about the job. It is crucial for them to add as much detail as possible to help pros understand their needs.
Select Availability: Customers select a time frame to indicate their availability, and see when a pro is available. Customers can also uncheck “Allow pro to suggest other dates” if their dates are not flexible.
Provide Contact Information: The final step is to provide contact information. Thumbtack will only give a customer's phone number to pros they choose to contact.
Submit Project: Once the form is complete, the project is submitted to the selected pro(s).

Managing Projects


The Plan Tab
The Plan tab on the Thumbtack app helps customers stay on top of all their projects. This is where they can prioritize tasks, set reminders, and manage all of their projects. Thumbtack’s comparison tools will help them decide whether to do it themselves or to hire a pro.
The Inbox Tab
Customers can respond to new messages from pros and reply back to them by going to their Inbox. This is the primary channel for new project communications. 
The Team Tab
After contacting a pro, we’ll add them to your Team tab. This is your trusted group of pros you can rely on. Message or re-book your favorite pros, or refer them to your friends and neighbors.
2. Process
This "Process" section guides Frontline Reps through the steps for helping both new customers and existing pros utilize Thumbtack as a customer to find and connect with pros, including how search results are organized after initial contact.
Steps: How to help a new customer find a pro on Thumbtack
For customers looking to start a project, they can follow the steps in the How to find a pro on Thumbtack — Thumbtack Help article. 
To help customers find the right pro, Thumbtack asks them a few questions about their project. Here are some tips for customers to keep in mind when they’re finding a pro on Thumbtack:
 
Adding as many details as possible helps pros better understand the project.
All new messages from pros will appear in their Inbox.
Once a project is submitted, the initial details can't be changed, so substantial changes may require starting a new project.
Other pros from search results may reach out to the customer about their project too. This way, the customer has plenty of options. The customer can respond to these other pros if they’d like. 
Steps: How a Thumbtack pro becomes a Thumbtack customer (Pro) 
When a pro needs to hire a pro for their own projects, they can easily use their existing pro account.
App: To hire other pros from the Thumbtack app, pros will need to download the Thumbtack app designed for customers (blue logo). The app with the black logo is for pros. They can log in using the same email and password as their pro account. Pros can check out the How to download the Thumbtack app Thumbtack Help article. 
Reps can refer to the internal Thumbtack App (Customer) KA for steps on how to download the app and the internal Customer App Features: Home Profile, Plan Tab and Team Tab (Customer) KA to learn more about the customer app. 
Desktop: To help an existing pro use Thumbtack as a customer for the first time, Frontline reps will help pros with the following steps:
Have the pro log in to their pro account. 
Follow the steps found in the How to find a pro on Thumbtack — Thumbtack Help article.
If the pro is logged into their pro account, a customer account will automatically be added. 
Pros can switch back and forth between their pro and customer accounts by selecting their photo in the upper right-hand corner and clicking Switch to customer or Switch to business. (See what it looks like below.)
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

3. Talking points
This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with customers about how Thumbtack works. Use these talking points to ensure consistent and accurate messaging.
What Thumbtack is
Support reps can use these talking points to explain Thumbtack's core function, detailing how it connects customers with pros for various projects.
English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Q: What is Thumbtack?
¿Qué es Thumbtack?
A: Thumbtack matches you with local pros. You tell us what’s next on your to-do list and we show you a list of nearby pros who fit the job. With the Thumbtack app, you can compare pro profiles and prices, chat with the pros you like, and (last but not least) check availability and hire pros who fit your projects.
Thumbtack le empareja con profesionales locales. Díganos qué sigue en su lista de tareas pendientes y le mostramos una lista de profesionales cercanos que se adaptan al trabajo. Con la aplicación Thumbtack, puede comparar perfiles profesionales y precios, hablar con los profesionales que le gustan y (por último, pero no menos importante) verificar la disponibilidad y contratar profesionales que se adapten a sus proyectos.

Customer asks about pricing for their project
Support reps can use these talking points when customers ask about pricing or have questions about budget and cost estimates.

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Q: Why can't I see a pro's pricing?

A: Every project is different — a pro's price can depend on details like scope, timing, and location. Rather than show a general estimate upfront, we encourage you to reach out and describe your project. That way, the pro can give you pricing that actually reflects what you need, not just a starting point that might not apply to your situation.

Q: How do I know if a pro is within my budget?

A: When you submit a request, we'll ask you about your project — and for some services, your budget too. Those details are shared with the pro so they can learn about your project needs.

Once you're in touch, you can share more about your project and discuss pricing, so the pro can give you pricing that reflects your specific needs. Every project can vary based on its scope, timing, location, and other details, so talking to a pro directly is the best way to get accurate pricing.

As you review pro profiles, you can see if they've shared any pricing details there and check reviews to see if other customers mentioned pricing in their experience. You can also check out our cost guides to see average prices for a service.

Q: How do I compare pros if I can't see their prices?

A: You can still compare pros using their profile details — reviews, photos, experience, and any pricing information they've chosen to share. If you'd like pricing from a few pros at once to compare, you can use the "get pricing from 3 pros" option where available, which sends your project details to a few matched pros so you can hear back from more than one.

Q: What if a pro's price ends up higher than I expected?

A: A pro's price reflects the specific details of your project, so it may be different from any average or estimate you've seen. If a quote feels higher than expected, you can ask the pro what's included and whether there's flexibility — or reach out to a few pros to compare before deciding who to hire.

Q: Am I obligated to hire a pro once they give me a price?

A: No. Getting a price from a pro doesn't commit you to hiring them. You and the pro only agree to move forward once you both settle on the final cost, date, and time — until then, you're free to keep exploring your options.

Q: I used to see prices when browsing pros — why did that change?

A: Thumbtack updated how pricing appears while you're browsing pros. Since every project can vary based on scope, timing, location, and your specific needs, we now encourage you to connect with a pro directly — that way they can give you pricing that reflects your actual project rather than a general estimate.

Q: What happens if I contact a pro and they're outside my budget?

A: You're not obligated to move forward. If a pro's pricing doesn't fit your budget, you can let them know, ask if there's flexibility, or reach out to other pros instead. You can also check out our cost guides beforehand to get a sense of typical pricing for your type of project..


How to find and contact pros 
Support reps can use these talking points to guide customers through the straightforward process for discovering and engaging with pros on the Thumbtack platform.

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
Q: How do I contact a pro?
¿Cómo me comunico con un profesional?
A: It’s easy to contact pros on Thumbtack. From your list of results, view the pro’s profile. You’ll see a few different options to contact them. Once you reach out, we’ll let the pro know you’re waiting to hear back from them and notify you when they reply.
Es fácil ponerse en contacto con profesionales en Thumbtack. De su lista de resultados, vea el perfil del profesional. Verá algunas opciones diferentes para comunicarse con ellos. Una vez que se comunique con el profesional, le informaremos al profesional que está esperando recibir noticias de él y le notificaremos cuando le responda.
Q: How do I find pros?
Q: ¿Cómo encuentro profesionales?
A: Once you tell us what service you need (house cleaning, handyman, etc.) and where you need it, you get a list of pros instantly. The list is real-time, so your results change as you use filters or update your zip code. If a certain pro catches your eye, go to their profile to contact them and discuss the details.
A: Una vez que nos diga qué servicio necesita (limpieza de la casa, personal de mantenimiento, etc.) y dónde lo necesita, obtendrá una lista de profesionales al instante. La lista es en tiempo real, por lo que sus resultados cambian a medida que usa filtros o actualiza su código postal. Si un profesional le llama la atención, vaya a su perfil para contactarlo y discutir los detalles.

Support reps will find a collection of resources in this section, including links to internal knowledge articles, and other relevant resources. Reps can share any external Help Center articles with customers  to help them as needed with how Thumbtack works. These resources may be referenced in the article or provide additional, related information.

Home Care and Routine Maintenance Resources (Customer)

Contents
Overview
Empowering homeowners with Thumbtack Home Care Resources
Navigating Insurance, Permits, and Licensing for Home Projects
Seasonal home maintenance checklists for year-round care
Resources
1. OVERVIEW
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article provides Thumbtack's customer-facing teams with an understanding of home care and routine maintenance resources. It covers how Thumbtack helps customers manage their home's upkeep, navigate essential aspects like insurance and permits for home projects, and utilize seasonal maintenance checklists for year-round care.
In Thumbtack's initiative to deepen our relationship with homeowners, we want our internal teams to have a better understanding of home care and routine maintenance. This article provides helpful resources that support reps can share with customers. 
Empowering homeowners with Thumbtack Home Care Resources
At Thumbtack, we're dedicated to helping customers build a deeper relationship with their home. This section provides valuable insights and resources to help them confidently manage their home's upkeep and maintenance.
Thumbtack App Features for Home Care
Thumbtack offers several in-app tools to help customers easily care for their home and manage projects:
Personalized Home Profile & Plan: Customers can create a unique home profile and receive a personalized plan for their home's upkeep through the Thumbtack app. This includes:
Custom Guides: The home page features guides with recommended projects based on the customer's home and the current season (e.g., lowering energy bills, baby-proofing).
"Your Plan" Tab: Helps customers track planned projects, prioritize tasks, set reminders, and decide between DIY and hiring a pro.
"Your Team" Feature: Customers can build a trusted team of pros they've previously contacted, making it easy to message, rebook, or refer them.
Customers can check out the How to get a personalized plan for your home – Thumbtack Help article to learn more.
Frontline reps can refer to the internal Customer App Features: Home Profile, Plan Tab and Team Tab (Customer) KA  for more details. 
Additional Thumbtack Home Care Resources
Beyond the app, customers have access to other Thumbtack resources for comprehensive home care:
Home Resource Center: Customers can utilize Thumbtack’s Home Resource Center | Thumbtack page, a central online hub offering project inspiration, how-to guides, repair steps, and cost guides.
Home Maintenance Services Page: Customers have Thumbtack’s Home Maintenance - Hire the perfect pro at a price right for you - Thumbtack page, which highlights Thumbtack's offerings for various home maintenance needs, including monthly, seasonal, yearly check-ups, and emergency services.
Home Repair Estimates Tool: Customers can use Thumbtack’s Thumbtack Home Repair Estimates (Repair Pricing tool) page to easily identify home repairs they should prioritize and get estimates for each repair by uploading their home inspection repair. (Frontline reps can refer to the internal Thumbtack Home Repair Estimate Tool (Customer) KA for more details)
Navigating Insurance, Permits, and Licensing for Home Projects 
When a customer is undertaking significant home projects, hiring a pro with the right credentials offers peace of mind. This section guides frontline reps in understanding and explaining the importance of insurance, permits, and licensing to ensure customers have a smooth and secure project experience.
Understanding Key Project Requirements
Insurance:
Recommendation: It's highly recommended that customers hire a pro with insurance for major projects to provide peace of mind.
Action for Customer: Before hiring, customers should ask the pro about their insurance coverage.
Resource for Customer: Refer customers to the How to verify a pro’s insurance – Thumbtack Help article.
Licensing and Permits:
Varies by Location and Project: A pro's license requirements and whether permits are needed depend on the laws of the customer's city and state, and the specific type of project.
Customer Verification: Customers should always confirm with the pro that they possess the proper licensure and credentials for the job.
Resource for Customer (Smart Hiring Guide): The Your Safety page (Smart Hiring guide) helps customers determine what occupational licensing to look for. It includes links to state occupational licensing board websites for verification.
Specific Questions: For specific licensing questions, customers should contact their state or local government directly.
Reps can refer to the internal License Credentials (Pro) KA for an overview of licensing on Thumbtack, including how verification works and what customers can check before hiring.
Permit Requirements Note (Internal for Reps):
Common Requirement: Most localities will require a permit for certain home projects (e.g., new construction, remodels, or additions).
Internal Resource: Frontline reps can refer to the internal ONLY  Permit Requirements sheet for more details.
Seasonal home maintenance checklist for year-round care 
A home's needs change with the seasons. This section provides practical, season-specific checklists to help customers stay on top of routine maintenance, ensuring their home is well-cared for all year long.
Customers can easily manage their home's upkeep with Thumbtack by creating a home profile. 
Thumbtack then generates a personalized plan for their home. The custom guides on the home page offer recommended projects tailored to the customer's home and the current season. These guides assist customers with various home care tasks, from lowering energy bills to baby-proofing and more.
For additional information, representatives can consult the  Customer App Features: Home Profile, Plan Tab and Team Tab (Customer)  KA. Once a customer sets up their Home Profile, their Home page is populated with personalized guides to help them with home maintenance.

[Image: rtaImage]

Here are a few areas inside and outside a home that customers should pay special attention to as the seasons change:
[Image: rtaImage]Spring: Focus on decluttering and organizing closets, garage, entryway, bedroom and home office.  Spring Home Maintenance Checklist | Thumbtack.com 
[Image: rtaImage]Summer: Pressure wash home exterior (garage door, patio, deck, driveway, etc.), clean your pool weekly and maintain your outdoor living spaces. Summer Home Maintenance Checklist | Thumbtack.com 
[Image: rtaImage]Fall: Clean out gutters, crawl space, fireplace and chimney.  2025 Fall Home Maintenance Checklist | Thumbtack.com
[Image: rtaImage]Winter: Steam clean carpets, clean shower heads, and schedule a deep clean before and after the holidays.  2025 Winter Home Maintenance Checklist | Thumbtack.com

Google Calendar Sync Removal (Pro)

Contents
Overview
How the Google Calendar sync worked (prior to being removed)
Impact on pros who had their Google Calendar synced (Pro)
Steps: How to help pros navigate the removal of the Google Calendar sync (Rep)
Talking points
Pro asks why Google Calendar is missing
Pro asks if Google Calendar integration will return
Pro asks why there was no notice before removal
Resources
1. OVERVIEW
▶ Google Calendar Sync Deprecation – Quick Facts
Removed: Aug 18, 2025
Why: Bug + low usage (~2% of pros)
Impact: Feature removed from app; no comms sent; existing blocked times remain 
Future plans: No plans to bring it back in current form
On August 18, 2025, the Google Calendar sync feature will be deprecated. This decision was made due to a bug in the system, low adoption rates (~2% of pros), and low usability. The feature will be completely removed from the pro app. Here’s what to expect: 
Any mention of Google Calendar integrations will be removed from the pro app.
The entire feature will be removed.
No communication or in-product notifications will be sent to pros regarding this change.
How the Google Calendar Sync Worked (prior to being removed)
The Google Calendar sync was a one-way sync that imported events from a pro's Google Calendar to their Thumbtack calendar for visibility only. The synced events didn't block off time on the Thumbtack calendar, so pros had to manually block out time to manage their availability. If a pro added or deleted a time from their Google Calendar, it would be reflected on their Thumbtack calendar. However, changes made on the Thumbtack calendar would not sync back to the Google Calendar.
Once synced, the calendar would automatically update every hour. If an error occurred during a later sync, Thumbtack would display a message to the pro prompting them to re-sync their calendar. Pros didn't need to use the same email for their Thumbtack account and their Google account. 
Impact on pros who had their Google Calendar synced (Pro)
Pros who have already synced their calendars will no longer see mentions of the feature on the platform. Any previous impacts the sync had on a pro's calendar, such as blocked calendar times, will remain.
Synced Google Calendar events did not block off time on the Thumbtack calendar; they were for visibility only. Therefore, there's no need to "remove" a Google Calendar event from Thumbtack. However, if a pro had manually blocked off time on their Thumbtack calendar due to a Google Calendar entry, those blocked times will remain after the sync feature is removed. 
Steps: How to help pros navigate the removal of the Google calendar sync (Rep)
Frontline reps can support pros who used the Google Calendar integration or pros with questions about the removal by doing the following things: 
Explain to pros that, "we no longer support this feature. We apologize for any inconvenience". 
Use the Talking points below to help navigate these conversations. 
3. TALKING POINTS
The following section provides frontline reps with talking points to use when navigating common questions a pro may have about Thumbtack removing the Google Calendar integration. 
Pro asks why Google Calendar is missing
This section provides reps with a talking point for when a pro contacts us asking why the Google Calendar integration has disappeared from their account. Use this when the pro says they previously had their calendar synced and now the option is gone. The talking point covers the deprecation date, the reason for removal, and what happens to any events that were already synced.

English talking points
Spanish talking points 
I had my Google Calendar synced and now it's gone and I don't see any option to resync it. What's going on?

I know it’s frustrating when a feature you’ve been using is no longer there. As of August 18, 2025, we removed the direct Google Calendar sync. The change was made because of a bug with the integration and very low usage — only about 2% of pros had it connected.

Any events already synced to your Thumbtack calendar (like blocked time) will stay in place, but you won’t be able to resync Google Calendar directly.

Pro asks if Google Calendar integration will return
This section provides reps with the talking point for when a pro wants to know if Thumbtack will bring back the Google Calendar integration in the future. It clearly states the current plan of not bringing it back. 

English talking points
Spanish talking points 
Does Thumbtack plan on bringing back the Google Calendar integration in the future?

We don’t have plans to bring it back in its current form. 

Pro asks why there was no notice before removal
This section provides reps with the talking point for addressing concerns about the lack of advance notice regarding Google Calendar’s removal. 

English talking points
Spanish talking points 
Why wasn’t I told the Google calendar sync option was going away, and how do I keep my Thumbtack calendar updated now?

I understand that’s frustrating. Because only about 2% of pros were actively using the feature, we didn’t send a broad announcement before removing it.

articles.fullText:
Go Live with “Activate Profile” (Pro)

Contents

Overview
Pro experience
Process
Steps: How to help a pro in "Go live" experiment (Rep
Resources
1. Overview
As of February 2026, pros’ profiles will automatically activate after 24 hours of passing EMR, but they have the option to Activate profile sooner by clicking the “Activate profile” button. Only pros who did not pass EMR will need to 'activate profile'. Pros who pass EMR during the onboarding flow are automatically activated, but with a more detailed screen of what they should expect.
NOTE: This article will be archived in the near future. The baseline article: Understanding and Completing Activation Requirements (Pro) KA is being updated to reflect this change.
Pro experience
EMR Requirements:
Complete business profile: Add a business name and service description, fill in basic personal information, including a birthdate and address, and upload a profile picture.
Targeting setup: Pros must have at least one service category set up (job preferences, travel area and weekly targeting budget set).
Get reviews: Depending on the EMR version, a pro may need to get one or more reviews from past customers.
Completed background check: Some EMR versions require pros to complete and pass a mandatory background check.
▶ Activation banner and checklist:  Before a pro passes EMR and only if they didn't pass EMR in onboarding,, they will see a banner that says, "You aren't showing in search results yet - finish X setup tasks to start getting leads" at the top of their EMR checklist. See screenshot below.[Image: AD_4nXev1KxQqt-_dk6CkfAvJuJb9LdvLfK7jAZiEpCwgoGEuGTLNzCVYlyHbYYneobz2Rh47No7e4SruuUT3bX8BJz-djMNc3e-gViEh7gUjt9dkytHg9hcIH36SCC_RA-__6w62QNUHg]
▶ Requirements met (pending activation):  Similar to Variant 1,  after passing EMR pros in variant 2 are shown a similar pop-up titled "Ready to start getting leads?". This pop-up informs them that their profile will automatically activate in 24 hours, but they can choose to activate sooner by clicking "Activate profile". See screenshot below.[Image: AD_4nXdoisqczVjc1fe8kGn5EAVctzAmzxrHhxCh-xtgtRTVH-buTzyJDgCU1JDMd5PwUe4fJBS5JjWfGyzmQg8MYH1u5_fvitDlOgj1cnsrZQ7CVAIPZKDnle5yPkqMZt5XETAIpBHFKw]
▶ Activation before 24 hours: If a pro clicks "Activate profile" on the checklist before 24 hours, they will see a brief "Adding you to search results" screen followed by the confirmation screen. See screenshot below.[Image: AD_4nXcLFtfBqCKG4cJJqLjBvuTKPyM2wtS3ZaMtRxkDk5T536esJqN314n-DpvBeaswh8AlGMb4HlIkl93zFuiJPP4WuVCeaKqHrtm9QJYTcYP1kB2VcjvzzxBUC2Uv7nLOPuEQkHyzxw]
▶ Activation after 24 hours: If a variant 2 pro takes no action and returns to the app after 24 hours, a confirmation pop-up will appear, titled "Congrats! You're now showing up in customer searches.". This pop-up will also explain that their credit card will be charged for leads when customers contact them[Image: AD_4nXdloQRuu9QSDIi7VHc7XxzpFgx1rH8HcvmUbsGJm9OpYdoPn1_W4HMlw30W4cI1e1K2toBEVrauqqqgfx0ZlrGKEuqfcSVsQYJJOKMmAwV_Qb6cMnpKYOkLXpkLrQBm1pr6MGgvrw]
Communications variant 2 pros receive:  They will receive a reminder push/SMS 12 hours after passing EMR, letting them know their profile will go live soon if they don't activate it manually. See comms below..
▶ 12-hour Reminder: If the pro has not activated their profile, they will receive a reminder email and push notification 12 hours after passing EMR. The reminder informs them that their profile will go live in 12 hours. The email's subject line is "Your profile will go live in 12 hours" and includes a CTA to "Activate your profile now".[Image: AD_4nXeknCUUbokBer0_08sfLFA5A1G7jnVyEmdo8K6jbSAZMmPUFJKC_Z9eT5nAVE1zwCvLKTztBfhEmdC_ndif5se8dcYjxI9xQONETbztFKZMU8fmfq3cxykgttk5FO7nLDIqOn469A]
▶ Confirmation Email: When the pro's profile goes live (either by clicking the button or automatically after 24 hours), they receive a confirmation email with the subject line "You're now showing up in customer searches".
2. Process
Steps: How to help pros in the "Go live" (Rep)
To help a pro with go live, frontline reps will follow these steps:
Ask the pro if they have completed their onboarding checklist (passed activation requirements).
Explain that their profile will automatically activate in 24 hours, but they can click the “Activate profile” button to go live sooner if they are ready.
3. Resources

 1. OVERVIEW
This internal knowledge article is your go-to guide for using Genesys to manage SMS and Chat interactions. Designed specifically for all frontline reps, it provides step-by-step instructions and best practices for navigating the Genesys system within Tack (Salesforce). Reps will learn how to efficiently handle non-voice communications, including accepting, transferring, and disconnecting interactions.
Key topics covered include accessing the Genesys interface, understanding routing rules, managing multiple conversations, and troubleshooting common issues.
Important: Support Op reps, please remember to verify user information using the "Verify Account Information KA" before providing help.
Pro and customer chat and SMS experience 
Both pros and customers can receive chat and SMS support. To learn more about the chat experience, frontline reps should refer to the X KA. 

Support Channel
Initiate contact
Hours of operation
Chat
Pros and customers can access chat in the app, and in various locations on the web platform. See  Thumbtack Chat Support (Customer) (Pro) KA to learn more. 
Monday - Friday 
6 am - 6 pm MT
SMS (text)
To initiate a text, pros and customers will text (518) 862-8225
Monday - Friday 
6 am - 6 pm MT
HOW TO ACCESS THE SMS AND CHAT INTERFACE 
Each department within Operations (e.g., Support, Trust and Safety, Account Management, Sales) has its own application in Tack customized to the department's needs. 
Sales reps can access the Genesys interface from the Sales Workplace, while Support reps can find it in the Customer Support application.

[Image: AD_4nXfq1yJFLxOAa3BBKYfcXgaTBTO7ZBMBwIsshQUKSTqnapO-UgudRFeTwansPg7NMDwtGOfg0ZE33sqh29uVKgCmXxx_yfIda4cEYPJQefmck95FalCP4M1dBW3e-8k49T5VKEmfoA]

Once you're in the correct application, you'll see two widget options in the lower left corner of the Tack screen:
Genesys (phone icon): This is where you manage the interaction, including transferring and disconnecting.
Chat & SMS (chat bubble icon): This is where you'll send and receive messages via SMS and web chat.

[Image: Image shows the 'Genesys' and 'Chat & SMS' widgets in Tack, located in the lower left corner.]

Click on the Chat & SMS widget to message a user, and click on the Genesys widget to go to the interaction log.
HOW TO NAVIGATE CHAT & SMS INTERFACE 
The Chat & SMS interface is the window where frontline reps send and receive messages via SMS and chat.
Here is an image of the chat or SMS window, along with a guide to the various components.

[Image: BzmbjW-VUkZM6LGDkzDMYyeOruaR6cMxYE-nUWuRbtVxhfZfRCM4RSP3mevtXDpnqIh0Fbwmg-CPIghJQmCEtEgxuAbMGkSw9-9c1fhD9MSqV6tHQF7ZwVSk8vhO1hKy582ZXYz_pMDgvbJ5EX7Tho0]

The name of the customer or pro will be displayed here
Copy the Interaction URL
The timer captures how long the you’ve been working that interaction
Access Canned responses[Image: EKILmXaHAWH77jitnWHwNE-8XxMXAga0kCqMX9pLLq6IzOlMCW2OHX26fU43ZukjLP8yWOJubTwzCojF_LwCoY5pIJM9a4AZHiRCuzynG2EqUYgNLyHOqE6w1TJnpKk0hf1lo384dCz4mgu87suT5UM] (Only used by Sales)
Access wrap-up codes [Image: pcoU-bSmoil-5FyfPe0IOAm2lJI0_-hgRLkr-PH6nrkfSaAnXeQOl-JMxSK6CIifSn6T_7Ap4vM6jH3-ZobeJgB8qAqDhkXQvEec1vQibBYFv8XWhaZALmyqI-fuO2mebp-iUXs8MBrLc6rgakglcY8]
This is a web chat interaction [Image: KfSmwBCZV2cW7cekDTf0WhNT2FLRh-uAxH7zn1XSNnCka3L85mvO51MKEwqHwRb-wOUVN0aHXbP2EW67bJTIIE7GgrFGpSHx70gsEwI0keLTQKEnoucnkhs6vou-bGunG95UG_hC2Pdd0UP8GB4PkM8] (see a closer look below)
This is a SMS interaction  [Image: tbQ69qdyZfUkZjZaFNoUDQYkM9DgMYIeJricVXYVFblOkuMTMDLxh0WZFmRGs5vxO0JweLmccXaBh-cDZRQMd4fHuHtTcKODNZ6MCmTkQqI7sL0c9yo2CqnHd93dltYoUqLfnP-I0HOCj100qu9BFAU](see a closer look below)
The free form text box to type in. 
Click enter to send the message or shift+enter to skip a line. 
User responses are in the orange chat bubbles
Rep responses are in the blue chat bubbles
Send emojis for chat and SMS interactions
Attach media to the message. 
Click the X to delete before sending.
ACTIVE CONVERSATION DETAILS

[Image: -guER1Raump7i8f7MoOrM2DKBhWzJDBFlXtC_p478wNiT9BdhjZfGwQpLsBm8P92szSM7vu9xixlIbqTLxvA0vcpYQwmBf2Ff-_XJTxkN_WbeRgtwjC5Koy_ING87MTUY00eajyciuXgfLmiZCsgvNQ]

Reps can view information about the user in the left column of the SMS & Chat window when handling an active chat or SMS. This information includes the following: 
Interaction type: 
Chat: The[Image: AD_4nXcSNuunJSk7OSsBZBdHXLu4jjDQ8Pb7iU6iFCPYQc1-YygxV2C_thTHu4HauCO3N3HdDCM-EoV0J5HplBSonWquZGV8kEDLwAaBs_5Yx1uW-BlN6Er3FndLEgYGFJme09e-e9QI3YyYmop7dkxOzqMAWSYd]symbol shows it’s a web chat interaction.
SMS: The[Image: AD_4nXcLrApDQe3HKYENfiDp-XYLWyXbQPISe6xiPCZXr5U_SpjYe3dGG7ah2XkdjgNET7pD-dUzeBhwJKpPD7hjVpnIJvc6H8qSI-9bdC3aA1yk3900QZPxGWXJTQlaEZ27PwRQH9SwWRQpHc12TTNRjiUu0s8]symbol shows it’s a SMS interaction. 
Contact information: The remote name of the active interaction (Guest) or phone number (e.g., +18016639266).
Interaction Status: The current state of the interaction (e.g., CONNECTED, HELD).
Queue Information: The name of the queue (e.g., "Customer Chat Support") if the interaction came through a queue.
Interaction Timer: Shows how long the interaction has been connected.
Active Interaction Indicator: When managing multiple chats, the currently selected interaction will be highlighted in green.
INTERACTION CONTROLS
The Genesys panel contains numerous interaction controls. The following table details the controls available for non-voice interactions:
Icon
Name
Description
[Image: -vHIMWEtzJp2qgOtbJM8n5Z2wxrRK5EdyO0PkSrKvH1zDFXuf3K0RCOU-J15_DqGqnf9jH_iJ1JRuojCALDINFE3tfBu2HUA-TuCnRnkO-iNoDdrZqA5_k0eWl_twOkV8pXwZSjGqRhtCrjjWDyhOQ8]
Pick up
Pick up (answer) an interaction.
[Image: CbuzKfq_P8zfeFhD1wlOUSsc2ScrdrbLrasljAz7adVetkHrYOLeZiMVDYu-XluS8x7vrR_24E5_9TmkFuVlVWXESrSvXJaNMu_vItVWuWy3IG0sdWazT-CJ_Kw5568bn-pTwPUSBAa81nSL61gUOds]
Transfer
Blind (cold) transfers an interaction to a queue or person. 
After the interaction transfers to the person or queue, Genesys sends you into after-call work. 
[Image: vuiPKKiJDVkJQosHpOiCF9-VPp3FANwNaSaj4nLrNarPbG2ViMDEFj7TafFzz8CdFPSxOZFTBXhvrw1pa0RpXLqpDe3JVSwGel1uOsMDtmok3L7lbaK_KTPpng5BcHNXNJ3tqHZJSM49vqOW3a0Xk_I]
Disconnect
Disconnect an interaction. 
After disconnecting, the interaction is still visible but remains in a deallocated state for 2 minutes so agents can finish updating the interaction log.
NOTE: For a list of all available controls for phone interactions, please refer to Genesys | Phone System KA.
HOW INTERACTIONS ARE ROUTED 
When a pro or customer reaches out with a callback or message reply, Genesys attempts to route it to the last rep who handled their previous interaction, as long as that rep is available and not already fully utilized. If that rep is not available, the system will route the interaction to the next available rep.
Less than 72 hours: Genesys will group multiple messages from the same customer as part of the same conversation, as long as the conversation's disconnected period is less than 72 hours. 
More than 72 hours: A new conversation will be started if there is a break longer than 72 hours since the last disconnect. 
For example, if a customer sends two messages and receives a response from a support rep, then sends two more messages several hours after the case was closed, this would create a new case but still be part of the same interaction thread.
HOW TIMERS WORK ON THE CHAT AND SMS INTERFACE
Interactions can have two timers:
After a rep answers an interaction, the timer to the lower right of the interaction card displays the duration of the interaction’s current state. For example, interacting, holding, or after-call work.
Above the interaction window, to the right of the contact and channel information, Genesys displays the duration of the selected interaction.

[Image: yR31d1AhHqnFRqsyABKxrBvYNKzR_fSiKFGXGovKn4R8muWkjmEWys8u768thE42CiX8PXNA7SLkUQ1uxAuwDnH94-jgH7ek4cFkkaP4tA1k_aqPZTdvLIindPc2ULd0H6Wfv-Eb9zEKqOGdhvvMtaE]

NOTE: There is no timer for letting reps know how much time they have left to accept. 

CHARACTER COUNT, ATTACHMENTS AND CANNED RESPONSES
With Genesys, frontline reps can easily send messages and add emojis, attach files, and use canned responses. 
To send your message, click Enter.
To shift to a new line, use Shift+Enter. 
Do not press Enter until you are finished with your message.
CHARACTER LIMITATIONS
▶ Chat character limits
For inbound chat messaging from pros or customers:
Character  limit of 4,089 characters 
Image attachments must be 10MB or smaller. 
Rep chat messages have a limit of 1,999 characters.
Reps will see the error “Maximum number of characters reached.” once the character limit has been reached.
▶ SMS limits
Rep responses can contain up to 669 characters and can include emojis. 
Emojis count as one character.
Reps will see the “-603 (10 messages)” prompt when you have reached the 669-character limit (message can be sent)
Error “Maximum number of characters reached.” means you’ve reached that limit.
ATTACHMENT SIZE
Genesys messaging have the following size limits for transferring file attachments in inbound and outbound messages: 
Web messaging: 10 MB limit
SMS messaging: 3 MB limit
Whenever a user sends an attachment, you will see the image or file in the messenger window. To download it, simply click on the image. You may need to log into Genesys before the download begins.
In case a graphic is displayed in the chat, you can hide it and then display it again as needed. To hide the graphic, click on "Collapse"
[Image: Vjp5wSCmrpw3kHF2snqc5gkaP8FQxb2p5E1gIe0t3eIelgHA9_ikZpBAGXPLohOsZMZjA9knk1cIuve3nyC7sC4ejisL1uI7iawr_SsbLAlUE_XIdagB2Hfem1KpX-Hv09fpaIS7RwJJrP5GXTyhefQ]
next to the file name. To display it again, click on "Expand" 
[Image: mhkqnLDcjt82vZmpPBqH-HIA2tWSVFEDRjQcC53UFTh0qeyZ-YvlPYGdxbOh84ePU52lIdHk64BRGvPoBA9ydvayRBzoNimo2HmiUEhm797pDm_7uWkWZaP7IdFk-m_2HzeV1ZIk12Z36pfaIesKuIo]
next to the file name.


[Image: 43hrxeO1pdcsXLz0YQLEcs4lTXzuvxas7NFpJiSQquNtbJtsbKIev_1e5sCE27T8VvIJjok6Rn_z7ANPh5S0tivZVYv6fyUQLEBEMXCMYcT3D6-KpoqA6XGWgL8GOtswIRfI7iC-_k3iuPgEPPlFAyM]
To delete an attachment before sending it, click the X in the lower right corner. You can only send one file at a time. (see image below) 

[Image: 7r1ay69sUhAVHC75GVaVlS3V0SfbRRYTLVtR5CoIl4znY_-oQqD9hwIkzgn3i_Sumajg4PHNS-6gkZJhNBw0C4iIkS4zTnCVsHJu6uti73NWSN1-7x6-XFMZdkOpnonG22Tl0I-xpgGw0pLazMFhHM4]
HOW TO USE AND SEND CANNED RESPONSES 
The Canned Responses feature is currently available to the Sales and Responsive Pro Non-Voice teams. 
Although you cannot add or edit canned responses from the library, you may contact Team Manager JJ Santos to request edits or new canned responses.
To access and send a canned response, follow these steps: 
In a message interaction, click Canned Responses [Image: vJRiP5zl1JQxsHIaI1jR3-0cAPnFUBdOIacfpvKexNHjZ485iWdJuagZzpJxro2b575T0lYhnnzM3KEyz1vEF9YseDXI_T4JIvysZnM5W_qlWLq36uj2-p4wNkdsh-ncdHq3rTrN3bSI-VYOHg2p_UI].
Find and select the response you want to use.
Click the Insert icon .
To complete the message, continue to type in the reply field. 
Click enter to send the message.

[Image: s3Nlj6bziSFQbR8dA9PuZK0aDZBTNTTMVBql5fRV0v0b6Q542-8HcBKTbNhCjymL7wiK-DOSjCnYuQGg3KpMMo61rh3sFYXaWOhlBKFflxWJLWEZefItEZov_iy53mMpr_rmNLRgke6XAGk6bSqEhRI]

2. PROCESS
How to receive an interaction
In order to receive new conversations you must be in the On Queue state. When new conversations arrive you will have a number of seconds to accept the conversation, and then respond to them.
Genesys does not have a response timer. 
Support teams - Your interactions are set to auto answer for you. 
Sales team – If you don’t accept a conversation within ~ 30 seconds, Genesys returns the interaction to the queue and places you into Not Responding. 
An alert appears to the upper right of the user interface, and your profile shows that you are on queue and not responding. 
To start accepting contacts again, select “Go Back On Queue” and to stop receiving contacts, select “Go Off Queue.”  
By default, if you lose your connection for less than 60 seconds, Genesys returns you to the status you had before the disconnect.
Chat and SMS interaction maximum 
Support will handle a max of 2 chats or SMS conversations at a time
Sales AEs can have a max of 10 SMS conversations at a time
SDRs can have a max of 3 SMS conversations at a time
(Rep) Steps: How to accept a new interaction 
Frontline reps will accept a non-voice interaction the same way they would answer a phone call. To do so, follow these steps: 
Log in as an agent and go on queue. The Interactions panel opens and new messages appear in the Active Interactions list. See Genesys | Phone System KA for login steps. 
Support teams - Your interactions are set to auto answer for you. 
Sales teams - If you decline or do not answer an interaction within a certain amount of time, Genesys places you into Not Responding status. While Not Responding, you don’t receive new interactions. Declined or not answered interactions are re-queued.
▶ Screenshot of Genesys panel[Image: yOiUzC9oGXV5e8U78uq1KN-iJeKBhG49JN-hcezVOZ3eOeo54iPhuyXvgZfRhNbpzNnMfddtDgPfP4QavRKph8OnARO5Jzm_IBUTTOvCACvK-GgMhBiPuO5CyLtrb_ARPM47G75qagzfwBO9gjoy2FY]
To begin a message interaction, click Pick Up [Image: -vHIMWEtzJp2qgOtbJM8n5Z2wxrRK5EdyO0PkSrKvH1zDFXuf3K0RCOU-J15_DqGqnf9jH_iJ1JRuojCALDINFE3tfBu2HUA-TuCnRnkO-iNoDdrZqA5_k0eWl_twOkV8pXwZSjGqRhtCrjjWDyhOQ8].
In the interaction alert, the counter indicates the amount of time the interaction has been in the queue. 
To alert you of a new interaction, Genesys plays a short audible alert. 
After you accept an interaction, at the top of the active interaction, Genesys displays the contact information for the interaction and its duration.
▶ Screenshot of chat window[Image: 5WVaOrqFL4AG6CHl1n7UC7-57J8Ti5YPKPX95CiQ6O6NtgLZt-Si5iBoFZKRuf2FA1k0pCCu4Q3rxJaXm7ZIJuL_LgrTQ25lcyVC7tSuP5MhSa4fPjHRwYGPTsp-s5ZyXSQT3YCQr9oT2b7ASm443p8]
Type your response to the incoming message. 
For Sales, to insert a canned response, see steps below. 
To send your message, click Enter. To shift to a new line, use Shift+Enter. Do not press Enter until you are finished with your message.
To continue the conversation, repeat steps 4–5 as needed.
Toggle between the Genesys panel widget [Image: -vHIMWEtzJp2qgOtbJM8n5Z2wxrRK5EdyO0PkSrKvH1zDFXuf3K0RCOU-J15_DqGqnf9jH_iJ1JRuojCALDINFE3tfBu2HUA-TuCnRnkO-iNoDdrZqA5_k0eWl_twOkV8pXwZSjGqRhtCrjjWDyhOQ8] and the messenger [Image: tyEAXxmT86aYPk7mKo4-4Lfm5uKvn-T0olAQLSC6oyLnFB5_xXa0ke5W-D6DVsPF3asc2alCxaYQXsNFhk5r8mumSaP0NSbdvw8e4FiIVf5ULAKq8xGgePXCTGbWNop-9TWYYmI-W0NRUXpN6ANgdVk]widget  along the button of Salesforce.
▶ Screeshot of lower left Tack[Image: jkIH5RGOf_xvvg3jTSjucx2lchDXYUP_NvaYscH26hb4N1jLfQ-rOnWrNcnEA-pMfTY5Km0skbgW-MADGB4dlUaN-fkb7cor07VNJPMLpmmKcvWPWGuD-PLMhKOiFVeoiSgU3-mjMmhv7D4KvsX-vck]
To end an interaction, see steps below.
Managing new messages 
When you receive a new message, you will see an orange burst 
[Image: CGkGZWOmQEnpCADhH6TtEDRs9fy42sttyJ7Q5eVzXZqe-1FDhQTdv0oAjZ7PcaubCvoHAxPkirkrnn2xymHaN0yM9Bcd8OfUNN6vXrQl-DRrMgJ57HB__ekr8iG9jvp6B3y3TfPFTlOBeMtAw6CgSMQ]
 appears on the chat window, and the interactions window. You will also see a “New Message” prompt in the messenger window which will clear when you reply to the user.
To send a message or file, you will click Enter on your keyboard. There is no “send” option in the messenger window. 
For chat conversations, both you and the customer can see when the other party is typing. 


[Image: eUgo1Juy7db8SHW1zOyCK5IS6QJXAPWtv5wJVFZ5fJMBFnHJjDMzTSAkByJFueXQlvp8GW3FRwLl4F9PnXuuoE7NB2dO2VrTQ4f2aZp9EmHfCd8AW_cWyO5I7y9u391karOSKIUathsmUMtc52qxAwU]
How to troubleshoot message failure errors 🔺
If you encounter a red triangle error 
[Image: xxPRDedEdToPUpNNsYc_GiiYjREeyPeo2Kb6nvN19TsOUiXJ4ZqFTPwd_xVj9coVux7Ebr8yZ25RoEbvcdBxc9P67db0RtKuHxvS3LhekoZqHQqURspGlWcVG6AU3wiElYcJ1y_xO7LbUnsd97zIfAA]
while sending or receiving messages through chat or SMS, here's what could be causing it:

 
▶ If we are trying to send the message and you get this error, it could be because:
For SMS: the pro or customer has opted out of text messages, or Genesys is not allowing us to send messages to them. This could be because they have opted out and we don't have it tracked, their phone is not set up to receive text messages, or is disconnected.
For Chat/Web Messaging: The pro or customer may have closed out the browser or chat window on their end, deactivating the session and preventing messages from being delivered.

[Image: 6r-01paaV2mGsdZrsniNHMtgANzEQEIB1NkSIeNxlJ2motoIbe6kaKS0qpKwfdrofawiEU2XHNBggC2uDRX-WpQoIYj2la3057F-h7Dx8Jr2O9pNUDu9KZsMH2CswtGGGq-SYJADmF0GXwUNVCoxXIg]

If you have tried to send the message multiple times without success, you may close the conversation.
You can also refer to the TackIT Help Desk article: SMS/Chat Message Failures 

 
▶ If the error occurred when we received a message:
Hover over the alert to see what the error is. If it says, "one or more unsupported media attachments have been removed," it means the attachment was too large to come in. See Attachment size. 
Check with the user to see what they tried to send, let them know it didn't come in, and find out what it was.
Talking point: “I noticed that your last message came through as blank. Can you please let me know what you were trying to send? It's possible that there was a character or size limit that caused the issue.” 

[Image: p5oQIGcEVALV17iEzFSSc1Z3Kg4n5zeimKd8W_QrY-MlvH1v9sx6fTzMWzPh4xuiEkTADjSUkeTX7P1eOA_S6mInzVEFp6syb_vMLx-FBfZFAu2Y4KXYkpvnfWl_-4mNYvBuTA-ADgYz4borvD3jiw8]

If you have further questions about this, please discuss with your manager the appropriate course of action (wrap-up code, next steps, etc.).
(Rep) Steps: How to manage multiple interactions 

Support reps will handle a max of 2 chats or SMS conversations at a time. Sales has a max of 4 SMS conversations. 
To accept a new interaction, click Pick up [Image: ewz0DbMmuoHyKP-g5vTfkixTbg3n40NfBugXrQjiiUb28ZrTwbyEf1aHluhLj7DL7tISup3IInJ0UoXdbTxe19R5IPni60At1-Mg0kZbL7_PK61zt7sUIcnoKUHykaHZkT7fmcmbP3ZIevZycECG1Lc] . 
Support teams - Your interactions are set to auto answer for you. 
Sales teams - If you decline or do not answer an interaction within a certain amount of time, Genesys places you into Not Responding status. While Not Responding, you don’t receive new interactions. Declined or not answered interactions are re-queued.
▶ Screenshot of Genesys panel[Image: _bC6OEaXVrgSEwFGhrcAia24xPeggPm2CUwV6QcwXM3FylBEqQbknhJujT0VHGnu_i8P-X0DkXBVw9SODEXDbGclndiTWFfbML5UZjcDR0c6QrDHAtmmKK9vEBx4U9_un5mo900JXz-z1Gtjah-Svtk]
After you accept an interaction, at the top of the active interaction, Genesys displays the contact information for the interaction and its duration.
On the left side, the Interactions list, new and current interactions appear. Each interaction appears separately in the list. To work with an interaction, select its card from the Interactions list.
When working on multiple interactions, the interaction you are on will be in green and say CONNECTED.
Type your response to the incoming message. 
To send your message, click Enter. To shift to a new line, use Shift+Enter. Do not press Enter until you are finished with your message.
To continue the conversation, repeat steps 4–5 as needed.
▶ Screenshot of chat window[Image: UJ4pGlSpRlkiRteDn2n1JbftDpzWJq5wpsnVGpuk0miWCH0UXoj0gc1u-hllDvrh7KwaRlmO7NyMNqzlWIN1bSnANnTZeu4PK5O8YRNvkfdIlcN5avOlrUFKsiW-cf8-G71wKEw6wLWElXb_bkSDh6c]
Toggle between the Genesys panel and Chat & SMS panel to manage the interactions (e.g., transfer, disconnect).
▶ Screenshot of Tack showing the two buttons[Image: hI-cm7r76MlOwvh6Xm3S48xNIb6I2hrzgLq_Zs6s1nqPjpiEcVDs6Scade1u0yVGUQYeOegDWxn2N_4DYbzREmF0jmu46_k3aTTFDtBtjtQxttFoZV3dDtHgdOX40vNe7VYnGnFkZ13BjwC3siPmQig]
To end an interaction, see steps below.

(Rep) Steps: How to transfer an interaction 

You will transfer a chat or SMS interaction the same way you would a phone call, however you can only perform a blind (cold) transfer. The Consult button does not appear in the Transfer window for chat and SMS interactions. 
When transferring, it's important to be cautious about who receives the chat. The system doesn't have built-in safeguards to prevent chats from being sent to the wrong person or queue. Therefore, it's best practice to double-check and ensure the transfer goes to the correct destination before finalizing it.
UPDATE: (effective January 10, 2024) When transferring a chat or SMS interaction to another rep, the transfer window will remain open until the rep accepts the interaction or you click Cancel. When the rep accepts the transfer, the transfer completes and the initial interaction drops off the interaction list.
The steps below are how to perform a blind transfer: 
While on an interaction, from the interaction panel, click the “Transfer” icon [Image: 2hkLWseEpjgJmsZqovkyt_Jx8ugsaupSyarSs8DFnKMElQ7WDSxz2jdRDe4HQNFQMsYeksCAnPC-pFoHnB2hxBFJ4TAbLEVgCS9vfuExqfZw5a5kLIr1QIPrPaSngsFRGZbqMYhCC1c9Fp7jxLzDtbQ] in the communications menu.
Start typing out the name of the person or queue and click enter. Select the intended person or queue from the list of suggestions. 
Expand your search by selecting both the “People” and “Queues” buttons from the top of the Transfer pop-up.
People appear first in the results, followed by queues and then external contacts. Each search is limited to 25 results.
▶ Screenshot of Genesys panel[Image: y-twkU_cR_1QjmyYVPxYNWySLNqc2V6wUx3Hp98gUIp_BIX4yPMTBNcehsPwHN_ehnekcYlrs0-4TItxxf9DXGla4dyuAsvQm6KovkA8z62HSapUymgmbXEHCvMAkUOH9NxTpX_v871s8-nAJf32fYY]
▶ Transfer to a person
When you click a person, statistics show the person’s status and number and type of interactions that the person is currently handling.
“Cannot transfer” will show if you try to transfer an interaction but the receiving rep is not assigned the permission to accept that media type.
[Image: w_ozcC65QKE9xkcsVODbAUeJFWkGUA9BqjkTicDDYRZiuvk217j8FXq4ECSOk5GN5FEXn6puH7mdWNtjbxt8CwjhLan0uLyhgkQ1D7tJYenxcLum4aLJnmVHc_mH9JhJj8r7pZeYHryYyocAQNDwLkU]Transfer to a person:
▶ Transfer to a queue:
When you click a queue, statistics for the queue appear.
Waiting – Number and type of interactions waiting in the queue.
Agents – Number of active and total agents in the queue.
EWT – Estimated wait time for an advocate to answer.
▶ Screenshot of statistics[Image: jdP_t2rYm_rWjFHjSdnfc6FGOcv1Wyit0CaHSXzTci6pPgIvp4eSyp-XJMkQBHhLNWb_W-Iz_e-zflBquSKezBY-on4N2vq0FMWbRreG-SLHHNLjTqfjWmO37G7w5ZOlQMXHsT5dJiHEyw55lNZLnaU]
Check the “Transfer Workspace” box to transfer the case or contact to the rep you are transferring the interaction to. (This applies to all Genesys interactions)
▶ Screenshot of Genesys panel[Image: 8ukmVXrxtoKL3t-_yAf-DBKKAk84PdAHxOUsu9_O49xZq0AWBRscPG38hp6eEeyO2b87r8ZXuyoaqPibWcmVtS4l_juU71hB4JS_LlQDSmRW8HGp5zvtS4HM3h5oBgeRK_kKr9Cm-HUaDL_rXIJFnAk]
Click the “Blind” button. The transfer window will remain open until the rep accepts the interaction or you click Cancel. 
Once the rep accepts the transfer, the transfer completes and the initial interaction drops off the interaction list.
▶ Screenshot of Genesys panel[Image: 4DOBkvjBWuvEHBcFTQYWB_cnzAAQ-IveP_OQMWDdvJ9WoffFefQvqcPJ-sP2Shu0pRi7Usbt5YYbd27IQnI66ice3w05xvhXD70lS6klRNrxlc6DFEV4UbpPRYFlGZGbc2Viw8wcf94HoFTK2hpcbMc]
Depending on your after call work settings, you will be put in ACW or immediately available to accept new interactions. 
Support teams are put in an ACW setting which enables agents to choose how long to remain in ACW status. Complete ACW to receive new interactions, or automatically become available at the end of the time specified. 
Boost and Sales teams have optional ACW settings which allows agents to opt out of selecting a wrap-up code after a call. 
(Rep) Steps: How to receive a transfer
There are a few things to note about accepting a transferred non-voice interaction: 
When receiving a transferred case, you will accept the interaction as usual.
Support teams - Your interactions are set to auto answer for you. 
Sales teams - If you decline or do not answer an interaction within a certain amount of time, Genesys places you into Not Responding status. While Not Responding, you don’t receive new interactions. Declined or not answered interactions are re-queued.
All non-voice transfers are Blind (cold) transfers. 
You can read the previous conversation to pick up where the conversation left off. 
The messenger will show any conversations that have taken place within 72 hours. If the user contacts us again outside of 72 hours, it creates a new interaction log. 
There is no way to identify in the Genesys panel that you are accepting a transferred interaction. If you work out of cases, you can see the previous interaction logged on the case. 
(Rep) Steps: How to send an outbound SMS 
You can send an SMS message regardless of the status you're in. 
Sending an outbound SMS is similar to making an outbound phone call, but there are a few differences. To send an SMS, follow the steps below.
Click Main Menu [Image: bxTTBRuqhefB0QNAi1LLDHktQwufag8k8S1aPL4yaffIkE8mQipi0KeESqZMEbdk6jMr8HlRO-RfWx_r6RdrcTTZD4xc0VNyIKbQ7r41NLaYgkgwshT8B6UUqN0DaVkPGeS-yqpJQhcSsz2tI-2iOu8].
Select New Interaction.
Select SMS [Image: NxE5U-I8lDAD5oYML0NHj3VNYAJLkW0LpfzdQCWEyGKnbUrTHZxD7s6p_r53iptuP_HnK_mP8YTtkw1yIblCB9l6dcN9kxWqh0BNsAQmjVJYg4H_-8PcpuCzMJcoB7u-UkrsHt3czUEKZTsaOazyOgg]
▶ Screenshot of Genesys panel[Image: 8H-CEhI1uuiVVMMMyy315dzJbhCHzujclNp_8c4o8ozj4HHscCXoGW5ePwIhD5mx4iefT9S0mYGzfnGK1FKcGhG7Ird_nFcUyj6bQ5WhQEdZTrfHBQ1faA0RgyisZEnuaUy6RAVcfC6i4fR8OBzhtPE]
Fill out the following fields:
On Behalf of Queue – Start typing out the name of your queue, and select it from the drop-down.
The Genesys panel only auto-completes and returns queue names in the search results for queues that you are a member of. The queue that you select must have an outbound SMS number associated with it.
Number – Start typing out or paste the number you want to send an SMS to. 
The Compose button remains unavailable until you enter both a valid queue name and a properly formatted SMS number.
▶ Screenshot of Genesys panel[Image: HObpv7dacB5fTfxFLp6H9fLP_04eiWlnYzBHtomFtC2bJCK7W5-6AnZr6x6qXBhWSI5DQJ6DPxMs2juk0N-0GVuEZnO8ZoWfS35Hhqgi6AxPGIJqkBxnmg-x81LrnE9F0gVsfVnzpqGOSQW9OUGoK1c]
Click Compose to start the interaction. The integration checks for recent SMS conversations with this contact (within the last 72 hours).
If no active SMS conversation exists, an SMS message interaction connects.
If an active SMS conversation exists, you’ll see the following prompt. Click Continue. In the Genesys panel, an SMS message interaction with the SMS message history connects.
▶ Screenshot of Genesys panel[Image: kKtU55Y7MYqGGz_Bljp5zNGZffY5haUYAKuksoPNApDvlZrSFxMORyg-DVgYwdGFJSSMOhXOmVx939qQ8IzxHNTY_Dq3LJTruaNvJKM42V2N9PR3LvQmpbOGOhS83aCnnUceOwyzZxbeqDxpTqo9Ki0]
After the SMS message interaction connects, you can blind transfer [Image: CbuzKfq_P8zfeFhD1wlOUSsc2ScrdrbLrasljAz7adVetkHrYOLeZiMVDYu-XluS8x7vrR_24E5_9TmkFuVlVWXESrSvXJaNMu_vItVWuWy3IG0sdWazT-CJ_Kw5568bn-pTwPUSBAa81nSL61gUOds] or disconnect [Image: vuiPKKiJDVkJQosHpOiCF9-VPp3FANwNaSaj4nLrNarPbG2ViMDEFj7TafFzz8CdFPSxOZFTBXhvrw1pa0RpXLqpDe3JVSwGel1uOsMDtmok3L7lbaK_KTPpng5BcHNXNJ3tqHZJSM49vqOW3a0Xk_I] the SMS message interaction. (Disconnecting the SMS message interaction before sending your first message cancels the SMS message.)
Click SMS.[Image: jEs7qLIxdZt0L7oIiECv84iqm5dHb9H_AMdG3r4inzEMia7mePSDBdZjgQPi5Iuz_8iHV06p5o4hrLqwGfoZBhWpOe_lo5SwCEMJijTQDm3dSs-bXtgeUeWF4lk7uWSsmlAyMzeYu1C5QwCgCy1-yOU]An Interactions window opens and turns green. In the Genesys panel, the SMS icon turns orange, indicating that an Interactions window is open or accessible.
▶ Screenshot of Genesys panel[Image: PQjt6rNH9dW25CnpBZ0GBM626fU905IPyJDqmxzj0zI2fTfRZWIBzPpGsCkCFQaD3uk56WJ00BOqWdrWd_mQi8lMOhJSQCZjL4zAKnCDRGOaIk3RKQok96hgjJvJmIUVy6u-87TuDx4YiPECCdLmGls]
Write your SMS messages in the Interactions window and click Enter to send the message. 
Recent SMS conversations within the last 72 hours may be visible.
▶ Screenshot of Genesys panel
[Image: gAzoh25Mv8R7sFANffPnd_rT6vpP6261sW9Ir1jKbHA9HY54gJU_u_viTjDExa8OsCX3z6Jce1Eht4eTi2KCQD6kSWng10mjej9Q-20f84JIfkGpPNAoloz8-w_GcUdX_djKCZeZXhYbeCzk1njfzWw]
To end the SMS conversation, follow the steps below. 
NOTE: If a user has opted out, there is no notice in Geneys, however, the SMS won’t be sent to the user.  Sales teams, you can find out whether someone has opted out of SMS by checking the "Contact Outreach Summary" section in tack (Salesforce). Look for the checkbox fields that indicate their opt-out status. It's important to regularly check for this information before sending an outbound SMS. 
(Rep) Steps: How to end an interaction in the Genesys panel
Important note about in-app chat termination: Users cannot end an in-app chat from their side. Even if the user is no longer there, the rep must close out the interaction in Genesys.  Additionally, if a user refreshes the page, it disrupts the chat, and the reps response will not be sent. 
To disconnect the interaction, navigate to the Genesys panel by clicking the [Image: -vHIMWEtzJp2qgOtbJM8n5Z2wxrRK5EdyO0PkSrKvH1zDFXuf3K0RCOU-J15_DqGqnf9jH_iJ1JRuojCALDINFE3tfBu2HUA-TuCnRnkO-iNoDdrZqA5_k0eWl_twOkV8pXwZSjGqRhtCrjjWDyhOQ8] widget along the bottom of tack (Salesforce). 
▶ Screenshot of bottom of Tack[Image: hOGJVW4hvCGfU_W6qdeIZYDbnIyM_E1BZs0n1xpFmi_3Rq5ygvuwdgb0XE-dWN8NL00wAYN0NHJxqOokH09zp7a6Q_aKy01m4H43pFfKOoHrlScaAnYPD_cUBhJ6mAxCD_VMgp2ohf68bqwWynVpgPk]
In the phone , click Disconnect [Image: vuiPKKiJDVkJQosHpOiCF9-VPp3FANwNaSaj4nLrNarPbG2ViMDEFj7TafFzz8CdFPSxOZFTBXhvrw1pa0RpXLqpDe3JVSwGel1uOsMDtmok3L7lbaK_KTPpng5BcHNXNJ3tqHZJSM49vqOW3a0Xk_I].
Once disconnected from the SMS conversation, the Wrap-up window automatically opens. 
▶ screenshot of Genesys Panel[Image: VVOaFU3iyCZaFrVVUSsyinWCZkYL-gXpSx5CylrocLG_nAa54Ww0ImZGcvOKOJv84N1B0ZA_QJwPpXRHhlZwq05c0cFUBKjduCrlLmuIkMXz6geW3LICoanHCPP0behbV7pJTuY11e_FmwxmqbbuaQA]
Depending on your after call work settings, you will be put in ACW or immediately available to accept new interactions. 
Support teams are put in an ACW setting which enables agents to choose how long to remain in ACW status. Complete ACW to receive new interactions, or automatically become available at the end of the time specified. 
Boost and Sales teams have optional ACW settings which allows agents to opt out of selecting a wrap-up code after a call. 
To complete wrap-up work, select your wrap-up code in the phone panel or in the Interactions window and click Done.
The SMS message interaction deallocates from your interaction list. In the example, the SMS icon remains orange [Image: jEs7qLIxdZt0L7oIiECv84iqm5dHb9H_AMdG3r4inzEMia7mePSDBdZjgQPi5Iuz_8iHV06p5o4hrLqwGfoZBhWpOe_lo5SwCEMJijTQDm3dSs-bXtgeUeWF4lk7uWSsmlAyMzeYu1C5QwCgCy1-yOU], indicating that the Interactions window is open or accessible.
If you close the Wrap-up window without clicking Done, the Wrap-up icon turns red [Image: HUMcDgU3o_I3F4Y1ii4m7H4CayKLS0Q3fs6ubt760noBcG6CGnq9i-Cuh2wxDAPkrTn45zpv9ABhhBMgwYD3Y6GEJbEHyZpdRPvWaRBGhABEjbVN3yge7r_EUpmGalYx0GGz9joaQbLq9-IhhyEj2ds], indicating that you must complete wrap-up work.
▶ Screenshot of Genesys panel[Image: 1LBhtSORYuBBDdy66BiehKHEDYw2Mgidp_BodK2RPmoU0U3QKywc5jlbSKFQAoCpZVGF88Yxybl9yt7xKXY8tMfd3hXeoJTr14-IU3F1Byc9120B5SVm2I_vHSIGf9kukC3vqVEa0bW1hhPu0V1Jmkk]
INTERACTION (TRANSCRIPT) LOGS
Transcripts provide insights of what took place and what was said during the interaction.
An interaction log will show any conversations that have taken place within 72 hours. If the user contacts us again outside of 72 hours, it creates a new interaction log. 
(Rep) Steps: How to access interaction logs from Tack
You will not see the interaction transcript in Tack. You can access the interaction URL from Tack, which will bring you to the Genesys web page. 
To access an interaction log from Tack, you will follow these steps:
From a Tack case, Navigate to the associated call task record by clicking on “Related
Scroll down to “Activity History” and click on the applicable interaction under the “Subject” column. 
Look under the Contact Center Information section
Click the Interaction URL. This will open a Genesys desktop window. 
Permissions to interaction logs are being worked on. You may receive an error “You are not authorized for this interaction." The KA will be updated once this has been worked out. 

[Image: mGmGw8TvCX4D0lDj-fMMgIc3UTpL4LtYRpkdWQmmGGJJOxwC2bdtihYlGvofkdmZg8sqU86pjZIe05CteWttyVdS-PyywM3IqGQz-KO9LUb8lZ9-WGzBI0C7hFGJ4CtA3o8qRTR59LIbufQns6Pxoak]

Follow the steps below to access interaction log from Genesys web browser.
(Rep) Steps: How to access interaction logs from Genesys web browser 
To see an interaction log (transcript), frontline reps can access them in Genesys in a web browser by following these steps: 
Navigate to Genesys in a web browser using Okta. 
Click Performance along the top. 
Select Workspace from the dropdown Workspace.
Click the row of the interaction whose transcript that you want to view.
Click the Transcript tab. 
Transcripts are divided into user and agent sections. On the left side of the page, every section includes a time stamp and an icon that indicates when the user or the agent sent the message or chat.
Permissions to interaction logs are being worked on. You may receive an error “You are not authorized for this interaction." The KA will be updated once this has been worked out. 
How to remove sensitive information from a chat or SMS 
If sensitive information is shared during an interaction, it's important to follow the Removing Sensitive Info From Genesys steps outlined in the Sensitive Account Information KA. This is crucial for security reasons and to maintain the safety of Thumbtack. 
How to block a user who is behaving inappropriately during a chat or SMS 
If a pro or customer you are working with behaves inappropriately while you’re trying to help them, you should follow the process steps on the Blocking Abusive Users KA.
4. INTERNAL FAQ
Do I need to update my name or profile photo for Genesys? 
No, ou will not have a Genesys profile to update your name or profile photo. The user you are chatting with will not see your name and photo. 
Does Genesys have a timer that counts down the time you have to answer an interaction? 
Genesys does not have a response timer.
Is the chat or SMS transcript available in Tack to read? 
No, you will not see the interaction transcript tack. You can access the interaction URL from tack which will bring you to the Genesys web page where you can review the transcript log. 
Can you warm transfer an SMS or chat interaction?
No, you can only blind (cold) transfer non-voice interactions. The Consult button does not appear in the Transfer window for chat and SMS interactions.
Can you block a pro or customer in Genesys? 
No. If a pro or customer you are working with behaves inappropriately while you’re trying to help them, you should follow the process steps on the Blocking Abusive Users KA.
How many interactions can a rep have at a time? 
Chat and SMS interaction maximum 
Service will handle a max of 2 chats or SMS conversations at a time
Sales AEs can have a max of 10 SMS conversations at a time
SDRs can have a max of 3 SMS conversations at a time

1. Overview
Thumbtack uses Genesys Cloud to manage phone, chat, and SMS interactions. The Genesys panel is within Salesforce, so there’s nothing to download.  However, email interactions are not included in the Genesys panel.
Genesys replaced several previous systems with a single platform, streamlining user interactions, including Five9, Gong, Teleopti, and Qualtrics. 
Navigate the Genesys Panel
Here's how Frontline reps can navigate the Genesys panel. Refer to the image below to see where each feature is located on the panel:
The status you enter will appear on the top and bottom of the panel and the widget tab. 
To close the Genesys panel, click Minimize[Image: rtaImage]in the upper-right corner. 
You can detach or reattach the Genesys panel by clicking New Window [Image: rtaImage]in the panel's upper-right corner. 
The interface has three menus to access different settings (main menu, communication menu, and activity status menu).
Use the Clock [Image: rtaImage] to see how long you’ve been in status. The timer resets when you change your status.
To access the Genesys panel, click Genesys [Image: rtaImage] in the widget panel of Salesforce. 

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ Main menu
Main menu (left menu) 
[Image: rtaImage]
: Use this menu to return to an interaction and to check your schedule (not all teams will use the schedule option)

Main menu options
Interactions: Manage your interactions for chat, SMS, and phone. This will take you back to any interactions you currently have going or that have ended recently.
Interaction Log: This function is deactivated for this first phase.
New Interaction: Start an outbound call or SMS
Agent Performance: Quickly view your real-time statistics for voice, callback, chat, email, and message, interactions.
User Inbox: Access call history, voicemails, and schedule notifications.
Agent Schedule: Support can check their schedule. Workforce Services will provide training on this for employees who will use this feature.
Settings: Change aspects of your notification, queue, and phone once it is set up.
Genesys Cloud: Desktop tab, opens to your Genesys profile on desktop. Use to troubleshoot, but if you have an issue, submit a Help Desk Ticket and someone will help you use this section.
Help: New tab opens Genesys Cloud knowledge base. You may need to use this section to troubleshoot, but if you have an issue, submit a Help Desk Ticket and someone will help you use this section. 

[Image: Main menu]

▶ User inbox [Image: rtaImage]
Depending on Frontline rep permissions, their access to the following features may vary (e.g., voicemail).
Reps can access call history, personal voicemails, evaluations, and schedule notifications through the User Inbox
[Image: AD_4nXdJ6QXf-_Rr9eP5zZ9PJrUEtuqhj-7e-8hZY7bL1ERlq6Oh3iPXHah-YksJobIX1DmTmK3m_2_baaRuIfbu_6DI8TQ4QCCHmNyaWLJMjzxWXMAUpvPPth_lcCvxxc7ZoOfoh8KKT2BUJlO_SUxD10Z52ntB]
.

If the inbox contains new notifications, an orange burst

Steps: How to set a voicemail greeting 

Use your phone to record and set up a custom voicemail greeting by following the steps below:
 
On your phone panel, start a "new interaction." 
Make sure you are not calling on behalf of a queue. The On Behalf of Queue field should be empty.
Dial *86
Say “Options” or press 3.
Note: If you have new voicemail messages, Genesys Cloud automatically prompts you to review them. To go to Options when you have new voicemail messages, press 3 when the attendant starts to review the first new message.
Say “Greetings” or press 2.
Say “Record greeting” or press 2.
Record your greeting.
Press # when you have finished recording your greeting.

To complete your voicemail greeting recording, choose one of the following options:
To save your recording, say “Save prompt” or press 1.
To listen to your recording, say “Review” or press 2.
To record again, say “Rerecord” or press 3.
To leave the menu without saving your recording, say “Cancel” or press 4.

Steps: How to mute your mic and place a caller on hold
When you mute your mic or place a caller on hold, the follow happens: 
Mute your mic so that you can hear the conversation but others cannot hear you. Muting a call only silences sound on your end of the call – you can still hear the other caller. 
Holding a call silences both parties. A one-to-one call on hold plays the hold music. In a conference call, no music plays.
If you’re on a call and must mute or hold that call, follow the below steps: 
Select the Hold or Mute on the communications menu.
The button will turn red to indicate you’ve placed the caller on hold or have muted your mic.)
To place one or more interactions on hold.
One interaction
Click the interaction.
Click Hold in the call controls.
To remove the hold, click All . Note: After placing one interaction on hold, clicking Hold causes the interactions to alternate between being held. 
Multiple interactions
Click the transfer interaction.
Click Hold in the call controls.
To remove the hold, click either Hold or All.
To resume the call, select the Hold or Mute button again. 
The red color will go away indicating the call is no longer on hold or you mic muted.
NOTE: Support reps must follow the hold time guidelines when placing a call on hold. See Phone  > Hold Times KA.

Steps: How to transfer a call
Calls can be transferred to other reps, skill groups, campaigns, and to internal or external parties. There are two methods of transferring:

Transfer type
Description
Blind transfer 
(cold transfer)
The call will be transferred to the receiving rep right away without speaking to the new recipient first. You should rarely use this option.You can also choose whether the call returns to you or is routed to the receiving agent’s voicemail if they don’t accept the transfer.
Consult transfer 
(warm transfer)
Before transferring the call, talk to the new rep and offer background details about the caller’s problem. Consult transfers are best practice and should be used most often. 
The Consult button does not appear for chat, and SMS interactions. 
Reps can transfer a call on any interaction. Please note that reps should do a consult (warm) transfer most of the time. 
Here’s  how to perform a consult transfer:
While on a call, from the phone panel, click the “Transfer” icon [Image: rtaImage] in the communications menu.
Start typing out the name of the person, queue, or number and click enter. Select the intended person or queue from the list of suggestions. 
Expand your search by selecting both the “People” and “Queues” buttons from the top of the Transfer pop-up.
People appear first in the results, followed by queues and then external contacts. Each search is limited to 25 results.
[Image: rtaImage]
Transfer to a person:
When you click a person, statistics show the person’s status and number and type of interactions that the person is currently handling.
If you click an external contact who has multiple phone numbers, a list of phone numbers appears. Hover over a phone number to see the type of number it is (work, cell) and select the phone number that you want to call.
“Cannot transfer” will show if you try to transfer an interaction but the receiving rep is not assigned the permission to accept that media type.
Transfer to a queue (See a list of Queues):
When you click a queue, statistics for the queue appear.
Waiting – Number and type of interactions waiting in the queue.
Agents – Number of active and total agents in the queue.
EWT – Estimated wait time for an advocate to answer.
Click Consult. When the transfer starts, you will see a Transfer interaction with the two calls below it. 
[Image: rtaImage]
If you have one call selected and press the Hold icon, it will toggle you over to the other call. E.g., if you select the destination call (it will turn green) and then click the Disconnect icon, it will only hang up on the destination call and keep the original call. Great for if you transfer to the wrong number. 
If you have one call selected and press the Hold icon, it will toggle you over to the other call.
If the intended recipient doesn’t answer or agree to the transfer, click Cancel [Image: rtaImage].
If the intended recipient does answer, a transfer interaction appears in the display that shows the number of connected participants, and a timer that indicates how long since the transfer was started.
To interact with one caller, click on the separate interactions using the icons in the communication menu.  E.g., if you select the destination call (it will turn green) and then click the Disconnect icon, it will only hang up on the destination call and keep the original call. Great for if you transfer to the wrong number. 
If you have one call selected and press the Hold icon, it will toggle you over to the other call.
To talk to all people simultaneously, click All  [Image: rtaImage]between the interactions. All turns green, indicating that the phone connection is live between all people.
Initially, the original call is on hold and you are connected to the person or queue that you selected to consult.
[Image: rtaImage]
When you are ready to transfer the call, click Transfer[Image: rtaImage] in the communication menu. Or you can cancel the transfer.
[Image: rtaImage]
Note: Clicking Cancel does not cancel the transfer. It only causes the Transfer dialog box to disappear.
To cancel a transfer, do the following steps:
Click the interaction that you called.
Click Disconnect in the call controls.
You remain connected to the original interaction.
To complete the transfer and send the original call to its destination, you must click Transfer[Image: rtaImage]  again, and then click the Complete button.
The transfer completes and the initial call drops off your interaction list.
[Image: rtaImage]

Steps: How to use after call work and wrap up codes
After call work (ACW) should be preferred immediately after the interaction before you can receive another interaction, which includes adding notes and designating wrap-up codes. 
Wrap-up codes and the interaction log are used by the Sales team. Support advocates will continue to add notes and case categorization to their cases. 
After disconnecting the call, you are prompted to select a wrap-up code (disposition) that best describes the outcome of the interaction. 
Support: Support reps will select the applicable wrap-up code and add notes and case categorization to their cases as usual. See Salesforce KA to for case categorization information.

You are now available to handle the next interaction.
NOTE: If you close the wrap-up popup without selecting a code and clicking done, the call will remain in wrap-up. If you have calls that you have not set the wrap-up for, they will remain in your interactions until you do. 
To complete the wrap-up, click Interactions from the Main Menu, and click the red person icon. This will open the wrap-up popup for that interaction and you can complete it. 
Steps: How interaction logs work [Sales only]
Support reps log their interactions by leaving notes and case categorization on the Salesforce case.
Interaction logs are used by the Sales team. 
Interaction logging, also known as activity logging or task logging, provides a history of interactions. 
Reps can continue to update interaction logs for two minutes after the interaction disconnects. 
After two minutes, the log becomes grayed out.

Troubleshoot common issues with the Genesys Panel
If you’re experiencing issues with your phone panel, logging out of Okta and back in will likely solve most issues. Below are comment issues you may encounter and how to resolve them:
Wrong Permissions – If your menu options don't have the right Status options in the Status Menu, you likely have the wrong permissions. Submit Help Desk Ticket to have them check your permissions. 
Wrong Queue – If you are on the wrong queue, reach out to your manager. 
Trouble Hearing or Being Heard – If you are having trouble hearing or being heard, you can adjust your phone settings by clicking Settings in the Main Menu.
Unable to Place Call  – If you try to place a call and you get the Unable to Place a Call error, either your phone is not connected or your permissions are not right. Follow the “unable to place call” steps below.
Call not attaching to record –  If the “name” and “related to” fields on the interaction screen aren’t associating the call with a record. Follow the “associate call to case” steps below. 
Stuck on a screen (e.g., interactions log) – If you find yourself stuck on the interaction log, or any screen, follow the applicable steps below. ▶ "Unable to place call" error

Open your Status Menu. Under your email address, you will see a blue phone icon. 
If it says select phone, click the text. 
If you see your name, your phone is connected, but your settings may need to be adjusted. Click your name and complete this troubleshooting. 
The Status Menu will close. Type your name in the Search for Phone field. 
Click your name in the drop down. 
​​NOTE: If you do not have your mic and speaker setup and allow the browser to access them, it can prevent you from making calls. When you first set up your phone, be sure to click allow on the access pop-up.
▶ How to check microphone and speaker settings
To make sure your microphone and speaker settings are correct, follow the below steps:
Open the Main Menu and select  Settings.
Select “WebRTC.”
From the drop down options, select the applicable mic and speaker devices.
