If you find yourself stuck on the interaction log, or any screen, you can either: 
Go the main menu and interactions in order to go back to the main screen or current call. 

[Image: AD_4nXeexnbdx2pe1_iOmfB-aBHIJ35hg-n1uCVZqZF3KqlYnp_wndN3ESLdjLcG7QHBsztc7Kc4h6Ffcop8ECg7Apq28VuXLGKjavw0eCiP5Fo7hmwBDXcyajE6aLRuu16-nP9frcBw9PaSOQFxoUDjPwDZglmn]

3. FAQ
Trust and Safety
Are we still able to listen to call recordings and live calls?
Yes, individuals will have access to recordings. Users can have the ability to listen to their calls and share them as well with appropriate individuals such as supervisors, managers, and QA. This is accomplished with staggered permissioning and should be tested by our users. 
Do users have access to photos we upload in Genesys?
We do not have any integration that will pull profile information from Genesys that is public facing in any way.
Do we need to use a specific campaign for calling out?
The ability to make outbound calls are set on the user permission level.  
How do we listen to our own recordings for QA?
We will be providing additional training on this at a later date. See  Call recording in Genesys Cloud overview for a general overview. 
If T&S internal transfers back to S&S will they go through call routing?
The user should be able to be placed directly in Queue without going through routing.
Is 3-way calls something we'll use for training/ mentorship, etc.?
This is something that needs to be determined at the individual team level. 
Is T&S using YCBM to make outbound calls? Or can users call us directly?
This process will remain the same, you will not have direct lines for you to be called directly. 
Why are we okay with auto-dialing now but NOT previously?
The laws around this are ever-evolving, as updates are made to those our legal team reviews and determine if certain restrictions can be lifted and/or if new ones need to be added on a case-by-case basis. 
Will calls still show up in our incidents?
Calls will be presented as Cases as well as Activities that are associated with a Contact. Your Cases should still be associated with Incidents, so there should not be any disruption in how they are presented to agents in that manner. 
Will transferring calls to support affect how a call is logged on an incident?
When a call is transferred from one person/team to another, it creates a new task. Each person that talks to the pro or customer will have a separate task created.
Will VM be enabled in case T&S wants to explore using that function?
Yes, agents have the ability to receive and listen to voicemails. They are able to receive notifications and listen to them via their phone panel in Salesforce. See Access your voicemail - Genesys Cloud Resource Center for general information about voicemails.
Will we have a direct phone number now?
No.
Will we still have local masked numbers for outbound?
This was not a requirement that was caught originally but we are looking into options here. The go-live assumption would be going live with the 800 number only and shortly following it up by adding those local masked numbers.
Sales
How do we integrate with Zoom to ensure Zoom calls are recorded and accounted for?
We do not currently plan to integrate with Zoom. See Calling into a Zoom through the phone panel KA.
What phone number will show up on the contractor's caller ID?
Contractors will have the same phone number as the queue or project they are working on.
Where can we add notes about the call / interaction?
After wrapping up a call, you will enter the dispo (Wrap-Up Codes) and then be able to edit the interaction log and enter your notes.
Will a pros call be routed back directly to us?
Yes, the number they see calling them should also be the callback number. If you own an opportunity, the call will route directly back to you.
Will "Secure Pause" allow us to take CC#'s over the phone again?
No. You should never use Secure Pause for taking CC information over the phone. The only time Secure Pause should be used in when sensitive personal information is being shared by the pro. You should be using Secure Pay to facilitate CC requests. 
Will there disposition options available same as five9?
Yes, these will appear as wrap-up codes with the same dispos as Five9. See Wrap-Up Codes KA. 
Will we be able to use Secure Pay for the $0 upfront Premium?
Yes, any payment or CC info that needs to be collected should go through Secure Pay. See Secure Pay KA. 
Will we have any better connections with Pro's or Is this better for them reaching us easier?
The goal of Genesys is to simplify both the outbound and inbound motions of connecting with our pros. As we further roll-out Genesys, we'll unlock a lot of Omni-Channel capabilities that will allow us to better reach pros and make it easier for pros to reach us.
Will we have our own Callback number? And/or our own voicemail greeting?
Callback numbers won't be available but if you own an opportunity, the pro will always route to you. You can set up your own Voicemail greeting through your phone panel. 
Will we need to be in "on queue" for SDR transfers?
You will need to be available or on queue to accept those.
Will we see which line the pro is calling in on? Inbound line- AE- to support- back to AE? The whole "paper trail" as it were?
Yes, you can see this within Genesys. There's not a way to see it in Salesforce, but you can click the recording link to see the whole journey of the call, including their time with the IVR and bots.
Will we still have the same calling campaigns?
No. Campaigns have been simplified into two, one for S2L and one for Pro Reengagement Team (PRT). See Queues for a full list of all department queues. 
Support
Are the disabled buttons or options eventually going to be enabled?
Some never will, some might depending on changes we make. No current concrete plans to change them.
Are we not able to have it auto answer? What happens if the advocate fails to accept the call for a period of time?
Support teams - Your interactions are set to auto answer for you. 
Sales teams - If you decline or do not answer an interaction within a certain amount of time, Genesys places you into Not Responding status. While Not Responding, you don’t receive new interactions. Declined or not answered interactions are re-queued.
Can advocates listen to call recordings?
Yes
Can “secure pause” be used if a caller says they don't allow us to record the call?
No, and managers have visibility into when secure pause is used. 
Does Genesys automatically create a case for every new interaction? Will OB calls automatically create cases?
No, it'll only create cases for incoming calls - when you make an outbound call you should be on the object you want the call associated with already (cases for Support, leads, opportunities, or contacts for Sales). This functions the same as Five9. See Salesforce KA for steps on creating a quick case. 
For advocates taking phone calls, do we still have visibility into the queue with Genesys?
Yes, though your managers may need to help you find the most helpful reports to look at - it might take us a week or two to figure out how to meet this need
Will advocates start doing warm transfers for misrouted pros?
Yes, we're keeping the process of warm transfers for misrouted pros.The process:
If there's no queue or wait time of 5 minutes, they will do a warm transfer.
If there's a queue/backlog of more than 5 minutes, they'll do a cold transfer.
How long will the wait time be before the system auto transfers the call back to the queue?
30 seconds

Should advocates add their photo in their Genesys profiles?
No expectation to do this for now.
Should advocates call customers back for disconnected calls? How?
Yes, advocates call customers back for disconnected calls. The workflow remains the same. They can call them back using "new in

Front Desk (Pro)

Contents

Process

(Rep) Steps: How to find and view pro's Front Desk details

Talking points
How Front Desk works
Front Desk onboarding call
Front Desk plan prices and billing
Make changes to Front Desk plan
Resources
1. OVERVIEW
Front Desk is a service that allows pros to optimize their business on Thumbtack. By having Front Desk ready to quickly respond to customers, pros can spend less time at the computer and more time making money. 
By offering an in-house messaging service, pros can better manage their leads and focus on what they do best. Our automatic messaging to the initial customer’s response has also increased customer satisfaction, keeping customers coming back. We want Thumbtack to be a place that fits different business needs, allowing pros to grow and optimize. To our knowledge, no other marketplace like ours offers an in-house service like this.
Front Desk can also be used with other CRMs, giving pros the power to manage their workflow more efficiently. 

Note: If frontline reps have questions that aren’t answered in this article, they can post in the #front-desk-service-and-support Slack channel.  

Pros can learn more about Front Desk Enrollment.
Key points 
Here's a list of key points about Front Desk that frontline reps should know when helping pros:
Front Desk is a Thumbtack service that handles initial customer responses, freeing up the pro's time.
Front Desk can be used with other CRMs, giving pros flexibility.
Front Desk responds to all leads 24/7.
Pros get notified of customer conversions.
A "chat" is an initial response to a customer's message.
Front Desk Starter Plan: $60/month, unlimited chats.
Front Desk Enterprise Plan: $500/month, unlimited chats (for 9+ locations).
Pros are manually billed for Front Desk via Stripe, on they day they are enabled. *Midmonth sign-ups are charged the full plan amount on initiation day. 
Plans auto-renew monthly. 
Front Desk charges are not visible on the pro's Payments page. 
Invoices are emailed; look for "Your receipt from Thumbtack, Inc." from invoice+statements+acct_1AuRvhCKg9WpKK5Y@stripe.com.
Reps should not change the API status in Admin for the pro; use the Slack workflow for changes.
Reps can use the Front Desk Dynamic Tracker sheet to see a pro’s plan details.
Reps should always double-check the User PK and Service PK before submitting a FDS Workflow.
Front Desk Update Form: For message changes, plan upgrades/downgrades, pauses, and resumes.
Front Desk Cancelation Form: For cancellations.
Pros need to provide 2 business days' notice for plan changes or cancellations.
UPDATES
Effective February 10, 2025, Front Desk plans will no longer be prorated. Pros will be charged the full monthly amount on the day they sign up for or resume their Front Desk plan.
For example, if a pro signs up or resumes their services on February 14, they are charged the full plan amount on February 14. They will be charged again on March 14th. 
NOTE: When upgrading from Starter to Enterprise, the pro will still be charged a one-time prorated amount for the difference in the base price between the original plan and the new plan. Subsequent charges will be billed at the new plan’s rate.
HOW FRONT DESK WORKS 
Pros can go to the Front Desk landing page to learn more and connect with a Front Desk representative. Here’s how pros enroll in Front Desk: 
Chat with a Front Desk team member to pick a price plan that meets their customer volume needs.
Let Thumbtack know how they want us to respond to their customers. Front Desk sends the initial response to all their leads. Thumbtack recommends thanking customers for their business or collecting more information as needed.


A chat is a reply to a customer's initial message on all leads. The Front Desk plan auto renews every month unless the pro requests to cancel. 
 FRONT DESK PLANS


Thumbtack offers two Front Desk plans to help pros manage their customer communications: 

Front Desk Plans
Cost
Includes
Starter
$60 monthly recurring charge
Unlimited chats
Enterprise 
$500 monthly recurring charge
Unlimited chats
(Exclusive to pros with 9+ accounts)
A chat is defined as any reply to a customer's initial message on all leads. Both plans automatically renew each month unless you request to cancel.
Front Desk auto-responder message
Front Desk uses a single, unified response template across all service categories to automatically send an initial reply to a customer's first message on any lead.
Pros will write a custom response. It can include: 
Business name
Preferred contact number*
Website link
Calendar link
Preferred signature information
Front Desk automatically appends "Hi {customer first name}," to the beginning of any customized response. 
Frontline reps can use this Gemini Gem to optimize a pros message. It’s trained on Thumbtack data, so it knows what causes customers to become unresponsive. Pro must verbally approve the message before a rep submits the request (follow (Rep) Steps: How to help a pro make changes to their Front Desk plan)
*NOTE: If the pros reply shares their phone number, they won’t be eligible for completely unresponsive customer refunds. Pros can update their messaging to remove their number so they are eligible. Follow the (Rep) Steps: How to help a pro make changes to their Front Desk plan. Reps can refer to the internal Completely unresponsive customer refunds (Pro) KA to learn more about these refund types.
TARGET AUDIENCE FOR FRONT DESK 
All pros are eligible for Front Desk (excluding T&S flagged pros). However, Thumbtack wants to focus on pros who will be able to get the most out of this service:
Pros who typically spend ~$100 or more per week
Pros who are pretty active and receive a lot of leads
Pros who want to improve their ranking and response time
Pros who are looking to win more of their leads with quicker replies
Pros who are popular in home categories (i.e., house cleaning, electricians, handymen, etc)
BENEFITS OF FRONT DESK 
A pro’s concierge works behind the scenes, day and night. Frontline reps can use the following benefits when speaking with pros: 
Save time. Front Desk is your ultimate resource to free up hours in your schedule. Front Desk responds to ALL leads, improving your overall response time which can also help improve your ranking.
Improve response times. Customers like quick responses, and Front Desk's average response time is 2 minutes. 
Improve conversion. Did you know, responding to customers within the first 5 minutes can help improve customer conversion?
Front Desk Pros have shown:
+20% more customer conversion
+28% improved customer satisfaction scores
Focus on what you do best. Front Desk means you spend less time checking emails and new messages, and more time making money on the job.
FRONT DESK BILLING AND INVOICES
Front Desk Billing: New sign-ups (or reactivation) are charged the full monthly amount on their activation date, regardless of the day of the month. Prorated billing is no longer available.
Front Desk Invoices: Pros are sent an email invoice and receipt for their Front Desk Service once they have been charged for their monthly plan. The invoice provides a breakdown of the cost. Pros can look for their receipt by searching their email inbox for:
Subject line: Your receipt from Thumbtack, Inc 
Email from: invoice+statements+acct_1AuRvhCKg9WpKK5Y@stripe.com
Front Desk charges typically come out between the 1st and the 5th of the month.
Important note to Frontline reps: 
At this time, pros are manually billed for Front Desk via Stripe. 
Front Desk charges will not be visible on the pro’s account Payments page. 
Reps can refer to the steps below to review the pros Front Desk plan details.
3. PROCESS
(PRO) STEPS: HOW TO MAKE CHANGES TO FRONT DESK PLAN 
Pros can make changes to their Front Desk plan by submitting one of the self-service forms below. 
Make updates: To update Front Desk messaging, upgrade or downgrade Front Desk plans, or pause or reactivate their Front Desk plan, pros should submit a request through the Front Desk Update Form.  
▶ Update Front Desk MessageA few things to know when a pro requests changes to messaging or interaction instructions:
Pros should leave clear and specific instructions of what changes are to be made. 
They should also confirm the details in the message, grammar, spacing, etc. are correct before submitting the form.
Reps can use this Gemini Gem to optimize the pro's message. It's trained on Thumbtack data, so it knows what causes customers to become unresponsive.
▶ Upgrade Front Desk PlanA few things to know when a pro upgrades from Starter to Enterprise.
To upgrade from the Starter plan to the Enterprise plan, pros must have 9+ locations. 
When upgrading, the pro will be charged a one-time prorated amount for the difference in the base price between the original plan and the new plan. 
Subsequent charges will be billed at the new plan’s rate.
▶ Downgrade Front Desk PlanA few things to know when a pro downgrades from Enterprise to Starter.
When downgrading, a pro’s new plan choice will go into effect in the next new month. 
Thumbtack requires a notice 2 business days ahead of a new billing month to ensure the pro is charged the new plan rate for the new month.
▶ Pause Front DeskA few things to know when a pro temporarily pause their Front Desk service plan: 
The pro is asked for a date the pause should go into effect and a reactivation date (ideally on the 1st day of the following month).
▶ Resume Front DeskWhen resuming Front Desk, the pro is billed the full monthly amount, regardless of the day of the month. Subsequent month charges will occur on the same day in the following month.
Cancel: To cancel their Front Desk plan, pros should submit a request through the Front Desk Cancelation Form. 
▶ Cancel Front DeskA few things to know when a pro cancels their Front Desk plan
Thumbtack requires a notice of 2 business days ahead of a new billing month to ensure the pro isn’t charged for the next month. 
The pro’s service will be canceled within 48 business hours. 
Once canceled, front desk chats will stop immediately. 
Pros will not be refunded or issued a prorated amount.
Frontline reps can provide the pro with either form link as needed. 
(REP) STEPS: HOW TO CHECK A PRO'S FRONT DESK STATUS IN ADMIN

4. TALKING POINTS
The following talking points (or FAQs) are designed to help Frontline Reps effectively communicate the value and details of Front Desk to pros. Use these points as a guide during conversations to address common questions. 
HOW FRONT DESK WORKS

English FAQs
Spanish FAQs
What is Front Desk?
¿Qué es Front Desk?
Front Desk is a service Thumbtack offers that allows pros to get back time in their day while we automatically respond to the initial customer's response. 
Pros who use Front Desk can keep their response time under two minutes by setting up responses and messaging strategies for the Front Desk team to work with. 
Front Desk es un servicio que ofrece Thumbtack que permite a los profesionales recuperar el tiempo de su día, mientras nuestro equipo dedicado de agentes responde a los mensajes de los clientes de nuestros profesionales. 
Los profesionales que usan Front Desk pueden mantener su tiempo de respuesta por debajo de los dos minutos configurando respuestas personalizadas y estrategias de mensajería para que le equipo de Front Desk trabaje.
Once I sign up, how does Front Desk work?
Una vez que me registre, ¿cómo funciona Front Desk?
When you purchase a Front Desk plan, your service will be activated 2 business days later. All leads that your active business receives will be responded to 24/7 by our live Front Desk team. The team provides your customers with fast, high quality engagement using information collected from you during onboarding. You will receive notifications of successful customer conversions via email (or text if you prefer).
Al comprar un plan de Front Desk, su servicio se activará después de 2 días hábiles. Todos los prospectos directos que reciba su negocio activo, serán respondidos las 24 horas del día los 7 días de la semana por nuestros agentes de Front Desk en vivo. Los agentes brindan a los clientes un compromiso rápido y de alta calidad utilizando la información recopilada del profesional durante la incorporación. Los profesionales recibirán transcripciones y notificaciones de conversiones de clientes exitosas por correo electrónico (o mensaje de texto si lo prefieren).
What impact can Front Desk make on my business?
¿Qué impacto puede tener en mi negocio?
This service has also helped free up countless hours of time, allowing pros to focus on running their businesses while ensuring their leads are engaged with and converted at high rates. 

Pros have seen average response times of under two minutes and increases in lead conversion by 20%. Customers are happy too -- reporting 26% higher satisfaction scores (LTC and NPS) when working with pros who use Front Desk. 
Este servicio también ha ayudado a liberar incontables horas de tiempo para que los profesionales se centren en dirigir sus negocios, al mismo tiempo que aseguran que sus clientes potenciales estén comprometidos y se aumente la tasa de conviercion. Los profesionales han visto tiempos promedio de respuesta de menos de 2 minutos y aumentos en la conversión de clientes potenciales del 20%. Los clientes también están contentos – informan de un 26% de satisfacción más alta (LTC y NPS) al trabajar con profesionales que utilizan Front Desk.
What counts as a chat ?
¿Qué cuenta como un chat?
One chat = One initial response to the initial customer's message. 
1 chat = 1 conversación. Esto puede significar 1 respuesta a la cotización inicial o una conversación de ida y vuelta, según las preferencias de los profesionales.
FRONT DESK ONBOARDING CALL



English FAQs
Spanish FAQs
What can I expect after scheduling a call with the Front Desk team?
¿Qué puedo esperar después de programar una llamada con el equipo de Front Desk?
At our soonest convenience, one of our Front Desk subject matter experts will reach out to you via phone on the number requested. From there, the expert will discuss your business volume on Thumbtack along with your current response time and conversion rates to find a Front Desk plan that best fits your needs.
Uno de nuestros agentes expertos en Front Desk se comunicara con usted a la mayor brevedad posible a el número solicitado. Desde allí, el representante discutirá el volumen de negocios del profesional en Thumbtack, junto con el tiempo actual de respuesta y las tasas de conversión, para discutir un plan de Front Desk que mejor se adapte a las necesidades del profesional.
FRONT DESK PLAN PRICES AND BILLING 

English FAQs
Spanish FAQs
What are Front Desk’s pricing plans?
X
STARTER – $60/month – unlimited chats
ENTERPRISE – $500/month – unlimited chats –  (built for businesses with 9+ locations)
Coming soon
What’s the upfront commitment of Front Desk from pros?
X
The full monthly amount is charged on the day of sign-up, regardless of the service activation date within that month.
Coming soon
How will I be billed for my Front Desk service?
¿Cómo se me facturará el servicio de recepción?
Front Desk is charged on a monthly basis with the amount based on the plan purchased. 

It should be noted that the full monthly amount is charged on the day of sign-up or plan resumption, regardless of the service activation date within that month.
For example, a pro enrolling into the Starter plan will be charged $60 the day they sign up. The next month, the $60 is charged on the same day.
Coming soon
What is the reasoning behind Front Desk’s pricing structure?
¿Cuál es el razonamiento detrás de la estructura de precios?
To accommodate the lead volume and customization needs of different businesses. This service allows pros to utilize a concierge service at a fraction of the price of an in-house assistant or other messaging support services. We offer this service so you can optimize your business all in one place.
Para acomodar el volumen de clientes potenciales y las necesidades de personalización de diferentes negocios. Este servicio le permite aprovechar un servicio de conserjería a una fracción del precio de un asistente interno u otros servicios de asistencia de mensajería. Ofrecemos este servicio para que pueda optimizar su negocio todo en un solo lugar.

MAKE CHANGES TO FRONT DESK PLAN


English FAQs
Spanish FAQs
Can I pause, resume, or make changes to my Front Desk service?
¿Puedo pausar, reanudar o hacer cambios en mi servicio?
Yes, you can pause or resume your service at any point by contacting support@thumbtack.com or fill out our Front Desk Update Request Form. We require a notice of 2 business days ahead of a new billing month to ensure you aren’t charged for the next month. 

You can also contact us or fill out this form at any point to request updates to your service, such as messaging updates, changes to preferred next steps with customers, etc.
XSí, puede pausar o reanudar su servicio en cualquier momento comunicándose con support@thumbtack.com o 866-501-5809. Requerimos un aviso de 2 días hábiles antes de un nuevo mes de facturación para garantizar que no se le cobre el próximo mes. También puede comunicarse con nosotros en cualquier momento para solicitar actualizaciones de su servicio, como actualizaciones de mensajes, cambios en los próximos pasos preferidos con los clientes, etc.
Can I upgrade or downgrade my Front Desk plans?
¿Puedo subir o bajar de categoría mis planes?
Yes, you can change the plan you enroll in by contacting support@thumbtack.com or fill out our Front Desk Update Request Form. When upgrading, you will be charged a one-time fee for the difference in the base price between the original plan and the new plan, and all subsequent charges will be billed at the new plan’s rate.
Sí, usted puede cambiar el plan en el que se inscribe comunicándose con support@thumbtack.com o llamando al 866-501-5809. Al actualizarlo se le cobrará una tarifa única por la diferencia en el precio base entre el plan original y el nuevo plan y todos los cargos posteriores se facturarán a la tarifa del nuevo plan.
Can I cancel my Front Desk service?
¿Puedo cancelar mi servicio de Front Desk?
You can reach out to support@thumbtack.com or fill out our Front Desk Update Request Form to cancel your Front Desk service. You can cancel at any point but we require a notice of 2 business days ahead of a new billing month to ensure you aren't charged for the next month.
Usted puede comunicarse con support@thumbtack.com o 866-501-5809 para cancelar su servicio de Front Desk. Puede cancelar en cualquier momento, pero requerimos un aviso de 2 días hábiles antes de un nuevo mes de facturación para garantizar que no se le cobre el próximo mes.

Contents

Overview

Talking points (pro)
Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) provides information for Frontline Reps about the "Flexible Request Form" feature, which allows customers to select "I'm flexible" or "I'm not sure" options in request forms. This KA explains how this affects pros (who cannot disable these options in targeting) and customers (who must actively select the flexible choices), and covers how to handle related feedback and inquiries.
Note on targeting terminology: You may see "Targeting" and "Job preferences" terms used interchangeably throughout our internal KA resources or in-product.
Shipped experience
On March 31, 2025, Thumbtack launched V1 of an experiment that allows customers to select “I’m flexible” and “I’m not sure” answer options to eligible customer request form questions. Pros aren’t able to adjust or filter out these flexible answer options in their targeting preferences (also known as "Job preferences"). Starting May 1, 2025, Thumbtack has shipped V1 of that experiment to all pros and customers. 
How flexible answer options work: 
Flexible answer options* aim to address the issue that customers currently don’t have an adequate way to express flexibility or uncertainty about their project scope. This often leads to under-expressed demand and fewer compatible matches for pros. By allowing customers to select flexible/uncertain answers, Thumbtack aims to connect pros with more potential customers who might have previously been hesitant to submit a request, ultimately resulting in more leads for pros businesses.
Customers can select flexible answer options in eligible request form questions, in order to proceed with submitting projects when they’re flexible or not sure about the answer. 
Request form questions: 
V1 (shipped): Questions for this experience can be found on the “Flexible/Uncertainty RF v1 (shipped to 100%)” tab of the internal only Request form question updates - master list.  
Customer choice: Unlike the  ‘allow pros to suggest alternative dates’  feature, these flexible request form questions won’t automatically be chosen by default. Meaning customers must actively choose these “I’m flexible” or “I’m not sure” answers in their request form.
Pro targeting preferences: Pros are not able to disable these flexible options in their targeting preferences. 
Pro lead labeling: Thumbtack labels these as flexible leads and matches them with pros based on certain targeting preferences, similar to leads with flexible calendar availability.
Pro quote sheet impact: For request form options that relate to quote sheets, if customers select flexible or unsure answers, it will bypass any dollar amount pros have defined for other options, meaning it won't add a dollar amount to the pro’s estimate. (Note: A specific list of which questions relate to quote sheets is not available.)
*Note for reps: Flexible answer options are different from flexible availability options in the request form. To learn more, reps can refer to the Understanding flexible options and pro targeting preferences section below. For a closer look at "Allow pros to suggest alternative dates," reps can refer to the internal  Availability (Pro) KA for details on how pros manage this feature, and the internal Lead Refunds (Pro) KA for information on refund eligibility related to it.
▶ What flexible preferences in project details (pro view):

[Image: AD_4nXcO9-XwDZI7AQTRAxGzO0OVBGQ0EFzlU8BUyNYHXJOVcq9zIHxjTZWs41ao6NJGLPg46dkoLEUW1FS5BNxSGAzEfYjFRTic2CSvgndohp7bU3UUNHhtYfV9ldHhS-_e8pNSbsN-]

The image shows a Thumbtack "Project Details" screen for a "Floor installation." It highlights customer-selected flexible options: "Where will the work take place?" is "I'm flexible," "What type of property is this?" is "I'm not sure," and "When do you need this Floor installation done?" is "I'm flexible." These responses indicate the customer's uncertainty or openness on project aspects.
Understanding flexible options and pro targeting 

To effectively manage leads and understand how customer preferences impact their business, it's important for pros to differentiate between two types of flexible options customers can indicate on a request form: flexible availability options and flexible answer options. This section will detail these differences and their implications for pro targeting.

1. Flexible Availability Options (e.g., "Allow pros to suggest alternative dates")

Customer Action: Customers must uncheck the “Allow pro to suggest other dates” if the dates they have selected are not flexible (this box is checked by default). 
Pro Control: In the baseline experience, pros can set their availability by blocking times off on their Thumbtack calendar to prevent receiving leads with this type of calendar flexibility.
Purpose: Primarily pertains to the timing or scheduling of the project.

2. Flexible Answer Options (e.g., "I'm flexible," "I'm not sure")

Customer Action: Customers must actively choose these specific options within eligible request form questions (introduced in V1). They are not automatically selected.
Pro Control: Pros cannot disable or filter out these specific "Flexible Answer Options" in their targeting preferences. This means pros will receive leads where customers have actively selected these choices.
Purpose: Relates to the scope, details, or specific requirements of the project, beyond just timing (e.g., property type, work location, etc.).

How Flexible Answer Options Impact Pros:

Existing Override: The targeting override for flexible answer options operates similarly to how "flexible availability" leads are handled.
Lead Labeling: Thumbtack labels leads with flexible answer options as flexible leads and matches them with pros based on general targeting preferences, acknowledging the customer's indicated flexibility.
Quote Sheet Impact: For request form options tied to pro quote sheets, if customers select 'flexible' or 'unsure' answers, any dollar amounts pros defined for other options will be bypassed. A specific list of these affected questions is not available.
For a more detailed understanding of how pros manage "Flexible Availability Options" (like "Allow pros to suggest alternative dates"), reps can refer to the internal Availability (Pro) KA , and for related refund policies, consult the internal Lead Refunds (Pro)  KA.
Key points
Here are some key points for Frontline reps helping pros who have received leads with "Flexible" or "Unsure" answers:
Customers must actively choose these flexible options; they are not selected by default.
When a customer selects "I'm flexible" or "I'm not sure," these options will be visible in the lead's project details.
Pros cannot disable or filter out these flexible/unsure options in their targeting preferences, meaning they will receive these leads. Pros can request refunds as usual. 
 Flexible selections do not affect the pro's quote sheet prices; any associated dollar amounts will be bypassed.
Frontline reps can find the specific questions that offer flexible/unsure options in the "Flexible/Uncertainty RF v1 (shipped to 100%)" tab of the internal only Request form question updates - master list sheet.
Customer experience
▶ 🤖 Background notes
[AI Context]: The "Customer experience" section details how customers interact with and utilize the flexible options in the request form, informing Frontline Reps on how to answer customer questions or provide guidance about these features.
Customers will have the option to select flexible or unsure answers to certain questions in eligible request forms (reps can refer to the internal only Request form question updates - master list for those questions). These options must be intentionally selected (it doesn’t automatically default to the flexible options).
For multi-select type questions, selecting a flexible or unsure option will remove any previously selected options.
▶ What it looks like: Request Form Flexible Options
The image below shows an example of a multiple choice question in a request form. And if the customer selects the flexible option of “I'm not sure,” then it'll remove the selection for “Home” or “Business.” 

[Image: AD_4nXdpVSretdltWhb5-LmpHihHhpMDb2TqZ0L9fF4FMH818MB5m-qf2t_0HnNr9MwFuq_4gQIBFs-feLf-xFAmdn5XYMD6gb1Hx6K7qFqfjHIJ_C9PDACQ6wRXTph1s4mzFTNNYxz7_w]

Pro experience
▶ 🤖 Background notes
[AI Context]: The "Pro experience" section outlines how the "Flexible Request Form" options appear to pros when customers select them and explains the limitations pros have regarding these options, providing essential context for Frontline Reps addressing pro concerns or questions.
Pros will see leads with “I’m flexible” or “I’m not sure” answers if the customer decides to select a flexible answer option in an eligible request form question. 
Targeting preferences: These flexible answers will not show up in the pro’s targeting preferences, so pros can’t remove these flexible options from their preferences. This means pros can’t choose whether or not they want to receive these flexible leads. 
Notifications and Lead labeling: Pros will not be notified of this change. However, these leads are labeled as flexible leads and match customers with pros based on certain targeting preferences, similar to leads with flexible calendar availability.
Quote sheet impact: For request form options that relate to quote sheets, if customers select flexible or unsure answers, it will bypass any dollar amount pros have defined for other options, meaning it won't add a dollar amount to the pro’s estimate. (Note: A specific list of which questions relate to quote sheets is not available.)
▶ What flexible preferences in project details (pro view):
The screenshot below shows an example of flexible options selected in a Floor installation request form

[Image: AD_4nXe4bJg42NatTSAApPy4xaJG9bCM3WSAM5vI3zx9eClzcU1j5fNJqQGVMr4Y9GladxbIPNK-DILfLApfEux4ZD1hLaRVRpw0MvTJbpuLmVpB2bRjo97u9tv-r49pHjPUC8TxqgYz4g]

Refunds: Pros can submit a refund request with "job outside of preferences" as the reason, as this situation falls under the existing refund policy, mentioning that they cannot un-target flexible or unsure answers. Refund Ops will handle these requests according to the standard refund policy.

Refund Policy for Flexible Request Form Experiment

The standard refund policy is in effect for pros who receive leads with "flexible" or "unsure" answers from customers, with specific conditions for this experiment.

Pros are eligible for refunds if they receive a lead that doesn't align with their specific targeting preferences due to a customer selecting "flexible" or "unsure" answers.
Pros should submit a refund request through the usual in-product process, selecting "job outside of preferences" as the reason and mentioning that they cannot un-target "flexible" or "unsure" answers.
▶ Internal information: Refund eligibility:
 Refund Ops will approve refund requests if:

The customer selected "flexible" or "unsure."
There are no targeting preferences for pros to opt out of these answers for the specific question.
The pro has set specific targeting preferences for that question (e.g., targeting only some options and not all).
Refunds will not be granted if the pro's preferences are set to accept all available options for that question.

Refund Ops will review and process requests, noting "flexmismatch" in the admin notes for tracking.

Key Takeaways
Pros will be charged for these leads initially.
Refunds for mismatched leads due to "flexible" or "unsure" answers (from experiment) are refunded as ‘jobs outside, as outlined above.
The standard refund process applies. Reps can refer to the internal Lead Refunds (Pro) KA  to learn more. 
End of internal only information.

2. Process
Steps: How to help impacted pros with refund requests (Rep) 
Support reps working with a pro who requests a refund because of preference mismatches due to customers selecting “unsure” or “flexible” will follow these steps:
Direct the pro to submit a refund request in-product
▶ Talking point:To request a refund for this lead, please submit a request using this link: https://www.thumbtack.com/profile/payments/. 
Let the pro know that they should select "job outside of preferences" as the reason for the refund request and mention that they are unable to untarget flexible or unsure answers.
▶ Talking point:For this specific situation, the best refund reason to select is 'job outside of preferences.' And, just so we have all the details, please also mention that those 'flexible' or 'not sure' answers weren't something you could un-target on your end.
Reminder: Don’t promise that the pro will receive a refund (as usual). Refer to the <Lead Refunds KA > for more refund information. 
Pros can also request a refund when they decline an exact match lead. Thumbtack asks the pro why they declined, and from there, they'll see the option to “Get help with a charge."
Steps: Sharing feedback on flexible request form options (Rep)
When a pro or customer provides feedback about the "Flexible Request Form" feature, frontliner reps will follow these steps to ensure it's properly logged:
Identify the User and Feedback Theme: Determine if the feedback is from a Pro or a Customer, and then select the most appropriate feedback theme from the table below.
Pro Feedback Themes:
[Targeting] Pro wants to opt out of the 'unsure' / 'flexible' answers: Use if the pro wants to remove flexible/unsure options from their targeting preferences but can't find them.
[Lead quality] Pros receiving more low quality leads due to flexible/unsure RF: Use if the pro reports receiving more low-quality leads because of the flexible/unsure options.
Customer Feedback Theme:
[Targeting] Cx found it easier to match with pros with flexible answers.: Use if the customer shares that the flexible/unsure options helped them find a suitable pro.

Fake or Scammy Leads (Pro)

Contents

Overview
Fake job warning signs
Refunds on scam/fake leads (terms of use violations)
Process
(Rep) Steps: How to help a pro concerned a lead is fake
(Pro) Steps: How to report a suspicious lead 
Talking points
How Thumbtack prevents scams
Pro says customer is fake or Thumbtack is a scam 
How to report a lead
Fake job warning signs
Pro wants refund on lead
Lead found not to be fake (Refund was denied) 
Resources
1. Overview 
Although Thumbtack has teams dedicated to verifying requests through automated processes and manual reviews, occasionally, illegitimate requests do get through.
When Thumbtack finds a lead that turns out to be a scam, the lead and the customer will be removed. Any affected pros are also refunded.
If a pro suspects any deceptive behavior from a customer, they can report it.
Common terms frontline reps may hear include: 
Spam, spammy
Scam, scammy
Fake, questionable, or suspicious
Deceptive, deceptive practice/s, DPI (deceptive practice identification)
NOTE: Frontline reps should no't mention Thumbtack's standing with the Better Business Bureau (BBB). Even though Thumbtack has an A+ rating, we don't want to call attention to the BBB.
▶ Internal info only: Thumbtack’s actions to prevent scam/fake leads
Thumbtack’s actions to prevent scam/fake leads include: 
Prevention: Before a request is shown to a pro, we have a contact verification process that flags suspicious requests for manual review.
Detection: We have models that review each request and message and flag them for manual review if they look suspicious.
Response: Ghosting (and blocklisting), deleting, or putting on hold a customer account, then refunding any affected pro accounts when applicable.
Hold placed on customer account
If Thumbtack suspects any deceptive behavior from a customer, Trust and Safety (T&S) will place a hold on the customer's account. This hold will remain in place until Thumbtack conducts a thorough investigation. The hold is typically lifted within 48 hours. If the investigate finds spammy behavior, the T&S team takes appropriate action by blocklisting and ghosting the customer account. To learn more, see Account Holds (Customer) KA.
If a pro suspects any deceptive behavior from a customer, they can report it.
▶ Talking point: What does Thumbtack do to prevent scams?
Leads on Thumbtack are one of our top priorities. We have teams dedicated to catching scams, both through automated processes and manual reviews. When we find a lead that turns out to be a scam, we remove the lead and the customer, then refund any affected pros.
Fake job warning signs (when to report) 
If a pro experiences behavior from a customer that makes them uncomfortable or seems suspicious, they should report it. This includes situations when a customer asks a pro to: 
Share unnecessary personal information (like social security number or banking information).
Contact or forward money to an outside party.
Wire funds via Western Union, Moneygram, or another wire service.
Receive payment through or sign up for an unfamiliar payment service.
Pay more for your services so you can pay other professionals.
▶ Talking point: When should I submit a report?
Thumbtack works hard to screen requests, but you should also be on the lookout. If something feels off, it probably is. If you experience behavior from a customer that makes you uncomfortable or seems suspicious, please report it. This could include situations when a customer asks you to: 
Share unnecessary personal information (like your social security number or banking information).
Contact or forward money to an outside party.
Wire funds via Western Union, Moneygram, or an other wire service.
Receive payment through or sign up for an unfamiliar payment service.
Pay more for your services so you can pay other professionals.
Reporting suspicious behavior helps us keep our site safe and trustworthy. Even though almost all Thumbtack customers are legitimate, we know there are rare exceptions. So, if you see something that doesn't look right, let us know.
Refunds on scam/fake leads (Terms of Use violations)
If a lead doesn’t meet Thumbtack’s Terms of Use, the pro will likely not have to pay for the lead, and Thumbtack will review the lead to confirm whether it violates the Terms of Use or not. 
When Thumbtack finds a lead that is confirmed to be scammy, the following happens: 
The lead will be deleted
The customer account will be blocklisted and ghosted
Affected pros will be refunded for the lead. 
Pro steps: If a pro receives a lead they feel is suspicious, they should report the customer to request a refund. Pros will find steps in the How to report suspicious activity – Thumbtack Help article.
NOTE: Before a refund is issued, the Proactive team needs to review the lead. Pros will receive an update within two to three business days.
2. Process
(Rep) Steps: How to help a pro concerned a lead is fake 
If a pro contacts support about a lead they believe is questionable or seems suspicious, Support reps can help them by following the steps below. 
Thank the pro for contacting Thumbtack about their concerns.
Talking point: 
Thanks for reporting this to us. I’m sorry you’re having this experience - I'm sure it can be frustrating to receive a lead you believe is [fake/a scam]. I’d like to gather some details about your experience so I can send this over to our Trust and Safety team who handles these issues.
Ask the pro what concerns them about the lead and note their details in the case in Tack. 
For example, did the customer ask them to:
Share unnecessary personal information like their social security number or banking information?
Contact or forward money to an outside party?
Wire funds through Western Union, Moneygram, or another wire service?
Talking point: 
Can you tell me what concerns you about this lead? Did they share unnecessary personal information with you, ask to contact or forward money to an outside part, or bring up wiring funds through a wire service?
Escalate the case by following the “report a new incident” steps in the internal Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA to the Proactive team.
Talking point: 
Thanks for sharing those details about your experience. I’ve sent them over to our Trust and Safety team who handles these issues to be reviewed. 
Tell the pro they’ll receive an update in two to three business days.
Talking point: 
Thank you again for reporting this to us. Our Trust and Safety team will conduct a thorough review of the lead and will reach out to you with updates as soon as they can. Please allow 1 to 2 business days for our team to investigate the issue. You’ll typically receive an update about your concern within two to three business days. 
Teach them how they can flag these in the future (through the invite email* or by clicking Report in the messenger). 
Talking point: 
Leads on Thumbtack is one of our top priorities. We have teams dedicated to catching scams, both through automated processes and manual reviews. In the future, if you believe a lead is a scam, you can use the “report” feature in the messenger with the customer or in the email notification. We’ll ask you to share the details of your concern and we'll send it directly to a specialized team to be reviewed. 
If the pro wants a refund, the Proactive team needs to review the lead before Thumbtack gives a refund. 
Talking point: 
I’m sorry you’re having this experience - I'm sure it can be frustrating to receive a lead you believe is [fake/suspicious/a scam]. I’m not able to issue a refund on the lead, because I’m not on the team that reviews these types of concerns. After reporting a lead, our Trust and Safety team conducts a thorough review of the lead and will reach out to you with updates as soon as they can. Please allow 1 to 2 business days for our team to investigate the issue. Additionally, you can track the status of a refund from your Payments page and in the messenger with a customer.
NOTE: If the pro believes the customer's phone number is fake, see the Invalid Phone Number section of the internal Lead Refunds (Pro) KA for talking points and more info. 
(Pro) Steps: How to report a suspicious lead
Reports are an important part of Thumbtack’s trust and safety efforts and help Thumbtack keep track of behavior that isn’t allowed on the. 
Pro steps: To report something, pros can go to messenger with the customer and click report. For full steps, pros will follow these steps in the How to report suspicious activity – Thumbtack Help 
Article. 
Thumbtack will review the report within 24 hours and share an update with the pro on any next steps Thumbtack took.
Tip! For email cases, frontline reps can send the pro email template: “Fake request: How to report a suspicious lead”
In-product view of reporting a lead in messenger 
Click “Report” in the messenger.

3. Talking points
How Thumbtack prevents scams
What does Thumbtack do to prevent scams?
Leads on Thumbtack is one of our top priorities. We have teams dedicated to catching scams, both through automated processes and manual reviews. When we find a lead that turns out to be a scam, we remove the lead and the customer and refund pros who were affected.
¿Qué hace Thumbtack para prevenir las estafas de cheques?
Los prospectos en Thumbtack son una de nuestras prioridades principales. Contamos con equipos dedicados a la detección de estafas, tanto a través de procesos automatizados como de revisiones manuales. Cuando encontramos un prospecto que resulta ser una estafa, lo eliminamos como prospecto y cliente y reembolsamos a los profesionales afectados.
Pro says the customer is fake or Thumbtack is a scam

These customers are fake! Your company is a scam.
We're your partner — fake requests do not benefit us, and it is something we would never do. We only succeed when your business succeeds. Sometimes it does take a few attempts before you get hired on Thumbtack, but we're here to help you find success.
I’d be happy to take a few minutes with you right now to look over your profile and job preferences to see if there’s anything I can help you improve or update.
Note for frontline rep: If the pro wants more evidence, offer to show them search results. In search results, they'll see real-time examples of pros in their area who are succeeding and getting hired. You can also refer them to our press page for more examples that can build trust.
¡Estos clientes son falsos! Tu empresa es una estafa.
Somos su socio: las solicitudes falsas no nos benefician y es algo que nunca haríamos. Solo tenemos éxito cuando su negocio tiene éxito. A veces se necesitan algunos intentos antes de que le contraten en Thumbtack, pero estamos aquí para ayudarle a encontrar el éxito.
Me complacerá tomar unos minutos con usted ahora mismo para revisar su perfil y sus preferencias laborales y ver si hay algo que pueda ayudarlo a mejorar o actualizar. 
[NOTE: See note in talking point above]
How to report a lead 
How can I report a lead I think is fake?
If you believe a lead is a scam, you can use the “report” feature in the messenger. We ask you to share the details of your concern and we'll send it directly to a specialized team to be reviewed. You’ll receive an update about your concern within two to three business days. 
¿Cómo puedo informar de un prospecto que creo que es falso?
Si cree que un prospecto es una estafa, puede utilizar la función “report” en el mensajero. Le pedimos que comparta los detalles de su inquietud y enviaremos la información directamente a un equipo especializado para su revisión. Recibirá una actualización sobre su inquietud en un plazo de dos a tres días laborales.
Fake job warning signs
What should I be looking out for to know if a job is fake?
While almost all of our jobs are from customers interested in hiring a pro, we know there are occasional exceptions. We're working to prevent these. Be sure to check the leads you receive for these possible warning signs:
Multiple leads from the same customer on the same day.
A customer who asks for personal information you wouldn’t normally share.
A customer who asks you to contact or forward money to an outside party.
¿Qué debo tener en cuenta para saber si un trabajo es falso?
Si bien casi todos nuestros trabajos provienen de clientes interesados en contratar a un profesional, sabemos que hay excepciones ocasionales. Estamos trabajando para prevenirlos. Asegúrese de verificar los prospectos que recibe en busca de estas posibles señales de advertencia:
Varias solicitudes del mismo prospecto el mismo día.
Un cliente que solicita información personal que normalmente no compartiría.
Un cliente que le pide que se comunique o que le envíe dinero a una tercera persona.
Pro wants refund on lead/booking charge
I want a refund on a lead I reported as being fake!
I’m not on the team that reviews these types of concerns, so I'm not sure. Our Trust and Safety team will conduct a thorough review of the lead and they’ll reach out to you with updates as soon as they can. Please allow 1 to 2 business days for our team to investigate the issue. 
Quiero que me devuelvan mi dinero, ¿cuándo recibiré un reembolso?
No estoy en el equipo que revisa este tipo de preocupaciones, así que no estoy seguro. Nuestro equipo de Confianza y Seguridad llevará a cabo una revisión extensa de los cargos y estarán en contacto con usted con más información lo más pronto posible. Por favor espere de 1 a 2 días laborales para que nuestro equipo investigue el problema.
Lead found not to be fake / refund denied

I think Thumbtack is a scam and I just want my money back. (found not to be a fake lead)
While we aren’t able to issue a refund back to your card I want to take a look at your account to see what we can do to help you be successful on Thumbtack. I can assure you that we are not in the business of scamming people. We wouldn’t be successful if we did that. We truly want you to be successful, so let’s take a look at these leads and your account together, and we’ll see what we can do.
Creo que Thumbtack es una estafa y solo quiero que me devuelvan mi dinero.
Si bien no podemos otorgar un reembolso a su tarjeta, quiero revisar su cuenta para ver qué podemos hacer para ayudarlo a tener éxito en Thumbtack. Le puedo asegurar que no estamos en el negocio de estafar a la gente. No tendríamos éxito si hiciéramos eso. Realmente queremos que tenga éxito, así que revisemos sus prospectos y su cuenta juntos, para ver qué podemos hacer.
The customer's phone number is fake! Why was my refund request denied?
[For talking point, see the Invalid Phone Number section of the internal Lead Refunds KA]

Contents
Overview
Program details and timelines
Detroit-Warren-Dearborn CBSA
Pet pros (Project Walnut)
Pro experience and messaging rules
Restrictions on free version of Front Desk
Initial message templates
Updates and service changes

1. OVERVIEW
In 2023 Thumbtack launched a market campaign offering a free version of Front Desk to pros in Detroit CBSA and pet pros. For specifics, refer to the program details and timelines section below. Pros who enrolled before the enrollment cutoff still have this free version active. There is currently no plan to revoke the free service for these specific pros.

This free version of Front Desk is different from the standard 30, 60, or 90-day Front Desk trials bundled when a pro purchases a Plus ($300), Premium ($600), or Enterprise ($1000+) prepaid sales package.

NOTE FOR REPS: Do not mention these free Front Desk offers to pros who are not explicitly included in these target audiences. 
Program details and timelines
Detroit-Warren-Dearborn CBSA Experiment
What it is: A market-based efficiency experiment that offered the top 50% (~600) of pros in the Detroit market Front Desk for free.
Target audience: Pros in Detroit-Warren-Dearnborn CBSA not enrolled in Front Desk
Timeline: 
Communications began February 13, 2023 
The activation "flip" occurred on February 20, 2023
Enrollment officially stopped around May 1, 2023
Current standing: Pros who successfully enrolled before the cutoff still have this free version active. There is currently no plan to revoke the free service for these specific pros.
▶ How to identify in Salesforce: Review the pro's contact page. Impacted users will display a prominent FD Detroit Flip flag.[Image: rtaImage]
Pet pros (Project Walnut)
What it is: A limited-time offer (not positioned to pros as an experiment or pilot) to improve customer experiences and prepare for an upcoming corporate retail partnership (in 2023).
Target Audiences:
Active pet pros: 1+ contact in the last 60 days and targeting turned on in the last 30 days (~3,100 pros). They were auto-enrolled on July 12, 2023, unless they opted out.
Dormant pet pros: No contacts in the last 60 days and targeting turned off for 180+ days (~30,000 pros). Offered an opt-in path through July 12, 2023, to encourage reactivation.
▶ Eligible pet categories:
Animal training and behavior modification (non-canine)
Aquarium services
Cat grooming
Dog daycare
Dog fence installation
Dog grooming
Dog training
Dog walking
House sitting
Pet boarding
Pet sitting
Timeline: 
Communications began June 29, 2023 
The activation "flip" for Active pros occurred on July 12, 2023
Enrollment (opt-in) officially stopped for Dormant pros on July 12, 2023
Current standing: Pros who successfully enrolled (opted-in) or were automatically enrolled before the cutoff still have this free version active. There is currently no plan to revoke the free service for these specific pros.
▶ How to identify in Salesforce: The pro’s Contact Page under the Campaign History section will show Project Walnut: Active Pet Pro Front Desk Flip[Image: rtaImage]
2. Pro experience and messaging rules
Restrictions on free version of Front Desk 

The free version of Front Desk provided under these programs has explicit product constraints compared to the standard, paid version:
Single-Template Limit: Like the baseline automated experience of Front Desk, pros in the free version of Front Desk are strictly limited to an initial conversation responder using a single response template across all of their service categories.
No Upgrades: Pros cannot upgrade to paid packages while they remain active on the free version of Front Desk
Initial message templates
 
Front Desk automatically appends "Hi {customer first name}," to the beginning of any customized response. Pros can choose from three generic templates or submit their own custom response:

Response Type
Template Text / Allowed Information
Prewritten option 1
"Hi [Customer name]! Thank you for choosing us. We’re excited to work with you on your project. Please reach out if you have any follow-up questions."
Prewritten option 1
"Hi [Customer name]! I got your request and would love to help you with your project. What would be the best way to communicate: phone or Thumbtack messaging?"
Prewritten option 1
"Hi [Customer name], I’d be happy to assist you but I need some additional information first. Please let me know a good time to call, or feel free to contact me directly."
Customized Option (Recommended)
Pros can write a custom reply. It can include: Business name, preferred contact number, website link, calendar link, and preferred signature information.

Note: Pro who were auto-enrolled but failed to select a message preference, Thumbtack randomly assigned one of the prewritten templates.
Updates & service changes
Pros can update their initial message or cancel/opt-out of the free offer at any time by filling out a Front Desk Update Form. The forms differ based on the campaign they are in: 
Pet pros: Front Desk Update Request Form
Detroit pros: Font Desk Update Request Form
Fulfillment SLAs: Any modifications or cancellation requests take 24 to 48 hours for the Front Desk team to fully process and deploy.
3. TALKING POINTS
This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros who get a free version of Front Desk. Use these talking points to ensure consistent and accurate messaging.

English talking points
What is Front Desk?
A: Front Desk is a service Thumbtack offers that allows pros to get back time in their day while our dedicated team of agents responds to your customer messages. 
Pros who use Front Desk can keep their response time under two minutes by setting up responses and messaging strategies for the Front Desk team to work with. 
What impact can this free version of Front Desk make on my business?
This service has also helped free up countless hours of time, allowing pros to focus on running their businesses while ensuring their leads are engaged with and converted at high rates. 
Pros have seen average response times of under two minutes and increases in lead conversion by 20%. Customers are happy too -- reporting 26% higher satisfaction scores (LTC and NPS) when working with pros who use Front Desk. 
Can I send different initial messages based on the category in this free version of Front Desk? 
We can only send the same message to all customers for all categories. 
Can I upgrade my free version of Front Desk?
No. In the free service, we can only send the same message to all customers for all categories. 
Can I cancel my free version of Front Desk?
You can reach out to support@thumbtack.com or fill out the [pet pros: Front Desk Update Request Form / Detroit pros: Font Desk Update Request Form] to cancel your Front Desk service. You can cancel at any point.
When does my free version of Front Desk begin and end?
Your free Front Desk offer will start sending responses to your leads on [Detroit: February 20, 2023 / Pet pros: July 12, 2023] and continue indefinitely. Before we make any changes to your free Front Desk offer, we will be sure to communicate changes well beforehand.
4. INTERNAL FAQS
If a pet pro previously opted out, can they opt back in for free? 
Yes.
What if a Detroit pro was already paying for Front Desk before the experiment? 
If a pro was using Front Desk and is in the experiment variant, we would inform them that they will no longer be billed for their service for an indefinite amount of time, which is subject to change. Any changes to their billing will always be communicated via email.
Can duplicate messages occur? 
Yes. Remind activated pros that because Front Desk replies instantly, they should avoid sending immediate manual text responses to avoid duplicate messaging.

There are two ways to experience the Thumbtack product outside the U.S., which include staging (also known as dogfooding) and the pro app simulator. Support reps can utilize the varying tools for different reasons. 
The Pro App Simulator is a clickable prototype designed to mimic the app’s visual flow using static images, similar to a slideshow.
Staging provides a live version of the product on the web, iOS, and Android within a controlled environment that mirrors production, with safeguards in place
Fun Fact: What is Dogfooding? Dogfooding refers to testing a product internally before it’s released to the public.
Important: Both staging and the pro app simulator are strictly for internal use and should not be shared externally.
▶ Key Points
Here are some high-level key points for Support reps to keep in mind when using staging and the simulator:
[Image: unchecked]Staging (Dogfooding) 
Purpose: Provides a live, controlled environment to experience the product without impacting real users.
Access: Requires specific login credentials.
Benefits: Offers the most authentic and up-to-date product experience.
Use Cases: Creating fake leads, responding to inquiries, testing processes like refunds, exploring the product.
[Image: unchecked]Pro App Simulator
Purpose: Mimics the app's visual flow using static images.
Access: No login required.

Feedback: Feedback on the simulator is encouraged via the Figma link..
Pro App Simulator

Use the simulator directly in this KA for easy access. However, if you prefer to open the simulator in Figma itself, you can do so using the provided link.
The simulator is a clickable prototype designed to mimic the app’s visual flow using static images, similar to a slideshow. Things to know about the simulator include: 
Does not require an actual email and password to log in making access seamless. 
Also Eliminates the risk of disrupting real pros and causing issues. 
Simulates key functionality visually but doesn’t offer the full app experience.
Does not reflect experiments or the latest product updates and is not an exact replica of the live app. 
Should not be used to replicate or troubleshoot bugs.
▶ Guidelines for using the simulator ▲ ▼

Support reps should follow these guidelines when using the simulator: 
The simulator is strictly for internal use and should not be shared externally.
It is not an exact replica of the live product and does not display ongoing experiments.
Access the simulator by clicking this LINK. Reps should consider bookmarking it for convenience.
Hotspots indicate the areas where navigation is possible within the simulator.
When to use the simulator: Reps can use the simulator while supporting pros to help them reference the product and navigate the app seamlessly. *Please note that it is not an exact replica of the live product.
When not to use the simulator:  Avoid using the simulator for troubleshooting bugs.
Staging (DogFooding)
Staging provides a live version of the product on the web, iOS, and Android within a controlled environment that mirrors production, with safeguards in place. Things to know about staging include: 
Eliminates the risk of disrupting real pros and causing issues. 
Offers the most authentic and up-to-date product experience.
Interacting with the product through staging offers an optimal experience. 
Allows you to create fake leads, respond to fake inquiries, and navigate processes like refunds.
To access the staging environment, visit d.thumbtack.com/pro, click "Login," and use the credentials provided by your manager. For detailed instructions on accessing staging on web, iOS, and Android, refer to the steps outlined in this slide deck.
For those without smartphones or who prefer not to install testing apps, staging on the web is an excellent option. Pair it with the Pro App Simulator to quickly view and interact with the iOS app.
For a closer look, see Guidelines for using staging
▶ Guidelines for using Staging

Support reps should follow these guidelines when using staging: 
Staging is strictly for internal use and should not be shared externally.
Refer to this slide deck for detailed instructions on accessing staging for web, iOS, and Android.
Test accounts have already been set up. Support reps should reach out to their manager for the login credentials. Note that these accounts use fake email addresses, so password recovery is not possible. Avoid resetting the password to prevent access issues.

When to use staging: Reps are encouraged to use staging to help pros and navigate the product while helping pros. Feel free to explore and experiment with staging to deepen your understanding of how the product works.
Disclaimer 
It’s important that Support reps understand the following disclaimer when using Staging or the Thumbtack Pro App Simulator: 
Staging and the Thumbtack Pro App Simulator are designed for demonstration purposes only. By using this Simulator, you agree that you will not, under any circumstances, share the Simulator and staging, or the images/screens contained therein with anyone who is not a Thumbtack employee. You may only use the Simulator/Staging to aid in troubleshooting or discussing product features with pros. Sharing this Simulator with persons not employed by Thumbtack will result in disciplinary action.
Additionally, by using this Simulator/Staging you understand that it may not fully reflect the current pro user experience. Certain features, buttons, or functionality may be missing, and some screens may not display the latest updates due to ongoing product changes. The Simulator does not include current experiments. By using the Simulator, you acknowledge and agree that it may not match the exact experience of Thumbtack pro users, and any differences are not indicative of the final product.
Keeping the simulator current
Staging offers the most up-to-date product experience.
The Field Enablement Design Team aims to update the Pro App Simulator with critical changes within one to two weeks. Non-critical updates may follow a monthly or quarterly schedule. Since the simulator is built using screenshots, product changes won’t be reflected immediately.
You can view the embedded simulator for a quick look or open the Figma link for the full interactive experience.
Leave feedback about the simulator

To leave feedback about the simulator, Support reps will need to open the simulator using the provided Figma link. Once the simulator is open in Figma, follow these steps:
Click the chat bubble in the top left corner of the simulator.
Select any area on the screen to leave a comment. 
Press ‘Escape’ to exit comment mode. 
While we may not be able to implement all suggestions, we encourage you to share your insights.
2. Internal FAQs 
Will there be an Android App Simulator?
Our engineering team has worked to align the Android and iOS apps, making them nearly identical. As a result, an Android Simulator is unlikely at this time. However, if significant differences between the apps arise and the success of this simulator warrants it, we may reconsider.
Will there be a Customer App Simulator?
We're evaluating the success of the iOS Pro App Simulator, and if it proves effective, we may consider developing a customer version.
How can I provide feedback on the simulator?
We welcome your feedback! To leave feedback about the simulator, open the Figma link and click the chat bubble in the top left corner of the simulator, select any area on the screen to leave a comment, and press ‘Escape’ to exit comment mode. Not all suggestions can be implemented, but we encourage you to share your thoughts.
How will the simulator be updated?
The simulator is built using screenshots, so changes won’t appear immediately. Critical updates will be reflected within a week or two, while non-critical updates may follow a monthly or quarterly schedule.
How can I access the simulator in the future?
You can access the simulator directly within this KA. You can also continue to use the Figma link provided.

Accordion body...
The Customer App Simulator is a valuable tool designed to help frontline reps understand and visualize the customer's journey and experience within the Thumbtack Customer app. This simulator represents the baseline customer-facing interface and does not cover experiments currently running in the live product. It provides a visual representation of the baseline experience, allowing reps to quickly reference screens, flows, and common customer interactions.
Note: This internal knowledge article is about the customer app simulator. For information on the Pro App Simulator or about staging/dog fooding, reps should refer to the internal Experience the Product: Staging and the Pro App Simulator (Rep) KA.
Key points
Frontline Reps can keep the following in mind when using the Customer App Simulator:
Purpose: The Customer App Simulator mimics the app's visual flow using static images.
Access: No login is required. It is embedded directly into this knowledge article (KA) and also accessible via a provided Figma link.
Benefits: It offers quick and easy access for reference and eliminates the risk of disrupting real customers.
Limitations: The Customer App Simulator covers the baseline experience. It does not reflect all features, updates, or experiments, and should not be used to replicate or troubleshoot bugs.

The simulator is a clickable prototype designed to mimic the customer app’s visual flow using static images, similar to a slideshow. 
Guidelines for using the customer app simulator
To ensure the simulator remains a helpful and accurate resource, please adhere to the following guidelines:
Internal Use Only: The Customer App Simulator is for internal Thumbtack use only. It is not to be shared with customers, pros, or any external parties.
Reference Tool: This simulator is a visual reference tool to aid your understanding of the customer app. It is not an exact, live replica of the current customer product and may not display ongoing experiments or real-time data.
▶ When to Use:
Frontline Reps can use the simulator in the following situations to effectively support customers and navigate the app.
To quickly reference how a particular feature or flow appears to a customer.
To understand the visual steps a customer might take during their app journey.
When supporting customers and needing a visual aid to follow their potential path in the app.
(Internal note: Please note that it is not an exact replica of the live product.)
▶ When NOT to Use:
Frontline Reps should avoid using the simulator in these specific scenarios to ensure accuracy and prevent issues
For troubleshooting customer-reported bugs or issues (refer to live app logs and relevant internal tools for this).
To demonstrate "live" functionality or specific customer accounts.
To test new features or experiments (use staging environments for this).
Avoid using the simulator for troubleshooting bugs.
Built-out experiences in the customer app simulator
Use the simulator to explore all tabs in the Customer app. Try booking a pro, using the search functionality, adding pros to your team, adding projects to your plan, messaging a pro, and more. Explore the app's flow to understand customer interactions better, test different scenarios, and get familiar with common customer journeys.
Disclaimer

Frontline Reps must understand the following disclaimer when using the Thumbtack Customer App Simulator:
The Thumbtack Customer App Simulator is designed for demonstration purposes only. By using this Simulator, Frontline Reps agree that they will not, under any circumstances, share the Simulator or the images/screens contained therein with anyone who is not a Thumbtack employee. Frontline Reps may only use the Simulator to aid in troubleshooting or discussing product features with customers. Sharing this Simulator with persons not employed by Thumbtack will result in disciplinary action.
Additionally, by using this Simulator, Frontline Reps understand that it may not fully reflect the current customer user experience. Certain features, buttons, or functionality may be missing, and some screens may not display the latest updates due to ongoing product changes. The Simulator does not include current experiments. By using the Simulator, Frontline Reps acknowledge and agree that it may not match the exact experience of Thumbtack customer users, and any differences are not indicative of the final product. 
Keeping the customer simulator current

The Field Enablement Design Team strives to keep the Customer App Simulator as up-to-date as possible.
Critical Updates: Updates related to critical bug fixes or major product launches should be reflected in the simulator within 24 hours of deployment.
Non-Critical Updates: Non-critical updates and general enhancements should typically be deployed to the simulator weekly, usually on Mondays.
How to leave feedback about the customer simulator


Frontline Reps feedback is crucial for improving the simulator. If you encounter any issues, notice discrepancies, or have suggestions for improvement, please provide feedback.
To leave feedback about the simulator, Frontline Reps will need to open the simulator using the provided Figma link. Once the simulator is open in Figma (Customer App Simulator Figma Link), Frontline Reps can follow these steps:
Click the chat bubble in the top left corner of the simulator.
Select any area on the screen to leave a comment. 
Press ‘Escape’ to exit comment mode. 
While we may not be able to implement all suggestions, we encourage you to share your insights.
2. Internal FAQs
Q: Can Frontline Reps use this simulator to troubleshoot a customer's specific issue, or will it show all the latest features and experiments?
A: No. The Customer App Simulator is a visual reference tool that replicates the baseline customer experience. It does not display real customer data, specific account states, all current features, or active experiments. Therefore, Frontline Reps should not use it for troubleshooting specific customer issues or to see the very latest product updates. For troubleshooting, Frontline Reps should use internal tools and refer to the applicable internal knowledge articles (see the resources section below).
Q: Where can I find information about the Pro App Simulator and Staging environments?
A: For details on the Pro App Simulator and Staging environments, please refer to the < Experience the Product: Staging and the Pro App Simulator (Rep) KA.

Lead price auction types

1. Overview
NOTE: This KA was previously titled “First Price Auction (Exact Lead Prices) (Pro) (Nationwide Launch)” and has been changed to “Exact Lead Prices Launch and Transition History”.
Purpose of this KA

This KA is preserved as historical reference for the transition from max lead prices to exact lead prices. It documents the January 2026 nationwide launch and the April–May 2026 transitions for previously excluded programs.  For the baseline experience, reps should refer to the internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA. 

What changed and why

Before January 2026, Thumbtack used a max lead prices model — sometimes called a second-price auction internally. Pros set the most they were willing to pay for a lead, but the amount they were actually charged could vary based on competition and other factors. Pros often paid less than their maximum, but the actual cost was unpredictable — it could change without the pro doing anything. This made it difficult to budget and plan.
On January 27, 2026, Thumbtack switched all baseline pros to exact lead prices. With this change, the price a pro sets is the price they pay — no more "up to" language, no more variability. If a pro sets $15 for a lead, they pay exactly $15.
The reason for the change was straightforward: pros consistently told Thumbtack that the old system was confusing. They could not predict what a lead would cost, which made it hard to understand their return on investment or plan their spending. Exact lead prices give pros full transparency and control — they always know what a lead will cost before they receive it.

Language note: When speaking with pros, always say "lead prices." The terms "first price auction," "FPA," "second price auction," and "max lead prices" are internal-only. Max lead prices can be used only as historical context when explaining what changed — for example, "before January 2026, pricing worked differently."
Phased rollout timeline and audience
