* [Internal note: Smart Match (Carrot): Only V1 pros were initially excluded from First Price Auction (FPA). But now both V1 and V2 use FPA (since Carrot V1 transitioned to V2 on May 11, 2026). For more information, see the internal Smart Match Program (Pro) (Experiment) KA.]
**Internal note: New Deal for Pros (NDFP): NDFP (Beta) used FPA but this pilot ended and transitioned to NDFP (MVP) on May 11, 2026. For MVP pricing and other details, see the internal New Deal for Pros KA.]
Price Transition: 
On the go live date, the system automatically adjusted bids lower in most cases to align with what the pro was recently paying.  The new exact prices were defaulted to amounts lower than their current maximum prices (unless at minimums).
Pro Experience & Action: 
Pros continued to see the "up to" (Max Lead Price) until the go-live date.  They were encouraged to wait until the go live date to review and adjust their new exact prices after the automatic default had been applied.
New pros: 
Some new pros who sign up on or after comms were sent out, were automatically onboarded into the FPA experience - with no modals or emails needed for them.
2026 rollout: Previously excluded programs

While FPA launched nationwide in January 2026, two specific groups — Smart Match (Carrot) and New Deal for Pros (NDFP) Beta — were initially excluded to protect their specialized pilot settings. These pros were transitioned to the FPA standard in a two-phased approach.
Phase 1: The auction flip (April 16, 2026)

In April, approximately 9,000 across previously excluded Smart Match V1, NDFP (Beta), and reactivated pros officially moved from "Second-Price" logic (paying up to a max) to "First-Price" logic (paying their exact bid).
The change: Pro bids were initialized at their current maximum (or ~10% lower) to ensure cost stability.
The UI "gap" for NDFP Beta pros: During this phase, some pros may have still seen "Up to $X" in their app. Even if the UI said "Up to," they were being charged their exact bid.
Comms: Pros received a 1-week advance notice email on April 6 and a "Day of Flip" follow-up on April 16.
Comms
▶ 1-week advance notice - April 6, 2026
On April 6, 2026, these pros were sent an email announcing changes to how lead pricing works starting April 16, 2026. 
The email explains that instead of setting a maximum price for leads, pros will set an exact price that they’ll always pay. Thumbtack automatically adjusted pros' current prices to fit the new system, and pros will be able to review and change their prices on or after April 16, 2026.
Note: Pros with multiple business profiles will only receive one email.

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ Day of launch - April 16, 2026
On April 16, 2026, pros were sent a reminder email about price changes. The email was sent to Smart Match, NDFP (Beta), and reactivated pros.
▶ Remaining (missed) pro announcement email - April 22, 2026
On April 22, 2026, pros who were missed were informed of price changes.
A small group of pros who had never created a bid before the week-prior comms went out on April 6, 2026, did not receive advance notice. They then created their first bid in the week between when the advance notice was sent and when the April 16, 2026, flip happened. This meant they set their prices in the legacy max lead prices experience but were then flipped to exact lead prices without receiving any advance communications.

[Image: rtaImage]

Phase 2: Program relaunch and UI alignment (May 11, 2026)

On May 11, 2026, the previously excluded pros from Smart Match V1 and NDFP (Beta) moved into the final versions of their programs.This transition resolves the UI "Up to" confusion for NDFP Beta pros and updates their experience to match the new platform standards.
To learn more about the Smart match experience, see the internal Smart Match Program (Pro) (Experiment) KA. For details about the NDFP experience, see the internal New Deal for Pros: Personalized Preferences and Smarter Lead Matching (Pro) KA. 
Nationwide comms – January 2026
Pre-flip announcement – January 20, 2026
▶ Email
Thumbtack sent an email on January 20, 2026, to pros active within the last year. The email explains the move from Max Lead Prices to Exact Lead Prices on January 27, 2026. This change gives pros more control and helps them know exactly what they will pay for a lead.
The email states that Thumbtack will automatically lower current Max Lead Prices to new Exact Price defaults (unless the price is already at the minimum). It asks pros to review and adjust their pricing settings before and after the launch on January 27, 2026.

[Image: rtaImage]

NOTE: Emails are sent by UserPK. This means pros with multiple businesses impacted will only receive 1 email ( the past rollouts sent 1 email per business).
▶ In product modal
Pros received the following in product modal on January 20,  2026 informing them that starting January 27, 2026, they will pay the exact lead price they set (not a maximum price), providing transparency and consistency. It notes that the new exact prices will be defaulted to amounts lower than their current prices (unless at minimums) and encourages them to review and adjust their prices on January 27, 2026.

[Image: rtaImage]

Day of flip announcement – January 27, 2026

▶ Email
The email announces that the change from maximum prices to exact prices is effective January 27, 2026, ensuring pros will pay exactly the amount they set (excluding discounts/promotions) for greater consistency and predictability. It confirms that the new exact prices were set to a default lower than the previous max lead prices (unless at minimum) and urges them to review and adjust their new prices immediately.

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ In product modal
Day of Flip In-Product Modal (January 27, 2026) confirms the transition from setting maximum lead prices to setting exact lead prices, which provides more consistency and transparency. It specifies that the exact prices have been set to a default at or below their previous max prices and prompts the pro to adjust these new exact prices now.

[Image: rtaImage]


2. Lead price auction types
Comparison: Max lead prices vs. Exact lead prices
Here's a table outlining the differences between the current experience (exact lead prices - First Price Auction) and the legacy experience (Second price auction - max lead prices): 

Feature
Second Price Auction 
(Legacy Experience)
First Price Auction 
(Current Experience)
External Term
Max Lead Prices
Lead Prices
Internal Term
Second Price Auction
First Price Auction (FPA)
What Pros Set
Maximum Lead Price (MLP) - the most a pro was willing to pay.
Lead Price - the exact price a pro will pay.
What Pros Pay
Charged the MLP or less, depending on competition and other factors.
Charged exactly the Lead Price they set.
Transparency
Less transparent; pros didn't always know the exact price they will pay.
More transparent; pros know exactly what they will pay for each lead.
Predictability
Less predictable; the actual cost per lead can vary.
More predictable; cost per lead is consistent and known upfront.
Control
Pros had some control by setting the maximum, but the actual price was influenced by other factors.
Pros have more direct control; they set the exact price they are willing to pay.
Pricing Tables
Showed "up to" prices, indicating a maximum.
"Up to" is removed, and the price shown is the exact price.
Pro Perception
Feedback indicated pros found it hard to understand and predict costs.
Aims to improve clarity and address concerns about understanding pricing.
Target Audience
Baseline pros were using the legacy experience prior to January 27, 2026.
Launched for baseline pros on January 27, 2026. Expanded in April 2026, to include ~9000 pros from some programs and reactivated accounts.
Reps can refer to the internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA to learn more. 
Max lead prices (Legacy experience)
Previously, in the legacy experience (second price auction), pros set max lead prices for each of their services and they were charged those amounts or less, based on how competitive other pros are, along with other factors. 
The max lead prices page showed “Your max lead prices:” with a table showing “Up to $X” for different types of jobs (e.g., mobile auto detailing shows a full service detail max lead price is up to $18 or house cleaning max lead price for 1 bedroom is up to $12) 
▶ What the max lead prices page looked like (second price auction)

[Image: rtaImage]

Exact lead prices (Baseline experience)
Lead prices are the exact prices pros pay for leads and they can see how competitive they are compared to other pros. For the baseline experience, reps should refer to the internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA. And pros can set their lead prices by following the steps in the How to set my lead prices — Thumbtack Help article.
The lead prices page shows “Your lead prices:” with a table showing “$X” for different types of jobs (e.g., TV mounting lead price is $30.62 or House cleaning lead price is $12 for 1 bedroom).
The “up to” on the pricing tables was removed and the pro pays the exact price shown. 
NOTE: When transitioning from the second price to the first price auction, a pro's lead prices were set to an amount that is at or below their previous max prices. Pros can adjust these new exact prices at any time.  
▶ What the lead prices page looks like for pros (first price auction)

[Image: rtaImage]

▶ NOTE: Answer Based Pricing (ABP) Functionality
For services where ABP is enabled, pros continue to see different rows for each job factor or dimension and will set exact prices for each listed in their pricing tables. These dimensions reflect differences in project size. 
For instance, in the "plumbing pipe installation or replacement" service category, a pro's lead price table will show different prices based on the installation size (e.g., a few pipes, one or more entire rooms, or an entire home). By setting a price for each dimension, pros can ensure that lead prices for smaller or lower-value jobs cost less, while larger scope jobs cost more.

[Image: rtaImage]

Setting higher prices is one of the ways to help their business be competitive.Pros can set higher prices for the leads that are most important to them so they’ll get more of those types of leads. 

3. Talking points
This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros about lead prices. Use these talking points to ensure consistent and accurate messaging. Frontline Reps can also refer to the internal Lead Prices (Pro) KA for more talking points.
New Pros (Onboarded to FPA)
Use this talking point for pros who are new to Thumbtack (signed up on or after January 20, 2026) and have only ever seen the "Lead Prices" (FPA) system.


English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: How do exact lead prices work (I’m confused about exact lead prices!)?
Q: ¿Cómo funcionan los precios exactos por prospecto? (¡No entiendo los precios exactos por prospecto!)
A: Welcome to Thumbtack! Here’s how it works:
You set the price: On your 'Lead Prices' page, you set the exact price you are willing to pay for a lead for each of your services.
What you set is what you pay: If you get a lead, you will pay that exact price. It gives you full transparency and makes your costs predictable.
You're in control: You can go to your 'Lead Prices' page at any time to see how your prices compare to other pros and adjust them to meet your business goals
A: ¡Bienvenido a Thumbtack! Así es como funciona:
Usted fija el precio: En su página Lead Prices (“Precios por prospecto”), establece el precio exacto que está dispuesto a pagar por un prospecto para cada uno de sus servicios.
Lo que fija es lo que paga: Si recibe un prospecto, pagará ese precio exacto. Esto le brinda total transparencia y hace que sus costos sean predecibles.
Usted tiene el control: Puede ir a su página Lead Prices (“Precios por prospecto”) en cualquier momento para ver cómo se comparan sus precios con los de otros profesionales y ajustarlos según los objetivos de su negocio.
Do I set a price for every service? 
¿Debo establecer un precio para cada servicio?
Yes, you will need to set your price for every service. 
Sí, deberá establecer un precio para cada uno de sus servicios.
What happens if I only set a price for some of my services but not for all of them?
¿Qué sucede si solo establezco un precio para algunos de mis servicios, pero no para todos?
You will be required to set a price for all categories -- if you exit out, you will be asked to re-set for all your categories.
Deberá establecer un precio para todas las categorías. Si sale del proceso antes de completarlo, se le pedirá que configure nuevamente los precios para todas sus categorías.
Existing pros (Transitioning to FPA)
Use these talking points for pros who were moved from "Max Lead Prices" to "Lead Prices" and have questions about the change.

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: What does this mean? How should I prepare for this change?
Q: ¿Qué significa esto? ¿Cómo debo prepararme para este cambio?
A: On January 27th, your new exact prices will default to amounts no higher than your current max prices.

To ensure that you’re comfortable with the new prices that you’ll be paying, we encourage you to adjust your prices once change is implemented. 
A: A partir del 27 de enero, sus nuevos precios exactos se establecerán de forma predeterminada en montos que no superen sus precios máximos actuales.

Para asegurarse de que se sienta cómodo con los nuevos precios que pagará, le recomendamos ajustar sus precios una vez que se haya implementado el cambio.
Q: What does it mean for my prices to be set to a default that is “at or below” my previous prices?
Q: ¿Qué significa que mis precios se establezcan de forma predeterminada “iguales o inferiores” a mis precios anteriores?
A: In the majority of cases, on January 27th, your max lead prices will become your exact prices. However, there are some cases where we anticipate your prices to increase significantly. In these cases to ensure you don’t see large changes to your pricing, Thumbtack will set your prices at a default price below your current max lead price. Remember that you can adjust your new exact prices at any time.
A: En la mayoría de los casos, el 27 de enero, sus precios máximos por prospecto se convertirán en sus precios exactos. Sin embargo, en algunos casos anticipamos que sus precios podrían aumentar significativamente. En esas situaciones, para evitar que vea cambios grandes en sus tarifas, Thumbtack establecerá sus precios con un valor predeterminado inferior a su precio máximo actual por prospecto. Recuerde que puede ajustar sus nuevos precios exactos en cualquier momento.
Q: Why is Thumbtack making this change? Are you just increasing prices?
Q: ¿Por qué Thumbtack está realizando este cambio? ¿Solo están aumentando los precios?
A: We’ve heard that it’s challenging to plan and budget when you don’t have transparency about what you’ll pay. That’s why we’re moving to exact prices instead of a max “up to” price. 

On January 27th, your exact prices will be set to a default that is at or below your current max lead prices.

If you’re not comfortable paying the price that your max lead prices are currently set to, it’s important that you update your prices before January 27. 

And remember, that these defaults are just what your prices are initially set to. You can adjust your lead prices at any time. 
A: Hemos escuchado que es difícil planificar y presupuestar cuando no se tiene transparencia sobre lo que pagará. Por eso estamos cambiando a precios exactos en lugar de un precio máximo "hasta".

El 27 de enero, sus precios exactos se establecerán en un valor predeterminado que será igual o inferior a sus precios máximos actuales por prospecto.

Si no se siente cómodo pagando el precio que sus precios máximos por prospecto están configurados actualmente, es importante que actualice sus precios antes del 27 de enero.

Y recuerde, estos valores predeterminados son solo los precios iniciales. Puede ajustar sus precios por prospecto en cualquier momento.
Q: If I update my prices prior to January 27, will that be applied immediately?
Q: Si actualizo mis precios antes del 27 de enero, ¿se aplicarán de inmediato?
A: Yes, if you update your prices before January 27th, that will be applied immediately and change your competitiveness level even though you’ll still have max lead prices until the cutover date.

For this reason, we encourage you to update your prices on or after January 27th so that your competitiveness doesn’t change.
A: Sí, si actualiza sus precios antes del 27 de enero, se aplicarán de inmediato y cambiarán su nivel de competitividad, aunque aún tendrá precios máximos por prospecto hasta la fecha de cambio.

Por esta razón, le recomendamos que actualice sus precios el 27 de enero o después, para que su competitividad no cambie.
Q: How does this affect my competitiveness/ranking?
Q: ¿Cómo afecta esto mi competitividad/clasificación?
A: In the majority of cases your competitiveness and ranking should remain the same. We encourage you to look at your lead prices page to make sure you’re comfortable with how competitive you are.
A: En la mayoría de los casos, su competitividad y clasificación deberían permanecer iguales. Le recomendamos que consulte su página de precios por prospecto para asegurarse de que se sienta cómodo con su nivel de competitividad.
4. Glossary
Glossary of First Price Auction terms for frontline reps to reference:
First Price Auction (FPA): An auction where pros pay exactly the price they bid. This differs from the previous second-price auction model. Internal term only. Do not use with pros.
Lead Prices: The exact price a pro will pay for a lead in the First Price Auction. This replaces the term "max lead price."
Max Lead Price (MLP): The maximum price a pro was willing to pay for a lead in the previous second-price auction model. This term is being phased out in the context of the First Price Auction.
Average Price Paid: The typical amount a pro has been paying for leads, used as a reference point for setting initial "lead prices" in Market B.
Cutover: The date when the auction mechanism switches from a second-price auction to a first-price auction.
Baseline Pros: Pros who are not included in the First Price Auction experiment and continue to operate under the second-price auction model.
MBT Pros: Pros who are included in the Market Based Test (First Price Auction experiment).
Important Notes for Reps
Internal vs. External Language: Use "lead prices" when talking to pros, not "First Price Auction" or "FPA."
Price Adjustments: Understand the implications of pros adjusting their prices before and after the cutover date in each market.
Transparency and Predictability: Emphasize the benefits of the First Price Auction, such as increased transparency, predictability, and control over pricing.

Enhanced Lead Quality Commitment (Customer Phone Number Verification)

Contents
Overview
Customer experience
Process
How customers verify their phone number during project submission
(Rep) Steps: How to Help Customer Resolve an 'Invalid Phone Number' Error During Project Submission (Troubleshooting)
Talking points
Customer talking point
Resources
1. Overview
Thumbtack is committed to providing high-quality leads to pros. To achieve this, Thumbtack has a customer phone number verification process. This process helps reduce spam, and fraudulent activity and improves the overall experience for both.
Phone Number Reuse Policy 
This section provides an overview of Thumbtack's commitment to lead quality, specifically detailing the customer phone number verification process and the new 3-user phone number reuse policy, and updated handling of blocklisted numbers.
To further enhance lead quality and prevent spam and fraudulent activity, Thumbtack has implemented a new policy: a single phone number can now be used for a maximum of three (3) customer accounts. If a phone number is associated with three or more existing customer accounts, the customer will be blocked from submitting their request and will receive the error message 'This phone number can't be used on your account' in the request flow.
Handling Blocklisted Phone Numbers
The previous check that prevented customers from adding blocklisted phone numbers during the request flow has been removed. Customers can now enter a blocklisted phone number in the request flow. However, requests submitted with a blocklisted phone number will be intercepted and deleted after submission. Customers will not be aware their request was flagged or deleted due to being blocklisted.
Identity Match Check: When a customer submits a project request with their phone number, Thumbtack verifies if the name associated with the phone number matches the name provided in the request. If there’s a mismatch, Thumbtack sends a verification code via text message to the customer. 
Refund Process Screening: Thumbtack also screens additional signals during refund requests to strengthen the verification process further. Reps can learn more in the Lead Refunds (Pro) | Article #000007615 KA under “Customer provided an invalid phone number.”
Internal only info: Customers will be automatically verified through Twilio. Reps will not be verifying customer's phone numbers.
Customer experience
The typical customer journey for submitting a project and verifying their phone number includes:
Customers submit a project request with their phone number.
The system checks if the phone number and name match.
If they match, the request is submitted and shared with pros.
If they don't match, the customer receives a text message with a verification code.
The customer enters the code to confirm their phone number.
If successful, the project request proceeds as usual.
New: Impact of 3-User Phone Number Limit.
If the customer's phone number is already associated with three or more other customer accounts, the customer will encounter the error message: 'This phone number can't be used on your account.' 
This error prevents the project from being submitted, and the customer will be unable to proceed in the request flow until a different phone number is entered.  The customer can then contact Thumbtack Support for help.
Customer Experience: Blocklisted Phone Numbers (not exceeding 3-user limit)
If the customer's phone number is blocklisted (and does not exceed the 3-user limit), they will be able to submit their request. However, the request will be intercepted and silently deleted after submission. The customer is not notified of this deletion at the time of submission. The customer may call in because their request 'didn't go through' or 'isn't visible.'
Verification Process: Customers may need to verify their phone number via text message if the name associated with their phone number doesn't match their request.
2. Process
This section outlines the steps involved in customer phone number verification during project submission and provides detailed troubleshooting guidance for frontline reps.
How customers verify their phone number during project submission 

This process outlines the process where customers verify their phone number when submitting a project request. 
Here’s what the customer experience looks like: 
Project submission: The customer fills out the project request form and their phone number (as usual) and clicks “Submit”. 
▶ Expand for in product view
[Image: AD_4nXdwVgHYr4bOmB86KZ0yWPVMY8LCOpUdOtnHUIqm63NHQHkIZ2L5aLYS3CVNZxPIBY6TZBFlQg1PEC9sfd-sj9N8IEpCsOdzTByNbBHyuEz1a14k5JC1NSsgKu0gZrg7NIHCD-ommh-XK5D2qi8e2JxNg2S7]
System check: On the backend, Thumbtack uses Twilio to verify a customer’s phone number by checking if the phone number and name match. (98% of scam requests are identified at this point)
Match found: If the phone number and name match, the customer's request is submitted and shared with relevant pros. Pros can now contact the customer to discuss their project needs.
▶ Expand for in product view[Image: AD_4nXfBRpDs9mduQPtOAmEfOye8f-U7LyzjkLx7GOep7Dso1B_TnR1bKlRU3z-G_A04qa4pMWRpxxg6U8RipjIHVZ1n_-7NAC35B06kSZZ4AYUnnUc6I6EgisFSMfD_xm2a7nDfpSpC]
Mismatch (SMS Verification): If the phone number and name do not match, Twilio starts an extra SMS Verification. 
▶ Expand for in product view[Image: AD_4nXexK6rs4uQwYQUpZgsgk30EEWbVf2LPkxRdevqHiIdQ54stXPOx690_VFNIuF1TLHbd8IYdVS-H00AsNcQA1oceMlj6BdrXTDgdpwyuZBxg3OiTz_oUIvEFaIGMfnO1B-GjP7aoRg]
The customer receives a text message with a verification code.
The customer enters the code on Thumbtack to confirm their phone number.
If successful, the request proceeds as usual.
Internal note: Effective March 23, 2026, if a connected phone number bypasses this SMS verification and lacks a matching customer name, the Pro is eligible for an invalid phone number refund. Refer to the internal Lead Refunds (Pro) KA for the full review process.
(Rep) Steps: How to Help Customer Resolve an 'Invalid Phone Number' Error During Project Submission (Troubleshooting)

To help a customer who is unable to submit a request due to the “invalid phone number” error, frontline reps will follow these steps: 
Initial assessment – Understand the customer's experience Begin by asking the customer what happened and any messages they saw. This helps determine the likely cause:
Did the customer see an error message like 'This phone number can't be used on your account' during the request submission process?
This indicates a 3-user limit issue.
Did the customer not see an error message during submission, but their project 'didn't go through' or 'isn't visible' after they submitted it?
This could indicate a blocklisted number issue (silent deletion post-submission) or another internal system issue.
Verify phone number & basic troubleshooting: Frontline reps should confirm the customer is using the correct phone number on their Thumbtack account.
▶ Talking point example
"I understand you're seeing an issue with your project request and phone number. That can be frustrating, and I'm here to help you figure this out. To get started, could you please confirm the phone number you're trying to use?"
Resolve phone number issues based on scenario
Customer received 'This phone number can't be used on your account' error (3-User Limit)
When a customer encounters this specific error, it means their phone number is associated with three or more other customer accounts, and the system prevented the request from being created.
Admin Visibility: There will be NO record of this project submission in Admin for reps to find. The system blocked the creation at an earlier stage.
Resolution – Manually Add Number in Admin: Frontline reps should use the Admin tool to manually add the phone number to the customer's account. This action bypasses the automatic uniqueness check and allows legitimate customers to proceed. Reps can refer to the internal Account Information (Customer) KA for detailed steps on how to do this.
Customer's project 'didn't go through' or 'isn't visible' (Potential Blocklisted Number or other internal issue)
If the customer did not receive an error during submission but their project is now missing, the phone number might be blocklisted (and was silently deleted after submission) or there may be another internal system issue.
Admin Check: Frontline reps should search for the customer's account in Admin.
Check the customer's deletion logs under 'Page Actions' for flags like 'Deleted by Fides' or 'Linked to banned user' that might indicate a blocklisted phone number caused a post-submission deletion.
Important: Frontline reps must NOT disclose to customers that their account is linked to another pro, about a "hold" status, or that their phone number is blocklisted. Avoid saying anything that reveals sensitive internal information.
Resolution – Suggest alternative phone number: If the Admin check points to a blocklisted number, or the root cause is unclear, and the customer is willing to try again, suggest they use a different phone number (if available) to submit a new project request.
▶ Talking point example"It appears there was a system issue with the phone number you provided, and your request couldn't be processed. Could you please try submitting your project again with a different phone number, if you have one available?"Contact Trust and Safety (for complex issues or no alternative number): If the customer does not have an alternative phone number, or if the Admin checks indicate a potential 'linked to pro on hold' scenario, or if the manual add for a 3-user limit issue failed for a system reason, contact the Trust and Safety team for help.
Contact Trust and Safety (for complex issues or no alternative number): If the customer does not have an alternative phone number, or if the Admin checks indicate a potential 'linked to pro on hold' scenario, or if the manual add for a 3-user limit issue failed for a system reason, transfer the case to  the Trust and Safety team using the T&S Salesforce transfer flow. For steps, see the Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA.
Post in the #ts-proactive-ops-questions Slack channel with:
Talking point 1: Blocklisted number, no alternative available: "After reviewing your account and going over the options with you, it looks like this needs a closer look from our specialized team — they have visibility into things I don't have access to on my end. I've gone ahead and sent your case over to them, and they'll follow up with you directly with an update. In the meantime, is there anything else I can help you with?"Talking point 2: 3-user limit, manual add failed: "I went ahead and tried to add this phone number to your account directly, but I wasn't able to get that to go through on my end. To make sure this gets resolved, I've sent your case to our specialized team so they can take a closer look. They'll follow up with you directly with an update."
For 'linked to pro on hold' scenario: "This customer is unable to submit a project request due to being linked to a pro on hold. Please check to see if we can remove ONLY the customer's account from the hold."
For 'linked to pro on hold' scenario: "This customer is unable to submit a project request due to being linked to a pro on hold. Please check to see if we can remove ONLY the customer's account from the hold."
If 3-user limit Admin tool failed: "This customer is unable to submit a project request due to the phone number exceeding the 3-user limit. We were unable to manually add the number via Admin. Please advise on next steps."
3. Talking points for customers

This section provides frontline reps with talking points to use when navigating conversations with pros and customers regarding the Enhanced Lead Quality Commitment. These talking points address common questions and concerns that may arise and provide clear answers. Reps should use these talking points as a guide to ensure consistent and accurate messaging.
Customer talking points

English
Spanish
Why do I need to verify my phone number? I'm worried about my privacy and how my data will be used.
¿Por qué necesito verificar mi número de teléfono? Me preocupa mi privacidad y cómo se utilizarán mis datos.
We understand your concern about privacy. Verifying your phone number is a crucial step in ensuring a safe and secure experience for both our customers and pros. It helps us prevent fraudulent activity and spam, protecting everyone involved. We take data security very seriously, and your information will only be used for verification purposes and to connect you with relevant pros.
Entendemos su preocupación por la privacidad. Verificar su número de teléfono es un paso crucial para garantizar una experiencia segura tanto para nuestros clientes como para los profesionales. Nos ayuda a prevenir actividades fraudulentas y spam, protegiendo a todos los involucrados. Tomamos muy en serio la seguridad de los datos, y su información solo se utilizará con fines de verificación y para conectarlo con los profesionales relevantes.
I don't understand why I'm being asked to verify my phone number. I already provided it in the request form.
No entiendo por qué se me pide que verifique mi número de teléfono. Ya lo proporcioné en el formulario de solicitud.
Sometimes, the name associated with a phone number doesn't match the name on a request. This can happen for various reasons, like a recent name change or a shared phone line. Verifying phone numbers helps us confirm that we're connecting real customers with the right pros and ensures a better experience for everyone.
A veces, el nombre asociado con un número de teléfono no coincide con el nombre de una solicitud. Esto puede ocurrir por diversas razones, como un cambio de nombre reciente o una línea telefónica compartida. Verificar los números de teléfono nos ayuda a confirmar que estamos conectando a clientes reales con los profesionales adecuados y garantiza una mejor experiencia para todos.
This is an extra step, and it's delaying my project request. Why can't you just trust that I'm a real customer?
Este es un paso adicional y está retrasando mi solicitud de proyecto. ¿Por qué no pueden simplemente confiar en que soy un cliente real?
I understand your frustration with the additional step. We implement these measures to protect all users on Thumbtack – both customers and pros. By verifying phone numbers, we reduce the amount of spam and fraudulent activity, which in turn helps pros respond faster to genuine inquiries like yours. Ultimately, it improves the overall experience for everyone. I apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.
Entiendo su frustración con el paso adicional. Implementamos estas medidas para proteger a todos los usuarios en Thumbtack, tanto clientes como profesionales. Al verificar los números de teléfono, reducimos la cantidad de spam y actividad fraudulenta, lo que a su vez ayuda a los profesionales a responder más rápido a consultas genuinas como la suya. En última instancia, mejora la experiencia general para todos. Le pido disculpas por cualquier inconveniente que esto pueda causar.
Why is my phone number showing as 'This phone number can't be used on your account'?
¿Por qué aparece el mensaje “This phone number can't be used on your account”?
I'm sorry to hear you're having trouble submitting your job request on Thumbtack. It looks like the phone number you're trying to use can't be used on your account right now because it's already connected to a few other accounts on our platform. To help keep Thumbtack working well for everyone, we limit how often a phone number can be used across different accounts. This helps make sure pros connect with unique and active customers. I can help you manually add this phone number to your account now.
Lamentamos que esté teniendo dificultades para enviar su solicitud de trabajo en Thumbtack. Parece que el número de teléfono que intenta usar no se puede vincular a su cuenta en este momento, ya que ya está asociado a varias cuentas en nuestra plataforma. Para que Thumbtack funcione correctamente para todos, limitamos cuántas veces puede usarse un número de teléfono en distintas cuentas. Esto ayuda a garantizar que los profesionales se conecten con clientes únicos y activos. Puedo ayudarle agregando manualmente este número de teléfono a su cuenta ahora mismo.
My project didn't go through, what happened?
Mi proyecto no se procesó, ¿qué ocurrió?
I'm sorry to hear your project didn't go through as expected. It appears there was a system issue with the phone number you provided, and your request couldn't be processed. Could you please try submitting your project again with a different phone number, if you have one available?"
Lamentamos que su proyecto no se haya procesado como esperaba. Parece que hubo un problema en el sistema con el número de teléfono proporcionado y no se pudo completar su solicitud.

Reference: How the Booking Inquiries Pilot Worked
Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) has been updated to reflect the conclusion of the Booking Inquiries pilot on August 18, 2025. Its purpose is to support frontline reps in answering questions from pros who were part of the pilot and are now transitioning back to Thumbtack's direct lead model.
Internal Terminology: Frontline reps may hear “Connect to Book” internally. Always use “booking inquiries” with pros.

End of Booking Inquiries Pilot
This section outlines the conclusion of the Booking Inquiries pilot program, detailing what this means for pros, how the change will be communicated, and the temporary refund policy in place to support affected pros.
What’s happening with Booking Inquiries:

Beginning August 18, 2025, the booking inquiries pilot will conclude for all pros currently participating. This means these pros will revert to Thumbtack's core experience, which is the direct lead model. This decision stems from a strategic pivot within New Hire Experiences (NHX) to focus on building a complete matchmaking product, deemed foundational for establishing a successful booking model.
While the booking inquiries pilot delivered valuable insights into how pros and customers connect on job details and build confidence to book, it also highlighted key components that need to be addressed for a scalable booking experience that delivers consistent outcomes and returns for pros. The learnings from this pilot are considered a significant win, shaping our roadmap with greater clarity and conviction on how to move from customer contact to hire.
Why the Booking Inquiries pilot will be ending:
Internal why for reps: This strategic recalibration is not a response to a failed experience, but a jumping point founded in a well of insights captured from NHX efforts, like booking inquiries, over the past half-year. Thumbtack acknowledges that the experience highlighted core problem areas that need to be addressed to create a sustainable booking and monetization model.
External why for pros: Booking inquiries was a pilot aimed at testing a first-of-its-kind booking model to address immediate pain points. The pilot showed key problems with getting reliable leads and ready customers. These issues must be fixed to provide consistently better quality leads for pros. Our priority is to address those core problems to provide consistently high quality leads. Therefore, booking inquiries are pausing for now with a commitment to deliver more jobs, not just leads.
Who is impacted by the Booking Inquiries pilot ending:

This change primarily impacts pros who have been participating in the Booking Inquiries pilot, specifically those in the Orlando-Kissimmee-Sanford, FL market targeting House Cleaning, Local Moving, and Furniture Moving & Heavy Lifting. Customers will not notice or be impacted by this change.
Thumbtack will proactively communicate the end of the booking inquiries pilot with the following segments of pros:
Pro Advisory Board (PAB): Pros who’ve been active participants in providing feedback that shaped the experience and future NHX strategy. They’ll receive a preliminary touchpoint with a higher level of transparency regarding the strategic shift.
Pros in the pilot who signed up BEFORE May 27, 2025: These pros opted into the original pilot that started in October, or were flipped or added to the experience after May 27. They have context around leads.
Pros in the pilot who signed up AFTER May 27, 2025: These are newer pros who signed up in the flipped market after the flip date. They’re aware of the booking inquiries pilot program, but since they didn’t onboard to the direct lead experience they may need more education on how it works.
Before and after August 18, 2025
Before August 18, 2025 (before being switched over to the direct lead experience), any booking inquiry a pro receives is treated as booking inquiries as usual. Pros in the pilot will still be able to communicate with the customer through the masked number, and won't be charged unless a booking is confirmed. 
On August 18, 2025 (after being switched over to the direct lead experience), any new lead a pro receives will be a direct lead that they auto-pay for and get the customers contact information upfront. 
How’s Thumbtack communicating the end of the Booking Inquiries pilot:

Thumbtack’s communication strategy is focused on positioning this change as a realignment towards a higher confidence strategy that aims to create innovative matchmaking experiences, building a solid foundation for future booking and hiring experiences. The following list shows proactive communication being sent to pros:
Pro Advisory Board (PAB): The decision will be communicated in advance through email and a short video overview with a higher level of transparency given their partnership.
Impacted pilot pros: All impacted pilot pros will receive messages through email, push notifications, and in-product surfaces beginning approximately two weeks ahead of the change (starting August 4, 2025). Reminder communications will follow.
Temporary Refund Policy for Booking Inquiries
This information is for internal use only. 
Pros might be used to getting free "connect to book" leads and talking to customers without paying. If they didn't see Thumbtack's messages, or if they don't understand why they're now being automatically charged for leads, they might ask for refunds.
To help pros who may be confused by the conclusion of the Booking Inquiries pilot, Thumbtack is providing a temporary, lenient in-policy refund policy specifically for booking inquiries. Here are the details for the Temporary refund policy:
Refund policy launch: August 18, 2025
Refund policy duration: Four weeks after the pilot concludes (September 15, 2025).
Refund policy: Pros will receive a one-time in-policy refund for refund requests related to the Booking Inquiries pilot ending.
▶ Refund process:
This information is for internal use only. 
Frontline reps can use these steps to identify when a pro is eligible for a refund due to the end of the pilot. This section details the situations that qualify for a refund, which will then be processed by the Refund Operations team.
Pros request refunds because they expected leads to be free, based on their previous experience with Booking Inquiries. 
The Refund Operations team will provide in-policy refunds for pros who dispute charges for leads because they were previously enrolled in Booking Inquiries. This includes, but is not limited to, situations where the pro was:
Unaware of the pilot ending (missed Thumbtack's communication).
Aware but didn’t know how this would affect them.
▶ Approval conditions for Refund Operations Team:
This information is for internal use only. 
Frontline reps can refer to this section to understand the specific criteria the Refund Operations team uses to formally approve and process a refund request due to the end of the pilot. These are the backend conditions. This information is for internal use only. 
Pro was previously enrolled in Booking Inquiries: This can be verified in Admin under the Pro’s Business page by checking for the message: "This pro had booking inquiries enabled.".
Pro hasn’t received a refund related to the Booking Inquiries pilot ending: This should be their first time reaching out about this specific issue.
The Refund Ops team will process in-policy refunds under "Approved Courtesy Refunds" and leave "CTB Rollback" in Admin notes for easier tracking
Talking points: End of booking inquiries pilot

Frontline reps can use the following talking points for common questions about the booking inquiries pilot ending.
Explaining why the booking injuries pilot ended
Frontline reps can use these talking points to clearly explain what is happening with the Booking Inquiries pilot and to announce its conclusion.

English talking points
Spanish talking points 
Q: What’s happening?
Q: 
A: Starting August 18th, the booking inquiries pilot will come to a close after successfully delivering insight into how to improve customer readiness and hiring experiences. This pilot launched with the intention to test a first-of-its-kind booking model built around pro and customer feedback.
A: 
The “Why” behind the decision to end the booking inquiries pilot 
Frontline reps can use these talking points to address questions about why the pilot is ending and to provide context on the decision. 

English talking points
Spanish talking points 
Q: Why are booking inquiries being removed? 
Q: 
A: Even though there’s been a positive response to booking inquiries, we found some pain points that need to be addressed in order to create an experience that consistently works well and provides a good ROI (return on investment) for pros. 
We learned that more work needs to be done. The feedback we received and the data we’ve gathered from booking inquiries gives us more confidence in how we can improve customer readiness to hire, match customers with pros more effectively, and enhance the overall hiring experience — leading to more reliable and better results for everyone.
A: 
Looking ahead: The future of bookings and lead quality 

Frontline reps can use these talking points to discuss what Thumbtack is working on next and to set expectations about the future of booking-related features.

English talking points
Spanish talking points 
Q: Will booking inquiries come back? 
Q: 
A: Thumbtack remains committed to the vision of high-quality leads and successful hires. While the booking inquiries feature was initially intended as a test for a first-of-its-kind booking model, we aim to now focus on improving customer readiness throughout the hiring journey, so pros can benefit from better lead quality with more ready customers. We don’t have current commitments to revisit bookings, but will be able to re-assess that strategy as we create a strong lead quality foundation.
A: 
Q: What is there to look forward to now?
Q: 
A: We are taking a more focused approach to tackling customer readiness and lead quality in efforts to ensure more consistent and better ROI for pros. To learn more about how we’re continuing our commitment to delivering better experiences for pros and customers, stay tuned for more information in the upcoming 2025 Pro Summit this Fall.
A: 
Q: What else is Thumbtack working on to improve lead quality for pros? 
Q: 
A: We’re directly focusing on customer readiness and creating new matchmaking experiences that aim to deliver more leads with higher quality. This includes improved refund protections, leveraging AI to enhance matching and hiring experiences, and building out more value for pros and customers to move towards a booking model in the future.

We’re also focusing on introducing masked call and text options for pros and customers, boosting customer trust by protecting their privacy. This also gives us valuable insights on what key information customers need to be ready to hire, which should lead to better returns for pros.
A: 
Addressing pro concerns about future costs after booking inquiries pilot ends

Frontline reps can use these talking points to address questions about future pricing models and why the free communication model is not continuing at this time. 

English talking points
Spanish talking points 
Q: Will there be another pilot with a free communication model?
Q: 
A: The intention is for pros to pay for committed jobs, not just leads. At this time, we aren’t able to determine what a future charge model would look like, but we’ll ensure pros have transparency into pricing for a model that charges fairly for the value delivered, keeping positive pro return on investment at the forefront.
A: 
Managing transition
Frontline reps can use these talking points to help pros understand how to manage any remaining booking inquiries and what to expect from new leads.

English talking points
Spanish talking points 
Q: What happens to booking inquiries that haven’t turned into bookings yet? 
Q: 
A: For any booking inquiry you receive before being switched over to the direct lead experience on August 18th, you’d treat those leads as booking inquiries as usual. That means you'll still be able to communicate with the customer through the masked number, and won't be charged unless a booking is confirmed. 
After being switched over to the direct lead experience on August 18th, any new lead will be a direct lead you auto-pay for and get the customers contact information upfront. 
A: 


3. Reference: How the Booking Inquiries Pilot Worked
This section is for reference to help answer specific questions from pros about their past experience.
Key Features of the Pilot
Free Communication: Pros could chat with customers for free via the Thumbtack messenger or use a masked phone number to call or text before any charges were applied.
Pay When Booked: Pros were only charged after a booking was confirmed by the customer.
Privacy: Contact information was kept private and masked until a booking was confirmed.
How Pros Were Identified for the Pilot
Soft Launch: In September 2024, Thumbtack launched booking inquiries to about 100 pros in the Orlando market.
Mandatory Flip: Starting May 27, 2025, all pros in Orlando offering House Cleaning, Local Moving, and/or Furniture Moving and Heavy Lifting services exclusively received booking inquiries for all their service categories. These pros could not opt-out.
How Reps Can Identify a Pro from the Pilot
Admin Page: The pro's Businesses / Services Admin page will have a message indicating they were part of the Orlando market flip.
Jobs Tab: If a rep impersonates the pro, the presence of a "Booking Inquiries" tab on their Jobs tab indicates they were in the pilot.
Costs and Payments During the Pilot
Inquiries were Free: Pros were not charged for replying to or declining a booking inquiry.
Charged on Confirmation: The cost of a confirmed booking was the same as a normal booking and was based on the pro's lead prices.

Direct Deposit and Stripe (Pro)

Contents
Overview
Stripe Verification: Required Information by Business Type
Direct deposit statuses on the pro’s earnings page
Direct deposit for preset jobs
Key points
Process
(Pro) Steps: How to set up direct deposit
(Pro) Steps: How to update direct deposit
Navigating the “Payout Gateway Account: Stripe Connect” page in Admin
Requirements reasoning codes for direct deposit setup (in Admin)
(Rep) Steps: How to view a pro’s direct deposit status in Admin (Troubleshoot)
Examples
Completed individual account
Completed company account

Talking points
SSN, EIN, Bank account questions

Pro has concerns about direct deposit (overcoming pro objections)
Impact on ranking and leads with direct deposit
Issues with direct deposit account
Use Thumbtack profile as pros business website
Resources 
1. Overview
Pro can receive payments from customers through Thumbtack by setting up direct deposit.This is required for preset jobs. Pros are prompted to set up direct deposit when they claim a preset job for the first time. Pros can claim preset jobs before their direct deposit is set up. However, it’s recommendation they do before completing a preset job.
Standard deposits typically take 3-4 business days and have no fees. Pros who are eligible for instant deposits can get paid in 30 minutes, including weekends and holidays, for a 1% fee for each instant deposit. Reps can refer to Instant Deposits (Pro) KA to learn more. 
NOTE: Prior to the sunset of Thumbtack Pay, pros had to have direct deposit setup to request or receive payments. See Thumbtack Pay (Pro) (Customer) (Sunset Jun 30, 2026) KA to learn more. 
How setting up direct deposit works 

To set up direct deposit, pros can navigate to their Earnings page on Thumbtack and follow the prompts. Direct deposit setup is a two-part process, which includes:
Verify identity through Stripe.  Pro provides either their full Social Security Number (SSN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) and a few personal details through Stripe. (See Information pros will need for Stripe verification below)
Add their bank account to Thumbtack. Pros enter their banking information (routing number and bank account number) on their Thumbtack account.  Pros setting up direct deposit will also go through 2-factor authentication.  For more information on payout Information verification reps can refer to the internal Instant deposits KA to learn more..
After the pro has submitted their information, it takes 1-3 business days for Stripe to verify their account. Once verified, the pro can begin requesting and receiving payments. 
For detailed steps, pros can follow the steps in the How to set up direct deposit – Thumbtack Help article. 
Frontline reps should remember the following info regarding direct deposit when helping pros:
Frontline reps should never fill out bank account information on behalf of the pro.
Before posting any payment-related questions, reps must first follow the steps on the Support for Payment Related Inquiries KA. If a pro needs to update their business type, reps should post in #ttod-for-service-support to get it updated.
Stripe Verification: Required Information by Business Type

During Stripe's identity verification process, pros will be required to submit either their full Social Security Number (SSN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN), along with some personal information. The specific information required varies depending on the professional's business type.
▶ Individual:  Individuals without an EIN
The information a pro will need for Stripe verification when setting up direct deposit as an individual include: 
Personal information such as: 
Legal name
Email address
Date of birth
Home address
Phone number
Full Social Security number
Business website
ID verification using either:
Driver’s license
Identity card
Passport
Banking details including both:
Routing number
Account number

▶ Company / Business: Employees of a company or have a business with an EIN
A company account needs to be activated by an executive, senior manager, or someone who has significant responsibility for the control and management of the business.
Business structures include:
Sole proprietorship 
Single-member LLC 
Multi-member LLC
Private partnership
Private corporation 
The information a pro will need for Stripe verification when setting up direct deposit as a company / business include:  
Legal business name
Full Employer Identification number
Business details such as: 
Registered business address and business phone number
Information from the person activating the account:
Legal name, email, job title, date of birth, home address. 
A list of anyone that has significant ownership (25%+) of the business
ID verification of person activating the account using either:
Driver’s license
Identity card
Passport
Banking details where you want the direct deposit to be sent including both:
Routing number
Account number
Note: If a pro register as the wrong type of business and needs to update it, frontline reps should post in #ttod-for-service-support to get it updated.

Direct deposit status on the pro's earnings page
A pro's Earnings page displays their deposit accounts, transactions, and payouts. Specifically, it shows:
The setup status of bank accounts (standard deposit) and debit cards (instant deposits) linked to their Thumbtack account.
A detailed list of payments received from customers.
The status and expected arrival dates of actual payouts (collections of one or more customer payments) sent to the pro's bank account.
When a pro sets up direct deposit (or instant deposits):
If Stripe verification is successful: Their Earnings page will display their bank account.
If Stripe verification fails: Their Earnings page will show a warning status of “Bank account issues” with an option to Update. Thumbtack will also notify the pro via email, push notification, and a global banner.
To learn more about direct deposit statuses and the Earnings page, reps should reference the internal Payouts on Thumbtack: Earnings Transactions and Deposits (Pro) KA. 
Direct deposit for preset jobs
It is recommended that pros set up direct deposit before completing a preset job to prevent payment delays or issues. 
After claiming a preset job, pros without a valid direct deposit will be guided through the setup process. The pro will see a call to action, sending them to the Earnings page to set it. An info modal on that page will give them more details.
After direct deposit setup, a confirmation modal will explain that Stripe's verification takes 1-3 business days. Once their bank account is added and verified, they’ll be able to receive payment after they finish the claimed job.
If they don't complete the direct deposit setup, they will receive notifications from Thumbtack before and after the job. 
Reminder: Pros have to indicate that the job was done to get the payment amount transferred to their Thumbtack account. They can do this by going to the messenger or updating the job status pill 
Key points
Frontline reps should keep the following key points in mind when helping pros set up direct deposit: 
After the pro submits their personal info, Stripe will need to confirm that their ID verification was successful. This process will take approximately 1-3 business days.
Pros can claim preset jobs before their direct deposit is set up. However, it’s recommended that they do before completing a preset job. 
Pros must be running the most up-to-date app version to see the direct deposit set-up feature. 
Pros must have either an SSN or EIN for direct deposit.
Business type cannot be changed by the pro after initial setup. If a pro needs to update their business type, frontline reps can post in #ttod-for-service-support to get it updated.
Frontline reps should NOT fill out bank account information on behalf of the pro

2. Process
(Pro) Steps: How to set up direct deposit


Pro steps: Pros can set up direct deposit by following the steps in the How to set up direct deposit – Thumbtack Help article.
To set up direct deposit, pros navigate to their Earnings page and click "Add Account." They'll be redirected to Stripe to verify their identity, providing either SSN/personal bank info (for "Individual" business type) or EIN/business bank info (for "Business" type). 
After verification (1-3 business days), they're returned to Thumbtack to enter bank account details. If Stripe verification for direct deposit is successful their earnings tab will show their bank account listed. However, if it fails the pro will receive a notification via email, push, and a global banner.
Note: Business type cannot be changed by the pro after initial setup. If a pro needs to update their business type, frontline reps can post in #ttod-for-service-support to get it updated.
(Pro) Steps: How to update direct deposit
Pro steps: Pros can update their direct deposit information by following the steps in the How to set up direct deposit – Thumbtack Help article. 
Pros update their direct deposit from their Earnings page. The pro will go through a 2 factor authentication when updating their payout method.* After updating their direct deposit information, the pro will see a pop-up on their earnings page telling them their details have been submitted and that verification will take a few days  (1-3 business days). 
If Stripe verification for direct deposit is successful their earnings tab will show their bank account listed. However, if it fails the pro will receive a notification via email, push, and a global banner.
For more information on payout Information verification reps can refer to the internal Instant deposits KA to learn more. 
Navigating the “Payout Gateway Account: Stripe Connect" page in Admin 
The “Payout Gateway Account: Stripe Connect” page in Admin shows frontline reps the status of a pro’s direct deposit (setup successful or failed) and their account information connected to Stripe. The page is divided into sections:
Account Information: This section contains fields for business type (Not set, Individual, Company, or Nonprofit) and payout enabled (yes, no, indicating whether Stripe can send payouts).
Individual Info: This section is filled out if "Individual" was selected as the business type, and includes fields for first and last name, date of birth, last 4 digits provided, and status.
Business Profile: URL link to the pro’s publicly available business website. (e.g., Facebook, Insta, Twitter, Thumbtack profile link, an app store link, etc.)
Company Info: This section is filled out if "Company" was selected as the business type, and includes fields for company name and company tax ID provided.
Requirements: This section contains fields for "Currently Due," "Eventually Due," and "Pending Verification." If the direct deposit setup fails, frontline reps can view reasoning codes in these fields to help troubleshoot Stripe payout issues.
▶ Screenshot of  “Payout Gateway Account: Stripe Connect” page in Admin

(Rep) Steps: How to view a pro's direct deposit status in Admin (Troubleshoot)
If a pro is having issues with their payout account, they should never be asked to contact Stripe.
To check if a pro has direct deposit set up or to view their Stripe connected account information, frontline reps can go to the Payout Gateway Account Details page in Admin.
Frontline reps can follow these steps to troubleshoot Stripe payout requirements for a pro:
In admin, pull up the pros account.
In the Actions column on the right-hand side, under “Payments,” select Payout Gateway Account Details.
▶ Screenshot of "Payout Gateway Account Details" button[Image: AD_4nXejjO1ztbjBSUAY213ULsshv9YCbzF6egaz6QM4HqMfCsT_h9VqVjhi1ILWNi3HGvonEaAJHUaSX0XZEgcxzyxTL4-Ov6Cl_LJ6ekiRB_fI0DEfK4KsxZ0igDozVKVuzBjwu9i3]
If the setup is successful, reps will see the pro’s Stripe Connected Account information and the “Requirements” fields will be blank.
If direct deposit setup fails, reps will see reasoning codes in the “Requirements” section on this page. Refer to the "reasoning code table " table within this KA to learn what the codes mean.
▶ Screenshot of "requirements" field in admin.[Image: AD_4nXeZER3ziAiFNt_UdH0CFFAqayflnZbt2YGvbl9XWNat2bFkUuWSxBTZGNhlHpW7K2mtjsR3KWtoXtuEDTGskUmnGFT8XIB5dF87Vt6LRFBxg15yX-TK4quWNrCN96LPs_1s4nOi8w]
▶ Requirements reasoning codes for failed direct deposit setup (in admin)

Requirements reasoning codes
What the code means 
business_profile.url
URL link to the Pro’s publicly available business website.
If the pro doesn’t have a business website, they can use the following instead: 
Thumbtack profile link. 
Go to profile, then select 'view as customer' and copy the URL.
A business social media profile URL.  e.g., Facebook, Insta, Twitter, ETC. 
An app store link
Or pros can select to “add a brief product description instead”, which takes them to a text box to briefly explain the services provided.
external_account
Pro’s Bank account and routing number.
Individual.address.city
Individual.address.line1
Individual.address.postal_code
individual.address.state
Pro’s full primary address
Individual.dob.day
Individual.dob.month
individual.dob.year
Pro’s date of birth
individual.first_name
individual.last_name
Pro’s first & last name
individual.email
Pro’s email address
individual.id_number
Pro’s government-issued ID number. 
SSN - Social Security Number
individual.phone
Pro’s phone number
tos_acceptance.date
Details on the account’s acceptance of the Stripe Services Agreement.
tos_acceptance.ip
The IP address from which the account Pro accepted their service agreement. This is done on the last ‘let’s review your details’ page. The pro selects submit to accept the Terms of Service (TOS).
company.tax_id
One or more documents that demonstrate proof of a company’s tax ID. Employee Identification Number (EIN)

3. Examples in Admin
▶ Completed individual account
The screenshot displays a Stripe Connected Account page in Admin for a pro with a individual business type with a verified payout account (completed).
The Account Information section shows the business type as Individual and payout enabled as True, indicating that Stripe can send payouts.

4. Talking points
 SSN, EIN, or bank account questions

English talking points
Spanish talking points
How can I apply for an EIN?
¿Cómo puedo solicitar un EIN?
You can find more information and links to resources on applying for an EIN here.
Puede encontrar más información y enlaces a recursos sobre cómo solicitar un EIN aquí.
What if I don’t have an SSN or EIN?
¿Qué pasa si no tengo un SSN o EIN?
You won’t be able to receive payments through Thumbtack unless you have an SSN or EIN for direct deposit. For leads, you can still receive payments in person or through a payment app for customers you have connected with via direct leads or opportunities. Claiming a preset job requires you to have direct deposit set up in order to be paid.
No podrá recibir pagos a través de Thumbtack a menos que tenga un SSN o EIN para depósito directo. Para prospectos exactos, aún puede recibir pagos en persona o a través de una aplicación de pago para clientes con los que se ha conectado a través de oportunidades o prospectos exactos. Reclamar un trabajo prepagado requiere que tenga un depósito directo configurado para recibir el pago. 
Direct deposit for preset jobs
Note: For additional talking points, frontline reps can refer to the Claimable Jobs (Pro) KA. 

English talking points
Spanish talking points
How do I set up direct deposit? 
¿Cómo configuro el depósito directo? 
After you claim a job, you’ll be taken directly to Stripe, our trusted payment partner, to set up direct deposit. You'll need to provide a few personal details including your full Social Security number or Employer Identification Number. After ID verification, you’ll be directed back to Thumbtack to enter your bank account and routing numbers. Once your bank account is added and verified, you’ll be able to receive payment after you finish a preset job.
Una vez que reclame un trabajo, se le dirigirá directamente a Stripe, nuestro socio de pagos de confianza, para configurar el depósito directo. Usted deberá proporcionar algunos datos personales, incluido su número completo de Seguro Social o su Número de identificación del empleador. Después de la verificación de identidad, se le dirigirá nuevamente a Thumbtack para ingresar los números de cuenta bancaria y ruta. Una vez que se agregue y verifique su cuenta bancaria, podrá recibir el pago después de finalizar un trabajo reclamado.
How do I receive payment?
¿Cómo recibo el pago?
Once you finish the job, you’ll be able to mark the job as complete by either clicking on a push notification or going to the messenger. Once you mark the job as complete, we’ll begin the transfer to your bank account. It typically takes 3-5 days to see the money in your bank account.
Una vez que termine el trabajo, podrá marcar el trabajo como completo haciendo clic en una notificación automática o yendo al mensajero. Una vez que marque el trabajo como completo, comenzaremos la transferencia a su cuenta bancaria. Por lo general, toma de 3 a 5 días ver el dinero en su cuenta bancaria.
NOTE: If the pro doesn’t mark the job as complete, as a fallback, after 24 hours Thumbtack will automatically begin the transfer process to the pro’s bank account. Frontline reps shouldn’t advertise this to pros as Thumbtack wants to encourage pros to mark the job as complete.
Pro has concerns about direct deposit (overcoming pro objections to direct deposit)
Frontline reps may encounter objections from pros who are hesitant to set up direct deposit. For example, a pro may state, “I refuse to set up direct deposit.”  To overcome these objections, frontline reps can utilize the following common objections and potential solutions to overcome them: 

Objection
English talking points
Spanish talking points
Fees: I’m worried Thumbtack will charge me or the customer a processing fee.
There are no fees for standard deposits. For instant deposits, there is a 1% fee for each instant deposit. Fees will never be hidden.
No hay cargos por los depósitos estándar. Para los depósitos instantáneos, hay una tarifa del 1 % por cada depósito instantáneo. Las tarifas nunca se ocultarán.
Effort: It will take too much time to set up direct deposit.
You’ll be able to complete the direct deposit set up in just a few easy steps, plus there’s a helpful step-by-step guide if you have any questions. There are 3 main steps to setting up direct deposit: adding your personal and business information, uploading a photo of a government-issued ID, and adding in your banking information.
Podrá completar la configuración del depósito directo en solo unos pocos sencillos pasos, además hay una útil guía paso a paso si tiene alguna pregunta. Hay 3 pasos principales para configurar el depósito directo: agregar su información personal y comercial, cargar una foto de una identificación emitida por el gobierno y agregar su información bancaria.
Security: I’m concerned about Thumbtack having access to my bank account/data.
Thumbtack doesn’t store your bank routing and account number. We use Stripe to process our payments, who stores this info. Stripe is a certified PCI Service Provider Level 1, which is the most stringent level of certification available in the payments industry. All card numbers are encrypted. You can read more about security at Stripe here.
Thumbtack no almacena su ruta bancaria ni su número de cuenta. Usamos Stripe para procesar nuestros pagos, quién almacena esta información. 1. OVERVIEW
Demand partners are businesses that generate demand for another business's advertisement inventory. These partnerships help Thumbtack pros be seen by more customers.
Pros will benefit from increased exposure, which means more opportunities for pros to be shown and get hired.
▶ Partner vs competitor
Some of Thumbtack's demand partners may seem like competitors to Thumbtack. The difference between a partner website and a competitor is the user experience.
Pros are not allowed to redirect customers from Thumbtack to a competitor's website. This is considered contact avoidance and violates our Terms of Use (ToU). See Contact Avoidance (Pro) KA to learn more. 
Customers on demand partner websites follow the same request process as any other Thumbtack customer. This means contacts from a partner website appear like all other Thumbtack contacts.

For example, Networx is considered a competitor website on the pro side and a partner website on the customer side. Pros can’t direct TT customers to Networx, but customers can submit a Thumbtack request from the Networx platform. 
Having Thumtack's request form embedded on partner websites provides additional advertising for Thumbtack pros, which helps them get hired more on Thumbtack. Learn more on the Job Request Forms (Customer) KA to learn more about the embedded request form. 
If a pro asks why customers can submit a Thumbtack request on a competitor's website, you can explain that pros benefit from increased exposure on our partner websites, providing more opportunities to be visible and hired.
Embedded request form flow
Thumbtack's embedded request form feature allows demand partner platforms to display the Thumbtack request form as a pop-up (iFrame) on their own site. When a customer clicks on a Thumbtack pro from a partner platform, a pop-up appears labeled "Powered by Thumbtack." The customer fills out the request form — including project details, zip code, and contact info — without leaving the partner's website.
The flow mirrors the standard Thumbtack request experience. Contacts submitted through an embedded form appear in Thumbtack like any other customer contact. See Job Request Forms (Customer) for more details.

To learn more about the Armis experience, See Armis Partnership KA. 
▶ Neighborly (PROTRADENET)
Neighborly® is a home services platform (similar to Thumbtack), but they deal primarily with franchisees that operate in multiple locations. They are one of the world’s largest franchising organizations with nearly 3,700 franchisees, and now, many of these franchises will be encouraged to sign up on Thumbtack.
To make the onboarding experience simple and easy for these pros, we’re pre-building profiles for these pros based on information provided by Neighborly®.
The Sales team is reaching out to these pros with their prebuilt profiles and asking if they want to claim their new Thumbtack profile. They’ll also be offering them a Prepaid Packages.
The Success team helps any pros who signed up after talking with sales get started and onboarded.
The Support teams can help these pros with basic account-related questions (like changing their password). If the pro would like to make changes to their targeting preferences, budget, or specifically asks to speak with their Success manager, transfer them.

Pros will benefit from increased exposure within Nextdoor search results and on Nextdoor topic pages. This means more opportunities for pros to be shown and get hired.
All pros nationwide who show up in Thumbtack search results are also eligible to show in Nextdoor, but it is the Nextdoor Algorithm that selects the pros to be surfaced.
