2. TALKING POINTS

NEIGHBORLY
 
How do I get more leads?
Many pros find they start getting more leads when they do four things: respond quickly (and consistently), get more reviews, build an engaging profile, and add pricing. Doing these four things can help you appear higher in search results, which means customers are more likely to see your business.
¿Cómo consigo más prospectos?
Muchos profesionales descubren que comienzan a obtener más clientes potenciales cuando hacen cuatro cosas: responder de manera rápida (y consistente), obtener más evaluaciones, crear un perfil atractivo y agregar precios. Hacer estas cuatro cosas puede ayudarlo a aparecer más alto en los resultados de búsqueda, lo que significa que es más probable que los clientes vean su negocio.
Why do I need to turn on targeting preferences?
Your targeting preferences are how we know which jobs you want (and which ones you auto-pay for). They’re also important in making sure you show up in the right search results. They’re how you find the right customers and get quality leads.
¿Por qué necesito activar las preferencias de enfoque?
Sus preferencias de enfoque son la forma en que sabemos qué trabajos desea (y cuáles paga automáticamente). También son importantes para asegurarse de que aparezcas en los resultados de búsqueda correctos. Son la forma de encontrar los clientes adecuados y obtener clientes potenciales de calidad.
What’s an exact match lead?
It’s a lead that matches all your targeting preferences. These are the leads you auto-pay for because they check all your boxes. You can still get leads from customers that don’t match your preferences (in fact, you probably will), but when that happens you decide if you’re interested.
¿Qué es un prospecto exacto?
Es un cliente potencial que coincide con todas sus preferencias de enfoque. Estos son los clientes potenciales por los que usted paga automáticamente porque marcan todas sus preferencias de enfoque. Todavía puede obtener clientes potenciales de prospectos que no coinciden con sus preferencias de enfoque (de hecho, probablemente lo hará), pero cuando eso sucede, usted decide si está interesado.
How fast do I need to respond to new leads?
The quicker the better. Customers that receive a fast response (within five minutes is best) are more than 50% more likely to respond to a pro. Plus, if you signed a 6- or 12-month contract, you're eligible for a promotional credit. Make sure you respond to new customers in under 30 minutes more than 80% of the time (during the hours of 8am and 8pm).
¿Qué tan rápido necesito responder a nuevos prospectos?
Cuanto más rápido, mejor. Los clientes que reciben una respuesta rápida (dentro de los cinco minutos es mejor) tienen más de un 50 % más de probabilidades de responder a un profesional. Además, si firmó un contrato de 6 o 12 meses, es elegible para un crédito promocional. Asegúrese de responder a los nuevos clientes en menos de 30 minutos más del 80 % del tiempo (durante el horario de 8 a. m. a 8 p. m.).
How do I get more reviews?
Glad you asked. Once you start working with Thumbtack customers, you should send them a review request — this ensures their review is marked as ‘verified’ on your profile.
For customers you worked with outside of Thumbtack, you can add up to 20 reviews. Try importing them from Google or sending individual customers a link to your review page. Find steps on how to do this in our help article about asking for reviews.
¿Cómo obtengo más evaluaciones?
Me alegro de que haya preguntado. Una vez que comience a trabajar con los clientes de Thumbtack, debe enviarles una solicitud de evaluación; esto garantiza que su evaluación se marque como "verificada" en su perfil.
Para los clientes con los que trabajó fuera de Thumbtack, puede agregar hasta 20 evaluaciones. Intente importarlos de Google o envíe a los clientes individuales un enlace a su página de evaluación. Encuentre los pasos para hacerlo en nuestro artículo de ayuda sobre cómo solicitar evaluaciones.
Do I need to take a background check?
We strongly encourage you to take a background check. In fact, we even cover the cost of taking it. It’s also a requirement for becoming a Top Pro on Thumbtack, which is a distinction we’re confident many Neighborly® pros will become. The background check must be taken by the Thumbtack account holder (the person listed on the account).
¿Necesito tomar una verificación de antecedentes?
Le recomendamos encarecidamente que realice una verificación de antecedentes. De hecho, incluso cubrimos el costo de llevarlo. También es un requisito para convertirse en Top Pro en Thumbtack, que es una distinción en la que estamos seguros de que se convertirán muchos profesionales de Neighborly®. La verificación de antecedentes debe ser realizada por el titular de la cuenta de Thumbtack (la persona que figura en la cuenta). 
Is my credit pack refundable?
No. As noted in your contract, packages aren’t refundable. However, there may be times when an individual lead qualifies for a refund. Check out our refund policy to learn more.
And keep in mind, when a lead matches your targeting preferences you qualify for The Quality Commitment.
¿Mi paquete de créditos es reembolsable?
No. Como se indica en su contrato, los paquetes no son reembolsables. Sin embargo, puede haber ocasiones en las que un prospecto individual califique para un reembolso. Consulte nuestra póliza de reembolso para obtener más información.
Y tenga en cuenta que cuando un prospecto coincide con sus preferencias de enfoque, califica para el Compromiso de calidad.
What happens after I spend my credit pack?
With a credit pack, the cost of leads are deducted from your Thumbtack balance. When your balance is gone, you’ll pay for leads with the credit card on your account. How much you spend depends on your weekly spend limit.
¿Qué sucede después de que gaste mi paquete de créditos?
Con un paquete de créditos, el costo de los prospectos se deduce de su saldo de Thumbtack. Cuando se agote su saldo, pagará los prospectos con la tarjeta de crédito de su cuenta. Cuánto gasta depende de su límite de gasto semanal.
What topics will you cover in the Get Started Workshop?
We know we’ve shared a lot of information with you. Our workshop is one way to learn the ins and outs of Thumbtack with our help. This is a resource available only to Neighborly® pros. We’ll have two weekly sessions, so join when it’s convenient for you.
¿Qué temas cubrirá en el Taller de inicio?Sabemos que hemos compartido mucha información con usted. Nuestro taller es una forma de aprender los entresijos de
Thumbtack con nuestra ayuda. Este es un recurso disponible solo para los profesionales de Neighborly®. Tendremos dos sesiones semanales, así que únase cuando sea conveniente para usted.
NEXTDOOR 
 
What is Nextdoor?
Nextdoor is a private social network to connect with your neighbors. Nextdoor members can search for local services directly on the site.
¿Qué es Nextdoor?
Nextdoor es una red social privada para conectarse con sus vecinos. Los miembros de Nextdoor pueden buscar servicios locales directamente en el sitio.
How does this partnership work?
When Nextdoor members search for local services, they can see up to three Thumbtack pros directly within the Nextdoor search results with information from the pros' profiles. When the customer chooses one of these pros, they will be shown a pop-up window that takes them through Thumbtack's request flow while still on the Nextdoor page where they can reach out directly.
¿Cómo funciona esta asociación?
Cuando los miembros de Nextdoor buscan servicios locales, pueden ver hasta tres profesionales de Thumbtack directamente dentro de los resultados de búsqueda de Nextdoor con información de los perfiles de los profesionales. Al seleccionar uno de estos profesionales, el cliente puede enviar una solicitud o ser dirigido al perfil del profesional en Thumbtack. En este caso, se le mostrará una ventana emergente que lo guiará a través del flujo de solicitudes de Thumbtack mientras permanece en la página de Nextdoor, donde puede comunicarse directamente con el profesional.
What is the benefit?
Pros will benefit from increased exposure within Nextdoor search results and on Nextdoor topic pages. This means more opportunities for pros to be shown and get hired.
¿Cuál es el beneficio?
Los profesionales se beneficiarán de una mayor exposición en los resultados de búsqueda de Nextdoor y en las páginas de temas de Nextdoor. Esto significa más oportunidades para los profesionales de ser visto y ser contratado.
What services are included?
Housecleaning, handymen, landscaping, local moving, furniture repair, pets, and lessons. Over time, the plan is to expand to more categories and we will share more info as it becomes available.
¿Qué servicios están incluidos?
Limpieza de la casa, personal de mantenimiento, jardinería, mudanzas locales, reparación de muebles, mascotas y lecciones. Con el tiempo, el plan es expandirse a más categorías y compartiremos más información a medida que esté disponible.
Which pros qualify?
All pros nationwide who show up in Thumbtack search results are also eligible to also show in Nextdoor.
¿Qué profesionales califican?
Todos los profesionales de todo el país que aparecen en los resultados de búsqueda de Thumbtack también son elegibles para aparecer en Nextdoor.

How can I get on Nextdoor?
There is no need to opt-in. If you rank in the top 3 on Thumbtack Results for your given market, your profile will automatically be exposed on Nextdoor search.
¿Cómo puedo acceder a Nextdoor?
No es necesario que se inscriba. Si se encuentra entre los 3 primeros en los resultados de Thumbtack para su mercado determinado, su perfil se mostrará automáticamente en la búsqueda de Nextdoor.
Will I be able to tell if a lead came from Nextdoor?
Users coming from Nextdoor will go through the request flow just like every other Thumbtack customer. This means that Nextdoor contacts will look like all other contacts.
¿Podré saber si un prospecto proviene de Nextdoor?
Los usuarios que acceden desde Nextdoor seguirán el flujo de solicitud, aterrizarán en su página de perfil y enviarán un mensaje de contacto, al igual que cualquier otro cliente de Thumbtack. Esto significa que los contactos de Nextdoor se verán como cualquier otro contacto.

Home: This is the customer's personalized dashboard. Think of it as their starting point, offering customized guides, timely recommendations based on the season, and ideas for new projects. (This replaced the old "Explore" tab).
Search: This is where customers find pros. They describe what they need, and our AI matches them with relevant professionals and comprehensive results. This feature is also available from the "Plan" tab.
Plan: This is the customer's central hub for managing all their home projects. They can organize, track progress, set reminders, and get cost estimates and insights into their return on investment. Projects are categorized into "Booked," "Planned," and "Done." (This replaced the old "Projects" tab).
Team: This is a curated list of all the pros a customer has contacted since 2019. It allows them to quickly re-book services (except for on-demand jobs), message their preferred pros, and even share trusted professionals with others. They can also view their project history with a specific pro directly from that pro's card.
Inbox: This is the primary communication channel for new messages from pros after a project request. It includes features like visual badges and smart sorting to help customers prioritize unread conversations. While "Team" manages ongoing relationships, "Inbox" is critical for new project communications and is the only way to access pro communications on the web.

Project Status Categories:
Projects within the Plan tab are effectively organized into distinct categories, providing a clear overview of their progress. At the top of the tab, customers will see statuses like 'Not started,' 'In progress,' and 'Done,' each indicating the number of projects currently in that phase.
More broadly, projects fall into these primary statuses:
Booked: These are projects for which a booking with a professional has been confirmed. For these projects, customers will see "Project details" options to review their booking.
Planned: This category includes projects customers have added to their plan, those for which they've filled out a request form, or projects where they've contacted a pro. Depending on the specific status, customers will have options like "View messages," "Find a pro," and "Get tips" for these projects.
Done: This status applies to projects that have been completed or marked as canceled by the customer. Clicking on "Done" will open a new page displaying a list of all their completed, canceled, or deleted projects.
It's crucial to remember that the project status shown here in the customer's Plan tab is separate from how a pro views the job status on their end.

After submitting a project, customers can respond to new messages from pros by going to their Inbox. Aside from the Team tab, it is an additional way to communicate with the pros they are working with.

The Inbox is the primary communication channel for new messages from pros after a project request. To improve responsiveness, the inbox includes several features to highlight unread messages.
Here are a few common terms with definitions: 
Unread message: A message in the customer's inbox that they have not yet opened or clicked on.
Read message: A message in the customer's inbox that they have opened or clicked on.
Nudge: A prompt displayed to the customer, such as the blue text "Sent X days ago. Reply?". Nudges appear for unread messages after 24 hours. 
Inbox Cues and Notifications
If a customer doesn't read a pro's message after 24 hours, they will see several inbox cues: These triggers include:

Inbox Message Sorting
To improve the likelihood of customers responding to unread messages from pros, the customer’s inbox is sorted in the following order: 
Priority 1: Unread message without a nudge
Priority 2: Unread message with a nudge
Priority 3: Read messages with a nudge
Priority 4: Read messages

Updating Project Status from the Inbox
When a customer clicks on an unread message, a prompt will appear asking, "Did you hire this pro?".

[Image: rtaImage]

This prompt is visible for 14 days if the customer has not responded. The customer can select one of three options to update the project's status for the pro:
▶ 'Yes, I’ve hired this pro'
If only one pro was contacted, the customer sees the message: “You indicated that you hired this pro.”
If more than one pro was contacted, the customer sees the message: “We let other pros you contacted know that they weren’t hired.”
▶ 'No, I’m going with someone else'The customer sees the message: “We let the pro know that you hired someone else.”
▶ 'I’m not pursuing this project'
If only one pro contacted, the customer sees the message: “We’ve let the pro know that you’re not pursuing this project.”
If more than one pro was contacted, the customer sees the message: “We’ve let this pro and all others you contacted know that you’re not pursuing this project.”

2. Process
 
Steps: How to create a home profile (Customer) 
The home profile helps customers manage and improve their home by providing a personalized plan based on their unique home and goals. Frontline reps can direct web customers to download the Thumbtack customer app to access this feature, as it is only available on the app. Reps can share the Download the Thumbtack App link with customers to have them enter their phone number to have Thumbtack text them a link to download the app. 
For full details on how customers can create and update their home profile, refer to the Help Center article: How to get a personalized plan for your home – Thumbtack Help
Customers can only have one home profile at this time. However, they can change their address within their home profile if needed to work on another home.
Internal info only: In future versions, we may build the option to have multiple home profiles (multiple addresses).
Steps: Update home profile details (Customer) 
Updating their Home Profile may adjust the personalized guides on their Home tab. For example, a customer address is tied to the seasonal recommendations we show them. 
Customers can update their home profile at any time by following these steps:
Open the Customer App and navigate to the “Home” tab. 
In the top left, click your address.
Click into each field you want to make updates to and then tap Done.
Note: Customers cannot view or update their home profile on the website. 

[Image: d7f8GT5Hs3-pPES1y-4z_RjVnhPX0y9heOKonaXo6jHAR842S4Kp77mewweUzAbMbjO_wq5UqSo14pDjF8xrEZoVj9YWMvezW2c-b_ra5_wgge6KF1eNtDC7seAOK0PKMZKMkcHmYDpFnHAxJTapPf4]
Steps: How to add a project to the plan tab (Customer) 
This section details the various methods customers can use to add projects to their Plan tab, enabling them to organize and manage all their home-related tasks in one convenient place.
Customers can add projects to their Plan tab using several methods:
Method 1: During Onboarding
Projects can be added as part of the initial home profile creation process when a customer first onboards.
Method 2: Using the "Add Project" Button on the Plan Tab
Navigate to the "Plan" tab in the customer app.
Click the blue "Add project" button in the lower right corner.
Describe your project or problem in the search bar. (Thumbtack will match your description with the most relevant category in the background.)
Tap "Add project."
Note: Adding a project this way allows customers to name the project in their own words (e.g., "snow removal for front sidewalk"). If a customer notices they were matched with the wrong category after adding a project, they can remove it and add a new one.
Method 3: Using the Bookmark Icon
Click the bookmark icon (often found on the Home page for recommendations, guides, and within home upkeep, or directly from search results) to save a project to your Plan.
Method 4: From Search Results
Projects can also be added directly from search results after finding a pro or service.
▶ What it looks like to add a project from the Plan tab:
A
[Image: VDVsZKG9ByAP9dZ7XBPue3qZR7ECB0y_vPE1bid9H2hwDY9HFykVEZ7kF3qWNmvt1j11Ft8K6GzZrhcQ2sgGJY7uJ61LznP9s3jK4pQ9QB8JAwqYzIWCN68Z7HPpwdeo1Fs3zsXs7xww9XpuAMWS-NM]


Steps: How to remove, archive, or mark project complete from plan tab (Customer) 
 
This section outlines the steps customers can take to remove, archive, or mark projects as complete from their Plan tab, ensuring their project list remains organized and reflective of current needs.
To remove a project from the Plan tab, customers will follow these steps:
Open the Customer App.
Navigate to the "Plan" tab.
Locate the project you wish to remove. Projects are displayed as "Project Cards" on this tab.

Once the customer has located the project card, they can remove it using one of the following methods:
Method 1: Using Quick Actions on Project Cards
Swipe Left on the project card to mark a project as complete.
Swipe Right on the project card to archive a project. When archiving, options will appear to "Archive this instance," "Archive all future," or "Cancel."
Method 2: Using the "More Actions" Menu (three dots)
Click the three dots ("...") on a project card.
Select "Archive" or "Delete" from the options.
NOTE: Projects that have been marked as done or canceled stay on the Plan page, but are moved to the Done section.
Steps: How to set or update a project reminder (Customer) 

When customers add a project to their Plan, they are prompted to set a reminder. If they don't set a reminder, an automatic monthly reminder is scheduled for them.
To update a project reminder, they will follow these steps: 
Open the Customer app and navigate to the “Plan” tab. 
Click into the applicable project. 
Scroll down and click the pencil next to set reminder. 
Set or update the reminder and tap Save. 
 
Note: Customers can also swipe left from the project card and click the purple bell icon that appears to add/update the reminder. 
▶ What it looks like to set a reminder from the "Your project" section on the "Plan tab.

[Image: RiXUyIFtM0VILiS7w5ryxshtKoB-WGoKLq94QAc-Of3FmgtN4qsuU7coZApl81A_uRkiY0JLnGaKup_wQXi8y_HT3IUq4rUDnvAHTRTw-6NtHppOKhhHzWkm3AdetRakKjoL3klo6J2fyZr_HD8nlrQ]

Steps: How to schedule a pro again from the team tab (Customer) 
To schedule a pro again (or re-book them) from the Team tab, customers will follow these steps:
Open the Thumbtack app and navigate to the Team tab.
Go to the "Your Team" sub-tab.
Locate the pro you wish to schedule again.
On the pro's card, tap the "Schedule/Book" option.
Review your new project details. These will be identical to your previous project with this pro. You can either:
Click "Edit project" to update the details if needed.
Click "Next" to move forward with the project using the current details.
Please note: This option supports direct leads, but on-demand jobs cannot be re-booked this way. New bookings initiated here will appear as a new request and message thread, similar to a booking from search results.
Steps: How to add or remove a pro from the team tab (Customer) 
This section provides detailed steps on how customers can add or remove pros from their "Your Team" and "Past Pros" sections within the Team tab, allowing them to manage their network of trusted pros.
Pros the customer has contacted on Thumbtack are automatically added to the“Past pros” section of their Team tab.  
▶ To Add a Pro to Your Team from Past Pros:
Customers will follow these steps to add a pro from their Team tab:
Open the Thumbtack app.
Go to your Team tab.
If the "Your Team" section is empty, customers can add pros by tapping the heart icon next to any pro listed in your "Past Pros" tab.
If they previously removed a pro from their "Your Team" section, customers can add them back by:
Tapping the heart icon on their card in the "Archived" page (which appears within "Past Pros" if you have archived pros).
Or, tapping the three dots (...) on their card and selecting "Unarchive."
Please note: If the customer archived a pro but later contacts them again for a new project, the pro will automatically be re-added to the "Past Pros" tab.
▶ To Remove a Pro from Your Team:
Customers will follow these steps to remove a pro from their Team tab:
Open the Thumbtack app.
Go to your Team tab.
In the "Your Team" section, find the pro you wish to remove.
If you are on an iPhone: Swipe left on the pro's card and tap the trash can icon.
If you are on an Android phone: Tap the three dots (...) on the pro's card and select "Remove."
▶ Important Notes for Frontline Reps:
If there is no existing message thread with a pro, the "Message" and "Schedule" options on their card will appear grayed out. Customers can still click the three dots to archive or cancel the project.
If a pro's business becomes deactivated, all actionable options (like "Message" or "Schedule") on their card within the "Team" tab will appear grayed out or may indicate "No longer on Thumbtack."

3. Talking points 
This section provides key talking points and suggested responses for frontline reps to use when discussing the Thumbtack customer app experience with both customers and pros.
Customer
 
General customer app overview 
These talking points help frontline reps introduce Thumbtack''s enhanced customer app, highlighting its purpose in empowering homeowners and connecting them with trusted pros.

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: Why should I use the Thumbtack app? 
Q: ¿Por qué utilizar la aplicación de Thumbtack?
A: With Thumbtack’s all-in-one homeownership app, you can: 
Organize your home project planning and execution effortlessly.
Make informed decisions with reliable cost estimates and ROI tips.
Connect with your team of previously booked pros
A: Con la aplicación integral para propietarios de viviendas de Thumbtack, usted puede:
Organizar la planificación y ejecución de sus proyectos de hogar sin esfuerzo.
Tomar decisiones informadas con estimaciones de costos confiables y consejos sobre el ROI.
Conectar con su equipo de profesionales previamente contratados.
Why are my messages sorted differently now? 
¿Por qué ahora mis mensajes están ordenados de forma diferente?
To help you see messages you haven't read, we're sorting your inbox. Unread messages will appear at the top, so you won't miss them. This helps you connect with pros who have responded to your request.
Para ayudarle a ver los mensajes que no ha leído, estamos ordenando su bandeja de entrada. Los mensajes no leídos aparecerán arriba para que no se le pasen. Esto le ayuda a conectarse con profesionales que ya respondieron a su solicitud.
What does it mean when a message is marked as "unread"? 
¿Qué significa cuando un mensaje está marcado como unread (“no leído”)?
It means we've noticed you haven't replied to the pro's message yet. We're highlighting it to make sure you see it and can respond if you're still interested.
Significa que notamos que usted todavía no ha respondido al mensaje del profesional. Lo resaltamos para asegurarnos de que usted lo vea y pueda responder si todavía le interesa.
How long will a message be marked as "unread"? 
¿Por cuánto tiempo un mensaje estará marcado como unread (“no leído”)?
The message will be marked as "unread" until you click on it again. The nudge text will stay visible for up to 14 days, or until you respond to the pro, make a hiring selection, or leave a review.
El mensaje estará marcado como unread (“no leído”) hasta que usted lo seleccione de nuevo. El texto de recordatorio seguirá visible por hasta 14 días, o hasta que usted responda al profesional, elija a quién contratar o deje una reseña.
What if I'm not interested in a pro anymore?
¿Qué pasa si ya no me interesa un profesional?
If you're no longer interested, you can respond to the pro to let them know (the best route in most cases) or you can decline the pro. We're also working on ways to make it easier to close conversations you're no longer interested in.
Si ya no le interesa, puede responderle al profesional para avisarle (en la mayoría de los casos, es la mejor opción) o puede rechazar al profesional. También estamos trabajando en formas de facilitar el cierre de conversaciones que ya no le interesan.
Understanding the Home profile
These talking points guide frontline reps in explaining the Home Profile feature to customers, detailing its role as a personalized digital assistant for homeowners and how it informs the app's tailored recommendations.

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Q: What’s the home profile? 
Q: ¿Qué es el perfil de la vivienda?
A: The home profile is where to help you manage and improve your home in a simple way. It's like having a personal digital assistant that keeps track of all the essential information and history of your home, making it super convenient for you to access whenever you need it.
A: El perfil de la vivienda es su herramienta integral para gestionar y mejorar su hogar de forma sencilla. Imagine tener un asistente digital personal que registra toda la información esencial y el historial de su propiedad, permitiéndole acceder a ella de manera práctica en cualquier momento.
How do I create a home profile? 
¿Cómo creo un perfil de hogar?
To create or update your home profile:
Log in through the Thumbtack app (or create your account, if you don't have one).
Answer a few questions about your home, inside and out, and tap Next.
Enter your address, then tap Next.
Answer a few more questions about what types of maintenance are important to you.
Next, select which projects are at the top of your list. Tap the bookmark symbol next to any project and we’ll save it to your plan. 
Then, tap Finish.
Para crear o actualizar su perfil de hogar, siga estos pasos:
Inicie sesión en la aplicación Thumbtack (o cree su cuenta si aún no dispone de una).
Responda algunas preguntas sobre las características interiores y exteriores de su hogar y seleccione "Siguiente".
Introduzca su dirección y luego seleccione "Siguiente".
Responda algunas preguntas adicionales sobre los tipos de mantenimiento que son importantes para usted.
A continuación, seleccione los proyectos que tienen mayor prioridad en su lista. Simplemente presione el símbolo de marcador junto a cualquier proyecto y lo guardaremos en su plan.
Finalmente, presione "Finalizar".
Why do you ask for my address?
¿Por qué solicitan mi dirección?
Entering your address on your Home Profile helps us show you accurate pricing, nearby pros and useful tips for your home. 
If you don’t have an address saved, you may be asked to add one when you submit a project. 
Ingresar su dirección en su perfil de hogar nos ayuda a mostrarle precios exactos, profesionales cercanos y consejos útiles para su hogar.
Si usted no tiene una dirección guardada, es posible que se le pida que agregue una cuando envíe un proyecto.
Why are some questions already answered when I submit a new project? (prefilled based on customer home profile)
¿Por qué algunas preguntas aparecen pre contestadas cuando envío un nuevo proyecto? (basado en el perfil de hogar del cliente)
We use your home profile details to easily prefill them to your new projects.
Utilizamos los detalles de su perfil de hogar para completar fácilmente esta información en sus nuevos proyectos.
Can I create another home profile if I have another home? 
¿Puedo crear otro perfil de hogar si tengo una vivienda adicional?
No, you can only add details for one home at a time. However, you can change your address within your home profile if needed to work on another home.
No, actualmente solo puede agregar detalles para una vivienda a la vez. Sin embargo, tiene la opción de cambiar su dirección dentro de su perfil de hogar si necesita trabajar en otra propiedad.

1. Overview
▶ KA summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) provides Frontline Reps with a quick reference to active experiments running on Thumbtack that are being tracked. It includes how to identify if a user (pro or customer) is assigned to an experiment and how to interpret experiment logs.
As the market and needs of Thumbtack's users change, Thumbtack adapts to stay competitive and relevant. Thumbtack reduces risk by testing possible changes and observing how pros and customers react. Thumbtack runs a variety of experiments and tracks outcomes to make informed decisions for the platform's future. Frontline Reps will likely be contacted by a user who is part of an experiment. Staying up to date with experiments is key for Frontline Reps to resolve user issues and accurately portray how Thumbtack works for each user.

Internal Only: This internal KA does not include experiments that should not cause the pro or customer to contact Thumbtack support. Frontline Reps should not expect all experiments to be listed in this KA.
Experiment and feature priority
Every experiment and feature launch is assigned a feature priority from P0 to P3. The level reflects two things: how much the change could affect support volume or sales, and how much enablement support (KAs, training, comms) it needs. 
For reps, it's a quick signal of how likely you are to get contacted about a launch and how much you'll need to know — a P0 is a major, often public launch you should expect questions about, while a P3 is usually internal tracking or tooling with little direct pro or customer impact. You'll see the priority noted near the top of each experiment's KA.

Priority
What it means
Examples
P0 — High impact and priority
Large, complex launches with public GTM and/or complex enablement (new or heavily edited KAs, Compass courses, external help content). Significant potential impact to support volume or sales based on population, duration, geos, or revenue critical path. Product surface area or outsized partner impact can make something P0 even without public GTM.
Thumbtack Numbers nationwide launch; Completely Unresponsive Customer Refunds
P1 — Medium impact and priority
Medium-complexity launches with GTM and/or enablement needed to properly support or sell. Potential to affect support volume or sales based on population, duration, geos, or revenue critical path.
Partial match opt-in leads launch, Smart Match nationwide launch; Download lead data; Google review import refresh; Self serve webhooks
P2 — Low impact, medium priority
Small-to-medium-complexity launches. Limited potential to drive support volume or affect sales. Enablement may be needed, usually a KA only.
New pro discount; Magic link (passwordless accounts); Go live with ‘Activate profile’; Occupation Bid Setting History (NDFP) Admin section
P3 — Low impact and priority
Small-complexity launches for tracking only. Generally no enablement needed and no expected impact on support volume or sales.
BOSUP Discount Offers section Admin tool; Discounts section Admin tool

4. Experiment assignments in Admin
Experiments can be assigned at different granularities depending on what the experiment is measuring and how it is structured. Not all experiments will show in Admin, and some experiments are assigned at the user level or on the business level.
User-Level Assignment (user_pk): Assignment is tied to the account/user level—all of a pro's businesses will receive the same treatment (e.g., all in variant).
Business-Level Assignment (business_pk): Assignment is tied to the individual business profile, which is useful when each business has a distinct geo location or market.
Experiment assignments log overview
The "Experiment assignments” log in Admin shows Frontline Reps which experiments a pro or customer is part of, and it provides other details about the experience. These are the columns in the Experiments log and what they mean:
Experiment: This column shows the name of the experiment. 
Bucket: This column indicates whether a pro or customer is impacted by the experiment or not.
“Baseline" or unassigned: The pro or customer is not part of the experiment.
Variant, Variant 1, or any other text: The pro or customer is impacted by the experiment.
There is an Experiment Assignments log on the User page and the Business page. Reps will look at the main User page if the experiment is assigned as the user_Pk (most common) and the Business page if the experiment is assigned at the business_pk level.

Steps: How to see if a pro or customer is assigned to an experiment (Rep)
These steps are for experiments assigned at the user level (user_pk).
To determine if a pro or customer is part of an experiment, Frontline Reps can check the "Experiment assignments" section on the main User page in Admin:
View the user in Admin. (See the internal Admin Tool KA for more information.)
Scroll down and find the "Experiment assignments” section. 
Click the arrow next to the section's title to expand and view the list of experiments the user may be assigned to.
Review the "Bucket" column: If the term "variant" (e.g., variant, variant_1) appears, the pro or customer is part of that experiment.
Steps: How to see if a pro’s business profile is assigned to an experiment (Rep)
These steps are for experiments assigned at the business level (business_pk).

To see if a pro's service is in an experiment, Frontline Reps will follow these steps:

1. Overview
Tl;dr CSC customers are offered a credit in the form of a $100 rebate towards their first project on Thumbtack. 
What
On October 31, 2024, Thumbtack launched a promotion by partnering with CSC Serviceworks, where we’ll offer their customers a one-time credit towards their first project. This credit comes in the form of a $100 rebate.
CSC Serviceworks is a leading provider of commercial laundry services. CSC Serviceworks caters to over 40 million residents, consumers, property managers, and owners daily, offering both physical machines and a digital app for their services. Additionally, CSC will soon offer apps that enable residents to complete rent payments, service requests, and more. 
Why
By launching this partnership, Thumbtack aims to establish itself as the primary home services provider for all customers using its CSC apps. Additionally, we hope this will attract new Thumbtack customers who will encourage potential long-term use and product loyalty.
If we see positive signals around this partnership and demand generation, we may scale the program and more deeply access CSC’s millions of monthly active users who visit their app to complete home services. 
How
Thumbtack will be highlighted on their CSC Marketplace as a featured partner.
To incentivize CSC customers to try Thumbtack, they’ll be offered a $100 rebate for their first Thumbtack project. Each customer can redeem this offer once within a 12-month period.
Before a customer can claim their rebate, they must complete a project on Thumbtack and have paid the pro. However, they don’t need to pay the pro through Thumbtack to be eligible for this rebate.
Once a rebate is approved, we'll send the cost of their project, up to $100, to their preferred payment method through our partner, Hyperwallet.
Rebate terms and conditions
The rebate is valid for Thumbtack users only.
The customer account must be in good standing.
The rebate is a one-time credit that can only be applied to one project.
The pro who completes this project must have an active profile on Thumbtack and must have been contacted by you through Thumbtack.
The customer’s project must be completed and their credit redemption request received within 6 months.
The customer must submit the credit form and attach their receipt within 30 days of paying for the project.
This rebate can’t be stacked with another discount. Only one discount can be used per project. If you have multiple discounts available, this rebate will be applied first.
On-demand bookings are not eligible for this rebate.
Thumbtack reserves the right to end or revoke a discount, rebate, or promotion as needed.
This rebate is subject to Thumbtack’s Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.
Pilot details

Launch date: October 31, 2024 
End date: TBD
Rebate details
CSC Customers will see the rebate offer starting Oct 31, 2024
Customers must redeem their discount within 6 months.
Impacted users
CSC customers on the CSC Marketplace 
Identify impacted users
The user will mention the offer
Customer experience
CSC customers on the CSC Marketplace will see Thumbtack featured on the marketplace with the rebate offer. To take advantage of this opportunity, the customer clicks the Redeem offer button.
Do’s and Don’ts
When helping Thumbtack customers with a Perplexity rebate, support reps should follow these guidelines: 
Do direct them to the help center link for help with any questions.
Do explain how Thumbtack works and help the customer book a pro.
Don’t mention the rebate to customers who haven’t asked about it first.
2. Process

(Customer) Steps: How to claim CSC rebate
Before a customer can claim their rebate, they must complete a project on Thumbtack and have paid the pro. However, they don’t need to pay the pro through Thumbtack to be eligible.
After hiring and paying the pro, customers can claim their rebate by following these steps: 
Submit their project details using this form. Details include:
Pro name
Total cost of project
Address where work was completed
Receipt 
Once the claim is approved, we’ll send their rebate through Hyperwallet.
It may take up to a week for a rebate to be approved. 
The customer will get an email from Hyperwallet with instructions on how to create an account and choose how to receive their rebate. 
NOTE: Customers must: 
Complete the project and pay the pro (before claiming the rebate).
Submit the redemption form with an attached receipt within 30 days of paying for the project.
(Customer) Steps: How to claim payment in Hyperwallet
Once the customer’s claim is approved, Thumbtack will send funds to Hyperwallet to issue the customer's rebate as a payment.
Hyperwallet will send an email to the email on file. The email includes a Claim Payment button.
Clicking “Claim Payment” from the email, they will enter the Hyperwallet redemption flow. 
Hyperwallet will need details in order to send the payment. The customer will need to:
Select a payment option (PayPal, Venmo, etc.)
Provide profile details
Add account info
After claiming their rebate the customer can track their payment and will receive an email once their payment has been processed. 
Customers are sent a final email once the payment has been processed. The rebate will appear in the account the customer provided. The customer should reach out to Hyperwallet with any concerns or questions.
3. Talking points 

English talking points
Spanish talking points
How do I claim my rebate?
¿Cómo reclamo mi reembolso?
Once you’ve completed a project and paid the pro, you’re ready to claim your rebate.
Submit proof of your project payment using this form. 
Once your claim is approved, we’ll send your rebate through our partner, Hyperwallet.
Follow the instructions in the email from Hyperwallet to create an account and choose how to receive your rebate.
You can also check out our help article on how to claim your rebate to learn more.
Una vez que haya completado un proyecto y pagado al profesional, estará listo para reclamar su reembolso.
Envíe el comprobante de pago de su proyecto utilizando este formulario. 
Una vez que su reclamación sea aprobada, le enviaremos su reembolso a través de nuestro socio, Hyperwallet. 
Siga las instrucciones en el correo electrónico de Hyperwallet para crear una cuenta y elegir cómo recibir su reembolso.
También puede consultar nuestro artículo de ayuda sobre cómo reclamar su reembolso para obtener más información.
How will I know when my rebate is approved?
¿Cómo sabré cuándo se aprueba mi reembolso?
It may take up to a week for a rebate to be approved. Once it’s approved you’ll get an email from Hyperwallet.
La aprobación de un reembolso puede tardar hasta una semana. Una vez que se apruebe, recibirá un correo electrónico de Hyperwallet.
Do I have to use my credits all at once?
¿Tengo que utilizar mis créditos de una sola vez?
Yes, the $100 off needs to be used on one project, up to $100. If your project costs more than $100, you’ll receive the full $100 back. If your project cost is less than $100, you’ll receive the entire cost of your project and forfeit the remaining amount.
Sí, el descuento de $100 debe utilizarse en un solo proyecto, hasta $100. Si su proyecto cuesta más de $100, recibirá el reembolso completo de $100. Si el costo de su proyecto es inferior a $100, recibirá el coste total de su proyecto y perderá la cantidad restante.
Does this offer expire? 
¿Esta oferta tiene fecha de vencimiento?
No, the offer does not expire.
No, la oferta no tiene fecha de vencimiento.
Can the offer be converted into cash value?
Se puede convertir la oferta en dinero en efectivo?
No, this offer cannot be converted into cash value.
No, esta oferta no se puede convertir en dinero en effective.
Do I have to use my credit on Thumbtack?
¿Tengo que utilizar mi crédito en Thumbtack?
Yes, this rebate is only available on Thumbtack. However, you’re free to choose whatever project and pro you’re interested in using for your project as long as it falls within the terms and conditions.
Sí, este reembolso solo está disponible en Thumbtack. Sin embargo, usted es libre de elegir cualquier proyecto y profesional que le interese para su proyecto, siempre que cumpla con los términos y condiciones.
Will I see my credits in the Thumbtack app?
¿Veré mis créditos en la aplicación Thumbtack?
No. This isn’t a credit you will see on your account. Instead, you’ll need to complete a project and submit your receipt for reimbursement. You can check out our help article on how to claim your rebate to learn more.
No. Este no es un crédito que verá en su cuenta. En su lugar, deberá completar un proyecto y enviar su recibo para obtener el reembolso. Puede consultar nuestro artículo de ayuda sobre cómo reclamar su reembolso para obtener más información.
Is there a cost to sign up or use Thumbtack?
¿Hay algún costo por registrarse o utilizar Thumbtack?
There is no cost to sign up for Thumbtack or use Thumbtack. Pricing for projects will vary by category and depending on the pricing the pro sets.
No hay ningún costo por registrarse en Thumbtack ni por utilizar Thumbtack. Los precios de los proyectos varían según la categoría y los precios establecidos por el profesional.

articles.fullText:
Contact Avoidance (Pro)

Contents
Overview
Update
Terms of use
What contact avoidance is and is not
How we prevent contact avoidance and circumvention 
Process
(Rep) Steps: Pro wants to know why we redacted info in profile description or FAQ section
(Rep) Steps: How to handle situations where contact avoidance is discovered 
Talking points
Media wont save
Profile description was redacted
Pro was sent a warning for contact avoidance
Pro account was deactivated for contact avoidance
Resources
1. Overview 
When a pro receives a customer's contact on Thumbtack, they're charged for that contact. However, some pros try to avoid paying by providing customers a way to contact them outside Thumbtack. This is known as contact avoidance (CA), and it’s against our Terms of Use. 
Frontline reps can usually spot proof of contact avoidance in the pro's profile picture, images, business name, description, uploaded photos, or Q&As section. Pros can add their contact information (address, phone number, website, and social media) to the business info section of their profile. However, pros are not allowed to add this information to other sections of their profile. 
The Trust and Safety team may remove a pro for repeat violations after issuing email warnings. 

NOTE to frontline reps: Some of the information in this article should not be shared with pros. It is crucial that in our discussions with pros (or customers), we don't explain what we consider contact avoidance is or what we look for. This could lead to pros circumventing the systems we have in place to catch contact avoidance. To help you navigate these conversations, use the talking points below. 
Terms of use 
Thumbtack’s Terms of Use states the following:  
As a user of the Platform/As a Service Member, you may not: use the Platform in any manner that circumvents your obligation to pay Thumbtack for access to services provided by the Platform; Submit User Content that damages the experience of any user, including but not limited to requests to download non-Thumbtack mobile applications and/or links that direct the user to mirrored websites where the user must enter information that is redundant with what has already been entered on Thumbtack.
What contact avoidance is and is not 
Thumbtack considered contact information to be a:
Phone number
Email address
Website (if pro is requesting to be booked there). 
Contact avoidance is only considered in the following scenarios:

Contact avoidance type
Example
Contact information in profile photos, images, or other media. 

[Image: Screenshot 2024-07-30 at 8.37.20 AM.png]
. 
[Image: Screenshot 2024-07-30 at 8.39.32 AM.png]

Screenshots show the profile photo has the pro's contact information, which is not allowed.
Creates distrust in Thumbtack and provides their contact info.
Please note: I don’t often use Thumbtack. For faster inquiries, please go to my yelp or Instagram and message me for pricing and appointment times.
Incentivizes the customer to contact them outside the platform and provides their contact info.
To get one week of private training classes absolutely free- go to my website and fill out application for fitness consultation!—only with strongselves can you get intense strength workout, lose abdominal fat and tone up 💪🏻 ⁣
Spelling out or alerting how they write their phone number and email to avoid being flagged in the system.
1: Please shoot me a call or text if interested! five five five - four four four five five five five or email exampleemailaddress at yahoo
2: Text me @ five five five five five five five
Tells the customer not to contact them on Thumbtack and provides their contact info.
1: I don't pay to contact people through this website, so please contact me directly for faster service.
2: Please do NOT use the TT system unless you are 100% willing to book. TT charges $30 just for a reply. We are easy to find on Google as well. Thomas tack handyman is on FB. 1two3four5six7eight9ten
Contact avoidance is NOT considered when:
A pro tells customers only to contact them if they're serious about booking but does not provide personal contact information. 
How Thumbtack prevents contact avoidance and circumvention 
Thumbtack's system automatically prevents pros from including contact information in their profiles. This includes standard formats of phone numbers and email addresses, as well as contact information hidden within images. 
Error message: If a pro attempts to add contact information, they'll receive an error message and be unable to save their profile until the information is removed.
Redactions: For less obvious attempts to share contact information, Thumbtack uses AI to automatically identify and redact the information, then send the pro a warning email. 
Manual removal: If the AI is unable to automatically remove the contact information, a work ticket is created for manual review.
Account Hold: If the specialist is still unable to remove the information, the account is placed on hold, and an email is sent to the pro letting them know about the action taken. For account holds, reps can refer to the Account Holds (Pro) KA. 

Contact Avoidance Type
Action Taken
Pro Notification
Account Status
Standard format
Error message displayed; pro must remove contact info to save profile
No
Not on hold
Less obvious format
AI identifies and replaces contact information with asterisks
Yes
Not on hold
Unable to redact
Pro's account is put on hold; the pro is notified via email with instructions to update their profile
Yes
On hold
Repeat violations
Pro's account may be removed by Trust and Safety
Yes
Removed
2. Process 
(Reps) Steps: Pro wants to know why we redacted info in their profile description or FAQ section 
If a pro contacts support wondering why their profile description has asterisks in it, frontline reps will follow these steps:
Explain to the pro that the redacted text violates Thumbtack’s terms of use. Don’t use the term contact avoidance or go into what Thumbtack considers contact avoidance. 
Talking point: Some of the text in your profile description violated our terms of use and has been redacted by our Trust and Safety Team. You can edit your profile and remove them. However, if it’s replaced with text that violates our terms of use, it will be redacted again.  
(Reps) Steps: How to handle situations where contact avoidance is discovered 
If a frontline rep notices a pro is trying to avoid paying for leads, follow these steps:
Review the pro’s account for contact avoidance by checking their:
Quotes
Business name
Business description
Question and answers section
Profile photo
Photos
If they’re avoiding paying for leads, add notes to the case, including the link to the quote or profile.
Escalate the case to the Trust and Safety team following the steps on the Trust and Safety Incidents KA.
In some cases, T&S may remove a pro from Thumbtack for repeat violations. If a pro calls about their account, use the talking points to help navigate these conversations.
3. Talking points

Media won’t save

Why can’t I save my image!?
Including contact information on your profile or in photos is viewed as an attempt to evade paying lead fees, which is a violation of our Terms of Use and not allowed on our platform. Our system detects when contact information is included in an image and won’t allow it to be saved. If you remove the contact information from the image, you will be able to save it.
¿Por qué no puedo guardar mi imagen?
Incluir información de contacto en su perfil o en fotos se considera un intento de eludir el pago de tarifas por prospectos, lo cual es una violación de nuestros Términos de Uso y no está permitido en nuestra plataforma. Nuestro sistema detecta cuando se incluye información de contacto en una imagen y no permitirá que se guarde. Si elimina la información de contacto de la imagen, podrá guardarla.
But the information is part of my company logo!
Any information that directs a customer outside of Thumbtack goes against our Terms of Use. Though the information is included in your company logo, it will still need to be removed or edited before it can be saved on your profile.
¡Pero la información es parte del logo de mi empresa!
Cualquier información que dirija a un cliente fuera de Thumbtack va en contra de nuestros Términos de Uso. Aunque la información esté incluida en el logo de su empresa, aún deberá ser eliminada o editada antes de que pueda ser guardada en su perfil.
Language from our Terms of Use if the pro asks:
“Using the Platform in any manner that circumvents, or that may be intended to circumvent, your obligation to pay Thumbtack for access to services provided by the Platform or by Service Professionals” (Terms of Use Prohibitions, Bullet 5)
Lenguaje de nuestros Términos de Uso si el profesional pregunta:
“Utilizar la Plataforma de cualquier manera que eluda, o que pueda estar destinada a eludir, su obligación de pagar a Thumbtack por el acceso a los servicios proporcionados por la Plataforma o por Profesionales de Servicio” (Prohibiciones en los Términos de Uso, Punto 5)
Profile description was redacted 
Why does my (or why does the pros) profile description have asterisks in it? 
Some of the text in your profile violated our terms of use and has been redacted by our Trust and Safety Team. You can update your profile, however, if it’s replaced with text that violates our terms of use, it will be redacted again.
¿Por qué mi (o por qué el perfil del profesional) descripción tiene asteriscos?
Parte del texto en su perfil violó nuestros términos de uso y ha sido redactado por nuestro Equipo de Confianza y Seguridad. Puede actualizar su perfil; sin embargo, si se reemplaza con texto que también viole nuestros términos de uso, será redactado nuevamente.
Can I edit my profile and remove the asterisks? 
Yes, you can edit your profile and remove them. However, if it’s replaced with text that violates our terms of use, it will be redacted again.
¿Puedo editar mi perfil y eliminar los asteriscos?
Sí, puede editar su perfil y eliminarlos. Sin embargo, si el texto reemplazado viola nuestros términos de uso, será redactado nuevamente.
What can I put in my profile description then? 
This section of your profile is where you give customers plenty of reasons to hire you. A great introduction should explain your qualifications — what makes you unique — and shows your personality.
Here are some tips for writing an introduction that will help customers see why you’re the right pro: 
Say some kind of hello.
Point out the details that make you different from other services (like if you’ve worked in your field for a long time, or have any specialties).
If you love what you do, say so! Passion is a powerful thing.
Keep your intro short and sweet. If you have more to say, add more detail in the Questions and Answers section of your profile.
¿Qué puedo poner en la descripción de mi perfil?
Esta sección de su perfil es donde debe ofrecer a los clientes razones suficientes para contratarlo. Una buena introducción debe explicar sus cualificaciones — lo que lo hace único — y mostrar su personalidad.
Aquí hay algunos consejos para redactar una introducción que ayudará a los clientes a ver por qué es el profesional adecuado:
Comience con algún tipo de saludo.
Destaque los detalles que lo diferencian de otros servicios (como si ha trabajado en su campo durante mucho tiempo o si tiene alguna especialidad).
¡Si ama lo que hace, dígalo! La pasión es algo poderoso.
Mantenga su introducción breve y concisa. Si tiene más que decir, agregue más detalles en la sección de Preguntas y Respuestas de su perfil.
Pro was sent a warning for contact avoidance
Why did I get a warning about avoiding paying for leads?
We wanted to let you know that it's a violation of our Terms of Use to tell customers not to contact you on Thumbtack. When you do this, you're avoiding paying for the lead, and if you continue to do this, we will close your account.
¿Por qué recibí una advertencia sobre evitar pagar por prospectos?
Queríamos informarle que es una violación de nuestros Términos de uso decirle a los clientes que no se comuniquen con usted en Thumbtack. Cuando hace esto, está evitando pagar por el prospecto y si continúa haciéndolo, se eliminará su cuenta.
 Pro account was deactivated for contact avoidance
Why was my account deactivated for avoiding paying for leads? I didn't see a warning email?
We reached out to you by email on [DATE] and [DATE], to let you know you violated our Terms of Use by asking customers to contact you outside of Thumbtack. We asked you to stop this behavior, but you didn’t, so we removed your account.
¿Por qué se desactivó mi cuenta por evitar pagar por prospectos? ¿No vi un correo electrónico de advertencia?
Nos comunicamos con usted por correo electrónico el [FECHA] y el [FECHA] para informarle que violó nuestros Términos de Uso al pedirles a los clientes que se comuniquen con usted fuera de Thumbtack. Le pedimos que detuviera este comportamiento, pero no lo hizo, por lo que eliminamos su cuenta.
You deactivated my account for avoiding paying for leads. Is there any way I can still use Thumbtack?
We don’t make these decisions lightly. Because we gave you multiple warnings, we won’t reconsider our decision.
Desactivaste mi cuenta por evitar pagar por prospectos. ¿Hay alguna forma de que pueda seguir usando Thumbtack?
No tomamos estas decisiones a la ligera. Debido a que le dimos varias advertencias, no volveremos a considerar nuestra decisión.
4. Resources 
Pro or Customer  
Thumbtack Help 
Terms of Use
Direct links
Profile
Rep

Account Holds (Pro)
Trust and Safety Incidents
Removed or Banned Users
Profile (Pro)

1. Overview
Consultative conversations are a powerful and essential approach for Support Reps to connect with pros, fostering deeper understanding and enabling the delivery of tailored solutions. This internal knowledge article (KA) (Consultative Conversations: A Guide for Support Reps) emphasizes a shift from transactional support—where reps simply answer questions—to a more engaged, relational interaction. In every consultative conversation, Support Reps actively listen, ask probing questions, and offer expert advice and insights. This approach is crucial for building stronger, more trusting relationships with pros, demonstrating a genuine investment in their success, and ultimately, enhancing their experience on the platform.

When to apply this approach: This consultative framework is designed to be integrated into all interactions. Whether a pro is new and seeking guidance, facing challenges, expressing frustration, or simply has a question, adopting a consultative mindset will elevate the quality and effectiveness of the support provided.

2. Process: How To Have A Consultative Conversation 
This section provides a step-by-step guide on how Support Reps can effectively have consultative conversations with pros, fostering trust and understanding while helping them succeed on the platform. These steps are designed to be adaptable, providing guidance whether a conversation is just beginning, addressing specific pro challenges, or moving towards actionable solutions.
▶ Step 1. Beginning of Interaction: Establishing a Strong Start and Building Rapport
This section provides Support reps with specific techniques and talking points for effectively opening conversations with pros, ensuring they feel heard and valued from the outset
Step one of the consultative conversation process involves Support Reps creating a positive initial impression and establishing rapport. This is crucial in every interaction, setting a welcoming tone whether the pro is new, a long-time user, or reaching out with a specific concern. To do this, support reps will follow these steps: 
▶ 1.1: Set the Stage: Support reps should begin by introducing yourself and establishing a rapport with the pro. Use a friendly and professional tone to create a comfortable atmosphere.
Talking point examples:
Warm greeting: Hi [Pro's Name], my name is [Your Name], and I'm with Thumbtack Support. I'm here to help you with any questions or concerns you might have.
Purpose of call:  Hi [Pro's Name], thanks for calling Thumbtack Support. I see you're a [Pro's Profession] in [Pro's City]. How can I help you get more out of Thumbtack today?
Enthusiastic welcome: Welcome to Thumbtack Support, [Pro's Name]. I'm [Your Name], and I'm excited to help you grow your business on our platform.
▶ 1.2: Active Listening: Support Rep should pay close attention to the pro's concerns, and acknowledge their feelings. Use verbal affirmations like "I understand" or "I hear you" to show that you're engaged.
Talking point examples: 
Acknowledge frustration: It sounds like you're feeling frustrated about [Pro's Concern]. I understand how that can be disappointing.
Validate Emotion: I understand that you're feeling [Pro's Emotion] about [Pro's Concern]. I'm here to listen and help you find solutions.
Offer Support: It sounds like you're facing some challenges with [Pro's Challenge]. I want to assure you that I'm here to support you every step of the way.
▶ Additional talking point examples:
Below are additional talking points that Support Reps can use in their conversations. 
Acknowledge Loyalty: I see you’ve been with us for [number] years. Thank you for your loyalty. We definitely appreciate you.
Recognize Achievement: I could see here that [pro accomplishment],  that’s impressive! Keep it up!
Compliment Effort: Great work on the <fill in the blank>. I can tell you’ve worked really hard on this.
Inquire About Business History: How long have you been in the [Pro service] business?
Understand Motivation: What got you started in the [Pro service] business?
▶ Step 2. Probing for Needs: Identifying Pro Challenges and Objectives:
This critical step allows Support Reps to move beyond surface-level inquiries and truly understand the pro's situation. 
Asking open-ended questions demonstrates a Support Rep's genuine interest in the pro's perspective, while probing questions help reps identify underlying issues, unspoken concerns, and true objectives. This step is particularly vital when a pro expresses frustration, confusion, or a vague problem, as it helps uncover the root cause and ensures you're addressing their actual needs.
Support Reps will follow these steps to do so:
▶ 2.1: Ask Open-Ended Questions: Support Reps should ask open-ended questions to encourage the pro to share more details about their situation. This will help you gain a deeper understanding of their needs and challenges. Instead of just yes or no questions, Support reps should try "Can you tell me more about that?" or "What's been your experience with this?" These get the conversation going and encourage discussion.
Talking point examples for asking open ended questions: 
Targeting Focus: Can you tell me more about [the types of jobs you're targeting?]
Challenges Encountered: What are some of the challenges you're facing in getting hired?
Specific Pain Points: What are your biggest pain points when it comes to finding new customers on Thumbtack?
Business Goals: How do you envision Thumbtack helping you achieve your long-term business goals?
▶ Additional examples that demonstrate asking open-end questions:
Below are additional talking points that support reps can use in their conversations when it comes to asking open ended questions. 
Example 1: Instead of, "Did you update your profile?" ask, "What changes have you made to your profile recently?" 
Example 2: Instead of, "Are you having trouble with leads?" ask, "What challenges are you experiencing with managing your leads?" 
Example 3: Instead of "Do you understand this?", try "What are your thoughts on the steps we have discussed today?"
▶ 2.2: Ask Probing Questions: Support Reps should ask follow-up questions to clarify specific points and uncover any underlying issues. These follow-up questions provide greater context and more time to form your answer, review their account, and gather relevant resources.
Talking point examples for asking probing questions: 
Search Visibility: You mentioned that [you're not showing up in search results]. Can you tell me more about [the types of jobs you’re not seeing yourself in search results for?]"
Review Status: Challenges encountered: I noticed that you haven't received any reviews yet. Have you considered reaching out to past customers to request reviews?
Detailed Elaboration: Specific pain points: You mentioned [Pro's Previous Statement]. Can you elaborate on that further?
Previous Actions Taken: What have you already tried to address this issue?
Confirm Understanding: I want to make sure that I really have an understanding of what you’re telling me. I’m hearing that [Pro's Previous Statement]. Is that correct?
▶ Additional probing question examples
Below are additional talking points that support reps can use in their conversations when it comes to asking probing questions. 
Seek clarity: Can you tell me a little more about it, please?
Inquire further: I really want to help here. Do you mind if I ask you a few more questions?
Reflect understanding: I want to make sure that I really have an understanding of what you’re telling me. I’m hearing that [xyz]
Ensuring completeness: If I skip anything important, please stop me and let me know.
Confirming Interpretation: If I’m understanding you correctly [xyz]
Offering help: Is there anything I can do for you today?
Requesting Elaboration: Please tell me more about your situation.
Exploring Alternatives:  Tell me what you see as your choices here.
Providing Anticipation: When we have the latest update about [xyz]
▶ Step 3. Exploring Solutions and Sharing Insights
Once pro needs are clearly identified, this section guides Support Reps through the collaborative exploration of solutions. It focuses on sharing relevant insights and data to help pros understand their situation better and work together to brainstorm potential solutions. This step is most effective after you've thoroughly probed for needs, allowing you to offer tailored insights and co-create solutions that directly address their challenges.
▶ 3.1: Offer Insights: Support Reps should share relevant insights and data to help the pro understand their situation better. This could include market trends, competitor analysis, or performance metrics from their Thumbtack profile.
Talking point examples: 
Response Rate Analysis: I'm seeing that [your response rate is a little lower than the average for your category]. [Responding promptly to customer inquiries can significantly increase your chances of getting hired].
Profile Completion: Pros with [complete profiles and high-quality photos] tend to attract more customers. Have you considered [adding more photos] to your profile?"
Success Strategies: Based on our data, pros with similar profiles to yours have seen success by [Sharing Relevant Data].
Regional Tactics: One effective strategy that other pros in your area are using is [Sharing Effective Strategy].
▶ 3.2: Brainstorm Solutions: Support reps should work with the pro to brainstorm potential solutions to their challenges. Encourage them to think creatively and consider different approaches
Talking point examples: 
Profile Improvement Ideas: Let's brainstorm some ways to improve your profile and make it stand out from the competition.
Discount Options: Have you thought about offering a discount for first-time customers to attract more leads?
Open to Suggestions: Let's explore some potential solutions together. What are your initial thoughts?
Collaborative Thinking: I have a few ideas that might be helpful, but I'm also interested in hearing your perspective.
▶ Step 4. Guiding Pros With Actionable Steps and Resources
This section outlines how Support Reps can develop actionable plans and provide helpful resources to pros, ensuring pros receive clear guidance and the necessary tools to implement recommendations and achieve their business goals. This step is the natural progression after collaboratively exploring solutions, translating discussions into concrete, easy-to-follow steps and providing the support materials needed for success.
▶ 4.1: Specific Recommendations: Support Reps should offer specific and actionable recommendations that the pro can implement. Provide clear guidance and support to help them take the next steps.
Talking point examples:

Pro Community: You could also consider joining the Thumbtack Pro Community to connect with other pros and learn from their experiences.

▶ 4.2: Helpful Resources: Support Reps should share relevant resources and tools that can help the pro implement the recommendations. This could include help center articles, video tutorials, or links to other helpful resources.
Talking point examples:

▶ Step 5. Ending Interactions with Clarity and Support
This final step guides Support Reps in effectively ending conversations with pros, focusing on summarizing key takeaways, confirming next steps, and offering ongoing support to ensure pros feel confident and empowered moving forward. A strong conclusion is essential for every interaction, reinforcing the value provided and leaving the pro with a clear understanding of what's next and that continued support is available.

▶ 5.1: Summarize and Confirm: Support Reps should summarize the key takeaways from the conversation and confirm the next steps with the pro. Ensure that they feel confident and empowered to move forward.

Talking point examples:

3. Process: How To Overcome Objectives and Address Concerns
In some cases, pros may express objections or pushback during the interaction. Their objections can stem from various reasons, such as feeling frustrated, skeptical, or a lack of understanding.
It's essential for support reps to address these objections constructively and move the conversation forward in a positive direction. Here are some strategies for overcoming objections:
▶ Step 1. Acknowledge Concern and Validate How They're Feeling
When a pro raises an objection, it's crucial for Support Reps to: 
Acknowledge their concern and validate their feelings. This shows the pro that Support Reps listen and that you understand their perspective. 
Reps should avoid interrupting or dismissing their concerns, even if you disagree.
Talking point examples for Support Reps: 
Example 1: I understand the concern you have with [e.g., the recent policy change]. It's important for me to hear your concerns and address them as best as I can.
Example 2: I appreciate you bringing this to my attention. It's helpful for me to understand your perspective so I can offer the most relevant support.
▶ Step 2. Ask Clarifying Questions to Understand Objections Fully
To address an objection effectively, it's essential for Support Reps to understand the root cause of the pro's concern. 
Ask clarifying questions to gather more information and gain a deeper understanding of the pros perspective.
Talking point examples for Support Reps: 
Example 1: Can you tell me more about what's causing your concern about [e.g., this feature]?
Example 2: I'm curious to hear more about your experience with [e.g., this issue.] Can you share some specific examples?
▶ Step 3. Provide Accurate Information and Correct Misconceptions
Sometimes, objections arise from a lack of understanding or misinformation. Support Reps should provide accurate and relevant information to address the pro's concerns and clear up any misconceptions.
Talking point examples for Support Reps to offer clarity and address concerns: 
Example 1: I'm happy to clarify how this feature works. It's designed to help you attract more customers by showcasing your expertise and experience.
Example  2: I understand your concern about [e.g., the recent policy change]. I'm happy to share [e.g., the rationale behind it] and [e.g., explain how it benefits both pros and customers.]
▶ Step 4. Offer Alternative Solutions and Workarounds
If the pro's objection is valid and cannot be directly addressed, Support Reps should offer alternative solutions or workarounds. This shows the pro that Support Reps are committed to finding a resolution that meets their needs.
Talking point examples for Support Reps: 
Example 1: I understand that this solution may not be ideal for your specific situation. Here's an alternative approach that you might find helpful.
Example 2: I'm happy to explore other options with you to find a solution that better meets your needs. Let's brainstorm some possibilities together.
▶ Step 5. Emphasize Benefits and Value Proposition of Thumbtack
When addressing objections, it's important for Support Reps to emphasize the benefits and value of Thumbtack's products, services, and policies. Reps should remind the pro how Thumbtack can help them achieve their business goals and build a thriving business.
Talking point examples for Support Reps:
Example 1: I understand your concern about the cost of this service. However, it's important to remember that Thumbtack provides a valuable platform for connecting with customers and growing your business. The investment you make in Thumbtack can lead to significant returns in the long run."
Example 2: I appreciate your feedback on this feature. We're always working to improve our products and services to better meet the needs of our pros. Your input is valuable to us.
Reps can follow the steps in the internal Product Feedback KA to submit a pros feedback. 
▶ Step 6. Maintain a Positive and Professional Demeanor
Throughout the conversation, it's crucial that Support Reps maintain a positive and professional tone, even if the pro is expressing frustration or negativity. Reps should avoid getting defensive or argumentative. Instead, focus on building rapport and finding common ground.
Talking point examples for Support Reps:
Example 1: I understand the challenges you're facing. I'm here to help you find a solution that works for you.
Example 2: I appreciate you sharing your concerns with me. I'm confident that we can work together to find a positive resolution.
4. Key Soft Skills: Enhancing Consultative Conversations
When Support Reps talk to a pro, it's about connecting with them as a person, not just ticking boxes off a list. Here's how Support Reps can make interactions feel real and friendly:
Personalize the Conversation: 
Support Rep should use the pros name and mention something they've already brought up. Instead of a script, Support Reps can try saying, "I see you've been with Thumbtack for a while—how's your experience been so far?" or "That sounds challenging. Let me see what I can do to help.”
▶ Additional examples that demonstrate ways of making conversations personalized
Instead of, "What's the issue?" try, "Hi [Pro's Name], I see you've been with Thumbtack for [time period]. What can I help you with today?"
If they mention a specific job type, say, "I mentioned you were interested in [job type]. How has that been going?"
Reference something from their profile, "I noticed you have some great photos of your [service]. They really showcase your skills."
Speak Naturally: 
Support Reps should keep it professional, but not too formal or stiff. Say, "I'm happy to help you," instead of "I will provide assistance." Just talk like you would in a normal conversation.
▶ Additional examples that demonstrate speaking naturally
Instead of, "Please provide your account details," say, "Could you share your account details with me, please?"
Instead of, "The system indicates an error," say, "It looks like there might be a slight hiccup in the system. Let me see what I can do to fix that for you."
Instead of "I'm just confirming your information", try "Let's double check a few details to make sure we have everything right"
Show You Care (empathy and validation): 
The Support Rep should let the pro know you understand their feelings. "I understand how that could be difficult" or "I get how that might feel like a setback" can make a big difference. It shows you're a human, not a robot.
▶ Additional examples that shows a pro that a Support Rep understand:
If they say, "This is so confusing!" respond with, "I totally get it. Navigating new systems can be tricky. Let's break it down step by step."
When they say, "I've tried everything," try, "I can hear the concern in your voice. It sounds like you've really put in a lot of effort. We'll find a solution."
For a pro who's worried about reviews, say "It's understandable that reviews are important to you and your business, as they really show your value to future customers"
Be Warm and Friendly: 
Tone matters! Support Reps should be upbeat. Support Reps should not sound like you're reading a script. Smiling while talking can help your voice sound more friendly too. Even standing up while on a call can help Support Reps with tone.
▶ Examples to demonstrate being warm and friendly:
Start with, "Good morning/afternoon, [Pro's Name]! How's your day going so far?"
When wrapping up, say, "It was great talking with you today, [Pro's Name]. Have a wonderful rest of your day!"
If there's a brief pause, add in, "Is there anything else I can help you with today?" in an upbeat tone.
Share a Little (but not too much): 
A quick "I've been there too" or "I had something similar happen. Let me help you navigate this" can make a Support Rep more relatable. Just a small touch to show you connect.
▶ Additional examples that demonstrate how to share brief to make things more relatable:
If they mention website issues, "Oh, I recently had some trouble with my own website too. It's so frustrating! I know how you feel."
When they talk about a complex job, "I've heard from other pros that [job type] can be challenging. It’s great that you’re taking it on."
"That sounds like a busy week. I had a similar experience with balancing tasks, let me show you a feature that may help you."
It's Okay to Pause: 
Support Reps should not rush to fill every silence. Sometimes people need a second to think and gather their thoughts. If the Support Reps does speak, just ask another question or just show you're still listening.
▶ Additional ways Support Reps can allow pauses in the conversation naturally:
If they sound hesitant, say, "Take your time. I want to make sure I understand everything fully."
After providing information, pause and then ask, "Does that make sense so far? Would you like me to explain anything in more detail?"
After they explain a problem, wait a few seconds before responding to show you're processing and considering their words.
Key Takeaway: Support Reps should treat each pro like you’re having a conversation with someone you know. Support reps should be friendly, listen actively, and make the interaction personal.
