Talking points
Credit card security and Stripe
Customers expired card automatically deleted
Resources

This article is for customers. To learn more about pro payments, see Payment Methods (Pro).
1. Overview
Thumbtack offers customers convenient and secure ways to handle payments for services, primarily for On-Demand Bookings. All credit and debit card payments are processed securely through Stripe, ensuring customer information remains confidential. Thumbtack does not accept prepaid cards.
When customers choose On-Demand Bookings, Thumbtack facilitates matching them with a high-quality pro for a pre-scheduled, fixed-price job. Customers will see the price upfront and provide their payment information at the time of booking.
The customer's card is authorized when the booking is made but is not charged until after the job is completed. If a customer needs to reschedule an On-Demand booking, they will be asked to re-input their credit card information to complete the updated booking.
NOTE: If a customer's card is not working, it's possible that it's a prepaid card. Stripe usually rejects prepaid cards. To resolve the issue, it's important to check if the card is prepaid.
Stripe: Thumbtack’s Secure Payment Processor
This section explains how Thumbtack utilizes Stripe to ensure the security and confidentiality of all credit card payments made on the platform.
All credit card payments are processed through Stripe, a secure site that keeps credit card information confidential. Thumbtack does not have access to a customers credit card information. 
Customers' credit card or bank statement may show charges from Stripe. The charges will update (usually within 48 hours) to show they’re from Thumbtack. 
Customers can learn more about how Stripe protects information by referring to Stripes Security at Stripe article. 
Reps can refer to Credit card security and Stripe talking points below to navigate these conversations.
How a customers payment method is first saved
This section outlines the process by which a customer's payment method is initially stored and managed within their Thumbtack account
When customers navigate to their profile menu, they will see the Payments section, where they can add or view saved cards.
▶ Screenshot of Payments section[Image: AD_4nXerb9WmpvS_v-6RXPCFc8PJjCgiq6P-sGSigEJ2qD_CnqIYJEoHOhiAsjfRqLl7vk4oNxJTwmPTQGZGN3qKW4aN6dZIOm6eDoHszOGciuFHZscurT0JNEUS4aWtznctb4DiMWhOL7VxdRZdnH5Erp2yInv1]
Customers who have never made a payment will see that there are no cards on file when they navigate to the payments section. They will see the option to add a card.
When making a payment for the first time, the card used will automatically be stored as their default payment and see the disclaimer regarding stored payments.
▶ Screenshot[Image: AD_4nXe7yzLC9neN8nEiU__3NE0xN72uCoOQoHfFMEBjXR0w-mD_hLdSgJPzIJzFK_Y-tJh0jUaYEfryztCx_8QyX4fcmKmwyA6_RFZCK2PcwHkCV7yfDQ-8ufI7bGynkcs0z3IIZXZc4ebMeYajCfkAUWGSQ-Cq]
When the customer makes additional payments, they will see the option to use one of their stored payments methods.
▶ Screenshot[Image: AD_4nXd02PXl_O_Su5KgX0sFVMairXS8Nh-88sfY-G8pYocLH08d2SZRxs5v8yVt9oERac6KhNFOvtEH0jTxwUunIGwJQLeLDjSqolf0Fo-OYwQ56Z43F1xo5tfn8X6rvYn9u9ljCv7e7bBJB1VR31GDUpCStT2S]
At any time,  can view, add, or delete their stored payment methods. 
Sales tax applied to customer payments on Thumbtack

This section clarifies how sales tax is automatically calculated and applied to customer payments for services on Thumbtack in applicable regions.
Thumbtack automatically collects sales tax from customers who reside in states and cities that charge it. This sales tax is applied to the customer's payment for On-Demand bookings. Customers will see the collected sales tax where applicable.
For example, Sales tax is automatically applied to in-app payments (On-Demand bookings) from customers for eligible services requested in the state of Washington and in Denver, Colorado.
At this time, customers won’t receive a detailed invoice for any payment exchanges. However, they do receive a receipt of payment via email to see how much they’re charged in sales tax. Sales tax is applied to the subtotal amount.
▶ Sales tax view on an On-Demand booking:

[Image: AD_4nXcYN7Vl9z3bMcG1VT9MniWkhKIC0PSq3jRoKEfz6fgyi2EjBy7ot2rOVqXZ_lm2-WIC9td7xzqNtwh3w3McXtweFEkDz9KA1B-iMFpEx7Y_SkMPxjfLs7KEkdIvm5ofPeAhEm38]

NOTE: If contacted by a customer who has questions about sales tax, Thumbtack does not extend additional tax information or explanations. Simply let them know that Thumbtack determines sales tax based on applicable local county/state requirements.
Customers expired card removed after failed payment 
This section describes the system's behavior when an expired payment card leads to a failed payment attempt, resulting in its automatic removal.

When a customer payment attempt fails due to the card being expired, the system will automatically delete that saved payment method. When a customer attempts to make a payment, they won't see the expired card in the dropdown list of saved payment method. 

Use the talking points below to help navigate these interactions. 
2. Process
Steps: How to manage a stored payment method (Customer) 
This sub-section provides detailed instructions for customers on how to manage their saved payment methods, including adding, viewing, and deleting cards.
Customers can have more than one payment method on file. When a customer makes a payment using a card not currently stored, it will automatically be added as the new default payment method. All stored payments will remain unless they are deleted by the customers or Thumbtack. 
Currently, it is not possible to edit an existing payment method. To make an update, customers should delete the existing card and a new card with the updated payment information.
At any time, customers can delete any of their stored payment methods so that it is not available for future use by visiting their payment settings. 
Device
Customer steps to manage their stored payment method on Thumbtack
App
Open the Thumbtack app.
Select Profile (from the main menu at the bottom).
Tap the gear icon in the top corner.
Select Payments.
Tap Add a credit card.
Enter your payment information and tap Save.
Desktop
Click the menu (or your photo) at the top right.
From the drop-down menu, choose Payments.  
Click Add a credit card. 
From here, enter your credit card details and click Add credit card. 
NOTE: Thumbtack frontline reps should never take a customers credit card information for them. Instead, walk them through how to add it themselves. See the internal Sensitive Account Information Handling Guidelines (Pro) (Customer) (Rep) KA for more information. 
▶ Screenshot: Image shows the Payment method section of the customers payments page. Customers can click on a card to delete or make it default.

[Image: AD_4nXf2kkMg0DOCDNHkqPNgukjGLkSGm5g2u16olSKBjydP-FphduxsCgoESvPLaBF4gTTwr5807Y6j3NeAgHwOC4uC3KONQTTSxW1tnUp4YgnoYBBO1mEEKnfAaSonxcqfFWGiAC1s2vmQNfaHuzd17Y2LpbHd]

▶ Screenshot: Image shows the Payment Method page once a customer has clicked on a specific card on the previous page. They will see the “Delete card” button only if the card they are on, is their detailed payment method.

[Image: OA0nyMWznKY1vqHpIqMXWVKf9h1sOydNtuYHAsKelvSFUluo1fea4JpTB6DJGVN7EhX2ji_UpbofRdekSjwt-aLES1ghQBNFT7xzjhpvx_2bwCGs75L6BNhD_qtu1XKDI2hLncgMwGzOmxhR0I2qFWI]

3. TALKING POINTS
This section provides pre-approved talking points for support reps to address common customer inquiries and concerns regarding payment methods.
Credit card security and Stripe

This sub-section offers prepared responses for reps to explain Thumbtack's credit card security measures and the role of Stripe in processing payments to customers on Thumbtack.

Is it safe to make purchases on Thumbtack? How do you protect my information?
We use Stripe to process credit card payments made on our site. We never receive your credit card information because it's kept in Stripe's secure credit card vault. That's just one part of Stripe's state-of-the-art security tools to maintain a high level of security (see Stripe’s website for more on this).
¿Es seguro realizar compras en Thumbtack? ¿Cómo protegen mi información?
Usamos Stripe para procesar los pagos con tarjeta de crédito realizados en nuestro sitio. Nunca recibimos la información de su tarjeta de crédito porque está guardada en la bóveda segura de tarjetas de crédito de Stripe. Esa es solo una parte de las herramientas de seguridad de última generación de Stripe para mantener un alto nivel de seguridad (consulte el sitio web de Stripe para obtener más información al respecto).
Why can't you update my credit card for me?
This is solely for your security. We want you to feel comfortable knowing that your credit card information isn’t shared with anyone.
¿Por qué no pueden actualizar mi tarjeta de crédito?
Esto es únicamente por su seguridad. Queremos que se sienta cómodo sabiendo que la información de su tarjeta de crédito no se comparte con nadie.
How secure is my credit card info?
We use Stripe to process all the credit card payments made on our site. Instead of Thumbtack storing your credit card information, Stripe stores it in their secure credit card vault and never passes the credit card information to us.
¿Qué tan segura es la información de mi tarjeta de crédito?
Usamos Stripe para procesar todos los pagos con tarjeta de crédito realizados en nuestro sitio. En lugar de que Thumbtack almacene la información de su tarjeta de crédito, Stripe la almacena en su bóveda segura de tarjetas de crédito y nunca nos pasa la información de la tarjeta de crédito.

Customers expired card automatically deleted
This sub-section provides talking points for reps to address customer questions about the automatic deletion of expired payment cards.

Will my card be automatically deleted once it hits the expiration date? 
No, our system currently only triggers the deletion of expired cards once there has been an unsuccessful payment attempt.
¿Se eliminará automáticamente mi tarjeta una vez que cumpla la fecha de vencimiento?
No, nuestro sistema actualmente solo activa la eliminación de tarjetas vencidas una vez que haya habido un intento de pago fallido.
Will I be notified if you delete an expired card? 
You won't be notified when an expired card is deleted, but you will receive an immediate notification if a payment is unsuccessful. In that case, you will be prompted to update your payment method. If you have a stored payment on Thumbtack, only non-expired cards will show in the dropdown of saved payments during the payment process. 
¿Recibiré una notificación si me eliminan una tarjeta vencida?
No recibirá una notificación cuando se elimine una tarjeta vencida, pero recibirá una notificación inmediata si un pago no se realiza correctamente. En ese caso, se le solicitará que actualice su método de pago. Si tiene un pago almacenado en Thumbtack, solo las tarjetas que no hayan vencido se mostrarán en el menú desplegable de pagos guardados durante el proceso de pago

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) (Bugs and Bug Reports) provides Frontline Reps with essential information for identifying, reporting, and managing bugs within the Thumbtack platform, ensuring accurate resolution for pros and customers.
A bug is an issue where the Thumbtack website, Thumbtack app, or Admin is not functioning as intended. Frontline Reps use Salesforce to submit bug reports received from pros and customers to the Bugs Team. 
When interacting with customers or pros, reps should not call an issue a "bug." Instead, use phrases like: "this doesn't look right."
Why Frontline Reps Report Bugs
Frontline Reps report bugs to:
Fix: Provide engineers with information necessary to figure out and fix the problem
Track: Monitor the volume of reports to determine how many pros or customers an issue is affecting.
Understand: Gather detailed information from each report to better diagnose the issue.
Bug vs. Product Feedback
It is crucial to distinguish between a bug and product feedback. If a pro or customer expresses dissatisfaction with a feature's design or desired functionality, it should be treated as Product Feedback, not a bug report. Frontline reps can refer to the internal Product Feedback KA to learn more. 
Internal Systems Note (Internal Only)
Problems with any of Thumbtack's other systems [Salesforce, Genesys (chat, phones, SMS) internet, etc.] are not handled by the Bugs Team. For these issues, reps should submit a Helpdesk ticket through the TackIT Help Desk Portal. For feedback on internal systems (e.g., Admin, BigQuery, Genesys, Salesforce, and Slack), reps will use the theme taxonomy on cases.
From Report to Fix: A Bug Report's Progress 
Here, Frontline Reps will find information about the typical lifecycle of a bug, from its initial report to its final resolution.
Pro or customer contacts support to report an issue.
Frontline rep submit a bug report in Salesforce.
The Bugs Team reviews all new issues, educates the agent if it’s not a bug, and passes it on to engineering if it is.
Engineering prioritizes bugs and fixes them.
Engineering informs the Bugs Team when a fix is complete.
The Bugs Team verifies the fix, posts the fixed bug in the #bugs channel, and updates the reps case with the fix information. The rep is then responsible for emailing the pro or customer.
The team will only notify reps once the issue is fixed and the bug report submitted is within 30 days.
Understanding Bug Fix Expectations 
This section provides Frontline Reps with essential information regarding the expected timelines and factors influencing the resolution of reported bugs
There are no timelines for fixes.
As soon as a new issue is reported, the Bugs Team begins tracking and investigating. 
The Bugs Team sends all bugs to our engineers, and they prioritize from there. 
Reps should not tell the pro or customer they will get an update within any specific timeline.
Do not ask the Bugs Team for a timetable for a fix, as they are unable to provide one.
A bug fixed update will be posted in the #bugs channel.

Key Points
This section highlights key points and best practices for Frontline Reps when identifying, reporting, and understanding the lifecycle of bugs. Reviewing these key points will help ensure accurate and efficient bug resolution.
Thoroughly investigate the reported issue
Reps are expected to thoroughly investigate the issue being reported by the pro or customer. Make sure to exhaust all available resources to determine if the issue is a bug.
Available resources:
Knowledge Articles
Thumbtack Help Center
Lessonly
Operations Consultants or managers
Submit a complete and accurate bug report
Ensure all fields are filled out completely and accurately to ensure a smooth bug report process for all parties involved.
Reps will either select a known bug and provide details about the user's experience OR submit a new bug report. 
Respond to follow-up questions from the Bugs team within 48 hours
The Bugs team may send a follow-up message to the reporting rep for the following reasons: providing workarounds, and other troubleshooting steps, and requiring additional information from the pro. 
Reporting reps are expected to respond within 48 hours.
When responding to the Bugs team, tag the agent and post the comment on the case. 
Submit the bug report to the correct pro or customer account
Ensure the bug report submitted is associated with the correct account.  
Some pros have multiple accounts. To check for multiple accounts, search for the phone number from Salesforce in Admin. 
One bug report per issue per pro or customer 
If pros are experiencing multiple issues, make sure to submit one bug report per issue. 
2. Process
This section guides Frontline Reps through the steps to take when a pro or customer contacts Thumbtack with a problem determined to be a bug.
If a pro or customer contacts Thumbtack with a problem, and we determine that it’s a bug, and Thumbtack determines it’s a bug, reps report it to our engineers so it can be fixed.

Steps: How to troubleshooting before submitting a bug report (Rep)
Before submitting a bug report, you’ll troubleshoot the issue to make sure it’s really a bug. If it isn’t a bug, troubleshooting often fixes the pro’s or customer’s issue.
Understand the issue: Ask detailed questions and try to replicate the issue on your end until you understand exactly what’s happening.
Don’t assume. Sometimes bugs turn out to be updates we didn’t know about.
Avoid technical jargon. Use plain, non-technical terms whenever possible. 
Instead of saying "this is a bug," say "this doesn't look right."
Keep the tone positive. 
Use phrases like: "That doesn't look right. I'll let our engineers know so they can fix it. Here's another way to do what you were trying to do. [WORKAROUND]"
Or: "That doesn't look right. [X] is how it should work. I'll let our engineers know so they can fix it."
Guide the user through troubleshooting steps: Walk the pro or customer through the general troubleshooting steps for their specific device or issues (e.g. not receiving emails).
Find troubleshooting resources: 
Start with the Troubleshooting [Link Directory] (Rep) KA, which links to relevant KAs with specific troubleshooting steps. 
Pros and customers can also reference the How to fix technical issues – Thumbtack Help article.
NOTE: If the pro or customer is unable or unwilling to troubleshoot, reps should still submit a bug report. Be sure to note that troubleshooting was not completed.  Even if engineers may not be able to fix the issue without troubleshooting, we still want a record of what happened.
Check for existing bugs: If the problem isn’t solved by troubleshooting, and you believe it’s a bug (not just a user error), search to see if the issue is already on file as an existing bug by following the Steps: How to submit a bug report (Rep).

4. Urgent bugs 
Frontline Reps can use this section to understand what qualifies as an urgent bug and how to report or escalate it correctly.
An urgent bug is defined as a critical system issue that severely impacts Thumbtack's primary functions, simultaneously affecting a significant number of professionals (pros) or customers. These high-impact issues commonly involve core areas such as:
Accepting leads
Submitting requests
Payments processing
User signup
Other essential functions

Guidelines for escalating urgent bugs 
Frontline reps should always submit a bug report first (by following the Steps: How to submit a bug report (Rep)). The Bugs Team is trained to identify and escalate urgent issues from these reports to the engineering team. However, if a rep encounters an urgent bug and believes it requires immediate attention, the rep can take additional steps to flag it.
When to Flag an Urgent Bug
Frontline reps should use their best judgment, and always troubleshoot first. An issue is considered urgent if it is a:
Widespread bug with significant impact to Thumbtack's core functions (e.g., messaging, submitting requests, payments, signup, or login).
A bug that you suddenly see affecting many pros all at once, and is related to a major function (like messaging, payments, etc.).
Note: If the issue is only affecting one pro or customer, or you cannot replicate it, it is likely not an urgent bug. Submit a standard bug report (follow Steps: How to submit a bug report (Rep)), and the Bugs Team will escalate it if necessary.
Steps: How to flag an urgent bug (Rep)
Frontline reps must first review the guidelines for escalating urgent bugs to determine if an issue meets the criteria before flagging it.
To ensure an urgent bug is seen quickly after reviewing those guidelines, reps will follow these steps:
Post in the #bugs Slack channel using @here and include:
A brief description of the issue.
A link to the affected pro or customer’s Admin page.
A screenshot (if possible).
If you do not receive a response within 5 minutes, escalate the issue to a manager.
Managers will then follow internal processes to further escalate the urgent bug.
NOTE: Flagging an urgent bug is the only time you should use @here in #bugs.

Steps: How to escalate an urgent bug (Managers only)
For urgent bugs requiring immediate attention beyond Frontline Rep flagging, managers are responsible for initiating these escalation steps to ensure the issue is addressed promptly. To do so, managers will follow these steps: 
Use Klaxon to page product operations (this will ring the team's personal cell phones).
Write a brief sentence summarizing the issue in the "Message" field, then select the team and click Submit.
If you get no response in five minutes, continue to the next step
Email eng@thumbtack.com and Slack #eng using @channel and include:
A brief description of the issue
Include admin links, anything else needed to immediately start investigating the issue.
Include screenshots if possible.
Sense of bug volume / impact if possible, etc.
If you get no response in five minutes, continue to the next step. 
Use Klaxon to page the relevant product team (this will ring the team's personal cell phones).
Look in the “on-call” or “Opsgenie” lines of the wiki above for the team’s Klaxon name. 
If unsure which team to page, just pick the one that looks closest. 
If the most relevant team has no on-call info listed, page the next-closest instead.
Write a brief sentence summarizing the issue in the "Message" field, then select the team and click Submit.
If you get no response in five minutes, continue to the next step. 
Slack #emergency using @channel.
Include the same information from step 5.
If you get no response in five minutes, continue to the next step.   
Repeat steps 3 - 4.
Steps: How to escalate website or Admin outages (Managers only)
This process is for Managers only and must be followed immediately when a significant portion of the website and/or Admin is down and the issue has not self-resolved within approximately one minute.
If the matter is non-urgent, submit a bug report instead (by following the Steps: How to submit a bug report (Rep)).
Manager Escalation Steps (Follow in Order):
Slack #bugs using @here. 
Wait 2 minutes. If no response after 2 minutes, proceed to Step 3.
Use Klaxon to ping sre and product operations (this will ring the team’s personal cell phones). 
Write a brief summary in the "Message" field.

Wait 2 minutes. If no response after 2 minutes, proceed to Step 7.

5. Internal FAQs
Frontline Reps can use these internal FAQs to better understand how bug reports are handled internally, including guidance for known issues and where to find updates.
Should I submit a report for a bug that is already known?
Yes. Reps will follow the Steps: How to submit a bug report (Rep).
Volume is one of the main factors that engineers use to determine priority of a bug. Also, each new report gives us more information on the issue. One pro might include a detail that another omitted. One might send a screenshot while another won’t.

Why was my bug report assigned to “tack bot” and closed immediately?
The Bugs Team trusts your judgment when you attach a report to a known bug. Since they’re not looking at every report (though they may do so in a random audit), there’s no reason for the report to stay open. Reports for known bugs are very important because they tell the Bugs Team which bugs are the most urgent.
Reps can refer to the Steps: What to do after submitting a bug report (Rep)
 
How can I find information or updates about a specific bug report?
Reps can follow the Steps: How to check the status of a bug report (Rep). 
If you still see your bug in Bug Search (without checking the “Fixed Bugs” box), it’s not fixed yet. When the bug you filed a report for is fixed, you’ll be notified by email.
Don’t ask the bugs agents about the timing of a fix. There isn’t a timetable on when bugs will be fixed. 
For any other questions, first ask the bugs agent handling the report. You can find who this is by looking at the details on the bug report (hover over the bug report’s name, at the bottom of the Bug Search tool). If you don’t get a response in 24 hours, ask #bugs in Slack.
If the bug report is assigned to “tack bot”, that means it was filed under a known bug, so there’s no assigned bugs agent. Go straight to the #bugs slack channel with questions.

Budget Increase Incentive (BOSUP & SOBU) (Pro)

Contents
Overview
Quick Comparison between BOSUP and SOBU
Budget Overserving Upsell (BOSUP)

Updates

View free lead balance

Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal Knowledge article (KA) (Budget Increase Incentive (BOSUP & SOBU) (Pro)) provides frontline reps with information on Budget Overserving Upsell (BOSUP) and Seasonal Overserving Budget Upsell (SOBU) offers. These offers incentivize pros to increase their weekly budgets in exchange for free leads, helping to manage marketplace health during periods of low supply or high demand. The article details the triggers, maintenance periods, and disqualification factors for both types of offers. [end of summary]
IMPORTANT - Guidelines for Frontline reps: This internal knowledge article contains sensitive information intended for internal Thumbtack use only. Frontline reps must adhere to the+  do’s and don’t +  guidelines during discussions with pros.
▶ [Internal Thumbtack information only:
Overserving is an internal term for when Thumbtack shows a pro in search results even after they have exhausted their weekly budget. This occurs in low-supply markets to ensure customers have enough options. While this benefits customers, it means the pro is missing out on potential leads.
To address this, pros are encouraged to increase their weekly budget to meet demand. In exchange, they receive free leads as a bonus. This is known internally as an overserving budget upsell offer. 
Thumbtack utilizes two primary types of budget upsell offers: BOSUP and SOBU. While both incentivize pros to increase their budget for free leads, they are triggered by different market conditions. These offers help manage marketplace health by ensuring customers have enough pros to choose from, especially in markets with low supply or during periods of high demand. ]
To learn more about a pro's weekly targeting budget, frontline reps can refer to the internal Weekly Targeting Budget KA.
Quick Comparison of BOSUP and SOBU
Thumbtack offers two main budget upsell incentives, BOSUP and SOBU. While both serve a similar purpose, they are activated under different market conditions. This comparison table highlights their key differences.

Feature
Budget Overserving Upsell (BOSUP)
Seasonal Overserving Budget Upsell (SOBU)
Trigger
Pro has exhausted their budget but is still visible in search results due to low market supply (category + zip code)
An anticipated or upcoming peak season with high customer demand.
Goal
To immediately help a pro capture existing, real-time demand.
To encourage a pro to prepare in advance for a busy season.
Budget Maintenance
Pro must maintain the new budget for 2 weeks.
Pro must maintain the new budget for 6 weeks.
Lead issuance and expiration
Free leads expire after 90 days from when they are awarded (after the 2-week period)
Free leads expire after 90 days from when they are awarded (after the 6-week period)
Budget Overserving Upsell (BOSUP)
This offer is triggered in real-time when a pro has already spent their budget but is still being shown in search results due to a low supply of pros in their specific category and zip code. Its goal is to help the pro immediately capture existing demand that they would otherwise miss.  This is a reactive offer, in contrast to the proactive Seasonal Overserving Budget Upsell (SOBU) offer.
BOSUP eligible conditions 
A pro is eligible for a BOSUP offer if they are being over served, which happens only when all of the following conditions are met:
Low Supply Market: The pro's category and zip code have fewer than four eligible pros.
Targeting On: The pro has their targeting preferences (also known as "Job preferences") turned on.
Search Visibility: The pro would have normally appeared in the search results for a given request.
Budget maintenance period
A 2-week period is required. The pro must maintain the increased budget for this full duration to be issued the free leads.
Differences between BOSUP and SOBU
The BOSUP program has unique features that distinguish it from the seasonal (SOBU) offers:
"Unlimited" budget shortcut: A pro can accept a BOSUP offer directly from their Budget page by selecting the "Unlimited" option. This action counts as acceptance, and a confirmation message will appear, notifying them that maintaining an unlimited budget for two weeks will unlock their free leads.
Varying offer structure: The offers a pro sees can change.
The first time a pro is eligible, they will typically see three different budget increase options to choose from.
On subsequent offers, they may see a single, enhanced offer to switch to an unlimited budget with an increased incentive.
Re-eligibility: Pros can become eligible for a new BOSUP offer after they have used all the free leads from a previous offer and have once again spent their new, higher budget. They will see the offer in-product but will not receive new email notifications for subsequent offers.
Seasonal Overserving Budget Upsell (SOBU)
This offer is triggered proactively to help pros prepare for predictable, seasonal increases in customer demand. Its goal is to encourage pros to raise their budget in advance to take full advantage of an entire upcoming peak season.
The special offer explains that we anticipate that demand for [category] will be higher soon and to increase their budget for the next 6 weeks and we'll give them free leads.  The number of free leads the pro receives depends on the budget increase option they select. 
Budget maintenance period: A 6-week period is required. The pro must maintain the increased budget for this full duration to be issued the free leads.
SOBU Eligibility
The pro must be targeting a category that experiences anticipated peak demand periods (e.g., landscaping in spring, accounting during tax season). 
NOTE: 
Eligible pros will not see regular BOSUP offers while a SOBU offer is active.
Once a pro accepts a SOBU offer, they won't be eligible for a new offer for at least 6 weeks (the full maintenance period).
Do not share specific eligibility criteria with pros to prevent gaming.
Updates
BOSUP Offer Visibility and Downgrade Clarify SHIPPED
On June 17, 2026, the BOSUP Offer Consolidation: Visibility and Downgrade Clarity experiment shipped to baseline. The updated experience puts all Budget Overserving Upsell (BOSUP) offers — fixed budget tiers and the unlimited budget option — on one page, and adds clear warnings if a pro tries to lower their budget after accepting an offer.
Refer to the internal BOSUP Offer Visibility & Downgrade Clarity (Pro) (Experiment shipped) KA to learn more. 
Key points
Frontline reps should keep the following in mind when handling questions about budget increase incentive offers.
Eligibility
Thumbtack does not explain to pros what qualifies them for free leads.
Pros cannot see whether they are eligible for budget overserving — this is intentional to avoid overserving pros when possible.
The number of free leads offered varies per offer.
Claiming an Offer
Pros can accept a BOSUP or SOBU offer by clicking "Claim offer" from the offer page.
For BOSUP only: a pro can also accept by selecting "Unlimited" on their Budget page when a BOSUP offer is active. This counts as acceptance and displays a confirmation that maintaining an unlimited budget for 2 weeks will unlock the free leads.
Tracking Progress
Pros have no dedicated place to view their free lead balance. Here's where reps and pros can find relevant information:

What to check
Where to find it
Pro's current weekly budget
Business-level Budget section (Business Admin page)
History of budget changes
Business Budget History section (Business Admin page)
Progress toward earning the reward
BOSUP Discount Offers section (Business Admin page)
Usage of earned free leads
Discounts section (User Admin page)
Maintenance Period & Disqualification
BOSUP requires the pro to maintain their increased budget for 2 weeks.
SOBU requires the pro to maintain their increased budget for 6 weeks.
An offer will be voided — and the pro will not receive free leads — if any of the following occur before the maintenance period ends:
Budget is decreased (most common reason)
Targeting is turned off, paused, or the business is hidden
Payment failure, including removing the only card on file
Using Free Leads
Once earned, free leads are applied automatically: the next new lead(s) the pro receives will be free until the balance runs out.
Accepting an offer and receiving free leads does not guarantee more leads or improve a pro's search ranking.
Pros earning free leads from an active BOSUP or SOBU offer will not be affected by the overserved contact opt-in experience — those contacts are granted as free until the balance is exhausted.
Free leads expire 90 days after being issued.
Do’s and don’ts
Frontline reps must adhere to the following guidelines during discussions with pros: 
Internal Terminology: Terms like “overserving,” "budget overserving upsell (BOSUP)," and "seasonal overserving budget upsell (SOBU)" are for internal use only and should not be used in conversations with pros.
Promotional Offer Framing: If a pro asks why they are receiving the offer, do inform them it is a promotional offer or a bonus to help them get more value by increasing their budget during periods of high demand.
Do Not Disclose Qualification Criteria: To prevent gaming the system, do not explain the specific criteria that make a pro eligible for these offers.
Use Approved Talking Points: Do use the approved talking points provided in the Talking points section of this KA. 
For questions regarding a pro not receiving free leads or a budget increase incentive offer:
Do check the BOSUP Discount Offers section (Business Admin page) Admin tool to confirm if an offer was sent to the pro and verify if the pro met the eligibility requirements in their account. 
Do notrun the lead incentives query for BOSUP offer information. Use the BOSUP Discount Offers section (Business Admin page) instead.
Do review the Investigate Free Leads and Discounts in Admin (Rep) KA to determine the specific offer the pro is referring to (e.g., budget increase incentive offer, seasonal targeting offer, etc)
Do file a bug report with the relevant support information if product errors are confirmed. (Refer to the internal Bugs and Bug Reports (Rep)  KA for steps. 
2. Pro Experience
How to claim BOSUP offer and use incentive 
Pros may be eligible for two types of promotional offers to help them get more leads during busy times: the standard Budget Overserve Upsell (BOSUP) and the Seasonal Overserving Budget Upsell (SOBU). While the process for claiming them is nearly identical, the key difference lies in the commitment required.
BOSUP offers are designed to meet general, real-time market demand and require a pro to maintain their increased budget for two weeks.
SOBU offers are specifically for peak seasons and require a pro to maintain their increased budget for six weeks.
The following steps outline the entire journey for a pro, from receiving an offer to using their free leads.
Offer Notification: A pro becomes aware of a budget increase offer in one of two ways:
Direct Notification: They receive an email or a push notification about the promotional offer.
▶ In-Product Discovery: The offer is visible within their Thumbtack account in several key locations:▶ On the Services page, under “Activity this week.”[Image: rtaImage]▶ On the Budget page.[Image: rtaImage]▶ On the Jobs page, under “Recommendations for your business.”[Image: rtaImage]
Claiming the Offer: To proceed, the pro must click the "Claim offer" button from any of the locations listed above. This action takes them to the main offer screen.
▶ On the offer screen, they can:
Select a specific offer (e.g., "increase budget by $50 for 3 free leads").
Choose to set an unlimited budget.
▶ Special note for BOSUP:
For a standard BOSUP offer, there is an alternative acceptance method. If the pro navigates to their Budget page and selects the "Unlimited" option directly, this action also counts as accepting the offer. A confirmation message will appear, notifying them that maintaining an unlimited budget for two weeks will unlock the free leads.
When pros are eligible for BOSUP, they have three budget increase options to select from. Every other time a pro is eligible for the offer, they'll see one option to increase their budget to unlimited with an increased incentive. Pros could be eligible for a new offer after they’ve used all the free leads and spent their new, higher budget again. They won’t receive multiple emails
▶ To finalize their choice, they will click "Confirm" or "Try unlimited budget"▶ What the BOSUP offer page looks like:[Image: rtaImage]▶ What the SOBU offer page looks like:
Fixed budget view
Unlimited budget view
[Image: rtaImage]Image description: Shows the Fixed budget view of the seasonal offer, as it shows on a mobile device
[Image: rtaImage]Image description: Shows the Unlimited budget view of seasonal offer, as it shows on a mobile device.
 Tracking the Offer: Once the offer is claimed, the pro's Budget page will display a banner tracking their progress. The messaging will be similar to one of the following:
"Keep this budget until [Date & Time] and your next [#] leads will be free."
"Maintain a weekly budget of at least $[X]. As a reward, your next [#] leads after [Date & Time] will be free."
Maintaining the Budget: To successfully earn the promotional leads, the pro must maintain their increased budget for a specific period. If they lower their budget before this period ends, the offer is voided, and they will not receive the free leads. The required maintenance periods are:
For BOSUP offers: 2 weeks
For SOBU offers: 6 weeks
Using the Free Leads: After the maintenance period is successfully completed, the pro is awarded the free leads. The next new leads the pro receives will automatically be free until all earned free leads have been used. The pro has 90 days to use the free leads before they expire.
NOTE: Accepting a budget increase offer and subsequently receiving free leads does not guarantee an overall increase in leads or enhance a pro's visibility within search results
How pros see if they have an active offer 
1. Offer Visibility
When a pro is eligible for a BOSUP or SOBU offer, it will be displayed prominently within their Thumbtack account to ensure they don’t miss the opportunity. The offer can be found in three main places:

On the Services page, under the “Activity this week” section.
On the Budget page, as a clear call-to-action.
On the Jobs page, listed under “Recommendations for your business.”

 
2. Tracking Progress Towards Free Leads
Once a pro accepts an offer, their Budget page becomes the central place to track their progress. A banner will appear that clearly states the requirements and the end date for the maintenance period.

The messaging will look similar to this:
"Keep this budget until [Date] at [time] and your next X leads will be free."
This banner provides a constant reminder and a clear goal, ensuring the pro knows exactly how long they need to maintain their new budget to earn the reward.

 
3. Viewing Earned Free Leads
After the pro successfully completes the budget maintenance period (2 weeks for BOSUP, 6 weeks for SOBU), the free leads are automatically credited to their account. Pros can't directly view their free lead balance or leads remaining. 

The pro can confirm they have received their leads for free by checking their Jobs page. The free leads will be clearly marked, and the lead will not be charged against their budget.
Reps can tell a pro how many leads they have remaining by looking at the Discounts section on the User Admin page. For steps, see Investigate Free Leads and Discounts in Admin (Rep) KA. 
3. Admin tools to view a pro’s BOSUP offers (Rep)

This section provides a guide to understanding a pro's budget and promotional offers. 
 
The Admin tool offers the most convenient way to access a pro's complete BOSUP and SOBU offer history and status, with real-time data updates (meaning each time you refresh the page, the data updates instantly). 
 
This gives reps all the necessary details without needing to run complex queries. On the Business Admin Page:
Business-level Budget: Shows a pro's existing, real-time budget for that business.*
Business Budget History: Provides a detailed log of every change the pro has made to their budget.*
BOSUP Discount Offers: Lists all budget increase incentives the pro has received and their current status.
* For details on these sections, refer to the internal Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro) KA. 
Reminder: When looking at timestamps, reps should remember the time zone difference (Admin uses the local device's time zone, while the query (BIgQuery) uses UTC).
 
NOTE: 
For deeper analysis including contact PKs, run the Lead Incentives Query. For steps, see the Investigate Lead Incentives in BigQuery (Rep) KA.
On the User Admin Page, reps refer to the Discounts section (of the Users Admin page) for a list of all successfully earned free leads and track their active redemption status, remaining balances, and expiration dates. For guidance on reading that section, see the Investigate Free Leads and Discounts in Admin (Rep) KA.
Where to view a pro’s progress toward free leads (BOSUP Discount Offers Admin section)
 
The BOSUP Discount Offers table on the Business page in Admin tracks a pro's progress through the earning phase of a budget incentive offer. Use this table to determine whether a pro successfully met the requirements for their offer and when their free leads will or did become available. This table only reflects BOSUP and SOBU offers — recommendation incentive or discount offers are not shown here.
 
▶ Here’s what the BOSUP Discounts Offers section looks like in Admin

[Image: rtaImage]

Screenshot of BOSUP Discount Offers field, which shows columns for Type of Offer, Accepted Time, Free Leads Count, Offer expiration date, Free leads grant date, Offer Status, Accepted Offer Level, and Accepted Budget Limit.
NOTE: Once the reward is successfully earned, it also appears here in the Discounts section (on the User page) to track the actual usage of those leads.
 
Breakdown of each column 
 
The table below explains what each column means and how to use it.
 

Column
What It Shows
How to Use It
Type of Offer
Identifies the promotion type (e.g., BUGDET_OVERSERVE).
Lets you know which budget maintenance period to look for (2 weeks vs. 6 weeks).
Accepted Time
The exact date and time the pro clicked to accept the offer.
This is the official start time of the budget maintenance period.
Free Lead Count
The number of free leads offered as the reward.
Confirms the bonus the pro was working towards. 

Only accepted offers will show here. If an offer was not accepted, this column will show as “N/A.”
Offer expiration date
The date the discount offer expires.
The pro must accept the offer before this date to be eligible.
Free leads grant date
The date the free leads will be granted if the pro successfully maintains their budget.
Use this as the target date. The pro must not lower their budget before this date. 

This date automatically accounts for all maintenance periods and experiment groups.
Offer Status
The current state of the promotion. This is the most important column for troubleshooting.
Available: The offer is ready for the pro, but they haven't accepted it yet.
Accepted and Pending: The offer is active. The pro is in their maintenance period, and leads will be granted once it ends.
Completed: Success. The pro met the requirements, and their leads have been issued. To view how many leads have been redeemed, head to the Discounts section on the User admin page.
Not completed: The pro didn't meet the requirements (for example, they changed their budget too early).
Expired: The offer window has closed and is no longer available.
Accepted Offer Level
Budget type (fixed amount or unlimited)
Use to see if the pro is using a fixed amount or an unlimited budget.
Accepted Budget Limit
The current budget limit
Use to see the amount the pro has set for their budget (for example: $1500, Unlimited)
 
NOTE: The "Free leads grant date" column in the BOSUP Discount Offers table is the single source of truth for when a pro's leads will be issued. It automatically accounts for the specific maintenance periods — reps do not need to calculate this manually.
Where to view a pro’s budget history 

The Business page in Admin provides reps with two fields to view a pros budget: 
Business-level Budget: Shows a pro's existing, real-time budget for that business.
Business Budget History: Provides a detailed log of every change the pro has made to their budget. If you are troubleshooting a voided BOSUP offer (pro didn’t get free leads), this section provides insight into why the offer was not successfully fulfilled.
For details on each section and how to use them, refer to the internal Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro) KA. 
4. Process
Steps: How to investigate a pro's missing free leads after accepting a budget increase incentive offer (Rep)
Common reasons offer is void
When a pro's budget increase offer is not completed (and pro didn’t receive their free leads), it's often due to specific actions taken before the required maintenance period is complete. Common reasons for an offer being voided include:
Decreasing the budget before the 2-week (BOSUP) or 6-week (SOBU) maintenance period has passed.
Turning off or pausing targeting (which includes hiding their business).
Experiencing a payment failure (which includes removing the only card on file).
These reasons will result in a "Not Completed” on the Business Budget History table.
Understanding these disqualification factors is crucial for frontline reps when investigating why a pro did not receive their free leads. 
Steps to investigate if offer was void

If a pro says they did not receive free leads after accepting a budget incentive offer, Support reps should investigate the "BOSUP Discount Offers" and "Budget History" sections in Admin. Follow these steps to determine the reason:
Step 1: Check "BOSUP Discount Offers" Admin section to confirm the result: This section tells you what happened with the offer.
▶ Go to the pro's Business Page.
In Admin, navigate to the "Business" tab, which is located under the "Models" section.
Enter the pro's Business PK or business name into the search bar and click "Search Businesses."
If needed, locate the pro's Business PK by going to their main user page and finding the "Businesses / Services" field.
Scroll down to the BOSUP Discount Offers table. 
Look for the relevant offer in the table.
Look at the “Offer Status” column.
Check the status of the offer in the “Offer Status” column. 
“Accepted and Pending:” The pro is still within their budget maintenance period. Advise them to keep their budget stable until the date shown in the “Free leads grant date” column passes.
“Completed:” The pro successfully met the requirements, and the leads were granted.
“Not Completed:” The pro did NOT meet the requirements and did not receive the free leads. Move to Step 2 to find out why.
Note the “accepted time” from the "BOSUP Discount Offers" table. This is when the maintenance period started.
Step 2: Check "Business Budget History" Admin section to find the reason: This section tells you why the offer was rejected.
Check the Business Budget History table. The most recent changes are at the top.
Find the row where the offer was accepted.
You can confirm this by matching the “created timestamp” to the offer's “accepted time.”
You will also see “Pro_Set_BOSUP_Offer-Accepted” in the budget settings context column.
Scan all the budget changes after this acceptance timestamp and before the Free leads grant date. Look for: 
Budget lowered — a row showing a reduced budget amount before the grant date. This is the most common reason.  If the pro lowered their budget (e.g., from "Unlimited" to "$50"), reps will see a row before the "Free leads grant date” date with the offer status as "Not Completed” due to this budget change.
Reps may see "Not completed” for other reasons:
Targeting turned off or business hidden — no budget change will show for this. To check targeting status, impersonate the pro. See the Making Account Changes on Behalf of Pro or Customer (Impersonation Guidelines) (Rep) KA for steps.  
Payment failure — no budget change will show for this. To check for a failed payment, see the Charges on Thumbtack: Payment Methods and Billing (Pro)  KA
Communicate findings: Based on your investigation, clearly explain to the pro why their offer was voided, referencing the specific disqualifying action. Remember to use approved talking points and avoid internal terminology like "overserving."

5. Talking points
This section provides frontline reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros about budget overserving upsell offers. Use these talking points to ensure consistent and accurate messaging.

English talking points 
Spanish talking points 
Why are you offering free leads if I increase my budget?
¿Por qué ofrecen prospectos gratis si aumento mi presupuesto?
A: You're seeing this because you're in a category or area that is experiencing high customer demand. By increasing your budget during these busier periods, you can get more leads and potentially earn more money. The free leads are a bonus to help you get even more value.
A: Usted ve esto porque su categoría o su área tiene mucha demanda de clientes.
Si aumenta su presupuesto durante estos periodos de más demanda, puede recibir más prospectos y también puede ganar más dinero. Los prospectos gratis son un beneficio adicional para que usted aproveche aún más.
How long are the free leads valid for?
¿Cuánto tiempo son válidos los prospectos gratis?
Once you've earned the free leads, they are valid for 90 days before they expire.
Una vez que usted obtenga los prospectos gratis, serán válidos por 90 días antes de vencer.
Does my new budget stay the same for the following weeks?
¿Mi nuevo presupuesto se mantiene igual en las semanas siguientes?
Yes. When you accept the offer, you are setting a new weekly budget. It will remain at that new amount by however much you selected.
Sí. Cuando usted acepta la oferta, establece un nuevo presupuesto semanal. Se mantendrá en ese nuevo monto, según lo que usted haya seleccionado.
Why should I increase my budget? 
¿Por qué debería aumentar mi presupuesto?
By increasing your budget during busier periods, you can get more leads and potentially earn more money. The free leads are a bonus to help you get even more value.
Si aumenta su presupuesto durante periodos de más demanda, puede recibir más prospectos y también puede ganar más dinero. Los prospectos gratis son un beneficio adicional para que usted aproveche aún más.
What happens if I lower my budget after I accept the offer?
¿Qué pasa si reduzco mi presupuesto después de aceptar la oferta?
If you lower your budget before the required maintenance period is over, the offer will be voided, and you will not be issued the free leads. You must keep the budget at or above the accepted amount for the full duration.
Si usted reduce su presupuesto antes de que termine el periodo de mantenimiento requerido, la oferta se anulará y usted no recibirá los prospectos gratis. Usted debe mantener su presupuesto en el monto aceptado o por encima de ese monto durante todo el periodo.
What do I need to do to get the free leads by increasing my budget?
¿Qué necesito hacer para obtener los prospectos gratis al aumentar mi presupuesto?
If you accept the offer, you'll need to increase your budget and keep it at that level for the required time period. After that period is over, if you've maintained the increased budget, you'll receive a number of free leads to use over the next 90 days

[For BOSUP: The requirement is to maintain the budget for two weeks.]
[For SOBU: The requirement is to maintain the budget for six weeks.]
Si usted acepta la oferta, deberá aumentar su presupuesto y mantenerlo en ese nivel durante el periodo requerido. Cuando termine ese periodo, si usted mantuvo el presupuesto aumentado, recibirá cierta cantidad de prospectos gratis para usar durante los próximos 90 días.
[For BOSUP: The requirement is to maintain the budget for two weeks.]
[For SOBU: The requirement is to maintain the budget for six weeks.]
Q: How long do I have to accept this offer to unlock free leads by increasing my budget 
¿Cuánto tiempo tengo para aceptar esta oferta y desbloquear prospectos gratis al aumentar mi presupuesto?
Because these offers are based on real-time market demand and seasonal changes, we can’t guarantee how long a specific offer will be available. It's best to claim it when you see it.
Como estas ofertas se basan en la demanda del mercado en tiempo real y en cambios de temporada, no podemos garantizar cuánto tiempo estará disponible una oferta específica. Lo mejor es reclamarla cuando la vea.
4. Internal FAQ
This section provides answers to frequently asked questions and is intended for internal frontline rep use only. This information should not be shared externally with pros.
Q: Will pros still get free leads if they updated their budget and shortly after they lowered it?
A: 
Pros will get the free leads if they accept the offer through the “Claim offer” upsell page or by selecting Unlimited on the Budget page when a BOSUP offer is active. Selecting Unlimited counts as acceptance and shows a confirmation that keeping Unlimited for two weeks will unlock the free leads. 
If they lower their budget shortly after accepting the offer, they will not receive the free leads
Q: Is the BOSUP upsell a one-time offer?
A: No, a pro will get an offer if they are eligible to be budget overserved (ran out of budget in a low supply market) and they do not have an existing offer. Meaning if they accepted an offer and they used up their free leads and budget again, they will receive another offer when budget overserved again. Currently, we cap the number of offers per pro at 3.

Q: If the pro increases their budget each week, will they get additional free leads?
A: No, they only get free leads when they accept the offer. Technically they cannot get more free leads from another offer until they've used the free leads and ran out of budget. We always apply the free leads discount first before using the budget.
Q: How do I see if a pro got their free leads?
A: To see if a pro received their free leads, frontline reps should follow the Steps: How to investigate a pro’s missing free leads after accepting a Budget Incentive Offer (Rep) section. For a detailed walkthrough example of this process, reps can refer to the Example: Walkthrough of checking if a pro got their free leads section below.
Q: What is the difference between "EXPIRED" and "NOT COMPLETED" in the BOSUP Discount Offers table?
A: “EXPIRED,” means the pro didn't accept the offer before the deadline. “NOT COMPLETED”, means the pro accepted the offer but didn't meet the requirements (for example, they lowered their budget before the maintenance period ended).
Q: What is the difference between the "BOSUP Discount Offers" table and the new "Discounts" section?
A: The BOSUP Discount Offers table (on the Business admin page) tracks the pro's progress toward earning a reward (e.g., maintaining their budget). Once the reward is successfully earned, it also appears in the Discounts section (on the User admin page) to track the actual usage (redemption) of those leads.
Example: Walkthrough of checking if a pro got their free leads
▶ 🤖 Background notes:
This section provides an example for internal training purposes and should not be used as a direct answer to rep queries. The scenario presented is for understanding how disqualification factors impact offer eligibility.
Sometimes, pros can get free leads if they increase their budget for a required time (in this example, it’s two weeks). Let's walk through how to check if they actually received those leads in Admin.
The Situation: A pro agrees to increase their budget to get 18 free leads, but then they change their mind and lower it again after only 6 days. Because they didn't keep the higher budget for the full 2 weeks, they won't get the free leads.
Here's how frontline reps can check in Admin: 
Go to “BOSUP Discount Offers”: 
This section shows the offer details like when the pro accepts it (January 27, 2025, at 10:59 PM CST). 
It also shows a “Free leads grant date”(February 10, 2025, at 10:59 PM CST). This is when 18 free leads would have been given if the budget had been kept high enough. 
Look at the “Offer Status.”
If it says “Accepted & pending”, this indicates the offer is pending until it becomes granted (the pro is in the 14-day period where they must maintain their budget). 
Once the "Free leads grant date" date and time pass, the system checks if the offer is still valid and updates the status to "Completed" or "Not Completed".
If it says “Not Completed,” that means the pro didn’t get the free leads.

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) provides Frontline Reps with information regarding the BOSUP Offer Consolidation: Visibility and Downgrade Clarity experiment that shipped to baseline on June 17, 2026. It details how Thumbtack moved from showing budget offers one at a time to showing all options on a single page, and adding clear warnings for budget downgrades.
On June 17, 2026, the BOSUP Offer Consolidation: Visibility and Downgrade Clarity experiment shipped to baseline. The experiment puts all Budget Overserving Upsell (BOSUP) offers — fixed budget tiers and the unlimited budget option — on one page, and adds clear warnings if a pro tries to lower their budget after accepting an offer.
A BOSUP (Budget Overserving Upsell) is an offer sent to "overserved" pros, encouraging them to increase their weekly budget to meet actual customer demand. In exchange, they receive free leads as a bonus.
Pros now see all four offer tiers (fixed and unlimited) at once when clicking a BOSUP "Special offer.”Clear warnings appear if a pro attempts to lower their budget below the required threshold, explaining the potential loss of free leads.
More details are in the Pro experience section below.
Updates
June 17, 2026 - this experiment shipped to baseline.
The special offers page has the “high” fixed-budget offer preselected (instead of unlimited)
The special offers page with an unlimited budget discount offer says “Get X free leads after 2 weeks. Plus, get 10% off all leads now”. (Previously said: “The best value per lead. After 2 weeks, your next X leads are free. Please, get 10% off all leads now.”)
Reduced reward for the unlimited budget 
(Launched to baseline experience) Unlimited budget discount offers are not  offered to pros who have: 
Not been active in the past 7 days OR
0 lifetime verified reviews OR
0 contacts in the last 30 days
0 contacts in the last 30 days
2. Pro experience

▶ Entry to offer: On the services and budget pages, pros will see a blue banner explaining they can get free leads when they try one of our budget offers with a clickable “View special offer.”[Image: rtaImage][Image: rtaImage]
▶ Consolidated special offer page: The pro will see all four budget increase offer tiers (fixed and unlimited) at once when clicking a BOSUP "Special offer. If a pro is eligible for an Unlimited Budget discount, that option is styled differently to highlight value.The page also explains the budget change will take effect immediately and after maintaining the higher budget for 2 weeks, the new leads they receive within a 90-day limit will be free, up to the number specific in the offer they accept.BOSUP offer only: [Image: rtaImage]BOSUP offer with unlimited budget discount offer: [Image: rtaImage]
Selecting a budget: The pro can either keep the high fixed budget offer that was preselected or select another option and click “Confirm.” For pros also eligible for an unlimited budget discount offer, the high fixed budget amount is preselected and pros can choose the “Don’t limit my budge.” option instead to benefit from the BOSUP offer and % discount. 
▶ Confirm offer selection:  A new screen will ask the pro to confirm their selection when accepting an offer and adjusting their budget. (e.g., Your budget will be updated immediately. Maintain this budget for 2 weeks to get your free leads). The pro will hit “Yes, I’m sure” to finish claiming the offer.[Image: rtaImage] 
▶ Confirmation page: An updated confirmation screen with clearer messaging will show their new budget amount and explain that if they keep their new budget for 2 weeks they will receive X free leads. If the pro had an unlimited budget discount offer, this screen will also explain that they start getting X% off leads immediately.Fixed budget: [Image: rtaImage]Unlimited budget with discount[Image: rtaImage]
▶ Claimed offer status: Once a pro has claimed an offer, their budget page will have a blue banner explaining “Maintain your current budget until X to get your X free leads.” This banner tells the pro the exact date down to the hour when they will get their free leads (e.g., Tue Mar 10 at 1pm)[Image: rtaImage]
▶ Warning message: If the pro goes to change their current budget to a custom amount below their current budget amount, they will now see a yellow banner explaining: “You’ll miss out on X free leads starting [date/time] if you set a budget below $[current budget amount].[Image: rtaImage]
Once the pro claims the offer, the discount does not expire. Thumbtack may end or change the promotion at any time, but we'll notify pros on the unlimited budget offer beforehand. 
3. Talking points
This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros about the Special Offer visibility and downgrade clarity experience.

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article for Thumbtack's Boost Team (Support Ops) outlines the team's purpose in improving customer retention and bringing revenue to the platform. It covers the process for handling customer leads (both warm and cold leads), best practices for customer interaction, cross-selling strategies, and guidelines for logging interactions, providing essential information for Reps.
Key points
Here are key points for the Boost team to remember regarding their objectives, processes, and customer interaction guidelines:
The Boost Team (Support Ops) aims to improve customer retention and generate revenue by working with customer leads.
The Boost team handles both "warm" real-time leads (Targeted Customer Assist (TCA)) and "cold" 24 - 48 hour old leads (Recover) where customers haven't received a positive pro response (PPR).
Boost assists customers by sending projects to pros, creating or modifying new projects, and suggesting alternative categories and cross-sells.
The team's top priority is to educate customers on using Thumbtack successfully and retaining them on the platform.
Boost serves repeat/existing, first-time, and Instant Booking customers, providing empathetic and proactive support.
Key guidelines for reps include calling between 8 am and 8 pm local time (avoiding Sundays/holidays for Recover leads), recording calls, confirming contact numbers, and using a double-tapping method for unanswered calls.
The process involves taking a lead, understanding the customer's needs before calling, and following specific steps for when a customer answers or doesn't.
Cross-selling strategies emphasize convenience, expanding on initial requests, future planning, pitching in the middle of calls, and using seasonal checklists.
Reps should focus on fulfilling net new requests and take an assertive approach when cross-selling.
The article details how to overcome common customer objections during calls.
Logging interactions accurately is crucial, with specific outcomes and reasons for churn to be selected.
Do's and Don’ts
To ensure effective customer interactions and lead management, Boost reps should adhere to these important "Do's and Don'ts":
Do call between 8 am to 8 pm local time (except for Rhode Island). 
Do not call before 8:00 am local time or after 8:00 pm local time
Do call during golden hour [e.g., during local lunch hours and after work hours (5pm onwards)
Do not call on Sundays or public holidays (Only Applicable for Recover Leads)
Public holidays: 
New Year's Day (January 1)
Birthday of Martin Luther King, Jr. (Third Monday in January)
Washington's Birthday (Third Monday in February)
Memorial Day (Last Monday in May)
Juneteenth National Independence Day (June 19)
Independence Day (July 4)
Labor Day (First Monday in September)
Columbus Day (Second Monday in October)
Veterans Day (November 11)
Thanksgiving Day (Fourth Thursday in November)
Christmas Day (December 25)
Do tell the caller that the call is being recorded. This is a legal requirement and can't be forgotten.
Do confirm the number the customer wants to provide to pros.
To increase the chances of connecting with a customer, try reaching out later in the day using the double-tapping method if the customer didn't answer the initial call.
To improve efficiency, try setting aside a specific time to respond to emails and text messages. 
What the Boost Team does
The Boost Team is a crucial part of Support Operations, dedicated to ensuring customer satisfaction and reducing churn. The Boost team works from warm and cold leads. 
Warm leads are in real-time, also known as Targeted Customer Assist (TCA) leads. These are customers who have requested help through the Thumbtack platform and provided a phone number. The Boost team contacts them shortly after to assist with their project. The team reaches out to the customer within 20-40 minutes of the customer submitting their request. This process can vary slightly, but the team usually makes an outbound call when a customer leaves a page or stops working on a project for a while.  
Cold leads are leads that are 24 - 48 hours old, and are also known as recover leads. If customers do not receive a positive pro response within that time, these leads become cold leads. The Boost team contacts these cold leads because customers who have had a poor experience will likely churn.
Boost helps customers by sending their project to one or two pros, creating a new project with the same details, or modifying the project details based on customer information to submit the best request with details. Boost also offers alternative categories and cross-sell to help customers find the right pro.

The Boost Team is not considered a cost center as they bring revenue to Thumbtack. Boost works from leads in Salesforce and helps repeat, existing, and first-time customers who haven't received a positive pro response within 24 hours. The Boost Team’s top priority is to educate customers on how to use Thumbtack to complete their projects successfully and retain them on the platform.
Customer segments for the Boost Team 
Boost caters to three customer segments, both of which require exceptional customer service, especially if the customer has had a negative experience or feel confused. The following table explains the three customer segments for the Boost Team in detail:
Customer Segment
Why these customers
How the Boost Team helps these customers
Repeat or existing customers who haven't received a positive pro response (PPR) from a pro within 24 hours.
While existing customers may have a better understanding of Thumbtack, it's still a poor experience if the customer doesn't receive a response from a professional.
Boost takes a proactive approach to understand the customer’s issue and offers the customer additional help when required.
First-time customers with at least 1+ PPR but haven’t engaged in any convos. 
Many first-time customers are confused about how to use Thumbtack. If a customer gets a PPR and doesn't respond, it may be because the customer is confused about how to use Thumbtack. 
Additionally, customers may reach out to fewer pros due to potential dissatisfaction (e.g., unprofessionalism, a higher-than-anticipated price, unavailability, etc.) with the initial responses from the pro(s). 
Boost’s concierge team is here to help customers understand how Thumbtack works and help customers connect with pros. 
Boost strives to be empathetic while addressing customer issues without coming across as aggressive. By offering additional help, Boost ensures customers have a positive experience on Thumbtack.
How Boost builds rapport with customers
Thumbtack takes pride in fostering long-term relationships with customers rather than just focusing on one-off transactions. These relationships are the foundation of Thumbtack’s success, so Boost is committed to providing customers with the highest level of care and support.

The Boost Team's approach centers around actively listening and showing genuine care, which helps to build trust and loyalty with customers. The following list gives tips on how Boost team members can build rapport with customers:
Begin each call with a warm greeting and a smile, which can help establish rapport and set a positive tone. 
Energy and attitude can be felt through the phone line, so conveying a positive and friendly demeanor is important whenever possible. 
It's also important to be authentic and let personality shine through, as this can help to build a connection with the customer.
Match the customer’s pace and show empathy whenever possible.
For example, if a customer is expressing concern about a sick pet, show empathy by expressing sympathy and relating to a similar experience, if applicable. 
Be in a supportive and empathetic position to address customer’s concerns effectively.
For more info on empathizing, see the “De-escalation Tools” section of the internal Standard Escalations and De-Escalation Guidelines (Rep) KA. 
By following these guidelines, the Boost team can create a positive and empathetic experience for customers, which can help to build strong and lasting relationships.
