2. Process
▶ 🤖 Background notes
[AI Context]: This section outlines the step-by-step process for handling customer leads, including pre-call activities, interaction guidelines, cross-selling strategies, and methods for overcoming common customer objections. It also details the various statuses for leads and important reminders for reps.
Steps: How to take a lead (Rep)
Boost team members will follow these steps to efficiently take and manage a lead in Salesforce.
In Salesforce, Click Next Best Maintain along the bottom to get a new lead/maintain. (See what it looks like below.)▶ What it looks like[Image: OeiWIL4ERIsA5sT7e6L5ce1YsInsTtMu_-JtOB8OZ7VsddmclIdncbFn-GiL7HJXiYMPvAGVZt3qFzr7Qe19TT405-dQxC9Lcx-GHIoV9fIv4-zvhcAaJUhdtzFeB3LwtPE6Vx0s2pF-zU-l-oQ8hgk]
To validate the phone for outbound, use this Phone Validator - Verify Phone Numbers for Free 
Click Go to Record to check the lead/maintain. (See what it looks like below.)▶ What it looks like[Image: kPf4u0XsOg9aBe01SJvjA28scg-ld_1O4MylA92A4C5CEGZyAl8gb0UAZyk-yfCfB3cgHDneVHjM77dYmzlQpoS9RQAVoV-Fyo2LZ_h8BkqjsRhxAjZRfyUwuEPSyAVH1ls1EbbDF5Hmn4tN2eZfUyA]
Mark the current lead status according to the outreach outcome. Please refer to the definitions below.
Lead statuses and when to use them
The following table shows the lead statuses and when Boost Reps use the different statuses:
Lead Status
Definition
New
When a lead comes into Salesforce, this is the default status that it is in pre-assignment
Attempting
As soon as a lead is assigned after clicking NextBestMaintain, a lead should be moved to this status by a Rep BEFORE any pre-call activities. This is the start of ticket handle time (call duration is tracked separately). The ticket should remain in this status during the call, email and SMS attempt.
Attempt Unsuccessful
If 1st attempts are unsuccessful, mark the ticket as “attempt unsuccessful” and move on to the next ticket. Reps can always come back to double tap later (and set tasks on Salesforce to remind to double tap at a certain time). 
2nd Attempt
This status should be used for: 
Double taps: Change the ticket status to “2nd attempt” before starting the double tap call, sms, email. 
Inbound calls: If a Rep receives an inbound call, the Rep is responsible for taking over and moving it forward. As soon as the call comes in, Reps should look up the phone number and update the lead/maintain status to “2nd attempt” prior to doing any work on the ticket. 
Unsuccessful
If the double tap is unsuccessful, update the ticket status to the same.
Convert (TCA only)
If the Rep converted a TCA lead (either helped submit a net new project or any additional Pros to existing request), ONLY then convert a lead to a maintain record and after submitting the project, product feedback etc. update status to “successful”
Successful
All maintains that were converted should end in this status
Lead logic
This section explains how leads are prioritized and populated in the system.
TCA: These leads are prioritized in queue based on speed to lead
Recovery:
1) These leads are currently randomized, lead scoring logic TBD in Q4 
2) Recovery leads will only populate starting 8am local standard time
Important reminders for lead management
For Boost Reps, here are important reminders to ensure effective lead management:
Reps should only call a TCA/Recover lead a maximum of two times. 
The value of an incremental call beyond that diminishes and it’s better to attempt another lead for the first time vs attempting one lead more than two times. 
Only attempt one lead at a time fully (aka Attempt 1 status should entail call, sms, email subsequently) prior to moving forward to the next lead. Reps can always come back to double tap the lead to maximize likelihood to convert.
What Reps should NOT do moving forward: Click "NextBestMaintain" send an SMS to one and move forward to the other lead and bulk call for the first time at a later time. 
Doing this affects operation and staff efficiency and creates data discrepancies which will affect goal settings, incentives etc.
Before moving forward to the next lead, please ensure that a lead status is updated and lead is disposed appropriately.
Steps: What to do before the call (Rep) 
For Boost Reps, here are the steps to take before making a call to a customer.
Steps for “cold” Recover leads:                                                                            
In Admin via the Maintain Number, scan the customers project(s) to get a basic understanding and background of the customer and their details. 
Approach the call with the homeowner in a consultative manner.
Identify what the homeowner needs help with, such as asking about the specific issue they are experiencing or offering potential solutions based on their situation.
Focus on showing empathy and understanding towards the homeowner, such as asking how they are and acknowledging their concerns. This will help build rapport and trust with the customer.
In Salesforce using the phone panel, call the customer with the phone number on the project request.
See the internal Genesys Phone System (Rep) KA to learn more. 
Steps for “warm” Targeting Customer Assist (TCA) leads:
In Salesforce, open the lead and scan through the customer’s request to get a basic understanding and background of the customer and their details. If the customer is an existing customer check the admin to gain more details of the customer’s project. 
Approach the call with the homeowner in a consultative manner.
Identify what the homeowner needs help with, such as asking about the specific issue they are experiencing or offering potential solutions based on their situation.
Focus on showing empathy and understanding towards the homeowner, such as asking how they are and acknowledging their concerns. This will help build rapport and trust with the customer.
Steps: What to do if the customer doesn’t answer (Rep)
If the customer doesn’t answer, Boost reps should follow these steps:
If the customer’s voicemail is set up, leave a voicemail. 
Send the customer text 1. 
To increase the chances of connecting with a customer, try reaching out later in the day using the double-tapping method if the customer doesn't answer the initial call. 
Send the customer text 2. 
If the customer responds via text, help them accordingly 

See the Templates section below for voicemail script and text templates. 
Steps: What to do if the customer answers (Rep)
For Boost reps, here are the steps to follow when a customer answers the call:
OPENER
Start the conversation by introducing yourself and identify who you are speaking with. Note that the Rep must disclose that the call is on a recorded line.
Talking point: Good [morning / afternoon], my name is [name]. I'm on Thumbtack's customer concierge team on a recorded line. You recently requested a [service category] project through our platform. Am I speaking with [Customer name]?"
If the customer says no. 
Confirm the name of the person on the other line. 
Request to speak to the account holder. 
If the account holder is not available:
Ask for an alternate number or best time for a callback.
If the phone number is no longer associated with the account holder:
Dispose the lead in Genesys and Salesforce as “Incorrect Phone number”
If the customer says yes, move to step 2.
RECOVERY 
Explain why you are reaching out. 
Talking point:  I wanted to check in with you and see whether you were able to find the right pro to complete your [service category] project or if I could help you find some additional pros to speak to and compare a few quotes?
If they say they haven’t found a pro or want additional quotes (if no, skip to step b): 
Talking point: Okay, not a problem, let me help you find another option! To confirm, you’re looking for somebody to help with [service category] (which of the two that they have submitted). 
Contact additional pros for the customer and move to step c)
Talking point:  “Great, I'll go ahead and send your request to another pro on your behalf through your account. These pros will then reply directly to you. 
Acknowledge their value: 
If the customer has not used Thumbtack before: 
Talking point: “I have your account pulled up and see that this is one of your first requests with us - welcome to the platform. I am excited to help you out!” 
Assist the customer with their project needs and cross sell where applicable. Check Cross-selling categories for suggestions
If the customer has used Thumbtack before: 
Talking point: “Thank you for using Thumbtack, I see you have used our platform in the past for [service categories]. How was your experience? 
Collect feedback if possible about past jobs. See the internal Product Feedback KA for more details. 
Identify the customers preferred contact method by asking if they use the app or web.
Talking point:  “Do you know how to contact pros through your account on our website or app?”
Handy benefit talking point – The reason I ask a lot of our customers find it really handy and useful to use that so feel free to download it, I can send you a link after our call
Guarantee benefit talking point – The reason I ask is because Thumbtack guarantees whenever you hire a Thumbtack pro. However, we only ensure that guarantee when the conversation is done in-app or at the very least the website
Safety benefit talking point –  The reason I ask is because it enables your safety when Thumbtack is able to monitor the pros messages with you.
NOTE: Reps should always encourage customers to communicate with pros through the Thumbtack app. It’s easier for customers to track messaging with pros and projects.
If the customer is not a Thumbtack app user: 
Talking point: Typically, users are able to manage their requests effectively through the app - I can assist you in downloading it. That way you will be able to have an easier time speaking to pros. 
Example: 
Kelly (customer): “I think just passing along my number should work for now”
Lyt (agent): “More than happy to do so, however, I will say it is much easier to keep track of your conversations and projects if you have the app. Majority of our customers are able to see a quicker turnaround time with responses there as well. I am going to send you the link so you have it accessible to download at any point in time - also happy to walk you through it if need be!”
App link to send: https://www.thumbtack.com/app/
If the customer refuses to download the Thumbtack app and requests to be contacted by the pro, Boost Reps can provide the pro with the customer's phone number. To do this, must verify the customer's number.
Example: 
Customer: “I’d like to be contacted via phone [call/SMS]”

Steps: Cross-selling guidelines (Rep) 
For Boost reps, here are the key guidelines for cross-selling to customers:
Focusing on fulfilling net new requests can have the biggest impact on revenue.
Take a proactive approach rather than reactive, meaning Boost Reps should aim to resolve as many issues as possible for the customer.
It's best to take an assertive approach by telling customers rather than asking open-ended questions.
This table outlines various cross-selling strategies, their positioning, benefits, and suggested talking points for Boost reps.
Cross-Selling Strategy 
Positioning 
Benefit
Talking Point 
Concierge convenience 
Customers have a lot on their plate..Thumbtack wants to make their lives easier, not more challenging.
Thumbtack does all of the leg work for customers so they are set up for a smooth experience from the start.
– A strategy that emphasizes the ease of using Thumbtack
– Customers know that Thumbtack and Reps will handle the difficult tasks
– This approach increases the customer's likelihood of using Thumbtack
Let me help find a solution to  the rest of your tasks..how can I make your life easier here?” 
“Walk me through what the next item is on your to-do list or a project you are thinking about..I am happy to drum up some ideas for you and reach out to pros so that way we can get the ball rolling here.
Cross Sell categories
Utilize the similar categories to branch out on the initial request (see Cross selling categories) 
– Expanding on initial requests helps trigger further thought processes 
– Encourages consideration of additional tasks or actions

Future planning
1.  Offer assistance for any upcoming work needed 
2. Determine scheduling for timelines 
3. Submit work if it's within 1-2 weeks 
4. Add info to future outreach tracker for work more than 1 month out 
5.  For big projects starting in ~ 2 months (like a bathroom or kitchen renovation), send requests out.

Rather than saying the pitch at the end, cross sell in the middle of the call to allow the customer a bit more time to process
Boost Reps should give less of a sense of ‘up-selling’ and more suggestive selling by having it flow during the conversation

Seasonal checklist

– Focus on what's needed for each season

Understand their ‘biggest’ priority
1. Identify the primary home-care concern
2. Provide support in that area
3. Better understanding needs beyond the current project
4. Demonstrate alignment with priorities for the future
Knowing what's important to customers beyond their current project helps with future outreach and demonstrates alignment with their goals and priorities.
Explain to me what your biggest home-care priority is at the moment..let’s figure out how we can help you achieve your goals here.

Talking point

Steps: Blocking Users in Salesforce (Leadership or Advanced Support Only)
Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
Important: This internal knowledge article specifically details the process for blocking abusive users. It is crucial to understand that these blocking processes are separate and distinct from the broader processes for handling unprofessional behavior, support abuse, and discrimination as outlined in the Unprofessional Behavior, Support Abuse, & Discrimination (Rep) KA. This KA focuses solely on when and how to block users, not on the initial responses or escalations related to various forms of user misconduct.
Working with pros and customers who are upset can be difficult because it can feel like they’re making the discussion personal. It’s important to take a step back during these calls and remember that the pro or customers aren't frustrated with you.
Frontline reps should approach these calls by de-escalating the call. Reps can refer to the internal Unprofessional Behavior, Support Abuse, & Discrimination (Rep) KA to learn more.
2. Blocking Abusive Users (For Frontline Reps)
Note to reps: This section will cover the actions taken to block a user, which is a final step that may be decided upon after the processes described in the internal Unprofessional Behavior, Support Abuse, & Discrimination (Rep) KA. This is not a guide for handling unprofessional behavior generally, but for enacting a user block.
Identifying when to consider blocking a caller 
If a caller exhibits inappropriate behavior while a frontline rep is helping them, blocking them from making future calls may be necessary. Here are examples of behaviors that may warrant blocking:
Harassment or threats
Discriminatory comments
Inappropriate language or comments
Repetitive or excessively disruptive behavior
Steps to report unprofessional behavior for manager review and potential blocking (Rep)
This process details the specific steps frontline reps should take when encountering unprofessional behavior during a call.
If the call has ended or the caller has disconnected:
Submit a request to the Advanced Service Team using the Assist app in Slack for help in determining next steps.
Navigate to #service_global_help-and-escalations.

Search for the user in Salesforce using their name, email, phone number, or user ID.

(Rep) Steps: How to run a query in Big Query

Glossary
Resources
1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) for Support Reps details how to effectively use BigQuery, a Google application, to run SQL queries and access vital pro account information. It outlines available queries, necessary input details, helpful tips, and step-by-step instructions for efficient data retrieval. The KA also includes a glossary of terms and relevant resources for further support.
BigQuery, a Google application that uses SQL programming, allows Support reps to run a query to see if a pro or customer recently made a change to their account. 
SQL codes are designed to gather the necessary information applicable to the query, allowing reps to change specific tags/codes in the prewritten query code to search for the information you want. 
For the query code, reps will refer to the S&S SQL Queries sheet. When running a query, Support reps should only change coding in the red text, all other text should not be modified. The sheet also has a notes section with more directions.

Tip: Reps can use Slackbot to quickly access this KA by using the trigger “Run support query.”
SQL queries available to support reps
Support reps can refer to the S&S SQL Queries sheet for query templates. The table below shows a list of queries Support reps can run:
Important Reminder: Support reps may be able to access some of the information in Admin, instead of running a query. For example, reps can refer to the Business page to view a pro’s budget and BOSUP history. Reps can refer to the internal Budget Overserving Upsell Knowledge article to learn more. 
Calendar and availability (Pro)

Information Needed
Why Use This Query?
Address
To see if a pro made changes to their address. It’s helpful if a pro claims a non-opt-in contact was made that didn't match their travel area. One thin gt note is that changing the address also changes the pro's travel areas to a 50-mile radius from the new zip code. That change is NOT reflected in the zip code queries below. 
Availability ruleset
To see when a pro made changes to their availability ruleset. 
Hide my business
To see when a pro hid or manually un-hid their business (go live). This is helpful if a pro says they got a lead while their business was hidden.  
Blocked off days in calendar
To see if a pro blocked off a day before or after a non-opt in contact was created. This is helpful when a pro claims the lead was created for a day they had blocked. 
Keep in mind, the following can be found in Admin: 
To see the last time a pro updated their Availability rules (can include time zone, lead time, business hours), refer to the Availability Rules section of the Business page in Admin. 
Job preference settings (Pro)

Information Needed
Why Use This Query?
Budget
To see when a pro set their budget and what the budget was set to. 
Job preferences
If a pro claims a non-opt-in contact was made that didn't match their job prefs. 
Pricing
(aka quote sheets)
To see what pros pricing was set to. This is helpful if a pro is claiming that a lead was sent with the wrong price.
Service (category) 
To see when services were added or removed to/from a pro's profile, and who did it (the pro? a TT employee?).
Targeting status 
To find out when a pro manually turned targeting on or off. This is helpful to see if targeting was on when a pro received a lead.
Travel preferences (zip codes)
If a pro claims a non-opt-in contact was made that didn't match their travel area.  When a pro made changes to their allowlist. What a pro's zip code allowlist was on a given day. When a given zip was removed from the allowlist via admin.
Keep in mind, the following can be found in Admin: 
To see the last time a pro turned targeting on for their service, and last time targeting was turned off, refer to the Targeting On/Off History on the main User Admin page
To see a pro's current weekly budget, refer to the Business-level budget section on  the Business page in Admin. 
To see a complete log of every change a pro has made to their budget for the past four weeks refer to the Business Budget History section on the Business page in Admin.
Pro Rewards (Pro)

Information Needed
Why Use This Query?
Rewards tier
To check what tier a pro was on the past cycle. Results will show the previous cycle's point, star rating, response rate and the tier level. 
Keep in mind, the following can be found in Admin: 
To see when a pro reached a specific tier/status OR the total points a pro earned per quarter,  refer to the Pro Rewards History section on the User page in Admin. Refer to the internal Thumbtack Pro Rewards (Pro) for steps and details. 
Incentive information (Pro)

Information Needed
Why Use This Query?
Incentives information (Discounts and free leads)
ONLY run the Incentives Query if the information is Admin is not enough. This query can be helpful to identify the specific leads a free lead or discount was applied to (contact PKs). Refer to the internal Investigate Lead Incentives in BigQuery (Rep) KA for steps and details. 
Keep in mind, the following can be found in Admin: 
To see a pro’s BOSUP offer history, maintenance period progress, and whether the pro met the requirements to earn free leads, refer to the BOSUP Discount Offers table on the Business page in Admin. 
To see all active and past discounts and free lead offers, how many leads have been used, balance remaining, expiration date, and discount type, refer to the Discount table on the User page in Admin. 
Messages and responding to leads (Pro or customer)

Information Needed
Why Use This Query?
All messages sent on a given quote/lead
To see all the messages on a given quote/lead, if you can't see them in-product.
Replied to lead
To check if the pro clicked on the reply button and if they abandoned/responded to the message
Notifications and device information (Pro or customer)

Information Needed
Why Use This Query?
Email log for a user
To see what emails were sent to a user. 
Text log for a user
To see what texts were sent to a user
Push notification log for a user
To see what push notifications we sent and when
Device info
To find out the phone model, phone OS, and app version the pro/cx is using. Note that the query doesn’t distinguish between iPhone models, but it does for Android models. This can be helpful when troubleshooting a bug. 
Common details needed to run a query
Before running a BigQuery query, it's crucial for Support reps to gather the correct details. These details act as the parameters for the repsr search, allowing reps to pinpoint the exact information needed. 

Most of the required information is highlighted in red within the query templates themselves (S&S SQL Queries), but here's a breakdown of the key data points reps will need to have on hand:
Pro PK ID - Can be located on the main admin page of the user’s account information. 
Service ID PK - Can be located within the business admin page of the pro. 
Specific Dates - Dates when a lead or project is required to start. It can be found within the actual admin project details. 
Category PK ID – Can be located on the categories tab of Admin. 
Refer to the internal Admin Tool (Rep) KA for more information. 
Tips for running query
Support rep should follow these guidelines when running a query: 
Dates: Pad the dates out by a few days each time, this helps ensure you're getting all the context. 
For example: If the rep wants to know what happened on 4/14, set the PARTITIONTIME to 4/12-4/16.
Timestamps: Many timestamps can be put into different time zones by changing the city in the relevant line. 
The codes all default to MST, which reps will see as /Denver. 
Even if the results of the query say UTC, it is showing reps what time it was in MST if /Denver is in use. 
Here are some of the possible time zone codes reps can choose:
America/Los_Angeles = Pacific Time
America/Denver = Mountain Time
America/Chicago = Central Time
America/New_York = Eastern Time
24-hour lag: All queries can lag by up to 24 hours. If a Support rep thinks the change was made in the last 24 hours, they should try looking again tomorrow.
Have pages of data to review? Change results per page to a higher number to save time.
If you use a query often, you can Create saved queries | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation. 
BigQuery is an internal tool. Do not share screenshots or query details externally.
2. Process
Steps: How to run a query in BigQuery (Rep) 
Important reminders:  BigQuery is an internal tool. Support reps should not share screenshots of the tool or details. If you're unsure about running a query, reach out to the Advanced Service team. Follow the Steps: How to ask AST for help with a query below. 
To start a query, Support reps will follow these steps: 
Copy the applicable query template on the S&S SQL Queries sheet (in column B).
In Big Query, paste the query template into the SQL field. 
Any query copied/pasted into BigQuery will have quotation marks (" ")  around the query. Reps will need to delete these in order to successfully run the query.

Big Query Results screenshot example

[Image: y9krN_JVgFHHm-8iwV8lmhSsCb1gljpVjfR40BMoz2WoFxWfyKSrOTlhv9kBSZab4Qqq7yVG69DP-jm3t8Dw3rRpK0OrNohWtdwn23QjtzR3gU_EIK7AFDAA88RW1VfOjx5BQbliMyoXKYwdnQ]

Let's walk through the process of running a query using BigQuery. Imagine you're looking at a screenshot of the BigQuery interface.
Where to run/play the code: In the BigQuery interface, there's a large text area labeled 'SQL Field' or something similar. This is where you'll paste the query code. It's the central area of the BigQuery window. To execute the query, there's a prominent 'Run' or 'Play' button, usually located above or alongside the SQL Field. Clicking this button starts the query execution.
Query code and editing: The query code itself is a block of SQL text within the SQL Field. The key part for reps is that the sections they need to edit are highlighted in RED within the S&S SQL Queries templates. These highlighted sections are where reps insert specific information like the 'Pro PK ID,' 'Service ID PK,' specific dates, or 'Category PK ID'. It's crucial to only modify these highlighted areas and leave the rest of the code intact.
Where the results will show: Once the query is successfully executed, the results appear in a table format below the SQL Field or in a designated 'Results' pane. The results are presented in rows and columns, showing the data retrieved from the BigQuery database. Reps can then review these results to find the information they were searching for.
How to save the code (if needed): If you have a query you'll use frequently, you can save it within BigQuery. There are options to 'Save Query' or similar, which allows you to name and store your query for future use. This feature prevents you from having to copy and paste the code each time.
Error handling: If there's an error in the query, BigQuery will display an error message directly below the SQL Field or in a separate 'Results' or 'Execution' pane. The error message usually provides details about what went wrong, such as a syntax error or an invalid ID. Reps should carefully read these error messages to troubleshoot any issues.
3. Glossary of Terms
Here's a glossary of terms mentioned through this article. 
BigQuery: A Google application that uses SQL programming to query and analyze large datasets. In this context, it's used by Support reps to investigate pro and customer account activity.
Pro PK ID: A unique identifier (Primary Key ID) for each pro within the Thumbtack system. It's essential for running queries specific to a particular pro. This ID can be found on the main pro admin page.
Service ID PK: A unique identifier (Primary Key ID) for each service category offered by a pro. Found within the pro’s business admin page.
Category PK ID: A unique identifier (Primary Key ID) for service categories within the Thumbtack system. Located on the categories tab of Admin.
SQL: Structured Query Language. The programming language used to interact with and retrieve data from databases like BigQuery.
Query: A request for data from a database. In this context, pre-written SQL queries help Support reps find specific information about pro activity.
UTC: Coordinated Universal Time. A standard time used as a reference for other time zones. However, the BigQuery queries default to and display times in MST (/Denver).
PARTITIONTIME: A specific date or date range used in BigQuery queries to filter data. It helps to narrow down searches to a specific timeframe (e.g., "If the rep wants to know what happened on 4/14, set the PARTITIONTIME to 4/12-4/16.").
Timestamps: Specific points in time recorded in the system. These may be presented in different time zones. The queries default to Mountain Standard Time (MST), indicated by "/Denver."

Reminder: When looking at timestamps, remember the time zone difference (Admin uses the local device's time zone, while the query (BIgQuery) uses UTC).
Steps: How to ask AST for help with a query 
For questions or if you’re unsure about running a query,  Support reps will  submit a request to the Advanced Service Team for help in determining next steps:
Navigate to #service_global_help-and-escalations.
Type Help others (or Others) to trigger the Assist workflow.
Select the "Global Help Others" request type. (If you selected the wrong type, click Cancel and start over.)
Click Open in a new window.
Complete all required fields, including:
A short summary of the question or issue.
The exact query (or link/screenshot) you’re running.
Any error text shown in BigQuery and the timeframe you’re checking.
Click Submit.

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal Knowledge Article provides Frontline Reps with essential troubleshooting steps for common issues experienced by pros and customers on the Thumbtack website, iOS app, and Android app.
Frontline Reps should use the information in this internal knowledge article to walk pros or customers through troubleshooting steps when issues occur with Thumbtack on the desktop site or app. 
Before troubleshooting an issue, Frontline Reps should first ask the pro or customer the following probing questions:
What device are you using, a phone or computer?
If a phone, Android or iOS?
If a computer, Mac or Windows? 
Are you using a browser or an app? If browser, which one?
What was clicked on or what are you trying to click on right now?

(Internal only): General troubleshooting should be done before Frontline Reps escalate to any additional teams.
Key points
Frontline Reps should remember these key points when helping pros and customers with basic troubleshooting:
First, ask probing questions to identify the device, browser or app, and specific actions taken by the pro or customer.
Follow general troubleshooting steps before escalating the issue to other teams.
Only send support articles from another site if the articles are from the manufacturer's official website (e.g., Apple's support site for iPhone issues).
Do’s and don’ts
Frontline Reps should follow these guidelines when helping pros and customers with basic troubleshooting:
Do follow general troubleshooting steps before escalating the issue.
Do send a support article from another site if the pro or customer needs help with specific technology, but make sure the article is from the manufacturer's site.
For example, if a pro or customer doesn't know how to close an app in iPhone X, Reps can send a link (like this one), but only if it's from Apple's website.
2. Process
Frontline Reps should follow these detailed steps to troubleshoot common technical issues encountered by pros and customers on the Thumbtack platform.
Note: After each troubleshooting step, check if the issue is resolved before proceeding.
Steps: How to troubleshoot issues on the web
Frontline Reps can help a pro or customer who is experiencing issues with the Thumbtack website by following these steps:
Log out and log back in
Frontline Reps can recommend this step to resolve various issues, such as when a customer is unable to click buttons or if a pro has changed accounts.
Clear cache and cookies
Frontline Reps can recommend clearing these to reset the browser and remove stored information. Frontline Reps can help pros and customers clear cache and cookies by following the steps for the specific device:
Safari on iOS
Go to Settings (located on the home screen).
From the Settings menu, tap Safari.
Tap Clear Cookies and Data within Safari’s settings (the option to clear browser history is also on this page).
Chrome on Android
Open Chrome and select the menu button.
Tap History from the menu.
Tap Clear Browsing Data and choose what to clear (browsing history, cache, cookies).
Desktop browser: 
Frontline Reps should ask the pro or customer which browser is being used. 
Search Google for instructions on how to clear cache and cookies for that browser.
Follow those instructions.
Disable adblockers or whitelist Thumbtack
Sometimes, adblockers can disrupt website functionality so disabling them may help.
Steps: How to troubleshoot issues on the iOS app
Frontline Reps can help a pro or customer who is experiencing issues with the Thumbtack iOS app by following these steps:
Update the device
The latest versions of the apps only work on iOS 12.0 or higher. So, if a pro or customer is having trouble with the iOS app, Frontline Reps can follow these steps: 
Check if the pro or customer is using a version of iOS below 12.0. 
Encourage the pro or customer to update their device.
Use the right app
There are two Thumbtack apps — one for customers and one for pros. Frontline Reps should make sure the pro or customer is using the right app:
Thumbtack customers should install the Thumbtack app with the blue logo.
The Thumbtack app with the black icon is for pros. 
Update the app
The pro or customer can update the Thumbtack app in the Apple App store by following these steps:
Open the App store from the device.
Tap Updates.
Scroll to find the Thumbtack app and tap Update.
Sign out and sign back in
Signing out and signing back in can often resolve app issues. Frontline Reps can help a pro or customer sign out and sign back in by following these steps:
The pro or customer can see the option to sign out by opening the app and going to Settings. 
Then, the pro or customer will need to sign back in with an email and password.

Uninstall and reinstall the app
Uninstalling and reinstalling the app can resolve various issues and will not remove any of the pro or customer’s leads, profile info, or settings. Frontline Reps can help a pro or customer uninstall and reinstall the Thumbtack app by following these steps:
Press and hold the Thumbtack app icon.
Tap the X that appears on the app.
Press the Home button to exit the app editing mode (app icons will stop shaking).
Pick an option below to download the app:
For pros
For customers

Steps: How to troubleshoot issues on the Android app
Frontline Reps can help a pro or customer who is experiencing issues with the Thumbtack Android app by following these steps:
Update the device
The latest versions of the apps only work on Android OS 5.0 or higher. So, if a pro or customer is having trouble with the Android app, Frontline Reps can follow these steps: 
Check if the pro or customer is using a version of Android below 5.0.
Encourage the pro or customer to update their device
Use the right app

There are two Thumbtack apps — one for customers and one for pros. Frontline Reps should make sure the pro or customer is using the right app.
Update the app
Pros and customers can update the Android app from the Google Play store by following these steps:
Open the Google Play store.
Tap the three-bar menu to access the Play Store settings.
Tap My apps and games.
Check the Updates tab for available updates.
Sign out and sign back in
Signing out and signing back in can often resolve app issues. Frontline Reps can help a pro or customer sign out and sign back in by following these steps:
The pro or customer will see the option to sign out by opening the app and going to Settings. 
The pro or customer will then need to sign back in with an email and password.
Clear cache and data storage
Clearing app cache and data (called storage in recent Android updates) makes the app start over with fresh, new information. This will not remove any of their leads, profile info, or settings.
Pros and customers can clear cache and data storage by following these steps:
Open the phone’s settings.
Select Application manager or Apps (the location and name vary based on the device).
Find and tap the Thumbtack app.
Tap Clear cache.
Tap Clear data/storage.
Reopen the app and sign in again.

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article, "Background Checks (Pro)," serves as a comprehensive guide for Thumbtack Frontline Support Agents on handling Pro background check inquiries. It covers the background check process, common talking points for Pros, and various resources for agents.
Background checks (BGC) helps keep Thumbtack a safe platform for users, and build trust with customers.
All pro account owners are required to take and pass a background check. The background checks are always free for the pro (Thumbtack covers the cost). The background check looks for criminal activity linked to a pros name and verifies their identity. The background check requires basic information like the pros name, date of birth, zip code, and social security number.
Background check results can take anywhere from an hour to 14 days to get back to Thumbtack. Publicly, Thumbtack tells pros results typically take around 5 - 7 business days to be processed.
To qualify for Thumbtack Pro Rewards, pros need to take a background check. Reps can refer to the internal Thumbtack Pro Rewards (Pro KA to learn more. 
Name on background check  

When a pro is asked to take a background check, Thumbtack populates the background check form with the name from their account. This means the name on the background check will always match the name on the account.
If a pro contacts Thumbtack saying they need to update the name on their account to take a background check: Frontline reps can direct them to fill out the ID Help Intake Form or use the Salesforce email template ‘Ask pro to send info to ID Help’. 
If the name on their account was spelled wrong, a pro may be unable to complete a background check. If this is the case: Frontline reps can direct them to fill out the ID Help Intake Form. 
Internal note: The name on a pro’s account cannot be changed to anything other than the original account owner’s to complete a background check.
Frontline reps can refer to the internal ID Help Guide KA for more info, along with the internal Account Information (Pro) KA. 
Checkr
Thumbtack uses Checkr, a vendor, to run background checks. Frontline reps should not mention any other vendors or screening methods Thumbtack uses.
Checkr is an accredited third-party background check provider that searches national and state criminal databases (though databases vary by state).
What the BGC looks for: 
In the check, they review the criminal history of the pro with a focus on convictions related to felonies, violent misdemeanors, and theft-related offenses. 
It reviews from when they were 18 until now and will not pull any removed/dismissed charges. It doesn’t pull a credit report.
Thumbtack looks at results on a case-by-case basis. 
Timeline on results: 
Background check results can take anywhere from an hour to 14 days to get back to us. 
Publicly, Thumbtack tells pros results typically take around 5 - 7 business days to be processed. 
Contact Checker about BGC results: 
Due to the sensitive nature of BGCs, Thumbtack cannot reach out to Checkr on behalf of the pro or discuss the results with the pro. 
Any pro who has questions about Checkr can reach out to them directly at (844)824-3257 or support@checkr.com.
Pros can also read about Checkr security (Privacy Policy | Checkr Legal) and check out their FAQs (Candidate Background Check Status and FAQ) on their website.

The following information is only for internal Thumbtack information only and should not be shared with external users. Frontline reps should use the approved talking points in this KA to navigate these conversations.

Background check results and timeline 

Background check results can take anywhere from an hour to 14 days to get back to us. Publicly, we tell pros results typically take around 5 - 7 business days to be processed.
If a pro calls about their background check before seven days have passed:
Do tell the pro Thumbtack will wait to see the results of their background check before making any decisions.
Don't bring up specific results or crimes with the pro or engage in “what if” scenarios or tell the pro if specific results will be okay or not.
Direct them to https://applicant.checkr.com. 
From there, they can check the status of their check and request copies of their results. 

Internal note: Due to the sensitive nature of BGCs, Thumbtack cannot reach out to Checkr on behalf of the pro or discuss the results with the pro. Any pro who has questions about Checkr can reach out to them directly at (844)824-3257 or support@checkr.com.
Pro passed background check (BGC meets Thumbtack requirements)
If the pro’s results do meet Thumbtack's requirements, the pro will receive the background check badge in the “Credentials” section on their profile. If the account was disabled, it will be reactivated.

Do direct pros to their results for more details or applicant.checkr.com for more details.
Pro failed background check (BGC doesn’t meet Thumbtack requirements)
If the pro’s results don't meet Thumbtack's requirements, the pro is removed from Thumbtack.
Pros who have been removed from Thumbtack because of background check results won’t be added back. However, sometimes it’s possible to have charges removed from the pro's record. Frontline reps can refer to the section below to learn more. 
Additionally, if the pro was removed (and Thumbtack will not reconsider their account), the Trust and Safety team will refund the pro's credit balance to the card on their account. Frontline reps can see the refund section below to learn more. 
A few things to note: 
Thumbtack doesn't make these decisions lightly. Careful consideration has been given to how Thumbtack handles background checks. 
Thumbtacks standards regarding background checks apply to all pros, with no exceptions. 
Thumbtack’s decision wasn’t made because of them specifically or because of their specific background. Any pro with these same results would have the same action taken.

Internal note: Frontline reps should not reactivate any accounts closed for background check results or bring up their specific results or crimes.
Dispute results | Pro has charged removed or results change
The pro has seven days to dispute the convictions with Checkr before Thumbtack takes action. If the seven days pass, and Thumbtack doesn't hear anything, action is taken.
The pro will need to contact Checkr [email support@checkr.com or call (844)824-3257] to dispute their background check results. Checkr will help the pro get their information updated.
If, in the future, the pro says there are changes to their background check results, they can resubmit for an updated background check. Thumbtack will determine the pro's eligibility based on the most recent background check results on file.

Antes de reactivar su cuenta, necesitamos que complete una verificación de antecedentes. Una vez que se complete y apruebe la verificación de antecedentes, activaremos su cuenta.
La verificación de antecedentes es completamente gratuita para usted y es una forma de ganar confianza de inmediato con los clientes de Thumbtack.
Qué hacer a continuación:
Busque el correo electrónico que le enviamos sobre cómo realizar la verificación de antecedentes. Intente buscar "Urgente: acción requerida para cotizar en Thumbtack" o "Acción requerida: realizar una verificación de antecedentes gratuita".
Seleccione el enlace de verificación de antecedentes en el correo electrónico.
Complete el formulario de verificación de antecedentes. La verificación de antecedentes le pedirá información básica como su nombre, fecha de nacimiento, código postal y número de seguro social.
Recibirá los resultados de la verificación de antecedentes en un plazo de 5 a 7 días hábiles. Puede comprobar el estado de sus resultados en el sitio web de Checkr.
Puede visitar Thumbtack Help para obtener más información sobre el proceso de verificación de antecedentes.
Pro didn’t pass background check (account removed)
This section provides talking points for frontline reps to address situations where a pro's account has been removed due to failing a background check, outlining Thumbtack's policy and any available recourse.

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
My account was removed based on the background check results, and I'm frustrated.
Mi cuenta fue eliminada basada en los resultados de la verificación de antecedentes y estoy frustrado.
We can understand your frustration with being removed due to the results of your background check. This isn’t a decision we make lightly, but we’re unable to list your business on Thumbtack.
Although we will not change this decision, we appreciate the time you took to complete the background check. We wish you the best with your business in the future.

NOTE TO REP: If, in the future, the pro says there are changes to their background check results, they can resubmit for an updated background check. Thumbtack will determine the pro's eligibility based upon the most recent background check results on file. 
Podemos entender su frustración por ser removido debido a los resultados de su verificación de antecedentes. Esta no es una decisión que tomamos ligeramente, pero no podemos incluir su empresa en Thumbtack.
Aunque no cambiaremos esta decisión, agradecemos el tiempo que se tomó para completar la verificación de antecedentes. Le deseamos lo mejor con su negocio en el futuro.

Pro passed background check (account reinstated) 
This section provides talking points for frontline reps to inform pros whose accounts were on hold that they have passed their background check and their account has been reinstated, along with information about the background check badge.

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
I took the background check. Is my account reactivated?
Hice la verificación de antecedentes. ¿Se reactivó mi cuenta?
Thanks for taking the time to complete a background check with Checkr. We’re showing that your background check is complete. We’ve reactivated your account so you can start meeting customers. You should’ve received your background check results in an email from Checkr. If you can’t find the email in your inbox, make sure to check your spam folder. You can also contact Checkr directly with any questions at support@checkr.com.
Gracias por tomarse el tiempo para completar una verificación de antecedentes con Checkr. Mostramos que su verificación de antecedentes está completa. Reactivamos su cuenta para que pueda comenzar a conocer clientes. Debería haber recibido los resultados de la verificación de antecedentes en un correo electrónico de Checkr. Si no puede encontrar el correo electrónico en su bandeja de entrada, asegúrese de revisar su bandeja de correo no deseado o Spam. También puede contactar a Checkr directamente con cualquier pregunta enviando un correo electrónico a support@checkr.com.
Concerns or disputes with background check results
This section provides talking points for frontline reps to guide pros who have concerns or wish to dispute their background check results, including how to contact Checkr and the process for re-evaluation.

English FAQ
Spanish FAQ
What if my background check results aren’t correct?
¿Qué pasa si los resultados de mi verificación de antecedentes no son correctos?
Due to the personal nature of background checks, we can’t discuss the details of your background check with you. If you have concerns with your results, contact Checkr directly at support@checkr.com. After working with Checkr to correct any inaccuracies, please contact us with your results.
Debido a la información personal de las verificaciones de antecedentes, no podemos discutir los detalles de su verificación de antecedentes con usted. Si tiene inquietudes con sus resultados, comuníquese con Checkr directamente a support@checkr.com. Después de trabajar con Checkr para corregir cualquier inexactitud, comuníquese con nosotros con sus resultados.
Why can't you contact Checkr about my background check results for me?
¿Por qué no puede comunicarse con Checkr acerca de los resultados de mi verificación de antecedentes?
Due to the personal nature of background checks, we can’t discuss the details of your background check with you. Because of that, Checkr will only speak to you, or the person listed on your Thumbtack account. If you have concerns with your results, contact Checkr directly at support@checkr.com.
Debido a la información personal de las verificaciones de antecedentes, no podemos discutir los detalles de su verificación de antecedentes con usted. Por eso, Checkr solo hablará con usted o con la persona registrada en su cuenta de Thumbtack. Si tiene inquietudes con sus resultados, comuníquese con Checkr directamente enviando un correo electrónico a support@checkr.com
What if I don’t pass (the background check)?
¿Qué pasa si no me aprueban?
If your background check isn’t clear, your results may affect your eligibility to be on Thumbtack.
Our primary focus with background check results are convictions related to felonies, violent misdemeanors, and theft-related offenses. We look at this on a case-by-case basis and I wouldn’t be able to discuss specific results or hypotheticals about charges. We’ll review your results once we receive them.
  Si su verificación de antecedentes no es clara, sus resultados pueden afectar su elegibilidad para estar en Thumbtack.
Nuestro enfoque principal con los resultados de la verificación de antecedentes son las condenas relacionadas con delitos graves, delitos menores violentos y delitos relacionados con el robo. Analizamos estos resultados caso por caso y no podría discutir resultados específicos o hipotéticos sobre cargos. Revisaremos sus resultados una vez que los recibamos.
What if I already know there are convictions on my background check?
¿Qué pasa si ya sé que hay condenas en mi verificación de antecedentes?
You still have the option of taking a background check. We can't determine what action we'll take until we see your results.
Our primary focus with background check results are convictions related to felonies, violent misdemeanors, and theft-related offenses. We look at results on a case-by-case basis and I wouldn’t be able to discuss specific outcomes or hypotheticals about charges.
We’ll review your results once we receive them.
Aún tiene la opción de realizar una verificación de antecedentes. No podemos determinar qué acción tomaremos hasta que veamos sus resultados.
Nuestro enfoque principal con los resultados de la verificación de antecedentes son las condenas relacionadas con delitos graves, delitos menores violentos y delitos relacionados con el robo. Observamos los resultados caso por caso y no podría discutir resultados específicos o hipotéticos sobre cargos.
Revisaremos sus resultados una vez que los recibamos.

Availability: Business Hours, Calendar, and Hide a Business (Pro)

Contents
Overview
Updates
Hide my business UX experiment (July 14, 2026)

Customer timeline vs pro matching
Customer Timeline Options
Availability Flexibility Toggle
Handling Mismatches & Refunds
Why a pro may receive leads that conflict with their calendar
Availability Requirements
Business hours

Lead times

Process

Thumbtack calendar and blocking time off
What "Hide my business" mean and when to use it
Resources
1. Overview
It’s important for pros to share when they’re available so they appear in relevant customer searches. A pros availability applies to all jobs. Pros can update their availability (and block out specific days) any time.
Pros have multiple tools to manage their Thumbtack availability, which include: 
Business hours: Pros' business hours let customers know when they’re typically available. Pros may still receive messages outside these times. 
Calendar: Although using the calendar is optional, pros can use it to block off days (e.g., one-time events, a vacation or a booked project) so they don’t show up in customers' search results for those days. 
Lead time: Pros can control how much notice they need before a job and how far in advance customers can send job requests. 
Hide my business: Pros can temporarily hide their business (for up to 30 days) when unavailable, like on vacation.
Business hours and calendar settings are set at the business profile level. This means:
Settings are distinct per profile: If a pro manages multiple business profiles, they must set up and update the availability for each one individually.
Applies to all categories within a profile: If a pro offers four different service categories (e.g., Plumbing, HVAC, Electrical, and Roofing) under one business profile, these business hours and calendar settings apply to all four categories simultaneously.
Updates

Hide my business UX experiment 

Starting July 14, 2026 Thumbtack will run an experiment that improves the "Hide My Business" feature by making it easier for pros to temporarily step away from Thumbtack. 
Experiment details:
Launch date: July 14, 2026
End date: TBD
Priority: P2 — low impact and medium priority
Key changes in this experiment experience include: 
New entry points to make Hide My Business easier to find: 
Hide my business option added on Services page below Manage lead prices (replacing the buried three-dot overflow menu)
Hide my business option added on Settings page under Tools. 
Status: When a pro has their business hidden they will see: 
Your business is hidden status banner on the Jobs tab with a “Manage date” button.  
A “Until X/X/XX” pill with the date their business goes live next to the two new entry points.
Adjustable end date: Pros can edit their end date while their business is hidden. 
All other Hide My Business settings and functions remain unchanged (e,g., can’t schedule a future start date, 30 day max hide window, when and how a pro is hidden or goes live). 
▶ What the entry points and banner looks like
Services page
Settings page
For you page

[Image: rtaImage]


[Image: rtaImage]

How pros hide their business or edit timeframe
When pros hide their business (or edit timeframe), they will select an end date as usual. In the experiment, the start date will always be today and will show the hidden window timeframe and number of days below the calendar. The “confirm” (or update) button will be blocked if they select a date that isn’t today or is more than 30 days.  
▶ Hide business

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

▶ Edit dates while hidden

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

▶ Talking points
For more talking points, see What "Hide my business" mean and when to use it below. 
Where do I find Hide My Business?
You can find it in a few places: on the Services tab and in your Settings under Tools. Click "Hide My Business" to get started. If your business is already hidden, you’ll also have a banner on your Jobs tab. 
How long can I hide my business?
You can choose your end date — anywhere from today up to 30 days out. Your business will be hidden immediately when you confirm, and you'll be automatically reactivated on the end date you pick. You'll get a reminder notification about 1 day before your business goes live again. You can also adjust your end date at any time while hidden — shorten it to come back sooner, or extend it, up to 30 days from when you first hid your business.


Matching: How pros availability impacts customer searchs
To help pros maximize their visibility and understand the leads they receive, it is important to explain how customer selections in search results and request forms impact which pros appear. Customers specify their availability at two key points: 
▶ during their initial search ("What's your timeline?")[Image: rtaImage]…
▶ on the request form ("When do you need this job to start?").[Image: rtaImage]
Customer timeline vs pro matching
This table illustrates how pros are filtered in search results and what the project details page displays based on the customer's selected timeline.

Customer timeline in search and request form
How search results are filtered (pro availability)
Pro matching logic
What the Project Details Page Shows
“Within 48 hours”
Does filter search results to pros available on the next 3 days.
Pros are only matched to jobs if they are available on the selected dates.*
The actual dates that map to the next 3 days (e.g., Jul 1-3).
“Within a week”
Does filter search results to pros available on the next 7 days.
Pros are only matched to jobs if they are available on the selected dates.*
The actual dates that map to the next 7 days (e.g., Jul 1-7).
– “Flexible on timeline” (search results) 
“I haven’t decided yet” (request form)
– Further out (request form only)
Does not filter search results based on pro availability.
Pros can still match even if the date(s) is blocked.
“Flexible on timeline.”
Specific dates 
(Customer can selects up to 7 dates)
Does filters search results to pros available on the exact dates selected.
Pros are only matched to jobs if they are available on the selected dates. *
The exact dates the customer selected (E.g., July 18-19, 21). 
*Flexibility toggle: I can work with the pro’s schedule if they aren’t available at the time I chose.* (request form only)
n/a
Pros can still match even if the date(s) is blocked.
“Open to other dates.” 
* This only applies IF the flexible toggle is turned off. If it’s on, pros are not filtered out based on their availability. 
Customer Timeline Options

Customers choose a general timeline for their project rather than a specific time of day. 
If the customer is firm (specific dates): Search results are filtered to only show pros available at those times.
If the customer is flexible: If they select "Flexible on timeline" or "I haven’t decided yet," the search results are not filtered by the pro’s calendar.
Availability Flexibility Toggle
▶ The request form includes a toggle labeled “I can work with the pro’s schedule if they aren’t available in the time I chose”.

[Image: rtaImage]

Default Setting: This toggle is ON by default. Customers can turn this off if their selected dates are firm and not flexible.
Filtering: When this toggle is on, search results are not filtered by pro availability, and pros will not be "matched" based on their calendar or business hours ‘closed’ days.
Toggle on: 
With the flexibility toggle on, the pro’s unavailable dates do not apply. This means a pro may still receive a lead for a blocked date. 
Toggle off:
With the flexibility toggle off, a pro may still receive a lead for a blocked date if:
The customer selects “I haven’t decided yet” or “further out”.
The customer selected multiple dates . The pro only needs to be available for one of those dates to receive the lead.
If a pro wants to stop receiving all leads (including flexible ones) for a specific period, they must use the "Hide my business" feature.
Other flexible preferences in request forms

Customers may also select flexible answers for other project details (e.g., "I'm flexible" or "I'm not sure").
Pros cannot adjust these flexible options in their targeting preferences.
Reps should encourage pros to engage with these customers. Since the customer is "flexible," they are often open to the pro’s professional recommendations.
Internal Reference: Reps can see the Flexible Answer Options on Request Form (Customer) (Pro) KAs to learn more. 
Handling Mismatches & Refunds
If a pro receives a lead for a date they are unavailable, they should: 
First try to offer alternative dates or solutions to the customer.
If a mutual time cannot be found, the pro may be eligible for a refund. Pros can submit a refund request by following the steps in the ​​How to request a refund – Thumbtack Help article. 
Internal Reference: Reps can see the Lead Refunds (Pro) KAs to learn more. 
Why a pro may receive leads that conflict with their calendar 
This table quickly explains why a pro might still get a lead even if their calendar seems to conflict with the flexible time options the customer chose.

If the pro is...
Will they see the lead?
Unavailable for part of a multi-day request (Specific date)
Yes (If they are free for at least one requested slot).
Blocked on a specific date, but customer is "Flexible"
Yes (The toggle allows pros to suggest new dates).
Hiding their business
No (This is the only way to stop flexible leads).
Availability requirements

To ensure a high-quality experience for customers and to maximize lead potential for pros, Thumbtack requires all business profiles to meet minimum availability standards. These requirements also prevent pros from setting up their availability in ways that don't allow them to receive leads. These rules also determine when "blue dots" appear on the pro's calendar.
These requirements include both business hours (Mon-Sun hours) and lead times. 
Business hours: Pros must have a minimum of 12 hours of total availability per week to appear in search results and receive leads. 
Calculation: This is calculated only by business hours. It does not include any day(s) a pro has blocked off on their calendar. E.g., If a pro is available for 3 hours each day, Monday - Friday, they have 15 hours of availability. 
Validation Error: If a pro attempts to save "Defined specific business hours" that result in less than 12 hours of availability, the system will display the following error and prevent saving: "At least 12 hours of availability is required for your business to show up in search results."
Lead times: The system is designed to automatically enforce availability requirements by only offering compliant options in the settings. 
Maximum Advance Notice: Pros cannot require more than 7 days of notice before a job begins.
Minimum Job Request Window: Customers must be able to schedule a pro at least 14 days into the future. 
Business hours
Business hours are where pros set their weekly work schedule. Business hours are set at the business profile level rather than by individual service category. This means:
Pros with multiple business profiles must manage the hours for each one separately.
If a profile contains multiple service categories, the business hours apply to all of them simultaneously.
Pros have two options for their business hour settings:
Use any open day or time (Default): New profiles are set to this by default to ensure pros immediately meet availability requirements to show up in search results and receive leads.
Under this setting, business hours will not be displayed on the pro's profile.
Pros will be eligible for leads at any time they are not otherwise blocked on their calendar.
Define specific business hours:  Pros can set specific hours for each day of the week to let customers know when they are typically available (e.g., Mon-Fri, 9 am–5 pm).
Closing specific days: To indicate they are closed on a specific day or days (recurring), pros can uncheck the box next to that day. This will stop the pro from receiving leads for that day every week.
Once defined, these hours will be visible on the pro's profile.
Note: If a pro manually changes their specific hours to "Use any open day or time,” the hours will again be hidden from the profile view.
▶ What the business hour settings looks like on the Android app

[Image: rtaImage]

Availability requirements for business hours
To show up in search results, a pro's business hour settings must reflect at least 12 hours of availability per week. If a pro attempts to save "Defined specific business hours" that total less than 12 hours of availability, they will see a warning. They will be unable to save their changes until their hours and lead times meet the minimum requirement.
▶ Warning pros see when setting less than 12 hours of availability

[Image: rtaImage]

Important Reminders:
Customer Messaging: Regardless of the setting or the hours displayed, customers can still message pros at any time.
Search Eligibility: Because the system defaults to "Use any open day or time," new pros are automatically eligible for search results without needing to manually define a schedule.
Lead Time

Lead time settings are governed by the availability requirements which also control how pros appear in search.
The system ensures lead time settings remain compliant by only showing valid options. Although the interface restricts choices to those that meet requirements, pros can still adjust their preferences within these approved ranges. Lead time can be adjusted at any time in a pros business hours settings. 
A pro’s lead time includes: 
“How much notice do you need to do a job?”
Options: Same day, or 1 to 7 days 
By default, this is set to “1 day” 
Same day is the least amount of notice the pro can choose. Pros can choose ‘same day’ if they are open to accepting jobs anytime during the current day.
By selecting one to seven days notice (or same day), pros decide how quickly they can be scheduled for. 
“How far in advance can customers send job requests?”
By default, this is set to “24 months”
Pros can set this by days, weeks, or months. Options include: 
Days: 14 days (minimum) up to 30 days or No Limit.
Weeks: 2 weeks (minimum) up to 30 weeks or No Limit.
Months: 1 month (minimum) up to 30 months or No Limit.
Time zone: Ensure the time zone is set correctly to align with the pros local time. 
▶ What the lead time settings looks like on the Android app

[Image: rtaImage]

Thumbtack calendar
Using the Thumbtack calendar is optional, but it's a key tool for pros to manage their specific availability. Pros can use it to block off specific dates. This will update their availability (overrides their business hours), but pros may still receive requests with flexible timing.  
The calendar is set at a business profile level which means if a pro has one profile with three service categories, the calendar and business hours apply to all three services. If a pro has multiple business profiles, the pro will need to set up their availability individually per business profile. 
Navigating the Thumbtack calendar
Reps should understand that pros see their calendar in two main parts: 
A "Monthly Calendar" view: This gives a high-level overview, showing blue dots on generally available days.
A "Day-by-Day View": This shows a detailed list of business hours and any specific "blocked time".
▶ See what the two main calendar parts look like:

[Image: rtaImage]

 
Monthly Calendar view
The monthly calendar provides a high-level overview of a pro's availability for the entire month.
Blue dot: The day is eligible to receive new leads for that day. This means it meets both conditions: 
All Availability Requirements (e.g., X days notice, up to X months out) AND
The pro has open business hours defined for that day. (e.g., "9am - 5pm").
Note: A pro may still receive leads for a different day even if the current day is blocked or outside business hours.
Date with black strikethrough: The pro is blocked from matching with new leads (or showing in search results) for any of the following reasons:
The pro has manually blocked off a range of dates themselves 
The pro's business hours are set to "Closed" for that day.
▶ What the calendar looks like on the Android app

[Image: rtaImage]

NOTE: A day with both defined business hours and a manual block will display both the blue dot and the black strikethrough. If a day has defined business hours but is also manually blocked, it will show both the blue dot and the black strikethrough. (E.g., In the screenshot above, a pro has Friday business hours set to 10 am - 1 pm but has also manually blocked off Friday, April 3rd for an HVAC job in SLC).
Day-by-Day View (List View)
This day to day view of a pros calendar shows specific availability and manual blocks for each day.
Gray block (specific unavailability): The pro has manually blocked off their calendar to show as unavailable. This overrides their business hours.
▶ What the day to day calendar looks like to the Android app

[Image: rtaImage]


Block off dates in calendar

Pros will see a blue "Block time" button, this is an action button. The time is currently open, and the pro can click this to block off specific days or times. The “Blocked time” button will be gray when the day is in the past, meaning the pro cannot block time off. 

When a pro clicks the “Block time” button, they will be taken to the "When are you busy?" screen. Here they can enter:

Title (optional): To name the blocked event.
Details (optional): For any helpful notes.
All day: A toggle if the block is for the full day.
Start / End: The specific dates and times to mark as unavailable.
Block date as unavailable

To block off dates, pros will select the blue "Block time" button or by clicking “Block time” on the specific day they want to block. They are taken to the When are you unavailable? page. This page explains that pros can mark days when they're unavailable and they won't receive job requests on those days, but may still receive messages from customers. Pros will fill out when they are unavailable, including: 

Title (optional): To name the blocked event.
Details (optional): For any helpful notes.
Start / End: The specific date range to mark as unavailable. 

To save, the pro will click “Mark as unavailable.” 
▶ What the “When are you unavailable” screen looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Remove (or update) blocked date
 To remove or change a block:
On Web: Pros can click the gray block and have the option to "Edit" (which lets them change the days of that blocked time) or "Unblock this time."
On App: Pros can click the gray block, but the only option is to "Unblock this time." They cannot edit an existing block on the app. If a pro blocks a range of multiple days at the same time, unblocking any single day within that range will unblock all the days in the original block.
NOTE: Pros can only block future days off. The “Block time” in the weekly view will be grayed out for days in the past.
▶ What it looks like on the app to unblock time

[Image: rtaImage]
[Image: rtaImage]

Calendar integrations [NOT SUPPORTED] 
The Thumbtack calendar is optional for pros to use and requires manual updates for availability. This means the Thumbtack calendar does not automatically reflect new bookings or changes in job status from external sources.
Integrations: While pros can connect third-party integrations for features like leads and messaging, availability integration is not supported.
Hide my business
The hide my business feature gives pros a way to pause leads without worrying about maintaining their rank in search results.
[Internal Thumbtack info:  Frontline reps may hear this referred to as “vacation mode” internally. When talking about this feature with pros, reps should only refer to it as “hide my business.”]
▶ In-product view of hiding your business

[Image: AD_4nXc-jRo5n87TVEsArRscMZZaK0eNEHoHHHGx6IPUuV6jeaBnk2dndfNzBMSq1uvWnqZa-R-AtkW34sMH5ueUDpnVlfy8Y4KKtEDVb7LL9SfhTG8G75zwGGcyKznQcxStu6cGMfteSA]

Hide a business 
Pros can hide one or more businesses at a time for up to 30 days at a time. 
Pros will select to hide their business from the services page. They will select an end date and click “Hide business now” to save. The pro’s business will be hidden immediately when they click “Hide my business now” and will reappear in search results at 8 am local time on the date they choose.
