About the Agent Pro List Tool
Adding pros and uploading files
Sharing list and client access
Resources
1. Overview
The Agent Pro List Tool, launched by Thumbtack on April 21, 2025, is a free resource designed for vetted real estate agents. This tool allows agents to cultivate and share a personalized list of trusted home service pros with their clients, fostering client trust and loyalty. Agents can include their own contact information on this list.
Agents are not restricted to Thumbtack pros and can easily upload existing lists using various file formats or manually input pro details. Once signed up, vetted real estate agents can add pros to their list and share it with clients via a unique link or QR code, providing clients with easy access to the curated list.

[Image: rtaImage]

Important note to frontline reps: 
Throughout this article, “agent” specifically means a real estate agent using the Agent Pro List tool, and “client” refers to the real estate agent's client, regardless of whether they are a Thumbtack customer or not.
Benefits: 
For Real Estate Agents: This tool helps agents guide and educate their clients while staying top-of-mind for current and future business.  
For Homeowners (clients): The tool provides a list of trusted pros, offering guidance during the home buying process.
How to identify Real Estate Agent using the tool 
Frontline reps can check Admin to see if a Real Estate Agent is sign up to use the tool by following these steps: 
Look for the ‘Real Estate Agent Section’ in Admin. 
If the agent has signed up, the section will appear expanded.
▶ Admin view: Agent has signed up ("Real Estate Agent Section" in Admin is expanded):

▶ Admin view: Agent has not signed up ("Real Estate Agent Section" in Admin is collapsed):

How Real Estate Agents use the Agent Pro List Tool
Real Estate Agents can access the Agent Pro List tool by signing up on the Agent Pro List landing page.
Once signed up, agents can:
Add pros either by manual entry or by uploading a file (which can be a PDF, spreadsheet, or image).
Customize their personal page with their information.
Share their finalized pro list with clients using a unique link, a QR code, or a Canva template.
▶ What the Agent Pro List Tool looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

How Clients of the Agent use the tool  
Clients of the Real Estate Agent can utilize the Agent Pro List tool to:
Access the agent's curated list of pros through a shared link.
Contact the recommended pros directly from the list.
Search Thumbtack for additional service providers.
2. Process
(Rep) Steps: How to help agents sign up for the Agent Pro List tool (Rep) 
This section outlines the steps Frontline Reps should take to guide real estate agents in using the Agent Pro List tool.
Sign-Up: Direct agents to the Agent Pro List landing page.
Build Pro Team (Add Pros): After signing up, they will be prompted to either manually input each of their pro’s contact information or upload a document file.
Manual Input: Agents can manually input the contact information for each of their trusted pros.
File Upload: Agents can upload a document file containing their existing list, and the information will be uploaded for them, free of charge.
Accepted File Types for Upload: 
Documents: PDF, DOC/DOCX, PAGES, TXT, RTF
Spreadsheets: XLS/XLSX, NUMBERS, CSV
Images: JPG, JPEG, PNG, WEBP, HEIC/HEIF
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Personalize Page (Add Agent Info): The agent can customize their personal page to ensure they are the primary point of contact. 
Profile photo
Brokerage 
Team name
Real Estate License number
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Share the Finalized List: Once setup is complete, the agent will be provided with three primary assets to share their list:
A unique link.
A QR code.
A Canva template.
The unique link can be used to share the list directly with clients, or it can be copied and used on sales collateral, in email signatures, or on LinkedIn.
(Note: Agents can log back in at any time to edit, delete, or add new pros to their list after initial setup).
(Rep) Steps: How to help agents having issues accessing the tool (Rep)
This section outlines the steps Frontline Reps should take to troubleshoot common issues with the Agent Pro List tool. 
If an agent is having trouble accessing the tool, frontline reps will follow these steps: 
Check for the ‘Real Estate Agent Section’ in Admin.
If this section is automatically expanded, they have signed up for the tool. 
If this section is automatically collapsed, they have not signed up. 
3. Talking points
About the Agent Pro List Tool
Who is this available to?
Agents are vetted through the Thumbtack team and have gone through an onboarding process in order to access the Agent Pro List. 
Is Agent Pro List free?
Yes, Agent Pro List is 100% free and was developed with real estate agents in mind to help you grow your business.
Where is the Agent List available?
This is only available on dWeb and mWeb. Native apps are not currently supported.
Is my agent pro list a lead generation tool?
Agent Pro List is primarily a tool for creating lasting relationships with your current clients, rather than direct lead generation. When you share your pro list with clients, you help them solve their immediate home project needs with pros you trust. Plus, every time they look at your pro list, your agent info will be front and center. If your clients share your pro list with their friends and family, your agent info will also be shared, potentially expanding your network.
Adding pros and uploading files 
How do I add pros to my profile?
You’ll be prompted after signing up to either manually input each of your pro’s contact info or you can upload a PDF, image or other document file and we’ll upload them for you — free of charge.
What file types are allowed in the pro list upload?
Documents:
.pdf
.doc / .docx
.pages
.txt
.rtf
Spreadsheets:
.xls / .xlsx
.numbers
.csv
Images:
.jpg, .jpeg
.png
.webp
.heic / .heif
Can I edit my list after I’ve signed up?
Yes, once you've created your account you can log back in at any time to edit or delete your existing pros, and add new ones.
Sharing list and client access
Will my clients have access to Thumbtack pros?
Yes, they will have the option to search for additional pros on Thumbtack.
How can I share my list?
Once you’ve added all of your pros to your list and complete your account setup, you’ll be given a unique link that can be shared directly with your clients or copied and used on sales collateral, LinkedIn, email signature, etc.
Will my service professionals be added to Thumbtack for anyone to find?
No, your pros will not be uploaded to Thumbtack. When you add pros, their contact details appear on your pro list for anyone who has the link to your list.

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article serves as a comprehensive guide to the Thumbtack Admin Portal for Frontline Reps. It details how to access and navigate the Admin tool, covering key updates, important terminology, and search functionalities. The article also provides a breakdown of Pro and Customer Admin pages, outlining sections like account details, services, requests, quotes, and reviews.
The Thumbtack employee interface—commonly referred to as Admin, the Admin Portal, or Admin 2.0—is the primary tool for managing pro and customer accounts.
NOTE: Admin 2.0 is the updated version of the Thumbtack Admin tool that has replaced Legacy Admin. This KA is currently being updated to align with Admin 2.0; sections will be refreshed as more pages are migrated. For support with Admin 2.0, visit the #admin Slack channel.
Note on targeting terminology: You may see "Targeting" and "Job preferences" terms used interchangeably throughout our internal KA resources or in-product.
Usage & Privacy Guidelines
Access to Admin is a privilege that provides entry to sensitive user and employee data. To ensure security and compliance, all Frontline Reps must adhere to these standards:
Tacknet: In order to connect to Admin, you must be connected to Tacknet  (Thumbtack’s VPN) Thumbtack computers should be automatically connected to VPN. See Page: TackNet (VPN) at Thumbtack to learn more. 
Need-to-Know Basis: Only access the specific data required for your current task. Avoid viewing highly sensitive information unless necessary.
No Data Storage: Never store sensitive Thumbtack data on personal or shared drives (e.g., Google Drive, Dropbox, or local laptop files).
System Integrity: Do not attempt to circumvent system protections or security protocols.
Professional Use: Thumbtack data and tools are company property and must only be used to do necessary tasks as outlined in company policy and relevant internal KAs. 
Impersonation & Sensitive Data
Admin allows reps to impersonate a pro or customer to troubleshoot or complete actions on their behalf.
For guidelines on making account changes while impersonating, refer to the internal Making Account Changes on Behalf of Pro or Customer (Impersonation Guidelines) (Rep) KA
For details on handling sensitive account information, refer to the internal Sensitive Account Information KA. 
What pages of Admin this KA covers
This KA does not cover all Admin pages. It focuses on the three primary pages of Admin 2.0. Each page has been updated to provide more granular detail for reps:

Page
Description 
User Admin
Focuses on individual account details, including profile info, user status, credits, payment history, and login logs.
Businesses (fka. Services) Admin
Focuses on business-specific data, such as licensing, service categories, availability rules, and business verification.
Negotiations (fka. Bids or quotes) Admin
Manages the lifecycle of a lead (formerly quotes/bids). Includes project details, interaction logs, scheduling, and marketplace payments.
Legacy to Cobalt Messenger (May 2024)

All Frontline Reps have been switched from the Legacy version of the Thumbtack messenger (when logged in as a user) to the cobalt-powered version. To learn more, Frontline Reps can see the internal Cobalt Messenger Dogfooding Guide.
If there are any issues with the Cobalt messenger, Frontline Reps can report it in two ways:
Fill out the Cobalt messenger bug report form. For steps, see How to report messenger issues.
Submit a report using the Slack channel #cobalt-messenger-feedback.

Internal Note: Frontline reps should not use the internal term “legacy” or “cobalt” when speaking with pros or customers.

2. Process
For Frontline Reps, this section outlines the essential processes for effectively utilizing the Admin tool. It details how to access the Admin portal, the various search functionalities available within Admin, and guidelines for impersonating users when necessary.
Steps: How to access Admin (Rep)
Frontline reps can access Admin by following these steps:
▶ Connect to Tacknet (Thumbtacks VPN).To connect to Thumbtack Admin, Frontline Reps must be connected to Taacknet For help connecting to VPN, refer to the Page: TackNet (VPN) at Thumbtack. Thumbtack computers should be automatically connected to VPN. 
Go to https://admin.thumbtack.io/auth/signin
Sign in with Okta.
Follow the prompts to log in.
Another way to get to the Admin portal is through the links provided in Salesforce. These links usually redirect Frontline reps to customer, pro, request, and quote pages.
Steps: How to search in Admin (Rep) 
Once logged into Admin and on the "Users" page (https://admin.thumbtack.io/users), reps will see the "Models" column on the left side below the "Recently viewed" section. The Models section has the following options: Users, Businesses, Projects, and Negotiations.

3. User Admin
The "User Admin" section (https://admin.thumbtack.io/users/) provides a comprehensive overview of user accounts, encompassing both pros and customers. It details profile information, available actions (such as account status changes and payment management), and various account details including contact preferences, verification statuses, and membership information. This section serves as a central hub for managing and understanding individual user data within the Admin tool.

Profile
The Profile provides identifying information about the pro. 
The following image shows a screenshot of the Profile section in a user’s Admin page.

[Image: AD_4nXfjZN8kR_ORw8gbXVMld2bAsnvNsaZgtVf94zBFF0wBV5k1ejvA09QkwdOZAd2lBoZAeTfbUmM0BMfixrJAVznguzfLqe7vAKsDowJIEs-88lbr0uFMyye_qu5n0n82rd7udwbscQ]

Frontline reps can use the following list to understand the different sections within the Profile section of the user’s Admin page:
Profile photo: The image the pro or customer uploaded as their profile photo in their Thumbtack account.
Name: Found in large, bold letters at the top of the page. This is the account owner’s name.
PK ID: Primary Key (for database management purposes) serves the same function as the customer ID
Legacy ID: No longer relevant in Thumbtack’s tools, kept for legacy software. Unique identifier consistent regardless of changes on account.
Account status: Shows the status of the pro or customer’s account (e.g. enabled, disabled, ghosted, or account hold).
Pro and/or Customer pill: Pro pill for pros and customer pill for customers. If the user is both, this pill will say “Both Pro & Customer.”
Log in as user: This action allows the Frontline rep to log into the user’s account to view and make changes in the account (as if the Frontline rep is the pro or customer). See the internal Impersonation Guidelines KA to learn more.
Actions
When a user (customer or pro) needs to be 'actioned,' Frontline Reps can access the user through the Actions menu at the right-hand side of the user’s Admin. (See what it looks like below.)
▶ What it looks like

[Image: rtaImage]


[Image: rtaImage]
Basic

Create new user: Frontline reps should refrain from using this action. See the internal Impersonation Guidelines KA for more information.
Edit user: This is where specified teams (specifically ID Help) may make adjustments to the pro’s details. Frontline reps should refrain from making any changes here.
Add service: This action leads to Thumbtack.com/pro which is a URL Frontline Reps can share with a pro who wants to sign up for a new Thumbtack account or add a new service if they already have an account.
Reset password: This action allows Frontline Reps to help pros reset their password by sending a password reset email to the email address on file in the pro’s account.

[Image: rtaImage]
Account status

Admin Delete: This action allows Frontline Reps to delete the pro’s account upon pro's request. Used by all teams.
Admin Ghost: This action is used only by the Trust & Safety team for when a pro needs to be ghosted.
Admin Undelete: This action allows Frontline Reps to undelete the users account upon request and account being in good standing. Used by all teams.
Admin Unghost:  This action is used only by the Trust & Safety team for when a pro needs to be unghosted.
Add Pro Account Hold: This action is used only by the Trust & Safety team when adding a pro account hold.
Remove Pro Account Hold: This action is used only by the Trust & Safety team when moving a pro account hold.
Add Customer Account Hold: This action is used only by the Trust & Safety team when adding a customer account hold.
Remove Customer Account Hold: This action is used only by the Trust & Safety team when removing a customer account hold.
Deletion and Ghost Logs: Frontline reps from all teams can view this to see why an account was removed or ghosted to better help the pro.
Pro Account Hold Logs: Frontline reps from all teams can view this to see why an account is on hold to better help the pro.
Customer Account Hold Logs: Frontline reps from all teams can view this to see why an account is on hold to better help the pro.

[Image: rtaImage]
Payments

Payout Getaway Account Details: This option shows the details of the pro’s payout information they connected for Thumbtack payments through Stripe. Frontline Reps can see details such as the pro’s business account, individual information, and which bank they’re with.
▶ Pro-Payment Summary: This action shows a summary of the pros’ balance, paid balance, promo balance, and total amount purchased on Thumbtack. Below that, below Journal Entries, Frontline Reps can view the details of each individual payment a pro has made, including the ID link to that negotiation, type of charge or refund it was, the dollar amount, and date of payment
For steps on processing refunds for prepaid packages or preloaded balances, including how to access the Prepaid Package List page, Frontline Reps should refer to the internal Prepaid Package Refunds (Pro)  KA.
Promotional Credits: This action allows Frontline Reps to grant the pro courtesy credit. Reps will fill out a credit amount in dollars, the reason for the courtesy credit, and any additional notes. Additional Admin actions on this page can be used to revoke credit and view credit logs (on Legacy Admin). 
View Payout Eligibility: This action shows if the pro is eligible for payouts on Thumbtack, if the pro has opted out of payouts, why a pro may be ineligible for payouts, and any payout method cooldowns. This is where Frontline Reps can opt a pro out of payouts if the pro specifically requests it and override a payout cooldown. Frontline Reps can see the internal Instant Deposits (Pro) KA to learn more.
Refund Requests: This action allows Frontline Reps to view instances where a pro has requested a refund on a negotiation (quote or contact) they paid for. Reps can see details like the refund status, the problem, the decision, the amount, and more. Frontline reps can refer to the internal Lead Refunds (Pro)  KA to learn more.
Marketplace: Earnings History: Goes to the Legacy Admin to view a Transfer/Payout Log that isn’t functional anymore. Frontline Reps will want to use the credits section of Admin to find payments for pros instead.

[Image: rtaImage]
Trust & Safety

The options found in the Trust & Safety section of the Actions menu are used only by the Trust & Safety team.

[Image: rtaImage]
Events

The options found in this Events section of the Actions menu are used for specific teams only. Frontline Reps won’t need to use this option and should refrain from clicking it.
Details
For Frontline Reps, the "Details" section offers a comprehensive overview of a user's account information in Admin, including contact preferences, account status, and eligibility for various Thumbtack programs.
The following image shows a screenshot of the Details section in a user’s Admin page.

[Image: AD_4nXd6Ba930TVzuhKFDA_NhoM6LSMfExS-o6okN_kt8UTqICYnoyH10AI351aXT_1YYthB-uocZJuxA3V-oqC3wCZaKwO1mPyJKs60au4hyFcKyMW5COp70u251jFCz8VFve0gtV4HSg]

Frontline reps can use the following list to understand the information found within the Details section of the pro’s Admin page:
Email: Email address on file, this is where all email notifications must go. Must be unique (no email can be associated with multiple accounts). If the pro has unsubscribed to Thumbtack’s emails, an option to Re-subscribe will be present. Frontline Reps can see the internal Notifications (Pro) KA under “(Rep) Steps: How to help a pro when emails aren't being sent”  to learn more.
Privileges: For specific teams only. Frontline Reps don’t use these Privileges.
Proofreading portal permissions: For specific teams only. Frontline Reps don’t use these permissions.
Time zone: The pro’s timezone based on their address in their account.
Signed up: When the pro first signed up on Thumbtack and created their account.
Signup source: The method through which the user signed up for Thumbtack.
Contact preferences: This shows the type of notification preferences that the pro is set up to receive. Frontline Reps can see the internal Notifications (Pro) KA to learn more about adjusting notification preferences.
Identity status: Shows whether Thumbtack was able to verify the pro’s identity or not.
Pro Account hold flags: Indicates if the pro has a hold on their account. Frontline Reps can see the internal Account Holds (Pro) KA for more information.
Customer Account hold flags: Indicates if the customer has a hold on their account. Frontline Reps can see the internal Account Holds (Customer) KA for more information.
Banned status: Shows if the pro is blocklisted or not blocklisted. Frontline Reps can see the internal Removed or Banned Users (Pro) (Customers) KA for more information.
Referral program: If the pro is eligible for Thumbtack’s referral program or not. This shows if the pro has been banned from receiving incentive credits.
Instant Deposits Eligibility: This shows if the pro has met the requirements and is eligible for instant deposits not. Frontline Reps can see the internal Instant Deposits (Pro) KA for more information.
Terms accepted: When the pro accepted Thumbtack’s terms of use.
Num free contacts: The number of free contacts this pro has received.
Pro loyalty Member Status: This is a quick way for Frontline Reps to see where the pro is at with their Thumbtack Pro Rewards status. See the internal Thumbtack Pro Rewards (Pro) KA for more information.
Silver, Gold, or Platinum: This reflects the pro's current Pro Reward status.
Not a member: This means the pro hasn't started receiving leads yet.
Member: This means the pro has begun receiving leads but they haven’t hit the minimum tier for Silver yet.
Has Active Top Pro Badge: True indicates that the pro currently has a Top Pro badge, false indicates the pro doesn’t have the badge.
Membership Status: Shows if the pro has subscribed to Thumbtack’s Plus membership as a customer. Frontline Reps can see the internal Thumbtack Plus Membership (Customer) KA for more information.
Membership Creation Date: When the customer signed up for Thumbtack’s Plus membership.
Membership Renewal Date: When the customer’s Thumbtack Plus Membership subscription renews.
Real Estate Agent Section
This section is used to identify if a real estate agent has signed up (enrolled) for the Agent Pro List tool and their enrollment status This information helps Frontline Reps guide real estate agents and troubleshoot any access issues they might encounter with the Agent Pro List tool.
If the section appears expanded, the agent has successfully signed up for the tool.
If the section appears collapsed, the agent has not yet signed up.
Frontline reps can refer to the internal Agent Pro List Tool for Real Estate Agents KA to learn more. 
Pro Statuses
This section shows whether a pro is banned from Pro Referral Incentives and if there are any sales gating. Frontline Reps should not make any adjustments to this section. Reps can refer to the internal Referral Program (Pro) KA to learn more.
Banned from Pro Referral Incentives? > Box is checked if user has been banned

Pro Rewards History 
This section in Admin provides a historical view of a pro’s points, tiers, and badges. It can be used to resolve disputes regarding past performance. The data refreshes every ~8 hours. 
Tier Requirements Table: A reference for the specific point and service goals required for Silver, Gold, and Platinum.
Status History Table: Shows the specific tier reached for every quarter.
Period: Rewards quarter [e.g., Q3 (Jun 2026 - Aug 2026)
Status: 
Platinum
Gold
Silver
Member 
Record Created 
Point History Table: Displays total points earned per quarter and awards given.
Period: Rewards quarter [e.g., Q3 (Jun 2026 - Aug 2026)
Total points: Total points earned per quarter 
Awards: Awards given.
Show: Expandable view to see a line-by-item breakdown. [e.g., Bid: 76 (7,600 pts)]
Shows the Point Type (e.g., Integration, Bid), the Point Value, and the Date issued.
Customer accounts will show Pro Rewards History (no data)
Reps can refer to the internal Thumbtack Pro Rewards (Pro) KA to learn more.
Credits
The Credits section provides Frontline Reps with insights into:
Total spend: The total amount a pro has spent on Thumbtack so far.
Thumbtack balance: The pro’s current Thumbtack balance.
Charge status: If the pro has experienced any payment error.
In batch payment: If the pro is eligible for in batch payments (spent over $1,000 on Thumbtack and no history of payment failures). 
Balance Refill: If the pro has auto refill turned on for preloading their balance.
Reps can refer to the internal Payment Methods (Pro) KA to learn more about a pro’s Thumbtack balance, charge status, and in batch payments.
Note: The “Grant Prepaid Credit” is for the Sales team only and is not used by Frontline reps. The “Is Manually Invoiced” feature is also not used by Frontline reps.
App Test Data
This section isn’t used by Frontline reps.
Custom Push Notifications
This section isn’t used by Frontline reps.
Customer Contact Details
This shows when the pro accepted the customer contact payment terms (when the pro went from the Pay-Per-Quote model to being charged under the Pay-Per-Contact model). Frontline Reps should not adjust anything in this section.
Customer Contacts
Customer contacts are not shown by default due to being slow to load the data. Frontline Reps can select the option to Click to load, and the User’s Admin page will reload with the Customer Contacts available to view when the section is selected again.
The following list explains the information found within the Customer contacts section of Admin:
Negotiation: Shows the service category and hyperlinks to the negotiation (quote or bid) page for more details.
Customer: First and last name of the customer. Click the link to view the customer’s admin page for more information on that customer.
Event type:
CUSTOMER_SENT_MESSAGE

PENDING_CHARGE_FOR_OPT_IN_CONTACT

Verifications
This section shows methods by which the pro’s identity has been verified, such as their email address, their license, social media, or by performing a background check. It will show if the pro has been badged for being verified and any other details associated with their verification. 
NOTE: Frontline Reps should not use the Trash icons under the Actions column or make any changes to this section.
Businesses / Services
This section lists all businesses owned by this pro. The following list explains the different columns in the table found in this section:
PK: The unique identification number for the pro’s business.
Business: Name of the pro’s business as it appears on their profile. Clicking the business name here will redirect to the pro’s Business Admin page for more details.
Location: The address which the business is located, indicated in the pro’s business profile.
Created date: The date and time of when the business profile was created on Thumbtack.
Status: Shows whether the pro’s business profile is currently active or has been deleted.
Review link: Redirects to the page to write a review for the pro. Reps can copy and share this URL with the pro so the pro can ask customers for reviews.
Actions:
[Image: rtaImage]The person icon: this action takes Frontline reps to view the pro’s customer-facing public profile (while impersonating them).
[Image: rtaImage]The pencil icon: this action takes Frontline reps to the pro’s internal profile (where the pro is able to make edits to the profile).
The “Clone business” icon: this action starts the process to create new, cloned business profiles from an existing profile. Reps refer to internal  "Clone a Business Profile in Admin" KA.
The “Delete business” icon: This action allows a rep to delete a business, such as the original "shell" profile after a successful clone. Reps refer to internal  "Clone a Business Profile in Admin" KA.
Discounts
This section shows Frontline Reps all incentives and free leads awarded to a pro after redemption. 
Once a pro claims an offer and is awarded with the incentive it appears here to track the actual usage of those leads. 
Incentive offers include: 
BOSUP Offers (See internal Budget Increase Incentive (BOSUP & SOBU) (Pro) KA)
Unlimited Budget Discounts (see internal Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro) KA) 
Incentives on recommendation cards (See internal Incentivized Recommendation Cards (Pro) KA)
NOTE: The BOSUP Discount Offers section of the Business Admin page shows the pro's progress toward earning a reward (e.g., maintaining their budget). There’s a Discounts table on the Business Admin page that is the same table as this Discounts table.
This table outlines the fields in the Discounts section:

Field
Description
Discount ID
The unique internal identifier for the specific lead grant or discount.
Business
The name of the pro's business where the discount applies.
Status
The current lifecycle state:
ACTIVE: (available for use),
DEPLETED (all leads used), or
EXPIRED (time limit for free lead redemption reached). 
Percentage off 
The discount rate applied to the lead price.
Free leads (total / redeemed)
A counter showing usage (for example, “5 / 2” means the pro was awarded 5 leads and has used 2 so far). 
Awarded
The timestamp indicating exactly when the free leads were added to the pro's account. 
Expires
The timestamp indicating when the remaining unused leads will be removed. 
Category PK restriction
Lists specific category IDs if the discount is restricted to certain services.
Recommendation type
The internal campaign or incentive type (for example BOSUP Offer, Unlimited Budget Discount, or Targeting Expansion).

Negotiations (fka Quotes/Bids)

Request category: The service category the request came from.
Requestor: The name of the customer who created the request. Click the link to view the customer’s admin page for more information on that customer.

Status

STATUS_PICKED: Pro is marked as hired.
STATUS_CANCELED: No Intent, project canceled, or quote declined.

Yes: instant match 
No: custom quoting
Syndication Type: When a customer contacts a pro directly (usually through search results), the lead is “syndicated” to the pro. Looking at the syndication type of a lead can tell Frontline Reps more information about how the customer found and contacted the pro.

Addresses
Pros can enter multiple addresses and set one as default. This section shows all addresses a pro has entered and which address is currently associated with each business profile. Under the “For Service” column, it shows which address is associated with which business profile. This table also shows whether the address was able to be verified or if it was a bad address (not able to be verified).

Phone numbers
Pros can enter multiple phone numbers and set one as default. This table shows the phone number entered in by the pro, which service profile it's associated with, whether the phone number has been selected as the default number, if the pro has SMS verified that phone number, and if the number was identity match verified. Frontline reps can see the internal Notifications (Pro) and Impersonation Guidelines to learn more.

Frontline Reps can learn more in the internal Account Information (Customer) KA in the “Phone number” section and also in the Impersonation Guidelines KA.
Licenses
Professional licenses or certificates this pro has, such as an electrician's certificate with the local standards organization. Frontline Reps can see the internal Licenses (Pro) KA for more information on licenses.

Referrals that have been made by this pro, referring other pros to Thumbtack. Frontline reps can use this field to troubleshoot missing referral bonuses. Frontline reps can refer to the Internal Referral Program (Pro) KA to learn more.

Requests currently in Jobs Feed
After a customer creates a contact, other pros can see the job details and reach out to that customer. This section displays project requests that are currently visible in a pro's Jobs Feed. These are also known as "Opportunities." This feed lists jobs fetched for all of the pro’s businesses within a 150-mile radius (unless the job is remote), sorted by newest first.
Important Notes:
If a pro quotes or passes on a job, it will no longer appear in this section.
In some cases, if nearly 200 jobs are available and the pro uses a sort order other than "newest first," some jobs visible to the pro might not appear here.

Request Type: The type of opportunity available.
Requester: The customer's name who created the request.
Viewed Status: Whether the pro has viewed the job yet.
Quotes Sent: If any quotes have been sent to the customer for this job.

Shows if the pro has completed activation onboarding. Reps can refer to the internal Understanding and Completing Activation Requirements (Pro) KA for more details. Frontline Reps should not use the waive option here.

Occupation Targeting
The Occupation Targeting section is used to see if a pro is eligible for the new pro deal experience and what their enrollment status is. Reps should refer to the New Deal for Pros: Personalized Preferences and Smarter Lead Matching (Pro) KA to learn more.

The "Experiment assignments (EAS deprecated)” has been officially deprecated and should not be updated anymore. Frontline Reps should see the “Experiment Assignments” section instead.
Experiment Assignments
The "Experiment assignments” log in Admin shows Frontline Reps which experiments a pro or customer is part of, and it provides other details about the experience. 
These are the columns in the Experiments log and what they mean:
Experiment:  This column shows the name of the experiment.
Bucket: This column indicates whether a user is impacted by the experiment or not.
"Baseline" or unassigned: The user is not part of the experiment.
Variant, Variant 1, or any other text: The user is impacted.
Participation time: This column only shows N/A and isn’t being used at this time.
Internal Only: Frontline Reps cannot opt users in or out of experiments; therefore, Frontline Reps should not make any changes in the experiment assignments log in Admin.
Frontline Reps can refer to the internal Current Running Experiments (Rep) KA to learn more about experiments, including the steps to see which experiments a user or pro’s service is assigned to.

Active AI Matching Experiments (Rep)

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) serves as a centralized source of truth for Frontline Reps regarding Thumbtack's current AI-driven matching experiments. It compares the four key initiatives—Assured Exact Match, Smart Match, Matchmaker Expansion, and Personalized Preferences—highlighting differences in matching logic, charging models, and refund policies.
Thumbtack is simultaneously running distinct experiences to test how Artificial Intelligence (AI) can better match pros with customers. While all experiences leverage AI to improve lead relevance, they function differently regarding how matches are made, how pros are charged, and how refunds are handled.
The goal of these concurrent experiences is to determine the most effective way to:
Increase supply utilization: Ensure customers find a pro even when exact-match inventory is low.
Improve match quality: Use AI to predict successful matches beyond rigid checkbox targeting.
Simplify pro workflows: Test new ways for pros to receive and pay for leads without constant manual management.
Comparison: Active AI Matching Experiments 
The following table outlines the key differences between the active matching pilots reps may encounter.

Feature
Assured Exact Match
Smart match leads (Carrot)
Smarter lead matching (NDFP)
Audience
Pro
Pro
New + Existing pros
Target market

Nationwide
Existing pros: Baltimore, Maryland DMA and Washington, D.C. (Hagerstown) DMA
New pros: Baltimore, and Washington DMA and 50% of new pros
Can a pro be in more than one experience
Yes
Yes
No
Targeting Basis
Existing Job Types: Uses AI to infer missing details to confirm matches against existing preferences.
Existing Job Types: Works with the pro's existing job types by expanding them slightly. This does not impact travel areas.
New Taxonomy: Replaces categories with trades
Matching Logic
AI infers details from customer chats to validate an exact match.
AI predicts strong fit for jobs outside exact preferences.
AI automatically learns and updates preferences based on pro activity.
Active Management
Standard Services Page: Pros manage standard Job Types.
Standard Services page: Pros manage standard job preferences on the Services page. AI preferences are only refined during the "Not what I do" refund flow.
“Refine your matches” page: Dedicated page where pros can add or delete job types they most and least want from a defined catalog.
Charging Model
Auto-charged. Pro is automatically charged for the lead (if pro accepts all job types)
Auto-charged: Pro is automatically charged for the lead.
Auto-charged. Value-based (estimated job value).
Refunds and protections
Standard Policy: Pro must request a refund manually if there is a mismatch.
"Easy" Refunds. Pro can decline for "Not what I do" to refine preferences and receive a refund.
Skill-set mismatch: Pro declines as "Not what I do" to trigger auto-refund and refinement.
Duplicate customers: Refunds are granted if the pro gets a duplicate customer, even if the jobs are different. 
Opt-in / Opt-out
Auto-Opt-In
Enrollment Defaults: 
-Standard eligible pros are auto opted in. Can opt out and back in again anytime on their Services page.
- Single-business managed, national, and integrated pros can manually opt in.
- Multi-business accounts are excluded (can't opt in or out).
- Existing pros in the target markets are made eligible to enroll.
- New pros signing up in the target markets are automatically onboarded into smarter lead matching during sign-up. They cannot opt out of the experience.
Knowledge article
Assured Exact Match (Pro) (Experiment)
Smart match leads (Pro)
Smarter lead matching (New deal for pros) (Pro)
Current AI experiments
This section provides a brief breakdown of each experiment's scope and target audience. For full details on a specific experiment, refer to the linked resources.
Assured Exact Match 
Goal: Improve auto-charge coverage for leads generated via the new AI-driven "Dynamic Questions" flow (NCX leads) by validating matches via AI inference.
Audience: Customers nationwide on native only, pros nationwide 
Launched February 3, 2026
 Key Detail: Pros are auto-charged if they have broad targeting (all job types selected) or if AI infers the job matches their preferences.
Resources: Internal Assured Exact Match (Pro) (Customer) (Experiment) KA
Feedback theme in Salesforce: When logging feedback themes, reps should use the existing feedback item titled:  [Lead Quality] Pro had issue with lead that came from Assured Exact Match
Smart Match leads program (Carrot) (Nationwide)
Goal: To help pros get more jobs and better leads by looking beyond their specific targeting preferences.
Launched: June 17, 2026 is when smart matching launched nationwide
Key details:
This feature automatically sends and charges pros for leads that fall slightly outside their defined targeting preferences (specifically job types) when Thumbtack’s AI predicts a strong fit.
These are called “smart match” leads.
The pro can decline the lead before replying and select "Not what I do." A refund is issued automatically.
Resources:
Internal Smart match leads (Pro) KA
What are smart match leads? - Thumbtack Help article
Feedback theme in Salesforce: When logging feedback themes, reps should use the existing feedback item titled: [Targeting] User Feedback Regarding Smart Match Leads
New Deal for Pros (Smarter Lead Matching)
Goal: Overhaul the entire targeting system by replacing "Categories" with "Occupations" and using AI to learn preferences over time.
Launch:
Existing pros: April 20, 2026
New pros signups on or after June 2, 2026
Key Details: 
Pros manage broad trades (e.g., "Plumber" vs. "Pipe Repair"). AI learns what they do based on their accepts/declines. 
Leads matched through AI-learned trade/job-type preferences; lead price is a trade-level min/max range
Automatic refund trigger: Decline lead ("Can't do it") → "Not what I do" (before replying). Issues refund + AI generates/updates a job-type preference
Resources
What is smarter lead matching? - Thumbtack Help article 
Internal Smarter lead matching (New deal for pros) (Pro) KA
2. Process
Steps: How to identify which AI matching experiment a pro is in (Rep) 
Most of these experiments do not appear in the standard "Experiment assignments" section of Admin. Instead, Frontline Reps must use the specific checks below to confirm a pro's enrollment.
Check the pro's Location:
Miami, FL: Assured Exact Match
Check Admin (Occupation Targeting):
Go to the Occupation Targeting section in Admin.
If you see “MVP is enabled” the pro is enrolled in Smarter lead matching (NDFP). 
If you see “This user is eligible for MVP” the existing pro is eligible to enroll in Smarter lead matching (NDFP). 
Check Admin (Negotiations/Lead Type):
Navigate to the Negotiations tab for a specific lead.
Look at the Syndication Type and Next Gen Matching Status:
TARGETING_V2_NOT_ENROLLED_CONTACT_FREE: Smarter lead matching (NDFP). (Lead came from outside the pro's NDFP test market and matched via legacy category targeting settings)
ASSURED_EXACT_MATCH_CONTACT_DIRECT or _OPT_IN: Assured Exact Match
TARGETING_V2_NOT_ENROLLED_AUTO_CHARGE: Smart match lead
On the Refund Request Details page:
If "Is smart charge bid? (aka carrot test)" displays "Yes," it's a smart match lead

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article (KA) (Account Information: Manage Account Settings and Status (Pro)) provides guidelines for frontline reps on managing Thumbtack account settings and status for pros. It covers various topics such as login and password troubleshooting, email address changes, verified business information, and account transfers due to events like a deceased owner. The article also details processes for reactivating and deactivating accounts, including how to overcome common objections from pros and resolve issues with profile visibility in Google Search.
When working with pros on Thumbtack, frontline reps must confirm that they are speaking to the account owner before sharing information or making any changes regarding the account.
For privacy reasons, Thumbtack cannot disclose personal information about an individual’s account to anyone other than the account owner.*
Frontline reps must stick to this policy to protect sensitive information and maintain trust.
When making changes to a pros account or providing account information, reps can Verify the account and review the internal sensitive account info and Making Account Changes (Impersonation Guidelines) KAs.
*Some accounts have an authorized user added. To verify an authorized user, reps can refer to the internal Verifying account info KA.
[Internal frontline rep info only: Creating a new account is not allowed if the original account is on hold/blocklisted or deleted by Thumbtack or to avoid negative reviews. If a pro's Thumbtack account is placed on hold with a blocklist, or the account has been deleted by a Thumbtack employee and/or blocklisted, we do not want the pro creating a new account. The new account will be removed and the pro will be in a deletion loop. Thumbtack also does not want pros creating new accounts to avoid negative reviews.]

Key points
This section highlights key points for reps to reference when helping pros with their accounts.
Login key points  
Pros can log in using email and password or via their Facebook, Google, or Apple accounts.
They may need to re-login after 30 days of inactivity, using a new device, or clearing cache and cookies.
Email address key points
Pros can update their email address themselves if they have access to the current email on file.
If they cannot access the current email, they must submit the ID Help Intake Form with a photo of their government-issued ID. 
Creating a new account to avoid an email change is not allowed.
Password key points 
Pros can set up or reset their password using the password reset link.
Reps cannot reset passwords for pros due to security reasons.
If a pro cannot access their email for a password reset, they must request to update their email address by submitting the ID Help Intake Form.
Account transfers
There are certain reasons Thumbtack allows and doesn’t allow account transfers. 
Pros request an account transfer by submitting the ID Help Intake Form. 
Deceased account owner
If contacted by someone reporting a pro's death, reps must verify the contact's identity and determine whether they want to transfer or close the account.
For account transfers and closures, reps must turn off targeting, check for recent transactions, and potentially issue refunds for unread leads
Advanced Service or Managers may need to get involved for refunds.
Reactivate account
Pros can request reactivation through the activation request form.
Reps must check for blocklists or multiple reactivation/deactivation requests before reactivating.
Accounts deleted for community standards violations should not be reactivated and won't be reconsidered.
Deactivate account
Pros can request reactivation through the activation request form.
Reps must check for blocklists or multiple reactivation/deactivation requests before reactivating.
If a pro has a past-due balance, they cannot deactivate their account on their own. They must resolve the balance or have a rep manually deactivate it, understanding that the balance will still be due.
2. Account settings 
This section outlines how Thumbtack pros can manage their account settings, covering login, password, email, verified business, and legal name information, and how frontline reps can help them.
Login
This section details how pros can access their Thumbtack accounts using an email and password, or through linked Facebook, Google, or Apple accounts, and how frontline reps can troubleshoot login issues.

Ways of logging in
Login with email: Pros can log in to Thumbtack using an email address and create a password. 
Thumbtack password: If a pro hasn't created a password yet, they can set one up: Reset your password . If a pro is having password trouble, they should reset their password (How to update my password – Thumbtack Help) .
Other login options: 
Pros also have the option to log in to their Thumbtack account using their Facebook, Google or Apple account. When a pro logs in with their Facebook, Google or Apple account, they'll enter their login credentials in a pop-up window. However, if they are already signed in to Facebook, Google, or Apple in another browser, they will not need to re-enter their information.
Magic Link: Pros can select 'Continue with magic link' on the login page. This sends an email with a link that logs them in immediately without needing a password. The link expires after 30 minutes.
Reasons pro is prompted to log in
There are a few scenarios when a pro may be prompted to log in again:
They haven't logged in to their account within 30 days.
They're using a new device.
They've recently cleared their cache and cookies. 
Steps: How to log in to account (Pro)
 To login to their Thumbtack account, pros will follow the steps in the How to log in – Thumbtack Help article.
Steps: How to help pro troubleshoot login issues (Rep)
Frontline reps helping a pro with login issues should start by verifying the account is active. If a pro is having password trouble, they should reset their password (How to update my password – Thumbtack Help)  or use the Magic Link option to log in immediately. 

Note: If using Magic Link, advise the pro to check their spam folder if the email doesn't appear. The link expires in 30 minutes.
If the pro can’t log in, Support reps should check to see if their account is active by following these steps: 
Search the pro’s account in admin.
Check under the pros name, to see if the account is Enabled or Disabled.
If the account is disabled, click Deletion Logs under “Page Actions” to see why.
Check if the account was deleted by a user or a Thumbtack specialist. 
If a Thumbtack specialist deleted the account for a clear violation of Thumbtack’s community standards, don’t reactivate the account.
If the reason is not because of a community standards violation, reactivate the account.
Reps can suggest they use 'Continue with magic link' on the login page. This allows them to log in without recalling a password
If they request a Magic Link but don't see the email, ask them to check their spam folder. 
Remind them that the link expires after 30 minutes. 
Note: The 'Email sent' screen will appear even if an account does not exist for that email address (to prevent security enumeration), so ensure they are using the correct email address associated with their account.
If the issue persists, they can click 'Forgot password' to reset their credentials.
NOTE: Reps can refer to the internal Removed or Banned Users KA for more information on Thumbtack violations, or see Thumbtack User Guidelines. 
Password
This section provides guidelines for pros to set up or reset their passwords and explains how frontline reps can address password issues when email access is unavailable, while emphasizing that reps cannot reset passwords directly.

Steps: How to create a password (Pro) 
If a pro hasn’t created a password yet, they can set one up here. Pro’s can check out the How to update my password – Thumbtack Help article to learn more.
Note: Pros can also log in without a password using the Magic Link option, which allows users (both with and without a password set) to access their account via an email link.
Password guidelines
Pros should make sure they're only using the following characters when creating their password:
Letters: Aa to Zz
Numbers: 0 to 9
Symbols: . * & , - @ ' ( ) + ? ! # %
Password resets and security
Thumbtack prioritizes the security of our pros. Therefore, Thumbtack does not provide temporary passwords to pros for password reset. Instead, reps can send a password reset email allowing the pro to update their password. 
If a pro cannot access their email address to reset their password, they can change the email address on their Thumbtack account by submitting the ID help form, see Pro can’t access email address on their Thumbtack account below (or create a new account with their new email*). Thumbtack never provides a temporary password to pros or customers.
*[Internal frontline rep info only: 
Pros are not permitted to create new accounts if the original account is:
On hold/blocklisted
Deleted by Thumbtack
Being created to avoid negative reviews. 
If a pro creates a new account under these circumstances, it will be removed, and they will be unable to create new accounts.] 
A pro might have password or login issues because their account is deactivated. If that's the case, Reps can refer to the internal Removed or Banned Users KA to see why the account was deactivated.
Pro can't access the email address on their Thumbtack account to reset password

Steps: Request email address change in order to reset password (Pro)
If the pro cannot access the email address associated with their Thumbtack account to reset their password, they will have to:
Request an email change (before they can do the password reset) by submitting the ID Help Form. When submitting the form, pros must include a photo of their government-issued ID. 
Once the Trust and Safety team updates the email address, the pro can reset their password and regain access to their account. 
Reps can refer to the internal ID Help Guid KA to learn more
Steps: How to help pro troubleshoot password issues (Rep)
 
Support reps should encourage a pro to change their own password. However, reps should help pro’s having password issues.
Note: If the pro cannot access the email address associated with their Thumbtack account, they'll need to request an email change before they can do the password reset. Reps will refer to the Pro can’t access email address on their Thumbtack account process below.
To help a pro with password issues, Support reps will determine if the pro needs help login by following these steps:
Ask the pro if they can log in or not. 
If the pro can log in, they can change their password by going to Settings > Account > Password. Reps can also send them this direct link.
If the pro can't log in, they can go to our login page and click Forgot password. The pro should receive an email to reset their password.
If the pro doesn't get the email, reps should check their account in Admin for a subscribe button next to their email.
If the “Subscribe” button is next to their email, they are not receiving Thumbtack emails. Reps will click “Subscribe” and ask the pro to click “Forgot password” again. If they're still not receiving Thumbtack emails, they can reach out to their email domain to retrieve this reset. 
If the “Subscribe” button is not there, and they’re not getting the reset password email, reps should verify their email and perform email troubleshooting. 
Note: If the pro cannot access the email address associated with their Thumbtack account, they'll need to request an email change before they can do the password reset.
If they’re still not getting the email, submit a bug report. Reps can refer to the internal Bugs KA for steps.
Email
This section explains how pros can update their email address, including steps for self-service updates and the process for requesting changes if they no longer have access to their current email, and how frontline reps can help with email address issues.
The email address on a pro’s account is the primary piece of information Thumbtack uses to make changes to their account including changes that would cause charges to their account. To protect pro’s safety and avoid any risk of fraud, Thumbtack isn’t able to change a pro’s email address for them. 
Email access: Pros with access to their current email address on file can update their email address themselves on a desktop browser or Android app (without going through ID help). Pros on iOS should use a desktop browser to update their email address. 
No access to email: If the pro cannot access the email address associated with their Thumbtack account, they will have to request an email change by submitting the ID Help Form.
Steps: Update email address (Pro)
If a pro wants to update their email address, they should follow these steps:
▶ Desktop browser steps
How pros update their email address on desktop: 
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Click your profile photo at the top right.
Select Settings from the menu.
Select Account.
Select Email.
Under the email field, click Change your email address.
The link will guide them to check their email inbox to proceed with updating their email address. If they no longer have access to that email address, they will be prompted to fill out the ID Help form instead. (See what it looks like below.)▶ What it looks like[Image: AD_4nXcl3aHmSsKC8SyqJNdqKb_gtBtp4xe6JeGypb7E7W52JXZRfPkAgHMVLJI4m_yVB7EyDttGPlOPAEyyvof-ItSn9W2JP5jsuS0PEFUVgRx1VmurfMi2oYLmpM4JhPLpNbErkp8O4w]
Open the email and click Change email address.
Enter the new email address.
Click Save.
▶ Android App steps
How pros update their email address on the Thumbtack app:  
Open the Thumbtack app.
Tap Profile from the main menu below.
Tap the gear icon at the top right.
Tap Account details.
Tap Email.
Under the email field, click Change your email address.
The link will guide them to check their email inbox to proceed with updating their email address. If they no longer have access to that email address, they will be prompted to fill out the ID Help form instead. (See what it looks like below.)▶ What it looks like
[Image: AD_4nXcl3aHmSsKC8SyqJNdqKb_gtBtp4xe6JeGypb7E7W52JXZRfPkAgHMVLJI4m_yVB7EyDttGPlOPAEyyvof-ItSn9W2JP5jsuS0PEFUVgRx1VmurfMi2oYLmpM4JhPLpNbErkp8O4w]
Open the email and tap Change email address.
Enter the new email address.
Click Save.
Steps: How to help pro troubleshoot email address issues (Rep)
If a pro has trouble accessing their account, Support reps will follow these steps:
Make sure the pro is using the right email address. 
Next, ask the pro if they’re having issues with their email, password, or both. If they're unsure, continue through these steps.
Confirm in Admin that the email address listed under their account matches the address they tried to log in with.
If the email address matches, the issue is likely a password problem. Follow the steps under the password problem section. 
If the email address doesn’t match, the pro will need to follow the ID help process. Reps will follow the steps outlined in the internal  ID Help Guide KA.

▶ Contents (RC)
Legal name
Business name (and verified business)
Account status 
Account transfers
Account transfer guidelines
(Rep) Steps: How to help pro requesting an account transfer
Deceased account owner
(Rep) Steps: How to help someone reporting a pro death
(Rep) Steps: Transfer account due to account owner death
(Rep) Steps: Close account due to account owner death
(OC or Manager) Steps: Refund a pros Thumbtack balance after reports of account owner death
Legal name (Change or update)
This section outlines the process for pros to update their legal name on their account and how frontline reps can help with these requests.
Thumbtack requires pros to use their legal name when signing up for Thumbtack. Pro’s should also take a background check to help build trust and credibility with customers. It also helps Thumbtack verify the pro is a real person. The person listed on the pros Thumbtack account should be the business owner. 
Pro steps: If a pro needs to update their name they can submit the ID Help Intake Form. They can expect a response within 2 - 3 business days.
Frontline reps can refer to the internal ID Help Guide KA to learn more. 
Business name (and verified businesses)
This section details the criteria for businesses to become verified and receive a "Verified business" badge, and how frontline reps can guide pros through the process of updating verified business information.
Business name
Pro’s can update their business name at any time. During sign up, if a pro doesn’t add a business name, Thumbtack will created one using the pros account name. 
To update their business name, pros will follow the steps on the How to edit my business profile – Thumbtack Help article. However, one thing to note is that if the pro has a verified business, they can directly edit their account information.
Verified business
Thumbtack uses a third-party vendor to verify the business’ information and to make sure it meets these standards. 
Businesses that are verified receive a badge on their profile that says “Verified business.” The verified business badge is only available to a select group of pros. 
Thumbtack use these profile badges to help customers hire with confidence and  identify when a business or franchisor is verified. To maintain that confidence (and to make sure we’re displaying accurate information), verified businesses can’t directly edit their account information (see what happens after a pro's business is verified).
▶ Qualifications: A business or franchise can become verified when certain qualifications are met, including:
Has a business name and address verified in our vendor’s database
Is incorporated for two or more years
Doesn’t have any bankruptcies within the last five years
Doesn’t have any unsatisfied liens or judgments of more than $100
Doesn’t have any liens greater than $5,000 within the last 5 years 
The parameters above apply to small- and medium-sized businesses only. Thumbtack may verify larger corporations under alternative standards that are more appropriate for businesses of their size. Lien information for all businesses is based only on publicly filed information located by our third-party vendor at the time of verification.

How to change business name when business is verified (Pro)
If a pro wants to change their business name and their business is verified (so the business name is locked), they should:
Submit the ID Help form, including a clear photo of their government-issued ID and documentation proving the business name change (e.g., updated Articles of Incorporation, DBA filing, or business registration papers).
The response time for this process is from 2 - 3 business days. The ID Help team will verify the submitted documents, remove the current credentials from the pro's profile, and allow them to change their business name. 
Afterwards, the pro will need to resubmit their license and business verification with the new business name.
Pros can also check out the What is a verified business? article to learn more. 

Frontline reps can refer to the internal Business Verification KA and the ID Help Guide KA.

3. Account status
This section details the various statuses a Thumbtack pro account can have, including information on account transfers, handling deceased account owners, reactivation, and deactivation, and how frontline reps can help with these processes.
Account transfers
This section explains the conditions under which Thumbtack allows account transfers, such as due to the account owner's death or the sale of a company, and how frontline reps can guide pros through the transfer request process.
Account transfer guidelines
Occasionally, a pro may need to transfer their account to another person. Depending on the reasons, the transfer may or may not be permitted. The table below outlines when Thumbtack allows account transfers.

Account transfer eligibility 
Description 
Account transfers are  allowed  if the account owner:
Has passed away. See account transfer due to death. 
Has sold the company and all of its assets to a new owner.
Changes the manager of a franchise location.
Leaves the company, but no other changes are being made to the business. (Example: The business isn’t being sold but the person managing the account leaves the company.)
Account transfer are not allowed if the account owner wants:
The name on the account to match a license they’re uploading. Reps ca reference the internal Licenses KA.
To transfer the account to a spouse or a friend.
Someone else to run their account for them.
An account transfer won’t apply to situations where the pro still owns the business, but they want someone else to run the account. We prefer to have the owner of the business listed. A pro can add an authorized user instead.
Steps: How to request an account transfer (Pro)
Pros will submit the ID Help Form to request an account transfer with the supporting documentation. They can expect a response within 2 - 3 business days. They can refer to the How to transfer ownership of your account – Thumbtack Help article to learn about approved documentation. 
Frontline reps can reference the internal ID Help Guide KA for steps. 
​​​​​​Steps: How to help pro requesting an account transfer (Rep) 
If a pro wants to transfer their account for a reason Thumbtack allows, Support reps will follow these steps:
Make sure the pro understands that transferring the ownership of their account means they give up the rights to make any changes or access the account.
Have the pro go to ID Help Intake Form to request an account transfer with the supporting documentation. They can expect a response within 2 - 3 business days. Reps will reference the internal ID Help Guide KA for steps
Take notes in the case with the reason the pro requested an account transfer. (i.e., the previous owner sold their business to a new owner) 
NOTE: For a request to transfer or close an account due to a pro passing away, follow the below steps.
Deceased account owner

This section outlines the steps frontline reps should follow when contacted by someone reporting a pro's death, including how to verify the account and manage requests for account transfer or closure.
Steps: How to help someone reporting a pro death (Rep)
In the unfortunate event that a Support rep is contacted by a friend or family member requesting to transfer or close an account due to the account owner passing away, reps will follow these steps:

On behalf of Thumbtack, thank them for reaching out to us, and express that our team is sorry for their loss. 
Ask if they want to transfer the account or if they intend to close it. 
Let them know you can help, and that you are going to ask some questions and make some updates to make sure that no further charges happen.
If they want to transfer the account, follow the transferring account steps below. 
If they want to close the account, follow the closing account steps below. 

▶ Steps: Transfer account due to account owner death (Rep)
If the person reporting the account owner death requests to transfer the account, Support reps will follow these steps: 
Ask the contact if they can verify the account. Reps will reference the internal Verify Account Information KA for steps. 
If the contact is not able to verify email on the account, address, DOB, or other verification data:
Case classification: Event > Pro Passed Away > Pro > Ops > Account Transfer > Pro Death > Pro reported to be deceased, account being deactivated
Case notes: “(contact name) is unable to verify the account. (Insert any information they are able to share).” 
Proceed to the next step
Turn off targeting for all services on the account, regardless of state of verification. Reps canreference the internal Targeting Preferences KA. 
Ask the contact for the date of the pro’s passing.
Check for transactions since that date to see if any of the leads have been viewed or responded to and add that information in the case notes. 
For refunds, Thumbtack will refund the pro's Thumbtack balance back to the pro’s bank account for any unread and unresponded to leads after the date of the pro’s passing. 
If the date of passing is 6 months or less, the rep can proceed to the next step. 
If the date of passing is more than 6 months, the rep should submit a request to the Advanced Service Team using the Atlassian Assist app in Slack: 
Before posting in Slack, perform a quick online search for the obituary of the pro. To do this, simply open Google and search for "Obituary for [Pros first and last name] [State pro lived in]." Advanced Service will need the link to the obituary.
Navigate to the #service_global_help-and-escalations Slack channel.
Use a keyword like “Help others” or “Others” to trigger the Assist app workflow.
Select the "Global Help Others" (Trust & Safety) request type and fill out the form with all necessary details.
Once the rep has approval from Advanced Service, proceed to the next step.
If there were leads, and none were read or responded to, refund the lead back to the pro’s payment method. 
When refunding leads to a pros Thumbtack balance, follow the applicable process on the internal Lead Refunds KA. 
NOTE: Use the following format to enter notes in Admin: Case # and pro specific reason: 
Case-xxxxxxxx Refund due to account owner death 
To transfer balance to pros card, follow the steps under “how to help these pros” on the internal Transfer Pros Cashable Balance Back To Card KA and start on step 8.
If there are leads that were viewed or responded to since the date of passing, these would not be refunded.
To transfer the account, let the contact know they need to submit our ID Help form and let them know they should expect an agent to reach out within 2 - 3 business days. See ID Help Guide KA to learn more. 

▶ Steps: Close account due to account owner death (Rep)
If the person reporting the account owner death requests to close the account, Support reps will follow these steps: 
Ask the contact if they can verify the account. Reps will reference the internal Verify Account Information KA. 
If the contact is not able to verify email on the account, address, DOB, or other verification data:
Case classification: Event > Passed Away > Pro Ops Account Deactivate account Pro Death Pro reported to be deceased, account being transferred to new owner
Case notes: “(contact name) is unable to verify the account. (Insert any information they are able to share).”
Proceed to the next step.
Deactivate the account, regardless of state of verification. 
When closing the account in Admin, note the name of the person reporting the pro as being deceased and include whether they were able to verify the account in the deletion logs in Admin and add notes to case notes. 
Ask the contact for the date of the pro’s passing. 
Check for transactions since the date of the pros passing to see if any of the leads have been viewed or responded to and add that to the case notes.
For refunds, Thumbtack will refund the pro’s Thumbtack balance back to the pro’s bank account for any unread and unresponded to leads after the date of the pro’s passing. 
If the date of passing is 6 months or less, the rep can follow the steps to process the refund. 
If the date of passing is more than 6 months, the rep should submit a request to the Advanced Service Team using the Atlassian Assist app in Slack: 
Before posting in Slack, perform a quick online search for the obituary of the pro. To do this, simply open Google and search for "Obituary for [Pros first and last name] [State pro lived in]". Advanced Service will need the link to the obituary. 
Navigate to the #service_global_help-and-escalations Slack channel.
Use a keyword like “Help others” or “Others” to trigger the Assist app workflow.
Select the "Global Help Others" (Trust & Safety) request type and fill out the form with all necessary details.
Once the rep has approval from Advanced Service, proceed to the next step.
If there were leads, and none were read or responded to, refund the lead to the pro’s payment method. 
To refund leads to a pros balance, follow the applicable process to refund any leads on the internal Lead Refunds KA. 
To transfer balance to pro’s cards, follow the steps under “how to help these pros” on the internal Transfer Pros Cashable Balance Back To Card KA and start on step 8.
If there are leads that were viewed or responded leads since date of passing, reps should submit a request to the Advanced Service Team using the Atlassian Assist app in Slack:
Navigate to the #service_global_help-and-escalations Slack channel.
Use a keyword like “Help others” or “Others” to trigger the Assist app workflow.
Select the "Global Help Others" (Trust & Safety) request type and fill out the form with all necessary details.


▶ Steps: Provide Service rep with next steps (AS or Manager)
Advanced Service and managers will confirm that the previous steps above were completed by the rep before providing next steps. 
If the Support rep has found that the date of death doesn’t align with the last lead that was viewed or responded to, Advanced Service or managers will do the following: 
Check the Support reps work.
Request documentation for date of deceased.
Do not ask for a death certificate.
Online resources that our advocates can look up are acceptable, such as: newspapers or public record sources.
If the source looks inauthentic or there is a question of the source likely being inauthentic, reach out to Cass Abernathy via Slack.
Rep should check if the documented death date and last date of Thumbtack account activity align. 
If the last activity happens after the death date, but there does seem to be an end to account activity, refund from the date where no further leads receive a response
Proceed with either closing or transferring the account.
