Reactive account 
This section describes the process for pros to reactivate their Thumbtack accounts and the important checks frontline reps must perform before reactivating an account.
Steps: How to reactivate account (Pro)
To activate their Thumbtack account, pros will submit the reactivation form. As soon as they submit the form, Thumbtack will get back to them within 2 - 3 business days. Pros can refer to the How to reactivate an account – Thumbtack Help to learn more
Note: The pro needs to fill out the information themselves.

Steps: How to help a pro reactivate their account (Rep)
When a pro wants to reactivate their account, it’s important Support reps check a few things before reactivating, including: 
Review the reason an account was deleted by clicking Deletion logs under "Page Actions"
Double-check that the account hasn’t been blocklisted by Trust and Safety. This is listed in Admin on the user's service profile under “Banned status.”
If a user reaches out,  but has been deleted by T&S or for a ToS violation, transfer the case to Trust and Safety using the Salesforce transfer flow. For steps, see Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA. 
Ensure there are not three or more requests for reactivation in three months. If there are, escalate the case to your manager to determine next steps. If there aren’t, move to the steps below
Before walking a pro through the steps to reactivate their account, Support reps should make sure there aren’t any concerns on the account that need to be addressed (T&S or otherwise) by following these steps: 
Check the pro’s Admin status. Deactivated accounts will say "Deleted" or "Disabled" below their name.
Check that the account has not been Blocklisted by Trust and Safety. 
To see why an account is disabled, click Deletion Logs under “Page Actions”. 
Check the “User” column to see if the account was deleted by the pro, Thumbtack specialist or an automated deletion. 
In addition, make sure there are not three or more requests for reactivation in three months. If there are, reps should follow the steps under “Multiple requests for deactivation/reactivation” section. 
In “Page Actions” (on the top right side of the page), click Admin Undelete. 
Note: To reactivate a service profile, reps will need to find the deleted service under “Services” first. 
Add the reason for reactivating the account or service profile.
Click Confirm to activate the account or profile. 
Deactivate account
This section covers how pros can self-deactivate their accounts, important considerations before deactivation, strategies for frontline reps to overcome objections, and the steps for manually deactivating an account.
Steps: How to deactivate Thumbtack account (Pro)
Pros can deactivate their account on their own by going to their Settings page and selecting “account.” From there, pros will have the option to ‘Deactivate account.’. However, pros with a past-due balance on their account are not able to deactivate their account themselves.
Additionally, instead of deactivating their account, pros can also take a break from Thumbtack by hiding their business (How to pause leads by hiding your business) or turning off notifications (How to update notifications – Thumbtack Help). 
Pros can follow the steps in the How to deactivate a pro account. – Thumbtack Help article to deactivate their account. 

[Image: AD_4nXdlcbqdYuJihsRsMTa9SXkFuFYLeuYf7QMffZQmGsBb8jdpJW95muhs0Q5iIHQtzeC-FqlJzncpPBNZYYIZUo2poVcXSxHnqKnt1v_DWMKyN11obAFfMnioL8CT03_LH40UHxWPHw]

Screenshot: The image above shows the Account section on a pros Settings page with options for: ‘Hide business temporarily,’ ‘Deactivate account,’ and ‘Request access to or delete personal data.’
Important Considerations Frontline Reps must review before deactivating a pro account
Before helping a pro with account deactivation, frontline reps must inform them of the following and ensure pros understand that: 
Data deletion vs. Deactivation: 
Selecting ‘Request access to or delete personal data’ on their settings page will take the pro through the Data deletion and removal process (outlined in the internal Sensitive information KA). 
This process can take up to 45 days, during which the pro's account remains active and continues to be charged for leads.
Frontline reps should ensure the pro is aware of this before moving forward with this step.  
Hide business temporarily: 
As an alternative to deactivating their account, pros can take a break from Thumbtack by hiding their business or turning off targeting.
Pro steps: How to pause leads by hiding your business Thumbtack Help article.
Loss of account access: 
Deactivating their account means they will lose access to all projects, profile information, and reviews (both written and received) on Thumbtack.
If a customer deactivates their account, any verified reviews they left will remain visible on the pro's profile (unless the customer's account was blocklisted). 
Reps should note that creating a new account to avoid negative reviews, or if the original account is on hold/blocklisted or deleted by Thumbtack, is not permitted.
Unsubscribe from notifications: 
Before deactivation, pros must unsubscribe from notifications to stop receiving promo emails and texts. 
Pro steps: How to unsubscribe – Thumbtack Help article.
Reps can reference the internal Notifications (Pro) for steps. 
Past due balance: 
Pros with a past-due balance cannot deactivate their account independently.
They must either resolve the balance or request a manual deactivation from a Thumbtack rep, acknowledging that the past-due balance will still be owed.
Overcoming a pro objections for deactivating their pro account (Rep)
Thumbtack wants to help our pros find success on Thumbtack. If they ask a frontline rep to deactivate their account, the rep start with asking why. Depending on why they would like to stop using Thumbtack, Thumbtack might be able to help. 
Pro objections: Common objections may include:  
Moving out of the country
No longer offering their service
Business closing down
Illness/injury
Overcoming objections: Use the pro objections listed in Step 2 below to identify concerns and offer solutions, coaching and alternative actions (e.g., adjusting targeting preferences) before proceeding with deactivation.
Conditions beyond Thumbtack’s concerns: Some reasons for deactivation are unavoidable (e.g., moving out of the country, no longer offering the service, business closing, illness/injury).
Steps: How to help a pro requesting to deactivate their account (Rep)

To help a pro deactivate their account, walk them through the steps to take it themselves. If they’re unable to deactivate their account on their own, Support reps will follow these steps:
NOTE: To stop receiving promo emails and texts, pros must unsubscribe from notifications before deactivating their account. Reps can refer to the internal Notifications (Pro) KA.
Understand the reason: Start with asking the pro why to understand the reason for deactivation. 
▶ Email requests: If contacted by email, reps will follow these steps:
Check the email to see if there is a reason they are requesting to deactivate their account.
If the pro did or did not provided a reason for deactivation, AND the Thumbtack can’t offer a solution, use the email template “Deactivate account: pro wants to delete their account”
If they did provide a reason for deactivation, AND the rep can address their concern (e.g., not winning/hearing back, pro thinks cost is too high, etc.), the rep should offer a solution..
Attempt to overcome objections: Try to overcome any objections or concerns the pro shares by offering solutions and coaching.   
▶ Pro objection: Leads costs too much! Deactivate my account."The pro may share feedback about the cost of meeting new customers, Thumbtack not being worth the investment they made, etc.
Check the pro’s payment history to get a better sense of how much money the pro has invested.
How to track my spending – Thumbtack Help 
Explain how Thumbtack is like an advertising investment. With Thumbtack, they are targeting and advertising to customers interested in their service and in their area.
Coach the pro how to rank better in search results (like building their profile). 
Reps can find coaching tips in the internal Search Results and Rank KA.
▶ Pro objection: The leads I get are low-quality leads! Deactivate my account."The pro may mention that they are unhappy with the quality of the leads they receive or with the type of customers they meet on Thumbtack.The best way to identify this concern is to receive feedback about customer quality directly from the pro. If they identify this as a concern, the rep can use it as an opportunity to better learn their needs and find ways Thumbtack can work for them.
Acknowledge their concern. Thumbtack wants them to feel excited about the customers they meet on Thumbtack, not skeptical or disappointed.
Learn more about the types of customers they’re interested in. 
Confirm or walk through the pro’s preferences with them. 
My job preferences – Thumbtack Help 
Remind them they can always update their preferences if they’re not meeting the right customers. Many pros are skeptical about Thumbtack because they don’t understand the customer journey. 
Here’s a guide to how customers find you. – Thumbtack Help 
Explain more about search results and how customers typically find and hire through Thumbtack. 
How to improve my rank in search results – Thumbtack Help 
See if there’s a specific lead they are concerned about and offer to look into it for them. 
Let them know Thumbtack is more than happy to look into leads if they’re ever concerned.
▶ Pro objection: "I'm not getting hired! Deactivate my account."Pros will often openly express their frustration about not finding success on Thumbtack. 

If the rep is not sure if this is the pros concern, check their insights. Reps cab reference the internal Performance Dashboard KA.
Acknowledge their concern and be empathetic. Not winning the job can be disappointing, especially when the pro puts their best effort forward.
▶ Talking point when pro says "No one is hiring me!"
English talking point
Spanish talking point: Nadie me está contratando.
I’m sorry you’re having trouble getting hired on Thumbtack. I know how frustrating it is not to hear back from a customer. I really want your business to succeed on Thumbtack, and I think I can help [COACHING]. One thing you could do is [COACHING]. I’ve seen a lot of professionals find success by doing this and, if you’re willing to give it a try, I believe it will increase your chances of getting hired.
Lamento que tenga problemas para que le contraten en Thumbtack. Sé lo frustrante que es no recibir noticias de un cliente. Realmente quiero que su negocio tenga éxito en Thumbtack, y creo que puedo ayudar [COACHING]. Una cosa que podría hacer es [COACHING]. He visto a muchos profesionales tener éxito al hacer esto y, si está dispuesto a intentarlo, creo que aumentará sus posibilidades de ser contratado.
Offer coaching and remind them that Thumbtack is here to help them succeed. 
Explain how search results work, and the importance of responsiveness.
How to improve my rank in search results – Thumbtack Help
Reps can refer to the internal Search results and ranking KA. 
▶ Pro objection: "I'm getting too many notifications! Deactivate my account."The best way to identify this concern is to receive this feedback directly from the pro or customer. The number of notifications a pro or customer wants to receive is different from person to person.
To see how many emails Thumbtack has sent a pro or customer, check the "Emails sent" section in Admin. Reps can also check the pro or customer’s notifications page to see which notifications are currently on or off.
Acknowledge their concern and apologize for overwhelming them with notifications.
▶ Talking point when pro says "I'm getting too many emails/texts/push notifications."I'm getting too many emails/texts/push notifications.I'm sorry we've been sending too many emails. That definitely wasn’t our intention and we don’t want to overwhelm you. I can help you adjust your notification settings so that you hear from us less or not at all. I’ll also show you where you can adjust these settings for the future. That way, you can continue using Thumbtack on your terms and get our notifications however much (or little) you want.Spanish talking point: Recibo demasiados correos electrónicos / mensajes de texto / notificaciones automáticas.Lamento que le enviamos demasiados correos electrónicos. Definitivamente esa no era nuestra intención y no queremos abrumarlo. Puedo ayudarle a ajustar la configuración de sus notificaciones para que tenga menos noticias nuestras o ninguna. También le mostraré dónde puede ajustar esta configuración para el futuro. De esa manera, puede continuar usando Thumbtack bajo sus términos y recibir nuestras notificaciones por mucho (o poco) que desee.
Explain how they can edit their notification settings, or turn off notifications.
How to update notifications – Thumbtack Help
Reps can reference the internal Notifications KA to learn more. 
Check deletion log: If the pro still wants to deactivate after trying to overcome their objections, reps should check the pros deletion log. 
To do this, click “Deletion logs” in the Actions field under Legacy Admin Accounts. 
Address any account issues: 
▶ Multiple requests: If there are no concerns (like multiple deletion and reactivation requests or T&S concerns), skip to step 6. If there are concerns like multiple deletion and reactivation requests, reps will follow the applicable steps below
▶ If there are two deactivation or reactivation requests in the last ~ two months, reps will:
 Let the pro know that if they keep deactivating and reactivating their account, there's a chance that Thumbtack will deny their reactivation request.
Talking point: Deactivation of an account is intended to be permanent. If a pro plans to be away temporarily, they should utilize pausing their targeting or hiding their business instead.
Note: Instead of deactivating their account, pros should either pause targeting or hide their business, which will prevent them from showing up in search results. Reps can refer to the internal Targeting Preferences (Pro) and Availability (Pro) KA for steps.
▶ If there are three or more deactivation or reactivation requests in the last three months, reps should submit a request to the Advanced Service Team using the Atlassian Assist app in Slack:
Navigate to the #service_global_help-and-escalations Slack channel.
Use a keyword like “Help others” or “Others” to trigger the Assist app workflow.
Select the "Global Help Others" (Trust & Safety) request type and fill out the form with all necessary details. Advanced Service will determine the next steps, including whether we will deactivate or reactivate the account.
If there are additional concerns that need further review, Advanced Service can escalate the case to a Case Manager by completing this form.
▶ Past due balance: If the pro has a past due balance, they cannot deactivate their account on their own.
Explain that the system automatically prevents self-service deactivation due to the outstanding balance.
Provide the pro with options:
Pay the Balance: Update their payment method and pay the balance to proceed with standard online deactivation (if they wish to keep the account active).
Manual Deactivation with Acknowledgment: The rep can manually deactivate the account, but the pro must acknowledge:
The past-due balance will remain on their account.

Resources
1. OVERVIEW
When working with customers on Thumbtack, frontline reps must confirm that they are speaking to the account owner before sharing information or making any changes regarding the account. 
Frontline Reps should refer to the following internal Knowledge Articles (KAs) when making changes to a customer’s account or providing account information:
Verify Account Information (Pro) (Customer))
Sensitive Account Information Handling Guidelines (Pro) (Customer) (Rep)
Making Account Changes on Behalf of Pro or Customer (Impersonation Guidelines) (Rep)
If a customer contacts a Frontline Rep regarding an account hold or if their account has been ghosted, reps can refer to the internal Account Holds (Customer) KA for guidance.
2. Account settings 

Login 
Ways to log into Thumbtack:
On the app, customers can log in using SMS verified login*. Customers can also log in with an email and password, Google, Apple (iOS only), or Facebook account. However, the customer will need a phone number to log into the customer app. This helps us verify that the person logging in is a real person. It also lets us use the phone number as a secondary contact method.
*SMS verified login: Some phone numbers may be ineligible for SMS verified login. For details on eligibility and troubleshooting, frontline reps can refer to the internal SMS Verified Login (Customer) KA.
On the web and desktop, customers can log in with an email address and password, a magic link, or Facebook, Google, or Apple.  
A magic link is a passwordless option where customers click 'Continue with magic link' to receive a login link via email. They will enter their email address and click ‘Send magic link.’ They will see an “Email sent' screen, even if an account does not exist for that email address (to prevent security enumeration). From their email, the customer will click “Log in to Thumbtack” which logs them in immediately without needing a password. The link expires after 30 minutes.
▶ What the login field looks like on web

[Image: rtaImage]

To log in, customers will follow the steps in the How to log in – Thumbtack Help article. The steps vary based on how they’re logging in and with what device.  If a customer hasn’t created a password yet, they can set one up on the: Reset your password page. 
Scenarios when customer is prompted to log in
There are a few scenarios when a customer may be prompted to log in again:
Haven’t logged into their account on the app within 30 days 
Haven’t logged in to their account on web within 180 days 
Are using a new device.
Have recently cleared their cache and cookies. 
Frontline reps helping a customer with login issues should start by verifying the account is active by following the (Rep) Steps: How to help customer with login issues (troubleshoot). If a customer is having password trouble, they should reset their password (How to update my password – Thumbtack Help) .
(Rep) Steps: How to help customer with login issues (troubleshooting)
First, reps should ask the customer how they are trying to log in. If the customer is trying to login on the app, they may have issues with SMS verified login. See SMS Verified Login (Customer) KA for common issues and fixes.
Additionally, if a customer is having password trouble, they should reset their password (How to update my password – Thumbtack Help) . 
If the customer can’t log in, Support reps should check to see if their account is active by following these steps: 
In Admin, pull up the customer’s account. 
Check under the customer's name to see if the account is Enabled or Disabled.
If the account is disabled, click Deletion Logs under “Page Actions” to see why.
Check if the account was deleted by a user or a Thumbtack specialist. 
If the reason is because of a clear violation of Thumbtack’s community standards and a Thumbtack specialist deleted the account, do not reactivate the account.
See Removed or Banned Users (Pro) (Customer) KA > Use Guideline Removal for more information on Thumbtack violations, or see Thumbtack User Guidelines.
If the reason is not because of a community standards violation, reactivate the account.
Reps can suggest they use 'Continue with magic link' on thumbtack.com/login. This allows them to log in without recalling a password
If they request a Magic Link but don't see the email, ask them to check their spam folder. 
Remind them that the link expires after 30 minutes. 
Note: After clicking “Send magic link” they see an 'Email sent' screen, even if an account does not exist for that email address (to prevent security enumeration). Rep should ensure they are using the correct email address associated with their account.
If the issue persists, they can click 'Forgot password' to reset their credentials.
Phone number
This section outlines Thumbtack's customer phone number policies and provides steps for frontline reps to manually add a phone number to  a customer's account in Admin.
When a customer creates an account on Thumbtack or submits a request, they'll need to add their phone number. 
Phone number policy
Purpose: Thumbtack uses phone numbers for identity-matching to ensure all customer phone numbers are real. Thumbtack is implementing this policy to help improve the quality of job leads for pros. 
3-User Reuse Limit: A single phone number can be associated with a maximum of three (3) customer accounts.
Customer Impact: If a customer attempts to use a phone number linked to four or more accounts, they will be blocked from submitting a request and will see the error message: 'This phone number can't be used on your account'.
Blocklisted Numbers: Customers can enter a blocklisted number, but any requests submitted with it will be silently deleted after submission. Customers will not be aware their request was flagged or deleted due to being blocklisted
Frontline reps should be aware that sometimes good customers might legitimately need to use the same phone number for more than one account. 
Legitimate Reasons for Manual Add:
The customer has a work and a personal email, both used on Thumbtack with the same cell phone number.
The customer is also a pro and has a separate customer account.
The customer lost access to an old email and is now using a new one with the same phone number.

If a customer is unable to submit a job request due to the 'This phone number can't be used on your account' error (3-user limit), and the rep has verified their legitimate need, the rep can bypass the automatic check and manually add the phone number in Admin. When frontline reps use this tool, no extra verification is needed for the phone number.
(Rep) Steps: How to manually add a phone number to a customer's account
This process is to help a customer who is unable to submit a job request (due to the 3-user limit error) or add a phone number to their existing account. 
Frontline reps will follow this process if a customer is unable to submit a job request due to the 'This phone number can't be used on your account' error (3-user limit). If the rep confirms the customer's legitimate need, the rep can bypass the automatic check and manually add the phone number in Admin by following these steps: 
NOTE: Reps can use the Phone number talking point below to help navigate these conversations
Review the Legitimate Reasons for Manual Add above to confirm the customer's situation qualifies:
In Admin, pull up the customer's account page.
▶ Scroll down to the "Phone numbers" section.'
[Image: rtaImage]
Click the Phone numbers section to open up the phone numbers table. 
▶ Type in the 10-digit phone number (include the area code) the customer gives you.
[Image: rtaImage]
▶ Click “Add Phone Number” to save.
[Image: rtaImage]
▶ After successfully adding the phone number, a confirmation message will display: "Phone number added successfully."
[Image: rtaImage]
Refresh the page to view the newly added number in the table. 
For more in-depth troubleshooting of phone number errors and detailed talking points regarding these policies, frontline reps can refer to the internal Enhanced Lead Quality Commitment (Customer Phone Number Verification Code Validation) KA. 
Passwords
When a customer starts a search on Thumbtack, they may not be required to set up a password for their account. Customers can access their account using Magic Login (a link sent to their email) without a password. Customers can also view their projects by clicking the links in Thumbtack’s emails sent to them. 
Steps: How to create a password (Customer)
If a customer hasn’t created a password yet, they can set one up: Reset your password. Customers can check out the How to update my password – Thumbtack Help article to learn more.
Password guidelines 
Customers should make sure they're only using the following characters when creating their password:
Letters: Aa to Zz
Numbers: 0 to 9
Symbols: . * & , - @ ' ( ) + ? ! # %

Password resets 
Thumbtack prioritizes the security of our customers. Therefore, Thumbtack does not provide temporary passwords to customers for password reset. Instead, Thumbtack sends a password reset email allowing them to update their passwords. 
If a customer cannot access their email address to reset their password, they can create a new account with their new email. Thumbtack never provides a temporary password to customers.
A customer might have password or login issues because their account is deactivated. If that's the case, reps can refer to the internal Removed or Banned Users KA to see why the account was deactivated.
(Rep) Steps: How to help customer set a password
If a customer needs help setting a password, frontline reps can guide them through the following steps (or skip to step 5 and send them this link: www.thumbtack.com/reset-password). 
Go to www.thumbtack.com and click Log in.
They should enter the email address where they've been getting emails about their project.
In the password field, type in any password and select Log In. 
A notification will appear prompting you to create a password. Click Please create one now.
Enter your email address, then click Send Reset Link
Thumbtack will email them with a link to finish setting up their password. This should arrive within a few minutes, but if they don't see it, have them check their spam / junk folder. 
After they set up their password, they should be able to log in normally from the homepage to view their projects or start new ones. 
Frontline reps can use the following related email templates:
Password Reset - Customer needs to create a password
Password Reset - Link not working - Customer have stated they didn’t receive a reset password email after using the link.
Password: login issues - account deactivated
(Rep) Steps: How to help customer with password issues (troubleshooting)
Support reps should encourage customers to change their own password. However, reps should help customer’s having password issues. 
To help a customer with password issues, Support reps will determine if the customer needs help login by following these steps:

Determine if the customer needs help logging in.
If they can log in, they can change their password by going to Settings > Account > Password, or
Reps can send them this direct link.
If they can't log in, they can go to our login page and click Forgot password. They should receive an email to reset their password.
If they don't get the email, check their account in Admin. 
If the “Subscribe” button is visible next to their email, they are not receiving our emails.
Click Subscribe and ask the customer to click Forgot password again. If they're still not receiving our emails, they can reach out to their email domain to retrieve this reset.
If you don't see the "Subscribe" button and they’re not getting the reset password email, verify their email and perform email troubleshooting (as needed).
If they’re still not getting the email, submit a bug report.
If a customer cannot access their email address to reset their password, they can create a new account with their new email.
Frontline reps can use the following related email templates:
Password Reset - “I can’t get into my email.” - Customer doesn’t have access to email on their account
Password: login issues - account deactivated
Email
 
A customer’s email is the primary piece of information Thumbtack uses to make changes to their account. In order to protect our user’s safety and avoid any risk of fraud, Thumbtack is unable to change their email address for them.
For security reasons, if a customer needs to change their email, they will need to go through the ID Help process. Let the customer know the turnaround is ~3-5 business days. See internal ID Help Reference Guide KA for steps.
Additionally, customers aren’t able to update their email address on their own. If a user attempts to make changes to their email, they will receive an error message stating "Something went wrong. Try again." This error will persist and Thumbtack ask that frontline reps do not submit a bug report regarding this issue.
(Rep) Steps: How to help customer with email address issues (troubleshooting)
If a customer has trouble accessing their account, Support reps will follow these steps: 
Make sure they’re using the right email address. 
Next, ask them if they’re having issues with their email, password, or both. If they're unsure, continue through these steps.
Confirm in Admin that the email address listed under their account matches the address they tried to log in with.
If the email address matches, the issue is likely a password problem. 
If the email address doesn’t match, the pro will need to follow the ID help process. 
Tell the customer to request the email update through the ID Help form. Let the customer know the turnaround is ~3-5 business days. See ID Help Reference Guide KA for steps.

Name on account
Customers can change the name on their account. They don't need to share their ID (or other identifying documents) like pros do when they change their name. 
Frontline reps should:
Encourage customers to use their real name. 
​​Related email template: Ask pro or customer to use legal name - for pros and customers. 
Let them know that when Thumbtack notifies pros about a new job, Thumbtack share their first name and last initial with pros. 
If their name doesn't seem legitimate, pros may not want to work with them. It's important for pros to know they're working with a real person because they pay to meet customers on Thumbtack.
Customer steps: If a customer needs to update their name they can follow the steps on the How to update personal information as a customer – Thumbtack Help article. 
How customer can become a pro
For customers to add to their existing account and become a Thumbtack pro, they will follow these steps: 
Create a password for the account (it they haven't already).
Log in to account.
Go to Thumbtack’s pro sign-up page.
Follow the prompts to sign up as a Thumbtack pro.
After signing up, the customer will need to add to their pro profile before they can start meeting customers. They can learn more about the profile by visiting Thumbtack Help.
Frontline reps can utilize the related email templates: “Customer account details: becoming a pro”
3. Account status
 
Deactivation 
 
(Customer) Steps: How to deactivate account 
Customer steps: To deactivate their account, customers will follow the steps on the How to deactivate a customer account article. 
(Rep) Steps: How to help a customer requesting to deactivate their account
To help a customer deactivate their account, walk them through the steps to do it themselves by submitting the reactivation form. If they’re unable to deactivate their account on their own, Support reps will follow these steps:
Shareable resource: How to reactivate an account – Thumbtack Help 
▶ BEFORE DEACTIVATING (Overcoming customer objections for deactivating account)
Thumbtack wants to help our customers find success on Thumbtack. If a customer asks a frontline rep to deactivate their account, the rep should start by asking why. Depending on why they would like to stop using Thumbtack, the rep might be able to help.  
Objections can be overcome by identifying concerns and offering solutions, but some conditions are beyond our control. These conditions might include:
Moving out of the country
Confusion or lack of understanding of Thumbtack
Too many notifications 
Illness/injury
A few things frontline reps need to remember when helping customers deactivate their account include: 
Support reps keep the following in mind before deactivating an account for a customer: 
Before a frontline rep walks a customer through the steps to deactivate their account, use the information about overcoming objections to help them. 
Walk the customer through the steps to take to deactivate their account themselves. If they’re unable to deactivate their account on their own, Support reps keep the following in mind before deactivating. 
Do make sure there are not three or more requests for reactivation in three months. If there are, escalate the case to your manager to determine next steps
Reps should make sure the customer knows:  
That when they deactivate their account they lose access to all projects, profile information, and reviews written or received on Thumbtack. 
Any verified reviews they left will remain visible on the pro's profile (unless the customer's account was blocklisted).
They must unsubscribe from notifications to stop receiving promo emails and texts.
Reps can reference Notifications (Customers) KA to learn more. 
How to handle common customer objections around deactivation requests 
 
Frontline reps can use the below information about overcoming objections to help a customer before deactivating their account.

Common objection for deactivating account
How to help the customer
Confusion or lack of knowledge
Check how long the customer has been on Thumbtack to get an overall understanding of their experience on the site.
If the customer only recently signed up, or has very little activity on their account, this could show they might not understand the benefits of Thumbtack.
Too many notifications
The best way to identify this concern is to receive this feedback directly from the customer. The number of notifications a customer wants to receive is different from person to person.
To see how many emails we’ve sent a customer, check the "Emails sent" section in Admin. 
Reps can also check the customer’s notifications page to see which notifications are currently on or off.
▶ (Rep) Steps: Customer requests deactivation via email
If a customer requests an account deactivation via email, frontline reps will follow the steps below:
Is the customer from California? 
If so, follow the California Consumer Privacy Act outline in the Sensitive Account Information KA.
What was their reason for deactivation?
If they did provide a reason for deactivation, and we can address their concern, offer a solution.
▶ (Rep) Steps: Customer requests deactivation  via phone / chat/ text
If a customer requests an account deactivation via phone / chat/ text, frontline reps will follow the steps below: 
Start with the why and try to understand the reason for deactivation.
Try to overcome any objections or concerns the customer shares by offering solutions and coaching. 
If we can’t overcome or address their concerns, follow the below steps to deactivate 
Before ending contact with the customer, thank them for contacting us and sharing their feedback with us.
Talking point: Thanks for sharing your feedback about [XYZ] with me. While we're sorry to see you go, we value your input and will use it to improve.
Talking point: Thanks for taking the time to share your experience with me. We wish you the best, and please feel free to reach out to us if you decide to give Thumbtack another shot in the future. 
(Rep) Steps: How to deactivate account on customer's behalf 
 
Steps before deactivating account
To help a customer deactivate their account, frontline reps should walk them through the steps to take to do it themselves. If they’re unable to deactivate their account on their own, reps should do the following before deactivating the account for them.
Check their deletion log under Page Actions in Admin.
If there are three or more requests in three months, follow the steps under Multiple requests for deactivation or reactivation.
Verify at least two additional pieces of information that isn’t general or public information. See Verify Account Information KA to learn more.
For example, their sign up date, zip code of last request, most recent request type, etc.
If you review their deletion log and there are no concerns, deactivate the account.
Steps to deactivate account in Admin
After following the above steps, the frontline can will deactivate a customer's account for them by following these steps: 
Tell them that when they deactivate their account, they'll lose access to their projects, profile information, and the reviews they've left.
If they still want to deactivate their account, in “Actions” (on the top right side of the page), under Legacy Admin Accounts, click Admin Delete. 
Fill out the applicable fields on the deletion page. 
Select a delete reason
Provide a Salesforce task number such as a case or work ticket number
Provide an linked account PK IDs
In the notes box add the reason you're reactivating the account or service profile.
[Image: 7ghdwdIuFMoPTFVzt3gOgRVDRu0FTDuGKicfF3UarhtxxqcMZouAQLTE5g3UBJbCq7vuN4KUJSJy5Bo-bsrV1AlSg0VUFrL8RSYqqRSrDbHb6-wMsvVv5xeqUPotrvcXI1aOIB6pHVqPfVQ-S-e_4k0]
Click Confirm to deactivate the account.
(Rep) Steps: How to handle customer with multiple requests for deactivation / reactivation 
 

If a customer requests to deactivate or reactivate their account and there are three or more deactivation or reactivation requests in the last three months, follow the below steps. 
Review their Deletion Log (under Page Actions in Admin).
If there are no concerns like multiple deletion and reactivation requests: 
Reactivate or deactivate the account as usual. 
If there are two deactivation or reactivation requests in the last ~ two months:  
Let the customer know that if they keep deactivating and reactivating, there's a chance that we will deny their reactivation request.
Talking point: Deactivation of an account is intended to be permanent. 
If there are three or more deactivation/reactivation requests in the last three months:
Submit a request to the Advanced Service Team using the Assist app in Slack for help in determining next steps. 
Navigate to the #service_global_help-and-escalations Slack channel.
Type Escalation (or Esc Other) to trigger the Assist workflow.
Select the "Escalation Others" request type. (If you selected the wrong type, click Cancel and start over.)
Click Open in new window
Complete all required fields including: 
Count of deactivation/reactivation requests and timeframe (e.g., “3 in 90 days”).
Link or summary of Deletion logs reviewed.
Any Trust & Safety / ban-status context from Admin.
Clear ask (e.g., review for reactivation denial/approval).
Click Submit.
Reactivate an account
(Customer) Steps: How to reactivate a customer account
Customer steps: To activate their Thumbtack account, customers will submit the reactivation form. As soon as they submit the form, Thumbtack will get back to them within 2-3 business days. Customers can refer to the How to reactivate an account – Thumbtack Help to learn more. 
(Rep) Steps: How to help a customer reactivate their account
 
When a customer wants to reactivate their account, it’s important Support reps check a few things before reactivating.
Do review the reason an account was deleted by clicking Deletion logs under "Page Actions"
Do double-check that the account hasn’t been blocklisted by Trust and Safety. This is listed in Admin on the user's service profile under “Banned status.”
Do make sure there are not three or more requests for reactivation in three months. If there are, follow the steps under Multiple requests for deactivation or reactivation.
If a customer wants to reactivate their account, frontline reps will follow these steps: 
Find the customer’s account in Admin.
Check their deletion log under Page Actions in Admin.
Deactivated accounts will say "Deleted" or "Disabled" in Admin.
See the reason an account was deleted by clicking Deletion logs under “Page Actions”
Before a rep reactivates an account, double-check that the account hasn’t been blocklisted by Trust and Safety. This is listed in Admin on the user's service profile under “Banned status.”
If they have been deactivated for a T&S concern, transfer the case using the salesforce transfer flow. For steps, see Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA.
Make sure there aren’t any concerns on the account that need to be addressed (T&S or otherwise).
If there are three or more deactivations / reactivations in three months, don’t reactivate the account. Follow steps under “Multiple requests for reactivation/deactivation” section.
In “Page Actions” (on the top right side of the page), click Admin Undelete.
Add the reason you're reactivating the account.
Click Confirm to activate the account.  
Data Summary and Deletion
(Rep) How to help a customer requesting a summary of or deletion of their data
If a customer reaches out wanting a summary of their account information or permanent deletion of their data, they will submit the Data Retrieval or Deletion Request form. For frontline reps to learn more about this process, refer to the Sensitive Account Information| Article #000010703.
Users can also begin this process by selecting Request access to or delete personal data (Delete My Account Data on IOS and Android) in their account settings.

[Image: AD_4nXeN8NyMeNZxctMSAgu-7Otw7ivWVln_cNAN9hfT13m6tMLc1vKU-fw4EXWUNdnzfX_XhzXuvILsEsdJZJ3SbbraefgCf-YC7WvAaCphYfKO7rMwPxdGStD49VoGUs6uHtGmZzQ_]


4. Talking points 

 Login
Customer asked to log in
Why do I have to log in so often? (Customer is on the app)
We've updated our account security settings so you're now asked to log in every 30 days. This helps us protect your account and keep your business and personal information private.
¿Por qué tengo que iniciar sesión con tanta frecuencia?
Hemos actualizado la configuración de seguridad de nuestra cuenta, por lo que ahora se le pedirá que inicie sesión cada 30 días. Esto nos ayuda a proteger su cuenta y mantener la privacidad de su información comercial y personal.
Why do I have to log in so often? (Customer is on web)
We've updated our account security settings so you're now asked to log in every 180 days. This helps us protect your account and keep your business and personal information private.
¿Por qué tengo que iniciar sesión con tanta frecuencia?
Hemos actualizado la configuración de seguridad de nuestra cuenta, por lo que ahora se le pedirá que inicie sesión cada 180 días. Esto nos ayuda a proteger su cuenta y mantener la privacidad de su información comercial y personal.
Login issues 
Why can't I log in? (account deactivated by customer)
I'm sorry to hear you've had trouble logging in to your account. Our system shows that your Thumbtack account was deactivated by user on [DATE], which is why you weren’t able to log in. I’ve reactivated your account, so you can now log in.
If you have any trouble remembering your password, you can reset your password. You’ll receive a password reset email with next steps. If you don’t see an email, be sure to check your spam folder.
¿Por qué no puedo iniciar sesión? (cuenta desactivada)
Lamento saber que ha tenido problemas para iniciar sesión en su cuenta. Nuestro sistema muestra que el usuario desactivó su cuenta Thumbtack el [FECHA], por lo que no pudo iniciar sesión. He reactivado su cuenta, por lo que ahora puede iniciar sesión.
Si tiene algún problema para recordar su contraseña, puede restablecerla. Recibirá un correo electrónico para restablecer la contraseña con los siguientes pasos. Si no ve un correo electrónico, asegúrese de revisar su bandeja de correo no deseado.
Phone number
 
Customer is unable to submit a job request (due to phone number)
I'm sorry to hear you're having trouble submitting your job request on Thumbtack. It looks like the phone number you're trying to use is already linked to a few other accounts on our platform. To help keep Thumbtack working well for everyone, we limit how often a phone number can be used across different accounts. This helps make sure pros connect with unique and active customers. I can help you with this by manually adding this phone number to your account for you now.
El cliente no puede enviar una solicitud de trabajo (por número de teléfono)
Lamento que esté teniendo problemas para enviar su solicitud de trabajo en Thumbtack. Parece que el número de teléfono que está intentando usar ya está vinculado a varias cuentas en nuestra plataforma. Para que Thumbtack funcione correctamente para todos, limitamos la cantidad de veces que un número de teléfono puede usarse en diferentes cuentas. Esto nos ayuda a garantizar que los profesionales se conecten con clientes únicos y activos. Puedo ayudarle con esto agregando manualmente este número de teléfono a su cuenta ahora mismo. Solo indíqueme si desea que lo haga, y con gusto me encargaré de ello.

Password
Password guidelines
What are the guidelines for passwords?
Make sure you're only using the following characters when creating your password:
Letters: Aa to Zz
Numbers: 0 to 9
Symbols: . * & , - @ ' ( ) + ? ! # %
¿Cuáles son las normas para las contraseñas?
Asegúrese de que solo está utilizando los siguientes caracteres al crear su contraseña:
Letras: Aa a Zz
Números: 0 a 9
Símbolos:. * &, - @ '() +? ! #%
Customer wants rep to reset their password 
Will you reset my password for me?
For security reasons, I can't reset your password myself, but I can walk you through how to reset it on your end. If it’s easier, I can also send you an email to reset your password. Let's start by making sure your account is active and double-checking your email address.
¿Puedes restablecer mi contraseña?
Por razones de seguridad, no puedo restablecer su contraseña yo mismo, pero puedo explicarle cómo restablecerla. Si es más fácil, también puedo enviarle un correo electrónico para restablecer su contraseña. Comencemos asegurándonos de que su cuenta esté activa y revisando su correo electrónico.
Customer can’t remember password

I can't remember my password
I'm sorry you're having trouble logging in. Reset your password and we'll send you an email with next steps. Check your spam folder if you don’t find the email in your inbox.
When you choose a new password, remember passwords are case-sensitive and they must contain at least eight characters.
No recuerdo mi contraseña
Lamento que tenga problemas para iniciar sesión. Restablezca su contraseña y le enviaremos un correo electrónico con los siguientes pasos. Revise su bandeja de correo no deseado si no encuentra el correo electrónico en su bandeja de entrada.
Cuando elija una nueva contraseña, recuerde que las contraseñas distinguen entre mayúsculas y minúsculas y deben contener al menos ocho caracteres.
Customer did’t request a password reset 
I didn't request a password reset
Thank you for reaching out and letting us know you didn’t request your password to be reset. Since you didn’t request it, we recommend that you update your password for security purposes. You can do so in your settings.
Make sure your password is strong by using a combination of letters, numbers and symbols. Phrases also are stronger than just a single word. The following characters are accepted when creating your password:
- Letters: Aa to Zz
- Numbers: 0 to 9
- Symbols: . * & , - @ ' ( ) + ? ! # %
No solicite un restablecimiento de contraseña
Gracias por comunicarse con nosotros y hacernos saber que no solicitó el restablecimiento de su contraseña. Como no lo solicitó, le recomendamos que actualice su contraseña por motivos de seguridad. Puede hacerlo en su configuración.
Asegúrese de que su contraseña sea segura utilizando una combinación de letras, números y símbolos. Las frases también son más fuertes que una sola palabra. Se aceptan los siguientes caracteres al crear su contraseña:
- Letras: Aa a Zz
- Números: 0 a 9
- Símbolos:. * &, - @ '() +? ! #%
Email address
I need to update my email address.
I can email you with the information on how to update your email address. That way you can have it for the future.
Necesito actualizar mi dirección de correo electrónico.
Le puedo enviar un correo electrónico con la información sobre cómo actualizar su dirección de correo electrónico. De esa manera, podrá tenerla para el futuro.
Can’t you just change it for me?
I’m sorry, but your email is the primary piece of information we use to make changes to your account, including changes that would cause charges to your account. In order to protect your safety and avoid any risk of fraud, we are unable to make that change for you.
¿No pueden cambiarlo por mí?
Lamento mucho no poder hacerlo. Su dirección de correo electrónico es la información más importante que usamos para realizar cambios en su cuenta, incluidos los cambios que podrían generar cargos. Para proteger su seguridad y evitar cualquier riesgo de fraude, no podemos cambiar esa información por usted.
Deactivation requests
Customer wants to deactivate account   
I want to deactivate my account.
I’m happy to help you. Is there a specific reason why you’ve decided to deactivate your account? If there is, I’d love to learn more about your experience so we can improve.
Quiero desactivar mi cuenta.
Estoy feliz de poder ayudarle. ¿Existe algún motivo específico por el que haya decidido desactivar su cuenta? Me encantaría saber más sobre su experiencia para que podamos mejorar.
Handling objections around deactivation requests 
I don't understand how Thumbtack works.
I’d like to explain a little more about how Thumbtack works, because I think Thumbtack could work really well for you if you’re willing to give it another shot.
No entiendo cómo funciona Thumbtack.
Me gustaría explicar un poco más sobre cómo funciona Thumbtack, porque creo que Thumbtack podría funcionar muy bien para usted si está dispuesto a darle otra oportunidad.
I'm getting too many emails/texts/push notifications.
I'm sorry we've been sending too many emails. That definitely wasn’t our intention and we don’t want to overwhelm you. I can help you adjust your notification settings for marketing emails so that you hear from us less or not at all. I’ll also show you where you can adjust these settings for the future. That way, you can continue using Thumbtack on your terms and get our notifications however much (or little) you want.
Recibo demasiados correos electrónicos / mensajes de texto / notificaciones automáticas.
Lamento que le enviamos demasiados correos electrónicos. Definitivamente esa no era nuestra intención y no queremos abrumarlo. Puedo ayudarle a ajustar la configuración de sus notificaciones para que tenga menos noticias nuestras o ninguna. También le mostraré dónde puede ajustar esta configuración para el futuro. De esa manera, puede continuar usando Thumbtack bajo sus términos y recibir nuestras notificaciones por mucho (o poco) que desee.
Reactivation request
Customer thought account was deactivate but it's active
Why is my account disabled? (account is active, but notifications were off)
It looks like your account is still active, but your notifications are turned off. I’ve turned them back on for you, so you’ll start seeing our notifications within 24 hours. I'll send you our article with steps for adjusting your notifications. 
¿Por qué mi cuenta está desactivada? (la cuenta está activa, pero las notificaciones están desactivadas)
Parece que su cuenta aún está activa, pero sus notificaciones están desactivadas. Ya las volví a activar, por lo que comenzará a ver nuestras notificaciones en 24 horas. Le enviaré nuestro artículo con los pasos para ajustar sus notificaciones.
Reactivate request but customer account won’t be reconsidered 
I don’t agree with the decision to not reactivate my account. How can I dispute it? (decision won’t be reconsidered)
The Trust and Safety team doesn’t make these decisions lightly. Because of this, the decision won’t be reconsidered.
No estoy de acuerdo con la decisión de no reactivar mi cuenta. ¿Cómo puedo disputarlo? (la decisión no será reconsiderada)
El equipo de Confianza y Seguridad no toma estas decisiones a la ligera. Debido a esto, la decisión no será reconsiderada.
Why can’t you give me more information about why my account won’t be reactivated?
I understand this means a lot to you. Accounts are removed by our Trust and Safety team for a variety of reasons. Because of this, I don’t have specific details to share with you, but you can find that information in the email we sent you about your account.
If you would like more information, you can find an email from noreply@thumbtack.com or support@thumbtack.com. We sent it to the email address on your account – be sure to check your spam folder.
¿Por qué no puede proveer más información sobre la razón por la cual no se reactivará mi cuenta?
Entiendo que esto significa mucho para usted. Nuestro equipo de Confianza y Seguridad elimina las cuentas por diversas razones. Debido a esto, no tengo detalles específicos para compartir con usted, pero puede encontrar esa información en el correo electrónico que le enviamos sobre su cuenta.
Si desea obtener más información, puede encontrar un correo electrónico de noreply@thumbtack.com o support@thumbtack.com. Lo enviamos a la dirección de correo electrónico de su cuenta; asegúrese de revisar su bandeja de correo no deseado.

1. Overview
▶ 🤖 Background notes
This section gives an overview of account holds on pro accounts. It lists the reasons a pro account may be on hold.
An account hold (previously called "quote gating") prevents a pro from appearing in search results or pursuing new opportunities until they either resolve an issue with their account or finish certain sign-up steps.
A pro can have more than one hold at a time. Holds are placed for any of the following reasons (each is detailed in Section 3):
Profile issues
General issues / needs coaching (includes content removal  and refund gaming)
Past due balance
Chargebacks
Early fraud warnings (EFW)
Open dispute in Thumbtack Solution Center (TSC)
Reactive incidents or concerning reviews
Identity status / ID verification
What pros can do while on hold 
When a pro’s account is placed on hold, they will receive an email with information about what actions they need to take. Additionally, pros will see a banner at the top of their account informing them of actions they need to take (“Heads-up! You’re not appearing in search results…).
▶ Example 1: The Heads-ups banner explains, “A customer opened a dispute with you in the Thumbtack Solution Center. Find a resolution now.

[Image: 4rjXw8IyzhRz5ra1ws_OKLw2YwK0yNC6O-8cNCZKtxQYMECyzcQ2Ein8kRF-hsAL7jHWrbxuhrIwWQUtLmdO5pVua1YcQ_FBurQQn2uaK9yFN4vX_J5uJuwoIVxFsbhTs51dLBiUiBMkyKz1TKgyivf1oPQf_MsXvLx-7rIVBN6S3Mn0GXDK-yDhJQ]

▶ Example: 2: The Heads-up banned explains, “You can’t access leads until you resolve a payment error.”

[Image: bYVQjq7oK69BAvtpyjCaRsDGk14qb5rV9MCnXXnF5JzSLAHEQXH5M1D2xGV0USDj9tzNm4SAZTjkjtuPjgSws5d69HutdomaviYKIiQQCS96qMFfb8rLxFJt5250ydcW-PO9Odkb2rmT1oTo8nYGMw6V1MvGljYCp0kKWnFzdtDjbhuoHj-dbVEr1A]

They can still:
Log in to their account
View messages they've already sent
Access their account settings
Update their profile
Depending on the reason, the hold either clears automatically once the pro fixes the issue, or must be removed manually by T&S. (See Section 4.)
For related scenarios, see the Checking account statuses and Handling deleted requests sections of the internal Removed or Banned Users (Pro) (Customer) KA.
Automatic profile quality checks
Thumbtack automatically runs checks in the background during sign-up and whenever a pro's profile is created or their business introduction or Q&A section is edited. These cover two things: the pro's identity and verification status, and the quality of their profile content.
Profile quality checks
If content issues are detected, the profile is placed on hold until the pro resolves them. The pro is not notified unless action is taken — when a hold is placed, they receive an automated email and see a banner prompting them to update their profile. A profile may be held for:
Not in English
"Test" or gibberish content
Non-US service location
Barter or free services
Contact avoidance
Mismatched category
Other
(See Profile issues below for how reps handle these holds.)
How account holds are removed (automatically and manually)
Some account holds will be automatically removed once a pro makes the needed updates, and others require a T&S specialist to manually remove them. An account hold can only be removed by a T&S specialist (Incident Ops and Proactive Ops).
Account holds that clear automatically

A pros account hold will be removed automatically once they've updated their profile to meet our community standards. It can take up to 15 minutes for their service profile to be re-verified and automatically restored.

Frontline reps should follow these steps when helping a pro with an account hold: 
Review the profile on their own, and explain to the pro why their profile is on hold and how they can update their profile. 
Don’t slack #ts-incident-ops-questions to remove the hold. 
Don't send a profile to Trust and Safety to remove an account hold if the pro hasn't updated their profile. Even if they say they'll "do it later."

Account holds that need manually review

Once a rep believes the pro's profile meets our Terms of Use, the rep:
Transfer the case to Trust and Safety using the Salesforce Transfer flow. Make sure to include the Pros admin link in the internal case notes.
See Trust and Safety Incidents (Pro) (Customer) KA for transfer steps

ID verification and multiple identities
This section discusses account holds related to the verification of account ownership, particularly when multiple identities are associated with an account.
In the past, we weren’t consistently verifying the account owner. This led to accounts having 2+ names and identities, making it hard for us to verify the account owner. 
To improve trust and safety on Thumbtack:
 
We require pros with 2+ identities to verify who owns the account by filling out the ID Help Intake Form. This includes pros who have uploaded a license that doesn't match their account name. 
In order for us to verify a pro's license, the first and last name, and the business name on both the license and the Thumbtack account must match. See Licenses KA. 
If pros don’t get this info to us within seven business days, we’ll remove the account until we receive and review their information. It typically takes about seven business days to review each ID submission.
Steps: How to handle deletion log notes for ID verification: (Rep)
If a frontline rep reviews a pro’s deletion log and sees that it mentions ID verification, follow these steps: 
Guide the pro to their inbox to find the email we sent them.
Let them know we’re asking for this info to build trust and safety on our site.
Use the talking points below to help navigate these conversations. 
Tell the pro to fill out the ID Help Intake Form. This shouldn’t be sent to any other support channels. 
Use the macro ‘Ask pro to send info to ID Help’.
Ask them to explain why there are multiple identities on their account.
Let them know that they don’t have to send this information to us if they don’t want to, but they won’t be able to use Thumbtack if they don’t.
For more info on ID Help, refer to the internal ID Help Guide KA.

Thumbtack uses AI to automatically identify and redact contact information. Refund gaming

Frontline Reps can use the following information to help pros whose accounts are on hold for misusing the refund policy.
What it means
The pro is suspected of "gaming" (misusing) the refund policy (e.g., submitting altered screenshots or coaching customers to lie for refunds).  
[Internal details only:  Thumbtack uses a three-warning system for refund gaming:
1st and 2nd occurrence: Advanced Service team places a hold and sends a warning. The pro must acknowledge the policy to lift the hold.
3rd occurrence: The account is permanently deactivated and blocklisted.
Revenue check: For pros with over $1,000 in annual revenue, AST reviews the case more carefully before deactivating.]
Where it appears in Admin
Pro Account hold flags (Details): User has general issues or needs coaching
Pro account hold logs (notes): "1st/2nd Refund gaming warning sent"

How pros resolve this account hold reason: 
For the 1st and 2nd warnings, the pro must reply to the warning email to acknowledge and agree to Thumbtack’s Terms of Use, Code of Conduct, and Refund Policy. 
Once acknowledged, the Advanced Service Team (AST) will lift the hold. 
Afterward, any future refund requests or disputes by the pro will be treated as business as usual.

How reps can help pros with this type of hold reason:
Direct the pro to find the "Refund Policy Violation Warning" email in their inbox or spam folder. 
Explain that they must reply to that email to resolve the issue. 
Do not provide specific examples of the detected gaming. (See talking point: “Can you show me exactly what I did wrong or give me examples of "gaming?”).
[Internal note: To identify gaming indicators in a refund request, see “Steps: How to handle suspected refund gaming (Rep)” in the internal Lead Refunds (Pro) KA.]
▶ Internal Process: Advanced Service Team (AST) Workflow for gaming holds
As part of Thumbtack’s Terms of Use for gaming violations, AST will follow a structured and consistent process: Pros will receive two warnings, and on the third occurrence, the account will be eligible for deactivation.
AST will follow these steps when they get a new refund gaming report:
Check the pro’s account for signs of refund gaming. To identify gaming indicators, see “Steps: How to handle suspected refund gaming (Rep)” in the internal Lead Refunds (Pro) KA.
Reach out to #weekly-leads-caliberations-refunds and tag Akiko. Provide details that were gathered after investigating.
If AST confirms that the pro is misusing Thumbtack’s refund policy:
Determine if the pro is in a managed account. For help with how to confirm if a pro is in a managed account see the internal Managed Accounts (Pro) KA.
If the pro is not in a managed account: Proceed with “Confirmed refund gaming: 1st & 2nd Warning (AST Process)” below.
If the pro has a managed account: Reach out to the pro’s account manager (AM). The AM can connect with the pro directly and provide coaching.
If AST can’t confirm that the pro is misusing Thumbtack’s refund policy, let the rep know so the rep can handle the case as usual.
▶ Confirmed refund gaming: 1st & 2nd Warning (AST Process):
If AST confirms that the pro is refund gaming and its the first or second occurrence, AST will follow these steps:
AST will use a tracker to monitor cases and document the actions taken for pros confirmed to be engaging in gaming.
Create a Quick Case with the subject “Refund Policy Violation Warning.” 
Add an “Unprofessional Behavior” flag in Salesforce. 
▶ Unprofessional Behavior pill should contain:
Case number.
Actions taken.
Examples: 
“Case XXXXX | Issued 1st Refund Gaming Warning & placed pro’s account on blocklisted hold. Pro must reply to the email confirming acknowledgement and agreement with our TOU, Code of Conduct and Refund Policy before the hold can be reviewed for removal.”
“Case XXXXX | Issued 2nd Refund Gaming Warning & placed pro’s account on blocklisted hold. Pro must reply to the email confirming acknowledgment and agreement with our TOU, Code of Conduct and Refund Policy before the hold can be reviewed for removal. If a pro is found to repeat this behavior in the future, the account will be permanently closed.”
Place pro’s account on hold:
In the pro’s admin page, click Add Pro Account Hold.
Select User has general issues or needs coaching.
Enter the case number, the actions completed, and the next steps needed.
Example: “Case XXXXXX | 1st/2nd Refund gaming warning sent. Pro must acknowledge and agree to our TOU, Code of Conduct & Refund policy.”
Send email template: "1st Refund Gaming Warning" or "2nd Refund Gaming Warning" depending on which warning the pro is on.
Within the quick case, provide a summary of events like actions implemented, and planned next steps. 
Close the case under Support > Escalations > Escalations Support.
If the pro responds to the email with push backs or asking for clarification, AST can use the email templates "Refund Gaming - Pro Pushes back" or "Refund Gaming – Clarification on Warning."
▶ To lift a hold for refund gaming (AST Process):
If the pro acknowledges the Refund Gaming Warning Email for the first or second refund gaming occurrence, AST will follow these steps:
Once the pro acknowledges the Refund Gaming Warning Email, go to Admin and click Remove Pro Account Hold. 
Reason: User has been coached for the given issues.
Salesforce ticket number: Enter the case number associated with the refund gaming warning email.
Example: “Case xxxxx | Pro acknowledged and agreed to 1st/2nd Refund gaming warning email.”
Reply to the pro using the “Refund Gaming – Pro Acknowledges Warning” email template. 
Add notes in the case and actions taken.
Close the case under Support > Escalations > Escalations Support.
▶ Deactivating the account for refund gaming (business decision) (AST Process):
AST will follow these steps if its the pro’s 3rd occurrence of refund gaming:
Before deactivating an account on the third refund gaming occurrence, AST should review the pro’s revenue to help determine the next steps:
For low-revenue professionals, deactivation can proceed once the warning threshold is met (unless the account is managed). Proceed with step 2.
For higher-revenue professionals ($1,000 revenue per year and above), the situation should be reviewed more carefully before moving forward with the deactivation. Use the email template: "Refund Gaming - Special Cases Final Warning"
Create a quick case with the subject: Refund Policy Violation Warning.
Add an unprofessional warning flag in Salesforce.
▶ Unprofessional pill should contain:
Case number.
Actions taken.
Example: “Case XXXX | Pro’s account will no longer be reconsidered due to refund gaming. Business decision.”
Deactivate the pro’s account, and any other accounts the pro may have.
Open the pro’s admin page and select Admin Delete.
Choose Other for the reason.
Add details to the Notes.

Add a blocklist to the pro’s account.
Open the pro’s admin page and select Add User to Blocklist.

Block the pro from Phone Support.
In the case, click the pro’s name in the Thumbtack user section.
Scroll down to Routing and Segmentation.

If they haven’t received an email, go to the pro’s Admin page.
Check their service.
Review the deletion log.
Explain to the pro why their service was removed and guide them to create a new service that meets our community guidelines.
5. Talking points
Frontline Reps can use the following externally approved talking points when navigating conversations with customers regarding account information.
General account hold

English talking points
Spanish talking points
Why is my account on hold? What does that mean? 
¿Por qué está en alto mi cuenta? ¿Qué significa eso?
An account hold means there’s an issue with your account and you won’t appear in search results or be able to reach out to new customers until you take care of it. I’d be happy to let you know what you need to do, but if you have specific questions I’ll need to get you over to our Trust and Safety Team who handles these issues.
Un alto de cuenta significa que hay un problema con su cuenta y que no aparecerá en los resultados de búsqueda ni podrá comunicarse con nuevos clientes hasta que lo solucione. Me complace informarle lo que debe hacer, pero si tiene preguntas específicas, tendré que ponerlo en contacto con nuestro Equipo de Confianza y Seguridad el cual se encarga de estos problemas.
Why am I not appearing in search results anymore?
¿Por qué ya no aparezco en los resultados de búsqueda?
It looks like you have a few things to take care of before you can start appearing in search results. If you have specific questions I’ll need to get you over to our Trust and Safety Team who handles these issues.
Parece que tiene algunas cosas de las que ocuparse en su cuenta antes de que pueda comenzar a aparecer en los resultados de búsqueda. Me complacerá informarle lo que debe hacer, pero si tiene preguntas específicas, tendré que ponerlo en contacto con nuestro Equipo de seguridad y confianza (Trust and Safety), que se encarga de estos problemas.
Can you show me exactly what I did wrong or give me examples of "refund gaming"?
 ¿Puede mostrarme exactamente qué hice mal o darme ejemplos de "manipulación de reembolsos"?
We understand you’d like more details, and while we can’t share specific examples to protect the integrity of our detection system, please know that every action was carefully reviewed before being taken.
 Entendemos que quiera recibir más detalles. Aunque no podemos compartir ejemplos específicos para proteger la integridad de nuestro sistema de detección, sepa que revisamos cuidadosamente cada acción antes de realizarla.
Account verification removal

English talking points
Spanish talking points.
Why was my account removed? 
¿Por qué se eliminó mi cuenta?
We’re always working to make Thumbtack safer for pros and customers. As part of that effort, we’re asking pros to send a photo of a government-issued photo ID (like a driver’s license). We emailed you with the steps to take, so let’s check your inbox.
Siempre estamos trabajando para hacer que Thumbtack sea más seguro para profesionales y clientes. Como parte de ese esfuerzo, estamos pidiendo a los profesionales que envíen una foto de una identificación válida (como una licencia de conducir). Le enviamos un correo electrónico con los pasos a seguir, así que vamos a revisar su bandeja de entrada.
I didn’t even see the warning email. 
Ni siquiera vi el correo electrónico de advertencia.
If you can’t find the email, try searching your spam folder. In the meantime, I can walk you through what you need to do. You can fill out the ID Help Intake Form. We’ll reach out with any updates about it.

(Via Email: Send the template ‘Ask pro to send info to ID Help’.)
Si no encuentra el correo electrónico, intente buscar en su carpeta de spam. Mientras tanto, puedo guiarte a través de lo que necesitas hacer. Puede llenar el Formulario de Admisión de Ayuda de identificación. Nos pondremos en contacto con cualquier actualización al respecto.
