What the fix budget discount experiment is
Starting July 20, 2026 (date subject to change), Thumbtack is testing a fixed budget discount (FBD), which gives pros 5% off all exact match leads. 
What’s a fixed budget? 
Based on a pro's market and lead price settings, Thumbtack provides a recommended budget, which is a specific dollar amount. Pros will only see this recommended amount if it is higher than their current budget. This option is distinct from a custom budget and may be referred to as a recommended, fixed, or set budget. 
Reps can refer to the internal Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro) KA, "Understanding Recommended Budgets" section, for how the Recommended budget amount is calculated.
Why Thumbtack is running this experiment
Internal why: The unlimited budget discount drove strong revenue and lead gains, but many pros who accepted it switched back to a fixed budget within days — removing their budget cap entirely felt too risky for them. This experiment targets those same pros with a smaller, more accessible commitment.
External why: To give pros a way to save on leads with predictable spend control, without requiring them to remove their weekly budget cap.
How the experiment works 
Pros who are eligible for the existing unlimited budget discount (UBD) may now see a second option: increase their weekly budget to a fixed budget to earn 5% off leads, instead of setting an unlimited budget to earn 10% off.
What a pro sees depends on which offers they're eligible for at that moment — the fixed budget discount (5% off), the unlimited budget discount (10% off), and BOSUP (free leads after maintenance period) are three separate offers a pro can be eligible for in different combinations. 
If a pro accepts a fixed budget discount offer, the discount will be applied to all their leads and does not apply to opportunities, prepaid jobs, or other lead types. 
Reps can refer to Pro experience below for the three combinations this experiment can produce and how they differ.
Experiment details
This section provides details about the Fixed budget discount experiment. 
[Internal note: Experiment dates below are anticipated and subject to change. Thumbtack may adjust the launch date, end the experiment early, or extend it based on results.]
Experiment run dates: July 20, 2026 
Duration: ~ 8 weeks 
Anticipated end date:  ~ September 14, 2026
Who is included:  Pros eligible for the unlimited budget discount. For a closer look, see Fixed budget eligibility below. 
Who is excluded: 
New pros within their first 30 days on Thumbtack
Pros already on an unlimited budget.
Location: Nationwide 
Internal name: Fixed Budget % Discount (FBD)
External name: Special offer
Priority level: P2 — low impact and medium priority (See the “Experiments and feature priority levels” section in the Current Running Experiments (Rep) KA).
Fixed budget discount eligibility
Pros who are eligible for the existing unlimited budget discount may now see a fixed budget discount offer. To be eligible for an unlimited budget discount (UBD), the pro must be in an underserved market. 
One thing to note is that these offers aren't shown to pros in an underserved market who have: 
Not been active in the past 7 days OR
0 lifetime verified reviews OR
0 contacts in the last 30 days
Multi-business users are also eligible for these offers. As of July 1, 2026, the discount system operates at the user level, not the business level. This means a discount earned on a pro's user account can be used by any business profile. This restriction was lifted the day before this experiment's July 2, 2026 launch, so multi-business pros are included in FBD and UBD from the start.
[Internal note: Pros who already had a user-level unlimited budget discount before July 1, 2026 aren't affected by this change, unless they lower their budget and later accept a new offer — in which case the user-level system applies to that new offer.]
Fixed budget discount terms
This section outlines the specific terms and conditions for the fixed budget discount (FBD) offer:
FBD persists as long as the pro keeps a fixed budget.
FBD is removed immediately if a pro switches to a budget lower than what they have set. 
FBD can upgrade to UBD if eligible. Doing so removes the 5% discount and applies the 10% discount instead.
UBD can downgrade to FBD if eligible. Doing so removes the 10% discount and applies the 5% discount instead.  
FBD does not apply to opportunities, prepaid jobs , or other lead types. 
Thumbtack may modify or end this promotion at any time. If the promotion ends, Thumbtack will notify pros in advance.
NOTE: This offer may not always appear in a pros account. Availability can change and Thumbtack may update or remove the offer in the future. See Fixed budget eligibility to learn more.
How this works with other discounts and promotions
There are various programs that give pros a discount on leads, credits toward future leads, and free leads. Here’s how those different programs work with the fixed budget discount: 

Discount or promotion
What it is
Stacks with the fixed budget discount?
How it’s applied
Unlimited budget discount
10% off exact match leads
No — mutually exclusive. A pro earns one discount at a time.
Pro either gets 5% or 10%, not both. 
BOSUP (Budget Overserving Upsell)
Free leads 
Compatible.
Discount applies after free leads are gone or expired (free leads are the higher-value benefit, so they're used first)
SLA rebates (Large Local / National accounts)
Credit to Thumbtack balance
Yes — SLA rebates are contractual credits tied to a MASA and operate independently from per-lead discounts.
Lead is discounted and uses credits from Thumbtack balance to pay for it.
Other platform promotions
Discount, credit to Thumbtack balance, or free leads
Yes. (the same way the UBD is today)
Only one discount applies per lead — see note on multiple discounts/promos below. (e.g., free leads used before discount is)
Note on multiple discounts or promotions When a pro has more than one discount or free-lead offer active at the same time, only one applies to a given lead. Thumbtack applies the higher-value discount first and uses it up completely before a lower-value discount begins. Expiration date only decides the order when two discounts are the exact same value. 
Note: The fixed budget discount experiment excludes pros within their first 30 days of Thumbtack. This means there’s no overlap between the new pro discount and being eligible for the FBD. 
2. Pro experience
Baseline experience (Pro)
Today, a pro eligible for the unlimited budget discount has one path to a discount: remove their weekly budget cap entirely (set it to unlimited) to earn 10% off leads. On the Weekly budget page and the Special offer page, a pro may also see a recommended budget amount (fixed budget). A pro who keeps their budget at a recommended or custom amount, without going unlimited, pays full price for leads.
Reps can refer to the internal Weekly Targeting Budget (Pro) KA >  "Unlimited Budget Discount Offer" section, to learn more about the baseline experience.

Experiment experience (Pro)
An eligible pro's recommended budget option — on the same Weekly budget page and Special offer page described above — now also carries a 5% discount tag. The pro earns this discount by setting their weekly budget at or above their recommended budget amount, instead of removing their budget cap entirely to earn the existing 10% unlimited budget discount.
Where pros see an offer is the same as the baseline experience - recommendation cards and a banner on their services page. Both have a “Learn more” to click on which takes them to the special offers page.

Offers a pro may see
Which offers a pro actually sees depends on which of the three programs — fixed budget discount (FBD), unlimited budget discount (UBD), and BOSUP — they're eligible for. This experiment produces at least three distinct combinations:
FBD + UBD  (no BOSUP)
FBD + BOSUP (no unlimited budget option/off)
FBD + UBD  + BOSUP
The two discounts don't stack — a pro earns one discount at a time. A pro on the FBD can upgrade to UBD at any time ONLY if still eligible. Doing so removes the 5% discount and applies the 10% discount instead. 
Unlimited budget + fixed budget offers
Eligible pros who still have budget left for the week and are eligible for an unlimited budget, will see two options on the special offers page: 
Switch to unlimited: Pro sets no budget cap and gets 10% off all exact match leads.
Set to $X per week: Pro sets a recommended budget and gets 5% off all exact match leads. 
To claim the offer, the pro will select the option they want and click “Confirm new budget.” The confirmation screen will explain that they will get a percentage discount on all eligible leads while staying in control of their weekly spend. 
▶ What the special offer and confirmation screens look like

[Image: Image: Special offers page showing Switch to unlimited (10% off leads) and Set to $X per week (5% off leads)]
[Image: Image: Confirmation modal that explains pro gets discount on all eligible leads while staying in control of your weekly spend.]
 

Unlimited budget + fixed budget + BOSUP offer 
An eligible pro may see an offer with four budget options to select from: an unlimited budget and three options to set a fixed budget. And depending on which offer they select, they can get a discount and free leads (BOSUP). 
Unlimited budget: Pro gets 10% off all eligible leads (no free leads are given for selecting this offer)
Fixed budget: Pro selects one of the three budget options, each a specific amount with a different number of free leads. The 5% fixed budget discount only applies to the highest budget increase option. 
For example, an offer may show options to set their budget to:
Don’t limit my budget (10% off leads, no free leads)
$500 for 5 free leads AND 5% off all leads
$400 for 4 free leads
$300 for 3 free leads 
From the special offer page, the pro selects the 5% off (with X free leads) and clicks “Confirm.”
The confirmation screen covers the 5% discount applied  to eligible leads and will get X free leads without lowering their budget for at least 2 weeks. It also mentions the free leads expire after 90 days and if they lower their budget, the discount will end and may not be offered again.
▶ What the special offer and confirmation screens look like

[Image: Image: Special offers page - options: unlimited budget (10% off), $X for X free leads + 5% off, and two options with budget amount and free leads]
[Image: Image: Confirmation modal explains 5% discount on eligible leads, get X free leads to keep budget at least 2 wks]
 

Fixed budget off + BOSUP (no unlimited budget offer) 
An eligible pro may see an offer with three options to select from. Each option has a different budget amount and comes with free leads. The highest budget option is the only one that comes with a fixed discount (5% off exact match leads). 
For example, the screenshots below show options to set their budget to:
$500 for 5 free leads AND 5% off all leads
$400 for 4 free leads
$300 for 3 free leads 
If the pro selects one of the two lower budget options, they will get free leads if they maintain their budget during the maintenance period (2 weeks) but won’t get the discount on leads. 
The pro selects the 5% off option (that also has free leads) and clicks “Confirm” to claim the offer. The confirmation screen explains they’ll get 5% off all eligible leads and free leads if they keep their budget for at least 2 weeks. It also covers free leads expire after 90 days and if they lower their budget, the discount will end and may not be offered again. 
▶ What the special offer and confirmation screens look like

[Image: Image: Special offers page with three budget options, all include free leads. First (highest) budget option also comes with 5% off]
[Image: Image: Confirmation modal explains 5% off eligible leads, get free leads if budget is kept for at least 2 weeks.]
 

Losing the discount
When a pro claims a fixed budget discount (FBD) and BOSUP (free leads) offer, the confirmation page will explain that if they lower their budget, the discount will end and may not be offered again. 
On their budget page, if a pro select “Set a customer amount” or “Set to $X per week” (a recommended budget that’s lower than what is currently set), they’ll see the following warning: 
You'll lose your 5% discount if you lower your budget below $XXX
If a pro sets a custom budget that’s higher than what’s currently set, they will keep the 5% discount. A pro on the FBD can upgrade to unlimited at any time ONLY if still eligible. Doing so removes the 5% discount and applies the 10% discount instead. 
Once a lower budget is saved, the discount is removed immediately. 
▶ What the warning looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

How pros confirm a lead was discounted
Any easy way for a pro to see the discount they receive is on the job details page. Next to the cost of the lead will have a 5% discount offer with the dollar amount that was dedicated from the cost of the lead. 
▶ What the job details page looks like

[Image: Image: Job details with lead price section highlighted. Example is: Direct lead $45.45 5% off offer -$2.27 Total $43.18]

From the Activity tab on their Payments page, pros can click on a line item to see transaction details which includes the discount. The pros receipt will also show the discount in dollars saved, not a percentage. 
3. Talking points

This section provides Frontline Reps with approved talking points for communicating with pros about the fixed budget discount. Use these talking points to ensure consistent and accurate messaging.


English talking point
Q: I’m not ready to switch to this higher budget right now. How long will I have access to this offer?
A: You should always set your budget to what makes the most sense for you and your business. This offer may not always appear in your account and availability can change. Thumbtack may update or remove this offer in the future. As a reminder, you can always try unlimited and change back if you feel it isn't working for you.
Q: How long does the discount last?
A: The discount stays active as long as your budget stays at or above the recommended amount. There is no expiration date at this time. You keep saving as long as your budget stays at that level. If you lower your budget below that amount, the discount will be removed.
Q: Does the 5% fixed budget discount apply to all of my leads?
A: The 5% discount applies to all leads, as long as your business account remains on a fixed budget. The discount does not apply to opportunities, claimable jobs, or other optional lead types. 
Q: Can I switch to an unlimited budget later?
A. Yes, you can always upgrade to unlimited. If you switch to an unlimited budget, you’ll get the higher Unlimited Budget Discount instead. You won’t receive both discounts at the same time.
4. Resources
This section offers Frontline Reps a collection of resources, including links to internal knowledge articles and other materials. Reps can share relevant Help Center articles and external resources with the users as needed.  
Resources for FRONTLINE REPS

Budget Increase Incentive (BOSUP & SOBU) (Pro

Jobber enhanced integration (Pilot)

Contents

Overview
What Jobber is + how it works
Pilot details
How to identify Jobber pros in pilot

Customer experience
How to help pros calling about Jobber

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
This internal knowledge article helps frontline reps support the Jobber Integration pilot for Thumbtack Neighborhoods. It covers how the pilot builds an enhanced CRM integration with Jobber to help power the Neighborhoods feed, along with how it changes the pro experience, and what pros will see and be asked to consent to.

Status
Phase 1 launch 
Phase 2 launch
Feature priority
Impacted user
Live
July 20, 2026
August 3, 2026
P2 — Low impact, medium priority
Thumbtack pros using Jobber, in Neighborhood markets
What is the Jobber integration pilot?
Thumbtack is updating the existing Thumbtack app in the Jobber app marketplace.Today, the Neighborhoods "Happening Soon" feed shows placeholder upcoming service visits (USVs) rather than real, scheduled jobs.
This pilot builds an enhanced CRM integration with Jobber so that pro schedules flow into Thumbtack and populate the USV feed with real, anonymized job data — date, neighborhood, and that a pro is booked nearby.
What Jobber is + how it works

Jobber is a Field Service Management (FSM) software that helps home service business pros organize their entire operation — scheduling jobs, managing crews, invoicing customers, and collecting payments. 
How Jobber works today

New leads created on Thumbtack flow one-way into a pro's Jobber account where they can see their customers’ contact information and details about the job.
▶ What the Thumbtack app on Jobber looks like today (not changing):

[Image: rtaImage]


What's changing (this pilot)

The integration becomes enhanced. All job info in a pro's Jobber account (not just jobs that originated on Thumbtack) flows back into Thumbtack, including:
Job created
Job scheduled / rescheduled
Job status (complete, canceled, etc.)
Job value
Job details
Thumbtack uses this inbound job data to populate anonymized USVs in the Neighborhoods feed.
Because Jobber's data-sharing scope is expanding to include this job info, pros will be asked to re-authorize their Jobber connection via a banner in Jobber (details in Pro experience).
For now, the integration keeps working as-is even if a pro doesn't re-authorize. Re-authorization becomes required once Thumbtack updates its backend API connection — expected around October 15, 2026 (date subject to change). After that point, integrations that haven't been re-authorized will stop working.
NOTE: Thumbtack leads continue to flow to the pro's Jobber account as they do today — that direction of the sync isn't changing.
Pilot details
This section provides details about the Jobber integration pilot, including assignment, launch and end date, and expected impact.
Phases
Phase 1 — Beta
Launch: July 20, 2026 
Audience: ~10 pros enabling enhanced integration, backed by a small outreach campaign.
Goal: Confirm inbound job data is flowing correctly. Once data is flowing, the team (EPAD) tests and irons out issues before opening more broadly.
Phase 2 — Scale
Launch: ~August 3, 2026
Audience: All Jobber-connected pros in Neighborhoods markets.
Goal: Get as many eligible pros as possible to enable the integration, backed by an outreach campaign in eligible markets.
Proactive outreach campaign
Email + Pro Success calls for Jobber pros in Tampa, FL and Charlotte, NC, encouraging them to enable two-way sync.
Pros outside Neighborhoods markets will not receive proactive outreach. However, they may see a Re-athorizate banner in Jobber and could reach out with questions.
Naming
Internal name: Jobber Integration 
External name: Not yet finalized — do not use an external-facing name until confirmed.
Priority level: 
P2 — Low impact, medium priority 
(See the “Experiments and feature priority levels” section in the Current running experiments and pilots (Rep) KA). 
How to identify Jobber pros in pilot
There is no flag, pill, or banner identifying a pro as "in the Jobber pilot.” 
A pro’s job data only starts flowing into Thumbtack once they've consented and turned on the integration. There's nothing visibly different for the pro to notice either way.
To see whether a pros data is flowing in on the backend, reps can refer to the Aug 3rd Target Pro List (internal doc). Reps can search for a pro using their name, email phone number, and user PKID.
See if pro has Jobber quickly 
From the main Pro’s Admin page, reps can look at the Partnership field to see if it says JOBBER. 

[Image: rtaImage]

Confirm active Jobber integration
Reps can also confirm whether any pro has an active Jobber integration by searching "Jobber" in the Supply Partners API section in Admin. Note: this surfaces all integrations platform-wide, not just pilot pros. For pilot eligibility, use the Aug 3rd Target Pro List, not this Admin search.
You’ll go to the pro’s business page in Admin and scroll down to Supply Partners API. You can search Jobber in the search bar.  If the pro has an active Jobber integration, the “is active” column will say Yes. 

[Image: rtaImage]

Pros sending data to power Neighborhoods feed
To see whether a pro's job data is flowing in on the backend in a Neighborhood-enabled market, reps can refer to the Jobber Inbound Data for Neighborhoods + Nationwide Summary  dashboard
Refer to the Thumbtack Neighborhoods V1 (Pro) (Customer) (Pilot) KA to learn more about the neighborhood feed and upcoming service visits. 
Background: How StreetFair used CRM integrations
This isn't a brand-new concept — StreetFair already proved out the core idea before joining Thumbtack.
On StreetFair, pros could directly sync CRM/FSM tools — including Jobber and ServiceTitan — and that sync was used to populate upcoming service visits (USVs), the same underlying concept Neighborhoods uses today. StreetFair's "direct sync" model is effectively the predecessor to this Jobber pilot.
When StreetFair sunset on May 15, 2026, none of those integrations carried over automatically. Pros had to re-link their CRM/FSM tool from scratch within their new Thumbtack account. 
For scale: platform-wide, Thumbtack currently has roughly 1,600 pros integrated with Jobber who received a lead in the past 30 days. Of those, about 20 are former StreetFair pros who re-linked Jobber to their Thumbtack account after the acquisition — a small subset of the existing Jobber-integrated pro base, not the whole thing, and independent of this pilot.
Rep note: If a former StreetFair pro asks whether this is "the same thing StreetFair had," the answer is yes in spirit — it's the same USV-populating idea, rebuilt natively on Thumbtack rather than migrated. Don't imply any StreetFair data or settings transferred; the pro's current Jobber connection to Thumbtack is a new one they set up themselves.
2. User experience
Pro experience
No workflow change. Pros continue to manage jobs in Jobber the same way they always have — Thumbtack leads still flow into Jobber automatically as before.
Nothing breaks if a pro ignores the banner. The connection keeps working until Thumbtack's backend API update (~Oct 15, 2026, subject to change) — after that, un-reauthorized integrations stop working.
Re-authorization 
As covered in What Jobber is + how it works, the expanded data scope means pros need to reauthorize their Jobber connection. Here's what that looks like for them:
▶ A banner in Jobber prompting all Jobber-integrated pros (pilot markets and beyond) to reauthorize access. This is Jobber's standard pattern for any connected app whose permissions change.[Image: rtaImage]
This is the only comms non-pilot-market pros will see — there's no other messaging planned for them.
▶ An updated consent screen reflecting the new access.Only difference: “and jobs” is added[Image: rtaImage]
▶ What the previous consent screen looked like

[Image: rtaImage]

How pros reconfigure / reauthorize access: 
From the banner in Jobber, click Re-Authorize to see the updated OAuth consent screen — it does not show up anywhere in the Thumbtack pro app.
Click Allow Access to approve the updated scope and agree to Jobber's Terms of Service.
Customer experience
There is no customer-facing change in this pilot. The only downstream effect is that the Neighborhoods "Happening Soon" feed will reflect real scheduled jobs instead of placeholder +14 day visits, making the feed more accurate and credible over time as more pros enable the integration.
3. How to help pros calling about jobber
Reps are not expected to be Jobber or integration experts. Use the sections above to understand what this pilot is, why it exists, and what pros will see — that's enough context to recognize what a pro is calling about.
For pros who contact support with actual integration questions, don't try to troubleshoot the technical side yourself: route the call using the decision table below.
Decision: which team handles the call?

If the pro is asking...
Route to
A general question about how the Jobber–Thumbtack integration works today
e.g., "How do leads flow into my Jobber account?", a sync error, or any CRM issue not specific to Neighborhoods
Partnership support (standard process. Steps in Thumbtack Partner Integrations: Activation and Troubleshooting (Pro) KA)
A Neighborhoods + Jobber pilot-specific question, and the pro is on the Aug 3rd Target Pro List 
e.g., “Can homeowners see my customers' job details?"
Post in the #neighborhoods-support Slack channel
A Neighborhoods/pilot-specific question from a pro outside the target list / markets/
Post in the #neighborhoods-support Slack channel
Pros outside Neighborhoods markets may see a re-athorizate banner in Jobber and could reach out with questions. Here’s what reps can say if a pro asks about re-authorization: 
Thumbtack is investing in more enhanced integrations so that we can increase lead quality and the pro experience on Thumbtack.

Your guide to your first two weeks on Thumbtack
[Image: Pill Pro]
[Image: Neighborly Pro Banner]
Welcome to Thumbtack! In this guide, you’ll learn all about how Thumbtack works, hear our best tips, and see them in action through videos and activities.
You’ll learn all about:
How Thumbtack works
Attracting the types of jobs you want
Managing your leads
Managing your money
Responding to your first lead
Ready to dig in? If you don’t have time to do it all today — no sweat! Bookmark this guide on your web browser to make it easier to come back to.
Let’s get started.
SECTION 1
How Thumbtack works
Customers come to Thumbtack every day looking for pros to help them complete their jobs. Pros like you!
In this video, you’ll learn the basics of Thumbtack and how to get your business in front of the right customers.
[Video: Get to know Thumbtack (2:52)]
The rest of this guide will walk you through what to do in your first two weeks on Thumbtack. And we’ll share tips and resources to support you along the way.
SECTION 2
Attracting the types of jobs you want
Getting the right leads can mean a lot of different things. Firstly, do you know what your target market is? Think about what your ideal jobs are — the kind of jobs you really want. Who are those customers?
Then, learn how you can attract those customers to your Thumbtack profile.
Identify your target market
What kind of jobs would be best for your business right now? We’ve listed some questions to help you think through your target market and get your business goals down on paper.
After you decide which jobs you want on Thumbtack, you can refine your matches to let us know which customers you want to be shown to.
To get your ideal leads:
Refine your matches in your Services to tell us the types of jobs you want more of (and less of)
Update your travel areas on your Profile to tell us where you work — this applies across all of your trades.
Update your availability on your Calendar to let us know when you’re available.
As you get set up, we'll suggest job types based on the details you shared when you signed up. You can review and adjust these anytime from your Services page — look for Refine your matches under your trade. Add job types to “Get more like these” or “Get less like these” to help us send you the right leads.
These preferences act as signals that help us learn what's the best fit for your business. The more feedback you give us (like refining your matches or declining leads that aren't right for you), the better your matches get over time.
When you get a lead that matches your preferences, you'll be charged automatically based on your lead price range (more about this in the next section).
Attract your ideal customers
Now that you’ve set the types of jobs you want, how will you draw your ideal customer in? Answer: your profile.
Your profile is how you show customers you’re the best pro for their job. Build an engaging profile and let customers know all about your business. Think about how you talk about your services and how your photos look from a customer’s perspective — what would those customers want to see or read?
Get reviews Before a customer decides to hire you, they want to know what it’s like to work with you. That’s where reviews come in.
Since you’re new to Thumbtack you can get up to 10 reviews from any past customers by sharing your review link. Once Thumbtack customers start hiring you, they can leave you verified reviews. There’s no limit to how many verified reviews you can get.
Or get a head start by adding up to 100 reviews on your Thumbtack profile by importing them over from your Google Business Profile. Learn more about adding Google reviews.
Upload photos Think about the jobs you want and add photos of those types of jobs to your profile. Be sure to write helpful captions for each photo. If a customer sees a photo on your profile similar to what they’re looking to get done, they’ll know they can trust you to do their job. And get creative. Who doesn’t love a before-and-after photo?
[Interactive: Profile Walkthrough Activity — https://xd.adobe.com/embed/2d3cf6df-c9b4-4891-9d9a-dcc8707ec79b-786f/?hints=off]
[Interactive: Attracting the types of jobs - Checklist - Section 2 — https://xd.adobe.com/embed/ce0c821b-3625-4d36-8348-6fa01bfb8062-9b5f/?hints=off]
SECTION 3
Managing your leads
Let’s dive into the reason you’re on Thumbtack right now — jobs.
Customers come to Thumbtack with work to be done. They answer a few questions and then browse pros in their area. If a customer is interested in learning more about you or hiring you right away, they’ll reach out.
Here are the ways you can connect with customers on Thumbtack:
Leads
What are they?
Leads are customers who saw your profile in their search results and reached out to you. These leads match the types of jobs you want and are found in the For you tab on your Jobs page.
Pricing and payments
Because they match your preferences, you pay for these leads automatically. You choose your lead price range for each trade, and we'll use the estimated value of the job to land on a fair price within that range. We’ll cover lead prices in the next section.
Claimable jobs
What are they?
Claimable jobs are ready to go — they match your preferences, and the customer already scheduled the date and time. All you need to do is claim it.
These jobs are available to pros who offer specific service types and meet certain criteria (like having 3 or more reviews). You’ll find them in the For you tab on your Jobs page, where you can browse the details and claim the jobs that are a good fit for you.
Pricing and payments
Thumbtack takes a percentage of the customer's payment, rather than having you pay for the lead upfront. You'll be able to see how much you'll earn for the job before you claim it.
Once you let us know you've completed the job (and set up direct deposit), you’ll get paid. It can take 3-4 business days to show up in your bank account (or, for a 1% fee, earnings can be deposited instantly).
Opportunities
What are they?
Opportunities are customers who haven’t hired a pro yet — they’re still looking for quotes.
You can reach out to these customers to let them know you’re interested in their job, and they can hire you if they think you’re a good fit.
Opportunities are a great way to fill gaps in your schedule. They can be found in the Opportunities tab of your Jobs page.
Pricing and payments
Opportunities have separate pricing from other leads. You’ll see the cost of the Opportunity upfront, and you’re only charged if you decide to reach out and the customer responds to your message.
Take a look at the interactive tool below to see the different leads and get a better understanding of where you’ll find them on your account.
[Interactive: Leads Tour Activity [New pro asset] — https://xd.adobe.com/embed/2cbc659c-e604-4e31-bbc8-4716be03ec01-79ef/?hints=off]
Pro tip
When you first sign up, you can purchase a credit package to get started. When you purchase a package, you get extra credit on your account for free to use on future leads.
SECTION 4
Managing your money
In this section, we'll talk about what you pay for on Thumbtack and how to manage your money. To keep track of your spending and stay within your goals, you’ll set a lead price range, and a weekly budget, and then preload your account balance.
Lead prices
For each trade, you set a lead price range — a minimum and maximum you're willing to pay for a lead. When a lead comes in, we'll use the estimated value of that job to land on a fair price within your range. Smaller, simpler jobs cost less; larger, more complex jobs cost more. You'll never be charged above your maximum.
As you adjust your range, we’ll show you an estimate of how many leads you can expect and how competitive you are in your market. Moving your range up increases your competitiveness and how many leads you get. Moving it down does the opposite. You can update your range anytime from Lead prices on your Services page.
Budget
Based on your lead price range, we’ll recommend a budget. Your budget is a weekly spending limit for leads. It controls how much you can spend in a week. Whenever you get a lead, the cost of that lead counts toward your budget. Once you reach your budget for the week, you’ll stop receiving new leads until your budget resets the following Monday.
Pro tip
If you reach your budget amount for the week but want more leads, you can increase your budget amount. Or you can look into Opportunities since these don’t count toward your budget.
Account balance
Next, let’s talk about your account balance. Preloading your account balance is optional, but it makes payments simpler. As for leads, you'll pay for them using your balance until it runs out.
The amount you preload to your balance is up to you. You could deposit enough to get you through a month, or you could decide to refill your balance weekly — whatever makes the most sense for you.
If you leave auto-refill turned on, your account balance is automatically refilled whenever it runs out.
Tip
Your payment history will show a breakdown of all your charges. You’ll see the cost of each lead and any discounts that were applied.
[Interactive: Paid checklist — https://xd.adobe.com/embed/7753e7bb-32c5-4712-968c-8b6bee73d77e-2200/]
SECTION 5
Responding to your first lead
You’re all set up and ready to go, and you just received your first lead on Thumbtack. Now what? Let’s go over how responding thoughtfully (and quickly!) can help you make the most out of each message — and get your first of many hires.
Send a great message
How should you respond? Before jumping in, read through the customer’s job details and message to understand their unique needs. Then, follow these tips:
Personalize your message. For example, greet the customer by their name.
Provide them with helpful details about their specific job.
Mention your skills and credentials to show you’re qualified for the job.
Give the customer clear next steps so they know how to move forward with you.
Do a last-minute spell check and make sure your message covers everything you want to say before you send it off.
Respond quickly to new leads
Each minute counts. Try to respond or call as quickly as possible — you might catch the customer online and when they’re motivated to hire. But if you can’t get to it right away, aim to respond within an hour.
Here’s why responsiveness matters:
You're more likely to hear back from customers.
It affects your rank in search results.
It helps you qualify for Gold and Platinum Pro Rewards.
Responding thoughtfully and quickly? Sounds like a tall order. Luckily we’ve got a few tools that can help:
Download our pro app to be notified of new leads while you’re on the go.
Use AI-written replies to respond faster with a draft tailored to the lead — send it as-is, edit it, or write your own.
Createquick replies to make responding to customers faster and easier.
Let Front Desk manage your messages for you — so you can stay focused on the job at hand.
Connect your Thumbtack account to apps to manage your leads and messages alongside the other tools you already use.
Follow up with customers
If you don’t hear back from a customer, try sending them a follow-up message to reconnect and move things forward. We recommend sending a follow-up message after about 24 - 48 hours.
Tip
Want to see how a specific lead is progressing? Open your messenger with the customer, tap the three-dot menu (on the top right corner), and select View Competition. Here you can check response times and customer activity for that lead. Responding quickly and keeping your conversation on Thumbtack can also help you qualify for certain refunds.
[Interactive: Messaging Activity [New pro asset] — https://xd.adobe.com/embed/6cb39d34-ac1d-454d-a28b-53520fb40795-39e0/?hints=off]
[Interactive: Messaging - Checklist - Section 4 — https://xd.adobe.com/embed/23595f5e-9c6e-4d5d-8379-2201e973f3b5-760a/?hints=off]
IN CONCLUSION
One last note
Congrats! You’ve learned the basics of Thumbtack. And if you apply what you learned as you read, you’re set up and ready to start meeting new customers.
Over time, you’ll learn what works best for your business and what Thumbtack customers look for in a pro. So keep refining your matches on your Services page, tweak your messages, and change up your profile regularly.
As you get comfortable on Thumbtack, we’ll be here for you along the way. Check out Thumbtack Help any time you have a question or want to learn more.
Eager to keep learning? Don’t stop here, check out these resources.
Build your brand: In this course, learn the basics of building your brand for online audiences.
Get ready to grow: Learn how the tools on Thumbtack can help you grow and expand your business.
Connect with the Thumbtack Community: Built by pros for pros, it’s a place to network, share resources, and exchange ideas and advice.

articles.fullText:
Refund policy for smarter lead matching
[Image: Pill Pro]
With smarter lead matching, you have added protections if a lead isn't the right fit for your business. This article covers the refund situations specific to smarter lead matching. For other refund situations (like a job that falls outside your calendar availability) see our Refund policy for pros.
How it works
Some refunds are automatic and are triggered when you decline a lead. For others, you'll need to request a refund for our team to look into.
Refund criteria and steps
You may qualify for a refund with smarter lead matching if:
 The job doesn't match your skills
If you receive a lead for work you don't do, decline it and select Not what I do as your reason.
App
Open the Thumbtack Pro app.
Tap Jobs (from the main menu below).
Open the lead.
Select Can’t do it.
Tap Yes, decline.
Let us know why you declined the job by selecting Not what I do and explain why.
Answer a few clarifying questions to help us understand the types of jobs you want.
Confirm if the new preference is correct.
Desktop
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Go to your Jobs.
Open the lead.
Select Can’t do it.
Click Yes, decline.
Let us know why you declined the job by selecting Not what I do and explain why.
Answer a few clarifying questions to help us understand the types of jobs you want.
Confirm if the new preference is correct.
If you confirm the suggested preference, we'll issue an automatic refund for the lead you just declined and apply that preference to your future leads.
You get a duplicate lead from the same customer
If the same customer contacts you again — whether it's about the same job or a different one — you can request a refund for the duplicate contact.
Other refund situations
Situations like an invalid customer phone number, a lead that violates our Terms of Use, or a job that falls outside your calendar availability aren't specific to smarter lead matching — see our Refund policy for pros for those.
Tip
The Can’t do it option is available only if you haven’t already chosen to reply to the customer. If you already replied to the customer but realize it’s a job you can’t do, request a refund through the typical process instead.
What happens next
Most refund requests are reviewed within 24-48 hours. If a situation needs further review, it can take up to four days. Once approved, refunds are added to your Thumbtack balance to use on future leads.
You can track a refund request the same way you would any other Thumbtack refund. See How to request a refund for steps and what each status means.
Frequently asked questions
Am I guaranteed a refund if I decline a lead?
Selecting Not what I do and completing the decline flow makes you eligible for an automatic refund in most cases. But if you've already replied to the customer, your request is reviewed by our team and may take more time.
How long does a refund take?
Once you confirm your new preference, automatic refunds are processed immediately. For refund requests submitted outside of the lead declining process, most reviews are completed within 24–48 hours. If a situation needs further review, the review can take up to four days.
Will declining a lead affect the leads I get in the future?
Yes. When you select Not what I do, we use your explanation to build a new preference that helps us avoid sending you similar leads going forward.
Can I undo a preference created from a decline?
Once you confirm a new preference, it can't be edited for 45 days. In the meantime, you can still manage your other job preferences from the “Refine your matches” section on your Services page.

articles.fullText:
What is smarter lead matching?
[Image: Pill Pro]
Note
Some pros have AI-powered matching. Check your Services page — if you see Refine your matches under your trade, this article applies to you. If you don't see that option, this experience isn't currently available for your account.
Smarter lead matching uses AI to match you with the jobs you're best suited for It has a deeper understanding of the work you do, so we can connect you with higher-quality leads and the right customers. As you give feedback on the leads you get, you teach us how to give you better matches over time.
How it works
Here's what you need to know about how smarter lead matching works for your business:
AI-powered matching: We start with the details you shared when you signed up to find your initial matches. As you interact with leads (we’ll explain what this means below), our AI learns your specific preferences. This ensures that we can connect you with more of the right customers.
Refine your matches: View and manage what our AI has learned about your business anytime. You can adjust your job types to better match the kinds of jobs you want.
Set your lead prices: You'll set one price range for an entire trade. We use the estimated job value to determine the final cost of the lead — ensuring a fair price for high-value jobs versus smaller, simpler ones.
Stronger protections and refunds: If you receive a lead that isn't a fit for your skills, select Can’t do it and choose Not what I do as the reason. We’ll issue a refund, and our lead matching system will learn from what you shared — leading to higher quality leads over time.
Tip
We’ve set default lead price ranges to get you started. Adjust your prices for each trade to stay in control of what you pay. Keep in mind that a higher maximum lead price helps you stay competitive for the jobs you want most.
How to improve my matched leads
With each new lead, you can either reply to the customer or tell us that you can’t do the job (and why). Providing this feedback is the best way to get better leads faster.
Receiving a new lead
If you receive a lead that doesn't fit your skills, follow these steps to decline it:
App
Open the Thumbtack Pro app.
Tap Jobs (from the main menu below).
Open the lead.
Select Can’t do it.
Tap Yes, decline.
Let us know why you declined the job by selecting Not what I do and explain why.
Answer a few clarifying questions to help us understand the types of jobs you want.
Confirm if the new preference is correct.
Desktop
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Go to your Jobs.
Open the lead.
Select Can’t do it.
Click Yes, decline.
Let us know why you declined the job by selecting Not what I do and explain why.
Answer a few clarifying questions to help us understand the types of jobs you want.
Confirm if the new preference is correct.
When you confirm the new preference is correct, we'll apply it to your future leads and refund the lead you just declined.
Tip
The Can’t do it option is available only if you haven’t already chosen to reply to the customer. If you already replied to the customer but realize it’s a job you can’t do, request a refund through the typical process instead.
Adjusting learned matches
You can adjust your learned matches by following these steps:
App
Open the Thumbtack Pro app.
Tap Services (from the main menu below).
Scroll down to the trade you want to edit and select the option to Refine your matches.
Tap Add to search for types of jobs you want to see more (or less) of. Or tap X to remove a job from either list.
Desktop
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Go to your Services.
Scroll down to the trade you want to edit and select the option to Refine your matches.
Tap Add to search for types of jobs you want to see more (or less) of. Or tap X to remove a job from either list.
Tip
If you want to remove a preference that was learned from a refund request, you’ll need to wait 45 days before you can remove it.
Tune up your lead matches periodically
In addition to refining your lead matches anytime, we'll check in periodically to see how your recent leads are going. Reviewing your recent leads helps us keep your matches up to date and improve the types of jobs you're matched with. We may also credit your account for sharing your feedback.
For each job type, use the slider to tell us whether you want more or fewer leads like it — you don't need to change every one, just the ones that feel off. If you're active in more than one trade, you'll go through them one at a time. We'll use your answers to improve the leads you get.
Manage your lead prices
Set one price range per trade to control what you pay for leads.
App
Open theThumbtack Pro app.
Tap Services (from the main menu below).
Tap Lead prices.
Adjust the slider for each trade — moving it left means fewer, lower-cost leads; moving it right means more, higher-cost leads.
Tap Save.
Desktop
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Go to your Services.
Tap Lead prices.
Adjust the slider for each trade — moving it left means fewer, lower-cost leads; moving it right means more, higher-cost leads.
Click Save.
Within your range, the price of any specific lead depends on the job details — higher-value jobs cost more, while simpler jobs cost less. Tap Why lead prices vary on the Lead prices page for trade-specific examples.
When you get a new lead, you'll see a "What you paid" breakdown showing your price range at the time the lead came in, the lead cost, any discount that applied, and the total.
Enhanced protections
You have extra protections, on top of our standard refund policy, to ensure you only pay for the jobs you want.
Skill mismatch refund: If a job doesn't match your skills, let us know by declining the new lead and selecting Not what I do. We'll make it right by refunding you.
Duplicate customer refund: If the same customer contacts you, you can request a refund (regardless of whether it's for the same job or not).
See our Refund policy for smarter lead matching for full eligibility details and timing.
What's next
Here’s how to set yourself up for success with smarter lead matching:
Update your lead prices: Lead price ranges for trades are initially set at a default amount, make sure to update them.
Refine your lead matches: To get better tailored leads faster, review and add job types you want more (or less) of.
Adjust your travel areas: Manage where you work for all your trades from your business profile.
Frequently asked questions
I can't find the type of job I do. What can I do?
If you don't see the job type you're looking for when refining your matches, let us know:
App
Open theThumbtack Pro app.
Tap Services (from the main menu below).
Scroll down to the trade you want to edit and select the option to Refine your matches.
Tap Add to search for types of jobs you want to see more.
If it's not listed, select Can't find the job type you need? Tell us and describe what you're looking for.
Tap Submit feedback.
Desktop
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Go to your Services.
Scroll down to the trade you want to edit and select the option to Refine your matches.
Tap Add to search for types of jobs you want to see more (or less) of.
If it's not listed, select Can't find the job type you need? Tell us and describe what you're looking for.
Click Submit feedback.
Your suggestion will be reviewed by our team, though it won't be added right away.
When your job types can't capture every detail about the work you do, use your business profile to set clear expectations. State any specific limitations or specialties to save time and make sure the right customers reach out.
How do I add a new trade to my account?
You can add a new trade to your profile from your Services page:
App
Open theThumbtack Pro app.
Tap Services (from the main menu below).
Tap the three-dot menu (on the top right corner).
Select Add a trade.
In the search bar, type the trade you want to provide (we'll suggest a few based on what you enter).
Choose the trade you want to add from the drop-down menu.
Tap Add trade.
Desktop
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Go to your Services.
Click the three-dot menu (on the top right corner).
Select Add a trade.
In the search bar, type the trade you want to provide (we'll suggest a few based on what you enter).
Choose the trade you want to add from the drop-down menu.
Click Next below.
Click Add trade.
After adding a new trade, be sure to:
Refine your matches: Add job types you’ll likely want (or don’t want) for the new trade. You'll be matched with leads based on those job types, so set it up for the work you always want to do.
Review your lead prices: Check and set your price range for the new trade.
Review your budget: Your weekly budget covers leads across all of your trades — so make sure it's still enough to get the leads you want.
What am I actually charged for a lead
You're only charged when a customer messages you directly about a job. When those customers reach out, you're covered by our Quality Commitment. Once a customer reaches out, it's up to you to respond quickly and win the job. Learn more about getting hired with your messages.

¿Qué es la pestaña Apps?
[Image: Pill Pro (Spanish)]
La pestaña Apps (“Aplicaciones”) es el lugar central para las aplicaciones disponibles en Thumbtack. Aquí puede explorar las aplicaciones disponibles, conectarlas a su cuenta y consultar su estado.
Cómo encontrar sus aplicaciones
App
Abra la aplicación Thumbtack Pro.
Seleccione Profile (“Perfil”) en el menú principal inferior.
Seleccione el ícono de engranaje (en la esquina superior derecha).
Seleccione Apps & Integrations (“Aplicaciones e Integraciones”).
Computadora
Inicie sesión en su cuenta de Thumbtack.
Haga clic en Apps (“Aplicaciones”), en la parte superior de la página.
Desde aquí, puede conectarse a una nueva aplicación, consultar el estado de sus integraciones activas o configurar un webhook personalizado.
Cómo usar la pestaña Apps
Una vez que esté en la pestaña Apps, verá algunas secciones. Esto es lo que puede hacer en cada una.
Aplicaciones conectadas
Aquí puede ver sus aplicaciones activas y lo que hacen. Esta sección solo aparece cuando ha vinculado al menos una aplicación a su cuenta de Thumbtack.
Estado: Las conexiones activas aparecen como Connected (“Conectado”). Si algo no funciona, verá el estado Error en su lugar.
Qué se comparte: El tipo de datos que se comparten, como prospectos o mensajes, aparece debajo de la integración (por ejemplo, “Los prospectos y mensajes de Thumbtack se están enviando a su cuenta”).
Tip
¿Quiere conectar una nueva aplicación? Los pasos varían según la aplicación que esté conectando. También puede conectarse mediante un webhook en una computadora.
Sus aplicaciones destacadas
Estas son aplicaciones destacadas que usted no ha conectado. Seleccione una aplicación y luego Learn more (“Más información”), o vea la lista completa de aplicaciones de socios en nuestro Marketplace.
¿No ve la aplicación que usa?
Si su aplicación no aparece en nuestro Marketplace, deberá usar una opción personalizada. Esta sección le ofrece recursos para crear esas opciones personalizadas.
Para conocer los pasos para configurar, probar o solucionar problemas con un webhook, consulte este artículo.
Preguntas frecuentes
¿Cómo desconecto una aplicación?
Deberá desconectarla directamente desde la aplicación o el sitio web del socio, no desde Thumbtack. Para conocer los pasos, visite el centro de ayuda de la aplicación.
¿Cómo desconecto un webhook?
A diferencia de las aplicaciones de socios, puede eliminar un webhook directamente desde su pestaña Apps (“Aplicaciones”). Seleccione Manage webhooks (“Administrar webhooks”) en una computadora y luego elimine el webhook que ya no necesite.
No veo la aplicación que uso. ¿Qué puedo hacer?
Consulte las opciones de webhook o del portal para desarrolladores en la sección Don't see an app you use? (“¿No ve la aplicación que usa?”), o comuníquese con nosotros para que podamos ayudarle.
Nota: Este contenido ha sido traducido del inglés solo por conveniencia. La traducción no tiene efectos jurídicos y no debe basarse en ella. Consulte la versión en inglés en help.thumbtack.com.
¿Necesita ayuda? ¡Estamos aquí para usted!
¿Necesita ayuda? Contáctenos a través de nuestra página de soporte. ¡Únase a nuestra comunidad! Conéctese con otros profesionales en la comunidad de Thumbtack en español. Comparta sus experiencias, haga preguntas y encuentre consejos útiles.

articles.fullText:
What is the Apps tab?
[Image: Pill Pro]
The Apps tab is your home for the apps available on Thumbtack. Here, you can browse available apps, connect them to your account, and check their status.
How to find your apps
App
Open the Thumbtack Pro app.
Tap Profile (from the main menu below).
Tap the gear icon (in the top right corner).
Tap Apps & Integrations.
Desktop
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Click Apps (at the top of the page).
From here, you can connect to a new app, check the status of your active integrations, or set up a custom webhook.
How to use the Apps tab
Once you’re on the Apps tab, you’ll see a few sections. Here’s what you can do in each.
Apps connected
This is where you can see your live apps and what they do. This section only shows once you’ve linked at least one app to your Thumbtack account.
Status: Active connections show as Connected. If something’s wrong, you’ll see an Error status instead.
What’s shared: The type of data being shared, like leads or messages, is listed under the integration (for example, “Thumbtack leads and messages are being sent to your account”).
Tip
Want to connect a new app? The steps vary depending on which app you’re connecting. You can also connect via webhook on a desktop.
Your top apps
These are featured apps that you haven’t connected. Select an app to Learn more, or see the full list of partner apps on our marketplace.
Don’t see an app you use?
If your app isn’t listed in our marketplace, you’ll use a custom option. This section gives you resources to build those custom options.
For steps to set up, test, or troubleshoot a webhook, check out this article.
Frequently asked questions
How do I disconnect an app?
You’ll need to disconnect it directly through the partner’s app or website, not through Thumbtack. For steps, visit the app’s help center.
How do I disconnect a webhook?
Unlike partner apps, you can delete a webhook directly from your Apps tab. Select Manage webhooks on a desktop, then delete the webhook you no longer need.
I don’t see the app I use. What can I do?
Check out the webhook or developer portal options in the “Don’t see an app you use?” section, or reach out to us so we can help.

1. Overview
▶ KA Summary
[start of summary]
This internal knowledge article (KA) provides Frontline Reps with details on the Project Tab experiment. It covers the transition from the legacy "Plan" tab to the new "Projects" tab, the deprecation of the Your team tab, and how to address customer inquiries about these changes
[end of summary]

Customer
What the Project Tab experiment is
Starting August 3, 2026, Thumbtack will launch a Customer A/B test, updating the "Plan" tab to a new "Projects" tab on both web and native (app) platforms.
Why Thumbtack is running the experiment
▶ Internal why
Customer research showed that "Projects" is a stronger match for how customers describe their work. The legacy Home Care modules (like goals and insights) see under 1.3% engagement, and the Your team tab drives minimal usage. Clearing this content frees up space for future project guidance and re-engagement work.]
External-facing why: Customers told us they think of this work as projects, not plans. We renamed and cleaned up this tab to make it easier to manage your active projects in one place.
How the experiment works
For customers assigned to the variant, a renamed Projects tab appears in their main navigation (previously the Plan tab). This tab continues to support managing active projects, but legacy Home Care-era features and the dedicated Your team tab have been removed.
What the updated main menu looks like

[Image: rtaImage]

Experiment details
This section provides details about the Project Tab experiment, including assignment, launch dates, and expected impact.
Launch date: August 3, 2026
Anticipated end date: Approximately 3 weeks after launch.
Important Note: End date has not been finalized. Experiment timelines are fluid and may be extended, concluded early, or shipped permanently based on results. Details will be shared closer to this date.
Who is included: All Home page (Web) and Explore page (Native) visitors (50/50 split, ~8,061,854 expected sample size)
Markets/Location: All markets
Internal name: Project Tab V0 (2026_07_project_tab_v0)
External name: Projects tab
Priority level: P2 — Low impact, medium priority
How to identify impacted users
Frontline Reps can confirm whether a customer is included in this experiment using either of the following methods:
Check "Experiment assignments" in the customer's profile (preferred method) to see whether they're assigned to this experiment.
Log in as the customer and check whether they see the Projects tab (variant) or the "Plan" tab (baseline) in their primary navigation.

[Image: rtaImage]

Customer experience
Baseline experience (Customer)
In the baseline experience, customers use the Plan tab in the primary navigation. This tab includes legacy Home Care-era content such as Insights, "Your goals this year," and an "Add projects" call to action (CTA). Additionally, customers have access to a separate Your team tab to manage pro relationships.
Reps can refer to the Customer App Features: Home Profile, Plan Tab and Team Tab (Customer) KA for a closer look. 

Experiment experience (Customer)
In the experiment variant, the Plan tab is renamed to Projects (with a "Your projects" header on the app). Projects are grouped by simplified plain-language statuses like "Waiting for a response" or "Completed," rather than legacy Home Care statuses. The "Insights" and "Your goals this year" sections, along with the "Add projects" CTA, are fully removed. The entire "Your team" tab is also removed.

[Image: rtaImage]

2. Process
Steps: How to help a customer manage pro relationships without the Your team tab (Rep)
Frontline Reps can walk customers through the following steps to find pro relationships without the deprecated Your team tab:
Navigate to the new Projects tab.
Select the specific in-progress or past project.
View and manage pro relationships from within the individual project hub.
3. Talking points 
Frontline Reps can use the following externally approved talking points when navigating conversations with customers regarding the missing tabs.

English talking point
Q: Why did the "Plan" tab change to "Projects"?
A: We want to make it easier to find and manage your active projects in one place. The name "Projects" better matches what the tab actually helps you do.
Q: What happened to "Your team"?
A: The separate "Your team" tab has been removed. Instead, you can see and manage your pro relationships from within each project.
Q: Did I lose any of my saved goals or insights?
A: The "Insights" and "Your goals this year" sections have been removed from this tab as part of the update. Your active and past projects are still there, organized by status.
Q: How do I find my in-progress vs. past projects now?
A: Your Projects tab now groups projects by status (for example, if it’s “in progress” and “past”), so it's easier to see what needs your attention versus what's already done.
4. Resources
Frontline Reps will find a collection of valuable resources in this section, including links to internal knowledge articles, external Help Center articles, and other relevant documentation. These resources may be referenced in the article or provide additional, related information. Frontline reps can use these resources to help customers with navigating the new Projects tab.

How to pay a pro
[Image: Pill Customer]
You pay the pro directly, in the way you both agree on. Here's how it works.
Agree on payment with the pro
Every pro handles payment a little differently. Before the work begins, chat with the pro in your Inbox to agree on:
How you'll pay. For example, check or a payment app (like Venmo or Zelle).
When you'll pay. All at once when the work is done, or in parts as the job moves along (like a deposit and final payment).
The total cost. Ask what's included, and what could add to the price.
Tip
Many pros list the payment methods they take on their profile, and some share starting price details in their Business FAQs. That can give you an idea of cost, but always finalize the cost with the pro about your specific job.
Paying an invoice
Some pros send invoices through Thumbtack. The invoice shows you the payment methods the pro takes, and you pay them directly (for example, through Venmo or by check). If the pro sends you one, we'll let you know. You can see these invoices in your messages with the pro.
Follow these steps to open the invoice from your messages:
App
Open the Thumbtack app.
Tap Inbox (from the main menu below).
Tap the conversation with the pro.
Tap View invoice details.
Desktop
Log in to your Thumbtack account.
Select Inbox.
Select the conversation with the pro.
Select View invoice details.
The invoice shows the total amount and lets you pick how to pay. When you select a payment method, you'll see the pro's payment details, like their username, email, or a QR code you can scan. Then you pay them directly in the payment app. If the pro takes checks, the invoice shows you who to make the check payable to.
Tip
On-Demand bookings work a little differently. You pay for those through Thumbtack, and your card is charged once the job is done.
Keep your payments safe
There are things you can do to keep your payments safe, like putting your agreement in writing, and keeping track of each payment. For the full list, review our safety tips for paying a pro before your project starts.
Ready to start your next project?
[Button: Find a pro]
Frequently asked questions
How do I pay my pro?
You pay your pro directly, using the method you agree on. On-Demand bookings are the exception. You pay those through Thumbtack.
What payment methods do pros take?
It varies by pro. Common options include check or payment apps (like Venmo, Zelle, PayPal, or Square). Check the pro's profile or ask them in your messages.
Should I pay a deposit before the work starts?
Some pros ask for a deposit, especially for large projects. If you pay one, ask about the pro's refund policy and keep your receipt.
